en.question: What happens to your medical care if you are in an accident and are a registered organ donor?

choices.A: Doctors will prioritize organ preservation over saving your life.
choices.B: The number one priority is to save your life.
choices.C: You will be transferred to a special organ donor hospital.
choices.D: Your family must pay for your emergency medical care.

en.explanation: The manual states that it is a myth that becoming a donor affects medical care. The fact is: 'If you are admitted to a hospital, the number one priority is to save your life.'

en.question: What symbol will appear on your Alabama driver license if you choose to be an organ donor?

choices.A: A green ribbon
choices.B: A red cross
choices.C: A red heart
choices.D: A blue star

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'The title "organ donor" with a red heart will appear on your license.'

en.question: According to the manual, approximately how often is someone added to the national organ transplant waiting list?

choices.A: Every minute
choices.B: Every 10 minutes
choices.C: Every hour
choices.D: Every day

en.explanation: The manual states that 'Someone is added to the list every ten minutes, and approximately 18 people will die each day while waiting for an organ.'

en.question: If you agree to donate your organs, what is the financial cost to your family or estate for the donation?

choices.A: A flat fee of $500
choices.B: The cost of the removal operation
choices.C: Half of the funeral costs
choices.D: There is no financial cost for organ or tissue donation

en.explanation: The manual clarifies a common myth by stating: 'There is no financial cost to the donor’s family or estate for organ or tissue donation.'

en.question: Which agency issues driver licenses in Alabama?

choices.A: Department of Transportation
choices.B: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency, Driver License Services
choices.C: Department of Motor Vehicles
choices.D: Highway Safety Office

en.explanation: Chapter 1 of the manual states, 'The Alabama Law Enforcement Agency, Driver License Services, issues driver licenses.'

en.question: An applicant whose Alabama driver license has been expired for over how many years must pass the required driver examination?

choices.A: One year
choices.B: Two years
choices.C: Three years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: The manual states, 'All applicants who have not been licensed in Alabama or whose Alabama license has been expired for over three years must pass the required driver examination.'

en.question: If you hold a valid out-of-state driver license that has not been expired for over one year, what are you exempt from when applying for an Alabama license?

choices.A: Paying the license fee
choices.B: Passing a driver examination
choices.C: The vision screening
choices.D: Providing identification

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'A holder of an out of state license which has not been expired over one year does not have to pass a driver examination.'

en.question: Which of the following vehicles may be operated temporarily on an Alabama highway without a driver license?

choices.A: A commercial delivery truck
choices.B: A farm tractor
choices.C: A motorcycle
choices.D: A recreational vehicle (RV)

en.explanation: The manual lists exemptions to the driver license requirement, including 'Any person while driving any farm tractor or implement of husbandry temporarily operated or moved on the highway.'

en.question: Do military personnel from other states stationed in Alabama need to obtain an Alabama driver license?

choices.A: Yes, within 30 days of arriving in Alabama.
choices.B: Yes, unless they live on a military base.
choices.C: No, as long as they are at least 16 and have a valid driver license from their home state.
choices.D: No, military personnel are completely exempt from needing any driver license.

en.explanation: An Alabama driver license is not required for 'A resident at least 16 years old who has in his immediate possession a valid driver license issued to him in his home state or country. This includes military personnel from other states and their families stationed in Alabama...'

en.question: A non-resident who has a valid driver license from their previous state of residence may drive without an Alabama license for how many days after becoming an Alabama resident?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: The manual states that 'A non-resident who has a valid driver license from the state of previous residence may drive without an Alabama license for 30 days after becoming a resident of the state.'

en.question: A non-resident at least 16 years old from a country that does not require licensing may drive in Alabama for up to how many days in a calendar year?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: The manual states that a non-resident from a country without licensing requirements may operate a motor vehicle 'for not more than 90 days in any calendar year, if the vehicle operated is duly registered for the current year in the home country...'

en.question: Which of the following non-residents is permitted to drive in Alabama without an Alabama driver license?

choices.A: A part-time student with no home state license
choices.B: A full-time student properly enrolled in an Alabama school who holds a valid license from their home state
choices.C: A tourist who has been in the state for 120 days
choices.D: A person whose out-of-state license was recently suspended

en.explanation: An Alabama license is not required for 'Any non-resident full time student properly enrolled and registered in a school, college, university, or trade school in this state, who holds a valid license from his home state or country.'

en.question: Under Alabama law, a driver license shall NOT be issued to any person under what age?

choices.A: 14 years of age
choices.B: 15 years of age
choices.C: 16 years of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: The 'Who Cannot Be Licensed' section explicitly states that an Alabama driver license shall not be issued to 'Persons under 16 years of age.'

en.question: Can you obtain an Alabama driver license if your driving privilege is suspended or revoked in another state?

choices.A: Yes, if the suspension was for a minor offense.
choices.B: Yes, after paying an out-of-state transfer fee.
choices.C: No, a license shall not be issued to anyone whose driving rights are suspended or revoked in any state.
choices.D: No, unless you pass the Alabama road test again.

en.explanation: The manual states that an Alabama driver license shall not be issued to 'Any person whose driving rights or privilege is suspended or revoked in any state.'

en.question: An Alabama driver license will not be issued to a person if they have a physical or mental impairment that:

choices.A: Requires them to wear glasses while driving.
choices.B: Prevents them from safely operating a motor vehicle in the opinion of the ALEA or examining officer.
choices.C: Requires them to drive an automatic transmission vehicle.
choices.D: Prevents them from passing a physical fitness test.

en.explanation: A license shall not be issued to 'Any person afflicted with or suffering from a physical or mental impairment which, in the opinion of the ALEA or examining officer, will prevent [them from safely operating a motor vehicle].'

en.question: According to Alabama law, a person under the age of 19 cannot be licensed if they are not in compliance with which requirement?

choices.A: Voter registration
choices.B: Secondary school graduation or current attendance
choices.C: Selective Service registration
choices.D: Employment verification

en.explanation: An Alabama driver license shall not be issued to any person under the age of 19 that is not in compliance with Alabama Act 93-368, which requires secondary school graduation or current attendance.

en.question: If an applicant for an Alabama Driver License presents exactly two forms of identification, what must be true about these documents?

choices.A: Both documents must contain a photograph.
choices.B: At least one must contain a photograph and one must be from the 'Primary Listing'.
choices.C: Both documents must be from the 'Secondary Listing'.
choices.D: Neither is required to have a photograph if they are notarized.

en.explanation: Applicants must present two forms of identification, at least one of which contains a photograph, and one form must be from the 'Primary Listing'.

en.question: What documentation must an applicant transferring an out-of-state driver license present?

choices.A: Their out-of-state license, Social Security card, and one other form from the 'Primary Listing'
choices.B: Only their out-of-state license and a birth certificate
choices.C: Three forms of non-photo identification
choices.D: Their out-of-state license and a high school diploma

en.explanation: Applicants transferring an Out of State driver license must present their Out of State driver license, Social Security card (or acceptable document) AND one other form from the 'Primary Listing'.

en.question: Which of the following would make a document unacceptable for proving identification?

choices.A: It is an original document.
choices.B: It is a copy certified by the issuing agency.
choices.C: Correction fluid (white-out) has been used on pertinent information.
choices.D: It is printed on colored paper.

en.explanation: A document would be unacceptable if correction fluid (white-out) has been used on pertinent information, among other alterations or damages.

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable document to prove your Social Security Number?

choices.A: A utility bill with your name on it
choices.B: A W2 Tax Form
choices.C: A library card
choices.D: A current lease agreement

en.explanation: An original W2 Tax Form is listed as one of the acceptable documents required as proof of a Social Security number.

en.question: For a notarized document to be accepted, the notary's commission expiration date must be:

choices.A: Within the next 30 days
choices.B: Legible and current on the date the document was notarized
choices.C: Valid for at least one year from the date of application
choices.D: Left blank

en.explanation: Notarized documents must meet several requirements, including that the complete date the notary's commission expires must be legible and must have been current on the date the document was notarized.

en.question: How much allowable time remaining in the United States must immigration documents reflect to be acceptable?

choices.A: At least 30 days
choices.B: At least 60 days
choices.C: At least 90 days
choices.D: At least 160 days

en.explanation: Immigration documents must reflect at least 160 days allowable time remaining in the United States.

en.question: All applicants under the age of 19 must present which of the following forms?

choices.A: A current Student Enrollment/Exclusion Form (DL-1-93)
choices.B: A signed parental consent waiver
choices.C: A medical clearance form
choices.D: A proof of employment form

en.explanation: All applicants under the age of 19 must present a current Student Enrollment/Exclusion Form (DL-1-93) completed and signed by authorized personnel.

en.question: What specific document is required for all 15-year-old applicants to prove their date of birth?

choices.A: A school ID with photo
choices.B: A Certified U.S. Birth Certificate issued by a designated agency
choices.C: A Social Security Card
choices.D: A W2 Tax Form

en.explanation: A Certified U.S. Birth Certificate issued by an agency designated by state or federal authority is required for all 15-year-old applicants under Title 36-6-8(b).

en.question: How are driver license written examinations administered to hearing impaired applicants?

choices.A: Through a live interpreter provided by the applicant
choices.B: Using automated testing equipment in American Sign Language
choices.C: By reading a braille version of the test
choices.D: By watching a closed-captioned video

en.explanation: Written examinations can be administered to the hearing impaired in American Sign Language using automated testing equipment at certain Driver License offices.

en.question: Who is eligible to take an Oral Examination for their driver's license?

choices.A: Any applicant who prefers speaking over writing
choices.B: Applicants who are unable to read and comprehend the knowledge tests
choices.C: Only applicants transferring an out-of-state license
choices.D: Only applicants under the age of 16

en.explanation: Oral Examinations are available for applicants that are unable to read and comprehend the knowledge tests.

en.question: At what age may a person obtain a restricted Learner License in Alabama?

choices.A: 14 years old
choices.B: 15 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: Any person 15 years of age may obtain a restricted Learner License for the purpose of learning to safely and effectively operate a motor vehicle.

en.question: The 'Y' restriction on a Class D Alabama driver license indicates that the holder may operate a motor vehicle only while accompanied by a person who is at least:

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 19 years old
choices.C: 21 years old
choices.D: 25 years old

en.explanation: The 'Y' restriction indicates that the holder may operate a motor vehicle while accompanied by a person who is 21 years old.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a 'Primary Document' for identification purposes?

choices.A: Marriage License
choices.B: Current U.S. Passport
choices.C: Medical Insurance ID Card
choices.D: Selective Service Card

en.explanation: A current US Passport is listed under 'PRIMARY DOCUMENTS', whereas Marriage Licenses, Medical Insurance ID Cards, and Selective Service Cards are 'SECONDARY DOCUMENTS'.

en.question: If an applicant has been previously deported from the United States, what additional documentation must they present?

choices.A: A letter of recommendation from a U.S. citizen
choices.B: Proof from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that their legal presence status has been restored
choices.C: A valid foreign driver's license
choices.D: A certificate of naturalization

en.explanation: An applicant who has been deported from the United States must present proof from the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that their legal presence status has been restored.

en.question: What does a 'Y' restriction on a Class D Alabama driver license indicate?

choices.A: The holder must wear corrective lenses while driving.
choices.B: The holder may operate a motor driven cycle only.
choices.C: The holder may operate a motor vehicle with a licensed driver occupying the seat beside them.
choices.D: The holder is restricted to driving during daylight hours only.

en.explanation: According to the manual, the 'Y' restriction indicates that the holder may operate a motor vehicle with a licensed driver occupying the seat beside the driver.

en.question: How long must a person who is 16 but under 18 years of age hold a Learner License before they can take the road test for a regular driver license?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months or until their 18th birthday
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: The manual states that a person 16 but under 18 years of age must have held a Learner License for six months or until their 18th birthday before taking the road test.

en.question: A 14 or 15-year-old may obtain a restricted license to operate a motor driven cycle that does not exceed what weight and engine displacement?

choices.A: 200 pounds and 150cc
choices.B: 250 pounds and 200cc
choices.C: 300 pounds and 250cc
choices.D: 150 pounds and 100cc

en.explanation: The manual states that a 14 or 15-year-old may obtain a restricted license to operate a motor driven cycle weighing not more than 200 pounds, nor exceeding 150cc engine displacement.

en.question: What restriction is placed on a Class M Alabama driver license issued to a 14 or 15-year-old for a motor driven cycle?

choices.A: A 'Y' restriction
choices.B: A 'B' restriction
choices.C: An 'M' restriction
choices.D: An 'A' restriction

en.explanation: Upon passing the required examination, a 14 or 15-year-old applicant will be issued a Class M Alabama driver license with a 'B' restriction, indicating they may operate a motor driven cycle only.

en.question: At what age may a person obtain an Alabama vessel license upon passing the required examination?

choices.A: 10 years of age or older
choices.B: 12 years of age or older
choices.C: 14 years of age or older
choices.D: 16 years of age or older

en.explanation: The manual specifies that any person 12 years of age or older may obtain a vessel license upon passing the required vessel examination.

en.question: What is the fee for taking the driver license knowledge test in Alabama?
en.explanation: The fee for each knowledge test is $5.00, and no checks are accepted.

en.question: Who must accompany a 16-year-old applicant when they take the road test?

choices.A: A licensed driving instructor
choices.B: Any licensed driver over 21
choices.C: A parent or guardian
choices.D: No one is required to accompany them

en.explanation: The manual states that sixteen-year-old applicants must be accompanied by a parent or guardian for the road test.

en.question: Does a 17-year-old applicant need to be accompanied by a parent or guardian for the road test?

choices.A: Yes, all applicants under 18 require a parent or guardian.
choices.B: Yes, unless they have completed driver's education.
choices.C: No, a 17-year-old applicant doesn't have to be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
choices.D: No, but they must be accompanied by a licensed driving instructor.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a seventeen-year-old applicant doesn't have to be accompanied by a parent or guardian for the road test.

en.question: Which of the following will cause an immediate failure and termination of the road test?

choices.A: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
choices.B: A dangerous action
choices.C: Parking slightly crooked
choices.D: Driving a vehicle with a manual transmission

en.explanation: Causes for immediate failure and termination of the road test include a violation of a traffic law, a dangerous action, any preventable accident, or a lack of cooperation/refusal to perform a maneuver.

en.question: Who is permitted to ride in the vehicle as a passenger during your road test?

choices.A: A parent or guardian
choices.B: A licensed driving instructor
choices.C: A friend or sibling
choices.D: No passengers or pets are permitted

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that no passengers or pets are permitted in the vehicle during the road test.

en.question: What may happen if you operate a motor vehicle in violation of the restrictions imposed on your driver license?

choices.A: You will be required to retake the knowledge test.
choices.B: You will receive a warning letter.
choices.C: It may result in the loss of your license.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be permanently confiscated.

en.explanation: The manual states that operation of a motor vehicle in violation of restrictions may result in the loss of your license.

en.question: Which of the following is required equipment for the vehicle used during the road test?

choices.A: A backup camera
choices.B: Two separate methods of applying brakes
choices.C: A GPS navigation system
choices.D: Custom window tinting

en.explanation: The equipment required for the examination includes a rear view mirror, horn, windshield wipers, two separate methods of applying brakes, muffler, headlights, rear tail lights, valid license plate, stop light, directional signals, and seat belts.

en.question: How does the Alabama driver manual define a motorcycle?

choices.A: A motor vehicle with four wheels and a saddle
choices.B: A motor vehicle having a seat or saddle, designed to travel on not more than three wheels, excluding a tractor
choices.C: Any two-wheeled vehicle weighing over 500 pounds
choices.D: A motorized bicycle with an engine displacement under 50cc

en.explanation: A motorcycle is defined as a motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the use of the rider and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground but excluding a tractor.

en.question: What happens if you do not pass the vision examination when applying for a license?

choices.A: You are permanently disqualified from driving in Alabama.
choices.B: You must take the road test during daylight hours only.
choices.C: You will be required to have your eyes examined by a licensed eye specialist and return the report.
choices.D: You must pay an additional fee to retake the vision test immediately.

en.explanation: If you don't pass your vision examination, you will be required to have your eyes examined by a licensed eye specialist and return the report to the examiner.

en.question: What should you do to indicate to the examiner that you are aware of conditions around you while backing the vehicle during the road test?

choices.A: Look exclusively at the backup camera screen
choices.B: Honk the horn three times
choices.C: Turn your head and look over your right shoulder
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: During the test, you should turn your head when you observe traffic and look over your right shoulder while backing to indicate to the examiner you are aware of conditions around you.

en.question: What is the minimum age requirement to obtain a Vessel License in Alabama?

choices.A: 12 years old
choices.B: 14 years old
choices.C: 15 years old
choices.D: 16 years old

en.explanation: According to the manual's minimum age requirements table, you must be at least 12 years old to obtain a Vessel License.

en.question: When arriving for your road test, what is required regarding the vehicle you bring?

choices.A: It must be a dual-control training vehicle.
choices.B: It must be driven to the test by a licensed driver.
choices.C: It must be rented from a certified driving school.
choices.D: It must have a gross vehicle weight under 10,000 pounds.

en.explanation: Unless you already have a legal right to drive, you must come for the road test in a vehicle driven by a licensed driver who must remain to drive it away if you fail.

en.question: How long is the grace period during which your Alabama driver license remains valid after its expiration date?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: Alabama law provides a grace period of 60 days after the expiration date of a driver license for renewal purposes, and the license remains valid for this time period.

en.question: How many days do you have to notify the License Services Division after changing your address within Alabama?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: After changing your address within Alabama, you have 30 days in which to notify the License Services Division of the new address.

en.question: Which class of license is generally required for all standard passenger vehicles?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class C
choices.C: Class D
choices.D: Class M

en.explanation: A Class D license is required for generally all passenger vehicles, except vehicles in Classes A, B, C, or M.

en.question: What criminal charges may apply if a person makes a false affidavit to obtain a duplicate driver license?

choices.A: Embezzlement
choices.B: Forgery, Perjury, or both
choices.C: Identity theft only
choices.D: Traffic violation only

en.explanation: Any person making a false affidavit in obtaining a duplicate driver license may be charged with Forgery, Perjury, or both under the Criminal Code of Alabama.

en.question: How long is an Alabama driver license valid before it expires?

choices.A: Two years after it is issued
choices.B: Four years after it is issued
choices.C: Five years after it is issued
choices.D: Eight years after it is issued

en.explanation: Your driver license expires four years after it is issued, and the expiration date is shown on the license.

en.question: What is the fee for taking the Class D Operator knowledge test?
en.explanation: According to the Knowledge Test Fees schedule, the fee for a Class D Operator knowledge test is $5.00.

en.question: A Class A Commercial Driver License (CDL) is required for combination vehicles with a Gross Combination Weight Rating (GCWR) exceeding 26,000 pounds, provided the towed vehicle exceeds what weight?

choices.A: 5,000 pounds
choices.B: 10,000 pounds
choices.C: 15,000 pounds
choices.D: 26,000 pounds

en.explanation: Class A applies to combination vehicles with a GCWR exceeding 26,000 pounds, provided the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of the vehicle being towed exceeds 10,000 pounds.

en.question: A Class C Commercial Driver License is required for vehicles weighing 26,000 lbs or less if they are placarded for hazardous materials or designed to seat more than how many people?

choices.A: 10 people including the driver
choices.B: 12 people including the driver
choices.C: 15 people including the driver
choices.D: 20 people including the driver

en.explanation: Class C licenses are for vehicles weighing 26,000 lbs GVWR or less that are placarded for hazardous materials or designed to seat more than 15 people including the driver.

en.question: If it appears you have a physical or mental impairment affecting your driving, what may you be required to furnish to the state?

choices.A: A new road test fee
choices.B: A statement from a doctor showing your medical history and present condition
choices.C: A certificate of completion from a defensive driving course
choices.D: A signed affidavit from an immediate family member

en.explanation: You may be required to furnish a statement from a doctor showing your medical history and present condition as it pertains to your driving ability if you have a physical or mental impairment.

en.question: Up to how many years after its expiration date can an Alabama driver license be renewed without taking an examination?

choices.A: 1 year
choices.B: 2 years
choices.C: 3 years
choices.D: 4 years

en.explanation: An Alabama driver license may be renewed without examination within a 3-year period after expiration, though it is illegal to operate a vehicle with an expired license.

en.question: What is the minimum age requirement to obtain an Alabama Non-Driver Identification Card?

choices.A: There is no age requirement
choices.B: 12 years old
choices.C: 14 years old
choices.D: 15 years old

en.explanation: According to the minimum age requirements table in the manual, there is 'No Age Requirement' for an Identification Card.

en.question: While you can renew your license online or at a kiosk, what action requires you to see a driver license examiner in person?

choices.A: Paying the renewal fee
choices.B: Updating your digital license on a smartphone
choices.C: Adding or removing license classes, restrictions, and endorsements
choices.D: Requesting a duplicate license after losing the original

en.explanation: The manual states that to change your address or to add or remove license classes, restrictions, and endorsements, you must see a driver license examiner.

en.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) criteria for a single vehicle to require a Class B commercial driver license?

choices.A: Exceeds 10,000 pounds
choices.B: Exceeds 16,000 pounds
choices.C: Exceeds 26,000 pounds
choices.D: Exceeds 32,000 pounds

en.explanation: According to the manual, Class B includes single or combination vehicles where the GVWR of the single vehicle exceeds 26,000 pounds.

en.question: Which CDL endorsement is required to operate a vehicle with double or triple trailers?

choices.A: Endorsement T
choices.B: Endorsement X
choices.C: Endorsement H
choices.D: Endorsement N

en.explanation: The manual states that Endorsement T is required for double/triple trailers.

en.question: At what age may a licensed vessel operator operate a motorized watercraft alone, if they were born after January 1, 2002?

choices.A: 12 years old
choices.B: 14 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 21 years old

en.explanation: The Boating Safety Enhancement Act mandates that a licensed operator, 14 years old or older, may operate alone.

en.question: When operating a motor vehicle in Alabama, when must you present your driver license to a law enforcement officer?

choices.A: Only if you are involved in a crash
choices.B: Only if you are issued a traffic citation
choices.C: Upon his or her request
choices.D: Only at official state border checkpoints

en.explanation: In Alabama, a driver must be prepared to present their driver license to any law enforcement officer upon his or her request.

en.question: What is the minimum reinstatement fee for a person whose driver license has been canceled, suspended, revoked, or disqualified?
en.explanation: Any person whose driver license has been canceled, suspended, revoked, or disqualified must pay a reinstatement fee of not less than $100.

en.question: If your license reinstatement is the result of a drug-related conviction, what is the additional fee required?
en.explanation: The manual states that reinstatement resulting from drug related convictions require an additional $25 fee.

en.question: Which of the following offenses requires the Director to revoke your driver license?

choices.A: Racing on the highways
choices.B: Fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer
choices.C: Three reckless driving convictions within 12 months
choices.D: Failure to maintain SR-22 insurance

en.explanation: The Director must revoke your license upon receiving a record of your conviction for three reckless driving convictions within 12 months. The other choices are grounds for suspension.

en.question: Your driver license may be suspended if you are ages 15 through 18 and do which of the following?

choices.A: Receive one speeding ticket
choices.B: Withdraw from school under certain conditions prior to graduation
choices.C: Drive between midnight and 6 AM
choices.D: Fail to pass a vision test

en.explanation: Your driver license may be suspended if you are ages 15 through 18 and withdraw from school under certain conditions prior to graduation.

en.question: How many points are assessed against your driving record for Reckless Driving or Reckless Endangerment involving a motor vehicle?

choices.A: 2 Points
choices.B: 4 Points
choices.C: 5 Points
choices.D: 6 Points

en.explanation: According to the Alabama Point System, Reckless Driving or Reckless Endangerment involving operating a motor vehicle results in 6 points.

en.question: Passing a stopped school bus will result in how many points being added to your driving record?

choices.A: 3 Points
choices.B: 4 Points
choices.C: 5 Points
choices.D: 6 Points

en.explanation: The Alabama Point System assigns 5 points for Passing Stopped School Bus.

en.question: How many points are assessed for speeding 26 mph or more over the speed limit?

choices.A: 2 Points
choices.B: 3 Points
choices.C: 4 Points
choices.D: 5 Points

en.explanation: Speeding 26 mph or More Over Speed Limit results in 5 points being assessed against your driving record.

en.question: Which of the following violations results in exactly 2 points being assessed to your driving record?

choices.A: Following too closely
choices.B: Failure to yield right of way
choices.C: Improper lane violation
choices.D: Wrong side of road/illegal passing

en.explanation: An Improper Lane Violation is a 2-point offense. Following too closely is 3 points, failure to yield is 5 points, and wrong side of road is 4 points.

en.question: According to the Alabama point system schedule, how long will your license be suspended if you accumulate 15-17 points in a 2-year period?

choices.A: 60 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 120 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: The suspension schedule states that accumulating 15-17 points in a 2-year period results in a 90-day suspension.

en.question: Accumulating 24 or more points in a 2-year period will result in a license suspension of what duration?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: 120 days
choices.C: 180 days
choices.D: 365 days

en.explanation: According to the point system schedule, 24 and above points in a 2-year period results in a 365-day suspension.

en.question: Persons born before what date are exempt from the vessel license examination, but must still have the vessel class issued?

choices.A: January 1, 2002
choices.B: April 28, 1954
choices.C: January 1, 1994
choices.D: April 28, 1984

en.explanation: The manual states that persons born before April 28, 1954 are exempt from examination but are required to go to their driver license office to have vessel class issued.

en.question: How many points are added to your driving record for making an improper turn?

choices.A: 2 Points
choices.B: 3 Points
choices.C: 4 Points
choices.D: 6 Points

en.explanation: According to the manual, making an improper turn results in 2 points being added to your driving record.

en.question: If a driver accumulates 18-20 points in a 2-year period, how long will their driver license be suspended?

choices.A: 60 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 120 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: The suspension schedule states that accumulating 18-20 points in a 2-year period results in a 120-day suspension.

en.question: What must you do before turning the ignition key if you are driving a vehicle equipped with a manual transmission?

choices.A: Depress the brake pedal only
choices.B: Push in the clutch
choices.C: Shift into drive
choices.D: Turn on the parking lights

en.explanation: If you are driving a hand-shift vehicle equipped with a manual transmission, you must push in the clutch before turning the ignition key.

en.question: When starting from a parallel parking place, what should you do before pulling into traffic?

choices.A: Honk your horn to warn approaching vehicles
choices.B: Look over your shoulder and in rear view mirrors
choices.C: Pull out quickly to merge with the flow of traffic
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: In preparing to leave a parallel parking spot, look over your shoulder as well as in rear view mirrors and wait until the way is clear before pulling into traffic.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must signal your intentions before making a turn?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must signal your intentions at least 100 feet before making the turn.

en.question: Why is it recommended to use hand and arm signals in addition to signal lights during the daytime?

choices.A: It is required by state law for all turns
choices.B: Signal lights are automatically disabled during daylight hours
choices.C: Reflection of bright sunlight may make it difficult for other motorists to see flashing signal lights
choices.D: Hand signals are the only legal way to signal a turn

en.explanation: During the daytime, hand and arm signals may be used in addition to signal lights because the reflection of bright sunlight may make it difficult for other motorists to see your flashing signal light.

en.question: When making a left turn from a four-lane or divided highway, which lane should you turn from?

choices.A: The far right lane
choices.B: The lane nearest the center line or traffic divider
choices.C: The shoulder of the road
choices.D: Any lane as long as you signal

en.explanation: For a left turn, move to the lane nearest the center line or traffic divider and turn from the inside lane.

en.question: Where are three-point turns NOT permitted?

choices.A: On residential streets
choices.B: In empty parking lots
choices.C: On curves or near the top of hills where you cannot be seen within 500 feet
choices.D: On any two-lane roadway

en.explanation: Three-point turns are not permitted on interstate freeways, on curves, or near the top of hills where you cannot be seen by drivers of other vehicles approaching from either direction within 500 feet.

en.question: What is the proper technique for driving through a curve?

choices.A: Accelerate before entering the curve and brake while rounding it
choices.B: Maintain a constant high speed throughout the curve
choices.C: Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate slightly when actually rounding it
choices.D: Coast through the curve with the vehicle in neutral

en.explanation: A driver should enter a curve slow enough to enable him to accelerate slightly when actually rounding the curve.

en.question: Under Alabama law, what is the minimum distance a motor vehicle must maintain when passing a person on a bicycle?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 5 feet
choices.D: 6 feet

en.explanation: Alabama state law requires that you pass a person on a bicycle with a distance of not less than three feet between your motor vehicle and the person on a bicycle.

en.question: While bicyclists must generally ride as close as practicable to the right curb, under which situation are they allowed to move away from it?

choices.A: When they want to ride side-by-side with three other bicycles
choices.B: When reasonably necessary to avoid road hazards like debris or opening car doors
choices.C: When they are traveling faster than the speed limit
choices.D: When they are riding on a sidewalk

en.explanation: Bicyclists must ride as close to the right curb as practicable except when reasonably necessary to avoid road or traffic conditions such as debris, opening of car doors, pedestrians, etc.

en.question: What does Alabama law state regarding bicycles on sidewalks?

choices.A: Bicycles must use the sidewalk if the speed limit is over 35 mph
choices.B: Bicycles are allowed on sidewalks if they yield to pedestrians
choices.C: It is illegal for people on bicycles to ride on the sidewalk
choices.D: Only bicycles with training wheels may use the sidewalk

en.explanation: In Alabama, it is illegal for people on bicycles to ride on the sidewalk.

en.question: At what age are people on bicycles required to wear a securely fastened protective helmet in Alabama?

choices.A: Under the age of 12 years
choices.B: Under the age of 16 years
choices.C: Under the age of 18 years
choices.D: All ages are required to wear a helmet

en.explanation: People on bicycles who are under the age of 16 years are required to wear a securely fastened protective helmet when riding on public roadways.

en.question: If a motor vehicle driver needs to turn across an established bicycle lane, what should they do?

choices.A: Turn from the main traffic lane and cut across the bicycle lane quickly
choices.B: Honk to clear the bicycle lane before turning
choices.C: Drive into the bicycle lane prior to making the turn, ensuring it does not encroach upon a bicyclist's safety
choices.D: Stop in the main traffic lane and wait for the bicycle lane to be completely empty for 500 feet

en.explanation: When turning across a bicycle lane, the driver shall drive the motor vehicle into the bicycle lane prior to making the turn and shall make the turn so long as such preparation for a turn shall not encroach upon the safety of the person on the bicycle.

en.question: How many days will your license be suspended if you accumulate 24 or more points in a 2-year period?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: 120 days
choices.C: 180 days
choices.D: 365 days

en.explanation: According to the point schedule, accumulating 24 and above points in a 2-year period results in a 365-day suspension.

en.question: What should you do if the road is narrow and you are unable to safely pass a person on a bicycle?

choices.A: Blast your horn to warn them to move over
choices.B: Pass them closely at a high speed
choices.C: Remain behind them at a safe interval until you can pass safely
choices.D: Flash your high beams until they pull off the road

en.explanation: If the road is narrow and you are unable to safely pass a person on a bicycle, do not follow too closely and do not blast your horn. Remain behind at a safe interval until you are able to pass.

en.question: How does wet weather affect a person riding a bicycle?

choices.A: It increases their visibility to other drivers
choices.B: It greatly reduces their braking ability
choices.C: It improves their tire traction on the road
choices.D: It requires them to ride on the sidewalk

en.explanation: During wet weather, the braking ability of a bicycle is greatly reduced. Motorists should be prepared to compensate for the cyclist's decreased ability to slow or stop.

en.question: Which action accounts for a large percentage of car and motorcycle injury-producing accidents?

choices.A: Cars making left turns in front of an oncoming motorcyclist
choices.B: Motorcyclists passing cars on the right
choices.C: Cars rear-ending motorcycles at stop signs
choices.D: Motorcyclists failing to use their turn signals

en.explanation: Left turns in front of an oncoming motorcyclist account for a large percentage of car/cycle injury producing accidents because drivers may fail to pick the cyclist out of traffic or judge their speed.

en.question: Why should you be extra cautious when a motorcycle's turn signal is blinking?

choices.A: Motorcycle turn signals are often dimmer than car signals
choices.B: Turn signals on most motorcycles are not automatically self-canceling
choices.C: Motorcyclists use turn signals to indicate they are stopping
choices.D: It means the motorcycle is experiencing mechanical failure

en.explanation: Turn signals are not automatically self-canceling on most motorcycles. At times, the rider may forget to turn the signal off, so you must be sure the vehicle is actually turning before proceeding.

en.question: What is the recommended following distance you should maintain behind a motorcyclist under normal conditions?

choices.A: 1 second
choices.B: 2 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds
choices.D: 5 seconds

en.explanation: Following distance behind the motorcyclist should be the same 2-second following distance given any other vehicle.

en.question: If a motorcyclist is riding far to one side of a wide lane, what should you do?

choices.A: Move into the same lane alongside the motorcycle to pass
choices.B: Honk your horn to let them know you are sharing the lane
choices.C: Never move into the same lane alongside the motorcycle
choices.D: Pass them closely on the side they are avoiding

en.explanation: Drivers should never move into the same lane alongside a motorcycle even if the lane is wide and the cyclist is riding far to one side. It is not only illegal, but extremely hazardous.

en.question: How might a motorcyclist react when crossing metal or grated bridges?

choices.A: They will speed up to cross quickly
choices.B: They may quickly change direction or slow down due to a wobbling sensation
choices.C: They will move into the oncoming traffic lane
choices.D: They will come to a complete stop before crossing

en.explanation: Metal or grated bridges create a wobbling sensation in the front tire of the motorcycle. This may cause an inexperienced motorcyclist to quickly change direction or slow down.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in a truck or bus driver's side blind spot?

choices.A: You are within 50 feet of the rear of the truck
choices.B: You cannot see the driver's face in their side-view mirror
choices.C: The truck's turn signals are flashing
choices.D: You are driving on the right side of the truck

en.explanation: If you can't see the driver's face in the side-view mirror, the driver can't see you, meaning you are in their Side No-Zone (blind spot).

en.question: How far can the huge blind spot directly behind a truck or bus extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 150 feet
choices.D: Up to 200 feet

en.explanation: Unlike cars, trucks and buses have huge no-zones directly behind them that may extend as far as 200 feet.

en.question: What should you do when following a large vehicle at night?

choices.A: Keep your high beams on to increase visibility
choices.B: Always dim your headlights
choices.C: Flash your headlights repeatedly
choices.D: Turn off your headlights temporarily

en.explanation: When following a large vehicle at night, always dim your headlights. Bright lights will blind the driver when they reflect off the side mirrors of the bus or truck.

en.question: When passing a large vehicle, when is it safe to pull back in front of it?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the front of the truck
choices.B: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror
choices.C: When the truck driver flashes their headlights
choices.D: After you have maintained your speed for 5 seconds

en.explanation: Look for the entire front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror before pulling in front and don't slow down.

en.question: According to a National Safety Council study, how much distance does a loaded truck need to stop safely at 55 miles per hour?

choices.A: 193 feet
choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 350 feet
choices.D: 430 feet

en.explanation: A National Safety Council study found that at speeds of 55 miles per hour, a passenger car needs 193 feet to stop safely and a loaded truck needs 430 feet.

en.question: What might a motorcyclist do when approaching a rough railroad grade crossing?

choices.A: Rise off the seat to help cushion the shock
choices.B: Accelerate rapidly to jump the tracks
choices.C: Lay the motorcycle down to slide under the crossing gate
choices.D: Stop and walk the motorcycle across the tracks

en.explanation: At railroad grade crossings, the cyclist may rise off the seat to help cushion the shock of a rough crossing.

en.question: How can fast-moving, large trucks affect motorcyclists on the highway?

choices.A: They provide a slipstream that improves the motorcycle's fuel efficiency
choices.B: They create windblasts that can move the motorcyclist out of their path of travel
choices.C: They block crosswinds, making it safer for the motorcycle
choices.D: They force the motorcycle to stop completely

en.explanation: Fast-moving, large trucks have been known to create windblasts, which can startle a motorcyclist, and under certain conditions, actually move the motorcyclist out of the path of travel.

en.question: Why should you avoid passing a truck on the right when its right turn signal is blinking?

choices.A: The truck will speed up to make the turn.
choices.B: Trucks swing wide to the left to safely make a right turn, and you could become trapped.
choices.C: The truck driver is required to yield to you.
choices.D: Passing on the right is always illegal.

en.explanation: Truck and bus drivers need to swing wide to the left to safely make a right turn. If you attempt to pass on the right, the driver will not be able to see you and you will become trapped.

en.question: Which way should you turn your wheels when parking facing uphill where there is a curb?

choices.A: Toward the curb
choices.B: Away from the curb
choices.C: Parallel to the curb
choices.D: Straight ahead

en.explanation: When facing uphill with a curb, you must turn your wheels away from the curb and shift into low gear or PARK.

en.question: How should you position your wheels when parking facing downhill, with or without a curb?

choices.A: Turn wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
choices.B: Turn wheels away from the curb.
choices.C: Keep the wheels perfectly straight.
choices.D: Turn wheels to the left.

en.explanation: When parking facing downhill, with or without a curb, you should turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.

en.question: Parking is NOT allowed within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: Parking is NOT allowed within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

en.question: You are prohibited from parking within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: Parking is NOT allowed within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

en.question: Alabama's child restraint law requires that children must be restrained when riding in motor vehicles through what age?

choices.A: Age 5
choices.B: Age 10
choices.C: Age 12
choices.D: Age 15

en.explanation: Alabama's child restraint law requires that children through age 15 must be restrained when riding in motor vehicles in Alabama.

en.question: What is the fine for violating Alabama's child restraint law, in addition to points being assessed against the driver's record?
en.explanation: Violators of the child restraint law will have points assessed against their driver record, in addition to incurring a fine of $25.

en.question: Until what age or weight must an infant be placed in a rear-facing infant-only or convertible seat?

choices.A: At least 6 months or 15 pounds
choices.B: At least 1 year of age or 20 pounds
choices.C: At least 2 years of age or 30 pounds
choices.D: At least 3 years of age or 40 pounds

en.explanation: The law requires an infant-only seat or convertible seat used in the rear-facing position until an infant is at least 1 year of age or 20 pounds.

en.question: According to accident records, over 90 percent of highway crashes are caused by:

choices.A: Mechanical failures
choices.B: Poor weather conditions
choices.C: Driver error and improper attitude
choices.D: Poorly maintained roads

en.explanation: Accident records show that over 90 percent of the highway crashes are caused by driver error, lack of knowledge, inattention, physical or mental condition, improper attitude or faulty judgment.

en.question: What is "highway hypnosis"?

choices.A: A condition of drowsiness or unawareness brought on by monotony.
choices.B: A visual impairment caused by oncoming headlights.
choices.C: A state of panic caused by heavy traffic.
choices.D: A mechanical failure of the vehicle's steering system.

en.explanation: Expressway drivers are subject to "highway hypnosis" - a condition of drowsiness or unawareness brought on by monotony; the sound of the wind, the tires on the pavement, and the steady hum of the engine.

en.question: To avoid fatigue on long trips, how often is it advisable to take regular rest stops?

choices.A: Every 50 miles or 1 hour
choices.B: Every 100 miles or every two hours
choices.C: Every 200 miles or every four hours
choices.D: Only when you run low on fuel

en.explanation: It is advisable to take regular rest stops - every 100 miles or every two hours. Get out of the car and walk around - stretch your legs and relax.

en.question: What is the fine for a first-time offense of texting while driving in Alabama?
en.explanation: The fine for violating the texting while driving law is $25 for a first-time offense, $50 for a second offense and $75 for a third or subsequent offense.

en.question: How far away must you park from a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection?

choices.A: At least 10 feet
choices.B: At least 15 feet
choices.C: At least 20 feet
choices.D: At least 30 feet

en.explanation: Parking is NOT allowed within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended precaution if you must use a cellular phone while driving?

choices.A: Engage in intense or complicated conversations to stay awake.
choices.B: Place calls while moving in congested traffic.
choices.C: Use a speaker phone or hands-free device.
choices.D: Hold the phone tightly in your left hand while steering with your right.

en.explanation: If you do use a cellular phone, take precautions such as: Use speaker phone/hands-free device, avoid intense conversations, and avoid talking in congested traffic.

en.question: How many points are placed on a driver's record for each texting while driving offense?

choices.A: One point
choices.B: Two points
choices.C: Three points
choices.D: Four points

en.explanation: For each texting while driving offense, a two-point violation will be placed on the offender's driving record.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended way to combat 'highway hypnosis'?

choices.A: Stare fixedly at the center line of the road
choices.B: Rely on 'stay-awake drugs' to maintain focus
choices.C: Keep shifting your eyes from one area of the roadway to another
choices.D: Turn on the interior dome light of your vehicle

en.explanation: To combat highway hypnosis, you should keep shifting your eyes from one area of the roadway to another and focus them on various objects near and far.

en.question: The amount of alcohol in an average 'shot of whiskey' or a glass of wine is approximately equal to the amount of alcohol in:

choices.A: Half a bottle of beer
choices.B: One bottle of beer
choices.C: Two bottles of beer
choices.D: Three bottles of beer

en.explanation: The manual states that the amount of alcohol in one bottle of beer is about equal to that in an average shot of whiskey or a glass of wine.

en.question: Which of the following statements about alcohol is true?

choices.A: Alcohol is a stimulant.
choices.B: Alcohol improves coordination and reflexes.
choices.C: Alcohol is a depressant.
choices.D: Impairment only occurs after legal intoxication is reached.

en.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant, not a stimulant. It causes drowsiness, blurred vision, and slowed reflexes, and impairment can occur before legal intoxication is attained.

en.question: Under Alabama law, it is unlawful for a person under 21 years of age to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

choices.A: .02% or more
choices.B: .04% or more
choices.C: .05% or more
choices.D: .08% or more

en.explanation: It is unlawful for persons under 21 years of age to operate a vehicle if their blood alcohol content is .02% or more.

en.question: What is the legal blood alcohol content (BAC) limit for commercial vehicle operators in Alabama?
en.explanation: It is unlawful for commercial vehicle operators to drive with a blood alcohol content of .04% or more.

en.question: What is the driver license suspension period for a first DUI conviction in Alabama?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For a first DUI conviction, in addition to fines and possible jail time, the driver license will be suspended for 90 days.

en.question: Under the Implied Consent Law, what happens if a driver arrested for DUI refuses to submit to a chemical breath test?

choices.A: They will be issued a warning.
choices.B: Their driver license will be suspended.
choices.C: They will receive a mandatory 48 hours in jail.
choices.D: They will be fined $600 immediately.

en.explanation: A driver under arrest for DUI who refuses to submit to chemical breath tests when directed by an officer shall have his driver license suspended.

en.question: Which of the following is the only effective way to sober up after drinking alcohol?

choices.A: Drinking black coffee
choices.B: Taking a cold shower
choices.C: Eating a heavy meal
choices.D: Allowing time for the liver to break down the alcohol

en.explanation: Black coffee, food, or a cold shower might wake you, but they will not sober you. Once alcohol is in the blood stream, it must be broken down by the liver, and this process takes time.

en.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with drugs?

choices.A: The alcohol cancels out the side effects of the drugs.
choices.B: It simply doubles the effect of the drug.
choices.C: It multiplies the effects and can cause serious harm or death.
choices.D: It has no significant effect on the mind or body.

en.explanation: The use of alcohol and drugs together produces serious effects. It doesn't just double the effect; it multiplies and, when overdone, has caused death.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the cause of most rear-end collisions?

choices.A: Speeding through intersections
choices.B: Following too closely
choices.C: Driving under the influence of alcohol
choices.D: Failing to use turn signals

en.explanation: Most rear-end collisions are caused by following too closely. Drivers must allow enough following distance to stop if necessary.

en.question: A fourth or subsequent DUI conviction in Alabama is classified as a:

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor
choices.B: Class B misdemeanor
choices.C: Class C felony
choices.D: Traffic infraction

en.explanation: A fourth conviction or subsequent DUI conviction is a Class C felony, carrying heavy fines, a five-year license revocation, and potential imprisonment.

en.question: What is the recommended method to determine a safe following distance under good weather conditions?

choices.A: The one-car-length rule
choices.B: The two-second rule
choices.C: The four-second rule
choices.D: The 15-foot rule

en.explanation: The manual introduces the 'two-second rule' as a positive and easy-to-apply formula for maintaining a safer following distance.

en.question: If road and weather conditions are not good, you should increase your following distance to:

choices.A: A three-second count
choices.B: A four or five-second count
choices.C: A six-second count
choices.D: Ten car lengths

en.explanation: The manual states that if road and weather conditions are not good, you should increase your following distance to a four or five second count.

en.question: Which of the following is a factor that determines the actual stopping distance of your vehicle?

choices.A: The color of your vehicle
choices.B: The time of day
choices.C: Mental and physical reaction time of the driver
choices.D: The number of passengers in the vehicle

en.explanation: Actual stopping distances depend upon many factors, including the mental and physical reaction time of the driver.

en.question: How can wind affect your vehicle's stopping distance?

choices.A: A strong tail wind can make it harder to stop suddenly at high speeds.
choices.B: A strong head wind increases your stopping distance.
choices.C: Crosswinds cause the brakes to lock up.
choices.D: Wind direction has no effect on stopping distance.

en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers may not realize the difference a strong tail wind can make when trying to stop suddenly at high speed.

en.question: If you are involved in a traffic crash, when should you move an injured person?

choices.A: Immediately, to get them out of the roadway.
choices.B: Only if it is absolutely necessary to remove them from fire or other dangers.
choices.C: When they ask you to help them stand up.
choices.D: You should always move them to the shoulder of the road.

en.explanation: You should avoid moving the injured unless it is absolutely necessary to remove them from areas threatened by fire or other dangers common to a crash scene.

en.question: What information are you required to give to other persons involved in a crash with you?

choices.A: Your name, address, registration number, and show your driver license.
choices.B: Your name, phone number, and social security number.
choices.C: Only your insurance information.
choices.D: Your driver license number and vehicle identification number (VIN).

en.explanation: You must give your name, address, and registration number and show your driver license to other persons involved in any type of accident.

en.question: Under what circumstances must a written Form SR-31 be sent within 30 days of a crash?

choices.A: After every crash, regardless of damage or insurance.
choices.B: If there is an injury, fatality, or damage of $500 or more, and the 'at fault' party was not insured.
choices.C: Only if the crash occurred on a state highway.
choices.D: If both parties were insured at the time of the accident.

en.explanation: A written Form SR-31 must be sent within 30 days if there is an injury, fatality, or damage of $500 or more, and the 'at fault' party was not insured at the time of the mishap.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle hits an unattended parked vehicle?

choices.A: Drive away if there is no visible damage.
choices.B: Wait in your car until the owner returns.
choices.C: Notify the police, attempt to locate the owner, or leave a written notice with your name and address.
choices.D: Leave your insurance card under the windshield wiper and drive away.

en.explanation: If your vehicle hits an unattended vehicle, you must either notify the police, make an attempt to locate the owner, or leave a written notice in a conspicuous place giving your name and address.

en.question: What does a round, yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing is exactly 100 feet ahead.
choices.B: A highway railroad crossing is ahead and is placed 750 feet before the track.
choices.C: You must come to a complete stop immediately.
choices.D: The railroad crossing ahead has no gates or flashing lights.

en.explanation: The round railroad warning sign is yellow with a black X and the letters RR. It means a highway railroad crossing is ahead and is placed 750 feet before the track.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is required to stop before crossing ANY railroad crossing?

choices.A: Passenger cars
choices.B: Motorcycles
choices.C: School buses
choices.D: Pickup trucks towing a boat

en.explanation: School buses, church buses, passenger buses, and trucks transporting flammables, explosives, or other hazardous materials are required to stop before crossing any railroad crossing.

en.question: When approaching a railroad crossing where you are required to stop, what is the proper stopping distance from the tracks?

choices.A: 5 to 10 feet
choices.B: 15 to 50 feet
choices.C: 50 to 100 feet
choices.D: At least 100 feet

en.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop within 15 to 50 ft.

en.question: To avoid stalling while crossing railroad tracks, a driver with a manual transmission should:

choices.A: Shift into a higher gear while crossing.
choices.B: Shift into neutral and coast across.
choices.C: Not change gears while crossing the track.
choices.D: Accelerate rapidly and shift gears halfway across.

en.explanation: To avoid stalling, a driver should not change gears while crossing the track. If your vehicle has a manual transmission, shift down and do not change gears while crossing.

en.question: If you approach a railroad crossing and the gates are lowered, you must:

choices.A: Drive around the gates if you cannot see a train coming.
choices.B: Stop and remain stopped until the gates are raised and lights are no longer flashing.
choices.C: Stop, look both ways, and proceed slowly around the gates.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert the train operator before crossing.

en.explanation: When gates are being lowered the red flashing lights will warn you to stop. Remain stopped until the gates are raised and lights are no longer flashing. It is against the law to go around gates.

en.question: How do large, wide tires affect a vehicle's stopping ability according to the manual?

choices.A: They always increase stopping distance regardless of the surface.
choices.B: They help stop quicker on smooth, dry surfaces but skid or hydroplane easier on wet surfaces.
choices.C: They cut through standing water better than narrow tires.
choices.D: They lose stopping power overall because of less rubber on the road.

en.explanation: Large, wide tires may help stop quicker on smooth, dry surfaces, but will skid or hydroplane easier on slippery or wet surfaces.

en.question: If an injury or fatal crash occurs within a municipality, who must be notified by the quickest means of communication?

choices.A: The State Troopers
choices.B: The local police
choices.C: The Department of Transportation
choices.D: The local hospital

en.explanation: Any injury or fatal crash must be reported to the local police if it occurs within a municipality, or to the State Troopers if it happens on a state highway.

en.question: What should you do if you are driving a vehicle with a manual transmission and need to cross railroad tracks?

choices.A: Shift to a higher gear to cross the tracks quickly.
choices.B: Shift down and do not change gears while crossing the tracks.
choices.C: Put the vehicle in neutral and coast across the tracks.
choices.D: Shift into reverse if you see a train approaching.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if your vehicle has a manual transmission, you should shift down and do not change gears while crossing the tracks.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take a freight train traveling at 55 mph to come to a complete stop?

choices.A: About half a mile
choices.B: Less than 500 feet
choices.C: A mile or more
choices.D: Two miles

en.explanation: The manual states that a freight train traveling at 55 mph takes a mile or more to stop, which is the length of 18 football fields.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your vehicle stalls on a railroad crossing?

choices.A: Try to restart the engine while watching for a train.
choices.B: Get everyone out of the vehicle immediately and away from the tracks.
choices.C: Stay in the vehicle and call a tow truck for assistance.
choices.D: Shift into neutral and try to push the vehicle off the tracks.

en.explanation: If your vehicle stalls on a crossing, the manual instructs to get everyone out of the vehicle immediately and away from the tracks, then call local law enforcement.

en.question: What are the three types of traffic signs classified according to their function?

choices.A: Regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs
choices.B: Stop, yield, and speed limit signs
choices.C: Construction, school zone, and railroad signs
choices.D: Interstate, highway, and local road signs

en.explanation: The three types of traffic signs are classified according to function. They are regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs.

en.question: When more than one vehicle arrives at the same time at a 4-way stop, which vehicle is allowed to leave first?

choices.A: The vehicle furthest to the left
choices.B: The vehicle furthest to the right
choices.C: The largest vehicle
choices.D: The vehicle traveling the fastest

en.explanation: When more than one vehicle arrives at the same time at the 4-way stop, the vehicle furthest to the right is allowed to leave first.

en.question: What colors are warning signs that are used in construction areas?

choices.A: Black and yellow
choices.B: Fluorescent yellow
choices.C: Black and orange
choices.D: White and red

en.explanation: Warning signs are generally black and yellow, except those used in construction areas which are black and orange.

en.question: What does a fluorescent yellow warning sign indicate?

choices.A: Construction zones and detours
choices.B: Pedestrian crossings and school zones
choices.C: Railroad crossings and low clearances
choices.D: Highway exits and rest areas

en.explanation: According to the manual, fluorescent yellow indicates pedestrian crossings and school zones.

en.question: Where are "minimum" speed limits usually posted?

choices.A: In school zones and residential areas
choices.B: On freeways and other controlled access highways
choices.C: Near railroad crossings
choices.D: In construction zones

en.explanation: The manual notes that "Minimum" limits are usually posted on freeways and other controlled access highways.

en.question: Where is a "NO PASSING ZONE" warning sign typically placed?

choices.A: On the right side of a four-lane highway
choices.B: On the left side of a two-lane road
choices.C: Above the center of an intersection
choices.D: On the right side of a one-way street

en.explanation: The "NO PASSING ZONE" sign is placed on the left side of a two-lane road to warn of the beginning of a no passing zone.

en.question: What is the minimum clearance required when passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: The manual specifies that a 3 foot minimum clearance is required when passing a cyclist.

en.question: What does a Shared Lane Marking (Sharrow) inform road users of?

choices.A: That bicycles are prohibited on this road
choices.B: That people on bicycles might occupy the travel lane
choices.C: That a designated bike lane is ending
choices.D: That pedestrians have the right-of-way

en.explanation: Shared Lane Markings (Sharrow) inform road users that people on bicycles might occupy the travel lane.

en.question: According to the manual, a motorist is how many times more likely to die in a crash involving a train compared to other crashes?

choices.A: 10 times
choices.B: 20 times
choices.C: 40 times
choices.D: 100 times

en.explanation: A motorist is 40 times more likely to die in a crash involving a train.

en.question: In addition to being operated by or under the direction of a physically handicapped person, what must a vehicle visibly display to legally park in a handicapped parking space?

choices.A: A special license plate frame
choices.B: A handicapped sticker
choices.C: A doctor's note on the dashboard
choices.D: A hazard light signal

en.explanation: You must not park in a handicapped space unless the vehicle is operated by/under the direction of a physically handicapped person AND the vehicle visibly displays the handicapped sticker.

en.question: Under what condition are double right turns permitted at an intersection?

choices.A: Whenever there are two right-turn lanes
choices.B: Only at intersections that are properly signed
choices.C: Only during daylight hours
choices.D: Whenever traffic is light

en.explanation: Double right turns are only permitted at intersections that are properly signed. At intersections that aren't signed, follow the rules for right turns.

en.question: What does a "YIELD" sign mean?

choices.A: Stop completely before entering the intersection
choices.B: Maintain your speed and merge into traffic
choices.C: Slow down so you can yield the right of way to pedestrians and vehicles
choices.D: Accelerate to match the speed of intersecting traffic

en.explanation: The YIELD sign means slow down so you can yield the right of way to pedestrians crossing the roadway and to vehicles on the intersecting street or highway.

en.question: In which direction does traffic flow in a roundabout?

choices.A: Clockwise
choices.B: Counter-clockwise
choices.C: In both directions
choices.D: Straight through the central island

en.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that usually does not include a traffic signal and flows in a counter-clockwise direction around a central island.

en.question: When entering a roundabout, who must you yield to?

choices.A: Traffic entering from the left
choices.B: Traffic already in the roundabout
choices.C: Traffic entering from the right
choices.D: Pedestrians only

en.explanation: Motorists must enter from the right -- yielding to traffic already in the roundabout -- and follow the circle to the right.

en.question: What color are guide or informational signs that direct motorists to services like hospitals or gas stations?

choices.A: Green and white
choices.B: Brown and white
choices.C: Blue and white
choices.D: Black and white

en.explanation: Guide or informational signs are blue and white for services.

en.question: Where does zero mileage begin for mileposts erected along state highways?

choices.A: At the north and east state lines
choices.B: At the south and west state lines or junctions where routes begin
choices.C: At the capital city of the state
choices.D: At the geographic center of the state

en.explanation: Zero mileage should begin at the south and west state lines or at junctions where routes begin.

en.question: What color are centerlines painted on two-lane highways to separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

choices.A: White
choices.B: Yellow
choices.C: Red
choices.D: Blue

en.explanation: Under the Uniform Code, centerlines are to be painted yellow on two lane highways.

en.question: What does a double solid white line indicate?

choices.A: Travel is in opposite directions and passing is permitted.
choices.B: Travel is in the same direction and crossing the lines is prohibited.
choices.C: Travel is in the same direction and crossing is permitted with caution.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for high-occupancy vehicles.

en.explanation: A double solid white line is used to delineate a travel lane where travel is the same direction and is permitted on both sides of the line, but crossing the double lines is prohibited.

en.question: When are yellow lines used as edge striping?

choices.A: For right edgelines on two-lane roads
choices.B: For left edgelines on divided roadways where traffic cannot pull entirely off the roadway
choices.C: To mark pedestrian crosswalks
choices.D: To indicate a school zone ahead

en.explanation: Occasionally yellow lines are used for left edgelines on divided roadways where traffic cannot pull entirely off the roadway, for marking of obstructions and islands.

en.question: What does a circular steady yellow traffic signal mean?

choices.A: Speed up to beat the red light
choices.B: Stop immediately in the intersection
choices.C: Clear the intersection
choices.D: Proceed with caution without stopping

en.explanation: A circular steady yellow means clear the intersection. It follows a green signal. You must not enter the intersection when the red signal comes on.

en.question: What must you do when approaching a railroad crossing with flashing red light signals?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed if no train is visible
choices.B: Stop because a train is near, and do not proceed until safe
choices.C: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly
choices.D: Yield to vehicles behind you

en.explanation: Always stop when the lights begin to flash because a train is near. Do not proceed until you can do so safely.

en.question: What does a steady green arrow indicate?

choices.A: You may proceed in the direction of the arrow while opposing traffic must stop.
choices.B: You must yield to opposing traffic before turning.
choices.C: The protected turning movement is ending.
choices.D: You may only go straight through the intersection.

en.explanation: GREEN ARROWS permit you to proceed in the direction of the arrow while opposing traffic must stop.

en.question: What does a "STEADY RED X" lane use control signal mean?

choices.A: You may drive in the lane with caution.
choices.B: You must stop and wait for a green arrow.
choices.C: You shall not drive in the lane over which the signal is located.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for left turns only.

en.explanation: A driver facing a "STEADY RED X" indication shall not drive in the lane over which the signal is located.

en.question: According to the manual, who do traffic laws apply to?

choices.A: Only drivers of motor vehicles
choices.B: Drivers of vehicles and operators of motorcycles, but not bicyclists
choices.C: Drivers of vehicles, operators of motorcycles and bicycles, and pedestrians
choices.D: Only vehicles traveling on interstate highways

en.explanation: Traffic laws apply to all who use the streets and roads - drivers of vehicles, operators of motorcycles and bicycles, and pedestrians.

en.question: What is the statutory speed limit on an unpaved road in Alabama unless otherwise posted?

choices.A: 25 miles per hour
choices.B: 30 miles per hour
choices.C: 35 miles per hour
choices.D: 45 miles per hour

en.explanation: According to the manual, the statutory speed limit is 35 miles per hour on an unpaved road.

en.question: What is the statutory speed limit in an urban district?

choices.A: 20 miles per hour
choices.B: 25 miles per hour
choices.C: 30 miles per hour
choices.D: 35 miles per hour

en.explanation: The manual states that the statutory speed limit is 30 miles per hour in an urban district.

en.question: Which of the following best describes Alabama's basic speed law?

choices.A: You must always drive at the exact posted speed limit.
choices.B: You must never drive a vehicle at a speed that is faster than reasonable under existing conditions.
choices.C: You must drive 5 mph below the speed limit during inclement weather.
choices.D: You may exceed the speed limit by 10 mph if passing another vehicle.

en.explanation: Alabama's basic speed law provides that you must never drive a vehicle at a speed that is faster than reasonable under existing conditions, considering road, weather, and vehicle conditions.

en.question: Where must you stop your vehicle at a STOP sign if there is no marked stop line?

choices.A: Before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection.
choices.B: Directly next to the STOP sign.
choices.C: Ten feet before the intersection.
choices.D: In the middle of the intersection to get a clear view.

en.explanation: If no stop line is marked, the vehicle must stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection.

en.question: Under what condition may you make a left turn after stopping for a red traffic light?

choices.A: You may never make a left turn on a red light.
choices.B: If you are turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
choices.C: If you are driving on a one-way street and turning onto a one-way street with traffic moving from right to left.
choices.D: If there is no oncoming traffic for at least 500 feet.

en.explanation: You may make a left turn after stopping if you are driving on a one-way street and the street you turn left onto is a one-way street with traffic moving from right to left.

en.question: How should you treat an intersection if the traffic light is inoperative?

choices.A: Treat the intersection as a yield sign.
choices.B: Treat the intersection as you would a four-way stop.
choices.C: Proceed through the intersection without stopping if the way is clear.
choices.D: Wait at the intersection until law enforcement arrives.

en.explanation: The manual states that if the traffic light is inoperative, you must treat the intersection as you would a four-way stop.

en.question: When you are required to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, how far away must you stop?

choices.A: At least 10 feet from the bus.
choices.B: At least 15 feet from the bus.
choices.C: At least 20 feet from the bus.
choices.D: At least 50 feet from the bus.

en.explanation: When a school bus is displaying flashing red signals and an extended stop area, you must stop at least 20 feet from the bus.

en.question: When are you NOT required to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children?

choices.A: When you are traveling on a two-lane highway.
choices.B: When you are on a four-lane undivided highway.
choices.C: When you are on a divided highway with four or more lanes and the bus is stopped in the opposing roadway.
choices.D: When you are running late and no children are visible.

en.explanation: A stop is not required on a divided highway having four or more lanes which permits at least two lanes of traffic to travel in opposite directions when meeting a school bus stopped in the opposing roadway.

en.question: In rural areas, how far in advance do school buses use flashing amber lights to pre-warn drivers they are preparing to stop?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 300 feet

en.explanation: In rural areas, the flashing amber lights are used at least 300 feet before stopping to warn other drivers.
