en.question: What is a possible consequence of failing to comply with a restriction code on your driver license?

choices.A: You will be required to retake the driving test
choices.B: You could receive a citation and have your license suspended
choices.C: Your vehicle will be impounded for 30 days
choices.D: You will receive a warning letter from the DMV

en.explanation: If you have a restriction on your license and do not comply with the requirements, you could receive a citation and have your license suspended.

en.question: What does Restriction Code G indicate on a Florida driver license?

choices.A: Corrective Lenses
choices.B: Business Purposes Only
choices.C: Daylight Driving Only
choices.D: Employment Purposes Only

en.explanation: Restriction Code G stands for 'Daylight Driving Only. (Dawn to dusk)'.

en.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a standard Florida ID card, assuming no disabled parking permit is being applied for?

choices.A: 5 years of age
choices.B: 12 years of age
choices.C: 15 years of age
choices.D: 16 years of age

en.explanation: To obtain an ID card, you must be 5 years of age or older (unless applying for a disabled parking permit, which has no age restriction).

en.question: How long is a Florida ID card valid for a person who is 10 years old?

choices.A: 2 years
choices.B: 4 years
choices.C: 6 years
choices.D: 8 years

en.explanation: ID cards issued to persons 5-14 years of age will be valid for four years; all others will be valid for eight years.

en.question: Can a person hold both a Florida driver license and a Florida ID card at the same time?

choices.A: Yes, if they pay a dual-issue fee
choices.B: Yes, but only if they are over 18
choices.C: No, they must surrender their driver license to get an ID card
choices.D: No, unless they have a disabled parking permit

en.explanation: Persons holding a driver license who wish to obtain a Florida ID card must surrender their driver license. You are prohibited from holding both a driver license and an ID card at the same time.

en.question: How can a homeless person obtain a Florida ID card at no cost?

choices.A: By providing a letter from a local homeless shelter verifying their status
choices.B: By showing a food stamp EBT card
choices.C: By swearing an oath in front of a notary public
choices.D: By applying online through MyDMVPortal

en.explanation: If you are homeless, you can get an ID card at no cost. You must provide a current letter from a local homeless shelter verifying that you are homeless.

en.question: Who is required by state law to comply with Federal Selective Service System requirements when applying for a driver license or ID card?

choices.A: All US citizens over the age of 18
choices.B: Any male US citizen or immigrant who is at least 18 but less than 26 years old
choices.C: Any person applying for a commercial driver's license
choices.D: Any male who is 16 years old applying for a learner's license

en.explanation: State law requires any male who is a US citizen or immigrant, who is at least 18 years old but less than 26 years old, to comply with Federal Selective Service System requirements.

en.question: How long do sexual predators and offenders have to report in person to a driver license service center after a change in name or address?

choices.A: 24 hours
choices.B: 48 hours
choices.C: 2 working days
choices.D: 30 calendar days

en.explanation: Sexual predators and offenders must report in person to a driver license service center... within 48 hours after any change in name or address.

en.question: According to the manual, how many lives could you save by registering as an organ and tissue donor?

choices.A: Up to 4 lives
choices.B: Up to 6 lives
choices.C: Up to 8 lives
choices.D: Up to 10 lives

en.explanation: By registering as a donor, you could save up to eight lives.

en.question: What document must an honorably discharged US veteran provide to get the 'Veteran' designation on their license?

choices.A: A military ID card
choices.B: A letter from a VA hospital
choices.C: A copy of their DD214 or other approved discharge document
choices.D: A state-issued birth certificate

en.explanation: The veteran will need to provide a copy of their DD214 or other approved discharge document at the time of issuance to have the 'Veteran' designation placed on their license.

en.question: How many days do you have to obtain a new driver license after changing your mailing or residential address?

choices.A: 10 calendar days
choices.B: 15 calendar days
choices.C: 30 calendar days
choices.D: 60 calendar days

en.explanation: You must obtain a new driver license within 30 calendar days of any change to your mailing or residential address.

en.question: Which of the following documents is acceptable to change your name on your driver license?

choices.A: A notarized letter from a parent
choices.B: A utility bill in your new name
choices.C: An original or certified government issued marriage certificate
choices.D: A new Social Security card

en.explanation: To change your name, you will need to present an original or certified government issued marriage certificate, divorce decree, or court order as a name change document.

en.question: What must Canadian Citizens do before applying for a name change on their Florida driver license or ID card?

choices.A: Change their name on their Canadian passport
choices.B: Surrender their Canadian passport to the DMV
choices.C: Apply for a United States passport
choices.D: Change their name on their USCIS documents

en.explanation: According to the manual, Canadian Citizens must change their name on their Canadian passport before applying for a name change on their driver license or ID card.

en.question: Under what condition is the replacement fee waived for a stolen Florida driver license?

choices.A: If you apply for a replacement online within 24 hours
choices.B: If you provide a copy of the police report in person and make no changes to the card
choices.C: If you have maintained a clean driving record for the past three years
choices.D: If you are a student under the age of 18

en.explanation: If the card was stolen and you provide a copy of the police report (in person), the replacement fee is waived as long as you are not making any changes to the card.

en.question: How long are Class E driver licenses generally valid for in Florida?

choices.A: 4 to 6 years
choices.B: 5 to 10 years
choices.C: 6 to 8 years
choices.D: 8 to 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states that Class E driver licenses are valid for six to eight years.

en.question: Which of the following is a reason your Florida driver license may NOT be renewed?

choices.A: You have an unpaid parking ticket from another state
choices.B: You did not answer a summons which involved a traffic violation
choices.C: You are over the age of 80
choices.D: You lost your previous driver license

en.explanation: Your license may not be renewed if you did not answer a summons which involved a traffic violation, among other reasons such as suspension or lack of documentation.

en.question: You are NOT eligible to renew your driver license online if:

choices.A: You are a US citizen
choices.B: Your previous renewal was done in person at a field office
choices.C: Your previous renewal was by phone, mail, or online
choices.D: You are over the age of 65

en.explanation: You are not eligible for online renewal if your previous renewal was by phone, mail, or online.

en.question: What is required for all drivers who are 80 years of age or older when renewing their driver license?

choices.A: They must pass a driving skills test
choices.B: They must pass a vision exam
choices.C: They must pass a written knowledge exam
choices.D: They must complete a Basic Driver Improvement course

en.explanation: All drivers who are 80 years of age or older and who are renewing their driver license are required to pass a vision exam.

en.question: What is the fee for an initial Class E Florida driver license?
en.explanation: The initial license fee for a first Florida license is $48.

en.question: What is the delinquent fee for a driver license renewal application received after the expiration date?
en.explanation: Application for renewal received after the license expiration date (midnight of your birthday) requires a $15 late fee.

en.question: What is the administrative fee to reinstate a driver license after an alcohol and drug-related offense?
en.explanation: The reinstatement administrative fee for alcohol & drug-related offenses is $130.

en.question: What is the insurance reinstatement fee for a first suspension due to failure to maintain PIP insurance?
en.explanation: The fee for failure to maintain PIP insurance for a 1st suspension is $150.

en.question: How much does a written re-test (Class E Knowledge Exam) cost in Florida?
en.explanation: The fee for written re-tests (Class E Knowledge Exam) is $10.

en.question: Who is exempt from paying certain driver license fees, such as initial and renewal fees?

choices.A: All drivers over the age of 80
choices.B: Any veteran honorably discharged with a 100% service-connected disability
choices.C: Active duty law enforcement officers
choices.D: Any driver who has not received a traffic citation in 10 years

en.explanation: Any veteran honorably discharged from the Armed Forces who has been determined by the Veterans Administration to have a 100% service-connected disability is exempt from paying certain driver license fees.

en.question: If you have never held a driver license in any jurisdiction, what must you complete before applying for a Florida driver license?

choices.A: A Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) course
choices.B: A Traffic Law Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) course
choices.C: An advanced defensive driving course
choices.D: A 50-hour supervised driving log

en.explanation: If you have never held a driver license in any state, country, or jurisdiction, you must complete a TLSAE course before applying for a driver license in the state of Florida.

en.question: If you are under 21 and receive a notice of suspension for driving with a Blood Alcohol Level (BAL) of .02 to .05, what must you do to reinstate your driver license on a hardship basis?

choices.A: Pay a $500 fine and serve 10 days in jail
choices.B: Complete a Traffic Law Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) course
choices.C: Retake the driving skills test
choices.D: Wait until you turn 21 years old

en.explanation: If you are under 21 years old and receive a notice of suspension for driving with a BAL of .02 to .05, you must complete a TLSAE course in order to reinstate your driver license on a hardship basis.

en.question: Under which of the following circumstances are you required to complete a Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) course?

choices.A: You had one crash resulting in $200 of property damage.
choices.B: You were at fault in a crash and someone was transported to the hospital.
choices.C: You received a parking ticket in a school zone.
choices.D: Your vehicle broke down on the highway.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you must complete a basic driver improvement course if you were a driver in a crash, found at fault, and someone was transported to the hospital.

en.question: How many times in a lifetime can a person elect to attend a Basic Driver Improvement course to avoid points on their driving record?

choices.D: Unlimited

en.explanation: The manual states that a person may make no more than five elections in a lifetime to attend a basic driver improvement course to withhold points.

en.question: You may NOT elect to attend a Basic Driver Improvement course for a non-criminal moving violation if you were charged with exceeding the speed limit by more than:

choices.A: 10 MPH
choices.B: 15 MPH
choices.C: 20 MPH
choices.D: 30 MPH

en.explanation: The manual specifies that you may not elect to attend a basic driver improvement course if you were charged with exceeding the speed limit by more than 30 MPH.

en.question: Which course must you complete to reinstate your driving privileges if your Florida driver license was suspended for points or as a habitual traffic offender (non-DUI)?

choices.A: Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) Course
choices.B: Advanced Driver Improvement (ADI) Course
choices.C: Traffic Law and Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE)
choices.D: Licensed DUI Program

en.explanation: If your Florida driver license was suspended for points, as a habitual traffic offender (non-DUI), or by court order, you must complete an advanced driver improvement course.

en.question: What is the minimum acceptable field of vision for an applicant or licensed driver in Florida?

choices.B: The use of telescopic lenses to meet visual standards is not recognized.

choices.D: Contact lenses are not permitted during the vision test.

en.question: How many questions are on the Class E Knowledge Exam?

en.question: Which of the following vehicle defects will cause the examiner to refuse to give you a driving skills test?

choices.A: The vehicle has an automatic transmission.

en.question: During the backing up maneuver on the driving skills test, you must back up a distance of 50 feet at a slow speed while:

choices.A: Looking exclusively at the rear-view camera monitor.
choices.B: Using only your side mirrors.
choices.C: Looking to the rear without using the rear-view mirror or camera monitor.
choices.D: Keeping one hand on the emergency brake.

en.explanation: For the backing up maneuver, you must back up 50 feet at a slow speed while looking to the rear, and you must not use the rear-view mirror or rear-view camera monitor.

en.question: On the driving skills test, what is the minimum following distance you must maintain behind other cars?

choices.A: One to two seconds
choices.B: Two to three seconds
choices.C: Three to four seconds
choices.D: Five to six seconds

en.explanation: During the driving exam, you must keep a minimum following distance of three to four seconds to follow at a safe distance.

en.question: When performing the signal and turn maneuver on the driving exam, you must signal your turn for the last:

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 150 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: The manual requires that you get into the proper lane and signal your turn for the last 100 feet.

en.question: If you elect to attend a Basic Driver Improvement course for a traffic citation, you must inform the Clerk of Court and pay an election fee within how many days of receiving the citation?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 45 days

en.explanation: Within 30 days from the date you received the traffic citation and prior to attending class, you must inform the Clerk of Court and pay an election fee.

en.question: Who is eligible to take the Class E Knowledge Exam online through an approved third-party provider?

choices.A: Students under 18 years old
choices.B: Anyone applying for a commercial driver license
choices.C: Drivers over the age of 65
choices.D: All applicants regardless of age

en.explanation: The manual states that students under 18 may take the knowledge exam online through approved third-party providers.

en.question: If an applicant is blind in one eye or has 20/200 vision or worse in one eye, what must the vision in the other eye be to pass the screening?

choices.A: 20/20 or better
choices.B: 20/30 or better
choices.C: 20/40 or better
choices.D: 20/50 or better

en.explanation: If one eye is blind or 20/200 or worse, the other eye must be 20/40 or better with or without corrective lenses.

en.question: Who is permitted to ride in the vehicle with you during the driving skills exam?

choices.A: A licensed parent or guardian
choices.B: A driver education instructor
choices.C: No other passengers, unless a language interpreter is necessary
choices.D: Up to one family member

en.explanation: The manual specifies that no other passengers are permitted during the exam unless a language interpreter is necessary.

en.question: When preparing to make a turn, for what distance must you signal before turning?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 150 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: According to the driving skills test guidelines, you must get into the proper lane and signal your turn for the last 100 feet.

en.question: During the driving skills test, what size space will you be required to turn your car around in for the three-point turn?

choices.A: 10–20 foot space
choices.B: 20–40 foot space
choices.C: 40–60 foot space
choices.D: 50–70 foot space

en.explanation: The manual states that for a Three Point Turn, you must turn the car around in a 20–40 foot space.

en.question: What are the minimum insurance coverage requirements for motor vehicles operating on Florida roadways?

choices.A: $5,000 PIP and $10,000 PDL

en.explanation: Every owner or person in charge of operating a motor vehicle on Florida roadways must have a minimum of $10,000 in Personal Injury Protection (PIP) AND a minimum of $10,000 in Property Damage Liability (PDL) coverage.

en.question: You must comply with Florida's insurance laws if you own a motor vehicle that has been in the state for how many days during the last 365 days?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: You must comply with the insurance laws if you own a motor vehicle that has been in the state for 90 days (consecutive or non-consecutive) during the last 365 days.

en.question: What must you do before canceling your Florida motor vehicle insurance to prevent the suspension of your driver's license?

choices.A: Notify your local police department.
choices.B: Turn in your vehicle license plate to a driver license service center.
choices.C: Pay a $150 cancellation fee.
choices.D: Obtain a temporary driving permit.

en.explanation: The manual requires you to turn in your plate to any driver license service center before canceling your insurance to prevent the suspension of your license and to avoid reinstatement fees.

en.question: What is the penalty for showing a law enforcement officer a falsified insurance card or one you know has been canceled?

choices.A: A warning and a $50 fine
choices.B: A first-degree misdemeanor
choices.C: A second-degree misdemeanor
choices.D: A third-degree felony

en.explanation: If you show a law enforcement officer an insurance card when you know the insurance has been canceled—or if you falsify the card—you may be arrested and charged with a second-degree misdemeanor.

en.question: If you are convicted of a DUI in Florida, how long must you maintain the higher required insurance coverage limits?

choices.A: 1 year
choices.B: 3 years
choices.C: 5 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: Florida law requires you to have higher coverage limits (such as $100,000 BIL for one person) when convicted of a DUI, and this higher coverage must be in effect for three years after your DUI conviction.

en.question: What are the driving curfew restrictions for a minor holding a learner's license during their first 3 months?

choices.A: They may drive until 10 pm.
choices.B: They may only drive during daylight hours.
choices.C: They may drive until midnight.
choices.D: They may drive at any time if accompanied by someone 18 or older.

en.explanation: Minors holding a learner’s license must be accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older, and must only drive during daylight hours for the first 3 months.

en.question: Between what hours is a 16-year-old licensed driver prohibited from driving, unless driving to/from work or accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older?

choices.A: 10 pm and 5 am
choices.B: 11 pm and 6 am
choices.C: 12 am and 6 am
choices.D: 1 am and 5 am

en.explanation: A 16-year-old licensed driver may not drive between 11 pm and 6 am unless driving to or from work or accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older.

en.question: What is the driving curfew for a 17-year-old licensed driver who is not driving to work and is unaccompanied?

choices.A: 10 pm to 6 am
choices.B: 11 pm to 6 am
choices.C: Midnight to 5 am
choices.D: 1 am to 5 am

en.explanation: A 17-year-old licensed driver may not drive between 1 am and 5 am, unless driving to or from work or accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older.

en.question: What is the penalty for illegally using a disabled parking permit that does not belong to you?

choices.A: A $100 fine and 1 point on your license
choices.B: A second-degree misdemeanor punishable by a $500 fine or up to 6 months in jail
choices.C: A first-degree misdemeanor punishable by a $1,000 fine
choices.D: Immediate revocation of your driver's license for 1 year

en.explanation: Anyone who obtains or uses a permit that does not belong to them can be charged with a second degree misdemeanor, punishable by a $500 fine or up to 6 months in jail, and the vehicle can be towed.

en.question: During the driving skills test, what is considered proper posture?

choices.A: Resting your left elbow in the window while steering with your right hand.
choices.B: Keeping both hands on the steering wheel and not resting your elbow in the window.
choices.C: Leaning back comfortably with one hand at the 12 o'clock position.
choices.D: Keeping your hands at the 10 and 2 positions while resting your elbow on the center console.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to use proper posture: 'Keep both hands on the steering wheel and do not rest your elbow in the window.'

en.question: If your driver's license is suspended for failing to maintain proper insurance, can you obtain a temporary license to drive to work?

choices.A: Yes, but only if you pay a $150 fee.
choices.B: Yes, you can get a hardship license for work purposes only.
choices.C: No, you will not be able to get a temporary license for any reason.
choices.D: No, unless you get a signed waiver from your employer.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'If your driver license or license plate is suspended for not having insurance, you won’t be able to get a temporary license for any reason, not even to go to work.'

en.question: According to the driving skills test guidelines, which lane should you generally drive in unless you are on a one-way street?

choices.A: The left lane
choices.B: The center lane
choices.C: The right lane
choices.D: The lane with the least traffic

en.explanation: Under 'Stay in Proper Lane', the manual states to 'Drive in the right lane except on a one-way street.'

en.question: Which of the following actions is a violation of the Driver License Law that can result in jail time or a fine?

choices.A: Allowing an unlicensed person to use your car.
choices.B: Forgetting your driver's license at home while driving.
choices.C: Driving a rental car out of state.
choices.D: Parking in a metered space without paying.

en.explanation: Under 'Violations of the Driver License Law', offenses that can put you in jail or require a fine include 'Allowing an unlicensed person to use your car, or renting a motor vehicle to someone without a license.'

en.question: Under Florida's Implied Consent Law, what happens if you refuse to take a breath, blood, or urine test for the first time?

choices.A: Your license will automatically be suspended for one year.
choices.B: You will be fined $500.
choices.C: Your license will be suspended for 18 months.
choices.D: You will be required to attend a 12-hour DUI school.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you refuse to take the tests when asked, your license will automatically be suspended for one year.

en.question: What is the penalty for a second refusal to submit to a breath, blood, or urine test?

choices.A: A 6-month license suspension
choices.B: An 18-month license suspension and a first degree misdemeanor
choices.C: A $1,000 fine and 50 hours of community service
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver license

en.explanation: According to the manual, a second refusal will result in an 18 month suspension and a first degree misdemeanor.

en.question: In DUI cases involving death or serious injury, which of the following is true regarding blood tests?

choices.A: You are only required to take a blood test if you consent.
choices.B: You will be required to take a blood test with or without your consent.
choices.C: Blood can only be drawn if you are conscious.
choices.D: A blood test is optional if you pass a breath test.

en.explanation: The manual states that in DUI cases involving death or serious injury, you will be required to take a blood test with or without your consent, and blood may be drawn even if you are unconscious.

en.question: Under the Zero Tolerance law, what happens if a driver under 21 years of age is stopped and has a breath or blood alcohol level (BAL) of .02 or higher?

choices.A: Their driving privilege will be suspended for six months.
choices.B: They will be fined $500.
choices.C: They must install an ignition interlock device for one year.
choices.D: Their license will be permanently revoked.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that any driver under 21 years of age who is stopped by law enforcement and has a BAL of .02 or higher will automatically have their driving privilege suspended for six months.

en.question: What is the penalty for throwing more than 15 pounds of litter onto a roadway in Florida?

choices.A: A $100 fine
choices.B: A $500 fine and 2 points on your driving record
choices.C: A first-degree misdemeanor, up to a $1,000 fine, and 3 points on your driving record
choices.D: A second-degree misdemeanor and a 6-month license suspension

en.explanation: If you throw more than 15 pounds of litter, you can be charged with a first-degree misdemeanor, fined up to $1,000, and receive 3 points on your driving record.

en.question: How many points will you receive on your driver license for passing a stopped school bus?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 6 points

en.explanation: The penalties for passing a stopped school bus include four points on your driver license.

en.question: If passing a stopped school bus results in the serious injury or death of another person, what is the minimum license suspension period?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 years
choices.D: 5 years

en.explanation: If passing results in serious injury or death, penalties include suspension of license for a minimum of one year.

en.question: According to Florida law, what are the safety restraint requirements for children ages 4 and 5?

choices.A: They must be in a rear-facing safety seat.
choices.B: They must be in either a safety seat or a booster seat.
choices.C: They are only required to wear a standard lap belt.
choices.D: They are exempt from safety restraint laws if riding in the back seat.

choices.B: The driver of the vehicle

choices.C: A 10-year-old child riding in the back seat
choices.D: A driver with a learner's permit

en.explanation: Florida law exempts an employee of a newspaper home delivery service while delivering newspapers from safety belt requirements.

en.question: What is the maximum speed limit allowed on any roadway in Florida?

choices.D: 1 year

choices.D: It must be equipped with an ignition interlock device.

en.question: Which of the following actions is considered illegal road damage in Florida?

choices.C: Driving with snow chains during a storm
choices.D: Parking a heavy truck on a residential street

en.explanation: The manual states that it is against the law to damage the roads by driving on the rim of a flat tire or by any other means.

en.question: What is the fine for a first offense of exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 MPH?

en.question: What happens to speeding fines when the infraction occurs within a school zone or construction zone?

choices.A: They are waived if you take a driving course.
choices.B: They are reduced by half.
choices.C: They are doubled.
choices.D: They are tripled.

choices.D: If you are caught speeding 10 mph over the limit.

en.question: If you are convicted of your third traffic offense that caused a crash within 36 months, which of the following must you complete?

choices.C: Surrendering your vehicle to the state
choices.D: Paying a mandatory $5,000 fine

en.question: What is the penalty if you accumulate 18 points on your driving record within an 18-month period?

choices.B: A 3-month suspension
choices.C: A 6-month suspension
choices.D: A 1-year suspension

en.explanation: Accumulating 18 points within an 18-month period results in a 3-month suspension of your driving privileges.

en.question: How many points are added to your driving record for passing a stopped school bus (not resulting in serious injury or death)?

choices.A: 3 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: According to the Common Violations and Associated Point Value table, passing a stopped school bus results in 4 points.

en.question: How many points are assessed if texting while driving results in a crash?

choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points added to the primary offense
choices.D: 9 points added to the primary offense

en.explanation: If texting resulted in a crash, +6 points are added to the primary offense.

en.question: Which of the following violations will result in your license being SUSPENDED rather than revoked?

choices.A: Failing to pay child support
choices.B: A felony for drug possession
choices.C: Racing on the highway
choices.D: Three cases of reckless driving within one year

en.explanation: Failing to pay child support is listed under reasons your license will be suspended. Drug possession, racing, and three cases of reckless driving are reasons for revocation.

en.question: Under what circumstance can your driver's license be CANCELED?

choices.A: You fail to pay a traffic fine.
choices.B: You give false information or identification.
choices.C: You are convicted of racing on the highway.
choices.D: You fail to stop for a school bus.

en.question: If you refuse to submit to a breath test and wish to appeal your administrative suspension, within how many days of your arrest must you apply for a hearing?

choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: If you refuse to submit to a breath, urine, or blood test and wish to appeal this suspension, you must apply for a formal or informal review hearing within 10 days of your date of arrest.

en.question: What vehicle adjustment is recommended for older drivers who have difficulty turning their head to check blind spots?

choices.A: Getting a steering knob
choices.B: Installing a larger side mirror
choices.C: Using an assistive device for the seatbelt
choices.D: Removing the rearview mirror

en.question: Which of the following is considered a risky driving time that older drivers are advised to avoid?

choices.A: Mid-day traffic
choices.B: Driving on local residential streets
choices.C: Dusk, dawn, and nighttime
choices.D: Clear, sunny weather

en.explanation: Older drivers are advised to avoid risky driving times, which include dusk, dawn, and nighttime, as well as bad weather, rush-hour traffic, and fast-paced highways.

en.question: What are the three main categories of driver distraction?

choices.A: Visual, Manual, and Cognitive
choices.B: Visual, Auditory, and Physical
choices.C: Mental, Physical, and Emotional
choices.D: Cognitive, Auditory, and Manual

en.explanation: According to the manual, the three main categories of driver distraction are Visual (taking your eyes off the road), Manual (taking your hands off the steering wheel), and Cognitive (thinking about anything other than driving).

en.question: Why is texting considered one of the most dangerous distracted driving behaviors?

choices.A: It requires the driver to look down for at least 5 seconds.
choices.B: It involves visual, manual, and cognitive distractions simultaneously.
choices.C: It causes the driver to take both hands off the steering wheel.
choices.D: It is the only distraction that is illegal in Florida.

en.explanation: The manual states that texting involves all three categories of distractions (visual, manual, and cognitive), making it one of the most dangerous of distracted driving behaviors.

en.question: In Florida, it is illegal to operate a motor vehicle while using a wireless communications device in a handheld manner in which of the following areas?

choices.A: Residential neighborhoods
choices.B: Interstate highways
choices.C: Designated school crossings, school zones, or work zones
choices.D: Any road with a speed limit under 30 mph

en.explanation: Florida law prohibits a person from operating a motor vehicle while using a wireless communications device in a handheld manner in a designated school crossing, school zone, or work zone.

en.question: What is the first thing affected after a person consumes an alcoholic beverage?

choices.B: Vision
choices.C: Judgment
choices.D: Balance

en.question: How long must a DUI (Driving Under the Influence) conviction remain on your driving record in Florida?

choices.A: 10 years
choices.B: 25 years
choices.C: 50 years
choices.D: 75 years

en.explanation: Because drinking alcohol and driving is so dangerous, the penalties are very tough. A DUI conviction must remain on your driving record for 75 years.

en.question: To avoid drowsy driving on long trips, how often should you take a break?

choices.A: Every 50 miles or 1 hour
choices.B: Every 100 miles or 2 hours
choices.C: Every 200 miles or 4 hours
choices.D: Only when you start to feel your eyes closing

en.question: What is a likely consequence of mixing alcohol with allergy or cold medications?

choices.B: It often multiplies the effects of the alcohol and drugs.
choices.C: It will only affect your vision, but not your judgment.
choices.D: The alcohol will prevent the medication from working.

en.question: If another driver is threatening you or intentionally driving dangerously around you, what should you do?

choices.A: Make eye contact to show you are not intimidated.
choices.B: Speed up to stay ahead of them.
choices.C: Remain calm, put distance between you, and call *FHP or 911 if you need help.
choices.D: Flash your headlights and honk your horn to warn them.

en.question: If you are a non-resident who accepts employment or enrolls children in a Florida public school, how many days do you have to obtain a Florida registration certificate and license plate?

choices.C: 30 days

en.question: Which of the following vehicles requires a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) verification before it can be titled and registered in Florida?

en.question: For most privately owned vehicles, when does the vehicle registration expire?

en.question: How early can you renew your vehicle registration before its expiration date?

choices.B: Up to 60 days prior

en.question: What is the purpose of the Florida Safe Mobility for Life program?

choices.A: To provide free vehicle registration for low-income families.
choices.B: To improve the safety, access, and mobility needs of Florida’s aging road users.
choices.C: To train new teenage drivers on highway safety.
choices.D: To offer discounted auto insurance for drivers with clean records.

en.explanation: The Florida Safe Mobility for Life program provides information and resources to raise awareness and to improve the safety, access, and mobility needs of Florida’s aging road users.

en.question: How can illegal drugs and controlled substances, such as marijuana, affect a person's driving abilities?

choices.A: They improve reaction time in emergency situations.
choices.B: They sharpen vision during nighttime driving.
choices.C: They can give a false sense of alertness and self-confidence or make a person drowsy.

en.question: While most vehicle registrations expire on the owner's birthday, when do registrations for mobile homes and semi-trucks expire?

en.question: When do standard vehicle registrations typically expire in Florida?

choices.B: On December 31st of each year

en.question: What is the yearly registration renewal deadline for mobile homes and semi-trucks/semi-trailers?

choices.B: December 31
choices.C: The first owner's birthday
choices.D: January 1

en.explanation: The manual states that mobile homes and semi-trucks/semi-trailers renew yearly by December 31.

en.question: According to Florida equipment standards, how far ahead must low beam headlights show objects?

choices.A: 150 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 450 feet
choices.D: 1,000 feet

en.explanation: Low beam headlights must show objects 150 feet ahead and be visible from 1,000 feet.

en.question: From what distance must your vehicle's brake lights be visible in the daytime?

choices.A: 150 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: A vehicle must have two red brake lights that are visible from 300 feet in the daytime.

en.question: Your vehicle's horn must be loud enough to be heard from a distance of:

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The equipment standards require a horn that can be heard from a distance of 200 feet.

en.question: What is the minimum required tire tread depth for vehicles?

choices.A: 1/16 of an inch
choices.B: 2/32 of an inch
choices.C: 3/32 of an inch
choices.D: 4/32 of an inch

en.explanation: Tires should have a minimum tread of at least 3/32 of an inch or greater, and no worn spots showing the ply.

en.question: Which of the following lighting equipment is NOT permitted on a standard civilian vehicle?

choices.A: Amber directional signals
choices.B: White license plate lights
choices.C: Red lights visible from the front
choices.D: Two red taillights

en.explanation: Red lights visible from the front or blue lights are not permitted, as they are for emergency/law enforcement vehicles only.

en.question: Which of the following is strictly prohibited for a driver to wear while operating a vehicle?

choices.A: Sunglasses
choices.B: A hat with a wide brim
choices.C: Headsets or headphones
choices.D: Prescription eyeglasses

en.explanation: The manual lists 'Headsets/headphones worn by driver while operating a vehicle' under Equipment NOT Permitted.

en.question: Which statement is true regarding the use of air bags in a vehicle?

choices.A: They are a replacement for wearing a safety belt.
choices.B: They are designed to work with safety belts, not replace them.
choices.C: They eliminate the need for collision warning systems.
choices.D: They only deploy when conventional brakes fail.

en.explanation: Air bags are designed to work with safety belts to protect occupants during a collision and are NOT a replacement for wearing a safety belt.

en.question: What is the primary difference between Collision Warning Systems and Collision Intervention Systems?

choices.A: Warning systems take action to avoid a crash, while intervention systems only alert the driver.
choices.B: Warning systems only alert the driver, while intervention systems take action to avoid a crash.
choices.C: Warning systems use cameras, while intervention systems use radar.
choices.D: Warning systems only work in reverse, while intervention systems work moving forward.

en.explanation: Collision Warning Systems only provide warnings to drivers and do NOT take action to avoid a crash, whereas Collision Intervention Systems are designed to take action to avoid a crash.

en.question: How should a driver use an Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) in an emergency situation?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly to avoid skidding.
choices.B: Press down hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer out of danger.
choices.C: Remove steady pressure from the brake pedal to engage the system.
choices.D: Lightly tap the brakes while turning the steering wheel sharply.

en.explanation: Drivers with ABS need to press down hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer out of danger. Pumping the brakes will disengage the ABS.

en.question: If your vehicle has conventional brakes (no ABS) and you lose traction in an emergency, what must you do to stop?

choices.A: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly to the floor.
choices.B: Pump the brakes.
choices.C: Apply the parking brake immediately.
choices.D: Shift the vehicle into neutral and coast to a stop.

en.explanation: Drivers with conventional brakes must pump the brakes in order to stop in an emergency situation where traction is lost and the vehicle slides.

en.question: Bumper height limitations for automobiles and pickup trucks in Florida are governed by the vehicle's:

choices.A: Modified or altered weight
choices.B: Gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR)
choices.C: Net shipping weight
choices.D: Passenger capacity

en.explanation: Height limitations are governed by the net shipping weight of the vehicle, not the modified or altered weight.

en.question: What is a potential consequence of tampering with your vehicle's emissions control devices?

choices.A: Higher gas mileage
choices.B: Increased vehicle efficiency
choices.C: Lower air pollution
choices.D: Lower gas mileage and increased air pollution

en.explanation: Tampering with pollution control devices can cause damage to your vehicle, increased air pollution, lower gas mileage, and less vehicle efficiency.

en.question: Your vehicle must have at least one rear-view mirror that provides a view of the highway at least how far to the rear?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 300 feet

en.explanation: The equipment standards require at least one rear-view mirror with a view 200 feet to the rear.

en.question: When towing another vehicle or trailer, the drawbar or towing connection must generally not be longer than:

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.explanation: The drawbar/towing connection must not be more than 15 feet long unless you are towing poles, pipes, machinery, or other objects that cannot be easily taken apart.

en.question: On a passenger vehicle, a load may not extend beyond the fenders on the left side or more than how many inches beyond the fenders on the right side?

choices.A: 4 inches
choices.B: 6 inches
choices.C: 8 inches
choices.D: 12 inches

en.explanation: Passenger vehicles must not be driven on any highway with a load extending beyond the fenders on the left side of the vehicle or extending more than 6 inches beyond the line of the fenders on the right side.

en.question: During the day, if a load extends more than four feet beyond the rear of a vehicle, it must be marked with:

choices.A: Red flags at least 18 inches square
choices.B: White flags at least 12 inches square
choices.C: Two red lamps
choices.D: One amber strobe-type lamp

en.explanation: During the day, red flags at least 18 inches square must mark the extremities of a load that extends beyond the sides of a vehicle and more than four feet beyond its rear.

en.question: What does a double solid white line on the roadway indicate?

choices.A: You may cross to change lanes when safe.
choices.B: Crossing the line or changing lanes is not allowed.
choices.C: It separates lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
choices.D: You may cross only to pass a bicyclist.

en.explanation: Double solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and crossing a double solid line or changing lanes is not allowed.

en.question: If you are driving on a road with double yellow lines where the line on your side is broken and the line on the left is solid, what are you permitted to do?

choices.A: You may not pass under any circumstances.
choices.B: You may pass when it is safe to do so.
choices.C: You are in a reversible lane.
choices.D: You must turn left at the next intersection.

en.explanation: When double yellow lines are broken on the right ('your side' of the line) and solid on the left, passing is permitted in this lane when safe to do so.

en.question: When are motorized vehicles allowed to drive in exclusive bike lanes?

choices.A: When passing a slower vehicle.
choices.B: During rush hour traffic.
choices.C: They are never allowed to drive in bike lanes, but may cross them when turning.
choices.D: When the lane is marked with 'sharrows'.

en.explanation: Motorized vehicles are not allowed to drive in bike lanes; they may cross over them when turning at intersections, but only when no bicyclists are present in the bike lane.

en.question: What type of information is indicated by a fluorescent yellow-green traffic sign?

choices.A: Construction and maintenance warning
choices.B: Guide or directional information
choices.C: High emphasis warning of school, pedestrian, and bicycling activity
choices.D: Areas of public recreation and cultural significance

en.explanation: Fluorescent Yellow Green signs provide a high emphasis warning of school, pedestrian, and bicycling activity.

en.question: Which color is used for traffic signs that direct you to areas of public recreation, cultural, and historical significance?

choices.A: Blue
choices.B: Green
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: Brown

en.explanation: Brown signs indicate areas of public recreation, cultural, and historical significance.

en.question: On green guide signs in Florida, what do even-numbered routes indicate?

choices.A: North-South routes
choices.B: East-West routes
choices.C: Scenic routes
choices.D: Toll roads

en.explanation: On green guide signs, East-West routes have even numbers and North-South routes have odd numbers.

en.question: What brake requirement applies to a trailer or semitrailer weighing more than 3,000 pounds?

choices.A: It does not require its own brakes.
choices.B: It must have brakes that can be operated by the driver in the towing vehicle.
choices.C: It only requires an emergency parking brake.
choices.D: It must have hydraulic brakes independent of the towing vehicle.

en.explanation: A trailer or semitrailer weighing more than 3,000 pounds must have brakes that can be operated by the driver in the towing vehicle, designed to automatically stop the trailer if it breaks away.

en.question: What must you use when hauling loads like dirt, sand, or gravel that could fall or blow onto the roadway?

choices.A: Lock chains
choices.B: A white flag at least 12 inches square
choices.C: A close-fitting cover
choices.D: An amber strobe-type lamp

en.explanation: You must use a close-fitting cover when hauling loads which could fall or blow onto the roadway (e.g., dirt, sand, gravel).

en.question: On a two-way roadway with a center lane marked for left turns, what is true about the center lane?

choices.A: It can be used for passing slower vehicles.
choices.B: Drivers from either direction may use it for left turns.
choices.C: It is a reversible lane for rush-hour traffic.
choices.D: Only vehicles traveling North or East may use it.

en.explanation: On a two-way roadway with a center lane, drivers from either direction may use the center lane for left turns; you must not use it for passing.

en.question: What does a yellow painted curb typically indicate?

choices.A: A loading zone for commercial vehicles.
choices.B: A no parking zone near fire hydrants or intersections.
choices.C: A designated parking area for disabled drivers.
choices.D: A shared-use lane for bicycles.

en.explanation: Curbs are often marked yellow to indicate no parking zones near fire hydrants or intersections.

en.question: What does a single solid yellow line along the side of the road mark?

choices.A: The right edge of the roadway.
choices.B: A no-passing zone on a two-way street.
choices.C: The left edge of the roadway on divided highways and one-way streets.
choices.D: A bicycle lane.

en.explanation: A single solid yellow line marks the left edge of the roadway on divided highways and one-way streets.

en.question: How are East-West routes numbered on Green Guide Signs in Florida?

choices.A: With odd numbers
choices.B: With even numbers
choices.C: With letters
choices.D: With Roman numerals

en.explanation: According to the manual, East-West routes have even numbers and North-South have odd numbers.

en.question: What type of information do brown and white signs provide to drivers?

choices.A: Directions to services like gas and food
choices.B: Warnings about upcoming hazards
choices.C: Directions to scenic areas, parks, and historical sites
choices.D: Maximum safe speeds for exit ramps

en.explanation: Brown and White Signs direct you to scenic areas, parks, and areas of cultural/historical significance.

en.question: If two vehicles arrive at an All Way Stop at approximately the same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
choices.B: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
choices.C: The driver going straight must yield to the turning driver.
choices.D: The first driver to honk their horn has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: At an All Way Stop, if vehicles arrive at approximately the same time, each driver must yield to the driver on their right.

en.question: In which of the following areas are speeding fines doubled?

choices.A: Residential neighborhoods
choices.B: Active school and work zones
choices.C: Interstate highways
choices.D: Scenic routes

en.explanation: The 'Speeding Fines Doubled' sign is posted in active school and work zones, and fines will be doubled if you are cited for speeding in these areas.

en.question: What must you do when entering a right turn lane if you encounter bicyclists traveling straight?

choices.A: Honk to warn them to move out of the way.
choices.B: Speed up to pass them before turning.
choices.C: Yield to the bicyclists.
choices.D: Force them into the right turn lane with you.

en.explanation: When entering a right turn lane, you may encounter bicyclists traveling straight; you must yield to the bicyclists.

en.question: What is the rule for slower traffic regarding the left lane?

choices.A: Slower traffic must stay in the left lane at all times.
choices.B: Slower traffic must move out of the left lane when being overtaken by a faster vehicle.
choices.C: Slower traffic can use the left lane if traveling at least 10 mph under the speed limit.
choices.D: Slower traffic is only allowed in the left lane during rush hour.

en.explanation: Slower traffic must stay in the right lane unless passing and must move out of the left lane when being overtaken by a faster vehicle.

en.question: What is the normal shape and color of a warning sign?

choices.A: Red and octagonal
choices.B: White and rectangular
choices.C: Yellow and diamond-shaped
choices.D: Green and square

en.explanation: Warning signs are normally yellow and diamond-shaped. They alert drivers to conditions ahead and what to look out for.

en.question: What does the 'Divided Highway Ends' sign indicate?

choices.A: The highway will merge into a single lane.
choices.B: The divided highway ends 350 to 500 feet ahead and you will be on a two-way roadway.
choices.C: You must exit the highway immediately.
choices.D: The speed limit will increase in 500 feet.

en.explanation: The Divided Highway Ends sign indicates the divided highway ends 350 to 500 feet ahead, and you will then be on a roadway with two-way traffic.

en.question: What action should you be ready to take when you see a Hill/Downgrade warning sign?

choices.A: Shift to a higher gear to increase speed.
choices.B: Shift to a lower gear to control speed.
choices.C: Turn off your engine to save fuel.
choices.D: Apply the parking brake immediately.

en.explanation: The Hill/Downgrade sign means the road goes downhill ahead. You should slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control speed.

en.question: How should you treat an intersection if the traffic signal is out of order and no law enforcement is present?

choices.A: Treat it as a yield sign.
choices.B: Proceed through without stopping if the road is clear.
choices.C: Treat the light/intersection as a four-way stop sign.
choices.D: Only stop if you are turning left.

en.explanation: If a traffic signal is out of order and law enforcement is not present, treat the light/intersection as a four-way stop sign.

en.question: Under what condition are you permitted to make a left turn on a red light?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
choices.B: When turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street that has traffic moving to the left.
choices.C: When there is no oncoming traffic on a two-way street.
choices.D: Left turns on a red light are never permitted.

en.explanation: After stopping at a red light, you may turn left from a one-way street onto a one-way street that has traffic moving to the left.

en.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection and the traffic light turns yellow?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
choices.B: Stop if you can safely do so.
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn crossing traffic.
choices.D: Swerve into the adjacent lane to avoid stopping.

en.explanation: A yellow light is a warning that the light is changing to red. You should stop if you can safely do so, as it is extremely dangerous to be in an intersection when the light turns red.

en.question: What precautions should you take when you see a 'Slippery Surface' sign in wet weather?

choices.A: Speed up to maintain traction.
choices.B: Brake quickly if you need to stop.
choices.C: Drive slowly, don't speed up or brake quickly, and make turns at slow speeds.
choices.D: Shift into neutral while driving over the slippery surface.

en.explanation: When encountering a Slippery Surface sign in wet weather, you should drive slowly, avoid speeding up or braking quickly, and make turns at slow speeds.

en.question: What is the purpose of a Center Turn Lane?

choices.A: It is a passing lane for faster vehicles.
choices.B: It is shared, allowing left turns in both directions of travel.
choices.C: It is reserved exclusively for emergency vehicles.
choices.D: It is a dedicated lane for U-turns only.

en.explanation: The Center Turn Lane is a shared lane that allows left turns in both directions of travel.

en.question: What does the 'No Parking on Pavement' sign require you to do if you must stop?

choices.A: Stop in the center lane with your hazard lights on.
choices.B: Park on the pavement only if you have a disabled permit.
choices.C: Always park off the pavement of the roadway.
choices.D: Stop on the pavement for no more than 5 minutes.

en.explanation: The 'No Parking on Pavement' sign means that if you stop, you must always park off the pavement of the roadway.

en.question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?

choices.A: Yield to oncoming traffic without stopping.
choices.B: Treat it like a stop sign; stop and proceed when safe.
choices.C: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.D: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.

en.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. The manual states you must treat it like a stop sign; stop and proceed when safe.

en.question: What does a red X lane signal indicate?

choices.A: The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles only.
choices.B: You must slow down and proceed with caution in this lane.
choices.C: The lane signal is about to turn yellow.
choices.D: You must never drive in a lane under a red X.

en.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are opened or closed. The manual explicitly states: "Red X. Never drive in a lane under the red X."

en.question: What is the purpose of ramp signals?

choices.A: To warn drivers of an upcoming toll booth.
choices.B: To control the rate of vehicles entering an expressway.
choices.C: To indicate that a drawbridge is in operation.
choices.D: To warn drivers of construction zones ahead.

en.explanation: Ramp signals control the rate of vehicles entering an expressway and alternate between red and green.

en.question: In a construction zone, what do the downward sloping stripes on barricades and panel devices indicate?

choices.A: The direction traffic must travel.
choices.B: The presence of a flagger ahead.
choices.C: That the lane is closed ahead.
choices.D: The location of a pedestrian crosswalk.

en.explanation: Channeling devices alert drivers of unusual conditions. The manual notes that stripes on barricades and panel devices slope downward in the direction traffic must travel.

en.question: What should you do if you see a flashing yellow signal at a drawbridge?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop at the marked stop line.
choices.B: Speed up to cross the bridge before it opens.
choices.C: Slow down and prepare to stop because the drawbridge is in operation.
choices.D: Proceed at your normal speed as the bridge is closed to marine traffic.

en.explanation: When the yellow light is flashing at a drawbridge, it means the drawbridge is in operation. You must slow down and prepare to stop.

en.question: What should you do if you are already in the crosswalk when the DON'T WALK or raised hand signal begins flashing?

choices.A: Stop and wait in the middle of the crosswalk.
choices.B: Quickly finish crossing the street.
choices.C: Turn around and return to the sidewalk you started from.
choices.D: Wait for the countdown signal to reach zero before moving.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you are already in the crosswalk when the DON'T WALK or raised hand signal begins flashing, you should quickly finish crossing the street.

en.question: When approaching a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, what does a red flashing light indicate?

choices.A: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
choices.B: Proceed with caution; if no pedestrian is present and the intersection is clear, go.
choices.C: Slow down because a pedestrian has activated the push button.
choices.D: Stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk and remain stopped until the light turns off.

en.explanation: At a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, if there is a red flashing light, you should proceed with caution. If no pedestrian is present and the intersection is clear, you may go.

en.question: When stopping at a highway-railroad crossing, what is the minimum distance you must keep between your vehicle and the railroad tracks?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: When approaching a highway-railroad crossing, you must slow down and be ready to stop. Do not stop on the railroad tracks or within 15 feet of the crossing.

en.question: What do the white roadway markings in the shape of connecting X's at a railroad crossing indicate?

choices.A: A pedestrian crosswalk ahead.
choices.B: The dynamic envelope, which is a danger zone where road users should not stop.
choices.C: The location where you must stop if a train is approaching.
choices.D: A zone where passing is permitted.

en.explanation: The Dynamic Envelope consists of white roadway markings in the shape of connecting X's used to visually highlight the danger zone where road users should not stop.

en.question: Why should you be especially prepared to stop when following buses or trucks near a railroad crossing?

choices.A: They are required to stop at railroad crossings even when gates are up and lights are not flashing.
choices.B: They take longer to cross the tracks due to their size.
choices.C: They are not allowed to cross railroad tracks and must turn around.
choices.D: They must wait for a human flagger to guide them across.

en.explanation: You should be prepared to stop especially when following buses or trucks because many are required to stop at railroad crossings even when gates are up and lights are not flashing.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean at an intersection?

choices.A: The light is about to turn red; stop immediately.
choices.B: Turns are allowed in the direction of the arrow, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
choices.C: You have the right-of-way to turn; oncoming traffic has a red light.
choices.D: You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until the light turns green.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means turns are allowed in the direction of the arrow, but oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

en.question: What is the purpose of the "School Bus Stop Ahead" sign?

choices.A: To mark the end of a reduced speed school zone.
choices.B: To indicate that you must stop immediately for a school bus.
choices.C: To alert motorists of an upcoming school bus stop that may be unexpected or obscured.
choices.D: To warn drivers that children are currently crossing the road.

en.explanation: The School Bus Stop Ahead sign is used to alert motorists of an upcoming school bus stop that may be unexpected or obscured by roadway geometry, such as a curve or hill.

en.question: How should you approach an intersection with a solid green light?

choices.A: Accelerate to clear the intersection quickly.
choices.B: Approach at a speed that will allow you to slow down if the light changes.
choices.C: Stop before entering the intersection to check for cross traffic.
choices.D: Maintain your speed, as you have the absolute right-of-way.

en.explanation: When approaching a green light, you should go only if the intersection is clear, and approach at a speed that will allow you to slow down if the light changes.

en.question: What is the rule regarding driving around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?

choices.A: It is permitted if you can clearly see that no train is approaching.
choices.B: It is permitted only for motorcycles and bicycles.
choices.C: It is against the law to drive around or under a crossing gate that is down or being opened/closed.
choices.D: It is allowed if the warning lights have stopped flashing.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "It's against the law to drive around or under a crossing gate—either down or while being opened or closed."

en.question: If your vehicle's rear window is treated with a material that makes it non-transparent, what is legally required?

choices.A: A backup camera with a 180-degree view.
choices.B: Side mirrors on both sides allowing a rearview of at least 200 feet.
choices.C: A warning beep that sounds when the vehicle is in reverse.
choices.D: A special permit from the Department of Highway Safety.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if the rear window is covered by or treated with any material that makes it non-transparent, the vehicle must be equipped with side mirrors on both sides that allow the driver a rearview of at least 200 feet.

en.question: What is the recommended physical posture for a driver when backing up?

choices.A: Keep both hands on the steering wheel and look at the backup camera.
choices.B: Place your left arm on the window sill and look in the side mirror.
choices.C: Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and turn around to look through the rear window.
choices.D: Lean forward and look exclusively through the rearview mirror.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to place their right arm on the back of the passenger seat and turn around so that they can look directly through the rear window when backing up.

en.question: How does doubling your driving speed affect your braking distance and impact?

choices.A: They are 2 times greater.
choices.B: They are 3 times greater.
choices.C: They are 4 times greater.
choices.D: They are 8 times greater.

en.explanation: The manual states that doubling the speed means the braking distance and impact are 4 times greater.

en.question: Which three components make up a vehicle's total stopping distance?

choices.A: Visual distance, mechanical distance, and braking distance.
choices.B: Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance.
choices.C: Observation distance, reaction distance, and stopping distance.
choices.D: Blind spot distance, following distance, and braking distance.

en.explanation: Total stopping distance is defined as the total minimum distance your vehicle will travel, which includes perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance.

en.question: What is the minimum recommended following distance during favorable weather and traffic conditions?

choices.A: Two seconds.
choices.B: Three seconds.
choices.C: Four seconds.
choices.D: Six seconds.

en.explanation: The manual advises to keep a minimum following distance of four seconds during favorable weather and traffic conditions.

en.question: What is the minimum legal following distance when driving behind a fire truck responding to an emergency?

choices.A: 100 feet.
choices.B: 200 feet.
choices.C: 300 feet.
choices.D: 500 feet.

en.explanation: It is against the law to follow a fire truck responding to an emergency closer than 500 feet.

en.question: Outside of cities or towns, what is the minimum following distance for a truck following another truck?

choices.A: 100 feet.
choices.B: 200 feet.
choices.C: 300 feet.
choices.D: 500 feet.

en.explanation: A truck or any vehicle towing another vehicle must not follow within 300 feet of another truck or another vehicle in tow, except when passing or within cities or towns.

en.question: What should you do if you and another vehicle arrive at an intersection at approximately the same time?

choices.A: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
choices.B: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
choices.C: The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
choices.D: The vehicle traveling faster has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: If vehicles arrive at approximately the same time, each driver must yield to the drivers on their right.

en.question: When entering an open intersection, in which of the following situations must you yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: When you are traveling straight and another vehicle is turning right.
choices.B: When you enter a paved road from an unpaved road.
choices.C: When you enter an unpaved road from a paved road.
choices.D: When you are the first vehicle to arrive at the intersection.

en.explanation: At an open intersection, you must yield the right-of-way if you enter a paved road from an unpaved road.

en.question: In which direction does traffic flow in a roundabout?

choices.A: Clockwise.
choices.B: Counter-clockwise.
choices.C: Both directions depending on the lane.
choices.D: Straight through the center.

en.explanation: Roundabouts travel in a one-way, counter-clockwise direction.

en.question: Which lane should you use if you want to make a U-turn in a multi-lane roundabout?

choices.A: The right lane.
choices.B: The left lane.
choices.C: The center lane.
choices.D: The shoulder.

en.explanation: In a multi-lane roundabout, to go straight or left, and to make a U-turn, you must use the left lane.

en.question: What is the best way to check your blind spots before changing lanes?

choices.A: Look exclusively in your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Check your side mirrors for at least three seconds.
choices.C: Turn your head to make sure the areas are clear.
choices.D: Rely on your vehicle's backup camera.

en.explanation: Before you move to change lanes, pass, or make certain turns, you must turn your head to make sure your blind spots are clear.

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

choices.A: Speed up to increase the distance.
choices.B: Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn the driver.
choices.C: Slow down and keep to the right.
choices.D: Move to the left lane and maintain your speed.

en.explanation: The manual states that if your vehicle is being followed too closely, you should slow down and keep to the right.

en.question: If you triple your driving speed, how much greater will your braking distance and impact be?

choices.A: 3 times greater.
choices.B: 6 times greater.
choices.C: 9 times greater.
choices.D: 12 times greater.

en.explanation: Tripling the speed means the braking distance and impact are 9 times greater.

en.question: At a two-way stop, who has the right-of-way when one vehicle is turning and another is going straight?

choices.A: The turning vehicle must yield to the vehicle going straight.
choices.B: The vehicle going straight must yield to the turning vehicle.
choices.C: The vehicle that arrives second has the right-of-way.
choices.D: The vehicle on the left always has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: At a two-way stop, the turning vehicle yields to the vehicle going straight.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are NOT allowed on limited-access highways?

choices.A: Motor scooters with 150 cubic centimeter displacement or less
choices.B: Motorcycles with 250 cubic centimeter displacement
choices.C: Passenger vans
choices.D: Tow trucks

en.explanation: Pedestrians, hitchhikers, bicycles, animal-drawn vehicles, and motor-driven cycles/motor scooters (with 150 cubic centimeter displacement or less) are not allowed on limited-access highways.

en.question: What should you do if you reach the end of the acceleration lane when entering a limited access highway?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for a gap in traffic
choices.B: Adjust your speed to safely merge into traffic
choices.C: Force your way into the right lane
choices.D: Back up and try entering the ramp again

en.explanation: You should adjust your speed to safely merge into traffic when you reach the end of the acceleration lane. Do not stop unless traffic is too heavy and there is no space.

en.question: What type of collision is considered the greatest danger on limited access highways?

choices.A: Head-on collisions
choices.B: Rear-end collisions
choices.C: Side-swipe collisions
choices.D: Rollover crashes

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Don’t follow too closely. Rear-end collisions are the greatest danger on limited access highways.'

en.question: Under the Move Over Law, what must you do on a two-lane roadway when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

choices.A: Vacate the lane closest to the vehicle
choices.B: Stop your vehicle completely until the emergency is resolved
choices.C: Slow down to 20 MPH below the posted speed limit
choices.D: Maintain your speed but honk your horn to alert the workers

en.explanation: On a two-lane roadway, the Move Over Law requires you to slow down to 20 MPH below the posted speed limit.

en.question: If the posted speed limit is 20 MPH or less, how fast must you travel when passing a stationary utility vehicle with warning lights on a two-lane road?

choices.A: 15 MPH
choices.B: 10 MPH
choices.C: 5 MPH
choices.D: You must stop completely

en.explanation: On a two-lane roadway, if the speed limit is 20 MPH or less, you must travel at 5 MPH to comply with the Move Over Law.

en.question: When parallel parking next to a curb, how close must your right-hand wheels be to the curb?

choices.A: Within 6 inches
choices.B: Within 12 inches
choices.C: Within 18 inches
choices.D: Within 24 inches

en.explanation: You must park parallel to the curb in the direction of traffic, with right-hand wheels parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb or side of roadway.

en.question: Which way should you turn your steering wheel when parking uphill with a curb?

choices.A: Turn wheels to the right
choices.B: Turn wheels to the curb
choices.C: Turn wheels away from the curb
choices.D: Keep wheels perfectly straight

en.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, you must turn your wheels away from the curb.

en.question: It is against the law to park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: It is against the law to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

en.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right side of the road?

choices.A: As soon as your front bumper clears the other vehicle
choices.B: When you can see the tires of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
choices.C: After you have traveled 100 feet past the vehicle
choices.D: When the other driver flashes their headlights

en.explanation: Do not return to the right side of the road until you can see the tires of the vehicle you passed in your rear-view mirror.

en.question: You must return to the right side of the road before coming within how many feet of any approaching vehicle when passing?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must return to the right side of the road before coming within 200 feet of any approaching vehicle.

en.question: You must NOT pass on hills or curves where you cannot see at least how far ahead?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must not pass on hills or curves where you can’t see at least 500 feet ahead.

en.question: What does Florida law require you to do if you are driving in the left lane and are being overtaken from behind by a faster vehicle?

choices.A: Increase your speed to match the overtaking vehicle
choices.B: Move out of the left lane
choices.C: Tap your brakes to warn the driver
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: Florida Law states that a driver must move out of the left lane when being overtaken from behind by another vehicle traveling at a faster speed.

en.question: Under what condition is passing on the right legally permitted?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is driving too slowly in the right lane
choices.B: When you are driving on a single-lane road with a wide shoulder
choices.C: When the vehicle you are passing is making a left turn
choices.D: Passing on the right is never legal

en.explanation: Passing on the right is only legal when there are two or more traffic lanes moving in the same direction or the vehicle you are passing is making a left turn.

en.question: What is the standard speed limit in a municipal, business, or residential area in Florida?

choices.A: 20 MPH
choices.B: 30 MPH
choices.C: 45 MPH
choices.D: 55 MPH

en.explanation: According to the Florida Standard Speed Limits, the maximum speed in a municipal, business, or residential area is 30 MPH unless otherwise posted.

en.question: What happens to the force of impact when you double the speed of a car?

choices.A: It doubles.
choices.B: It triples.
choices.C: It increases four times.
choices.D: It increases nine times.

en.explanation: The manual states that when you double the speed of a car, you increase its force of impact four times.

en.question: What is the minimum speed limit on a highway where the posted speed limit is 70 MPH?

choices.A: 40 MPH
choices.B: 45 MPH
choices.C: 50 MPH
choices.D: 55 MPH

en.explanation: On highways, when the posted speed limit is 70 MPH, the minimum speed limit is 50 MPH.

en.question: What is the center lane of a three-lane or five-lane highway used for?

choices.A: Passing slower vehicles
choices.B: High Occupancy Vehicles (HOV)
choices.C: Emergency vehicles only
choices.D: Turning left only

en.explanation: The center lane of a three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for turning left.

en.question: What does it mean if you see red reflectors facing you on the lane lines?

choices.A: You are approaching a toll booth.
choices.B: You are on the wrong side of the road.
choices.C: The lane is closed for construction.
choices.D: You are approaching a stop line.

en.explanation: If you see red reflectors facing you on the lane lines, you are on the wrong side of the road and could have a head-on collision.

en.question: How far in advance must you give a turn signal before making a turn?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 150 feet
choices.D: At least 200 feet

en.explanation: You must give a turn signal at least 100 feet BEFORE making your turn.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the proper lane to finish a turn?

choices.A: A left turn must always be completed in the leftmost lane.
choices.B: A right turn may be completed in any lawfully available lane.
choices.C: A right turn must be finished in the right lane of the roadway entered.
choices.D: You may use your directional signals to tell drivers behind you that they can pass.

en.explanation: You must finish your turn in the proper lane. Turn right into the right lane of the roadway entered. A left turn may be completed in any lane lawfully available.

en.question: When is it appropriate to use a three-point turn?

choices.A: On a curve or hill where visibility is low.
choices.B: Only if the road is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block.
choices.C: On a highway to quickly reverse direction.
choices.D: Whenever there is a sign that prohibits U-turns.

en.explanation: Use a three-point turn only if the road is too narrow for a U-turn and you can’t go around the block. You must never make a three-point turn on a curve, a hill, the highway, or where U-turns are prohibited.

en.question: What should you do if a collision with an animal is inevitable?

choices.A: Swerve into oncoming traffic to avoid it.
choices.B: Swerve off the roadway into the shoulder.
choices.C: Do not swerve; keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway.
choices.D: Lock your brakes immediately to stop as fast as possible.

en.explanation: If collision is inevitable, do not swerve to avoid the animal. Keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway, as swerving can result in a more serious crash.

en.question: What lights should you use when driving in low visibility conditions such as fog or heavy rain?

choices.A: Parking lights
choices.B: High beam headlights
choices.C: Low beam headlights
choices.D: Hazard lights

en.explanation: Drive with lights on low beam. High beams will reflect off the fog and impair visibility even more. Parking lights are not a substitute.

en.question: What must you do when you turn on your windshield wipers in the rain?

choices.A: Turn on your hazard lights.
choices.B: Turn on your headlights.
choices.C: Increase your speed to clear the water from the tread.
choices.D: Shift into a lower gear.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'When you turn on your windshield wipers, turn on your headlights.'

en.question: What should you do if your brakes become wet after driving in heavy rain and do not hold well?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly and forcefully.
choices.B: Pull over and wait for them to air dry.
choices.C: Slow down and gently push on the brake pedal until they work again.
choices.D: Drive at a higher speed to generate heat in the brake pads.

en.explanation: If brakes become wet, they may pull to one side or not hold at all. If this happens, slow down and gently push on the brake pedal until your brakes are working again.

en.question: Up to what distance can high beam headlights reveal objects?

choices.A: 250 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 450 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: High beam headlights can reveal objects up to a distance of at least 450 feet and are most effective for speeds faster than 25 MPH.

en.question: Which vehicles are permitted to use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes?

choices.A: Any vehicle traveling over the speed limit.
choices.B: Vehicles with two or more occupants or registered hybrid/low emission vehicles.
choices.C: Commercial trucks and buses only.
choices.D: Vehicles preparing to make a left turn.

en.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with two or more occupants or hybrid/low emission vehicles (LEV).

en.question: What should you do if you come to a flooded roadway?

choices.A: Drive through slowly to avoid splashing.
