en.explanation: You may drive in Illinois without a valid Illinois driver's license if you are operating a road machine temporarily on the roadway or farm tractor between the farm buildings and nearby farmland.

en.question: What is required for the application process of a REAL ID-compliant document in Illinois?

choices.A: Only a valid out-of-state license
choices.B: Documentation confirming identity, Social Security number, residency, and signature
choices.C: A written exam and a driving test
choices.D: A 6-hour Adult Driver Education Course

en.explanation: The application process for a REAL ID-compliant document requires enhanced security measures, meaning you must provide documentation confirming your identity, Social Security number, residency, and signature.

en.question: What change regarding Temporary Visitors Driver's Licenses (TVDLs) took effect on July 1, 2024?

choices.A: They are now valid for 8 years.
choices.B: They require three proofs of residency.
choices.C: They will no longer be issued.
choices.D: They are only available to drivers under 21.

en.explanation: The manual states that effective July 1, 2024, Temporary Visitors Driver's Licenses (TVDLs) will no longer be issued, and eligible individuals can now apply for a standard driver's license.

en.question: How many documents proving Illinois residency are required when applying for a first-time REAL ID-compliant driver's license compared to a standard-issued license?

choices.A: One for REAL ID, two for standard
choices.B: Two for REAL ID, one for standard
choices.C: Three for REAL ID, two for standard
choices.D: Two for both REAL ID and standard

en.explanation: A first-time REAL ID applicant must present two documents to prove Illinois residency, whereas a first-time standard-issued applicant must present one document.

en.question: Who must properly complete and sign the application form for an Illinois Person with a Disability Identification Card?

choices.A: A licensed driving instructor
choices.B: A medical professional
choices.C: A notary public
choices.D: A Secretary of State facility manager

en.explanation: The manual specifies that the Application for an Illinois Person with a Disability Identification Card must be properly completed and signed by a medical professional.

en.question: Under what condition can a person over age 60 receive a duplicate driver's license at no cost if it was stolen?

choices.A: They must present a police report.
choices.B: They must apply online.
choices.C: They do not need a police report.
choices.D: They must wait until their next renewal date.

en.explanation: The manual notes that while applicants under age 60 must present a police report to get a free duplicate for a stolen license, persons over age 60 do not need a police report for a duplicate driver's license/ID card at no cost.

en.question: What should you do if you do not receive a driver's license renewal notice in the mail?

choices.A: Wait until the notice arrives to renew.
choices.B: Continue driving because your license is automatically extended.
choices.C: It is your responsibility to renew the license before expiration regardless of the notice.
choices.D: Request a temporary 90-day extension online.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'It is the driver's responsibility to renew the license before expiration, regardless of whether a renewal letter is received.'

en.question: When does a driver's license expire for a driver under the age of 21?

choices.A: On their 21st birthday
choices.B: Three months after their 21st birthday
choices.C: Six months after their 21st birthday
choices.D: On their 22nd birthday

en.explanation: For drivers under age 21, the driver's license expires three months after their 21st birthday.

en.question: How long is a driver's license valid for drivers between the ages of 81 and 86?

choices.A: One year
choices.B: Two years
choices.C: Three years
choices.D: Four years

en.explanation: According to the manual, for drivers ages 81-86, the license is valid for two years.

en.question: How often must drivers ages 87 and older renew their driver's license?

choices.A: Every six months
choices.B: Annually
choices.C: Every two years
choices.D: Every four years

en.explanation: The manual states that for drivers ages 87 and older, the license requires annual renewal.

en.question: After successfully completing the renewal process and paying the fee, how long is the temporary, secure paper driver's license valid?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: Upon payment and successful completion of any required testing, the Secretary of State will issue a temporary, secure paper driver's license/ID card, which is valid for 90 days.

en.question: Why might the post office fail to deliver your permanent driver's license to your provided address?

choices.A: If you did not pay for expedited shipping.
choices.B: If there is a forwarding order or hold-on mail service at the address.
choices.C: If you are not home to sign for the delivery.
choices.D: If the temporary license has already expired.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that driver's license and/or ID cards will not be delivered by the post office if there is a forwarding order or any type of hold-on mail service for the address you provided.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement to be eligible for the Safe Driver Renewal Program?

choices.A: The driver must be between the ages of 22 and 74.
choices.B: The driver must hold a commercial driver's license (CDL).
choices.C: The driver must have at least one minor traffic infraction.
choices.D: The driver must be applying for a REAL ID as a non-U.S. citizen.

en.explanation: To be eligible for Safe Driver Renewal, a driver must be ages 22-74, not hold a CDL, have no traffic infractions, and have verified Social Security information.

en.question: What is a potential penalty for presenting another person's driver's license or ID card as your own?

choices.A: A 30-day suspension of driving privileges.
choices.B: A fine of up to $500 and a warning.
choices.C: Possible imprisonment of up to five years and a 12-month suspension or revocation.
choices.D: Mandatory community service and a 6-month suspension.

en.explanation: Persons are subject to arrest, possible imprisonment of up to five years, and a 12-month suspension or revocation of their driving privileges for offenses including presenting another person's driver's license/ID card as their own.

en.question: If you have a physical or mental condition that may impair your safe operation of a motor vehicle, what might you be required to provide when applying for a driver's license?

choices.A: A waiver signed by a family member.
choices.B: A Medical Report completed by a licensed physician.
choices.C: A certificate of completion from a defensive driving course.
choices.D: A special insurance policy document.

en.explanation: In certain instances where physical or mental conditions may impair driving, you must provide a Medical Report completed by a licensed physician verifying your medical ability to safely operate a motor vehicle.

en.question: What must you do if your identity documents show a name different from your current legal name when applying for a first-time REAL ID?

choices.A: Bring additional documentation indicating the reason for the name change, such as a marriage certificate.
choices.B: Apply for a standard-issued driver's license instead.
choices.C: Wait 30 days for a background check to clear.
choices.D: Provide a sworn affidavit signed by a notary public.

en.explanation: If you bring identity documents with a name different from your current legal name, you must bring additional documentation indicating the reason for the name change (such as a certified marriage certificate, copy of divorce decree, etc.).

en.question: How many days do you have to present a completed Medical Report to DMV personnel after the physician signs it?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, the Medical Report must be presented to DMV personnel within 90 days from the date the physician signs it.

en.question: If you develop a medical condition that is likely to cause a loss of consciousness, within how many days must you notify the Secretary of State's office?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: The manual states that if you develop a medical condition likely to cause a loss of consciousness or ability to operate a vehicle safely, you must notify the Secretary of State's office within 10 days of becoming aware of the condition.

en.question: What happens to your Illinois driving record if you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving in another state?

choices.A: The offense will be ignored in Illinois.
choices.B: You must surrender your Illinois license immediately.
choices.C: The offense will be included on your Illinois driving record.
choices.D: You will be required to retake the driving exam.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that if you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving in another state, the offense will be included on your Illinois driving record.

en.question: At what age will applicants be asked to join the Illinois Organ/Tissue Donor Registry during the driver's license application process?

choices.A: Age 15 and older
choices.B: Age 16 and older
choices.C: Age 18 and older
choices.D: Age 21 and older

en.explanation: The manual states that applicants age 16 and older will be asked to join the Illinois Organ/Tissue Donor Registry.

en.question: Who is NOT eligible to register to vote when applying for an Illinois driver's license?

choices.A: Applicants applying for a Real ID-compliant license
choices.B: Non-U.S. citizens
choices.C: Applicants who are 18 years old
choices.D: Applicants updating their address

en.explanation: According to the manual, non-U.S. citizens applying for a driver's license are not eligible to register to vote.

en.question: Federal law requires males of what age group to register with the Selective Service System when applying for a driver's license?

choices.A: Ages 16-18
choices.B: Ages 18-21
choices.C: Ages 18-25
choices.D: Ages 21-30

en.explanation: The manual notes that federal law requires all males ages 18-25 to register with the Selective Service System.

en.question: What additional information can individuals provide when registering with the Illinois Emergency Contact Database?

choices.A: Their preferred hospital
choices.B: Information concerning disabilities or special medical needs
choices.C: Their vehicle registration details
choices.D: Their auto insurance policy number

en.explanation: Individuals registering with the Emergency Contact Database may also provide information concerning disabilities or special medical needs.

en.question: What is the fee for a standard driver's license for an applicant between the ages of 21 and 68?

choices.D: Free

en.explanation: The fee schedule in the manual lists the fee for a Driver's License, ages 21-68, as $30.

en.question: What is the additional fee to add or renew an M or L motorcycle classification on a driver's license?
en.explanation: In addition to the regular driver's license fee, an applicant will pay an additional $5 fee to add/renew an M or L motorcycle classification.

en.question: What is the fee for a duplicate driver's license for a person under age 60 if the license was stolen and a full police report is provided?

choices.A: Free

en.explanation: The manual states that a duplicate driver's license for someone under age 60 whose license was stolen is Free, provided a full police report is required.

en.question: Effective July 1, 2024, what happens to Temporary Visitor Driver's Licenses (TVDLs)?

choices.A: The fee will increase to $30.
choices.B: They will no longer be issued.
choices.C: They will be required for all non-residents.
choices.D: They will be valid for 90 days only.

en.explanation: Effective July 1, 2024, Temporary Visitor Driver's Licenses (TVDLs) will no longer be issued, and eligible individuals can apply for a standard driver's license.

en.question: Which of the following is required to obtain a driving record abstract by submitting a written request?

choices.A: Social Security Number
choices.B: Proof of vehicle insurance
choices.C: Driver's license number
choices.D: A police report

en.explanation: A written request for a driving record abstract must include your full name, date of birth, driver's license number, and the appropriate fee.

en.question: Where is the "GOLD STAR FAMILY" designation placed on an Illinois driver's license or ID card?

choices.A: On the front of the card
choices.B: On the back of the card
choices.C: Across the applicant's photo
choices.D: Next to the driver's license number

en.explanation: A "GOLD STAR FAMILY" designation may be placed on the back of an Illinois driver's license/ID card at the request of the applicant.

en.question: What is the fee for a driver's license for an applicant who is 87 years of age or older?

choices.A: Free

en.explanation: The fee schedule indicates that a Driver's License for ages 87 and older is Free.

en.question: Which of the following services can be completed online through the Secretary of State's expanded online services?

choices.A: Renewing a license plate sticker
choices.B: Taking the written driving exam
choices.C: Applying for a first-time Real ID
choices.D: Submitting a Medical Report for the first time

en.explanation: The expanded online services listed in the manual include renewing a license plate sticker.

en.question: How many attempts are allowed to pass each driver's license exam within one year from the date you paid your application fee?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: The manual states, "You are allowed three attempts to pass each exam within one year from the date you paid your application fee."

en.question: What is the penalty for taking any part of the driver's license exam for another person?

choices.A: A warning and a 30-day suspension
choices.B: A fine and a mandatory minimum seven days in jail
choices.C: A fine and a mandatory minimum 30 days in jail
choices.D: Permanent revocation of driving privileges

en.explanation: According to the manual, "Taking any part of the driver's license exam for another person is a criminal offense punishable by a fine and a mandatory minimum seven days in jail."

en.question: What is the minimum visual acuity required to drive without a daylight driving restriction?
en.explanation: The manual requires a "Minimum visual acuity of 20/40 with or without corrective lenses." Acuity between 20/41 and 20/70 is limited to daylight driving only.

en.question: If a driver's visual acuity is between 20/41 and 20/70, what restriction will be placed on their driving privileges?

choices.A: They must wear telescopic lenses.
choices.B: They are limited to daylight driving only.
choices.C: They can only drive with a licensed adult.
choices.D: They are restricted from driving on highways.

en.explanation: The manual states, "A driver with acuity between 20/41 and 20/70 is limited to daylight driving only."

en.question: How often must a driver take a written exam if they have traffic convictions on their record?

choices.A: Every 2 years
choices.B: Every 4 years
choices.C: Every 8 years
choices.D: Every 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states, "Every driver must take a written exam every eight years, except for a driver having no traffic convictions."

en.question: Which drivers are required to take a driving exam when renewing their driver's license?

choices.A: Drivers ages 65 and older
choices.B: Drivers ages 70 and older
choices.C: Drivers ages 75 and older
choices.D: Drivers ages 79 and older

en.explanation: The manual specifies, "Drivers ages 79 and older and any driver turning 79 or older who are renewing their driver's license must take a driving exam."

en.question: What will result in an automatic failure during the driving exam?

choices.A: Asking the examiner to repeat a direction
choices.B: Committing any traffic violation or dangerous action
choices.C: Adjusting the mirrors before putting the vehicle in motion
choices.D: Using the parking brake when parking on a hill

en.explanation: The manual states, "You will automatically fail the exam if you commit any traffic violation or any dangerous action while taking the exam."

en.question: When performing the backing maneuver during the driving exam, where should the driver look?

choices.A: Only in the rearview mirror
choices.B: Only in the side mirrors
choices.C: Turn their head to the right and watch to the rear
choices.D: Turn their head to the left and watch out the window

en.explanation: When backing the vehicle approximately 50 feet, the manual instructs to "turn your head to the right and watch to the rear when performing this maneuver."

en.question: On what days of the week can an applicant request an oral examination for the written test in person at a facility?

choices.A: Monday through Friday
choices.B: Monday through Thursday
choices.C: Weekends only
choices.D: Any day the facility is open

en.explanation: The manual states, "Oral examinations (for the written test) can be requested in person at any Secretary of State driver's license facility, Monday through Thursday."

en.question: How long is an instruction permit valid for a driver under age 18?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 12 months
choices.C: 24 months
choices.D: 36 months

en.explanation: The manual states, "The instruction permit is valid for 24 months..."

en.question: How long must a 15- to 17-year-old hold an instruction permit before obtaining a driver's license?

choices.A: At least 3 consecutive months
choices.B: At least 6 consecutive months
choices.C: At least 9 consecutive months
choices.D: At least 12 consecutive months

en.explanation: The manual states the permit "must be held for at least nine consecutive months before obtaining a driver's license if you are age 15-17."

en.question: At what age may an applicant apply for an instruction permit without taking a driver education course?

choices.A: 16 years old
choices.B: 16 and 6 months or older
choices.C: 17 years old
choices.D: 17 and 3 months or older

en.explanation: The manual states, "If you are age 17 and 3 months or older, you may apply for an instruction permit without taking a driver education course."

en.question: What are the requirements for the supervising adult when a teen is driving with an instruction permit?

choices.A: Age 18 or older with a valid license
choices.B: Age 21 or older, valid license, at least one year of driving experience, sitting in the front passenger seat
choices.C: Age 25 or older with a valid license, sitting anywhere in the vehicle
choices.D: Any licensed driver sitting in the front passenger seat

en.explanation: The manual states the adult must be "age 21 or older, has a valid license, and has at least one year of driving experience. This individual must sit in the front passenger seat adjacent to you."

en.question: How many hours of behind-the-wheel supervised driving are required for drivers under age 18 before being eligible to obtain a driver's license?

choices.A: 30 hours, including 5 hours at night
choices.B: 40 hours, including 10 hours at night
choices.C: 50 hours, including 10 hours at night
choices.D: 60 hours, including 15 hours at night

en.explanation: "Illinois law requires drivers under age 18 to have at least 50 hours of behind-the-wheel supervised driving, including 10 hours of nighttime supervised driving..."

en.question: What happens if an applicant is found cheating on the written exam?

choices.A: They fail the exam and are prohibited from retaking it for 30 days.
choices.B: They fail the exam and must pay a $500 fine.
choices.C: They fail the exam and are prohibited from retaking it for 6 months.
choices.D: They receive a warning and must restart the exam immediately.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Any applicant found cheating will fail the exam and be prohibited from retaking it for 30 days."

en.question: Which of the following documents must you bring to the DMV when applying for a driver's license before age 18?

choices.A: A 30-hour driving log
choices.B: A 50-hour driving log with proper signature
choices.C: A high school diploma
choices.D: Proof of vehicle ownership

en.explanation: According to the manual, when applying for a license before age 18, you must bring several documents, including a 50-hour driving log with proper signature.

en.question: Even if a student passes a road test conducted by their driver education instructor, they may still be required to pass a driving exam at the DMV if:

choices.A: They received a B in the course.
choices.B: Their birthday falls on a certain spot check date.
choices.C: They are under 16 years old.
choices.D: They are applying for a REAL ID.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Students whose birthdays fall on certain spot check dates must pass a driving exam administered at a DMV even though they may have taken and passed a road test conducted by their driver education instructor.'

en.question: Under the Cooperative Driver Testing Program, high school students may be exempt from taking a Secretary of State-administered driving exam if they complete their driver education course with a combined grade of:

choices.A: A or B
choices.B: A, B, or C
choices.C: Pass/Fail
choices.D: 90% or higher

en.explanation: High school students who successfully complete an accredited driver education course with a combined grade of A or B may be exempt from taking a Secretary of State-administered driving exam.

en.question: When does a Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate expire?

choices.A: One year from the date of issue
choices.B: On the student's 18th birthday
choices.C: On the same day as the student's instruction permit
choices.D: Six months after completing driver education

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate expires on the same day as the student's instruction permit and will not be extended.

en.question: If you are age 18, 19, or 20 and have not previously been licensed or completed an approved driver education program, you must:

choices.A: Complete a 6-hour Adult Driver Education Course
choices.B: Hold an instruction permit for 9 months
choices.C: Complete 50 hours of supervised driving
choices.D: Take a 12-hour defensive driving course

en.explanation: First-Time Drivers ages 18-20 who have not previously been licensed or completed an approved driver education program must complete a six-hour Adult Driver Education Course.

en.question: What are the nighttime driving restrictions for a driver in the Permit Phase (Age 15) from Sunday through Thursday?

choices.A: 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.B: 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.C: 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.D: Midnight to 5 a.m.

en.explanation: During the Permit Phase, nighttime driving restrictions are Sun.-Thurs., 10 p.m.-6 a.m., and Fri.-Sat., 11 p.m.-6 a.m.

en.question: How long must a driver in the Permit Phase hold their instruction permit before moving to the next phase?

choices.A: A minimum of 3 months
choices.B: A minimum of 6 months
choices.C: A minimum of 9 months
choices.D: A minimum of 12 months

en.explanation: Under the Permit Phase guidelines, the permit must be held for a minimum of nine months.

en.question: Under Illinois law, any wireless/cellphone use while driving, including a hands-free device, is prohibited for drivers under what age (except in emergencies)?

choices.A: Age 18
choices.B: Age 19
choices.C: Age 20
choices.D: Age 21

en.explanation: The manual states across all GDL phases that any wireless/cellphone use while driving, including a hands-free device, is prohibited for a driver under age 19, except in the case of an emergency.

en.question: During the first 12 months of the Initial Licensing Phase (Ages 16-17), the number of passengers is limited to:

choices.A: One person under age 20, unless they are a sibling, stepsibling, child, or stepchild
choices.B: Two people under age 18
choices.C: Only family members of any age
choices.D: No passengers are allowed

en.explanation: For the first 12 months of licensing, or until the driver turns 18, the number of passengers is limited to one person under age 20, unless the passenger(s) is a sibling, stepsibling, child, or stepchild of the driver.

en.question: To move from the Initial Licensing Phase to the Full Licensing Phase without restrictions extending beyond age 18, a driver must maintain a conviction-free driving record for how long before turning 18?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: A driver in the Initial Licensing Phase must maintain a conviction-free driving record for six months before turning 18. A traffic conviction may extend restrictions beyond age 18.

en.question: If a parent or legal guardian gives initial consent for a minor to obtain a driver's license, when can they cancel the minor's license?

choices.A: Only if the minor receives a traffic ticket
choices.B: Only within the first 6 months of licensing
choices.C: At any time, for any reason, until the driver turns 18
choices.D: They cannot cancel it once the license is issued

en.explanation: The parent/legal guardian who gave initial consent may cancel the minor's license at any time, for any reason, until the driver turns 18 by contacting the Secretary of State's office.

en.question: A driver under age 21 is limited to how many court supervisions for serious traffic offenses?

choices.A: Zero
choices.B: One
choices.C: Two
choices.D: Three

en.explanation: According to the Related Laws section, a driver under age 21 is limited to one court supervision for serious traffic offenses.

en.question: If a driver under age 18 wishes to obtain court supervision for a traffic violation, they must attend traffic safety school and:

choices.A: Pay a $500 fine
choices.B: Surrender their license for 30 days
choices.C: Appear in court with a parent/legal guardian
choices.D: Retake the written driving exam

en.explanation: To obtain court supervision for a traffic violation, a driver must attend traffic safety school. If they are under age 18, they must appear in court with a parent/legal guardian.

en.question: A student under age 18 who drops out of high school can have the driver education completion notation placed on their record if they:

choices.A: Pay an additional fee to the Secretary of State
choices.B: Have written verification of enrollment in a GED or alternative program
choices.C: Wait until they turn 19
choices.D: Complete 100 hours of supervised driving

en.explanation: Students under age 18 who drop out of high school cannot have the completion notation placed on their record unless they meet certain exceptions, such as the instructor having written verification of enrollment in a GED or alternative program.

en.question: During the Permit Phase, a driver must practice driving for a minimum of 50 hours. How many of those hours must be at night?

choices.A: 5 hours
choices.B: 10 hours
choices.C: 15 hours
choices.D: 20 hours

en.explanation: The Permit Phase requires drivers to practice driving a minimum of 50 hours, including 10 hours at night, supervised by a parent or adult age 21 or older.

en.question: What is the penalty for a driver under age 21 who is convicted of two or more moving violations within a 24-month period?

choices.A: A minimum 30-day driver's license suspension
choices.B: A minimum 6-month driver's license suspension
choices.C: Permanent revocation of driving privileges
choices.D: A warning letter and a mandatory fine

en.explanation: According to the manual, a driver under age 21 who is convicted of two or more moving violations within a 24-month period will have their driver's license suspended for a minimum of 30 days.

en.question: What happens if a person under age 21 receives court supervision for possession or consumption of alcohol while an occupant of a motor vehicle?

choices.A: A warning is issued to their parents
choices.B: Their vehicle is impounded for 30 days
choices.C: They receive a three-month driver's license suspension
choices.D: They receive a minimum six-month driver's license suspension

en.explanation: A person under age 21 who receives court supervision for possession, consumption, purchase, or receipt of alcohol will receive a three-month driver's license suspension if the offense occurred while the person was an occupant of a motor vehicle.

en.question: When stopped by law enforcement, where should the driver keep their hands?

choices.A: In their lap or pockets
choices.B: Reaching for the glove box to get their registration
choices.C: Clearly in sight on the steering wheel
choices.D: Outside the driver's side window

en.explanation: During a traffic stop, you should stay in the vehicle with both hands clearly in sight on the steering wheel until the police officer instructs you otherwise.

en.question: If you are being pulled over by an unmarked police vehicle and cannot identify the driver as law enforcement, what is an acceptable action?

choices.A: Speed up to get away from the vehicle
choices.B: Stop immediately in the middle of the traffic lane
choices.C: Drive carefully to the nearest police station or call 911
choices.D: Exit your vehicle and approach the unmarked car to ask for ID

en.explanation: If you cannot identify an unmarked police vehicle and/or the driver as law enforcement, drive slowly below the speed limit and pull over at a well-lit location, drive to the nearest police station, or call 911.

en.question: What does signing a traffic ticket issued by a police officer mean?

choices.A: It is an admission of guilt for the traffic violation.
choices.B: It is only an acknowledgment of receiving the ticket.
choices.C: It waives your right to present your case in traffic court.
choices.D: It means you agree to pay the fine immediately.

en.explanation: Signing a ticket is not an admission of the driver's guilt — only an acknowledgment of receiving the ticket.

en.question: At what age does Illinois law allow the use of hands-free devices or Bluetooth technology while driving?

choices.A: Age 16 and older
choices.B: Age 18 and older
choices.C: Age 19 and older
choices.D: Age 21 and older

en.explanation: Hands-free devices or Bluetooth technology is allowed for persons age 19 and older.

en.question: Which of the following headset configurations is permitted while driving in Illinois?

choices.A: A dual-ear headset for listening to music
choices.B: A single-sided headset or earpiece
choices.C: Noise-canceling headphones over both ears
choices.D: No headsets of any kind are permitted

en.explanation: Illinois law prohibits the use of headsets while driving, but using a single-sided headset or earpiece with a wireless/cellphone device is permitted.

en.question: Under what circumstance is a driver allowed to use a cellphone that is NOT hands-free?

choices.A: When stopped at a red traffic light in drive
choices.B: When reporting an emergency
choices.C: When driving on a rural highway with no other cars around
choices.D: When using the phone's speakerphone function while holding it

en.explanation: The only time you can use a cellphone that is not hands-free is to report an emergency, while parked on the shoulder, or when stopped due to normal traffic being obstructed and the vehicle is in neutral or park.

en.question: If your proof of insurance is stored on your cellphone, what should you do when a police officer requests it during a traffic stop?

choices.A: Quickly reach for your phone before the officer approaches
choices.B: Inform the officer of that fact and follow their directions before retrieving it
choices.C: Refuse to show it because cellphones are prohibited while driving
choices.D: Toss the phone to the officer through the window

en.explanation: If proof of insurance is stored for display on a cellphone, inform the police officer of that fact and then follow the officer's directions before retrieving the information.

en.question: What may happen to a person under age 18 who is charged with an offense due to a crash where a passenger was seriously injured or killed?

choices.A: They may be denied issuance or renewal of their driver's license.
choices.B: They must pay a mandatory $5,000 fine.
choices.C: They will only receive a warning if alcohol was not involved.
choices.D: They must retake the written driving exam within 10 days.

en.explanation: Persons under age 18 who are charged with an offense due to a crash where a passenger was seriously injured or killed may be denied issuance/renewal of their driver's license. Alcohol need not play a factor.

en.question: If you are stopped by law enforcement at night, what is an acceptable action to take to assist the officer?

choices.A: Turn off your headlights completely
choices.B: Turn on your vehicle's interior light
choices.C: Shine a flashlight at the approaching officer
choices.D: Exit the vehicle so the officer can see you clearly

en.explanation: If you are being stopped at night, it is acceptable to turn on your vehicle's interior light.

en.question: Is it legal in Illinois to use a cellphone while driving if you are holding the device and using the speakerphone feature?

choices.A: Yes, because speakerphone is considered hands-free.
choices.B: Yes, as long as you are over age 18.
choices.C: No, holding the device and using speakerphone is not considered hands-free and is a violation.
choices.D: No, unless you are driving under 30 mph.

en.explanation: Using a cellphone while holding the device and using the speaker phone is not considered hands-free and is a violation of Illinois law.

en.question: Why should you NOT exit your vehicle during a traffic stop unless asked to do so by the police officer?

choices.A: It is illegal to stand on the shoulder of a highway.
choices.B: Getting out of the vehicle can be perceived as aggressive behavior and a threat to the officer's safety.
choices.C: You might accidentally lock your keys inside the vehicle.
choices.D: The officer needs to inspect the exterior of your vehicle first.

en.explanation: Do not exit your vehicle unless asked to do so. Getting out of the vehicle can be perceived as aggressive behavior and a threat to the police officer's safety.

en.question: A driver may use a non-hands-free cellphone when stopped due to normal traffic being obstructed, provided that:

choices.A: The vehicle is in neutral or park.
choices.B: The driver keeps one foot firmly on the brake pedal.
choices.C: The delay is expected to last more than five minutes.
choices.D: The driver is over the age of 21.

en.explanation: The only time you can use a cellphone that is not hands-free is... while stopped due to normal traffic being obstructed and the vehicle is in neutral or park.

en.question: Under Illinois law, when is the only time you can legally use a cellphone that is not hands-free while driving?

choices.A: When stopped at a red traffic light.
choices.B: To report an emergency.
choices.C: When driving on a rural highway with no other traffic.
choices.D: When making a quick phone call that lasts less than one minute.

en.explanation: The manual states that the only time you can use a cellphone that is not hands-free is to report an emergency, while parked on the shoulder, or while stopped due to normal traffic being obstructed and the vehicle is in neutral or park.

en.question: What penalty may a driver face if they cause a crash involving a bicyclist or pedestrian due to distracted driving?

choices.A: A mandatory written warning.
choices.B: A maximum fine of $100.
choices.C: Criminal penalties and incarceration.
choices.D: Immediate vehicle impoundment for 30 days.

en.explanation: If you are in a crash with a motor vehicle, bicyclist, pedestrian, or any road user caused by distracted driving, you may face criminal penalties and incarceration.

en.question: Who is required by Illinois law to wear a safety belt in a passenger vehicle?

choices.A: Only the driver and front-seat passengers.
choices.B: All drivers and passengers age 8 and older in both the front and back seats.
choices.C: Only passengers under the age of 18.
choices.D: Only the driver, unless the vehicle lacks air bags.

en.explanation: Illinois law requires all drivers and passengers (front and back seat) age 8 and older to wear safety belts even if the vehicle is equipped with air bags.

en.question: What is the proper way to wear the shoulder strap of a safety belt?

choices.A: Tucked under the arm to prevent neck irritation.
choices.B: Placed behind the back if it restricts movement.
choices.C: Snug across the body at or near the neck or face.
choices.D: Positioned loosely across the stomach.

en.explanation: The shoulder strap should be comfortable and cross the body at or near the neck or face. It should never be placed behind the back or under the arm.

en.question: What is the desirable distance a driver should maintain between themselves and the steering wheel air bag?

choices.A: 5-7 inches
choices.B: 10-12 inches
choices.C: 15-18 inches
choices.D: 20-24 inches

en.explanation: A distance of 10-12 inches between the driver and the air bag is desirable, especially for short, elderly, or pregnant drivers.

en.question: Until what age does Illinois law require children to be properly secured in a rear-facing child restraint system?

choices.A: Age 1, regardless of weight or height.
choices.B: Age 2, unless they weigh more than 40 pounds or are more than 40 inches tall.
choices.C: Age 4, unless they weigh more than 50 pounds.
choices.D: Age 8, regardless of weight or height.

en.explanation: Effective Jan. 1, 2019, Illinois law requires children to be properly secured in a rear-facing child restraint system until age 2 unless they weigh more than 40 pounds or are more than 40 inches tall.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on interstates and tollways in Illinois?

choices.A: 55 mph
choices.B: 60 mph
choices.C: 65 mph
choices.D: 70 mph

en.explanation: The speed limit for interstates and tollways is 70 mph, unless otherwise posted.

en.question: What is the standard speed limit in alleys in Illinois?

choices.A: 10 mph
choices.B: 15 mph
choices.C: 20 mph
choices.D: 25 mph

en.explanation: The speed limit in alleys is 15 mph, unless otherwise posted.

en.question: When are motorists required to obey the posted construction zone speed limit?

choices.A: Only when construction workers are visibly present.
choices.B: Only during daylight hours.
choices.C: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
choices.D: Only Monday through Friday.

en.explanation: Motorists must obey the posted construction zone speed limit 24 hours a day, seven days a week, regardless of the presence of workers.

en.question: What must a driver do when approaching a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle using visual signals (flashing lights)?

choices.A: Maintain speed and honk the horn to alert the workers.
choices.B: Yield, change to a lane away from the workers when possible, and proceed with caution.
choices.C: Stop immediately in the current lane and wait for instructions.
choices.D: Accelerate to pass the emergency scene as quickly as possible.

en.explanation: Illinois law requires motorists to yield, change to a lane away from the emergency workers when possible, and proceed with caution while reducing speed.

en.question: Illinois law prohibits photography and the use of wireless/cellphones within what distance of an emergency scene?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1,000 feet

en.explanation: Illinois law prohibits photography and the use of wireless/cellphones within 500 feet of an emergency scene, except in certain circumstances.

en.question: Under what conditions does the 20 mph school zone speed limit apply?

choices.A: On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted.
choices.B: 24 hours a day on any day school is in session.
choices.C: On school days between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. regardless of whether children are present.
choices.D: Only when a crossing guard is actively directing traffic.

en.explanation: The school zone speed limit is 20 mph on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted.

en.question: How should a motorist react when encountering an organized funeral procession?

choices.A: Drive between the vehicles in the procession to cross the intersection.
choices.B: Join the procession to secure the right of way through traffic.
choices.C: Yield the right of way to all vehicles in the procession.
choices.D: Pass the procession on the right shoulder.

en.explanation: Motorists encountering a funeral procession must yield the right of way to all vehicles in the procession and should NOT drive between vehicles or join the procession.

en.question: If two vehicles on different roadways arrive at a four-way stop intersection at the exact same time, who has the right of way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the left.
choices.B: The vehicle on the right.
choices.C: The vehicle traveling at a higher speed.
choices.D: The vehicle making a left turn.

en.explanation: When two vehicles on different roadways arrive at a four-way stop intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.

en.question: What should you do if you are making a left-hand turn into oncoming traffic, enter the intersection while the light is green, and the light turns red before you can complete the turn?

choices.A: Back up out of the intersection immediately.
choices.B: Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait for the next green light.
choices.C: You may finish the turn even though the light turns red.
choices.D: Abandon the left turn and turn right instead.

en.explanation: When making a left-hand turn into oncoming traffic, if you enter an intersection while the light is green, you may finish the turn even though the light turns red.

en.question: When two vehicles on different roadways reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the left
choices.B: The vehicle on the right
choices.C: The vehicle traveling at a higher speed
choices.D: The vehicle turning left

en.explanation: When two vehicles on different roadways reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.

en.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane highway, you must return to your lane before getting within what distance of an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must return to your lane before getting within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: Is it legal to flash your turn signals as a courtesy or 'do pass' signal to other drivers behind you?

choices.A: Yes, but only on two-lane highways.
choices.B: Yes, if the vehicle behind you is tailgating.
choices.C: No, it is against the law.
choices.D: No, unless you are driving a commercial vehicle.

en.explanation: It is against the law to flash turn signals as a courtesy or 'do pass' signal to other drivers.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must keep between your vehicle and a bicyclist or pedestrian you are passing on the road?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or bicyclist on any road, including the shoulder or a dedicated bicycle lane, you must keep a minimum distance of 3 feet from them.

en.question: In which of the following situations is passing on a two-lane, two-way roadway strictly prohibited?

choices.A: In any construction zone.
choices.B: On a one-way street.
choices.C: When the vehicle ahead is making a left turn.
choices.D: When you have two or more clear lanes in each direction.

en.explanation: Passing on a two-lane, two-way roadway is not allowed in a construction zone. All construction zones in Illinois are no passing zones.

en.question: When driving on an interstate highway, when are you allowed to drive in the left lane?

choices.A: At any time, as long as you are driving the speed limit.
choices.B: Only when passing another vehicle, or under specific exceptions like traffic congestion or weather conditions.
choices.C: Only when you are driving faster than the posted speed limit.
choices.D: Only when you are within 5 miles of your intended exit.

en.explanation: When driving on an interstate highway, you may not drive in the left lane(s) except when passing another vehicle. Exceptions include congestion, weather conditions, hazards, or yielding to emergency vehicles.

en.question: How far in advance must you give a continuous turn signal in a business or residential area?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: In a business or residential area, you must give a continuous turn signal for at least 100 feet before turning.

en.question: What is the correct hand and arm signal for slowing down or stopping?

choices.A: Left arm extended straight out to the left.
choices.B: Left arm extended straight up.
choices.C: Left arm extended down.
choices.D: Right arm extended straight out.

en.explanation: To slow down or stop using hand and arm signals, the left hand and arm are extended down.

en.question: When waiting at an intersection to make a left turn, how should your vehicle's wheels be positioned?

choices.A: Pointed to the left.
choices.B: Pointed to the right.
choices.C: Pointed straight ahead until starting to make the turn.
choices.D: Turned slightly toward the curb.

en.explanation: When making a left turn, you should point the wheels straight ahead until starting to make the turn.

en.question: When you are on the terminating highway of a 'T' intersection with no traffic control signs or signals, what must you do?

choices.A: Proceed without stopping, as you have the right-of-way.
choices.B: Yield to cross traffic.
choices.C: Sound your horn and proceed.
choices.D: Speed up to merge smoothly.

en.explanation: You must yield to cross traffic when on the terminating highway of a 'T' intersection with no traffic control signs or signals.

en.question: Passing on a two-lane, two-way roadway is not allowed within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Passing on a two-lane, two-way roadway is not allowed within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.

en.question: What is the recommended method for opening a vehicle door on the side where traffic is moving, to help check for oncoming vehicles and bicyclists?

choices.A: The French Swing
choices.B: The Dutch Reach
choices.C: The Blind Spot Check
choices.D: The Two-Hand Push

en.explanation: You should consider using your right hand to open the vehicle door to allow you to turn and check for oncoming vehicles and bicyclists. This is more commonly known as the Dutch Reach.

en.question: Even if you have a green light, you may not enter an intersection unless:

choices.A: You are turning right.
choices.B: There is enough space to allow passage of other vehicles and/or pedestrians.
choices.C: You are driving an emergency vehicle.
choices.D: You honk your horn to warn crossing traffic.

en.explanation: A driver may not enter an intersection or drive within a marked crosswalk unless there is enough space to allow passage of other vehicles and/or pedestrians.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding backing up your vehicle on a controlled-access roadway?

choices.A: You may back up on the shoulder if you miss your exit.
choices.B: You may back up in the right lane if traffic is clear.
choices.C: You may not back up on any shoulder or roadway of a controlled-access roadway.
choices.D: You may back up only during daylight hours.

en.explanation: You may not back up on any shoulder or roadway of any controlled-access roadway.

en.question: Under what condition are you prohibited from making a U-turn on curves and hills?

choices.A: Unless you can see for at least 500 feet in all directions.
choices.B: Unless you can see for at least 200 feet in all directions.
choices.C: Unless you are in a rural area.
choices.D: Unless you use your hazard signals.

en.explanation: The manual states you must not turn around on curves and hills unless you can see for at least 500 feet in all directions.

en.question: Which turn signal should you use to let other drivers know you are exiting a roundabout?

choices.A: Left turn signal
choices.B: Right turn signal
choices.C: Hazard signal
choices.D: No signal is required

en.explanation: When exiting a roundabout, you must use your vehicle's right turn signal to let other drivers know you are exiting.

en.question: When are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm?

choices.A: When traveling on a two-lane roadway in a rural area.
choices.B: When traveling in the opposite direction on a four-lane roadway.
choices.C: When you are in a parking lot located on school property.
choices.D: When traveling on a private road.

en.explanation: A vehicle is not required to stop for a school bus when both vehicles are on a four-lane roadway and the bus is stopped in the opposite direction from which a driver is traveling.

en.question: What is the mandatory fine for a conviction of passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended?
en.explanation: If convicted of passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you will be subject to a mandatory fine of $300 and community service.

en.question: What is the required stopping distance from a railroad crossing if there is a posted stop sign or flashing electric signal?

choices.A: 5 to 10 feet
choices.B: 10 to 20 feet
choices.C: 15 to 50 feet
choices.D: 50 to 100 feet

en.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop within 15-50 feet if there is a posted stop sign, if the electric signal is flashing, or if the crossing gate is lowered.

en.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, in which direction should you move after getting out?

choices.A: Straight away from the tracks
choices.B: At a 45-degree angle in the direction of the train
choices.C: At a 45-degree angle away from the direction of the train
choices.D: Parallel to the tracks

en.explanation: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, get out immediately and move away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle in the direction of the train to stay safe from forward flying debris.

en.question: What should a driver with a manual transmission do when crossing railroad tracks?

choices.A: Shift into neutral while crossing
choices.B: Change gears while crossing to maintain speed
choices.C: Shift down before reaching the tracks and do not change gears while crossing
choices.D: Accelerate and upshift while crossing

en.explanation: If a vehicle has a manual transmission, shift down before reaching the tracks. To avoid stalling, do not change gears while crossing the track.

en.question: What must you do when moving out of an alley or driveway in an urban area before entering the sidewalk area?

choices.A: Honk your horn and proceed slowly
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles on the street
choices.D: Flash your headlights

en.explanation: In urban areas, you must come to a complete stop when moving out of an alley, building, private road, or driveway and before entering the sidewalk area.

en.question: How should you turn your front wheels when parking facing downhill on a street with curbing?

choices.A: Turn the wheels away from the curb
choices.B: Turn the wheels toward the curb
choices.C: Keep the wheels pointing straight ahead
choices.D: Turn the wheels toward the center of the road

en.explanation: If you park on a street with curbing and your vehicle is facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb so your vehicle will roll toward the curb.

en.question: When parallel parking on a street with two-way traffic, how close must your right-hand wheels be to the curb?

choices.A: Within 6 inches
choices.B: Within 12 inches
choices.C: Within 18 inches
choices.D: Within 24 inches

en.explanation: When parking on streets with two-way traffic, park so the right-hand wheels are parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the striped area on the pavement next to an accessible parking space?

choices.A: It may be used for parking if you have a disabled parking placard.
choices.B: It may be used for parking only for less than 15 minutes.
choices.C: Vehicles may not use this striped area for parking under any circumstances.
choices.D: It is reserved for electric vehicles only.

en.explanation: A striped area on the pavement next to an accessible parking space is part of the reserved space. Vehicles may not use this striped area for parking even if they have a disabled parking placard or disability license plates.

en.question: Which of the following is a place where stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited?

choices.A: On a one-way street
choices.B: In a marked, buffered, or barrel-protected bike lane
choices.C: Within 50 feet of a driveway
choices.D: On a street without curbing

en.explanation: Stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited in a marked, buffered, or barrel-protected bike lane.

en.question: How far in advance will a school bus give a warning before a stop in a rural area?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: A warning will be given by the school bus at least 100 feet (200 feet in rural areas) in advance of a stop.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are required by law to stop at almost all railroad crossings?

choices.A: Vehicles towing a trailer
choices.B: Vehicles carrying people for hire
choices.C: Electric vehicles
choices.D: Motorcycles

en.explanation: Vehicles required by law to stop at most all railroad crossings are vehicles carrying people for hire, school buses, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

en.question: How far away must a driver park or stand their vehicle from a fire hydrant?

choices.A: At least 10 feet
choices.B: At least 15 feet
choices.C: At least 20 feet
choices.D: At least 30 feet

en.explanation: According to the manual, standing or parking a vehicle is prohibited within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

en.question: It is illegal to stand or park a vehicle within how many feet of a STOP sign, YIELD sign, or traffic control signal?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that standing or parking a vehicle is prohibited within 30 feet of a STOP sign, YIELD sign, or traffic control signal.

en.question: Under Illinois law, it is illegal to operate a vehicle's sound system at a volume that can be heard from what distance?

choices.A: 50 feet or more
choices.B: 75 feet or more
choices.C: 100 feet or more
choices.D: 150 feet or more

en.explanation: Illinois law states that you may not operate any sound system at a volume that can be heard 75 feet or more from a vehicle being driven on a highway.

en.question: How should a driver proceed if they are waiting within an intersection to make a left turn and the traffic signal turns red?

choices.A: Wait in the intersection until the light turns green again.
choices.B: Back up out of the intersection immediately.
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic and complete the turn.
choices.D: Stop and wait for a police officer to direct traffic.

en.explanation: If a driver is within an intersection waiting to make a left turn and the traffic signal light turns red, they should yield to oncoming traffic and complete the turn.

en.question: What is the penalty for being convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus?

choices.A: A suspension of the vehicle registration.
choices.B: A suspension of driving privileges.
choices.C: A $30 fine.
choices.D: A warning for the first offense.

en.explanation: The penalty for being convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus is a suspension of driving privileges.

en.question: In a business or residential district, for what distance should a continuous turn signal be given before making a left or right turn?

choices.A: Not less than 50 feet
choices.B: Not less than 75 feet
choices.C: Not less than 100 feet
choices.D: Not less than 200 feet

en.explanation: A continuous turn signal must be given for not less than 100 feet before turning in a business or residential district.

en.question: What must drivers do when approaching a construction area?

choices.A: Increase their speed to get out of the way quickly.
choices.B: Honk their horn several times to alert workers.
choices.C: Turn on their hazard lights and maintain speed.
choices.D: Slow down, stop all wireless telephone communications, and yield the right of way.

en.explanation: When approaching a construction area, drivers should slow down, stop all wireless telephone communications, and yield the right of way.

en.question: When must a driver slow down for a school zone?

choices.A: On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m., when children are present and signs are posted.
choices.B: Only during school recess periods.
choices.C: At all times, including weekends and holidays.
choices.D: On school days between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. regardless of signs.

en.explanation: A driver must slow down for a school zone on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m., when children are present and signs are posted.

en.question: What should a driver do if they are pulled over by law enforcement and need to get their insurance or registration from the glove box?

choices.A: Quickly reach into the glove box before the officer approaches.
choices.B: Exit the vehicle to hand the documents to the officer.
choices.C: Inform the police officer before reaching into the glove box.
choices.D: Wait for the officer to open the passenger door and check the glove box.

en.explanation: If drivers need to obtain insurance or vehicle registration information from the glove box, they should inform the police officer before doing so.

en.question: When a train is approaching, all vehicles are required to stop within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?

choices.A: Between 5 and 10 feet
choices.B: Exactly 10 feet
choices.C: Between 15 and 50 feet
choices.D: Between 50 and 100 feet

en.explanation: All vehicles are required to stop between 15 and 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing when a train is approaching.

en.question: If a pedestrian must walk on a roadway with two-way traffic because there is no sidewalk or shoulder, how should they walk?

choices.A: Facing away from oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Facing oncoming traffic.
choices.C: In the center of the roadway.
choices.D: On the right side of the lane with the flow of traffic.

en.question: Which of the following statements about hitchhiking is true according to Illinois law?

choices.A: It is legal as long as the pedestrian stays on the shoulder.
choices.B: It is illegal to stand on the roadway to ask for a ride.
choices.C: It is legal only during daylight hours.

en.question: Under what conditions may a pedestrian age 18 or older skate on a public roadway?

choices.A: Where the posted speed limit is 45 mph or less, from sunrise to sunset.
choices.B: Where the posted speed limit is 55 mph or less, at any time of day.
choices.C: Only in designated residential districts with a 20 mph speed limit.
choices.D: Skating on public roadways is strictly prohibited for all ages.

en.explanation: Pedestrians ages 18 or older may skate on public roadways where the posted speed limit is 45 mph or less from sunrise to sunset as long as vehicular traffic is not impeded.

en.question: If a driver must stop their vehicle in an emergency on a highway outside a business or residential district, they must ensure there is a clear view of the vehicle for at least how many feet in each direction?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: In an emergency, drivers may stop their vehicle and park only if there is a clear view of 200 feet in each direction.

en.question: What is the legal limit for the number of passengers allowed in the front and rear seats of a vehicle?

choices.A: As many as can comfortably fit without obstructing the driver's view.
choices.B: No more people than there are seat belts available.
choices.C: A maximum of three people in the front seat and four in the rear.
choices.D: There is no limit as long as the vehicle is not overloaded with freight.

en.explanation: Illinois law states there should be no more people in the front and rear seats as there are seat belts.

en.question: What is the most common situation that causes a motorcycle crash at an intersection?

choices.A: A motorcycle rear-ending an automobile at a stop sign.
choices.B: An oncoming automobile making a left turn in front of a motorcycle.
choices.C: A motorcycle attempting to pass an automobile on the right.
choices.D: An automobile making a right turn while a motorcycle is in its blind spot.

en.explanation: The manual states that more than 50% of all motorcycle crashes occur at intersections, and the most common situation occurs when an oncoming automobile makes a left turn in front of a motorcycle.

en.question: What may a motorcyclist do if a red light fails to turn green after 120 seconds?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection after yielding the right of way to oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed immediately.
choices.C: Make a right turn on red, but never proceed straight.
choices.D: Dismount and walk the motorcycle across the intersection.

en.explanation: If a red light fails to turn green after 120 seconds, a motorcyclist may proceed through an intersection after yielding the right of way to oncoming traffic.

en.question: How should a driver handle lane sharing with a motorcycle?

choices.A: Share the lane if the motorcycle is staying to the far right.
choices.B: Share the lane only in heavy traffic conditions.
choices.C: Never share the lane, as the motorcyclist is entitled to the entire lane.
choices.D: Share the lane if the road surface is dry and clear.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Although there may be enough room in the traffic lane for an automobile and a motorcyclist, remember that the motorcyclist needs the room to maneuver safely and is entitled to the entire lane. Do not share the lane."

en.question: What is the recommended minimum following distance a driver should allow when behind a motorcycle?

choices.A: One to two seconds
choices.B: Two to three seconds
choices.C: Three to four seconds
choices.D: Five to six seconds

en.explanation: Drivers should allow at least three to four seconds following distance when behind a motorcycle so the motorcyclist has enough time to maneuver in an emergency.

en.question: Which of the following is required to legally operate an autocycle on Illinois roadways?

choices.A: A Class M motorcycle license
choices.B: A valid Illinois driver's license
choices.C: A commercial driver's license (CDL)
choices.D: A special autocycle endorsement

en.explanation: An autocycle is a three-wheeled vehicle with a steering wheel and seating that does not require straddling. The operator must have a valid Illinois driver’s license to legally operate it.

en.question: How much passing space must a motorist leave when passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: At least 1 foot from the edge of the vehicle's side mirror.
choices.B: At least 2 feet from the edge of the vehicle's side mirror.
choices.C: At least 3 feet from the edge of the vehicle's side mirror.
choices.D: At least 5 feet from the edge of the vehicle's side mirror.

en.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, motorists must do so slowly and leave at least 3 feet of passing space from the edge of the vehicle’s side mirror.

en.question: What should a motorist do if they are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on the right?

choices.A: Speed up and make the turn before the bicyclist reaches the intersection.
choices.B: Honk to warn the bicyclist to stop, then make the turn.
choices.C: Squeeze past the bicyclist on the left and turn sharply.
choices.D: Let the bicyclist go through the intersection first before making the right turn.

en.explanation: If motorists are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on the right, they should let the bicyclist go through the intersection first before making a right turn.

en.question: Why should a driver consider using their right hand to open the vehicle door after parking?

choices.A: It prevents the door from opening too wide into traffic.
choices.B: It forces the driver's upper body to turn and look behind for oncoming cyclists.
choices.C: It is required by Illinois state law for all drivers.
choices.D: It allows the driver to exit the vehicle more quickly.

en.explanation: Using your right hand to open the car door will force your upper body to turn and look behind for oncoming cyclists, giving you a better opportunity to check your surroundings.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to operate a Class 3 low-speed electric bicycle?

choices.A: 14 years old
choices.B: 15 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: Persons may operate a Class 3 low-speed electric bicycle only if they are 16 years of age or older.

en.question: What is the maximum number of bicyclists allowed to ride side by side on a standard public roadway?

choices.A: One (single file only)
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: Bicyclists may ride side by side on the roadway as long as traffic is not impeded. Riding more than two abreast is prohibited except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles.

en.question: What is required if a moped or scooter is carrying two people?

choices.A: A sidecar attached to the right side of the vehicle.
choices.B: A seat and footrest for the passenger.
choices.C: An engine with at least 2 horsepower.
choices.D: A special passenger permit from the DMV.

en.explanation: According to the manual, mopeds or scooters carrying two people must have a seat and footrest for the passenger.

en.question: What should you do when your vehicle is being passed by a motorcycle?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent the motorcycle from passing.
choices.B: Move onto the shoulder to give the motorcycle more room.
choices.C: Maintain your lane position and speed.
choices.D: Brake sharply to let the motorcycle pass quickly.

en.explanation: When being passed by a motorcycle, you should maintain your lane position and speed, allowing the motorcycle to complete the maneuver.

en.question: When is a vehicle allowed to park or idle in a designated bike lane?

choices.A: Only when picking up or dropping off passengers.
choices.B: Only if there are no bicyclists currently present in the lane.
choices.C: Only during nighttime hours.
choices.D: Vehicles are never allowed to park or idle in designated bike lanes.

en.explanation: Vehicles are not allowed to drive, park, idle, or drop off or pick up passengers in designated bike lanes even if bicyclists are not present.

en.question: What type of driver's license is required to operate a scooter with an engine displacement of 150cc or greater?

choices.A: Any valid Illinois driver's license
choices.B: A Class L motorcycle license
choices.C: A Class M motorcycle license
choices.D: No license is required

en.explanation: According to the manual, if a scooter has an engine with 150cc displacement or greater, it is considered a motorcycle and a Class M license is required.

en.question: How old must you be to operate a low-speed electric scooter on Illinois roadways?

choices.A: 15 years of age or older
choices.B: 16 years of age or older
choices.C: 18 years of age or older
choices.D: 21 years of age or older

en.explanation: The manual states that you must be 18 years of age or older to operate a low-speed electric scooter.

en.question: Why should you always dim your headlights when following a truck at night?

choices.A: Bright lights will drain your vehicle's battery faster.
choices.B: Bright lights will blind the drivers of large vehicles when they reflect off the large side mirrors.
choices.C: Bright lights make it difficult for oncoming traffic to see the truck.
choices.D: Bright lights can cause the truck's taillights to appear dimmer.

en.explanation: You should always dim headlights when following a truck at night because bright lights will blind the drivers of large vehicles when they reflect off the large side mirrors.

en.question: What should a driver do when passing a large truck at night to let the truck driver know their intent?

choices.A: Sound the horn continuously until the pass is complete.
choices.B: Turn on the hazard lights.
choices.C: Blink the vehicle's headlights.
choices.D: Drive closely alongside the truck's cab.

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to blink the vehicle's headlights when passing a truck to let the truck driver know, especially at night.

en.question: What does Illinois law require you to do when approaching a disabled vehicle using hazard lights on a four-lane highway?

choices.A: Stop immediately and offer assistance.
choices.B: Change lanes away from the disabled vehicle if it is safe to do so.
choices.C: Maintain your speed and stay in your current lane.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert the disabled vehicle's driver.

en.explanation: When approaching any disabled vehicle using hazard lights on a four-lane highway, Illinois law requires drivers to change lanes away from the disabled vehicle if it is safe to do so.

en.question: When towing one vehicle with another using a drawbar, what is the maximum distance allowed between the two cars in most cases?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.explanation: Illinois law states that when towing one vehicle with another, the distance between the two cars should not exceed 15 feet in most cases.

en.question: After how many hours can law enforcement request an abandoned vehicle be towed from a highway in an urban area at the owner's expense?

choices.A: 2 hours
choices.B: 10 hours
choices.C: 24 hours
choices.D: 48 hours

en.explanation: Law enforcement may request that a vehicle be towed at the owner's expense if it has been left along a highway in an urban area after 10 hours.

en.question: Low-speed vehicles may operate on any street with a posted speed limit of:

choices.A: 25 mph or less.
choices.B: 30 mph or less.
choices.C: 35 mph or less.
choices.D: 45 mph or less.

en.explanation: Low-speed vehicles may operate on any street with a posted speed limit of 30 mph or less unless prohibited by the local municipality.

en.question: What is the normal speed range for slow-moving vehicles such as farm vehicles and animal-drawn vehicles?

choices.A: 5-20 mph

en.explanation: Normal speeds for slow-moving vehicles range from 5-20 mph.

en.question: When lights are required, what type of signal must be mounted as high as possible on the rear of a slow-moving vehicle?

choices.A: A solid red light visible for 100 feet.

choices.C: A rotating blue light visible for 300 feet.
choices.D: A flashing white light visible for 1000 feet.

en.question: Why should you never sound a horn when near a horseback rider or other livestock?

choices.A: It is a violation of local noise ordinances.
choices.B: The sound may frighten the animal and cause a crash.
choices.C: It will cause the rider to lose their right-of-way.

en.explanation: Never sound a horn when near a horse or other livestock, as the sound may frighten it and cause a crash.

en.question: In Illinois, it is illegal to drive if your Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is at or above what percentage?

en.question: Can you be convicted of Driving Under the Influence (DUI) if your Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is less than .08%?

choices.A: No, you can only be convicted if your BAC is exactly .08% or higher.
choices.B: Yes, but only if you are under 21 years of age.
choices.C: Yes, you can be convicted if your driving ability is impaired.
choices.D: No, a BAC under .08% is considered legally safe in all circumstances.

en.explanation: You can be convicted of Driving Under the Influence (DUI) if your BAC is less than .08% but your driving ability is impaired.

en.question: Which of the following is the only effective way to remove the effects of alcohol from your system?

choices.A: Drinking strong coffee
choices.B: Taking a cold shower
choices.C: Eating a heavy meal
choices.D: Time

en.explanation: Time is the only way to remove the effects of alcohol. Food, coffee, and showers do not speed up the process.

en.question: What type of driver's license is required to operate a moped on Illinois roadways?

choices.A: A Class M motorcycle license
choices.B: A Class L motorcycle license
choices.C: Any valid Illinois driver's license
choices.D: A commercial driver's license (CDL)

en.question: Under Illinois law, what is the legal limit for cannabis tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) concentration in whole blood while operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: 2 nanograms or more per milliliter

choices.D: 10 nanograms or more per milliliter

choices.B: 10 years

choices.A: You automatically consent to submit to certain tests to determine if you are under the influence.

choices.B: 6 months

choices.C: 45 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.question: What is the minimum revocation period for a first DUI conviction in Illinois?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 3 years
choices.D: 5 years

choices.D: 5 years

en.question: In which of the following vehicles is it legal for passengers to consume alcoholic beverages?

choices.D: 24 hours

choices.B: An eight-hour defensive driving course

en.question: What are the potential penalties for providing alcohol to a person under age 21?

choices.B: The indefinite withdrawal of driving privileges by the Secretary of State's office

en.question: After a driver's license is revoked, what is the minimum amount of time a driver must generally wait before they are eligible to reapply for a license?

en.question: For a driver under age 21, how many traffic violation convictions within a 24-month period will result in a driver's license suspension?

choices.C: Four
