es.explanation: Esta señal advierte sobre tráfico de doble sentido más adelante. Es posible que esté saliendo de una carretera de un solo sentido o de una autopista dividida y se encuentre con vehículos que viajan en la dirección opuesta.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué condición de la carretera advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Condiciones de carretera con hielo
choices.B: La carretera puede estar resbaladiza cuando está mojada
choices.C: Camino sinuoso más adelante
choices.D: Pavimento irregular

es.explanation: Una señal de "resbaladizo cuando está mojado" advierte que la superficie de la carretera puede volverse muy resbaladiza durante la lluvia o en condiciones de humedad. Reduzca su velocidad y evite frenar o girar bruscamente.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un bache o resalto en la carretera
choices.B: Una superficie de carretera irregular
choices.C: Una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante
choices.D: Construcción de carreteras

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte sobre una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante. Es posible que deba ajustar su velocidad y cambiar a una marcha más baja, especialmente en camiones o al remolcar.

es.question: ¿Para qué le advierte esta señal que se prepare?

choices.A: Una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante
choices.B: Un semáforo más adelante
choices.C: Un cruce escolar
choices.D: Un control policial

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte sobre un semáforo más adelante. Esté preparado para detenerse si la luz está en rojo o amarillo. Esta señal se coloca a menudo donde el semáforo puede no ser visible desde la distancia.

es.question: ¿Qué le indica esta señal que debe esperar más adelante?

choices.A: Una señal de ceda el paso
choices.B: Un semáforo
choices.C: Una señal de alto (STOP) donde debe detenerse
choices.D: Un reductor de velocidad

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante. Comience a reducir la velocidad y prepárese para detenerse por completo en la señal de alto.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un cruce de ferrocarril más adelante
choices.B: Un cruce de caminos o intersección más adelante
choices.C: Un hospital más adelante
choices.D: Un cruce de peatones

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay un cruce de caminos o una intersección de 4 vías más adelante. Esté atento al tráfico que ingresa desde los caminos laterales.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Una intersección en T más adelante
choices.B: Un camino lateral que entra por la derecha
choices.C: Una curva en la carretera
choices.D: Un callejón sin salida

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte sobre un camino lateral que entra por la derecha. Esté atento a los vehículos que ingresan a la carretera desde el camino lateral.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: Los carriles se están fusionando
choices.B: Un carril está terminando
choices.C: Se está añadiendo un nuevo carril; no es necesario incorporarse
choices.D: Giro a la derecha obligatorio

es.explanation: Una señal de carril añadido significa que un nuevo carril se une a la carretera sin requerir una incorporación. El tráfico que entra desde la rampa tiene su propio carril nuevo.

es.question: ¿Qué prohíbe esta señal?

choices.A: Detenerse en cualquier momento
choices.B: Estacionarse en esta área
choices.C: Permanecer parado o con el motor encendido
choices.D: Cargar o descargar

es.explanation: Una señal roja y blanca de NO ESTACIONAR (NO PARKING) significa que no puede estacionar su vehículo en esta área. Puede detenerse brevemente para subir o bajar pasajeros.

es.question: ¿Quién tiene permitido estacionar en un espacio marcado con esta señal?

choices.A: Cualquier persona por menos de 15 minutos
choices.B: Solo personas de la tercera edad
choices.C: Solo vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de discapacidad vigente
choices.D: Cualquier conductor con un pasajero que tenga una discapacidad

es.explanation: Una señal azul con el símbolo de la silla de ruedas marca el estacionamiento reservado para personas con discapacidades. Solo los vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de matrícula de estacionamiento para personas con discapacidad vigente pueden estacionar en estos espacios. Las infracciones conllevan multas elevadas.

en.question: What visual indicator on an Indiana license, ID, or permit signifies that it is a Real ID?

choices.B: In a timely and accurate manner while ensuring security and transparency
choices.C: By offering free credential replacements to all Hoosiers
choices.D: Through exclusively online platforms

choices.A: Heavy Machinery Operator's License

choices.D: Recreational Vehicle (RV) License

choices.A: Retired Reserve Indicator

choices.D: Overseas Deployment Indicator

choices.A: Driver Safety Program
choices.B: Highway Watch Program
choices.C: Hoosier Helper Initiative
choices.D: Accident Forgiveness Program

en.question: What term does the Indiana Driver's Manual use to describe drivers with multiple severe traffic offenses?

choices.A: Chronic Traffic Offenders
choices.B: Habitual Traffic Violators
choices.C: Repeat Moving Violators
choices.D: High-Risk Motorists

en.explanation: Chapter 5 of the manual covers points and suspensions, including a specific section dedicated to 'Habitual Traffic Violators'.

en.question: Which of the following is a specific category of traffic signs discussed in the manual?

choices.A: Traffic Suggestion Signs
choices.B: Traffic Guidance Signs
choices.C: Traffic Enforcement Signs
choices.D: Traffic Observation Signs

en.explanation: Chapter 6 of the manual covers Traffic Signs and Signals, which includes a specific section on 'Traffic Guidance Signs'.

en.question: According to the manual's section on safe vehicle operation, what vehicle maintenance topic is specifically addressed alongside tire pressure?

choices.A: Oil Life
choices.B: Brake Pad Wear
choices.C: Tread Depth
choices.D: Coolant Levels

en.explanation: Chapter 7 of the manual covers Safe Vehicle Operation, which includes a section specifically titled 'Tire Pressure and Tread Depth'.

en.question: Which of the following driving behaviors are specifically addressed in the Safe Vehicle Operation chapter?

choices.A: Distracted Driving and Aggressive Driving
choices.B: Joyriding and Street Racing
choices.C: Tailgating and Brake Checking
choices.D: Carpooling and Ridesharing

en.explanation: Chapter 7 of the manual covers Safe Vehicle Operation, which includes specific sections on 'Distracted Driving' and 'Aggressive Driving'.

en.question: What specific type of cycle, other than a motorcycle, has its own section under Restrictions and Endorsements?

choices.A: Bicycles
choices.B: Motor Driven Cycle (MDC)
choices.C: Electric Scooters
choices.D: All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)

en.explanation: Chapter 2 of the manual covers Restrictions and Endorsements, including a specific section for the 'Motor Driven Cycle (MDC)'.

en.question: What format are credentials issued to Indiana residents who are under 21 years of age?

choices.A: Horizontal format
choices.B: Vertical format
choices.C: Square format
choices.D: Booklet format

en.explanation: All credentials issued to Indiana residents who are under 21 years of age have a vertical format and display the dates the cardholder turns 18 and 21 years of age.

en.question: What does a star marker in the upper right-hand corner of an Indiana credential indicate?

choices.A: The driver is an organ donor.
choices.B: The driver has a commercial driver's license.
choices.C: The credential is Real ID-compliant.
choices.D: The driver is under 21 years of age.

en.explanation: A star marker appears in the upper right-hand corner to indicate that a credential is Real ID-compliant and may be used as identification for federal purposes.

en.question: How long does a new Indiana resident have to obtain a new Indiana driver's license?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: When you become an Indiana resident, you have 60 days to obtain a new Indiana driver's license.

en.question: If you are a new Indiana resident who has never held a valid driver's license from another state, how long must you hold an Indiana learner's permit before applying for a driver's license?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: If you have never held a valid driver's license from another state, you must hold an Indiana learner's permit for 180 days before you can apply for an Indiana driver's license.

en.question: What tests must you pass if your out-of-state driver's license has been expired for more than five years?

choices.A: Only a standard vision screening
choices.B: Only a knowledge exam
choices.C: A knowledge exam and a driving skills test
choices.D: A driving skills test and a physical exam

en.explanation: If your out-of-state driver's license has been expired for more than five years, you must pass a knowledge exam and a driving skills test to obtain an Indiana driver's license.

en.question: What test is required for an 18-year-old new resident whose out-of-state driver's license has been expired for less than five years?

choices.A: A driving skills test
choices.B: A knowledge exam
choices.C: A physical examination
choices.D: A hearing test

en.explanation: If your out-of-state driver's license has been expired for less than five years, or you have held an unrevoked out-of-state driver's license for less than one year, you must pass a knowledge exam to obtain an Indiana driver's license.

en.question: Which of the following is considered evidence of Indiana residency?

choices.A: Being a temporary employee in the state
choices.B: Being a registered voter in Indiana
choices.C: Being enrolled at a post-secondary institution without claiming Indiana residency
choices.D: Being an active-duty military member claiming residency in another state

en.explanation: Evidence of Indiana residency includes maintaining a residential address in Indiana, being a registered voter in Indiana, or having a dependent enrolled in an elementary or secondary school located in Indiana.

en.question: Who is eligible to receive an Indiana Identification Card at no cost?

choices.A: Any individual under the age of 18
choices.B: Individuals who are or will be 18 years of age on or before the next General or Municipal Election
choices.C: Any new resident of Indiana
choices.D: Individuals who have surrendered an out-of-state driver's license

en.explanation: Identification cards are issued at no cost to individuals who are or will be 18 years of age on or before the next General or Municipal Election.

en.question: What is the deadline established by the DHS and TSA for requiring a Real ID-compliant credential to board an aircraft?

choices.A: January 1, 2010
choices.B: December 31, 2022
choices.D: January 1, 2026

en.explanation: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Transportation Security Administration (TSA) have established May 7, 2025, as the deadline for when they will begin requiring those boarding an aircraft using a driver's license or identification card to have a Real ID-compliant credential.

en.question: Which of the following documents is NOT explicitly listed as required to upgrade to a Real ID-compliant credential?

choices.A: Proof of identity
choices.B: Proof of lawful status
choices.C: Social Security number
choices.D: Proof of vehicle insurance

en.explanation: To upgrade to a Real ID-compliant credential, you must provide original versions or certified copies of your identity, lawful status, Social Security number, and proof of Indiana residency. Proof of vehicle insurance is not required.

en.question: What happens if the BMV discovers an applicant holds a credential from another state during the verification process?

choices.A: The applicant must pay a dual-residency fee.
choices.B: The applicant will be required to surrender the out-of-state credential.
choices.C: The applicant will be issued a temporary Indiana credential for 60 days.
choices.D: The applicant is permanently banned from obtaining an Indiana credential.

en.explanation: If during verification, the BMV discovers another credential has been issued to an applicant in another state... the applicant will be required to surrender the out-of-state credential before the BMV will process an application for an Indiana credential.

en.question: What dates are prominently displayed on an Indiana credential issued to a resident under 21 years of age?

choices.A: The dates the cardholder turns 18 and 21 years of age
choices.B: The dates the cardholder turns 16 and 18 years of age
choices.C: The dates the cardholder obtained their permit and license
choices.D: The dates of the next General and Municipal Elections

en.explanation: All credentials issued to Indiana residents who are under 21 years of age have a vertical format and display the dates the cardholder turns 18 and 21 years of age.

en.question: In addition to providing required documentation, what screening must all new Indiana residents pass when obtaining an Indiana driver's license?

choices.A: A standard hearing screening
choices.B: A standard vision screening
choices.C: A drug and alcohol screening
choices.D: A physical agility screening

en.explanation: Individuals in all the above listed categories must also present documentation proving your identity, lawful status, Social Security number, and Indiana residency... You are also required to pass a standard vision screening.

en.question: Which of the following individuals is NOT considered an Indiana resident for the purpose of obtaining a credential?

choices.A: A person maintaining a residential address in Indiana and not claiming residency elsewhere
choices.B: A registered voter in Indiana
choices.C: A person with a dependent enrolled in an Indiana elementary school
choices.D: Active-duty military personnel in the armed forces who do not claim Indiana as their state of residence

en.explanation: For the purposes of obtaining a credential, active-duty military personnel in the armed forces who do not claim Indiana as their state of residence are not considered Indiana residents.

en.question: If you are 18 years of age or older and hold a valid out-of-state driver's license, which of the following items can you bring to the branch to apply for an Indiana license?

choices.A: A copy of your high school diploma
choices.B: A copy of your official driving record
choices.C: A letter from your previous state's governor
choices.D: A utility bill from your previous state

en.explanation: If you are at least 18 years of age and you hold a valid out-of-state driver's license, you must bring one of the following three items to the branch: your current out-of-state driver's license, a copy of your official driving record, or a verification letter.

en.question: How long is a standard Indiana identification card valid for?

choices.A: 2 years
choices.B: 4 years
choices.C: 6 years
choices.D: 8 years

en.explanation: According to the manual, an identification card and an MDC endorsement are valid for six years.

en.question: If you are applying for an Indiana identification card but already hold a credential from another state, what must you do?

choices.A: Keep both credentials as long as they are from different states
choices.B: Surrender the other credential to the Indiana BMV
choices.C: Pay an additional fee to hold multiple credentials
choices.D: Destroy the out-of-state credential yourself

en.explanation: Indiana residents cannot hold more than one credential at the same time. Therefore, you must surrender any other credential to the Indiana BMV to complete an application for an identification card.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to obtain a Motor Driven Cycle (MDC) endorsement on an identification card?

choices.A: 14 years of age
choices.B: 15 years of age
choices.C: 16 years of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: Identification cards may provide privileges to operate a Motor Driven Cycle (MDC) as long as you are at least 15 years of age and pass an MDC knowledge exam.

en.question: If you are under 16 years of age applying for a learner's permit, which of the following is NOT an acceptable document to prove driver education enrollment?

choices.A: A Certificate of Driver Education Enrollment from the school
choices.B: A certificate dated two weeks prior to the start of the class
choices.C: An online course certificate of completion for theoretical training
choices.D: A document proving enrollment in a BMV licensed Behind-the-wheel training provider

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the online course certificate of completion for theoretical training is not an acceptable document to prove enrollment.

en.question: How long is a standard learner's permit valid from the date of issuance?

choices.A: 1 year
choices.B: 2 years
choices.C: 4 years
choices.D: 6 years

en.explanation: According to the Learner's Permit Validity section, learner's permits are valid for two years from the date of issuance.

en.question: You must retest when renewing your learner's permit if it has been expired for more than how many days?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: If you are visiting a BMV branch to renew your learner's permit and it has been expired more than 180 days, you are required to retest.

en.question: If you are under 16 years of age and practicing driving with a relative, what is the minimum age the licensed relative must be?

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 21 years old
choices.C: 25 years old
choices.D: 30 years old

en.explanation: You may practice driving with a licensed driver who has valid driving privileges and is 25 years of age or older, provided they are related to you by blood, marriage, or legal status.

en.question: How early must you arrive at a BMV branch before it closes to take the computer-based knowledge exam?

choices.A: At least 15 minutes
choices.B: At least 30 minutes
choices.C: At least 45 minutes
choices.D: At least 1 hour

en.explanation: You must arrive at the branch at least 30 minutes before the branch closes to take the computer-based knowledge exam that day.

en.question: What must you do if you fail the driver's knowledge exam?

choices.A: Retake it immediately after paying a fee
choices.B: Wait at least 30 minutes to retake it
choices.C: Wait until the next business day to retake it
choices.D: Wait one full week to retake it

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you fail the knowledge exam, you must wait until the next business day to retake it.'

en.question: A driver renewing their Indiana driver's license must take the knowledge exam if they have at least how many active points on their driving record?

choices.A: 2 or more active points
choices.B: 4 or more active points
choices.C: 6 or more active points
choices.D: 8 or more active points

en.explanation: The driver's knowledge exam is required for a driver who has six or more active points on an Indiana driving record and is renewing their driver's license.

en.question: What should you do if you normally wear glasses or contacts while driving and are taking the vision screening?

choices.A: Remove them to test your natural vision
choices.B: Wear them during the vision screening
choices.C: Only wear them if you fail the initial screening
choices.D: Provide a doctor's note instead of taking the screening

en.explanation: If you normally wear glasses or contacts while driving, you should inform the BMV branch personnel and wear them during the vision screening.

en.question: If you are under 18 years old and applying for a learner's permit, you must provide an emergency contact who is at least what age?

choices.A: 18 years of age or older
choices.B: 21 years of age or older
choices.C: 25 years of age or older
choices.D: Any age as long as they are a relative

en.explanation: An individual less than 18 years old applying for a learner's permit is required to provide an emergency contact that is at least 18 years of age or older.

en.question: If you are under 18 and under the care of the Department of Child Services (DCS), you may practice driving with a non-relative licensed driver if they are approved by DCS and at least what age?

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 21 years old
choices.C: 25 years old
choices.D: 30 years old

en.explanation: If under the care of the Department of Child Services, you may choose to practice driving with a licensed driver who is 25 years of age or older and approved by the Department of Child Services.

en.question: If you fail the computer-based knowledge exam, how long must you wait before you can retake it?

choices.A: Until the next business day
choices.B: 48 hours
choices.C: 7 days
choices.D: 14 days

en.explanation: If you fail the knowledge exam, you must wait until the next business day to retake it.

en.question: When scheduling a driving skills exam at the BMV, what is the maximum amount of time in advance you can schedule the appointment?

choices.A: One week
choices.B: Two weeks
choices.C: Three weeks
choices.D: One month

en.explanation: A driving skills exam may be scheduled no more than three weeks, and no less than 48 business hours, ahead of time.

en.question: Which of the following is a valid reason for a BMV examiner to reject a vehicle for the driving skills exam?

choices.A: The vehicle has a manual transmission
choices.B: The vehicle has an inoperative door
choices.C: The vehicle is more than 10 years old
choices.D: The vehicle does not have a backup camera

en.explanation: Examples of reasons vehicles may be rejected for the driving skills exam include an inoperative door, unsafe tires, missing bumper, broken glass/mirrors, or not being properly registered.

en.question: Which of the following actions will result in an automatic failure of the driving skills exam?

choices.A: Leaving your turn signal on after a completed lane change
choices.B: Failing to check your blind spot
choices.C: Backing over a curb
choices.D: Reversing too fast

en.explanation: Backing over a curb is listed as an action that shall result in the automatic failure of the driving skills exam. The other options are actions that could affect your final score or cause you to fail, but are not listed as automatic failures.

en.question: Who is allowed in the vehicle with you when you take the driving skills exam?

choices.A: A licensed parent or guardian
choices.B: A certified driving instructor
choices.C: Only the BMV examiner or authorized BMV personnel
choices.D: Anyone with a valid driver's license

en.explanation: No one other than the BMV examiner(s) conducting the skills exam or other authorized BMV personnel is allowed in your vehicle when you take the driving skills exam.

en.question: What happens if you fail a third driving skills exam while holding a learner's permit?

choices.A: You must wait two months before taking the exam again
choices.B: Your learner's permit is permanently revoked
choices.C: You must retake the driver education course
choices.D: You must wait six months before taking the exam again

en.explanation: Upon failure of a third driving skills exam while holding a learner’s permit, you must wait for two months from the date of the last failed driving skills exam before taking the exam again.

en.question: Who has the first order of preference to sign a sworn statement of financial liability for an applicant under 18 years of age?

choices.A: The noncustodial parent
choices.B: The guardian having custody of the minor
choices.C: Any adult willing to assume the obligation
choices.D: The parent having custody of the minor applicant

en.explanation: The lawful order of preference for financial liability is first the parent having custody of the minor applicant (or a designee specified by the custodial parent).

en.question: What happens if the adult who co-signed for financial liability files a written request to withdraw their financial liability for a minor?

choices.A: The minor must pay a fine
choices.B: The minor's learner's permit or driver's license will be canceled
choices.C: The minor must find a new co-signer within 30 days to keep their license
choices.D: The minor is restricted to driving only to and from school

en.explanation: A written request to withdraw financial liability will cancel the minor’s learner’s permit or driver’s license.

en.question: If a minor applicant is under the care of the Department of Child Services (DCS), what must they provide instead of an adult's signature for financial liability?

choices.A: A letter of recommendation from a judge
choices.B: Proof of a motor vehicle insurance policy meeting minimum liability standards
choices.C: A cash deposit of $1,000 to the BMV
choices.D: Proof of completion of an advanced defensive driving course

en.explanation: If the DCS applicant is applying for a driver’s license or learner’s permit, the applicant must also provide proof of a motor vehicle insurance policy that meets the minimum liability standards set forth in Indiana law.

en.question: If you are applying for a driver's license and are under the age of 21, what type of license will you receive?

choices.A: A restricted license
choices.B: A commercial driver's license (CDL)
choices.C: A probationary driver's license
choices.D: A learner's permit

en.explanation: If you are under the age of 21, then your driver’s license is considered a "probationary" license.

en.question: During the driving skills exam, which of the following will cause an automatic failure?

choices.A: Failing to use a seat belt
choices.B: Failing to use the defroster when needed
choices.C: Driving too slowly
choices.D: Slowing speed when changing lanes

en.explanation: Failure to use a seat belt is listed under the actions that shall result in the automatic failure of the driving skills exam. The other options are actions that could affect your final score or cause you to fail, but are not automatic failures.

en.question: How much does the BMV charge to administer a driving skills exam?

choices.D: There is no charge

en.explanation: There is no charge for the driving skills exam administered by the BMV.

en.question: How old must you be to apply for a driver's license if you have NOT completed a BMV licensed driver education program?

choices.A: 16 years and 90 days of age
choices.B: 16 years and 180 days of age
choices.C: 16 years and 270 days of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: According to the manual, you must be at least 16 years and 270 days of age without completion of a BMV licensed driver education program.

en.question: How long is a standard driver's license valid for a person who is 80 years old?

choices.A: Two years
choices.B: Three years
choices.C: Four years
choices.D: Six years

en.explanation: The manual states that a driver's license is valid for three years if you are aged 75 through 84.

en.question: During the first 180 days of holding a probationary driver's license, which of the following passengers are you allowed to drive with unaccompanied by a qualifying adult?

choices.A: Your friends from school
choices.B: Your sibling
choices.C: Your cousin
choices.D: Your neighbor

en.explanation: You may drive with your child, stepchild, sibling, step or half-sibling, or spouse without another accompanying individual during the first 180 days after obtaining your probationary driver's license.

en.question: For the first 180 days after obtaining your probationary driver's license, you may not drive between what hours?

choices.A: 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
choices.B: 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.C: Midnight and 5 a.m.
choices.D: 9 p.m. and 6 a.m.

en.explanation: The manual states: "For the first 180 days after obtaining your probationary driver's license, you may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m."

en.question: When is a probationary driver's license holder permitted to use a telecommunications device while operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: When using a hands-free device
choices.B: When texting a parent or guardian
choices.C: When stopped at a red light
choices.D: When making a 911 emergency call

en.explanation: Indiana law prohibits all drivers from operating a motor vehicle while using any form of telecommunications device unless the device is being used to make a 911 emergency call.

en.question: The BMV is required to suspend a juvenile's driving privileges upon notification from a school administrator if the juvenile:

choices.A: Receives a single detention
choices.B: Is determined to be a habitual truant
choices.C: Fails a driver education course
choices.D: Is late to school three times

en.explanation: Indiana law requires the BMV to suspend the driving privileges of a juvenile if they are under an expulsion/exclusion/second suspension, have withdrawn from school, or have been determined to be a habitual truant.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to apply for a Commercial Driver's License (CDL) with passenger and/or school bus endorsements?

choices.A: 18 years of age
choices.B: 21 years of age
choices.C: 25 years of age
choices.D: 16 years and 270 days

en.explanation: You must be at least 18 years of age to apply for a CDL and 21 years of age to apply for a CDL with passenger and/or school bus endorsements.

en.question: If you are applying for a driver's license and are at least 18 years of age, how many hours of supervised driving practice must you complete?

choices.A: 30 hours
choices.B: 40 hours
choices.C: 50 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: If you are applying for a driver's license and you are at least 18 years of age, you must complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving practice.

en.question: Of the required 50 hours of supervised driving practice, how many hours must be completed at night (unless you have a daytime-only restriction)?

choices.A: 5 hours
choices.B: 10 hours
choices.C: 15 hours
choices.D: 20 hours

en.explanation: At least 10 hours of supervised driving practice must be completed at night, unless you have a daytime-only restriction on your learner's permit.

en.question: If you obtain a driver's license before the age of 21, your probationary driver's license is valid until you are:

choices.A: 21 years of age exactly
choices.B: 21 years and 30 days of age
choices.C: 21 years and 90 days of age
choices.D: 25 years of age

en.explanation: Your probationary driver's license is valid until you are 21 years and 30 days of age.

en.question: After applying for a new credential, within how many calendar days will it arrive at your mailing address?

choices.A: 7 calendar days
choices.B: 10 calendar days
choices.C: 14 calendar days
choices.D: 21 calendar days

en.explanation: Your credential will be sent to the mailing address on file with the BMV and will arrive at your mailing address within 14 calendar days.

en.question: For what reasons are photo-exempt identification cards available?

choices.A: Medical reasons only
choices.B: Religious reasons only
choices.C: Both medical and religious reasons
choices.D: Privacy reasons only

en.explanation: Photo-exempt learner's permits and driver's licenses are available for medical and religious reasons. Photo-exempt identification cards are available for religious reasons only.

en.question: When applying for a driver's license, which of the following is true regarding the knowledge and skills exams?

choices.A: The skills exam must be completed prior to the knowledge exam
choices.B: The knowledge exam must be completed prior to the skills exam
choices.C: Both exams must be taken on the same day
choices.D: The knowledge exam is waived if you pass the skills exam

en.explanation: To obtain a driver's license, you must pass a knowledge exam for the driver's license you want to obtain, which must be complete prior to the skills exam.

en.question: After holding a probationary license for 180 days (and being under 18), you may drive during restricted hours if you are participating in, going to, or returning from:

choices.A: A school-sanctioned activity
choices.B: A friend's house
choices.C: A local sporting event as a spectator
choices.D: A public park

en.explanation: You may drive during the restricted periods if you are participating in, going to, or returning from lawful employment, a school-sanctioned activity, or a religious event.

en.question: An Indiana CDL allows the holder to operate commercial motor vehicles with gross vehicle weight ratings in excess of:

choices.A: 10,000 pounds
choices.B: 16,000 pounds
choices.C: 20,000 pounds
choices.D: 26,000 pounds

en.explanation: An Indiana CDL allows the holder to operate commercial motor vehicles or combination of vehicles with gross vehicle weight ratings in excess of 26,000 pounds.

en.question: What happens if you change your mailing address with the United States Postal Service but forget to update it with the Indiana BMV?

choices.A: The USPS will automatically forward your credential to your new address.
choices.B: Your credential will be held at the local post office for pickup.
choices.C: Your credential will not be forwarded, preventing delivery.
choices.D: The BMV will email you a digital copy of your credential instead.

en.explanation: The manual states that credentials will only be mailed to the address on file with the BMV and will not be forwarded. Failure to update your address with the BMV will prevent delivery.

en.question: Under Indiana law, who is required to wear a seat belt when a motor vehicle is in motion?

choices.A: Only the driver and front-seat passengers
choices.B: All occupants of a motor vehicle equipped with a standard installation seat belt
choices.C: Only passengers under the age of 18
choices.D: The driver, unless they are operating a commercial vehicle

en.explanation: Indiana law requires all occupants of a motor vehicle equipped with a seat belt that is standard equipment installed by the manufacturer to wear the seat belt any time the vehicle is in motion.

en.question: When is it legally permissible to use a telecommunications device to type or read a text message while operating a moving motor vehicle?

choices.A: When traveling at speeds under 15 mph
choices.B: When stopped at a red traffic light
choices.C: When using hands-free technology or making a 911 emergency call
choices.D: When driving on a rural highway with no other traffic

en.explanation: Indiana law prohibits typing, transmitting, or reading a text or email while operating a moving vehicle unless the device is used with hands-free or voice-operated technology, or to make a 911 emergency call.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a restricted telecommunications device under Indiana's driving laws?

choices.A: A wireless telephone
choices.B: A personal digital assistant (PDA)
choices.C: A text messaging device
choices.D: Citizen band (CB) radio equipment operated by a licensed operator

en.explanation: The definition of a telecommunications device does not include citizen band (CB) radio equipment operated by a person licensed by the FCC.

en.question: What does Restriction G indicate when placed on an Indiana driver's license?

choices.A: Glasses or contact lenses required
choices.B: Outside rearview mirrors required
choices.C: Daylight driving only
choices.D: Interlock device required

en.explanation: According to the Base Driver's License Restrictions chart, Restriction G stands for 'Daylight Driving Only'.

en.question: What are the permitted riding hours for an individual holding a motorcycle learner's permit?

choices.A: Between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM
choices.B: One-half hour before sunrise until one-half hour after sunset
choices.C: From sunrise to sunset only
choices.D: There are no time restrictions for permit holders

en.explanation: If you hold a motorcycle learner's permit, you may only ride during the period of one-half hour before sunrise and one-half hour after sunset.

en.question: If you are obtaining your Indiana driver's license for the first time, what is the minimum age requirement to get a motorcycle endorsement at the same time?

choices.A: 15 years of age
choices.B: 16 years of age
choices.C: 16 years and 90 days of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: You can get a motorcycle endorsement at the same time as your first driver's license provided you are 16 years and 90 days of age or older and have completed a motorcycle safety course.

en.question: To be defined as a Motor Driven Cycle (MDC) under Indiana law, the vehicle's cylinder capacity must not exceed:

choices.A: 35 cubic centimeters
choices.B: 50 cubic centimeters
choices.C: 150 cubic centimeters
choices.D: 250 cubic centimeters

en.explanation: Indiana law defines a vehicle as an MDC if, among other requirements, it has a cylinder capacity not exceeding 50 cubic centimeters.

en.question: Which of the following is a restriction that applies to the operation of a Motor Driven Cycle (MDC)?

choices.A: Must operate at no more than 35 miles per hour
choices.B: May carry one passenger if they wear a helmet
choices.C: Can be operated on interstate highways
choices.D: Must be operated in the center of the roadway

en.explanation: Restrictions for operating an MDC include operating at no more than 35 miles per hour, not carrying passengers, and not operating on an interstate highway.

en.question: Which of the following features is required for a three-wheeled motor vehicle to be legally defined as an autocycle in Indiana?

choices.A: Handlebars for steering
choices.B: Anti-lock brakes
choices.C: A saddle-style seat
choices.D: A cylinder capacity under 50cc

en.explanation: An autocycle must be equipped with a roll cage/hoops, safety belts, anti-lock brakes, and be designed to be controlled with a steering wheel and pedals.

en.question: What credential is required to legally operate an autocycle on Indiana roadways?

choices.A: A motorcycle learner's permit
choices.B: A motorcycle endorsement
choices.C: A valid Indiana driver's license
choices.D: A commercial driver's license (CDL)

en.explanation: You may operate an autocycle on Indiana roadways if you possess a valid Indiana driver's license. A motorcycle learner's permit or endorsement is not required.

en.question: Which of the following is prohibited when operating an autocycle?

choices.A: Driving on interstate highways
choices.B: Using the autocycle for a driving skills exam for a driver's license
choices.C: Operating the vehicle without a motorcycle helmet
choices.D: Carrying a passenger in the enclosed seating area

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that an autocycle 'May not be used for the purpose of a driving skills exam for a driver's license.'

en.question: A for-hire endorsement allows the credential holder to operate a motor vehicle designed to transport fewer than how many passengers for hire?

choices.A: 10 passengers
choices.B: 12 passengers
choices.C: 15 passengers
choices.D: 16 passengers

en.explanation: A for-hire endorsement provides privileges to operate a motor vehicle designed to transport fewer than 16 passengers, including the driver, for the purpose of transporting passengers for hire.

en.question: What are the age and experience requirements to obtain a for-hire endorsement in Indiana?

choices.A: At least 16 years old with 6 months of driving experience
choices.B: At least 18 years old and held a valid Indiana driver's license for at least one year
choices.C: At least 21 years old with a clean driving record
choices.D: At least 18 years old and held a valid Indiana driver's license for at least two years

en.explanation: According to the manual, a for-hire endorsement may be issued to Indiana residents who are at least 18 years of age and who have held a valid Indiana driver's license for at least one year.

en.question: Does the Indiana BMV require a medical examination report to issue a driver's license with a for-hire endorsement?

choices.A: Yes, it must be updated every two years.
choices.B: Yes, but only for drivers over the age of 65.
choices.C: No, the BMV does not require a medical examination report for a for-hire endorsement.
choices.D: No, unless the driver is transporting hazardous materials.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'The BMV does not require a medical examination report in order to issue a driver's license with the for-hire endorsement.'

en.question: Which of the following is NOT considered transporting for hire according to the Indiana driver's manual?

choices.A: Operating a ride share vehicle
choices.B: Operating a medical services vehicle
choices.C: Operating a cab or limousine
choices.D: Operating a bus used to carry passengers for compensation

en.explanation: The manual explicitly lists 'Operating a medical services vehicle' as an exception that is not considered transporting for hire.

en.question: Under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, what happens if an individual who is 18 years of age or older declares their intention to be an organ donor?

choices.A: Their family members can override the decision at the time of death.
choices.B: They must renew their declaration every four years.
choices.C: Their family members cannot override their intention at the time of death.
choices.D: They must carry a separate organ donor card at all times.

en.explanation: The manual states that under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, individuals 18 years of age and older may declare their intention to be organ donors and their family members cannot override their intention at the time of death.

en.question: What document must a veteran provide to obtain a veteran indicator on their credential?

choices.A: A Common Access Card (CAC)
choices.B: A DD 214 issued by the United States Department of Defense
choices.C: A letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs
choices.D: A valid military ID card

en.explanation: To obtain the veteran indicator, you must provide a DD 214 issued by the United States Department of Defense verifying your discharge.

en.question: Indiana law requires the operator of a watercraft to carry a valid driver's license if the engine produces more than how many horsepower?

choices.A: 5 horsepower
choices.B: 10 horsepower
choices.C: 15 horsepower
choices.D: 25 horsepower

en.explanation: Indiana law requires the operator of a watercraft with an engine that produces more than 10 horsepower to carry a valid driver's license.

en.question: If you are 15 years of age or older and do not have a driver's license, what must you do to legally operate a watercraft with an engine over 10 horsepower?

choices.A: Successfully complete an approved boater education course and carry a valid Indiana ID card.
choices.B: Have a licensed adult over the age of 21 in the watercraft with you.
choices.C: Apply for a temporary watercraft permit at the BMV.
choices.D: You cannot operate a watercraft under any circumstances without a driver's license.

en.explanation: If you are 15 or older without a driver's license, you may operate a watercraft only after successfully completing an approved boater education course, and you must have a valid Indiana identification card in your possession.

en.question: What happens to your ability to operate a watercraft if your driver's license is suspended?

choices.A: You may only operate a watercraft during daylight hours.
choices.B: You may operate a watercraft if you complete a boater education course.
choices.C: You may not operate a watercraft.
choices.D: You may operate a watercraft as long as it has less than 25 horsepower.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If your driver's license is suspended, you may not operate a watercraft.'

en.question: When does a parking placard issued for a temporary disability expire?

choices.A: On the date indicated by the health care provider or one year after issuance, whichever occurs first.
choices.B: Two years from the date of issuance.
choices.C: On the driver's next birthday.
choices.D: Six months from the date of issuance.

en.explanation: If you have a temporary disability, your parking placard expires on the date indicated by the health care provider or one year after the date of issuance, whichever occurs first.

en.question: What is the fee for obtaining a permanent parking placard in Indiana?

choices.D: There is no fee for a permanent parking placard.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'There is no fee for a permanent parking placard.'

en.question: Is it permissible to park in the diagonally striped space next to a reserved parking space if you have a valid parking placard?

choices.A: Yes, but only for loading and unloading passengers.
choices.B: Yes, if the main reserved space is already occupied.
choices.C: No, parking in the diagonally striped space is prohibited at all times.
choices.D: No, unless you are driving a wheelchair-accessible van.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Parking in the diagonally striped space next to a reserved parking space is prohibited at all times, even with a valid placard.'

en.question: When does an Indiana probationary driver's license expire?

choices.A: At midnight on the driver's 21st birthday.
choices.B: When the card holder is 21 years and 30 days of age.
choices.C: Four years from the date of issuance.
choices.D: At midnight on the driver's 18th birthday.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a probationary driver's license expires when the card holder is 21 years and 30 days of age.

en.question: If your birthday falls on a day when BMV branches are closed, when does your credential expire?

choices.A: At midnight on the day before your birthday.
choices.B: At midnight on your birthday regardless of BMV hours.
choices.C: At midnight on the next business day.
choices.D: Seven days after your birthday.

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'If your birthday falls on a day when BMV branches are closed, your credential expires at midnight on the next business day.'

en.question: Can you receive points on your driver record for infractions committed while operating a watercraft?

choices.A: No, watercraft infractions are handled separately from driving records.
choices.B: Yes, if you operate your watercraft recklessly, while intoxicated, or break private watercraft laws.
choices.C: Yes, but only if you are operating a watercraft with more than 50 horsepower.
choices.D: No, unless the watercraft is involved in a collision with a motor vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you operate your watercraft recklessly, while intoxicated, or break private watercraft laws, you may have points assessed against your driver record.

en.question: How early can you renew your driver's license with a for-hire endorsement before it expires?

choices.A: Up to 30 days before it expires.
choices.B: Up to 90 days before it expires.
choices.C: Up to six months before it expires.
choices.D: Up to one year before it expires.

en.explanation: You may renew your driver's license with a for-hire endorsement at any Indiana BMV branch or online up to one year before the license expires.

en.question: At what time does an Indiana driver's license typically expire on your birthday?

choices.A: Noon
choices.C: Midnight

en.explanation: According to the manual, all other credentials expire at midnight on your birthday. If the branch is closed, it expires at midnight on the next business day.

en.question: What must you do to renew a driver's license that has been expired for three years?

choices.A: Pay a penalty and pass a vision screening only
choices.B: Pay a penalty, pass a knowledge exam, and pass a vision screening
choices.C: Pass a driving skills exam and vision screening
choices.D: Pay a penalty, pass a knowledge exam, driving skills exam, and vision screening

en.explanation: If you are renewing a driver's license that has been expired for at least 180 days but not more than five years, you must pay an administrative penalty, pass a knowledge exam, and pass a standard vision screening.

en.question: How far in advance can a U.S. citizen or individual with permanent lawful status renew their driver's license?

choices.A: Up to 30 days before expiration
choices.B: Up to 6 months before expiration
choices.C: Up to 12 months before expiration
choices.D: Up to 24 months before expiration

en.explanation: A driver's license or identification card may be renewed by U.S. citizens or individuals with permanent lawful status up to 24 months before the credential expiration.

en.question: If you are at least 21 years of age and have six or more active points on your driving record, what is required to renew your driver's license?

choices.A: You must take a driving skills exam
choices.B: You must take the knowledge exam
choices.C: You must complete a Driver Safety Program
choices.D: You must pay double the renewal fee

en.explanation: If you are at least 21 years of age and have six or more active points on your driving record, you must take the knowledge exam to renew your driver's license.

en.question: If you are temporarily living outside Indiana serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, how long does your driver's license remain valid following your discharge?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: Your driver's license remains valid for 90 days following your discharge from service, post-deployment, or after you are no longer temporarily residing outside Indiana because of service.

en.question: Within how many days must you notify the BMV and apply for an amended credential after changing your principal address?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: If you have an Indiana credential, you must notify the BMV of a change of your principal (legal) address and apply for an amended credential within 30 days of the address change.

en.question: What must you do before visiting a BMV branch to officially change your name on your driver's license?

choices.A: Change your name on your vehicle registration online
choices.B: Visit a Social Security Administration office and wait at least one business day
choices.C: Update your mailing address at a BMV Connect kiosk
choices.D: Complete a Driver Safety Program

en.explanation: You must visit a Social Security Administration office to officially change your name on Social Security documentation and allow at least one business day after your name change transaction is completed before visiting a BMV branch.

en.question: How many points are assessed to your driving record for speeding 16 to 25 miles per hour over the speed limit?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: According to the point values table, speeding 16 - 25 miles per hour over the speed limit results in 4 points.

en.question: How long do points stay active on your Indiana driver record?

choices.A: One year from the conviction date
choices.B: Two years from the conviction date
choices.C: Three years from the conviction date
choices.D: Five years from the conviction date

en.explanation: Points stay active on your driver record for two years from the conviction date.

en.question: How many point credits can an Indiana driver receive for completing a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program (DSP)?

choices.A: A two-point credit
choices.B: A three-point credit
choices.C: A four-point credit
choices.D: A six-point credit

en.explanation: Any Indiana driver may complete a DSP course from a BMV-approved provider and receive a four-point credit.

en.question: The BMV may require drivers 21 years of age and older to complete a Driver Safety Program (DSP) if they are convicted of how many traffic offenses within a 12-month period?

choices.A: Two or more
choices.B: Three or more
choices.C: Four or more
choices.D: Five or more

en.explanation: The BMV may require drivers 21 years of age and older who are convicted of two or more traffic offenses within a 12-month period to complete a BMV-approved DSP course.

en.question: What is the state minimum insurance standard for property damages in any one accident in Indiana?
en.explanation: The state minimum insurance standard includes $25,000 for property damages in any one accident, commonly referred to as part of the 25/50/25 liability insurance.

en.question: If the BMV requests proof of financial responsibility, within how many days must the Certificate of Compliance (COC) be received electronically from your insurer?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: The COC must be received electronically from your insurer and processed by the BMV within 90 days of the BMV's mailing of a request to verify financial responsibility.

en.question: How many points are assessed for driving while suspended or participating in a speed contest on the road?

choices.A: 4 points
choices.B: 6 points
choices.C: 8 points
choices.D: 10 points

en.explanation: The manual lists both 'Driving while suspended' and 'Speed contest on road' as violations that result in 8 points.

en.question: What is the maximum number of times you may replace your credential online before you are required to visit a BMV branch?

choices.A: 3 times
choices.B: 5 times
choices.C: 10 times
choices.D: 15 times

en.explanation: You may replace your credential online a maximum of 10 times before you are required to visit a BMV branch for a replacement.

en.question: What is the state's minimum motor vehicle liability protection in Indiana?
en.explanation: The manual states that the state's minimum motor vehicle liability protection is 25/50/25.

en.question: How many days do you have for your insurer to electronically process a Certificate of Compliance (COC) after the BMV mails a request to verify financial responsibility?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: The COC must be received electronically from your insurer and processed by the BMV within 90 days of the BMV's mailing of a request to verify financial responsibility.

en.question: What is the purpose of an SR22 form?

choices.A: To report a traffic accident to the BMV
choices.B: To demonstrate proof of future financial responsibility
choices.C: To cancel an existing insurance policy
choices.D: To register a company-owned vehicle

en.explanation: Indiana law requires that you have your insurance provider electronically file proof of future financial responsibility with an SR22 form in order for your driving privileges to be reinstated.

en.question: What happens if the BMV receives an SR26 notice from your insurance provider while you have an SR22 requirement?

choices.A: Your driving privileges will be suspended until an effective SR22 is received or the period expires.
choices.B: Your insurance premiums will be reduced.
choices.C: You will be required to retake the driving skills test.
choices.D: Your vehicle registration will be permanently revoked.

en.explanation: If the BMV receives an SR26 (cancellation of SR22 insurance) notice, Indiana law requires the BMV to suspend your driving privileges until it receives an effective SR22 policy, or until the SR22 requirement period expires.

en.question: What is the reinstatement fee for a first no-insurance suspension that occurred after January 1, 2015?
en.explanation: Reinstatement fees are $250 for a first no-insurance suspension that occurred after Jan. 1, 2015.

en.question: How can a driver reinstate their driving privileges without paying a no-insurance reinstatement fee?

choices.A: By completing a defensive driving course
choices.B: By submitting proof of future financial responsibility (SR22) and maintaining it continuously for 180 days
choices.C: By paying the original traffic ticket in full
choices.D: By writing an appeal letter to the BMV

en.explanation: A driver may reinstate their driving privileges without having to pay a no-insurance reinstatement fee by having their insurance provider electronically submit proof of future financial responsibility (SR22 form) and maintain SR22 continuously for 180-days.

en.question: Operating a vehicle is considered a criminal offense if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is in excess of what legal limit?
en.explanation: Operating a vehicle while intoxicated or with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) in excess of the legal limit (.08) is a criminal offense.

en.question: Which of the following is listed as a primary factor in determining an individual's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

choices.A: The individual's height
choices.B: The type of alcohol consumed
choices.C: The individual's body weight
choices.D: The amount of food eaten before drinking

en.explanation: The primary factors in determining an individual's BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly the alcohol is consumed, and the individual's body weight.

en.question: What is the penalty for a motorist who fails a chemical test for alcohol?

choices.A: A 90-day suspension of driving privileges
choices.B: A 180-day suspension of driving privileges
choices.C: A one-year suspension of driving privileges
choices.D: A two-year suspension of driving privileges

en.explanation: A motorist who fails a chemical test will face a suspension of driving privileges for 180 days.

en.question: If a motorist refuses to submit to a chemical test, how long will their driving privileges be suspended?

choices.A: 180 days
choices.B: One year
choices.C: Two years
choices.D: Three years

en.explanation: A motorist who refuses to submit to a chemical test will face a suspension of driving privileges for one year.

en.question: What is the function of an ignition interlock device?

choices.A: It tracks the vehicle's speed and location for law enforcement.
choices.B: It mechanically tests the driver's blood alcohol level before the car can be started.
choices.C: It automatically contacts emergency services in the event of a crash.
choices.D: It prevents the vehicle from exceeding the posted speed limit.

en.explanation: The court may also require the installation of an ignition interlock device, which mechanically tests the driver's blood alcohol level before his or her car can be started.

en.question: How does a conviction for operating a watercraft while intoxicated affect your driving record?

choices.A: It has no effect on your motor vehicle driving record.
choices.B: It results in a warning letter but no suspension.
choices.C: It is forwarded to the BMV and becomes part of your driver record.
choices.D: It only affects your boating license, not your driver's license.

en.explanation: A conviction of operating a watercraft while intoxicated is forwarded to the BMV and the conviction becomes part of your driver record.

en.question: What action can the BMV take if a court determines a parent is delinquent in paying child support?

choices.A: Immediately suspend the delinquent parent's driving privileges.
choices.B: Confiscate the parent's vehicle.
choices.C: Double the parent's vehicle registration fees.
choices.D: Require the parent to retake the driving skills test.

en.explanation: A court that has determined a parent is delinquent in paying child support may order the BMV to immediately suspend the delinquent parent's driving privileges.

en.question: What will happen if you submit a payment to the BMV for services or fees and the payment is not honored (e.g., a bounced check)?

choices.A: You will receive a warning letter giving you 30 days to pay.
choices.B: Your driving privileges will be indefinitely suspended.
choices.C: You will be required to perform community service.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be impounded.

en.explanation: The BMV will indefinitely suspend your driving privileges if you submit payment to the BMV for any services or fees and that payment was not honored.

en.question: How much does it cost to view your driver record online at IN.gov/BMV?

choices.A: $5.00 per view
choices.B: $10.00 annually
choices.C: There is no charge.
choices.D: $15.00 for a certified copy

en.explanation: Your first resource should be to check your driver record, which you may view anytime at no charge at IN.gov/BMV.

en.question: What is the cost of purchasing an Official Driver Record in Indiana?

choices.A: Free

en.explanation: According to the manual, an Official Driver Record may be purchased for $4.

en.question: How long does it typically take the BMV to process reinstatement information once it is received from a court?

choices.A: Up to 48 hours
choices.B: Up to 5 business days
choices.C: Up to 10 business days
choices.D: Up to 30 days

en.explanation: Processing by the BMV may take up to 10 business days once the reinstatement information is received from the court.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the Viewable Driver Record?

choices.A: It costs $4 to view.
choices.B: It can be used as an official transcript for employers.
choices.C: It cannot be printed and should not be used as an official transcript.
choices.D: It is only available at a BMV Connect kiosk.

en.explanation: The Viewable Driver Record cannot be printed and should not be used as an official transcript of your driver record.

en.question: Under Section A of the Habitual Traffic Violator (HTV) laws, how long will a driver's privileges be suspended if they accumulate two judgments within a 10-year period for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated resulting in death?

choices.A: 5 years
choices.B: 10 years
choices.C: 15 years
choices.D: For life

en.explanation: Drivers who accumulate two judgments within a 10-year period for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated resulting in death will have their driving privileges suspended for life.

en.question: A driver who accumulates three major offenses, such as reckless driving or drag racing, within a 10-year period will face a driving privilege suspension of what length?

choices.A: 3 years
choices.B: 5 years
choices.C: 10 years
choices.D: For life

en.explanation: Under Section B, drivers who accumulate three major offenses from the provided list within a 10-year period will have their driving privileges suspended for 10 years.

en.question: What is the penalty for a driver who accumulates 10 or more traffic violations in a 10-year period, including at least one major offense?

choices.A: A 1-year suspension
choices.B: A 5-year suspension
choices.C: A 10-year suspension
choices.D: A lifetime suspension

en.explanation: Under Section C, an HTV is subject to a five-year driving privilege suspension for accumulating 10 or more traffic violations in a 10-year period, one of which is a major offense.

en.question: What does a 'Restriction 5' on an Indiana driver's license indicate?

choices.A: The driver must wear corrective lenses.
choices.B: The driver is restricted to daylight driving only.
choices.C: The driver has been granted hardship, probationary, conditional, or specialized driving privileges.
choices.D: The driver must operate a vehicle with an ignition interlock device.

en.explanation: A 'Restriction 5' is placed on the driver's license of a person who has been granted hardship, probationary, conditional, or specialized driving privileges by court order.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement for a person who has been granted specialized driving privileges by a court?

choices.A: Maintain an effective SR22 on file with the BMV.
choices.B: Complete a defensive driving course every 6 months.
choices.C: Only drive a vehicle with a manual transmission.
choices.D: Surrender their validly issued credential to the BMV.

en.explanation: A person granted specialized driving privileges must maintain an effective SR22 on file with the BMV for the duration of the specialized driving privileges.

en.question: What type of information do brown traffic signs indicate?

choices.A: Temporary traffic conditions
choices.B: Road services and amenities
choices.C: Nearby recreational and cultural interest sites
choices.D: Permitted movements and directions

en.explanation: Brown traffic signs indicate nearby recreational and cultural interest sites, such as a state park.

en.question: A traffic sign displaying information about amenities at an upcoming exit will typically have what background color?

choices.A: Green
choices.B: Blue
choices.C: White
choices.D: Orange

en.explanation: Blue traffic signs display road services and information, such as amenities at an upcoming exit.

en.question: Which color is used for traffic signs that warn drivers of temporary traffic conditions, such as highway construction?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: Red
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: Brown

en.explanation: Orange traffic signs warn drivers of temporary traffic conditions, often due to highway construction and maintenance projects.

en.question: What do white traffic signs typically display?

choices.A: Traffic regulations such as speed limits
choices.B: Warnings for specific road hazards
choices.C: Directions to nearby hospitals
choices.D: Recreational and cultural interest sites

en.explanation: White traffic signs display traffic regulations, such as speed limits, that drivers must obey, as well as helpful information like state highway markers.

en.question: A 'Slippery When Wet' sign is an example of a sign that prepares drivers for specific road conditions. What color is its background?

choices.A: Red
choices.B: Orange
choices.C: Yellow
choices.D: Green

en.explanation: Yellow or fluorescent yellow-green signs prepare drivers for specific road conditions and hazards ahead. A 'Slippery When Wet' sign is an example of a traffic sign with a yellow background.

en.question: What do red traffic signs convey to drivers?

choices.A: Permitted movements and guidance
choices.B: Traffic regulations that require immediate action to avoid threats to safety
choices.C: Nearby school zones and pedestrian crossings
choices.D: Temporary traffic conditions due to construction

en.explanation: Red traffic signs convey traffic regulations that require drivers to take immediate action to avoid threats to traffic safety, such as a 'Wrong Way' sign.

en.question: Which of the following offenses is considered a major offense under Section A of the Habitual Traffic Violator laws, potentially leading to a 10-year suspension if two judgments are accumulated?

choices.A: Nine speeding tickets in a 10-year period
choices.B: Reckless homicide resulting from operation of a motor vehicle
choices.C: Driving with a suspended license
choices.D: Failing to use a turn signal

en.explanation: Reckless homicide resulting from operation of a motor vehicle is listed under Section A as a major offense resulting in injury or death.

en.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green traffic signs warn drivers of?

choices.A: Highway construction zones
choices.B: Nearby schools, pedestrians, and bicycles
choices.C: Upcoming railroad crossings
choices.D: Traffic regulations requiring immediate action

en.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn drivers of nearby schools, pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, and school bus routes.

en.question: Where are pennant-shaped traffic signs posted and what do they indicate?

choices.A: On the right side of the road to indicate a school zone
choices.B: On the left-hand side of two-way roads to warn not to pass on the left
choices.C: At intersections to indicate a required stop
choices.D: Before railroad crossings to warn of approaching trains

en.explanation: Pennant-shaped traffic signs are posted on the left-hand side of two-way roads to warn drivers not to pass other vehicles on the left.

en.question: What type of hazard or condition does a circular traffic sign alert drivers to?

choices.A: Upcoming railroad crossings
choices.B: Slippery road conditions
choices.C: Sharp curves ahead
choices.D: Highway construction zones

en.explanation: Circular traffic signs alert drivers to upcoming railroad crossings.

en.question: A five-sided traffic sign indicates that you are approaching:

choices.A: A stop intersection
choices.B: A yield intersection
choices.C: An area near a school where children may be crossing
choices.D: A no-passing zone

en.explanation: Five-sided traffic signs warn drivers that they are entering an area near a school in which children may be crossing the road.

en.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem indicates that the vehicle cannot exceed what speed?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour
choices.B: 20 miles per hour
choices.C: 25 miles per hour
choices.D: 30 miles per hour

en.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem has an orange, fluorescent center and red reflective borders, and indicates a slow-moving vehicle which cannot exceed 25 miles per hour.

en.question: What colors make up a slow-moving vehicle emblem?

choices.A: A yellow background with black borders
choices.B: An orange, fluorescent center and red reflective borders
choices.C: A red center with white reflective borders
choices.D: A fluorescent yellow-green center with black borders

en.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem has an orange, fluorescent center and red reflective borders.

en.question: What do orange traffic signs generally indicate?

choices.A: Driver services and recreation areas
choices.B: Highway construction and maintenance zones
choices.C: School zones and pedestrian crossings
choices.D: Traffic regulations that must be obeyed immediately

en.explanation: Orange highway construction traffic signs warn drivers to be careful when approaching construction zones.

en.question: What should you do if you are approaching an intersection and facing a steady yellow light, but you are too close to stop safely?

choices.A: Brake hard and stop in the intersection
choices.B: Speed up to beat the red light
choices.C: You may complete your movement through the intersection
choices.D: Pull over to the right side of the road immediately

en.explanation: If you are facing a steady yellow light, your right of way is ending. If you are approaching the intersection and are too close to stop safely, you may complete your movement.

en.question: When turning left at an intersection with a green light displayed without an arrow, how many vehicles may move into the intersection at a time to turn?

choices.A: As many as can fit
choices.B: Only one vehicle at a time
choices.C: Two vehicles at a time
choices.D: No vehicles may enter until the light turns red

en.explanation: If you are facing a green light displayed without an arrow, you may turn through an intersection as long as the intersection is clear... Only one vehicle at a time may move into an intersection to turn left.

en.question: What does a yellow flashing arrow for a turning movement mean?

choices.A: You have the right of way and oncoming traffic must yield
choices.B: You may proceed with the turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic
choices.C: You must come to a complete stop and wait for a green arrow
choices.D: The intersection is closed to turning traffic

en.explanation: A yellow flashing arrow for a turning movement means that you may proceed with the turn only after you have yielded the right of way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

en.question: Under what condition are you permitted to turn left through an intersection with a solid red light?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street
choices.B: When turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street
choices.C: When turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street
choices.D: You are never permitted to turn left on a red light

en.explanation: You may turn left through an intersection with a red light or arrow if you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement before making a permissible right turn on a red light?

choices.A: Slow down to 5 mph before turning
choices.B: Come to a full stop and check for vehicles and pedestrians
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn cross traffic
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: To turn right through an intersection with a red light or arrow, when permissible, you must come to a full stop, check to make sure that there are no vehicles and pedestrians in the path of your turn or about to enter the path of your turn...

en.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a yellow flashing light displayed without an arrow?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop and wait for a green light
choices.B: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop
choices.C: Slow down and use caution when traveling through the intersection
choices.D: Accelerate to clear the intersection quickly

en.explanation: A yellow flashing light displayed without an arrow at an intersection means that you should slow down and use caution when traveling through an intersection.

en.question: What does an equilateral triangle traffic sign indicate?

choices.A: Warns drivers to slow down and be prepared to come to a complete stop to yield
choices.B: Indicates a school zone is ahead
choices.C: Alerts drivers to an upcoming railroad crossing
choices.D: Marks the beginning of a no-passing zone

en.explanation: Traffic signs with three sides of equal length warn drivers to slow down when approaching an intersection, and to be prepared to come to a complete stop in order to yield to other drivers or pedestrians.

en.question: What is the purpose of a supplemental plaque added to the bottom of a stop sign?

choices.A: To indicate the speed limit of the cross street
choices.B: To indicate directions in which the intersection must stop
choices.C: To warn of a nearby school zone
choices.D: To provide distance to the next town

en.explanation: Supplemental plaques are sometimes added to the bottom of stop signs to indicate directions in which the intersection must stop.

en.question: What does a yellow flashing light displayed without an arrow at an intersection mean?

choices.A: Stop and wait for a green light.
choices.B: Slow down and use caution when traveling through the intersection.
choices.C: You have the right-of-way and do not need to slow down.
choices.D: The traffic signal is broken and should be treated as a four-way stop.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a yellow flashing light displayed without an arrow means that you should slow down and use caution when traveling through an intersection.

en.question: If you and another driver arrive at a red flashing light at the same time at an intersection where all traffic is required to stop, who must yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the right.
choices.B: The vehicle on the left.
choices.C: The vehicle traveling faster.
choices.D: The vehicle turning right.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you arrive at the same time as another driver at an intersection where all traffic is required to stop, the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way.

en.question: Under what condition may a person operating a motorcycle proceed through a steady red light that fails to change to green?

choices.A: After coming to a complete stop for at least two minutes and exercising due caution.
choices.B: After honking the horn and waiting 30 seconds.
choices.C: Only if there is a police officer present to direct traffic.
choices.D: Motorcycles are never allowed to proceed through a steady red light.

en.explanation: Operators of motorcycles and motor driven cycles approaching an intersection controlled by a traffic signal may proceed through a steady red light if the operator comes to a complete stop for at least two minutes and exercises due caution.

en.question: Does the rule allowing motorcycles to proceed through a steady red light after waiting two minutes apply to autocycles?

choices.A: Yes, autocycles follow all motorcycle rules.
choices.B: Yes, but they must wait three minutes instead of two.
choices.C: No, this rule does not apply to autocycles.
choices.D: No, autocycles must treat all red lights as yield signs.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the rule allowing operators to avoid prolonged waits at red lights by waiting two minutes does not apply to autocycles.

en.question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a non-operating traffic signal?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection without stopping if the road is clear.
choices.B: Stop before entering the intersection and yield to vehicles that arrived before you or are to your right.
choices.C: Treat the intersection as a yield sign and slow down.
choices.D: Wait until a traffic enforcement officer arrives to direct traffic.

en.explanation: If approaching an intersection with a non-operating signal, you should stop before entering and proceed with caution after yielding to cross-traffic, vehicles that stopped before you, vehicles that arrived at the same time on your right, and pedestrians.

en.question: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon display immediately after a pedestrian activates it?

choices.A: A steady red light.
choices.B: A flashing yellow light.
choices.C: A steady yellow light.
choices.D: Two flashing red lights.

en.explanation: Once activated by a pedestrian, the pedestrian hybrid beacon will display a flashing yellow light to allow drivers to clear the crossing.

en.question: What do yellow lane markings indicate on a roadway?

choices.A: They separate multiple lanes of traffic going in the same direction.
choices.B: They indicate a bus or transit lane.
choices.C: They separate multiple lanes of traffic going in opposite directions.
choices.D: They indicate a pedestrian crossing zone.

en.explanation: According to the manual, yellow lane markings separate multiple lanes of traffic going in opposite directions.

en.question: When passing another vehicle, how much distance must you leave before returning to the right side of the road in front of an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: No less than 50 feet.
choices.B: No less than 100 feet.
choices.C: No less than 200 feet.
choices.D: No less than 500 feet.

en.explanation: You must return to the right side of the road no less than 100 feet before any oncoming vehicle when passing.

en.question: What should you do to check your blind spot before changing lanes?

choices.A: Rely entirely on your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Briefly turn your head toward the lane that you are entering.
choices.C: Honk your horn to alert vehicles in your blind spot.
choices.D: Flash your headlights twice.

en.explanation: When changing lanes, you should briefly turn your head toward the lane that you are entering to make sure that there is no vehicle in your blind spot.

en.question: In which of the following situations is it dangerous and illegal to pass another vehicle?

choices.A: When driving on a road with a broken yellow line.
choices.B: Within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.
choices.C: When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the speed limit.
choices.D: On a multi-lane highway with broken white lines.

en.explanation: It is dangerous and illegal to try to pass other vehicles within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle is passing you on the left-hand side of the road?

choices.A: Increase your speed to prevent them from passing.
choices.B: Move into the left lane to block them.
choices.C: Allow the other vehicle to pass safely and do not increase your speed.
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn them of oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: If another vehicle is passing you on the left-hand side of the road, allow the other vehicle to pass safely and do not increase your speed.
