choices.C: A properly installed booster seat in the back seat.
choices.D: An adult safety belt in the front seat.

en.explanation: Children between the ages of 4 and 8, who are no more than 4 feet 9 inches tall, should ride in the back seat in a properly installed booster seat.

en.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle to avoid injury from an air bag in the event of a crash?

choices.A: In the front passenger seat with the seat pushed all the way back.
choices.B: In the rear seat of the vehicle.
choices.C: In the front seat, provided they are wearing a seatbelt.
choices.D: In the driver's lap.

en.explanation: Children age 12 and under should sit in the rear seat of the vehicle to avoid injury from an air bag in the event of a crash.

en.question: When accelerating a vehicle with a manual transmission, what will happen if you release the clutch suddenly?

choices.A: The vehicle will smoothly increase in speed.
choices.B: The vehicle will jerk forward, and the engine may stall.
choices.C: The drive wheels will lock up and skid.
choices.D: The parking brake will automatically engage.

en.explanation: If you release the clutch suddenly, the vehicle will jerk forward, and the engine may stall.

en.question: What should you do if your drive wheels begin to spin when accelerating on a slippery surface?

choices.A: Press harder on the accelerator to gain traction.
choices.B: Shift into a higher gear immediately.
choices.C: Take your foot off the accelerator.
choices.D: Pump the brakes rapidly.

en.explanation: If you use too much power, the drive wheels may spin, and you could lose control. If the drive wheels begin to spin, take your foot off the accelerator.

en.question: When backing up your vehicle, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?

choices.A: In the opposite direction you want the vehicle to move.
choices.B: In the direction you want the vehicle to move.
choices.C: Keep the wheel straight and use the mirrors to guide you.
choices.D: Turn the wheel left to go right, and right to go left.

en.explanation: The steering wheel is always turned in the direction you want the vehicle to move, whether moving forward or in reverse.

en.question: What is the correct hand position on the steering wheel?

choices.A: Both hands on the inside of the steering wheel rim.
choices.B: One hand at the top of the wheel and one at the bottom.
choices.C: Both hands on the outside of the steering wheel on opposite sides.
choices.D: Palms gripping the wheel tightly with thumbs tucked under the rim.

en.explanation: Both hands should be placed on the outside of the steering wheel on opposite sides. Your grip should be firm but gentle, using your fingers instead of your palms, and you should never turn the wheel while gripping it from the inside of the rim.

en.question: Why are air bags not helpful during a secondary collision?

choices.A: They are designed to remain inflated for several minutes.
choices.B: They deploy only once and deflate quickly after impact.
choices.C: They only deploy when the vehicle is hit from the rear.
choices.D: They automatically disable the vehicle's seatbelts.

en.explanation: Since air bags deploy only once and deflate quickly after impact, they will not be helpful during a secondary collision.

en.question: How can you direct the air bag at your chest instead of your face?

choices.A: Lean forward as close to the steering wheel as possible.
choices.B: Raise your seat or use a cushion and/or adjust the steering wheel downward.
choices.C: Adjust the steering wheel upward toward your head.
choices.D: Recline your seat all the way back.

en.explanation: To direct the air bag at your chest instead of your face, raise your seat or use a cushion and/or adjust the steering wheel downward.

en.question: How should you properly grip the steering wheel while driving?

choices.A: With your palms and thumbs wrapped around the inside of the rim
choices.B: Using your fingers with your thumbs up along the face of the steering wheel
choices.C: With your hands placed firmly at the 12 o'clock position
choices.D: Gripping tightly from the inside of the steering wheel rim

en.explanation: The manual states to use your fingers instead of the palms of your hands and keep your thumbs up along the face of the steering wheel. You should never turn the wheel while gripping it from the inside of the rim.

en.question: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel when using hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?

choices.A: Left hand between 10 and 11 o'clock, right hand between 1 and 2 o'clock
choices.B: Left hand between 9 and 10 o'clock, right hand between 2 and 3 o'clock
choices.C: Left hand between 7 and 8 o'clock, right hand between 4 and 5 o'clock
choices.D: Left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock, right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock

en.explanation: When using hand-to-hand steering, your left hand grasps the wheel between 7 and 8 o'clock and your right hand grasps the wheel between 4 and 5 o'clock.

en.question: Why is the 2 and 10 o'clock hand position no longer recommended for steering?

choices.A: It causes the driver to fatigue more quickly
choices.B: It makes it difficult to reach the turn signals
choices.C: It can be dangerous in vehicles equipped with driver side air bags
choices.D: It reduces the turning radius of modern vehicles

en.explanation: The manual notes that the 2 and 10 o'clock position is not recommended because it can be dangerous in vehicles equipped with air bags.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you use hand-over-hand steering?

choices.A: When driving forward at highway speeds above 55 mph
choices.B: When turning the wheel at low speeds, such as when parking
choices.C: When making evasive maneuvers to avoid a hazard
choices.D: When backing up in a straight line

en.explanation: You should use hand-over-hand steering when turning the wheel at low speeds, such as at an intersection or when parking the vehicle.

en.question: When taking evasive action to avoid a hazard, why is it critical to limit steering input to no more than 180 degrees?

choices.A: To prevent the engine from stalling
choices.B: To avoid locking the anti-lock brakes
choices.C: To prevent the steering wheel from locking in place
choices.D: To prevent traction loss and crossing into oncoming traffic

en.explanation: It is critical to limit steering to not more than 180 degrees because using more input causes traction loss, and often the vehicle moves across the roadway into the path of oncoming vehicles.

en.question: When is the only time it is recommended to use one-hand steering with your hand at the 12 o'clock position?

choices.A: When driving on a straight, empty highway
choices.B: When backing a vehicle to the left or right while turning in the seat to see
choices.C: When operating the windshield wipers or headlights
choices.D: When making a sharp U-turn at an intersection

en.explanation: The only time that 12 o'clock is recommended is when backing a vehicle to the left or right and the driver must turn in the seat in order to see the path of travel to the rear.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do before backing up your vehicle?

choices.A: Shift into reverse and accelerate quickly
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn pedestrians
choices.C: Check behind your vehicle before you get in
choices.D: Adjust your rearview mirror to see the ground directly behind your bumper

en.explanation: Before backing your vehicle, you must check behind your vehicle before you get in, because children or small objects cannot be seen from the driver's seat.

en.question: Which of the following statements about right-of-way laws is true?

choices.A: The law gives the right-of-way to the largest vehicle at an intersection
choices.B: The law states who must yield the right-of-way, but does not give anyone the right-of-way
choices.C: The law gives pedestrians the right-of-way only when they are in a marked crosswalk
choices.D: The law automatically gives the right-of-way to vehicles turning left

en.explanation: The manual states: "The law says who must yield the right-of-way to another roadway user; it does not give anyone the right-of-way."

en.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway or alley, what must you do?

choices.A: Honk your horn to warn pedestrians to clear the sidewalk
choices.B: Yield to pedestrians
choices.C: Proceed quickly to avoid blocking the sidewalk
choices.D: Stop only if there is a stop sign present

en.explanation: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot you must yield to pedestrians.

en.question: Why should you avoid using your horn when yielding to a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?

choices.A: It is illegal to use a horn in residential areas
choices.B: It could confuse or frighten the visually impaired pedestrian or guide dog
choices.C: It signals other drivers to pass you
choices.D: It will cause the traffic light to change

en.explanation: Pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane must be given the right-of-way always. Do not use your horn as it could confuse or frighten the visually impaired pedestrian or guide dog.

en.question: What is the right-of-way rule at an uncontrolled intersection with no stop signs or traffic signals?

choices.A: Yield to vehicles coming from the left
choices.B: The vehicle traveling the fastest has the right-of-way
choices.C: Yield to vehicles already in the intersection and those coming from the right
choices.D: Stop and wait for another driver to wave you through

en.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where there is no stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal, you must yield to vehicles in the intersection and those coming from the right.

en.question: If two vehicles arrive at a 4-way stop at the exact same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the left
choices.B: The vehicle on the right
choices.C: The vehicle traveling straight
choices.D: The vehicle making a right turn

en.explanation: At a 4-way stop, if more than one vehicle arrives at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first.

en.question: When are you permitted to enter an intersection?

choices.A: As soon as the traffic light turns green, regardless of traffic ahead
choices.B: Only when you can get completely through it without blocking traffic flow
choices.C: Whenever you are turning right on red
choices.D: When the vehicle behind you honks its horn

en.explanation: You may not enter an intersection unless you can get through it without blocking traffic flow. You should wait until traffic ahead clears so that you are not blocking the intersection.

en.question: On a horizontally mounted traffic light, where is the red light located?

choices.A: On the far right
choices.B: In the middle
choices.C: On the far left
choices.D: It alternates depending on the intersection

en.explanation: In some metropolitan areas, traffic lights are horizontal, instead of vertical, where the red light is on the left, the yellow light is in the middle and the green light is on the right.

en.question: What must you do when turning left at a steady green traffic light?

choices.A: Turn immediately, as you have the absolute right-of-way
choices.B: Yield to oncoming traffic flow and pedestrians before turning
choices.C: Wait for a green arrow before making the turn
choices.D: Stop completely and wait for the light to turn yellow

en.explanation: Turning left at a steady green traffic light means you may turn but only when the intersection is clear to do so. You should always yield to the oncoming traffic flow and pedestrians.

en.question: What should you do if you are approaching an intersection and the traffic light turns to a steady yellow?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the intersection before the light turns red.
choices.B: Stop immediately wherever you are on the road.
choices.C: Slow down and come to a complete stop if traffic flow to the rear allows.
choices.D: Proceed through the intersection without reducing your speed.

en.explanation: A steady yellow traffic light means the light is about to change to red. You should slow down and come to a complete stop if traffic flow to the rear allows.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?

choices.A: Stop and wait for a green light.
choices.B: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.C: The traffic light is broken and should be treated as a four-way stop.
choices.D: Yield to traffic on the right only.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow traffic light means slow down and proceed with caution. You should be prepared to stop for any traffic flow that may be entering the intersection.

en.question: Under what circumstances is a left turn permitted on a steady red traffic light?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street.
choices.B: Left turns on red are never permitted under any circumstances.
choices.C: When moving from a one-way street onto another one-way street, or from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
choices.D: Only between the hours of midnight and 6:00 AM.

en.explanation: Some left turns may be permitted on red when moving from a one-way street onto another one-way street or from a two-way street onto a one-way street, after checking for traffic and pedestrians.

en.question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?

choices.A: The same as a yield sign.
choices.B: The same as a stop sign.
choices.C: The same as a steady yellow light.
choices.D: Proceed without stopping if the intersection is clear.

en.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means you must stop behind a stop line, crosswalk, or intersection before entering and use the same procedure as you would at a stop sign.

en.question: What shape and color are most warning signs?

choices.A: Rectangular and white with black lettering.
choices.B: Circular and yellow with black lettering.
choices.C: Diamond shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols.
choices.D: Octagonal and red with white lettering.

en.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black lettering or symbols and are diamond shaped.

en.question: What does a round yellow warning sign with an 'X' symbol and black 'RR' letters indicate?

choices.A: You are currently crossing railroad tracks.
choices.B: A highway-railroad grade crossing is ahead.
choices.C: The railroad crossing is closed for repairs.
choices.D: Trains are not currently operating on the tracks ahead.

en.explanation: A round yellow warning sign with an 'X' symbol and black 'RR' letters is placed along the road prior to a highway-railroad grade crossing to caution you to slow down and be prepared to stop.

en.question: Approximately how much distance does a 100-car freight train traveling at 55 mph need to stop?

choices.A: 500 feet.
choices.B: Half a mile.
choices.C: More than a mile.
choices.D: Two miles.

en.explanation: A 100-car freight train traveling at 55 mph will need more than a mile to stop, which is about 18 football fields, once the train is set into emergency braking.

en.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train is approaching, what is the safest immediate action?

choices.A: Stay in the vehicle and call 911.
choices.B: Get everyone out and run in the direction from which the train is approaching.
choices.C: Get everyone out and run in the same direction the train is traveling.
choices.D: Try to push the vehicle off the tracks.

en.explanation: If you stall your vehicle when crossing railroad tracks, get everyone out of the vehicle and far away from the tracks, run in the direction from which the train is approaching to avoid being injured by flying debris.

en.question: Why is it wise not to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks?

choices.A: It damages the vehicle's transmission.
choices.B: It causes the tires to lose traction on the metal rails.
choices.C: You might stall your vehicle on the tracks.
choices.D: It is illegal to shift gears in an intersection.

en.explanation: The manual states it is wise not to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks just in case you might stall.

en.question: What information is provided on the blue Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a highway-rail grade crossing?

choices.A: The train schedule for that specific crossing.
choices.B: A toll-free dispatch number and a DOT number identifying the crossing's exact location.
choices.C: The speed limit for trains passing through the crossing.
choices.D: The distance to the nearest hospital.

en.explanation: The ENS sign provides a toll-free dispatch number for each railroad, and directly below the dispatch number is a Department of Transportation number that identifies the exact location of the crossing.

en.question: What colors are typically used for construction, maintenance, or emergency operation work zone signs?

choices.A: Yellow with black letters.
choices.B: Red with white letters.
choices.C: Orange with black letters or symbols.
choices.D: Green with white letters.

en.explanation: Work zone signs are generally diamond or rectangular shaped and orange with black letters or symbols.

en.question: What must you do when facing a red arrow traffic light?

choices.A: Yield to oncoming traffic and then proceed in the direction of the arrow.
choices.B: Stop, and do not go in the direction of the arrow until the green arrow or light returns.
choices.C: Treat it as a four-way stop.
choices.D: Turn in the direction of the arrow only if there are no pedestrians.

en.explanation: A RED Arrow means you must stop, and you may not go in the direction of the arrow until the green arrow or light returns on the signal.

en.question: What should you be aware of at a highway-railroad grade crossing with more than one train track?

choices.A: You are not required to stop if the first track is clear.
choices.B: There may be more than one train crossing, and the number of tracks will usually be posted.
choices.C: Trains will always travel in the same direction on all tracks.
choices.D: The speed limit is automatically reduced to 10 mph.

en.explanation: At crossings with more than one track, signs warn you that there is more than one track and there may be more than one train crossing. It is important to check for more than one track, train, or railroad vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following warning signs may be fluorescent yellow?

choices.A: Stop signs and Yield signs.
choices.B: Highway-railroad grade crossing signs.
choices.C: School zones, school crossing, and pedestrian crossing signs.
choices.D: Construction and maintenance detour signs.

en.explanation: Some warning signs may be fluorescent yellow, such as school zones, school crossing and pedestrian crossing.

en.question: If you are stopped at an intersection and the light turns green, what must you do before proceeding?

choices.A: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
choices.B: Allow crossing traffic to clear the intersection before you go ahead.
choices.C: Accelerate quickly to establish the right-of-way.
choices.D: Turn right immediately, regardless of other traffic.

en.explanation: If you are stopped at the intersection and the light turns green, you must allow crossing traffic to clear the intersection before you go ahead.

en.question: What is the penalty for speeding in a work zone?

choices.A: Fines are tripled
choices.B: Fines are doubled
choices.C: Your license is automatically suspended
choices.D: You must attend traffic school

en.explanation: According to the manual, fines for speeding in a work zone are doubled.

en.question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a red slash over a symbol indicate?

choices.A: The action shown is prohibited
choices.B: You must yield to the action shown
choices.C: The action shown is recommended
choices.D: A hazard is ahead

en.explanation: The manual states that some regulatory signs have a red circle with a red slash over a symbol, and these signs prohibit certain actions.

en.question: When should you drive the maximum legal speed limit posted on a sign?

choices.A: At all times to prevent traffic backups
choices.B: Only during daylight hours
choices.C: Only in ideal driving conditions
choices.D: Whenever you are in the left lane

en.explanation: The maximum limit should be driven only in ideal driving conditions, and you must reduce your speed when weather or traffic conditions require it.

en.question: When are you required to obey a 'School Speed Limit When Flashing' sign?

choices.A: Between 8 AM and 5 PM on weekdays
choices.B: Only when the lights on the sign are flashing
choices.C: Whenever children are visible on the sidewalk
choices.D: At all times during the school year

en.explanation: The manual states that the reduced speed limit in a school zone is required only when flashing; otherwise, you should obey the roadway's standard speed limit.

en.question: What is the shape and color of a Yield sign?

choices.A: A red octagon with white letters
choices.B: A yellow diamond with black letters
choices.C: A red and white downward pointing triangle
choices.D: A white rectangle with black letters

en.explanation: A yield sign is a red and white downward pointing triangle with red letters.

en.question: What is the proper use of a shared center lane?

choices.A: Passing slower vehicles
choices.B: Through traffic during rush hour
choices.C: Left turning vehicles from either direction
choices.D: Emergency parking only

en.explanation: A shared center lane is reserved for the use of left turning vehicles from either direction and is not to be used for through traffic or passing other vehicles.

en.question: Under what condition must you NOT enter an intersection?

choices.A: If the traffic light has just turned green
choices.B: If traffic conditions do not permit you to clear the intersection completely
choices.C: If there are pedestrians waiting on the corner
choices.D: If you are turning right on a red light

en.explanation: You must not enter an intersection if traffic conditions do not permit you to clear the intersection completely, as this would block traffic.

en.question: Which sign is a square with a white horizontal line inside a red circle?

choices.A: Stop
choices.B: Yield
choices.C: Wrong Way
choices.D: Do Not Enter

en.explanation: A square sign with a white horizontal line inside a red circle means you cannot enter (Do Not Enter).

en.question: On a green destination sign, what does it mean if the word 'Exit' is written on the left side of the sign?

choices.A: The exit is closed
choices.B: The exit lane or ramp is to the left
choices.C: The exit is for carpools only
choices.D: The exit lane or ramp is to the right

en.explanation: If the word 'Exit' is written on the left side of an exit sign, the exit lane or ramp is to the left.

en.question: What color are service signs that show the location of rest areas, gas stations, hotels, or hospitals?

choices.A: Green
choices.B: Brown
choices.C: Blue
choices.D: Fluorescent pink

en.explanation: Service signs are blue signs that are square or rectangular shaped with white lettering or symbols. They show the location of services like rest areas, gas stations, hotels, or hospitals.

en.question: What color are temporary incident signs used for natural disasters or hazardous material spills?

choices.A: Orange with black lettering
choices.B: Fluorescent pink with black lettering
choices.C: Yellow with black lettering
choices.D: Red with white lettering

en.explanation: Incident signs are temporary and let you know about road user incidents, natural disasters, or spills. These signs are fluorescent pink with black lettering.

en.question: When driving on a road with both a solid and a dashed yellow line between opposing lanes, when are you permitted to pass?

choices.A: Only if the solid yellow line is on your side
choices.B: Only if the dashed yellow line is on your side and a safe gap is available
choices.C: At any time if you sound your horn
choices.D: Passing is never permitted on roads with yellow lines

en.explanation: Where there is both a solid and a dashed yellow line between opposing lanes of traffic, you should not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side. If the dashed line is on your side, you may pass if a safe gap in traffic is available.

en.question: What do two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic indicate?

choices.A: Neither side may pass, but you may cross to turn when gaps exist
choices.B: Both sides may pass if a safe gap is available
choices.C: The lane is a shared center turn lane
choices.D: You are approaching a one-way street

en.explanation: Two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic means neither side may pass. However, you may cross a solid yellow line to turn when gaps in traffic flow exist.

en.question: What does a solid white line between lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction mean?

choices.A: You may freely change lanes
choices.B: You must stay within the lane unless a special situation requires a lane change
choices.C: The lane is ending and you must merge left
choices.D: You are entering a school zone

en.explanation: A solid white line between lanes of traffic means that you must stay within the lane unless a special situation requires a lane change.

en.question: If there is no 'NO TURN ON RED' sign at a traffic light, what must you do before turning right on red?

choices.A: Slow down to 5 mph and proceed without stopping
choices.B: Stop at the stop line and check for traffic and pedestrians
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn crossing traffic
choices.D: Wait for the light to turn yellow before turning

en.explanation: If there is not a NO TURN ON RED sign at the traffic light, after stopping at the stop line and checking for traffic and pedestrians, you may turn right on red.

en.question: When leaving a driveway, alley, or building area such as a gas station, where must you stop?

choices.A: Just past the sidewalk so you can see traffic.
choices.B: You do not need to stop unless pedestrians are present.
choices.C: Behind the sidewalk.
choices.D: In the nearest travel lane.

en.explanation: If you are leaving a driveway, alley or building area, it is required that you stop just as you would if there was a stop sign. You should stop behind the sidewalk, and you must yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and traffic.

en.question: In a reversible lane, what does a flashing yellow 'X' signal mean?

choices.A: The lane is not available.
choices.B: You can use the lane beneath it for general travel.
choices.C: The use of the lane is changing and you should move out.
choices.D: The lane is for turning only.

en.explanation: Signals above the lanes designate traffic flow in reversible lanes. A flashing yellow 'X' means the lane is for turning only.

en.question: What does a steady yellow 'X' signal above a reversible lane indicate?

choices.A: The lane is for turning only.
choices.B: The use of the lane is changing, and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe.
choices.C: You may use the lane for passing.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for buses.

en.explanation: A steady yellow 'X' means that the use of the lane is changing, and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe to do so.

en.question: What symbol is often posted at the side of the road or painted on the road surface to mark a reserved lane?

choices.A: A white diamond
choices.B: A yellow circle
choices.C: A red octagon
choices.D: A green square

en.explanation: Reserved lanes are marked by special lane marking signs stating that the lane is reserved for special use and often have a white diamond posted at the side of the road or painted on the road surface.

en.question: What does an 'HOV 3' sign indicate about a reserved lane?

choices.A: Vehicles must travel at least 3 mph over the speed limit.
choices.B: The lane is reserved for vehicles with at least three people in them.
choices.C: The lane is reserved for heavy commercial vehicles with 3 axles.
choices.D: Only hybrid or electric vehicles may use the lane.

en.explanation: HOV signs or markings mean 'High Occupancy Vehicles' and indicate lanes reserved for vehicles with two or more people in them. 'HOV 3' means there must be at least three people in the vehicle to use that lane.

en.question: If you miss a turn or exit while driving, what should you do?

choices.A: Stop and carefully back up in the travel lane.
choices.B: Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
choices.C: Go on to where it is safe to turn around.
choices.D: Make a U-turn across the median.

en.explanation: If you miss a turn or exit, do not back up. A driver should go on to where it is safe to turn around.

en.question: When driving on a road with three or more lanes traveling in the same direction, which lane should you generally use?

choices.A: The left-most lane
choices.B: The right-most lane
choices.C: The center travel lane
choices.D: The shoulder

en.explanation: On a road with three or more lanes traveling in the same direction, use the center travel lane, especially when there is a lot of traffic entering or exiting the traffic flow.

en.question: Which of the following is a rule regarding passing on multi-lane roads?

choices.A: The right-most lane is intended for passing slower vehicles.
choices.B: You may pass on the paved shoulder if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
choices.C: The left-most lane is intended to be used for passing slower vehicles.
choices.D: Passing on the right is always the safest option.

en.explanation: On multi-lane roads, the left-most lane is intended to be used for passing slower vehicles.

en.question: When making a turn at an intersection where there are no signs or lane markings to control turning, you should:

choices.A: Turn into the farthest lane to allow room for other vehicles.
choices.B: Turn into the closest lane to you that is going in the direction you want to go.
choices.C: Always turn into the center lane.
choices.D: Swing wide to the opposite side before turning.

en.explanation: As a safety precaution, turn into the closest lane to you that is going in the direction you want to go. This way, you will cross the fewest lanes of traffic.

en.question: What is a common danger of swinging wide to the left before making a right turn?

choices.A: You might hit a pedestrian in the crosswalk.
choices.B: The driver behind you may think you are changing lanes and try to pass you on the right.
choices.C: Your vehicle will lose traction and skid.
choices.D: You will be forced to enter a reversible lane.

en.explanation: On right turns, avoid swinging wide to the left before making the turn. When moving into the other lane, the driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or going to turn left and may try to pass you on the right.

en.question: What is the safest way to change direction if you find yourself headed in the incorrect direction on a city street?

choices.A: Make a U-turn in the middle of the street.
choices.B: Perform a forward two-point turnabout in a busy intersection.
choices.C: Turn right and go around the block.
choices.D: Cross the median strip.

en.explanation: The safest way to change direction is to turn right and go around the block. This avoids most left turns across traffic.

en.question: If you need to turn around while driving on the interstate system, you must:

choices.A: Use the crossover areas reserved for emergency vehicles.
choices.B: Cross the median strip carefully.
choices.C: Go to the next exit and turn around.
choices.D: Pull onto the shoulder and wait for a gap in traffic to turn.

en.question: When performing a two-point turnabout using a driveway, what is considered the safest method?

en.question: According to the manual, what is the most difficult and dangerous way to perform a turnabout?

choices.A: A U-turn
choices.B: A forward two-point turnabout
choices.C: A three-point turnabout
choices.D: Navigating a roundabout

en.question: If you must make a U-turn, how should you position your vehicle before beginning the turn?

choices.B: Move as far to the right as you can
choices.C: Straddle the center line
choices.D: Stop in the middle of the intersection

en.question: What speed should you slow down to when entering a roundabout or traffic circle?

choices.B: 15 to 20 mph
choices.C: 25 to 30 mph
choices.D: 35 to 40 mph

en.question: Who has the right-of-way when you are entering a roundabout?

choices.A: Entering traffic
choices.B: Circulating traffic
choices.C: Vehicles on the right
choices.D: Large trucks only

en.question: How should you use your turn signals if you are going straight through a traffic circle or roundabout?

choices.B: Signal 'right' while approaching the roundabout
choices.C: No signal is needed while approaching, but signal 'right' before the exit you want to take
choices.D: No turn signals are required at any point

en.question: What specific hazard should you avoid driving alongside in a traffic circle or roundabout?

en.question: When are you required to stop for a school bus?

choices.D: When the bus is stopped at a railroad crossing

en.question: When entering your parked vehicle on the street, how should you approach the driver's door?

en.question: Which way should you turn your steering wheel when parking downhill, whether with or without a curb?

choices.C: Keep the wheels perfectly straight
choices.D: Turn the wheels slightly to the left

en.question: How should you turn your steering wheel when parking your vehicle uphill and there is NO curb?

choices.A: Sharply toward the edge of the road
choices.B: Sharply away from the edge of the road
choices.C: Keep the wheels straight
choices.D: Turn the wheels to the left

en.question: When exiting a perpendicular or angle parking space, how far should you move straight back before turning the steering wheel?

choices.D: You should turn the steering wheel immediately as you start reversing

en.question: In which direction do vehicles travel around the raised center island of a roundabout?

choices.B: Counterclockwise
choices.C: In a figure-eight pattern
choices.D: Whichever direction is shortest to the exit

en.question: If there is a center turning lane between the roadways, are you required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights on the opposite side of the road?

choices.D: No, you only stop if the bus is on your side of the road.

en.question: According to the manual, you are prohibited from parking within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

en.question: When parking your vehicle parallel to the curb, you must not park more than:

en.question: How far ahead should you look when driving in the city?

en.question: To identify potential problems in your travel path, you should maintain a visual lead of:

en.question: At 60 mph, approximately how long and how far does it take to react to a problem and bring the vehicle to a stop on dry pavement?

choices.D: Left and straight ahead only

en.question: What should you do when preparing to turn left at an intersection?

choices.C: Turn your wheels to the left while waiting for a gap.

en.question: How should you approach a highway-railroad grade crossing?

choices.D: 10 to 12 seconds

choices.B: At least 5 seconds

choices.A: When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.
choices.B: When you can see the complete front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
choices.C: As soon as you are parallel with the passed vehicle's front bumper.
choices.D: When the passed vehicle flashes its headlights.

en.explanation: You should continue to pass until the complete front of the passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror before signaling and returning to the lane.

en.question: What should you do when you become aware that another vehicle wants to pass you?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from passing.
choices.B: Move to the left side of the lane and slow down.
choices.C: Move to the right side of the lane and maintain a constant speed.
choices.D: Flash your headlights and tap your brakes.

en.explanation: When being passed, you should keep right, move to the right side of the lane, and maintain a constant speed to allow the driver to pass you.

en.question: As a general rule, why should you only pass one vehicle at a time?

choices.A: It is illegal to pass more than one vehicle at a time.
choices.B: Passing multiple vehicles requires too much fuel.
choices.C: It is difficult to determine the amount of time needed, which may be 20 to 30 seconds.
choices.D: Your vehicle's engine may overheat.

en.explanation: The manual advises to only pass one vehicle at a time since it is difficult to determine the amount of time needed to pass, which may be as many as 20 to 30 seconds.

en.question: How does an oncoming vehicle that is more than 25 seconds away generally appear to a driver?

choices.A: It appears to be moving extremely fast.
choices.B: It appears to be standing still.
choices.C: It appears to be swerving.
choices.D: It appears larger than it actually is.

en.explanation: According to the manual, an oncoming vehicle that is more than 25 seconds from your vehicle generally appears to be standing still.

en.question: When driving at 55 to 60 mph, how far ahead must you be able to see to safely pass on a hill or curve?

choices.A: At least 1/4 of a mile.
choices.B: At least 1/3 of a mile.
choices.C: At least 1/2 of a mile.
choices.D: At least 1 mile.

en.explanation: You must be able to see at least 1/3 of a mile or about 20 to 25 seconds ahead when driving at 55 to 60 mph to safely pass near hills and curves.

en.question: What is the best way to handle overtaking a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle is approaching?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the pedestrian before the vehicle arrives.
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn both the pedestrian and the vehicle.
choices.C: Move into the oncoming lane and force the other vehicle to slow down.
choices.D: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first so you take hazards one at a time.

en.explanation: To minimize hazards, take them one at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first so that your vehicle can pass only one roadway user at a time.

en.question: In Kansas, when are you required by law to turn on your headlights during inclement weather?

choices.A: Whenever you drive over 60 mph.
choices.B: Whenever the windshield wipers are used.
choices.C: Only when driving on interstate highways.
choices.D: Only between sunset and sunrise.

en.explanation: Many states including Kansas require you to turn on your headlights whenever the wipers are used on the vehicle.

en.question: Why should you turn on your headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun?

choices.A: To help drivers coming towards you see your vehicle.
choices.B: To reduce the glare on your own windshield.
choices.C: To conserve your vehicle's battery power.
choices.D: Because the sun's rays can damage your headlights.

en.explanation: When driving away from a rising or setting sun, drivers coming towards you may have trouble seeing your vehicle. Your headlights will help them see your vehicle.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you give your horn a light tap?

choices.A: When greeting a friend on the sidewalk.
choices.B: When encouraging a slow driver to speed up.
choices.C: When visibility ahead is limited, such as exiting a narrow alley.
choices.D: When driving near a blind pedestrian.

en.explanation: A light tap on the horn is appropriate when visibility ahead is limited, such as a steep hill, a sharp curve, or exiting a narrow alley.

en.question: When is it appropriate to use a SHARP BLAST of your vehicle's horn?

choices.A: When telling another driver they made an error.
choices.B: When a pedestrian is about to run into the street.
choices.C: When you are stuck in heavy traffic.
choices.D: When you want a vehicle to move out of your way.

en.explanation: If there is danger, you should use a sharp blast of the horn, such as when a pedestrian or bicyclist is about to walk, run, or ride into the street.

en.question: When should you absolutely NOT use your horn?

choices.A: When a bicyclist appears to be moving into your lane.
choices.B: When passing a driver who starts to turn into your lane.
choices.C: When near blind pedestrians.
choices.D: When another vehicle is in danger of hitting you.

en.explanation: The manual lists several occasions when you should not use your horn, including when near blind pedestrians.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you must stop, where should you try to stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Just over a hill to protect it from the wind.
choices.B: Just around a curve so it is out of the main traffic flow.
choices.C: In the center lane with your emergency flashers on.
choices.D: Off the road and where other roadway users have a clear view of it.

en.explanation: If you must stop, get your vehicle off the road and stop where other roadway users have a clear view of your vehicle. Do not stop just over a hill or around a curve.

en.question: You should not pass another vehicle if there is a highway-railroad grade crossing ahead within what time frame?

choices.A: 5 to 10 seconds.
choices.B: 10 to 15 seconds.
choices.C: 20 to 25 seconds.
choices.D: 30 to 40 seconds.

en.explanation: The manual states you should not pass if there is a railroad grade crossing within the 20 to 25 second area ahead.

en.question: What is an appropriate way to signal an emergency if your vehicle breaks down?

choices.A: Tie a red cloth to the steering wheel.
choices.B: Tie a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror, or door handle.
choices.C: Stand in the middle of the roadway and wave your arms.
choices.D: Sound your horn continuously until help arrives.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a white cloth attached to a vehicle indicates a disabled vehicle. You should tie a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror, or door handle, or lift the hood to signal an emergency.

en.question: Where should you place emergency flares to warn other drivers that your vehicle is disabled?

choices.A: 50 to 100 feet behind the vehicle
choices.B: 100 to 150 feet behind the vehicle
choices.C: 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle
choices.D: 300 to 500 feet in front of the vehicle

en.explanation: The manual states to place emergency flares about 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle, giving other drivers some time to change lanes if necessary.

en.question: In urban areas, when should you signal before making a turn or a lane change?

choices.A: 50 feet or 1 to 2 seconds before
choices.B: 100 feet or 3 to 5 seconds before
choices.C: 200 feet or 3 to 5 seconds before
choices.D: 500 feet or 5 to 7 seconds before

en.explanation: In urban areas, you must signal 100 feet or 3 to 5 seconds before making a turn or a lane change.

en.question: At speeds above 40 mph, what is the proper distance to signal before making a turn or a lane change?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 150 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: At speeds above 40 mph, you should signal 200 feet or 3 to 5 seconds before making a turn or a lane change.

en.question: If you plan to turn at an intersection but there is a side street just before it, when should you signal?

choices.A: As soon as you see the intersection.
choices.B: Before you reach the side street.
choices.C: Wait until you have passed the side street before signaling.
choices.D: You do not need to signal if there is a side street.

en.explanation: If turning at an intersection, you should wait until you have passed the side street before signaling your intentions, so other drivers do not pull into your travel path assuming you are turning into the side street.

en.question: How can you warn other roadway users that you are stopping or reducing speed at a place where they may not expect it?

choices.A: Turn on your high beam headlights.
choices.B: Tap the brake pedal three or four times lightly.
choices.C: Sound your horn for three seconds.
choices.D: Use hand signals out the window.

en.explanation: When stopping or reducing speed at a place where another driver may not expect it, tap the brake pedal three or four times lightly to warn other roadway users.

en.question: According to the manual, having a Driver's License is considered a:

choices.A: Constitutional right
choices.B: Privilege, not a right
choices.C: Requirement for all citizens
choices.D: Federal right

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that having a Driver's License is a privilege, not a right.

en.question: If you are a minor with a Driver's License, who is responsible for the financial consequences of your driving?

choices.A: Only the minor driver
choices.B: The state government
choices.C: The insurance company exclusively
choices.D: You and your parent(s) or guardian(s)

en.explanation: If you are a minor, you and your parent(s) or guardian(s) will be responsible for the financial consequences of your driving.

en.question: What is a limitation associated with driving a larger vehicle?

choices.A: They are harder for other drivers to see.
choices.B: They can be less stable and have reduced visibility around the vehicle.
choices.C: They accelerate much faster than smaller vehicles.
choices.D: They have a tighter turning radius.

en.explanation: The manual notes that larger vehicles can be less stable and have reduced visibility around the vehicle.

en.question: Good decision making while driving starts with:

choices.A: A fast reaction time
choices.B: Good visual search
choices.C: Knowing the speed limit
choices.D: Having a newer vehicle

en.explanation: To prepare for the decision-making process, it is very important to search actively in the area around your vehicle. Good decision making starts with good visual search.

en.question: When deciding a course of action to lessen a driving risk, your actions are generally limited to changing direction, communicating, or:

choices.A: Changing your speed
choices.B: Changing your destination
choices.C: Exiting the vehicle
choices.D: Turning off your headlights

en.explanation: Generally, you are limited to changing your direction (moving left or right), changing your speed (slowing, stopping, or speeding up), or communicating (signaling or sounding your horn).

en.question: When overtaking a pedestrian who is walking along the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

choices.A: Honk your horn so the pedestrian moves over.
choices.B: Speed up to pass the pedestrian quickly.
choices.C: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
choices.D: Keep driving, as the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.

en.explanation: The 'Test Your Knowledge' section states that when overtaking a pedestrian with an oncoming vehicle approaching, you should slow down and let the vehicle pass first.

en.question: What should you do if your turn signal does not cancel properly after making a turn or lane change?

choices.A: Leave it on until the next turn.
choices.B: Tap the brakes three times to reset it.
choices.C: Cancel the signal manually so other roadway users do not become confused.
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights.

en.explanation: Drivers must cancel the signal if it has not cancelled by itself, so other roadway users do not become confused by an incorrect signal.

en.question: When trying to avoid a collision, what are your three main options?

choices.A: Brake, steer, or accelerate
choices.B: Honk, brake, or swerve
choices.C: Accelerate, honk, or steer
choices.D: Brake, brace for impact, or close your eyes

en.explanation: In avoiding a collision, you have three options: brake, steer or accelerate.

en.question: If your vehicle has an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) and you need to stop quickly, you should:

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly to avoid skidding
choices.B: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it
choices.C: Apply the brakes gently and steer away from the hazard
choices.D: Press the brake pedal until it locks, then release it

en.explanation: With ABS, if you need to stop quickly, press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it. Do not let up on the brake pedal.

en.question: If you must stop quickly and your vehicle does NOT have an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do if the brakes lock-up and the vehicle starts to skid?

choices.A: Keep pressing the brake pedal as hard as possible
choices.B: Shift the vehicle into neutral and pull the parking brake
choices.C: Ease up on the brake pedal and then reapply with control
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the opposite direction of the skid

en.explanation: Without ABS, if the brakes lock-up, you will feel the vehicle start to skid. Ease up on the brake pedal and then reapply with control.

en.question: Which of the following is true about steering quickly to avoid a collision?

choices.A: You can usually stop the vehicle quicker than you can steer it
choices.B: You should steer in the opposite direction you want the vehicle to go
choices.C: In most cases, you can steer the vehicle quicker than you can stop it
choices.D: You should take one hand off the wheel to brace yourself

en.explanation: In most cases, you can steer the vehicle quicker than you can stop it. You should consider steering in order to avoid a collision.

en.question: In which situation might it be best to accelerate to avoid a collision?

choices.A: When you are approaching a sharp curve too quickly
choices.B: When another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room in front of you
choices.C: When a pedestrian suddenly steps into the crosswalk ahead of you
choices.D: When you experience a front tire blowout

en.explanation: Sometimes it is best or necessary to accelerate to avoid a collision. This may happen when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or from behind and there is room to the front of your vehicle to get out of danger.

en.question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction and go into a skid, where should you look?

choices.A: Fixate directly on the hazard you are trying to avoid
choices.B: Look into the on-coming lane
choices.C: Look at your pedals to ensure your feet are positioned correctly
choices.D: Visually look for open space in the direction you want to go

en.explanation: If your vehicle begins to lose traction, visually look for open space. You must pay attention to where your vehicle can go on the roadway and do not fixate on the hazard you are trying to avoid.

en.question: How can you tell if traction is lost to the front tires during a skid?

choices.A: The vehicle moves sideways without any additional steering input
choices.B: The vehicle continues straight while you are steering
choices.C: The steering wheel begins to shake violently
choices.D: The rear of the vehicle fishtails

en.explanation: To recognize traction loss: If the vehicle continues straight while steering, traction is lost to the front tires.

en.question: If your vehicle's rear tires lose traction, how should you steer?

choices.A: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of your intended path
choices.B: Hold the steering wheel perfectly straight and apply the brakes hard
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the intended path of travel
choices.D: Steer toward the on-coming lane to regain balance

en.explanation: If rear traction is lost, turn the steering wheel in the direction of the intended path of travel (the direction you want to go) and continue to steer and counter-steer until the vehicle is traveling straight.

en.question: What should you do to protect yourself if your vehicle is about to be hit from the rear?

choices.A: Lean forward over the steering wheel
choices.B: Press yourself against the back of your seat and put your head against the head restraint
choices.C: Take your foot off the brake pedal so your vehicle can roll forward
choices.D: Unbuckle your seatbelt so you can exit the vehicle quickly

en.explanation: If your vehicle is hit from the rear, your head and body will be thrown backwards. Press yourself against the back of your seat and put your head against the head restraint, and be ready to apply your brakes.

en.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from the front, what is a recommended action to lessen the impact?

choices.A: Try to turn the vehicle to have a glancing blow rather than being struck head on
choices.B: Accelerate to push through the impact
choices.C: Turn off the engine before the collision occurs
choices.D: Throw your arms in front of your face and let go of the steering wheel

en.explanation: If your vehicle is about to be hit from the front it is important to try to have a glancing blow rather than being struck head on. This means that if a collision is going to happen, you should try to turn the vehicle.

en.question: What is the first thing you should try if your brakes stop working while driving?

choices.A: Shift into reverse
choices.B: Pull the parking brake as hard and fast as you can
choices.C: Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times
choices.D: Turn off the ignition immediately

en.explanation: If your brakes stop working, rapidly pump the brake pedal several times. This will often build up enough brake pressure to allow you to stop.

en.question: Which of the following is the correct response to a tire blowout?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately to stop the vehicle
choices.B: Grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and slow down gradually
choices.C: Accelerate slightly to maintain control of the vehicle's momentum
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the direction of the blowout

en.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the accelerator pedal, and do not brake.

en.question: If the engine shuts off while you are driving, what should you do?

choices.A: Shift to neutral, brake with steady pressure, and pull off the roadway
choices.B: Shift to park immediately to stop the vehicle
choices.C: Let go of the steering wheel as it will be locked and impossible to turn
choices.D: Pump the brakes rapidly and honk your horn

en.explanation: If the engine shuts off while you are driving, keep a strong grip on the steering wheel, shift to neutral and look for an escape path, brake with steady pressure, slow down then pull off the roadway.

en.question: What should you do if your accelerator pedal gets stuck in the down position?

choices.A: Reach down and try to pull the pedal up with your hands while driving
choices.B: Shift to neutral, steer smoothly, brake gently, and pull off the roadway
choices.C: Turn off the ignition immediately while still in the lane of traffic
choices.D: Shift into a lower gear and apply the parking brake forcefully

en.explanation: In the case of accelerator failure, shift to neutral and search for an escape path, steer smoothly, brake gently and pull off the roadway.

en.question: If your wheels leave the pavement and drop off onto an uneven surface, why should you avoid braking hard?

choices.A: It will damage your brake pads
choices.B: It can put your vehicle into a skid and make it difficult to steer
choices.C: It will cause your tires to blow out
choices.D: It will stall the engine

en.explanation: When your wheels leave the pavement, do not brake hard, as this can put your vehicle into a skid and make it difficult to steer. Instead, gently apply the brakes.

en.question: What is the recommended speed you should slow down to before attempting to return to the pavement after a drop-off?

choices.A: 10 mph or less
choices.B: 15 mph or less
choices.C: 25 mph or less
choices.D: 35 mph or less

en.explanation: If your wheels leave the pavement, you should steer straight ahead and slow to 25 mph or less before attempting to return to the roadway.

en.question: How much should you turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement after an uneven surface drop-off?

choices.A: About one quarter-turn
choices.B: About one half-turn
choices.C: A full 360-degree turn
choices.D: As sharply as possible

en.explanation: When there is a gap in traffic from all directions, turn the steering wheel about one quarter-turn to return to the pavement. DO NOT OVERSTEER.

en.question: Which type of crash is much more likely to result in serious injury or death compared to other types of crashes?

choices.A: Rear-end collisions
choices.B: Sideswipes
choices.C: Rollovers
choices.D: Low-speed fender benders

en.explanation: Rollovers are much more likely than most other types of crashes to result in serious injury or death, accounting for one of every three passenger vehicle occupant deaths.

en.question: What percentage of all rollover crashes involve no other vehicle besides the one that rolls over?

choices.A: Less than 20%
choices.B: About 40%
choices.C: Exactly 50%
choices.D: More than 80%

en.explanation: Single vehicle crashes are more common for rollovers. More than 80% of all rollovers involve no other vehicle besides the one that rolls over.

en.question: Why are sport utility vehicles (SUVs), vans, and pickups more likely to experience a rollover crash than passenger cars?

choices.A: They have smaller tires
choices.B: They have higher centers of gravity
choices.C: They are driven at higher speeds
choices.D: They lack anti-lock braking systems

en.explanation: Rollover crashes are more common for SUVs, vans, pickups, and small trucks due to their higher centers of gravity, which makes them top heavy and more likely to tip over.

en.question: What is the most effective way to reduce the risk of injury or death in a rollover crash?

choices.A: Gripping the steering wheel tightly
choices.B: Using your safety belt
choices.C: Ducking below the dashboard
choices.D: Unlocking the doors

en.explanation: The most effective way to reduce the risk of injury or death in a rollover is to use your safety belt. Without safety belts occupants can be thrown from the vehicle.

en.question: When driving at night, your lower beam headlights will let you see clearly about how far ahead?

choices.A: 50 to 100 feet
choices.B: 150 to 200 feet
choices.C: 250 to 300 feet
choices.D: 350 to 400 feet

en.explanation: Your lower beam headlights will let you see clearly about 150 to 200 feet ahead.

en.question: What is the maximum safe driving speed when using your high beam headlights at night, which allow you to see 350 to 400 feet ahead?

choices.A: 45 mph
choices.B: 55 mph
choices.C: 65 mph
choices.D: 75 mph

en.explanation: Your high beam headlights will let you see clearly about 350 to 400 feet ahead. Driving at a speed that allows you to stop within this distance is about 65 mph.

en.question: How much should you increase your following distance when driving on unfamiliar roadways at night?

choices.A: By at least one additional second
choices.B: By at least two additional seconds
choices.C: By at least three additional seconds
choices.D: By at least four additional seconds

en.explanation: You need to increase your following distance by adding at least one additional second for night driving conditions and at least two additional seconds for driving on unfamiliar roadways at night.

en.question: If you cannot see any farther than 100 feet ahead due to thick fog or heavy rain, you cannot safely drive faster than:

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 30 mph
choices.C: 40 mph
choices.D: 50 mph

en.explanation: When you cannot see any farther than 100 feet ahead due to rain, snow, blowing dust, smoke, or thick fog, you cannot safely drive faster than 30 mph.

en.question: Which lights should you use for the best visibility when driving in fog, snow, or heavy rain during the day?

choices.A: High beams
choices.B: Parking lights only
choices.C: Low beams and fog lights
choices.D: Emergency flashers

en.explanation: When driving in fog, snow or heavy rain use your low beams and fog lights for best visibility, even during the day.

en.question: If the sun is directly behind you while driving, what hazard should you be aware of?

choices.A: Your engine may overheat
choices.B: Oncoming drivers may not be able to see your turn signals or vehicle due to glare
choices.C: Your headlights will automatically turn off
choices.D: Your vehicle's stopping distance will increase

en.explanation: If the sun is behind you, be aware that oncoming drivers may not be able to see your turn signals or your vehicle because of glare.

en.question: What is the minimum following interval you should use under normal driving conditions?

choices.A: 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds
choices.D: 5 seconds

en.explanation: Use the minimum 3 second following interval, increasing the following interval by an additional second for any unusual weather or traffic conditions.

en.question: If you are driving and a tire suddenly goes flat, what should you do?

choices.A: Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
choices.B: Slow down gradually and do not brake.
choices.C: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can.
choices.D: Steer sharply to the right side of the road.

en.explanation: If a tire suddenly goes flat, you should slow down gradually and do not brake.

en.question: As a pedestrian, if there is no sidewalk available, where should you walk?

choices.A: On the right side of the street with the flow of traffic.
choices.B: In the center of the road.
choices.C: On the left side of the street facing oncoming traffic.
choices.D: On the shoulder of the road in either direction.

en.explanation: If there is no sidewalk, you should walk on the left side of the street facing the oncoming traffic.

en.question: What should a pedestrian do if the flashing "DON'T WALK" signal appears while they are already crossing the street?

choices.A: Stop in the middle of the crosswalk and wait for the next signal.
choices.B: Turn around and go back to the starting curb.
choices.C: Run as fast as possible to the other side.
choices.D: Finish crossing the street.

en.explanation: If the flashing "DON'T WALK" signal appears when you are crossing the street, you may finish crossing the street.

en.question: What is a driver's responsibility when a pedestrian is crossing the street outside of a crosswalk (jaywalking)?

choices.A: Sound the horn and proceed without stopping.
choices.B: Yield and stop for the pedestrian.
choices.C: Swerve around the pedestrian.
choices.D: Maintain speed as the pedestrian does not have the right-of-way.

en.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians always. Even if they are not in a crosswalk and crossing the street where they should not be (jaywalking), you must stop for them.

en.question: When a pedestrian is crossing a street guided by a dog or carrying a white cane, what must a driver do?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.B: Honk to let the pedestrian know a vehicle is approaching.
choices.C: Come to a complete stop.
choices.D: Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.

en.explanation: You must always yield the right-of-way to persons who are visually impaired. When a pedestrian is crossing a street guided by a dog or carrying a white cane, you must come to a complete stop.

en.question: When approaching a stopped vehicle from behind on a multi-lane road, what should you do?

choices.A: Pass the vehicle quickly on the left.
choices.B: Pass the vehicle quickly on the right.
choices.C: Sound your horn and pass the vehicle.
choices.D: Slow down and do not pass until you are sure there are no pedestrians crossing in front of it.

en.explanation: When approaching a stopped vehicle from behind, slow down and do not pass until you are sure that there are no pedestrians crossing in front of it. This is true even on multi-lane roads.

en.question: How are bicyclists classified when used on roadways?

choices.A: As pedestrians.
choices.B: As vehicles that must follow the same rules of the road as motorized vehicles.
choices.C: As recreational equipment with no specific road rules.
choices.D: As slow-moving hazards that must yield to all cars.

en.explanation: Bicyclists are considered vehicles when used on roadways. They are expected to follow the same rules of the road as motorized vehicles.

en.question: On which side of the roadway are bicyclists generally required to ride?

choices.A: The left side.
choices.B: The right side.
choices.C: The center lane.
choices.D: Any side they prefer.

en.explanation: As a bicyclist, you are required to ride on the right side of the roadway.

en.question: Are bicyclists allowed to ride side-by-side in a single lane?

choices.A: No, they must always ride single file.
choices.B: Yes, they are allowed to ride two abreast or two wide in a lane.
choices.C: Yes, but only on weekends.
choices.D: No, unless they are in a designated bike lane.

en.explanation: Bicyclists are allowed to ride two abreast or two wide in a lane. Doing this creates a tight vehicular density so that cars may pass more efficiently.

en.question: Under the Dead Red Law, what may a bicyclist do if a traffic signal does not respond to their bicycle?

choices.A: Ride onto the sidewalk and cross at the pedestrian crosswalk.
choices.B: Wait until a car arrives to trigger the signal.
choices.C: Cross the intersection after waiting a reasonable amount of time, without impeding cross-traffic.
choices.D: Turn right and make a U-turn to avoid the light.

en.explanation: Under the Dead Red Law, if you reach an intersection and the traffic signal will not respond to your bicycle, after waiting what you determine is a reasonable amount of time, you may cross the intersection.

en.question: What lighting equipment is required for a bicyclist riding at dusk?

choices.A: A taillight only.
choices.B: A headlight is required, and a taillight is highly recommended.
choices.C: Both a headlight and a flashing taillight are required.
choices.D: No lighting is required if wearing reflective clothing.

en.explanation: Use of a headlight at dusk is required, but a taillight is highly recommended to give you further visibility.

en.question: If you are driving and about to make a right turn, and there is a bicyclist ahead of you, what should you do?

choices.A: Speed up and pass the bicyclist immediately before the turn.
choices.B: Honk your horn to make the bicyclist yield.
choices.C: Slow down and let the cyclist clear the intersection before making your turn.
choices.D: Squeeze past the bicyclist in the same lane while turning.

en.explanation: If you are about to make a right turn, you must not pass a bicyclist immediately before the turn. To avoid a collision, you should slow down and let the cyclist clear the intersection before making your turn.

en.question: Why should you avoid sounding your horn close to bicyclists unless there is a chance of a collision?

choices.A: It is illegal to honk at bicyclists.
choices.B: It may startle them and cause them to steer into your path and crash.
choices.C: Bicyclists cannot hear horns over the wind.
choices.D: It will cause the bicyclist to stop suddenly.

en.explanation: Do not sound your horn close to bicyclists unless there is a chance of a collision. Sounding your horn to alert your presence may startle them and cause them to steer into your path and crash.

en.question: How do wet, sandy, or gravel-covered roadways affect bicyclists compared to motor vehicles?

choices.A: These conditions affect bicycles much more than vehicles, reducing their ability to brake or turn sharply.
choices.B: Bicycles handle these conditions better than motor vehicles.
choices.C: These conditions affect bicycles and motor vehicles equally.
choices.D: Bicycles are unaffected by sand or gravel.

en.explanation: Like motor vehicles, bicycles cannot brake as quickly or turn as sharply under these conditions. These conditions affect bicycles much more than vehicles.

en.question: What is the 'Dutch Reach' method used for?

choices.A: Signaling a left turn on a bicycle
choices.B: Safely exiting a vehicle by using your right hand to open the door
choices.C: Passing a bicyclist safely on a narrow road
choices.D: Checking blind spots while backing up

en.explanation: The 'Dutch Reach' method entails using your right hand to pull the handle to open the door, which inherently turns your body to provide better visibility of traffic approaching from the rear, helping avoid collisions with bicyclists.

en.question: What do 'sharrows' on the pavement indicate?

choices.A: A designated lane exclusively for bicycles
choices.B: A route with lower traffic volumes recommended for bicycles
choices.C: A recommendation of where in a lane a bicyclist should ride to flow easiest with traffic
choices.D: A pedestrian-only crossing zone

en.explanation: Sharrows are road markers on the pavement that provide a recommendation of where in a lane a bicyclist should ride to flow easiest with other traffic.

en.question: Why might a bicyclist be unable to use hand signals when turning or stopping?

choices.A: Hand signals are not legally required for bicyclists
choices.B: Road or traffic conditions may require them to keep both hands on the handlebars
choices.C: Bicycles are equipped with automatic turn signals
choices.D: Bicyclists only need to signal when riding in a designated bike lane

en.explanation: Keep in mind that a bicyclist may be unable to signal if road or traffic conditions require them to keep both hands on the handlebars.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding motorcycles and traffic lanes?

choices.A: A motorcycle is only entitled to half of a traffic lane
choices.B: You may pass a motorcycle in the same lane if there is enough room
choices.C: Two motorcycles may share a single traffic lane
choices.D: Motorcycles must ride on the shoulder of the road

en.explanation: Motorcycle/scooter/moped operators have the right to use a complete traffic lane, and two motorcycles/scooters/mopeds may share a lane. You should not pass them in the same lane.

en.question: According to the manual, a motorized bicycle or moped has a maximum design speed of no more than:

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: A motorized bicycle or moped has the capability of a maximum design speed of no more than 30 mph.

en.question: Nearly 40 percent of crashes involving a motorcycle, scooter, or moped and another motor vehicle are caused by:

choices.A: The motorcycle tailgating the other vehicle
choices.B: The other vehicle turning left in front of the motorcycle
choices.C: The motorcycle passing on the right
choices.D: The other vehicle stopping suddenly

en.explanation: Nearly 40 percent of crashes involving motorcycles/scooters/mopeds and another motor vehicle were caused by the other vehicle turning left in front of the motorcyclist/scooter/moped.

en.question: If you see a motorcycle approaching with its turn signal flashing, what should you do?

choices.A: Assume it is turning and proceed into its path
choices.B: Honk your horn to let the rider know you see them
choices.C: Do not pull out in front of it until you see that it is beginning to turn
choices.D: Speed up to cross the intersection before the motorcycle arrives

en.explanation: Do not assume a motorcycle/scooter/moped is turning when you see its turn signal flashing, as they may not self-cancel. Do not pull out in front of them until you see that they are beginning to turn.

en.question: What is the recommended following distance when driving behind a motorcycle, scooter, or moped in normal conditions?

choices.A: 1 to 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 to 4 seconds
choices.C: 5 to 6 seconds
choices.D: 7 to 8 seconds

en.explanation: When following a motorcyclist/scooter/moped, allow for a 3 to 4 second following distance or more in wet conditions.

en.question: Why must you always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle, scooter, or moped?

choices.A: High beams will drain the motorcycle's battery
choices.B: The blinding effect of high beams can be far more dangerous to them due to their vulnerability
choices.C: It is a signal that you are about to pass them
choices.D: High beams will cause the motorcycle's engine to stall

en.explanation: Always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle/scooter/moped. Because of their vulnerability, the blinding effect of your high beams can be far more dangerous to them than to drivers of motor vehicles.

en.question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights?

choices.A: Speed up and clear the intersection quickly
choices.B: Stop immediately in your current lane
choices.C: Move to the right, pull over to the curb or edge of the road, and stop
choices.D: Move to the left lane and slow down

en.explanation: When you hear a siren, or see a vehicle approaching with flashing lights, move to the right and pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop.

en.question: After an emergency vehicle with flashing lights passes you, how far away must you stay from it?

choices.A: At least 100 feet
choices.B: At least 200 feet
choices.C: At least 300 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: After the emergency vehicle passes, carefully look behind you for other vehicles, and when it is safe to do so return to the roadway. You must stay at least 500 feet away from the emergency vehicle.

en.question: If you are pulled over by law enforcement at night, what should you do to help the officer see inside your vehicle?

choices.A: Turn on your high beam headlights
choices.B: Turn on your interior lights
choices.C: Shine a flashlight out the window
choices.D: Step out of the vehicle immediately

en.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and if at night your interior lights to help the officer see that everything is in order inside the vehicle.

en.question: When pulled over by law enforcement, how should you handle providing your documents?

choices.A: Have them in your hand before the officer approaches the window
choices.B: Reach for them quickly to save the officer's time
choices.C: Tell the officer where they are located and reach for them slowly with one hand on the wheel
choices.D: Toss them onto the passenger seat for the officer to inspect

en.explanation: If the officer asks you for these documents, tell the officer where they are located and reach for them slowly with one hand on the wheel.

en.question: Under the Move-Over Law, what must you do when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle and wait for instructions
choices.B: Honk your horn to alert the emergency workers
choices.C: Vacate the closest lane if safe, or slow to a safe speed for the conditions
choices.D: Maintain your speed but turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: State law requires drivers approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights... to vacate the lane closest if safe and possible to do so, or slow to a speed safe for road, weather, and traffic conditions.

en.question: What should you do when a motorcycle, scooter, or moped is passing your vehicle?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from cutting you off
choices.B: Maintain your lane position and speed
choices.C: Move onto the shoulder of the road
choices.D: Brake sharply to let them pass faster

en.explanation: When a motorcycle/scooter/moped is passing your vehicle, you should maintain your lane position and speed. Allow them to complete the maneuver.

en.question: What must a driver do when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights while traveling in the same direction?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for instructions.
choices.B: Vacate the lane closest if safe, or slow to a safe speed.
choices.C: Honk to alert the emergency workers and maintain speed.
choices.D: Accelerate to pass the emergency vehicle quickly.

en.explanation: State law requires drivers approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights to vacate the lane closest if safe and possible to do so, or slow to a speed safe for road, weather, and traffic conditions.

en.question: In fatal crashes involving cars and commercial vehicles, police report that the car driver contributes to the cause of the crash what percentage of the time?

choices.A: Less than 30%
choices.B: Exactly 50%
choices.C: More than 70%

en.explanation: According to the manual, in more than 70% of all fatal crashes involving cars and commercial vehicles, police report that the car driver contributed to the cause of the crash.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in a large truck's side blind spot?

choices.A: You cannot see the truck's headlights in your rearview mirror.
choices.B: You cannot see the driver's face in the truck's side view mirror.
choices.C: The truck's turn signal is flashing.
choices.D: You are within 50 feet of the truck's rear bumper.

en.explanation: The manual states regarding Side No-Zones: "If you cannot see the driver’s face in the side view mirror, they cannot see you."

en.question: When passing a large vehicle, when is it safe to pull back in front of it?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the truck's front bumper.
choices.B: When you can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror.
choices.C: When the truck driver flashes their headlights.
choices.D: After you have maintained your speed for 5 seconds.

en.explanation: When passing a large vehicle, you should look for the whole front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror before pulling in front and maintaining speed.

en.question: How far can the huge blind spot directly behind a large vehicle extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 150 feet
choices.D: Up to 200 feet

en.explanation: Unlike cars, large vehicles have huge blind spots directly behind them that extend up to 200 feet.

en.question: Why might a large truck or bus swing wide to the left before making a right turn?

choices.A: To safely clear the corner of a curb or other obstruction.
choices.B: To allow cars to pass them on the right.
choices.C: To build up enough speed to complete the turn.
choices.D: To check their right-side blind spot.

en.explanation: When a truck or bus needs to make a right turn, they will sometimes swing wide to the left in order to safely turn right and clear the corner of a curb or other obstruction.

en.question: When meeting a truck coming from the opposite direction, why should you keep as far as possible to the right side of the roadway?

choices.A: To give the truck room to make a U-turn.
choices.B: To avoid wind turbulence that pushes the vehicles apart.
choices.C: To allow the truck driver to see your license plate.
choices.D: To prepare to pull over and stop.

en.explanation: You should keep as far as possible to the right side of the roadway to avoid a side swept crash and to reduce the wind turbulence between the two vehicles, which pushes the vehicles apart.

en.question: What is the purpose of stop lines at many intersections?

choices.A: To indicate where pedestrians are allowed to cross.
choices.B: To set vehicles farther back to give larger vehicles more turning space.
choices.C: To mark the beginning of a school zone.
choices.D: To show where the speed limit changes.

en.explanation: Stop lines help to set you farther back at an intersection to give larger vehicles more turning space. Always stop behind stop lines.

en.question: What is the purpose of runaway ramps on long downgrades?

choices.A: For slow-moving vehicles to pull over and let others pass.
