choices.B: For large vehicles that are out of control or cannot stop due to brake failure.
choices.C: For emergency vehicles to park and monitor traffic.
choices.D: For drivers to safely check their cargo and tires.

en.explanation: These ramps are to be used only by large vehicles that are out of control or cannot stop because of brake failure. Never stop or park in the area of these ramps.

en.question: At what maximum speed may you pass a safety zone set aside for pedestrians boarding trolleys and light rail vehicles, once it is safe to do so?

choices.A: 5 mph
choices.B: 10 mph
choices.C: 15 mph
choices.D: 20 mph

en.explanation: You may pass the safety zone as soon as it is safe to do so and at no faster than 10 mph.

en.question: When are you permitted to overtake and pass on the left of a trolley or light rail vehicle?

choices.A: Whenever the trolley is moving slower than the speed limit.
choices.B: Only when you are on a one-way street or directed by a traffic officer.
choices.C: Whenever the trolley is stopped to pick up passengers.
choices.D: You are never allowed to pass a trolley on the left.

en.explanation: Do not overtake and pass on the left of a trolley or light rail vehicle... except when you are on a one-way street. When the tracks are so close to the right side of the road that you cannot pass on the right, or when a traffic officer directs you, pass on the left.

en.question: What does a fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicate?

choices.A: The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
choices.B: The vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.
choices.C: The vehicle is an emergency responder.
choices.D: The vehicle is making wide right turns.

en.explanation: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of vehicles drawn by animals, farm equipment or construction equipment means the vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.

en.question: What is the normal speed range for animal-drawn vehicles?

choices.A: 5 to 8 miles per hour
choices.B: 10 to 15 miles per hour
choices.C: 15 to 20 miles per hour
choices.D: 20 to 25 miles per hour

en.explanation: Normal speeds for animal drawn vehicles range between 5 and 8 miles per hour.

en.question: Why should you avoid using your horn or "revving" your engine when passing an animal-drawn vehicle or horseback rider?

choices.A: It is illegal to use a horn in rural areas.
choices.B: It may scare the animal and cause a crash.
choices.C: It will cause the animal to stop moving completely.
choices.D: It violates noise ordinance laws.

en.explanation: Pass with caution and do not use your horn or "rev" the engine because this may scare the horse and cause a crash.

en.question: What should you do if you are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a two-way, single-lane roadway and causing vehicles behind you to slow down significantly?

choices.A: Speed up to match the flow of traffic.
choices.B: Pull to the side of the roadway when safe to let other vehicles pass.
choices.C: Turn on your hazard lights and remain in the center of the lane.
choices.D: Wave the vehicles behind you to pass on the shoulder.

en.explanation: If you are driving a slow-moving vehicle and must drive so slowly that other vehicles have to reduce speed to the rear, pull to the side of the roadway when safe to do so and let the other vehicles pass.

en.question: If a truck or bus needs to make a right turn and you are also turning right, you should:

choices.A: Quickly turn right before the truck or bus does.
choices.B: Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
choices.C: Wait until the truck or bus turns before turning right.
choices.D: Honk your horn to let the driver know you are there.

en.explanation: If a truck or bus needs to make a right turn and you are also turning right, you must wait until the truck or bus turns before turning right.

en.question: If a pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the street, not at a crosswalk (jaywalking), what must you do?

choices.A: You must stop for them.
choices.B: You do not have to stop for them.
choices.C: You should honk your horn and maintain your speed.
choices.D: Swerve into the oncoming lane to avoid them.

en.explanation: Even if a pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the street (jaywalking) and it is illegal, you must stop for them.

en.question: Motorcycle operators have the right to:

choices.A: Share a traffic lane with another vehicle.
choices.B: Use the shoulder of a roadway to pass.
choices.C: Use a complete traffic lane.
choices.D: Drive between lanes of stopped traffic.

en.explanation: Motorcycle operators have the right to use a complete traffic lane.

en.question: How should you adjust your driving when traveling on gravel or dirt roads compared to paved roads?

choices.A: Increase your speed to maintain traction.
choices.B: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
choices.C: Decrease your following distance to see the road better.
choices.D: Pump your brakes continuously to prevent skidding.

en.explanation: When driving on gravel or dirt, you must reduce your speed and increase your following distance, since it will take much longer to stop due to loss of traction.

en.question: During dry periods, gravel roads can become extremely dusty, reducing vision. What headlights should you use in this situation?

choices.A: High beam headlights
choices.B: Low beam headlights
choices.C: Parking lights only
choices.D: Fog lights only

en.explanation: During dusty conditions on gravel roads, it is recommended that you use low beam headlights to make your vehicle more visible to others, slow down and increase your following distance.

en.question: When driving over open bridge gratings or steel bridges, you should:

choices.A: Accelerate quickly to cross the bridge faster.
choices.B: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
choices.C: Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and increase your following distance.
choices.D: Change lanes frequently to find the best traction.

en.explanation: Due to reduced traction on open bridge gratings or steel bridges, you should keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and increase your following distance.

en.question: Many highway-railroad grade crossings on rural roads are marked only with a warning sign and a white X-shaped sign. What should you do when approaching one?

choices.A: Maintain your speed unless you see a train.
choices.B: Slow down, look both ways, and be prepared to stop.
choices.C: Honk your horn before crossing the tracks.
choices.D: Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.

en.explanation: Many highway-railroad grade crossings on rural roads typically do not have lights or crossing gates; therefore, you should always slow down, look both ways and be prepared to stop for a train before crossing.

en.question: At what distance should you dim your high beam headlights when an oncoming vehicle is approaching?

choices.A: Within about a one-block distance.
choices.B: Within 100 feet.
choices.C: Within 500 feet.
choices.D: Only when the other driver flashes their lights.

en.explanation: You should dim your high beams whenever you come within about a one-block distance of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim their high beam headlights, where should you look to keep from being blinded?

choices.A: Directly at the oncoming headlights.
choices.B: Toward the left side of the road.
choices.C: Toward the right side of the road.
choices.D: At your rearview mirror.

en.explanation: If a driver fails to dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road to keep from being blinded by their headlights.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you use your low beam headlights instead of high beams?

choices.A: When driving on an empty rural highway.
choices.B: When following another vehicle or in heavy traffic.
choices.C: When there are no oncoming vehicles.
choices.D: When you want to see twice as far down the road.

en.explanation: Use your low beams when following another vehicle, in heavy traffic, in fog, or when it is snowing or raining hard. Light from high beams will reflect, causing glare.

en.question: How much water does it take to reach the bottom of most passenger cars, potentially causing loss of control or stalling?

choices.A: 2 inches
choices.B: 6 inches
choices.C: 12 inches
choices.D: 2 feet

en.explanation: Remember, 6 inches of water will reach the bottom of most passenger cars, causing loss of control or possible stalling.

en.question: How much rushing water can carry away most vehicles?

choices.A: 6 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 2 feet

en.explanation: 2 feet of rushing water can carry away most vehicles.

en.question: What color are all temporary signs in highway work zones?

choices.A: Yellow background with black letters
choices.B: Orange background with black letters or symbols
choices.C: White background with red letters
choices.D: Green background with white letters

en.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols and tell you what to do.

en.question: When approaching a work zone that requires a lane change, when should you merge into the appropriate lane?

choices.A: As soon as possible at the first notice of the approaching work zone.
choices.B: Right before the lane closure begins.
choices.C: After passing the first orange warning sign.
choices.D: Whenever the vehicle ahead of you merges.

en.explanation: Merge as soon as possible. Motorists can help maintain traffic flow and posted speeds by moving to the appropriate lane at first notice of an approaching work zone.

en.question: What should you do when you first notice an approaching work zone?

choices.A: Speed up to get through the area quickly
choices.B: Move to the appropriate lane to maintain traffic flow
choices.C: Stop and wait for a pilot car to guide you
choices.D: Turn on your high beam headlights

en.explanation: The manual states to maintain traffic flow and posted speeds by moving to the appropriate lane at first notice of an approaching work zone.

en.question: How should you adjust your driving when passing through a mobile work zone?

choices.A: Resume normal speed as soon as you pass the workers
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn workers of your presence
choices.C: Observe the posted signs until you see the one that says 'End Road Work'
choices.D: Pull over to the shoulder until the mobile work zone has moved on

en.explanation: The manual states that for mobile work zones, you should observe the posted signs until you see the one that says, 'End Road Work,' because workers may still be present even if you don't see them immediately.

en.question: If an animal suddenly runs in front of your vehicle and a collision is inevitable, what is the safest alternative?

choices.A: Swerve into oncoming traffic
choices.B: Swerve off the roadway
choices.C: Hit the animal while retaining control of the vehicle
choices.D: Lock your brakes to stop immediately

en.explanation: The manual states that if a collision is inevitable, do not swerve to avoid the animal. The safest alternative may be hitting the animal while concentrating on keeping your vehicle under control and on the roadway.

en.question: During which months are animals most active, requiring extra caution from drivers?

choices.A: January through March
choices.B: April through June
choices.C: July through September
choices.D: October through December

en.explanation: The manual advises using caution when driving at dawn and dusk and between the months of October through December, when animals are most active.

en.question: What should you do if a dog runs out onto the roadway and begins chasing your vehicle?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle completely
choices.B: Swerve sharply to scare the dog away
choices.C: Slow down until the dog is near, then accelerate away
choices.D: Honk your horn continuously

en.explanation: The manual states that dogs chasing vehicles tend to approach in a straight line. You should slow down until the dog is near your vehicle, then accelerate away from the dog as it approaches.

en.question: If you think you have time to avoid hitting a deer in the road, why might you flash your headlights?

choices.A: To signal the deer to move out of the way
choices.B: Because deer tend to fixate on headlights and flashing them may cause the animal to freeze
choices.C: To blind the deer so it cannot run toward you
choices.D: To alert oncoming traffic to stop

en.explanation: The manual notes that deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing them may cause the animal to freeze in the road, potentially helping you avoid a collision.

en.question: What is the minimum passing score for the driver's knowledge test?
en.explanation: According to the manual, you must score an 80% to pass the knowledge test.

en.question: If you fail the knowledge test for the 4th time, how long must you wait before starting the process again?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 3 months
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: The manual states that if you fail to pass the 4th time, you will be required to wait 6 months from the most recent failed exam before starting the process again.

en.question: If you are under 17 years old, how long must you hold your Instruction Permit before you are eligible to take the Driver's License Test?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: One full year or until reaching age 17

en.explanation: If you are under 17 years old, you must hold your Instruction Permit for one full year or until reaching age 17 whichever comes first, before you are eligible to take the Driver's License Test.

en.question: Which way should your wheels face when parking uphill with a curb?

choices.A: Towards the curb
choices.B: Straight forward
choices.C: Away from the curb
choices.D: Parallel to the curb

en.explanation: According to the sample questions in the manual, when parking uphill with a curb, your wheels should face away from the curb.

en.question: When passing another vehicle, you should continue to pass until:

choices.A: You look in your side mirror and see the vehicle is behind you
choices.B: The complete front of the passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror
choices.C: The driver you just passed signals you to move over
choices.D: You are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle

en.explanation: The manual's sample questions indicate you should continue to pass another vehicle until the complete front of the passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.

en.question: Why is it important to stop at stop lines at an intersection?

choices.A: To give larger vehicles more turning space
choices.B: So the traffic light changes faster
choices.C: To give pedestrians more room to walk
choices.D: To avoid triggering red light cameras

en.explanation: According to the manual's sample questions, it is important to stop at stop lines to give larger vehicles more turning space.

en.question: When are roadways generally more slippery?

choices.A: When it first starts to rain, snow or sleet
choices.B: When it has been raining, snowing, or sleeting for a while
choices.C: When it has just stopped raining, snowing, or sleeting
choices.D: When the sun comes out after a rainstorm

en.explanation: The manual states that roadways are more slippery when it first starts to rain, snow or sleet.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle stalls when crossing railroad tracks and a train is approaching?

choices.A: Run across the tracks as far away as possible
choices.B: Run in the direction from which the train is approaching
choices.C: Run in the opposite direction from which the train is approaching
choices.D: Stay in the vehicle and call 911

en.explanation: The manual's sample questions advise that if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, you should run in the direction from which the train is approaching to avoid being struck by debris from the collision.

en.question: During the pre-trip inspection for the driving test, what will you NOT be required to do?

choices.A: Walk around the vehicle
choices.B: Point to or touch each item being inspected
choices.C: Open the hood or crawl under the vehicle
choices.D: Explain to the examiner what you are checking

en.explanation: The manual states that during the pre-trip inspection, you may have to walk around the vehicle, point to or touch items, and explain what you are checking, but you will NOT have to open the hood or crawl under the vehicle.

en.question: Where can you find the recommended tire pressure (psi) for your vehicle?

choices.A: On the sidewall of the tire
choices.B: In the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb
choices.C: On the dashboard indicator lights
choices.D: On the inside of the glove compartment door

en.explanation: To check tire pressure, the manual advises using the recommended psi located in the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle.

en.question: How do you perform the 'penny test' to check your tire's tread depth?

choices.A: Place the penny flat against the tire sidewall
choices.B: Place Lincoln's head into one of the lowest grooves of the tread
choices.C: Place the Lincoln Memorial side facing up in the tread
choices.D: Drop the penny from the top of the tire and see if it bounces

en.explanation: The 'penny test' is performed by holding Abraham Lincoln's body between your thumb and forefinger and placing Lincoln's head into one of the lowest grooves of the tire tread.

en.question: What is a potential consequence of driving with over-inflated tires?

choices.A: Increased effect of hydroplaning
choices.B: Reduced cornering ability
choices.C: Increased chance of tread separation and tire failure
choices.D: Excessive heat buildup due to increased flexing

en.explanation: According to the manual, over inflation increases the chance of tread separation and tire failure.

en.question: Why is it important to check under the vehicle for puddles or dripping fluids before driving?

choices.A: To ensure the air conditioning condensation is draining properly
choices.B: Fluid loss could indicate component failure in the transmission or fuel systems
choices.C: To check if the windshield washer fluid is full
choices.D: To verify that the tire pressure is correct

en.explanation: It is important to look for leaks because fluid loss could indicate component failure in areas where levels might not be readily checked, such as the transmission or fuel systems.

en.question: What must you NEVER do when checking your vehicle's coolant?

choices.A: Check the coolant level next to the radiator
choices.B: Fill it with a coolant/water solution
choices.C: Open the radiator cap on a hot car
choices.D: Check the driver's manual for the proper coolant ratio

en.explanation: The manual explicitly warns: 'Never open the radiator cap on a hot car! Wait until the car has cooled down first.'

en.question: If the outside temperature is over 85°F during your driving exam, what is required of your vehicle?

choices.A: The passenger window must roll down
choices.B: The air conditioner must work properly
choices.C: The heater must be disabled
choices.D: The windshield wipers must be turned on

en.explanation: For a vehicle used for the driving exam, if the outside temperature is over 85°F, the air conditioner must work properly.

en.question: How should a safety belt be properly placed on your body?

choices.A: Across your stomach and neck
choices.B: Across your hips and shoulder
choices.C: Loosely over your lap and behind your back
choices.D: Tightly across your thighs and under your arm

en.explanation: When checking your safety belt, you must make sure it is not ripped or frayed and properly place the safety belt across your hips and shoulder.

en.question: Why is it important to check that your vehicle's defroster is working properly?

choices.A: It cools the engine during hot weather
choices.B: It improves visibility, especially during cold weather
choices.C: It prevents the engine from freezing
choices.D: It clears dirt and debris from the outside of the windshield

en.explanation: It is important to make sure your defroster is working properly because it improves visibility, especially during cold weather.

en.question: How can you test if your vehicle's defroster is working during an inspection?

choices.A: Activate the fan and place your hand over the dashboard's vent
choices.B: Turn on the windshield wipers and spray washer fluid
choices.C: Open all windows and check for airflow
choices.D: Check the coolant level in the radiator

en.explanation: You can test the defroster by activating the fan and placing your hand over the dashboard's vent to ensure it is working properly.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of checking your dashboard indicator lights?

choices.A: To ensure the radio is receiving power
choices.B: To warn you if external lights like turn signals and high beams are active when not appropriate
choices.C: To measure the exact amount of fuel left in the tank
choices.D: To check the tire pressure from inside the car

en.explanation: It is important to make sure your indicator lights work because they help to warn you if external lights, such as turn signals and high beams, are still active when not appropriate.

en.question: What happens if your tire tread gets below the safe amount indicated by the 'penny test'?

choices.A: Your car's ability to grip the road in adverse conditions is greatly reduced
choices.B: Your vehicle will automatically fail the emissions test
choices.C: The tires will become over-inflated
choices.D: Your fuel efficiency will increase significantly

en.explanation: The manual states that if your tread gets below the safe amount (where Lincoln's head is covered), your car's ability to grip the road in adverse conditions is greatly reduced.

en.question: When practicing the pre-trip inspection with a parent, guardian, or friend, what are the requirements for that person?

choices.A: They must be a certified driving instructor
choices.B: They must be properly licensed and over the age of 21
choices.C: They must own the vehicle being inspected
choices.D: They must have a commercial driver's license (CDL)

en.explanation: The manual advises practicing the inspection with a parent/guardian or friend who is properly licensed and over the age of 21.

en.question: What is a consequence of low tire inflation or lack of tread?

choices.A: Decreased stopping distance
choices.B: Increased cornering ability
choices.C: Increased effect of hydroplaning
choices.D: Decreased chance of blowout

en.explanation: Low inflation or lack of tread increases the effect of hydroplaning, reduces cornering ability, and increases the chance of blowout from excessive heat buildup.

en.question: What should you do if only one of your brake lights is working when you test them?

choices.A: Continue driving as long as one light works.
choices.B: Replace the bulb or fuse, or get a professional to do it.
choices.C: Press the brake pedal harder to activate the second light.
choices.D: Use your turn signals to indicate you are stopping.

en.explanation: The manual states that if a friend does not see both brake lights when you step on the pedal, you should replace the bulb or fuse, or get a professional to do it.

en.question: When practicing for the basic vehicle control skills test, the licensed parent, guardian, or friend accompanying you must be over what age?
en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to practice these exercises with a parent/guardian or friend who is properly licensed and over the age of 21.

en.question: During the basic control skills test, what constitutes a 'reversal' error?

choices.A: Stopping without changing direction.
choices.B: Looking over your shoulder while backing up.
choices.C: Failing to use a turn signal while backing.
choices.D: Stopping and reversing direction to get a better position.

en.explanation: A reversal is defined as when you stop and reverse direction to get a better position. Stopping without changing direction does not count as a reversal.

en.question: Which part of your vehicle is allowed to touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone without being counted as an encroachment?

choices.A: The tires
choices.B: The bumpers
choices.C: The vehicle's mirrors
choices.D: The exhaust pipe

en.explanation: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors, is considered an encroachment.

en.question: If your turn signal cancels automatically while performing a basic control skills exercise, what must you do?

choices.A: Leave it off since the examiner already saw it.
choices.B: Reactivate it when necessary.
choices.C: Use hand signals instead.
choices.D: Stop the vehicle and restart the exercise.

en.explanation: The manual states that if your turn signal cancels automatically during an exercise, you must make sure to reactivate it when necessary.

en.question: When performing a parallel parking exercise, how close must you bring the vehicle to the curb side of the space?

choices.A: Within 6 inches
choices.B: Within 12 inches
choices.C: Within 18 inches
choices.D: Within 24 inches

en.explanation: For both right-side and left-side parallel parking, you must bring the vehicle within 12 inches of the curb side of the space without crossing boundaries.

en.question: When stopping behind another vehicle at an intersection or before a turn, what is considered a safe gap?

choices.A: One car length
choices.B: Two car lengths
choices.C: Stopping where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choices.D: Stopping where you can see the driver's face in their rearview mirror

en.explanation: A safe gap when stopping behind another vehicle is to stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

en.question: If you must stop before making a turn, how should you position your front wheels while waiting?

choices.A: Turned slightly to the right
choices.B: Turned slightly to the left
choices.C: Aimed straight ahead
choices.D: Turned in the direction of your intended turn

en.explanation: The manual states that if you must stop before making a turn, you should keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

en.question: What rule applies to changing lanes while driving through an intersection?

choices.A: You may change lanes if you use a turn signal.
choices.B: You may change lanes if the intersection is clear.
choices.C: Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
choices.D: You must change lanes to the right-most lane while in the intersection.

en.explanation: When driving through an intersection, the manual explicitly states: 'Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.'

en.question: After completing a turn or passing through an intersection with multiple lanes, which lane should you move into when it is safe to do so?

choices.A: The left-most lane
choices.B: The center lane
choices.C: The right-most lane
choices.D: The lane with the fastest traffic

en.explanation: After a turn or intersection, you should check your blind spots and mirrors, and move into the right-most lane when it is safe to do so (if not already there).

en.question: In a Forward Two-point Turnabout exercise, after pulling forward into a driveway or alley, what is your next step?

choices.A: Back the vehicle to the left into the street.
choices.B: Back the vehicle to the right into the street.
choices.C: Execute a U-turn within the alley.
choices.D: Drive forward through the alley to the next street.

en.explanation: In the Forward Two-point Turnabout, you pull forward into a driveway or alley, and then you will back the vehicle to the right into the street.

en.question: What is the first step in performing a Reverse Two-point Turnabout?

choices.A: Drive forward into the driveway or alley.
choices.B: Drive past the entrance to a driveway or alley.
choices.C: Back directly into the nearest intersection.
choices.D: Execute a three-point turn in the middle of the road.

en.explanation: For a Reverse Two-point Turnabout, you are asked to drive past the entrance to a driveway or alley and then back to the right into the street or alley.

en.question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is true regarding the examiner's instructions?

choices.A: The examiner will try to trick you into making an illegal maneuver.
choices.B: You will be asked to drive in an unsafe manner to test your reflexes.
choices.C: Directions will be given with plenty of time to do what the examiner has asked.
choices.D: The examiner will not give you any directions until the last second.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Directions will be given to you so you will have plenty of time to do what the examiner has asked. You will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner.'

en.question: During the basic control skills test, when must you perform head and traffic checks?

choices.A: Only when the examiner explicitly reminds you.
choices.B: Prior to entering or exiting a roadway or exercise area.
choices.C: Only when backing up.
choices.D: Only when parallel parking.

en.explanation: When performing an exercise, it is important to check traffic prior to entering or exiting a roadway. You must make sure the roadway is clear before entering back into traffic or leaving the exercise area.

en.question: What happens if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its exact final position as instructed by the examiner during a skills exercise?

choices.A: You will automatically fail the entire test.
choices.B: Points will be added to your score.
choices.C: You will be asked to repeat the exercise until you get it right.
choices.D: The examiner will take control of the steering wheel.

en.explanation: Under the 'Final Position' scoring section, it states: 'If you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, points will be added to your score.'

en.question: Are you allowed to change lanes while proceeding through an intersection?

choices.A: Yes, if you use a turn signal.
choices.B: Yes, if the lane is clear of traffic.
choices.C: No, you should not attempt lane changes at intersections.
choices.D: Only when you are preparing to make a right turn.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection' and 'Do not attempt lane changes at intersections.'

en.question: When entering an expressway, which of the following actions should you avoid?

choices.A: Using your turn signal.
choices.B: Checking your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
choices.C: Stopping or crossing over any solid painted lines.
choices.D: Increasing your speed to merge smoothly.

en.explanation: When entering an expressway, you should smoothly merge into the proper lane of traffic without stopping or crossing over any solid painted lines.

en.question: When approaching a curve, when is the best time to reduce your speed?

choices.A: While in the middle of the curve.
choices.B: Before entering the curve.
choices.C: After you have exited the curve.
choices.D: You should accelerate through the curve instead of braking.

en.explanation: Before entering the curve, you should reduce your speed so further braking is not required while in the curve.

en.question: What is the proper hand position on the steering wheel during the road test?

choices.A: One hand on the wheel and one on the gear shift.
choices.B: Both hands on the inside spokes of the wheel.
choices.C: Both hands on the outside of the steering wheel at all times.
choices.D: One hand at the 12 o'clock position.

en.explanation: You must keep both hands on the outside of the steering wheel at all times unless using other controls. Both hand-over-hand and hand-to-hand methods are acceptable.

en.question: When completing a right turn on a multiple lane road, which lane should you finish the turn in?

choices.A: The left-most lane.
choices.B: The center lane.
choices.C: Any lane that is open.
choices.D: The right-most (curb) lane.

en.explanation: According to proper lane usage rules, you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.

en.question: When stopping behind another vehicle at an intersection, how much space should you leave?

choices.A: Exactly one car length.
choices.B: Enough space to see the rear wheels of the vehicle in front of you.
choices.C: Three to four feet of space.
choices.D: Enough space to see the driver's head in their rearview mirror.

en.explanation: When stopping behind another vehicle, make sure you can see the rear wheels of the vehicle in front of you to maintain a safe distance.

en.question: Which of the following actions will result in an automatic failure on your road exam?

choices.A: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction.
choices.B: Using the hand-over-hand steering method.
choices.C: Failing to check your blind spots.
choices.D: Braking smoothly at a stop sign.

en.explanation: Not checking your blind spots during the road exam is listed as an automatic failure.

en.question: During the road exam, putting your vehicle over sidewalks or curbs unnecessarily will result in:

choices.A: A warning from the examiner.
choices.B: A two-point deduction.
choices.C: An automatic failure.
choices.D: A requirement to repeat the maneuver.

en.explanation: Putting the vehicle over sidewalks or curbs unnecessarily is an automatic failure on the road exam.

en.question: If one person will be doing all the driving on a trip, what is the recommended daily driving limit?

choices.A: 4 to 5 hours.
choices.B: 6 to 8 hours.
choices.C: 10 to 11 hours.
choices.D: 12 to 14 hours.

en.explanation: If one person will be doing all the driving, 6 to 8 hours of driving in any one day should be considered the limit.

en.question: When two or more persons can share the driving on a trip, total driving time in one day should not exceed:

choices.A: 8 to 9 hours.
choices.B: 10 to 11 hours.
choices.C: 14 to 15 hours.
choices.D: 16 to 18 hours.

en.explanation: When two or more persons can share the driving, total driving time should not exceed 10 to 11 hours.

en.question: When driving on major highways, how often should you take a 10 to 15-minute break?

choices.A: Every hour.
choices.B: Every 2 to 3 hours.
choices.C: Every 4 to 5 hours.
choices.D: Only when you need to refuel.

en.explanation: The manual recommends taking 10 to 15-minute breaks every 2 to 3 hours when driving on major highways.

en.question: When stopping at a stop sign or traffic signal, where should you stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Over the marked stop line so you can see cross traffic.
choices.B: Inside the pedestrian crosswalk.
choices.C: Before the marked stop line, crosswalk, or sidewalk.
choices.D: Slightly into the intersection.

en.explanation: When stopping at a stop sign or traffic signal, do not stop over a marked stop line, pedestrian crosswalk, sidewalk, or other marker, and do not stop in the intersection.

en.question: According to the manual, after what time are you more apt to fall asleep while driving?

choices.A: 8 p.m.
choices.B: 9 p.m.

en.explanation: You should avoid driving after dark when visibility is limited and particularly after 11 p.m. when you are more apt to fall asleep while driving.

en.question: What is a 'head check' when preparing to change lanes?

choices.A: Looking in your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Looking over your shoulder to check your blind spots.
choices.C: Nodding to the examiner before turning.
choices.D: Checking the dashboard gauges.

en.explanation: A head check involves checking your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

en.question: When are studded snow tires legal to use in Kansas?

choices.A: October 1 through March 1
choices.B: November 1 through April 1
choices.C: December 1 through March 31
choices.D: They are legal year-round

en.explanation: According to the manual, studded snow tires are only legal from November 1 through April 1.

en.question: On front-wheel drive vehicles, where is it best to install snow tires or 'all-season' tires?

choices.A: Only on the front wheels
choices.B: Only on the rear wheels
choices.C: On all four wheels
choices.D: On the right-side wheels only

en.explanation: The manual states that on front-wheel drive vehicles, it is best to put snow tires or 'all-season' tires on all four wheels, not just the front.

en.question: When sleet, freezing rain, or snow starts to fall, which areas of the road are likely to freeze first?

choices.A: Intersections and crosswalks
choices.B: Bridges, ramps, and overpasses
choices.C: Tunnels and underpasses
choices.D: Dirt and gravel roads

en.explanation: When sleet, freezing rain or snow starts to fall, remember that bridges, ramps, and overpasses are likely to freeze first.

en.question: If you become stranded in cold weather, how should you operate your vehicle's engine and heater to stay warm?

choices.A: Run the engine continuously until help arrives
choices.B: Run the engine for approximately 10 minutes each hour
choices.C: Run the engine for 30 minutes every two hours
choices.D: Do not run the engine at all to save fuel

en.explanation: The manual recommends running the engine for approximately 10 minutes each hour in order to charge the battery and warm the interior.

en.question: Why is it critical to keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow and debris if you are stranded in a vehicle?

choices.A: To prevent the engine from overheating
choices.B: To keep the battery from draining
choices.C: To prevent exhaust fumes from leaking into the vehicle and causing carbon monoxide poisoning
choices.D: To ensure the heater blows warm air instead of cold air

en.explanation: Keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow and debris because fumes from the exhaust can leak into the vehicle and can cause you to black out or even cause death.

en.question: How often should you inspect your tires when driving in very hot weather?

choices.A: Every hour or 50 miles
choices.B: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choices.C: Every four hours or 200 miles
choices.D: Only when you stop for fuel

en.explanation: When driving in hot weather, you should inspect the tires every two hours or every 100 miles.

en.question: What should you do if your tire pressure increases while driving in hot weather?

choices.A: Let some air out to prevent a blowout
choices.B: Do not let air out, or the pressure will be too low when the tires cool off
choices.C: Pour cold water on the tires to reduce the pressure
choices.D: Drive faster to cool the tires with wind resistance

en.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Do not let air out or the pressure will be too low when the tires cool off.

en.question: What specific road hazard should you watch out for on the pavement during very hot weather?

choices.A: Bleeding tar that can be very slippery
choices.B: Expanding concrete that causes large bumps
choices.C: Melting painted lines that obscure lanes
choices.D: Increased glare from dry asphalt

en.explanation: Tar in the road pavement frequently rises to the surface in very hot weather. Spots where tar 'bleeds' to the surface can be very slippery.

en.question: What should you do if you spot a tornado while driving?

choices.A: Seek shelter under the nearest bridge or overpass
choices.B: Stay in your vehicle and park on the shoulder
choices.C: Leave the vehicle for sturdy shelter or drive out of the tornado's path
choices.D: Drive into the center of the tornado to pass through it quickly

en.explanation: If you spot a tornado, either leave the vehicle for sturdy shelter or drive out of the tornado's path. Vehicles are easily tossed and destroyed.

en.question: Why should you avoid seeking shelter under bridges or overpasses during a tornado?

choices.A: They attract lightning strikes
choices.B: Winds will be stronger beneath the overpass due to a 'wind tunnel effect'
choices.C: They are likely to collapse from the rain
choices.D: They block the view of approaching emergency vehicles

en.explanation: Avoid seeking shelter under bridges or overpasses because winds will be stronger beneath the overpass due to a 'wind tunnel effect' and they provide little protection from flying objects.

en.question: What is the safest way to protect yourself in a vehicle during a lightning storm?

choices.A: Drive a convertible with the top down
choices.B: Park under a tall tree
choices.C: Stay in a hard-topped vehicle with all doors closed and windows up
choices.D: Use a radio connected to an external antenna to monitor the weather

en.explanation: Only a hard-topped vehicle will protect you in a lightning storm. Make sure all doors are closed and windows are up, and do not touch any metal surfaces.

en.question: If your vehicle is caught in a flood and you cannot open the door or side window, what is the recommended escape method?

choices.A: Wait for the water to recede completely
choices.B: Take a breath, kick the window out, go to the air pocket for one more breath, and escape
choices.C: Turn on the heater to evaporate the water
choices.D: Honk the horn continuously until someone opens the door from the outside

en.explanation: If you can’t get a side window open, take a breath and kick the window out. Go to the air pocket for one more breath and then escape.

en.question: If you are a commercial license holder and need to update your address, what must you do?

choices.A: Visit any local post office
choices.B: Contact the local County Treasurer only
choices.C: Visit any full-service Kansas Driver licensing office
choices.D: Update your address online using ikan.ks.gov

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you are a commercial license holder, you will need to visit any full-service Kansas Driver licensing office.'

en.question: Under Kansas' First-Person Consent law, who can reverse an individual's decision to be an organ donor if the individual is at least 18 years old?

choices.A: Their spouse
choices.B: Their parents
choices.C: Their doctor
choices.D: No one else may reverse that decision

en.explanation: The change to first-person consent means that an individual’s decision to donate is legally binding, and no one else may reverse that decision if the individual is at least 18 years old.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding organ and tissue donation in Kansas?

choices.A: An open casket funeral is not possible for donors
choices.B: The donor's family must pay a fee for the donation process
choices.C: People of all ages and medical histories are considered for potential donation
choices.D: Major religions generally oppose organ donation

en.explanation: The manual states that people of all ages and medical histories are considered for potential donation. It also notes that open casket funerals are possible, there is no cost to the family for donation, and all major religions approve of it.

en.question: How much does it cost the donor's family or estate for organ and tissue donation?

choices.A: A flat fee of $500
choices.B: It depends on the organs donated
choices.C: There is no cost
choices.D: The estate pays a percentage of the medical bills

en.explanation: The manual states, "There is no cost to the donor’s family or estate for organ and tissue donation."

en.question: Who is responsible for paying the funeral costs of an organ and tissue donor?

choices.A: The state registry
choices.B: The hospital
choices.C: The donor's family
choices.D: The organ recipient

en.explanation: According to the manual, "Funeral costs remain the responsibility of the family."

en.question: Is it possible to be an organ and tissue donor while still alive?

choices.A: No, donation is only possible after death
choices.B: Yes, living donation is possible
choices.C: Only for tissue donation
choices.D: Only for family members

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states, "Living donation is possible."

en.question: Which website should you visit to sign up directly in the Kansas state organ donor registry?

choices.A: https://www.mwtn.org/
choices.B: https://www.donatelifekansas.com/
choices.C: https://www.kansas.gov/donor
choices.D: https://www.ksrevenue.org/

en.explanation: The manual instructs, "To sign up in the state registry directly please visit https://www.donatelifekansas.com/"

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the financial aspects of organ donation?

choices.A: The family must pay for the donation procedure.
choices.B: Funeral costs are waived for organ donors.
choices.C: There is no cost to the donor's estate for the donation.
choices.D: The state covers all funeral expenses.

en.explanation: The manual states that "There is no cost to the donor’s family or estate for organ and tissue donation."

en.question: What website is provided in the manual for more general information about organ and tissue donation?

choices.A: https://www.mwtn.org/
choices.B: https://www.donatelifekansas.com/
choices.C: https://www.organdonor.gov/
choices.D: https://www.ksdot.org/

en.explanation: The manual states, "For more information, please visit our website at https://www.mwtn.org/"

en.question: Complete the organ donation slogan found in the manual: "SHARE YOUR LIFE. SHARE YOUR..."

choices.A: ORGANS.
choices.B: DECISION.
choices.C: FUTURE.
choices.D: LOVE.

en.explanation: The manual includes the promotional text: "SHARE YOUR LIFE. SHARE YOUR DECISION."

en.question: Which of the following is a false statement about organ and tissue donation according to the manual?

choices.A: Living donation is possible.
choices.B: Funeral costs remain the responsibility of the family.
choices.C: The donor's estate must pay a fee for tissue donation.
choices.D: You can sign up in the state registry online.

en.explanation: The statement that the estate must pay a fee is false. The manual states, "There is no cost to the donor’s family or estate for organ and tissue donation."

en.question: Complete the following phrase from the organ donation section: "LIVE IT. GIVE IT. ..."

choices.A: TODAY.
choices.B: FREELY.
choices.C: LIFE.
choices.D: HOPE.

en.explanation: The manual includes the slogan: "LIVE IT. GIVE IT. LIFE."

en.question: If a person decides to become an organ donor, what happens to their funeral expenses?

choices.A: They are paid by the organ procurement organization.
choices.B: They remain the responsibility of the family.
choices.C: They are covered by the state of Kansas.
choices.D: They are split between the family and the hospital.

en.explanation: The manual clearly states, "Funeral costs remain the responsibility of the family."

en.question: A family is worried that agreeing to organ donation will deplete the deceased's estate. What does the manual state?

choices.A: The estate will be charged a standard medical fee.
choices.B: The estate is only charged if multiple organs are donated.
choices.C: There is no cost to the donor's estate for organ and tissue donation.
choices.D: The estate must cover the surgical costs.

en.explanation: The manual assures that "There is no cost to the donor’s family or estate for organ and tissue donation."

en.question: What type of donation does the manual explicitly state is possible besides deceased donation?

choices.A: Living donation
choices.B: Financial donation
choices.C: Anonymous donation only
choices.D: Out-of-state donation only

en.explanation: The text explicitly notes, "Living donation is possible."

en.question: According to the manual, what two things are you encouraged to "SHARE" regarding organ donation?

choices.A: Your wealth and your time
choices.B: Your life and your decision
choices.C: Your health and your organs
choices.D: Your choice and your family

en.explanation: The manual concludes with the lines: "SHARE YOUR LIFE. SHARE YOUR DECISION."

en.question: Which of the following costs is NOT covered by the organ and tissue donation process?

choices.A: The cost of organ recovery
choices.B: The cost of tissue recovery
choices.C: Funeral costs
choices.D: The cost to the donor's estate

en.explanation: While there is no cost to the family or estate for the donation itself, the manual specifies that "Funeral costs remain the responsibility of the family."

en.question: How can a Kansas resident sign up for the state organ donor registry directly?

choices.A: By visiting https://www.donatelifekansas.com/
choices.B: By calling the local police department
choices.C: By visiting https://www.mwtn.org/
choices.D: By writing a letter to the governor

en.explanation: The manual states, "To sign up in the state registry directly please visit https://www.donatelifekansas.com/"

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What does this sign indicate?

choices.A: Left turn only
choices.B: Traffic flows in one direction — to the left
choices.C: Keep left of the median
choices.D: Highway exit to the left

en.explanation: A black and white ONE WAY sign with an arrow indicates that traffic on this street moves in only one direction — the direction the arrow points.

en.question: What does this sign prohibit?

choices.A: Right turns
choices.B: Left turns
choices.C: U-turns
choices.D: Passing other vehicles

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign with a U-turn arrow crossed out means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What does this sign instruct drivers to do?

choices.A: Merge right
choices.B: Turn right only
choices.C: Keep to the right of a divider or obstruction
choices.D: Right lane ends ahead

en.explanation: A white regulatory KEEP RIGHT sign with an arrow means you must keep to the right side of a traffic island, median, or obstruction.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What road condition does this sign warn about?

choices.A: A winding road
choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions
choices.D: A roundabout ahead

en.explanation: A reverse curve sign warns of two curves in opposite directions ahead. Slow down and be prepared for the road to curve first one way, then the other.

en.question: What does this sign warn you to expect?

choices.A: A single sharp curve
choices.B: A slippery road surface
choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead
choices.D: A hill ahead

en.explanation: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves or turns ahead. Reduce your speed and be alert for changing road conditions.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to prepare for?

choices.A: A lane ending
choices.B: Traffic merging from another road
choices.C: A divided highway beginning
choices.D: A road narrowing to one lane

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped merge sign warns that traffic from another road will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed and position.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to expect ahead?

choices.A: A yield sign
choices.B: A traffic signal
choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop
choices.D: A speed bump

en.explanation: This sign warns that there is a stop sign ahead. Begin slowing down and prepare to come to a complete stop at the stop sign.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

es.question: ¿Según el Manual de Conducción de Kansas, qué medida ha tomado la Legislatura de Kansas con respecto a enviar mensajes de texto mientras se conduce?

es.explanation: La carta del Gobernador señala que la Legislatura de Kansas actualizó las leyes de tránsito para prohibir el envío de mensajes de texto al conducir, ya que puede distraer peligrosamente a los conductores de la carretera.

choices.B: 100,000 millas

es.question: ¿Qué división dentro del Departamento de Ingresos de Kansas se esfuerza por hacer que su experiencia sea más rápida y conveniente?

choices.A: División de Vehículos
choices.B: División de Transporte

choices.D: División de Automovilistas

es.question: Según la introducción, ¿en qué se enfoca el examen de conducir para ayudarnos a todos a conducir de manera segura?

choices.A: 16 años de edad

choices.C: 18 años de edad

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima requerida para obtener una licencia de conducir no comercial Clase A o B?

choices.A: 16 años de edad
choices.B: 17 años de edad

choices.D: 21 años de edad

es.question: Al completar las horas de práctica de manejo requeridas, ¿qué edad mínima debe tener el adulto acompañante?

choices.B: 19 años de edad
choices.C: 21 años de edad
choices.D: 25 años de edad

es.explanation: El manual especifica que la práctica de manejo debe realizarse acompañado por un adulto que tenga 21 años de edad o más.

es.question: ¿Cuántas de las 50 horas de práctica de manejo requeridas deben completarse por la noche para una licencia No Comercial Clase C o M (Privilegios Menos Restringidos)?

choices.D: 20 horas

choices.D: 16 o 17 años de edad

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima requerida para obtener un Permiso de Instrucción Clase C o M en Kansas?

choices.A: 14 años de edad
choices.B: 15 años de edad
choices.C: 16 años de edad
choices.D: 18 años de edad

es.explanation: Según el manual, la edad mínima para un Permiso de Instrucción Clase C o M es de 14 años de edad o más.

es.question: ¿Cuántas horas de instrucción deben ofrecer las escuelas privadas de educación vial aprobadas?

choices.B: 8 horas de clase y 6 horas al volante

es.question: ¿De cuántos días dispone para obtener una licencia de conducir de Kansas después de mudarse al estado?

choices.B: 60 días
choices.C: 90 días
choices.D: 120 días

es.explanation: Se requiere que obtenga una licencia de conducir de Kansas dentro de los 90 días posteriores a su mudanza al estado.

es.question: Para calificar para un Permiso Agrícola (Farm Permit), el solicitante debe residir o estar empleado en una granja. ¿Cuál es el requisito de tamaño mínimo para la granja?

choices.B: 20 acres
choices.C: 40 acres
choices.D: 50 acres

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes es una restricción de conducción para un joven de 14 o 15 años con un Permiso Agrícola (Farm Permit)?

es.question: Al conducir con un Permiso de Instrucción (Clase C o M), ¿cuáles son los requisitos para el adulto supervisor en el asiento delantero?

choices.D: Debe tener al menos 25 años.

choices.C: 2 años
choices.D: 4 años

es.question: ¿Cuántas horas de conducción supervisada debe completar un solicitante de 15 años para obtener una Licencia Restringida?

choices.C: 40 horas
choices.D: 50 horas

es.question: ¿Cuántos pasajeros menores que no sean hermanos se le permite tener en el vehículo a un joven de 16 años con una Licencia Restringida?

choices.B: Solo uno

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes condiciones le impedirá obtener una licencia de conducir de Kansas?

es.question: ¿Qué departamento estatal coordina las audiencias administrativas sobre fallos en pruebas químicas y rechazos de pruebas?

choices.A: Departamento de Transporte
choices.B: Servicios al Conductor (Driver Services)
choices.C: Departamento de Educación
choices.D: Patrulla de Caminos (Highway Patrol)

es.explanation: Servicios al Conductor (Driver Services) coordina las audiencias administrativas sobre fallos en pruebas químicas y rechazos de pruebas, y gestiona los requisitos de comprobante de seguro.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes es la edad mínima para obtener una licencia de conducir sin restricciones (Unrestricted Driver's License) en Kansas?
es.explanation: La edad mínima para obtener una licencia de conducir sin restricciones en Kansas es de 17 años.

es.question: Para los solicitantes menores de 18 años que buscan una licencia sin restricciones, ¿cuántas horas de conducción nocturna debe certificar un padre o tutor?

choices.A: 5 horas
choices.B: 10 horas
choices.C: 15 horas
choices.D: 50 horas

es.explanation: Un padre o tutor debe firmar una declaración jurada que certifique al menos 50 horas de tiempo de conducción, con al menos 10 horas de noche, para los solicitantes menores de 18 años.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito mínimo de visión para aprobar el examen de la vista de la licencia de conducir?

choices.A: 20/20 en ambos ojos
choices.B: 20/30 en ambos ojos
choices.C: 20/40 en un ojo
choices.D: 20/50 en un ojo

es.explanation: La visión debe ser de al menos 20/40 en un ojo al realizar el examen en la estación de licencias de conducir, con o sin corrección.

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas tiene el examen de conocimientos para conductores de Kansas?
es.explanation: El examen de conocimientos requiere que responda 25 preguntas sobre las leyes de tránsito e identifique ciertas señales.

es.question: Si reprueba el examen escrito o el de conducción cuatro veces, ¿cuánto tiempo debe esperar antes de volver a realizarlo?

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 3 meses
choices.C: 6 meses
choices.D: 1 año

es.explanation: Después de la cuarta vez que repruebe cualquiera de los exámenes, debe esperar un mínimo de seis (6) meses desde el examen fallido más reciente antes de volver a intentarlo.

es.question: ¿Qué se requiere si su licencia de conducir ha estado vencida por más de un año?

choices.A: Debe pagar una multa de $50
choices.B: Debe completar un curso de conducción defensiva
choices.C: Debe someterse a todas las pruebas, incluidos los exámenes de la vista, escrito y de conducción
choices.D: Debe esperar 6 meses antes de solicitar una nueva licencia

es.explanation: Si la licencia de conducir ha estado vencida por más de 1 año, se requerirá realizar todas las pruebas, lo que incluye los exámenes de la vista, escrito y de conducción.

es.question: ¿Sus privilegios de conducir pueden ser suspendidos si es condenado por cuántas infracciones de tránsito en movimiento dentro de un período de doce meses?

choices.A: Dos
choices.B: Tres
choices.C: Cuatro
choices.D: Cinco

es.explanation: Sus privilegios de conducir pueden ser suspendidos por la condena de tres (3) infracciones de tránsito en movimiento dentro de un período de doce meses.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la sanción por la primera negativa a someterse a una prueba química para determinar el contenido de alcohol o drogas?

choices.A: Una suspensión de 6 meses
choices.B: Una suspensión obligatoria de 1 año
choices.C: Una suspensión obligatoria de 2 años
choices.D: Revocación permanente

es.explanation: Negarse a someterse a una prueba química conlleva una suspensión obligatoria de 1 año por la primera negativa.

es.question: No mantener un seguro de responsabilidad civil continuo en su vehículo resultará en:

choices.A: Una carta de advertencia
choices.B: Una suspensión de 30 días
choices.C: Una suspensión obligatoria indefinida
choices.D: Una revocación permanente

es.explanation: No mantener un seguro de responsabilidad civil continuo en su vehículo conlleva una suspensión obligatoria indefinida.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes condenas resultará en la revocación de sus privilegios de conducción?

choices.A: Transportar un recipiente abierto de licor
choices.B: No informar de un accidente de tráfico
choices.C: No comparecer a una cita judicial
choices.D: Intentar eludir a un oficial de policía

es.explanation: Intentar eludir a un oficial de policía figura como una infracción que puede dar lugar a la revocación de sus privilegios de conducción. Las otras opciones resultan en suspensión.

es.question: ¿Qué resultará en una revocación permanente de la licencia en Kansas?

choices.A: Una tercera infracción de tránsito en 12 meses
choices.B: Un quinto resultado de prueba de .08 o superior o la negativa a someterse a pruebas químicas
choices.C: No mantener el seguro de responsabilidad civil dos veces
choices.D: Transportar un recipiente abierto de licor

es.explanation: Un quinto resultado de prueba de .08 o superior o la negativa a someterse a pruebas químicas para determinar el contenido de alcohol/drogas en la sangre resultará en una revocación permanente de la licencia.

es.question: Los turistas extranjeros, profesores o empresarios con documentos de inmigración válidos pueden conducir en Kansas con una licencia extranjera o de otro estado válida existente por hasta:

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 6 meses
choices.C: 1 año
choices.D: 2 años

es.explanation: Los extranjeros (turistas, profesores o empresarios extranjeros) que estén aquí por hasta un año y posean documentos de inmigración válidos pueden conducir con una licencia válida si tienen al menos 16 años.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la clasificación de peso bruto vehicular máximo que puede operar con una licencia de conducir Clase C?

choices.A: Menos de 10,000 libras
choices.B: Menos de 26,001 libras
choices.C: Más de 26,001 libras
choices.D: Cualquier peso independientemente del tamaño

es.explanation: Según el manual, una licencia de conducir Clase C le permite operar vehículos con una clasificación de peso bruto vehicular de menos de 26,001 libras.

es.question: A menos que se indique lo contrario, ¿cuál es el límite de velocidad máximo en cualquier distrito urbano en Kansas?

choices.A: 20 millas por hora
choices.B: 25 millas por hora
choices.C: 30 millas por hora
choices.D: 35 millas por hora

es.explanation: El manual establece que, a menos que se indique lo contrario, el límite de velocidad máximo en pueblos o ciudades es de treinta (30) millas por hora en cualquier distrito urbano.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el límite de velocidad máximo en cualquier carretera de condado o municipio (Township) a menos que se indique lo contrario?

choices.A: 45 millas por hora
choices.B: 55 millas por hora
choices.C: 65 millas por hora
choices.D: 75 millas por hora

es.explanation: El manual establece el límite de velocidad máximo en cincuenta y cinco (55) millas por hora en cualquier carretera de condado o municipio, a menos que se indique lo contrario.

es.question: Según la ley de Kansas, el uso del cinturón de seguridad es una 'Infracción Primaria' (Primary Violation). ¿Qué significa esto?

choices.A: Un vehículo puede ser detenido únicamente si un oficial ve a un adulto sin cinturón en el asiento delantero o a un niño sin protección.
choices.B: Solo se le puede multar por una infracción del cinturón de seguridad si primero lo detienen por exceso de velocidad.
choices.C: Solo el conductor está obligado a usar el cinturón de seguridad.
choices.D: Las infracciones del cinturón de seguridad resultan en una suspensión inmediata de la licencia.

es.explanation: El uso del cinturón de seguridad es una 'Infracción Primaria' en Kansas, lo que significa que si un oficial de la ley ve a un adulto sin protección en un asiento delantero o a un niño sin protección en cualquier lugar del vehículo, el vehículo puede ser detenido únicamente por esa infracción.

es.question: ¿A qué edad debe un niño estar sujeto en un asiento de seguridad para niños o asiento elevado (booster seat) aprobado por el gobierno federal, a menos que mida más de 4'9" o pese más de 80 libras?

choices.A: Menores de 4 años de edad
choices.B: De 4 a 8 años de edad
choices.C: De 8 a 12 años de edad
choices.D: De 12 a 16 años de edad

es.explanation: El manual establece que todos los niños de 4 a 8 años de edad deben estar sujetos en un asiento de seguridad para niños o asiento elevado aprobado por el gobierno federal, a menos que el niño mida más de 4'9" O pese más de 80 libras.

es.question: ¿Con cuánta anticipación debe señalizar su intención de girar o cambiar de carril?

choices.A: Al menos 50 pies
choices.B: Al menos 100 pies
choices.C: Al menos 200 pies
choices.D: Al menos 500 pies

es.explanation: Todas las señales deben hacerse al menos 100 pies antes de realizar el movimiento o giro real.

es.question: No debe realizar un giro en "U" en ningún lugar donde no pueda ser visto por otros conductores durante al menos:

choices.A: 100 pies
choices.B: 200 pies
choices.C: 300 pies
choices.D: 500 pies

es.explanation: El manual establece: "No realice un giro en U en una curva, cerca de la cima de una colina o en cualquier lugar donde no pueda ser visto por otros conductores durante al menos 500 pies".

es.question: Al rebasar a otro vehículo en una carretera de dos carriles, ¿cuándo es seguro regresar al carril derecho?

choices.A: Tan pronto como pase el parachoques trasero del vehículo rebasado
choices.B: Cuando pueda ver toda la parte delantera del vehículo que acaba de rebasar en su espejo retrovisor
choices.C: Después de haber recorrido 100 pies más allá del vehículo
choices.D: Cuando el vehículo rebasado parpadee sus luces delanteras

es.explanation: El manual instruye a los conductores a no regresar al carril derecho demasiado pronto; espere hasta que pueda ver toda la parte delantera del vehículo que acaba de rebasar en su espejo retrovisor.

es.question: ¿En cuál de las siguientes situaciones NO se le permite rebasar a otro vehículo?

choices.A: En una calle de sentido único
choices.B: A menos de 100 pies de cruzar cualquier intersección o cruce de ferrocarril a nivel
choices.C: Cuando el vehículo de adelante circula por debajo del límite de velocidad
choices.D: En una carretera de varios carriles que se mueven en la misma dirección

es.explanation: No puede rebasar a menos de 100 pies de cruzar cualquier intersección o cruce de ferrocarril a nivel.

es.question: ¿Qué forma tiene la señal de advertencia de "Zona de no rebasar" (No Passing Zone)?

choices.A: Diamante
choices.B: Octágono
choices.C: Banderín
choices.D: Rectángulo

es.explanation: El manual establece que la de "Zona de no rebasar" es la única señal de advertencia con forma de banderín.

es.question: ¿Qué regla de distancia de seguimiento debe utilizar en condiciones climáticas adversas?

choices.A: La regla de los dos segundos
choices.B: La regla de los tres segundos
choices.C: La regla de los cuatro segundos
choices.D: La regla de los seis segundos

es.explanation: Si bien la regla de los dos segundos es para condiciones óptimas, el manual establece el uso de una regla de seguimiento de cuatro segundos en condiciones adversas.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer cuando un vehículo de emergencia se acerca por detrás mostrando luces rojas intermitentes y/o haciendo sonar una sirena?

choices.A: Aumentar la velocidad para mantenerse por delante del vehículo
choices.B: Detenerse inmediatamente en su carril actual
choices.C: Conducir inmediatamente hacia la derecha y detenerse sin bloquear ninguna intersección
choices.D: Moverse al carril izquierdo y reducir la velocidad

es.explanation: Cuando un vehículo de emergencia viene hacia usted o se acerca por detrás mostrando luces rojas intermitentes y/o haciendo sonar una sirena, debe conducir inmediatamente hacia la derecha y detenerse sin bloquear ninguna intersección.

es.question: ¿Cuándo NO se requiere que se detenga ante un autobús escolar que está detenido para recoger o dejar niños?

choices.A: Cuando viaja en la misma dirección que el autobús
choices.B: Cuando se aproxima al autobús en la calzada opuesta de una carretera dividida
choices.C: Cuando se encuentra en una carretera de dos carriles
choices.D: Cuando el autobús está detenido en un distrito residencial

es.explanation: El tráfico que se aproxima a un autobús escolar en la calzada opuesta de una carretera dividida no está obligado a detenerse.

es.question: Cuando dos vehículos entran en una intersección desde diferentes calzadas aproximadamente al mismo tiempo sin controles de tráfico, ¿quién tiene el derecho de paso?

choices.A: El conductor de la derecha deberá ceder el paso al vehículo de la izquierda
choices.B: El conductor de la izquierda deberá ceder el paso al vehículo de la derecha
choices.C: El vehículo que viaja más rápido tiene el derecho de paso
choices.D: El vehículo más grande tiene el derecho de paso

es.explanation: Cuando dos vehículos entran en una intersección desde diferentes calzadas aproximadamente al mismo tiempo, el conductor de la izquierda deberá ceder el derecho de paso al vehículo de la derecha.

es.question: La ley de velocidad básica de Kansas exige que usted:

choices.A: Conduzca siempre al límite de velocidad indicado, independientemente del clima
choices.B: Nunca conduzca a una velocidad mayor de lo que sea razonable y prudente bajo las condiciones existentes en ese momento
choices.C: Conduzca 5 mph por debajo del límite de velocidad por la noche
choices.D: Iguale la velocidad de los vehículos a su alrededor

es.explanation: La ley de velocidad básica de Kansas exige que nunca conduzca un vehículo a una velocidad mayor de lo que sea razonable y prudente bajo las condiciones existentes en ese momento.

es.question: ¿Si se aproxima a un vehículo de emergencia estacionado con luces intermitentes en una autopista de varios carriles, cuál es la acción preferida?

choices.A: Tocar la bocina para alertar a los trabajadores de emergencia
choices.B: Detenerse inmediatamente en su carril actual
choices.C: Cambiarse a un carril que no esté junto al vehículo de emergencia detenido
choices.D: Mantener su velocidad y permanecer en el carril junto al vehículo

es.explanation: Al aproximarse por detrás a un vehículo de emergencia estacionado en una calle o autopista con dos o más carriles en cada dirección, debe proceder con la debida precaución y cambiarse a un carril que no esté junto al vehículo de emergencia detenido.

es.question: Si un vehículo que gira a la izquierda y un vehículo que sigue recto entran en una intersección desde direcciones opuestas al mismo tiempo, ¿quién debe ceder el paso?

choices.A: El vehículo que sigue recto
choices.B: El vehículo que gira a la izquierda
choices.C: El vehículo a la derecha
choices.D: Ninguno de los vehículos

es.explanation: El conductor de un vehículo que gira a la izquierda debe ceder el derecho de paso a los vehículos que se aproximan desde la dirección opuesta. Si ambos autos entran al mismo tiempo, el auto que sigue recto tiene el derecho de paso.

es.question: Usted tiene luz verde en una intersección, pero el tráfico está congestionado y no hay suficiente espacio para su vehículo al otro lado. ¿Qué debe hacer?

choices.A: Entrar en la intersección y esperar a que el tráfico se despeje
choices.B: Tocar la bocina hasta que el tráfico avance
choices.C: No entrar en la intersección hasta que haya suficiente espacio al otro lado
choices.D: Avanzar hacia el paso de peatones y esperar

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente: "No entre en una intersección, paso de peatones o cruce de ferrocarril (RR) a menos que haya suficiente espacio al otro lado para su vehículo. Aunque tenga luz verde, no puede entrar en una intersección si no hay espacio para cruzar por completo".

es.question: ¿Cuál es la distancia mínima que debe mantener al estacionar cerca de un hidrante de incendios?

choices.A: 10 pies
choices.B: 15 pies
choices.C: 20 pies
choices.D: 30 pies

es.explanation: NO se permite estacionar a menos de 15 pies de un hidrante de incendios.

es.question: ¿A cuántos pies del riel más cercano en un cruce de ferrocarril es ilegal estacionar?

choices.A: 15 pies
choices.B: 20 pies
choices.C: 30 pies
choices.D: 50 pies

es.explanation: NO se permite estacionar a menos de 50 pies del riel más cercano en los cruces de ferrocarril.

es.question: Al estacionar en paralelo a un bordillo, su vehículo no puede estar estacionado a más de:

choices.A: 6 pulgadas del bordillo
choices.B: 12 pulgadas del bordillo
choices.C: 18 pulgadas del bordillo
choices.D: 24 pulgadas del bordillo

es.explanation: NO se permite estacionar a más de 12” (12 pulgadas) de un bordillo.

es.question: Según la ley de Kansas, ¿cuál de las siguientes acciones está legalmente permitida mientras se conduce?

choices.A: Enviar un mensaje de texto
choices.B: Leer un correo electrónico
choices.C: Escribir un mensaje de texto
choices.D: Usar un dispositivo GPS

es.explanation: La ley de Kansas prohíbe el uso de cualquier dispositivo electrónico para "escribir, enviar o leer" una comunicación escrita mientras se conduce, pero explícitamente no incluye dispositivos GPS o informes meteorológicos.

es.question: Cuando se enfrente a un conductor agresivo, ¿por qué debe evitar hacer contacto visual?

choices.A: A veces puede enfurecer a un conductor agresivo
choices.B: Es ilegal en Kansas
choices.C: Le distraerá de mirar su velocímetro
choices.D: Les anima a rebasarle por la derecha

es.explanation: El manual aconseja evitar el contacto visual porque "el contacto visual a veces puede enfurecer a un conductor agresivo".

es.question: Para aprobar el examen de la vista de Kansas para una licencia de conducir, ¿qué agudeza visual debe tener como mínimo en al menos un ojo?
es.explanation: El examen de la vista mide que usted tenga al menos una visión de 20/40 en al menos un ojo, con o sin lentes correctivos.

es.question: ¿Por qué debe evitar el uso de lentes correctivos oscuros o teñidos al conducir de noche?

choices.A: Es ilegal usarlos en cualquier momento
choices.B: Reducen la luz que necesita para ver con claridad
choices.C: Magnifican el resplandor de los faros que vienen en sentido contrario
choices.D: Causan fatiga ocular más rápido que los lentes transparentes

es.explanation: Debe evitar el uso de lentes correctivos oscuros o teñidos por la noche porque "reducen la luz que necesita para ver con claridad en condiciones de conducción nocturna".

es.question: ¿Cómo puede ayudarle el sentido del oído mientras conduce?

choices.A: Le ayuda a determinar la velocidad exacta de los vehículos que vienen en sentido contrario
choices.B: Un cambio repentino en el zumbido de los neumáticos puede indicar un cambio en la superficie de la carretera
choices.C: Le permite escuchar informes meteorológicos sin radio
choices.D: Evita que experimente fatiga al conducir

es.explanation: El manual señala que un "cambio repentino en el zumbido de los neumáticos sobre el pavimento puede indicarle que la superficie de la carretera o los neumáticos han cambiado".

es.question: Para prevenir la fatiga durante viajes largos, ¿con qué frecuencia debe programar descansos adecuados?

choices.A: Cada 50 millas o 1 hora
choices.B: Cada 100 millas o 2 horas
choices.C: Cada 200 millas o 4 horas
choices.D: Solo cuando empiece a salirse de su carril

es.explanation: Antes de un viaje, debe programar descansos adecuados, aproximadamente cada 100 millas o 2 horas durante viajes largos.

es.question: Si necesita tomar una siesta para combatir la fatiga al conducir, ¿cuál es la duración recomendada?

choices.A: De 5 a 10 minutos
choices.B: De 15 a 20 minutos
choices.C: De 45 a 60 minutos
choices.D: Al menos 2 horas

es.explanation: El manual recomienda buscar un área de estacionamiento segura para tomar una siesta de 15 a 20 minutos para evitar un choque relacionado con la fatiga.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la mejor manera de prevenir la fatiga al conducir?

choices.A: Beber dos tazas de café
choices.B: Dormir lo suficiente
choices.C: Tomar una ducha fría
choices.D: Conducir entre la medianoche y las 6 a.m.

es.explanation: Según el manual, la mejor manera de prevenir la fatiga es dormir.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes se considera una posible distracción que ocurre fuera de un vehículo en movimiento?

choices.A: Ajustar los controles de climatización
choices.B: Atender a niños o mascotas
choices.C: Leer vallas publicitarias u otros anuncios en la carretera
choices.D: Usar un sistema de posicionamiento global (GPS)

es.explanation: El manual enumera la lectura de vallas publicitarias u otros anuncios en la carretera como una posible distracción que podría ocurrir fuera de un vehículo en movimiento.

es.question: Si necesita mirar un mapa mientras conduce, ¿qué debe hacer?
