choices.C: Leave the windows rolled down for ventilation
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: The law requires you to turn off the engine and remove the key when you leave a vehicle. You should also always lock your vehicle.

en.question: How should you turn your wheels when parking on a hill with no curb?

choices.A: So the vehicle will roll straight backward
choices.B: So the vehicle will go off the road should it roll
choices.C: So the vehicle will roll into the center of the street
choices.D: Keep the wheels perfectly straight

en.explanation: If there is no curb, turn the wheels so the vehicle will go off the road should it roll.

en.question: Who is legally allowed to park in a designated handicapped parking area?

choices.A: Anyone who is only parking for a few minutes
choices.B: Any vehicle displaying a handicapped decal, regardless of passengers
choices.C: Vehicles displaying an official permit and transporting a disabled person
choices.D: Senior citizens over the age of 65

en.explanation: Handicapped Parking is only for vehicles displaying an official permit and transporting a disabled person.

en.question: On a limited access highway, what is illegal regarding the left lane?

choices.A: Using it to pass slower vehicles
choices.B: Remaining in the left lane
choices.C: Driving at the posted speed limit
choices.D: Using it to turn left

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that remaining in the left lane on a limited access highway is illegal.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your turn at an intersection?

choices.A: Stop and back up quickly
choices.B: Make a U-turn immediately
choices.C: Go on to the next intersection and work your way back
choices.D: Pull over to the wrong side of the road

en.explanation: If you miss your turn, go on to the next intersection and work your way back to where you want to go.

en.question: If you have already started through an intersection when the traffic light changes, what should you do?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the intersection
choices.B: Keep going and follow through
choices.C: Put your vehicle in reverse
choices.D: Swerve into the nearest lane

en.explanation: If you have already started through an intersection when the light changes, keep going. Last-second changes can cause collisions.

en.question: How should you check your 'blind spots' when changing lanes?

choices.A: By looking in your rearview mirror
choices.B: By looking in your side mirrors
choices.C: By turning your head and looking over your shoulder
choices.D: By honking your horn

en.explanation: Check your 'blind spots' by turning your head and looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

en.question: When entering a multi-lane highway, who has the right of way?

choices.A: The existing traffic on the highway
choices.B: The vehicle entering the highway
choices.C: The largest vehicle
choices.D: The vehicle moving the fastest

en.explanation: The existing traffic has the right of way, so make sure it is clear before you merge.

en.question: When exiting a roadway, when should you slow down to your exiting speed?

choices.A: While still on the main roadway
choices.B: After moving to the deceleration lane
choices.C: Before signaling your intention
choices.D: Just before you reach the exit ramp curve

en.explanation: You should maintain your vehicle speed as long as you are on the main roadway, then signal, move to the deceleration lane, and slow to your exiting speed.

en.question: Under Kentucky law, when must a pass be completed in relation to an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: Before coming within 50 feet of the oncoming vehicle
choices.B: Before coming within 100 feet of the oncoming vehicle
choices.C: Before coming within 200 feet of the oncoming vehicle
choices.D: Before coming within 500 feet of the oncoming vehicle

en.explanation: Kentucky law requires that a pass be completed before coming within two hundred (200) feet of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know you have enough room to return to the driving lane?

choices.A: When you are one car length ahead
choices.B: When you can see the complete front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
choices.C: When the passed vehicle flashes its headlights
choices.D: When you are parallel to the passed vehicle's front bumper

en.explanation: You should continue to pass until the complete front of the passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror before returning to the driving lane.

en.question: How should you treat a curve or a hill when considering passing another vehicle?

choices.A: Treat it as an oncoming vehicle and do not start to pass
choices.B: Honk your horn and pass quickly
choices.C: Accelerate to pass before the curve or hill
choices.D: Pass only if the vehicle ahead is moving below the speed limit

en.explanation: Any time your view is blocked by a curve or a hill, you should assume there is an oncoming vehicle just out of sight. Treat a curve or a hill as an oncoming vehicle and do not start to pass.

en.question: When passing a bicycle on a road with only one lane traveling in the same direction, what is the minimum distance you must keep between your vehicle and the bicycle?

choices.A: 1 foot
choices.B: 2 feet
choices.C: 3 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: If there is only one lane for traffic traveling in the same direction, pass to the left keeping at least three (3) feet between your vehicle and the bicycle or electric low-speed scooter.

en.question: What happens if you are still in the left lane when you reach a 'no passing zone'?

choices.A: You have the right of way to finish passing
choices.B: You are violating the law
choices.C: You must speed up to complete the pass legally
choices.D: You must force the vehicle on the right onto the shoulder

en.explanation: Kentucky law requires that a pass be completed before reaching the beginning of a 'no passing zone'. If you are still in the left lane when you reach it, you are violating the law.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must maintain when passing a bicycle or electric low-speed scooter?

choices.A: Two (2) feet
choices.B: Three (3) feet
choices.C: Four (4) feet
choices.D: Five (5) feet

en.explanation: The manual states to use reasonable caution in passing if space is not available to have a minimum distance of three (3) feet between your vehicle and the bicycle or electric low-speed scooter.

en.question: When passing a bicycle or electric low-speed scooter, you may drive to the left of the center line in a no-passing zone ONLY if:

choices.A: You sound your horn before crossing the line.
choices.B: You are traveling at less than 25 mph.
choices.C: The roadway to the left is clear for a sufficient distance to permit passing safely.
choices.D: The bicycle is traveling under 10 mph.

en.explanation: You may drive to the left of the center line in a no-passing zone to pass a bicycle or scooter only if the roadway to the left is clear for a sufficient distance to permit passing safely and avoid interference with oncoming traffic.

en.question: Ideally, how far ahead should you try to look down your planned path of travel?

choices.A: 5 to 10 seconds
choices.B: 10 to 15 seconds
choices.C: 20 to 30 seconds
choices.D: 45 to 60 seconds

en.explanation: According to the manual, ideally, you should try to look at what is occurring 20 to 30 seconds in front of your car to give yourself time to adjust and plan driving movements.

en.question: What is the unposted speed limit on interstate highways and parkways in Kentucky?

choices.A: 55 MPH
choices.B: 60 MPH
choices.C: 65 MPH
choices.D: 70 MPH

en.explanation: When the speed limit is not posted, sixty-five miles per hour (65 MPH) is the speed limit on interstate highways and parkways in Kentucky.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a business or residential district?

choices.A: 25 MPH
choices.B: 35 MPH
choices.C: 45 MPH
choices.D: 55 MPH

en.explanation: Thirty-five miles per hour (35 MPH) is the speed limit in a business/residential district when not posted.

en.question: What is the speed limit in an off-street parking facility offered for public use?

choices.A: 10 MPH
choices.B: 15 MPH
choices.C: 20 MPH
choices.D: 25 MPH

en.explanation: The speed limit in an off-street parking facility offered for public use, whether publicly or privately owned, shall be fifteen miles per hour (15 MPH).

en.question: If heavy rain, snow, or thick fog limits your visibility to 100 feet or less, you cannot safely drive faster than:

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 35 mph
choices.D: 45 mph

en.explanation: In a heavy rain, snowstorm, or a thick fog, you may not be able to see more than 100 feet ahead. When you cannot see any farther than that, you cannot safely drive faster than 25 miles per hour.

en.question: When approaching a curve, when is the best time to reduce your speed?

choices.A: Before entering the curve
choices.B: While at the sharpest point of the curve
choices.C: After entering the curve
choices.D: Just as you exit the curve

en.explanation: Always reduce speed before entering the curve to a safe speed. Hard braking after entry to a curve could cause the vehicle tires to lose traction.

en.question: If your vehicle begins to skid on a slippery road and is equipped with anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should:

choices.A: Pump the brakes gently.
choices.B: Apply steady pressure to the brakes.
choices.C: Slam on the brakes repeatedly.
choices.D: Pull the emergency brake immediately.

en.explanation: Pump your brakes gently, unless your vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes, in which case you should apply steady pressure to the brakes.

en.question: Hydroplaning occurs when:

choices.A: Your brakes lock up on an icy road.
choices.B: The steering tires start to ride up on pooled water.
choices.C: You drive through a flooded roadway and stall the engine.
choices.D: Your vehicle loses power steering in heavy rain.

en.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when the steering tires start to ride up on any pooled water, similar to the action of water skis, and are not contacting the actual roadway surface.

en.question: What is the average perception time for an alert driver to recognize they must stop?

choices.A: ¼ to ½ second
choices.B: ½ to ¾ second
choices.C: ¾ to 1 second
choices.D: 1 to 2 seconds

en.explanation: Perception time is the time and distance it takes you to recognize you must stop. The average perception time for an alert driver is ¾ second to 1 second.

en.question: At 50 mph on dry pavement with good brakes, approximately how many feet does it take for your brakes to slow and stop your vehicle (braking distance)?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 158 feet
choices.D: 250 feet

en.explanation: Braking distance is the time and distance it takes for your brakes to slow and stop your vehicle. At 50 mph on dry pavement with good brakes, it can take about 158 feet.

en.question: What is the recommended minimum following distance between your car and the vehicle in front of you?

choices.A: 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds
choices.D: 6 seconds

en.explanation: You should always try to keep a minimum following distance of 4 seconds between your car and the vehicle in front.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you INCREASE your following distance beyond the 4-second minimum?

choices.A: When driving on dry pavement during the day.
choices.B: When following a motorcycle.
choices.C: When driving in a residential district.
choices.D: When approaching a green traffic light.

en.explanation: You should increase your following distance when following motorcycles, because motorcyclists can turn and change lanes much quicker than other vehicles.

en.question: When you are being passed by another vehicle, Kentucky law requires you to:

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from passing.
choices.B: Move to the left lane.
choices.C: Give way to the right in favor of the overtaking vehicle.
choices.D: Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: When being passed, Kentucky law requires the operator of a vehicle about to be overtaken and passed shall give way to the right in favor of the overtaking vehicle.

en.question: Why should you allow extra following distance when driving behind a motorcycle?

choices.A: Motorcycles are heavier than passenger cars.
choices.B: Motorcyclists can turn and change lanes much quicker than other vehicles.
choices.C: Motorcycles require a longer stopping distance than cars.
choices.D: Motorcycles are required by law to stop at all railroad crossings.

en.explanation: Motorcyclists can turn and change lanes much quicker than other vehicles. Allow extra space to react to motorcycles.

en.question: What should you do if you find yourself driving slightly to the rear of another vehicle in their blind spot?

choices.A: Honk your horn continuously to alert them of your presence.
choices.B: Maintain your current speed and lane position.
choices.C: Either speed up or drop back so you do not remain in the blind spot.
choices.D: Turn on your high beam headlights.

en.explanation: You may be in their blind spot, and it reduces the space you may need to avoid a crash. Either speed up or drop back, but do not remain in another driver's blind spot.

en.question: When a tractor-trailer is passing you, how should you adjust your vehicle's position?

choices.A: Move to the inside portion of your lane closer to the truck.
choices.B: Move to the outside portion of your lane to leave a little more space.
choices.C: Straddle the center line to give the truck room.
choices.D: Pull completely off the roadway onto the shoulder and stop.

en.explanation: When a passing vehicle is a tractor trailer, leave a little more space between you and that vehicle by moving to the outside portion of your lane.

en.question: What is the proper procedure when approaching parked vehicles on the shoulder of an interstate highway?

choices.A: Honk your horn and maintain your current lane.
choices.B: Speed up to pass the parked vehicles as quickly as possible.
choices.C: Move to the left lane safely before passing them and then back to the right lane.
choices.D: Stop behind the parked vehicle to see if the driver needs assistance.

en.explanation: When approaching these vehicles, move to the left lane safely before passing them and then back to the right lane after passing.

en.question: What must you do if you pass your intended exit on an interstate or freeway?

choices.A: Carefully back up on the shoulder of the road.
choices.B: Make a U-turn through the grassy median.
choices.C: Stop in your lane and wait for traffic to clear before backing up.
choices.D: Proceed to the next exit and work your way back to where you want to go.

en.explanation: If you have passed your exit on an interstate or freeway, never back up or try to turn around. Proceed to the next exit and work your way back.

en.question: During what time period must your vehicle's headlights be illuminated?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise.
choices.B: From one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise.
choices.C: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.
choices.D: Only when it is completely dark outside.

en.explanation: Headlights must be illuminated during the period from one-half (1/2) hour after sunset to one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise.

en.question: According to the manual, what type of turn signals must your vehicle have?

choices.A: Mechanical signals only.
choices.B: Hand signals only.
choices.C: Both mechanical and hand signals.
choices.D: Automatic sensor signals.

en.explanation: Your vehicle must have mechanical signals. Hand signals cannot be used.

en.question: Should you use your turn signal if you do not see any other vehicles around?

choices.A: No, it is unnecessary and wastes battery power.
choices.B: Yes, signal every time you change direction because the vehicle you do not see is the most dangerous.
choices.C: Only if you are driving at night or in bad weather.
choices.D: Only if you are driving on a multi-lane highway.

en.explanation: Signal every time you change direction, even when you do not see anyone else around. The vehicle you do not see is the most dangerous.

en.question: What are the three primary options a driver has to avoid a crash or reduce its impact?

choices.A: Honking, flashing lights, or swerving.
choices.B: Braking, steering, or accelerating.
choices.C: Downshifting, braking, or bracing for impact.
choices.D: Closing eyes, braking, or turning off the engine.

en.explanation: You have three options to avoid the crash or to reduce its impact. These options are braking, steering, or accelerating.

en.question: What is the general guideline for braking in an emergency if your vehicle is equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly to avoid skidding.
choices.B: Press lightly on the brake pedal and gradually increase pressure.
choices.C: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep applying pressure.
choices.D: Apply the parking brake while simultaneously pressing the foot brake.

en.explanation: The general guidelines for using ABS are: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep applying pressure. ABS will work only if you keep the pressure on the brake pedal.

en.question: When quickly steering around a problem in the roadway, what should you do after you have cleared the obstacle?

choices.A: Accelerate rapidly to regain any lost speed.
choices.B: Steer in the opposite direction to straighten out your vehicle.
choices.C: Slam on the brakes to come to a complete stop.
choices.D: Take your hands off the wheel to let the car self-correct.

en.explanation: When you have cleared the problem, steer in the opposite direction to straighten out your vehicle, gain control, and start slowing.

en.question: If your vehicle begins to skid sideways, how should you steer to regain control?

choices.A: Turn the wheel in the opposite direction of the skid.
choices.B: Keep the steering wheel perfectly straight.
choices.C: Turn the wheel in the direction the back of the vehicle is skidding.
choices.D: Turn the wheel sharply left and right until traction returns.

en.explanation: If you begin to skid sideways, you need to turn the wheel in the direction the back of the vehicle is skidding. This will allow the front of the vehicle to line up with the back.

en.question: How should you slow your vehicle if you are skidding in a straight line and do NOT have anti-lock brakes?

choices.A: Brake as hard as possible and hold the pedal down.
choices.B: Pump the brakes gently.
choices.C: Apply the emergency parking brake immediately.
choices.D: Shift the vehicle into reverse.

en.explanation: If you do not have anti-lock, do not brake hard. This will only lock your wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, slow the vehicle by pumping the brakes gently.

en.question: How can you help keep a driver behind you at a safe following distance?

choices.A: By frequently tapping your brakes to warn them.
choices.B: By speeding up and slowing down unpredictably.
choices.C: By keeping a steady speed, signaling in advance, and keeping more space to the front.
choices.D: By turning on your hazard lights while driving.

en.explanation: You can help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance by keeping a steady speed, signaling in advance, and keeping more space to the front of your vehicle before reducing speed or turning.

en.question: What is the most important vehicle control to use during a skid?

choices.A: The accelerator pedal
choices.B: The brake pedal
choices.C: The steering wheel
choices.D: The parking brake

en.explanation: According to the manual, continue to correct your steering until you recover completely from the skid. The most important vehicle control to use during a skid is the steering wheel.

en.question: If your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes and you begin to skid, what should you do?

choices.A: Brake hard to stop the vehicle immediately
choices.B: Slow the vehicle by pumping the brakes gently
choices.C: Shift into neutral and coast until you stop
choices.D: Pull the parking brake quickly

en.explanation: If you do not have anti-lock brakes, do not brake hard, as this will lock your wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, slow the vehicle by pumping the brakes gently.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle's wheels leave the paved road and drop onto an uneven surface?

choices.A: Panic steer immediately back onto the pavement
choices.B: Brake hard and stop on the shoulder
choices.C: Slow down gradually and turn quickly back onto the pavement when safe
choices.D: Accelerate to regain traction before turning back

en.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the paved road, avoid panic steering. Slow down gradually, when safe to do so, and turn quickly back onto the pavement.

en.question: Under Kentucky law, what must you do if you are involved in a non-injury accident?

choices.A: Leave the vehicles exactly where they are until a tow truck arrives
choices.B: Move the damaged vehicles to the shoulder of the roadway
choices.C: Drive home and report the accident the next day
choices.D: Wait for an officer before moving the vehicles out of the traffic lane

en.explanation: In accordance with Kentucky law (KRS 189.580), when involved in a non-injury accident, you must move the damaged vehicles to the shoulder of the roadway.

en.question: If you are involved in a collision resulting in property damage exceeding $500 and no law enforcement officer investigates, how long do you have to file a written report with the Kentucky State Police?

choices.A: 24 hours
choices.B: 5 days
choices.C: 10 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: Any person involved in an automobile collision resulting in property damage exceeding $500 not investigated by an officer shall file a written report with the Kentucky State Police within ten (10) days.

en.question: What should you do if you collide with a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner?

choices.A: Leave the scene immediately if there is no visible damage
choices.B: Wait by the vehicle until the owner returns
choices.C: Call a tow truck to remove the parked vehicle
choices.D: Leave a note with your name, address, driver license number, license plate number, and the date and time

en.explanation: If the collision involves a parked vehicle and you cannot locate the owner, leave a note where it can be seen including your name, address, driver license number, license plate number, along with the date and time of the collision.

en.question: When should you attempt to remove an injured individual from a collision scene?

choices.A: Immediately upon arriving at the scene
choices.B: Only in life-threatening emergencies
choices.C: Whenever they ask to be moved
choices.D: If they are blocking traffic

en.explanation: Only in life-threatening emergencies should you attempt to remove an individual from a collision. If possible, wait for an Emergency Medical Technician or ambulance.

en.question: If your brakes stop working while driving, what is the first step you should take?

choices.A: Turn off the engine immediately
choices.B: Shift into reverse
choices.C: Use the parking brake by pulling or pushing it slowly
choices.D: Pump the accelerator pedal

en.explanation: If your brakes stop working while driving, use the parking brake. Pull on the handle or push the foot pedal slowly so you will not lock the rear wheels and cause a skid.

en.question: How should you respond if a tire blows out or suddenly goes flat while driving?

choices.A: Brake hard and stop in the lane
choices.B: Grip the steering wheel firmly, keep straight, and slow down gradually without braking hard
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the opposite direction of the blowout
choices.D: Accelerate to maintain control of the vehicle

en.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, slow down gradually by taking your foot off the accelerator, and do not brake hard.

en.question: If your engine shuts off while you are driving, you should be aware that:

choices.A: The steering wheel will lock completely and cannot be turned
choices.B: The steering wheel may be difficult to turn, but you can still turn it
choices.C: The brakes will automatically apply themselves
choices.D: The vehicle will immediately come to a complete stop

en.explanation: If the engine shuts off while driving, keep a strong grip on the steering wheel. Be aware that the steering wheel may be difficult to turn, but you can turn it.

en.question: What is the correct action to take if your vehicle is accelerating out of control due to a stuck accelerator?

choices.A: Turn off the engine, shift to neutral, and search for an escape path
choices.B: Shift into park while moving
choices.C: Pull the parking brake as hard as possible
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply back and forth

en.explanation: If your vehicle is accelerating out of control, turn off the engine, shift to neutral, search for an escape path, steer smoothly, brake gently, and pull off the roadway.

en.question: Where should you place emergency flares if your vehicle breaks down on the highway?

choices.A: 10 to 20 feet behind the vehicle
choices.B: 50 to 100 feet behind the vehicle
choices.C: 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle
choices.D: 500 to 600 feet behind the vehicle

en.explanation: Try to warn other roadway users by placing emergency flares about 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle, giving other drivers some time to change lanes if necessary.

en.question: When making a right or left turn on a red light, you must:

choices.A: Honk your horn to warn pedestrians to clear the crosswalk
choices.B: Be prepared to yield the right of way to pedestrians
choices.C: Proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are coming
choices.D: Wait for a green light if any pedestrians are visible on the sidewalk

en.explanation: When making a right or left turn on red, you must be prepared to yield the right of way to pedestrians.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to yield the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or accompanied by an assistance dog?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense
choices.B: A fine up to $100
choices.C: A fine up to $250
choices.D: Immediate license suspension

en.explanation: Kentucky law requires operators to yield to a blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or accompanied by an assistance dog. Failure to yield is a violation that could result in a fine up to $250.

en.question: Who has the right-of-way if a pedestrian is crossing a roadway at a point other than within a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection?

choices.A: The pedestrian always has the right-of-way
choices.B: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles
choices.C: Vehicles must stop and wait for the pedestrian regardless of location
choices.D: The right-of-way goes to whoever arrived first

en.explanation: Every pedestrian crossing a roadway at a point other than within a marked crosswalk or within an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for failing to yield the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian in Kentucky?
en.explanation: Failure to yield the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian is a violation that could result in a fine up to two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

en.question: When stopping for a blind pedestrian at a crosswalk, how close should you stop your vehicle to the crosswalk if there is no advanced stop bar?

choices.A: At least 10 feet away
choices.B: No more than 5 feet from the crosswalk
choices.C: More than 15 feet away
choices.D: Inside the crosswalk

en.explanation: Do not stop your vehicle more than five (5) feet from the crosswalk, unless there is an advanced stop bar. A blind pedestrian uses the sound of your vehicle as a guide.

en.question: Why must drivers of electric and hybrid vehicles be extra alert around blind pedestrians?

choices.A: These vehicles have larger blind spots.
choices.B: Blind pedestrians may be unaware of their presence due to the silent nature of these vehicles.
choices.C: These vehicles accelerate faster than standard vehicles.
choices.D: The headlights on these vehicles are less visible during the day.

en.explanation: Drivers of electric and hybrid vehicles must be extra alert to blind pedestrians, as they may be unaware of your presence due to the silent nature of these vehicles.

en.question: What is the recommended minimum amount of space a driver should allow when passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: One foot
choices.B: Two feet
choices.C: Three feet
choices.D: Five feet

en.explanation: At least three feet of space is recommended when passing bicyclists and the passing vehicles should move back into the right lane only when well clear of the bicyclist.

en.question: How far in advance must a bicyclist give a signal before making a turn?

choices.A: 25 feet
choices.B: 50 feet
choices.C: 100 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: The signal shall be given intermittently for the last fifty (50) feet traveled by the vehicle (bicycle) before the turn.

en.question: Which of the following is a rule that bicyclists must follow?

choices.A: Ride on the sidewalk whenever possible.
choices.B: Ride against the flow of traffic.
choices.C: Never ride on interstates and parkways.
choices.D: Ride at least three abreast to increase visibility.

en.explanation: Rules for Bicyclists state that they must "Never ride on interstates and parkways." They are also prohibited from riding on sidewalks and must ride with traffic.

en.question: When riding a bicycle at night, what lighting equipment is required?

choices.A: A white light on both the front and rear.
choices.B: A red light on the front and a white reflector on the rear.
choices.C: A white light visible from the front and a red reflector or light visible from the rear.
choices.D: Only reflective clothing is required.

en.explanation: When riding at night, operate the bicycle with a white light visible from the front and a red reflector or light visible from the rear.

en.question: What is the maximum designed speed of an electric low-speed scooter on a paved level surface?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour
choices.B: 20 miles per hour
choices.C: 25 miles per hour
choices.D: 30 miles per hour

en.explanation: An electric low-speed scooter is designed to operate at a maximum speed of twenty (20) miles per hour on a paved level surface.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to operate an electric low-speed scooter on a highway, bicycle lane, or bicycle path?

choices.A: 14 years of age
choices.B: 15 years of age
choices.C: 16 years of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: A person sixteen (16) years of age or older, may operate an electric low-speed scooter on a highway, bicycle lane, or bicycle path.

en.question: During what times must an electric low-speed scooter's lights be illuminated?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise.
choices.B: From one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise.
choices.C: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.
choices.D: At all times when operating on a highway.

en.explanation: These lights shall be illuminated from one-half (1/2) hour after sunset to one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise or at other times when there is low visibility.

en.question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, you should:

choices.A: Share the lane with the motorcycle to improve traffic flow.
choices.B: Allow the motorcyclist a full lane width.
choices.C: Honk your horn when passing them.
choices.D: Follow them at a 2-second distance.

en.explanation: Allow a motorcyclist a full lane width. Do not share the lane. The motorcycle needs space for the motorcyclist to react to other traffic.

en.question: Why should you not assume a motorcycle is turning just because its turn signal is flashing?

choices.A: Motorcycle turn signals are often used as hazard lights.
choices.B: Motorcyclists use turn signals to indicate they are slowing down.
choices.C: Motorcycle turn signals may not self-cancel and the rider may have forgotten to turn them off.
choices.D: The turn signal indicates the motorcycle is changing gears.

en.explanation: Do not assume a motorcycle is turning when you see its turn signal flashing. Motorcycle turn signals may not self-cancel, and the motorcyclist may have forgotten to turn them off.

en.question: What is the minimum recommended following distance when driving behind a motorcyclist?

choices.A: 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds
choices.D: 6 seconds

en.explanation: When following a motorcyclist, allow for a minimum 4-second following distance or more in wet conditions, or you may not have enough time or space to avoid a crash.

en.question: Why should a driver avoid slowing down or stopping quickly in front of a bicyclist?

choices.A: Bicycles are not equipped with brakes.
choices.B: A motor vehicle's brakes are more powerful than a bicycle's and could cause a crash.
choices.C: The bicyclist will be forced to ride onto the sidewalk.
choices.D: It is illegal to brake in front of a bicycle.

en.explanation: Avoid slowing down or stopping quickly. A motor vehicle’s brakes are more powerful than a bicycle’s and you could cause a crash.

en.question: What should you do if a blind pedestrian takes a step back and pulls in their cane at a crosswalk?

choices.A: Honk your horn to let them know it is safe to cross.
choices.B: Give them verbal directions to cross the street.
choices.C: Wait until they step forward again.
choices.D: Treat it as a definite sign that you should go.

en.explanation: If the person takes a step back and pulls in the cane that is a definite sign you should go.

en.question: Under ideal conditions, how much distance does a loaded truck traveling at 55 mph require to come to a complete stop?

choices.A: At least 150 feet
choices.B: At least 200 feet
choices.C: At least 250 feet
choices.D: At least 335 feet

en.explanation: According to the manual, a loaded truck with good tires and properly adjusted brakes traveling at 55 mph requires at least 335 feet before coming to a complete stop.

en.question: How can you determine if you are driving in a large truck's side blind spot?

choices.A: If you are within 50 feet of the truck's rear bumper
choices.B: If you cannot see the driver's face in the side view mirror
choices.C: If you are driving in the left lane next to the truck
choices.D: If you can see the truck's headlights in your rearview mirror

en.explanation: The manual explains that if you cannot see the driver's face in the side view mirror, he or she cannot see you, meaning you are in their blind spot.

en.question: How far can the blind spot directly behind a large commercial vehicle extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 200 feet
choices.D: Up to 300 feet

en.explanation: Unlike cars, large vehicles have huge blind spots directly behind them that extend up to 200 feet.

en.question: When passing a large vehicle, when is it safe to pull back in front of it?

choices.A: As soon as you clear the front bumper of the truck
choices.B: When you can see the whole front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror
choices.C: When the truck driver flashes their headlights
choices.D: After you have maintained your speed for 3 seconds

en.explanation: The manual advises that when passing a large vehicle, you should look for the whole front of the vehicle in your rear-view mirror before pulling in front and maintaining speed.

en.question: Why do large trucks sometimes swing wide to the left when making a right turn?

choices.A: To allow cars to pass them on the right
choices.B: To safely clear the corner of a curb or other obstruction
choices.C: To build up speed before entering the new road
choices.D: To check their right-side blind spots

en.explanation: When a truck or bus needs to make a right turn, the driver will sometimes swing the vehicle wide to the left to safely turn right and clear the corner of a curb or other obstruction.

en.question: Why are stop lines placed at many intersections?

choices.A: To indicate where pedestrians are allowed to cross
choices.B: To mark the boundary of a school zone
choices.C: To set vehicles farther back to give larger vehicles more turning space
choices.D: To show where the speed limit changes

en.explanation: Many intersections are marked with stop lines to set you farther back at an intersection to give larger vehicles more turning space.

en.question: When stopped behind a truck on an upgrade, where should you position your vehicle?

choices.A: As close to the truck's rear bumper as possible
choices.B: To the right of your lane
choices.C: To the left of your lane where the driver can see you
choices.D: In the center of the lane with your hazard lights on

en.explanation: When stopped behind a truck on an upgrade, stay to the left of your lane where the driver can see you and allow extra space in case the truck drifts backwards.

en.question: What must vehicles carrying hazardous materials do at all railroad crossings?

choices.A: Slow down to 15 mph
choices.B: Stop only if a train is approaching
choices.C: Sound their horn before crossing
choices.D: Stop at all railroad crossings

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings.

en.question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see a vehicle displaying flashing red or blue lights?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the road quickly
choices.B: Stop immediately in your current lane
choices.C: Drive to the right side of the road or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop
choices.D: Move to the left lane and slow down

en.explanation: When you become aware of an approaching emergency vehicle with flashing red/blue lights or a siren, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop.

en.question: It is unlawful to follow any emergency vehicle closer than:

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: According to Kentucky law, it is unlawful to follow any emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet.

en.question: What should you do with your hands when pulled over by law enforcement?

choices.A: Keep them in your lap
choices.B: Keep them on the steering wheel
choices.C: Use them to immediately search for your license
choices.D: Hold them out the window

en.explanation: During a traffic stop, you should keep your hands on the steering wheel and limit movements so the officer does not think you are hiding or searching for something.

en.question: If you are pulled over by law enforcement at night, what should you do to help the officer?

choices.A: Turn off your headlights
choices.B: Turn on your high beams
choices.C: Turn on your interior lights
choices.D: Step out of the vehicle immediately

en.explanation: If pulled over at night, you should turn on your interior lights to help the officer see that everything is in order inside the vehicle.

en.question: When a law enforcement officer asks for your documents during a traffic stop, what is the proper procedure?

choices.A: Quickly reach into your glove box to retrieve them
choices.B: Tell the officer where they are located before reaching for them slowly
choices.C: Ask the officer to retrieve them for you
choices.D: Hand the officer your entire wallet

en.explanation: When requested to provide documents, you should first tell the officer where they are located, then reach for them slowly with one hand on the wheel.

en.question: What do move-over laws require drivers to do when approaching a roadside incident?

choices.A: Stop and offer assistance to emergency personnel
choices.B: Maintain speed but honk the horn to warn workers
choices.C: Slow down and change lanes
choices.D: Pull over to the right shoulder and stop

en.explanation: Move-over laws require drivers to slow and change lanes when approaching a roadside incident to protect law enforcement, EMS, and fire department personnel.

en.question: Under Kentucky's move-over laws, what should a driver do when approaching an emergency vehicle stopped on the shoulder of a four-lane highway?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for the vehicle to leave.
choices.B: Approach slowly and move into the left lane if it is safe to do so.
choices.C: Maintain speed and stay in the right lane.
choices.D: Honk to alert the emergency workers of your presence.

en.explanation: Kentucky law requires drivers to approach slowly and move into the left lane on four-lane highways if it is safe to do so when approaching stopped police or emergency vehicles.

en.question: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicates that the vehicle is traveling at what speed?

choices.A: Less than 15 mph
choices.B: Less than 25 mph
choices.C: Less than 35 mph
choices.D: Less than 45 mph

en.explanation: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of vehicles drawn by animal, farm equipment, or construction equipment means the vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.

en.question: Why should you avoid using your horn or revving your engine when passing a horseback rider or animal-drawn vehicle?

choices.A: It is illegal to use a horn in rural areas.
choices.B: It may scare the horse and cause a crash.
choices.C: It will cause the animal-drawn vehicle to speed up.
choices.D: The rider cannot hear approaching vehicles anyway.

en.explanation: When sharing the road with animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders, you should pass with caution and not use your horn or rev the engine because this may scare the horse and cause a crash.

en.question: When crossing a two-lane public highway on an All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV), what is the maximum distance you are allowed to travel on the highway?

choices.A: One-tenth (1/10) of a mile
choices.B: Two-tenths (2/10) of a mile
choices.C: Five-tenths (5/10) of a mile
choices.D: One mile

en.explanation: While crossing a two-lane public highway, the operator shall cross at as close to a 90-degree angle as practical and shall not travel on the highway for more than two-tenths (2/10) of a mile.

en.question: What is required for a person under sixteen (16) years of age to operate an All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV)?

choices.A: Direct parental supervision and approved protective headgear
choices.B: A valid instruction permit and daylight hours only
choices.C: A special ATV license and reflective clothing
choices.D: They are strictly prohibited from operating an ATV under any circumstances

en.explanation: If under sixteen (16) years of age, a person shall not operate an ATV except under direct parental supervision, and not without approved protective headgear at all times the vehicle is in motion.

en.question: When driving at night, when should you use your low beam headlights instead of high beams?

choices.A: When driving on unfamiliar roadways
choices.B: When driving in fog, rain, or snow
choices.C: When there are no oncoming vehicles
choices.D: When driving on rural highways

en.explanation: You should use your low beams when following another vehicle, and in fog, rain, or snow. Light from your high beams may cause glare in these conditions.

en.question: At what distance must you dim your headlights when approaching an oncoming vehicle at night?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must dim your lights whenever you come within 500 feet of oncoming vehicles, and within 300 feet of any vehicle you are following.

en.question: How much should you increase your following distance when driving on unfamiliar roadways at night?

choices.A: Add at least one additional second
choices.B: Add at least two additional seconds
choices.C: Add at least three additional seconds
choices.D: Add at least four additional seconds

en.explanation: You should increase your following distance by adding at least one additional second for night driving conditions and at least two additional seconds for driving on unfamiliar roadways at night.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles has the right-of-way over a funeral procession at an intersection?

choices.A: A public transit bus
choices.B: A commercial delivery truck
choices.C: A train or locomotive
choices.D: A vehicle turning right on red

en.explanation: A funeral procession has the right-of-way at an intersection. The only exceptions are when the right-of-way is required by an emergency vehicle, directed otherwise by a police/safety officer, or when the vehicle is a train or locomotive.

en.question: What is the potential penalty for violating the laws regarding funeral processions in Kentucky?

choices.A: A $50 fine
choices.B: A $100 fine or 30 days in jail
choices.C: A $250 fine or 90 days in jail
choices.D: A $500 fine and license suspension

en.explanation: If you violate the funeral procession law, you may receive a $250 fine or 90 days in jail.

en.question: Under what conditions are fines doubled in a Kentucky highway work zone?

choices.A: Only when workers are present, regardless of signage
choices.B: When signs are displayed informing drivers of double fines and at least one bona fide worker is present
choices.C: At all times within the designated work zone
choices.D: Only during nighttime construction hours

en.explanation: Kentucky law allows for fines to be doubled in a highway work zone when signs are displayed informing drivers that fines are double in it, and additionally, at least one bona fide worker must be present.

en.question: What colors are used for work zone signs?

choices.A: Yellow background with black letters
choices.B: Orange background with black letters
choices.C: White background with red letters
choices.D: Green background with white letters

en.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background and black letters or symbols.

en.question: What should you do to keep from being momentarily blinded if an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on?

choices.A: Flash your high beams repeatedly
choices.B: Look directly at the oncoming headlights
choices.C: Look toward the right side of the road
choices.D: Close your eyes briefly until the vehicle passes

en.explanation: If a vehicle comes toward you with their high beams on, look toward the right side of the road to keep from being distracted or momentarily blinded by their headlights.

en.question: What lighting equipment is required when operating an All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) on a public highway?

choices.A: At least two headlights and one taillight
choices.B: At least one headlight and two taillights illuminated at all times
choices.C: Only a flashing yellow strobe light
choices.D: Headlights are only required if driving at night

en.explanation: A person who operates an ATV on a public highway must have at least one headlight and two taillights illuminated at all times.

en.question: What part of the slow-moving vehicle symbol is visible during night driving?

choices.A: The fluorescent orange center
choices.B: The reflective red border
choices.C: The flashing yellow beacon
choices.D: The solid black triangle

en.explanation: During the day, you will see the fluorescent orange triangle in the center of the symbol. During night driving, you will see the reflective red border of the symbol.

en.question: What should you do when driving on gravel or dirt roads to handle reduced traction?

choices.A: Increase your speed to maintain momentum
choices.B: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance
choices.C: Pump your brakes continuously
choices.D: Drive closer to the vehicle ahead to follow their tracks

en.explanation: According to the manual, traction can be reduced on gravel or dirt roads. You should reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and realize you may skid when trying to stop.

en.question: Who generally has the right of way when approaching a narrow or single-lane bridge?

choices.A: The larger vehicle
choices.B: The vehicle traveling at a higher speed
choices.C: The first driver to arrive at the bridge
choices.D: The vehicle traveling uphill

en.explanation: When encountering narrow and single-lane bridges, you should take turns crossing; generally, the first driver to the bridge has the right of way.

en.question: How should you adjust your driving when crossing open bridge gratings or steel bridges?

choices.A: Increase your speed to cross quickly
choices.B: Reduce your speed and maintain a firm grip on the steering wheel
choices.C: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel to allow the tires to follow the grating
choices.D: Apply your brakes firmly while crossing

en.explanation: Open bridge gratings or steel bridges can reduce your traction. You should reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and maintain a firm grip on the steering wheel.

en.question: What type of license is required to operate an autocycle?

choices.A: A commercial driver's license (CDL)
choices.B: A valid operator's license
choices.C: A motorcycle license or endorsement
choices.D: A special autocycle permit

en.explanation: An operator of an autocycle is not required to obtain a motorcycle license or endorsement, and may operate the vehicle if the operator is in possession of a valid operator's license.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding headgear requirements for autocycle operators?

choices.A: They must wear a DOT-approved helmet at all times
choices.B: They are exempt from any headgear requirements
choices.C: They must wear a helmet only if driving over 40 mph
choices.D: They must wear a helmet unless the autocycle has a fixed top

en.explanation: The manual states that an operator of an autocycle is exempt from any headgear requirements.

en.question: How should cargo weight be distributed when loading a trailer to reduce the possibility of sway?

choices.A: 50 percent in the front and 50 percent in the back
choices.B: 40 percent in the front and 60 percent in the back
choices.C: 60 percent in the front and 40 percent in the back
choices.D: 100 percent evenly distributed across the middle

en.explanation: Trailers must be loaded heavier in the front to reduce sway. Sixty percent of the cargo weight of a trailer should go in the front (nearest the towing vehicle) and 40 percent in the back.

en.question: If your trailer begins to sway or whip while driving, what is the correct action to take?

choices.A: Apply the brakes firmly and immediately
choices.B: Increase your speed to pull the trailer straight
choices.C: Steer straight and reduce speed gradually without applying the brakes
choices.D: Swerve slightly in the opposite direction of the sway

en.explanation: If the trailer begins to sway or whip, steer straight and reduce speed gradually, do not apply the brakes. Never increase speed.

en.question: What is the maximum recommended speed for most vehicle-trailer combinations?

choices.A: 45 mph
choices.B: 55 mph
choices.C: 65 mph
choices.D: 70 mph

en.explanation: The manual states that the maximum recommended speed for most vehicle-trailer combinations is 55 mph.

en.question: When backing up a trailer, where should you place your hand on the steering wheel to make it easier to direct the trailer?

choices.A: At the top of the steering wheel
choices.B: At the bottom of the steering wheel
choices.C: On the left side of the steering wheel
choices.D: On the right side of the steering wheel

en.explanation: When backing up a trailer, go slowly and keep your hand at the bottom of the steering wheel. To move the trailer left, move your hand to the left; to move right, move your hand to the right.

en.question: What should you do if your trailer starts to jackknife while you are backing up?

choices.A: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the left
choices.B: Accelerate in reverse to push through the jackknife
choices.C: Stop, pull ahead to straighten out, and start again
choices.D: Apply the emergency brake immediately

en.explanation: If the trailer starts to jackknife while backing up, you should STOP and pull ahead to straighten out, then start again.

en.question: When towing a trailer and approaching a downgrade (hill), when should you slow down?

choices.A: Before starting down the hill
choices.B: Halfway down the hill
choices.C: At the bottom of the hill
choices.D: You should speed up to maintain momentum

en.explanation: When going down a grade while towing a trailer, you must slow down BEFORE starting down the hill.

en.question: If a pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the street illegally (jaywalking), what must you do?

choices.A: Honk your horn and maintain your speed
choices.B: Swerve into the oncoming lane to avoid them
choices.C: Stop for them
choices.D: You do not have to stop for them

en.explanation: Even if a pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the street illegally (jaywalking), you must stop for them.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding motorcycle operators on the roadway?

choices.A: They must share a traffic lane with another vehicle
choices.B: They have the right to use a complete traffic lane
choices.C: They are required to drive on the shoulder of the roadway
choices.D: They must yield their lane to larger passenger vehicles

en.explanation: Motorcycle operators have the right to use a complete traffic lane.

en.question: When driving at night, when is it appropriate to use your high beam headlights?

choices.A: When fog, rain, or snow is present
choices.B: When you are following another vehicle closely
choices.C: When there is no oncoming traffic approaching
choices.D: When driving in a well-lit urban area

en.explanation: When driving at night, you should use your high beams when there is no oncoming traffic approaching.

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What does this sign indicate?

choices.A: Left turn only
choices.B: Traffic flows in one direction — to the left
choices.C: Keep left of the median
choices.D: Highway exit to the left

en.explanation: A black and white ONE WAY sign with an arrow indicates that traffic on this street moves in only one direction — the direction the arrow points.

en.question: What does this sign prohibit?

choices.A: Right turns
choices.B: Left turns
choices.C: U-turns
choices.D: Passing other vehicles

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign with a U-turn arrow crossed out means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What does this sign instruct drivers to do?

choices.A: Merge right
choices.B: Turn right only
choices.C: Keep to the right of a divider or obstruction
choices.D: Right lane ends ahead

en.explanation: A white regulatory KEEP RIGHT sign with an arrow means you must keep to the right side of a traffic island, median, or obstruction.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What road condition does this sign warn about?

choices.A: A winding road
choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions
choices.D: A roundabout ahead

en.explanation: A reverse curve sign warns of two curves in opposite directions ahead. Slow down and be prepared for the road to curve first one way, then the other.

en.question: What does this sign warn you to expect?

choices.A: A single sharp curve
choices.B: A slippery road surface
choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead
choices.D: A hill ahead

en.explanation: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves or turns ahead. Reduce your speed and be alert for changing road conditions.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to prepare for?

choices.A: A lane ending
choices.B: Traffic merging from another road
choices.C: A divided highway beginning
choices.D: A road narrowing to one lane

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped merge sign warns that traffic from another road will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed and position.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to expect ahead?

choices.A: A yield sign
choices.B: A traffic signal
choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop
choices.D: A speed bump

en.explanation: This sign warns that there is a stop sign ahead. Begin slowing down and prepare to come to a complete stop at the stop sign.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

es.question: ¿Quién figura como Comisionado de la Policía Estatal de Kentucky en el texto del manual proporcionado?

choices.A: Phillip Burnett, Jr.
choices.B: John Beshear
choices.C: Michael Dossett
choices.D: Richard Sanders

es.explanation: Según el texto introductorio del manual, Phillip Burnett, Jr. es el Comisionado de la Policía Estatal de Kentucky.

choices.B: Sección Dos
choices.C: Sección Tres
choices.D: Sección Cuatro

choices.A: Sección Uno
choices.B: Sección Dos

choices.D: Sección Nueve

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes temas se trata en la Sección Tres: Estar en forma para conducir?

choices.A: Registro de vehículos motorizados
choices.B: Fatiga
choices.C: Bolsas de aire (Air Bags)
choices.D: Marcas en el pavimento

es.question: Si necesita informarse sobre las Leyes de Seguridad para Niños Pasajeros, ¿qué sección del manual debe consultar?

choices.A: Sección Dos
choices.B: Sección Tres

choices.D: Sección Cinco

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido enumera las "Leyes de Seguridad para Niños Pasajeros" bajo la Sección Cuatro: Antes de Conducir.

es.question: ¿Qué significan las siglas ADAS en la Sección Cuatro del manual?

choices.A: Conducción y dirección automáticas
choices.B: Sistemas Avanzados de Asistencia al Conductor (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems)
choices.C: Conducción y seguridad adaptativas
choices.D: Sistemas automatizados de alerta al conductor

es.explanation: La Sección Cuatro de la Tabla de Contenido enumera las "Funciones de seguridad de los Sistemas Avanzados de Asistencia al Conductor (ADAS)".

es.question: ¿Qué sección se titula "Conducción Básica" y cubre el arranque del motor, el movimiento, la detención, la dirección y la marcha atrás?

choices.A: Sección Cuatro
choices.B: Sección Cinco
choices.C: Sección Seis
choices.D: Sección Siete

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido muestra que la Sección Cinco se titula "Conducción Básica" e incluye temas como arrancar el motor, avanzar, detenerse, maniobrar el volante y retroceder.

es.question: ¿En qué sección se puede encontrar información sobre las Marcas en el Pavimento y las Señales de Tráfico?

choices.A: Sección Cinco: Conducción Básica
choices.B: Sección Seis: Reglas de la Carretera
choices.C: Sección Siete: Conducción General
choices.D: Sección Ocho: Consejos para una Conducción Segura

es.explanation: Según la Tabla de Contenido, las "Señales de Tráfico" y las "Marcas en el Pavimento" se encuentran en la Sección Seis: Reglas de la Carretera.

es.question: ¿Bajo qué sección se encuentran las "Reglas para Autobuses Escolares"?

choices.A: Sección Cuatro
choices.B: Sección Seis
choices.C: Sección Siete
choices.D: Sección Nueve

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido ubica las "Reglas para Autobuses Escolares" dentro de la Sección Siete: Conducción General.

es.question: La Sección Siete cubre la "Conducción General". ¿Cuál de los siguientes es un tema incluido en esta sección?

choices.A: Rotondas y círculos de tráfico
choices.B: Búsqueda visual
choices.C: Inspección de su vehículo
choices.D: Donación de órganos

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido enumera "Rotondas y círculos de tráfico" como un tema bajo la Sección Siete: Conducción General.

es.question: Si un conductor desea leer sobre 'Control de velocidad' y 'Distancia de frenado', debe buscar en:

choices.A: Sección cinco
choices.B: Sección seis
choices.C: Sección siete
choices.D: Sección ocho

es.explanation: Según el índice, el 'Control de velocidad' y la 'Distancia de frenado' se tratan en la Sección ocho: Consejos para una conducción segura.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el título de la Sección nueve?

choices.A: Reglas de la carretera
choices.B: Consejos para una conducción segura
choices.C: Situaciones de emergencia y cómo evitar choques
choices.D: Conducción general

es.explanation: El índice titula la Sección nueve como 'Situaciones de emergencia y cómo evitar choques'.

es.question: ¿Qué sección contiene información sobre la 'Donación de órganos'?

choices.A: Sección uno
choices.B: Sección dos
choices.C: Sección tres
choices.D: Sección diez

es.explanation: El índice enumera la 'Donación de órganos' como un tema en la Sección dos: Información general.

es.question: 'Emociones, conducción agresiva y furia al volante' es una subsección de ¿qué sección principal?

choices.A: Sección tres: Estar en condiciones para conducir
choices.B: Sección seis: Reglas de la carretera
choices.C: Sección ocho: Consejos para una conducción segura
choices.D: Sección nueve: Situaciones de emergencia

es.explanation: Según el índice, 'Emociones, conducción agresiva y furia al volante' se encuentra en la Sección tres: Estar en condiciones para conducir.

es.question: ¿Dónde puede encontrar información sobre la 'Programación de exámenes' y los 'Requisitos y preparación para los exámenes'?

choices.A: Sección uno
choices.B: Sección dos
choices.C: Sección cuatro
choices.D: Sección cinco

es.explanation: El índice muestra que los 'Requisitos y preparación para los exámenes' y la 'Programación de exámenes' se encuentran en la Sección uno: La licencia de conducir.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito de edad mínima para solicitar una licencia de operador Clase D en Kentucky?

choices.A: 15 años de edad
choices.B: 16 años de edad
choices.C: 17 años de edad
choices.D: 18 años de edad

es.explanation: Según el manual, los solicitantes de una licencia de operador Clase D deben ser residentes de Kentucky y tener al menos 16 años de edad.

es.question: ¿Qué clase de licencia de conducir de Kentucky está restringida únicamente a ciclomotores (mopeds)?

choices.A: Clase C
choices.B: Clase D
choices.C: Clase E
choices.D: Clase M

es.explanation: El manual establece que la licencia Clase E es solo para ciclomotores.

es.question: No se requiere una Licencia de conducir comercial (CDL) para un agricultor que conduce un vehículo agrícola dentro de ¿qué distancia desde su punto de origen?

choices.A: 50 millas
choices.B: 100 millas
choices.C: 150 millas
choices.D: 200 millas

es.explanation: No se requiere una CDL para un conductor de vehículos utilizados exclusivamente en el transporte agrícola de la granja al mercado, que sean propiedad y estén operados por el agricultor o sus empleados, y que se utilicen dentro de las 150 millas del punto de origen.

es.question: Se requiere una Licencia de conducir comercial Clase C para un solo vehículo de menos de 26,001 libras si tiene carteles de materiales peligrosos o si está diseñado para transportar a más de ¿cuántas personas (incluido el conductor)?

choices.A: 10 personas
choices.B: 12 personas
choices.C: 15 personas
choices.D: 16 personas

es.explanation: Se requiere una CDL Clase C para cualquier vehículo individual con una clasificación de peso bruto combinado de menos de 26,001 libras que tenga carteles de materiales peligrosos o esté diseñado para transportar a más de dieciséis (16) personas, incluido el conductor del vehículo.

es.question: ¿Qué se requiere para un solicitante de licencia Clase D que sea menor de 18 años?

choices.A: Deben completar un curso de conducción defensiva.
choices.B: Un padre o tutor legal debe firmar la solicitud.
choices.C: Deben tener un cosignatario para el seguro del vehículo.
choices.D: Deben aprobar un examen médico físico.

es.explanation: El manual especifica que si el solicitante es menor de 18 años, un padre o tutor legal debe firmar la solicitud.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes deben aprobar todos los solicitantes por primera vez para obtener una Licencia de Operador Clase D?

choices.A: Exámenes de visión, conocimientos y habilidades
choices.B: Solo exámenes de visión y conocimientos
choices.C: Solo exámenes de conocimientos y habilidades
choices.D: Exámenes de visión, médicos y habilidades

es.explanation: Todos los solicitantes por primera vez de una Licencia de Operador Clase D deben aprobar los exámenes de visión, conocimientos y habilidades.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes NO es un requisito para obtener una licencia de ciclomotor (moped) Clase E?

choices.A: Un examen de visión
choices.B: Un examen de conocimientos generales
choices.C: Un examen de habilidades
choices.D: Tener al menos 16 años de edad

es.explanation: Se requiere que los solicitantes aprueben los exámenes de conocimientos generales y de visión para que se les otorgue una licencia de ciclomotor. Sin embargo, no se requiere un examen de habilidades ni un permiso.

es.question: Por definición en Kentucky, un ciclomotor (moped) es una bicicleta motorizada capaz de alcanzar una velocidad máxima de no más de:

choices.A: 20 millas por hora
choices.B: 25 millas por hora
choices.C: 30 millas por hora
choices.D: 35 millas por hora

es.explanation: Un ciclomotor se define como una bicicleta motorizada capaz de alcanzar una velocidad máxima de no más de treinta (30) millas por hora.

es.question: Para ser clasificado como un ciclomotor (moped), el vehículo debe tener una cilindrada que no exceda los:

choices.A: 30 centímetros cúbicos
choices.B: 50 centímetros cúbicos
choices.C: 100 centímetros cúbicos
choices.D: 150 centímetros cúbicos

es.explanation: La definición de un ciclomotor incluye tener una cilindrada que no exceda los cincuenta (50) centímetros cúbicos.

es.question: Según el manual del conductor de Kentucky, ¿cuál de las siguientes personas NO es elegible para una licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Una persona que usa lentes correctivos.
choices.B: Una persona que es incapaz de entender las advertencias de la carretera en el idioma inglés.
choices.C: Un no residente que trabaja en Kentucky.
choices.D: Un joven de 17 años con la firma de un padre.

es.explanation: El manual enumera varias condiciones bajo las cuales una persona no es elegible para una licencia, incluyendo a cualquier persona que sea incapaz de entender las advertencias o direcciones de la carretera en el idioma inglés.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes conductores está exento de necesitar una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL)?

choices.A: Un conductor voluntario de un autobús de iglesia.
choices.B: Un conductor de autobús de escuela pública.
choices.C: Un operador de un vehículo recreativo no utilizado para el comercio.
choices.D: Un mecánico que realiza una prueba de conducción de un camión comercial.

es.explanation: No se requiere una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) para los operadores de vehículos recreativos que no sean para el comercio. Los conductores voluntarios, los conductores de autobuses escolares y los mecánicos que operan vehículos comerciales sí requieren una CDL.

es.question: Se requiere una Licencia de Conducir Comercial Clase A para una combinación de vehículos con una clasificación de peso bruto combinado de 26,001 libras o más, siempre que el vehículo remolcado exceda las:

choices.A: 5,000 libras
choices.B: 8,000 libras
choices.C: 10,000 libras
choices.D: 15,000 libras

es.explanation: Una CDL Clase A es para cualquier combinación de vehículos con una clasificación de peso bruto combinado de 26,001 libras o más, siempre que la clasificación de peso bruto vehicular del vehículo remolcado sea superior a 10,000 libras.

es.question: ¿Quién de los siguientes NO está obligado a obtener una licencia de conducir de Kentucky para conducir en el estado?

choices.A: Un nuevo residente que se mudó recientemente a Kentucky de forma permanente.
choices.B: Un miembro militar en servicio activo que posee una licencia válida de otro estado.
choices.C: Un joven de 16 años que conduce un automóvil familiar a la escuela.
choices.D: Un conductor comercial que transporta mercancías dentro del estado.

es.explanation: No se requiere una licencia de conducir de Kentucky para los miembros de las fuerzas armadas en servicio activo y sus dependientes que posean una licencia válida de otro estado.

es.question: ¿Se aplican los requisitos de la Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) a los conductores voluntarios, como los conductores de autobuses de iglesias?

choices.A: No, los conductores voluntarios siempre están exentos de los requisitos de la CDL.
choices.B: Sí, los requisitos de la CDL se aplican a los conductores voluntarios que operan vehículos motorizados comerciales.
choices.C: Solo si conducen a través de las fronteras estatales.
choices.D: Solo si se les paga un estipendio por su tiempo.

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente que los requisitos de la CDL se aplican a los conductores voluntarios, como los conductores de autobuses de iglesias, conductores de autobuses de escuelas públicas y privadas, mecánicos, vendedores, etc.

es.question: ¿Qué clase de licencia de conducir de Kentucky se requiere específicamente para operar una motocicleta?

choices.A: Clase B
choices.B: Clase C
choices.C: Clase D
choices.D: Clase M

es.explanation: Según el manual, la licencia Clase M es para motocicletas.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes se requieren para obtener una licencia de ciclomotor en Kentucky?

choices.A: Exámenes de la vista, de conocimientos generales y de habilidades
choices.B: Solo exámenes de la vista y de conocimientos generales
choices.C: Solo exámenes de conocimientos generales y de habilidades
choices.D: Solo exámenes de la vista y de habilidades

es.explanation: Según el manual, los solicitantes deben aprobar los exámenes de conocimientos generales y de la vista para que se les otorgue una licencia de ciclomotor. No se requiere un examen de habilidades ni un permiso.

es.question: ¿Dónde es ilegal operar un ciclomotor?

choices.A: En cualquier vía pública con un límite de velocidad superior a 35 mph
choices.B: En autopistas de acceso limitado donde la velocidad mínima es de más de 30 mph
choices.C: En zonas residenciales con un límite de velocidad inferior a 25 mph
choices.D: En cualquier carretera estatal o interestatal

es.explanation: El manual establece que los ciclomotores NO pueden operarse en autopistas de acceso limitado donde la velocidad mínima sea superior a treinta (30) millas por hora (mph).

es.question: ¿Qué equipo de seguridad se requiere legalmente para los operadores de ciclomotores en Kentucky?

choices.A: Casco y protección ocular
choices.B: Solo casco
choices.C: Solo protección ocular
choices.D: No se requiere legalmente ni casco ni protección ocular

es.explanation: El manual señala que los operadores de ciclomotores no están obligados a usar cascos ni dispositivos de protección ocular, aunque se recomiendan encarecidamente.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes está excluido de la definición legal de una motocicleta?

choices.A: Un vehículo impulsado por motor con dos ruedas
choices.B: Un vehículo impulsado por motor con un sillín
choices.C: Un vehículo en el que el operador viaja en una cabina cerrada
choices.D: Un vehículo impulsado por motor con tres ruedas

es.explanation: Una motocicleta se define como un vehículo impulsado por motor con un asiento o sillín y no más de tres ruedas, excluyendo específicamente ciclomotores, tractores y vehículos en los que el operador y los pasajeros viajan en una cabina cerrada.

es.question: ¿Dónde puede un conductor operar legalmente una minimoto o un scooter motorizado sin una licencia de conducir?

choices.A: En calles residenciales
choices.B: En propiedad privada
choices.C: En parques públicos
choices.D: En carreteras con un límite de velocidad inferior a 25 mph

es.explanation: El manual establece que el único lugar donde un conductor puede conducir u operar legalmente vehículos pequeños como minimotos o scooters motorizados sin una licencia de conducir y equipo de seguridad es en propiedad privada.

es.question: ¿Quién es elegible para solicitar un permiso de instrucción de motocicleta sin necesidad de la firma de un padre o tutor?

choices.A: Cualquier persona que tenga al menos 16 años
choices.B: Cualquier persona que posea una licencia de ciclomotor
choices.C: Una persona que tenga al menos 18 años de edad
choices.D: Una persona que tenga al menos 21 años de edad

es.explanation: Una persona que tenga al menos dieciocho (18) años de edad puede solicitar un permiso de instrucción para operar una motocicleta. Si la persona es menor de 18 años, la solicitud debe estar firmada por un padre o tutor legal.

es.question: ¿Cómo puede un solicitante de una licencia de motocicleta quedar exento de los exámenes escritos y de habilidades?

choices.A: Al tener un permiso de motocicleta por más de un año
choices.B: Al completar con éxito un curso de capacitación para conductores RideSmartKY aprobado
choices.C: Al tener una licencia de conducir válida de otro estado
choices.D: Al aprobar un examen de la vista con visión 20/20

es.explanation: Los solicitantes de una licencia de motocicleta estarán exentos de los exámenes escritos y de habilidades de la licencia si presentan evidencia satisfactoria de haber completado con éxito un curso de capacitación para conductores aprobado (RideSmartKY).

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima requerida para solicitar una licencia de operador, de motocicleta o de ciclomotor de Kentucky?

choices.A: 15 años
choices.B: 16 años
choices.C: 17 años
choices.D: 18 años

es.explanation: Para ser elegible para solicitar una licencia de operador, una licencia de motocicleta o una licencia de ciclomotor de Kentucky, debe haber cumplido dieciséis años.

es.question: ¿Qué sucede si un padre o tutor legal retira su responsabilidad por un conductor menor de edad?

choices.A: El menor debe pagar una multa para seguir conduciendo
choices.B: El permiso o la licencia del menor serán cancelados
choices.C: El menor está restringido a conducir solo durante las horas del día
choices.D: El menor debe volver a tomar los exámenes escritos y de la vista

es.explanation: Un padre o tutor legal tiene el derecho de retirar su responsabilidad en cualquier momento. Una vez que se recibe e ingresa el formulario de retiro, el permiso o la licencia del menor se cancelará hasta que se firme otra solicitud.

es.question: ¿Cuáles son las tres fases de obtención de la licencia para conductores menores de 18 años en el Programa de Licencia de Conducir Graduada (GDL)?

choices.A: Permiso de aprendizaje, licencia restringida, licencia comercial
choices.B: Permiso de instrucción, licencia provisional, licencia intermedia
choices.C: Permiso de aprendizaje, licencia intermedia, licencia completa sin restricciones
choices.D: Licencia de ciclomotor, permiso de aprendizaje, licencia completa sin restricciones

es.explanation: Los conductores menores de 18 años deben pasar por tres fases de obtención de licencia: un permiso de aprendizaje (Learner's Permit), una licencia intermedia (Intermediate License) y luego una licencia completa sin restricciones (Full Unrestricted License).

es.question: ¿Al solicitar un permiso, qué documento debe ser emitido por la escuela del solicitante?

choices.A: Una copia certificada de su expediente académico
choices.B: Un Formulario de Verificación de Cumplimiento Escolar (School Compliance Verification Form)
choices.C: Una carta de recomendación del director
choices.D: Una tarjeta de identificación de estudiante
