en.explanation: The manual lists various features of public ways, including 'High Occupancy Vehicle lanes (HOV).'

en.question: What will happen if you fail to pay or appear in another jurisdiction for a motor vehicle violation?

choices.A: The violation is dismissed after 30 days.
choices.B: The Massachusetts RMV will take action against you when learning of these events.
choices.C: You will only be penalized if you return to that specific state.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be immediately impounded in Massachusetts.

en.explanation: If you fail to pay or appear in another jurisdiction for a violation, the RMV will take action against you when learning of these events.

en.question: In addition to English, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, and Vietnamese, in what other language is the Massachusetts Driver's Manual currently available online?

choices.A: French
choices.B: German
choices.C: Haitian Creole
choices.D: Italian

en.explanation: The manual is currently available online in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, Haitian Creole, and Vietnamese.

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, what does the acronym 'JOL' refer to in the Massachusetts licensing system?

choices.A: Junior Operator License
choices.B: Joint Ownership License
choices.C: Judicial Order of Licensing
choices.D: Juvenile Offender Law

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists the 'Junior Operator License Law' and subsequently refers to it as 'JOL' in sections like 'Requirements to Obtain a JOL.'

en.question: Based on the Table of Contents, what does the acronym 'WFMA' stand for?

choices.A: Winter Fleet Management Association
choices.B: Work and Family Mobility Act
choices.C: Wayfinding and Motorist Assistance
choices.D: Western Federal Motorway Administration

en.explanation: The Table of Contents includes a section titled 'Work and Family Mobility Act (WFMA).'

en.question: What is the consequence for drivers who violate the law by holding or supporting an electronic device while driving?

choices.A: They will be required to retake the road test.
choices.B: Fines and other penalties will be imposed.
choices.C: Their vehicle will be permanently confiscated.
choices.D: They will receive a warning for the first three offenses.

en.explanation: The manual states that 'Fines and other penalties will be imposed for violators of the hands-free law.'

en.question: How can motorists follow the Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles on Twitter for the latest news?

choices.A: @MassDOT
choices.B: @MassRMV
choices.C: @DriveMass
choices.D: @BostonRMV

en.explanation: The manual advises motorists to 'follow the RMV on Twitter @MassRMV' for the latest RMV news.

en.question: According to the manual's section on sharing the road, why should drivers always pay attention to bicycling and walking?

choices.A: Because bicycles are allowed on Interstate highways.
choices.B: Because pedestrians always have the right-of-way on expressways.
choices.C: Because bicycling and walking may be used in conjunction with transit.
choices.D: Because bicycles travel at the same speeds as motor vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Bicycling and walking may be used in conjunction with transit, so always pay attention.'

en.question: According to the Vulnerable Road Users Law, how should a driver safely pass a bicyclist?

choices.A: Honk the horn to alert them before passing closely
choices.B: Pass at a close distance to avoid oncoming traffic
choices.C: Leave a safe distance of at least 4 feet when passing
choices.D: Speed up to pass them as quickly as possible

en.explanation: Under the Vulnerable Road Users Law, drivers must leave a safe distance of at least 4 feet when passing vulnerable road users such as bicyclists.

en.question: Which of the following is classified as a Civil Motor Vehicle Infraction (CMVI) rather than a criminal violation?

choices.A: Operating Under the Influence (OUI)
choices.B: Speeding
choices.C: Leaving the scene of a crash
choices.D: Vehicular homicide

en.explanation: Speeding is considered a Civil Motor Vehicle Infraction (CMVI). OUI, leaving the scene of a crash, and vehicular homicide are serious criminal violations.

en.question: What is the penalty if a driver accumulates three surchargeable events within a two-year period?

choices.A: A permanent license revocation
choices.B: Mandatory installation of an Ignition Interlock Device
choices.C: Completion of a mandatory Driver Retraining Course
choices.D: A 30-day jail sentence

en.explanation: If you accumulate three or more surchargeable events within a two-year period, your license will be suspended unless you complete a mandatory Driver Retraining Course.

en.question: What is the mandatory permit or license suspension period for a Junior Operator (16 1/2 to 18 years old) cited for their first speeding offense?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: Under the Mandatory Suspensions for Junior Operators, a first speeding offense results in a 90-day license suspension.

en.question: What is the legal Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) limit for drivers who are 21 years of age or older?
en.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to operate a motor vehicle with a Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) of 0.08% or higher.

en.question: What is the license suspension period for a driver over 21 years old who refuses a chemical test for the first time?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 180 days
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: Under the Implied Consent Law, a driver over 21 who refuses a chemical test for the first time faces an automatic 180-day license suspension.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the standard speed limit in a thickly settled or business district?

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 30 mph
choices.C: 40 mph
choices.D: 50 mph

en.explanation: The fundamental speed law sets the speed limit in a thickly settled or business district at 30 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

en.question: How must a driver react to a flashing red traffic signal?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Stop completely, yield the right-of-way, and proceed when safe
choices.C: Maintain speed but watch for crossing pedestrians
choices.D: Stop and wait for the light to turn green

en.explanation: A flashing red traffic signal is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to right-of-way traffic, and proceed when it is safe.

en.question: What do solid yellow lane lines on a roadway indicate?

choices.A: Traffic is moving in the same direction and passing is allowed
choices.B: Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited
choices.C: The lane is ending and you must merge right
choices.D: You are approaching a railroad crossing

en.explanation: Solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is not allowed.

en.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection with four-way stop signs at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the left
choices.B: The vehicle on the right
choices.C: The vehicle that is turning left
choices.D: The larger vehicle

en.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

en.question: Under the Rules for Passing, when is it legally permissible to pass another vehicle on the right?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit
choices.B: When the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is sufficient paved space on the right
choices.C: When you are in a hurry and the left lane is blocked
choices.D: Passing on the right is never legally permissible

en.explanation: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and you can do so safely without driving off the paved roadway.

en.question: According to parking regulations, what is the minimum distance you must maintain when parking near a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 20 feet

en.explanation: Parking regulations prohibit parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant to ensure emergency vehicles have adequate access.

en.question: When driving in winter conditions, what is the recommended technique for stopping safely on an icy road?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes at the last moment
choices.B: Pump the brakes rapidly and steer sharply
choices.C: Begin slowing down well in advance and apply the brakes gently
choices.D: Shift into neutral and let the vehicle coast to a stop

en.explanation: During winter driving, roads can be slick. It is safest to begin slowing down well in advance and apply the brakes gently to avoid skidding.

en.question: Which drivers are required to have an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) installed in their vehicle?

choices.A: Drivers with a single speeding ticket
choices.B: Drivers seeking license reinstatement after two or more OUI offenses
choices.C: All Junior Operators during their first six months of driving
choices.D: Drivers who have been involved in an at-fault crash

en.explanation: An Ignition Interlock Device (IID) is mandatory for drivers who have two or more Operating Under the Influence (OUI) offenses and are seeking a hardship license or full reinstatement.

en.question: What is the purpose of a channelizing island in a roadway?

choices.A: To provide a designated parking area for disabled vehicles
choices.B: To direct traffic flow and separate vehicles moving in the same or opposite directions
choices.C: To indicate the presence of a school zone
choices.D: To mark the beginning of a highway exit ramp

en.explanation: Channelizing islands are used to direct traffic flow, separate opposing lanes of traffic, or guide vehicles into proper lanes at intersections.

en.question: Under the Hands-Free Law, when is it permissible to use a handheld mobile electronic device?

choices.A: When stopped at a red light.
choices.B: When stopped at a stop sign.
choices.C: When the vehicle is stationary and not in a public travel lane.
choices.D: When pulled over on the side of a busy highway.

en.explanation: According to the Hands-Free Law, handheld device use is only allowed if the vehicle is stationary and is not located in a public travel lane. It is not allowed at red lights or stop signs.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the ONLY true way to protect yourself from drowsy driving?

choices.A: Drinking caffeinated beverages.
choices.B: Getting enough sleep and not driving when tired.
choices.C: Rolling down the windows for fresh air.
choices.D: Turning up the volume on the radio.

en.explanation: The manual states that the ONLY true way to protect yourself from drowsy driving is to get enough sleep and to not drive when you feel tired.

en.question: To help prevent drowsy driving, the manual recommends avoiding driving between which hours if possible?

choices.A: 10 p.m. and 4 a.m.
choices.B: Midnight and 6 a.m.
choices.C: 2 a.m. and 8 a.m.
choices.D: 8 p.m. and midnight.

en.explanation: When possible, avoid driving between midnight and 6 a.m. If you must drive at that time, be alert for signs of drowsiness.

en.question: When passing a vulnerable road user such as a bicyclist or pedestrian, what is the minimum safe passing distance you must leave?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: The Vulnerable Road User Law requires that when you pass a vulnerable road user, you must leave a safe passing distance of at least 4 feet between your vehicle and the road user.

en.question: When passing a vulnerable road user, what action is legally permitted if it is safe to do so?

choices.A: Honking continuously until you pass.
choices.B: Speeding up to pass them quickly.
choices.C: Crossing the center line to use part of the next lane.
choices.D: Passing them on the right shoulder.

en.explanation: If it is safe, you may use all or part of the lane next to you and you may cross the center line if necessary when passing a vulnerable road user.

en.question: How does an increase in speed affect a driver's vision?

choices.A: It improves peripheral vision.
choices.B: It reduces the driver's 'cone of vision'.
choices.C: It eliminates blind spots.
choices.D: It has no effect on a driver's vision.

en.explanation: An increase in speed reduces a driver's 'cone of vision' and increases the risks of crashes and serious injuries.

en.question: What is a common cause of a 'courtesy crash'?

choices.A: Yielding the right-of-way at a four-way stop.
choices.B: Waving people in through stopped traffic.
choices.C: Using turn signals too early.
choices.D: Leaving too much following distance.

en.explanation: Waving people in through stopped traffic, or driving through traffic when someone waves you in, creates a dangerous situation and can easily result in a 'courtesy crash'.

en.question: Under the Driver Removal Law, what must you do after a crash that involves only property damage?

choices.A: Leave the vehicles exactly where they are until police arrive.
choices.B: Move the vehicles out of travel lanes to a safe location.
choices.C: Wait for a tow truck before moving the vehicles.
choices.D: Exchange information while standing in the travel lane.

en.explanation: After a crash involving property damage only, the Driver Removal Law requires that vehicles be moved out of travel lanes to a safe location so they do not cause additional accidents.

en.question: Which class of Massachusetts driver's license is the most common and is used for passenger vehicles, vans, and small trucks?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class B
choices.C: Class C
choices.D: Class D

en.explanation: The Class D license, which is most common, is for passenger vehicles, vans, and small trucks.

en.question: Which class of license allows you to operate a motorcycle in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class C
choices.C: Class D
choices.D: Class M

en.explanation: The Class M license allows you to operate motorcycles.

en.question: Which license classes are known as commercial driver's licenses (CDLs) and allow you to operate large vehicles like trucks and buses?

choices.A: Classes A, B, and C
choices.B: Classes B, C, and D
choices.C: Classes C, D, and M
choices.D: Classes A, D, and M

en.explanation: Class A, B, and C licenses, which are known as commercial driver's licenses (CDLs), allow you to operate large vehicles, like trucks and buses.

en.question: What is the minimum age for a U.S. resident living outside of Massachusetts to drive in the state using a valid out-of-state driver's license?

choices.A: 15 years of age
choices.B: 16 years of age
choices.C: 17 years of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: A U.S. resident, who is at least 16 years of age and lives outside of Massachusetts, may drive in Massachusetts using a valid out-of-state driver's license.

en.question: Due to the Work and Family Mobility Act, what is no longer required to obtain a Standard Driver’s License (Class D or M) in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Proof of lawful presence
choices.B: A passing score on the road test
choices.C: Proof of residency in Massachusetts
choices.D: Payment of license fees

en.explanation: Beginning July 1, 2023, the Massachusetts RMV will not require customers to provide proof of lawful presence to obtain a Standard Driver’s License (Class D or M), due to the Work and Family Mobility Act.

en.question: If you need to use a mobile electronic device, what does the Hands-Free Law explicitly forbid you from doing?

choices.A: Using voice commands to make a call.
choices.B: Stopping on the side of a busy road or highway to use the device.
choices.C: Using the device while parked in a designated parking lot.
choices.D: Using a GPS navigation system mounted to the dashboard.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Do NOT stop on the side of a busy road or highway to use a mobile electronic device.'

en.question: Which of the following is mentioned in the manual as a sign of drowsiness while driving?

choices.A: Driving above the speed limit.
choices.B: Crossing lines or hitting rumble strips.
choices.C: Checking the rearview mirror frequently.
choices.D: Gripping the steering wheel tightly.

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to be alert for signs of drowsiness, such as crossing lines or hitting rumble strips.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of driving without your valid out-of-state or out-of-country driver's license in your possession in Massachusetts?

choices.A: A $100 fine
choices.B: A $250 fine
choices.C: A $500 fine
choices.D: A $1,000 fine

en.explanation: According to the manual, a violation of Section 10 (not having your valid out-of-state or out-of-country driver's license in your possession) is a criminal violation and a first offense is subject to a fine of $500.

en.question: If you move to Massachusetts and become a resident, how long is the grace period to obtain a Massachusetts driver's license?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: There is no grace period

en.explanation: The manual states: "If you become a resident of Massachusetts, you must obtain a Massachusetts driver's license to retain your driving privileges. There is no grace period."

en.question: If your Massachusetts driver's license expires during active military service, how long may you use it to operate a motor vehicle after your honorable discharge?

choices.A: Up to 30 days
choices.B: Up to 45 days
choices.C: Up to 60 days
choices.D: Up to 90 days

en.explanation: If you have a Massachusetts driver's license that expired during your active service, you may use that license to operate a motor vehicle for up to 60 days after your honorable discharge from military service.

en.question: If you are 15 years old and hold a valid driver's license from another state that allows you to drive, are you permitted to drive in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Yes, as long as you have your out-of-state license in your possession.
choices.B: Yes, but only if accompanied by a parent or guardian.
choices.C: No, no person under the age of 16 may drive in Massachusetts.
choices.D: No, unless you obtain a Massachusetts learner's permit.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "No person under the age of 16 may drive in Massachusetts. This is true even if you have a driver's license (or learner's permit) issued in a state or U.S. territory or another country that allows operation of a motor vehicle by a person less than 16 years of age."

en.question: What is the minimum age requirement to receive a Class D or Class M driver's license in Massachusetts?

choices.A: 16 years old
choices.B: 16 1/2 years old
choices.C: 17 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: You can obtain a learner's permit at age 16, but you may not receive a Class D or a Class M driver's license until you are at least 16 1/2 and have met all other requirements.

en.question: How old must you be to apply for a Commercial Driver's License (Class A, B, or C) in Massachusetts?

choices.A: 16 years old
choices.B: 18 years old
choices.C: 21 years old
choices.D: 25 years old

en.explanation: A note in the manual specifies: "You must be at least 18 years old to apply for a Commercial Driver's License (Class A, B, or C)."

en.question: What is a potential consequence of forging a parent or guardian's signature on a learner's permit or license application?

choices.A: A $500 fine
choices.B: License suspension or revocation
choices.C: Mandatory community service
choices.D: A written warning

en.explanation: The manual states that for minors applying for permits or licenses, "Forging a signature may result in license suspension or revocation."

en.question: According to the RMV's facial image policy, are applicants allowed to wear eyeglasses for their driver's license photo?

choices.A: Yes, if they are prescription glasses.
choices.B: Yes, as long as there is no glare on the lenses.
choices.C: No, eyeglasses are not allowed, even if the applicant normally wears them.
choices.D: No, unless they are reading glasses.

en.explanation: The facial image policy clearly states: "Eyeglasses, including reading or prescription glasses, are not allowed, even if the applicant normally wears them."

en.question: Which of the following is acceptable under the RMV's facial image policy for a driver's license photo?

choices.A: Temporary facial tattoos
choices.B: Permanent facial tattoos
choices.C: Bluetooth headsets
choices.D: Surgical masks

en.explanation: The manual notes that "Permanent facial tattoos are acceptable but temporary tattoos are not. Bluetooth headsets are not acceptable." It also states that surgical masks are not acceptable.

en.question: To be eligible for a full Class D or M license, what is the minimum visual acuity required in your better eye (corrected)?
en.explanation: To be eligible for a Class D or M license, your vision must be at least 20/40 visual acuity in your better eye (corrected) for a full license.

en.question: Under what condition might you be eligible for a "daylight only" driver's license?

choices.A: If your corrected vision is between 20/50 and 20/70 in the better eye.
choices.B: If your horizontal peripheral vision is less than 90 degrees.
choices.C: If you fail the color vision screening.
choices.D: If you are under 18 years old.

en.explanation: The manual states: "If your corrected vision is between 20/50 and 20/70 in the better eye, you may be eligible for a daylight only license."

en.question: How many degrees of horizontal peripheral vision (both eyes together) are required to be eligible for a full Class D or M license?

choices.A: 90 degrees
choices.B: 100 degrees
choices.C: 120 degrees
choices.D: 140 degrees

en.explanation: You must have at least 120 degrees of horizontal peripheral vision (both eyes together) for a full license.

en.question: When you apply for a license, the RMV checks your information with the Problem Driver Pointer System (PDPS). What does this system do?

choices.A: It checks your credit score for unpaid parking tickets.
choices.B: It stores information about license suspensions and revocations for drivers in all 50 states.
choices.C: It verifies your legal residency status in Massachusetts.
choices.D: It tracks your vehicle registration and insurance history.

en.explanation: The Problem Driver Pointer System (PDPS) stores information about license suspensions and revocations for drivers in all 50 states.

en.question: What happens if you apply for a Massachusetts driver's license while holding a valid license from another state participating in the State-to-State program?

choices.A: You will be allowed to keep both licenses.
choices.B: You must surrender your Massachusetts license when traveling out of state.
choices.C: The other participating state will cancel your driver's license issued by them.
choices.D: You will be charged double the standard licensing fee.

en.explanation: Massachusetts is part of the State-to-State program, which will cancel any driver’s license or state issued ID card issued by the other participating state when a Massachusetts license or ID Card is issued.

en.question: What is the difference in cost between a REAL ID Massachusetts Driver's License and a Standard Massachusetts Driver's License?

choices.A: The REAL ID costs $25 more.
choices.B: The Standard license costs $10 more.
choices.C: The REAL ID costs twice as much.
choices.D: The cost is the same for both card types.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states regarding REAL ID and Standard Massachusetts Cards: "The cost is the same for both card types."

en.question: Under the Work and Family Mobility Act (WFMA), which of the following credentials still requires proof of lawful presence to obtain?

choices.A: A Standard Class D Driver's License
choices.B: A Standard Class M Driver's License
choices.C: A Commercial Driver's License (CDL)
choices.D: A 5-year Standard Driver's License

en.explanation: The WFMA does not affect Commercial Driver's Licenses (CDLs), REAL IDs, Standard ID Cards, or Liquor IDs. Lawful presence is still required for all of these.

en.question: Which license class is typically required to operate standard passenger vehicles such as cars, SUVs, or family vans?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class B
choices.C: Class C
choices.D: Class D

en.explanation: A Class D license is for any single vehicle or combination of vehicles that does not meet the definition of Class A, B, C, or M, which typically includes passenger vehicles such as cars, SUVs, or family vans.

en.question: A Class C driver's license is required for a vehicle that does not meet the definition of Class A or B, but is designed to transport how many passengers (including the driver)?

choices.A: 8 or more
choices.B: 10 or more
choices.C: 16 or more
choices.D: 20 or more

en.explanation: A Class C license is required for a vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers including the driver, or one that is required to be placarded for hazardous materials.

en.question: What is the maximum length of time a Standard Massachusetts driver's license is valid for?

choices.A: 3 years
choices.B: 4 years
choices.C: 5 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: A Massachusetts driver's license is valid for a maximum of five years and typically expires on your birthday. A Standard License will always be valid for five years.

en.question: If you renew your license before your 21st birthday and receive a vertical license with 'Under 21' printed on it, what happens to the card when you turn 21?

choices.A: The license becomes immediately invalid and must be replaced.
choices.B: It remains valid until its expiration date.
choices.C: You must obtain a horizontal license within 30 days.
choices.D: You are restricted to driving only during daylight hours.

en.explanation: If you renew your license or ID card before your 21st birthday, you will receive a vertical license or ID card. This license or ID card will remain valid to expiration, even after you turn 21.

en.question: If you pass the driver's license vision test by wearing glasses or contact lenses, your license will be issued with which restriction code?

choices.A: Code A
choices.B: Code B
choices.C: Code C
choices.D: Code I

en.explanation: If you pass the driver's license vision test by wearing glasses or contact lenses, your driver's license will be issued with a 'Corrective Lenses' restriction, which is code letter B.

en.question: What must you do if you develop a medical condition that affects your ability to drive?

choices.A: Wait until your license expires to notify the RMV.
choices.B: Stop driving immediately and surrender your license to the police.
choices.C: Report the condition to the RMV's Medical Affairs.
choices.D: Only drive with a licensed passenger over the age of 21.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you develop a medical condition that affects your ability to drive, you must report the condition to the RMV by calling Medical Affairs.

en.question: In Massachusetts, any motor vehicle operator or motorcyclist is considered a Junior Operator if they are between what ages?

choices.A: 15 and 17
choices.B: 16 and 18
choices.D: 17 and 21

en.explanation: Any motor vehicle operator or motorcyclist between the ages of 16 1/2 and 18 is considered a Junior Operator.

en.question: How long must an applicant for a Junior Operator's License (JOL) have a valid learner's permit before taking the road test?

choices.A: At least 3 consecutive months
choices.B: At least 6 consecutive months
choices.C: At least 9 consecutive months
choices.D: At least 12 consecutive months

en.explanation: An applicant for a JOL must have a valid learner's permit for at least six consecutive months before taking the road test.

en.question: What happens to the six-month learner's permit requirement for a Junior Operator if their permit is suspended?

choices.A: The suspension time counts toward the six months.
choices.B: The six-month period is reduced to three months.
choices.C: The permit is invalidated and the six months will start anew when the suspension is lifted.
choices.D: The applicant must wait until they are 18 to take the road test.

en.explanation: Any suspension will invalidate the permit and the six months will start to run anew when the suspension is lifted.

en.question: An RMV-approved driver education and training program for a Junior Operator includes how many hours of classroom instruction?

choices.A: 12 hours
choices.B: 20 hours
choices.C: 30 hours
choices.D: 40 hours

en.explanation: A Junior Operator applicant must successfully complete an RMV-approved driver education and training program, which includes 30 hours of classroom instruction.

en.question: In addition to driver education, how many hours of supervised, behind-the-wheel driving must a Junior Operator applicant complete (as shown by a certified statement from a parent or guardian)?

choices.A: 12 hours
choices.B: 20 hours
choices.C: 30 hours
choices.D: 40 hours

en.explanation: Applicants must complete at least an additional 40 hours of supervised, behind-the-wheel driving as shown by a certified statement provided by a parent or guardian.

en.question: How many driver's licenses or ID cards are you allowed to hold at one time in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Only one
choices.B: Two, as long as one is a REAL ID and one is a Standard ID
choices.C: Two, provided they are from different states
choices.D: Up to three, including a Liquor ID

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'You may hold only one driver’s license or ID Card at a time.'

en.question: How many hours of supervised, behind-the-wheel driving must a student complete with a parent or guardian if they do NOT take a driver skills development program?

choices.A: 30 hours
choices.B: 40 hours
choices.C: 50 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: The manual states you must complete at least an additional 40 hours of supervised, behind-the-wheel driving as shown by a certified statement provided by a parent or guardian.

en.question: During the first six months of holding a Junior Operator License (JOL), you may not drive with passengers under age 18 unless accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least:

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 21 years old
choices.C: 25 years old
choices.D: 30 years old

en.explanation: You may not operate a motor vehicle with passengers under 18 unless accompanied by a person who is at least 21 years old, has at least one year of driving experience, holds a valid license, and is sitting beside you.

en.question: A Junior Operator may not operate a motor vehicle without a parent or legal guardian between the hours of:
en.explanation: As the holder of a JOL, you may not operate a motor vehicle between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless you are accompanied by one of your parents or your legal guardian.

en.question: Between 12:30 a.m. and 1:00 a.m., the Junior Operator night restriction is enforced as a 'secondary enforcement,' meaning:

choices.A: You will only receive a warning for your first offense.
choices.B: Law enforcement can only cite you if you are lawfully stopped for another violation.
choices.C: The penalty is reduced to a secondary fine.
choices.D: Only state troopers can enforce the restriction.

en.explanation: Secondary enforcement means the provisions of the law shall be enforced by law enforcement agencies only when a Junior Operator has been lawfully stopped for a violation of the motor vehicle laws or some other offense.

en.question: What is the license suspension period for a Junior Operator's first offense of violating the passenger or night restriction?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: If you violate the passenger restriction or the night restriction, you will be subject to a license suspension of 60 days for a first offense.

en.question: If a Junior Operator commits a first speeding offense, their license will be suspended for:

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For a first speeding offense, you will be suspended for 90 days; for a subsequent offense, you will be suspended for one year.

en.question: Under what condition may a driver under age 18 use a mobile electronic device while operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: When using a hands-free accessory
choices.B: When stopped at a red light
choices.C: Only for reporting an emergency
choices.D: When using a GPS navigation app

en.explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use any mobile electronic device for any reason while operating a motor vehicle. The only exception is for reporting an emergency.

en.question: To obtain a REAL ID Driver's License, how many documents must you present that prove your Massachusetts residency?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: To apply for a REAL ID Driver's License, you must present 2 documents that prove your Massachusetts residency.

en.question: When presenting identification documents to the RMV, which of the following is acceptable?

choices.A: A high-quality photocopy
choices.B: A notarized photocopy
choices.C: A laminated original document
choices.D: An unlaminated original document

en.explanation: The manual states that all documents must be originals unless otherwise indicated. Photocopies will not be accepted, and laminated documents are not acceptable.

en.question: If you have been denied a Social Security Number, your written Denial Notice from the SSA must not be older than:

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: If you have applied for an SSN with the SSA and been denied, you must present the written Denial Notice (not more than 60 days old) the SSA provided you.

en.question: If your application for a license is denied by the RMV, within how many days must you file an appeal?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: If your application is denied, you may file an appeal within ten days after you received a written denial from the RMV.

en.question: What is the fee required to file a formal appeal with the Board of Appeals on Liability Policies and Bonds?
en.explanation: A formal appeal may be filed only with the Board of Appeals on Liability Policies and Bonds at the address below with a check or money order for $50.

en.question: What is the penalty for a Junior Operator's first drag racing offense?

choices.A: 90-day suspension
choices.B: 180-day suspension
choices.C: One-year suspension
choices.D: Three-year suspension

en.explanation: You will face additional suspension periods of one year for a first drag racing offense and three years for a subsequent offense.

en.question: How many hours of instruction on the driver's education curriculum must a parent or guardian participate in (unless completed within the past 5 years)?

choices.A: 2 hours
choices.B: 4 hours
choices.C: 6 hours
choices.D: 12 hours

en.explanation: A parent or guardian must participate in two hours of instruction on the driver’s education curriculum (unless they have participated within the past five years).

en.question: What happens to the six-month passenger restriction period if a Junior Operator's license is suspended?

choices.A: The restriction period is completely restarted.
choices.B: The restriction period stops running temporarily during the suspension.
choices.C: The restriction is permanently lifted.
choices.D: The restriction period continues to run during the suspension.

en.explanation: The six-month passenger restriction period will stop running, temporarily, during any suspension. When your JOL is reinstated, you will still have to complete the remainder of the six-month restriction period.

en.question: How long is a Massachusetts learner's permit valid for?

choices.A: Up to one year
choices.B: Up to two years
choices.C: Up to four years
choices.D: Up to five years

en.explanation: The manual states that a learner's permit is valid up to two years while you practice your driving skills.

en.question: What is the fee required to take the learner's permit exam?
en.explanation: To earn your learner's permit, you must pay a $30 learner's permit exam fee, which covers the cost of your exam.

en.question: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass the learner's permit exam?

choices.A: 15 out of 25
choices.B: 18 out of 25
choices.C: 20 out of 25
choices.D: 25 out of 25

en.explanation: To pass the exam, you must answer 18 questions correctly out of the 25 multiple-choice questions.

en.question: What is the allotted time limit to complete the Class D or M learner's permit exam?

choices.A: 15 minutes
choices.B: 20 minutes
choices.C: 25 minutes
choices.D: 30 minutes

en.explanation: You must answer 18 questions correctly within the allotted time of 25 minutes.

en.question: What is the penalty if you are found responsible for cheating on the learner's permit exam?

choices.A: You will not be allowed to hold any type of driver's license or permit for 30 days.
choices.B: You will not be allowed to hold any type of driver's license or permit for 60 days.
choices.C: You must pay a $100 fine and retake the exam.
choices.D: You will be permanently banned from obtaining a driver's license.

en.explanation: If you are found responsible for cheating, you will not be allowed to hold any type of driver's license or permit for 60 days.

en.question: When driving with a Class D learner's permit, you must be accompanied by a licensed operator who meets which of the following requirements?

choices.A: At least 18 years old with 6 months of driving experience
choices.B: At least 21 years old with at least one year of driving experience
choices.C: At least 25 years old with a clean driving record
choices.D: Any licensed driver regardless of age or experience

en.explanation: You must be accompanied by a licensed operator who occupies the passenger seat next to you, is at least 21 years old, holds a valid license, and has at least one year of driving experience.

en.question: If you are under 18 and hold a Class D learner's permit, you may not drive between 12:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by:

choices.A: A licensed driver who is at least 21 years old.
choices.B: A sibling who is at least 18 years old.
choices.C: A parent or legal guardian who is a validly licensed operator with at least one year of driving experience.
choices.D: A certified driving instructor.

en.explanation: If you are under 18, you may not drive between 12:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian who is a validly licensed operator with at least one year of driving experience.

en.question: Which of the following is a limitation of operating a motorcycle with a Class M learner's permit?

choices.A: You may only carry one passenger.
choices.B: You can drive only during daylight hours (between sunrise and sunset).
choices.C: You are not required to wear a helmet if you are over 21.
choices.D: You may drive at any time of day or night.

en.explanation: A Class M learner's permit allows you to operate a motorcycle with limitations, including that you can drive only during daylight hours (between sunrise and sunset).

en.question: Can a Massachusetts learner's permit be used as an identification document for travel on most airlines and cruise ships?

choices.A: Yes, it is a fully accepted state-issued photo ID for all travel.
choices.B: Yes, but only for domestic flights within the United States.
choices.C: No, it is a document that grants conditional driving privileges and is not intended for travel identification.
choices.D: No, unless it is accompanied by a birth certificate.

en.explanation: The manual states that a learner's permit is not intended to be used as an identification document for travel and will not be accepted by most airlines or cruise ships.

en.question: Who is eligible to choose to take an audio version of the learner's permit exam?

choices.A: Only individuals with a documented medical condition.
choices.B: Only individuals who do not speak English as their primary language.
choices.C: Anyone can choose to take an audio exam without additional documentation.
choices.D: Only individuals who schedule the exam at least two weeks in advance.

en.explanation: According to the manual, anyone can choose to take an audio exam. The exam does not need to be scheduled in advance and you do not need to present any additional documentation to be eligible.

en.question: If you are under 18 years old, what additional requirement must be met when submitting a learner's permit application?

choices.A: You must have a parent or guardian sign your application.
choices.B: You must provide a letter of recommendation from your high school.
choices.C: You must prepay your road test fees.
choices.D: You must have completed a driver's education course before applying.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that if you are under 18, you must have your parent or guardian sign your application.

en.question: In what language(s) are Class A, B, and C (CDL) learner's permit exams available?

choices.A: English and Spanish only
choices.B: English only
choices.C: Over 30 different languages
choices.D: Any language requested in advance

en.explanation: The manual states that Class A, B, and C learner's permit exams are only available in English (per federal regulation).

en.question: What must you do if your learner's permit expires before you pass the road test?

choices.A: Pay a $15 renewal fee to extend it for one year.
choices.B: Re-take the learner's permit exam and pay the required fees.
choices.C: Request an extension online without taking any exams.
choices.D: Take the road test immediately before applying for a new permit.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'If your learner's permit expires, you must re-take the learner's permit exam and pay the required fees.'

en.question: If you are under 18 years old, between what hours are you prohibited from driving unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian?
en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers under 18 may not drive between 12:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian who is validly licensed with at least one year of driving experience.

en.question: When driving a motorcycle with a Class M learner's permit, when are you NOT required to wear eyeglasses, goggles, or a protective face shield?

choices.A: When driving at speeds under 30 mph.
choices.B: When you are wearing a US DOT standard helmet.
choices.C: When the motorcycle has a windshield or screen.
choices.D: When driving during daylight hours.

en.explanation: You must wear eyeglasses, goggles, or a protective face shield unless the motorcycle you are driving has a windshield or screen.

en.question: How many hours of supervised driving must a driver under 18 complete before applying for a Class D license (assuming they have not completed a driver skills development program)?

choices.A: 20 hours
choices.B: 30 hours
choices.C: 40 hours
choices.D: 50 hours

en.explanation: You must complete 40 hours of supervised driving, which is reduced to 30 hours if you completed a driver skills development program.

en.question: What is the maximum number of Class D road tests you are allowed to attempt in a 12-month period?

choices.A: Three
choices.B: Four
choices.C: Five
choices.D: Six

en.explanation: For a Class D license, you are not allowed to attempt more than six road tests in a 12-month period.

en.question: What must you do if you fail two Class M road tests?

choices.A: Wait 6 months before scheduling another test.
choices.B: Enroll in and successfully complete a beginner rider course.
choices.C: Pay a double fee for the third test.
choices.D: Surrender your Class M learner's permit.

en.explanation: For a Class M license, if you fail two road tests, you must enroll in and successfully complete a beginner rider course before you can schedule another test.

en.question: How much notice must you give to cancel or reschedule a road test without paying an additional fee?

choices.A: More than 24 hours
choices.B: More than 48 hours
choices.C: More than 72 hours
choices.D: More than 1 week

en.explanation: There is no additional fee if you cancel or reschedule with more than 72 hours notice.

en.question: If you fail a road test or do not appear for your scheduled test, how long must you wait before taking another test?

choices.A: At least 7 days
choices.B: At least 14 days
choices.C: At least 21 days
choices.D: At least 30 days

en.explanation: If you fail a road test or do not appear for your scheduled test, you must wait at least 14 days before taking another test.

en.question: What is one benefit of successfully completing the Massachusetts Rider Education Program (MREP)?

choices.A: You do not need to take an RMV Class M road test.
choices.B: You are exempt from wearing a helmet for the first year.
choices.C: You can carry passengers on a learner's permit.
choices.D: You receive a discount on your vehicle registration.

en.explanation: If you successfully complete an MREP course, you do not need to take an RMV Class M road test.

en.question: Which of the following animals is allowed in the vehicle during a road test?

choices.A: An emotional support animal
choices.B: A trained service animal
choices.C: A small pet in a carrier
choices.D: No animals are allowed under any circumstances

en.explanation: Road Test Examiners may reject road tests if animals are present, but trained service animals are allowed in the vehicle. Emotional support animals are not.

en.question: Which of the following road tests does NOT require you to bring a qualified sponsor?

choices.A: A Class D road test
choices.B: A Class M road test
choices.C: A commercial driver's license road test
choices.D: A license conversion road test

en.explanation: According to the manual's section on being prepared for the road test, a sponsor is not required for a Class M road test.

en.question: If you are under age 18, how long must you maintain a clean driving record immediately preceding the date you apply for a road test?

choices.A: 3 consecutive months
choices.B: 6 consecutive months
choices.C: 9 consecutive months
choices.D: 12 consecutive months

en.explanation: If you are under age 18, you must maintain a clean driving record for the six consecutive months immediately preceding the date you apply for the test.

en.question: What happens if you are late for your scheduled road test appointment?

choices.A: You will be tested but penalized 10 points.
choices.B: You will be tested if you arrive within 15 minutes.
choices.C: You will not be tested and you will be required to pay the road test fee.
choices.D: You will not be tested but your fee will be refunded.

en.explanation: Road tests are scheduled close together; you must be on time. If you are late for your appointment, you will not be tested and you will be required to pay the road test fee.

en.question: What must you do prior to taking a road test if you disclose a medical condition that might affect your ability to operate a motor vehicle?

choices.A: Submit medical clearance from your physician.
choices.B: Take a specialized written exam.
choices.C: Bring a registered nurse as your sponsor.
choices.D: Complete an additional 10 hours of supervised driving.

en.explanation: If you disclose a physical, mental, or medical condition or are taking medications that might affect your driving ability, you must submit medical clearance from your physician prior to taking a road test.

en.question: What is required for an applicant under 18 years old to get a Class M license?

choices.A: Bring a sponsor to the road test
choices.B: Complete the MREP basic rider course
choices.C: Take the road test in a passenger vehicle
choices.D: Have a clean driving record for one year

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are under 18 years old, you are not eligible for an RMV Class M road test and must complete the MREP basic rider course to get a Class M license.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement for a Class D road test sponsor?

choices.A: Must be at least 18 years old
choices.B: Must have at least one year of driving experience
choices.C: Must hold a valid foreign driver's license
choices.D: Must sit in the front passenger seat

en.explanation: A sponsor must be at least 21 years old, have at least one year of driving experience, and have a valid driver's license issued by their home state.

en.question: Without approval from the RMV Road Test Program, what is the maximum number of applicants a person can sponsor within a one-year period?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Five

en.explanation: Operators are not allowed to sponsor more than three different applicants within a one-year period without approval from the RMV Road Test Program.

en.question: Where must your sponsor sit during a Class D road test?

choices.A: In the front passenger seat next to the driver
choices.B: In the rear seat behind the driver
choices.C: In the rear seat behind the examiner
choices.D: In the bed of a pickup truck if no rear seat is available

en.explanation: The manual states that the examiner will sit next to you, and your sponsor must sit in the rear seat behind the driver.

en.question: Why must the vehicle used for a road test have an accessible parking brake?

choices.A: So the sponsor can assist with parking
choices.B: So the examiner can make an emergency stop
choices.C: To test the driver's ability to park on a hill
choices.D: To ensure the vehicle passes state inspection

en.explanation: The vehicle must have an accessible parking brake so the examiner can make an emergency stop if necessary.

en.question: If you use an out-of-state registered vehicle for your road test, what is the minimum required property damage insurance coverage you must prove?
en.explanation: For an out-of-state registered vehicle, you must show proof of insurance coverage equal to Massachusetts minimum limits, which includes $5,000 for property damage.

en.question: What additional documentation is required if you are using a rented vehicle for your road test?

choices.A: A bill of sale from the rental company
choices.B: A letter from the rental company authorizing use for a road test
choices.C: Proof of a commercial driver's license
choices.D: A second foot brake installed in the vehicle

en.explanation: If renting the vehicle, you must show the rental agreement and a letter from the rental company on its letterhead authorizing you and your sponsor to use the vehicle for a driver's license road test.

en.question: Which type of license plate is strictly prohibited on a vehicle used for a road test?

choices.A: Out-of-state plates
choices.B: Dealer plates
choices.C: Farm plates
choices.D: Repair plates

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "You will not be allowed to take a road test in a vehicle with a repair plate."

en.question: How does the RMV handle vehicles equipped with specialized features like back-up cameras during a road test?

choices.A: The devices must be completely disabled before the test begins
choices.B: The vehicle will be rejected and the test canceled
choices.C: The devices do not need to be disabled, but your skills without relying only on them will be tested
choices.D: You are required to use these features to pass the test

en.explanation: Specialized features like back-up cameras do not need to be disabled, but the examiner will test your driving skills and abilities without relying only on these features.

en.question: During the road test, approximately how far will the examiner ask you to back the vehicle?

choices.A: 20 feet
choices.B: 50 feet
choices.C: 100 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: During a road test, you should be prepared to demonstrate your ability to back the vehicle approximately 50 feet.

en.question: If you are deaf or hard of hearing, who arranges for an interpreter for your road test?

choices.A: The applicant must hire their own interpreter
choices.B: The sponsor must act as the interpreter
choices.C: The Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
choices.D: The RMV examiner assigned to the test

en.explanation: Once the test is booked, the Driver Licensing Department will contact the Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to arrange for an interpreter.

en.question: Which of the following is listed as a common reason for failing a road test?

choices.A: Arriving exactly on time instead of 15 minutes early
choices.B: Not knowing the hand signals
choices.C: Using a vehicle with a centrally located parking brake
choices.D: Paying your road test fees online

en.explanation: Not knowing the hand signals is explicitly listed in the manual under "Common Reasons for Failing a Road Test."

en.question: A vehicle cannot be used for a road test if it has which of the following?

choices.A: A back-up camera
choices.B: A 'donut' (limited use spare) tire
choices.C: A centrally located parking brake
choices.D: GPS-guided independent operation

en.explanation: The manual states that a vehicle cannot be used for a road test if one of its tires has been replaced by a 'donut' (limited use spare) tire.

en.question: What is the rule regarding conversation between you and your sponsor during the road test?

choices.A: You may converse freely to help ease your nerves
choices.B: Your sponsor may give you verbal directions on how to park
choices.C: You and your sponsor are not allowed to converse unless authorized by the examiner
choices.D: You must communicate with your sponsor using hand signals only

en.explanation: During the road test, you and your sponsor/interpreter are not allowed to converse unless authorized by the examiner.

en.question: What may happen if you pass your road test but fail to pay your license fees within 60 days?

choices.A: Your learner's permit will be permanently revoked.
choices.B: You may be required to retake the road test at your expense.
choices.C: You will be charged a late fee of $50.
choices.D: Your temporary license will automatically be extended.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you do not pay within 60 days of passing your road test, you may be required to retake the road test at your expense.

en.question: Can the receipt you receive at the RMV Service Center be used as a state-issued photo ID for boarding an airplane?

choices.A: Yes, it is valid for all domestic and international travel.
choices.B: Yes, but only if accompanied by a birth certificate.
choices.C: No, the receipt is not valid for identification.
choices.D: No, unless it has a special travel stamp from the RMV.

en.explanation: The manual states that the receipt serves as a temporary license but is not valid for identification, meaning it will not be accepted by most airlines or cruise ships for travel as a state-issued photo ID.

en.question: Where does Massachusetts law require you to keep your driver's license when operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: In the glove compartment of the vehicle.
choices.B: On your person or within easy reach inside your vehicle.
choices.C: Displayed visibly on the dashboard.
choices.D: In a secure location at your home.

en.explanation: Whenever you operate a motor vehicle in Massachusetts, the law requires you to carry a valid driver's license on your person or within easy reach inside your vehicle.

en.question: When converting an out-of-state Junior Operator License, how many hours of supervised driving must you log if you have NOT completed a driver skills development program?

choices.A: 20 hours
choices.B: 30 hours
choices.C: 40 hours
choices.D: 50 hours

en.explanation: The manual requires you to log an additional 40 hours of supervised driving, which is reduced to 30 hours only if you completed a driver skills development program.

en.question: Under what condition will you be exempt from the passenger restriction when converting an out-of-state Junior Operator License?

choices.A: If you are at least 17 years old.
choices.B: If you have had a valid license for a full six months without suspension or revocation.
choices.C: If you pass a written exam in Massachusetts.
choices.D: If you have completed 50 hours of supervised driving.

en.explanation: If your driving record indicates you have had a valid license for a full six months, without suspension or revocation, you will not be subject to the passenger restriction.

en.question: To be eligible to convert an out-of-state learner's permit to a Massachusetts permit, the out-of-state permit must have been issued less than how long ago?

choices.A: Six months ago
choices.B: One year ago
choices.C: Two years ago
choices.D: Five years ago

en.explanation: To be eligible for permit conversion, you must present the current out-of-state permit issued less than two years ago.

en.question: Why is an original certified driving record required when converting a license from Canada, Mexico, or a U.S. Territory?

choices.A: Because their driving records are not available for electronic review by the RMV through the Problem Driver Pointer System.
choices.B: Because their driving tests do not meet Massachusetts minimum standards.
choices.C: Because they use a different vehicle classification system.
choices.D: Because they do not require a written learner's permit exam.

en.explanation: An original certified driving record is required from these jurisdictions because their driving records are not available for electronic review by the RMV through the Problem Driver Pointer System.

en.question: A Puerto Rican birth certificate will only be accepted for identification by the RMV if it was issued on or after what date?

choices.A: January 1, 2000
choices.B: September 11, 2001
choices.C: July 1, 2010

en.explanation: The manual specifies that a Puerto Rican birth certificate will only be accepted for identification if it was issued on or after July 1, 2010.

en.question: How old must a U.S. citizen be to register to vote when conducting a permit, license, or ID transaction in Massachusetts?

choices.A: At least 15 years old
choices.B: At least 16 years old
choices.C: At least 18 years old
choices.D: At least 21 years old

en.explanation: The manual states: 'You must be a U.S. citizen and at least 16 years old to register to vote.' (You must be at least 18 to actually vote).

en.question: What is the fee to add the 'Veteran' indicator to your Massachusetts driver's license or ID card?

choices.D: There is no additional fee

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states, 'There is no additional fee for the Veteran's Indicator.'

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable document to prove honorable discharge for the Veteran's Indicator?

choices.A: A handwritten Honorable Discharge form
choices.B: A typed DD-214 indicating honorable discharge
choices.C: A standard military ID card
choices.D: A letter of recommendation from a commanding officer

en.explanation: Acceptable proof includes a DD-214, DD-215, or an Honorable Discharge form. The manual notes that the information on the form must be typed (not handwritten).

en.question: What does the heart symbol on a Massachusetts driver's license or ID represent?

choices.A: The driver has a medical heart condition.
choices.B: The driver is a veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces.
choices.C: The driver is in the Massachusetts Donor Registry and has consented to organ/tissue donation.
choices.D: The driver has completed an advanced driver skills development program.

en.explanation: The heart symbol indicates that you are in the Massachusetts Donor Registry and have consented to organ/tissue donation.

en.question: If you are currently a registered organ donor, what must you do when renewing your license or ID card to remain in the registry?

choices.A: Pay an additional $5 fee.
choices.B: Check 'yes' on question one of the license or ID card renewal form.
choices.C: Submit a new medical evaluation form.
choices.D: Get a new photograph taken at the RMV.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Even if you are currently a registered donor, you still need to check 'yes' on question one of the license or ID card renewal form in order to remain in the donor registry.'

en.question: What is the RMV's policy regarding violent or abusive conduct by road test applicants and sponsors?

choices.A: A warning is issued for the first offense.
choices.B: The applicant must pay a fine before continuing the test.
choices.C: The RMV has a zero tolerance policy.
choices.D: The road test is delayed by 30 days.

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'The RMV has a zero tolerance policy for violent or abusive conduct by road test applicants and sponsors.'

en.question: Can you be an organ and tissue donor if you do not currently have the heart symbol on your license or ID?

choices.A: Yes, you can register anytime online and your name will be in the Donor Registry's database.
choices.B: No, you must order a new license with the symbol immediately to be a donor.
choices.C: Yes, but only if you carry a separate physical donor card at all times.
choices.D: No, the heart symbol is legally required to authorize donation.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Yes. You can register as an organ/tissue donor anytime on Mass.Gov/RMV. You don't need to get a new license/ID. Your license/ID won't have the heart symbol, but your name will be in the Donor Registry's database.'

en.question: Do you need to carry a separate donor card if you have the heart symbol on your Massachusetts license?

choices.A: Yes, at all times.
choices.B: Yes, but only when driving out of state.
choices.C: No, the heart symbol indicates you are in the Donor Registry.
choices.D: No, unless you are under 18 years old.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you do not need to carry a donor card if you have the heart symbol on your license, as it indicates you are in the Massachusetts Donor Registry.

en.question: How much notice must you give to cancel a road test appointment to avoid being charged the $35 fee?

choices.A: 24 hours
choices.B: 48 hours
choices.C: 72 hours
choices.D: 1 week

en.explanation: The manual states that if you cancel your appointment with less than 72 hours notice, you will still be charged the $35 fee.

en.question: Which group is exempt from paying driver's license transaction fees in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Senior citizens over 65
choices.B: Disabled Veterans with or qualifying for Disabled Veteran plates
choices.C: Active duty military personnel
choices.D: State employees

en.explanation: Disabled Veterans do not pay any fees for driver's license transactions if they have Disabled Veteran plates or if they have qualified for them with Medical Affairs.

en.question: What must you do if your vehicle's directional signals or brake lights stop working?

choices.A: Drive only during daylight hours.
choices.B: Use hand signals when turning or slowing until they are fixed.
choices.C: Turn on your hazard lights continuously.
choices.D: Stop driving the vehicle immediately and have it towed.

en.explanation: If the directional signals or brake lights on your vehicle stop working, you must have them fixed right away and use hand signals when turning or slowing until they are fixed.

en.question: Which of the following is a legal restriction on glass tinting for passenger vehicles?

choices.A: You cannot tint your side windows at all.
choices.B: You can darken your windshield up to 35 percent.
choices.C: It is illegal to tint your windshield.
choices.D: Rear windows can be darkened up to 50 percent.

en.explanation: The manual states that you can darken your side and rear windows up to 35 percent, but it is illegal to tint your windshield.

en.question: What is the fine for a driver who is not wearing a safety belt?
en.explanation: Any driver who is not wearing a safety belt can be fined $25.

en.question: Under Massachusetts law, a driver can be fined $25 for which of the following unbelted passengers?

choices.A: Any passenger over the age of 18
choices.B: A passenger who is 16 or 17 years old
choices.C: Each passenger age 12, 13, 14, or 15
choices.D: Passengers riding in a taxi

en.explanation: A driver can be fined $25 for each passenger age 12, 13, 14, or 15 who is not wearing a safety belt. Passengers 16 and older are fined directly.

en.question: Which of the following individuals is required to wear a safety belt under Massachusetts law?

choices.A: A driver of a vehicle manufactured before July 1966
choices.B: A passenger in an emergency vehicle
choices.C: A driver of a passenger motor vehicle under 18,000 lbs
choices.D: An employee of the U.S. Postal Service driving while working

en.explanation: Massachusetts law requires every person in a passenger motor vehicle (including vans and small trucks under 18,000 lbs.) to wear a safety belt. The other options are listed as specific exemptions.

en.question: Infants and small children must sit in federally approved child passenger restraints until they reach what age or height?

choices.A: 6 years old or 50 inches tall
choices.B: 7 years old or 54 inches tall
choices.C: 8 years old or 57 inches tall
choices.D: 9 years old or 60 inches tall

en.explanation: Infants and small children must sit in federally approved child passenger restraints until they are at least eight years old or at least fifty-seven inches tall.

en.question: Where is the safest place for a child to sit in a passenger vehicle?

choices.A: The front passenger seat
choices.B: The back middle seat
choices.C: The back right seat
choices.D: The back left seat

en.explanation: The manual states that the safest place for a child to sit is in the back seat, and the back middle seat is best.

en.question: According to the Guide to Child Safety Seats, what is the weight limit for an infant seat?

choices.A: Up to 15 pounds
choices.B: Up to 20 pounds
choices.C: 20 to 40 pounds
choices.D: 40 to 80 pounds

en.explanation: The Guide to Child Safety Seats specifies that an infant seat is for children up to 20 pounds.

en.question: When worn correctly, safety belts lower the chance of death or serious injury in a crash by about:

choices.A: 25 percent
choices.B: 50 percent
choices.C: 75 percent
choices.D: 90 percent

en.explanation: When worn correctly, safety belts lower the chance of death or serious injury in a crash by about 50 percent.

en.question: How many red stop (brake) lights must a passenger vehicle have in the back?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: The manual states that the vehicle must have three red stop (brake) lights in the back.

en.question: How is the Massachusetts safety belt law enforced?

choices.A: You can be stopped and fined solely for not wearing a seat belt.
choices.B: You can only get a fine for the safety belt law when you are stopped for a traffic violation.
choices.C: Safety belt fines are only issued if you are involved in a crash.
choices.D: Police use traffic cameras to issue safety belt citations by mail.

en.explanation: The manual notes that you can only get a fine for the safety belt law when you are stopped for a traffic violation (secondary enforcement).

en.question: What is the restriction on using a spot light on a passenger vehicle?

choices.A: It can only be used to read signs or as an emergency light if headlights are broken.
choices.B: It can be used at any time to improve visibility in fog.
choices.C: It must shine at least four feet above the roadway.
choices.D: It can be used to warn oncoming drivers of a hazard.

en.explanation: A passenger vehicle may have a spot light that can only be used to read signs or as an emergency light if the headlights are not working.

en.question: How should a lap safety belt be properly worn?

choices.A: Loosely across the stomach
choices.B: Low, tight, and flat over the hips
choices.C: Under the arm and across the chest
choices.D: Tightly across the thighs and knees

en.explanation: According to the manual, a lap belt should fit low, tight, and flat over the hips and should not be twisted.

en.question: According to the manual, hitting the windshield at 30 mph is comparable to what?

choices.A: Falling from the roof of a one-story house
choices.B: Falling from the third story of a building
choices.C: Being tackled by a professional football player
choices.D: Hitting a brick wall at 60 mph

en.explanation: The manual states that hitting the windshield at 30 mph is like falling from the third story of a building and hitting the pavement.

en.question: Where should an infant in a rear-facing child safety seat be placed if the vehicle has a passenger-side airbag?

choices.A: In the front seat with the seat pushed all the way back
choices.B: In the front seat with the airbag deactivated
choices.C: In the back seat of the vehicle
choices.D: In the front seat facing forward

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that infants in back-facing child safety seats should never be in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger-side air bag. Children are always safest when riding in the back seat.

en.question: What is the legal exception for wearing an earplug while driving in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Drivers of any age may wear two earplugs if listening to GPS instructions
choices.B: Drivers 18 or older can use one earplug for use with a cell phone
choices.C: Drivers under 18 can use one earplug for listening to music
choices.D: Any driver can wear noise-canceling headphones to reduce stress

en.explanation: It is illegal to wear a radio headset or headphones that restrict attention, but if you are 18 or older, you can use one earplug for use with a cell phone.

en.question: What is the rule regarding televisions installed inside a motor vehicle?

choices.A: They must be mounted on the dashboard for the front passenger
choices.B: They can be visible to the driver as long as the volume is muted
choices.C: They must be behind the front seat and not visible to the driver
choices.D: They are completely illegal to have in any part of the vehicle

en.explanation: Any television installed in a vehicle must be behind the front seat and not visible to the driver to prevent distraction.

en.question: Under what conditions are children under 12 years old generally allowed to ride in the bed of a pickup truck?

choices.A: When accompanied by an adult
choices.B: When traveling on residential streets at any speed
choices.C: They are not allowed, with very limited exceptions that never exceed 5 mph
choices.D: When they are seated flat on the bed of the truck

en.explanation: Children under 12 years old are not allowed to ride in the beds of pickup trucks, with very limited exceptions, and never at speeds more than five mph.

en.question: When is a driver who is 18 or older permitted to use a hand-held mobile electronic device?

choices.A: When stopped at a red light or stop sign
choices.B: When driving under 15 mph in heavy traffic
choices.C: When the vehicle is stationary and not located in a public travel lane
choices.D: When pulled over on the shoulder of a busy highway

en.explanation: Handheld device use is only allowed if the vehicle is stationary and is not located in a public travel lane. It is not allowed at red lights, stop signs, or on the side of a busy road/highway.

en.question: What is the ONLY exception that allows a driver under 18 to use a mobile electronic device while driving?

choices.A: To answer a call from a parent or guardian
choices.B: To use a GPS navigation application
choices.C: To report an emergency
choices.D: To change the music playlist while stopped at a red light

en.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot use any mobile electronic device for any reason while driving. The only exception is for reporting an emergency.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of using a hand-held mobile electronic device while driving?

choices.A: A $50 fine
choices.B: A $100 fine
choices.C: A $250 fine and a distracted driving program
choices.D: A 30-day license suspension

en.explanation: The penalty for a 1st offense of violating the hand-held mobile electronic device law is a $100 fine.

en.question: According to the manual, at what speeds do eight out of ten motor vehicle crashes occur?

choices.A: 25 mph or less
choices.B: 40 mph or less
choices.C: 55 mph or less
choices.D: 65 mph or more

en.explanation: The manual states that eight out of ten crashes happen at speeds of 40 mph or less.

en.question: What type of crash are front air bags specifically designed to protect you from?

choices.A: Rear-end crashes
choices.B: Side-impact crashes
choices.C: Rollover crashes
choices.D: Head-on crashes

en.question: How must a GPS device or cell phone be used for navigation by an adult driver?

choices.A: It must be held in the driver's right hand
choices.B: It must be affixed to the vehicle temporarily or permanently
choices.C: It must be kept in the passenger seat
choices.D: It must be operated by a passenger only

en.explanation: GPS devices (including cell phones) can be used if the device is affixed, either temporarily or permanently, in the motor vehicle for the purpose of providing navigation assistance.

en.question: Why is it important to maintain space around your vehicle while driving?

choices.A: To allow pedestrians to cross the street anywhere
choices.B: To prevent other drivers from passing you
choices.C: In case you need to suddenly change lanes to avoid a crash
choices.D: To improve your vehicle's fuel efficiency

en.explanation: Defensive driving requires you to maintain space around your vehicle in case you need to suddenly change lanes to avoid a crash.

en.question: What are the consequences if you crash and injure someone or damage property because you were using a mobile electronic device?

choices.A: You will receive a warning and a small fine
choices.B: You will face criminal charges and lose your license
choices.C: You will only have to pay for the property damage
choices.D: You will be required to retake the road test

en.explanation: It is a crime to injure a person or damage property because of negligent driving. If you crash because you were using a mobile electronic device, you will face criminal charges and lose your license.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for tailgating another vehicle?

en.question: What is the minimum legal tread depth for your vehicle's tires?

choices.A: 1/32 inches
choices.B: 2/32 inches
choices.C: 3/32 inches
choices.D: 4/32 inches

en.question: When are you required to use your headlights and taillights based on the time of day?

choices.A: From one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise
choices.B: From one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise
choices.C: From sunset to sunrise
choices.D: Only when it is completely dark outside

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the use of headlights during the day?

en.question: How much following distance should you maintain behind a motorcycle?

choices.A: At least two seconds
choices.B: At least three seconds
choices.C: At least four seconds
choices.D: At least five seconds

en.explanation: You should keep more space (at least four seconds) behind a motorcycle than you would for another vehicle.

en.question: Where must registration stickers be placed on your license plate?

choices.A: In the upper left corner

choices.D: In the lower right corner

en.question: What should you do if you need to stop quickly and your vehicle is equipped with antilock brakes?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly
choices.B: Never pump the brakes
choices.C: Lightly tap the brakes until you stop
choices.D: Apply the parking brake simultaneously

en.question: To avoid the glare of headlights from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?

choices.C: To the lower right side of your lane

en.question: What is the recommended action if another driver is tailgating you?

en.question: Compared to passenger vehicles, how much stopping distance might large trucks require?

choices.B: One and a half times the stopping distance
choices.C: Two times the stopping distance
choices.D: Three times the stopping distance

en.question: In which of the following situations is it appropriate to use your horn?

choices.D: To try to get other vehicles moving in a traffic jam

en.question: From what distance must your license plate number be visible at night?

choices.A: 30 feet
choices.B: 50 feet
choices.C: 60 feet
choices.D: 100 feet

en.question: Which of the following is a key principle of defensive driving regarding right-of-way?

choices.A: Right-of-way is something you should always take if the law allows.
choices.B: Right-of-way is something you give to prevent unsafe traffic situations.
choices.C: Right-of-way belongs to the larger vehicle.

en.question: Approximately how far ahead do high beam headlights normally let you see?

choices.D: Within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle ahead

en.question: If an oncoming driver does not change their high beams to low beams, where should you look to avoid the glare?

choices.A: Straight at the oncoming headlights

choices.C: To the lower right side of your lane
choices.D: At your inside rearview mirror

en.question: According to the manual, drowsy driving crashes most often involve:

choices.D: Pedestrians being struck in crosswalks

en.question: Under the Vulnerable Road Users Law, what is the minimum safe passing distance you must leave between your vehicle and a vulnerable road user?

choices.C: At least four feet

choices.D: A driver operating a snowplow

choices.D: Parking lights to avoid blinding other drivers
