choices.C: A registered motorized scooter
choices.D: A Class M learner's permit

en.explanation: The manual states, 'You cannot renew an expired license if you have unpaid parking violations, unpaid excise taxes, outstanding court warrants, outstanding E-ZPass/Fast Lane violations, or Tobin Bridge violations.'

en.question: What should you do if you are driving at night and a bicyclist is coming toward you?

choices.A: Flash your high beams to warn them of your presence.
choices.B: Dim your headlights.
choices.C: Turn off your headlights temporarily.
choices.D: Honk your horn.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'Dim your headlights at night if a bicyclist is coming toward you.'

en.question: What is a consequence of having unpaid parking violations in Massachusetts?

choices.A: Your vehicle will be immediately impounded.
choices.B: You cannot renew your driver's license or vehicle registration.
choices.C: You will be charged with a criminal offense.
choices.D: Your insurance rates will automatically double.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you do not pay a parking violation, you will not be able to renew your driver's license or vehicle registration.

en.question: How many days do you have to pay the required fine or request a hearing for a civil motor vehicle infraction (CMVI)?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 20 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: If you get a citation from a police officer for a civil motor vehicle infraction (CMVI), you must pay the required fine or request a hearing to dispute it within 20 days.

en.question: What happens to the $25 filing fee if you request a hearing for a civil citation and the court finds you NOT RESPONSIBLE for ALL violations?

choices.A: It is kept as an administrative fee.
choices.B: It is applied to your next vehicle registration.
choices.C: It is refunded to you.
choices.D: It is donated to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund.

en.explanation: If you are found NOT RESPONSIBLE by the court for ALL violations on the civil citation, the $25 filing fee will be refunded.

en.question: What is the lowest penalty for driving above the speed limit in Massachusetts?
en.explanation: The lowest penalty for driving above the speed limit is a $105 fine.

en.question: If you drive more than 10 miles per hour (mph) over the speed limit, how much must you pay for each additional mph over the first 10?
en.explanation: If you drive more than ten miles per hour (mph) over the speed limit, you must pay an extra $10 for each mph you were traveling above the first ten.

en.question: By law, all fines for speeding violations include a $50 surcharge that goes toward which of the following?

choices.A: The Highway Maintenance Fund
choices.B: The Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund
choices.C: The Public Safety Training Fund
choices.D: The Safe Driver Insurance Plan

en.explanation: By law, all fines for speeding violations include a $50 surcharge. The entire surcharge goes to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund.

en.question: What happens to the speeding fine if you are caught speeding in a posted work zone?

choices.A: It is doubled.
choices.B: It is tripled.
choices.C: An extra $100 is added.
choices.D: Your license is immediately revoked.

en.explanation: If you are caught speeding in a posted work zone, the speeding fine is doubled.

en.question: Your license will be suspended for 30 days if you are found guilty of how many speeding violations in a 12-month period?

choices.A: Two
choices.B: Three
choices.C: Four
choices.D: Five

en.explanation: Your license will be suspended for 30 days if you are found guilty for three speeding violations in a 12-month period.

en.question: If you have a Junior Operator's License, what is the penalty for a first-offense speeding violation?

choices.A: A 30-day license suspension
choices.B: A 60-day license suspension
choices.C: A 90-day license suspension
choices.D: A one-year license suspension

en.explanation: If you have a Junior Operator's License, a 1st offense will cause a 90-day license suspension.

en.question: A police officer may arrest you and you may face criminal charges if you refuse to do which of the following?

choices.A: Answer questions about your destination
choices.B: Sign your name in front of the officer
choices.C: Allow the officer to search your trunk
choices.D: Take a roadside breathalyzer test

en.explanation: A police officer may arrest you and you may face criminal charges if you refuse to sign your name in front of the officer, show your license, or give your name and address.

en.question: You are considered more than 50 percent at fault for a crash if your insurance company finds you at fault and has paid more than what amount for collision or damage?
en.explanation: You are more than 50 percent at fault for a crash if your insurance company finds you at fault according to the Standards of Fault and has paid more than $1000 for collision, limited collision, or damage to someone else's property.

en.question: You must complete the Massachusetts Driver Retraining Course if you accumulate how many surchargeable events within a two-year period?

choices.A: Two
choices.B: Three
choices.C: Five
choices.D: Seven

en.explanation: If you have three surchargeable events within a two-year period, your license may be suspended and the RMV will send you a letter telling you to complete a Driver Retraining course.

en.question: How long is the Driver Retraining program for drivers who have accumulated three or more surchargeable events?

choices.A: One four-hour session
choices.B: An eight-hour program
choices.C: A twelve-hour program
choices.D: Two eight-hour sessions

en.explanation: The manual states that the Driver Retraining program is an eight-hour program, typically held in two four-hour sessions or one eight-hour Saturday session.

en.question: Does completing the Driver Retraining course remove offenses or surcharges from your driving record?

choices.A: Yes, it removes the most recent offense.
choices.B: Yes, it clears all surcharges.
choices.C: No, it does not remove offenses or surcharges.
choices.D: No, but it reduces your insurance premium by half.

en.explanation: According to the manual, completing the Driver Retraining course does not remove offenses or surcharges from your driving record.

en.question: What is the cost of an unattested driving record ordered online?
en.explanation: The manual states that if you do not need the driving record to be attested, you can order an unattested driving record online for $8.

en.question: If you are caught using somebody else's license or ID, how long can the RMV suspend your driving privileges even if you are not convicted?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: The RMV can suspend your driving privileges for six months (or one year after a conviction) for using somebody else's license/ID, even if you are not convicted.

en.question: For a driver 18 years or older, what is the mandatory suspension period for three speeding violations within any one-year period?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For drivers 18 and older, three speeding violations within a one-year period results in a mandatory 30-day suspension.

en.question: Which of the following makes a driver a 'Habitual Traffic Offender' according to Massachusetts law?

choices.A: Three surchargeable events within a two-year period
choices.B: Seven surchargeable events within a three-year period
choices.C: Three major moving violations within a five-year period
choices.D: Three speeding violations within a one-year period

en.explanation: A Habitual Traffic Offender is defined as having a total of three major moving violations or any combination of twelve major or minor moving violations within a five-year period.

en.question: What is the mandatory suspension period for a Habitual Traffic Offender?

choices.A: One year
choices.B: Two years
choices.C: Three years
choices.D: Four years

en.explanation: The mandatory suspension period for a Habitual Traffic Offender is four years.

en.question: If a Junior Operator is convicted of violating the passenger restriction for the first time, how long will their license be suspended?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: A first offense conviction for violating the passenger or night restriction results in a 60-day suspension for a Junior Operator.

en.question: What is the suspension period for a Junior Operator convicted of their first speeding offense?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: A first speeding conviction for a Junior Operator results in a mandatory 90-day suspension.

en.question: Which of the following is required to reinstate a Junior Operator's license after a first speeding conviction?

choices.A: Paying a $100 reinstatement fee
choices.B: Taking a new learner's permit exam and a new road test
choices.C: Completing an alcohol education program
choices.D: Serving a one-year suspension

en.explanation: Reinstatement after a first speeding conviction for a Junior Operator requires a new learner's permit exam, a Driver Attitudinal Retraining course, and a new road test.

en.question: For a driver 18 years or older, what is the penalty for accumulating seven surchargeable events within a three-year period?

choices.A: A 30-day suspension
choices.B: A 60-day suspension
choices.C: A 90-day suspension
choices.D: A four-year suspension

en.explanation: Any combination of moving violations and surchargeable crashes that total seven surchargeable events within a three-year period results in a 60-day suspension.

en.question: Under Massachusetts law, what additional suspension applies to a Junior Operator convicted of a first offense for Operating to Endanger or Leaving the Scene of a Crash?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 90, section 24p requires a 180-day suspension for a first offense of Operating to Endanger, Leaving the Scene of a Crash, and other specific offenses for Junior Operators, in addition to any other penalty required by law.

en.question: How many times is a Junior Operator required to take the State Courts Against Road Rage (SCARR) course if mandated?

choices.A: Every time they commit a moving violation
choices.B: Once per year
choices.C: Only one time
choices.D: Until they turn 21

en.explanation: The manual states, 'A Junior Operator will only be required to take the SCARR course one time.'

en.question: Which of the following non-driving reasons can cause the RMV to suspend your driver's license?

choices.A: Failing to pay a parking ticket
choices.B: Failing to pay Massachusetts income tax
choices.C: Dropping out of high school
choices.D: Failing to vote in a state election

en.explanation: The RMV is required by law to suspend a driver's license for several reasons not related to driving, including if you 'Have failed to pay Massachusetts income tax.'

en.question: If your license is suspended for making a bad payment to the RMV, what additional fee must you pay to clear the bad payment?
en.explanation: If your license was suspended for a bad payment, you must pay the original fee, a license reinstatement fee, and a $15 fee to clear your bad payment.

en.question: What is the license suspension period for a conviction of motor vehicle homicide?

choices.A: 1 to 5 years
choices.B: 5 to 10 years
choices.C: 15 years to Lifetime
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: The criminal offenses and suspensions table lists the suspension period for motor vehicle homicide as '15 years–Lifetime'.

en.question: What is the fee to reinstate your license after a third conviction for operating under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
en.explanation: The fee to reinstate a license after a third conviction for operating under the influence of alcohol or drugs is $1,200.

en.question: If your license is suspended in another state, what document must you bring to the RMV to prove it has been reinstated?

choices.A: A reinstatement letter or driving record that is less than 30 days old
choices.B: A signed letter from a judge in the other state
choices.C: A receipt showing you paid your out-of-state fines
choices.D: A new driver's license from the other state

en.explanation: When your license is reinstated in the other state, you must bring either a reinstatement letter or a current driving record from that state, which cannot be over 30 days old.

en.question: How does the Massachusetts RMV treat traffic offenses you commit in another state?

choices.A: They are ignored unless they involve a crash.
choices.B: They are treated as if they happened in Massachusetts if they are a 'like' offense.
choices.C: They only result in a fine, not a suspension.
choices.D: They are recorded but do not affect your Massachusetts driving record.

en.explanation: Each U.S. state must tell the Massachusetts RMV about any traffic offenses you commit there. These offenses will be treated as if they happened in Massachusetts if they are a 'like' offense.

en.question: What must you do to reinstate your license if it has been suspended for two years or more?

choices.A: Pay a $5,000 fine.
choices.B: Complete 100 hours of community service.
choices.C: Pass a learner's permit exam and a road test.
choices.D: Surrender your vehicle registration.

en.explanation: For license suspensions of two years or more, you must also pass a learner's permit exam and road test to reinstate your license.

en.question: How does alcohol affect your ability to drive safely?

choices.A: It acts as a stimulant and improves reaction time.
choices.B: It is a depressant that affects vision, reaction time, coordination, and judgment.
choices.C: It only affects your driving if you drink more than three servings.
choices.D: It improves your coordination but impairs your vision.

en.explanation: Alcohol is a drug. It is a depressant that affects your vision, reaction time, coordination, and judgment.

en.question: Each year in the United States, alcohol causes nearly what percentage of all highway deaths?
en.explanation: Each year in the United States, alcohol causes nearly 40% of all highway deaths.

en.question: What is the maximum prison term for a first offense conviction of Operating Under the Influence (OUI)?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 1/2 years
choices.D: 5 years

en.explanation: The penalties table for a first offense of Operating a Motor Vehicle Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs lists the maximum prison term as 2 1/2 years.

en.question: What is the license suspension period for a Junior Operator convicted of a first offense for using a mobile electronic device (text or phone)?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: A Junior Operator convicted of a first offense for the Use of a Mobile Electronic Device (text or phone) faces a 60-day license suspension.

en.question: Even if the operation of a vehicle is not required, what is the license suspension period for defacing real or personal property with graffiti?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: One year

en.explanation: The manual states that defacing real or personal property, spraying paint or applying stickers or other graffiti results in a one-year suspension (or delay of one year in obtaining a License).

en.question: What type of violation is driving with a suspended or revoked license in Massachusetts?

choices.A: A minor civil infraction
choices.B: A criminal motor vehicle violation
choices.C: A non-moving violation
choices.D: A parking violation

en.explanation: Driving with a suspended or revoked license is a criminal motor vehicle violation. You may face a large fine and/or jail sentence, as well as additional penalties.

en.question: What is the fine range for a first offense of Operating Under the Influence (OUI) of alcohol or drugs?
en.explanation: According to the penalties chart, the fine for a first offense OUI is $500–$5,000.

en.question: According to the manual, how much more likely is the risk of a crash when alcohol use is combined with marijuana use?

choices.A: Two times more likely
choices.B: Five times more likely
choices.C: Ten times more likely
choices.D: Twelve times more likely

en.explanation: The manual states that alcohol use combined with marijuana use makes the risk of a crash twelve times more likely.

en.question: Which of the following drinks contains about the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce beer?

choices.A: A 12-ounce glass of wine
choices.B: A 5-ounce glass of wine
choices.C: A 3-ounce serving of 80-proof liquor
choices.D: An 8-ounce glass of wine

en.explanation: A 12-ounce beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a 1.5-ounce serving of 80-proof liquor all contain about the same amount of alcohol (about 1/2 ounce).

en.question: What is the only effective way to get alcohol out of your body and sober up?

choices.A: Drinking black coffee
choices.B: Taking a cold shower
choices.C: Allowing time to pass
choices.D: Eating a heavy meal

en.explanation: There is no quick way to sober up. Drinking coffee, taking a cold shower, exercising, or eating might make you feel more alert, but only time will rid you of the effects of alcohol.

en.question: If you are over age 21 and fail a chemical test, how long will your license be suspended?

choices.A: 30 days or until the conclusion of the court case, whichever is shorter
choices.B: 180 days
choices.C: One year
choices.D: 30 days plus an additional 180 days

en.explanation: For drivers over age 21, the license is suspended for 30 days or until the conclusion of the court case, whichever is shorter, for failing a chemical test.

en.question: What does the Massachusetts Implied Consent Law require of every licensed driver?

choices.A: To carry proof of insurance at all times
choices.B: To agree to consent to a breathalyzer or blood test in certain cases
choices.C: To allow police to search their vehicle without a warrant
choices.D: To take an alcohol education course before getting a license

en.explanation: Massachusetts has an Implied Consent Law, which means every licensed driver in the state must agree to consent to a breathalyzer or blood test in certain cases.

en.question: Under the Massachusetts 'zero-tolerance' law, drivers under 21 will face penalties for having a Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) as low as:
en.explanation: Massachusetts has a 'zero-tolerance' law for drivers under 21. Any driver under 21 will face penalties for having a BAC of 0.02 or higher.

en.question: How many Operating Under the Influence (OUI) offenses must you have to be required to install an Ignition Interlock Device for a hardship license or reinstatement?

choices.A: One or more
choices.B: Two or more
choices.C: Three or more
choices.D: Four or more

en.explanation: If you had two or more operating under the influence offenses and are eligible for a hardship license or for license reinstatement, you must have an Ignition Interlock Device.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?

choices.A: Your body weight
choices.B: The kind of alcoholic beverage you drink
choices.C: The amount of food you ate before drinking
choices.D: The length of time you have been drinking

en.explanation: Your BAC depends on body weight, amount of alcohol, food eaten before drinking, time spent drinking, and processing speed. The manual explicitly states: 'The kind of beverage you drink does not matter.'

en.question: What is the license suspension penalty for a Fifth Offense OUI conviction?

choices.A: Five years
choices.B: Eight years
choices.C: Ten years
choices.D: Lifetime

en.explanation: According to the Penalties for Operating a Motor Vehicle Under the Influence chart, a Fifth Offense (Felony) results in a Lifetime license suspension.

en.question: Approximately how much can one standard drink (e.g., a 12-ounce beer) raise an average person's Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?
en.explanation: Any one of the standard drinks listed (12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, 1.5 oz liquor) can raise an average person's BAC by 0.02.

en.question: If you are required to use an Ignition Interlock Device, how long must you keep using it after your license has been fully reinstated?

choices.A: Six months
choices.B: One year
choices.C: Two years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: You must keep using the Ignition Interlock Device for two more years after your license has been reinstated.

en.question: What is the initial license suspension period for a driver under age 18 who fails a chemical test, before any reductions for an alcohol education program?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 180 days
choices.C: 30 days plus an additional 180 days
choices.D: 30 days plus an additional one year

en.explanation: For drivers under age 18, the license is suspended for 30 days, plus an additional one year for failing a chemical test.

en.question: How does alcohol physically and mentally affect your driving abilities?

choices.A: It improves your reflexes but distorts your vision
choices.B: It slows your reflexes and increases the time you need to react
choices.C: It decreases your confidence and makes you overly cautious
choices.D: It helps you concentrate better on the road

en.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your reflexes, increases the time you need to react, and distorts your vision and judgment. It also often makes you feel more confident, causing you to take chances.

en.question: If you are required to use an Ignition Interlock Device, what must your vehicle have in order to schedule a road test online?

choices.A: A center console brake and a seat for the sponsor
choices.B: A backup camera and dual controls
choices.C: A manual transmission and a passenger side brake
choices.D: A certified driving instructor as a sponsor

en.explanation: To schedule a road test online with an Ignition Interlock Device, you must provide a vehicle that has the device installed, has a center console brake, and has a seat for the sponsor.

en.question: If you are under 21 years old and you buy, or try to buy, alcohol, your license will be suspended for how long?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 180 days
choices.D: One year

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are under 21 and you buy, or try to buy, alcohol, your license will be suspended for 180 days.

en.question: Under the Open Container Law, what is the fine if you are convicted of having an open alcoholic drink inside your vehicle?
en.explanation: If you are convicted of having an open alcoholic drink inside your vehicle, you will be fined $100 to $500.

en.question: If you use a false license or ID, the RMV can suspend your license for up to how long even without a conviction?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: Six months
choices.D: One year

en.explanation: M.G.L.c.90,§22(e) allows the RMV to suspend your license or right to operate in Massachusetts for up to six months for using a false ID. A conviction is not required.

en.question: How does smoking or eating marijuana affect your driving abilities?

choices.A: It improves your reaction time to sudden events.
choices.B: It lowers your ability to handle a quick series of tasks and causes a bad loss of night vision.
choices.C: It makes you feel more awake and aware for a short time.
choices.D: It has no effect on driving because it has been decriminalized.

en.explanation: Marijuana lowers your ability to handle a quick series of tasks and makes it difficult to respond to unexpected events. It also causes a bad loss of night vision.

en.question: What is a dangerous side effect of using stimulants like diet pills or pep pills before driving?

choices.A: They cause an immediate loss of hearing.
choices.B: They make you feel unaware of where you are and that you do not care.
choices.C: The initial alertness is always followed by fatigue, nervousness, dizziness, and lack of concentration.
choices.D: They permanently improve your night vision.

en.explanation: Stimulants make you feel more awake and aware for a short time, but this is always followed by fatigue, nervousness, dizziness, and a lack of concentration.

en.question: Which of the following is a reason the RMV will refuse to renew your driver's license?

choices.A: Unpaid fines for parking violations
choices.B: A single speeding ticket from three years ago
choices.C: Failure to wash your vehicle regularly
choices.D: Having a vehicle older than 15 years

en.explanation: The RMV will refuse to renew your license if you have unpaid fines for parking violations, among other unpaid fines, taxes, or outstanding warrants.

en.question: At a vehicle speed of 40 mph, what percentage of pedestrians are seriously injured or killed in a crash?
en.explanation: The manual states that at a speed of 40 mph, 73% of pedestrians are seriously injured or killed in a crash.

en.question: What does the fundamental speed law require you to do?

choices.A: Always drive at the exact posted speed limit.
choices.B: Never travel so fast that it is not safe, regardless of the posted speed limit.
choices.C: Drive 10 mph below the speed limit at all times.
choices.D: Match the speed of the vehicles around you, even if they are speeding.

en.explanation: The fundamental speed law states you must never travel so fast that it is not safe. You must lower your speed if there are poor driving conditions, even if the posted limit is higher.

en.question: What is the minimum speed limit in the Boston Harbor tunnels (Callahan, Sumner, and Ted Williams)?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 40 mph

en.explanation: There is a minimum speed of 20 mph in the Boston Harbor tunnels (Callahan, Sumner, and Ted Williams).

en.question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a school zone?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 30 mph

en.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, your speed would not be reasonable and proper if you drive over 20 mph in a school zone.

en.question: How is a "thickly settled district" defined in Massachusetts?

choices.A: An area where buildings are fewer than 200 feet apart for a distance of 1/4 mile or more.
choices.B: Any road that has a sidewalk.
choices.C: An area where buildings are fewer than 500 feet apart for a distance of 1 mile.
choices.D: A zone within 1,000 feet of a school or hospital.

en.explanation: A "thickly settled district" is an area where buildings are fewer than 200 feet apart for a distance of 1/4 mile or more.

en.question: Can you get an Operating Under the Influence (OUI) charge for driving while taking prescription drugs?

choices.A: No, prescription drugs are legal and exempt from OUI laws.
choices.B: Yes, it is illegal to operate a motor vehicle while impaired by any substance, including prescription drugs.
choices.C: Only if the prescription drug is mixed with alcohol.
choices.D: Only if the prescription is not in your name.

en.explanation: You can be considered OUI with prescription drugs. It is illegal to operate a motor vehicle while impaired by any substance.

en.question: If you have an outstanding court warrant, what must you present to the RMV before renewing your license?

choices.A: A letter from your attorney
choices.B: A recall notice from the court
choices.C: A receipt showing you paid a fine
choices.D: A new passport or birth certificate

en.explanation: For an outstanding court warrant, a recall notice from the court is required before renewing your license. No other documents will be accepted by the RMV.

en.question: What is the speed limit on roads near schools in Massachusetts?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 30 mph

en.explanation: The manual states that the speed limit on roads near schools is 20 mph.

en.question: How is a 'thickly settled district' defined in the driver's manual?

choices.A: An area where buildings are fewer than 200 feet apart for a distance of 1/4 mile or more.
choices.B: An area where buildings are fewer than 100 feet apart for a distance of 1/2 mile or more.
choices.C: Any residential zone with a posted speed limit of 30 mph.
choices.D: A business district with more than 500 residents per square mile.

en.explanation: A 'thickly settled district' is an area where buildings are fewer than 200 feet apart for a distance of 1/4 mile or more.

en.question: If you drive 40 mph in a heavy rainstorm on a highway with a speed limit of 50 mph, what could happen?

choices.A: You are driving safely within the legal limit and cannot be penalized.
choices.B: You can get a ticket for driving too fast.
choices.C: You must turn on your hazard lights to maintain that speed.
choices.D: You are required to pull over until the rain stops.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you drive 40 mph in a heavy rainstorm on a highway with a speed limit of 50 mph, you can get a ticket for driving too fast.

en.question: Under what circumstances can you make a left turn on a steady red light?

choices.A: Whenever there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Only between the hours of midnight and 6 AM.
choices.C: When driving on a one-way street and turning left onto another one-way street.
choices.D: You may never make a left turn on a red light in Massachusetts.

en.explanation: You can turn left on a red light when driving on a one-way street and turning left onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles.

en.question: What does a flashing red circle traffic signal mean?

choices.A: The traffic signal is broken and you should proceed with caution.
choices.B: It means the same as a STOP sign; you must come to a complete stop.
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic but you do not need to stop.
choices.D: Stop only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk.

en.explanation: A flashing red circle means the same as a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop, obey right-of-way laws, and proceed when safe.

en.question: What action should you take when approaching a steady yellow circle traffic signal?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red.
choices.B: Stop if it is safe to do so, as the signal is changing from green to red.
choices.C: Proceed with caution without reducing your speed.
choices.D: Treat it as a yield sign and merge with traffic.

en.explanation: A steady yellow circle means the traffic signal is changing from green to red. You must stop if it is safe.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow indicate?

choices.A: You have the right-of-way to turn and all other traffic must yield.
choices.B: You cannot make a turn in the direction of the arrow.
choices.C: You may turn in the direction of the arrow when there is an adequate gap in oncoming traffic.
choices.D: The lane is closed ahead and you must merge right.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows you to turn left or right in the direction of the arrow when oncoming traffic has a green light but there is a break in traffic. You must ensure there is an adequate gap.

en.question: What should you do if you approach an intersection where the traffic signals are blacked out and not functioning?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection at your normal speed.
choices.B: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
choices.C: Wait at the intersection until a police officer arrives.
choices.D: Proceed as though there is a stop sign in all directions.

en.explanation: If signals are blacked out and not functioning, be cautious and proceed as though there is a stop sign in all directions.

en.question: Which of the following is a rule regarding pedestrians and crosswalks?

choices.A: You may pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian if the left lane is clear.
choices.B: You must never pass a vehicle that is stopped or slowing for a pedestrian.
choices.C: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles if the crosswalk has no signal.
choices.D: You can block a crosswalk if you are waiting to make a right turn.

en.explanation: Under 'Laws for Drivers', the manual explicitly states: 'Never pass a vehicle that is stopped or slowing for a pedestrian.'

en.question: What does a brown traffic sign indicate?

choices.A: Motorist services such as gas or food.
choices.B: Construction or maintenance warning.
choices.C: Recreational, historic, or scenic site.
choices.D: Incident management.

en.explanation: According to the manual's section on sign colors, a brown sign indicates a recreational, historic, or scenic site.

en.question: Which color is used for incident management signs?

choices.A: Orange
choices.B: Fluorescent Pink
choices.C: Purple
choices.D: Fluorescent Yellow-Green

en.explanation: The manual specifies that Fluorescent Pink is used for incident management signs.

en.question: When approaching a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB), what must you do when the top two red lights are solid?

choices.A: Proceed with caution.
choices.B: Prepare to stop.
choices.C: Stop for pedestrians.
choices.D: Stop and proceed with caution if clear.

en.explanation: When the top two red lights are solid on a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, you must stop for pedestrians.

en.question: When turning into a driveway or parking lot, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The turning vehicle has the right-of-way over pedestrians.
choices.B: You must yield to pedestrians when turning into a driveway or parking lot.
choices.C: Pedestrians must wait for all turning vehicles to pass.
choices.D: The vehicle exiting the parking lot has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: Under 'Laws for Drivers,' the manual states: 'You must yield to pedestrians when turning into a driveway or parking lot.'

en.question: What is the proper procedure when approaching a STOP sign?

choices.A: Slow down to 5 mph and proceed if the intersection is clear.
choices.B: Come to a complete stop before any crosswalk or stop line painted on the pavement.
choices.C: Stop only if there is cross traffic approaching.
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn other drivers before rolling through.

en.explanation: When approaching a stop sign, you must stop before any crosswalk or stop line painted on the pavement. Come to a complete stop; just slowing down is not enough.

en.question: What must a driver do when a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon is activated and its amber lights are flashing?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the crosswalk quickly.
choices.B: Stop for pedestrians.
choices.C: Move to the left lane to avoid the crosswalk.
choices.D: Treat it as a yield sign and proceed if no pedestrians are visible.

en.explanation: When a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon is activated, amber lights flash in an irregular pattern, and you must stop for pedestrians.

en.question: At an intersection controlled by a 4-WAY or ALL WAY STOP sign, which vehicle has the right of way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the right
choices.B: The first vehicle to arrive at the intersection
choices.C: The vehicle traveling straight
choices.D: The largest vehicle

en.explanation: According to the manual, at a 4-WAY or ALL WAY stop, the first vehicle in the intersection or four-way stop has the right of way.

en.question: What type of information do blue guide signs provide to motorists?

choices.A: Highway directions and interchanges
choices.B: Public recreational areas and state parks
choices.C: Motorist services such as gas, food, and lodging
choices.D: Traffic laws and regulations

en.explanation: The manual states that blue signs list motorist services, like gas, food, and lodging.

en.question: Which color guide sign directs drivers to public recreational areas, state and national parks, and points of interest?

choices.A: Green
choices.B: Blue
choices.C: Brown
choices.D: Yellow

en.explanation: Brown signs direct you to public recreational areas, state and national parks, points of interest, and scenic sites.

en.question: What does a regulatory sign featuring a red circle with a diagonal slash indicate?

choices.A: A hazard is ahead
choices.B: Something is prohibited
choices.C: You must yield the right-of-way
choices.D: A detour is required

en.explanation: Regulatory signs that use a red circle with a diagonal slash mean that something is prohibited.

en.question: If a railroad crossing's red lights begin to flash, what is the minimum distance you must stop before the light post or gate?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 20 feet

en.explanation: If the lights begin to flash at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet before the light post or gate.

en.question: When driving through a work zone, what should you do if a traffic officer's directions conflict with existing traffic signs or signals?

choices.A: Follow the traffic signs and signals
choices.B: Obey the traffic officer's directions
choices.C: Stop and wait for the signs to change
choices.D: Pull over and call 511

en.explanation: You must always obey directions of a traffic officer, even when they overrule signs, signals, or pavement markings.

en.question: What is the FIRST thing you must do when approaching a work zone?

choices.A: Change lanes immediately
choices.B: Turn on your hazard lights
choices.C: Slow down and look for guidance
choices.D: Stop and wait for a civil flagger

en.explanation: The manual states that when approaching a work zone, the FIRST thing you must do is SLOW DOWN and look for guidance on how to safely travel through the area.

en.question: What does a double solid white line separating two lanes of traffic indicate?

choices.A: Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed
choices.B: Traffic is moving in the same direction and crossing the line is not allowed
choices.C: Traffic is moving in opposite directions and crossing is not allowed
choices.D: Traffic is moving in the same direction and you may cross to change lanes

en.explanation: A double solid white line separates two lanes of traffic going in the same direction. Crossing a double solid white line is not allowed.

en.question: Under what circumstances should you cross a single solid white line separating lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction?

choices.A: Whenever you need to pass a slower vehicle
choices.B: Only when you need to avoid danger
choices.C: When you are preparing to make a left turn
choices.D: You may never cross a solid white line under any circumstances

en.explanation: You can go in the same direction on both sides of a solid white line, but you should not cross it unless you need to avoid danger.

en.question: When are you permitted to cross two solid yellow lines?

choices.A: When passing a slow-moving vehicle
choices.B: When turning left and it is safe to do so
choices.C: When traveling on a one-way street
choices.D: Never

en.explanation: Two solid yellow lines prohibit vehicles from crossing them to pass another vehicle. You may not cross these lines unless turning left when it is safe to do so.

en.question: What does a white diamond symbol painted on the roadway surface indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing is ahead
choices.B: A shared lane for bicycles and motor vehicles
choices.C: A special lane restriction, such as 'high occupancy vehicle (HOV) only'
choices.D: A pedestrian crosswalk

en.explanation: A white diamond symbol means there is a special lane restriction, like 'high occupancy vehicle (HOV) only' or 'bus only.'

en.question: What is the purpose of Shared Lane Markings (Sharrows) on a roadway?

choices.A: To indicate a lane exclusively reserved for bicycles
choices.B: To warn drivers of an upcoming school zone
choices.C: To help bicyclists position themselves in a shared lane and avoid parked vehicle doors
choices.D: To mark the boundary of a pedestrian crosswalk

en.explanation: Shared Lane Markings (Sharrows) help bicyclists position themselves in the right location and direction in a shared lane, helping them avoid being hit by the open door of a parked vehicle.

en.question: What colors are typically used for warning signs that alert drivers to hazards or changes in conditions ahead?

choices.A: Red and white
choices.B: Blue and white
choices.C: Green and white
choices.D: Yellow and fluorescent yellow-green

en.explanation: Yellow and fluorescent yellow-green warning signs warn you of hazards or changes in conditions ahead.

en.question: At a railroad crossing, how can you tell if there is more than one track crossing the road?

choices.A: The crossbuck sign will be painted yellow
choices.B: The number of tracks is posted below the white crossbuck sign
choices.C: There will be two separate stop lines painted on the pavement
choices.D: The warning bell will ring at a faster pace

en.explanation: If more than one track crosses a road, the number of tracks is posted below the crossbuck.

en.question: What is the purpose of the Highway Division's 511 phone service?

choices.A: To request emergency medical assistance
choices.B: To report a stolen vehicle
choices.C: To get up-to-date information about traffic, weather, and construction
choices.D: To schedule a driving test appointment

en.explanation: You can use the 511 phone service to get up-to-date information about traffic and weather conditions and construction projects, and to report problems on the road.

en.question: When is a motor vehicle permitted to drive in a bicycle lane?

choices.A: Whenever the adjacent travel lane is blocked
choices.B: Only when turning on or off the road
choices.C: When passing a slower vehicle
choices.D: Motor vehicles are never allowed in a bicycle lane

en.explanation: According to the manual, motor vehicles may only drive in bicycle lanes when turning on or off the road.

en.question: What does an advisory bicycle lane with dashed lines indicate?

choices.A: Motor vehicles are strictly prohibited from entering the lane.
choices.B: Bicyclists must yield to motor vehicles before entering the lane.
choices.C: Motor vehicles may use the lane space when necessary, but must yield to bicyclists first.
choices.D: The lane is reserved exclusively for high-occupancy vehicles.

en.explanation: Advisory bicycle lanes are dashed to indicate that motor vehicles may use the lane space when necessary, but they must always yield to bicyclists first.

en.question: What should you do if you are stopped at a red light where there is green pavement?

choices.A: Stop directly on the green pavement to trigger the traffic sensor.
choices.B: You should not stop on the green pavement.
choices.C: Proceed through the red light if no bicyclists are present.
choices.D: Pull over to the right side of the green pavement.

en.explanation: The manual states that at a red light, you should not stop on green pavement, which is used in areas where there could be road sharing conflicts.

en.question: What does a yield line painted across an intersection look like?

choices.A: A pair of solid white lines
choices.B: A series of triangles painted next to each other
choices.C: Diagonal yellow stripes
choices.D: A single solid red line

en.explanation: An intersection with a yield sign may have a YIELD line painted across it, which looks like a series of triangles painted next to each other.

en.question: Under what condition may you drive over or park on a channelizing island?

choices.A: When you need to pass a slow-moving vehicle
choices.B: When your vehicle breaks down
choices.C: Only when directed to do so by a police officer
choices.D: When the adjacent lane is closed for construction

en.explanation: You cannot drive over or park a motor vehicle upon any channelizing island, unless directed to do so by a police officer.

en.question: As a general rule, when are you allowed to use a highway breakdown lane for travel or passing?

choices.A: Whenever traffic is backed up
choices.B: During specific posted times on some highways
choices.C: When you are driving a high-occupancy vehicle
choices.D: You are never allowed to use a breakdown lane for travel

en.explanation: As a general rule, do not use a highway breakdown lane for travel or passing. On some highways, however, you may use the breakdown lane for travel during specific times.

en.question: Which of the following is a situation where you are required to use your turn signals?

choices.A: Pulling away from a curb
choices.B: Driving straight through an intersection
choices.C: Stopping at a stop sign
choices.D: Yielding to a pedestrian in a crosswalk

en.explanation: You must signal in certain situations, including changing lanes, turning, pulling away from a curb, pulling over, and entering or exiting an expressway.

en.question: When is it legal to change lanes in the middle of an intersection?

choices.A: When there is no oncoming traffic
choices.B: When you are preparing to make a left turn
choices.C: When the lane you are in is blocked
choices.D: It is never legal to change lanes in the middle of an intersection

en.explanation: Never change lanes in the middle of an intersection. It is illegal and dangerous.

en.question: What should you do if you come to a curve in the road and cannot see ahead?

choices.A: Move to the center of the road and honk your horn
choices.B: Keep to the right and slow down
choices.C: Accelerate to get through the blind spot quickly
choices.D: Turn on your high beam headlights

en.explanation: If you come to a curve in the road and cannot see ahead, keep to the right and slow down.

en.question: Which of the following is a special rule for motorcycles regarding lane usage?

choices.A: Motorcycles may ride up to three abreast in a single lane.
choices.B: Motorcycles are encouraged to ride along pavement lines in heavy traffic.
choices.C: Motorcycles must not ride along pavement lines, between lanes of traffic.
choices.D: Motorcycles must always use the breakdown lane on highways.

en.explanation: Special rules for motorcycles state that riders must not ride along pavement lines, between lanes of traffic, and should ride no more than two abreast.

en.question: What is the proper action to take if you miss your exit on the highway?

choices.A: Stop and carefully back up on the shoulder
choices.B: Make a U-turn at the next median crossing
choices.C: Get off the highway at the next exit
choices.D: Slow down and reverse in the breakdown lane

en.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not stop. Never back up on the highway. Get off the highway at the next exit.

en.question: How far in advance must you signal your exit before reaching a highway exit ramp?

choices.A: At least 100 feet
choices.B: At least 250 feet
choices.C: At least 500 feet
choices.D: At least 1000 feet

en.explanation: Be sure to signal your exit at least 500 feet before you reach the exit ramp.

en.question: On an expressway with three or more lanes in your direction, which lane should you use for passing?

choices.A: The far right lane
choices.B: The middle lane
choices.C: The far left lane
choices.D: The breakdown lane

en.explanation: On an expressway with three or more lanes in your direction, use the far right lane for slower driving, the middle lane for faster driving, and the far left lane for passing.

en.question: To avoid "highway hypnosis" on a long trip, how often should you stop and stretch?

choices.A: Every hour or every 50 miles
choices.B: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choices.C: Every three hours or every 150 miles
choices.D: Every four hours or every 200 miles

en.explanation: If you plan to drive far, stop and stretch every two hours or every 100 miles to avoid highway hypnosis and fatigue.

en.question: What are the three steps you must remember when changing lanes?

choices.A: (1) look, (2) signal, (3) move
choices.B: (1) signal, (2) look, (3) move
choices.C: (1) brake, (2) signal, (3) move
choices.D: (1) accelerate, (2) look, (3) move

en.explanation: When changing lanes, remember these three steps: (1) look, (2) signal, (3) move.

en.question: If you plan to drive far, how often should you stop and stretch?

choices.A: Every hour or 50 miles
choices.B: Every two hours or 100 miles
choices.C: Every three hours or 150 miles
choices.D: Every four hours or 200 miles

en.explanation: The manual advises that if you plan to drive far, you should stop and stretch every two hours or every 100 miles.

en.question: What is the safest course of action if your vehicle breaks down on the highway?

choices.A: Stand near the travel lane to wave for help
choices.B: Move to the breakdown lane and stand outside your vehicle
choices.C: Move to the breakdown lane or shoulder and stay in your vehicle
choices.D: Leave your vehicle in the travel lane and walk to the nearest exit

en.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it to the breakdown lane or shoulder as far from the travel lane as you can, and stay in your vehicle. Standing near the travel lane is dangerous.

en.question: What information can you obtain by dialing the Highway Division's 511 phone service?

choices.A: Emergency medical dispatch services
choices.B: Up-to-date information about traffic, weather conditions, and construction projects
choices.C: Direct connection to the local police department
choices.D: Automated driver's license renewal instructions

en.explanation: The Highway Division has a 511 phone service that provides up-to-date information about traffic, weather conditions, and construction projects.

en.question: How far in advance must you signal your intention to turn while driving on a highway?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 250 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that you must signal your turn at least 100 feet before making a turn, but on a highway, you must signal at least 500 feet before a turn.

en.question: You should not make a U-turn at the crest of a hill or near a curve where you cannot be seen by other drivers from what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Do not make a U-turn at the crest of a hill, near a curve, or anyplace where you or other drivers cannot see 500 feet away.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding a center lane marked as a common left-turn lane?

choices.A: You may use it to pass slower vehicles
choices.B: You may travel in it for up to 200 feet before turning
choices.C: You may not travel in a center turning lane
choices.D: It is reserved exclusively for emergency vehicles

en.explanation: On some two-way roads, a center lane may be marked as a common left-turn lane. The manual explicitly states: 'You may not travel in a center turning lane.'

en.question: When preparing to make a three-point turn, how large of a gap in traffic should you wait for before completing the turn?

choices.A: 5-10 seconds
choices.B: 10-15 seconds
choices.C: 20-30 seconds
choices.D: 40-50 seconds

en.explanation: When performing a three-point turn, you must check for traffic and pedestrians and wait until you have a 20-30 second gap to complete the turn.

en.question: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'right-of-way' rules?

choices.A: They give you the absolute legal right to proceed first
choices.B: They are based on safety and courtesy, and right-of-way is something you give, not take
choices.C: They only apply at intersections controlled by traffic lights
choices.D: They allow you to force other drivers to yield to your vehicle

en.explanation: Right-of-way rules are based on safety and courtesy. They do not give you any 'rights.' The manual states: 'Remember, the right-of-way is something you give, not take.'

en.question: When approaching an intersection not controlled by signs or signals, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: Any vehicle coming from your left
choices.B: Any vehicle that has entered the intersection from your right or is coming from your right
choices.C: Only commercial vehicles and transit buses
choices.D: Vehicles that are turning left across your path

en.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield the right-of-way to any vehicle that has entered the intersection from your right or is coming from your right.

en.question: If you and another vehicle arrive at a four-way stop at the exact same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle directly to your right
choices.B: The vehicle directly to your left
choices.C: The vehicle that is traveling straight
choices.D: The vehicle that is turning right

en.explanation: At a four-way stop, if vehicles stop at the same time, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle directly to your right.

en.question: What must you do when entering a paved thoroughfare from a private road, driveway, or unpaved road?

choices.A: Slow down and merge seamlessly into traffic
choices.B: Sound your horn and proceed without stopping
choices.C: Stop and give the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles on the road you are entering
choices.D: Yield only if there is a posted yield sign

en.explanation: When entering a paved thoroughfare from a private road, a driveway, or an unpaved road, you must stop and then give the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles on the road you are entering.

en.question: If you are turning at an intersection, how should you handle a bicyclist going straight through the same intersection?

choices.A: Speed up to cut in front of the bicyclist
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn the bicyclist to stop
choices.C: Yield to the bicyclist going straight through
choices.D: Force the bicyclist to turn with you

en.explanation: When driving through an intersection, be especially alert for bicyclists. If you're turning, you must yield to bicyclists going straight through an intersection and never cut in front of them.

en.question: When driving through an intersection, when are you legally allowed to block the intersection or crosswalk?

choices.A: When traffic is backed up and you have a green light
choices.B: When you are making a left turn
choices.C: When you are driving a commercial vehicle
choices.D: It is never legal to block an intersection or crosswalk

en.explanation: It is illegal to block an intersection with your vehicle. You may only enter an intersection or drive across a crosswalk if there is enough room for you to drive through safely.

en.question: In what direction does traffic travel in a rotary?

choices.A: Clockwise
choices.B: Counter-clockwise
choices.C: In a figure-eight pattern
choices.D: Straight through without turning

en.explanation: According to the manual, traffic travels counter-clockwise in a rotary.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit while driving in a rotary?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for traffic to clear.
choices.B: Put your vehicle in reverse to back up to the exit.
choices.C: Go around again and position your vehicle to properly and safely exit.
choices.D: Make a sharp right turn from the inner lane immediately.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you miss your exit, don’t get upset. Check the traffic around you. If it is safe to do so, go around again and position your vehicle to properly and safely exit the rotary. Do not stop in the rotary.'

en.question: What is the maximum speed you should travel when driving in a roundabout?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour
choices.B: 25 miles per hour
choices.C: 35 miles per hour
choices.D: 40 miles per hour

en.explanation: Roundabouts are used on busy streets and their small size requires vehicles to reduce speed to 25 miles per hour or less.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to wave another driver in through stopped traffic?

choices.A: It is illegal to use hand gestures while driving.
choices.B: It can cause a 'courtesy crash' because oncoming traffic still has the right-of-way.
choices.C: It distracts pedestrians in the crosswalk.
choices.D: It automatically transfers the right-of-way to the turning vehicle.

en.explanation: Waving people in through stopped traffic creates a dangerous situation and can easily result in a crash. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way, regardless of whether someone is waving at you.

en.question: Which of the following areas is legally permitted for passing another vehicle?

choices.A: The breakdown lane
choices.B: The shoulder of the road
choices.C: The sidewalk
choices.D: None of the above

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Never use a breakdown lane, the shoulder of a road, or a sidewalk for passing another vehicle.'

en.question: When crossing a broken yellow line to pass another vehicle, how far ahead must you be able to see clearly?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 400 feet

en.explanation: If you are crossing a broken yellow line to pass, you must be able to see clearly at least 400 feet in front of you.

en.question: When passing on the left, you must return to the right lane before an oncoming vehicle comes within how many feet of you?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 400 feet

en.explanation: You must return to the right lane before any oncoming vehicle comes within 200 feet of you.

en.question: Under which of the following circumstances are you permitted to pass a vehicle on the right?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit.
choices.B: When the vehicle ahead is making, or is about to make, a left turn.
choices.C: When you are driving on a two-way street with a single lane in each direction.
choices.D: When the vehicle ahead is stopped at a crosswalk.

en.explanation: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle you are passing is making, or is about to make, a left turn, on a one-way street, or on a road where traffic moves in one direction.

en.question: What must you do if you are being passed by another vehicle?

choices.A: Speed up to maintain your position.
choices.B: Move to the left lane.
choices.C: Slow down and stay to the right.
choices.D: Sound your horn to warn the passing driver.

en.explanation: If you are being passed by another vehicle, you must slow down and stay to the right. Allow the other driver to pass safely. Do not speed up.

en.question: What does the 'move-over law' require you to do when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a multi-lane highway?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for the vehicle to leave.
choices.B: Maintain your speed and stay in your current lane.
choices.C: Yield the right-of-way by safely moving over to a lane that is not next to the emergency vehicle.
choices.D: Honk your horn to acknowledge the emergency vehicle.

en.explanation: The 'move-over law' requires that you proceed with caution, reduce your speed, and if on a highway with at least four lanes, safely move over to a lane that is not next to the lane the emergency vehicle is occupying.

en.question: What is the recommended action to take when confronted by an aggressive driver?

choices.A: Make eye contact to show you are not intimidated.
choices.B: Challenge the driver by matching their speed.
choices.C: Attempt to get out of their way and avoid eye contact.
choices.D: Follow them to report their license plate number.

en.explanation: When confronted by an aggressive driver, you should attempt to get out of their way, do not challenge that person, avoid eye contact, and ignore rude gestures.

en.question: When are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with its flashing red lights and stop sign extended?

choices.A: When you are traveling in the opposite direction on a two-lane road.
choices.B: When the school bus is stopped on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier.
choices.C: When you are running late for work.
choices.D: When there are no children visible around the bus.

en.explanation: The only exception to the school bus stopping law is if a school bus has stopped on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier between travel directions.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first violation of failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?

choices.A: A $100 fine and a warning.
choices.B: A license suspension and a $250 fine.
choices.C: A $500 fine and vehicle impoundment.
choices.D: Mandatory community service.

en.explanation: A first violation of the law requiring you to stop for a school bus with flashing lights can cause a license suspension and a $250 fine.

en.question: How can you tell if you are tailgating a large truck?

choices.A: You are within 100 feet of the truck.
choices.B: You cannot see the truck's rearview mirrors.
choices.C: You can read the truck's license plate.
choices.D: You are driving slower than the truck.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you cannot see a truck’s rearview mirrors, you are tailgating.'

en.question: Which lane should you use to enter a multiple-lane rotary if you intend to make a three-quarter-turn or a U-turn?

choices.A: The right lane
choices.B: The left lane
choices.C: The breakdown lane
choices.D: Any lane is acceptable

en.question: According to studies, how much distance might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop compared to a passenger vehicle?

choices.B: One and a half times as far
choices.C: Twice as far
choices.D: Three times as far

en.explanation: Studies by the National Safety Council and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety show that a fully loaded tractor trailer may take twice as far to stop as a passenger vehicle.

en.question: When a trolley is letting passengers on or off, what is the closest distance you may drive to the trolley passenger step?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 8 feet
choices.C: 10 feet
choices.D: 12 feet

en.explanation: State law requires that you must not drive closer than eight feet of a trolley passenger step when the trolley is letting passengers on or off.

en.question: What type of sign is typically attached to the back of farm vehicles, construction rigs, and other slow-moving vehicles?

choices.A: A yellow diamond sign
choices.B: A red and white triangular sign
choices.C: An orange warning sign
choices.D: A green rectangular sign

en.explanation: Most farm vehicles, construction rigs, and other slow-moving vehicles have orange warning signs attached to the back.

en.question: Funeral processions have the right-of-way at intersections, EXCEPT when they must yield to:

choices.A: Pedestrians in crosswalks
choices.B: Oncoming traffic with a green light
choices.C: Emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens
choices.D: Public transport buses

en.explanation: Funeral processions have the right-of-way at intersections, with the EXCEPTION that they must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens or when directed by law enforcement.

en.question: If you are driving as part of a funeral procession on a highway with a speed limit of 55 MPH or higher, what is the maximum speed you are allowed to drive?

choices.A: 45 MPH
choices.B: 50 MPH
choices.C: 55 MPH
choices.D: 60 MPH

en.explanation: If driving as part of a funeral procession, you must not drive faster than 55 MPH on a highway with a speed limit of 55 MPH or higher.

en.question: If your vehicle is NOT part of a funeral procession, which of the following actions is permitted?

choices.A: Driving between procession vehicles if you are in a hurry
choices.B: Joining the procession to bypass traffic
choices.C: Passing the procession on the right on a multiple-lane highway if the procession is in the far left lane
choices.D: Crossing an intersection on a green light while the procession is passing through a red light, even if it crosses their path

en.explanation: You may not pass a procession on a multiple lane highway on the procession’s right, unless the procession is in the far left lane.

en.question: What is the penalty for being cited for speeding in a "work area"?

choices.A: Your license will be suspended for 30 days
choices.B: The fine will be doubled
choices.C: You will receive a warning for the first offense
choices.D: You must attend a driver retraining course

en.explanation: If you are cited for speeding in a “work area”, the fine will be doubled.

en.question: What must you do if you are passing an animal being led, ridden, or driven, and the animal looks scared?

choices.A: Honk your horn lightly to warn the animal
choices.B: Accelerate to pass the animal quickly
choices.C: Pull your vehicle to the side and stop
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights and continue at the same speed

en.explanation: If the animal you are passing looks scared, you must pull your vehicle to the side and stop.

en.question: When parking your vehicle, you must always make sure to leave a clear roadway for passing traffic that is at least how wide?

choices.A: 8 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 12 feet
choices.D: 15 feet

en.explanation: You must always make sure that you leave at least a 12-foot wide, clear roadway for traffic to pass.

en.question: If you park in a business or residential district, what is the maximum distance your vehicle can be from the curb (unless angled parking is allowed)?

choices.A: 6 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 24 inches

en.explanation: If you park in a business or residential district, your vehicle must be no more than 12 inches from the curb. The only exception is if angled parking is allowed.

en.question: State law requires you to take several actions when leaving your vehicle by itself. Which of the following is NOT explicitly listed as one of these required actions?

choices.A: Stop the motor
choices.B: Set the parking brake
choices.C: Turn on your hazard lights
choices.D: Remove your key and lock the door

en.explanation: When you leave your vehicle by itself, state law requires you to stop the motor, set the parking brake, make sure the ignition is locked, remove your key, and lock the door. Turning on hazard lights is not listed.

en.question: When slowly backing up to parallel park, where should you look?

choices.A: Directly out your rear window
choices.B: In your rearview mirror
choices.C: In your side mirrors
choices.D: At your backup camera display

en.explanation: When slowly backing up to parallel park, the manual instructs to "Look directly out your rear window. Do not use your mirrors."

en.question: Why should you avoid passing a truck or bus on the right unless absolutely necessary?

choices.A: Large vehicles are required to drive in the far left lane
choices.B: Large vehicles travel faster downhill
choices.C: Large vehicles make wide turns and may move left before turning right
choices.D: Passing on the right is illegal on all multiple-lane highways

en.explanation: Do not pass a truck or bus on the right unless absolutely necessary. Large vehicles make wide turns, and sometimes they must move to the left before making a wide turn to the right.

en.question: If a large vehicle is coming toward you on an undivided road, why should you stay to the right?

choices.A: To give the large vehicle room to pass other cars
choices.B: To avoid being sideswiped or shaken by air turbulence
choices.C: To prepare for a right turn
choices.D: To allow the large vehicle to see your headlights better

en.explanation: If a large vehicle is coming toward you on an undivided road, stay to the right. You will avoid being sideswiped or shaken by air turbulence.

en.question: When parking uphill against a curb, which way should you turn your vehicle's front wheels?

choices.A: Inward, toward the curb
choices.B: Outward, toward the travel lane
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: Inward, toward the edge of the road

en.explanation: When parking uphill against a curb, you must turn your wheels outward, toward the travel lane to stop it from rolling downhill if the brake fails.

en.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle within how many feet of a fire hydrant or fire lane?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 20 feet

en.explanation: In Massachusetts, you may not park your vehicle within ten feet of a fire hydrant or fire lane.

en.question: What is the penalty for parking in a posted bus stop in Massachusetts?
en.explanation: The penalty for parking in a posted bus stop is $100.

en.question: You are prohibited from parking your vehicle within how many feet of an intersection?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.explanation: You may not park your vehicle within 20 feet of an intersection.

en.question: What is the minimum fine for the wrongful use of a disabled person or veteran plate or placard?
en.explanation: The fine for wrongful use of a disabled person or veteran plate or placard is a minimum of $500.

en.question: How must you dispose of used motor oil and transmission fluid?

choices.A: Pour it down a storm drain
choices.B: Throw it in the regular trash
choices.C: Return it to the place you bought it
choices.D: Leave it at a local fire station

en.explanation: You must return used motor oil, transmission fluid, and other hazardous materials to the place you bought them. The garage or store that sold it to you is responsible for disposing of it.

en.question: If no sidewalk is available, where should a pedestrian walk?

choices.A: On the shoulder facing traffic
choices.B: On the shoulder in the same direction as traffic
choices.C: In the center of the travel lane
choices.D: In the bicycle lane only

en.explanation: When no sidewalk is available, pedestrians should walk on the shoulder facing traffic.

en.question: A bicycle helmet approved by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission must be worn by a bicycle operator or passenger under what age?

choices.A: 12 years old
choices.B: 14 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: A bicycle helmet approved by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission must be worn by a bicycle operator or passenger under 16 years old.

en.question: Under what age is it illegal to transport a child on a bicycle?

choices.A: Under 1 year old
choices.B: Under 2 years old
choices.C: Under 3 years old
choices.D: Under 4 years old

en.explanation: You cannot transport a child under the age of one year on a bicycle.

en.question: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, a bicyclist must have a white front lamp visible from up to how many feet?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 600 feet

en.explanation: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, you must have a white lamp in front visible from up to 500 feet.

en.question: A bicycle must have a proper working brake system capable of stopping from 15 MPH within what distance?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: You must have a proper working brake system to stop from 15 MPH within 30 feet.

en.question: What is the maximum number of bicycles that can be operated side-by-side on a roadway?

choices.A: One (single file only)
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: No more than two bicycles can be operated side-by-side.

en.question: To avoid opening car doors, bicyclists should ride outside the 'door zone' by keeping at least how far from parked cars?

choices.A: One foot
choices.B: Two feet
choices.C: Three feet
choices.D: Five feet

en.explanation: Bicyclists should ride outside of the 'door zone' (at least three feet from parked cars) and watch for opening car doors.

en.question: A bicyclist must report a crash to the police if it involves personal injury or property damage in excess of what amount?
en.explanation: You must report any crash involving personal injury and any crash involving property damage in excess of $100 to the police in the municipality where it occurred.

en.question: When passing a bicycle in a narrow lane, what is the minimum distance you must maintain between your vehicle and the bicyclist?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that if a lane is too narrow to pass a bicycle at a safe distance, you must wait until it is safe and stay at least four feet away when passing.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a driver or passenger who opens a vehicle door into an oncoming bicycle?
en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers and passengers can be fined up to $100 for opening a vehicle door into an oncoming bicycle.

en.question: Are bicyclists legally allowed to ride two side-by-side on the road?

choices.A: No, they must always ride single file.
choices.B: Yes, but on a road with more than one lane in the direction of travel, they must stay in one lane.
choices.C: Yes, and they may occupy multiple lanes if needed.
choices.D: No, unless they are passing another bicyclist.

en.explanation: The manual notes that bicyclists can ride two bicycles side-by-side. However, on a road with more than one lane in the direction of travel, they must stay in one lane.

en.question: Why might a bicyclist legally choose not to use a hand signal to indicate a turn?

choices.A: Hand signals are only required for motor vehicles.
choices.B: They are traveling below 10 mph.
choices.C: Both hands are needed for the bicycle's safe operation.
choices.D: They are riding in a designated bicycle lane.

en.explanation: Bicyclists must signal their intent to stop or turn, but the signal does not have to be made if both hands are needed for the bicycle's safe operation.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Dutch Reach' method?

choices.A: To safely pass a bicyclist on a narrow road.
choices.B: To open a vehicle door with the far hand, forcing the body to turn and see approaching bicyclists.
choices.C: To allow bicyclists to make a two-stage left turn at an intersection.
choices.D: To steer a vehicle safely out of a skid.

en.explanation: The 'Dutch Reach' method involves opening the door with your far hand, which forces your body to turn and better allows you to see approaching bicyclists before opening the door.

en.question: What must a driver do when approaching a red light at an intersection with a green 'bicycle box' painted on the pavement?

choices.A: Stop inside the bicycle box to trigger the traffic light sensor.
choices.B: Stop behind the bicycle box, even when it is empty, and wait for a green light.
choices.C: Enter the bicycle box only if turning right on red.
choices.D: Honk to clear the bicycle box before proceeding.

en.explanation: Drivers must stop behind the bicycle box (even when it's empty) and wait for a green light.

en.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights approaches while you are in the middle of an intersection?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the intersection and wait for it to pass.
choices.B: Put your vehicle in reverse and back out of the intersection.
choices.C: Drive through the intersection and pull over to the right as soon as it is safe.
choices.D: Pull over to the left side of the intersection.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'NEVER stop in the middle of an intersection. Drive through the intersection and pull over as soon as it is safe.'

en.question: It is illegal to follow closer than what distance behind an emergency vehicle responding to an alarm?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: According to the manual, it is illegal to follow closer than 300 feet behind an emergency vehicle responding to an alarm.

en.question: Under the 'move-over law,' what must you do when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a highway with at least two lanes traveling in your direction?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle immediately and wait for instructions.
choices.B: Maintain your speed but move to the left lane.
choices.C: Reduce your speed and safely move to a lane that is not next to the emergency vehicle.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert the emergency workers of your presence.

en.explanation: The move-over law requires drivers to reduce speed and yield the right-of-way by safely moving over to a lane that is not next to the lane the emergency vehicle is in.

en.question: According to the RMV Crash Data Department, approximately what percentage of highway crashes involve drivers under 25 years old?

choices.A: 15 percent
choices.B: 25 percent
choices.C: 40 percent
choices.D: 60 percent

en.explanation: The manual states that about 40 percent of highway crashes involve drivers under 25 years old, mostly caused by driver inexperience.

en.question: How far should bicyclists ride from parked cars to avoid getting hit by opening vehicle doors?

choices.A: At least 1 foot
choices.B: At least 2 feet
choices.C: At least 3 feet
choices.D: At least 5 feet

en.explanation: Bicyclists should ride at least three feet from parked cars to avoid doors and stay outside of the 'door zone'.

en.question: What is the rule regarding bicyclists wearing headphones or earbuds?

choices.A: They may wear them in both ears if the volume is kept low.
choices.B: They are completely prohibited from wearing any headphones.
choices.C: They must not wear headphones or earbuds in both ears while biking.
choices.D: They can wear them only when riding in a separated bicycle lane.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Do not wear headphones or earbuds in both ears while biking.'

en.question: Which of the following is a critical safety rule for bicyclists sharing the road with large vehicles?

choices.A: Always pass a moving tractor trailer on the right.
choices.B: Never pass a moving tractor trailer on the right.
choices.C: Ride directly in the rear blind spot to draft behind the truck.
choices.D: Pass buses on the right to avoid oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: The manual warns bicyclists to be especially careful around large vehicles and states, 'Never pass a moving tractor trailer on the right.'

en.question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights, which of the following actions is unacceptable?

choices.A: Pulling as close as possible to the right side of the road.
choices.B: Using your right turn signal to indicate you are pulling over.
choices.C: Slowly rolling while the emergency vehicle passes.
choices.D: Stopping completely until the vehicle has passed.

en.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches, you must pull to the right and stop. The manual specifies that 'Slowly rolling is not acceptable.'

en.question: When turning left at an intersection, what must a driver do if a bicycle is approaching from the opposite direction?

choices.A: Speed up to complete the turn before the bicycle arrives.
choices.B: Yield the right of way to the bicycle if it is close enough to be an immediate hazard.
choices.C: Honk to warn the bicyclist to stop.
choices.D: Proceed with the turn, as motor vehicles have the right of way over bicycles.

en.explanation: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction, including a bicycle, if it is in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

en.question: If you need assistance from a police officer who is in a parked cruiser, where should you position your vehicle?

choices.A: Directly behind the police cruiser
choices.B: Beside the police cruiser in the travel lane
choices.C: In front of the police cruiser
choices.D: Across the street from the police cruiser
