choices.B: Hará que el agua entre de golpe y su vehículo podría volcarse.
choices.C: Atrapará la bolsa de aire en el asiento trasero.
choices.D: Desplegará las bolsas de aire innecesariamente.

es.explanation: Si su automóvil cae al agua, no debe abrir la puerta porque eso haría que el agua entrara de golpe y su vehículo podría volcarse.

es.question: Si hay un incendio mientras conduce por un túnel, ¿qué debe hacer con las llaves de su vehículo?

choices.A: Llevárselas con usted cuando salga del vehículo.
choices.B: Tirarlas por la ventana.
choices.C: Dejarlas en el vehículo para ayudar al personal de emergencia.
choices.D: Esconderlas debajo del asiento del conductor.

es.explanation: En caso de incendio en un túnel, debe detenerse, apagar el motor, salir de su vehículo y dejar las llaves en el vehículo para ayudar al personal de emergencia.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes está explícitamente prohibido al entrar en un túnel en Massachusetts?

choices.A: Combustible diésel
choices.B: Propano
choices.C: Vehículos comerciales
choices.D: Camionetas de pasajeros

es.explanation: Al entrar en un túnel, están prohibidos los materiales peligrosos, incluido el propano.

es.question: Según la Ley de Retiro del Conductor (Driver Removal Law), ¿qué debe hacer si se ve involucrado en un choque sin heridos?

choices.A: Dejar los vehículos exactamente donde están hasta que llegue la policía.
choices.B: Mover los vehículos fuera de los carriles de circulación a un lugar seguro.
choices.C: Esperar a una grúa antes de intentar mover los vehículos.
choices.D: Dirigir el tráfico alrededor de su vehículo mientras lo deja en el carril de circulación.

es.explanation: Si no hay heridos, la Ley de Retiro del Conductor exige que los vehículos se muevan fuera de los carriles de circulación a un lugar seguro.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene para presentar un informe de accidente ante el RMV y la policía local si se ve involucrado en un choque con daños a la propiedad de $1,000 o más?

choices.A: 2 días
choices.B: 3 días
choices.C: 5 días
choices.D: 10 días

es.explanation: Dentro de los cinco días posteriores al choque, debe presentar un informe de accidente tanto al RMV como al departamento de policía local por cualquier choque con daños a la propiedad de $1,000 o más.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer si lesiona a un animal, como un perro o un gato, en un accidente de vehículo motorizado?

choices.A: Mover al animal a un lado de la carretera e irse de la escena.
choices.B: Llevar al animal a la clínica veterinaria más cercana de inmediato.
choices.C: Notificar a la policía local y, si es posible, al dueño del animal.
choices.D: Presentar un informe de accidente ante el RMV dentro de las 24 horas.

es.explanation: Si ha lesionado a un gato, perro o cualquier otro animal, debe notificar a la policía local y, si es posible, al dueño del animal.

es.question: Al brindar primeros auxilios de emergencia en la escena de un choque, ¿por qué debería cubrir a una persona lesionada con una manta o un abrigo?

choices.A: Para ocultar sus heridas a otros conductores.
choices.B: Para proporcionar calor y prevenir el estado de choque (shock).
choices.C: Para evitar que se muevan.
choices.D: Para elevar su temperatura corporal por encima de lo normal.

es.explanation: Los consejos de primeros auxilios de emergencia indican cubrir a la persona lesionada con una manta o un abrigo para proporcionar calor y prevenir el estado de choque (shock).

es.question: ¿Cuál es una posible consecuencia de abandonar la escena de un choque sin identificarse adecuadamente?

choices.A: Solo recibirá una advertencia si es su primera infracción.
choices.B: Se le requerirá tomar un curso de conducción defensiva.
choices.C: Podría ser acusado penalmente de una infracción por "abandonar la escena".
choices.D: Sus tarifas de seguro disminuirán.

es.explanation: Si abandona la escena después de un choque sin identificarse adecuadamente, podría ser acusado penalmente de una infracción por "abandonar la escena".

es.question: ¿Cuál es la sanción máxima por abandonar la escena de un choque que causa daños a otro vehículo o propiedad?

choices.A: Hasta $200 o hasta dos años de prisión, o ambos
choices.B: Hasta $500 y un año de prisión
choices.C: Hasta $1000 y seis meses de prisión
choices.D: Una multa obligatoria de $500 y la revocación de la licencia

es.explanation: Según el manual, abandonar la escena después de un choque que cause daños a otro vehículo o propiedad puede resultar en sanciones de hasta $200 o hasta dos años de prisión, o ambos.

es.question: ¿A qué sanción se enfrenta si abandona la escena de un choque que causa lesiones personales a una persona (que no resulten en muerte)?

choices.A: Hasta $500 y un año de prisión
choices.B: Hasta $1000 y prisión de hasta dos años
choices.C: Hasta $2000 y cinco años de prisión
choices.D: Hasta $5000 y diez años de prisión

es.explanation: El manual establece que abandonar la escena después de un choque que cause lesiones personales (que no resulten en muerte) conlleva una sanción máxima de hasta $1000 y prisión de hasta dos años.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer si golpea y lesiona o mata a un gato o perro con su vehículo?

choices.A: Mover al animal a un lado de la carretera e irse
choices.B: Notificar al dueño del animal o a la policía local
choices.C: Llevar al animal a la clínica veterinaria más cercana de inmediato
choices.D: Presentar un informe por escrito ante el RMV dentro de los 5 días

es.explanation: El manual establece: 'Si golpea y lesiona o mata a un gato o perro y no notifica al dueño del animal o a la policía local, puede ser multado bajo el Capítulo 272 de las M.G.L., Sección 80H'.

es.question: ¿Durante cuánto tiempo puede estar sujeto a recargos en el seguro tras una condena penal por abandonar la escena de un choque?

choices.A: Hasta dos años
choices.B: Hasta cuatro años
choices.C: Hasta seis años
choices.D: Hasta diez años

es.explanation: Cualquier condena penal puede resultar en costos de libertad condicional y usted puede estar sujeto a hasta seis años de recargos en el seguro.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer si pasa por un choque y la policía y los vehículos de emergencia ya están allí?

choices.A: Detener su vehículo para ver si puede ayudar a la policía
choices.B: Reducir la velocidad para 'curiosear' y tomar fotos para evidencia
choices.C: Reducir su velocidad, conducir con cuidado y no detenerse ni reducir la velocidad para 'curiosear'
choices.D: Tocar la bocina para advertir a los trabajadores de emergencia de su presencia

es.explanation: Si la policía y los vehículos de emergencia están presentes, debe reducir su velocidad y conducir con cuidado. El manual establece explícitamente: 'No se detenga ni reduzca la velocidad para curiosear. Esto es peligroso y causará un problema de tráfico'.

es.question: Si usted es el primero en llegar a la escena de un choque y tiene bengalas o triángulos de emergencia, ¿dónde debe colocarlos?

choices.A: 50 pies o más por delante y por detrás del choque
choices.B: 100 pies o más por delante y por detrás del choque
choices.C: 200 pies o más por delante y por detrás del choque
choices.D: 500 pies o más por delante y por detrás del choque

es.explanation: Si alguien tiene bengalas, triángulos de emergencia o reflectores, debe colocarlos a 200 pies o más por delante y por detrás del choque para advertir a otros conductores.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer si han caído cables eléctricos sobre un vehículo involucrado en un choque?

choices.A: Decirle a las personas que están dentro que permanezcan allí hasta que llegue el personal de emergencia
choices.B: Retirar con cuidado los cables del vehículo usando un objeto no conductor
choices.C: Indicar a los ocupantes que salten fuera del vehículo sin tocar el marco de metal
choices.D: Abrir las puertas desde afuera para ayudar a los ocupantes a escapar

es.explanation: El manual advierte: 'Si han caído cables eléctricos sobre un vehículo, dígale a las personas que están dentro que permanezcan allí hasta que llegue el personal de emergencia. No toque el vehículo'.

es.question: ¿Bajo qué condiciones está legalmente obligado a presentar un informe de choque por escrito ante el RMV?

choices.A: Solo si alguien muere o resulta herido, independientemente de los daños a la propiedad
choices.B: Si alguien muere o resulta herido, o si hay $1,000 o más en daños a la propiedad
choices.C: Si hay $500 o más en daños a la propiedad
choices.D: Solo si el choque involucra a más de dos vehículos

es.explanation: Debe informar cualquier choque de vehículo motorizado en el que esté involucrado que cause la muerte o lesiones a alguien, o que cause $1,000 o más en daños a la propiedad.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene para presentar un informe de choque por escrito ante el RMV después de un choque que califique?

choices.A: Dentro de las 24 horas
choices.B: Dentro de 3 días
choices.C: Dentro de 5 días
choices.D: Dentro de 10 días

es.explanation: Debe presentar un informe por escrito ante el RMV dentro de los cinco días posteriores al choque.

es.question: Cuando se le requiere presentar un informe de choque, ¿a qué tres entidades debe enviar una copia?

choices.A: Al RMV, al departamento de bomberos local y a su compañía de seguros
choices.B: Al departamento de policía local, a su compañía de seguros y al RMV
choices.C: A la Policía Estatal, al RMV y al Departamento de Transporte
choices.D: A su compañía de seguros, a la compañía de seguros del otro conductor y al RMV

es.explanation: Los informes completados deben enviarse a: 1. El departamento de policía local donde ocurrió el choque, 2. Su compañía de seguros y 3. El RMV.

es.question: Según los consejos de 'Conducción Ecológica' (Green Driving), ¿cómo afecta el conducir a más de 60 mph el consumo de combustible de su vehículo?

choices.A: El consumo de combustible aumenta aproximadamente un cinco por ciento por cada cinco millas por hora que se conduzca por encima de las 60 mph
choices.B: El consumo de combustible disminuye en un dos por ciento por cada cinco millas por hora que se conduzca por encima de las 60 mph
choices.C: El consumo de combustible sigue siendo el mismo siempre que use el control de crucero
choices.D: El consumo de combustible aumenta en un diez por ciento por cada milla por hora que se conduzca por encima de las 60 mph

es.explanation: El manual establece: 'El consumo de combustible aumenta aproximadamente un cinco por ciento por cada cinco millas por hora que se conduzca por encima de las 60 mph'.

es.question: ¿Cuánto pueden aumentar su consumo de combustible los arranques rápidos y las paradas bruscas?

choices.A: En un 10 por ciento
choices.B: En un 25 por ciento
choices.C: En un 40 por ciento
choices.D: En un 50 por ciento

es.explanation: Los arranques rápidos y las paradas bruscas pueden aumentar el uso de combustible en un 40 por ciento, pero reducen el tiempo de viaje en solo un cuatro por ciento.

es.question: Según la ley estatal de Massachusetts, ¿cuál es el tiempo máximo que se permite que un vehículo esté en ralentí (motor encendido sin movimiento)?

choices.A: Un minuto
choices.B: Tres minutos
choices.C: Cinco minutos
choices.D: Diez minutos

es.explanation: La ley estatal de Massachusetts prohíbe dejar el motor en ralentí por más de cinco minutos.

es.question: Al hacer varios mandados, ¿cómo debe 'encadenar' sus viajes para obtener una mejor economía de combustible?

choices.A: Ir primero a su destino más cercano para ahorrar tiempo
choices.B: Ir primero a su destino más lejano para calentar el motor más rápidamente
choices.C: Hacer todas sus paradas durante la hora pico para evitar altas velocidades
choices.D: Dejar el auto en ralentí en cada parada para mantener el motor caliente

es.explanation: El manual sugiere que cuando realice varias paradas, debe ir primero a su destino más lejano para calentar el motor más rápidamente y obtener una mejor economía de combustible.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: Reducir la velocidad y proceder con precaución
choices.B: Detenerse por completo
choices.C: Ceder el paso al tráfico que viene en sentido contrario
choices.D: Detenerse solo si hay otros vehículos presentes

es.explanation: Una señal de PARE (STOP) roja y octagonal significa que debe detenerse por completo en la línea de parada, el paso de peatones o antes de entrar en la intersección. Verifique el tráfico y los peatones antes de continuar.

es.question: ¿Qué le obliga a hacer esta señal?

choices.A: Detenerse por completo
choices.B: Acelerar para incorporarse al tráfico
choices.C: Reducir la velocidad y ceder el paso al tráfico y a los peatones
choices.D: Continuar sin detenerse

es.explanation: Una señal de CEDA EL PASO (YIELD) roja y blanca en forma de triángulo significa que debe reducir la velocidad y ceder el derecho de paso al tráfico y a los peatones. Debe detenerse si es necesario para permitir que otros pasen de manera segura.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: Camino cerrado adelante
choices.B: No se permite estacionar
choices.C: No entre en esta calzada
choices.D: Calle sin salida adelante

es.explanation: Una señal roja y blanca de NO ENTRE (DO NOT ENTER) significa que no debe entrar en la carretera o rampa donde está colocada esta señal. Generalmente se ve en las rampas de salida de las autopistas o en calles de un solo sentido donde entrar lo pondría en la trayectoria del tráfico en sentido contrario.

es.question: Si ve esta señal, ¿qué debe hacer?

choices.A: Hacer un giro en U
choices.B: Continuar conduciendo con cuidado
choices.C: Detenerse y retroceder o dar la vuelta — va en sentido contrario
choices.D: Acelerar para salir del área rápidamente

es.explanation: Una señal roja y blanca de SENTIDO CONTRARIO (WRONG WAY) significa que está viajando en contra del tráfico en una calle de un solo sentido o en una rampa de autopista. Deténgase inmediatamente y dé la vuelta o retroceda de manera segura.

es.question: ¿Qué indica esta señal?

choices.A: Solo giro a la izquierda
choices.B: El tráfico fluye en una sola dirección — hacia la izquierda
choices.C: Manténgase a la izquierda de la mediana
choices.D: Salida de la autopista a la izquierda

es.explanation: Una señal de UN SOLO SENTIDO (ONE WAY) en blanco y negro con una flecha indica que el tráfico en esta calle se mueve en una sola dirección — la dirección hacia la que apunta la flecha.

es.question: ¿Qué prohíbe esta señal?

choices.A: Giros a la derecha
choices.B: Giros a la izquierda
choices.C: Giros en U
choices.D: Rebasar a otros vehículos

es.explanation: Una señal reglamentaria blanca con una flecha de giro en U tachada significa que los giros en U están prohibidos en este lugar.

es.question: ¿Qué acción está prohibida por esta señal?

choices.A: Girar a la derecha
choices.B: Girar a la izquierda
choices.C: Hacer un giro en U
choices.D: Seguir recto

es.explanation: Una señal reglamentaria blanca que muestra una flecha de giro a la izquierda tachada significa que no se permiten los giros a la izquierda en esta intersección.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: No se permite el giro en U
choices.B: No se permite el giro a la izquierda
choices.C: No se permite el giro a la derecha
choices.D: No se permite rebasar

es.explanation: Una señal reglamentaria blanca que muestra una flecha de giro a la derecha tachada significa que los giros a la derecha están prohibidos en este lugar.

es.question: ¿Qué indica esta señal?

choices.A: El camino se estrecha adelante
choices.B: No rebase a otros vehículos en esta zona
choices.C: Tráfico en ambos sentidos adelante
choices.D: Manténgase a la derecha

es.explanation: Una señal en forma de banderín en blanco y negro de ZONA DE NO REBASAR (NO PASSING ZONE) significa que no se le permite rebasar a otros vehículos en esta área. Marca el comienzo de una zona de no rebasar.

es.question: ¿Qué instruye esta señal a los conductores?

choices.A: Incorporarse a la derecha
choices.B: Solo giro a la derecha
choices.C: Mantenerse a la derecha de un divisor u obstrucción
choices.D: El carril derecho termina adelante

es.explanation: Una señal reglamentaria blanca de MANTÉNGASE A LA DERECHA (KEEP RIGHT) con una flecha significa que debe mantenerse en el lado derecho de una isla de tráfico, mediana u obstrucción.

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de señal es esta, según su forma y color?

choices.A: Una señal de advertencia
choices.B: Una señal de guía
choices.C: Una señal reglamentaria
choices.D: Una señal de construcción

es.explanation: Las señales rectangulares blancas con letras negras son señales reglamentarias. Las señales de límite de velocidad le indican la velocidad máxima legal para el área bajo condiciones ideales.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal amarilla en forma de diamante?

choices.A: Un zoológico o parque de animales adelante
choices.B: Los ciervos cruzan frecuentemente la carretera en esta área
choices.C: Zona de caza adelante
choices.D: Un refugio de vida silvestre cercano

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de diamante con la silueta de un ciervo advierte que los ciervos cruzan frecuentemente la carretera en esta área. Reduzca la velocidad y esté atento a los animales, especialmente al amanecer y al anochecer.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Zona escolar más adelante
choices.B: Cruce de peatones más adelante
choices.C: Sendero para caminatas cercano
choices.D: Parada de autobús más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de rombo con una figura de un peatón advierte sobre un cruce de peatones más adelante. Esté preparado para detenerse ante los peatones que crucen la calle.

es.question: ¿Qué indica la forma de esta señal?

choices.A: Un cruce de ferrocarril
choices.B: Una zona de construcción
choices.C: Una zona escolar o cruce escolar
choices.D: Una zona de hospital

es.explanation: Una señal en forma de pentágono (5 lados) de color amarillo verdoso fluorescente indica una zona escolar o un cruce escolar. Reduzca la velocidad y esté atento a los niños.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal circular amarilla?

choices.A: Una rotonda más adelante
choices.B: Una zona de hospital
choices.C: Un cruce de ferrocarril más adelante
choices.D: Una zona de no rebasar

es.explanation: Una señal circular amarilla con una X negra y dos letras R es la señal de advertencia anticipada de un cruce de ferrocarril más adelante. Reduzca la velocidad, mire y escuche si vienen trenes.

es.question: ¿Dónde vería normalmente esta señal?

choices.A: En un cruce escolar
choices.B: En un cruce de ferrocarril
choices.C: En la entrada de un hospital
choices.D: En un puente peatonal

es.explanation: La señal blanca en forma de X (aspa de San Andrés) se coloca en los cruces de ferrocarril. Significa que debe ceder el paso a los trenes. Si se aproxima un tren, debe detenerse.

es.question: ¿Qué indica esta señal amarilla en forma de rombo?

choices.A: El camino termina más adelante
choices.B: Giro a la derecha obligatorio
choices.C: Una curva a la derecha más adelante
choices.D: Desvío más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de rombo con una flecha curva advierte de una curva en el camino más adelante. Reduzca la velocidad antes de entrar en la curva.

es.question: ¿En qué se diferencia esta señal de una señal de curva?

choices.A: Indica un giro menos pronunciado
choices.B: Advierte de un giro brusco que requiere una mayor reducción de velocidad
choices.C: Significa girar a la derecha solamente
choices.D: Solo se utiliza en autopistas

es.explanation: Una señal de giro brusco (con una flecha más angulada) indica un giro más cerrado que una señal de curva. Debe reducir su velocidad de manera más significativa antes de este giro.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué condición de la carretera advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un camino sinuoso
choices.B: Una sola curva más adelante
choices.C: Una serie de dos curvas en direcciones opuestas
choices.D: Una rotonda más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal de curva inversa advierte de dos curvas en direcciones opuestas más adelante. Reduzca la velocidad y esté preparado para que el camino gire primero en un sentido y luego en el otro.

es.question: ¿Qué le advierte que espere esta señal?

choices.A: Una sola curva cerrada
choices.B: Una superficie de carretera resbaladiza
choices.C: Una serie de curvas o giros más adelante
choices.D: Una colina más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal de camino sinuoso advierte de una serie de curvas o giros más adelante. Reduzca su velocidad y esté alerta a los cambios en las condiciones de la carretera.

es.question: ¿Para qué le indica esta señal que se prepare?

choices.A: Un carril que termina
choices.B: Tráfico que se incorpora desde otra carretera
choices.C: El comienzo de una autopista dividida
choices.D: Una carretera que se estrecha a un solo carril

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de rombo de incorporación advierte que el tráfico de otra carretera se incorporará a su carril. Esté preparado para ajustar su velocidad y posición.

es.question: ¿De qué advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Puente más adelante
choices.B: El camino se estrecha más adelante
choices.C: El carril termina
choices.D: La autopista dividida termina

es.explanation: Esta señal de advertencia indica que el camino más adelante se vuelve más estrecho. Esté preparado para una reducción del ancho de la vía y ajuste su posición en el carril.

es.question: ¿Qué indica que hay más adelante esta señal?

choices.A: El camino termina
choices.B: Tráfico de doble sentido
choices.C: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.D: Salida de la autopista

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que el camino más adelante se convierte en una autopista dividida con una mediana o barrera que separa el tráfico en direcciones opuestas. Manténgase a la derecha.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.B: La autopista dividida termina y se reanuda el tráfico de doble sentido
choices.C: Un área de incorporación más adelante
choices.D: Construcción de carretera más adelante

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que la autopista dividida está terminando. El tráfico en sentido opuesto ya no estará separado por una mediana. Prepárese para el tráfico de doble sentido.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.B: Una zona de rebase más adelante
choices.C: Tráfico de doble sentido más adelante: el tráfico se mueve en ambas direcciones
choices.D: Un cambio de carril más adelante

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte sobre tráfico de doble sentido más adelante. Es posible que esté saliendo de una vía de un solo sentido o de una autopista dividida y se encuentre con vehículos que viajan en la dirección opuesta.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué condición de la carretera advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Condiciones de carretera con hielo
choices.B: La carretera puede estar resbaladiza cuando está mojada
choices.C: Camino sinuoso más adelante
choices.D: Pavimento irregular

es.explanation: Una señal de "resbaladizo cuando está mojado" advierte que la superficie de la carretera puede volverse muy resbaladiza durante la lluvia o condiciones de humedad. Reduzca su velocidad y evite frenar o girar bruscamente.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un bache o resalto en el camino
choices.B: Una superficie de carretera irregular
choices.C: Una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante
choices.D: Construcción de carretera

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante. Es posible que deba ajustar su velocidad y cambiar a una marcha más baja, especialmente en camiones o al remolcar.

es.question: ¿Para qué le advierte esta señal que se prepare?

choices.A: Una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante
choices.B: Un semáforo más adelante
choices.C: Un cruce escolar
choices.D: Un retén policial

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de un semáforo más adelante. Prepárese para detenerse si la luz está en rojo o amarillo. Esta señal a menudo se coloca donde el semáforo puede no ser visible desde la distancia.

es.question: ¿Qué le indica esta señal que espere más adelante?

choices.A: Una señal de ceda el paso (YIELD)
choices.B: Un semáforo
choices.C: Una señal de alto (STOP) donde debe detenerse
choices.D: Un reductor de velocidad (tope)

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante. Comience a reducir la velocidad y prepárese para detenerse por completo en la señal de alto.

es.question: ¿De qué advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un cruce de ferrocarril más adelante
choices.B: Un cruce de caminos o intersección más adelante
choices.C: Un hospital más adelante
choices.D: Un cruce de peatones

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay un cruce de caminos o una intersección de 4 vías más adelante. Esté atento al tráfico que ingresa desde los caminos laterales.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Una intersección en T más adelante
choices.B: Un camino lateral que entra por la derecha
choices.C: Una curva en el camino
choices.D: Un callejón sin salida

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de un camino lateral que entra por la derecha. Esté atento a los vehículos que ingresan a la carretera desde el camino lateral.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: Los carriles se están incorporando
choices.B: Un carril está terminando
choices.C: Se está añadiendo un nuevo carril; no es necesario incorporarse
choices.D: Se requiere giro a la derecha

es.explanation: Una señal de carril añadido significa que un nuevo carril se une a la carretera sin requerir incorporación. El tráfico que entra desde la rampa tiene su propio carril nuevo.

es.question: ¿Qué prohíbe esta señal?

choices.A: Detenerse en cualquier momento
choices.B: Estacionarse en esta área
choices.C: Permanecer parado o dejar el motor encendido
choices.D: Cargar o descargar

es.explanation: Una señal de NO ESTACIONAR (NO PARKING) roja y blanca significa que no puede estacionar su vehículo en esta área. Puede detenerse brevemente para subir o bajar pasajeros.

es.question: ¿Quién tiene permitido estacionarse en un espacio marcado con esta señal?

choices.A: Cualquier persona por menos de 15 minutos
choices.B: Solo personas de la tercera edad
choices.C: Solo vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de discapacidad válido
choices.D: Cualquier conductor con un pasajero que tenga una discapacidad

es.explanation: Una señal azul con el símbolo de la silla de ruedas marca el estacionamiento reservado para personas con discapacidades. Solo los vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de matrícula de estacionamiento para personas con discapacidad válido pueden estacionarse en estos espacios. Las infracciones conllevan multas elevadas.

en.question: What is the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration's goal regarding fatalities on Maryland's roads?

choices.A: Reduce fatalities by 50%
choices.B: Reach zero fatalities
choices.C: Limit fatalities to under 100 per year
choices.D: Decrease fatalities in work zones only

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message states, 'Our goal is to reach zero fatalities (no deaths) on Maryland’s roads, because even one life lost is one too many.'

en.question: According to the Administrator's Message, which of the following is a responsibility every time you get behind the wheel?

choices.A: Drive sober
choices.B: Drive at least 10 mph under the speed limit
choices.C: Only wear a seat belt on highways
choices.D: Yield to motorcycles only at night

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message explicitly lists 'Drive sober' as one of the responsibilities every driver has every time they get behind the wheel.

en.question: The Administrator's Message reminds new drivers that driving is considered a:

choices.A: Constitutional right
choices.B: Privilege
choices.C: Requirement for citizenship
choices.D: Federal mandate

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message states, 'It is important to remember that driving is a privilege, and you play a part in making sure that everyone stays safe on our roads.'

en.question: To help keep everyone safe on the road, the Administrator's Message specifically advises drivers to look how many times for motorcycles?

choices.A: Once
choices.B: Twice
choices.C: Three times
choices.D: Only when changing lanes

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message includes 'Look twice for motorcycles' in its list of responsibilities for making safe choices behind the wheel.

en.question: Where can you find the Online Driver Test Tutorial to test your understanding of the rules of the road?

choices.A: On the MVA mobile app
choices.B: At any local public library
choices.C: On the MVA website at mva.maryland.gov/drivers
choices.D: By calling the TTY number

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message states that the Online Driver Test Tutorial is located on the MVA website, mva.maryland.gov/drivers.

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, which section covers the Rookie Driver/Graduated Licensing System?

choices.A: Section 1
choices.B: Section 2
choices.C: Section 3
choices.D: Section 4

en.explanation: According to the Table of Contents, Section 2 is titled 'Licensing Requirements and Process' and includes the 'Rookie Driver/Graduated Licensing System'.

en.question: Which of the following topics is categorized under 'Dangerous Driving Behaviors' in Section 6 of the manual?

choices.A: Hydroplaning
choices.B: Distracted Driving
choices.C: Highway-Railroad Crossings
choices.D: Passing

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Distracted Driving' under Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.

en.question: The 'Drug and Alcohol Test – Implied Consent' rule is covered under which section of the manual?

choices.A: Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors
choices.B: Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops
choices.C: Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties
choices.D: Section 10: Other Important Information

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Drug and Alcohol Test – Implied Consent' under Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties.

en.question: Section 7, 'Sharing the Road,' includes information on interacting with which of the following?

choices.A: Slow Moving Vehicles
choices.B: Funeral Processions
choices.C: School Buses
choices.D: Traffic Circles

en.explanation: According to the Table of Contents, Section 7: Sharing the Road includes a subsection specifically on 'School Buses'.

en.question: If you need to learn about driving in fog or inclement weather, which section of the manual should you consult?

choices.A: Section 3: Basic Driving
choices.B: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings
choices.C: Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions
choices.D: Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops

en.explanation: The Table of Contents shows that 'Driving in Fog' and 'Driving in Inclement Weather' are covered in Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.

en.question: What is the TTY phone number provided for the Hearing Impaired to contact the Maryland MVA?
en.explanation: The contact information on the first page of the manual lists the TTY for the Hearing Impaired as 1-800-492-4575.

en.question: According to the Administrator's Message, how will a new driver get better at driving?

choices.A: By driving only during daylight hours
choices.B: With more experience on different roads and under different conditions
choices.C: By avoiding heavy traffic entirely
choices.D: By only driving with a supervising driver

en.explanation: The Administrator's Message states, 'you will get better at driving with more experience on different roads, under different conditions, and in different environments.'

en.question: The 'Move Over Law' is discussed in which section of the Maryland Driver's Manual?

choices.A: Section 3: Basic Driving
choices.B: Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors
choices.C: Section 7: Sharing the Road
choices.D: Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops

en.explanation: According to the Table of Contents, the 'Move Over Law' is located in Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.

en.question: Which of the following is listed as a requirement under Section 1: Driving Tests Requirements?

choices.A: Vision Screening
choices.B: Co-Signer Application
choices.C: Provisional License
choices.D: Organ Donor

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Vision Screening' as subsection A under Section 1: Driving Tests Requirements.

en.question: According to the copyright information in the manual, which of the following actions is prohibited?

choices.A: Using the content for free to study the Maryland Vehicle Law
choices.B: Reading the manual online
choices.C: Any unauthorized reprint, use, distribution, or sale of the material
choices.D: Sharing the manual with a driving instructor

en.explanation: The copyright section explicitly states, 'Any unauthorized reprint, use, distribution, or sale of this material is prohibited.'

en.question: What is the minimum visual acuity required in each eye to qualify for a Maryland driver's license?
en.explanation: To qualify for a driver's license, the applicant must have visual acuity of at least 20/40 in each eye.

en.question: How many questions are on the Maryland driver's knowledge test, and how much time do you have to complete it?

choices.A: 20 questions, 15 minutes
choices.B: 25 questions, 20 minutes
choices.C: 30 questions, 25 minutes
choices.D: 50 questions, 45 minutes

en.explanation: There are 25 questions on the knowledge test, and you will have 20 minutes to take the test.

en.question: When bringing a vehicle to the MVA for your driving skills test, the vehicle must have at least:

choices.A: A quarter tank of gas
choices.B: A half tank of gas
choices.C: Three-quarters of a tank of gas
choices.D: A full tank of gas

en.explanation: The vehicle used for the driving skills test must be safe to drive, have no windshield cracks affecting vision, and have at least a half tank of gas.

en.question: Who is allowed in the vehicle with you during the driving skills test?

choices.A: Only you and the MVA examiner, plus an approved interpreter if needed
choices.B: You, the MVA examiner, and your supervising driver
choices.C: You, the MVA examiner, and one family member
choices.D: You, the MVA examiner, and your driver education instructor

en.explanation: Only you and the person giving you the test are allowed in the vehicle during the test. An interpreter that the MVA approves can also be in the car if you need one.

en.question: What is the maximum penalty for littering on state roads in Maryland?

choices.A: A $500 fine
choices.B: A $1000 fine and 15 days in prison
choices.C: A $1500 fine or 30 days in prison
choices.D: A $2000 fine or 60 days in prison

en.explanation: Fines for littering can cost up to $1500 or 30 days in prison.

en.question: When applying for a noncommercial driver's license, how many documents must you bring to prove that you live in Maryland?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: When you apply, you must bring two documents that prove that you live in Maryland.

en.question: Which of the following types of documents will the MVA accept when you apply for a driver's license?

choices.A: Original documents or certified copies
choices.B: Notarized photocopies
choices.C: High-quality color photocopies
choices.D: Documents with erased and corrected information

en.explanation: You must bring original documents or copies certified by the agency that provided them to you. The MVA will not accept photocopies, notarized copies, or documents with changed or erased information.

en.question: What class of license is a standard noncommercial driver's license used for regular cars, pickup trucks, and vans?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class B
choices.C: Class C
choices.D: Class M

en.explanation: A noncommercial driver's license allows you to drive regular vehicles like cars, pickup trucks, and vans. It is also called a Class C driver's license.

en.question: How long is a Type 1 Learner's Instructional Permit valid for?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 18 months
choices.D: Up to 2 years

en.explanation: If you have never had a noncommercial driver's license you must get a Type 1 Learner's Instructional Permit. The Permit lasts up to 2 years.

en.question: A Type 2 Learner's Instructional Permit is required if you:

choices.A: Have never had a driver's license before
choices.B: Already have a driver's license and want a different class of license
choices.C: Are under 16 years old
choices.D: Have had your license suspended for a moving violation

en.explanation: If you already have a driver's license and want a different class of driver's license, you must apply for a Type 2 Learner's Instructional Permit.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to apply for a Learner's Instructional Permit if you are under 25 years old?

choices.A: 15 years and 6 months
choices.B: 15 years and 9 months
choices.C: 16 years
choices.D: 16 years and 3 months

en.explanation: Applicants younger than 25 must be at least 15 years and 9 months old.

en.question: How many total practice driving hours must an applicant under 25 years old complete with a supervising driver?

choices.A: 14 hours
choices.B: 30 hours
choices.C: 45 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: Applicants younger than 25 must practice driving at least 60 hours with a supervising driver.

en.question: If an applicant is 25 years old or older, how many practice driving hours must they complete before taking the driving skills test?

choices.A: 14 hours
choices.B: 30 hours
choices.C: 45 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: Applicants 25 years old and older must complete at least 14 practice hours with a supervising driver.

en.question: How long must an applicant who is 25 years old or older hold their Learner's Instructional Permit before becoming eligible for a Provisional License?

choices.A: At least 14 days
choices.B: At least 30 days
choices.C: At least 45 days
choices.D: At least 9 months

en.explanation: Applicants 25 years old and older must have their permit for at least 45 days before they are eligible for a Provisional License.

en.question: If you are convicted of a moving violation while holding a Learner's Instructional Permit, how long must you hold the permit from the date of the conviction before becoming eligible for a Provisional License?

choices.A: 45 days
choices.B: 3 months
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 9 months

en.explanation: At any age, if you have been convicted of or given a Probation Before Judgement (PBJ) for a moving violation, you must hold the Learner's Instructional Permit at least 9 months following the most recent date you were convicted.

en.question: How long must a driver under age 18 hold their Learner's Instructional Permit without a violation before being eligible for a Provisional License?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 18 months

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are under age 18, you must hold the Permit for at least 9 months without a violation before being eligible for a Provisional License.

en.question: If you are 25 years or older, how many practice driving hours must be recorded on your Practice and Skills Log to get a Provisional License?

choices.A: 14 hours
choices.B: 30 hours
choices.C: 45 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: The manual states that you must submit a Practice and Skills Log showing you completed at least 60 practice hours driving with a supervising driver, or 14 hours if you are 25 or older.

en.question: What happens when you meet all the requirements to graduate from a Provisional License to a regular Driver's License?

choices.A: You must retake the driving skills test.
choices.B: You must visit an MVA branch to apply for the upgrade.
choices.C: The MVA will automatically switch your license and mail you a card.
choices.D: You must complete another 60 hours of supervised driving.

en.explanation: When you have met all the requirements, the MVA will automatically switch your Provisional License to a Driver's License and a card showing the switch will be mailed to you.

en.question: Who is eligible to co-sign a minor's application for a license if the minor is married?

choices.A: Any licensed driver over the age of 21.
choices.B: The minor's husband or wife, if they are 18 or older.
choices.C: Only a parent or legal guardian.
choices.D: An MVA approved driving instructor.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you are married and your husband or wife is 18 or older, they can co-sign. You must provide proof that you are married.'

en.question: How can a co-signer cancel a minor's driver's license?

choices.A: By verbally requesting cancellation at any MVA branch.
choices.B: By submitting a written request to the MVA's Administrative Adjudication Division.
choices.C: By confiscating the minor's physical license card.
choices.D: By removing the minor from their auto insurance policy.

en.explanation: The co-signer may cancel a minor's license by submitting a written request to the MVA's Administrative Adjudication Division.

en.question: If you have an out-of-country license, which of the following is required to get a Maryland license?

choices.A: A 3-hour roadway safety driving education program.
choices.B: A 14-hour supervised driving log.
choices.C: A letter of recommendation from the embassy.
choices.D: A minimum of 18 months of driving experience in Maryland.

en.explanation: To get a Maryland license with an out-of-country license, you must successfully complete a vision screening, knowledge test, driving skills test, and a three-hour roadway safety driving education program approved by the MVA.

en.question: If the MVA offers the knowledge test in your spoken language, how many times must you take it before you are allowed to use an interpreter?

choices.A: 2 times
choices.B: 3 times
choices.C: 5 times
choices.D: You cannot use an interpreter if the test is offered in your language.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If we offer the knowledge test in the language that you speak, you must take it at least 5 times before using an interpreter.'

en.question: Which of the following is a rule regarding interpreters providing services for knowledge or skills testing at the MVA?

choices.A: The MVA charges a standard fee for the interpreter's services.
choices.B: The interpreter must be a family member of the applicant.
choices.C: The interpreter may also certify the customer's residence.
choices.D: The interpreter may not provide other services to the customer being tested.

en.explanation: Interpreters providing services for knowledge/skills testing may not provide other services to the customer being tested, such as certifying residence or conducting driving school business.

en.question: What documentation will the MVA ask you to provide to obtain a Developmental Disability Disclosure Card?

choices.A: A signed letter from a licensed physician.
choices.B: Court documents proving legal guardianship.
choices.C: Medical records detailing your specific disability.
choices.D: The MVA will NOT ask you to provide documentation about your disability.

en.explanation: Carrying a Developmental Disability Disclosure Card is voluntary, and the manual explicitly states: 'MVA will NOT ask you to provide information or documentation about your disability to get this card.'

en.question: What documents must you have with you before you drive a vehicle?

choices.A: A valid permit or license, and the vehicle registration card.
choices.B: A valid permit or license, and your birth certificate.
choices.C: The vehicle title and proof of insurance.
choices.D: A Developmental Disability Disclosure Card and a valid license.

en.explanation: Before you drive, you must have a valid Learner's Permit or driver's license, and vehicle registration card with you.

en.question: What does the manual describe as 'defensive driving'?

choices.A: Assuming other drivers will always follow the rules of the road.
choices.B: Searching ahead and being ready to change speed or lanes to identify risks.
choices.C: Yielding the right-of-way only when directed by a traffic signal.
choices.D: Driving at a constant speed regardless of road conditions.

en.explanation: The manual defines defensive driving as: 'By searching ahead and being ready to change speed or change lanes, you can drive more safely and have time to identify risks. This is called defensive driving.'

en.question: Who should you yield the right-of-way to if you and another driver arrive at an intersection at the same time?

choices.A: The driver on your left.
choices.B: The driver on your right.
choices.C: The driver going straight.
choices.D: The driver turning left.

en.explanation: You should yield the right-of-way to the driver on your right, if both of you arrive at an intersection at the same time.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended step to manage risk while operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: Assume that other drivers will do what they are supposed to do.
choices.B: Decrease the time you have to respond to your surroundings.
choices.C: Maintain a safe distance between your vehicle and other people using the road.
choices.D: Rely solely on your mirrors to know what is happening around your vehicle.

en.explanation: To manage risk, the manual recommends that you 'Maintain a safe distance between your vehicle and other people using the road' and explicitly says 'Do not assume that other drivers will do what they are supposed to do.'

en.question: What is a restriction placed on a Provisional Driver's License?

choices.A: You must drive with a supervising driver at all times.
choices.B: You are not allowed to drive on interstate highways.
choices.C: You are restricted from having passengers and driving at night.
choices.D: You must log an additional 60 hours of practice driving.

en.explanation: A Provisional Driver's License permits you to drive without supervision but with restrictions, such as no passengers and no driving at night.

en.question: When making a left turn, you must yield the right-of-way to:

choices.A: Drivers in the opposing traffic lane
choices.B: Drivers behind you
choices.C: Drivers turning right from the intersecting road
choices.D: No one, you automatically have the right-of-way

en.explanation: You should yield the right-of-way to drivers in the opposing traffic lane when you are making a left turn.

en.question: What does the posted speed limit represent?

choices.A: The suggested speed for all weather conditions
choices.B: The minimum legal speed you can travel
choices.C: The maximum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions
choices.D: The speed you must maintain regardless of traffic

en.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal (perfect) conditions.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to drive at a speed significantly lower than other traffic?

choices.A: It causes excessive wear on your brakes
choices.B: It encourages other vehicles to constantly pass you, increasing the chances of a crash
choices.C: It is illegal on all Maryland roads
choices.D: It decreases your ability to handle curves

en.explanation: Driving at a speed lower than other traffic encourages other vehicles to constantly pass you, which increases the chances of a crash.

en.question: Under ideal driving conditions, what is the minimum following distance recommended by the MVA?

choices.A: 1 to 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 to 4 seconds
choices.C: 5 to 6 seconds
choices.D: 10 seconds

en.explanation: The MVA recommends a minimum following distance of 3 to 4 seconds under ideal driving conditions.

en.question: When following vehicles that stop often, such as buses or delivery vans, you should increase your following distance to:

choices.A: Two or three seconds
choices.B: Three or four seconds
choices.C: Four or five seconds
choices.D: Seven or eight seconds

en.explanation: When following vehicles that stop often, you should increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead of you to four or five seconds, and possibly more if needed.

en.question: When is it generally acceptable to drive to the left of the center of the road?

choices.A: When you are passing another vehicle going in the same direction
choices.B: When you are approaching a blind curve
choices.C: When you are driving in a residential area
choices.D: When you are preparing to park on the right shoulder

en.explanation: You should keep your vehicle to the right of the center of the road unless you are passing another vehicle going in the same direction, a sign/signal allows it, or there is an obstacle.

en.question: When making a legal U-turn, which lane should you turn into?

choices.A: The inside or left-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction
choices.B: The outside or right-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction
choices.C: The center turn lane
choices.D: Any available lane

en.explanation: When making a U-turn, after yielding to traffic and ensuring the way is clear, turn into the outside or right-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction.

en.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

choices.A: Honk your horn to alert the other driver
choices.B: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
choices.C: Flash your high beams
choices.D: Ensure you are at least 10 feet ahead of the passed vehicle

en.explanation: When passing, you must see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror before returning to the lane you came from.

en.question: In which of the following situations is it illegal to pass another vehicle?

choices.A: On an unobstructed one-way road with two or more lanes
choices.B: When the other vehicle is about to make a left turn
choices.C: When crossing or within 100 feet of an intersection
choices.D: When you are on an unobstructed road with two or more lanes moving in the same direction

en.explanation: You may not pass when crossing or within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing.

en.question: What must you do when another vehicle is passing you?

choices.A: Speed up to get out of their way
choices.B: Move onto the right shoulder
choices.C: Yield to the other vehicle and not increase your speed
choices.D: Honk your horn to acknowledge them

en.explanation: When being passed by another vehicle, you must yield to the other vehicle and not increase your speed.

en.question: When parking a vehicle with a manual transmission, you should set the parking brake and:

choices.A: Place the vehicle in neutral
choices.B: Place the vehicle in gear
choices.C: Place the vehicle in 'park'
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the left

en.explanation: When parking, you should set your parking brake and place the vehicle in gear if it has a manual transmission (or in 'park' if it has an automatic transmission).

en.question: When are you permitted to disobey a traffic control device?

choices.A: When you are running late for an emergency
choices.B: When a police officer tells you to do something different
choices.C: When there is no other traffic around
choices.D: When you are driving a commercial vehicle

en.explanation: The only time you do not have to obey all traffic control devices is when a police officer, other emergency personnel, or a school crossing guard tells you to do something different.

en.question: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right at a steady red signal:

choices.A: Without stopping if the intersection is clear
choices.B: Only if you are in the rightmost lane and honk your horn
choices.C: After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic
choices.D: Only between the hours of 6 AM and 6 PM

en.explanation: Unless a sign prohibits turning on red, after coming to a complete stop, you may turn right. You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all other traffic.

en.question: What should you do if you approach an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection without stopping if you have the right-of-way
choices.B: Stop at a clearly marked stop line or before entering the crosswalk
choices.C: Treat the intersection as a yield sign
choices.D: Wait for a police officer to arrive

en.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, you must stop at a clearly marked stop line. If there is no clearly marked stop line, you must stop before entering a crosswalk.

en.question: What does a fluorescent pink traffic sign indicate?

choices.A: School zones and pedestrian crossings
choices.B: Emergency traffic incidents
choices.C: Construction and maintenance work areas
choices.D: Recreation and cultural interest areas

en.explanation: According to the manual, fluorescent pink signs are used to indicate emergency traffic incidents.

en.question: What does a steady yellow 'X' lane use signal mean?

choices.A: You can use the lane for a left turn.
choices.B: You must never drive in that lane.
choices.C: You should move out of the lane as soon as you safely can.
choices.D: You may drive in the lane but must reduce your speed.

en.explanation: A steady yellow 'X' signal means you should move out of the lane as soon as you safely can.

en.question: Which sign shape is used exclusively to warn of school zones and mark school crossings?

choices.A: Diamond
choices.B: Pentagon
choices.C: Pennant
choices.D: Octagon

en.explanation: The pentagon (five-sided) shape warns you of school zones and marks school crossings.

en.question: How should a driver respond to a flashing red traffic signal?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.
choices.B: Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when clear.
choices.C: Stop only if other vehicles are approaching the intersection.
choices.D: Yield to traffic on the right without coming to a full stop.

en.explanation: For a flashing red signal, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, yield to all other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clear.

en.question: What type of information is typically found on brown traffic signs?

choices.A: Destinations, distances, and directions
choices.B: Services like food, gas, and rest areas
choices.C: Recreation and cultural interest areas
choices.D: Construction and maintenance work areas

en.explanation: Brown traffic signs indicate recreation and cultural interest areas.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow 'X' signal above a reversible lane indicate?

choices.A: The lane is closed to all traffic.
choices.B: You must move out of the lane immediately.
choices.C: You can use the lane for a left turn, sharing it with opposite traffic.
choices.D: You have the exclusive right-of-way to travel straight.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow 'X' signal or two-way left-turn arrows mean you can use the lane for a left turn, and you will likely be sharing the lane with left-turning vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

en.question: What should you do if you are approaching an intersection and the signal changes to a steady yellow?

choices.A: Speed up to beat the red light.
choices.B: Stop immediately, even if you are in the middle of the intersection.
choices.C: Carefully continue through if you are too close to the intersection to stop safely.
choices.D: Reverse your vehicle to clear the crosswalk.

en.explanation: A steady yellow signal gives you time to stop safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely, carefully continue through the intersection.

en.question: Which color is used for signs that warn of school, pedestrian, and bicycle crossings?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: Fluorescent Yellow-Green
choices.C: White
choices.D: Orange

en.explanation: Fluorescent Yellow-Green is the color used for school, pedestrian, and bicycle signs.

en.question: What is the purpose of mile marker signs located on interstate highways?

choices.A: They indicate the current maximum speed limit.
choices.B: They provide location information in case you need emergency assistance.
choices.C: They show the exact distance to the next gas station or rest area.
choices.D: They mark the beginning of a new county or state line.

en.explanation: Mile marker signs provide location information you can use if you need someone to find you, such as a tow truck or emergency personnel.

en.question: When a crosswalk signal shows a solid red light to drivers, what must the driver do?

choices.A: Stop and wait until the light changes.
choices.B: Slow down and proceed if no pedestrians are visible.
choices.C: Stop, then proceed with caution.
choices.D: Honk to warn pedestrians before crossing.

en.explanation: According to the crosswalk signals chart, a solid red light for drivers means 'Stop!' and they must wait while pedestrians cross.

en.question: Which shape is used to identify the location of a highway-rail grade crossing?

choices.A: Round
choices.B: Crossbuck
choices.C: Trapezoid
choices.D: Diamond

en.explanation: The Crossbuck shape identifies the location of a highway-rail grade crossing.

en.question: What is the correct action when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop and wait for a green light.
choices.B: Treat it as a four-way stop.
choices.C: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.D: Accelerate to clear the intersection quickly.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution.

en.question: What do rectangular signs with black lettering on a white background typically indicate?

choices.A: General warnings of hazards ahead
choices.B: Regulatory information and traffic laws you must obey
choices.C: Directions to hospitals and airports
choices.D: Emergency traffic incidents

en.explanation: Rectangular (4-Sided) Signs that are Black on White regulate traffic. They are about traffic laws and you must obey them.

en.question: What type of information do Service Information and Guide Signs provide?

choices.A: The speed limit on the upcoming road
choices.B: Businesses and services you can find if you take certain exits
choices.C: The route number and type of road
choices.D: Areas where parking is strictly prohibited

en.explanation: According to the manual, Service Information and Guide Signs identify the businesses and services (such as lodging, hospitals, gas, and food) you can find if you take certain exits.

en.question: What does a single broken yellow line on the road indicate?

choices.A: Traffic is traveling in the same direction and lane changing is prohibited.
choices.B: Traffic is traveling in opposite directions and passing with care is permitted.
choices.C: It marks the right edge of the roadway.
choices.D: It indicates a reversible lane where traffic flows change direction.

en.explanation: A single broken yellow line separates lanes where vehicles are traveling in opposite directions, and passing with care is permitted in either direction.

en.question: Where are single solid yellow lines typically used?

choices.A: On the right edge of a two-way road
choices.B: To separate general lanes from HOV lanes
choices.C: To mark left edge lines on divided highways, one-way roads, and ramps
choices.D: In the center of a two-way road where passing is permitted

en.explanation: The manual states that a single solid yellow line marks left edge lines on divided highways, one-way roads, and ramps.

en.question: What is the purpose of double (side-by-side) broken yellow lines?

choices.A: They mark the edges of reversible lanes.
choices.B: They indicate a shared two-way left-turn lane.
choices.C: They mark a pedestrian crosswalk.
choices.D: They separate bicycle lanes from motor vehicle lanes.

en.explanation: Double broken yellow lines mark the edges of reversible lanes, which are lanes where traffic flows in one direction sometimes and the other direction other times.

en.question: Are you allowed to turn left across a double solid yellow line?

choices.A: No, crossing a double solid yellow line is strictly prohibited under all circumstances.
choices.B: Yes, but only if you are passing a slow-moving vehicle.
choices.C: Yes, you may make a left turn across it, such as when turning into a driveway.
choices.D: Yes, but only during daylight hours.

en.explanation: While passing is not allowed in either direction, the manual specifies that you may make a left turn across a double solid yellow line, for example, when turning into a driveway.

en.question: How are yield lines marked on the pavement?

choices.A: As a single solid white line
choices.B: As rows of small triangles across the lane
choices.C: As double solid yellow lines
choices.D: As a single dotted white line

en.explanation: Yield lines are marked as rows of small triangles across the lane that show where a vehicle must yield to other vehicles or pedestrians.

en.question: What is one purpose of shared-use lane markings for bicycles?

choices.A: To prohibit motor vehicles from using the lane
choices.B: To indicate where bicycles must park
choices.C: To discourage biking in the wrong direction
choices.D: To warn bicyclists of an upcoming railroad crossing

en.explanation: Shared-use lane markings alert drivers that bicyclists may be on the road, tell bicyclists where to ride, and discourage biking in the wrong direction.

en.question: According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, how much more likely is a crash to result in death on a road with a 65 mph speed limit compared to a 45 or 50 mph limit?

choices.A: It is equally likely
choices.B: More than twice as likely
choices.C: Nearly five times as likely
choices.D: Ten times as likely

en.explanation: A crash on a road with a speed limit of 65 mph or higher is more than twice as likely to result in death than a crash on a road with a speed limit of 45 or 50 mph.

en.question: When driving in reduced visibility situations, what should you use as a guide to stay in your lane?

choices.A: The taillights of the vehicle ahead of you
choices.B: The center double yellow line
choices.C: The lines on the edge of the road or the right side of the road
choices.D: The headlights of oncoming traffic

en.explanation: When driving in reduced visibility situations, you should use the lines on the edge of the road or the right side of the road as a guide.

en.question: Under Maryland law, you must turn on your headlights anytime there is not enough light to clearly see at least how far in front of your vehicle?

choices.A: 300 feet
choices.B: 500 feet
choices.C: 1,000 feet
choices.D: 1,500 feet

en.explanation: You must turn on your headlights anytime there is not enough light to clearly see at least 1,000 feet in front of your vehicle.

en.question: Maryland law requires you to turn on your headlights when you are:

choices.A: Driving in the left lane of a divided highway
choices.B: Using your windshield wipers in inclement weather
choices.C: Approaching a railroad crossing
choices.D: Parking on the side of a road at night

en.explanation: Maryland law requires that you turn on your headlights when using your windshield wipers in inclement weather.

en.question: When using high beam headlights, at what distance must you change to low beams when following another vehicle?

choices.A: 100 feet or less
choices.B: 200 feet or less
choices.C: 300 feet or less
choices.D: 500 feet or less

en.explanation: You must change to low beams when following a vehicle that is 300 feet or less in front of you.

en.question: What should you do to avoid being blinded by the headlights of oncoming traffic at night?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams to see better
choices.B: Look slightly to the right of the lane you are traveling in
choices.C: Close one eye until the vehicle passes
choices.D: Stare directly at the center line of the road

en.explanation: Do not stare into the headlights of traffic coming toward you. Instead, look at the road in front of you, or slightly to the right of the lane you are traveling in.

en.question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?

choices.A: High beam headlights only
choices.B: Low beam headlights only
choices.C: Parking lights only
choices.D: Emergency flashers and high beams

en.explanation: When driving in fog, you should use low beam headlights only, and also use fog lights if you have them.

en.question: What should you do if the fog is so thick that you cannot safely drive your vehicle?

choices.A: Stop in the middle of your lane and wait for it to clear
choices.B: Turn on your high beams and drive at 10 mph
choices.C: Pull completely off the road to a safe location and turn on your emergency flashers
choices.D: Follow closely behind a large truck to use its taillights as a guide

en.explanation: If the fog is so thick that you cannot safely drive your vehicle, pull completely off the road to a safe location and turn on your emergency flashers.

en.question: If your vehicle does NOT have an anti-lock braking system (ABS), what should you do to prevent skidding on wet or icy roads?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes firmly.
choices.B: Pump the brakes.
choices.C: Pull the emergency brake.
choices.D: Shift into neutral and coast.

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'If your vehicle does not have an anti-lock braking system, pump the brakes to prevent skidding.'

en.question: Which areas of the road tend to freeze before the rest of the road?

choices.A: Intersections and crosswalks
choices.B: Ramps and bridges
choices.C: Tunnels and underpasses
choices.D: Straightaways and shoulders

en.explanation: The manual warns that 'Ramps and bridges freeze before roads.'

en.question: What is 'black ice'?

choices.A: Ice that forms exclusively at night
choices.B: A thick layer of snow mixed with dirt
choices.C: A thin layer of ice on blacktop roads that is hard to see
choices.D: Ice that forms only on bridges and overpasses

en.explanation: The manual describes black ice as a thin layer of ice on blacktop (asphalt) roads that can be very hard or impossible to see, caused by ice or snow melting and re-freezing.

en.question: Which of the following items is recommended to keep in your car's emergency kit for traction on snow and ice?

choices.A: Kitty litter or sand
choices.B: Extra engine oil
choices.C: A spare tire
choices.D: Road flares

en.explanation: The Emergency Kit Supplies list in the manual includes 'Kitty litter or sand (for traction on snow and ice).'

en.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is a basic rule to help regain control?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately.
choices.B: Steer in the opposite direction of the skid.
choices.C: Steer in the direction you are skidding.
choices.D: Close your eyes and brace for impact.

en.explanation: If your vehicle begins to skid, basic rules include to 'Steer in the direction you are skidding' and to release the accelerator or brake pedal.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle begins to hydroplane?

choices.A: Apply the brakes firmly.
choices.B: Take your foot off the gas and keep your vehicle going straight.
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel sharply to regain traction.
choices.D: Accelerate to push through the water.

en.explanation: If you start to lose control due to hydroplaning, the manual instructs: 'Take your foot off the gas. Do not apply your brakes. Keep your vehicle going straight. Slow down until you get control back.'

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are required to stop before every railroad crossing?

choices.A: Motorcycles and mopeds
choices.B: Passenger cars and SUVs
choices.C: Buses, school buses, and trucks carrying hazardous materials
choices.D: Emergency vehicles with flashing lights

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Buses, school buses, and trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before every railroad crossing.'

en.question: If you have an emergency on or near a railroad crossing, what should you do first?

choices.A: Stay in the vehicle and call 911.
choices.B: Get out of the vehicle and move away from the tracks.
choices.C: Try to push the vehicle off the tracks yourself.
choices.D: Wave a flag to stop the oncoming train.

en.explanation: The manual advises: 'If you have an emergency on or near a railroad crossing, get out of the vehicle and move away from the tracks.'

en.question: What color are the signs that indicate a work zone?

choices.A: Green
choices.B: Blue
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: Red

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'Orange is the color for work zones. If you see orange signs when driving, pay close attention...'

en.question: In a work zone, what do flashing blue lights indicate?

choices.A: Workers are present
choices.B: Highway maintenance vehicles are ahead
choices.C: Active speed cameras
choices.D: A detour is approaching

en.explanation: The manual's section on Lights In Work Zones specifies that 'Flashing blue lights' indicate 'Active speed cameras'.

en.question: What do flashing amber or yellow lights in a work zone mean?

choices.A: Active speed cameras
choices.B: Active work zone or workers present
choices.C: Highway maintenance vehicles
choices.D: The work zone has ended

en.explanation: The manual states that 'Flashing amber/yellow lights' mean 'Active work zone/workers present'.

en.question: When approaching a traffic circle (roundabout), who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: Vehicles entering the traffic circle
choices.B: Traffic already in the circle
choices.C: Vehicles on the right side
choices.D: Larger vehicles such as trucks and buses

en.explanation: The manual dictates: 'When you come to a traffic circle, you must always yield to traffic already in the circle.'

en.question: When preparing to exit a multi-lane traffic circle, what should you do?

choices.A: Turn on your left turn signal and stop.
choices.B: Turn on your right turn signal and move to the outside lane after passing the exit before yours.
choices.C: Accelerate rapidly to cut in front of other vehicles.
choices.D: Sound your horn to warn other drivers you are exiting.

en.explanation: The manual explains: 'When preparing to exit, turn on your right turn signal and move to the outside lane after you pass the exit before the one you plan to take.'

en.question: What is the purpose of an acceleration lane when entering an interstate?

choices.A: To pass slower vehicles on the right.
choices.B: To adjust your speed to the flow of traffic already on the interstate.
choices.C: To park your vehicle in an emergency.
choices.D: To safely exit the highway.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to the flow of traffic already on the interstate.

en.question: What should you do if you exit an interstate at the wrong place?

choices.A: Stop and back up on the shoulder.
choices.B: Make a U-turn on the exit ramp.
choices.C: Continue until you are off the exit ramp and look for a way to re-enter.
choices.D: Stop in the deceleration lane and wait for traffic to clear.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you exit at the wrong place, continue until you are off the exit ramp. Then look for a way to re-enter the road. Never stop and back up on any part of the highway.'

en.question: When are you allowed to stop on the shoulder of an interstate or limited access highway?

choices.A: When you need to answer a cell phone call.
choices.B: When you want to take a rest break.
choices.C: Only when your vehicle is disabled or you have another emergency.
choices.D: When you need to check your GPS.

en.explanation: You may stop on the shoulder, but only when your vehicle is disabled (stops running) or you have another emergency.

en.question: How must other vehicles react to a funeral procession?

choices.A: They must yield the right-of-way even if they have a green signal.
choices.B: They can proceed normally if they have a green signal.
choices.C: They should honk their horn to show respect.
choices.D: They may pass the procession on the right side.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Even if they have a green signal, other vehicles must yield the right-of-way to vehicles in a funeral procession.'

en.question: A slow-moving vehicle sign on the back of a vehicle warns that the vehicle is traveling at what speed?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour or less
choices.B: 25 miles per hour or less
choices.C: 35 miles per hour or less
choices.D: 45 miles per hour or less

en.explanation: Some slow moving vehicles may have the slow-moving sign on the back to warn you they are only going 25 miles per hour or less.

en.question: In Maryland, a driver is considered to be driving under the influence of alcohol when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at or above what level?
en.explanation: Maryland considers drivers to be driving under the influence of alcohol when their blood alcohol concentration is .08 or higher.

en.question: What is the legal consequence if a driver under the age of 21 is stopped by law enforcement and has been drinking?

choices.A: They will receive a warning for the first offense.
choices.B: Their license will be suspended or revoked.
choices.C: They must attend a mandatory defensive driving class without losing their license.
choices.D: They will only be fined if their BAC is .08 or higher.

en.explanation: If you are not yet 21 years old and law enforcement stops you and you have been drinking, your license will be suspended or revoked.

en.question: Which of the following is considered part of the 'passenger area' where open containers of alcohol are illegal?

choices.A: Only the driver's seat.
choices.B: The trunk of the vehicle.
choices.C: Any place the driver or passengers can easily reach from where they are sitting.
choices.D: Only the back seats of the vehicle.

en.explanation: The passenger area of a vehicle includes the driver and passenger seats, and any place the driver or passengers can easily reach from where they are sitting.

en.question: What can happen if you are convicted of a drunk or drugged driving offense with a child in your vehicle?

choices.A: The judge can double your fine and jail time.
choices.B: Your vehicle will be permanently confiscated.
choices.C: You will be banned from driving for life.
choices.D: You will receive a standard traffic ticket.

en.explanation: If you are convicted of a drunk or drugged driving offense with a child in your vehicle, the judge can double your fine and jail time.

en.question: Which of the following is an example of aggressive driving?

choices.A: Yielding the right-of-way to pedestrians.
choices.B: Using turn signals before changing lanes.
choices.C: Making unsafe lane changes and tailgating.
choices.D: Driving in the right lane when traveling slower than traffic.

en.explanation: Examples of aggressive driving include: speeding, tailgating, ignoring traffic signals and devices, making unsafe lane changes, not yielding the right-of-way, and unsafe or illegal passing.

en.question: What is the cell phone usage rule for drivers who are under 18 years old?

choices.A: They may use a cell phone hands-free at any time.
choices.B: They may text while stopped at a red light.
choices.C: They may not use a cell phone while driving, except to make a 911 emergency call.
choices.D: They may use a hand-held cell phone if they have a parent in the car.

en.explanation: If you are under 18 years old, you may not use a cell phone while driving, even hands-free. The only exception is that you may use it to make a 911 emergency call.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding cell phone use while driving for adults in Maryland?

choices.A: It is legal to text while driving if you are on an interstate.
choices.B: It is illegal to use a hand-held cell phone, but hands-free use is allowed.
choices.C: All cell phone use, including hands-free, is completely illegal for all drivers.
choices.D: You may hold your phone to make a call if you are driving under the speed limit.

en.explanation: It is illegal to use a hand-held cell phone, including texting, while driving. You can use your phone for calls while driving if you are not holding it (hands-free).

en.question: How does not getting enough sleep affect your ability to drive?

choices.A: It increases your reaction time and improves awareness.
choices.B: It slows reaction time, decreases awareness, and impairs judgment.
choices.C: It only affects your vision but not your judgment.
choices.D: It makes you more likely to drive aggressively but does not impair coordination.

en.explanation: Sleepiness slows reaction time, decreases awareness, and impairs judgment, just like drugs or alcohol.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a danger sign that you are driving while drowsy?

choices.A: Remembering the last few miles clearly
choices.B: Keeping a consistent speed
choices.C: Having wandering, disconnected thoughts
choices.D: Checking your mirrors frequently

en.explanation: According to the manual, danger signs for drowsy drivers include having wandering, disconnected thoughts, not remembering driving the last few miles, and keeping changing your speed.

en.question: What are the potential consequences of being arrested for impaired driving in Maryland?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense
choices.B: Big fines, possible jail time, and thousands of dollars in court costs
choices.C: Only a temporary license suspension
choices.D: Mandatory community service without fines

en.explanation: The manual states that being arrested for impaired driving has serious consequences including big fines, possible jail time, and thousands of dollars in court costs.

en.question: According to the manual, what proportion of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving?

choices.A: One-quarter
choices.B: One-third
choices.C: One-half
choices.D: Two-thirds

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that one-third of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving.

en.question: If a vehicle ahead of you is stopped at a crosswalk, what must you do?

choices.A: Pass the vehicle on the left
choices.B: Honk to alert the pedestrians
choices.C: Pass the vehicle on the right if there is room
choices.D: Not pass the stopped vehicle

en.explanation: The manual states as a basic rule for crosswalks: 'You may not pass any vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk.'

en.question: What must you do immediately after seeing or hearing an approaching emergency vehicle using its signals?

choices.A: Speed up to get out of its way
choices.B: Move as close as possible to the edge of the road and stop
choices.C: Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection
choices.D: Continue at your current speed but move to the right lane

en.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its signals, you must move as close as possible to the edge of the road, stay out of intersections, and remain stopped until it has passed.

en.question: What should you do if you approach a tow truck stopped on the side of the road and cannot safely move to a non-adjacent lane?

choices.A: Maintain your speed and honk your horn
choices.B: Stop completely until the tow truck leaves
choices.C: Slow down to a safe speed and prepare to stop if necessary
choices.D: Accelerate to pass the vehicle quickly

en.explanation: If it is not possible to move over to a lane not immediately adjacent to a stopped emergency or service vehicle, you must slow down to a safe speed and prepare to stop if necessary.
