en.explanation: You may pass on the right when the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn, provided you do not drive off the paved or main traveled portion of the roadway.

en.question: You are prohibited from driving to the left side of the roadway to pass another vehicle when your view is obstructed within how many feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: No vehicle shall be driven to the left side of the roadway when the view is obstructed upon approaching within 100 feet of any bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

en.question: When you are turning left at an intersection, you must:

choices.A: Yield to oncoming vehicles going straight.
choices.B: Take the right-of-way over all other vehicles.
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles turning right.
choices.D: Wait for the traffic light to turn yellow before proceeding.

en.explanation: At intersections, drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight.

en.question: At an intersection where there is no stop sign or traffic signal, who must you yield to?

choices.A: Vehicles coming from the left
choices.B: Vehicles coming from the right
choices.C: Vehicles turning left
choices.D: Vehicles entering from a driveway

en.explanation: At an intersection where there is no stop sign or traffic signal (with the exception of roundabouts), drivers must yield to vehicles coming from the right.

en.question: What should you do if you are in an intersection when you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching with its siren and flashing lights?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.
choices.B: Pull over to the left edge of the intersection and stop.
choices.C: Drive through the intersection before pulling over to the right edge of the road.
choices.D: Speed up to clear the intersection and stay ahead of the emergency vehicle.

en.explanation: If you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over to the right edge of the road. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.

en.question: When approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying lighted red or red and blue lights on a multi-lane roadway, what must you do if it is safe?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for the vehicle to move.
choices.B: Make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to the stationary vehicle.
choices.C: Honk your horn to alert the emergency workers.
choices.D: Maintain your speed and stay in the adjacent lane.

en.explanation: You must proceed with caution and, if safe to do so, make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to the stationary vehicle.

en.question: How far in advance will a school bus flash its amber warning lights before coming to a designated stop?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Amber warning lights will flash 500 feet before the bus comes to a designated stop to load or unload school children.

en.question: During the backing portion of the driving skills test, the examiner will check to see if you:

choices.A: Rely solely on your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Look over your right shoulder to see through the rear glass.
choices.C: Back up at a speed of at least 15 mph.
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights before backing.

en.explanation: When testing for backing, the examiner will check if you are looking over your right shoulder to see through the rear glass.

en.question: When approaching a roundabout intersection, you must:

choices.A: Yield to traffic already in the circle and pedestrians in the crosswalks.
choices.B: Enter without stopping as you have the right-of-way.
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles entering from the right.
choices.D: Stop in the middle of the roundabout to let other vehicles enter.

en.explanation: When approaching a roundabout intersection, always yield to traffic in the circle and pedestrians in the crosswalks. Wait for a gap in traffic before entering.

en.question: In which of the following situations are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing?

choices.A: When traveling in the same direction on a two-lane road
choices.B: When traveling in the opposite direction on a highway with four or more lanes
choices.C: When traveling in the opposite direction on a two-lane road
choices.D: When following the bus on a two-lane, one-way street

en.explanation: You do not have to stop when you are traveling the opposite direction of a school bus on a highway containing four or more lanes of traffic.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you should signal before making a turn?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that you should signal at least 100 feet before you turn so the other drivers can be ready.

en.question: Where is it specifically prohibited to make a U-turn?

choices.A: On a straight, flat two-lane highway
choices.B: At an intersection controlled by a traffic signal or police officer
choices.C: On a residential street with no traffic
choices.D: In a designated two-way left-turn lane

en.explanation: Never make a U-turn at a location that is marked with a 'No U-Turn' sign or at an intersection controlled by a traffic signal or police officer.

en.question: Why should you avoid swinging wide to the left before making a right turn?

choices.A: It will cause your vehicle to lose traction
choices.B: The driver behind you may think you are turning left and try to pass on the right
choices.C: It is illegal to cross the center line under any circumstances
choices.D: It will trigger the traffic signal sensors incorrectly

en.explanation: If you swing wide to the left before a right turn, the driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or going to turn left, and may try to pass you on the right.

en.question: What is the maximum distance a vehicle may travel in a center two-way left-turn lane?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1,000 feet

en.explanation: The manual specifies that you must not use a two-way left-turn lane as a travel lane, and a vehicle may not travel in this lane for more than 500 feet.

en.question: Which of the following maneuvers is strictly prohibited when entering a roundabout?

choices.A: Yielding to pedestrians
choices.B: Making a left turn to enter
choices.C: Slowing down before entering
choices.D: Making a slight right turn

en.explanation: When approaching a roundabout, the manual explicitly states to 'NEVER make a left turn to enter a roundabout.'

en.question: Who has the right-of-way at a roundabout?

choices.A: Vehicles entering the roundabout
choices.B: Vehicles already within the roundabout
choices.C: Large trucks approaching the roundabout
choices.D: Vehicles exiting the roundabout

en.explanation: When traveling through a roundabout, vehicles within the roundabout have the right of way.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your intended exit while traveling through a roundabout?

choices.A: Stop and wait for traffic to clear before backing up
choices.B: Make a U-turn inside the roundabout
choices.C: Continue through the roundabout until you reach your appropriate exit
choices.D: Change lanes immediately to force your way out

en.explanation: If you miss your exit, you must continue through the roundabout until you reach your appropriate exit.

en.question: How should you react if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are driving inside a roundabout?

choices.A: Stop immediately inside the roundabout to let it pass
choices.B: Speed up and exit as quickly as possible
choices.C: Exit immediately and pull to the right
choices.D: Pull over to the center island

en.explanation: NEVER stop while inside a roundabout. If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in the roundabout, exit immediately and pull to the right.

en.question: What is the purpose of a truck apron in a roundabout?

choices.A: It is a designated parking area for disabled vehicles
choices.B: It is a passing lane for passenger cars and SUVs
choices.C: It provides extra space for the rear wheels of large trucks when turning
choices.D: It is a safe zone for pedestrians to cross

en.explanation: A truck apron is the paved area on the inside of the roundabout for the rear wheels of large trucks to use when turning. It is not to be used by cars, SUVs, or pickup trucks.

en.question: How does a driver navigate a J-turn intersection?

choices.A: By crossing all lanes of traffic directly to the opposite side
choices.B: By turning right, merging into the far left lane, and then making a left turn
choices.C: By entering a circular island and yielding to the left
choices.D: By using a center two-way left-turn lane to merge

en.explanation: At a J-turn intersection, drivers turn right in the same direction of traffic, merge into the far left lane, and then make a left turn in the direction they intend to travel.

en.question: According to the manual, local governments have the authority to create traffic ordinances that do which of the following?

choices.A: Issue driver's licenses
choices.B: Prohibit the use of sound-producing warning devices
choices.C: Change the state's minimum driving age
choices.D: Eliminate the need for vehicle registration

en.explanation: Cities and towns may have regulations to do several things, including to 'Prohibit the use of sound-producing warning devices.'

en.question: When making a turn where there are no signs or lane markings, which lane should you turn into?

choices.A: The lane furthest from the one you came from
choices.B: The center lane, regardless of direction
choices.C: The lane closest to the one you came from
choices.D: Any lane that is free of traffic

en.explanation: If there are no signs or lane markings to control turning, you should turn from the lane that is closest to the direction you want to go, and turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.

en.question: Which of the following is a restriction when using a two-way left-turn lane?

choices.A: You cannot use it to slow down before making a left turn
choices.B: You must not use it when entering the roadway from a side street
choices.C: You can only use it if you are driving a commercial vehicle
choices.D: You must travel in it for at least 500 feet before turning

en.explanation: The manual states regarding two-way left-turn lanes: 'do not use this lane when entering the roadway from a side street.'

en.question: When traveling in the same lane as a motorcycle, you should:

choices.A: Share the lane to improve traffic flow.
choices.B: Not share the lane, as the motorcyclist needs the entire lane.
choices.C: Drive closely behind them to reduce wind resistance.
choices.D: Pass them within the same lane if it is wide enough.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you should not share a lane with a motorcycle because the motorcyclist needs the entire lane for safety reasons.

en.question: What is required to legally drive a motorcycle on public streets?

choices.A: A standard Class F driver license only.
choices.B: A valid driver license with a motorcycle endorsement or a motorcycle license.
choices.C: A commercial driver license (CDL).
choices.D: A special permit from the highway patrol.

en.explanation: To drive any motorcycle on the public streets, you must have a valid driver license with a motorcycle endorsement or a motorcycle license.

en.question: What is the "No-Zone" in reference to large trucks and buses?

choices.A: The designated parking area for commercial vehicles.
choices.B: The blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in the front of the vehicle.
choices.C: The lane restricted for trucks traveling up steep grades.
choices.D: The area near weigh stations where cars are not allowed.

en.explanation: A truck or bus has blind spots on each side, in the rear and in the front where an automobile cannot be seen. These blind spots are referred to as the "No-Zone."

en.question: Approximately how long does it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph to come to a complete stop?

choices.A: 130 to 140 feet.
choices.B: 200 feet.
choices.C: Almost 400 feet.
choices.D: Over 600 feet.

en.explanation: While an average passenger car at 55 mph can stop in about 130-140 feet, a fully loaded tractor-trailer may take almost 400 feet to come to a complete stop.

en.question: What should you do as a pedestrian if a flashing "Don't Walk" sign appears while you are already crossing the street?

choices.A: Stop in the middle of the crosswalk and wait.
choices.B: Turn around and return to the curb you started from.
choices.C: Run as fast as possible to the other side.
choices.D: Finish crossing the street.

en.explanation: The manual states that if the flashing "Don't Walk" sign appears when you are crossing the street, you may finish crossing the street.

en.question: When passing a large truck, when is it safe to reenter the lane in front of the truck?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the front of the truck.
choices.B: When you can see the cab of the truck in your rearview mirror.
choices.C: Immediately after you activate your right turn signal.
choices.D: When the truck driver flashes their headlights.

en.explanation: After you pass a truck, make sure you can see the cab of the truck in your rearview mirror before reentering the lane.

en.question: As a motorcycle rider, how much clearance should you leave when passing to the left of a parked or moving vehicle?

choices.A: One to two feet.
choices.B: Three to four feet.
choices.C: Five to six feet.
choices.D: At least one full lane width.

en.explanation: Motorcycle riders should leave three to four feet of clearance when passing to the left of a parked or moving vehicle to avoid suddenly opened car doors or to allow for a vehicle to swerve.

en.question: If a pedestrian crosses the road in the middle of a block where there is no crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The pedestrian always has the right-of-way.
choices.B: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way to all traffic.
choices.C: Vehicles must stop and yield to the pedestrian.
choices.D: The right-of-way belongs to whichever party is moving faster.

en.explanation: When crossing in the middle of the block without a crosswalk, a pedestrian must yield the right-of-way to all traffic.

en.question: Why might a large truck swing out to the left before making a turn?

choices.A: To allow cars to pass on the right.
choices.B: As the first step in making a right turn due to their large size.
choices.C: To check their left-side blind spots.
choices.D: To gain more speed before entering the intersection.

en.explanation: Because of their size, large trucks may swing out to the left as the first step in making a right turn.

en.question: If a vehicle ahead of you has stopped or slowed down for a pedestrian, you should:

choices.A: Honk your horn to warn the pedestrian and proceed.
choices.B: Pass the vehicle on the left if the lane is clear.
choices.C: Pass the vehicle on the right using the shoulder.
choices.D: Not pass the vehicle.

en.explanation: As a driver, you must not pass a vehicle that has stopped or slowed down for a pedestrian.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to underestimate the speed of an approaching tractor-trailer?

choices.A: Because they often appear to be traveling faster than they actually are.
choices.B: Because their large size makes them appear to be traveling more slowly than their actual speed.
choices.C: Because they frequently speed up when approaching intersections.
choices.D: Because their headlights are dimmer than passenger cars.

en.explanation: Never underestimate the size and speed of an approaching tractor-trailer. Because of its large size, a tractor-trailer often appears to be traveling more slowly than its actual speed.

en.question: Why might a motorcyclist suddenly change speed or lane position?

choices.A: To prevent cars from passing them.
choices.B: To react to bad road conditions like manhole covers or road debris.
choices.C: Because their vehicles are lighter and harder to steer on smooth pavement.
choices.D: To signal that they are about to make a U-turn.

en.explanation: Motorcyclists change speed and lane position when encountering bad road conditions, such as manhole covers, diagonal railroad tracks, road debris, or in strong winds.

en.question: According to the manual, municipalities, cities, and towns have the authority to enact regulations that:

choices.A: Issue commercial driver licenses.
choices.B: Prohibit commercial vehicles from using certain streets.
choices.C: Override state highway speed limits on interstates.
choices.D: Exempt motorcycles from helmet laws.

en.explanation: Cities and towns may have regulations to do several things, including prohibiting commercial vehicles from using certain streets.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving too closely behind a large truck or bus?

choices.A: You cannot see the driver in his or her rearview mirrors.
choices.B: You can read the license plate clearly.
choices.C: The truck's brake lights appear excessively bright.
choices.D: You are within 100 feet of the vehicle.

en.explanation: If you are driving behind a truck or a bus and cannot see the driver in his or her rearview mirrors, the driver of that vehicle cannot see you.

en.question: If you are walking as a pedestrian and there is no sidewalk available, how should you walk?

choices.A: Walk in the same direction as traffic.
choices.B: Walk facing traffic.
choices.C: Walk in the center of the road.
choices.D: Walk on the right side of the road regardless of traffic flow.

en.explanation: The manual states that pedestrians should walk facing traffic when no sidewalk is available.

en.question: What must a driver do when a pedestrian guided by a dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street?

choices.A: Honk the horn to alert them
choices.B: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.C: Come to a complete stop
choices.D: Steer around the pedestrian

en.explanation: When a pedestrian is crossing a street or highway guided by a dog or carrying a white cane (or a white cane with a red tip), vehicles must come to a complete stop.

en.question: When must you obey a slower speed limit in a school zone?

choices.A: Only during morning hours
choices.B: When lights are flashing or children are present
choices.C: Only when a crossing guard is present
choices.D: At all times, 24 hours a day

en.explanation: You must obey a slower speed limit in a school zone when lights are flashing or children are present.

en.question: When passing a bicycle or moped, you should:

choices.A: Squeeze past them if the lane is narrow
choices.B: Honk your horn to make them move over
choices.C: Give them a full lane width
choices.D: Pass as closely as possible

en.explanation: When you are passing, give bicycles and mopeds a full lane width. Do not squeeze past these road users.

en.question: When are you permitted to cross a designated bicycle lane?

choices.A: When passing another motor vehicle
choices.B: When turning or when entering or leaving the roadway
choices.C: Whenever you need extra room to maneuver
choices.D: You are never allowed to cross a bicycle lane

en.explanation: You may cross a bicycle lane when turning or when entering or leaving the roadway. You must yield to bicyclists in a bicycle lane.

en.question: When riding a bicycle or moped on public streets, you should:

choices.A: Always ride against traffic
choices.B: Always ride with traffic, never against it
choices.C: Ride on the sidewalk whenever possible
choices.D: Weave in and out of parked cars

en.explanation: On public streets and highways, you have the same rights and responsibilities as a motor vehicle operator. Always ride with traffic, never against it.

en.question: Where is it illegal to ride a moped?

choices.A: On residential streets
choices.B: On public streets and highways
choices.C: On any part of the federal interstate highway system
choices.D: On roads with a speed limit over 35 mph

en.explanation: The law does not allow you to ride a moped on any part of the federal interstate highway system.

en.question: The brakes on a moped or bicycle must be able to stop the vehicle within:

choices.A: 15 feet when traveling 10 mph
choices.B: 25 feet when traveling 10 mph
choices.C: 50 feet when traveling 20 mph
choices.D: 100 feet when traveling 30 mph

en.explanation: Your brakes must be able to stop you within 25 feet when traveling ten mph.

en.question: When riding a bicycle between 1/2 hour after sunset and 1/2 hour before sunrise, you must have a white light on the front visible from at least:

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 600 feet

en.explanation: You must have a White Light on the front of your bicycle or carried by you that other drivers can see from 500 feet.

en.question: When riding a bicycle at night, your rear red reflector or rear red light must be visible when reflected by low beam headlights at:

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 600 feet

en.explanation: You must have a Rear Red Reflector, at least two square inches, or a Rear Red Light that drivers can see when reflected by their vehicles’ low beam headlights at 600 feet.

en.question: Does the operation of an electric bicycle require a driver license?

choices.A: Yes, a standard operator license is required
choices.B: Yes, a motorcycle license is required
choices.C: No, it does not require an operator or motorcycle license
choices.D: Yes, a commercial driver license is required

en.explanation: Operation of an electric bicycle as defined by 301.010 RSMo does not require the rider to hold an operator license or motorcycle license.

en.question: Which of the following has the right-of-way at all intersections regardless of any traffic control device (except for emergency vehicles)?

choices.A: Bicyclists
choices.B: Mopeds
choices.C: An organized funeral procession
choices.D: Pedestrians outside of crosswalks

en.explanation: An organized funeral procession has the right-of-way at all intersections regardless of any traffic control device, except for emergency vehicles or when directed otherwise by law enforcement officials.

en.question: If you are driving a vehicle in a funeral procession, what must you use?

choices.A: Your high beam headlights
choices.B: Your horn at every intersection
choices.C: Your flashing emergency lights
choices.D: Your left turn signal continuously

en.explanation: Every vehicle in the procession must use its flashing emergency lights.

en.question: A bicyclist may move toward the middle or left of the lane when:

choices.A: The lane is too narrow to share with another vehicle
choices.B: They want to ride side-by-side with a friend
choices.C: They are traveling slower than the flow of traffic
choices.D: They are approaching a hill

en.explanation: You may move more toward the middle or left of the lane or roadway, as appropriate when: Making a left turn; Avoiding hazards; The lane is too narrow to share with another vehicle; or There is a right-turn-only lane and you are going straight.

en.question: When does an organized funeral procession have the right-of-way at an intersection?

choices.A: Only when the traffic light is green.
choices.B: At all intersections regardless of traffic control devices, except for emergency vehicles.
choices.C: Only at four-way stops.
choices.D: They never have the right-of-way over regular traffic.

en.explanation: According to the manual, an organized funeral procession has the right-of-way at all intersections regardless of any traffic control device, except for emergency vehicles or when directed otherwise by law enforcement.

en.question: If you are not involved in an organized funeral procession, what is the rule regarding passing the procession?

choices.A: You may pass at any time if you honk your horn.
choices.B: You may pass only if you use the right shoulder.
choices.C: You must never pass a funeral procession under any circumstances.
choices.D: You may not pass any vehicle in the procession except where a passing lane has been specifically provided.

en.explanation: The manual states that drivers not involved in a funeral procession must not attempt to pass any vehicle in the procession except where a passing lane has been specifically provided.

en.question: What number should you dial on your cellular phone to report a road rage incident after safely exiting the roadway?

choices.B: *55 (or 911 if you are in a metropolitan area)
choices.C: *HP

en.explanation: When confronted with road rage, the manual advises to exit the roadway to a safe area and dial *55 (or 911 if you are in a metropolitan area).

en.question: What is the maximum penalty if a judge finds you guilty of littering?

choices.A: A $500 fine and 30 days in jail.
choices.B: A $1,000 fine and/or up to one year in jail.
choices.C: A $2,000 fine and license suspension.
choices.D: A $100 fine and community service.

en.explanation: Littering is against the law. If a judge finds you guilty of littering, you may have to pay up to a $1,000 fine and/or spend up to one year in jail.

en.question: Where are you normally allowed to park on a one-way street?

choices.A: Only on the right side.
choices.B: Only on the left side.
choices.C: On either the right or left side.
choices.D: Parking is never allowed on one-way streets.

en.explanation: The manual states that on one-way streets, you may normally park on either the right or left side of the street.

en.question: When exiting a parked vehicle on a street, how should passengers, especially children, exit?

choices.A: On the street side to avoid pedestrians.
choices.B: On the curb side.
choices.C: From the trunk.
choices.D: Whichever side is closest to their seat.

en.explanation: The manual advises to always have passengers, especially children, exit the vehicle on the curb side to avoid traffic.

en.question: Which way should you turn your wheels when parking on a hill to prevent the vehicle from rolling into traffic?

choices.A: Sharply towards the center of the road.
choices.B: Straight ahead.
choices.C: Sharply towards the side of the road.
choices.D: Slightly towards the left lane.

en.explanation: When you park on a hill, you should turn your wheels sharply towards the side of the road so that if the vehicle starts to roll downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

en.question: Which of the following is a designated no-parking zone?

choices.A: Alongside a curb that is painted yellow.
choices.B: On the right side of a one-way street.
choices.C: In a designated parking garage.
choices.D: On a street with a speed limit over 35 mph.

en.explanation: The manual lists several areas where you cannot park, including alongside a curb that is painted yellow.

en.question: What is the fine for illegally parking in a space marked with the International Symbol of Access (handicapped parking)?

choices.A: No less than $10 and no more than $50.
choices.B: No less than $50 and no more than $300.
choices.C: Exactly $500.

en.explanation: Violators who park illegally in handicapped spaces, when convicted, shall be punished by a fine of no less than fifty dollars ($50) and no more than three hundred dollars ($300).

en.question: When is it illegal to use a handicapped person's placard to park in a designated handicapped space?

choices.A: When the handicapped person is driving the vehicle.
choices.B: When the handicapped person is being dropped off.
choices.C: When the handicapped person is not being transported at the time.
choices.D: When the vehicle is parked for less than 15 minutes.

en.explanation: It is illegal to use a handicapped person’s placard or license plates to park in designated handicapped parking spaces if the handicapped person is not being transported at the time.

en.question: When beginning to parallel park, how far to the left of the vehicle ahead of the parking space should you stop?

choices.A: About 6 inches.
choices.B: About 1½ feet.
choices.C: About 3 feet.
choices.D: About 5 feet.

en.explanation: To begin parallel parking, you should stop even with the vehicle ahead of the parking space about 1½ feet to the left of that vehicle.

en.question: On a highway with four or more lanes, when are you allowed to drive in the left lane?

choices.A: At any time, as long as you are driving the speed limit.
choices.B: Only when you are driving a commercial vehicle.
choices.C: When passing slower traffic, letting another driver enter safely, or preparing for a left turn.
choices.D: Only during daylight hours.

en.explanation: On highways with four or more lanes, always keep to the right unless you are passing slower traffic, letting another driver have room to enter safely, or getting ready to make a legal left turn.

en.question: When is it permissible to pass a vehicle on the right?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit.
choices.B: When the vehicle ahead is making a left turn, provided you do not use the shoulder or unpaved part of the highway.
choices.C: Whenever there is enough room on the right shoulder.
choices.D: It is never permissible to pass on the right.

en.explanation: You can use the right lane when passing a vehicle that is making a left turn. However, you must never use the shoulder or unpaved part of the highway to pass.

en.question: What is the best way to check your "blind spots" before passing a vehicle on a four-lane highway?

choices.A: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
choices.B: Rely entirely on your inside rearview mirror.
choices.C: Briefly look over your shoulder.
choices.D: Flash your headlights.

en.explanation: Looking over your left shoulder is important because it allows you to check for "blind spots," which are spaces you cannot see with your rearview mirrors.

en.question: How should you secure your vehicle when parking if it has a manual transmission?

choices.A: Leave it in neutral and do not set the parking brake.
choices.B: Leave it in park and set the parking brake.
choices.C: Leave the vehicle in gear and set the parking brake.
choices.D: Leave the keys in the ignition.

en.explanation: The manual instructs to always set your parking brake when you park and to leave the vehicle in gear if it has a manual transmission.

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle begins to pass you?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from passing.
choices.B: Move to the left lane.
choices.C: Tap your brakes to warn the driver.
choices.D: Stay in your lane and do not increase your speed.

en.explanation: The manual states, "If another vehicle begins to pass you, stay in your lane and do not increase your speed."

en.question: If you are driving much slower than other vehicles and traffic is piling up behind you, what should you do?

choices.A: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.
choices.B: Speed up to exceed the speed limit.
choices.C: Pull over and let them pass when it is safe to do so.
choices.D: Turn on your emergency flashers and stop in the lane.

en.explanation: The manual states, "If vehicles are piled up behind you, pull over and let them pass when it is safe to do so."

en.question: If you must stop on the shoulder of the highway in an emergency, how can you alert other drivers?

choices.A: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.
choices.B: Turn on your emergency flashers and raise the hood.
choices.C: Honk your horn continuously.
choices.D: Flash your high-beam headlights.

en.explanation: The manual states, "You can stop on the shoulder of the highway in an emergency. If you do, alert other drivers by turning on your emergency flashers. It is also helpful to raise the hood, or tie a white cloth to the antenna."

en.question: When entering a highway using an entrance ramp and acceleration lane, what should you do?

choices.A: Stop at the end of the acceleration lane and wait for a gap.
choices.B: Drive slowly until you merge into the left lane.
choices.C: Increase your speed to match the speed of the vehicles on the highway.
choices.D: Yield the right-of-way by stopping immediately on the ramp.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Use the ramp and acceleration lane to increase your speed to match the speed of the vehicles on the highway."

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a controlled access highway?

choices.A: Stop and back up to the missed exit.
choices.B: Make a U-turn through the median.
choices.C: Pull onto the shoulder and wait for traffic to clear before backing up.
choices.D: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.

en.explanation: The manual states, "If you miss your exit, DO NOT stop, back up, or try to turn around on the highway. You will have to get off the highway at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed."

en.question: What is a unique feature of driving through a Diverging Diamond Interchange (DDI)?

choices.A: You must stop at all entrance ramps.
choices.B: You will travel on the left side of the roadway for a short distance.
choices.C: You are required to drive in a complete circle.
choices.D: You must yield to traffic entering from the left.

en.explanation: The manual states, "When driving through a DDI, you will travel on the left side of the roadway for a short distance."

en.question: How can you avoid "highway hypnosis" while driving?

choices.A: By constantly moving your eyes and watching traffic and signs.
choices.B: By staring straight ahead at the center line.
choices.C: By driving slightly above the speed limit.
choices.D: By keeping your windows rolled up and the radio off.

en.explanation: The manual states, "You can avoid highway hypnosis by constantly moving your eyes and watching the traffic and highway signs around you."

en.question: What is the cellular phone number to call in an emergency on Missouri roadways?

choices.C: *HP

en.explanation: The manual states, "The cellular number to call in an emergency is *55."

en.question: What does a yellow pavement line on the roadway indicate?

choices.A: It separates traffic traveling in the same direction.
choices.B: It marks the right edge of the road.
choices.C: It separates traffic traveling in opposite directions.
choices.D: It indicates a pedestrian crosswalk.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Yellow separates traffic traveling in opposite directions."

en.question: What does a center marking consisting of two solid yellow lines indicate?

choices.A: Traffic on the other side is moving in the same direction.
choices.B: You may cross the lines to pass if the way is clear.
choices.C: You should never cross the two solid yellow lines to pass.
choices.D: You are approaching an intersection.

en.explanation: The manual states, "The yellow lines tell you the traffic on the other side of the lines is moving in the opposite direction. You should never cross the two solid yellow lines to pass."

en.question: When required to stop because of a sign or signal, where must you stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Just past the stop line so you can see traffic.
choices.B: Before your vehicle reaches the stop line or crosswalk.
choices.C: Inside the crosswalk.
choices.D: At least 20 feet before the stop line.

en.explanation: The manual states, "When required to stop because of a sign or signal, you must stop before your vehicle reaches the stop line or, if there is one, the crosswalk."

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you have a flat tire, what should you NEVER do?

choices.A: Turn on your emergency flashers.
choices.B: Try to change a tire if it means you have to be in a traffic lane.
choices.C: Tie a white cloth to the antenna or door handle.
choices.D: Place emergency flares behind the vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Never stand in the roadway. Do not try to change a tire if it means you have to be in a traffic lane."

en.question: What must you do when approaching an intersection with a crosswalk but no marked lines?

choices.A: Proceed without yielding if there are no lines painted on the road.
choices.B: Yield to pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk.
choices.C: Sound your horn to warn pedestrians before driving through.
choices.D: Stop only if a traffic signal is currently red.

en.explanation: The manual states that not all crosswalks are marked, and you must yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk. You must be alert for pedestrians when crossing intersections that do not have defined crosswalks.

en.question: You are in a dual-use lane and want to turn. The traffic signal shows only a straight arrow. What should you do?

choices.A: Turn cautiously if the intersection is clear of oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Proceed straight and turn at the next available intersection.
choices.C: Wait for the turn arrow to appear before making your turn.
choices.D: Merge into the adjacent lane to make your turn.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you want to turn in a dual-use lane and only the straight arrow is showing, you must wait for the turn arrow.

en.question: Why should you never pass a vehicle on the shoulder of the road?

choices.A: It is illegal unless you are driving a commercial vehicle.
choices.B: Other drivers will not expect you to be there and may pull off the road without looking.
choices.C: The shoulder is reserved strictly for law enforcement vehicles.
choices.D: Shoulders are always too soft to support the weight of a passenger vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual warns to never pass on the shoulder because "Other drivers will not expect you to be there and may pull off the road without looking."

en.question: If a traffic officer signals for you to stop at a green light, what must you do?

choices.A: Proceed cautiously because the traffic light is green.
choices.B: Stop, because you must obey traffic officers at all times.
choices.C: Honk your horn to get the officer's attention before proceeding.
choices.D: Pull over to the shoulder and wait for the light to turn red.

en.explanation: You must obey traffic officers at all times. If an officer gives directions, you must do what they say and ignore any traffic signs or signals, including stopping at a green light.

en.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.B: The traffic signal is broken and you automatically have the right-of-way.
choices.C: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
choices.D: Stop and wait for the light to turn solid green.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign.

en.question: How should you treat an intersection where the traffic signals are dark or not working?

choices.A: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
choices.B: Proceed through the intersection without stopping.
choices.C: Treat the intersection as a yield sign.
choices.D: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

en.explanation: The manual states that dark signals, or traffic signals that aren't working, operate as a four-way stop.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow indicate when you are turning left?

choices.A: You have a protected turn and opposing traffic is stopped.
choices.B: You are allowed to turn but must wait for an adequate gap in opposing traffic.
choices.C: You must stop and wait for a solid green arrow.
choices.D: The traffic signal is about to turn red.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow tells you that you are allowed to drive in the direction the arrow is pointing but are required to wait for an adequate gap in the opposing traffic prior to making your turn.

en.question: What color is used for traffic signs indicating public recreation and cultural interests?

choices.A: Blue
choices.B: Green
choices.C: Brown
choices.D: Orange

en.explanation: The manual's sign color chart indicates that Brown is used for Public Recreation & Cultural Interests.

en.question: Which sign shape is used exclusively for warning signs?

choices.A: Octagon
choices.B: Vertical Rectangle
choices.C: Diamond
choices.D: Pennant

en.explanation: According to the sign shapes chart in the manual, the Diamond shape is used for Warning signs.

en.question: What shape is a school zone or school crossing sign?

choices.A: Pentagon
choices.B: Round
choices.C: Triangle
choices.D: Horizontal Rectangle

en.explanation: The manual's sign shapes chart specifies that a Pentagon shape is used for School signs.

en.question: What does an "Added Lane" sign indicate?

choices.A: Two lanes of traffic will soon become one lane.
choices.B: Traffic from another road is entering, but no merging is necessary because a lane has been added.
choices.C: You must merge left to allow entering traffic to join the roadway.
choices.D: The road will soon become two-way traffic divided by a median.

en.explanation: The "Added Lane" sign means traffic from another road will be entering the road, and no merging is necessary because a lane has been added.

en.question: What is the difference between a Curve sign and a Turn sign?

choices.A: A Turn sign indicates a recommended maximum speed of 30 mph or less, while a Curve sign is for recommended speeds less than the posted limit but generally higher than 30 mph.
choices.B: A Curve sign is only used on divided highways, while a Turn sign is used on two-lane roads.
choices.C: A Turn sign means you must come to a complete stop, while a Curve sign means you only need to slow down.
choices.D: There is no difference; they are used interchangeably on all roads.

en.explanation: The manual states a turn sign warns of a sharp turn where the recommended maximum speed is 30 mph or less, whereas a curve sign warns of a curve where the recommended speed is less than the posted speed limit.

en.question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle mean?

choices.A: The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
choices.B: The vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.
choices.C: The vehicle is broken down and cannot move.
choices.D: The vehicle is a wide load and you cannot pass.

en.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle is a Slow Moving Vehicle sign, which means the vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.

en.question: How are shared center lanes marked on the pavement?

choices.A: By double solid white lines on each side.
choices.B: By a single dashed white line in the center.
choices.C: By a solid yellow and dashed yellow line on each side.
choices.D: By double solid yellow lines on each side.

en.explanation: The manual states that shared center lanes are marked on each side by a solid yellow and dashed yellow lines.

en.question: What shape and color are most regulatory signs?

choices.A: Diamond-shaped and yellow
choices.B: Round and blue
choices.C: Square or rectangular and white with black or red letters
choices.D: Triangular and orange

en.explanation: Many regulatory signs are square- or rectangular-shaped and are white, with black or red letters or symbols.

en.question: If you approach a stop sign at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where must you stop?

choices.A: At the exact location of the stop sign
choices.B: Before entering the intersection
choices.C: Ten feet before the intersection
choices.D: You do not need to stop if the intersection is clear

en.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must pull up and stop near the edge of the intersection before entering it.

en.question: Under normal roadway conditions, what is the minimum speed you may drive on an interstate highway in Missouri?

choices.A: 30 mph
choices.B: 40 mph
choices.C: 45 mph
choices.D: 50 mph

en.explanation: You may not drive slower than 40 mph on interstate highways under normal roadway conditions.

en.question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the default speed limit in any city, town, or village in Missouri?

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: The speed limit in any city, town, or village is 25 mph, unless posted otherwise.

en.question: What is the maximum speed limit on lettered roads in Missouri, unless posted otherwise?

choices.A: 45 mph
choices.B: 50 mph
choices.C: 55 mph
choices.D: 60 mph

en.explanation: According to the maximum speed guide in the manual, the speed limit for lettered roads is 55 mph.

en.question: When you must stop at a railroad crossing because the red lights are flashing or the gate is down, how far from the tracks must you stop?

choices.A: 5 to 10 feet
choices.B: 10 to 15 feet
choices.C: 15 to 50 feet
choices.D: 50 to 100 feet

en.explanation: You must stop within 15 to 50 feet before the railroad tracks if the red lights are flashing or the gate is down.

en.question: Why is it advised not to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks?

choices.A: It damages the transmission.
choices.B: It causes the vehicle to speed up too quickly.
choices.C: Your vehicle might stall.
choices.D: It is illegal.

en.explanation: It is not wise to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks, just in case your vehicle might stall.

en.question: A white, X-shaped "crossbuck" sign at a railroad crossing has the same meaning as which other sign?

choices.A: Stop sign
choices.B: Yield sign
choices.C: Do Not Enter sign
choices.D: Speed Limit sign

en.explanation: A white, X-shaped sign or "crossbuck" is located at the railroad crossing. This sign has the same meaning as a "yield" sign; therefore, you must yield to trains at crossings.

en.question: What color are work zone signs?

choices.A: Fluorescent orange
choices.B: Bright yellow
choices.C: Neon green
choices.D: Reflective white

en.explanation: Work zone signs are fluorescent orange and indicate some type of work is being performed on or alongside the roadway.

en.question: In which type of work zone will you find a flagger providing traffic control to oncoming vehicles?

choices.A: A mobile work zone
choices.B: A shoulder work zone
choices.C: A two-lane, two-way roadway with one lane closed
choices.D: A multi-lane interstate with all lanes open

en.explanation: A Flagging Operation is work that takes place on a two-lane, two-way roadway with one lane closed. A flagger(s) will be present at the beginning and end points of the work zone providing traffic control.

en.question: What should a driver expect to see when approaching a mobile work zone?

choices.A: A permanent concrete barrier
choices.B: A protective vehicle with a flashing arrow panel
choices.C: A detour sign directing traffic off the highway
choices.D: A temporary stoplight

en.explanation: When approaching the mobile work zone, a driver should expect to see a protective vehicle in the lane with a flashing arrow panel designating the correct lane to merge to.

en.question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a red slash over a symbol indicate?

choices.A: You must yield the right-of-way.
choices.B: You are approaching a hazard.
choices.C: You cannot do something, such as a U-turn.
choices.D: You must stop immediately.

en.explanation: Some regulatory signs have a red circle with a red slash over a symbol. These indicate you cannot do something, for example, no left turn, or no U-turn.

en.question: What should you do if you see a "Wrong Way" sign and realize you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic?

choices.A: Honk your horn and continue driving slowly.
choices.B: Reverse your vehicle until you reach the intersection.
choices.C: Pull off the road as quickly and safely as possible, turn around, and go back.
choices.D: Stop in your lane and wait for traffic to clear.

en.explanation: If you made a wrong turn and have entered a lane of oncoming traffic, you must, as quickly and safely as possible, pull off the road, turn around and go back.

en.question: What color and shape are guide signs that show direction and distance to various locations?

choices.A: Square or rectangular, blue with white lettering
choices.B: Square or rectangular, green or brown with white lettering
choices.C: Diamond-shaped, yellow with black lettering
choices.D: Circular, green with white lettering

en.explanation: Guide signs are square or rectangular, and are green or brown with white lettering. They show direction and distance to various locations such as cities, airports, and state lines.

en.question: Which signs show the location of various services, such as rest areas and hospitals?

choices.A: Guide signs
choices.B: Route signs
choices.C: Service signs
choices.D: Emergency reference markers

en.explanation: Service signs are square or rectangular, and are blue with white letters or symbols. They show the location of various services, such as rest areas and hospitals.

en.question: How are north-south routes identified on route signs?

choices.A: By even numbers
choices.B: By odd numbers
choices.C: By three-digit even numbers
choices.D: By three-digit odd numbers

en.explanation: North-south routes are identified by odd numbers. East-west roads are identified by even numbers.

en.question: On an interstate traveling west to east, how are the exit numbers arranged?

choices.A: They start at zero on the east and increase as you drive west.
choices.B: They start at zero on the west and increase as you drive east.
choices.C: They are numbered randomly based on the county.
choices.D: They start at zero at the state capital and increase outward.

en.explanation: Interstates traveling west/east are numbered starting from the west and going east. This means exit numbers start at zero and increase as you drive east.

en.question: How often are emergency reference markers located along the outside shoulder of the interstate?

choices.A: Every one-tenth of a mile
choices.B: Every two-tenths of a mile
choices.C: Every half mile
choices.D: Every full mile

en.explanation: The reference markers are located every two-tenths of a mile, so motorists will always be in sight of a sign.

en.question: What is the proper way to wear a vehicle seat belt?

choices.A: The lap belt low and snug across the hips and the shoulder belt across the chest.
choices.B: The lap belt across the stomach and the shoulder belt under the arm.
choices.C: The lap belt low across the hips and the shoulder belt behind the back.
choices.D: The lap belt loosely across the thighs and the shoulder belt across the neck.

en.explanation: Seat belts should always be worn with the lap belt low and snug across the hips and the shoulder belt across the chest. Shoulder belts should never be placed under the arm or behind the back.

en.question: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recommends drivers sit with at least how much space between the center of their breastbone and the center of the steering wheel?

choices.A: Five inches
choices.B: Eight inches
choices.C: Ten inches
choices.D: Twelve inches

en.explanation: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recommends drivers sit with at least ten inches between the center of their breastbone and the center of the steering wheel to prevent injury from a deploying air bag.

en.question: According to Missouri law, who must be properly restrained when accompanying an intermediate driver license holder?

choices.A: Only the driver and front seat passengers
choices.B: Only children under the age of 12
choices.C: Only passengers in the back seat
choices.D: ALL passengers in the vehicle

en.explanation: Missouri law requires that ALL passengers accompanying an intermediate driver license holder must be properly restrained.

en.question: Under Missouri's Child Passenger Restraint Law, what is required for a child who is less than four years old?

choices.A: They may use a standard vehicle safety belt if they weigh over 30 pounds.
choices.B: They must be secured in a child passenger restraint system appropriate for that child, regardless of weight.
choices.C: They must be secured in a booster seat.
choices.D: They are allowed to ride unrestrained in the back seat.

en.explanation: Children less than four years old, regardless of weight, shall be secured in a child passenger restraint system appropriate for that child.

en.question: A child who is six years old, weighs 50 pounds, and is 4'5" tall must be secured in what type of restraint?

choices.A: A standard vehicle safety belt
choices.B: A rear-facing infant restraint
choices.C: A child passenger restraint system or booster seat
choices.D: No restraint is required by law

en.explanation: Children at least four years of age but less than eight years of age, who also weigh at least 40 pounds but less than 80 pounds, and are also less than 4'9" tall shall be secured in a child passenger restraint system or booster seat.

en.question: When approaching an intersection as a defensive driver, what should you do even if other traffic has a red light or stop sign?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
choices.B: Look to the left and right.
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
choices.D: Rely completely on the traffic signal to keep others from crossing.

en.explanation: At an intersection, look to the left and right, even if other traffic has a red light or a stop sign. Do not rely on traffic signals or signs to keep others from crossing in front of you.

en.question: What is the recommended hand position on the steering wheel?

choices.A: Left hand at 10 o'clock and right hand at 2 o'clock
choices.B: Left hand between 7 & 9 o'clock and right hand between 3 & 5 o'clock
choices.C: Both hands resting at the 6 o'clock position
choices.D: Left hand at 12 o'clock and right hand on the gear shift

en.explanation: Use a proper grip. Place your left hand between the seven & nine o'clock positions and your right hand between the three & five o'clock positions on the steering wheel.

en.question: Why should you never turn your vehicle's ignition key to the "lock" position while the vehicle is still in motion?

choices.A: It will cause the engine to overheat.
choices.B: It will permanently damage the transmission.
choices.C: It will cause the steering wheel to lock, resulting in a loss of control.
choices.D: It will deploy the vehicle's air bags.

en.explanation: Never turn your vehicle's ignition key to the "lock" position while your vehicle is still in motion. This will cause the steering wheel to lock if you try to turn the steering wheel, and you will lose control of your vehicle.

en.question: What is a good way to measure a safe following distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you?

choices.A: The one car length rule
choices.B: The three second rule
choices.C: The five second rule
choices.D: The ten foot rule

en.explanation: A good way to measure your safe following distance is to use the "three second rule." Count slowly, "one-thousand one, one-thousand two, one-thousand three" after the vehicle ahead passes an object.

en.question: What should you do if you are being followed too closely (tailgated) by another driver and there is a right lane available?

choices.A: Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn the driver.
choices.B: Speed up to increase the distance between vehicles.
choices.C: Move over to the right lane.
choices.D: Stop your vehicle in the lane.

en.explanation: If you are followed too closely or "tailgated" by another driver, and there is a right lane, move over to the right.

en.question: If you are overtaking a bicycle and an oncoming vehicle is approaching at the same time, what is the safest action to take?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the bicycle before the vehicle reaches you.
choices.B: Honk your horn so the bicycle moves off the road.
choices.C: Move closer to the bicycle to leave room for the oncoming vehicle.
choices.D: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first so you can give extra room to the bicycle.

en.explanation: The manual advises taking potential hazards one at a time. If overtaking a bicycle with an oncoming vehicle approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first so you can give extra room to the bicycle.

en.question: A vehicle's total stopping distance is equal to:

choices.A: Braking distance plus following distance.
choices.B: Reaction distance plus braking distance.
choices.C: Reaction distance plus following distance.
choices.D: Braking distance minus reaction distance.

en.explanation: According to the manual, your stopping distance equals your reaction distance plus your braking distance.

en.question: How far in advance should you try to signal before making a turn or lane change?

choices.A: At least 50 feet.
choices.B: At least 100 feet.
choices.C: At least 200 feet.
choices.D: At least 500 feet.

en.explanation: The manual states that you should try to signal at least 100 feet before you make your move.

en.question: If you plan to turn, but there are other streets or driveways between you and where you want to turn, you should:

choices.A: Signal at least 500 feet in advance regardless of the driveways.
choices.B: Turn on your signal immediately to warn other drivers early.
choices.C: Wait until you have passed the other streets or driveways before signaling.
choices.D: Use your hand signals instead of your vehicle's turn signals.

en.explanation: The manual advises that if there are other streets, driveways, or entrances between you and where you want to turn, wait until you have passed them to signal.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the only acceptable reason to use your horn?

choices.A: To show anger or frustration at another driver.
choices.B: To warn other drivers.
choices.C: To let a slow driver know you want to pass.
choices.D: To greet pedestrians or bicyclists.

en.explanation: The manual states there is only one reason to use your horn: to warn other drivers. It should not be used as a display of anger or frustration.

en.question: Under normal driving conditions, when is it legal to drive slower than the posted minimum speed?

choices.A: It is never legal under normal driving conditions.
choices.B: When you are driving a newly purchased vehicle.
choices.C: When you are looking for a specific address.
choices.D: When you are driving in the right lane.

en.explanation: It is against the law to drive slower than the posted minimum speed under normal driving conditions. You may only drive more slowly in bad weather, heavy traffic, or on a bad road.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended practice to avoid deadly carbon monoxide poisoning?

choices.A: Leave the motor running in a closed garage to warm up the vehicle.
choices.B: Use the heater in a parked vehicle with the windows closed.
choices.C: Leave the vents open when following closely behind another vehicle.
choices.D: Do not drive with a defective muffler or exhaust system.

en.explanation: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, the manual explicitly states: "Do not drive with a defective muffler or exhaust system."

en.question: During which months do most deer-related crashes occur?

choices.A: February, March, and April.
choices.B: June, July, and August.
choices.C: January, May, and October through December.
choices.D: September and October only.

en.explanation: The manual states that most deer-related crashes occur in January, May, and October through December.

en.question: Why should you avoid applying too much brake pressure if a deer crash is unavoidable?

choices.A: It will cause your airbags to deploy prematurely.
choices.B: It can cause the front end of the vehicle to drop, allowing the deer to strike the passenger compartment.
choices.C: It will cause the deer to freeze in the headlights.
choices.D: It will lock your steering wheel and prevent you from swerving.

en.explanation: Too much brake pressure can cause the front end of the vehicle to drop down, striking the deer in the legs and allowing the body to come into the passenger compartment.

en.question: Where can you find the recommended PSI (pounds per square inch) for your vehicle's tires?

choices.A: On the sidewall of the tire itself.
choices.B: In the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jam.
choices.C: On the vehicle's steering column.
choices.D: On the engine block.

en.explanation: The manual states to check the tire pressure using the recommended PSI located in the vehicle owner’s manual or the driver’s side door jam of the vehicle.

en.question: When using the penny test to check tire wear, your tires are considered unsafe and have greatly reduced grip if the tread is below approximately:

choices.A: 1/32 of an inch.
choices.B: 2/32 of an inch.
choices.C: 3/32 of an inch.
choices.D: 4/32 of an inch.

en.explanation: The manual states that if your tread gets below approximately 2/32 of an inch, your car's ability to grip the road in adverse conditions is greatly reduced.

en.question: What should you do with your hands when stopped by a law enforcement officer?

choices.A: Keep them hidden under your legs.
choices.B: Reach into the glove compartment to retrieve your registration.
choices.C: Keep them on the steering wheel so they are easily observable.
choices.D: Wave them out the window to signal the officer.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "Keep your hands on the steering wheel so they are easily observable" when stopped by law enforcement.

en.question: If you have a weapon in your vehicle during a traffic stop, when should you inform the law enforcement officer?

choices.A: Only if the officer asks to search the vehicle.
choices.B: Upon first contact with the officer.
choices.C: After you have handed over your driver's license.
choices.D: You are not required to inform the officer.

en.explanation: The manual states: "If you have a weapon(s) in the vehicle, inform the officer upon first contact."

en.question: If you see that a crash with a deer is unavoidable, what does the manual advise you to do?

choices.A: Swerve off the road to the right.
choices.B: Swerve into the path of oncoming traffic.
choices.C: Do not swerve.
choices.D: Accelerate to minimize the impact time.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "If you see that a crash is unavoidable, do not swerve. Swerving off the road or into the path of an oncoming car can increase the risk of injury."

en.question: What does your signature on a traffic ticket indicate?

choices.A: An admission of guilt.
choices.B: A waiver of your right to an attorney.
choices.C: Acceptance of the ticket, but not an admission of guilt.
choices.D: An agreement to pay the fine immediately.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Your acceptance and signature on a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt; however, the refusal to sign a traffic ticket may result in your arrest."

en.question: When are you required to turn on your headlights at night?

choices.A: From 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise.
choices.B: From ½ hour after sunset until ½ hour before sunrise.
choices.C: Only when it is completely dark outside.
choices.D: From sunset to sunrise.

en.explanation: For driving at night, you should turn your headlights on from ½ hour after sunset until ½ hour before sunrise.

en.question: When driving at night, you should use your low beams when you come within what distance of an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You should use your low beams when you come within 500 feet (about one block) of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: How far ahead do your headlights let you see when driving at night?

choices.A: About 200 feet
choices.B: About 350 feet
choices.C: About 500 feet
choices.D: About 600 feet

en.explanation: Do not overdrive your headlights. Your headlights only let you see about 350 feet ahead.

en.question: You must use your headlights any time weather conditions require the use of:

choices.A: Your defroster
choices.B: Your windshield wipers
choices.C: Your emergency flashers
choices.D: Your fog lights

en.explanation: The manual states, "You must use your headlights any time weather conditions require the use of your windshield wipers."

en.question: What is the recommended safe following distance when driving on snow or ice?

choices.A: Two to three seconds
choices.B: Three to four seconds
choices.C: Five to seven seconds
choices.D: Eight to ten seconds

en.explanation: It will take longer to stop your vehicle when driving on snow or ice. Be sure to leave a safe distance, about eight to ten seconds, between your vehicle and any vehicle ahead of you.

en.question: Which parts of the road will freeze and become slippery before other parts?

choices.A: Intersections
choices.B: Bridges and overpasses
choices.C: Curves
choices.D: Uphill grades

en.explanation: Remember that bridges and overpasses will freeze and become slippery before other parts of the road.

en.question: At what speed can hydroplaning begin to happen on wet pavement?

choices.A: Any speed over 25 mph
choices.B: Any speed over 35 mph
choices.C: Any speed over 45 mph
choices.D: Any speed over 55 mph

en.explanation: Hydroplaning refers to a loss of traction and control on wet pavement, and it can happen at any speed over 35 mph.

en.question: What should you do if you think your tires are hydroplaning?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately.
choices.B: Pump the brakes rapidly.
choices.C: Take your foot off the accelerator and slow down.
choices.D: Steer sharply toward the shoulder of the road.

en.explanation: If you think your tires are hydroplaning, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down. Do not hit the brakes as this may cause you to skid.

en.question: If your vehicle is equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do during an emergency braking situation?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly.
choices.B: Maintain a firm and continuous pressure on the brake while steering.
choices.C: Take your foot off the brake and use the emergency brake.
choices.D: Press the brake lightly and avoid steering.

en.explanation: If your car is equipped with ABS, maintain a firm and continuous pressure on the brake while steering to enable the four-wheel ABS to work properly. Do not pump your brakes.

en.question: How should you handle a vehicle skid?

choices.A: Hit the brakes and hold the steering wheel straight.
choices.B: Gently turn your steering wheel in the direction that your rear wheels are sliding.
choices.C: Turn your steering wheel in the opposite direction of the skid.
choices.D: Accelerate to regain traction.

en.explanation: To handle a skid, take your foot off the accelerator, DO NOT hit the brakes, and gently turn your steering wheel in the direction that your rear wheels are sliding.

en.question: When driving in fog, you should keep your headlights on:

choices.A: High beam
choices.B: Low beam
choices.C: Auto setting
choices.D: Parking lights only

en.explanation: Keep your headlights on low beam. In fog, you will see less if your lights are on high beam.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor?

choices.A: Turn off the ignition key immediately.
choices.B: Shift to a high gear.
choices.C: Pump the brake pedal fast and hard several times.
choices.D: Pull the emergency brake as hard as you can.

en.explanation: If your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor, pump the brake pedal fast and hard several times. If that does not work, use your emergency or parking brake gradually.

en.question: What should you do to assist with visibility if you are pulled over by a law enforcement officer at nighttime?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams.
choices.B: Turn on your hazard lights and exit the vehicle.
choices.C: Turn on your interior lights as soon as you stop.
choices.D: Shine a flashlight out the window.

en.explanation: If it’s nighttime, the officer may direct a spotlight at your vehicle once stopped. To assist with visibility, turn on your interior lights as soon as you stop to help the officer see inside your vehicle.

en.question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct action to take regarding the brakes?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately to stop.
choices.B: Pump the brakes rapidly to maintain control.
choices.C: Do not hit the brakes until the vehicle is almost stopped.
choices.D: Apply steady, hard pressure to the brakes.

en.explanation: During a tire blowout, you should take your foot off the accelerator but do not hit the brakes. Apply the brakes only when the vehicle is almost stopped.

en.question: What should you do if your wheels run off the paved edge of the road?

choices.A: Jerk the steering wheel sharply to the left to get back on the road.
choices.B: Accelerate to regain traction on the dirt.
choices.C: Slam on the brakes to stop immediately.
choices.D: Hold the steering wheel tightly and take your foot off the accelerator.

en.explanation: If your wheels run off the paved edge, hold the steering wheel tightly, take your foot off the accelerator, and do not hit the brakes. Only apply gentle brake pressure if necessary.

en.question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what gear should you shift into?

choices.A: Park
choices.B: Reverse
choices.C: Neutral
choices.D: First gear

en.explanation: If your accelerator becomes stuck, you should shift to neutral, apply the brakes, and try to drive safely off the road.

en.question: If a vehicle is approaching head-on in your lane, why should you NOT swing over into the left lane?

choices.A: The left lane is reserved for passing only.
choices.B: The other driver may pull back over into that lane, too.
choices.C: It is illegal to cross the center line in an emergency.
choices.D: Your vehicle will lose traction if you turn left.

en.explanation: When a vehicle is approaching head-on, DO NOT swing over into the left lane because the other driver may pull back over into that lane, too. Instead, pull over to the right and sound your horn.

en.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train is approaching, in which direction should you run after exiting the vehicle?

choices.A: In the direction the train is heading.
choices.B: In the direction the train is coming from.
choices.C: Perpendicular to the tracks.
choices.D: Parallel to the tracks in either direction.

en.explanation: Run in the direction the train is coming from. If you run in the direction the train is heading, you may be hit with debris when the train hits your vehicle.

en.question: According to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), 12- and 15-passenger vans are inherently unstable when carrying more than how many passengers?

choices.A: Six
choices.B: Eight
choices.C: Ten
choices.D: Twelve

en.explanation: The NTSB has determined that 12- and 15-passenger vans are inherently unstable when loaded to the level for which they are designed, carrying more than ten passengers.

en.question: What is a potential penalty if you injure or kill someone because you were drinking or using drugs while driving?

choices.A: Spend two to seven years in jail.
choices.B: Pay a maximum fine of $1,000.
choices.C: Lose your driver license for one year.
choices.D: Complete 100 hours of community service.

en.explanation: If you injure or kill someone because you were drinking or using drugs while driving, you may spend two to seven years in jail, pay a $5,000 fine, and/or lose your driver license for five years.

en.question: If a police officer stops you and your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) level is .08% or more, how many days after receiving the notice will your license be suspended or revoked?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: The officer will take your license away and give you a notice stating that your license will be suspended or revoked (and you will not be able to legally drive) after 15 days.

en.question: What is the maximum jail time for a first offense of Driving While Intoxicated (DWI)?

choices.A: Up to 30 days
choices.B: Up to six months
choices.C: Up to one year
choices.D: Up to four years

en.explanation: For a 1st Offense DWI or BAC of .08% or more, you may spend up to six months in jail and pay up to a $500 fine.

en.question: Under Missouri's Abuse and Lose Law, for how long may your driver license be taken away if you are younger than 21 and possess or use alcohol while driving?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: If you are younger than 21 years of age, your driver license may be taken away for 90 days if you possess or use alcohol or drugs while driving a vehicle.

en.question: What is the driver license penalty for a first offense Minor in Possession (MIP)?

choices.A: 15-day suspension
choices.B: 30-day suspension
choices.C: 90-day suspension
choices.D: One-year revocation

en.explanation: For a 1st Offense Minor in Possession (MIP), the consequence is a 30-day suspension of your driver license.

en.question: What should you do if your hood suddenly flies open and blocks your vision while driving?

choices.A: Roll down the window so you can look around whatever is blocking your view.
choices.B: Slam on the brakes and stop in your lane immediately.
choices.C: Turn on your high beam headlights to see through the gap.
choices.D: Accelerate to force the hood back down.

en.explanation: If your hood suddenly flies open or something else blocks your vision, roll down the window so you can look around whatever is blocking your view, turn on your emergency flashers, and pull off the road.

en.question: If your vehicle's headlights go out, what is the first thing you should try?

choices.A: Pull off the road immediately without signaling.
choices.B: Try the dimmer switch or headlight switch.
choices.C: Turn on your interior dome light.
choices.D: Honk your horn continuously.

en.explanation: If your vehicle's headlights go out, try the dimmer switch or headlight switch, as that might turn them on again.

en.question: To get your license back after it is taken away under the Abuse and Lose Law, you must provide proof of insurance (SR-22 filing) for how long?

choices.A: Six months
choices.B: One year
choices.C: Two years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: To get your license back under the Abuse and Lose Law, you must provide proof of insurance for two years (SR-22 filing), pay a $45 fee, submit a SATOP form, and retake the complete driver exam.

en.question: What is the consequence for a first-offense Minor in Possession (MIP) or having a BAC of more than .02% as a minor?

choices.A: 30-day suspension
choices.B: 90-day suspension
choices.C: One-year revocation
choices.D: 60-day suspension

en.explanation: According to the manual, a 1st Offense for Minor in Possession (MIP) or having a BAC of more than .02% results in a 30-day suspension.

en.question: What penalty does a young person face for a third Minor in Possession (MIP) offense?

choices.A: 30-day suspension
choices.B: 90-day suspension
choices.C: One-year revocation
choices.D: Five-year revocation

en.explanation: The manual states that a 3rd Offense for Minor in Possession (MIP) results in a one-year revocation.

en.question: Who is exempt from filing proof of insurance (SR-22) for a first-offense intoxication-related charge?

choices.A: Commercial drivers with a BAC of .04%
choices.B: Minors with a BAC of .02% or more
choices.C: Drivers over 21 with a BAC of .08%
choices.D: Anyone who refused a chemical test

en.explanation: There is one exception to the SR-22 rule: Minors with a BAC of .02% or more do not have to file proof of insurance on a first-offense.

en.question: What happens to your driver license if you refuse to take a chemical test to determine your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?

choices.A: It is suspended for 30 days.
choices.B: It is suspended for 90 days.
choices.C: It is taken away for one year.
choices.D: It is permanently revoked.

en.explanation: If a police officer stops you and you refuse to take a chemical test to determine your BAC, your driver license will be taken away for one year.

en.question: What vehicle components is an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) connected to?

choices.A: The transmission, brakes, and steering wheel
choices.B: The ignition, horn, and headlights
choices.C: The speedometer, radio, and wipers
choices.D: The exhaust, battery, and alternator

en.explanation: An ignition interlock device (IID) is a mechanical unit that is connected to the vehicle’s ignition, horn, and headlights.

en.question: If required, what is the minimum amount of time an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) must be maintained from your reinstatement date?

choices.A: Three months
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: Two years

en.explanation: The IID must be maintained for a minimum of six months from your reinstatement date without any violations in the last three months.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first-offense conviction of failing to have an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) installed as required by law?

choices.A: A 30-day suspension
choices.B: A 90-day suspension
choices.C: A one-year revocation
choices.D: A five-year revocation

en.explanation: If you receive a ticket for failing to have an IID installed as required by law and you are convicted in court, your driving privilege will be revoked for one year.

en.question: How do the penalties for Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) differ if the impairment is caused by drugs instead of alcohol?

choices.A: Drug impairment carries a lighter penalty.
choices.B: Drug impairment carries a harsher penalty.
choices.C: The penalties are exactly the same.
choices.D: Drug impairment only results in a warning for the first offense.

en.explanation: The penalties for DWI in Missouri are exactly the same regardless of whether the impairment is from drugs or alcohol.

en.question: What is the maximum prison sentence and fine for a DWI conviction in Missouri?

choices.A: Up to 30 days in prison and a $100 fine
choices.B: Up to 6 months in prison and a $500 fine
choices.C: Up to 1 year in prison and a $1,000 fine
choices.D: Up to 5 years in prison and a $5,000 fine

en.explanation: The punishment for those convicted of DWI is up to six months in prison and a fine of up to $500 and the loss of driving privileges.

en.question: What is the illegal Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) limit for a commercial vehicle driver in Missouri?

choices.A: 0.02% or more
choices.B: 0.04% or more
choices.C: 0.06% or more
choices.D: 0.08% or more

en.explanation: It is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.08% or more, but the limit is 0.04% for commercial vehicle drivers.

en.question: How can diet pills and "uppers" affect a driver after the initial short-term alertness wears off?

choices.A: They improve night vision and reaction time.
choices.B: They cause a person to be nervous, dizzy, and unable to concentrate.
choices.C: They permanently increase the driver's attention span.
choices.D: They lower the driver's blood alcohol content.

en.explanation: Pep pills, “uppers,” and diet pills can make a driver more alert for a short time. Later, however, they can cause a person to be nervous, dizzy, and not able to concentrate.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding driving under the influence of marijuana in Missouri?

choices.A: It is legal as long as the driver has a medical marijuana card.
choices.B: It is only illegal if combined with alcohol.
choices.C: It is never legal or safe to drive while under the influence of marijuana.
choices.D: It is legal if the driver's BAC is below 0.08%.
