en.explanation: Even though medical marijuana was approved by Missouri voters effective in 2020, it is never legal or safe to drive while under the influence of marijuana.

en.question: According to research studies, what is a negative effect of marijuana on drivers?

choices.A: Decreased lane weaving
choices.B: Improved judgment of time and distance
choices.C: Poor reaction time
choices.D: Increased coordination

en.explanation: Research studies have shown negative effects of marijuana on drivers, including an increase in lane weaving, poor reaction time, and altered attention to the road.

en.question: What is one of the greatest predictors of someone developing a substance use disorder or addiction?

choices.A: Early use of harmful substances
choices.B: Driving a commercial vehicle
choices.C: Taking over-the-counter allergy medication
choices.D: Having a fully developed brain

en.explanation: One of the greatest predictors of someone developing an addiction is early use. A young person’s under-developed brain can become damaged quicker and more severely.

en.question: How long must proof of insurance (SR-22) be kept on file with the Driver License Bureau for an intoxication-related offense?

choices.A: Six months
choices.B: One year
choices.C: Two years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: Proof of insurance must be kept on file with the Driver License Bureau for two years.

en.question: According to Missouri state law, how many points will be added to your driving record if you are convicted of speeding?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 6 points

en.explanation: The manual states that under state law violations, a conviction for speeding carries a point value of 3 points.

en.question: What action will the Department take if you accumulate a total of 4 points in 12 months?

choices.A: Suspend your license for 30 days
choices.B: Revoke your license for one year
choices.C: Send you a point accumulation advisory
choices.D: Require you to retake the driving test

en.explanation: If you accumulate a total of 4 points in 12 months, the Department will send you a point accumulation advisory.

en.question: Your driving privilege will be suspended if you accumulate how many points in an 18-month period?

choices.A: 4 or more points
choices.B: 6 or more points
choices.C: 8 or more points
choices.D: 12 or more points

en.explanation: If you accumulate a total of 8 or more points in 18 months, your driving privilege will be suspended.

en.question: If you accumulate 8 points in 18 months, how long will your first driving privilege suspension last?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: The consequences for accumulating 8 points in 18 months include a 30-day suspension for the 1st suspension.

en.question: Which of the following point accumulations will result in your driving privilege being revoked for one year?

choices.A: 8 or more points in 12 months
choices.B: 12 or more points in 12 months
choices.C: 12 or more points in 24 months
choices.D: 18 or more points in 36 months

en.explanation: Your driving privilege will be revoked for one year if you accumulate 12 or more points in 12 months, 18 or more points in 24 months, or 24 or more points in 36 months.

en.question: What must you do to reinstate your driving privilege after a non-alcohol related point suspension?

choices.A: Pay a $50 fee and retake the written test
choices.B: Submit proof of insurance (SR-22) and pay a $20 reinstatement fee
choices.C: Complete a defensive driving course and pay a $20 fee
choices.D: Submit proof of insurance (SR-22) and pay a $45 fee

en.explanation: For a non-alcohol related point suspension or revocation, you will need to submit proof of insurance (SR-22) and pay a $20 reinstatement fee.

en.question: After your driving privilege is reinstated, your points are reduced to four. How are your remaining points reduced after one year of driving without getting new points?

choices.A: Reduced to zero
choices.B: Reduced by one-half
choices.C: Reduced by one-third
choices.D: Reduced by two points

en.explanation: After one year of driving without getting new points on your record, the remaining points will be reduced by one-third.

en.question: What is a potential consequence if you are convicted of driving while your license is suspended?

choices.A: Your driving privilege may be revoked for one year
choices.B: You will receive 4 points on your record
choices.C: Your vehicle will be permanently confiscated
choices.D: You will be convicted of a felony

en.explanation: If you drive while your license is suspended, your driving privilege may be revoked for one year after you are convicted.

en.question: If you fail to appear in court for a traffic violation, how many days does the court give you to pay the fines before notifying the Driver License Bureau?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: When you fail to appear in court for a traffic violation, the court will give you 30 days to pay the fines before notifying the Driver License Bureau (DLB).

en.question: How many days do you have to apply for a title after buying a vehicle to avoid paying a penalty fee?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: When you buy a vehicle, you must apply for a title within 30 days. If you do not apply within 30 days, you will have to pay a penalty fee.

en.question: Where does the Missouri driver's manual recommend keeping your vehicle's title?

choices.A: In the vehicle's glove compartment
choices.B: Under the driver's seat
choices.C: In the trunk of the vehicle
choices.D: Not in your vehicle

en.explanation: A title is a very important personal document. The manual explicitly states: Do NOT keep your title in your vehicle.

en.question: When buying a new vehicle in Missouri, what document will the dealer give you to indicate the vehicle has never been registered?

choices.A: A Manufacturer's Statement of Origin (MSO)
choices.B: An ID/OD verification form
choices.C: A salvage title
choices.D: A bill of sale only

en.explanation: For a new vehicle bought in Missouri, the dealer will give you a title application and an assigned Manufacturer’s Statement of Origin (MSO), which indicates the vehicle is new and has never been registered.

en.question: For which vehicles is a proper odometer disclosure required when buying or selling?

choices.A: All vehicles regardless of age
choices.B: Vehicles model year 2011 and newer until the vehicle reaches 20 years old
choices.C: Only vehicles manufactured before 2011
choices.D: Vehicles that are more than 20 years old

en.explanation: When you buy or sell a vehicle, the seller must write the mileage reading on the title assignment if the model year is 2011 or newer and the vehicle is less than 20 years old.

en.question: If you buy a used vehicle and the title assigned to you is an out-of-state title, what must you obtain?

choices.A: A new Manufacturer's Statement of Origin
choices.B: An identification number and odometer (ID/OD) verification form
choices.C: A Missouri salvage title
choices.D: A special permit from the highway patrol

en.explanation: If the title assigned to you is an out-of-state title, you must get an identification number and odometer (ID/OD) verification form completed by a licensed inspection station.

en.question: How many points will be assessed to your driving record for obtaining a driver license by misrepresentation?

choices.A: 3 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 8 points
choices.D: 12 points

en.explanation: According to the point value chart in the manual, obtaining a driver license by misrepresentation results in 12 points.

en.question: What is the registration fee for a passenger vehicle based on in Missouri?

choices.A: The vehicle's gross weight
choices.B: The vehicle's taxable horsepower
choices.C: The vehicle's age
choices.D: The vehicle's zone and gross weight

en.explanation: If you are registering a passenger vehicle, your registration fee will be based on your vehicle's taxable horsepower.

en.question: Under what condition are you eligible to obtain a two-year registration for your vehicle during an even-numbered year?

choices.A: If you have a clean driving record
choices.B: If your vehicle has an odd-numbered model year
choices.C: If your vehicle has an even-numbered model year
choices.D: If you pay double the processing fee

en.explanation: During an even-numbered year (like 2018) you may register for two years if your vehicle has an even-numbered model year.

en.question: When renewing your vehicle registration, a current certificate of safety and/or emissions inspection must have been completed within the last:

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: You must provide a current certificate of safety and/or emissions inspection done within the last 60 days, if applicable.

en.question: How many days do you have to report the sale of your motor vehicle by submitting a Notice of Sale (Form 5049)?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: State law requires you to report the sale of your motor vehicle or all-terrain vehicle by completing a Notice of Sale (Form 5049) and submitting it to any license office or to the address on the form within 30 days.

en.question: How many times per year can you replace stolen license plates and tabs at no cost (excluding the processing fee) if you sign a notarized affidavit?

choices.A: One time
choices.B: Two times
choices.C: Three times
choices.D: Unlimited times

en.explanation: State law allows you to replace stolen license plates and tabs up to two times per year at NO COST (a $9.00 processing fee is applicable) if you sign a notarized affidavit certifying the plates or tabs were stolen.

en.question: What is the minimum level of liability coverage required by state law for property damage per crash?
en.explanation: The minimum level of coverage required by state law includes $25,000 per crash for property damage.

en.question: What is the minimum required liability insurance coverage for bodily injury per person?
en.explanation: The minimum level of coverage required by state law includes $25,000 per person for bodily injury.

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable way to show proof of insurance when registering a vehicle?

choices.A: A verbal statement from your insurance agent
choices.B: A hand held electronic device showing your policy
choices.C: A photocopy of your vehicle title
choices.D: A bank statement showing an insurance payment

en.explanation: Acceptable ways to provide proof of insurance include a hand held electronic device, an original ID card, a policy or binder, or a paid insurance receipt.

en.question: To qualify to be self-insured in Missouri, you must have more than how many vehicles?

choices.A: 5 vehicles
choices.B: 10 vehicles
choices.C: 25 vehicles
choices.D: 50 vehicles

en.explanation: To be self-insured, you must have more than 25 vehicles and be able to show you can and will pay for damage caused by your vehicles.

en.question: If your driver license and license plates are suspended for failing to keep insurance, what form must you file to prove you have insurance?

choices.A: Form 5049
choices.B: SR-22
choices.C: Form 1099
choices.D: SR-10

en.explanation: The most common way to file proof of insurance is through an SR-22 insurance filing. Contact your insurance company or agent to file the SR-22 form.

en.question: What is the penalty for a second suspension within two years for failing to maintain insurance?

choices.A: 30-day suspension and a $100 fee
choices.B: 90-day suspension and a $200 fee
choices.C: 6-month suspension and a $300 fee
choices.D: 1-year suspension and a $400 fee

en.explanation: For two suspensions (within two years of each other), your driver license and/or license plates will be suspended for 90 days. You must also pay a $200 fee and file proof of insurance for three years.

en.question: What fee must you pay to reinstate your license after a third suspension for failing to maintain insurance?
en.explanation: For three (or more) suspensions, your driver license and/or license plates will be suspended for one year. You must also pay a $400 fee and file proof of insurance for three years.

en.question: What happens if you are at fault in an accident and do not pay for the damages you caused?

choices.A: Your vehicle will be impounded for 30 days.
choices.B: Your driver license and/or vehicle license plates will be suspended for one year.
choices.C: You will be required to retake the driving test.
choices.D: You will receive a warning letter from the Department of Revenue.

en.explanation: If you are at fault in an accident and do not pay for the damages you caused, your driver license and/or vehicle license plates will be suspended for one year.

en.question: State law requires you to have uninsured motorist coverage of what amount for bodily injury per crash?
en.explanation: The law also requires you to have uninsured motorist coverage of $25,000 for bodily injury per person and $50,000 for bodily injury per crash.

en.question: If you do not receive a vehicle registration renewal notice in the mail, what are you required to do?

choices.A: Wait until the notice arrives before renewing.
choices.B: Drive legally without renewing until the Department contacts you.
choices.C: You are still required by law to renew your license plates before they expire.
choices.D: Apply for a completely new title and registration.

en.explanation: If you do not receive the notice, you are still required by law to renew your license plates before they expire.

en.question: What is the penalty if you receive two driver license suspensions within two years of each other?

choices.A: Your license will be suspended for 30 days and you must pay a $100 fee.
choices.B: Your license will be suspended for 90 days and you must pay a $200 fee.
choices.C: Your license will be suspended for 1 year and you must pay a $400 fee.
choices.D: Your license will be permanently revoked.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you have two suspensions within two years of each other, your driver license and/or license plates will be suspended for 90 days, and you must pay a $200 fee and file proof of insurance for three years.

en.question: If you accumulate three or more suspensions, your driver license and/or license plates will be suspended for how long?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 1 year
choices.D: 3 years

en.explanation: The manual states that for three (or more) suspensions, your driver license and/or license plates will be suspended for one year, and you must pay a $400 fee.

en.question: What should you do if you are involved in a traffic crash with a parked vehicle?

choices.A: Leave immediately if there is no visible damage to your vehicle.
choices.B: Leave a note on the windshield and drive away without reporting it.
choices.C: Do not leave, as leaving the scene of a traffic crash is a crime.
choices.D: Wait 10 minutes and leave if the owner does not appear.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Even if you have a crash with a parked vehicle, do not leave. Leaving the scene of a traffic crash is a crime."

en.question: Under Missouri's "Move It" law, what are you required to do if you are involved in a minor, non-injury traffic crash?

choices.A: Leave your vehicle exactly where it is until the police arrive.
choices.B: Move your vehicle onto the shoulder or other nearby location off the roadway.
choices.C: Wait for a tow truck to move your vehicle.
choices.D: Drive immediately to the nearest police station.

en.explanation: A state law requires vehicles involved in minor, non-injury crashes to move off the road onto the shoulder or other nearby location to prevent major pileups and traffic backups.

en.question: According to the Missouri driver's manual, secondary crashes cause what percentage of fatalities in Missouri?

choices.A: 10 percent
choices.B: 18 percent
choices.C: 25 percent
choices.D: 30 percent

en.explanation: The "Move It" law helps reduce the chance of motorists being involved in secondary crashes, which cause 18 percent of fatalities in Missouri.

en.question: If you are required to file an accident report with the Department of Revenue, within how many days must it be filed?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: Under certain circumstances, state law requires the accident report to be filed within 30 days.

en.question: You must report an accident to the Driver License Bureau if someone involved did not have liability insurance and there is property damage exceeding what amount?
en.explanation: You must report an accident if someone involved did not have liability insurance AND there is damage to one or more person's property in excess of $500, or there was personal injury or death.

en.question: What may happen to your driving privilege if you strike a highway worker or emergency responder within a designated construction, work, or emergency zone?

choices.A: It will be suspended for exactly 30 days.
choices.B: It may be revoked.
choices.C: You will receive a warning and a fine.
choices.D: You will be required to take a defensive driving course.

en.explanation: If you are involved in a motor vehicle crash and struck a highway worker or emergency responder within a designated construction, work, or emergency zone, your driving privilege may be revoked.

en.question: How long is a standard vehicle safety inspection certificate valid for showing proof of inspection?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: If your vehicle passes the safety inspection, the inspection station will give you a certificate of inspection to show as proof. The certificate is good for 60 days.

en.question: Motor vehicles are exempt from the safety inspection requirement for the first ten years following the model year of manufacture provided they have less than how many miles on the odometer?

choices.A: 50,000 miles
choices.B: 100,000 miles
choices.C: 150,000 miles
choices.D: 200,000 miles

en.explanation: Motor vehicles for the first ten years following the model year of manufacture and having less than 150,000 miles on the odometer are exempt from the safety inspection requirement.

en.question: Which of the following types of vehicles is exempt from the Missouri safety inspection requirement?

choices.A: All passenger cars over 5 years old
choices.B: All motorcycles
choices.C: All trailers
choices.D: All commercial trucks

en.explanation: The manual lists "All trailers" as one of the exceptions to the safety inspection requirement.

en.question: Your vehicle must have at least two functioning red taillights and reflectors that other drivers can see from what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Under required equipment, the manual states your vehicle must have at least two functioning red taillights and reflectors that other drivers can see from 500 feet.

en.question: If your passenger car was made after June 30, 1964, what is the minimum seat belt requirement for the front seat?

choices.A: One set of seat belts
choices.B: Two sets of seat belts
choices.C: Three sets of seat belts
choices.D: Seat belts are only required in the back seat

en.explanation: The manual states: "Seat Belts — If your passenger car was made after June 30, 1964, it must have two sets of seat belts in the front seat."

en.question: If your vehicle was manufactured after 1967, what mirrors must it be equipped with to pass a safety inspection?

choices.A: Only an inside rearview mirror.
choices.B: Only an outside rearview mirror.
choices.C: An inside and an outside rearview mirror.
choices.D: Two outside rearview mirrors.

en.explanation: The manual states: "Mirrors — If your vehicle was made after 1967, it must have an inside and an outside rearview mirror."

en.question: What is the maximum allowed height for bumpers on passenger vehicles when measured at the highest point from the ground?

choices.A: 18 inches
choices.B: 22 inches
choices.C: 26 inches
choices.D: 30 inches

en.explanation: The manual states: "Bumpers on passenger vehicles may not exceed 22 inches above the ground when measured at the highest point."

en.question: If you have a truck licensed in excess of 12,000 pounds and receive only one license plate, where must it be placed?

choices.A: On the rear of the truck
choices.B: On the front of the truck
choices.C: Inside the front windshield
choices.D: On either the front or the rear

en.explanation: If you have a truck licensed in excess of 12,000 pounds, you will only receive one plate, which must be placed on the front of the truck.

en.question: Your vehicle must have a white light shining on the rear license plate so that the plate can be seen from what distance?

choices.A: 25 feet
choices.B: 50 feet
choices.C: 100 feet
choices.D: 150 feet

en.explanation: Your vehicle must have a white light shining on the rear license plate so the plate can be seen from 50 feet.

en.question: Special equipment is required if a load overhangs the rear of your vehicle by more than how many feet?

choices.A: Two feet
choices.B: Three feet
choices.C: Four feet
choices.D: Five feet

en.explanation: You need special equipment if something in your vehicle overhangs the rear by more than five feet.

en.question: When towing another vehicle, what is the maximum distance your towline can keep the vehicles apart?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.explanation: When you are towing another vehicle, your towline must keep the vehicles within 15 feet of each other.

en.question: A "slow moving vehicle" sign must be displayed on the rear of any vehicle moving at or below what speed from sunset to ½ hour before sunrise?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 30 mph

en.explanation: From sunset to ½ hour before sunrise, any vehicle moving 25 mph or slower must have a “slow moving vehicle” sign.

en.question: Between which dates are studded snow tires permitted on vehicles in Missouri?

choices.A: October 1 to March 1
choices.B: November 1 to April 1
choices.C: November 15 to April 15
choices.D: December 1 to March 31

en.explanation: Your vehicle may have studded snow tires only from November 1 to April 1.

en.question: What is the maximum permitted light blockage for tinting on front door windows?
en.explanation: Tinting or sun-screening material is permitted on the side and rear windows (front door windows at no more than 65% light blockage).

en.question: What is the maximum width allowed for any vehicle without a special permit?

choices.A: 8 feet
choices.B: 8½ feet
choices.C: 9 feet
choices.D: 9½ feet

en.explanation: The maximum width of any vehicle is 8½ feet.

en.question: What is the maximum height of any vehicle on highways outside of a commercial zone or designated highways?

choices.A: 13½ feet
choices.B: 14 feet
choices.C: 14½ feet
choices.D: 15 feet

en.explanation: The maximum height on all other highways (outside commercial zones and designated highways) is 13½ feet.

en.question: How far beyond the city limits does the commercial zone for St. Louis City extend?

choices.A: 2 miles
choices.B: 12 miles
choices.C: 15 miles
choices.D: 18 miles

en.explanation: The commercial zone for St. Louis City extends 18 miles beyond the city limits.

en.question: Motor vehicle carriers may carry loads that extend beyond their legal length limits, but the load must not extend more than:

choices.A: Two feet beyond the front or three feet beyond the rear
choices.B: Three feet beyond the front or four feet beyond the rear
choices.C: Four feet beyond the front or five feet beyond the rear
choices.D: Five feet beyond the front or six feet beyond the rear

en.explanation: Loads must not extend more than three feet beyond the front or four feet beyond the rear of the vehicle.

en.question: What is the maximum gross weight allowed on all highways in Missouri, except where bridge structures are posted with lesser limits?

choices.A: 60,000 pounds
choices.B: 70,000 pounds
choices.C: 80,000 pounds
choices.D: 90,000 pounds

en.explanation: The maximum gross weight allowed on all highways in Missouri is 80,000 pounds, except where bridge structures are posted with lesser weight limits.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement to receive an oversize or overweight permit?

choices.A: The load on your vehicle must be reducible.
choices.B: You must have property damage and bodily injury liability insurance.
choices.C: You must be driving a vehicle licensed for farm use.
choices.D: You must have a minimum of five axles.

en.explanation: To receive an oversize or overweight permit, the load on your vehicle must be non-reducible, you must have property damage and bodily injury liability insurance, and you must pay a permit fee.

en.question: Which type of commercial vehicle is prohibited from carrying liquid-burning pot torches (flares) as emergency warning devices?

choices.A: Vehicles transporting solid waste.
choices.B: Vehicles licensed for more than 12,000 pounds.
choices.C: Vehicles transporting explosive or flammable material.
choices.D: Vehicles operating solely intrastate.

en.explanation: The combination of three flares, three fuses, and two red flags must not be carried by vehicles transporting explosive or flammable material or using flammable compressed gas as a motor fuel.

en.question: If you are driving a bus or truck, what is the minimum distance you must maintain when following another bus or truck outside of a business or residential district?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: If you are driving a bus or truck, you must not follow another bus or truck any closer than 300 feet. However, you may follow closer when in a business or residential district, or when passing.

en.question: What is the recommended following distance rule for a commercial vehicle based on its length?

choices.A: Keep at least one second between you and the vehicle in front for each ten feet of length in your vehicle.
choices.B: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle in front for each ten feet of length.
choices.C: Keep at least one second for every twenty feet of length.
choices.D: Keep a standard four-second following distance regardless of length.

en.explanation: For each ten feet of length in your vehicle, keep at least one second between you and the vehicle in front of you. For example, a 40-foot vehicle requires four seconds.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is required to stop within 15 to 50 feet before railroad tracks?

choices.A: A commercial vehicle licensed for 18,000 pounds or less.
choices.B: A solid waste hauler.
choices.C: A school bus.
choices.D: Any vehicle carrying a non-reducible load.

en.explanation: You must stop within 15 to 50 feet before the railroad tracks if you are driving a school bus, a motor vehicle carrying passengers for hire, or a vehicle carrying certain hazardous materials.

en.question: To compensate for off-tracking when making a right turn in a large vehicle, you should:

choices.A: Begin the turn as far to the right as possible.
choices.B: Begin the turn as far to the left as possible.
choices.C: Accelerate quickly through the turn.
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply before moving forward.

en.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels take a shorter path than the front wheels. To compensate for off-tracking, begin a right-turn as far to the left as possible.

en.question: All commercial motor vehicles must stop at weigh stations EXCEPT those licensed for:

choices.A: 12,000 pounds or less.
choices.B: 18,000 pounds or less.
choices.C: 26,000 pounds or less.
choices.D: 36,000 pounds or less.

en.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must stop at weigh stations except those licensed for 18,000 pounds or less or otherwise exempted by law, unless directed by a peace officer.

en.question: If you are being tailgated by another vehicle, what is the safest course of action?

choices.A: Flash your brake lights to warn the tailgater.
choices.B: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
choices.C: Make a sudden stop to force the tailgater to back off.
choices.D: Slow down and increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front of you.

en.explanation: To avoid a crash with a tailgater, you should slow down, avoid sudden turns or stops, increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front of you, and do not flash your taillights or brake lights.

en.question: According to the manual, what is considered by far the most high-risk driving distraction?

choices.A: Eating and drinking
choices.B: Adjusting the radio
choices.C: Text messaging
choices.D: Talking to passengers

en.explanation: Because text messaging requires visual, manual, and cognitive attention from the driver, it is by far the most high risk distraction.

en.question: What is the proper way to travel with a pet in a moving vehicle?

choices.A: Allow the pet to sit on your lap to keep it calm.
choices.B: Secure the pet in a pet carrier, portable kennel, or specially designed harness.
choices.C: Let the pet roam freely in the back seat.
choices.D: Hold the pet with one hand while steering with the other.

en.explanation: Properly secure your pet in a pet carrier, portable kennel, or specially designed pet harness when you are driving. Never allow your pet to sit on your lap while you are driving.

en.question: What information must be clearly visible on a commercial motor vehicle that is regularly used for commercial purposes and licensed for over 36,000 pounds?

choices.A: The driver's license number of the operator.
choices.B: The name of the owner and the address the vehicle is operated from.
choices.C: The maximum gross weight allowed for the vehicle.
choices.D: The vehicle's exact length and width.

en.explanation: The following information must be clearly visible on commercial motor vehicles: The name of the owner; the address the vehicle is operated from and the number issued to a motor carrier.

en.question: When checking the space overhead for your commercial vehicle, you should:

choices.A: Always trust that posted heights at bridges are correct.
choices.B: Only check for clearance when driving on unpaved roads.
choices.C: Not assume that posted heights at bridges or underpasses are correct.
choices.D: Rely on the vehicle behind you to warn you of low clearances.

en.explanation: Make sure you have enough space over your vehicle at all times. Do not assume that posted heights at bridges or underpasses are correct.

en.question: A commercial motor vehicle used for intrastate commerce licensed for more than 12,000 pounds must carry a fire extinguisher rated at least:

choices.A: 2 A:B
choices.B: 5 B:C
choices.C: 10 B:C
choices.D: 15 A:C

en.explanation: Any other commercial motor vehicle used for intrastate or interstate commerce that is licensed for more than 12,000 pounds must carry... One fire extinguisher. The extinguisher must be rated at 5 B:C or more.

en.question: How does the weight and length of your vehicle affect crossing or entering traffic?

choices.A: A heavier vehicle accelerates faster, requiring a smaller gap.
choices.B: The length of the vehicle does not affect the time it takes to cross the road.
choices.C: A long or heavily weighted vehicle needs a larger gap to cross the road than a car.
choices.D: Heavy vehicles have the right-of-way, so gap size is irrelevant.

en.explanation: Your acceleration rate varies with the weight of your vehicle. And your time to cross the road is also affected by the length of your vehicle. In a long or heavily weighted vehicle, you will need a larger gap to cross the road than you would in a car.

en.question: When is the best time to adjust your vehicle's controls, such as the climate controls, mirrors, or radio?

choices.A: While stopped at a yield sign
choices.B: Before you begin to drive
choices.C: While driving on a straight road
choices.D: Only when driving under 30 mph

en.explanation: The manual states that you should adjust your vehicle's controls (climate controls, mirrors, radio, seat, etc.) before you begin to drive to decrease your risk of a crash.

en.question: If you need to adjust the climate control or navigation system while driving, what is a recommended safe practice?

choices.A: Ask your passengers to adjust them for you
choices.B: Steer with your knees while adjusting
choices.C: Wait until you are on the highway
choices.D: Pull over to the left shoulder immediately

en.explanation: The manual recommends asking your passengers to adjust the radio, climate control, navigation system, etc., for you to avoid distracted driving.

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following is considered a visual distraction outside your window that can be dangerous to concentrate on?

choices.A: Your vehicle's speedometer
choices.B: A crash scene
choices.C: The rearview mirror
choices.D: The road ahead

en.explanation: Looking out your window at a crash scene, billboard, pulled-over vehicle, or scenic view can be a distraction if you concentrate on getting a good look at it.

en.question: Under the electronic communication device law, what is a driver prohibited from doing while the vehicle is in motion?

choices.A: Using voice-operated functions
choices.B: Physically holding a cellphone with any part of their body
choices.C: Utilizing in-car Bluetooth
choices.D: Listening to a podcast

en.explanation: While the vehicle is in motion, drivers are prohibited from physically holding or supporting a cellphone with any part of their body.

en.question: While driving a motor vehicle in motion, which of the following actions involving a cellphone is illegal?

choices.A: Sending a text message using voice-to-text features
choices.B: Manually typing or reading a text-based message
choices.C: Engaging a hands-free call with a single touch
choices.D: Listening to a digital audio recording

en.explanation: Drivers are prohibited from manually typing, writing, sending, or reading text-based messages while the vehicle is in motion.

en.question: The electronic communication device law allows drivers to:

choices.A: Watch a video or movie
choices.B: Broadcast a live video on social media
choices.C: Engage a hands-free voice call with a single touch or swipe
choices.D: Hold the phone on their shoulder while talking

en.explanation: The law allows drivers to place or receive voice calls utilizing voice-operated or hands-free functions that can be engaged/disengaged with a single touch or swipe.

en.question: How are drivers legally permitted to send or receive text-based communications while driving?

choices.A: By typing with one hand
choices.B: Through voice-to-text features
choices.C: Only while stopped at a red light
choices.D: By having the phone resting on their lap

en.explanation: The law allows drivers to send or receive text-based communication through voice-to-text features.

en.question: For a transportation network company driver to legally use a device to relay information through a digital network while driving, the device must be:

choices.A: Held in the driver's hand
choices.B: Placed on the passenger seat
choices.C: Affixed or mounted to the vehicle
choices.D: Kept in the glove compartment

en.explanation: A company driver may use a device to relay information through a transportation network company's digital network provided the device is affixed or mounted to the vehicle.

en.question: Prior to January 1, 2025, drivers violating the provisions of use of an electronic communication device may be subject to:

choices.A: A warning
choices.B: An infraction
choices.C: License suspension
choices.D: A felony charge

en.explanation: Prior to January 1, 2025, drivers violating these provisions of use of an electronic communication device may be subject to a warning.

en.question: What potential penalty do commercial drivers face if they violate the electronic communication device section?

choices.A: Disqualification
choices.B: A mandatory retake of the driving test
choices.C: A permanent ban from driving any vehicle
choices.D: Confiscation of their cargo

en.explanation: Commercial drivers violating this section may be subject to disqualification, and fines and criminal penalties may also apply.

en.question: According to the manual's index, what does the acronym 'BAC' stand for?

choices.A: Basic Auto Control
choices.B: Blood Alcohol Content
choices.C: Breathalyzer Assessment Check
choices.D: Bureau of Automotive Crashes

en.explanation: The index of the manual lists BAC as standing for Blood Alcohol Content.

en.question: Based on the manual's index, a Class E license is known as a:

choices.A: Commercial Driver License
choices.B: Full Driver License
choices.C: For-Hire License
choices.D: Intermediate License

en.explanation: The index lists the Class E license as a 'For-Hire License'.

en.question: What does the acronym 'GDL' stand for in the Missouri driver's manual?

choices.A: General Driving Limits
choices.B: Graduated Driver License Law
choices.C: Guided Driver Learning
choices.D: Gross Driving Liability

en.explanation: The index refers to GDL as the Graduated Driver License Law.

en.question: What does the 'DHH' notation on a driver's license application indicate?

choices.A: Driver Has Handicaps
choices.B: Deaf or Hard of Hearing
choices.C: Department of Highway Health
choices.D: Driving Hazard History

en.explanation: The index lists the 'DHH' Notation as being for Deaf or Hard of Hearing Applicants.

en.question: What is the Highway Patrol Statewide Toll Free Emergency Assistance Number?
en.explanation: According to the contact information section, the Highway Patrol Statewide Toll Free Emergency Assistance Number is 1-800-525-5555.

en.question: What number can you dial from a cellular phone to reach the Highway Patrol Statewide Emergency Assistance?

choices.C: *HP

en.explanation: The manual states that you can dial *55 from a cellular phone for Highway Patrol Statewide Emergency Assistance.

en.question: Which phone number should you call for General Information regarding Driver License Questions?
en.explanation: The contact information lists (573) 751-1887 as the number for General Information regarding Driver License Questions.

en.question: What number provides 24/7 Automated Information for Driver License Questions?
en.explanation: The manual lists (573) 526-2407 as the 24/7 Automated Information line for Driver License Questions.

en.question: If you have general Motor Vehicle Questions, which phone number should you contact?
en.explanation: The contact information section provides (573) 526-3669 for General Information regarding Motor Vehicle Questions.

en.question: Where is the State Highway Patrol Troop A located?

choices.A: Macon
choices.B: Lee's Summit
choices.C: Springfield
choices.D: Rolla

en.explanation: According to the contact information, State Highway Patrol Troop A is located in Lee's Summit.

en.question: Which State Highway Patrol Troop is located in Jefferson City?

choices.A: Troop C
choices.B: Troop E
choices.C: Troop F
choices.D: Troop H

en.explanation: The contact information lists Troop F as being located in Jefferson City.

en.question: What class of license is designated for a Motorcycle License?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class C
choices.C: Class M
choices.D: Class ND

en.explanation: The index lists the Motorcycle License as a (Class M) license.

en.question: What abbreviation is used in the manual to denote a Nondriver Identification Card?

choices.A: NI
choices.B: ND
choices.C: NIC
choices.D: NDI

en.explanation: The index lists the Nondriver Identification Card with the abbreviation (ND).

en.question: According to the manual's index, traffic signs are categorized by which of the following characteristics?

choices.A: Colors, Shapes, and Types
choices.B: Size, Reflectivity, and Placement
choices.C: Regulatory, Warning, and Guide
choices.D: Speed, Direction, and Distance

en.explanation: The index breaks down the 'Traffic Signs' section into three subcategories: Colors, Shapes, and Types.

en.question: The manual includes a specific exemption for Required Documentation for which group of people?

choices.A: Military Veterans
choices.B: Senior Citizens
choices.C: Out-of-state transfers
choices.D: Teen drivers

en.explanation: The index lists a section titled 'Required Documentation Exemption for Senior Citizens'.

en.question: If you need to contact State Highway Patrol Troop I, which city are they located in?

choices.A: Rolla
choices.B: Macon
choices.C: Willow Springs
choices.D: Lee's Summit

en.explanation: The contact information lists State Highway Patrol Troop I as being located in Rolla.

en.question: The manual's section on Traffic Crashes specifically covers which two subtopics?

choices.A: Insurance Claims and Liability
choices.B: What To Do and Reporting A Crash
choices.C: Moving Vehicles and First Aid
choices.D: Police Reports and Towing

en.explanation: The index lists 'What To Do' and 'Reporting A Crash' as the specific subtopics under Traffic Crashes.

en.question: According to the index, the Vision Test section includes specific information about what scenario?

choices.A: Wearing contact lenses
choices.B: Failing The Vision Test
choices.C: Laser eye surgery
choices.D: Night blindness

en.explanation: The index explicitly lists 'Failing The Vision Test' as a subtopic under the Vision Test section.

en.question: What is the number-one contributing circumstance to traffic crashes in Missouri?

choices.A: Speeding
choices.B: Driving under the influence
choices.C: Driver inattention
choices.D: Weather conditions

en.explanation: According to the manual, the number-one contributing circumstance to traffic crashes in Missouri is driver inattention.

en.question: According to Missouri law, what must you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching?

choices.A: Speed up to get out of the way
choices.B: Stop immediately in your current lane
choices.C: Yield the right-of-way, drive as far to the right as possible, and stop
choices.D: Move to the left lane and slow down

en.explanation: The law requires motorists to yield the right-of-way and immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as far as possible to the right of, the traveled portion of the highway and stop.

en.question: How long must you remain stopped when you pull over for an approaching emergency vehicle?

choices.A: For at least one minute
choices.B: Until the emergency vehicle has passed
choices.C: Until you can safely merge back into traffic
choices.D: Until the emergency vehicle is out of sight

en.explanation: Motorists must stop and remain in such position until the emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise directed by an officer.

en.question: If you are approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights and changing lanes would be unsafe, what does the law require you to do?

choices.A: Stop in the roadway until the vehicle leaves
choices.B: Proceed with due caution and reduce your speed
choices.C: Accelerate to pass the vehicle quickly
choices.D: Pull over to the right and wait for instructions

en.explanation: If changing lanes would be unsafe or impossible, you must proceed with due caution and reduce the speed of the vehicle, maintaining a safe speed for road conditions.

en.question: What is the penalty for violating the law regarding approaching a stationary emergency vehicle?

choices.A: A Class C felony
choices.B: A Class A misdemeanor
choices.C: A traffic infraction with a $50 fine
choices.D: A warning for the first offense

en.explanation: Violation of the section regarding approaching a stationary emergency vehicle is a Class A misdemeanor.

en.question: Under what circumstance are you NOT required to pull over to the right and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle?

choices.A: When you are in a hurry
choices.B: When you are driving on a one-way street
choices.C: When otherwise directed by a police or traffic officer
choices.D: When the emergency vehicle is in the opposite lane of a divided highway

en.explanation: You must pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise directed by a police or traffic officer.

en.question: The 2017 revision to the Move Over law applies to stationary vehicles displaying which colors of lights?

choices.A: Green or purple lights
choices.B: Red, red and blue, or amber and white lights
choices.C: Only red lights
choices.D: Only blue lights

en.explanation: The law applies to motorists approaching a stationary emergency vehicle displaying lighted red or red and blue lights, or vehicles displaying amber or amber and white lights.

en.question: According to the manual, what two factors were involved when officers were struck and killed by vehicles?

choices.A: Speeding and reckless driving
choices.B: Impaired driving or not paying attention
choices.C: Vehicle malfunction and poor weather
choices.D: Nighttime driving and lack of visibility

en.explanation: The manual states that eight officers were killed after being struck by a vehicle whose driver was either impaired or not paying attention.

en.question: When required to yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, where should you position your vehicle?

choices.A: Parallel to and as far as possible to the right of the traveled portion of the highway
choices.B: In the center median of the highway
choices.C: As far to the left as possible
choices.D: In the nearest intersection

en.explanation: The law requires motorists to immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as far as possible to the right of, the traveled portion of the highway.

en.question: To be required to change lanes away from a stationary emergency vehicle, the roadway must have at least how many lanes proceeding in the same direction?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: The lane change requirement applies if on a roadway having at least four lanes with not less than two lanes proceeding in the same direction as the approaching vehicle.

en.question: What must you do if you approach a stationary vehicle displaying amber or amber and white lights on the side of the road?

choices.A: Treat it as a normal vehicle and maintain speed
choices.B: Proceed with caution and yield the right-of-way by changing lanes if possible
choices.C: Stop and offer assistance
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn them of your approach

en.explanation: The law requires motorists approaching vehicles displaying amber or amber and white lights to proceed with caution and yield the right-of-way by making a lane change if possible.

en.question: What is the primary message of the "Safety is on Your Shoulders" section regarding stationary emergency vehicles?

choices.A: Always stop and help stationary vehicles
choices.B: Slow down and move over away from stationary vehicles with emergency equipment activated
choices.C: Speed up to clear the area quickly
choices.D: Take pictures of the emergency scene for reporting

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Please slow down and move over away from stationary vehicles along the side of the road with their emergency equipment activated. IT'S THE LAW."

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What does this sign indicate?

choices.A: Left turn only
choices.B: Traffic flows in one direction — to the left
choices.C: Keep left of the median
choices.D: Highway exit to the left

en.explanation: A black and white ONE WAY sign with an arrow indicates that traffic on this street moves in only one direction — the direction the arrow points.

en.question: What does this sign prohibit?

choices.A: Right turns
choices.B: Left turns
choices.C: U-turns
choices.D: Passing other vehicles

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign with a U-turn arrow crossed out means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What does this sign instruct drivers to do?

choices.A: Merge right
choices.B: Turn right only
choices.C: Keep to the right of a divider or obstruction
choices.D: Right lane ends ahead

en.explanation: A white regulatory KEEP RIGHT sign with an arrow means you must keep to the right side of a traffic island, median, or obstruction.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What road condition does this sign warn about?

choices.A: A winding road
choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions
choices.D: A roundabout ahead

en.explanation: A reverse curve sign warns of two curves in opposite directions ahead. Slow down and be prepared for the road to curve first one way, then the other.

en.question: What does this sign warn you to expect?

choices.A: A single sharp curve
choices.B: A slippery road surface
choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead
choices.D: A hill ahead

en.explanation: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves or turns ahead. Reduce your speed and be alert for changing road conditions.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to prepare for?

choices.A: A lane ending
choices.B: Traffic merging from another road
choices.C: A divided highway beginning
choices.D: A road narrowing to one lane

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped merge sign warns that traffic from another road will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed and position.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to expect ahead?

choices.A: A yield sign
choices.B: A traffic signal
choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop
choices.D: A speed bump

en.explanation: This sign warns that there is a stop sign ahead. Begin slowing down and prepare to come to a complete stop at the stop sign.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas debe responder correctamente para aprobar el examen de conducir escrito de Missouri?
es.explanation: Según el manual, debe responder correctamente 20 de las 25 preguntas de opción múltiple para aprobar el examen escrito.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes personas NO está obligada a tener una licencia de conducir de Missouri para conducir en Missouri?

choices.A: Un nuevo residente de Missouri que tiene una licencia de otro estado.
choices.B: Un estudiante de tiempo completo con una licencia de conducir válida de su estado de origen.
choices.C: Un residente de Missouri de 16 años que planea conducir.
choices.D: Un conductor comercial de otro estado que se mudó a Missouri hace 20 días.

es.explanation: El manual establece que no necesita una licencia de conducir de Missouri si es un estudiante de tiempo completo y tiene una licencia de conducir válida de su estado de origen.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima elegible para obtener un Permiso de Instrucción estándar en Missouri?

choices.C: 15 y medio

es.explanation: La edad elegible para un Permiso de Instrucción, que es el primer paso en el Programa de Licencia de Conducir Graduada (GDL) de Missouri, es de 15 años.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer con el registro de examen de conducir emitido por la Patrulla de Carreteras del Estado de Missouri?

choices.A: Guárdelo en su guantera como un permiso temporal válido.
choices.B: Envíelo por correo al Departamento de Ingresos dentro de los 30 días.
choices.C: Llévelo a una oficina de licencias local para solicitar el permiso o licencia real.
choices.D: Preséntelo a un adulto con licencia antes de comenzar la práctica de manejo.

es.explanation: El registro del examen de conducir no es válido como permiso o licencia. Debe llevar su copia del registro y otros documentos requeridos a su oficina de licencias local para solicitar el permiso o licencia real.

es.question: ¿Cuándo comienza oficialmente el período de permiso requerido de seis meses para una licencia intermedia?

choices.A: En su cumpleaños número 15.
choices.B: Cuando apruebe el examen escrito.
choices.C: Cuando la Patrulla de Carreteras del Estado de Missouri emita su registro de examen.
choices.D: Tras la emisión del permiso de instrucción temporal en la oficina de licencias.

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente que el período de permiso de seis meses requerido para una licencia intermedia no comienza hasta la emisión del permiso de instrucción temporal.

es.question: ¿A qué edad puede solicitar un Permiso de Instrucción de Motocicleta SIN que se le requiera completar un curso de capacitación para conductores de motocicletas aprobado?

choices.B: 15 y medio

es.explanation: Si tiene 16 años o más, puede solicitar un permiso de instrucción de motocicleta y no se requiere el curso de capacitación para conductores de motocicletas.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes es una restricción para una persona de 15 años y medio que tiene un Permiso de Instrucción de Motocicleta?

choices.A: Solo pueden conducir dentro de un radio de 100 millas de su hogar.
choices.B: Se les permite llevar a un pasajero.
choices.C: Solo pueden operar una motocicleta de no más de 250 cc.
choices.D: Se les permite conducir de noche si van acompañados por un adulto.

es.explanation: Para una persona de 15 años y medio, el permiso permite conducir solo durante el día, dentro de un radio de 50 millas de su hogar, una motocicleta de no más de 250 cc y sin pasajeros.

es.question: ¿Qué clase de licencia es la licencia de conducir básica, también conocida como licencia de operador, para conductores de 18 años o más?

choices.A: Clase A
choices.B: Clase E
choices.C: Clase F
choices.D: Clase M

es.explanation: La Licencia de Conducir Completa (Clase F) es la licencia de conducir básica, también llamada licencia de operador, y la edad elegible es 18 años.

es.question: Si ya tiene una licencia Clase F, ¿qué examen NO se requiere al solicitar una Licencia para Alquiler (Clase E)?

choices.A: Examen de la vista
choices.B: Examen de señales de tránsito
choices.C: Examen escrito
choices.D: Examen de manejo

es.explanation: Al realizar el examen para una licencia Clase E, si ya tiene una licencia Clase F, no se requiere un examen de manejo.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes documentos NO figura explícitamente como verificación requerida al obtener una nueva licencia o permiso?

choices.A: Verificación de estatus legal
choices.B: Número de seguro social
choices.C: Comprobante de inscripción en la escuela secundaria
choices.D: Residencia en Missouri

es.explanation: Cualquier persona que obtenga una nueva licencia o permiso debe mostrar verificación de estatus legal, identidad (nombre legal completo), número de seguro social y residencia en Missouri. El comprobante de inscripción en la escuela secundaria no figura en la lista.

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas de opción múltiple tiene el examen escrito de conducir de Missouri?
es.explanation: Para evaluar sus conocimientos sobre las leyes de tránsito, deberá realizar un examen escrito de 25 preguntas de opción múltiple.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima elegible para obtener una Licencia de Alquiler (Clase E)?
es.explanation: La edad elegible para una Licencia de Alquiler (Clase E) es de 18 años.

es.question: Si usted es menor de 21 años, su permiso o licencia:

choices.A: Será válido por solo seis meses.
choices.B: Lo identificará como menor de edad.
choices.C: Requerirá que conduzca solo durante las horas del día.
choices.D: Le prohibirá conducir en la autopista.

es.explanation: El manual establece que si usted es menor de 21 años, se le expedirá un permiso o licencia que lo identifique como menor de edad.

es.question: ¿Bajo qué condición puede una persona operar un tractor agrícola en una autopista sin una licencia de conducir de Missouri?

choices.A: Si tiene al menos 14 años de edad.
choices.B: Si lo opera para fines relacionados con la agricultura.
choices.C: Si permanece dentro de un radio de 50 millas de su granja.
choices.D: Si tiene un permiso de instrucción válido.

es.explanation: No necesita una licencia de conducir de Missouri si opera o maneja o traslada temporalmente cualquier tractor o implemento agrícola en una autopista para fines relacionados con la agricultura.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad elegible para solicitar una licencia Clase E en Missouri?
es.explanation: Según el manual, la edad elegible para una licencia Clase E es de 18 años.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes personas NO está obligada a obtener una licencia de alquiler (Clase E)?

choices.A: Un conductor que transporta 14 pasajeros o menos para un centro de cuidado infantil.
choices.B: Un conductor de entrega de una floristería que transporta bienes por un pago.
choices.C: Una persona que presta servicios de entrega de comida preparada para un restaurante de comida rápida.
choices.D: Un conductor que opera un vehículo de carga de un empleador que pesa 20,000 libras.

es.explanation: Las personas que prestan servicios de entrega de comida preparada para entidades como un restaurante de comida rápida o una charcutería (delicatessen) no están obligadas a obtener una licencia Clase E.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes debe aprobar para obtener una licencia o permiso Clase M?

choices.A: Solo un examen de habilidades en motocicleta.
choices.B: Los exámenes escritos de Clase F y Clase M, de la vista, de señales de tránsito y de habilidades en motocicleta.
choices.C: Solo los exámenes escritos y de la vista de Clase M.
choices.D: Un examen de habilidades de conducción en un vehículo de pasajeros estándar.

es.explanation: Para obtener una licencia Clase M, deberá aprobar los exámenes escritos de Clase F y Clase M, de la vista, de señales de tránsito y de habilidades en motocicleta.

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de licencia se requiere para operar una bicicleta motorizada en las vías públicas?

choices.A: Un endoso de motocicleta Clase M.
choices.B: Una licencia de alquiler Clase E.
choices.C: Una licencia de operador válida (o de una clasificación superior).
choices.D: Una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL).

es.explanation: Un conductor que opera una bicicleta motorizada no está obligado a obtener un endoso de motocicleta; sin embargo, debe poseer una licencia de operador válida (o de una clasificación superior).

es.question: ¿Qué edad debe tener para obtener una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) con un endoso de Materiales Peligrosos o de Autobús Escolar?

choices.A: 16 años
choices.B: 18 años
choices.C: 21 años
choices.D: 25 años

es.explanation: Debe tener al menos 21 años de edad para obtener una CDL con un endoso de Materiales Peligrosos o de Autobús Escolar.

es.question: ¿Cuándo vence generalmente una identificación estándar con foto para no conductores (Clase ND)?

choices.A: En su fecha de nacimiento en el tercer año después de su solicitud.
choices.B: En su fecha de nacimiento en el sexto año después de su solicitud.
choices.C: Nunca vence.
choices.D: Diez años a partir de la fecha de emisión.

es.explanation: Su identificación de no conductor vence en su fecha de nacimiento en el sexto año después de su solicitud.

es.question: ¿Si tiene 70 años o más y solicita una identificación de no conductor que no cumple con REAL ID, por cuánto tiempo es válida la tarjeta?

choices.A: 3 años
choices.B: 6 años
choices.C: Se emite sin fecha de vencimiento.
choices.D: 10 años

es.explanation: Si tiene 70 años o más, su identificación de no conductor se emitirá sin fecha de vencimiento, a menos que solicite una tarjeta que cumpla con REAL ID.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes se requieren si está transfiriendo una licencia de conducir de otro estado a Missouri?

choices.A: El examen de conducir de cuatro partes.
choices.B: Solo el examen de habilidades de conducción.
choices.C: Los exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito.
choices.D: No se requieren exámenes.

es.explanation: Si está transfiriendo su licencia de conducir de otro estado, debe entregar la licencia de su estado de residencia anterior y realizar los exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito.

es.question: Debe realizar el examen de conducir de cuatro partes si su licencia de conducir de Missouri ha estado vencida por más de:

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 90 días
choices.C: 6 meses (184 días)
choices.D: 1 año (365 días)

es.explanation: Debe realizar el examen de conducir de cuatro partes si su licencia de conducir de Missouri ha estado vencida por más de seis meses (184 días).

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes NO es un documento aceptable para demostrar el estatus legal para una licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Un pasaporte estadounidense válido y vigente.
choices.B: Un certificado de nacimiento de un hospital.
choices.C: Un Certificado de Ciudadanía de EE. UU.
choices.D: Un Certificado de Nacimiento de EE. UU. certificado emitido por una agencia de registros vitales.

es.explanation: Los certificados de nacimiento de hospitales y las tarjetas de registro de nacimiento no son aceptables como prueba de estatus legal.

es.question: Los solicitantes de 65 años o más que renueven una licencia no comercial que no cumpla con REAL ID pueden estar exentos de presentar ¿qué tipo de documento?

choices.A: Documentos del lugar de nacimiento.
choices.B: Prueba de residencia en Missouri.
choices.C: Prueba del Número de Seguro Social.
choices.D: Prueba de identidad.

es.explanation: Si está renovando un permiso, licencia de conducir o identificación de no conductor no comercial que no cumple con REAL ID y tiene 65 años o más, puede estar exento de presentar documentos del lugar de nacimiento.

es.question: ¿Qué dos datos deben contener los documentos utilizados para verificar su identidad?

choices.A: Su nombre legal completo y su número de seguro social.
choices.B: Su nombre legal completo y su fecha de nacimiento.
choices.C: Su fecha de nacimiento y su dirección residencial.
choices.D: Su firma y fotografía.

es.explanation: Los documentos utilizados para verificar la identidad deben contener su nombre legal completo y su fecha de nacimiento.

es.question: ¿Cuántos documentos que verifiquen la residencia en Missouri se requieren para obtener un documento que cumpla con REAL ID?

choices.A: Un documento
choices.B: Dos documentos
choices.C: Tres documentos
choices.D: Cuatro documentos

es.explanation: Para obtener un documento que cumpla con REAL ID, debe proporcionar dos documentos que verifiquen la residencia en Missouri.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes NO es aceptable para usar como dirección residencial al solicitar una licencia de Missouri?

choices.A: Un apartado postal (P.O. Box).
choices.B: El lugar donde una persona está físicamente presente y considera su hogar.
choices.C: Un hogar verdadero, fijo y principal.
choices.D: Un hogar permanente al que una persona tiene la intención de regresar.

es.explanation: Un apartado postal (P.O. Box) no es aceptable como dirección residencial. Debe mostrar un comprobante de dirección residencial y una dirección postal alternativa (si corresponde).

es.question: Si un solicitante menor de 21 años no puede proporcionar un documento aceptable para la verificación de una dirección residencial en Missouri, ¿cuál es una alternativa aceptable?

choices.A: Puede usar una factura de servicios públicos de un amigo.
choices.B: Un padre o tutor legal puede proporcionar un documento en su nombre.
choices.C: Está exento de proporcionar prueba de residencia.
choices.D: Debe esperar hasta cumplir 21 años para presentar la solicitud.

es.explanation: Si es menor de 21 años y no puede proporcionar un documento aceptable de la lista para la verificación de una dirección residencial en Missouri, un padre o tutor legal puede proporcionar dicho documento en su nombre.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes documentos NO es aceptable para proporcionar su Número de Seguro Social para una solicitud de licencia de Missouri?

choices.A: Un comprobante de salarios e impuestos W-2.
choices.B: Una tarjeta de Seguro Social laminada.
choices.C: Un formulario 1099.
choices.D: Un talón de pago con su nombre y Número de Seguro Social.

es.explanation: El manual establece que la tarjeta del Seguro Social debe ser original, estar firmada y no estar laminada.

es.question: ¿Si necesita cambiar su primer o segundo nombre en su licencia de conducir, qué documento debe presentar?

choices.A: Un acta de nacimiento enmendada
choices.B: Una licencia de matrimonio certificada
choices.C: Una orden judicial certificada
choices.D: Una sentencia de divorcio certificada

es.explanation: Según el manual, se requiere una orden judicial certificada para un cambio de primer nombre o un cambio de segundo nombre.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo es válido un Permiso de Instrucción de Missouri?

choices.A: 0 a 6 meses
choices.B: 0 a 12 meses
choices.C: La duración de un curso aprobado
choices.D: 1 año no renovable

es.explanation: La tabla de tarifas de permisos del manual indica que un Permiso de Instrucción es válido por un periodo de 0 a 12 meses.

es.question: ¿Cuál es una posible sanción por desobedecer las restricciones de conducción impuestas en su licencia?

choices.A: Se le requerirá volver a tomar el examen escrito
choices.B: Puede ser acusado de conducir sin licencia
choices.C: Su vehículo será confiscado de inmediato
choices.D: Recibirá una carta de advertencia

es.explanation: El manual establece: 'Si desobedece la(s) restricción(es), puede ser acusado de conducir sin licencia y, si es declarado culpable, se sumarán puntos a su historial de conducción'.

es.question: ¿Qué indica el código de restricción 'C' en una licencia de conducir de Missouri?

choices.A: Lentes correctivos
choices.B: Restringido a 45 MPH
choices.C: Conducción solo durante el día
choices.D: Licencia intermedia

es.explanation: De acuerdo con la tabla de Códigos de Restricción del manual, el código 'C' significa Conducción solo durante el día (Daylight Driving Only).

es.question: Debe presentar una declaración médica al Departamento de Ingresos (Department of Revenue) si ha tenido ataques epilépticos, convulsiones o desmayos, ¿dentro de qué plazo previo a su solicitud de licencia?

choices.A: 3 meses
choices.B: 6 meses
choices.C: 12 meses
choices.D: 2 años

es.explanation: Se requiere una remisión médica si ha tenido ataques epilépticos, convulsiones o desmayos dentro de los seis meses anteriores a su solicitud de licencia.

es.question: Si un médico o un oficial de la ley cree que usted tiene una condición médica que lo convierte en un conductor inseguro, ¿qué formulario deben presentar al Departamento?

choices.A: Formulario de Variación Médica
choices.B: Formulario de Restricción No Codificada
choices.C: Informe de Condición del Conductor (Formulario 4319)
choices.D: Formulario 1099

es.explanation: El manual establece que las personas autorizadas que crean que usted tiene una condición médica que lo convierte en un conductor inseguro deben completar un Informe de Condición del Conductor (Formulario 4319) y enviarlo al Departamento.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para que se le otorgue un endoso de Autobús Escolar (S) en Missouri?
es.explanation: El manual especifica que se puede otorgar un endoso de autobús escolar a conductores de 21 años o más que posean una licencia Clase E o una licencia comercial con un endoso de Pasajeros (P).

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo se suspenderá un endoso de autobús escolar si el conductor no pasa una prueba de drogas, alcohol o sustancias químicas?

choices.A: 6 meses
choices.B: 1 año
choices.C: 3 años
choices.D: Permanentemente

es.explanation: Un endoso de autobús escolar puede ser suspendido por un año si una persona no pasa cualquier prueba de drogas, alcohol o sustancias químicas administrada de acuerdo con las leyes federales o estatales.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes se requieren para agregar un endoso de motocicleta (M) a una licencia existente?

choices.A: Solo examen escrito y examen de habilidades
choices.B: Solo examen de la vista y de habilidades
choices.C: Solo examen escrito y examen de señales de tránsito
choices.D: Examen escrito, de la vista, de señales de tránsito y un examen de habilidades

es.explanation: Para agregar el endoso de motocicleta a una licencia existente, deberá aprobar el examen escrito de motocicleta, el de la vista, el de señales de tránsito y un examen de habilidades en una motocicleta o mototriciclo.

es.question: ¿Con cuánta anticipación puede renovar su licencia de conducir de Missouri antes de que venza?

choices.A: Hasta 30 días
choices.B: Hasta 3 meses
choices.C: Hasta 6 meses
choices.D: Hasta 1 año

es.explanation: El manual establece: 'Puede renovar su licencia hasta seis meses antes de que venza'.

es.question: ¿Qué exámenes debe realizar cada vez que renueva su licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Exámenes escrito y de conducción
choices.B: Exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito
choices.C: Exámenes de la vista y escrito
choices.D: Exámenes de conducción y de señales de tránsito

es.explanation: De acuerdo con la sección de recordatorios de renovación, 'Cada vez que renueve, se le requerirá realizar el examen de la vista y el de señales de tránsito'.

es.question: ¿Bajo qué circunstancia puede solicitar una renovación anticipada de su licencia de conducir más allá del periodo estándar de renovación de 6 meses?

choices.A: Si va a cumplir 21 años
choices.B: Si va a salir del estado o del país por un tiempo prolongado
choices.C: Si va a comprar un vehículo nuevo
choices.D: Si ha perdido su recordatorio de renovación

es.explanation: El manual establece una excepción: 'Si va a salir del estado o del país por un tiempo prolongado, puede solicitar una renovación anticipada de su licencia de conducir en su oficina local de licencias'.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el costo de una tarjeta de identificación para no conductores (Nondriver ID Card) solo para fines de votación para un solicitante que tiene 17 años y medio?
es.explanation: La tabla de tarifas de licencias indica que el costo de una tarjeta de identificación para no conductores (solo para fines de votación) para una edad mínima de 17 años y medio es de $0.00.

es.question: Si no renueva su licencia de conducir dentro de los seis meses (184 días) posteriores a su fecha de vencimiento, ¿qué exámenes adicionales debe realizar?

choices.A: Solo el examen de la vista
choices.B: Solo el examen de señales de tránsito
choices.C: Los exámenes escrito y de conducción
choices.D: Un examen químico

es.explanation: Si no renueva su licencia dentro de los seis meses (o 184 días) posteriores a su fecha de vencimiento, tendrá que realizar los exámenes escrito y de conducción, además de los exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito.

es.question: ¿Cuánto tiempo tiene un miembro de las fuerzas armadas para renovar una licencia vencida de otro estado sin volver a examinarse después de una baja honorable?

choices.A: Hasta 30 días
choices.B: Hasta 90 días
choices.C: Hasta seis meses
choices.D: Hasta un año

es.explanation: Missouri permite una renovación sin volver a examinarse para los miembros de las fuerzas armadas cuya licencia haya vencido mientras estaban fuera del estado, por un periodo de hasta seis meses a partir de la baja honorable o dentro de los 90 días posteriores al restablecimiento de la residencia.

es.question: ¿Cuál es una opción para ahorrar tiempo si su licencia se pierde o es robada y vence dentro de los próximos seis meses?

choices.A: Conducir sin licencia hasta que venza
choices.B: Renovar su licencia anticipadamente en lugar de obtener un duplicado
choices.C: Solicitar un permiso temporal de 30 días
choices.D: Esperar hasta la fecha de vencimiento para solicitar una nueva

es.explanation: Si su licencia se pierde, es robada o se destruye y vence dentro de los próximos seis meses, puede renovar su licencia anticipadamente en lugar de obtener un duplicado para ahorrar tiempo y dinero.

es.question: ¿Puede renovar su licencia de conducir no comercial mientras su privilegio de conducir está suspendido?

choices.A: No, debe esperar hasta que se levante la suspensión
choices.B: Sí, pero solo si vuelve a realizar el examen de conducción
choices.C: Sí, puede realizar los exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito y renovarla
choices.D: No, las licencias suspendidas se cancelan permanentemente

es.explanation: Si poseía una licencia de conducir no comercial, puede realizar los exámenes de la vista y de señales de tránsito y renovar su licencia incluso mientras su privilegio de conducir esté suspendido.

es.question: ¿Qué símbolo aparece en la parte frontal de su licencia de conducir si autoriza un indicador de donante de órganos?

choices.A: Un lazo azul
choices.B: Un corazón rojo con un estandarte verde
choices.C: Una cruz verde
choices.D: Una insignia roja de alerta médica

es.explanation: Si dice 'sí' para agregar el símbolo de donante de órganos, aparecerá un corazón rojo con un estandarte verde en la parte frontal de su permiso de instrucción, licencia de conducir o identificación de no conductor.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la tarifa para colocar el símbolo de donante de órganos en su licencia de conducir o para ser agregado al registro?

choices.D: No hay ningún cargo

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente: 'No hay ningún cargo por colocar el símbolo en su permiso de instrucción, licencia de conducir o identificación de no conductor, ni por incluir su nombre en el registro'.

es.question: Al solicitar una licencia de conducir, ¿el empleado está obligado a preguntarle si desea realizar una donación monetaria a cuál de los siguientes fondos?

choices.A: Al fondo de mantenimiento de carreteras
choices.B: Al fondo de donantes de órganos o al fondo de concientización sobre la ceguera
choices.C: Al fondo de escuelas públicas
choices.D: Al fondo de asistencia para veteranos

es.explanation: Cuando solicita una licencia de conducir, permiso o identificación de no conductor, el empleado debe preguntarle si desea realizar una donación monetaria al fondo de donantes de órganos o al fondo de concientización sobre la ceguera.

es.question: ¿Qué indica la anotación 'DHH' en una licencia de conducir de Missouri al personal de emergencia?

choices.A: El conductor es un Ayudante de Carretera Designado (Designated Highway Helper)
choices.B: El conductor tiene una autorización del Departamento de Salud y Hospitales
choices.C: El conductor es sordo o tiene dificultades auditivas (DHH)
choices.D: El conductor tiene un endoso de transporte pesado dual

es.explanation: La anotación 'DHH' permite que las fuerzas del orden o el personal médico y de emergencia determinen fácilmente si usted es sordo o tiene dificultades auditivas en caso de una emergencia.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el costo adicional al agregar inicialmente un indicador de seguridad para navegantes a su licencia de conducir?

choices.A: No hay costo adicional

es.explanation: Se agregará un costo adicional de $1 a las tarifas de procesamiento estándar cuando se agregue inicialmente el indicador de identificación de navegante a una licencia de conducir o a un documento de identificación de no conductor.

es.question: ¿Qué se requiere para que se coloque un indicador de discapacidad permanente en su licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Una solicitud verbal en la oficina de licencias
