choices.C: The duration your turn signal must be on before changing lanes
choices.D: The maximum time you can look away from the road

en.explanation: The "two-second rule" says that you should allow two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead of you passes a given point and the time your vehicle reaches the same point, ensuring a safe following distance.

en.question: Why is it important to check over your shoulder before changing lanes?

choices.A: To see if law enforcement is following you
choices.B: To ensure your rear-view mirror is adjusted properly
choices.C: To be certain the blind spot is clear
choices.D: To check the speed of the vehicle behind you

en.explanation: Important rules about changing lanes include checking over your shoulder to be certain the blind spot is clear.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the purpose of blowing your horn before passing another vehicle?

choices.A: To warn oncoming traffic to move over
choices.B: To place the driver ahead under a legal obligation to help you pass
choices.C: To signal pedestrians to clear the roadway
choices.D: To indicate that you are traveling above the speed limit

en.explanation: The manual states to blow the horn to signal the driver ahead, as the horn signal places the driver of the vehicle you are passing under a legal obligation to help you pass.

en.question: When making a right turn, why should you stay close to the right edge of the road?

choices.A: To allow faster vehicles to pass on your left
choices.B: To prevent another vehicle from moving between your vehicle and the curb
choices.C: To get a better view of oncoming traffic
choices.D: To avoid triggering traffic light sensors

en.explanation: For right turns, stay close to the right edge of the road, so that another vehicle cannot move between your vehicle and the curb.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must maintain to the left of the vehicle you are passing?

choices.A: 1 foot
choices.B: 2 feet
choices.C: 3 feet
choices.D: 4 feet

en.explanation: The law requires the passing driver to pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle being passed.

en.question: When is it illegal to pass another vehicle on a curve or hill?

choices.A: When you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead
choices.B: When you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead
choices.C: When you cannot see at least 100 feet ahead
choices.D: When you cannot see at least 300 feet ahead

en.explanation: Passing is always unsafe and usually illegal on any curve or hill where the driver cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.

en.question: In which of the following situations is passing on the right permitted?

choices.A: On a two-lane road with a solid yellow line
choices.B: When passing a vehicle that is in the left-turn lane
choices.C: At any intersection in a rural area
choices.D: When the vehicle ahead is driving too slowly

en.explanation: Exceptions where passing on the right is allowed include when passing a vehicle that is in the left-turn lane.

en.question: What is the penalty for increasing your speed and failing to give way to a passing vehicle if it results in a crash causing bodily injury or property damage?

choices.A: A written warning
choices.B: A felony charge
choices.C: A misdemeanor charge
choices.D: Immediate license revocation

en.explanation: If you increase speed and fail to give way to a passing vehicle, you will be charged with a misdemeanor if a crash occurs resulting in bodily injury or property damage.

en.question: What is the maximum speed you should travel when backing your vehicle?

choices.A: 5 mph
choices.B: 10 mph
choices.C: 15 mph
choices.D: 20 mph

en.explanation: When backing your vehicle, you should back very slowly, not more than 10 mph, because your vehicle is harder to control and to stop.

en.question: What is the proper technique for maintaining a full view of what is behind your vehicle while backing?

choices.A: Depend entirely on your rearview and side mirrors
choices.B: Steer with your right hand and look out the driver's side window
choices.C: Steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the back window
choices.D: Ask a passenger to guide you while you look straight ahead

en.explanation: To maintain a full view of what is behind the vehicle, steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the back window; do not depend on mirrors alone.

en.question: How far away from a fire hydrant must you park?

choices.A: At least 10 feet
choices.B: At least 15 feet
choices.C: At least 20 feet
choices.D: At least 25 feet

en.explanation: You should not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or entrance to a fire station.

en.question: When parking on the shoulder of a highway, your parked vehicle must be visible to approaching drivers from both directions for a distance of at least:

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Parking on the shoulder is against the law unless the parked vehicle can be seen by approaching drivers from both directions for a distance of at least 200 feet.

en.question: Where do more than one-third of fatal traffic crashes involving motor vehicles occur?

choices.A: On interstate highways
choices.B: At railroad crossings
choices.C: At intersections
choices.D: In parking lots

en.explanation: Crashes occur most frequently at intersections, and more than one-third of fatal traffic crashes involving motor vehicles occur at intersections.

en.question: If two vehicles reach an intersection without traffic signs or signals at the same time, who has the right of way?

choices.A: The vehicle to the left
choices.B: The vehicle to the right
choices.C: The vehicle traveling faster
choices.D: The vehicle turning left

en.explanation: In intersections without traffic signs or signals, when two or more vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right of way.

en.question: When two facing vehicles approach an intersection at the same time, and one driver wants to go straight while the other wants to turn left, who has the right of way?

choices.A: The driver turning left
choices.B: The driver going straight ahead
choices.C: The driver who signals first
choices.D: Neither driver

en.explanation: If one driver is going straight while the other wants to turn left, the driver who wants to turn must wait. Therefore, the driver who is traveling straight ahead has the right of way.

en.question: What should you NEVER do while moving straight ahead through an intersection?

choices.A: Change lanes
choices.B: Maintain a steady speed
choices.C: Look for pedestrians
choices.D: Keep your hands on the steering wheel

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Never change lanes while you are moving straight ahead through an intersection.'

en.question: In which direction do all vehicles in a traffic circle or roundabout travel?

choices.A: Clockwise
choices.B: Counterclockwise
choices.C: Straight across
choices.D: In a figure-eight pattern

en.explanation: All vehicles in a traffic circle travel to the right around the circle in a counterclockwise direction.

en.question: Who has the right of way in a roundabout or traffic circle?

choices.A: Vehicles entering the roundabout
choices.B: Vehicles already in the roundabout
choices.C: Vehicles exiting the roundabout
choices.D: Vehicles traveling at higher speeds

en.explanation: Vehicles already in the circle have the right of way, and drivers entering must yield to any vehicles or bicyclists already in the roundabout.

en.question: What is the typical required travel speed in a modern roundabout?

choices.A: 5-10 mph

en.explanation: The modern roundabout is much smaller than older traffic circles and requires vehicles to travel at lower speeds (15–20 mph), making them safer.

en.question: Who has the right-of-way at a roundabout?

choices.A: Approaching vehicles entering the roundabout
choices.B: Vehicles and bicyclists already in the roundabout
choices.C: Pedestrians walking through the middle of the roundabout
choices.D: Vehicles entering from the right side

en.explanation: The manual states that drivers yield to any vehicles or bicyclists already in the roundabout, and those already in it do not yield to approaching vehicles.

en.question: Which lane should you use to make a left turn or U-turn in a multi-lane roundabout?

choices.A: The right lane
choices.B: The center lane
choices.C: The left lane
choices.D: The truck apron

en.explanation: In a multi-lane roundabout, you stay in the left lane to go straight through the roundabout or make a left turn or U-turn.

en.question: What should you do if you are already inside a roundabout and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and sirens approaches?

choices.A: Stop immediately inside the roundabout to let them pass
choices.B: Pull over to the inside island of the roundabout
choices.C: Speed up and complete your turn before exiting
choices.D: Exit the roundabout first, then pull over

en.explanation: If drivers are already in the roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches, they must exit first, then pull over to let the emergency vehicle pass.

en.question: When required to stop at a railroad crossing, what is the required stopping distance from the nearest rail?

choices.A: Within 25 feet, but not less than 10 feet
choices.B: Within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet
choices.C: Within 100 feet, but not less than 25 feet
choices.D: Exactly 15 feet

en.explanation: The driver of the vehicle shall stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad and shall not proceed until he/she can do so safely.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles does a train have to yield the right-of-way to?

choices.A: Police vehicles with sirens on
choices.B: Ambulances responding to an emergency
choices.C: Fire trucks with flashing lights
choices.D: None of the above; trains always have the right-of-way

en.explanation: Trains have the right-of-way over all highway traffic including police, fire and ambulance emergency vehicles.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take a train traveling at 55 mph to come to a complete stop?

choices.A: Less than half a mile
choices.B: About 1500 feet
choices.C: More than a mile
choices.D: Exactly 500 feet

en.explanation: A train that is traveling at 55 mph takes more than a mile to come to a stop.

en.question: What should you do if you are crossing railroad tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or the gates start to come down?

choices.A: Stop immediately and back up
choices.B: Keep moving to finish driving through the crossing
choices.C: Stop and abandon your vehicle
choices.D: Put your vehicle in reverse and carefully back out

en.explanation: If you happen to be crossing the tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or gates start to come down, do not stop, do not backup, KEEP MOVING. The warning signals allow enough time to finish crossing.

en.question: What should you do if the railroad crossing gate on the far side of the tracks comes down before you get across?

choices.A: Stop on the tracks and wait for the train
choices.B: Put your vehicle in reverse to avoid the gate
choices.C: Drive through the gate because it is flexible
choices.D: Exit your vehicle and manually lift the gate

en.explanation: Railroad crossing gates cannot trap you or your vehicle; drive through the gate. It is flexible and will not block you in.

en.question: What information is found on the Emergency Notification System (ENS) 'Blue Sign' at a railroad crossing?

choices.A: The train schedule and speed limit
choices.B: The crossing identification number, railroad company name, and emergency phone number
choices.C: The distance to the next highway exit
choices.D: The local police department's non-emergency number

en.explanation: The ENS sign, known as the 'Blue sign,' contains the railroad crossing identification number, name of the railroad company and an emergency telephone number to report emergencies.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your vehicle stalls on or near the railroad tracks?

choices.A: Try to restart the engine for at least one minute
choices.B: Call a tow truck while sitting in the vehicle
choices.C: Get out immediately and move away from the tracks
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn the approaching train

en.explanation: If your vehicle stalls on or near the tracks GET OUT IMMEDIATELY. Move away from your vehicle and the tracks.

en.question: How should a bicyclist navigate a multi-lane roundabout?

choices.A: Ride along the shoulder of the roundabout
choices.B: Pick the appropriate lane and stay in the middle of it
choices.C: Always use the truck apron
choices.D: Dismount and walk the bicycle through the center island

en.explanation: Bicyclists should pick the appropriate lane before entering a multi-lane roundabout and stay in the middle of their chosen lane. They should not ride along the shoulder.

en.question: Why should you not proceed to move immediately after a train has passed a crossing?

choices.A: You must wait for a police officer to wave you through
choices.B: The crossing gates need time to reset their sensors
choices.C: There may be another train moving in the opposite direction or following the first train
choices.D: You must wait exactly three minutes before crossing

en.explanation: Do not proceed to move immediately after the train has passed — there may be another train moving in the opposite direction from or following the first train.

en.question: What is the purpose of the concrete island, or truck apron, in a roundabout?

choices.A: It is a designated parking area for emergency vehicles
choices.B: It is a safe zone for pedestrians to cross
choices.C: It helps big trucks maneuver around the roundabout
choices.D: It is a lane specifically for bicyclists

en.explanation: Big trucks should use the concrete island — called the truck apron — to help drivers maneuver around the roundabout.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are required to stop at railroad crossings, meaning you should be prepared to stop behind them?

choices.A: Motorcycles and bicycles
choices.B: School buses and vehicles transporting hazardous materials
choices.C: Delivery vans and pickup trucks
choices.D: Emergency vehicles with sirens off

en.explanation: Be prepared to stop for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses, motor vehicles carrying passengers, for-hire vehicles or vehicles transporting explosives or hazardous materials.

en.question: Where should pedestrians walk when navigating a roundabout?

choices.A: Through the middle of the roundabout
choices.B: Along the truck apron
choices.C: In the marked crosswalks along the outside of the roundabout
choices.D: In the left lane of the roundabout

en.explanation: Pedestrians should use marked crosswalks along the outside of the roundabout, and not walk through the middle of it.

en.question: Why should you pay special attention to bicyclists when approaching and moving through an intersection?

choices.A: They are required to yield to all motor vehicles.
choices.B: They are required to use the sidewalk at intersections.
choices.C: A crash can occur between a bicyclist moving straight and a motorist turning right.
choices.D: They travel faster than motor vehicles through intersections.

en.explanation: Because bicyclists ride to the right of motor vehicle traffic, the potential exists for a crash between the bicyclist who is moving straight ahead through the intersection and the motorist who is turning right.

en.question: If you intend to make a turn in a city and find that you are not in the proper lane, what should you do?

choices.A: Stop and wait for traffic to clear before changing lanes.
choices.B: Continue to the next intersection and turn there.
choices.C: Quickly change lanes if you use your turn signal.
choices.D: Back up to the previous intersection.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you intend to make a turn and find that you are not in the proper lane, you should continue to the next intersection and turn there.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in another driver's blind spot?

choices.A: You are driving in the center lane.
choices.B: You cannot see the inside rear-view mirror of the car ahead.
choices.C: The vehicle ahead is a large commercial truck.
choices.D: You are following closer than two seconds.

en.explanation: Avoid driving side-by-side, especially in another driver's blind spot. If you cannot see the inside rear-view mirror of the car ahead, you are probably in the driver's blind spot.

en.question: When driving on a one-way street, which lanes should you use for through-travel?

choices.A: The rightmost lane.
choices.B: The leftmost lane.
choices.C: The center lane(s).
choices.D: The outside lanes.

en.explanation: On a one-way street, use the center lane(s) for through-travel and the outside lanes for turning.

en.question: Why is driving on rural roads often considered more dangerous than driving in heavy city traffic?

choices.A: There are more stop signs and traffic signals.
choices.B: The roads may not be as wide and lighting is often not as good.
choices.C: There is a higher volume of commercial truck traffic.
choices.D: The speed limit is generally lower.

en.explanation: Driving on rural roads is often more dangerous because the road may not be as wide, the lighting is often not as good, and/or the travel speeds may be higher.

en.question: What is the proper procedure for entering an interstate highway?

choices.A: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap in traffic.
choices.B: Use the acceleration lane until your speed matches other traffic, then merge safely.
choices.C: Merge directly into the left lane to avoid slow traffic.
choices.D: Yield to traffic on the interstate by slowing down in the acceleration lane.

en.explanation: When entering the interstate, use the acceleration lane until your vehicle's speed matches that of the other traffic and then merge safely.

en.question: If a vehicle breakdown forces you to stop on the interstate, what should you do to signal for help?

choices.A: Stand in the travel lane and wave your arms.
choices.B: Tie a white cloth on the radio aerial or left-door handle and raise the hood.
choices.C: Place a red flag on the rear bumper.
choices.D: Honk your horn continuously until help arrives.

en.explanation: If a vehicle breakdown forces you to stop, move far off the road. Tie a white cloth on the radio aerial or left-door handle and raise the hood.

en.question: When leaving an interstate highway, you should:

choices.A: Slow down in the travel lane before entering the deceleration lane.
choices.B: Signal your turn well in advance and enter the deceleration lane without slowing down first.
choices.C: Brake hard as soon as you enter the deceleration lane.
choices.D: Wait until you are in the deceleration lane to use your turn signal.

en.explanation: When leaving the highway, signal your turn well in advance, and without slowing down, enter the deceleration lane. Proceed at the posted exit speed limit.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your intended exit on an interstate highway?

choices.A: Proceed to the next exit and leave the highway there.
choices.B: Slow down and carefully back up on the shoulder.
choices.C: Make a U-turn through the median.
choices.D: Stop in the travel lane and wait for traffic to clear before backing up.

en.explanation: If you miss an exit, do not slow down, back up or try to turn around. Proceed to the next exit and leave the highway there instead.

en.question: When you engage the high-beam headlights at night, you should be able to see a person who is how far away?

choices.A: 75 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: When you engage the high-beam headlights at night, you should be able to see a person who is 200 feet away.

en.question: According to North Carolina law, taillights must be red in color and visible for at least:

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Taillights must be red in color and visible for at least 500 feet.

en.question: How should you adjust your vehicle's side mirrors before beginning to drive?

choices.A: To show the scene directly behind the vehicle.
choices.B: To show the scene to the left and right rear, barely reflecting the side of the vehicle.
choices.C: To completely eliminate all blind spots.
choices.D: To show the front tires of the vehicle.

en.explanation: Adjust the side mirrors to show the scene to the left and right rear of the vehicle. The mirrors should barely reflect the side of the vehicle.

en.question: What does it indicate if your brake pedal gradually lowers under the pressure of your foot?

choices.A: The anti-lock braking system is engaging.
choices.B: The brake pads are brand new.
choices.C: The hydraulic system must be checked.
choices.D: The tires are underinflated.

en.explanation: If the pedal gradually lowers under the pressure of your foot, the hydraulic system must be checked.

en.question: What is the correct way to use an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) when stopping?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly.
choices.B: Brake hard and keep firm and steady pressure on the brake pedal.
choices.C: Lightly tap the brake pedal multiple times.
choices.D: Release pressure on the brake pedal if you feel it vibrating.

en.explanation: With ABS, it is important to brake hard and keep firm and steady pressure on the brake pedal while stopping. Pumping the brake pedal or releasing the steady pressure will reduce the effectiveness of the ABS.

en.question: What is the minimum allowable tread depth for tires to be considered safe in North Carolina?

choices.A: 1/32-inch
choices.B: 1/16-inch
choices.C: 1/8-inch
choices.D: 1/4-inch

en.explanation: According to the manual, tires are considered unsafe if they have less than 1/16-inch-tread depth.

en.question: What is a negative consequence of driving with over-inflated tires?

choices.A: They wear out more quickly on the outer edges.
choices.B: They increase the likelihood of a blowout.
choices.C: They reduce traction and wear heavily on the middle of the tread.
choices.D: They improve fuel economy by 10%.

en.explanation: The manual states that over-inflated tires reduce traction and wear heavily on the middle of the tread.

en.question: To help prevent carbon monoxide poisoning from a potential exhaust leak, what does the manual suggest?

choices.A: Keep the air conditioning on high at all times.
choices.B: Keep a window open about one inch while traveling.
choices.C: Replace the muffler every 10,000 miles.
choices.D: Drive with the hazard lights on.

en.explanation: Because a leak in the exhaust system can allow poisonous carbon monoxide gas to enter the vehicle, it is suggested that you keep a window open about one inch while traveling.

en.question: Which of the following is a sign that your vehicle may have a problem with its suspension system?

choices.A: The vehicle sways freely, leans heavily to one side during a turn, or bounces continuously.
choices.B: The engine stalls when idling for more than a couple of minutes.
choices.C: The steering wheel vibrates when traveling over 60 mph.
choices.D: The exhaust system releases excessive smoke and noise.

en.explanation: If a vehicle sways freely, leans heavily to one side during a turn or seems to bounce continuously, there may be a problem with the suspension system.

en.question: According to the 'Drive Green' section, abrupt starts and hard stops can increase fuel consumption by up to:
en.explanation: Driving green means adopting simple habits; the manual notes that abrupt starts and hard stops can increase fuel consumption by 40%.

en.question: Every five miles per hour you drive over 60 mph can cost you up to an additional:

choices.A: 10 cents a gallon
choices.B: 15 cents a gallon
choices.C: 30 cents a gallon
choices.D: 50 cents a gallon

en.explanation: The manual states that every five miles over 60 mph can cost you up to an additional 30 cents a gallon.

en.question: How far ahead should a good driver try to scan on the roadway?

choices.A: 3 to 5 seconds ahead
choices.B: 5 to 10 seconds ahead
choices.C: 10 to 15 seconds ahead
choices.D: 20 to 30 seconds ahead

en.explanation: Good drivers try to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead on the roadway (about one city block) to avoid last minute moves.

en.question: About how often should you check your mirrors to see if a vehicle is following too closely?

choices.A: Every 5 seconds
choices.B: Every 10 seconds
choices.C: Every 30 seconds
choices.D: Every 60 seconds

en.explanation: The manual advises checking the mirrors about every 10 seconds to see if any vehicle is following too closely.

en.question: What is the proper way to check your blind spots before making a lane change?

choices.A: Rely entirely on your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder.
choices.C: Flash your headlights and wait for a response.
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn vehicles in your blind spot.

en.explanation: Because mirrors leave blind spots, before you make any lane changes or turns, you should quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to see what is in the blind spot.

en.question: If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, you must signal your turn at least:

choices.A: 50 feet before turning
choices.B: 100 feet before turning
choices.C: 200 feet before turning
choices.D: 500 feet before turning

en.explanation: Normally you signal at least the last 100 feet before turning, but if the speed limit is 45 mph or more, you must signal at least the last 200 feet before turning.

en.question: What is the correct hand signal for a right turn?

choices.A: Hold the left arm and hand straight out and point the first finger.
choices.B: Hold the left arm straight out and the forearm and hand straight up, palm facing forward.
choices.C: Point the left arm and hand down, palm facing back.
choices.D: Wave the left hand in a circular motion.

en.explanation: To signal a right turn using hand signals, hold the left arm straight out and the forearm and hand straight up, palm facing forward.

en.question: How do you use a hand signal to indicate that you are stopping or slowing down?

choices.A: Point the left arm and hand down, palm facing back.
choices.B: Hold the left arm straight out and point the first finger.
choices.C: Hold the left arm straight out and the forearm straight up.
choices.D: Flash your brake lights three times.

en.explanation: To signal stopping and slowing down, point the left arm and hand down, palm facing back.

en.question: If you are faced with approaching vehicles to your left and a child on a bicycle to your right, how should you adjust your vehicle?

choices.A: Give equal room to both hazards.
choices.B: Move closer to the child on the bicycle to avoid the vehicles.
choices.C: Sound your horn continuously until the hazards clear.
choices.D: Give the child more room, even if it means moving closer to the oncoming vehicles.

en.explanation: When dealing with two or more unavoidable dangers, give the most room to the greatest or most likely danger. The child is most likely to make a sudden move, so give the child more room, even if it means moving closer to oncoming vehicles.

en.question: What color are the warning signs used strictly to identify highway work zones?

choices.A: Yellow signs with black letters
choices.B: Orange signs with black letters
choices.C: White signs with black letters
choices.D: Red signs with white letters

en.explanation: A highway work zone can be easily identified by unique orange warning signs with messages in black letters, which are reserved strictly to identify work zones.

en.question: How far away must your vehicle's horn be loud enough to be heard?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: Every licensed motor vehicle must be equipped with a horn that is loud enough to be heard for at least 200 feet.

en.question: What is a major cause of rear-end crashes in work zones?

choices.A: Driving faster than the posted speed limit
choices.B: Driving slower than the surrounding traffic
choices.C: Failing to use turn signals when shifting lanes
choices.D: Using high-beam headlights

en.explanation: According to the manual, driving slower than the surrounding traffic is a major cause of rear-end crashes in work zones.

en.question: Under North Carolina law, when are you required to use your headlights?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less
choices.B: From dusk to dawn and when visibility is 500 feet or less
choices.C: Only when driving on unlit rural roads at night
choices.D: From 8 PM to 6 AM regardless of weather conditions

en.explanation: The law requires use of headlights from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less.

en.question: What should you do if an approaching vehicle does not dim its headlights at night?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams and leave them on until they pass
choices.B: Look directly at the oncoming headlights to gauge their distance
choices.C: Blink your high beams once, and look slightly to the right if they still do not dim them
choices.D: Pull off the road immediately and turn off all your lights

en.explanation: The manual advises that you can remind the driver by blinking your high beams once. If they still do not dim the lights, keep yours on low beam and look slightly to the right so you will not be looking directly into the headlights.

en.question: How much does stopping distance increase on slippery pavement compared to dry pavement?

choices.A: It remains the same if you have anti-lock brakes
choices.B: It increases from two to 10 times farther
choices.C: It increases by exactly 50 percent
choices.D: It increases from 15 to 20 times farther

en.explanation: Stopping distances on slippery pavement increases from two to 10 times farther than on dry pavement.

en.question: Why are roads considered more dangerous for the first 10 to 15 minutes after rain has begun to fall?

choices.A: The rain washes away the reflective paint on lane markings
choices.B: Rain combines with oil, dirt, dust, and rubber to create a slick surface
choices.C: Drivers tend to speed up to reach their destinations before the storm worsens
choices.D: The water immediately causes severe hydroplaning at any speed

en.explanation: For the first 10 to 15 minutes, rain combines with oil from asphalt and vehicles, and with dirt, dust and rubber to create a slick surface.

en.question: At what speed can hydroplaning begin?

choices.A: As low as 15 miles per hour
choices.B: As low as 30 miles per hour
choices.C: As low as 45 miles per hour
choices.D: As low as 55 miles per hour

en.explanation: Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 miles per hour and in water little more than 1/8 inch deep.

en.question: What is the recommended action if your vehicle begins to hydroplane?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately to regain traction
choices.B: Jerk the steering wheel sharply to the right
choices.C: Take your foot off the gas pedal and resist your instinct to use the brakes
choices.D: Turn on your cruise control to maintain a steady speed

en.explanation: If you do begin to hydroplane, take your foot off the gas pedal. Resist your instinct to use the brakes. Keep your steering wheel straight and let the car's momentum decrease.

en.question: Which tire condition increases your chance of hydroplaning?

choices.A: Tires with deep, open treads
choices.B: Tires inflated to the high side of the manufacturer's specifications
choices.C: Tires with worn tread that are under-inflated
choices.D: Snow tires used during the summer

en.explanation: Tires with worn tread and those that are under inflated have less grip on the road surface, increasing your chance of hydroplaning.

en.question: According to the manual, how much fast-moving water does it take to sweep a car off the highway?

choices.A: 2 inches
choices.B: 6 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 24 inches

en.explanation: There have been reports that six inches of fast moving water can sweep a car off the highway and 12 inches of fast moving water can float a car or cause it to turn over.

en.question: What must North Carolina motorists do whenever they are using windshield wipers due to inclement weather?

choices.A: Turn on their emergency flashers
choices.B: Drive at least 15 mph below the posted speed limit
choices.C: Turn on their headlights
choices.D: Drive only in the right-hand lane

en.explanation: All North Carolina motorists are required to use headlights whenever they are using windshield wipers due to inclement weather.

en.question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?

choices.A: High beam headlights
choices.B: Low beam headlights
choices.C: Parking lights only
choices.D: Emergency flashers only

en.explanation: If you must drive during fog: Turn on the low beam headlights.

en.question: What should you do if you have extreme trouble seeing while driving in fog?

choices.A: Stop in the middle of your lane and wait for the fog to clear
choices.B: Turn on your high beams and speed up to exit the fog bank quickly
choices.C: Pull far off the roadway, stop, secure the vehicle, and turn on emergency flashers
choices.D: Roll down your windows and honk your horn continuously while driving

en.explanation: If you have extreme trouble seeing, you need to: Pull far off the roadway; Stop, secure the vehicle and turn on its emergency flashers; and Leave the vehicle from the passenger side and stay away from the road.

en.question: Which areas of the road are often the first to freeze as the temperature drops?

choices.A: Intersections and crosswalks
choices.B: Shady spots, bridges, and overpasses
choices.C: Highways with heavy traffic
choices.D: Tunnels and underpasses

en.explanation: As you drive, watch for shady spots, bridges and overpasses since these places are often the first to freeze as the temperature drops.

en.question: How much should you increase your stopping distance when slowing down on snowy or icy roads?

choices.A: Allow at least two times the normal stopping distance
choices.B: Allow at least three times the normal stopping distance
choices.C: Allow at least five times the normal stopping distance
choices.D: Allow at least ten times the normal stopping distance

en.explanation: When you are starting or stopping on snowy or icy roads: Allow at least three times the normal stopping distance to slow down.

en.question: When driving on ice and packed snow, how much stopping distance should you allow?

choices.A: Twice the normal stopping distance
choices.B: At least three times the normal stopping distance
choices.C: Four times the normal stopping distance
choices.D: The same as normal stopping distance

en.explanation: The manual states that when driving on ice and packed snow, you should allow at least three times the normal stopping distance to slow down.

en.question: At what times of day are wildlife most active and likely to be on the road?

choices.A: Mid-morning and early afternoon
choices.B: Only during the darkest hours of the night
choices.C: Dawn, dusk, and the first few hours after dark
choices.D: High noon and late afternoon

en.explanation: According to the manual, wildlife can appear anywhere, anytime; however, they are most active at dawn, dusk, and in the first few hours after dark.

en.question: Why should you be cautious about using high beams when animals are directly ahead?

choices.A: High beams can confuse or 'freeze' some animals.
choices.B: High beams will cause the animal to charge the vehicle.
choices.C: High beams make it harder for the driver to see eye shine.
choices.D: High beams will permanently blind the animal.

en.explanation: The manual advises to only use high beams when there is no oncoming traffic and no animals directly ahead, because high beams can confuse or 'freeze' some animals, causing the 'deer in headlights' behavior.

en.question: If you hit an animal and pull off to the side of the road, what should you do next?

choices.A: Approach the animal to check its injuries.
choices.B: Stay in your car, lock your doors, and turn on hazard lights.
choices.C: Drag the animal off the roadway immediately.
choices.D: Exit the vehicle and wave down other drivers for help.

en.explanation: If you hit an animal, the manual instructs you to pull off to the side of the road safely, stay in your car, lock your doors, and turn on hazard lights. You should not approach the animal as it may be dangerous.

en.question: If your vehicle is equipped with an automatic transmission and your brakes fail, what should you do?

choices.A: Shift into park and turn off the engine.
choices.B: Pump the gas pedal to build brake fluid pressure.
choices.C: Apply the emergency brake and move the gear control lever into the low-range position.
choices.D: Shift into neutral and coast until the vehicle stops.

en.explanation: In the event of brake failure in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, you should apply the emergency brake and move the gear control lever into the low-range position.

en.question: How can you help dry wet brakes?

choices.A: Drive at a high speed for several miles.
choices.B: Drive a short distance and apply light pressure to the brake pedal.
choices.C: Pump the brake pedal rapidly while in neutral.
choices.D: Pull over and let the brakes air dry for an hour.

en.explanation: You can help dry wet brakes by driving a short distance and applying light pressure to the brake pedal. The friction generates heat that evaporates the water.

en.question: To prevent excessive wear on your brakes when moving down a long hill or steep grade, you should:

choices.A: Ride the brake pedal the entire way down.
choices.B: Shift into neutral and coast down the hill.
choices.C: Turn off the engine to reduce speed.
choices.D: Shift to a lower gear at the top of the hill before you descend.

en.explanation: To prevent excessive wear on brakes when moving down a long hill or steep grade, use a lower gear instead of the brake pedal to control speed. It is best to shift to the lower gear at the top of the hill before descending.

en.question: What is one of the steps you should take if your gas pedal sticks?

choices.A: Shift to neutral and apply firm pressure to the brakes without locking the wheels.
choices.B: Turn off the ignition immediately and remove the key.
choices.C: Shift into reverse to counteract the forward motion.
choices.D: Slam on the brakes as hard as possible to lock the wheels.

en.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, the manual recommends shifting to neutral and applying firm pressure to the brakes without locking the wheels, as well as tapping the pedal or finding a safe place to pull off.

en.question: If a tire blowout occurs while driving, what should you do first?

choices.A: Immediately apply the brakes hard to stop quickly.
choices.B: Hold the steering wheel tightly and try to keep the vehicle straight.
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel sharply toward the shoulder.
choices.D: Accelerate slightly to maintain control of the vehicle.

en.explanation: If a blowout occurs, you should hold the steering wheel tightly and try to keep the vehicle straight on your side of the road, and reduce speed by lifting your foot from the accelerator without immediately applying the brakes.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you need help, how should you signal other drivers?

choices.A: Stand in the middle of the road and wave your arms.
choices.B: Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood.
choices.C: Flash your high beams continuously.
choices.D: Place a red flag on the rear bumper and stand behind the vehicle.

en.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down and you need help, the manual states you should tie a white cloth to the left door handle or the radio aerial and raise the hood of the vehicle.

en.question: If an approaching vehicle crosses the center line into the path of your vehicle, you should:

choices.A: Steer into the left lane to avoid them.
choices.B: Speed up to get past them quickly.
choices.C: Reduce speed immediately, sound your horn, and keep to the right.
choices.D: Stop immediately in your lane and flash your headlights.

en.explanation: If an approaching vehicle crosses the center line into your path, you should reduce speed immediately, sound your horn, and keep to the right even if this means running off the road.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle runs off the pavement and onto the shoulder?

choices.A: Immediately apply the brakes and jerk the steering wheel back toward the road.
choices.B: Slowly remove your foot from the accelerator and steer straight ahead.
choices.C: Accelerate to get back onto the pavement quickly.
choices.D: Shift into neutral and coast until you stop.

en.explanation: If your vehicle runs off the pavement, you should not immediately apply the brakes or try to turn back. Instead, slowly remove your foot from the accelerator and steer straight ahead.

en.question: If you find yourself in a skid, in which direction should you turn the steering wheel?

choices.A: In the opposite direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding.
choices.B: Keep the steering wheel perfectly straight.
choices.C: In the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding.
choices.D: Toward the right shoulder of the road regardless of the skid direction.

en.explanation: If you find yourself in a skid, you should ease your foot off the accelerator and turn the steering wheel in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding.

en.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear and there are no vehicles in front of you, you should:

choices.A: Press the accelerator and move away as quickly as possible.
choices.B: Slam on your brakes to brace for the impact.
choices.C: Shift into reverse and back up.
choices.D: Turn off your engine and release the seatbelt.

en.explanation: If you are about to be hit from the rear and there are no vehicles in front of you, the manual advises to press the accelerator and move away as quickly as possible.

en.question: How does the law protect individuals who stop and render aid at the scene of an accident?

choices.A: It guarantees them financial compensation for their time.
choices.B: It protects them from civil liability except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.
choices.C: It grants them immunity from all future traffic violations.
choices.D: It requires the at-fault driver's insurance to pay them a reward.

en.explanation: The law protects persons who stop and render aid at the scene of an accident from civil liability except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.

en.question: What should you do if you find yourself in a skid?

choices.A: Brake firmly and hold the steering wheel straight.
choices.B: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction the rear is skidding.
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding.
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to regain traction.

en.explanation: If you find yourself in a skid, you should ease your foot off the accelerator and turn the steering wheel in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding.

en.question: If you are involved in a crash on a main lane with no injuries or fatalities, what should you do with your vehicle?

choices.A: Leave it exactly where it is until police arrive.
choices.B: Move it out of the travel lane onto the shoulder if it can be driven safely.
choices.C: Drive it immediately to the nearest repair shop.
choices.D: Abandon the vehicle and walk to safety.

en.explanation: If the crash occurred on a main lane... and there are no injuries or fatalities, each vehicle should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder of the road provided it can be driven safely under its own power.

en.question: When are you required by law to make an immediate report of a crash to law enforcement?

choices.A: Only when a person is killed.
choices.B: Only when damage to property is over $5,000.
choices.C: When any person is killed or injured, or total property damage appears to be $1,000 or more.
choices.D: Whenever the crash involves more than two vehicles.

en.explanation: You are required by law to make an immediate report to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency of any crash when any person is killed or injured or the total damage to vehicles and other property appears to amount to $1,000 or more.

en.question: If you damage property in a crash and do not know the owner, what must you do?

choices.A: Leave the scene immediately.
choices.B: Wait at the scene for exactly one hour.
choices.C: Write down all the information you can gather and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer.
choices.D: Leave a note with your phone number on the damaged property.

en.explanation: If you do not know the occupants of the other vehicle or the owner of damaged property, write down all the information you can gather and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to yield to a pedestrian when making a right turn on a red light?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense.
choices.B: A penalty of not more than $500 and not less than $100.
choices.C: A mandatory 30-day license suspension.
choices.D: A fine of exactly $50.

en.explanation: Failure to yield to a pedestrian under these circumstances will result in a penalty of not more than $500 and not less than $100.

en.question: What does a yellow arrow traffic signal indicate?

choices.A: The protected green arrow signal is about to turn to a regular circular green, circular red, or red arrow signal.
choices.B: You have the right-of-way to make the turn without yielding.
choices.C: You must stop immediately and not proceed until it turns green.
choices.D: The traffic light is malfunctioning.

en.explanation: A yellow arrow indicates that the 'protected' green arrow signal is about to turn to a regular circular green signal, circular red signal or red arrow signal.

en.question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a malfunctioning traffic light due to a power outage?

choices.A: Yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed without stopping.
choices.B: Proceed as though the intersection is controlled by a stop sign on all approaches.
choices.C: Wait until a law enforcement officer arrives.
choices.D: Treat the intersection as a yield sign.

en.explanation: When approaching an intersection with a traffic light that has malfunctioned due to a power outage... you should approach the intersection and proceed as though the intersection is controlled by a stop sign on all approaches.

en.question: What does a flashing red signal mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.B: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
choices.C: It has the same meaning as a stop sign.
choices.D: Yield to oncoming traffic but do not stop.

en.explanation: The flashing red signal has the same meaning as the stop sign: stop and do not proceed to move until you can enter the intersection without interfering with approaching traffic.

en.question: What must a driver do when facing a flashing yellow arrow for a turn?

choices.A: Stop and wait for a solid green arrow.
choices.B: The turn is permitted, but the driver must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
choices.C: The driver has the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must yield.
choices.D: Prepare to stop because the light is turning red.

en.explanation: When the flashing yellow arrow is shown, the indicated turn is permitted but drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

en.question: When making a U-turn on a solid green arrow, what must you do?

choices.A: Yield to opposing right-turning traffic when both have a green arrow.
choices.B: Proceed without yielding to any traffic.
choices.C: Stop and wait for a circular green light.
choices.D: Yield to all traffic behind you.

en.explanation: U-turning traffic should yield to opposing right turning traffic when both movements simultaneously have their respective green arrow.

en.question: What should you do if a ramp meter signal is dark or not emitting any light?

choices.A: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
choices.B: Treat it as a four-way stop.
choices.C: Proceed without stopping and enter the freeway by merging or yielding as normal.
choices.D: Pull over to the shoulder and report the broken signal.

en.explanation: When the display is dark or not emitting a red or green display, a vehicle may proceed without stopping and enter the freeway by merging or yielding as normal conditions allow.

en.question: How do hybrid beacons operate when first activated by a pedestrian?

choices.A: They immediately turn solid red.
choices.B: They flash yellow, then go steady yellow, and then steady red to allow vehicles to stop safely.
choices.C: They flash red continuously until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
choices.D: They display a green arrow for pedestrians.

en.explanation: Once activated, the beacons will flash yellow for a few seconds, then go steady yellow and steady red for a few more seconds to allow moving vehicles to safely stop.

en.question: Where is a stop sign usually posted?

choices.A: Exactly at the intersection line.
choices.B: 6 to 50 feet from the intersection.
choices.C: 100 feet before the intersection.
choices.D: 50 to 100 feet from the intersection.

en.explanation: The stop sign is usually posted six to 50 feet from the intersection.

en.question: If there is no stop line or marked crosswalk at a stop sign, where must the driver stop?

choices.A: Even with the stop sign itself.
choices.B: 10 feet before the intersecting street.
choices.C: Before entering the intersection where they have a view of the intersecting street.
choices.D: In the middle of the intersection to check for traffic.

en.explanation: If there is no stop line or marked crosswalk, the driver must stop before entering the intersection where he/she has a view of the intersecting street.

en.question: What is the shape and color of a yield sign?

choices.A: Octagon shaped, red and white
choices.B: Triangular shaped with the point at the bottom, red and white
choices.C: Diamond shaped, black and yellow
choices.D: Pennant shaped, yellow and black

en.explanation: According to the manual, the yield sign is triangular shaped with the point at the bottom, and it is red and white with the word 'YIELD' in large letters.

en.question: Where is the pennant-shaped yellow 'DO NOT PASS' warning sign located?

choices.A: On the right side of the road
choices.B: Suspended over the center of the intersection
choices.C: On the left side of the road
choices.D: On the right shoulder before a curve

en.explanation: The manual states that the pennant-shaped yellow warning sign is located on the left side of the road and points to the beginning of the no-passing zone.

en.question: What do diamond-shaped signs that are orange with black messages warn drivers about?

choices.A: Railroad crossings
choices.B: School zones
choices.C: Construction or maintenance areas
choices.D: No-passing zones

en.explanation: Diamond-shaped caution or warning signs that are orange with black messages warn about construction or maintenance areas.

en.question: Which sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing?

choices.A: A circular sign with a black cross and the letters 'RR' on a yellow background
choices.B: A white crossbuck sign with 'RAILROAD CROSSING' in black
choices.C: A diamond-shaped yellow sign with a black train symbol
choices.D: A pentagon-shaped sign with a black cross

en.explanation: A circular sign, with a black cross and the black letters 'RR' on a yellow background, gives advance warning of a railroad crossing.

en.question: What does a five-sided (pentagon) sign warn drivers of?

choices.A: A hospital zone
choices.B: A school zone or a school crossing
choices.C: A pedestrian crosswalk
choices.D: An upcoming stop sign

en.explanation: The five-sided (or pentagon) sign warns of a school zone or a school crossing, where drivers should be especially watchful for children.

en.question: According to the manual, how are odd-numbered highways generally routed?

choices.A: East and west
choices.B: North and south
choices.C: In a circular loop around a city
choices.D: Diagonally across the state

en.explanation: The manual states that odd-numbered highways generally run north and south.

en.question: What shape is the route marker for a North Carolina (N.C.) highway?

choices.A: Shield
choices.B: Rectangle
choices.C: Diamond
choices.D: Circle

en.explanation: According to the guide/informational signs section, North Carolina route markers are diamond shaped.

en.question: What is the purpose of yellow pavement lines on a roadway?

choices.A: To separate travel lanes moving in the same direction
choices.B: To mark the right edge of the roadway
choices.C: To indicate a crosswalk
choices.D: To separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions

en.explanation: Yellow lines separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate travel lanes moving in the same direction.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding a special center lane reserved for two-way left-turn movements?

choices.A: It can be used for passing slower vehicles
choices.B: It must not be used for passing or merging into traffic
choices.C: It is reserved exclusively for emergency vehicles
choices.D: It can be used as a regular travel lane during rush hour

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the two-way left-turn lane must not be used for passing another vehicle or for the purpose of merging into traffic.

en.question: What do red reflective pavement markers indicate to a motorist?

choices.A: The location of a nearby fire hydrant
choices.B: A school zone is approaching
choices.C: Wrong-way movements
choices.D: A railroad crossing is ahead

en.explanation: Red markers indicate wrong-way movements for motorists. Blue reflective pavement markers indicate nearby fire hydrants.

en.question: If a traffic officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light, what should you do?

choices.A: Obey the traffic light
choices.B: Obey the officer's hand signals instead of the traffic light
choices.C: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop
choices.D: Honk your horn to acknowledge the officer

en.explanation: Under special circumstances, an officer may be directing the flow of traffic. If so, you must obey the officer's hand signals instead of the normal traffic signals or signs.

en.question: Are bicyclists subject to Driving While Impaired (DWI) laws?

choices.A: No, because bicycles are not motorized vehicles
choices.B: Yes, because state law considers bicycles to be vehicles
choices.C: Only if they are riding on a state highway
choices.D: Only if they are involved in a collision

en.explanation: Because bicycles are vehicles, bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as other drivers, which includes DWI laws.

en.question: What lighting equipment is required by law for a bicycle ridden at night?

choices.A: A front light visible for at least 300 feet and a rear red light or reflector visible for at least 200 feet
choices.B: A front light visible for 500 feet and a rear red light visible for 500 feet
choices.C: Only a rear red reflector visible for 100 feet
choices.D: Reflective clothing and a flashing helmet light

en.explanation: At night, the law requires that a bicycle be equipped with a light on the front visible for a distance of at least 300 feet and a red light or reflector on the rear visible for a distance of at least 200 feet.

en.question: In which direction should bicyclists ride on the roadway?

choices.A: Against the flow of traffic to see oncoming cars
choices.B: On the left side of the road
choices.C: With the flow of traffic, on the right side of the road
choices.D: On the sidewalk whenever possible

en.explanation: It is especially important for bicyclists to go with the flow of traffic, NOT against the flow. They must ride right, with the traffic.

en.question: Who is required by law to wear an approved protective bicycle helmet?

choices.A: All bicycle riders regardless of age
choices.B: Only bicycle riders riding on interstate highways
choices.C: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16
choices.D: Only passengers riding in a bicycle seat

en.explanation: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16 must wear an approved protective bicycle helmet and must be seated on a saddle seat.

en.question: What are the weight and height requirements for a passenger to be required to sit in a bicycle restraining seat?

choices.A: Less than 30 pounds or less than 30 inches in height
choices.B: Less than 40 pounds or less than 40 inches in height
choices.C: Less than 50 pounds or less than 48 inches in height
choices.D: Less than 60 pounds or less than 50 inches in height

en.explanation: According to the manual, a passenger weighing less than 40 pounds or less than 40 inches in height must be seated in a bicycle restraining seat.

en.question: When walking along a road as a pedestrian, where should you walk?

choices.A: On the right side of the road moving with traffic
choices.B: On the right side of the road facing traffic
choices.C: On the left side of the road facing traffic
choices.D: On the left side of the road moving with traffic

en.explanation: The manual states that pedestrians should always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic.

en.question: According to the manual, which groups make up most of the pedestrians killed in motor vehicle crashes?

choices.A: Teenagers and young adults
choices.B: Construction workers and joggers
choices.C: People walking at crosswalks and intersections
choices.D: Children, elderly persons, or those who have been drinking alcoholic beverages

en.explanation: The manual notes that most of the pedestrians killed are children, elderly persons or those who have been drinking alcoholic beverages.

en.question: How far behind a tractor-trailer does the rear blind spot (NO-ZONE) extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 200 feet
choices.D: Up to 300 feet

en.explanation: Truckers have serious blind spots or NO-ZONES into which a car can disappear from view, including up to 200 feet in the rear.

en.question: What is a general rule for motorists sharing the road with a tractor-trailer?

choices.A: If you can see the truck's tires, you are at a safe distance
choices.B: If you can't see the truck driver in their side-view mirror, they can't see you
choices.C: Always pass a large truck on the right side
choices.D: Tailgate the truck to reduce wind resistance and improve gas mileage

en.explanation: A general rule for motorists sharing the road with a tractor-trailer is, 'if you can't see the truck driver in their side-view mirror, they can't see you.'

en.question: How much clear roadway may it take to safely pass a trailer and the towing vehicle?

choices.A: One-quarter mile
choices.B: One-half mile
choices.C: Three-quarters of a mile
choices.D: One full mile

en.explanation: You should use extreme caution while passing a trailer and the towing vehicle, as it may take you a half mile of clear roadway to safely pass.

en.question: When passing a moped, you must stay at least how far to the left?

choices.A: One foot
choices.B: Two feet
choices.C: Three feet
choices.D: Four feet

en.explanation: A moped should travel using the right side of the lane. To pass a moped, you must stay at least two feet to the left.

en.question: In most motorcycle crashes involving a car in North Carolina, who is usually at fault?

choices.A: The motorcyclist
choices.B: The driver of the car
choices.C: Both drivers equally
choices.D: Neither, as weather is usually the primary factor

en.explanation: About two-thirds of motorcycle crashes in North Carolina involve a car. In most of these crashes, the driver of the car is at fault, usually claiming they did not see the motorcycle.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to operate a moped on a public roadway in North Carolina?

choices.A: 14 years old
choices.B: 15 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: In North Carolina you must be at least 16 years old to operate a moped on a public roadway or public vehicular area.

en.question: Why do large trucks require additional turning room?

choices.A: Because their brakes heat up quickly on downhill grades
choices.B: Because their rear wheels do not follow the path of their front wheels
choices.C: Because they have larger blind spots than passenger cars
choices.D: Because they accelerate much slower than passenger vehicles

en.explanation: Large trucks require additional turning room because their rear wheels do not follow the path of their front wheels.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding moped operators and driving while impaired (DWI) laws?

choices.A: Moped operators are exempt from DWI laws because mopeds are not considered motor vehicles.
choices.B: DWI laws only apply to moped operators if they are traveling over 20 mph.
choices.C: Driving while impaired laws that apply to drivers of other motor vehicles also apply to moped operators.
choices.D: Moped operators face lesser penalties for DWI than car drivers.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that driving while impaired laws that apply to drivers of other motor vehicles also apply to moped operators.

en.question: What is a potential hazard you should be aware of when a vehicle towing a trailer brakes suddenly?

choices.A: The trailer may detach from the towing vehicle
choices.B: The sudden braking might cause the trailer to jackknife
choices.C: The towing vehicle's engine will likely stall
choices.D: The trailer's brakes will overheat and catch fire

en.explanation: When you approach a vehicle towing a trailer, be aware that sudden braking might cause the trailer to jackknife.

en.question: What document can serve as proof of ownership for a moped if the operator does not have a Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin (MCO)?

choices.A: A notarized bill of sale from the dealership
choices.B: An Affidavit of Facts for the Registration of a Moped form (MVR-58)
choices.C: A valid North Carolina driver license
choices.D: A previous owner's registration card

en.explanation: The manual states that if an operator does not have an MCO for their vehicle, they can fill out an Affidavit of Facts for the Registration of a Moped form (MVR-58) to serve as proof of ownership.

en.question: What is the minimum fine for a first-time littering conviction in North Carolina?

choices.A: A minimum fine of $100
choices.B: A minimum fine of $250
choices.C: A minimum fine of $500
choices.D: A minimum fine of $1,000

en.explanation: When litter is thrown or blown from a vehicle, the driver is held responsible. If convicted, the minimum fine is $250, and the maximum fine is $1,000.

en.question: If a second littering offense occurs within three years of a prior offense, what is the maximum fine upon conviction?
en.explanation: Any second or subsequent littering offense within three years after the date of a prior offense is punishable by a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $2,000, if convicted.

en.question: How often does a volunteer group agree to pick up litter when joining the Adopt-A-Highway Program?

choices.A: Once a month
choices.B: Twice a year
choices.C: At least four times a year
choices.D: Six times a year

en.explanation: To join the Adopt-A-Highway program, a group agrees to pick up litter at least four times a year along a two-mile section of state-maintained roadway.

en.question: Which type of driver license record check is usually required for court appearances?

choices.A: A non-certified full history
choices.B: A certified copy of the record
choices.C: A non-certified three-year history
choices.D: A copy of address history

en.explanation: The manual specifies that a certified driver license record check usually is required for court appearances.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is exempt from being registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles?

choices.A: Mopeds
choices.B: Motor homes
choices.C: Exempt road construction equipment
choices.D: Fleet vehicles

en.explanation: Except for owners of exempt farm vehicles and exempt road construction equipment, every vehicle owner must register their motor vehicle with the Division of Motor Vehicles.

en.question: What must a new North Carolina resident moving from out-of-state provide to title and register their vehicle?

choices.A: A valid out-of-state driver's license and a North Carolina Temporary Driving Certificate (TDC)
choices.B: A certified copy of their driving record
choices.C: An Affidavit of Facts (MVR-58)
choices.D: A North Carolina voter registration card

en.explanation: If you are a new North Carolina resident moving from out-of-state, your valid out-of-state driver’s license, along with your North Carolina Temporary Driving Certificate (TDC) will be required to title and register your vehicle.

en.question: According to North Carolina law, which of the following is prohibited regarding license plates?

choices.A: Displaying the plate on the rear of the vehicle
choices.B: Using plastic license plate covers
choices.C: Having validation stickers on the plate
choices.D: Displaying the expiration date

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that plastic license plate covers are prohibited under GS 20-63g.

en.question: What information is required to change the physical address on your vehicle registration online?

choices.A: Your social security number and date of birth
choices.B: Your vehicle license plate number, the last five characters of the vehicle title number, and a valid email address
choices.C: A certified copy of your driving record and proof of insurance
choices.D: Your out-of-state driver's license and a Temporary Driving Certificate

en.explanation: To change your address online, you will need your vehicle license plate number, the last five characters of the vehicle title number, and a valid email address.

en.question: What is the official transfer document required to register a new vehicle in North Carolina?

choices.A: A notarized bill of sale
choices.B: The manufacturer's certificate of origin
choices.C: A certificate of self-insurance
choices.D: A non-certified full history record

en.explanation: Before a vehicle can be registered, proper proof of ownership is required. For new vehicles, the manufacturer's certificate of origin is the official transfer document.

en.question: Within how many days must a license or ID holder update their physical address with the DMV after moving within North Carolina?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: Within 60 days of moving within North Carolina, a license or ID holder must update their physical address with the DMV and get a duplicate license or ID.

en.question: What is the penalty if the DMV is notified that a vehicle owner is operating a motor vehicle without proper liability insurance?

choices.A: The vehicle will be impounded for 60 days
choices.B: The vehicle's license plate could be revoked for 30 days
choices.C: The driver's license will be permanently suspended
choices.D: The owner must pay a $1,000 minimum fine

en.explanation: If the DMV is notified that a vehicle owner is operating a motor vehicle without proper liability insurance, the vehicle’s license plate could be revoked for 30 days.

en.question: In North Carolina, a certificate of self-insurance can be used as proof of liability insurance for fleets of at least how many vehicles?

choices.A: 5 or more vehicles
choices.B: 10 or more vehicles
choices.C: 15 or more vehicles
choices.D: 25 or more vehicles

en.explanation: Liability insurance can be in the form of a policy from a licensed company, cash or bond deposited with the State Treasurer, or a certificate of self-insurance for fleets of 25 or more vehicles.

en.question: What is the minimum amount of liability insurance required for property damage in a crash in North Carolina?
en.explanation: The minimum amount of liability insurance required is $25,000 for all property damage in a crash.

en.question: How long is the grace period honored by North Carolina for expired liability insurance policies?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: North Carolina does not honor a grace period.

en.explanation: North Carolina does not honor a grace period. A grace period is an agreement between the Insured and the insurance company only.

en.question: Within how many days prior to a vehicle's registration expiration must it receive a safety or safety and emission inspection?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: Within 90 days prior to the registration expiration, all self-propelled vehicles are required to receive a safety or safety and emission inspection to renew their registration.

en.question: What should you do to avoid a fine or penalty before terminating or canceling your vehicle's liability insurance?

choices.A: Notify your local county assessment office.
choices.B: Surrender the vehicle's valid license plate.
choices.C: Apply for a duplicate title.
choices.D: Pay the Tag & Tax Together fee.

en.explanation: To avoid a fine or penalty, surrender a vehicle's valid license plate prior to the termination or cancellation of liability insurance.

en.question: When transferring ownership of a motor vehicle, the reassignment of ownership on the certificate of title must be made in the presence of:

choices.A: A DMV inspector
choices.B: A law enforcement officer
choices.C: A Notary Public
choices.D: An insurance agent

en.explanation: In order for the transfer to be valid, the reassignment must be made in the presence of a Notary Public and the actual delivery of the vehicle to the new owner must be made.

en.question: Under what conditions can license plates be transferred from one vehicle to another?

choices.A: If the vehicles are of the same category, ownership is in the same name, and insurance coverage has been continuous.
choices.B: If the new vehicle is less than three years old and has less than 70,000 miles.
choices.C: If the transfer is done within 15 days of purchasing the new vehicle.
choices.D: License plates can never be transferred between vehicles in North Carolina.

en.explanation: License plates can be transferred from one vehicle to another of the same category provided ownership is in the same name and insurance coverage has been continuous.

en.question: If a certificate of title is lost or stolen, how long must you wait before a duplicate title can be issued after the application and fee are received?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: A duplicate title cannot be issued until 15 days after the application and fee are received by the DMV.

en.question: What does the "Tag & Tax Together" program require vehicle owners to do?

choices.A: Pay for registration renewal tags and vehicle property taxes in one payment.
choices.B: Pay for vehicle inspection and registration renewal in one payment.
choices.C: Pay for a duplicate title and license plate transfer at the same time.
choices.D: Pay for liability insurance and vehicle property taxes in one payment.

en.explanation: The "Tag & Tax Together" program requires one payment for both bills. Both tag renewals and tax payments must be paid in full to renew a vehicle’s annual registration.

en.question: Who is responsible for establishing the value of a vehicle for property tax purposes in North Carolina?

choices.A: The N.C. Division of Motor Vehicles
choices.B: The local county assessment office
choices.C: The DMV License & Theft Bureau
choices.D: The vehicle's insurance company

en.explanation: DMV is not involved in establishing the value of a vehicle for property tax purposes. The local county assessment office determines the tax based on the make and model of the registered vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is exempt from the "Tag & Tax Together" law?

choices.A: Passenger cars
choices.B: Mopeds
choices.C: Light-duty trucks
choices.D: Motorcycles

en.explanation: The Tag & Tax Together law covers all motor vehicles except: Vehicles exempt from registration, Manufactured homes, Mobile classrooms and offices, Semi-trailers registered on a multi-year basis, Motor vehicles owned or leased by public service companies, Park Model Trailers, and Mopeds.

en.question: If a vehicle fails its annual inspection, it is entitled to be re-inspected at the same station without paying another inspection fee within how many days?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: A vehicle that fails inspection is entitled to be re-inspected at the same station within 60 days without paying another inspection fee.

en.question: A vehicle may be exempt from an emissions inspection if it is light-duty, gasoline powered, within the three most recent model years, and has less than how many miles on the odometer?

choices.A: 30,000 miles
choices.B: 50,000 miles
choices.C: 70,000 miles
choices.D: 100,000 miles

en.explanation: The law exempts emission testing for vehicles that are registered in or sold in North Carolina if they are within the three most recent model years and have less than 70,000 miles on the odometer.

en.question: What is the allowable light transmittance for tinted windows in North Carolina?

choices.A: No less than 20%
choices.B: No less than 35%
choices.C: No less than 50%
choices.D: No less than 75%

en.explanation: The allowable light transmittance for tinted windows is no less than 35%.

en.question: Who has the authority to change motor vehicle laws and fees in North Carolina?

choices.A: The Governor
choices.B: The North Carolina General Assembly
choices.C: The DMV Commissioner
choices.D: The Department of Transportation

en.explanation: The manual states that motor vehicle laws and fees are subject to change by the North Carolina General Assembly.

en.question: According to the handbook, what is subject to change by the North Carolina General Assembly?

choices.A: Only motor vehicle laws
choices.B: Only DMV fees
choices.C: Motor vehicle laws and fees
choices.D: Federal highway regulations

en.explanation: The manual notes that motor vehicle laws and fees are subject to change by the North Carolina General Assembly.

en.question: Where can you access the North Carolina Driver Handbook online?

choices.A: NCDOT.gov
choices.B: MyNCDMV.gov
choices.C: NCHighwayPatrol.org
choices.D: NorthCarolina.gov

en.explanation: The North Carolina Driver Handbook is available online at MyNCDMV.gov.

en.question: What search term is recommended to find the manual on MyNCDMV.gov?

choices.A: Driving Rules
choices.B: License Guide
choices.C: Driver Handbook
choices.D: DMV Manual

en.explanation: The handbook is available online at MyNCDMV.gov by searching "Driver Handbook."

en.question: In which city is the North Carolina DMV Headquarters located?

choices.A: Raleigh
choices.B: Charlotte
choices.C: Rocky Mount
choices.D: Greensboro

en.explanation: The DMV Headquarters is located at 1515 N. Church Street, Rocky Mount, NC 27804.

en.question: What is the street address of the North Carolina DMV Headquarters?

choices.A: 1515 N. Church Street
choices.B: 100 E. Main Street
choices.C: 500 Capital Blvd
choices.D: 1200 DMV Drive

en.explanation: The DMV Headquarters is located at 1515 N. Church Street, Rocky Mount, NC 27804.

en.question: Which of the following services is provided at the DMV Headquarters in Rocky Mount?

choices.A: Driver license issuance
choices.B: Vehicle registration
choices.C: Title transfers
choices.D: None of the above

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that no driver license/ID or title/registration services are provided at the DMV Headquarters location.

en.question: If you need to register a newly purchased vehicle, should you visit the DMV Headquarters at 1515 N. Church Street?

choices.A: Yes, it is the main processing center
choices.B: Yes, but only on weekdays
choices.C: No, title and registration services are not provided at this location
choices.D: No, they only process driver licenses

en.explanation: The manual states that no title/registration services are provided at the DMV Headquarters location.

en.question: Can you obtain a North Carolina ID card at the DMV Headquarters in Rocky Mount?

choices.A: Yes, ID cards are issued there
choices.B: No, driver license and ID services are not provided at this location
choices.C: Yes, but only for renewals
choices.D: Yes, but only for first-time applicants

en.explanation: The manual clearly notes that no driver license/ID services are provided at the DMV Headquarters location.

en.question: How does the North Carolina DMV encourage drivers to stay connected and engaged online?

choices.A: By subscribing to a monthly magazine
choices.B: By staying engaged on social media
choices.C: By calling a weekly hotline
choices.D: By attending town hall meetings

en.explanation: The manual includes a prompt to "STAY ENGAGED ON SOCIAL MEDIA."

en.question: What is the official web address provided for the North Carolina DMV?

choices.A: NCDMV.com
choices.B: MyNCDMV.gov
choices.C: NCDOT.gov
choices.D: DriveNC.org

en.explanation: The official website listed in the manual is MyNCDMV.gov.

en.question: Which statement is true regarding the North Carolina Driver Handbook?

choices.A: It is only available in print format
choices.B: It can be found online at MyNCDMV.gov
choices.C: It is mailed to all registered drivers annually
choices.D: It cannot be accessed by the general public

en.explanation: The manual states, "The North Carolina Driver Handbook is available online at MyNCDMV.gov by searching Driver Handbook."

en.question: If a driver needs to renew their driver license in person, why is the Rocky Mount DMV Headquarters an incorrect destination?

choices.A: It is permanently closed to the public
choices.B: It only handles commercial driver licenses
choices.C: No driver license or ID services are provided at this location
choices.D: It requires a six-month advance appointment

en.explanation: The text explicitly states, "(No driver license/ID or title/registration services provided at this location)" regarding the DMV Headquarters.

en.question: What is the revision date of the North Carolina Driver Handbook provided in this text?

choices.A: January 2024
choices.B: May 2025
choices.C: December 2023
choices.D: July 2025

en.explanation: The text states that the handbook was "Revised May 2025."

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
