en.explanation: A motorist should look at least 12 seconds ahead. While driving at 25 mph in a city, this means about a block ahead.

en.question: When studded snow tires may be used in New Jersey:

choices.A: October 1 to March 31
choices.B: November 15 to April 1
choices.C: December 1 to March 15
choices.D: All year round

en.explanation: In NJ, motorists may use studded snow tires between November 15 and April 1.

en.question: How far back should a warning device be placed during an emergency highway stop?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet (about 120 paces)
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Put a warning device at least 300 feet back (about 120 paces).

en.question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers age 21 and older in New Jersey?
en.explanation: In NJ, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-50)

en.question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers under age 21?
en.explanation: For individuals under 21, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.01% or higher. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-50.14)

en.question: What is the only thing that can make a person sober?

choices.A: Coffee
choices.B: A cold shower
choices.C: Fresh air
choices.D: Time

en.explanation: The only thing that can make a person sober is time. Alcohol is removed slowly by the body.

en.question: How much alcohol is in each of these: 12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, 1.5 oz 86-proof liquor?

choices.A: Different amounts in each
choices.B: About the same - approximately 1/2 ounce of alcohol
choices.C: Beer has the most
choices.D: Wine has the least

en.explanation: Every drink contains about a 1/2 ounce of alcohol. It's not what you drink but how many drinks you have.

en.question: At a BAC slightly above 0.05%, the risk of causing a crash:

choices.A: Stays the same
choices.B: Doubles
choices.C: Triples
choices.D: Quadruples

en.explanation: At a BAC slightly above 0.05%, the risk doubles. At 0.10% it's 6 times as great. At 0.15% it's 25 times as great.

en.question: What is New Jersey's implied consent law?

choices.A: Consent to a vehicle search
choices.B: By using NJ roadways, motorists agree to submit to a breath test after arrest for DUI
choices.C: Consent to a field sobriety test
choices.D: Consent to a blood draw at any time

en.explanation: NJ's implied consent law means motorists have agreed to submit to a breath test given by law enforcement after an arrest for DUI. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-50.4a)

en.question: What is the penalty for refusing a breath test in New Jersey?

choices.A: A warning
choices.B: Loss of driving privileges, surcharge of $1,000/year for 3 years, and ignition interlock
choices.C: A $100 fine
choices.D: 30-day suspension only

en.explanation: Refusal results in loss of driving privileges, a violation surcharge of $1,000/year for three years, and an ignition interlock device.

en.question: After alcohol, what is the drug most often found with drivers involved in crashes?

choices.A: Cocaine
choices.B: Prescription painkillers
choices.C: Marijuana
choices.D: Methamphetamine

en.explanation: After alcohol, marijuana is the drug most often found with drivers involved in crashes.

en.question: Four factors that determine BAC are:

choices.A: Type of alcohol, gender, time of day, mood
choices.B: Quantity of alcohol consumed, body weight, how quickly drinks are consumed, food eaten
choices.C: Type of alcohol, height, exercise level, sleep
choices.D: Gender, medications, temperature, altitude

en.explanation: BAC is determined by: quantity consumed, body weight, how quickly drinks are consumed, and food eaten.

en.question: What percentage of alcohol is eliminated through breath, urine, and sweat?
en.explanation: 90% of alcohol is oxidized by the liver. The other 10% is eliminated in breath, urine, and sweat.

en.question: What is the fine for a first DUI offense with BAC of 0.08% to less than 0.10%?
en.explanation: First DUI offense with BAC 0.08% to <0.10%: $250-$400 fine, plus various surcharges and fees.

en.question: What is the annual surcharge for a DUI conviction?

choices.A: $250 per year for 2 years
choices.B: $500 per year for 3 years
choices.C: $1,000 per year for 3 years
choices.D: $1,500 per year for 5 years

en.explanation: $1,000 annual surcharge for three years for first and second DUI offenses. (N.J.S.A. 17:29A-35)

en.question: What is the penalty for driving without insurance (first offense)?

choices.A: $100 fine
choices.B: $300-$1,000 fine, 1-year license suspension, community service
choices.C: Warning only
choices.D: $50 fine and 2 points

en.explanation: First offense: $300-$1,000 fine, 1-year license suspension, $250/year surcharge for 3 years, and community service.

en.question: How many points are assessed for speeding 1-14 mph over the limit?

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: 3 points
choices.D: 4 points

en.explanation: Exceeding maximum speed 1-14 mph over the limit: 2 points.

en.question: How many points are assessed for reckless driving?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Reckless driving: 5 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-96)

en.question: How many points are assessed for tailgating?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Tailgating: 5 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-89)

en.question: How many points are assessed for improper passing of a school bus?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Improper passing of a school bus: 5 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-128.1)

en.question: How many points are assessed for leaving the scene of a crash with personal injury?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 5 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: Leaving the scene of a crash with personal injury: 8 points. Without injury: 2 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-129)

en.question: How many points are subtracted each year a motorist goes without a violation?

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: Up to 3 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Up to three points will be subtracted every year that a motorist goes without a violation or suspension. (N.J.S.A. 39:5-30.9)

en.question: At how many accumulated points does a motorist face a surcharge?

choices.A: 4 or more
choices.B: 6 or more
choices.C: 8 or more
choices.D: 12 or more

en.explanation: Motorists who accumulate six or more points within three years are subject to a surcharge of $150 for six points and $25 for each additional point.

en.question: How many points are assessed for racing on a highway?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Racing on highway: 5 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-52)

en.question: A habitual offender is a motorist whose license has been suspended how many times in how many years?

choices.A: Two times in two years
choices.B: Three times in three years
choices.C: Four times in five years
choices.D: Five times in ten years

en.explanation: A habitual offender is a motorist whose driver license has been suspended three times in three years.

en.question: What is the penalty for a hit-and-run involving bodily injury (first offense)?

choices.A: $500 fine and 30 days jail
choices.B: $2,500-$5,000 fine, up to 180 days jail, and 1-year license loss
choices.C: $1,000 fine and 6-month suspension
choices.D: $5,000 fine and permanent license loss

en.explanation: Hit-and-run with bodily injury: $2,500-$5,000 fine, up to 180 days jail, and 1-year license loss for first offense. Subsequent offense: permanent license loss.

en.question: How many points are removed by completing a Defensive Driving Course?

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: 3 points
choices.D: 4 points

en.explanation: Two points will be removed from accumulated points upon completion of a defensive driving course. (N.J.S.A. 39:5-30.9)

en.question: How many points are removed by completing the Driver Improvement Program?

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: 3 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: A motorist who completes a Driver Improvement Program will have three points removed.

en.question: How often can the MVC recognize a defensive driving course for point reduction?

choices.A: Once every 2 years
choices.B: Once every 3 years
choices.C: Once every 5 years
choices.D: Only once

en.explanation: The MVC will only recognize a defensive driving course once every five years for point reduction. (N.J.S.A. 39:5-30.9)

en.question: What is the fine for the first offense of driving while suspended?
en.explanation: First offense of driving while suspended: $500 fine and up to six months additional suspension.

en.question: A crash report must be sent to the MVC within how many days if no police report is filed?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: A written report must be sent to the MVC within 10 days if no police report is filed.

en.question: Crashes must be reported to police when damage exceeds:

choices.C: Any amount if there is personal injury
choices.D: Both B and C

en.explanation: NJ law requires motorists to notify police of crashes involving injury, death, or vehicle/property damage over $500.

en.question: Points from out-of-state violations added to NJ record:

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: Same as the violation's NJ equivalent
choices.D: None

en.explanation: Two points will be added to a driving record for traffic violations committed in other states.

en.question: The Safe Passing Law requires drivers to allow at least how much space when passing a cyclist on a single-lane road?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 6 feet

en.explanation: On a single-lane road, drivers must allow at least a 4-foot safety zone when passing vulnerable road users. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-92.4)

en.question: If 4 feet of passing space is not possible, what must a driver do?

choices.A: Honk and pass quickly
choices.B: Slow to 25 mph and be prepared to stop until safe to pass
choices.C: Stop completely until the cyclist moves
choices.D: Drive on the shoulder

en.explanation: If 4 feet is not possible, drivers must slow to 25 mph and be prepared to stop until they can pass safely.

en.question: Which vehicles must always yield the right-of-way to when they re-enter traffic?

choices.A: Police cars only
choices.B: Buses and postal vehicles
choices.C: Taxis and ride-share vehicles
choices.D: Trucks only

en.explanation: Motorists must yield to buses and postal vehicles when they re-enter the flow of traffic.

en.question: What is the most common cause of motorcycle crashes?

choices.A: Excessive speed by motorcyclists
choices.B: Poor road conditions
choices.C: A motorist's failure to detect and recognize motorcycles in traffic
choices.D: Mechanical failure

en.explanation: A motorist's failure to detect and recognize motorcycles in traffic is the most common cause of motorcycle crashes.

en.question: Trucks in bad weather can take how much longer to stop?

choices.A: 10 percent longer
choices.B: 25 percent longer
choices.C: 50 percent longer
choices.D: 75 percent longer

en.explanation: During bad weather, a truck, tractor-trailer, or bus can take as much as 25 percent longer to stop.

en.question: How far is the rear no-zone (blind spot) behind a large truck?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 300 feet

en.explanation: The rear no-zone behind a truck can extend up to 200 feet.

en.question: A motorist must stop when approaching a person using a white or metallic cane because:

choices.A: It is courtesy
choices.B: The person is visually challenged and the law requires it
choices.C: The person is elderly
choices.D: It is recommended but not required

en.explanation: The law requires all motorists to stop for blind persons using a white or metallic cane, or accompanied by a guide dog. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-37.1)

en.question: The pedestrian fatality rate jumps from 5% to 85% when a vehicle goes from what speed to what speed?

choices.A: 15 mph to 35 mph
choices.B: 20 mph to 40 mph
choices.C: 25 mph to 45 mph
choices.D: 30 mph to 50 mph

en.explanation: Vehicle-pedestrian crashes have a 5% fatality rate at 20 mph, but the rate jumps to 85% at 40 mph.

en.question: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, stop approximately how far before the crosswalk?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: Stop approximately 30 feet before a crosswalk on a multi-lane road to avoid blocking visibility for motorists in the second lane.

en.question: When approaching a horseback rider, a motorist must reduce speed to:

choices.A: 10 mph or less
choices.B: 15 mph or less
choices.C: 25 mph or less
choices.D: 35 mph or less

en.explanation: When approaching or passing a horseback rider or horse-drawn vehicle, motorists must reduce speed to 25 mph or less. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-72)

en.question: A freight train traveling at 55 mph can take how long to stop?

choices.A: 500 feet
choices.B: Half a mile
choices.C: A mile or more
choices.D: Two miles

en.explanation: A freight train traveling at 55 mph can take a mile or more to stop.

en.question: How far from a railroad crossing should you not pass other vehicles?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 300 feet

en.explanation: Do not pass other vehicles within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.

en.question: Bicyclists, skateboarders, and inline skaters have what status under NJ law?

choices.A: They have limited rights on roadways
choices.B: The same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles
choices.C: They must always yield to motor vehicles
choices.D: They may only use bike lanes

en.explanation: Under NJ law, bicyclists, skateboarders, and inline skaters have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

en.question: What is the speed limit for mopeds in New Jersey?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: Moped drivers may not exceed 25 mph.

en.question: What is an unmarked crosswalk?

choices.A: A crosswalk with faded paint
choices.B: A crosswalk at every intersection, even if not marked with painted lines
choices.C: A jaywalking area
choices.D: A crosswalk on private property

en.explanation: There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if it is not marked. This is known as an unmarked crosswalk.

en.question: Motor vehicle liability insurance is:

choices.A: Optional in New Jersey
choices.B: Mandatory in New Jersey
choices.C: Only required for new vehicles
choices.D: Only required for commercial vehicles

en.explanation: Motor vehicle liability insurance is mandatory in New Jersey. Every registered vehicle must have it. (N.J.S.A. 39:6B-1)

en.question: How long after moving to NJ must a vehicle be titled and registered?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: If a motorist moves into NJ, the vehicle must be titled and registered within 60 days or sooner if out-of-state registration expires first.

en.question: How often must passenger vehicles (5+ model years old) pass state inspection?

choices.A: Every year
choices.B: Every two years
choices.C: Every three years
choices.D: Every five years

en.explanation: Passenger vehicles more than five model years old must pass State inspections every two years.

en.question: New passenger vehicles less than five model years old receive a dealer sticker expiring:

choices.A: One year after registration
choices.B: Two years after registration
choices.C: Five years after initial registration
choices.D: Three years after registration

en.explanation: New passenger vehicles less than five model years old receive a sticker expiring five years after initial registration.

en.question: How soon must a vehicle be inspected after registering it when moving to NJ (if 5+ model years old)?

choices.A: 7 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: A vehicle five model years or older must be inspected within 14 days after registering it in NJ.

en.question: License plates must be visible from 50 feet at night. How high must they be mounted?

choices.A: At least 6 inches but less than 36 inches
choices.B: At least 12 inches but less than 48 inches above the ground
choices.C: At least 18 inches but less than 60 inches
choices.D: Any height

en.explanation: Plates must be at least 12 inches but less than 48 inches above the ground. (N.J.S.A. 39:3-33)

en.question: If a motorist terminates vehicle insurance, what must be done with the plates?

choices.A: Keep them for the next vehicle
choices.B: Return them to the MVC
choices.C: Destroy them
choices.D: Nothing

en.explanation: If a motorist terminates vehicle insurance, the plates must be returned to the MVC.

en.question: What is the fine for using license plate covers that obscure lettering?

choices.A: Up to $50
choices.B: Up to $100
choices.C: Up to $200
choices.D: Up to $500

en.explanation: Using license plate covers or holders that obscure or conceal lettering is a violation with a fine of up to $100.

en.question: What does a yellow traffic light mean?

choices.A: Speed up to get through
choices.B: Stop before entering the intersection unless too close to stop safely
choices.C: Proceed with caution
choices.D: Yield to oncoming traffic

en.explanation: When a yellow light follows green, a motorist must stop before entering the intersection unless too close to stop safely.

en.question: In New Jersey, what does a flashing red traffic light mean?

choices.A: Yield and proceed
choices.B: Stop, then proceed when safe
choices.C: Slow down
choices.D: Emergency vehicles approaching

en.explanation: A flashing red light requires a complete stop before proceeding when safe.

en.question: What does a 'stale green light' mean?

choices.A: A broken traffic signal
choices.B: A light that has been green for some time and may change soon
choices.C: A green arrow
choices.D: A green light at night

en.explanation: A stale green light is one that has been green for some time. Be prepared for it to change to yellow and then red.

en.question: In New Jersey, what does a broken center line on the road indicate?

choices.A: No passing
choices.B: Passing is allowed on the side with the broken line
choices.C: The road is under construction
choices.D: One-way traffic

en.explanation: One center line broken: Passing is allowed only on the side with the broken line.

en.question: What color is a warning sign in New Jersey?

choices.A: Red
choices.B: Green
choices.C: Yellow (diamond-shaped)
choices.D: Blue

en.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped.

en.question: What color is a regulatory sign (like stop or speed limit)?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: White with black lettering (or red for stop/yield)
choices.C: Green
choices.D: Blue

en.explanation: Regulatory signs are typically white with black lettering. Stop signs are red. Yield signs are red and white.

en.question: What shape is a stop sign?

choices.A: Circle
choices.B: Square
choices.C: Diamond
choices.D: Octagon (8 sides)

en.explanation: A stop sign is an octagon (8-sided) and is the only sign of this shape.

en.question: What color are guide/information signs on highways?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: White
choices.C: Green
choices.D: Orange

en.explanation: Green signs are guide/information signs found on highways showing directions and distances.

en.question: What color are construction zone signs?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: Red
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: Green

en.explanation: Construction zone warning signs are orange.

en.question: A single solid white line across the road at an intersection means:

choices.A: Merge
choices.B: Stop behind the line for a traffic signal or sign
choices.C: Speed up
choices.D: Construction zone ahead

en.explanation: A single solid white line across a road at an intersection means a motorist must stop behind the line for a traffic signal or sign.

en.question: What do blue highway signs indicate?

choices.A: Warnings
choices.B: Regulations
choices.C: Services (gas, food, hospital)
choices.D: Construction

en.explanation: Blue signs indicate services available near the highway, such as gas stations, food, and hospitals.

en.question: Littering from a moving vehicle can result in:

choices.A: A warning
choices.B: Fines up to $1,000 and possible loss of license
choices.C: A $50 fine
choices.D: Community service only

en.explanation: Fines up to $1,000 for throwing dangerous objects. If thrown from a moving vehicle, the motorist may lose his/her license. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-63)

en.question: What is carbon monoxide (CO) and why is it dangerous to drivers?

choices.A: A visible gas from exhaust
choices.B: An odorless, colorless gas present in vehicle exhaust
choices.C: A harmless byproduct of engines
choices.D: A gas that smells like rotten eggs

en.explanation: Carbon monoxide is an odorless, colorless gas present in a vehicle's exhaust that can be fatal.

en.question: In a crash, you should choose to hit:

choices.A: Something coming head-on
choices.B: Something not moving over something coming toward you; something that will give way over something hard
choices.C: The largest object available
choices.D: Nothing; always swerve off the road

en.explanation: Choose something moving in the same direction, then something not moving, over something coming head-on. Choose objects that give way (bushes) over hard objects.

en.question: In a traffic circle with no signs, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle entering the circle
choices.B: The vehicle approaching from the right
choices.C: The vehicle already in the circle
choices.D: The largest vehicle

en.explanation: The basic rule for uncontrolled intersections/circles: the vehicle to the left yields to the vehicle approaching from the right.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a highway?

choices.A: Back up on the exit ramp
choices.B: Stop and reverse on the highway
choices.C: Go to the next exit
choices.D: Make a U-turn

en.explanation: If a motorist misses an exit, go to the next exit. Never back up on an exit ramp or highway.

en.question: What is the minimum age to legally purchase or consume alcohol in New Jersey?
en.explanation: In NJ, a person must be age 21 or older to purchase, possess, or consume alcohol.

en.question: Kulesh's, Kuberts' and Bolis' Law establishes that illegal cell phone use while driving constitutes:

choices.A: A minor traffic offense
choices.B: Recklessness under vehicular homicide and assault by auto statutes
choices.C: A misdemeanor
choices.D: A parking violation

en.explanation: This law establishes illegal cell phone use while driving as recklessness under the vehicular homicide and assault by auto statutes.

en.question: What does 'no-zone' mean regarding trucks?

choices.A: No-parking zones near trucks
choices.B: Blind spots where the truck driver cannot see other vehicles
choices.C: Restricted speed zones
choices.D: No-pass zones on highways

en.explanation: No-zones are blind spots around trucks where the truck driver cannot see other vehicles.

en.question: The fine for violating the Safe Passing Law and causing bodily injury is:

choices.C: $500 and 2 motor vehicle penalty points

en.explanation: If bodily injury results: $500 fine and 2 points. If no injury: $100 fine and no points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-92.4)

en.question: What should a motorist do about an ABS braking system?

choices.A: Pump the brakes in an emergency
choices.B: Apply steady pressure; never pump ABS brakes or jerk the steering wheel
choices.C: Use them only in rain
choices.D: Tap them lightly

en.explanation: With ABS, apply steady pressure to the brake pedal. Never pump ABS brakes or violently jerk the steering wheel when braking.

en.question: The fine for failing to comply with the child passenger safety law is:

choices.A: Not less than $25 nor more than $50
choices.B: Not less than $50 nor more than $75, plus fees and court costs
choices.C: Not less than $100 nor more than $200

en.explanation: Failure to comply with child passenger safety law: fine of not less than $50 nor more than $75, plus fees and court costs.

en.question: When bright beams are used by an oncoming car, a motorist should:

choices.A: Flash high beams back at them
choices.B: Look to the right of the road until the vehicle passes
choices.C: Close one eye
choices.D: Speed up to pass quickly

en.explanation: Look to the right of the road until the vehicle passes. Never flash high beams at an approaching motorist.

en.question: It takes how long to recover from the glare of approaching high beams?

choices.A: 1 to 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 to 5 seconds
choices.C: 7 to 10 seconds
choices.D: 15 seconds

en.explanation: It can take three to five seconds to recover from the glare of approaching high-beam headlights.

en.question: What is the surcharge for DUI/Refusal to take a breath test?

choices.A: $500 per year for 3 years
choices.B: $750 per year for 3 years
choices.C: $1,000 per year for 3 years
choices.D: $1,500 per year for 5 years

en.explanation: The violation surcharge for DUI/Refusal is $1,000 per year for three years.

en.question: An ignition interlock device prevents a vehicle from starting if the driver's BAC exceeds:
en.explanation: An ignition interlock device prevents the vehicle from starting if the motorist's BAC exceeds 0.05%.

en.question: A school bus driver may use a cell phone only when:

choices.A: Hands-free at any time
choices.B: In an emergency or when the bus is parked safely off a highway
choices.C: When students are not on the bus
choices.D: Never

en.explanation: A school bus driver may not use a cell phone except in an emergency or when the bus is parked in a safe area off a highway. (N.J.S.A. 39:3B-25)

en.question: What penalty do pedestrians under 17 face for violating pedestrian laws?

choices.A: $10 fine
choices.B: $22 fine
choices.C: $54 fine
choices.D: Warning only

en.explanation: Pedestrians under 17 who violate pedestrian laws face a $22 fine. Adults face a $54 fine.

en.question: The idling violation fine ranges from:
en.explanation: Vehicle and property owners face fines of $250 to $1,000 for each idling violation. (N.J.S.A. 39:3-70.2)

en.question: Carrying open or unsealed alcoholic beverage containers in a vehicle results in a fine of:

choices.A: $100 first offense
choices.B: $200 first offense
choices.C: $300 first offense
choices.D: $500 first offense

en.explanation: $200 for a first offense and $250 or 10 days of community service for subsequent offenses. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-51a)

en.question: What is the minimum age for a moped license?
en.explanation: The minimum age for a moped license is 15 years old.

en.question: On wet pavement at 30 mph, the minimum safe following distance is:

choices.A: 3 car lengths
choices.B: 4 car lengths
choices.C: 6 car lengths
choices.D: 9 car lengths

en.explanation: On wet pavement at 30 mph, the minimum safe following distance is 6 car lengths.

en.question: On ice at 20 mph, the minimum safe following distance is:

choices.A: 4 car lengths
choices.B: 6 car lengths
choices.C: 10 car lengths
choices.D: 12 car lengths

en.explanation: On ice at 20 mph, the minimum safe following distance is 12 car lengths.

en.question: When entering a highway from an acceleration lane, a motorist should:

choices.A: Stop and wait for an opening
choices.B: Speed up to match traffic flow, yield to traffic, and enter the right lane
choices.C: Enter at any speed
choices.D: Enter the left lane for faster merging

en.explanation: Speed up to the flow of traffic when leaving the acceleration lane, yield to traffic already on the highway, and enter the right-hand lane when safe.

en.question: What is the correct braking technique with conventional (non-ABS) brakes when sliding?

choices.A: Stomp hard on the brake
choices.B: Release and reapply with less pressure until vehicle is under control
choices.C: Pump the brake rapidly
choices.D: Use the parking brake

en.explanation: If brakes lock, release the pedal and reapply with slightly less pressure. Repeat with less pressure until the vehicle is under control.

en.question: What is the DUI penalty for a third offense occurring within 10 years of the second (for offenses on/after 12/1/19)?

choices.A: 2-year license suspension
choices.B: 5-year license suspension
choices.C: 8-year license suspension
choices.D: Permanent license revocation

en.explanation: Third DUI offense on or after 12/1/19: 8-year license suspension, $1,000 fine, $1,500/year surcharge for 3 years.

en.question: What are Safe Corridors in New Jersey?

choices.A: Highways with reduced speed limits
choices.B: Highways where fines are doubled based on high crash rate statistics
choices.C: School zone areas
choices.D: Construction zones

en.explanation: Safe Corridors double fines on various state highways. They are designated based on crash rates 50% over the state rate and 1,000+ crashes in 3 years.

en.question: How many points are assessed for failure to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk?

choices.A: 1 point
choices.B: 2 points
choices.C: 3 points
choices.D: 4 points

en.explanation: Failure to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk: 2 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-35)

en.question: How many points are assessed for an improper U-turn?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Improper U-turn: 3 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-125)

en.question: How many points are assessed for failure to pass right of a vehicle proceeding in the opposite direction?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Failure to pass right of vehicle proceeding in opposite direction: 5 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-84)

en.question: How should a motorist approach a curve?

choices.A: Maintain speed through the curve
choices.B: Slow down before entering the curve and avoid drifting into another lane
choices.C: Accelerate through the curve
choices.D: Brake hard during the curve

en.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve and avoid drifting into another lane.

en.question: When a horseback rider signals by putting up their hand, a motorist must:

choices.A: Slow to 25 mph and pass
choices.B: Stop and remain stationary until the horse passes
choices.C: Honk to warn the horse
choices.D: Switch lanes and pass

en.explanation: At the signal of a horseback rider, the motorist must stop and remain stationary until the horse passes. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-72)

en.question: What is the most common cause of car fires?

choices.A: Engine overheating
choices.B: Fuel leaks
choices.C: Short circuits in the electrical system
choices.D: Cigarette smoking

en.explanation: Most car fires are caused by short circuits in the electrical system.

en.question: NJ law prohibits which type of lights from being on while a vehicle is moving forward?

choices.A: Fog lights
choices.B: Parking lights
choices.C: Backup lights
choices.D: Dashboard lights

en.explanation: It is against NJ law to have backup lights on while a vehicle is moving forward. (N.J.S.A. 39:3-52)

en.question: The Nikhil's Law Safety Pledge requires motorists to pledge to:

choices.A: Never speed
choices.B: Stop completely at stop signs, stay alert, use hands-free phones, plan ahead
choices.C: Always wear seat belts
choices.D: Never drink and drive

en.explanation: The Nikhil's Law pledge includes: Stop Completely, Stay Alert, Talk Safe (hands-free), and Plan Ahead.

en.question: What is the annual motorcycle registration fee in NJ?
en.explanation: NJ's annual motorcycle registration fee is $65.

en.question: How many points are assessed for improper passing of a frozen dessert truck?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: Improper passing of a frozen dessert truck: 4 points. (N.J.S.A. 39:4-128.4)

en.question: A motorist who accumulates 12-14 points or more will receive:

choices.A: A warning letter
choices.B: A Notice of Scheduled Suspension
choices.C: An automatic suspension
choices.D: A mandatory court appearance

en.explanation: Motorists who accumulate 12-14 or more points in a 24-month period receive a Notice of Scheduled Suspension.

en.question: Voter registration deadline before an election is:

choices.A: 7 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 21 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: Voter registration deadline is 21 days before an election.

en.question: What is the penalty for driving while suspended for a DUI-related offense?

choices.A: $200 fine
choices.B: $500 fine, 1-2 year additional suspension, possible 10-90 days imprisonment
choices.C: $100 fine and 30-day suspension
choices.D: Warning only

en.explanation: Driving while suspended for DUI/refusal: $500 fine, 1-2 year additional suspension, and possible 10-90 days imprisonment.

en.question: An underage driver (under 21) with BAC of 0.01% or more faces:

choices.A: A warning
choices.B: 30-90 day license suspension, 15-30 days community service, and IDRC participation
choices.C: $100 fine only
choices.D: Same penalties as adults

en.explanation: Underage first offense with BAC 0.01%-0.08%: 30-90 day suspension, 15-30 days community service, and IDRC/alcohol education program participation.

en.question: In New Jersey, when are you required to use your turn signal?

choices.A: Changing lanes.
choices.B: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
choices.C: Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Your turn signals should always be used when you make any movement to the left or right. You should use your signal when pulling into traffic from a curbside parking space, moving into a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

en.question: When driving on major highways:

choices.A: Stay alert.
choices.B: Keep your eyes moving.
choices.C: Be ready to react to road hazards.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: It is important to stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. To avoid "highway hypnosis," you should avoid looking at any one thing for more than a few seconds.

en.question: You are driving up a hill and are approaching a heavy truck from the rear. You should know that:

choices.A: The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.
choices.B: You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
choices.C: You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Drivers must be aware that large vehicles often travel at a speed slower than the posted speed limit, especially when driving on an incline, and should use caution when approaching a large vehicle from the rear. When on a hill with limited visibility, it is unlawful to pass another vehicle.

en.question: When you see other drivers around you acting or reacting in anger:

choices.A: Don’t make eye contact.
choices.B: Don't react with hand gestures.
choices.C: Distance yourself from the situation.
choices.D: All of these.

en.explanation: When other drivers are behaving angrily, you should take action to physically and mentally distance yourself from the situation. Avoid making eye contact with them, or making body movements or gestures that could provoke them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you safely can to put yourself out of danger.

en.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

choices.A: A deaf person.
choices.B: A person involved with a traffic study.
choices.C: A blind person.
choices.D: None of the above.

en.explanation: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian when the pedestrian is a blind person who is using a white cane or guide dog.

en.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

choices.A: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
choices.B: Stop and back up.
choices.C: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
choices.D: Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

en.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up, but go on to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. It is illegal to back up on a shoulder or a freeway.

en.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

choices.A: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
choices.B: Signal only if there is visible traffic.
choices.C: Signal only when driving at night.
choices.D: Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

en.explanation: Always signal your intentions when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not allow yourself to become lazy and form the bad habit of not following this law.

en.question: Taking drugs along with alcohol:

choices.A: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
choices.B: Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.
choices.C: Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
choices.D: Has no effect on your general driving ability.

en.explanation: Drugs (including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications) can affect your brain function and impair your ability to drive safely. Combining alcohol with other drugs will increase the risk of a crash.

en.question: When driving on wet pavement, it's important to remember:

choices.A: That pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
choices.B: That wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
choices.C: To give yourself additional space when coming to a stop.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Wet roadway surfaces can be dangerously slick, especially immediately following a rainfall. When you are driving on wet roads, your vehicle is traveling on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush on the road to reduce the risk of your wheels losing traction on the slick surface.

en.question: A diamond-shaped yellow sign with a curved arrow pointing right indicates:

choices.A: One-way road.
choices.B: No right turn.
choices.C: Exit.
choices.D: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.

en.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs with curve arrows warn drivers of upcoming sharp turns in the road.

en.question: A steady green light at an intersection means that you:

choices.A: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
choices.B: Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
choices.C: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
choices.D: May not turn right.

en.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign prohibits the turn. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians within the intersection.

en.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

choices.A: Is loose.
choices.B: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
choices.C: Is hidden beneath the seat.
choices.D: Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

en.explanation: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and the lower part of your abdomen. Shoulder belts should sit comfortably so that you can insert your fist between the belt and your chest.

en.question: If you stop along the road at night:

choices.A: Turn off all your lights.
choices.B: Use your parking lights only.
choices.C: Use your headlights only.
choices.D: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams turned on.

en.explanation: If you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights turned on. Be sure that other road users will be able to clearly see your vehicle.

en.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

choices.A: You are able to clearly see the road ahead.
choices.B: You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
choices.C: Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: You cannot pass safely when driving on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal and unsafe to do so.

en.question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean:

choices.A: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
choices.B: Passing is not allowed.
choices.C: Passing is allowed if you are at the top a hill.
choices.D: Passing is allowed during daylight only.

en.explanation: Yellow lines tell you that the traffic on the other side of the lines is moving in the opposite direction. You should never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

en.question: A driver can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

choices.A: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
choices.B: Even if it means driving off the pavement.
choices.C: On a narrow bridge.
choices.D: At any time.

en.explanation: If there is an available passing lane, you may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning left or waiting to turn left. It is also legal to pass on the right when driving on a multilane road with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction. You may never drive off the pavement or main-traveled portion of the road to pass another vehicle.

en.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

choices.A: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
choices.B: Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.
choices.C: Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
choices.D: Follow rules that would be in place if no children were present.

en.explanation: Be prepared to reduce your speed and use caution when directed to do so by a sign, crossing guard, or law enforcement officer. Always drive with extra caution in a school zone.

en.question: Signaling your intentions before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from a curb:

choices.A: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
choices.B: Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
choices.C: Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
choices.D: Is not necessary if the maneuver is done slowly.

en.explanation: When changing lanes or turning, signal your intentions well in advance. The law requires that you signal for at least 100 feet before you move your vehicle to the right or left. Before pulling away from a curb, always signal to inform passing drivers of your intentions.

en.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in the area where you are driving, you should:

choices.A: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
choices.B: Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
choices.C: Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
choices.D: Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is clear for them to pass you.

en.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in the area where you are driving, you must make every effort to give them a clear path of travel. If it is safe to do so, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to give the emergency vehicle an open pathway.

en.question: If you want to get off the freeway but you have missed your exit, you should:

choices.A: Go to the next exit.
choices.B: Make a U-turn through the median.
choices.C: Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
choices.D: Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

en.explanation: If you miss your exit, you should take the next exit. Do not stop or back up on the highway, swerve across multiple lanes to try to make the exit at the last second, or cross over the median to turn around. All of these maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.
choices.C: When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: When passing, you must always signal at least 100 feet in advance of your lane change. Always check behind you in your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.

en.question: At a four-way stop intersection in New Jersey, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
choices.B: The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.
choices.C: One driver should continue driving without stopping.
choices.D: One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

en.explanation: At four-way stops, traffic from all four directions must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection should move forward first. If two vehicles reach the intersection at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

en.question: You may drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway:

choices.A: As long as you aren't driving.
choices.B: If you are riding in the back seat.
choices.C: If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.
choices.D: Under no circumstances.

en.explanation: It is against the law to consume or possess any alcoholic beverage while on a public road or sidewalk. Additionally, storing an open alcoholic beverage container in an area of a motor vehicle normally occupied by the driver or passenger is prohibited on any public road.

en.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

choices.A: Maintain your normal driving speed.
choices.B: Stop and look for nearby police cars.
choices.C: Yield to pedestrians.
choices.D: Increase your normal driving speed.

en.explanation: Unless a posted sign prohibits it, you may turn right or left at a steady green light. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians within the intersection.

en.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

choices.A: Excessive stops.
choices.B: Sudden stops.
choices.C: Sudden turns.
choices.D: Excessive speed.

en.explanation: Your tires become less effective at clearing water from the road as you increase your speed. If you drive too fast, they may lose their grip entirely, leaving the vehicle sliding on a film of water. This is known as "hydroplaning."

en.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

choices.A: Must always be obeyed.
choices.B: Are merely suggestions.
choices.C: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
choices.D: Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

en.explanation: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals, and signs. These devices inform drivers of conditions on the roadway and help guide drivers safely to their destinations. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

en.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

choices.A: Railroad crossings.
choices.B: School zones.
choices.C: No passing zones.
choices.D: Hospitals.

en.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Drivers should not try to outdrive a train.

en.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

choices.A: Use alternate routes.
choices.B: Drive as you would on dry roads.
choices.C: Increase your following distance.
choices.D: Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

en.explanation: On slippery roads, you should increase your following distance. It may take more time to stop your vehicle than it would under normal conditions.

en.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

choices.A: Whoever started moving last
choices.B: The driver
choices.C: Whoever is slower
choices.D: The pedestrian

en.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians when they are crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

en.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?

choices.A: Allergy medicine
choices.B: Marijuana
choices.C: Cold remedies
choices.D: All of these choices

en.explanation: Many kinds of drugs can impair your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. It can be a criminal offense to drive while impaired by any drug.

en.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

choices.A: You cannot see without moving your head.
choices.B: Directly behind your vehicle.
choices.C: You see in your rearview mirror.
choices.D: You see in your side mirror.

en.explanation: Blind spots are areas that a driver cannot see without moving their head. They can be located to the sides of and behind a vehicle.

en.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

choices.A: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
choices.B: Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
choices.C: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
choices.D: Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

en.explanation: You cannot enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get completely through the intersection. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

en.question: A yellow diamond-shaped sign showing a traffic light symbol indicates:

choices.A: Continue at your current speed.
choices.B: You must stop ahead.
choices.C: Speeding is not allowed.
choices.D: There is a traffic signal ahead.

en.explanation: A yellow warning sign with a traffic signal symbol alerts drivers that there is a traffic signal ahead. Be prepared to stop.

en.question: Your first response to reduced visibility should be:

choices.A: Turning on your headlights.
choices.B: Reducing your speed.
choices.C: Turning on your windshield wipers.
choices.D: Looking for road edge markings to guide you.

en.explanation: Reducing your speed should be your first response to decreased visibility and dangerous road conditions.

en.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

choices.A: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
choices.B: When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
choices.C: No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
choices.D: Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

en.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross a road or street. Crosswalks may be marked by horizontal lines, vertical lines, or a combination of the two. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

en.question: You must yield to other drivers:

choices.A: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
choices.B: When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
choices.C: When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians who are on an intersecting sidewalk.

en.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

choices.A: Under no circumstances.
choices.B: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
choices.C: Only when other vehicles yield.
choices.D: None of the above.

en.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights.

en.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

choices.A: Has the right-of-way.
choices.B: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
choices.C: May force their way into traffic.
choices.D: Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

en.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you should yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely into traffic when you are able to do so.

en.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which of the following traffic signals?

choices.A: A solid green light
choices.B: A flashing yellow light
choices.C: A green arrow pointing left
choices.D: A flashing red light

en.explanation: A green steady arrow means you may pass through the intersection in the direction that the arrow is pointing. Oncoming traffic is required to stop for turning traffic.

en.question: Which is not a factor in determining the distance that it takes to stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Steering ability
choices.B: Braking distance
choices.C: Reaction distance
choices.D: Perception time

en.explanation: The distance required to stop your vehicle depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. This changes with speed and road conditions.

en.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

choices.A: May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
choices.B: Has a triangular shape.
choices.C: Is blue with black lettering.
choices.D: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

en.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often have attached advisory speed signs that show a recommended driving speed for drivers in the curves and turns. Although a driver may feel comfortable driving at a higher speed in fair weather, they should never do so under rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.

en.question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on the:

choices.A: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Presence of a stop sign.
choices.C: Use of your turn signals.
choices.D: Cars behind you.

en.explanation: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

en.question: Under New Jersey law, in which situations are you prohibited from passing another vehicle?

choices.A: On a hill or curve.
choices.B: When school bus lights are flashing.
choices.C: When approaching an intersection.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: You should never pass if there is an oncoming vehicle in the passing lane, if your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any other no passing zone. Unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane roadway with a median or shared center turn lane, you may not pass a stopped school bus that has its flashing red lights activated.

en.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

choices.A: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
choices.B: Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
choices.C: Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
choices.D: Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

en.explanation: Be prepared to reduce your speed and use caution when directed to do so by a sign, flagger, or law enforcement officer. Failure to do so is illegal and is dangerous to those working in construction zones.

en.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

choices.A: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
choices.B: Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.
choices.C: Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass.
choices.D: Keep moving slowly, staying to the right side of the road.

en.explanation: When driving on a two-lane roadway or undivided highway, you must yield to an emergency vehicle using its lights and/or siren, regardless of the direction from which it is approaching. Immediately drive as near as possible to the right side of the road and stop, taking care not to stop within an intersection.

en.question: You are coming to an intersection and have a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

choices.A: Honk your horn.
choices.B: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
choices.C: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
choices.D: Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them so they’ll think twice before crossing against a red light.

en.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and cars that may be caught in an intersection when you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians under every circumstance.

en.question: What is the correct procedure to enter a freeway in New Jersey?

choices.A: Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.
choices.B: Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.
choices.C: Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
choices.D: Always come to a complete stop first.

en.explanation: When merging into traffic, you should signal and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving. Always yield to other traffic when entering a roadway.

en.question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:

choices.A: Traffic moves faster at night.
choices.B: There is a larger volume of traffic at night.
choices.C: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
choices.D: Accidents occur more frequently at night.

en.explanation: Because it is dark, drivers cannot see as well at night as they can during the day. From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, or at any other time when persons or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, drivers must use their headlights.

en.question: Failing to adhere to restrictions placed on a Graduated Driver License:

choices.A: Is not a big deal.
choices.B: Will result only in points against the driver's license.
choices.C: Will result in no negative consequences.
choices.D: May result in a fine and license suspension.

en.explanation: A first-time driver with a Graduated Driver License (GDL) must adhere to strict driving restrictions. Failing to follow these restrictions may result in a fine of $100 and suspension of the GDL.

en.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: Either one
choices.B: The vehicle on the left
choices.C: The vehicle on the right
choices.D: Neither

en.explanation: At intersections that are controlled by signs or signals and at intersections that are uncontrolled, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right when two vehicles arrive to the intersection at the same time.

en.question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

choices.A: Is used only on one-way streets.
choices.B: Has the same meaning as a circular green traffic light, but traffic must turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
choices.C: Means that you may proceed, but only if the green arrow is accompanied by a circular green light.
choices.D: Points the way to an airport.

en.explanation: A green arrow has the same meaning as a circular green traffic light, but traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

en.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

choices.A: White
choices.B: Red
choices.C: Black
choices.D: Yellow

en.explanation: Yellow lines are used to divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

en.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

choices.A: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
choices.B: Use tires with proper air pressure.
choices.C: Replace tires with bad tread.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle glides on top of a thin layer of water between its tires and the road. Tires with low air pressure or bad tread can increase the risk of hydroplaning. Speeding also increases the risk.

en.question: To reduce the effects of headlight glare at night, you should look:

choices.A: Straight ahead.
choices.B: Over your shoulder.
choices.C: At the center of the road
choices.D: To the right edge of the road.

en.explanation: If oncoming drivers do not dim their headlights for you, keep your eyes on the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights because the glare may blind you for several seconds.

en.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

choices.A: Flashing red light.
choices.B: Steady yellow light.
choices.C: Yellow arrow.
choices.D: Flashing yellow light.

en.explanation: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign. At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only after the intersection is clear.

en.question: The effect that alcohol has on your reflexes and judgment:

choices.A: Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.
choices.B: Is less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.
choices.C: Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.
choices.D: Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

en.explanation: Consuming any type of alcohol can have negative effects on your reflexes and judgment. It does not matter which type of alcohol is consumed, only how much alcohol has entered a person's bloodstream.

en.question: To register a vehicle in New Jersey, you must be age ____ or older.
en.explanation: To register a motor vehicle in New Jersey, you must be at least 17 years old. You must have proof of identity and proof of vehicle ownership.

en.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. You should:

choices.A: Slam on your brakes.
choices.B: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
choices.C: Keep driving normally.
choices.D: Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

en.explanation: If you experience a tire blowout, do not immediately apply the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and steer to remain in your traffic lane. Reduce your speed gradually by releasing the accelerator and staying off the brakes. Once you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road into a safe area.

en.question: Increase your following distance when:

choices.A: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
choices.B: Exiting an expressway.
choices.C: Following a motorcycle.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: You should increase your following distance when you are behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision, when driving in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and if someone is tailgating you.

en.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:

choices.A: Turn left.
choices.B: Turn right.
choices.C: Stop.
choices.D: Start up.

en.explanation: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, they are indicating that they intend to stop. Adjust your driving accordingly if following a driver who is using this hand signal.

en.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

choices.A: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
choices.B: When turning left into a driveway.
choices.C: When the car in front of you is disabled.
choices.D: When passing to the right on a one-way street.

en.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

en.question: To ensure that your physical condition does not cause you to drive in an unsafe manner, you should:

choices.A: Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.
choices.B: Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.
choices.C: Drive within your physical limitations.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Your physical condition has an important bearing on your ability to drive safely. Drivers should be aware of their physical limitations and only drive if it is safe to do so.

en.question: Signs that are colored orange are:

choices.A: Work zone signs.
choices.B: Regulatory signs.
choices.C: School zone signs.
choices.D: Guide signs.

en.explanation: Highway work zones are established according to the type of work underway along the roadway. Signs in work areas are typically diamond-shaped, orange, have black letters or symbols, and serve as a warning that people are working on or near the highway.

en.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

choices.A: May be safely held by a strong adult.
choices.B: Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
choices.C: Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
choices.D: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

en.explanation: Special child seats are available for children who are too small to wear regular safety belts. No person is strong enough to safely hold onto a child of any size during an accident or sudden stop. Never allow a child to ride in a vehicle unless they are properly fastened into a seat.

en.question: Allowing a space cushion between your vehicle and its surroundings is important because it:

choices.A: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
choices.B: Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
choices.C: Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
choices.D: Keeps other drivers alert.

en.explanation: The only way to be sure you will have enough time to react to mistakes made by other drivers is to leave plenty of space between you and the vehicles around you.

en.question: You must pull over to the edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass:

choices.A: Regardless of your direction.
choices.B: Only if it is following you.
choices.C: Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
choices.D: None of the above.

en.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, regardless of whether it is approaching you from behind or from the opposite direction.

en.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, drivers should:

choices.A: Have their exhaust system checked regularly to be sure it does not leak.
choices.B: Keep their engine turned off when the car is in an enclosed garage.
choices.C: Close vents when following closely behind another car.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Carbon monoxide fumes are odorless and deadly. Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning are sudden weariness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. The only cure is an adequate supply of fresh air.

en.question: When changing lanes you should not:

choices.A: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
choices.B: Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.
choices.C: Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
choices.D: Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.

en.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic approaching you from behind. Use your turn signal to let other drivers know you plan to change lanes. Check for other drivers who also may be moving into the same lane.

en.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

choices.A: A rectangular red sign.
choices.B: A circular green sign.
choices.C: A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
choices.D: A triangular orange sign.

en.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Expect vehicles using this emblem to be driving at speeds of 25 mph or slower.

en.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

choices.A: Either side
choices.B: The center
choices.C: The right side
choices.D: The left side

en.explanation: If a vehicle approaching you is using its high beams and fails to dim them, you should glance toward the right side of the road. This will keep you from being blinded by the other vehicle’s headlights and will allow you to see well enough to stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

en.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

choices.A: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
choices.B: Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
choices.C: Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
choices.D: Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

en.explanation: When using a freeway exit ramp, do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

en.question: Snow and ice on a vehicle should be removed from:

choices.A: The vehicle's windows.
choices.B: The vehicle's hood.
choices.C: The top of the vehicle.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: State law requires motorists to remove all snow and ice from their vehicle before driving it. Fines may apply to drivers who do not follow this law.

en.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

choices.A: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
choices.B: There are pedestrians crossing.
choices.C: You are turning right.
choices.D: You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

en.explanation: If a steady yellow light appears when you are already within an intersection, you should continue through the intersection carefully.

en.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:

choices.A: Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
choices.B: Stop immediately.
choices.C: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
choices.D: Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

en.explanation: When approaching an intersection with a solid yellow traffic light, slow to a stop before entering the intersection, if it is safe to do so. If you can't stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

en.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

choices.A: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
choices.B: During daylight hours only.
choices.C: At any time.
choices.D: When making turns.

en.explanation: As a general rule, broken traffic lines may be crossed but solid lines may not. Solid yellow lines may be crossed only when the driver is making a turn.

en.question: When driving in rain, you must:

choices.A: Use low beam headlights.
choices.B: Use high beam headlights.
choices.C: Use parking lights.
choices.D: Use no lights.

en.explanation: In rainy conditions, you should use your low beam headlights.

en.question: Who is required to wear a seat belt in a moving motor vehicle?

choices.A: Just the driver
choices.B: Just adult passengers
choices.C: Just child passengers
choices.D: All occupants of the motor vehicle

en.explanation: Under state law, the driver and all passengers of a passenger vehicle must wear a seat belt. The failure of a driver, front seat passenger, or child under age 18 to wear a seat belt is a primary offense. The driver is responsible for all passengers under age 18. Under a secondary law, all unbuckled back seat occupants 18 years of age and older may be issued a summons if the vehicle has been stopped for a different reason.

en.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

choices.A: Decrease your speed.
choices.B: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
choices.C: Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
choices.D: Use your four-way flashers.

en.explanation: Driving more slowly than the flow of traffic can be hazardous. If you are on a two-lane, two-way road and driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you are required to pull off the road and let the other vehicles pass. Only drive significantly under the speed limit when conditions require it.

en.question: What is a potential danger of a leaking exhaust system?

choices.A: Cause excessive oil use.
choices.B: Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.
choices.C: Make you drowsy while driving.
choices.D: Set grass fires on country roads.

en.explanation: The exhaust system helps remove toxic gases, reduce the noise, and cool the hot gases coming from a running engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system can cause death in a very short time. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

en.question: A tractor-trailer could take up to ____ percent longer to stop under poor weather conditions than under ideal driving conditions.
en.explanation: When driving near a tractor-trailer, be aware of how its size will affect the way it is driven. Under poor weather conditions, the larger vehicle may take up to 25 percent longer to come to a complete stop than it would if being driven under ideal conditions.

en.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers and highway users must make allowances for:

choices.A: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
choices.B: The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
choices.C: The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
choices.D: The increased speed of larger vehicles.

en.explanation: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers and highway users must make allowances for the increased stopping distance required by the large vehicles. Drivers of smaller vehicles should remain in locations where they can be seen by the driver of the large vehicle and where their view of traffic is not blocked by the vehicle.

en.question: Vehicle stopping distances never depend on:

choices.A: Your own reaction time.
choices.B: The time of day.
choices.C: The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
choices.D: The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

en.explanation: The distance that a vehicle needs to stop depends on the motorist's reaction time, weather and visibility conditions, the vehicle's weight, the conditions of the vehicle's brakes, the condition and type of the vehicle's tires, roadway conditions, and speed.

en.question: A bicyclist who doesn’t obey traffic laws:

choices.A: Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.
choices.B: Can be ticketed.
choices.C: Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
choices.D: Will have their bicycle impounded.

en.explanation: All bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. Motorists and bicyclists who do not obey traffic laws can be ticketed.

en.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite direction?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: White
choices.C: Yellow and white
choices.D: Yellow, white, and black

en.explanation: Yellow lines are used in the center of the road to separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

en.question: Downward-facing triangular signs:

choices.A: Indicate school zones.
choices.B: Tell drivers to yield.
choices.C: Indicate construction zones.
choices.D: Indicate railroad crossings.

en.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs usually indicate that drivers should yield. Once the road is clear of traffic or pedestrians and it is safe to do so, drivers may proceed.

en.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

choices.A: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
choices.B: Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
choices.C: Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
choices.D: None of the above.

en.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction of your move to see if your blind spot is clear. Never rely on your mirrors alone.

en.question: When you are in a line of traffic that is crossing a railroad track that has no signals or gates:

choices.A: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
choices.B: You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
choices.C: You need to make sure there is space for your vehicle to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
choices.D: All of the above

en.explanation: If you are following another vehicle at a railroad crossing, check to make sure you have enough room to get all the way across before you drive onto the tracks. You should never try to pass another vehicle as you approach or cross a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

en.question: When you see a red octagonal (eight-sided) sign, you must:

choices.A: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
choices.B: Slow down without coming to a complete stop.
choices.C: Stop completely and wait for a green light.
choices.D: Slow down and check for traffic.

en.explanation: Any eight-sided (octagonal) sign is a stop sign. At an intersection with a stop sign, you must stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic in the intersection. Wait for the intersection to clear before proceeding.

en.question: To turn left from multilane, one-way streets and highways, you should start from:

choices.A: The middle of the intersection.
choices.B: The right lane.
choices.C: The left lane.
choices.D: Any lane.

en.explanation: To turn left from multilane streets and highways, start from the left lane.

en.question: What is true about a work zone in New Jersey?

choices.A: May be moving or stationary.
choices.B: Is marked with black and white signs.
choices.C: Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.
choices.D: All of the above.

en.explanation: Work zones are often stationary, but they may also be present in the form of moving vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones are marked by orange signs with black lettering or symbols. Slow down and pay extra attention when approaching or driving through a work zone.

en.question: When approaching a traffic signal displaying a flashing yellow arrow, drivers:

choices.A: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
choices.B: Should come to a complete stop.
choices.C: May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
choices.D: Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow indicates that left turns are allowed in the direction of the arrow. However, the oncoming traffic has a green light and you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

en.question: If two vehicles arrive to an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

choices.A: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
choices.B: The car on the left has the right-of-way.
choices.C: The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
choices.D: The car on the right shall yield to the car on the left.

en.explanation: If two vehicles arrive at the same time to an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left may then proceed when it is safe to do so.

en.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: Red
choices.C: Green
choices.D: White

en.explanation: Guide signs, sometimes known as destination signs, have a green background and provide directional and mileage information to specific destinations. They can be a helpful resource when driving in unfamiliar locations.

en.question: Is it legal cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

choices.A: Yes.
choices.B: No.
choices.C: If there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.D: If the vehicle ahead of you is driving under the speed limit.
