choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers moving into Nevada from another state must apply for a license within 30 days after becoming a resident.

en.question: Which of the following individuals living or working in Nevada is NOT required to get a Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: A part-time worker from another state
choices.B: A military member stationed in Nevada
choices.C: A college student who just established residency
choices.D: A new resident who moved from a foreign country

en.explanation: The manual states that you need a Nevada driver license if you live or work in Nevada, excluding border state employees or military members stationed in Nevada.

en.question: What is the minimum age requirement to apply for a Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: 15 years old
choices.B: 15 and a half years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: To get a Nevada license, you must complete an application form, visit a full-service DMV office, and be at least 16 years old.

en.question: For which of the following documents is a Social Security Number NOT necessary to obtain in Nevada?

choices.A: A commercial driver's license
choices.B: A Driver Authorization Card (DAC)
choices.C: A standard driver's license
choices.D: A motorcycle license

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that a Social Security Number is not necessary to obtain a Driver Authorization Card (DAC).

en.question: How long is a first-time Nevada driver's license valid for persons under the age of 65?

choices.A: 4 years
choices.B: 5 years
choices.C: 8 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: A first-time Nevada driver license issued to persons under age 65 will be valid for eight years.

en.question: What is the validity period of a driver's license for individuals aged 65 and older in Nevada?

choices.A: 2 years
choices.B: 4 years
choices.C: 6 years
choices.D: 8 years

en.explanation: According to the manual, driver licenses for individuals aged 65 and older are valid for four years.

en.question: How long are Nevada Identification Cards valid for?

choices.A: 4 years
choices.B: 5 years
choices.C: 8 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states that Identification Cards are valid for eight years.

en.question: If you present limited-term immigration documents with no departure date provided by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), when will your Nevada driver's license expire?

choices.A: In 1 year
choices.B: In 4 years
choices.C: In 8 years
choices.D: On your next birthday

en.explanation: If limited-term immigration documents are used, the expiration of your driver license will coincide with the departure date verified by DHS, or one year if no date is provided by DHS.

en.question: What responsibility does a co-signer take on when signing the application for a driver under 18 years old?

choices.A: They must ride in the passenger seat at all times.
choices.B: They share liability for any damages caused by the minor's negligence or willful misconduct while driving.
choices.C: They must pay for the minor's vehicle registration.
choices.D: They are required to take a written test alongside the minor.

en.explanation: If you are under 18 years old, a co-signer must sign your application. The co-signer shares liability for any damages caused by the minor's negligence or willful misconduct while driving.

en.question: How many driver's licenses or identification cards may a resident of Nevada hold at one time?

choices.A: One driver's license and one ID card
choices.B: Only one driver's license or identification card
choices.C: Up to two driver's licenses from different states
choices.D: One commercial license and one standard license

en.explanation: A resident of Nevada may hold only one driver's license or identification card.

en.question: What happens to your out-of-state driver's license when you apply for a Nevada license?

choices.A: It is destroyed by the DMV.
choices.B: It is sent back to your previous state.
choices.C: You are allowed to keep it as a valid secondary ID.
choices.D: It must be surrendered, voided, and then returned to you.

en.explanation: If you have a license or identification card from another jurisdiction, you must surrender it. All surrendered licenses and identification cards will be voided and returned to you.

en.question: Which test is mandatory for all new residents applying for a Nevada driver's license, even if other tests are waived?

choices.A: A written knowledge test
choices.B: A driving skills test
choices.C: A vision test
choices.D: A hearing test

en.explanation: Your vision will be tested when you apply for your Nevada driver's license. All other tests may be waived if certain criteria apply.

en.question: For a new Nevada resident, written and driving tests may be waived if they have had fewer than how many moving violations in the past 4 years?
en.explanation: All other tests may be waived if you have had fewer than 3 moving violations in the past 4 years.

en.question: On what day does a standard first-time Nevada driver's license typically expire?

choices.A: On the anniversary of the issue date
choices.B: On December 31st of the expiration year
choices.C: On your birthday
choices.D: Exactly 8 years from the date you applied

en.explanation: A first-time Nevada driver license issued to persons under age 65 will be valid for eight years and expires on your birthday.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly listed as a requirement to provide proof of when applying for a Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: Full legal name
choices.B: Nevada residency
choices.C: Age
choices.D: High school diploma or equivalent

en.explanation: To get a Nevada license, you must provide proof of your full legal name, age, Social Security Number (if issued), and Nevada residency. A high school diploma is not required.

en.question: Under what condition may the driving tests (other than the vision test) be waived when applying for a Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: You have had no DUI convictions within the past 7 years.
choices.B: You are at least 18 years old.
choices.C: You have had fewer than 5 moving violations in the past 4 years.
choices.D: You surrender a foreign passport.

en.explanation: Tests may be waived if you meet several criteria, including having no DUI convictions within the past 7 years, being age 21 or older, and having fewer than 3 moving violations in the past 4 years.

en.question: Who is NOT required to obtain a Nevada driver's license to drive in the state?

choices.A: A new resident who just moved to Nevada permanently.
choices.B: An active-duty member of the U.S. Armed Forces with a valid home state license.
choices.C: A person whose out-of-state license is currently suspended.
choices.D: A 15-year-old out-of-state tourist.

en.explanation: You do not need a Nevada license if you are an active-duty member of the U.S. Armed Forces and you have a valid license from your home state.

en.question: If your driving privilege is currently suspended or revoked in another state, what can you qualify for in Nevada?

choices.A: A restricted Nevada driver's license
choices.B: A temporary driving permit
choices.C: An identification card
choices.D: A Driver Authorization Card

en.explanation: If your driving privilege is suspended or revoked in another state, you will not be allowed a Nevada license until the issue is resolved, but you may qualify for an identification card during this period.

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable document to prove your Social Security Number?

choices.A: A handwritten paystub
choices.B: A W-2 form with your full SSN
choices.C: A hospital-issued birth certificate
choices.D: A Medicare card

en.explanation: Acceptable evidence of a Social Security Number includes a Social Security Card, a W-2 (with full SSN), IRS Form 1099, or a printed paystub with full legal name. Handwritten paystubs are not acceptable.

en.question: How is a Real ID compliant Nevada driver's license or ID card marked?

choices.A: With a silver hologram of the state seal
choices.B: With a gold Nevada outline and a star cutout
choices.C: With the phrase 'FEDERAL ID APPROVED'
choices.D: With a red border around the photograph

en.explanation: Real ID licenses or ID cards are marked with a gold Nevada outline and a star cutout, indicating the card meets federal identification standards.

en.question: What phrase is marked on a standard Nevada driver's license or ID card that does not meet federal identification standards?

choices.A: NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES
choices.B: STATE USE ONLY
choices.C: LIMITED TERM
choices.D: UNVERIFIED IDENTITY

en.explanation: Standard licenses or ID cards are marked with the phrase 'NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES' indicating the card does not meet federal identification standards.

en.question: How many documents proving Nevada residency must applicants present to meet Real ID requirements?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: To meet the new Real ID requirements, applicants must present two documents proving Nevada residency, such as utility bills or bank statements.

en.question: How long is a Nevada Driver Authorization Card (DAC) valid for?

choices.A: Two years
choices.B: Four years
choices.C: Six years
choices.D: Eight years

en.explanation: A Driver Authorization Card is valid for four years and will expire on your birthday.

en.question: How must all renewals and address changes for a Driver Authorization Card (DAC) be completed?

choices.A: Online through the DMV website
choices.B: By mailing a form to the DMV
choices.C: Over the phone
choices.D: In person

en.explanation: For a Driver Authorization Card, all renewals and address changes must be completed in person.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding a Driver Authorization Card (DAC)?

choices.A: It is valid for boarding commercial aircraft.
choices.B: It can be used to determine eligibility for state benefits.
choices.C: It is not valid for federal or state identification purposes.
choices.D: It is marked with a gold Nevada outline and a star cutout.

en.explanation: A Driver Authorization Card is not valid for federal or state identification purposes and cannot be used to determine eligibility for any benefits, licenses or services issued or provided by the State of Nevada.

en.question: What is required if you present a document in a foreign language to the Nevada DMV?

choices.A: It must be accompanied by an abstract translation.
choices.B: It must be translated to English by a DMV-approved translator.
choices.C: It must be notarized by a foreign consulate.
choices.D: It must be translated by the applicant.

en.explanation: Any document in a foreign language must be properly translated to English by a DMV-approved translator before it can be accepted. Abstract translations will not be accepted.

en.question: If your name is different from what is on your proof of identity document, what must you present?

choices.A: A handwritten letter explaining the name change
choices.B: A notarized affidavit from a family member
choices.C: Legal documentation such as a marriage certificate or court order
choices.D: A utility bill showing your new name

en.explanation: If your name is different, you will be asked to present legal documentation reflecting your name change, such as a marriage certificate, divorce decree, spouse's death certificate, adoption record or court order.

en.question: How many documents must an applicant present to prove their Nevada residency status?

choices.A: One original document
choices.B: Two original or certified copies
choices.C: Three original or certified copies
choices.D: Four documents of any kind

en.explanation: Every applicant must present an original or certified copy of any two approved documents which reflect a residential address in Nevada to prove residency.

en.question: What is the fee for an initial knowledge or skills test in Nevada?
en.explanation: A $25.00 fee is charged for all initial knowledge and/or skills tests administered.

en.question: What will result in an automatic failure during your driving skills test?

choices.A: Using the windshield wipers
choices.B: Using a cellular phone
choices.C: Asking the examiner a question
choices.D: Stopping on a grade

en.explanation: The manual states that the use of a cellular phone during a drive test will result in automatic failure.

en.question: Who is allowed to ride in the vehicle with you during your road test?

choices.A: A parent or legal guardian
choices.B: A licensed driving instructor
choices.C: A language translator
choices.D: No passengers or animals are allowed

en.explanation: Passengers and animals are not allowed in the vehicle during the road test.

en.question: Which of the following vehicle features are you NOT allowed to use during your driving test?

choices.A: Turn signals
choices.B: Windshield wipers
choices.C: Parking assist and cruise control
choices.D: Brakes and headlights

en.explanation: When taking your driving test, you will not be allowed to use certain safety features such as parking assist, cruise control, etc.

en.question: If you are under 18, your license may be revoked for 185 days if a test indicates your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is:

choices.A: At least 0.01% but less than 0.05%
choices.B: At least 0.02% but less than 0.08%
choices.C: At least 0.04% but less than 0.10%
choices.D: At least 0.08% but less than 0.15%

en.explanation: A young driver's license may be revoked for 185 days if a blood, breath or urine test indicates at least 0.02% but less than 0.08% by weight of alcohol in the blood.

en.question: What is the penalty for a young driver's first offense of habitual truancy?

choices.A: License suspended for at least 30 days but not more than 6 months
choices.B: License suspended for exactly 1 year
choices.C: License revoked for 185 days
choices.D: License suspended for up to 2 years

en.explanation: For a first offense of habitual truancy, a young driver's license will be suspended for at least 30 days but not more than 6 months or have issuance delayed for 30 days.

en.question: If a driver under 18 is found guilty of handling or possessing a firearm in violation of NRS 202.300 for the first time, their license will be:

choices.A: Suspended for 30 days
choices.B: Revoked for 185 days
choices.C: Suspended or issuance delayed for up to one year
choices.D: Suspended or issuance delayed for two years

en.explanation: For a first offense of handling or possessing a firearm in violation of NRS 202.300, your license will be suspended or issuance delayed for up to one year.

en.question: What color ink must be used to complete the Beginning Driver Experience Log?

choices.A: Red or black ink
choices.B: Blue or black ink
choices.C: Pencil only
choices.D: Any color ink

en.explanation: The Beginning Driver Experience Log must be completed in blue or black ink before arriving for your drive test.

en.question: How recent must the signature and date be on the DMV-301 Certification of Attendance form when submitted?

choices.A: Within the previous 14 days
choices.B: Within the previous 30 days
choices.C: Within the previous 60 days
choices.D: Within the previous 90 days

en.explanation: The DMV-301 form must be signed and dated within the previous 60 days from which the form is being submitted.

en.question: If you are not within 30 miles of a DMV-approved school and cannot access the internet, how many hours of behind-the-wheel experience must you complete?

choices.A: 40 hours
choices.B: 50 hours
choices.C: 80 hours
choices.D: 100 hours

en.explanation: If you are not within 30 miles of a DMV-approved school and it is not possible to access the internet, you need to complete 100 hours of behind-the-wheel driving experience.

en.question: If you are applying for a motorcycle license and must complete the 100 hours of driving experience, what is the rule regarding driving in the dark?

choices.A: 10 hours must be completed in the dark.
choices.B: 20 hours must be completed in the dark.
choices.C: Half of the hours must be completed in the dark.
choices.D: All 100 hours must be completed during daylight hours only.

en.explanation: If you are applying for a motorcycle license, all 100 hours of driving experience must be completed during daylight hours only.

en.question: What is the penalty for a driver under 18 who is found guilty of participating in an unauthorized speed contest?

choices.A: License suspended for 30 days
choices.B: License suspended for 90 days
choices.C: License suspended for not less than six months but not more than two years
choices.D: License revoked permanently

en.explanation: Your license may be suspended for a period of not less than six months but not more than two years if found guilty of participating in, or organizing, an unauthorized speed contest.

en.question: How much is the fee for any knowledge or skills retests needed before you can get your license?
en.explanation: A $10 fee is charged for any retests needed before you can get your license.

en.question: Between what hours is a minor prohibited from operating a motor vehicle, unless driving to or from a scheduled event?

choices.A: 9 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.B: 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
choices.C: 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.
choices.D: Midnight and 6 a.m.

en.explanation: The manual states that a minor shall not operate a motor vehicle between the hours of 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. unless driving to or from a scheduled event.

en.question: For the first 6 months after receiving their driver's license, 16 and 17-year-old drivers are not allowed to carry passengers under the age of 18 EXCEPT for:

choices.A: School classmates
choices.B: Immediate family members
choices.C: Co-workers
choices.D: Passengers with a valid driver's license

en.explanation: Applicants who are 16 or 17 years old will not be allowed to carry passengers under the age of 18 (except for immediate family members) for the first 6 months they drive.

en.question: When driving with a Class C Instruction Permit, you must be accompanied by a licensed driver who is seated beside you, has at least one year of licensed driving experience, and is at least:

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 21 years old
choices.C: 25 years old
choices.D: 19 years old

en.explanation: When driving with a Class C Instruction Permit, you must be accompanied by a licensed driver who is 21 years of age or older, has at least one year of licensed driving experience, and is seated beside you.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement for the supervising driver when you are driving with a Class M (Motorcycle) Instruction Permit?

choices.A: They must follow closely behind you in a car or truck.
choices.B: They must be riding as a passenger on your motorcycle.
choices.C: They must be in direct visual supervision while riding on a motorcycle.
choices.D: They must be at least 18 years old with six months of driving experience.

en.explanation: You must be in direct visual supervision of a licensed motorcycle driver on a motorcycle who is 21 years of age or older. The supervising driver is not allowed to be in a car or truck.

en.question: Which driver's license classification allows you to drive a single vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) over 26,000 pounds and tow a vehicle under 10,000 pounds?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class B
choices.C: Class C
choices.D: Class M

en.explanation: A Class B license allows you to drive a single vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) over 26,000 pounds and may tow a vehicle under 10,000 pounds.

en.question: What does Restriction G on a Nevada driver's license indicate?

choices.A: Driver needs to wear glasses or contact lenses
choices.B: Yearly vision examination required
choices.C: Daylight driving only
choices.D: Additional rearview mirrors required

en.explanation: According to the restrictions list in the manual, Restriction G means 'Daylight driving only'.

en.question: If you are 18 years of age or older, how long is a motorcycle instruction permit valid for?

choices.A: Six months
choices.B: One year
choices.C: Two years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: Motorcycle instruction permits issued to persons 18 years of age or older are valid for six months and may be renewed only once every five years.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing the motorcycle skills test administered by the DMV two or more times?

choices.A: A mandatory 30-day waiting period before retaking the test
choices.B: Permanent denial of future motorcycle instruction permits
choices.C: Revocation of your Class C driver's license
choices.D: Required completion of an approved motorcycle safety course

en.explanation: Failing the motorcycle skills test administered by the DMV two or more times will result in a permanent denial of future motorcycle instruction permits per NRS 483.280.

en.question: Prior to receiving a driver's license, minors must remain free of any at-fault crashes, moving violation convictions, and alcohol or drug convictions for how many months?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: Minors must remain free of any at-fault crashes, moving violation convictions and any type of alcohol or drug conviction for six months prior to receiving a driver's license.

en.question: The Endorsement F provides a Commercial License exemption for which of the following groups?

choices.A: Taxi and ride-share drivers
choices.B: Delivery drivers operating within 50 miles
choices.C: Firefighters while operating fire equipment
choices.D: Drivers transporting placarded amounts of hazardous materials

en.explanation: Endorsement F is a Commercial License exemption for firefighters while operating fire equipment, farmers under specific conditions, and military driving military vehicles on active duty.

en.question: When driving a Class C vehicle, the combination of the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle(s) may not exceed what maximum length?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 60 feet
choices.C: 70 feet
choices.D: 80 feet

en.explanation: Under the Class C and Endorsement J sections, the manual states that the combination of vehicles may not exceed 70 feet in length.

en.question: Which of the following is a restriction when driving with a motorcycle instruction permit?

choices.A: You may only drive on limited-access highways.
choices.B: You may carry a maximum of one passenger.
choices.C: You may drive during daylight hours only.
choices.D: You must ride within 30 miles of your home.

en.explanation: When driving with a motorcycle instruction permit, you may drive during daylight hours only. You may not carry passengers or drive on freeways or other high-speed roadways.

en.question: A commercial motor vehicle requires a Commercial Driver License (CDL) if it is designed to carry how many passengers, including the driver?

choices.A: 8 or more
choices.B: 10 or more
choices.C: 12 or more
choices.D: 16 or more

en.explanation: A commercial motor vehicle is defined as one that has a GVWR/GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, is designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is carrying hazardous materials.

en.question: What type of driver's license is required to operate a moped in Nevada?

choices.A: Only a Class M license is acceptable.
choices.B: Any classification of Nevada driver's license.
choices.C: A Class C license with an Endorsement J.
choices.D: A Commercial Driver License (CDL).

en.explanation: The manual states: 'You may operate a moped if you have a Nevada driver license (any classification) or you may apply for a Class M license with an accompanying restriction that will allow you to operate a moped only.'

en.question: Whose responsibility is it to renew a Nevada driver's license on or before its expiration date?

choices.A: The DMV
choices.B: The driver
choices.C: The postal service
choices.D: The local police department

en.explanation: Although a renewal notice is mailed to the address on file, it is your responsibility to renew on or before your expiration date.

en.question: How does Nevada handle driver's license expiration dates for military personnel?

choices.A: They are automatically extended for five years.
choices.B: They never expire while on active duty.
choices.C: Nevada does not automatically extend the expiration date.
choices.D: They are extended until 30 days after discharge.

en.explanation: Nevada does not automatically extend the license expiration date for military personnel. Active-duty military personnel who are temporarily out-of-state may renew through the mail.

en.question: Under Nevada law, how many days do you have to notify the DMV of an address or name change?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: Under Nevada law, you are required to notify the DMV of any address or name change within 30 days.

en.question: If you hold a commercial driver's license (CDL), how must you complete an address change?

choices.A: Online at the DMV website
choices.B: By mailing the DMV-22 form
choices.C: Over the phone
choices.D: In person

en.explanation: Address changes must be completed in person if you hold a commercial driver license.

en.question: Which of the following is required to change your name on your Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: You must complete the change online.
choices.B: You must mail a written request to the DMV.
choices.C: You must make the change in person at a local DMV office.
choices.D: You must wait until your license is up for renewal.

en.explanation: Name changes must be made in person at a local DMV office. You will be asked to complete an application and provide acceptable legal documentation.

en.question: Under what special circumstances might a restricted license be issued to a 14- or 15-year-old?

choices.A: If they have maintained a 4.0 GPA
choices.B: If they have demonstrated family hardship or need to drive to school
choices.C: If they are enrolled in a driver's education course
choices.D: If they are employed part-time

en.explanation: Restricted licenses may be issued, under special circumstances, to drivers age 14 and 15 who have demonstrated family hardship or who need to drive to and from school.

en.question: A restricted license may be issued to an individual whose license is suspended or revoked if they have served at least:

choices.A: One-quarter of their required suspension or revocation period.
choices.B: Half of their required suspension or revocation period.
choices.C: Three-quarters of their required suspension or revocation period.
choices.D: 30 days of their required suspension or revocation period.

en.explanation: Restricted licenses may be issued to individuals who have served half of their required suspension or revocation periods.

en.question: How long is a standard Nevada identification card valid for before it expires?

choices.A: 4 years
choices.B: 5 years
choices.C: 8 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: A Nevada identification card is valid for eight years and expires on your birthday unless limited-term immigration documents are presented.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to obtain a Nevada identification card?

choices.A: 10 years old
choices.B: 12 years old
choices.C: 14 years old
choices.D: 16 years old

en.explanation: If you want a Nevada identification card, you must be at least 10 years old.

en.question: What happens if you receive 12 or more demerits in a 12-month period while holding a Nevada identification card?

choices.A: Your identification card will be permanently revoked.
choices.B: You will be required to reinstate your driving privileges before you are eligible to receive a driver's license.
choices.C: You will be fined $1,000 and face jail time.
choices.D: The demerits are ignored because you do not hold a driver's license.

en.explanation: If you receive 12 or more demerits in a 12-month period while holding an ID card, you will be required to reinstate your driving privileges before you are eligible to receive a driver license.

en.question: How can a driver add a medical indicator to their Nevada driver's license or ID card?

choices.A: By verbally informing the DMV clerk during renewal.
choices.B: By presenting a completed Confidential Physician Report (DMV Form DLD-7).
choices.C: By showing a prescription bottle with their name on it.
choices.D: By paying an additional $15 fee at the time of issuance.

en.explanation: You must present a completed Confidential Physician Report (DMV Form DLD-7) indicating one of the medical codes that is listed on the form to add a medical indicator.

en.question: What is required for a minor to become an organ donor on their Nevada driver's license?

choices.A: They must wait until they turn 18.
choices.B: A parent or guardian must sign an affidavit on the DMV-002 application.
choices.C: They must pay a special registration fee.
choices.D: They must provide a doctor's note approving the donation.

en.explanation: Minors who wish to be organ donors may have a parent or guardian sign an affidavit on the DMV-002 application indicating the parent or guardian understands they cannot amend or revoke the donation.

en.question: If you are a registered organ donor and are taken to a hospital sick or injured, what is the medical staff's first priority?

choices.A: To contact the organ donation registry.
choices.B: To save your life.
choices.C: To notify your family of your donor status.
choices.D: To prepare for organ harvesting.

en.explanation: Your life always comes first. If you are sick or injured and taken to a hospital, the priority is always to save your life.

en.question: Which of the following is listed as a potential red flag for sex trafficking?

choices.A: Traveling alone with excessive luggage
choices.B: Not being in control of their own identification documents
choices.C: Asking for directions to the nearest police station
choices.D: Driving a vehicle with out-of-state license plates

en.explanation: Sex Trafficking Red Flags include: Lack of knowledge of whereabouts, not in control of own identification documents (ID/passport), restricted communication, and a fearful or submissive demeanor.

en.question: What should you do if you suspect someone is a victim of human trafficking?

choices.A: Confront the suspected trafficker directly.
choices.B: Alert the victim to your suspicions.
choices.C: Attempt a citizen's arrest.
choices.D: Report the suspicious activity to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security without confronting the trafficker.

en.explanation: Do not at any time attempt to confront a suspected trafficker directly or alert a victim to your suspicions. Report suspected human trafficking to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

en.question: What is the reinstatement fee for an alcohol or controlled substance related offense, excluding the victim's fee?
en.explanation: The manual states that the reinstatement fee for an alcohol or controlled substance related offense is $120.00 (with an additional $35.00 victim's fee).

en.question: How much does it cost to change only your address on your driver's license?
en.explanation: The fee schedule indicates that a 'Change of address only' costs $3.25.

en.question: If your vehicle is a 1970 model or newer, what type of seat belts must it have?

choices.A: Lap-type seat belts for front seat passengers only
choices.B: Lap-type seat belts for each passenger and shoulder harnesses for the front seat
choices.C: Shoulder harnesses for every passenger in the vehicle
choices.D: Lap-type seat belts only for passengers under age 18

en.explanation: If a vehicle is a 1970 model or newer, it must have lap-type seat belts for each passenger and shoulder harnesses for use in the front seat.

en.question: At what age are passengers required to wear safety belts if the vehicle is equipped with them, assuming they do not require a child restraint system?

choices.A: Age 4 and older
choices.B: Age 6 and older
choices.C: Age 8 and older
choices.D: Age 12 and older

en.explanation: The manual states that the driver and any passengers age six and older must wear safety belts if the vehicle is equipped with them.

en.question: Under Nevada law, children must be in an approved child restraint system if they are:

choices.A: Under age 5 and less than 40 inches tall
choices.B: Under age 6 and less than 57 inches tall
choices.C: Under age 7 and less than 60 inches tall
choices.D: Under age 8 and less than 50 inches tall

en.explanation: Children under age six and those who measure less than 57 inches tall must be in an approved child restraint system pursuant to NRS 484B.157.

en.question: Where and how must a child under the age of two be secured in a motor vehicle?

choices.A: In a forward-facing child restraint system in the back seat
choices.B: In a rear-facing child restraint system in the back seat
choices.C: In a rear-facing child restraint system in the front seat
choices.D: In a booster seat in the back seat

en.explanation: Children under the age of two must be secured in a rear-facing child restraint system in the back seat of the motor vehicle.

en.question: It is illegal to leave a child aged 7 or younger unattended in a vehicle if there is a significant risk, UNLESS they are supervised by a person who is at least:

choices.A: 10 years old
choices.B: 12 years old
choices.C: 14 years old
choices.D: 16 years old

en.explanation: Never leave a child aged 7 or younger unattended in a vehicle if conditions present a significant risk, unless supervised by and within sight of a person at least 12 years old.

en.question: What is the legal classification for the offense of leaving a dog or cat unattended in a vehicle during periods of extreme heat or cold?

choices.A: A civil infraction
choices.B: A misdemeanor offense
choices.C: A gross misdemeanor offense
choices.D: A felony offense

en.explanation: The manual notes that violations of the laws regarding unattended children and pets in vehicles are misdemeanor offenses.

en.question: Which of the following is a potential penalty for failing to properly restrain a child under age six who measures less than 57 inches?

choices.A: Vehicle impoundment
choices.B: Mandatory jail time
choices.C: Suspension of your driver's license
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver's license

en.explanation: Failure to restrain children under age six and those measuring less than 57 inches may result in fines, community service, and/or the suspension of your driver's license.

en.question: Why should you never put an infant in the front seat if the car has a passenger side airbag?

choices.A: The airbag can explode from the dashboard at 200 mph and smash into the safety seat
choices.B: The infant will block the driver's view of the right side mirror
choices.C: The airbag will fail to deploy if the seat is pushed too far back
choices.D: Front seats do not have the proper anchors for child safety seats

en.explanation: In a crash, the airbag explodes from the dashboard at 200 mph, smashing through the safety seat into the back of the baby's head.

en.question: If an older child must ride in the front seat of a vehicle equipped with airbags, what should you do?

choices.A: Deactivate the passenger side airbag
choices.B: Move the vehicle seat back as far as possible
choices.C: Have the child sit on a thick cushion
choices.D: Use only the lap belt without the shoulder harness

en.explanation: Older children may ride in the front if necessary, but the vehicle seat should be moved back as far as possible to protect the head from contact with a rapidly inflating airbag.

en.question: According to the 'Getting Ready to Drive' section, what should you do before starting the engine?

choices.A: Turn on the radio to check for traffic updates
choices.B: Adjust the driver's seat to improve visibility
choices.C: Rev the engine to warm it up
choices.D: Check the tire pressure

en.explanation: Before you start the engine, you should adjust the driver's seat to improve visibility and so all controls can be comfortably reached.

en.question: What is required to reinstate a suspended, revoked, or canceled license?

choices.A: Payment of a reinstatement fee, original license fee, and applicable testing fees
choices.B: Payment of a reinstatement fee only
choices.C: Completion of a defensive driving course
choices.D: A court order from a judge

en.explanation: Any license suspension, revocation, or cancellation requires payment of the reinstatement fee, the fee for an original license, and any applicable testing fees.

en.question: Who is authorized to use reasonable force to rescue a dog or cat left unattended in a vehicle during extreme temperatures?

choices.A: Any concerned citizen
choices.B: Only the vehicle's owner
choices.C: Law enforcement, firefighters, and other officials
choices.D: Animal shelter volunteers only

en.explanation: It is illegal to leave a dog or cat unattended in a vehicle during extreme heat or cold. Law enforcement, firefighters, and other officials may use reasonable force to rescue the animal.

en.question: How can a driver use the 'penny test' to check tire wear?

choices.A: Place a penny flat on the tire sidewall.
choices.B: Place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves.
choices.C: Drop a penny from one foot above the tire.
choices.D: Rub the penny against the tire tread to check for friction.

en.explanation: According to the manual, to check for wear using the penny test, you should select a point where the tread appears lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves.

en.question: Where can you find the recommended pounds per square inch (psi) for your vehicle's tires?

choices.A: On the tire's sidewall only.
choices.B: In the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb.
choices.C: On the steering wheel column.
choices.D: Under the hood on the engine block.

en.explanation: The manual states to check tire pressure using the recommended psi located in the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle.

en.question: What does a brown highway sign indicate?

choices.A: Driver services such as food and lodging.
choices.B: Road construction or repair warning.
choices.C: Recreation and scenic area information.
choices.D: General warning.

en.explanation: Standard sign colors dictate that brown means recreation and scenic area information.

en.question: What is the meaning of a pennant-shaped traffic sign?

choices.A: School zone.
choices.B: Yield right-of-way.
choices.C: No passing.
choices.D: Railroad crossing ahead.

en.explanation: According to the standard shapes section, a pennant (which is shaped like a flag) means 'no passing'.

en.question: How should you proceed at a four-way stop?

choices.A: The largest vehicle always has the right-of-way.
choices.B: Allow vehicles that reach the intersection before you to go first.
choices.C: Proceed immediately without stopping if the intersection is clear.
choices.D: Honk to indicate you are proceeding first.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'At a four-way stop, wait for other vehicles already in the intersection. Allow vehicles that reach the intersection before you to go first. Wait your turn!'

en.question: What must you do when approached by an emergency vehicle using a siren and red lights?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the intersection.
choices.B: Speed up to stay ahead of the emergency vehicle.
choices.C: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
choices.D: Move to the left lane and slow down.

en.explanation: You must drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. You should never stop in an intersection.

en.question: What is the consequence of traffic violations in work zones?

choices.A: Increased traffic fines.
choices.B: Immediate license suspension.
choices.C: Mandatory community service.
choices.D: Confiscation of the vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that violations in work zones result in increased traffic fines.

en.question: What must a driver do when approaching an intersection where the traffic control lights are not working?

choices.A: Treat the intersection as a yield sign.
choices.B: Come to a full stop before proceeding through the intersection.
choices.C: Proceed at the normal speed limit if no other cars are visible.
choices.D: Wait for a police officer to arrive before crossing.

en.explanation: When traffic control lights are not working, drivers must come to a full stop before proceeding through the intersection.

en.question: What is the proper response to a steady yellow traffic light if you are already in the intersection?

choices.A: Stop immediately where you are.
choices.B: Back up out of the intersection.
choices.C: Speed up to 'beat the light.'
choices.D: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.

en.explanation: If a driver is already in the intersection during a steady yellow light, they should continue moving and clear it safely. The manual warns: 'DO NOT speed up to beat the light.'

en.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

choices.A: Proceed with caution without stopping.
choices.B: Come to a full stop, as it has the same meaning as a stop sign.
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic but do not stop.
choices.D: The traffic light is about to turn green.

en.explanation: A flashing red light means that drivers must come to a full stop. The signal has the same meaning as a stop sign.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean?

choices.A: Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.
choices.B: Drivers have a protected turn and do not need to yield.
choices.C: Drivers cannot make the movement shown by the arrow.
choices.D: The signal is broken and drivers must wait for a green light.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. They may complete the turn when it is safe to do so.

en.question: Under what condition may a driver make a left turn at a red light?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
choices.B: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street that has traffic moving to the left.
choices.C: At any intersection between the hours of midnight and 6 AM.
choices.D: A left turn on red is never permitted under any circumstances.

en.explanation: Drivers may make a left turn at a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street that has traffic moving to the left.

en.question: Which shape is used exclusively for school zones and school crossings?

choices.A: Octagon
choices.B: Diamond
choices.C: Pentagon
choices.D: Circle

en.explanation: A pentagon (5 sides) is the standard shape used for school zones and school crossings.

en.question: When approaching a yield sign, what must you do regarding vehicles making a U-turn from an intersection?

choices.A: Honk to warn them you are proceeding.
choices.B: Yield the right-of-way to them.
choices.C: Proceed first, as U-turning vehicles must yield to all traffic.
choices.D: Stop and wait for a green light.

en.explanation: The manual states that at a yield sign, you must 'Yield the right-of-way to vehicles making a U-turn from an intersection.'

en.question: What should a pedestrian do if the 'Don't Walk' signal is flashing without a countdown timer and they have not yet entered the roadway?

en.question: What is the penalty in Nevada for violating the direction of a school crossing guard?

en.question: Under which condition is a U-turn permitted in a school zone in Nevada?

en.question: At an intersection where there are no traffic signs or signals, which vehicle should usually go first?

en.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction is sounding a siren or using flashing lights?

en.question: Who has the right-of-way on a highway when on foot and using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?

en.question: If you are turning left at an intersection, how do right-of-way rules apply to a vehicle going straight ahead that is already in the intersection?

en.question: What must a driver do when encountering a blind person using a white cane or guide dog on the road?

en.question: What is the speed limit in business and residential areas in Nevada unless otherwise posted?

en.question: Under Nevada's Basic Rule for driving, what does a 'reasonable or proper' speed mean?

en.question: What must you do if you are driving slower than other traffic on a road with two or more lanes moving in the same direction?

en.question: When entering a freeway using a merge or acceleration lane, what should you do?

en.question: How far ahead should you look down the road when driving on a freeway?

choices.D: 45 to 60 seconds

en.question: What does a driver need to do when a freeway entrance is equipped with an active ramp meter?

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is permitted to use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) ramp meter bypass lane without stopping?

choices.A: Turn front tires toward the curb
