choices.C: Keep front tires perfectly straight
choices.D: Turn rear tires toward the curb

en.explanation: When headed uphill and there is a curb, turn your front tires away from the curb.

en.question: You may not park your car within how many feet of a fire hydrant in a place where parallel parking is permitted?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: You may not park your car within 15 feet of a fire hydrant in a place where parallel parking is permitted.

en.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: You may not park your car within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad.

en.question: If you have car trouble and must use an emergency stopping area on a freeway, what should you do?

choices.A: Walk along the freeway to find the nearest exit
choices.B: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other traffic
choices.C: Stand in the traffic lane to wave down a passing car
choices.D: Turn off all lights to save battery power

en.explanation: If you have car trouble, move to the shoulder or emergency stopping area as soon as you safely can. Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other traffic. Walking along a freeway is dangerous.

en.question: When is it acceptable to stop your vehicle on a freeway?

choices.A: When you need to check your map or GPS.
choices.B: Only for an emergency.
choices.C: When you want to take a phone call.
choices.D: If you miss your exit and need to back up.

en.explanation: The manual strictly states: 'DO NOT STOP ON A FREEWAY EXCEPT FOR AN EMERGENCY.'

en.question: If you have car trouble on the freeway and must stop, what should you do to warn other traffic?

choices.A: Honk your horn continuously.
choices.B: Turn on your four-way flashers.
choices.C: Stand in the lane and wave your arms.
choices.D: Turn off all your lights so you are not a distraction.

en.explanation: If you have car trouble, you should move to the shoulder or emergency stopping area and 'Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other traffic.'

en.question: What is the minimum fine for illegally parking in a space marked with the international symbol of access?
en.explanation: The manual states that it is illegal for anyone without a valid placard or plate to park in these spaces, and 'The minimum fine for doing so is $250.'

en.question: Why should individuals with disabled placards be mindful of using spaces with loading zones when feasible?

choices.A: They are reserved for commercial delivery vehicles only.
choices.B: They cost more to park in than standard disabled spaces.
choices.C: They may be needed by individuals who require machinery, such as lifts, to exit and enter their vehicle.
choices.D: They have a shorter time limit than regular disabled spaces.

en.explanation: The manual asks individuals to be mindful of spaces with loading zones because they 'may be needed by individuals with a higher degree of impairment, who require the assistance of machinery, such as lifts, to exit and enter their vehicle.'

en.question: What is a key characteristic of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)?

choices.A: They are designed to completely replace the need for a human driver.
choices.B: They assist the driver but do not drive the vehicle by themselves.
choices.C: They allow the driver to sleep while traveling on freeways.
choices.D: They are only active when the vehicle is traveling above 50 mph.

en.explanation: The manual states that ADAS technologies 'assist the driver but do not drive the vehicle by themselves.'

en.question: Most vehicle warning systems are considered 'passive,' which means they:

choices.A: Automatically steer the vehicle away from danger.
choices.B: Apply the brakes forcefully to prevent a crash.
choices.C: Warn the driver of a potential issue but do not automatically prevent a problem or crash.
choices.D: Only operate when the vehicle is in reverse.

en.explanation: The manual explains that most warning technologies are passive, 'meaning they warn the driver of a potential issue but do not automatically prevent a problem or crash.'

en.question: Even if your vehicle is equipped with a back-up warning system or rear camera, what must you still do when backing up?

choices.A: Rely entirely on the dashboard display screen.
choices.B: Safely monitor and maneuver by checking mirrors and looking over your shoulder.
choices.C: Accelerate quickly to minimize the time spent in reverse.
choices.D: Turn off the warning system to avoid distraction.

en.explanation: The manual states the driver should not become complacent and must 'safely monitor and maneuver their vehicle during backing... These include checking side mirrors, rear-view mirror, over the shoulder (head checks)...'

en.question: Blind spot monitors warn drivers of other vehicles in their blind spots. Before changing lanes, a driver should always:

choices.A: Check their mirrors and look over their shoulders.
choices.B: Wait for the blind spot monitor to automatically steer the car.
choices.C: Honk their horn to alert vehicles in the blind spot.
choices.D: Turn off the blind spot monitor.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'The driver should always check their mirrors and look over their shoulders before changing lanes,' even when equipped with blind spot monitors.

en.question: Which camera technology helps drivers park by showing a virtual bird’s-eye view above the vehicle?

choices.A: Rear Cross-Traffic Alert
choices.B: Surround-View Monitor
choices.C: Curve Speed Warning
choices.D: Forward Collision Warning

en.explanation: The Surround-View Monitor or Around-View Monitor System helps drivers park 'by showing the vehicle’s surroundings through a virtual bird’s-eye view above the vehicle.'

en.question: Detection technologies generally alert the driver to bicycles, pedestrians, or obstacles when driving at low speeds of around:

choices.A: 10 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 40 mph
choices.D: 55 mph

en.explanation: The manual notes these systems alert the driver when an obstacle has been detected 'while driving at low speeds - generally around 25 mph.'

en.question: What is a limitation of a Forward Collision Warning System?

choices.A: It only works when the vehicle is in reverse.
choices.B: The warning system alone will not automatically brake for the driver.
choices.C: It only detects pedestrians, not other vehicles.
choices.D: It requires the driver to wear a special headset.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states regarding Forward Collision Warning Systems: 'The warning system alone will not automatically brake for the driver.'

en.question: When using parking sensors, what does a constant warning tone indicate?

choices.A: The system has malfunctioned.
choices.B: The vehicle is perfectly centered in the parking space.
choices.C: The vehicle is too close to an object.
choices.D: The parking brake is engaged.

en.explanation: According to the manual, when listening to parking sensors, 'a constant tone means the vehicle is too close to an object.'

en.question: Unlike passive warning systems, what is the primary purpose of Driver Assistance Systems technologies?

choices.A: To completely take over the driving task on freeways.
choices.B: To perform a component of the driving function, such as assisting with braking or steering.
choices.C: To alert emergency services if a crash occurs.
choices.D: To record video of the vehicle's surroundings for insurance purposes.

en.explanation: The manual states the primary purpose of Driver Assistance Systems technologies is 'to perform a component of the driving function in specific circumstances... such as braking or steering.'

en.question: What will an Automatic Emergency Braking System do if it senses stopped traffic ahead and the driver fails to respond?

choices.A: It will urgently apply the brakes.
choices.B: It will steer the vehicle into the adjacent lane.
choices.C: It will turn on the hazard lights and honk the horn.
choices.D: It will accelerate to clear the hazard quickly.

en.explanation: The manual states these systems 'sense slow or stopped traffic or objects ahead and will urgently apply the brakes if the driver fails to respond.'

en.question: Which technology is designed to return your vehicle to its lane if you begin to drift out of it?

choices.A: Rear Cross-Traffic Alert
choices.B: Lane Keeping Assist
choices.C: Blind Spot Monitor
choices.D: Curve Speed Warning

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Lane assistance systems return you to your lane if you drift out of it.'

en.question: What may happen if a driver does not react to a Lane Keeping Assist alert?

choices.A: The vehicle will automatically pull over to the side of the road.
choices.B: The feature may gently steer the driver back into their lane.
choices.C: The engine will automatically shut off.
choices.D: The emergency parking brake will be applied.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if the driver does not act after receiving a Lane Keeping Assist alert, the feature may gently steer the driver into their lane.

en.question: When is it advised NOT to use Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC)?

choices.A: During long road trips on open highways
choices.B: When driving above 50 mph
choices.C: In bad weather and other unsafe driving conditions
choices.D: During daylight hours

en.explanation: The manual states that in bad weather and other unsafe driving conditions, it is advised not to use Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC).

en.question: During the automatic parallel parking process, what is the driver still responsible for?

choices.A: Steering the wheel
choices.B: Finding the parking spot
choices.C: Accelerating to the speed limit
choices.D: Braking

en.explanation: While the automatic parallel parking system guides the vehicle and may require taking hands off the steering wheel, the manual specifies that the driver is still responsible for braking.

en.question: To avoid the glare from oncoming headlights at night, where should you look?

choices.A: Directly at the oncoming headlights
choices.B: Down and to the right side of your lane
choices.C: At your rearview mirror
choices.D: Up at the streetlights

en.explanation: To make night driving safer, the manual advises drivers not to look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles, but rather to look down and to the right side of their lane.

en.question: When are headlights legally required to be turned on based on the time of day?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise
choices.B: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
choices.C: From a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise
choices.D: Only when driving on unlit roads at night

en.explanation: Headlights are legally required from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise.

en.question: You must change to low beams when you are at least how many feet before any oncoming vehicles?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states to change to low beams when you are at least 500 feet before any oncoming vehicles.

en.question: You must change to low beams when you are following another vehicle within how many feet?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Drivers must change to low beams when they are 300 feet before any vehicle they are following.

en.question: Stopping distances on slippery roads may be how much greater than on dry pavement?

choices.A: 1.5 to 2 times greater
choices.B: 2 to 10 times greater
choices.C: 5 to 15 times greater
choices.D: 10 to 20 times greater

en.explanation: The manual warns that stopping distances on slippery roads may be 2 to 10 times greater than on dry pavement.

en.question: If your vehicle has an anti-lock braking system (ABS), how should you brake on snow and ice?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly
choices.B: Use a slow, light, touch-and-release pattern
choices.C: Apply firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal
choices.D: Use the emergency parking brake only

en.explanation: If your vehicle has an anti-lock braking system (ABS), a firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal is needed to activate the anti-lock feature.

en.question: Between what dates are studded snow tires permitted to be used?

choices.A: November 1 through March 31
choices.B: September 1 through May 31
choices.C: December 1 through February 28
choices.D: October 1 through April 30

en.explanation: Studded snow tires may only be used from October 1 through April 30.

en.question: If your brakes fail while driving, what is the FIRST thing you should try to do?

choices.A: Shift into 'park'
choices.B: Turn off the ignition
choices.C: Pump the brake pedal
choices.D: Steer into a ditch

en.explanation: If your brakes fail, the manual instructs you to first try pumping the brake pedal.

en.question: What should you NEVER do if your brakes fail?

choices.A: Use the emergency parking brake
choices.B: Shift to a lower gear
choices.C: Place the vehicle into 'park'
choices.D: Pump the brake pedal

en.explanation: In the event of brake failure, the manual explicitly states to NEVER place the vehicle into 'park'.

en.question: How should you dry wet brakes after driving through deep water?

choices.A: Drive at a high speed to air dry them
choices.B: Put the car in low gear, drive slowly, and lightly apply the brakes
choices.C: Shift to neutral and rev the engine
choices.D: Pump the brakes as fast as possible for one mile

en.explanation: To dry wet brakes, put your car in low gear, drive slowly and lightly apply the brakes, testing them about every 200 feet.

en.question: If your accelerator (gas pedal) sticks and pressing it hard does not release it, what should you do next?

choices.A: Shift to neutral, apply the brakes, and pull off
choices.B: Shift into reverse
choices.C: Turn off the engine immediately while in gear
choices.D: Apply the emergency parking brake only

en.explanation: If the gas pedal sticks and pressing it hard does not free it, you should shift to neutral, apply the brakes, and pull off.

en.question: Headlights are legally required whenever persons or vehicles cannot be clearly seen at a distance of:

choices.A: 500 feet
choices.B: 1,000 feet
choices.C: 1,500 feet
choices.D: 2,000 feet

en.explanation: Headlights are legally required whenever persons or vehicles cannot be clearly seen at a distance of 1,000 feet.

en.question: What should you NEVER do if your vehicle's accelerator (gas pedal) sticks?

choices.A: Shift to neutral
choices.B: Apply the brakes
choices.C: Place the vehicle into 'park'
choices.D: Pull off the highway to the right

en.explanation: The manual states that if your accelerator sticks, you should shift to neutral, apply the brakes, and pull off the highway, but NEVER place the vehicle into 'park.'

en.question: If your vehicle's engine catches fire, why should you avoid using water to extinguish it?

choices.A: Water will damage the engine block
choices.B: Burning gasoline will float on water and spread the fire
choices.C: Water will create toxic smoke
choices.D: The water will evaporate too quickly to be effective

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states, 'DO NOT USE WATER because burning gasoline will float on water and spread the fire.'

en.question: What is the correct action to take if you suddenly lose steering control and your vehicle continues to hold the lane?

choices.A: Apply the brakes quickly using maximum pressure
choices.B: Shift the vehicle into park immediately
choices.C: Ease up on the accelerator, slow down, and gently apply the brakes
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right

en.explanation: If your car continues to hold the lane after losing steering control, you should ease up on the accelerator, slow down, and then gently apply the brakes while using your four-way flashers.

en.question: If you see a vehicle coming toward you in your lane, why should you avoid swinging into the lane the approaching vehicle has left?

choices.A: It is illegal to cross the center line
choices.B: The other driver may suddenly realize their mistake and turn back into the proper lane
choices.C: You will lose your right-of-way privileges
choices.D: Your vehicle may lose traction on the center line

en.explanation: The manual warns not to swing into the lane the approaching vehicle has left because the other driver may suddenly realize his or her mistake and turn back into the proper lane.

en.question: Which of the following is a major factor in single-vehicle crashes where a vehicle runs off the highway?

choices.A: Driver fatigue
choices.B: Over-inflated tires
choices.C: Driving too slowly
choices.D: Using high-beam headlights

en.explanation: According to the manual, driver fatigue, inattention, and speeding are all major factors in crashes where a vehicle runs off the pavement.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle drifts onto the shoulder or you are forced off the road?

choices.A: Swerve back onto the pavement immediately
choices.B: Hit the brakes hard to stop quickly
choices.C: Stay on the shoulder until you have your vehicle completely under control
choices.D: Accelerate to regain traction

en.explanation: If you run off the pavement, do not try to swerve back onto the pavement. Instead, stay on the shoulder until you have your vehicle completely under control and gently ease back onto the road.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if you experience a tire blowout?

choices.A: Hit the brakes immediately
choices.B: Grip the steering wheel firmly
choices.C: Shift into neutral
choices.D: Turn on your windshield wipers

en.explanation: For safe recovery from a blowout, the manual advises to first grip the steering wheel firmly and ease up on the gas pedal, but do not hit the brakes.

en.question: According to the manual, how much water can cause a driver to lose control of their car?

choices.A: Less than 1 inch
choices.B: Exactly 6 inches
choices.C: 12 inches
choices.D: 2 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that less than 1 inch of water can cause a driver to lose control of his or her car.

en.question: Most vehicles can float in what depth of water?

choices.A: 6 inches or less
choices.B: 1 foot or less
choices.C: 2 feet or less
choices.D: 3 feet or less

en.explanation: The manual notes that most vehicles can float in 2 feet of water or less.

en.question: What is the penalty for speeding in a highway work zone?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense
choices.B: Fines for speeding double
choices.C: Immediate license suspension
choices.D: Fines triple

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that fines for speeding double in work zones.

en.question: In a highway work zone, what do orange speed limit signs indicate?

choices.A: They are regulatory and must be strictly obeyed
choices.B: They are advisory and indicate slower, safer speeds
choices.C: They indicate the minimum speed allowed
choices.D: They apply only to commercial vehicles

en.explanation: Black and white speed limit signs are regulatory, while orange speed limit signs are advisory and indicate slower, safer speeds.

en.question: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with non-flashing blue lights, what must a driver do if they cannot safely change lanes?

choices.A: Maintain the posted speed limit and proceed
choices.B: Stop immediately in the travel lane
choices.C: Decrease speed to less than the posted speed limit and proceed with caution
choices.D: Sound the horn to alert the emergency workers

en.explanation: When approaching stopped emergency vehicles, drivers must decrease their speed to less than the posted speed limit, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if they cannot safely move to a non-adjacent lane.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is authorized to use a paved highway shoulder marked for emergency use?

choices.A: A passenger car with a flat tire
choices.B: A public transit bus
choices.C: A commercial delivery truck
choices.D: A motorcycle

en.explanation: The manual lists authorized vehicles that may use a paved shoulder, which includes law enforcement, fire engines, ambulances, tow cars, coroner vehicles, and public transit buses.

en.question: Who causes most crashes between large commercial trucks and smaller cars?

choices.A: The commercial truck drivers
choices.B: The car drivers
choices.C: Pedestrians
choices.D: Poor road conditions

en.explanation: The manual states that most crashes between large commercial trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers.

en.question: What is a 'no-zone' in relation to large commercial vehicles?

choices.A: A designated parking area for trucks only
choices.B: A highway lane where commercial vehicles are prohibited
choices.C: The area around large trucks or buses where cars disappear into blind spots
choices.D: The stopping distance required for a commercial vehicle

en.explanation: The 'no-zone' is defined as the area around large commercial trucks or buses where cars 'disappear' into blind spots.

en.question: What is a 'no-zone' around a large commercial truck or bus?

choices.A: A designated parking area for trucks only.
choices.B: The area where cars disappear into blind spots.
choices.C: A zone where passing is strictly prohibited by law.
choices.D: The lane dedicated to commercial vehicles on highways.

en.explanation: The 'no-zone' is the area around large commercial trucks or buses where cars 'disappear' into blind spots, greatly increasing the possibility of a collision.

en.question: Compared to passenger cars, how much time and distance do large commercial trucks and buses need to stop?

choices.A: About the same time and distance.
choices.B: Nearly half the time and distance.
choices.C: Nearly twice the time and distance.
choices.D: Nearly three times the time and distance.

en.explanation: According to the manual, large commercial vehicles need nearly twice the time and distance to stop as cars.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to try to 'squeeze' between a commercial vehicle and the curb at an intersection?

choices.A: Commercial vehicles often swing wide to safely make turns and cannot see cars directly beside them.
choices.B: The curb lane is legally reserved for bicycles and mopeds only.
choices.C: Commercial vehicles accelerate much faster than cars when turning.
choices.D: It is illegal for passenger vehicles to drive in the right lane near intersections.

en.explanation: Large commercial truck and bus drivers sometimes need to swing wide to safely make a turn. They cannot see cars directly behind or beside them, making the 'squeeze play' an invitation to disaster.

en.question: Under Nevada law, when may motorcycles be operated two abreast in a single traffic lane?

choices.A: At all times, regardless of the drivers' consent.
choices.B: Only when traveling under 30 mph.
choices.C: With the mutual consent of the drivers.
choices.D: Motorcycles are never allowed to ride side by side.

en.explanation: Per NRS 486.351 (3), motorcycles and mopeds may be operated no more than two abreast in a single traffic lane with the consent of the drivers.

en.question: Why is it especially important to dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle?

choices.A: High beams will cause the motorcycle's engine to stall.
choices.B: The blinding effect of high beams can be far more dangerous to motorcyclists because they use balance to steer.
choices.C: Motorcycle headlights are not as bright as car headlights.
choices.D: High beams reflect off the motorcycle's mirrors and blind the driver behind them.

en.explanation: Because motorcyclists use their balance to steer their vehicles, the blinding effect of high beams can be far more dangerous to them than to drivers of cars or large commercial trucks.

en.question: In Nevada, a moped is defined as having a maximum speed of how many miles per hour on a flat surface?

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: Nevada defines mopeds based on motor size, horsepower, and a 30 miles per hour maximum speed on a flat or near-flat surface.

en.question: Moped operators must remain in the extreme right-hand lane of any road EXCEPT when:

choices.A: The moped is traveling at its maximum speed.
choices.B: Preparing to make a left turn within one-quarter mile.
choices.C: Driving in a residential neighborhood.
choices.D: The operator is wearing a brightly colored helmet.

en.explanation: Moped operators must remain in the extreme right-hand lane unless there is a single lane of traffic, they are preparing to make a left turn (within one-quarter mile), it is unsafe, or directed by a police officer.

en.question: When are you NOT required to stop for a school bus displaying a flashing red signal?

choices.A: When you are traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.
choices.B: When you are traveling in the opposite direction on a two-lane road.
choices.C: When you are running late for an emergency.
choices.D: When the school bus is stopped at a railroad crossing.

en.explanation: There is one exception to the rule of stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights: on divided highways, you are only required to stop when you are traveling in the same direction as the school bus.

en.question: What penalty may a motorist face for causing even a minor collision with a bicycle or intentionally interfering with its movement?

choices.A: A verbal warning from a police officer.
choices.B: A mandatory defensive driving course.
choices.C: A charge of reckless driving and a driver's license suspension.
choices.D: A permanent revocation of their vehicle registration.

en.explanation: Motorists who cause even a minor collision with a bicycle or pedestrian or who intentionally interfere with the movement of a bicycle may be charged with reckless driving. Penalties include a driver's license suspension.

en.question: Under what circumstance is a motorist allowed to drive in a designated bicycle lane?

choices.A: When passing a slower vehicle on the right.
choices.B: When traffic is heavily congested.
choices.C: When entering or leaving an alley or driveway.
choices.D: When preparing to park on the opposite side of the street.

en.explanation: Motorists may not stop, park or drive on a designated bicycle path or lane unless they are entering or leaving an alley or driveway, performing official duties, are directed by a police officer, or an emergency situation exists.

en.question: In Nevada, it is illegal for anyone under the age of 18 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on a paved highway UNLESS:

choices.A: They are wearing a seatbelt fastened to the truck bed.
choices.B: The vehicle is being used while farming or ranching.
choices.C: The truck is traveling under 25 mph.
choices.D: They are accompanied by an adult in the truck bed.

en.explanation: Anyone under the age of 18 may not ride in the bed of a flatbed or pickup truck on a paved highway in Nevada. Exceptions include being driven in an authorized parade or if the vehicle is being used while farming or ranching.

en.question: What should you keep in mind regarding a motorcycle's turn signals?

choices.A: They are usually brighter than a car's turn signals.
choices.B: They are not self-canceling on most motorcycles.
choices.C: They are only required on the rear of the motorcycle.
choices.D: They automatically activate when the motorcycle leans.

en.explanation: Turn signals are not self-canceling on most motorcycles. Before you make a lane change or turn that depends on a motorcycle's path, be sure you know what the motorcyclist is doing.

en.question: Which of the following is a cyclist NOT allowed to do while riding?

choices.A: Wear brightly colored clothing.
choices.B: Ride in a traffic lane.
choices.C: Use their right arm to signal a right turn.
choices.D: Wear a headset or cellular phone earpiece.

en.explanation: According to the manual's 'Cyclists Should Not...' section, cyclists should not wear a headset (headphones, cellular phone earpiece, etc.) when riding.

en.question: What must a driver do if they are turning right and a pedestrian is crossing the street on a green light?

choices.A: Honk to warn the pedestrian to move faster.
choices.B: Proceed carefully if there is enough room to go around.
choices.C: Yield to the pedestrian.
choices.D: The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual states that when a traffic signal turns green, drivers must yield to persons who are still crossing the street, and pedestrians have the right of way over motorists making a right-hand turn.

en.question: According to the manual, where does a crosswalk exist?

choices.A: Only where painted white lines are present on the road.
choices.B: Anywhere two streets intersect, even if it is not painted or marked.
choices.C: Only at intersections controlled by traffic signals or stop signs.
choices.D: Only in designated school zones.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that a crosswalk exists anywhere two streets intersect, even at a 'T' intersection, and exists even if it is not painted or marked.

en.question: If a vehicle ahead of you is slowing down or stopped at an intersection, what is it illegal for you to do?

choices.A: Stop behind the vehicle and wait.
choices.B: Honk your horn to alert the driver.
choices.C: Overtake the vehicle before determining why it slowed or stopped.
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights.

en.explanation: It is illegal for motorists to overtake any vehicle that is slowing down or stopped until the motorist slows down enough to determine why the other vehicle has slowed or stopped.

en.question: Why should you not stop your car more than five feet from a crosswalk when a blind or visually impaired pedestrian is waiting?

choices.A: The pedestrian uses the sound of your engine as a guide.
choices.B: It blocks the view of other drivers approaching the intersection.
choices.C: It is illegal to stop that far back from any intersection.
choices.D: The pedestrian needs to be able to touch your car with their cane.

en.explanation: The manual advises not to stop your car more than five feet from the crosswalk because a pedestrian who is blind or visually impaired uses the sound of your engine as a guide.

en.question: How does a blind or visually impaired pedestrian indicate that you can proceed?

choices.A: By waving their hand at your vehicle.
choices.B: By making direct eye contact with you.
choices.C: By taking a step back and pulling in their cane.
choices.D: By pointing their cane at your vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual states that if a blind or visually impaired pedestrian takes a step back and pulls in their cane, they are letting you know you can go.

en.question: What is the maximum total length of a vehicle combination that a non-commercial Class C driver may tow?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 60 feet
choices.C: 70 feet
choices.D: 80 feet

en.explanation: Non-commercial Class C drivers may tow a single vehicle or a combination of vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 10,000 pounds or less and a total length of no more than 70 feet.

en.question: What does Gross Combination Weight (GCW) refer to?

choices.A: The total weight of a single vehicle plus its load.
choices.B: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specified pressure.
choices.C: The total weight of a powered unit plus trailer(s) plus the load.
choices.D: The weight transmitted to the ground by one set of axles.

en.explanation: Gross combination weight (GCW) is defined as the total weight of a powered unit plus trailer(s) plus the load.

en.question: What is a consequence of having too much weight on the steering axle of a towing vehicle?

choices.A: The drive wheels may spin easily due to poor traction.
choices.B: It can make steering difficult and cause damage to the steering axle and tires.
choices.C: The vehicle will gain too much speed on uphill grades.
choices.D: The trailer is more likely to overturn on turns.

en.explanation: Improper weight balance can make handling unsafe. Too much weight on the steering axle can make steering difficult and cause damage to the steering axle and tires.

en.question: What happens if there is too little weight on the driving axles of a towing vehicle?

choices.A: The steering axle will be damaged.
choices.B: The vehicle will have poor traction and the drive wheels may spin easily.
choices.C: The trailer will become top-heavy.
choices.D: The brakes will fail immediately.

en.explanation: The manual states that too little weight on the driving axles can cause poor traction and the drive wheels may spin easily.

en.question: When hitching a trailer to a vehicle using a ball-and-hitch coupler, how should the safety chains be configured?

choices.A: Attached and crossed.
choices.B: Hanging loosely to touch the ground.
choices.C: Attached only to the right side of the hitch.
choices.D: Wrapped tightly around the ball attachment.

en.explanation: When hitching a trailer, you must make sure the safety chains are attached and crossed, and not tangled, pinched, or dragging.

en.question: If there is no sidewalk available, where should pedestrians walk?

choices.A: On the right side of the road moving with traffic.
choices.B: In the center of the road.
choices.C: On the side of the road facing the traffic.
choices.D: Pedestrians are not allowed on roads without sidewalks.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If there is a sidewalk, pedestrians should use it. If there is no sidewalk, pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic.'

en.question: If a crossing guard is present at a crosswalk, when may a motorist proceed?

choices.A: As soon as the guard lowers their stop sign.
choices.B: When the guard is completely out of the crosswalk.
choices.C: When the children have crossed, even if the guard is still in the road.
choices.D: After coming to a complete stop for 3 seconds.

en.explanation: If a crossing guard is present, motorists must wait until the guard is completely out of the crosswalk before proceeding.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended action when encountering a blind or visually impaired pedestrian?

choices.A: Give them verbal directions to help them cross safely.
choices.B: Honk lightly to let them know your vehicle is there.
choices.C: Wait 3-4 seconds to give them time to decide if they want to cross.
choices.D: Stop in the middle of the crosswalk to block other traffic for them.

en.explanation: The manual suggests giving blind or visually impaired pedestrians time to decide if they want to cross the street, noting that waiting 3-4 seconds is a good rule of thumb. It explicitly says do NOT give verbal direction, honk, or stop in the middle of a crosswalk.

en.question: What are two things a driver can do to prevent a trailer rollover?

choices.A: Go fast around turns and keep cargo piled high.
choices.B: Go slowly around turns and keep the cargo as close to the ground as possible.
choices.C: Overload the front axle and use a fifth-wheel hitch.
choices.D: Put the heaviest items on top and brake firmly in curves.

en.explanation: The manual states there are two things a driver can do to prevent a rollover: Go slowly around turns, and keep the cargo as close to the ground as possible.

en.question: What is a disadvantage of using a fifth-wheel hitch?

choices.A: It is highly unstable and prone to weight distribution issues.
choices.B: It takes up most of the space in the bed of the truck.
choices.C: It cannot be used with electric lines or safety chains.
choices.D: It requires the trailer to have a completely flat front end.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a disadvantage to a fifth-wheel hitch is that it takes up most of the space in the bed of the truck and requires that the remaining space behind the hitch assembly is kept clear for turning corners.

en.question: What must you do before backing your vehicle under a fifth-wheel trailer?

choices.A: Make sure the trailer brakes are locked.
choices.B: Disconnect all electric lines.
choices.C: Ensure the release arm is in the closed position.
choices.D: Empty the truck bed completely.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Before backing your vehicle under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are locked.'

en.question: After beginning an extended trip, within how many miles should you inspect the trailer and load-securing devices again?

choices.A: 10 miles
choices.B: 100 miles
choices.C: 50 miles
choices.D: 200 miles

en.explanation: The manual advises to 'Inspect the trailer and the load-securing devices again within 50 miles after beginning an extended trip.'

en.question: During an extended trip, how often should you make needed adjustments and inspect the trailer after the initial 50-mile check?

choices.A: Every 3 hours or 150 miles
choices.B: Every 2 hours or 100 miles
choices.C: Every 4 hours or 200 miles
choices.D: Every 5 hours or 250 miles

en.explanation: After the initial 50-mile check, you should 'Make any needed adjustments and inspect again after you have driven for 3 hours or 150 miles.'

en.question: How does the weight of a heavy vehicle affect its stopping distance?

choices.A: Empty trucks require greater stopping distances because they have less traction.
choices.B: Fully loaded trucks require much greater stopping distances than empty trucks.
choices.C: The weight of the vehicle has no effect on its stopping distance.
choices.D: Empty trucks stop faster because the brakes have less weight to absorb.

en.explanation: The manual explains that brakes, tires, springs, and shock absorbers on heavy vehicles are designed to work best when fully loaded. 'Empty trucks actually require greater stopping distances because they have less traction.'

en.question: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, which direction should you initially turn the steering wheel?

choices.A: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
choices.B: Keep the steering wheel perfectly straight.
choices.C: Turn the wheel sharply to the right regardless of direction.
choices.D: In the opposite direction you want the trailer to go.

en.explanation: When backing with a trailer, the manual instructs to 'turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction. Once the trailer starts to turn, you must turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.'

en.question: Why is backing toward the right side with a trailer considered very dangerous?

choices.A: The trailer is more likely to disconnect from the hitch.
choices.B: The steering wheel locks when turning right in reverse.
choices.C: You cannot see as well on the right side.
choices.D: It causes the trailer brakes to fail.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Backing toward the right side is very dangerous because you can’t see as well. If you back and turn toward the driver’s side, watch the rear of your vehicle by looking out the side window.'

en.question: If you see your trailer getting off course while backing, how should you correct the drift?

choices.A: Accelerate to straighten the trailer out.
choices.B: Apply the trailer brakes immediately.
choices.C: Turn the top of the steering wheel opposite to the drift.
choices.D: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

en.explanation: To correct drift immediately, 'As soon as you see the trailer getting off course, correct it by turning the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.'

en.question: If you are driving a large vehicle that must swing wide to make a right turn, how should you execute the turn?

choices.A: Turn wide as you complete the turn, keeping the rear close to the curb.
choices.B: Turn wide to the left as you start the turn.
choices.C: Back up before making the turn to get a better angle.
choices.D: Swing into the oncoming traffic lane before starting the turn.

en.explanation: The manual advises: 'If driving a vehicle that cannot make the right turn without swinging into another lane, turn wide as you complete the turn. Keep the rear of your trailer close to the curb.'

en.question: Why should you NOT turn wide to the left as you start a right turn with a large vehicle?

choices.A: It will cause the trailer to off-track into the curb.
choices.B: It requires too much steering effort and may lock the wheels.
choices.C: A following driver may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.
choices.D: The trailer's safety chains may break from the tension.

en.explanation: The manual warns: 'Don’t turn wide to the left as you start the turn. A following driver may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right. You could crash into the other vehicle as you complete your turn.'

en.question: When making a left turn with a large vehicle, why should you reach the center of the intersection before starting the turn?

choices.A: To allow oncoming traffic to pass on your right.
choices.B: To trigger the traffic light sensors in the intersection.
choices.C: To give pedestrians more time to cross the street.
choices.D: To prevent the left side of your vehicle from hitting another vehicle due to off-tracking.

en.explanation: On a left turn, make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before you start the turn because 'If you turn too soon, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle due to off-tracking.'

en.question: If there are two turning lanes for a left turn, which lane should a driver of a large vehicle take?

choices.A: The right-hand turn lane.
choices.B: The inside (left-hand) turn lane.
choices.C: Whichever lane has less traffic.
choices.D: The lane closest to the center line.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If there are two turning lanes, always take the right hand turn lane. Do not start in the inside lane because you may have to swing right to make the turn.'

en.question: How does the load of a trailer affect its overhead clearance?

choices.A: A loaded trailer is higher than an empty one.
choices.B: The load has no effect on the height of the trailer.
choices.C: An empty trailer is higher than a loaded one.
choices.D: A loaded trailer is wider, but the height remains the same.

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'The weight of a vehicle changes its height. An empty trailer is higher than a loaded one.'

en.question: Why should you not assume that the posted height at bridges and overpasses is always correct?

choices.A: Repaving or packed snow may have reduced the clearance since the height was posted.
choices.B: Signs are often vandalized or outdated.
choices.C: Bridges expand significantly in hot weather, lowering the clearance.
choices.D: The posted height only applies to passenger cars, not commercial vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual warns: 'Do not assume that the height posted at bridges and overpasses is correct. Repaving or packed snow may have reduced the clearances since the height was posted.'

en.question: Which of the following hazards can cause a heavily loaded vehicle to drag or get hung up underneath?

choices.A: Freshly painted crosswalks.
choices.B: Rumble strips on the highway.
choices.C: Wet asphalt.
choices.D: Railroad tracks sticking up several inches.

en.explanation: The manual notes that space underneath can be very small when heavily loaded, and 'Railroad tracks can stick up several inches... Don’t take a chance on getting hung up halfway across.'

en.question: When towing a combination of vehicles, where must the heaviest vehicle be placed?

choices.A: In the rear position
choices.B: In the first position behind the towing vehicle
choices.C: In the middle position
choices.D: It does not matter as long as it is secured

en.explanation: When towing a combination of vehicles, the heaviest vehicle must always be in the first position behind the towing vehicle. The lighter vehicle should be in the rear.

en.question: How does the stopping distance of a large combination vehicle change when it is empty compared to when it is fully loaded?

choices.A: It takes less time to stop when empty.
choices.B: It takes longer to stop when empty.
choices.C: The stopping distance is exactly the same.
choices.D: It cannot be determined without knowing the speed.

en.explanation: Large combination vehicles that are empty take longer to stop than when they are fully loaded. When lightly loaded, stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give poor traction.

en.question: What is the correct action to take if your trailer's wheels lock up and it begins to skid?

choices.A: Apply the trailer hand brake immediately.
choices.B: Steer sharply in the opposite direction.
choices.C: Release the brakes to get traction back.
choices.D: Accelerate to pull the trailer straight.

en.explanation: To recover from a trailer skid, you should release the brakes to get traction back. Do not use the trailer hand brake, as the brakes on the trailer wheels caused the skid in the first place.

en.question: What is the earliest and best way to recognize that your trailer has started to skid?

choices.A: Feeling a pull on the steering wheel
choices.B: Hearing the tires squeal
choices.C: Seeing it in your mirrors
choices.D: Feeling the vehicle slow down abruptly

en.explanation: The earliest and best way to recognize that the trailer has started to skid is by seeing it in your mirrors. Any time the brakes are applied hard, check the mirrors.

en.question: What is the minimum liability insurance coverage required for bodily injury or death of one person in any one crash in Nevada?
en.explanation: The state of Nevada requires minimum coverage of $25,000 for bodily injury or death of one person in any one crash.

en.question: Which of the following is a potential penalty for a lapse of vehicle insurance coverage in Nevada?

choices.A: A mandatory 6-month jail sentence
choices.B: Confiscation of the vehicle
choices.C: A reinstatement fee and fines starting at $250
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver's license

en.explanation: If a registration is suspended for a lapse of insurance, the driver will be required to pay a reinstatement fee and applicable fines starting at $250 and totaling up to $1,750.

en.question: If you are in a crash that is NOT investigated by law enforcement, under what circumstances must you submit a Report of Crash Form (SR-1)?

choices.A: Only if the crash involves a commercial vehicle
choices.B: If the crash causes $750 or more in damages or anyone is injured
choices.C: If the crash causes $1,000 or more in damages
choices.D: Only if the other driver does not have insurance

en.explanation: If you are in a crash that is not investigated by law enforcement and the crash causes $750 or more in damages or anyone is injured, you must complete and send a Report of Crash Form (SR-1).

en.question: How many days do you have to submit a Report of Crash Form (SR-1) to the DMV if it is required?

choices.A: 3 days
choices.B: 5 days
choices.C: 10 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: You must complete and send a Report of Crash Form (SR-1) within 10 days to the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles.

en.question: What should you do if you are involved in a crash with only property damage (no injuries) and your vehicle can be moved safely?

choices.A: Leave the vehicles exactly where they are until police arrive.
choices.B: Move to a location that does not obstruct traffic and return to the scene.
choices.C: Drive home and report the crash online.
choices.D: Wait in the middle of the road with your hazard lights on.

en.explanation: If there is only damage to a vehicle or other property (no injuries) and the vehicle can be moved safely, move to a location that does not obstruct traffic and return to the scene.

en.question: What must you do if you crash into an unattended vehicle?

choices.A: Leave the scene immediately if there is no visible damage.
choices.B: Wait by the vehicle for up to one hour.
choices.C: Give the owner your information either in person or by leaving a note.
choices.D: Call a tow truck to remove the unattended vehicle.

en.explanation: If the crash involves an unattended vehicle or other property, you must give the owner your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information, either in person or by leaving a note.

en.question: How does the Nevada DMV handle traffic violations that occur in other states?

choices.A: They are ignored as long as you pay the fine in the other state.
choices.B: They are added to your Nevada driving record.
choices.C: They only affect your record if they involve a DUI.
choices.D: They are placed on a separate out-of-state driving record.

en.explanation: Information about traffic crashes and convictions becomes part of your driving record. Even traffic violations that occur in other states are added to your Nevada driving record.

en.question: How long do convictions related to DUI (Driving Under the Influence) stay on your Nevada driving record?

choices.A: 3 years
choices.B: 5 years
choices.C: 7 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: Most violations are reportable to your insurance company for three years. Convictions related to DUI (Driving Under the Influence) stay on your record for seven years.

en.question: Under the Nevada demerit point system, your license will be suspended if you receive how many points in any 12-month period?

choices.A: 6 or more points
choices.B: 8 or more points
choices.C: 10 or more points
choices.D: 12 or more points

en.explanation: If you receive 12 or more points in any 12-month period, your license will be suspended.

en.question: If you have accumulated between three and 11 demerit points, how can you have three points removed from your record?

choices.A: By paying a $150 fine to the DMV
choices.B: By completing a traffic safety course at a DMV-approved school
choices.C: By driving violation-free for 6 months
choices.D: By retaking the written driving test

en.explanation: If you have accumulated between three and 11 points, you may have three points removed by completing a traffic safety course at a school approved by the DMV.

en.question: How many demerit points accumulated in a 12-month period will result in a driver's license suspension in Nevada?

choices.A: 8 or more
choices.B: 10 or more
choices.C: 12 or more
choices.D: 15 or more

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you receive 12 or more points in any 12-month period, your license will be suspended.

en.question: How many demerit points are assigned to your driving record for reckless driving?
en.explanation: The manual states that reckless driving is assigned 8 demerit points on your driving record.

en.question: What happens to your demerit points if you are convicted of a major traffic offense, such as a DUI?

choices.A: You receive 12 points.
choices.B: You receive 8 points.
choices.C: You receive 6 points.
choices.D: No demerit points are assigned, but your license is revoked.

en.explanation: A conviction of a major traffic offense, such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm, will result in your license being revoked. These offenses are not assigned demerit points.

en.question: Under Nevada law, it is unlawful to drive with an amount of marijuana in your blood greater than:

choices.A: 2 nanograms per milliliter
choices.B: 5 nanograms per milliliter
choices.C: 8 nanograms per milliliter
choices.D: 10 nanograms per milliliter

en.explanation: It is unlawful for any person to drive with an amount of marijuana in their system greater than two nanograms per milliliter of blood.

en.question: Under Nevada's Implied Consent Law, what is the penalty for failing to submit to a blood, breath, or urine test on your first offense?

choices.A: License revoked for 90 days
choices.B: License revoked for 185 days
choices.C: License revoked for 1 year
choices.D: License revoked for 3 years

en.explanation: If you fail to submit to these tests, your license will be revoked and you will not be eligible for a license for a period of one year for a first offense.

en.question: Under the Illegal Per Se Law, what administrative action is taken if a driver under 21 years of age has an alcohol concentration of .02%?

choices.A: Driver license is suspended for 90 days
choices.B: Driver license is revoked for 185 days
choices.C: Driver license is revoked for 1 year
choices.D: Driver license is revoked for 3 years

en.explanation: For a .02% alcohol concentration for drivers under 21 years of age, the administrative penalty is that the driver license is revoked for 185 days.

en.question: What is the minimum jail sentence or residential confinement for a second DUI offense within 7 years?

choices.A: 2 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 6 months

en.explanation: For a second DUI offense within 7 years, the criminal action includes a jail sentence or residential confinement of 10 days to 6 months.

en.question: What is the prison sentence for a DUI causing death or serious injury?

choices.A: 1 to 6 years
choices.B: 2 to 10 years
choices.C: 2 to 20 years
choices.D: 5 to 25 years

en.explanation: For a DUI causing death or serious injury, the criminal action includes a prison sentence of 2 to 20 years.

en.question: If you hold a Commercial Driver License (CDL), what alcohol concentration will trigger an Illegal Per Se administrative revocation?

choices.A: .02% or more
choices.B: .04% or more but less than .08%
choices.C: .06% or more
choices.D: .10% or more

en.explanation: An Administrative Illegal Per Se Action applies for an alcohol concentration of .04% or more but less than .08% if you hold a commercial driver license.

en.question: How can DUI offenders immediately reinstate their driving privileges?

choices.A: By paying a $1,000 fine
choices.B: By completing 200 hours of community service
choices.C: By installing an ignition interlock device at their own expense
choices.D: By attending a 3-month treatment program

en.explanation: The driving privileges of DUI offenders can be immediately reinstated if a driver license with an ignition interlock restriction is issued and an ignition interlock device is installed in any vehicle the motorist operates at his or her own expense.

en.question: Which of the following actions regarding your Nevada driver's license is illegal?

choices.A: Signing up for a free online DMV account
choices.B: Lending your license to someone else
choices.C: Checking your license expiration date online
choices.D: Printing your driver history

en.explanation: It is illegal to alter your license in any way, lend it to someone else or use another person’s license.

en.question: How many demerit points are assigned for following too closely?
en.explanation: According to the partial list of traffic violations, following too closely is assigned 4 demerit points.

en.question: What is required by the court for a driver under the age of 18 who is found to have been driving under the influence?

choices.A: A minimum 1-year prison sentence
choices.B: Lifetime disqualification from driving
choices.C: Evaluation for alcohol or drug abuse
choices.D: A $2,000 fine

en.explanation: A driver under the age of 18 who is found by juvenile court to have been driving under the influence will be required by the court to undergo evaluation for alcohol or drug abuse.

en.question: What is the fine range for a first DUI offense?
en.explanation: For a first DUI offense, the criminal action includes a fine of $400 to $1,000.

en.question: What is a court requirement for a driver under the age of 21 who is convicted of a DUI?

choices.A: Permanent loss of driving privileges
choices.B: Undergo evaluation for alcohol or drug abuse
choices.C: A minimum of 30 days in jail
choices.D: Surrender of the vehicle's title

en.explanation: A driver under the age of 21 who is convicted of a DUI will be required by the court to undergo evaluation for alcohol or drug abuse.

en.question: Nevada's open container law does NOT apply to which of the following areas?

choices.A: The passenger area of a standard pickup truck
choices.B: The back seat of a standard passenger car
choices.C: The living quarters of a motor home or house trailer
choices.D: The trunk of any vehicle

en.explanation: Nevada's open container law does not apply to the living quarters of motor homes or house trailers, or to the passenger areas of commercial buses, limousines or taxis.

en.question: If you are found guilty of a DUI offense, what will the court consider as an aggravating factor in determining your sentence?

choices.A: Having passengers under the age of 15 in the vehicle
choices.B: Driving a vehicle manufactured before 1968
choices.C: Having an out-of-state driver's license
choices.D: Driving during daylight hours

en.explanation: If you are found guilty of a DUI offense and you had passengers under the age of 15 in the vehicle you were driving, the court will consider that as an aggravating factor in determining your sentence.

en.question: If you plead or are found guilty of a DUI and a chemical test was conducted, what additional fine will the court impose?
en.explanation: If you plead guilty or are found guilty of DUI and a chemical test was conducted, the court will impose an additional $60 fine to cover the costs of the chemical analysis.

en.question: Which of the following driving behaviors is a clue that a driver may be under the influence of alcohol or drugs?

choices.A: Driving with the flow of traffic
choices.B: Using turn signals before changing lanes
choices.C: Driving at night with headlights off
choices.D: Stopping at a red light

en.explanation: Driving at night with headlights off is listed in the manual as one of the clues to driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

en.question: How can you report a suspected drunk driver or highway emergency on a cellular phone anywhere in Nevada?

choices.A: Dial *DUI (*384)
choices.B: Dial *NHP (*647)
choices.C: Dial *SOS (*767)

en.explanation: You can report a suspected drunk driver or any highway emergency on a cellular phone anywhere in Nevada by dialing *NHP (*647).

en.question: A driver's license will be suspended if they accumulate how many demerit points in a 12-month period?

choices.A: 6 or more
choices.B: 8 or more
choices.C: 10 or more
choices.D: 12 or more

en.explanation: A point suspension occurs when a driver accumulates 12 or more demerit points against their license in a 12-month period.

en.question: Your driver's license and vehicle registration will be suspended if you do not have liability insurance and are involved in a crash with more than what amount in damage?
en.explanation: If a crash occurs with more than $750 in damage (personal injury or property damage) and you do not have liability insurance, your driver license and vehicle registration are suspended.

en.question: Which of the following non-driving offenses can result in a person losing their driving privileges in Nevada?

choices.A: Truancy from school
choices.B: Being found guilty of a graffiti violation
choices.C: Violating a city noise ordinance
choices.D: Failing a high school class

en.explanation: A person's license can be suspended or revoked if they are found guilty of a graffiti violation.

en.question: How long do new residents have to register their vehicles after establishing residency in Nevada?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: Drivers must register their vehicles within 30 days of establishing residency in Nevada or at the time they obtain a driver license, whichever occurs earlier.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding vehicle liability insurance for new Nevada residents?

choices.A: Out-of-state insurance is accepted for the first 90 days.
choices.B: Out-of-state insurance is not accepted.
choices.C: Insurance is optional if the vehicle is paid off.
choices.D: You can use out-of-state insurance if your provider is nationally recognized.

en.explanation: Out-of-state insurance is not accepted. You must either notify your insurance carrier that you have moved or purchase a new policy in Nevada.

en.question: What must you do on the same day if you cancel your Nevada vehicle insurance and do not obtain new insurance?

choices.A: Park the vehicle in a private garage
choices.B: Notify the local police department
choices.C: Cancel your Nevada vehicle registration and surrender your license plates
choices.D: Apply for a non-operational permit

en.explanation: If a driver cancels their Nevada insurance and does not obtain new insurance, they must cancel their Nevada vehicle registration and surrender their license plates on the same day.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is exempt from the Emission Control Vehicle Inspection Report (Smog Check) in Clark and Washoe counties?

choices.A: A gasoline-powered vehicle from model year 2010
choices.B: A diesel-powered vehicle from model year 2005
choices.C: A hybrid-electric vehicle that is up to five model years old
choices.D: A gasoline-powered vehicle from model year 1995

en.explanation: Hybrid-electric vehicles that are up to five model years old are exempt from the smog check requirement.

en.question: What happens to a driver's license following a suspension or revocation period?

choices.A: It is automatically reinstated and mailed to the driver.
choices.B: The driver must reapply at a DMV office and pay reinstatement fees.
choices.C: The driver must retake the driving skills test only.
choices.D: The driver's insurance company will reinstate it automatically.

en.explanation: Licenses are not automatically reinstated following suspension or revocation. Drivers must reapply at a DMV office, present required documents, meet requirements, and pay reinstatement fees.

en.question: What slogan does the Nevada DMV use to encourage customers to use their website instead of visiting an office?

choices.A: Skip the wait, update your plate
choices.B: Get online, not in line
choices.C: Drive safe, save time
choices.D: Your DMV, anytime

en.explanation: The manual encourages customers to save time with the slogan 'GET ONLINE, NOT IN LINE' by visiting dmv.nv.gov.

en.question: Approximately how many online services does the Nevada DMV offer?

choices.A: Exactly ten
choices.B: More than a dozen
choices.C: More than two dozen
choices.D: Over fifty

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'The Nevada DMV offers more than two dozen online services.'

en.question: Which of the following is explicitly listed as an online service offered by the Nevada DMV?

choices.A: Address changes
choices.B: Vision tests
choices.C: Driving exams
choices.D: Vehicle inspections

en.explanation: The manual states that online services include 'address changes, movement permits and personalized plate orders.'

en.question: What type of permit can be obtained through the Nevada DMV's online services?

choices.A: Concealed carry permits
choices.B: Movement permits
choices.C: Construction permits
choices.D: Commercial parking permits

en.explanation: The manual lists 'movement permits' as one of the services available online.

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.B: Come to a complete stop

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What does this sign indicate?

choices.A: Left turn only
choices.B: Traffic flows in one direction — to the left
choices.C: Keep left of the median
choices.D: Highway exit to the left

en.explanation: A black and white ONE WAY sign with an arrow indicates that traffic on this street moves in only one direction — the direction the arrow points.

en.question: What does this sign prohibit?

choices.A: Right turns
choices.B: Left turns
choices.C: U-turns
choices.D: Passing other vehicles

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign with a U-turn arrow crossed out means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What does this sign instruct drivers to do?

choices.A: Merge right
choices.B: Turn right only
choices.C: Keep to the right of a divider or obstruction
choices.D: Right lane ends ahead

en.explanation: A white regulatory KEEP RIGHT sign with an arrow means you must keep to the right side of a traffic island, median, or obstruction.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What road condition does this sign warn about?

choices.A: A winding road
choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions
choices.D: A roundabout ahead

en.explanation: A reverse curve sign warns of two curves in opposite directions ahead. Slow down and be prepared for the road to curve first one way, then the other.

en.question: What does this sign warn you to expect?

choices.A: A single sharp curve
choices.B: A slippery road surface
choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead
choices.D: A hill ahead

en.explanation: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves or turns ahead. Reduce your speed and be alert for changing road conditions.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to prepare for?

choices.A: A lane ending
choices.B: Traffic merging from another road
choices.C: A divided highway beginning
choices.D: A road narrowing to one lane

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped merge sign warns that traffic from another road will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed and position.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to expect ahead?

choices.A: A yield sign
choices.B: A traffic signal
choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop
choices.D: A speed bump

en.explanation: This sign warns that there is a stop sign ahead. Begin slowing down and prepare to come to a complete stop at the stop sign.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

es.question: ¿En qué material se basa el examen de conocimientos para su licencia de conducir de Nevada?

choices.A: Únicamente en los Estatutos Revisados de Nevada
choices.B: En la información del Manual del Conductor de Nevada
choices.C: En las pautas federales de conducción
choices.D: En el libro de texto del curso de educación vial

es.explanation: De acuerdo con la introducción del manual, el examen de conocimientos para su licencia de Nevada se basa en la información contenida en este manual.

es.question: Si necesita encontrar la redacción exacta de leyes de tránsito específicas, ¿a qué debe referirse?

choices.A: Al Manual del Conductor de Nevada
choices.B: A los Estatutos Revisados de Nevada (NRS)
choices.C: Al manual del Departamento de Transporte
choices.D: A las pautas del departamento de policía local

es.explanation: El manual establece que no proporciona la redacción exacta de las leyes de tránsito. Para leyes específicas, debe consultar los Estatutos Revisados de Nevada (NRS).

es.question: ¿Dónde puede encontrar copias de los Estatutos Revisados de Nevada (NRS)?

choices.A: Solo en la oficina del DMV
choices.B: En bibliotecas públicas y en línea
choices.C: Exclusivamente en el capitolio estatal
choices.D: Solo comprándolas en la imprenta estatal

es.explanation: La introducción especifica que las copias de los NRS están disponibles en bibliotecas públicas y en línea en leg.state.nv.us/law1.html.

es.question: Según los cambios clave en la edición de 2024 del manual, ¿qué nueva información se agregó con respecto a los peatones?

choices.A: Información sobre los guardias de cruce en zonas escolares
choices.B: Información sobre peatones ciegos
choices.C: Información sobre las sanciones por cruzar la calle imprudentemente
choices.D: Información sobre el derecho de paso de los peatones en las rotondas

es.question: ¿Qué significan las siglas 'DAC' en el Manual del Conductor de Nevada?

choices.A: Tarjeta de Autorización de Conducir (Driver Authorization Card)
choices.B: Curso de Evaluación de Conducción (Driving Assessment Course)
choices.C: Departamento de Control de Automóviles (Department of Automobile Control)
choices.D: Certificación de Concientización del Conductor (Driver Awareness Certification)

es.explanation: El índice del Capítulo 1 enumera la 'Tarjeta de Autorización de Conducir (DAC)' como una sección.

es.question: ¿Qué significan las siglas 'CDL' en las clasificaciones de licencias?

choices.A: Licencia de Conducir Certificada (Certified Driver License)
choices.B: Licencia de Conducir Comercial (Commercial Driver License)
choices.C: Licencia Clase D (Class D License)
choices.D: Licencia de Conducir Urbana (City Driver License)

es.explanation: El índice del Capítulo 1 incluye una sección titulada 'Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL)'.

es.question: Según los cambios clave del manual, ¿qué información se agregó a la página 20?

choices.A: Indicadores médicos
choices.B: Donantes de órganos

choices.D: Tarjetas de identificación

es.explanation: La sección 'Cambios clave en esta edición' establece que se agregó información sobre indicadores médicos en la página 20.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes temas se cubre en la sección 'Conducción en autopistas' del Capítulo 3?

choices.A: Rotondas
choices.B: Carriles para vehículos de alta ocupación (HOV)

es.question: ¿En qué capítulo del Manual del Conductor de Nevada encontrará información sobre 'Niños y mascotas sin supervisión'?

choices.A: Capítulo 1 - Cómo obtener su licencia de conducir de Nevada
choices.B: Capítulo 2 - Abróchese el cinturón
choices.C: Capítulo 3 - Conducir de forma segura
choices.D: Capítulo 4 - Condiciones especiales de conducción

es.question: ¿Cuál es el propósito principal del Manual del Conductor de Nevada?

choices.A: Proporcionar la redacción legal exacta de todas las leyes de tránsito
choices.B: Servir como una guía de defensa legal integral

choices.D: Reemplazar los Estatutos Revisados de Nevada

es.explanation: La introducción establece: 'A medida que lea, encontrará información sobre los conocimientos, habilidades, capacidades y actitudes que necesita para conducir de forma segura'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes se enumera como un subtema bajo 'Rebasar a otro vehículo' en el Capítulo 3?

choices.A: Rebasar ciclistas
choices.B: Rebasar por el arcén (hombro)
choices.C: Rebasar en una zona escolar
choices.D: Rebasar vehículos de emergencia

es.explanation: El índice del Capítulo 3 enumera 'Rebasar ciclistas' y 'Rebasar vehículos estacionados' inmediatamente después de 'Rebasar a otro vehículo'.

es.question: ¿Dónde se encuentra la sede del Departamento de Vehículos Motorizados (DMV) de Nevada según el manual?

choices.A: Las Vegas
choices.B: Reno
choices.C: Carson City
choices.D: Henderson

es.explanation: La página del título indica la dirección del Departamento de Vehículos Motorizados como 555 Wright Way, Carson City, Nevada 89711-0400.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes temas se incluye en el Capítulo 1, 'Obtención de su licencia de conducir de Nevada'?

choices.A: Sistemas de frenos antibloqueo (ABS)
choices.B: Trata de personas – Ningún niño a la venta
choices.C: Teléfonos celulares y mensajes de texto
choices.D: Semáforos de rampa (Ramp meters)

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Trata de personas – Ningún niño a la venta' bajo el Capítulo 1.

es.question: ¿Qué establece el manual sobre su cobertura de las leyes de tránsito?

choices.A: Proporciona la redacción exacta de todas las leyes de tránsito
choices.B: Analiza cada ley de tránsito en Nevada
choices.C: No proporciona la redacción exacta de las leyes de tránsito y no las analiza todas
choices.D: Es el único documento legalmente vinculante para las leyes de tránsito en Nevada

es.explanation: La introducción establece explícitamente: 'Sin embargo, este manual no proporciona la redacción exacta de las leyes de tránsito y no las analiza todas'.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tienen los conductores que se mudan a Nevada desde otro estado para solicitar una licencia de conducir de Nevada?

choices.A: 10 días
choices.B: 15 días
choices.C: 30 días
choices.D: 60 días

es.explanation: Según el manual, los conductores que se mudan a Nevada desde otro estado deben solicitar una licencia dentro de los 30 días posteriores a convertirse en residentes.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes personas que viven o trabajan en Nevada NO está obligada a obtener una licencia de conducir de Nevada?

choices.A: Un trabajador a tiempo parcial de otro estado
choices.B: Un miembro militar estacionado en Nevada
choices.C: Un estudiante universitario que acaba de establecer su residencia
choices.D: Un nuevo residente que se mudó de un país extranjero

es.explanation: El manual establece que se necesita una licencia de conducir de Nevada si vive o trabaja en Nevada, excluyendo a los empleados de estados fronterizos o a los miembros militares estacionados en Nevada.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito de edad mínima para solicitar una licencia de conducir de Nevada?

choices.A: 15 años
choices.B: 15 años y medio
choices.C: 16 años
choices.D: 18 años

es.explanation: Para obtener una licencia de Nevada, debe completar un formulario de solicitud, visitar una oficina del DMV de servicio completo y tener al menos 16 años de edad.

es.question: ¿Para cuál de los siguientes documentos NO es necesario un Número de Seguro Social para obtenerlo en Nevada?

choices.A: Una licencia de conducir comercial
choices.B: Una Tarjeta de Autorización de Conducir (DAC)
choices.C: Una licencia de conducir estándar
choices.D: Una licencia de motocicleta

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente que no es necesario un Número de Seguro Social para obtener una Tarjeta de Autorización de Conducir (DAC).

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo es válida una licencia de conducir de Nevada por primera vez para personas menores de 65 años?

choices.A: 4 años
choices.B: 5 años
choices.C: 8 años
choices.D: 10 años

es.explanation: Una licencia de conducir de Nevada emitida por primera vez a personas menores de 65 años será válida por ocho años.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el período de validez de una licencia de conducir para personas de 65 años o más en Nevada?

choices.A: 2 años
choices.B: 4 años
choices.C: 6 años
choices.D: 8 años

es.explanation: Según el manual, las licencias de conducir para personas de 65 años o más son válidas por cuatro años.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo son válidas las tarjetas de identificación de Nevada?

choices.A: 4 años
choices.B: 5 años
choices.C: 8 años
choices.D: 10 años

es.explanation: El manual establece que las tarjetas de identificación son válidas por ocho años.

es.question: Si presenta documentos de inmigración de duración limitada sin una fecha de salida proporcionada por el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS), ¿cuándo vencerá su licencia de conducir de Nevada?

choices.A: En 1 año
choices.B: En 4 años
choices.C: En 8 años
choices.D: En su próximo cumpleaños

es.explanation: Si se utilizan documentos de inmigración de duración limitada, el vencimiento de su licencia de conducir coincidirá con la fecha de salida verificada por el DHS, o un año si el DHS no proporciona ninguna fecha.

es.question: ¿Qué responsabilidad asume un cosignatario al firmar la solicitud de un conductor menor de 18 años?

choices.A: Debe viajar en el asiento del pasajero en todo momento.
choices.B: Comparte la responsabilidad civil por cualquier daño causado por la negligencia o conducta dolosa del menor mientras conduce.
choices.C: Debe pagar el registro del vehículo del menor.
choices.D: Se le requiere realizar un examen escrito junto con el menor.

es.explanation: Si es menor de 18 años, un cosignatario debe firmar su solicitud. El cosignatario comparte la responsabilidad por cualquier daño causado por la negligencia o conducta dolosa del menor mientras conduce.

es.question: ¿Cuántas licencias de conducir o tarjetas de identificación puede tener un residente de Nevada a la vez?

choices.A: Una licencia de conducir y una tarjeta de identificación
choices.B: Solo una licencia de conducir o una tarjeta de identificación
choices.C: Hasta dos licencias de conducir de diferentes estados
