es.explanation: La señal blanca en forma de X (aspa) de cruce de ferrocarril se coloca en los cruces de vías férreas. Significa que debe ceder el paso a los trenes. Si se aproxima un tren, debe detenerse.

es.question: ¿Qué indica esta señal amarilla en forma de diamante?

choices.A: El camino termina más adelante
choices.B: Se requiere girar a la derecha
choices.C: Una curva a la derecha más adelante
choices.D: Desvío más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de diamante con una flecha curva advierte sobre una curva en el camino más adelante. Reduzca la velocidad antes de entrar en la curva.

es.question: ¿En qué se diferencia esta señal de una señal de curva?

choices.A: Indica un giro menos pronunciado
choices.B: Advierte de un giro brusco que requiere una mayor reducción de velocidad
choices.C: Significa girar a la derecha solamente
choices.D: Solo se utiliza en autopistas

es.explanation: Una señal de giro brusco (con una flecha más angulada) indica un giro más cerrado que una señal de curva. Debe reducir su velocidad de manera más significativa antes de este giro.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué condición de la carretera advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un camino sinuoso
choices.B: Una sola curva más adelante
choices.C: Una serie de dos curvas en direcciones opuestas
choices.D: Una rotonda más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal de curva inversa advierte sobre dos curvas en direcciones opuestas más adelante. Reduzca la velocidad y esté preparado para que el camino gire primero en un sentido y luego en el otro.

es.question: ¿Qué le advierte que espere esta señal?

choices.A: Una sola curva cerrada
choices.B: Una superficie de carretera resbaladiza
choices.C: Una serie de curvas o giros más adelante
choices.D: Una colina más adelante

es.explanation: Una señal de camino sinuoso advierte sobre una serie de curvas o giros más adelante. Reduzca su velocidad y esté alerta a los cambios en las condiciones de la carretera.

es.question: ¿Para qué le indica esta señal que se prepare?

choices.A: Un carril que termina
choices.B: Tráfico que se incorpora desde otra carretera
choices.C: El comienzo de una autopista dividida
choices.D: Una carretera que se estrecha a un solo carril

es.explanation: Una señal amarilla en forma de diamante de incorporación (merge) advierte que el tráfico de otra carretera se incorporará a su carril. Esté preparado para ajustar su velocidad y posición.

es.question: ¿De qué advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Puente más adelante
choices.B: El camino se estrecha más adelante
choices.C: El carril termina
choices.D: La autopista dividida termina

es.explanation: Esta señal de advertencia indica que el camino más adelante se vuelve más estrecho. Esté preparado para una reducción del ancho de la vía y ajuste su posición en el carril.

es.question: ¿Qué indica esta señal que hay más adelante?

choices.A: La carretera termina
choices.B: Tráfico de doble sentido
choices.C: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.D: Salida de la autopista

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que la carretera más adelante se convierte en una autopista dividida con una mediana o barrera que separa el tráfico opuesto. Manténgase a la derecha.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.B: La autopista dividida termina y se reanuda el tráfico de doble sentido
choices.C: Área de incorporación más adelante
choices.D: Construcción de carretera más adelante

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que la autopista dividida está terminando. El tráfico opuesto ya no estará separado por una mediana. Esté preparado para el tráfico de doble sentido.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Comienza una autopista dividida
choices.B: Zona de adelantamiento más adelante
choices.C: Tráfico de doble sentido más adelante: el tráfico se mueve en ambas direcciones
choices.D: Cambio de carril más adelante

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de tráfico de doble sentido más adelante. Es posible que esté saliendo de una vía de un solo sentido o de una autopista dividida y se encuentre con vehículos que viajan en la dirección opuesta.

es.question: ¿Sobre qué condición de la carretera advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Condiciones de carretera con hielo
choices.B: La carretera puede estar resbaladiza cuando está mojada
choices.C: Carretera sinuosa más adelante
choices.D: Pavimento irregular

es.explanation: Una señal de 'resbaladizo cuando está mojado' advierte que la superficie de la carretera puede volverse muy resbaladiza durante la lluvia o condiciones de humedad. Reduzca su velocidad y evite frenar o girar bruscamente.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un bache o resalto en la carretera
choices.B: Una superficie de carretera irregular
choices.C: Una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante
choices.D: Construcción de carretera

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de una colina o pendiente pronunciada más adelante. Es posible que deba ajustar su velocidad y cambiar a una marcha más baja, especialmente en camiones o al remolcar.

es.question: ¿Para qué le advierte esta señal que se prepare?

choices.A: Una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante
choices.B: Un semáforo más adelante
choices.C: Un cruce escolar
choices.D: Un control policial

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de un semáforo más adelante. Esté preparado para detenerse si la luz está en rojo o amarillo. Esta señal a menudo se coloca donde el semáforo puede no ser visible desde la distancia.

es.question: ¿Qué le indica esta señal que espere más adelante?

choices.A: Una señal de ceda el paso
choices.B: Un semáforo
choices.C: Una señal de alto (STOP) donde debe detenerse
choices.D: Un reductor de velocidad

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay una señal de alto (STOP) más adelante. Comience a reducir la velocidad y prepárese para detenerse por completo en la señal de alto.

es.question: ¿De qué advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Un cruce de ferrocarril más adelante
choices.B: Un cruce de caminos o intersección más adelante
choices.C: Un hospital más adelante
choices.D: Un cruce de peatones

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte que hay un cruce de caminos o una intersección de 4 vías más adelante. Esté atento al tráfico que entra desde las carreteras laterales.

es.question: ¿De qué le advierte esta señal?

choices.A: Una intersección en T más adelante
choices.B: Una carretera lateral que entra por la derecha
choices.C: Una curva en la carretera
choices.D: Un callejón sin salida

es.explanation: Esta señal advierte de una carretera lateral que entra por la derecha. Esté atento a los vehículos que entran a la autopista desde la carretera lateral.

es.question: ¿Qué significa esta señal?

choices.A: Los carriles se están fusionando
choices.B: Un carril está terminando
choices.C: Se está añadiendo un nuevo carril: no es necesario incorporarse
choices.D: Giro a la derecha obligatorio

es.explanation: Una señal de carril añadido significa que un nuevo carril se une a la autopista sin requerir incorporación. El tráfico que entra desde la rampa tiene su propio carril nuevo.

es.question: ¿Qué prohíbe esta señal?

choices.A: Detenerse en cualquier momento
choices.B: Estacionarse en esta área
choices.C: Permanecer parado o con el motor encendido
choices.D: Cargar o descargar

es.explanation: Una señal roja y blanca de NO ESTACIONAR (NO PARKING) significa que no puede estacionar su vehículo en esta área. Puede detenerse brevemente para subir o bajar pasajeros.

es.question: ¿Quién tiene permitido estacionarse en un espacio marcado con esta señal?

choices.A: Cualquier persona por menos de 15 minutos
choices.B: Solo personas de la tercera edad
choices.C: Solo vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de discapacidad válido
choices.D: Cualquier conductor con un pasajero que tenga una discapacidad

es.explanation: Una señal azul con el símbolo de la silla de ruedas marca el estacionamiento reservado para personas con discapacidades. Solo los vehículos que exhiban un cartel o placa de matrícula de estacionamiento para personas con discapacidad válido pueden estacionarse en estos espacios. Las infracciones conllevan multas elevadas.

en.question: According to the New York State Donate Life Registry, how many lives can just one person who donates their organs save?

choices.A: Up to 4 lives
choices.B: Up to 6 lives
choices.C: Up to 8 lives
choices.D: Up to 10 lives

en.explanation: The manual states that just one person who donates their organs can save up to eight lives.

en.question: If you hold a valid driver license from another state, what is the minimum age required to drive legally in New York State?
en.explanation: According to the manual, even if you are licensed somewhere else, people under age 16 cannot drive in New York State.

en.question: How many days do you have to get a New York driver license after becoming a permanent resident?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: Drivers who have moved to New York must turn in their out-of-state driver license and get a New York license within 30 days of becoming a permanent resident.

en.question: What is a possible consequence of altering or forging a driver license?

choices.A: A warning letter from the DMV
choices.B: Mandatory community service
choices.C: Suspension or revocation of the license and criminal prosecution
choices.D: A required defensive driving course

en.explanation: It is a crime to alter or forge any motor vehicle document, which may cause suspension or revocation of the driver license and criminal prosecution resulting in a fine or imprisonment.

en.question: You must have a Commercial Driver License (CDL) if you drive a vehicle that is made or used to carry how many persons in addition to the driver?

choices.A: 8 or more
choices.B: 10 or more
choices.C: 12 or more
choices.D: 15 or more

en.explanation: A CDL is required if you drive any vehicle that is made or used to carry 15 or more persons, in addition to the driver.

en.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a Class D Operator license without a driver education Certificate of Completion?
en.explanation: The minimum age for a Class D Operator license is 18, or age 17 with a driver education Certificate of Completion.

en.question: Which classes of mopeds are you allowed to operate with a standard Class D Operator license?

choices.A: Class A only
choices.B: Class B and C mopeds
choices.C: Class A and B mopeds
choices.D: No mopeds are allowed without a motorcycle license

en.explanation: The manual states that you can operate Class B and C mopeds with a Class D driver license.

en.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a Class DJ (Junior Operator) license?
en.explanation: The minimum age to obtain a Junior Operator, Class DJ license is 16.

en.question: Which class of license is required to transport passengers for hire in a vehicle designed to carry 14 or fewer passengers, such as a taxi or livery?

choices.A: Class C
choices.B: Class D
choices.C: Class E
choices.D: Class M

en.explanation: A Taxi/Livery, Class E license allows you to transport passengers for hire in a vehicle designed or used to carry 14 or fewer passengers.

en.question: An Enhanced Driver License can be used instead of a passport for which type of travel?

choices.A: International air travel to Europe
choices.B: Land and sea border crossings to and from Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean
choices.C: Any international travel worldwide
choices.D: Travel to South America by cruise ship

en.explanation: An Enhanced Driver License can be used for land and sea border crossings to and from the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean instead of a passport.

en.question: A Commercial Driver License (CDL) is required to drive a single vehicle with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of more than:

choices.A: 10,000 pounds
choices.B: 15,000 pounds
choices.C: 20,000 pounds
choices.D: 26,000 pounds

en.explanation: You must have a CDL if you drive any vehicle that has a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of more than 26,000 pounds.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding holding multiple driver licenses?

choices.A: You may hold a New York license and an out-of-state license simultaneously.
choices.B: It is illegal in most cases to hold a New York driver license and a driver license from another state at the same time.
choices.C: You are required to hold a license for every state you frequently drive in.
choices.D: You may hold up to two commercial driver licenses (CDL) legally.

en.explanation: In most cases, it is illegal to hold a New York driver license and a driver license from another state at the same time. It is also a violation of Federal and state law to hold more than one CDL.

en.question: A Class DJ (Junior Operator) license allows you to drive a vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of no more than:

choices.A: 5,000 pounds
choices.B: 10,000 pounds
choices.C: 15,000 pounds
choices.D: 26,000 pounds

en.explanation: A Junior Operator, Class DJ license allows you to drive a vehicle with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or less.

en.question: You must have a Commercial Driver License (CDL) if you drive a vehicle that:

choices.A: Carries any amount of commercial goods
choices.B: Is used for farming purposes only
choices.C: Carries hazardous materials required by federal law to contain a placard
choices.D: Tows a trailer weighing 2,000 pounds

en.explanation: The manual specifies that you must have a CDL if you drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials required by federal law to contain a placard.

en.question: If you have a motorcycle license and another type of driver license, how will they be displayed?

choices.A: On two separate documents
choices.B: Both classes will be listed on one document
choices.C: You must choose only one to be active
choices.D: The motorcycle license replaces the other license

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you have a motorcycle license and another type of driver license, both classes will be listed on one document (e.g., 'Class DM').

en.question: According to the REAL ID Act, what must every air traveler flying within the United States present to get through security at U.S. airports?

choices.A: A valid U.S. passport only
choices.B: A REAL ID, an Enhanced Driver License, or another acceptable form of federal identification
choices.C: A standard state-issued driver license and a birth certificate
choices.D: A Social Security card and a utility bill

en.explanation: Every air traveler flying within the United States must present a REAL ID, an Enhanced Driver License, or bring another acceptable form of identification determined by the federal government.

en.question: The Personal Use Vehicle 'R' endorsement is required for operating recreational or rental vehicles used to transport personal household goods if the vehicle exceeds what specifications?

choices.A: 10,000 pounds GVWR and/or 20 feet in length
choices.B: 18,000 pounds GVWR and/or 30 feet in length
choices.C: 26,000 pounds GVWR and/or 40 feet in length
choices.D: 32,000 pounds GVWR and/or 50 feet in length

en.explanation: The 'R' endorsement is required for operation of recreational and/or rental vehicles used to transport personal household goods when the vehicle is over 26,000 pounds GVWR and/or forty (40) feet in length.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the testing requirements to obtain an 'R' endorsement?

choices.A: You must pass both a written test and a road test.
choices.B: You must pass a written test, but no road test is required.
choices.C: No written test is required, but you must pass a road test.
choices.D: Neither a written test nor a road test is required.

en.explanation: To get an 'R' endorsement, you must pass a road test in the size and type of vehicle you will drive. The manual explicitly states, 'No written test is required.'

en.question: Who must accompany you for your 'R' endorsement road test?

choices.A: A licensed driving instructor.
choices.B: Any licensed driver over the age of 18.
choices.C: A driver who is at least 21 years old with a license valid for the vehicle you will drive during the test.
choices.D: A DMV official who holds a Commercial Driver License.

en.explanation: For the road test, a driver who is at least 21 years old, with a license valid for the vehicle you will drive during the test, must accompany you.

en.question: For how long will your first New York driver license be issued?

choices.A: Exactly 10 years
choices.B: A period not to exceed 5 years, on your month and day of birth
choices.C: A period not to exceed 8 years, on your month and day of birth
choices.D: Until you turn 21 years old

en.explanation: Your first New York driver license will be issued for a period not to exceed 5 years, on your month and day of birth.

en.question: When applying for your first license, you must present documents that prove your name. How many points must these proofs total?

choices.A: Four points or more
choices.B: Six points or more
choices.C: Eight points or more
choices.D: Ten points or more

en.explanation: Documents that prove your name are assigned a point value. You must present proofs that total six points or more.

en.question: When submitting documents to prove your name for a driver license application, what is a specific requirement for at least one of the proofs?

choices.A: It must contain your photograph.
choices.B: It must be issued by the federal government.
choices.C: It must have your signature.
choices.D: It must show your current residential address.

en.explanation: The manual states that when presenting proofs of your name that total six points or more, 'At least one of the proofs must have your signature.'

en.question: Which of the following documents has a value of 6 points when proving your name for a New York driver license?

choices.A: A valid U.S. Passport
choices.B: A U.S. Social Security Card
choices.C: A New York Photo Driver License or Non-Driver ID Card
choices.D: A U.S. Military Photo Identification Card

en.explanation: A New York Photo Driver License/Permit/Non-Driver ID Card (current or not expired for more than 2 years) has a value of 6 points.

en.question: How many points is a valid U.S. Passport worth when proving your identity for a New York driver license?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 6 points

en.explanation: According to the list of acceptable documents, a valid U.S. Passport or Passport Card has a value of 4 points.

en.question: If your proof of identity documents are not in English, what must you provide?

choices.A: A certified English translation
choices.B: A notarized letter from a U.S. citizen
choices.C: An international driving permit
choices.D: A verbal translation at the DMV office

en.explanation: The manual states that all proofs must be in English or accompanied by a certified English translation.

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable document to prove your date of birth?

choices.A: A U.S. High School Photo ID with Report Card
choices.B: A U.S. Utility Bill
choices.C: A U.S. Military Photo Identification Card
choices.D: A U.S. Major Credit Card

en.explanation: Under the 'Proof of Age' section, a U.S. Military Photo Identification Card is listed as an acceptable document to prove your date of birth.

en.question: To pass the vision test for a New York driver license, what visual acuity must you have in at least one eye?
en.explanation: To pass the vision test, you must have 20/40 vision in at least one eye with or without corrective lenses.

en.question: In addition to passing a vision and knowledge test, what must most drivers complete before taking a road test for their first license?

choices.A: A 10-hour defensive driving course
choices.B: An approved 5-hour Pre-Licensing Course
choices.C: A 15-hour behind-the-wheel training program
choices.D: A certified first aid and CPR class

en.explanation: The manual states that most drivers must also complete an approved 5-hour Pre-Licensing Course and pass a road test when applying for their first license.

en.question: What is the minimum vision requirement to pass the vision test for a New York driver's license?

choices.A: 20/20 vision in both eyes
choices.B: 20/30 vision in at least one eye
choices.C: 20/40 vision in at least one eye
choices.D: 20/50 vision in both eyes

en.explanation: According to the manual, to pass the vision test, you must have 20/40 vision in at least one eye with or without corrective lenses.

en.question: To pass the written test for a Class D license, how many questions must you answer correctly overall?

choices.A: At least 10 out of 20
choices.B: At least 14 out of 20
choices.C: At least 16 out of 20
choices.D: All 20 questions

en.explanation: The manual states that to pass the written test, you must correctly answer at least 14 of the 20 questions asked.

en.question: How many road sign questions must you answer correctly to pass the written knowledge test?

choices.A: One out of four
choices.B: Two out of four
choices.C: Three out of four
choices.D: Four out of four

en.explanation: The manual specifies that you must correctly answer two of the four questions about road signs to pass the written test.

en.question: What is the minimum age required for a student to take the written test through the DMV Online Knowledge Test Application (OKTA) program at a participating high school?

choices.A: 15 years old
choices.B: 15 years and 6 months old
choices.C: 15 years and 11 months old
choices.D: 16 years old

en.explanation: Before applying for a learner permit, students who are at least age 15 and 11 months can take the written test through the OKTA program.

en.question: When practicing driving with a learner permit, what are the requirements for your supervising driver?

choices.A: Must be at least 18 and have any valid license
choices.B: Must be at least 21, have a valid license for the vehicle type, and sit in the front seat
choices.C: Must be a licensed driving instructor
choices.D: Must be at least 25 and sit in the back seat

en.explanation: When you practice, you must be supervised by a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old, has a license valid for the type of vehicle you are driving, and is seated in the front seat with you.

en.question: If you have a Junior Permit and are driving in New York City (5 Boroughs) between 5 AM and 9 PM, what special equipment must the vehicle have?

choices.A: A backup camera
choices.B: A student driver sign
choices.C: Dual controls (dual brakes)
choices.D: Extra side mirrors

en.explanation: Under the regional restrictions for a Junior Permit in New York City between 5 AM and 9 PM, the vehicle must have dual controls (dual brakes).

en.question: Under a Junior Permit in Upstate New York (All Other Counties), who must supervise you if you drive between 9 PM and 5 AM?

choices.A: Any licensed driver over 18
choices.B: Any licensed driver over 21
choices.C: You must NOT drive during these hours
choices.D: Your parent, guardian, person 'in loco parentis,' driver education teacher, or driving school instructor

en.explanation: In Upstate counties between 9 PM and 5 AM, a Junior Permit holder must drive only under the immediate supervision of a parent, guardian, person 'in loco parentis,' driver education teacher, or driving school instructor.

en.question: According to the general rules for all drivers with learner permits, where are you strictly prohibited from driving?

choices.A: On any street within a park in New York City
choices.B: On any interstate highway
choices.C: In school zones during school hours
choices.D: On roads with a speed limit over 40 mph

en.explanation: If you hold a learner permit, you cannot drive on any street within a park in New York City or any bridge or tunnel under the jurisdiction of the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority.

en.question: Which of the following parkways in Westchester County are you NOT allowed to drive on with a learner permit?

choices.A: Northern State Parkway
choices.B: Taconic State Parkway
choices.C: Garden State Parkway
choices.D: Palisades Interstate Parkway

en.explanation: Learner permit holders cannot drive on the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River, or Taconic State parkways in Westchester County.

en.question: If you hold a Junior Learner Permit, what is the rule regarding passengers under the age of 21?

choices.A: You cannot have any passengers under 21
choices.B: You can have up to three passengers under 21
choices.C: You cannot drive with more than one passenger under 21 unless they are immediate family or your supervisor is a parent/guardian/instructor
choices.D: You can have as many passengers under 21 as there are seat belts

en.explanation: You cannot drive with more than one passenger under the age of 21 unless they are members of your immediate family or if your supervising driver is your parent, guardian, person 'in loco parentis,' driver education teacher or driving school instructor.

en.question: If you hold a junior permit, who is the only passenger allowed to sit in the front seat with you?

choices.A: Your supervising driver
choices.B: A sibling under 18
choices.C: Any passenger over 21
choices.D: No one is allowed in the front seat

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'If you hold a junior permit, the only passenger allowed in the front seat is your supervising driver.'

en.question: Before taking your road test, how many total hours of supervised driving practice is it important that you have completed?

choices.A: At least 20 hours
choices.B: At least 30 hours
choices.C: At least 40 hours
choices.D: At least 50 hours

en.explanation: Before you take the test, it is important that you have had at least 50 hours of practice.

en.question: Out of the total recommended hours of supervised driving practice before a road test, how many hours must be completed after sunset?

choices.A: At least 5 hours
choices.B: At least 10 hours
choices.C: At least 15 hours
choices.D: At least 20 hours

en.explanation: The manual states it is important to have at least 50 hours of practice, with at least 15 hours after sunset.

en.question: What must you complete before you can make a road test appointment?

choices.A: An advanced defensive driving course
choices.B: An approved safe driver course (Pre-Licensing course or driver education)
choices.C: A highway driving certification
choices.D: A vision re-test

en.explanation: Before you can make a road test appointment, you must first complete an approved safe driver course, which is fulfilled by a high school/college driver education course or a Pre-Licensing course.

en.question: If you have a Junior Permit and are driving in Long Island (Nassau & Suffolk) between 9 PM and 5 AM, what are the restrictions?

choices.A: You must be supervised by a parent or guardian
choices.B: You must NOT drive
choices.C: You must be supervised by any licensed driver over 21
choices.D: You can drive alone if going to work

en.explanation: According to the Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit chart, in Long Island (Nassau & Suffolk) between 9 PM and 5 AM, 'You must NOT drive.'

en.question: How long is the Pre-Licensing Course completion certificate valid for?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 years
choices.D: 5 years

en.explanation: According to the manual, when you complete the safe driving course, you will receive a certificate that is valid for one year.

en.question: Does the DMV-certified Point & Insurance Reduction Program (Defensive Driving Course) meet the Safe Driving course requirement for scheduling a road test?

choices.A: Yes, if completed online.
choices.B: Yes, for drivers over 18.
choices.C: No, it does not meet the requirement.
choices.D: Yes, if completed within the last 6 months.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'The DMV-certified Point & Insurance Reduction Program (a.k.a. Accident Prevention Course or Defensive Driving Course) does NOT meet the Safe Driving course requirement.'

en.question: At what age are you eligible to change a junior driver license to a senior driver license if you have completed a state-approved driver education course?
en.explanation: If you are 17, you are eligible for a senior driver license (Class D or M) if you have a junior driver license and have completed a state-approved high school or college driver education course.

en.question: How long must a junior driver hold their permit in valid status before they are allowed to take the road test?

choices.A: A minimum of 3 months
choices.B: A minimum of 6 months
choices.C: A minimum of 9 months
choices.D: A minimum of 12 months

en.explanation: For Junior Drivers with Permits, the manual states: 'Your permit must be held, in valid status for a minimum of six months in order to take the road test.'

en.question: How many hours of supervised practice driving must a parent or guardian certify that a junior driver has completed prior to the road test?

choices.A: 30 hours, including 10 hours after sunset
choices.B: 40 hours, including 10 hours after sunset
choices.C: 50 hours, including 15 hours after sunset
choices.D: 60 hours, including 15 hours after sunset

en.explanation: The Certification of Supervised Driving (MV-262) requires a parent or guardian to certify that the driver completed at least 50 hours of practice driving, including at least 15 hours after sunset.

en.question: What is a requirement for the supervising driver who accompanies you to the road test site?

choices.A: They must be at least 18 years old.
choices.B: They must be at least 21 years old and hold a valid license for the vehicle.
choices.C: They must be a certified driving instructor.
choices.D: They must be a parent or legal guardian.

en.explanation: If you drive to the road test site, you must bring a supervising driver who is at least 21 and holds a license valid for the vehicle you will drive during the road test.

en.question: What must motorcycle applicants bring to their road test to transport the license examiner?

choices.A: A motorcycle with a sidecar
choices.B: A second motorcycle for the examiner
choices.C: A car or truck and a licensed driver
choices.D: A certified motorcycle instructor

en.explanation: Motorcycle applicants must bring a car or truck and a licensed driver to transport the license examiner during the test.

en.question: How many points can be reduced from your driving record if you complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP)?

choices.A: Up to 2 points
choices.B: Up to 3 points
choices.C: Up to 4 points
choices.D: Up to 5 points

en.explanation: If you are eligible for point reduction, as many as four (4) points can be reduced from your driving record by completing the PIRP course.

en.question: How often can you complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP) for the purpose of point reduction?

choices.A: Every 12 months
choices.B: Every 18 months
choices.C: Every 2 years
choices.D: Every 3 years

en.explanation: You can complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program course every 18 months for the purpose of point reduction.

en.question: When driving with a Junior License, how many passengers under the age of 21 are allowed in the vehicle if they are NOT members of your immediate family?

choices.A: None
choices.B: No more than one
choices.C: No more than two
choices.D: No more than three

en.explanation: Under Junior Operator Restrictions, you cannot drive with more than one passenger under the age of 21 unless they are members of your immediate family.

en.question: According to the regional restrictions for a Junior License, when are you allowed to drive in New York City (the 5 Boroughs)?

choices.A: Between 5 AM and 9 PM only
choices.B: Only when accompanied by a parent or guardian
choices.C: Only when driving to or from school
choices.D: You must NOT drive at any time

en.explanation: The regional restrictions chart for a Junior License clearly states that in New York City (5 Boroughs), 'You must NOT drive' between 5AM - 9PM and 'You must NOT drive' between 9PM - 5AM.

en.question: If you hold a Junior License and drive in Upstate counties between 5 AM and 9 PM, what are the restrictions on driving alone?

choices.A: You may drive without being accompanied.
choices.B: You must be accompanied by a licensed parent or guardian.
choices.C: You may only drive alone to employment or school.
choices.D: You must not drive.

en.explanation: According to the regional restrictions chart, in Upstate (All Other Counties) between 5AM - 9PM, 'You may drive without being accompanied.'

en.question: What specific proof of employment must a Junior License holder carry to drive to work in Nassau or Suffolk counties?

choices.A: A recent pay stub
choices.B: A Certificate of Employment (MV-58A)
choices.C: A letter from their employer
choices.D: A copy of their work schedule

en.explanation: If you hold a Junior License and drive in the counties of Nassau or Suffolk, your employer can complete a Certificate of Employment (MV-58A) to serve as correct proof of employment.

en.question: What is a specific requirement for the passenger side seat belt in the vehicle used for a road test?

choices.A: It must be a five-point harness.
choices.B: It must be available and clean for use by the examiner.
choices.C: It must be inspected by a mechanic prior to the test.
choices.D: It must be disabled if the examiner prefers.

en.explanation: The manual states that the vehicle must be in good working order, and specifically notes: 'The passenger side seat belt must be available and clean for use by the examiner.'

en.question: What passenger restriction applies to a learner permit or junior license for a motorcycle or moped (Class M or MJ)?

choices.A: You may carry one passenger if they are wearing a helmet.
choices.B: You may carry immediate family members only.
choices.C: You cannot carry any passenger except your supervising driver.
choices.D: You may carry any passenger over the age of 21.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Your learner permit or junior license (Class M or MJ) does not allow you to carry any passenger except your supervising driver.'

en.question: Who is permitted to ride as a passenger when you are operating a motorcycle or moped with a Class M or MJ learner permit?

choices.A: Any family member
choices.B: Only your supervising driver
choices.C: Anyone over the age of 18
choices.D: No passengers are allowed under any circumstances

en.explanation: According to the manual, a learner permit or junior license (Class M or MJ) does not allow you to carry any passenger except your supervising driver.

en.question: How close must a supervising driver remain when you are operating a motorcycle or moped with a learner permit?

choices.A: Within 100 feet
choices.B: Within one-quarter mile
choices.C: Within one-half mile
choices.D: Within one mile

en.explanation: The manual states that your supervising driver must exercise general supervision and control by remaining within one-quarter mile.

en.question: How many days do you have to notify the DMV if you change your residential address?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: If you change your address, you must notify the DMV within 10 days by mail, on a Change-of-Address Form, or online.

en.question: How early can you renew your driver license before its printed expiration date?

choices.A: Up to 30 days
choices.B: Up to 45 days
choices.C: Up to 6 months
choices.D: Up to one year

en.explanation: The manual states that you can renew your license up to one year before its printed expiration date.

en.question: When applying for a REAL ID at the DMV, how many proofs of New York State residence must you provide?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: To get a REAL ID, you MUST bring to the office two proofs of New York State residence such as a utility bill or mortgage statement.

en.question: If you are renewing your driver license by mail or online, you must prove you have passed an eye test within what time frame?

choices.A: The past 30 days
choices.B: The past 60 days
choices.C: The past six months
choices.D: The past two years

en.explanation: If you renew by mail or through the DMV website, you must prove you have passed an eye test within the past six months (or within one year as determined by a licensed health care professional).

en.question: How long is your driver license automatically extended after being discharged from active military service?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: Six months
choices.D: One year

en.explanation: If you enter military service, your license can be automatically extended throughout your active service and for six months after discharge.

en.question: After establishing residency in New York State, how long do you have to apply for a New York driver license?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: To remain legally licensed, you must apply for a New York driver license within 30 days after you establish you are a New York State resident.

en.question: If you are 15 years old and hold a valid out-of-state driver license, what are the rules for driving in New York State?

choices.A: You may drive only if accompanied by a parent.
choices.B: You may drive during daylight hours only.
choices.C: You cannot drive in New York State under any circumstances.
choices.D: You may drive if you obtain a New York junior permit.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "If you are less than 16 years of age, you cannot drive in New York State even if you have an out-of-state license."

en.question: What does it mean if your driver license is "revoked"?

choices.A: It is taken away for a temporary period and automatically returned.
choices.B: It is cancelled and you must re-apply to the DMV once the period is over.
choices.C: You must pay a fine but can continue driving.
choices.D: You are restricted to driving only to and from work.

en.explanation: "Revocation" means your license (or privilege to drive) is cancelled. To get a new license, you must re-apply to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) once the revocation period is over.

en.question: How long will a junior permit or license be suspended if the driver is convicted of a serious traffic violation worth three or more points?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: Your permit, license or privileges will be suspended for 60 days if you are convicted of a serious traffic violation (three points or more) or two other violations.

en.question: What is the penalty for a driver with a junior permit who is convicted of a texting or cell phone violation?

choices.A: A 30-day suspension
choices.B: A 60-day suspension
choices.C: A 120-day suspension
choices.D: A permanent revocation

en.explanation: Your junior permit, license or privileges will be suspended for 120 days when you are convicted of a texting or cell phone violation.

en.question: What is the minimum amount of time you must hold a junior permit before you can schedule a road test?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 3 months
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: A junior permit must be held for a minimum of six months, excluding any time the permit is suspended or revoked, before a road test can be scheduled.

en.question: How long is the probation period for a newly licensed driver who is 18 or older when they pass their road test?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: If you are 18 or older when you pass your road test for a driver license, or obtain a license following revocation, you will be on probation for six months.

en.question: Which of the following convictions will result in a 60-day suspension for a newly licensed driver during their six-month probation period?

choices.A: A single parking ticket
choices.B: Speeding
choices.C: Failing to notify the DMV of an address change
choices.D: Driving with an expired inspection sticker

en.explanation: If you are convicted of DWAI (alcohol), speeding, reckless driving, following too closely, participating in a speed contest, or any two traffic violations while on probation, your license will be suspended for 60 days.

en.question: If you are convicted of a texting or cell phone violation while on a probationary license, how long will your license be suspended?

choices.A: 60 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 120 days
choices.D: 6 months

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are convicted of a texting or cell phone violation, your probationary license will be suspended for 120 days.

en.question: What is a possible consequence if you receive a traffic ticket and do not respond to it?

choices.A: Your vehicle will be immediately impounded.
choices.B: You could be found guilty by default conviction and your license suspended indefinitely.
choices.C: You will automatically receive 3 points on your driving record.
choices.D: You will be required to take a mandatory defensive driving course.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you do not respond that you have received the ticket, you could be found guilty by default conviction and your driver license will be suspended indefinitely.

en.question: From which of the following areas outside of New York State will moving traffic convictions be added to your New York State 'violation point' driving record?

choices.A: New Jersey and Pennsylvania
choices.B: Ontario and Quebec
choices.C: California and Florida
choices.D: All Canadian provinces

en.explanation: The New York State DMV does not record convictions of moving traffic violations in other jurisdictions, except traffic offenses committed in the provinces of Ontario and Quebec in Canada.

en.question: If you are over 21 years old and are convicted of an alcohol- or drug-related driving violation in another state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least:

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: If you are over 21 years old and are convicted of an alcohol- or drug-related driving violation (e.g., DUI) in another state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least 90 days.

en.question: What is the penalty if a driver under 21 years old is convicted of an alcohol or drug-related violation that occurred out of state?

choices.A: A 90-day suspension
choices.B: A 6-month revocation
choices.C: Revocation for at least one year
choices.D: A warning and a $500 fine

en.explanation: If you are under 21 years old and convicted of any alcohol or drug-related violation that occurred out of state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least one year.

en.question: What is the minimum revocation period for Aggravated driving while intoxicated (Agg-DWI) with a .18 blood alcohol content?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: 18 months

en.explanation: Aggravated driving while intoxicated (Agg-DWI), with .18 of one percent blood alcohol content (.18 BAC) carries a minimum one-year revocation.

en.question: A conviction for Driving while ability impaired by alcohol (DWAI) will result in a:

choices.A: 90-day suspension
choices.B: Six-month revocation
choices.C: One-year revocation
choices.D: 120-day suspension

en.explanation: The manual lists the penalty for Driving while ability impaired by alcohol (DWAI) as a 90-day suspension.

en.question: If a driver over age 21 refuses to take a chemical test for the first time, their license will be revoked for a minimum of:

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: 18 months

en.explanation: A chemical test refusal for drivers over age 21 results in a minimum one-year revocation.

en.question: Under the state's 'Zero Tolerance Law,' what happens if a driver under age 21 is found to have a BAC from .02 to .07?

choices.A: Their license is suspended for 90 days.
choices.B: Their license is suspended for six months.
choices.C: Their license is revoked for one year.
choices.D: They receive 3 points on their license.

en.explanation: Under the state's 'Zero Tolerance Law,' a driver under age 21 will have their license suspended for six months if found to have a BAC from .02 to .07.

en.question: Your driver license will be revoked for at least six months if you are found guilty of how many speeding and/or misdemeanor traffic violations within 18 months?

choices.A: Two
choices.B: Three
choices.C: Four
choices.D: Five

en.explanation: Your driver license will be revoked for at least six months if you are found guilty of three speeding and/or misdemeanor traffic violations within 18 months.

en.question: What is the penalty for operating an uninsured vehicle or allowing another person to operate your uninsured vehicle?

choices.A: A 90-day suspension
choices.B: A six-month suspension
choices.C: Revocation for at least one year
choices.D: An indefinite suspension until insurance is purchased

en.explanation: Your driver license will be revoked for at least one year if you operate or allow another person to operate your uninsured vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following will result in an indefinite suspension of your driver license?

choices.A: Failing to pay child support
choices.B: Getting two speeding tickets in a year
choices.C: Refusing a chemical test
choices.D: Passing a stopped school bus once

en.explanation: Your driver license will be suspended indefinitely if you fail to file an accident report, fail to pay child support, fail to pay taxes, or fail to fulfill a court judgment.

en.question: According to the DMV point system, how many points will you receive for speeding 21 to 30 MPH over the posted limit?

choices.A: 3 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: The point system table indicates that speeding 21 to 30 MPH over the posted limit results in 6 points.

en.question: How many points are added to your driving record for the use of a mobile telephone or portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.explanation: According to the point system table, the use of a mobile telephone or portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle results in 5 points.

en.question: When are point values charged against your driving record?

choices.A: On the date you are convicted
choices.B: On the date you commit the violation
choices.C: On the date you pay the ticket
choices.D: On the date the DMV processes the citation

en.explanation: According to the manual, the point values charged against your record are from the date you commit the violation, not the date you are convicted.

en.question: How many points accumulated within an 18-month period will result in a notification that your driver license will be suspended?

choices.A: 6 or more points
choices.B: 8 or more points
choices.C: 11 or more points
choices.D: 15 or more points

en.explanation: The manual states that if you get 11 or more points within 18 months, you will be notified by mail that your driver license will be suspended.

en.question: What is a benefit of taking a DMV-approved 'Motor Vehicle Accident Prevention Course'?

choices.A: It prevents a mandatory license suspension.
choices.B: It acts as a credit against future points.
choices.C: It reduces your Driver Responsibility Assessment fee.
choices.D: It can reduce your point total by up to four points.

en.explanation: You can reduce your point total by up to four points and save up to 10 percent on your auto liability and collision insurance premiums by taking a DMV-approved course.

en.question: If you are involved in a traffic crash in which another person is killed, what action can the DMV take even if you were not charged with a violation?

choices.A: Your license can be suspended or revoked after a DMV hearing.
choices.B: You will automatically be charged with vehicular manslaughter.
choices.C: You will be required to pay a $750 civil penalty.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be seized and forfeited immediately.

en.explanation: If you are involved in a traffic crash in which another person is killed, your license can be suspended or revoked after a DMV hearing even if you were not charged with a violation.

en.question: What is the non-refundable suspension termination fee in most cases if your driver license has been suspended for an exact period, like 30 or 90 days?

choices.A: 25 dollars
choices.B: 50 dollars
choices.C: 100 dollars
choices.D: 125 dollars

en.explanation: In most cases, if your driver license has been suspended for an exact period, your license will not be returned until you pay a non-refundable $50 suspension termination fee.

en.question: Under the 2019 law regarding stop-arm cameras on school buses, what is the penalty for a first violation of passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights?

choices.A: 100 dollars
choices.B: 150 dollars
choices.C: 250 dollars
choices.D: 300 dollars

en.explanation: The manual states that a first violation for passing a school bus caught on a stop-arm camera results in a penalty of $250.

en.question: What is the civil penalty for a chemical test refusal while driving a standard (non-commercial) motor vehicle?

choices.A: 250 dollars
choices.B: 500 dollars
choices.C: 550 dollars
choices.D: 750 dollars

en.explanation: The civil penalty for a chemical test refusal is $500 ($550 if while driving a commercial motor vehicle).

en.question: If you are convicted of Driving While Intoxicated (DWI), how much is the Driver Responsibility Assessment you must pay each year for three years?

choices.A: 100 dollars
choices.B: 150 dollars
choices.C: 250 dollars
choices.D: 500 dollars

en.explanation: If you are convicted of DWI, you will be required to pay a driver responsibility assessment of $250 each year for the next three years.

en.question: If you receive six points on your driving record in an 18-month period, you must pay a Driver Responsibility Assessment of $100 each year for three years. How much must you pay for each additional point received during that period?

choices.A: 10 dollars per point every year for three years
choices.B: 25 dollars per point every year for three years
choices.C: 50 dollars per point every year for three years
choices.D: 100 dollars per point every year for three years

en.explanation: For each additional point you receive during that period, you will be required to pay another $25 per point every year for three years.

en.question: Which of the following is a potential consequence of driving while your license is suspended or revoked?

choices.A: A mandatory fine of $50 to $100
choices.B: Mandatory community service for 100 hours
choices.C: Mandatory fines from $200 to $5,000 and possible vehicle seizure
choices.D: A permanent ban from obtaining a driver license in any state

en.explanation: It is a criminal offense to drive while your license is suspended or revoked, and there are mandatory fines from $200 to $5,000. The vehicle being driven could also be seized and forfeited.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of a title certificate?

choices.A: It allows a vehicle to be driven on public roads.
choices.B: It proves who owns the vehicle.
choices.C: It proves the vehicle has passed safety inspection.
choices.D: It serves as proof of auto liability insurance.

en.explanation: A registration allows a vehicle to be driven on public roads and highways. A title certificate proves who owns the vehicle.

en.question: What is the minimum age required to register a vehicle in New York State?

choices.D: There is no age requirement to register a vehicle.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'You must be at least 16 to register a vehicle. You can title a vehicle at any age.'

en.question: How many days does a new resident of New York State have to get a New York vehicle registration after establishing residence?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: A new resident of the state must get a New York registration within 30 days of establishing residence.

en.question: If you purchase a vehicle from someone other than a New York State registered dealership, how many days do you have to get the vehicle inspected after registering it?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: If you purchased the vehicle from someone other than a New York State registered dealership, you will receive a 10-day inspection extension sticker... You must then have the vehicle inspected within 10 days from the date of registration.

en.question: Under what condition will a motor vehicle office refuse to accept a title certificate?

choices.A: If the vehicle is more than 10 years old
choices.B: If the title certificate is folded or creased
choices.C: If information on the title is adjusted, erased, or canceled
choices.D: If the vehicle was previously registered in another state

en.explanation: A motor vehicle office will not accept a title certificate if the correct odometer or damage disclosure statement is not completed, or if information on the title is adjusted, erased or canceled.

en.question: What will happen if information on a title certificate, such as a name or signature, is adjusted, erased, or canceled?

choices.A: The DMV will charge an additional processing fee.
choices.B: The DMV will not accept the title certificate.
choices.C: The buyer must pay sales tax based on fair market value.
choices.D: The title will automatically be marked as 'Rebuilt Salvage.'

en.explanation: According to the manual, a motor vehicle office will not accept a title certificate if information on the title is adjusted, erased, or canceled, which includes any name or signature.

en.question: If you purchase a vehicle that is eight model years old or newer, what statements must be completed on the Certificate of Title?

choices.A: Only the odometer statement.
choices.B: Only the damage disclosure statement.
choices.C: Both the odometer and the damage disclosure statements.
choices.D: Neither statement is required for vehicles under ten years old.

en.explanation: The manual states that for a vehicle eight model years old or newer, the DMV will not register or title it unless the seller has completed, and the buyer has signed, both the odometer and the damage disclosure statements.

en.question: What must the DMV do before a vehicle described as 'Rebuilt Salvage' can be registered or titled?

choices.A: Examine the vehicle for stolen parts.
choices.B: Perform a strict emissions test.
choices.C: Verify the vehicle's fair market value.
choices.D: Issue a new vehicle identification number (VIN).

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'The DMV must examine every vehicle described as "Rebuilt Salvage", OR SIMILAR WORDS, for stolen parts before the vehicle can be registered or titled.'

en.question: When purchasing a vehicle from a private seller, what happens if the seller does not complete their side of the Statement of Transaction form for a vehicle sold below fair market value?

choices.A: The registration application will be permanently denied.
choices.B: You will be charged sales tax based on the current fair market value of the vehicle.
choices.C: You will be exempt from paying sales tax.
choices.D: The seller will be fined by the DMV.

en.explanation: If the form is not completed by the seller for a vehicle sold below fair market value, the manual notes that you will be charged sales tax based on the current fair market value of the vehicle.

en.question: When presenting an insurance identification card to register your vehicle, the information on the card must exactly match the:

choices.A: Name and Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) on the registration application.
choices.B: Name and address on your driver license.
choices.C: Odometer reading on the Certificate of Title.
choices.D: Purchase price on the Statement of Transaction.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that the name(s) and vehicle identification number (VIN) on the insurance identification cards must exactly match the information on the registration application.

en.question: For most vehicles with a maximum gross weight of not more than 18,000 pounds, registration fees are based on the vehicle's:

choices.A: Age.
choices.B: Purchase price.
choices.C: Weight.
choices.D: Horsepower.

en.explanation: Registrations for most vehicles with a maximum gross weight of not more than 18,000 pounds are valid for two years, and fees are based on vehicle weight.

en.question: Under what condition can you receive a refund for your registration fees if you have already used the vehicle plates or registration sticker for one day?

choices.A: If you return them within 30 days.
choices.B: If you sell the vehicle to a family member.
choices.C: If you transfer the registration to a motorcycle.
choices.D: By law, registration fees cannot be refunded if the plates or sticker are used even for one day.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'By law, registration fees cannot be refunded if you use the vehicle plates or registration sticker on your vehicle even for one day.'

en.question: What should you do before you trade in or sell your old vehicle to prevent being charged with parking tickets that are not yours?

choices.A: Scratch out the VIN on the dashboard.
choices.B: Remove the vehicle plates and the windshield registration sticker.
choices.C: Leave the plates on but remove the registration sticker.
choices.D: Report the vehicle as stolen to the DMV.

en.explanation: Before trading in or selling your old vehicle, you must make sure to remove the vehicle plates and the windshield registration sticker to prevent being charged with parking tickets that are not yours.

en.question: Which of the following is a reason you might NOT receive a registration renewal reminder in the mail?

choices.A: You have not answered three or more parking tickets.
choices.B: Your vehicle is more than ten model years old.
choices.C: You recently renewed your driver license.
choices.D: You purchased your vehicle from a private seller instead of a dealer.

en.explanation: The manual lists several reasons you will not receive a renewal reminder, including if you changed your address without notifying the DMV, if your registration is suspended or revoked, or if you did not answer three or more parking tickets.

en.question: What happens if your vehicle registration expiration date falls on a weekend or legal state holiday?

choices.A: You are given a 30-day grace period to renew.
choices.B: The registration expires immediately on the Friday before.
choices.C: The registration is automatically extended to midnight of the next business day.
choices.D: You must pay a late fee when renewing on the next business day.

en.explanation: If the expiration date falls on a weekend or legal state holiday, your registration is automatically extended to midnight of the next business day.

en.question: If a second party (someone who is not the registrant) brings a registration application into a DMV office, what identification must they provide?

choices.A: Only the original identification of the registrant.
choices.B: Only their own original identification.
choices.C: Their own original identification and either the original or a photocopy of the registrant's identification.
choices.D: A notarized letter from the registrant and the vehicle's title.

en.explanation: An application brought in by a second party must be accompanied by the original New York license/permit/non-driver ID for the second party and either the original or a photocopy for the registrant.

en.question: When is your vehicle required to be covered by liability insurance?

choices.A: Only when it is being driven on public roads.
choices.B: Only during the first year of registration.
choices.C: As long as it is registered, even if you do not drive it.
choices.D: Only if the vehicle is less than ten model years old.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Your vehicle must be covered by liability insurance as long as it is registered, even if you do not drive it.'

en.question: What is the minimum required liability insurance coverage against property damage for a single incident in New York State?
en.explanation: The minimum liability coverage required includes $10,000 against property damage.

en.question: What is the penalty if your vehicle is not insured for 90 days and you have not turned in your vehicle plates?

choices.A: Your vehicle will be repossessed by the DMV.
choices.B: Your driver license will be suspended.
choices.C: You will be required to take a defensive driving course.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be permanently branded as 'Rebuilt Salvage.'

en.explanation: According to the manual, if your vehicle is not insured for 90 days, unless you have turned in your vehicle plates, your driver license will also be suspended.

en.question: How do the rules for turning in vehicle plates differ for motorcycles when insurance is discontinued or expires?

choices.A: Motorcycle plates must be turned in within 24 hours of insurance expiration.
choices.B: You are not required to turn in the vehicle plate when motorcycle insurance is discontinued or expires.
choices.C: Motorcycle plates must be mailed directly to the DMV Call Center.
choices.D: You must turn in the plate only if the motorcycle is sold to a private party.

en.explanation: The manual specifies that while motorcycles must be insured, you are not required to turn in the vehicle plate when your motorcycle insurance is discontinued or expires.

en.question: What is the penalty if you are convicted of driving an uninsured vehicle in New York State?

choices.A: A fine of up to $1,000
choices.B: Your license or privilege to drive will be revoked for at least one year
choices.C: Your vehicle will be impounded for 30 days
choices.D: Your license will be suspended for 90 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are convicted of driving an uninsured vehicle, your license or privilege to drive in New York State will be revoked for at least one year.

en.question: If you purchase a vehicle from someone who is not a New York State dealer, how long do you have to get the vehicle inspected?

choices.A: Within 5 days after you register it
choices.B: Within 10 days after you register it
choices.C: Within 20 days after you register it
choices.D: Within 30 days after you register it

en.explanation: The manual states that if you purchase a vehicle from someone who is not a NYS dealer, you must have the vehicle inspected within 10 days after you register it.

en.question: To qualify for a waiver if your vehicle fails a first high enhanced or OBD II emissions inspection, how much must the attempted repairs cost?

choices.A: At least $250
choices.B: At least $300
choices.C: At least $450
choices.D: At least $500

en.explanation: The manual specifies that to qualify for a waiver, an attempt must be made to repair the malfunction and the cost for repairs must be at least $450.

en.question: Which of the following gasoline-powered vehicles is exempt from the exhaust emissions inspection and only subject to a safety inspection?

choices.A: A vehicle that is 10 model years old
choices.B: A vehicle that is 26 or more model years old
choices.C: A vehicle with a gross weight over 8,500 pounds
choices.D: A vehicle purchased from an out-of-state dealer

en.explanation: Exceptions to the exhaust emissions inspection include gasoline-powered vehicles that are 26 or more model years old, less than two model years old, or registered as historic.

en.question: What is the time and mileage limit for the DMV to receive a complaint against an auto repair shop?

choices.A: Within 30 days or 1,000 miles of the vehicle repairs
choices.B: Within 60 days or 2,000 miles of the vehicle repairs
choices.C: Within 90 days or 3,000 miles of the vehicle repairs
choices.D: Within 120 days or 4,000 miles of the vehicle repairs

en.explanation: By regulation, the DMV can receive a repair shop complaint only within 90 days or 3,000 miles (4,828 km) of the vehicle repairs, whichever comes first.

en.question: What do regulation signs normally look like?

choices.A: Yellow and diamond-shaped with black letters
choices.B: Green with white letters and symbols
choices.C: White rectangles with black letters or symbols
choices.D: Blue with white letters or symbols

en.explanation: The manual states that regulation signs normally are white rectangles with black letters or symbols, though some are different shapes or use red letters.

en.question: What is the normal shape and color of a warning sign?

choices.A: White and rectangular
choices.B: Yellow and diamond-shaped
choices.C: Orange and circular
choices.D: Red and octagonal

en.explanation: Warning signs normally are yellow and diamond-shaped, with black letters or symbols.

en.question: Which type of sign shows the location of services like rest areas, gas stations, or medical facilities?

choices.A: Destination signs
choices.B: Warning signs
choices.C: Route signs
choices.D: Service signs

en.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters or symbols and show the location of services like rest areas, gas stations, camping or medical facilities.

en.question: When approaching a stop sign where there is no stop line or crosswalk, where must you come to a full stop?

choices.A: At least 10 feet before the intersection
choices.B: Before you enter the intersection, at the point nearest the intersection that gives you a view of traffic
choices.C: Directly next to the stop sign
choices.D: After slowly rolling into the intersection to check for traffic

en.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before you enter the intersection, at the point nearest the intersection that gives you a view of traffic on the intersecting roadway.

en.question: What color are work area signs?

choices.A: Orange with black letters or symbols
choices.B: Yellow with black letters or symbols
choices.C: Red with white letters or symbols
choices.D: Green with white letters or symbols

en.explanation: Work area signs are orange, with black letters or symbols, indicating that people are at work on or near the roadway.

en.question: What must you do if you approach an intersection where the traffic lights are out of service?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection without stopping if the way is clear
choices.B: Yield to vehicles on your right and proceed with caution
choices.C: Come to a stop as you would for a stop sign
choices.D: Wait for a police officer to arrive before proceeding

en.explanation: State law requires that if the traffic lights or controls are out of service or do not operate correctly when you approach an intersection, you must come to a stop as you would for a stop sign.

en.question: Under what condition are you permitted to make a left turn at a steady red light?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way road onto a one-way road
choices.B: When turning from a one-way road into another one-way road after coming to a full stop and yielding
choices.C: When turning onto a multi-lane highway with a median
choices.D: You are never permitted to make a left turn on a red light in New York State

en.explanation: You can make a left turn at a steady red light when you turn from a one-way road into another one-way road after you come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way.

en.question: What is the rule for turning on a red light in New York City?

choices.A: You may turn right on red after coming to a full stop
choices.B: You may turn on red only between the hours of 10 PM and 6 AM
choices.C: You are not allowed to turn on a red light unless a sign that permits it is posted
choices.D: You may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'You are not allowed to turn on a red light in New York City unless a sign that permits it is posted.'

en.question: If a person moves to New York State, how long is their previous out-of-state vehicle inspection certificate valid?

choices.A: For 30 days after registering the vehicle in New York
choices.B: Until it expires or one year from the date it was issued, whichever occurs first
choices.C: It is not valid; the vehicle must be inspected immediately
choices.D: For 6 months from the date they establish residency

en.explanation: If a person moves to NYS, an inspection certificate that was issued before is valid until it expires or one year from the date it was issued, whichever occurs first.

en.question: What are you required to do with your vehicle plate if your motorcycle insurance is discontinued or expires?

choices.A: Turn it in to the DMV immediately
choices.B: Mail it to your insurance company
choices.C: You are not required to turn in the vehicle plate
choices.D: Destroy the plate and request a new one when re-insured

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Motorcycles must be insured, but you are not required to turn in the vehicle plate when your motorcycle insurance is discontinued or expires.'

en.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

choices.A: The traffic signal is broken; proceed with caution.
choices.B: Stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.
choices.C: Slow down and prepare to stop.
choices.D: Yield to all traffic on your right.

en.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a STOP sign: Stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow 'X' light above a highway lane indicate?

choices.A: Do not drive in this lane.
choices.B: Move from this lane immediately.
choices.C: This lane can only be used for a left turn.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for high-occupancy vehicles.

en.explanation: A flashing yellow 'X' above the pavement indicates that this lane can only be used for a left turn.

en.question: What does it indicate if a solid edge line angles toward the center of the road?

choices.A: The road is narrower ahead.
choices.B: You are approaching a toll booth.
choices.C: The speed limit is decreasing.
choices.D: You must merge into the left lane.

en.explanation: An edge line that angles towards the center of the road shows that the road is narrower ahead.

en.question: What is the difference between white and yellow lane lines?

choices.A: White lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; yellow lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.
choices.B: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
choices.C: White lines indicate parking zones; yellow lines indicate no-parking zones.
choices.D: White lines are used on highways; yellow lines are used on city streets.

en.explanation: Lines that separate lanes of traffic that move in the same direction are white. Lines that separate traffic that moves in opposite directions are yellow.

en.question: If you are driving on a road with a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, and you are on the side with the solid line, what are you permitted to do?

choices.A: You may pass other vehicles if the road ahead is clear.
choices.B: You cannot pass other vehicles or go across the line except to make a left turn into a driveway.
choices.C: You may cross the line to pass slow-moving farm equipment only.
choices.D: You are never allowed to cross the solid line for any reason.

en.explanation: Solid line with broken line: If you are on the side with the solid line, you cannot pass other vehicles or go across the line except to make a left turn into a driveway.

en.question: When are you allowed to cross double solid lines on the roadway?

choices.A: When passing a vehicle traveling below the speed limit.
choices.B: When you need to turn left to enter or leave the highway, such as to a driveway.
choices.C: When the vehicle ahead of you is stopped for a pedestrian.
choices.D: You may never cross double solid lines under any circumstances.

en.explanation: Double solid lines: You cannot pass or change lanes. You cannot go across the lines except to turn left to enter or leave the highway (e.g. to or from a driveway or to do a U-turn).

en.question: What does a diamond symbol painted on the roadway indicate?

choices.A: A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.
choices.B: The lane is reserved for buses, HOVs, bicycles, or other special vehicles.
choices.C: The lane ends ahead and you must merge.
choices.D: You are approaching a railroad crossing.

en.explanation: The diamond symbol indicates the lane is reserved for buses, HOV (High-Occupancy Vehicles) like car-pools and van-pools, bicycles or other special vehicles.

en.question: If a traffic officer signals you to drive through a red light, what must you do?

choices.A: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
choices.B: Obey the officer and drive through the red light.
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn other drivers before proceeding.
choices.D: Pull over to the side of the road until the light changes.

en.explanation: Directions given by traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals or pavement markings. If an officer signals you to drive through a red light or stop sign, you must do it.

en.question: If you and an approaching driver from the opposite direction reach an intersection at the same time, and you want to turn left while they are going straight, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: You have the right-of-way because you are turning.
choices.B: The driver going straight has the right-of-way.
choices.C: Whoever enters the intersection first has the right-of-way.
choices.D: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: If drivers approaching from opposite directions reach an intersection at about the same time, a driver that turns left must yield to traffic that moves straight or turns right.

en.question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your vehicle's wheels?

choices.A: Keep your wheels turned to the left to prepare for the turn.
choices.B: Keep your wheels turned to the right to avoid blocking traffic.
choices.C: Keep your wheels straight to prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.
choices.D: It does not matter how your wheels are positioned.

en.explanation: When you enter the intersection, keep to the right of the center line. Keep your wheels straight to prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic if your vehicle is hit from behind.

en.question: At an intersection not controlled by signs or signals, if two drivers arrive at right angles at the same time, who must yield?

choices.A: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
choices.B: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
choices.C: The driver going faster has the right-of-way.
choices.D: The driver on the wider road has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: At intersections not controlled by signs or signals, or where two or more drivers stop at STOP signs at the same time and they are at right angles, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

en.question: What does a single solid line separating lanes of traffic indicate?

choices.A: You cannot pass or change lanes under any circumstances.
choices.B: You can pass or change lanes freely as long as you signal.
choices.C: You can pass or change lanes, but only when obstructions or traffic conditions make it necessary.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles only.

en.explanation: One solid line: You can pass other vehicles or change lanes, but you can only do so when obstructions in the road or traffic conditions make it necessary.

en.question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time at right angles, who must yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
choices.B: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
choices.C: The driver going faster has the right-of-way.
choices.D: The driver turning left has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: At intersections not controlled by signs or signals, or where two or more drivers stop at STOP signs at the same time and they are at right angles, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

en.question: What must you do when entering a street from a private driveway or parking lot?

choices.A: Sound your horn and proceed into traffic.
choices.B: Yield only to vehicles approaching from your left.
choices.C: Stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic on the roadway and to pedestrians.
choices.D: Merge into traffic without stopping if you are turning right.

en.explanation: A vehicle that enters a roadway from a driveway, private road or another place that is not a roadway, must stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic on the roadway and to pedestrians.

en.question: What should you do if you want to cross an intersection but traffic is backed up on the other side?

choices.A: Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
choices.B: Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.
choices.C: Proceed slowly and force your way into the traffic line.
choices.D: Turn right instead of going straight.

en.explanation: You cannot enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get completely through the intersection. Wait until traffic ahead clears, so you do not block the intersection.

en.question: Are you required to pull over for an emergency vehicle approaching you in the opposite lane of a two-way roadway?

choices.A: Yes, you must pull over and stop.
choices.B: No, only if it is traveling in your lane.
choices.C: No, but you must slow down.
choices.D: Yes, but only if there is no physical divider.

en.explanation: You must pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle even if it is headed toward you in the opposite lane of a two-way roadway.

en.question: What must you do if you hear an emergency siren close by but do not know exactly where the emergency vehicle is?

choices.A: Stop immediately in your current lane.
choices.B: Speed up until you see the vehicle.
choices.C: Safely pull over to the right-side edge of the road and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.
choices.D: Continue driving at the speed limit while checking your mirrors.

en.explanation: If you hear a siren or air-horn close by but do not know exactly where the emergency vehicle is, you must safely pull over to the right-side edge of the road and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

en.question: Under the Move Over Law, what must a driver do when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a multi-lane highway?

choices.A: Stop immediately next to the emergency vehicle.
choices.B: Maintain speed but move to the right shoulder.
choices.C: Reduce speed and move from the lane adjacent to the emergency vehicle, if safe to do so.
choices.D: Sound the horn to warn the emergency workers.
