en.explanation: Drivers must reduce speed on all roads when encountering such vehicles, but on parkways, interstates and other controlled access roads with multiple lanes, drivers are further required to move from the lane adjacent to the emergency or hazard vehicle unless traffic or other hazards prevent doing so safely.

en.question: What does a flashing green light on a personal vehicle indicate?

choices.A: A volunteer fire fighter responding to an alarm.
choices.B: A volunteer ambulance or rescue squad member.
choices.C: A snow plow or tow truck.
choices.D: A rural mail delivery vehicle.

en.explanation: Personal vehicles driven by volunteer fire fighters responding to alarms are allowed to display blue lights and those driven by volunteer ambulance or rescue squad members can display green lights.

en.question: Are you legally required to yield the right-of-way to a personal vehicle displaying a flashing blue light?

choices.A: Yes, they are considered authorized emergency vehicles.
choices.B: Yes, but only if they also sound a siren.
choices.C: No, but you should yield as a courtesy if you can safely do so.
choices.D: No, you should maintain your speed and right-of-way at all times.

en.explanation: The vehicles that display blue, green or amber lights are not authorized emergency vehicles. Their drivers must obey all traffic laws. While you are not required to yield the right-of-way, you should yield as a courtesy if you can safely do so.

en.question: How far ahead of a turn or lane change does the law require you to signal?

choices.A: At least 50 feet (15 m)
choices.B: At least 100 feet (30 m)
choices.C: At least 200 feet (60 m)
choices.D: At least 300 feet (90 m)

en.explanation: The law requires you to signal a turn or lane change with your turn lights or hand signals at least 100 feet (30 m) ahead.

en.question: Why should you keep your wheels straight while waiting in an intersection to make a turn?

choices.A: It prevents your power steering fluid from overheating.
choices.B: It helps you accelerate faster when the light turns green.
choices.C: If you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into the oncoming lane of traffic.
choices.D: It makes it easier for pedestrians to see your vehicle.

en.explanation: Keep your wheels straight until you actually begin to make your turn. If your wheels are turned, and you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into the oncoming lane of traffic.

en.question: When making a turn, what should you remember about the path of your rear wheels?

choices.A: They will travel outside the path of the front wheels.
choices.B: They will travel inside the path of the front wheels.
choices.C: They will follow the exact same path as the front wheels.
choices.D: They will skid if you do not brake during the turn.

en.explanation: Remember that your rear wheels will travel inside the path of the front wheels, nearer to the curb (right turn) or to traffic headed toward you (left turn).

en.question: What is a common cause of crashes involving motorcycles and other vehicles?

choices.A: The motorcycle is driving too slowly.
choices.B: The driver of the other vehicle fails to see the motorcycle.
choices.C: The motorcycle's headlights are too bright.
choices.D: The motorcycle fails to signal before turning.

en.explanation: Most crashes that involve motorcycles and other vehicles are caused because the driver of the other vehicle has failed to see the motorcycle.

en.question: When making a left turn from a two-way road into another two-way road, how should you approach the turn?

choices.A: From the far right lane of the roadway.
choices.B: From the left half of the roadway.
choices.C: From the right half of the roadway closest to the center.
choices.D: By swinging wide to the right before turning left.

en.explanation: When making a left turn from a two-way road into a two-way road, approach the turn from the right half of the roadway closest to the center.

en.question: From which lane are you permitted to make a U-turn?

choices.A: The right shoulder.
choices.B: The far right lane.
choices.C: The left portion of the lane nearest to the centerline.
choices.D: Any lane as long as there is no oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: You can make a U-turn only from the left portion of the lane nearest to the centerline of the roadway, never from the right lane.

en.question: What is the penalty for violating the Move Over Law?

choices.A: It is punishable as a moving violation.
choices.B: It results in an automatic license suspension.
choices.C: It is considered a felony offense.
choices.D: It carries no penalty but a written warning.

en.explanation: Violations of this law [the Move Over Law] are punishable as a moving violation.

en.question: According to New York State law, in which of the following locations is it strictly prohibited to make a U-turn?

choices.A: On a narrow, two-way street
choices.B: In a school zone
choices.C: At an intersection with a green left-arrow signal
choices.D: In a residential driveway

en.explanation: The manual states that it is prohibited for a vehicle to make a U-turn in a school zone, as well as on limited access expressways and in business districts of New York City.

en.question: How far away must other drivers be able to see your vehicle for you to legally make a U-turn near a hill or curve?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You cannot make a U-turn near the top of a hill, a curve, or any other location where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from 500 feet (150 m) away in either direction.

en.question: What is the first step you must take when making a three-point turn?

choices.A: Signal left and steer across the road
choices.B: Turn your steering wheel as far to the right as possible
choices.C: Signal with your right turn signal, then pull over to the right and stop
choices.D: Check your interior rear-view mirror and back up

en.explanation: To make a three-point turn, step 1 is to signal with your right turn signal, then pull over to the right and stop.

en.question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do to ensure safety?

choices.A: Share the lane if the lane is wide enough
choices.B: Give the motorcycle the same full-lane width as other vehicles
choices.C: Pass on the right side only
choices.D: Sound your horn before moving into their lane space

en.explanation: When you pass a motorcycle, remember to give the motorcycle the same full-lane width as other vehicles are allowed. Never move into the same lane space as a motorcycle.

en.question: How far in advance must you use your turn signal or hand signal to indicate your intention to change lanes?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: The law requires you to use turn signal lamps or hand and arm signals to indicate your intention to change lanes at least 100 feet (30 m) before you make a lane change.

en.question: You are prohibited from passing a vehicle on the left if you are within how many feet of a railroad crossing on a two-way roadway?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle on the left if you are within 100 feet (30 m) of a railroad crossing on a two-way roadway.

en.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, you must be able to safely return to the right lane before any oncoming vehicle comes within what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle on the left if you cannot safely return to the right lane before any oncoming vehicle comes within 200 feet (60 m) of you.

en.question: Why should you quickly look over your shoulder before changing lanes to pass?

choices.A: To check for emergency vehicles in the distance
choices.B: Because it is illegal to use your mirrors while passing
choices.C: To ensure you do not exceed the speed limit
choices.D: Because correctly adjusted mirrors still leave blind spots

en.explanation: Never depend on your mirrors when you prepare to change lanes. Even correctly adjusted mirrors will leave 'blind spots' behind both sides of your vehicle.

en.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, how do you know it is safe to return to the right lane?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the other vehicle's front bumper
choices.B: When you can see the front bumper of the passed vehicle in your interior rear-view mirror
choices.C: Immediately after you activate your right turn signal
choices.D: When you are 100 feet ahead of the passed vehicle

en.explanation: Before you return to the right lane, signal and look at your interior rear-view mirror and make sure you can see the front bumper of the vehicle you passed.

en.question: Under which of the following conditions are you permitted to pass another vehicle on the right?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the speed limit
choices.B: When you are on a narrow, one-lane dirt road
choices.C: When a vehicle ahead makes a left turn
choices.D: By driving onto the unpaved shoulder of the road

en.explanation: You can pass a vehicle on the right only in specific conditions, such as when a vehicle ahead makes a left turn, provided you can pass safely without driving on or across the shoulder.

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle passes you on the left?

choices.A: Increase your speed to prevent them from passing
choices.B: Move onto the right shoulder of the road
choices.C: Decrease your speed slightly and stay centered in your lane
choices.D: Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic

en.explanation: If another vehicle passes you on the left, decrease your speed slightly and stay centered in your lane.

en.question: How far away must you stop from a school bus that is flashing its red lights?

choices.A: At least 10 feet
choices.B: At least 15 feet
choices.C: At least 20 feet
choices.D: At least 50 feet

en.explanation: When a stopped school bus flashes its red light(s), traffic that approaches from either direction must stop before it reaches the bus. You should stop at least 20 feet (6 m) away from the bus.

en.question: If you are driving on a divided highway and a school bus on the opposite side of the highway stops with its red lights flashing, what must you do?

choices.A: Proceed with caution since the highway is divided
choices.B: Stop, as the law applies on all roadways in New York State
choices.C: Slow down to 15 mph and pass carefully
choices.D: Stop only if children are actively crossing your side of the highway

en.explanation: This law applies on all roadways in New York State. You must stop for a school bus even if it is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

en.question: What is the penalty for being convicted of passing a stopped school bus three times within three years?

choices.A: A maximum fine of $250
choices.B: A mandatory defensive driving course
choices.C: Your driver license will be revoked for a minimum of six months
choices.D: Your vehicle will be impounded for 30 days

en.explanation: If you are convicted of three of these violations in three years, your driver license will be revoked for a minimum of six months.

en.question: What do flashing yellow warning lights on a school bus indicate?

choices.A: The bus is broken down and needs assistance
choices.B: The bus is preparing to stop to load or discharge passengers
choices.C: You are required to stop immediately
choices.D: The bus is accelerating to merge into traffic

en.explanation: Before a school bus stops to load or discharge passengers, the driver will usually flash yellow warning lights. When you see them, decrease speed and be prepared to stop.

en.question: What is the minimum fine for a first violation of passing a stopped school bus?
en.explanation: According to the manual, the fine when you pass a stopped school bus ranges from a minimum of $250 for a first violation to a maximum of $1,000 for three violations in three years.

en.question: Under the stop-arm camera law, what is the penalty for a third violation of passing a stopped school bus within 18 months?
en.explanation: The manual specifies that a third violation (or more) within 18 months caught by a stop-arm camera carries a penalty of $300.

en.question: When you have finished parallel parking, how close must your wheels be to the curb?

choices.A: No more than one foot (30 cm)
choices.B: No more than eighteen inches
choices.C: No more than two feet
choices.D: No more than six inches

en.explanation: The manual states: "In your final parking position, your wheels must be no more than one foot (30 cm) from the curb."

en.question: Where should you look when backing up your vehicle during a parallel parking maneuver?

choices.A: Only in your side mirrors
choices.B: Through the rear window
choices.C: Only in your interior rear-view mirror
choices.D: At your backup camera screen exclusively

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "Look through the rear window, not the mirrors, when you back up" during parallel parking.

en.question: Which way should you turn your steering wheel when parking on a hill?

choices.A: Away from the curb
choices.B: Toward the curb or side of the road
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: Parallel to the center line

en.explanation: When parking on a hill, the manual states to "Turn the wheels toward the curb or side of the road, so they will keep your vehicle from heading into traffic."

en.question: What does a NO PARKING sign indicate?

choices.A: You cannot stop for any reason.
choices.B: You may only stop to obey a traffic signal.
choices.C: You can make a temporary stop to load or discharge merchandise or passengers.
choices.D: You can park if you remain in the driver's seat.

en.explanation: According to the manual, "A NO PARKING sign means you can make a temporary stop to load or discharge merchandise or passengers."

en.question: What are you permitted to do at a NO STANDING sign?

choices.A: Temporarily stop to load or discharge passengers without exiting the vehicle.
choices.B: Stop to load or unload merchandise.
choices.C: Park for less than 5 minutes.
choices.D: Leave the vehicle running while you run an errand.

en.explanation: The manual states: "A NO STANDING sign means you can only make a temporary stop to load or discharge passengers. The driver cannot exit the vehicle."

en.question: How far must you stay from a fire hydrant when parking, stopping, or standing, unless a licensed driver remains in the vehicle?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: You cannot park, stop or stand within 15 feet (5 m) of a fire hydrant, unless a licensed driver remains in the vehicle to move it in an emergency.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must maintain when parking or standing near a crosswalk at an intersection?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: Parking or standing is not allowed within 20 feet (6 m) of a crosswalk at an intersection.

en.question: You are not allowed to park or stand within what distance of a STOP sign, YIELD sign, or traffic light?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that parking or standing is not allowed within 30 feet (10 m) of a traffic light, STOP sign or YIELD sign.

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must park away from a railroad crossing?

choices.A: 15 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: According to the manual, "You cannot park your vehicle within 50 feet (15 m) of a railroad crossing."

en.question: When are you legally allowed to park in a space reserved for persons with disabilities?

choices.A: Anytime, as long as you have a disabled parking permit in the vehicle.
choices.B: Only if you have a permit or plates AND the person who received them is in the vehicle.
choices.C: If you are running a quick errand for a disabled family member.
choices.D: If all other regular parking spaces are currently occupied.

en.explanation: You can park in reserved spaces only if you have a permit or vehicle plates for persons with disabilities and only when the person who received the permit or vehicle plates is in the vehicle.

en.question: Why must you avoid parking in the spaces with diagonal stripes next to reserved disabled parking areas?

choices.A: They are reserved exclusively for emergency vehicles.
choices.B: They are loading zones for delivery trucks.
choices.C: They provide necessary access for wheelchairs and vehicles with special equipment.
choices.D: They are designated for shopping cart storage.

en.explanation: The manual warns: "Do not park in the spaces with diagonal stripes next to reserved parking areas. These spaces are needed to give access to those with wheelchairs and vehicles with special equipment."

en.question: What is one of the penalties for making a false statement on an application for disabled vehicle plates?

choices.A: A mandatory license revocation
choices.B: A warning letter from the DMV
choices.C: A mandatory defensive driving course
choices.D: A 30-day vehicle impoundment

en.explanation: It is a misdemeanor to make a false statement on an application for vehicle plates, and you would be subject to a mandatory license revocation and could face a fine, incarceration, or both.

en.question: What is the mandatory surcharge added to penalties for shopping center parking violations?
en.explanation: According to the manual, a mandatory surcharge of $30 will be added to each penalty for a shopping center parking violation.

en.question: What is the recommended seating position and hand placement while driving?

choices.A: Slouching with one hand on the bottom of the wheel.
choices.B: Sitting in a comfortable but vertical position with both hands on the steering wheel.
choices.C: Leaning back with one hand on the wheel and one on the window.
choices.D: Sitting as close to the steering wheel as possible with hands at the top.

en.explanation: You should sit in a comfortable but vertical position and keep both hands on the steering wheel. Slouching or using only one hand makes it dangerous to control your vehicle.

en.question: When approaching an intersection where another driver has a STOP or YIELD sign, what should you assume?

choices.A: The other driver will always stop or yield.
choices.B: The other driver will wave you through the intersection.
choices.C: It is better to assume the other driver will not stop.
choices.D: The other driver has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: The manual advises to anticipate errors by other drivers and states, 'It is better to assume the other driver will not stop' even if they approach a STOP or YIELD sign.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a dangerous driving distraction according to the manual?

choices.A: Checking your mirrors every few seconds.
choices.B: Scanning the road ahead.
choices.C: Engaging in stressful or emotional conversations with passengers.
choices.D: Keeping both hands on the steering wheel.

en.explanation: The manual lists avoiding arguments and stressful or emotional conversations with passengers as a necessary step to prevent distracted driving.

en.question: What is the primary difference between aggressive driving and road rage?

choices.A: Aggressive driving involves breaking a criminal law, while road rage involves breaking a traffic safety law.
choices.B: Aggressive driving generally involves the violation of a traffic safety law, while road rage involves the breaking of a criminal law.
choices.C: Aggressive driving only happens on highways, while road rage happens on city streets.
choices.D: There is no difference; the terms mean the exact same thing.

en.explanation: According to the manual, aggressive driving generally involves the violation of a traffic safety law, while road rage involves the breaking of a criminal law.

en.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you on the road, what is the best course of action?

choices.A: Make eye contact to show you are not intimidated.
choices.B: Challenge them by increasing your speed.
choices.C: Do not make eye contact and try to move away safely.
choices.D: Return their gestures and shouts to defend yourself.

en.explanation: When an aggressive driver confronts you, you should not make eye contact, remain calm, and try to move away safely.

en.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is following you?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle and get out to confront them.
choices.B: Drive to the nearest police station.
choices.C: Pull over to the shoulder and wait for them to pass.
choices.D: Drive to your home and lock the doors.

en.explanation: If an aggressive driver is following you, the manual explicitly states: 'do not stop or get out of your vehicle. Drive to the nearest police station.'

en.question: How should a defensive driver view the right-of-way?

choices.A: As a complete right that should never be yielded.
choices.B: As a rule that only applies to pedestrians.
choices.C: As something to be prepared to yield to other highway users to avoid a crash.
choices.D: As a guarantee that other drivers will stop for you.

en.explanation: If you have the right-of-way, do not think of it as a complete right. Be prepared to yield the right-of-way to other highway users to avoid a crash.

en.question: If no speed limit is posted on a highway in New York, what is the maximum speed you may legally drive?

choices.A: 45 mph
choices.B: 50 mph
choices.C: 55 mph
choices.D: 65 mph

en.explanation: You must obey the speed limit. If no limit is posted, drive no more than 55 mph (88 km/h).

en.question: Unless another limit is posted, what is the default speed limit in New York City?

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: The manual notes that some cities have unposted speed limits less than 55 mph, stating specifically that the speed limit is 25 mph in New York City unless another limit is posted.

en.question: Can you receive a speeding ticket if you are driving below the posted speed limit?

choices.A: No, as long as you are below the posted limit, you cannot be ticketed.
choices.B: Yes, if your speed is 'not reasonable' for hazardous weather or road conditions.
choices.C: Yes, but only if you are driving in a school zone.
choices.D: No, police only issue tickets for exceeding the posted limit.

en.explanation: Even if you drive below the limit on a hazardous highway, a police officer could ticket you for a speed 'not reasonable' for the conditions.

en.question: Why do some highways have minimum speed limits?

choices.A: To increase the amount of toll revenue collected.
choices.B: To keep a smooth traffic flow and prevent dangerous conditions caused by slow drivers.
choices.C: To encourage drivers to use local roads instead.
choices.D: To ensure drivers reach their destinations faster.

en.explanation: To keep a smooth traffic flow, some highways have minimum speed limits. Driving slower than the minimum can interfere with traffic flow and create a dangerous condition.

en.question: According to the manual, what proportion of crashes involve rear-end collisions, normally because a person is following too closely?

choices.A: 1 of every 10 crashes
choices.B: 2 of every 10 crashes
choices.C: 4 of every 10 crashes
choices.D: 6 of every 10 crashes

en.explanation: Four of every 10 crashes involve rear-end collisions, normally because a person is following too closely (tailgating).

en.question: Which of the following can be a penalty for behaviors associated with road rage?

choices.A: Fines, imprisonment, and court-ordered probation.
choices.B: A mandatory upgrade to a commercial driver license.
choices.C: A requirement to retake the written permit test only.
choices.D: A warning letter with no further legal action.

en.explanation: Endangering, threatening or assaulting another person is illegal. These behaviors can result in severe penalties that include fines, imprisonment, court-ordered probation, and license revocation or suspension.

en.question: What is the maximum restricted speed for vehicles within a roundabout?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 45 mph

en.explanation: Roundabouts are designed so that the speed of all vehicles is restricted to 30 mph (50 km/h) or less within the roundabout.

en.question: How should a driver interact with a bicyclist riding in a roundabout?

choices.A: Honk to warn them to move over
choices.B: Pass them quickly on the left
choices.C: Do not pass the bicycle in the roundabout
choices.D: Force them to use the pedestrian crosswalk

en.explanation: Bicyclists are permitted to ride within the roundabout in the lane just as other vehicles do. The manual states: 'Please do not pass a bicycle in the roundabout.'

en.question: What signal should you use when approaching your exit in a roundabout?

choices.A: Left turn signal
choices.B: Right turn signal
choices.C: Hazard lights
choices.D: No signal is required

en.explanation: As you approach your exit in a roundabout, you must turn on your right turn signal.

en.question: Which of the following is a rule for pedestrians navigating a roundabout?

choices.A: Cross directly to the central island
choices.B: Walk in the circular roadway
choices.C: Cross only at designated crosswalks
choices.D: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles

en.explanation: Pedestrians should cross only at the designated crosswalks and never cross to the central island. They also have the right-of-way over vehicles.

en.question: Which of the following is a symptom of drowsy driving?

choices.A: Hyper-focusing on the road ahead
choices.B: Remembering the last few miles in vivid detail
choices.C: Drifting between lanes or hitting rumble strips
choices.D: Reacting to hazards faster than usual

en.explanation: Symptoms of fatigue include drifting between lanes, tailgating, missing traffic signs, or drifting off the road and hitting rumble strips.

en.question: To prevent drowsy driving on long trips, how often should you schedule regular stops?

choices.A: Every 50 miles or one hour
choices.B: Every 100 miles or two hours
choices.C: Every 200 miles or four hours
choices.D: Only when you need to refuel

en.explanation: Before embarking on a trip, you should schedule regular stops for every 100 miles or two hours to prevent fatigue.

en.question: If you suspect you are drowsy while driving, how long should you nap after pulling off into a safe area?

choices.A: 5 to 10 minutes
choices.B: 15 to 45 minutes
choices.C: 1 to 2 hours
choices.D: At least 4 hours

en.explanation: If you are drowsy, you should pull off into a safe area away from traffic and take a brief nap of 15 to 45 minutes.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take for caffeine to enter the bloodstream and promote short-term alertness?

choices.A: 5 minutes
choices.B: 15 minutes
choices.C: 30 minutes
choices.D: 60 minutes

en.explanation: It takes about 30 minutes for caffeine to enter the bloodstream to promote short-term alertness.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of speaking into a hand-held mobile telephone while driving in New York State?

choices.A: A fine up to $100 and 2 license points
choices.B: A fine up to $200 and 5 license points
choices.C: A fine up to $250 and 3 license points
choices.D: A fine up to $450 and license suspension

en.explanation: For a first offense of using a hand-held mobile telephone while driving, you could be required to pay a fine up to $200 and receive five license points.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a third or subsequent offense of texting while driving committed within 18 months?
en.explanation: A third or subsequent offense of texting while driving (all committed within 18 months) carries a fine of up to $450.

en.question: What happens to a driver with a probationary or junior license who is convicted of texting while driving for the first time?

choices.A: They receive a warning letter
choices.B: They receive a 60-day suspension
choices.C: They receive a 120-day suspension
choices.D: Their license is revoked for one year

en.question: How often must a vehicle be inspected to be legally operated or parked on public highways in New York?

choices.A: At least once every 6 months
choices.B: At least once a year
choices.C: At least once every two years
choices.D: Only when the vehicle is sold

en.explanation: No person shall operate or park a vehicle on public highways unless it has been inspected at least once a year.

en.question: What should you do if your brakes pull to one side because they are wet?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly for one minute
choices.B: Dry them by riding the pedal lightly
choices.C: Shift into a lower gear and avoid braking
choices.D: Pull over and wait for them to air dry

en.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side may be wet. If wet, you can dry them by riding the pedal lightly.

en.question: What is the minimum legal tire tread depth required by law?

choices.A: 1/32nds of an inch
choices.B: 2/32nds of an inch
choices.C: 3/32nds of an inch
choices.D: 4/32nds of an inch

en.explanation: The law requires that your tires have at least 2/32nds of an inch (.16 cm) of tread.

en.question: When checking your tire tread depth with a penny, what indicates that your tires are too worn and need replacement?

choices.A: You can see all of Abraham Lincoln's head
choices.B: Lincoln's head is completely hidden
choices.C: You can only see Lincoln's hair
choices.D: The penny falls out of the groove

en.explanation: Place Lincoln’s head first into the deepest looking groove. If you can see all of his head, your tires are too worn and you should not drive on them.

en.question: How can you check if your tire tread depth is too worn using a penny?

choices.A: If you can see all of Abraham Lincoln's head when placed head first into the deepest groove
choices.B: If Lincoln's head is completely covered by the tire tread
choices.C: If the penny falls over when placed in the groove
choices.D: If the penny sits flush with the outer tire wall

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you place Lincoln's head first into the deepest looking groove and can see all of his head, your tires are too worn and should not be driven on.

en.question: When is it appropriate to use your vehicle's horn?

choices.A: To express anger at other drivers or pedestrians
choices.B: To warn other drivers or pedestrians of possible problems
choices.C: To greet friends walking on the sidewalk
choices.D: To encourage the driver in front of you to drive faster

en.explanation: The manual states the horn is important safety equipment that could become your only means of warning other drivers or pedestrians of possible problems, and it should not be used to express anger.

en.question: In New York State, approximately what percentage of all motor vehicle fatalities involve impaired driving?

choices.A: 10 percent
choices.B: 25 percent
choices.C: More than 40 percent
choices.D: 60 percent

en.explanation: The manual states that in New York State, more than 40 percent of all motor vehicle fatalities involve impaired driving.

en.question: Why are driver license revocation penalties more severe for young drivers who drive under the influence?

choices.A: They generally drive faster than older drivers
choices.B: They make up 7 percent of impaired drivers in fatal crashes despite being only 4 percent of the driving population
choices.C: They are more likely to drive without insurance
choices.D: They consume more alcohol on average than older drivers

en.explanation: Drivers under age 21 are approximately 4 percent of the driving population, but 7 percent of the impaired drivers involved in fatal crashes. This is one reason revocation penalties are more severe for young drivers.

en.question: How does alcohol affect your vision at night?

choices.A: It improves your ability to see in the dark
choices.B: It reduces your ability to recover from the glare of headlights
choices.C: It makes headlights appear dimmer
choices.D: It increases your peripheral vision

en.explanation: The manual notes that alcohol reduces your ability to recover from the glare of headlights, making it especially dangerous to drink and drive after dark.

en.question: When do the effects of alcohol consumption on your driving abilities begin?

choices.A: Only after your BAC reaches .08 percent
choices.B: When you start to feel intoxicated
choices.C: With the first drink
choices.D: After you have consumed three drinks in one hour

en.explanation: The manual states that the effects of alcohol consumption can begin long before you become intoxicated or even legally impaired and begin with the first drink.

en.question: What Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) level is considered legal evidence of intoxication in New York State?

choices.A: .02 percent or higher
choices.B: .05 percent or higher
choices.C: .08 percent or higher
choices.D: .18 percent or higher

en.explanation: A BAC of .08 percent or higher is evidence of intoxication. A BAC of more than .05 percent is evidence of impairment, and .18 percent or more is aggravated DWI.

en.question: A Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) of more than .05 percent is legal evidence of what offense?

choices.A: Aggravated driving while intoxicated
choices.B: Driving while ability impaired
choices.C: Driving while intoxicated
choices.D: Chemical test refusal

en.explanation: According to the manual, a BAC of more than .05 percent is legal evidence that you are impaired.

en.question: Can you be convicted of an alcohol or drug-related driving offense without a chemical test?

choices.A: No, a chemical test is always required by law to prove impairment
choices.B: Yes, but only if you confess to the offense in writing
choices.C: Yes, the testimony of a police officer about your driving and behavior can provide enough evidence
choices.D: No, unless there is video evidence of you consuming alcohol

en.explanation: The manual states that the testimony of a police officer about the way you drive, your appearance, and behavior can provide enough evidence to convict you, even without a chemical test.

en.question: Which of the following factors does NOT determine your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?

choices.A: How much alcohol you drink
choices.B: Your body weight
choices.C: How much time passes between drinks
choices.D: The type of alcoholic beverage you drink

en.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on the type of beverage you drink, how fit you are, or how you can 'hold your liquor.'

en.question: Which of the following drinks contains the most alcohol?

choices.A: 1 1/2 ounces of 80-proof liquor
choices.B: 5 ounces of wine (12% alcohol)
choices.C: 12 ounces of beer (5% alcohol)
choices.D: They all contain about the same amount of alcohol

en.explanation: The manual states that 1-1/2 ounces of liquor, 5 ounces of wine, 12 ounces of beer, and 12 ounces of wine cooler contain about the same amount of alcohol. None is 'safer to drink' than the others.

en.question: What is the only effective method to reduce your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?

choices.A: Drinking black coffee
choices.B: Taking a cold shower
choices.C: Not drinking over a period of time
choices.D: Vigorous exercise

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the only method to effectively reduce your BAC is not to drink over a period of time. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC.

en.question: What does New York's 'Implied Consent' law mean?

choices.A: You consent to a vehicle search if pulled over by law enforcement
choices.B: You consent to take a chemical test for BAC when you drive in the state
choices.C: You consent to pay all traffic fines immediately upon receiving a ticket
choices.D: You consent to have your license suspended if you get a speeding ticket

en.explanation: Under New York's 'Implied Consent' law, when you drive a car in the state you are considered to have given your consent to take a chemical test to measure your BAC.

en.question: What happens to your driver license if you are found guilty of an alcohol or drug-related violation?

choices.A: You receive a warning for the first offense
choices.B: You must retake the driving test within 30 days
choices.C: The court must revoke or suspend your license when you are sentenced
choices.D: Your license is restricted to daytime driving only

en.explanation: If you are found guilty of any alcohol or drug-related violation, the court must revoke or suspend your driver license when you are sentenced.

en.question: On average, how long does it take the body of a 150-pound male to remove the alcohol from one standard drink?

choices.A: 30 minutes
choices.B: Approximately one hour
choices.C: Two hours
choices.D: Four hours

en.explanation: For a 150-pound male, each standard drink increases his BAC by about .02 percent. On average, it takes the body approximately one hour to remove that much alcohol.

en.question: Under New York's "Implied Consent" law, what do you consent to by driving a car in the state?

choices.A: Allowing police to search your vehicle without a warrant
choices.B: Taking a chemical test to measure your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)
choices.C: Paying all traffic tickets within 30 days
choices.D: Having your vehicle impounded if you are arrested

en.explanation: Under New York's "Implied Consent" law, when you drive a car in the state, you are considered to have given your consent to take a chemical test to measure your BAC.

en.question: What happens to your driver license if you refuse to take a chemical test after being arrested for an alcohol or drug-related violation?

choices.A: It is suspended when you are arraigned in court.
choices.B: It is permanently revoked immediately.
choices.C: You receive a warning but keep your license until trial.
choices.D: It is restricted to driving to and from work only.

en.explanation: If you refuse to take the test after being arrested, your driver license will be suspended when you are arraigned in court on the alcohol or other drug-related charge.

en.question: The DMV will permanently deny any application for license reinstatement if a driver has how many alcohol or drug-related driving convictions in their lifetime?

choices.A: Two
choices.B: Three
choices.C: Four
choices.D: Five

en.explanation: The DMV will permanently deny reinstatement if the applicant has four alcohol or drug-related driving convictions or incidents in their lifetime.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a "serious driving offense" under New York's repeat offender regulations?

choices.A: Accumulating 10 points for driving violations within a 10-year period
choices.B: A fatal crash
choices.C: A parking ticket in a school zone
choices.D: Failing to yield the right-of-way at a stop sign

en.explanation: A serious driving offense includes a fatal crash, a driving-related penal law conviction, an accumulation of 20 or more points within 25 years, or two 5+ point convictions within 25 years.

en.question: Under New York's "zero tolerance" law, it is a violation for a person under 21 to drive with a measurable BAC in what range?

choices.D: .08 and higher

en.explanation: Under the state's "zero tolerance" law, it is a violation for a person under 21 to drive with any BAC that can be measured (.02 to .07).

en.question: What is the penalty for a first Zero Tolerance violation for a driver under age 21?

choices.A: A 30-day license suspension and a $50 fine
choices.B: A 6-month license suspension, a $100 termination fee, and a $125 civil penalty
choices.C: A 1-year license revocation and a $500 fine
choices.D: Mandatory imprisonment for 5 days

en.explanation: After a finding of a first Zero Tolerance violation, the driver license will be suspended for six months, and the driver must pay a $100 suspension termination fee and a $125 civil penalty.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a first conviction of possessing an open container of an alcoholic beverage in a motor vehicle on a public highway?
en.explanation: The penalty for a first conviction of the Open Container Law is a fine up to $150, a mandatory surcharge, a crime victim assistance fee, and possible imprisonment of 15 days.

en.question: Who is exempt from the Open Container Law regarding alcoholic beverages?

choices.A: Drivers of commercial trucks
choices.B: Passengers in vehicles like stretch limousines that display a valid commerce certificate
choices.C: Passengers in the backseat of any standard passenger vehicle
choices.D: Drivers who are over the age of 25

en.explanation: The Open Container law exempts passengers in vehicles like stretch limousines and other vehicles that display a commerce certificate or permit issued by the U.S. or NYS Department of Transportation.

en.question: What is the consequence of using a driver license to illegally purchase beverages that contain alcohol?

choices.A: A fine of $500
choices.B: Suspension of your driver license or privilege to apply for a license
choices.C: Mandatory community service
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver license

en.explanation: State law requires the suspension of your driver license or privilege to apply for a license if you use it as proof of age to illegally purchase beverages that contain alcohol.

en.question: Aggravated Driving While Intoxicated (AGG-DWI) applies to drivers with a Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) of at least:
en.explanation: Aggravated Driving While Intoxicated (AGG-DWI) applies to a Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) of 0.18 and higher.

en.question: What is the maximum jail sentence for a first offense of Driving While Intoxicated (DWI)?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: For a 1st Offense of Driving While Intoxicated (DWI), the maximum jail sentence is up to 1 year.

en.question: If a driver is approved for license reinstatement after a 5-year denial period due to repeated alcohol-related convictions, how long must they use an interlock device?

choices.B: 2 years

en.question: Under the Open Container Law, it is a traffic infraction for a driver or passenger in a motor vehicle on a public highway to:

choices.D: Drink a non-alcoholic beverage

en.explanation: It is a traffic infraction for a driver or passenger in a motor vehicle on a public highway, street or road to consume marijuana/cannabis.

en.question: What is the required license action for a first offense of Driving While Ability Impaired (DWAI)?

choices.A: 30-day suspension
choices.B: 90-day suspension
choices.C: 6-month revocation
choices.D: 1-year revocation

en.question: What is the maximum jail sentence for a second DWAI offense within 5 years?

choices.A: Up to 15 days
choices.B: Up to 30 days
choices.C: Up to 90 days
choices.D: Up to 180 days

en.explanation: The manual states that a 2nd Offense DWAI within 5 years carries a jail sentence of up to 30 days.

en.question: Under Leandra's Law, committing an alcohol-related offense with a child in the vehicle is a class E felony if the child is under what age?

choices.B: 14 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: Leandra's Law states that drivers who commit alcohol-related offenses with a child under 16 years old in the vehicle may be charged with a class E felony.

en.question: How long must a driver typically maintain an ignition interlock device on their vehicle after a DWI conviction?

choices.B: At least 6 months
choices.C: At least 12 months
choices.D: At least 24 months

en.explanation: Courts must order persons convicted of DWI or aggravated DWI to install and maintain an ignition interlock on any vehicle they own or operate for at least 12 months.

en.question: A conditional driver license will be revoked if the motorist is convicted of any traffic offense EXCEPT:

choices.A: Speeding
choices.B: Failure to yield
choices.C: Parking, stopping, or standing
choices.D: Running a red light

en.explanation: The manual notes that a conditional driver license will be revoked if the motorist does not comply with court terms or for a conviction for any traffic offense except parking, stopping or standing.

en.question: If you are arrested for driving while impaired or intoxicated and your license is already suspended or revoked, what is the maximum mandatory fine you face?
en.explanation: If impaired or intoxicated when you are arrested while driving with a suspended or revoked license, the maximum mandatory fine is $5,000 and the vehicle can be seized.

en.question: What is the maximum jail term you can face if you kill or cause injury to another person because of an alcohol or drug-related violation?

choices.A: 10 years
choices.B: 15 years
choices.C: 20 years
choices.D: 25 years

en.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should always:

choices.B: Stay in your lane and in the same gear
choices.C: Speed up to cross as quickly as possible
choices.D: Stop on the tracks to check for trains

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "When crossing tracks, always stay in your lane and in the same gear."

en.question: When approaching an active grade crossing with flashing red lights and lowered gates, when is it legal to proceed?

choices.A: As soon as the train has passed, even if the gates are down
choices.B: When the gates are completely raised and the lights are off
choices.C: When the gates start to rise and you can see clearly
choices.D: If you are driving a small vehicle that can fit under the gate

en.question: If flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, or a bell indicate an approaching train, you must stop at least how far from the tracks?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.question: What does a yellow sign with black letters "RR" and an "X" symbol mean?

choices.B: There is a railroad crossing ahead
choices.C: The railroad crossing is closed
choices.D: You are approaching a crossbuck sign

en.question: What shape is a crossbuck sign at a railroad crossing?

choices.B: A diamond
choices.C: An "X"
choices.D: An octagon

en.question: When judging the distance and speed of an approaching train, you should remember that:

choices.B: Trains are closer and faster-moving than you think
choices.C: Trains can stop quickly if they see a vehicle on the tracks
choices.D: Trains will always sound a horn before you can see them

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to "Remember that the train you see is closer and faster-moving than you think, and be aware that trains cannot stop quickly."

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended strategy to avoid driving while impaired?

choices.C: Drive only on local roads instead of highways
choices.D: Keep the windows down to stay alert

en.question: Under what circumstances should you attempt to cross railroad tracks?

choices.A: Only when you are certain your entire vehicle will clear all of the tracks
choices.B: Whenever the vehicle ahead of you begins to cross
choices.C: If the train is more than 100 feet away
choices.D: If the crossing does not have flashing lights

en.explanation: The manual warns: "Do not under any circumstances, attempt to cross any railroad tracks unless you are certain your entire vehicle will clear all of the tracks."

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?

choices.A: Try to restart the engine immediately
choices.B: Get everyone out of the car and get away from the tracks
choices.C: Stay in the vehicle and call 911
choices.D: Push the vehicle off the tracks

en.explanation: If you stall on the tracks for any reason, the manual states you must GET OUT (including everyone in the car) and get away from the tracks, even if you do not see a train.

en.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train is approaching, in which direction should you run?

choices.A: Down the track in the same direction the train is moving
choices.B: Directly away from the tracks at a 90-degree angle
choices.C: Toward the train but away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle
choices.D: Parallel to the tracks in the opposite direction of the train

en.explanation: If a train is approaching, run toward the train but away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle. Running in the same direction as the train can cause you to be hit with debris when the train hits your vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is required to stop at all railroad crossings?

choices.A: Passenger cars with children
choices.B: Motorcycles
choices.C: School buses with or without passengers
choices.D: Delivery trucks

en.question: What should you do if you enter an expressway going in a different direction than you intended?

choices.A: Carefully back up on the entrance ramp
choices.B: Cross the median when there is a break in traffic
choices.C: Pull over to the shoulder and make a U-turn
choices.D: Stay on the expressway until the next exit

en.explanation: If you enter an expressway going a different direction than you intended, or at the wrong exit, stay on the expressway until the next exit. It is dangerous to back up on an entrance ramp or cross a median.

en.question: If an expressway entrance lane is too short to allow acceleration to expressway speed, what is the safest method to enter?

choices.A: Force your way into the right lane

choices.C: Drive on the shoulder until you reach expressway speed
choices.D: Honk your horn so other drivers yield to you

en.question: How far in advance must you signal your exit before reaching the expressway exit ramp?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: Make sure to signal your exit at least 100 feet (30 m) before you reach the exit ramp.

en.question: What does 'driving within the range' of your headlights mean?

choices.B: Keeping your headlights aimed at the road surface
choices.C: Using high beams whenever you are driving over 40 mph
choices.D: Staying within 350 feet of the vehicle ahead of you

en.explanation: Your headlights cover about 350 feet ahead. It is important that you drive at a speed that allows you to stop safely within that distance. This is called 'driving within the range' of your headlights.

en.question: By law, during what times must you use your headlights?

choices.B: From one-half hour after the sun sets to one-half hour before the sun rises
choices.C: Only when there are no streetlights
choices.D: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise

en.explanation: The law requires you to use your headlights from one-half hour after the sun sets to one-half hour before the sun rises, when visibility is less than 1,000 feet, and when you use your windshield wipers.

en.question: You must dim your headlights to low beam when you are within what distance of an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Your headlights must be on low beam when you are within 500 feet (150 m) of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: What should you do to help avoid the glare of an approaching vehicle's high beams?

choices.C: Move your eyes to the right and use the road edge as a guide
choices.D: Turn on your interior roof light

en.explanation: To help avoid the glare of approaching high beams, move your eyes to the right. Use the road edge as a guide until the approaching vehicle passes by.

en.question: What is 'hydroplaning'?

choices.B: When your tires begin to ride on the water that is on top of the road pavement
choices.C: When fog mixes with rain to create zero visibility
choices.D: When your windshield wipers cannot keep up with heavy rain

en.explanation: In heavy rain, your tires can begin to ride on the water that is on top of the road pavement. This is called 'hydroplaning' and can cause complete loss of traction and control of steering.

en.question: Which headlights should you use for better visibility during rain, fog, or snow?

choices.B: Low beams
choices.C: Daytime running lights
choices.D: Parking lights

en.explanation: Headlights on high beams reflect rain, fog and snow as it falls, making it harder to see. For better visibility during these weather conditions, keep your headlights on low beam.

en.question: New York State law requires you to turn on your headlights when weather conditions require the use of:

choices.B: The defroster
choices.C: Fog lights
choices.D: Hazard lights

en.question: When preparing your vehicle for winter driving, what tire combination should you never use?

choices.B: Radial and non-radial tires
choices.C: Studded and non-studded tires
choices.D: Wide and narrow tires

en.question: When are tires with metal studs legally permitted to be used in New York State?

choices.B: October 16 through April 30
choices.C: September 1 through May 31
choices.D: They are illegal year-round

en.question: Which of the following is a rule regarding tire usage on your vehicle?
