choices.B: Never combine radial and non-radial tires on the same vehicle.
choices.C: Snow tires should only be placed on the front wheels.
choices.D: Metal studs must be used on all tires during winter.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Never combine radial and non-radial tires on the same vehicle."

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle's rear wheels start to skid to the left?

choices.A: Steer to the right.
choices.B: Steer to the left.
choices.C: Keep the steering wheel perfectly straight.
choices.D: Brake hard immediately.

en.explanation: To recover from a rear-wheel skid, you should turn the steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is trying to go. If your rear wheels slide left, steer left.

en.question: What is the first step you should take if your front wheels begin to skid?

choices.A: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the direction of the skid.
choices.B: Pump the brakes rapidly.
choices.C: Take your foot off the gas and shift to neutral.
choices.D: Accelerate to regain traction.

en.explanation: If your front wheels skid, the manual advises to take your foot off the gas and shift to neutral or push in the clutch, but do not try to immediately steer.

en.question: Which areas of the road are likely to freeze first when sleet or freezing rain begins to fall?

choices.A: Intersections and crosswalks
choices.B: Tunnels and underpasses
choices.C: Bridges, ramps, and overpasses
choices.D: Heavily traveled multi-lane highways

en.explanation: When sleet, freezing rain, or snow begins to fall, remember that bridges, ramps, and overpasses will freeze first.

en.question: During which time of day is deer activity the highest, increasing the risk of collisions?

choices.A: Midday and early afternoon
choices.B: Late at night
choices.C: Dawn and dusk
choices.D: Rush hour traffic in the morning only

en.explanation: Daily deer activity is highest at dawn and dusk, which often is the highest time of travel for motor-vehicle commuters.

en.question: What should you do if you experience a tire blowout while driving?

choices.A: Brake hard and steer sharply off the road.
choices.B: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
choices.C: Accelerate slightly to maintain control of the vehicle.
choices.D: Pump the brakes rapidly until the vehicle stops.

en.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake until your vehicle is controlled.

en.question: If your vehicle suddenly will not respond when you steer, why should you initially keep your foot off the brake pedal?

choices.A: Because braking will cause the engine to stall.
choices.B: Because a sudden change in speed could send the vehicle out of control.
choices.C: Because the brakes are connected to the steering column.
choices.D: Because you need to accelerate to regain steering fluid pressure.

en.explanation: During steering failure, the balance of the vehicle will allow it to continue going straight, but a sudden change in speed (such as braking) could send it out of control.

en.question: Why should you NOT turn off the ignition if your gas pedal becomes stuck?

choices.A: It will cause the engine to catch fire.
choices.B: You could lose steering control or lock your steering wheel.
choices.C: The brakes will immediately lock up.
choices.D: The vehicle will accelerate faster.

en.explanation: If your gas pedal is stuck, do not turn off the ignition as you could lose your steering control or lock your steering wheel.

en.question: What is the correct action to take if your wheels accidentally move off the pavement?

choices.A: Swerve sharply back onto the pavement immediately.
choices.B: Accelerate to get the wheels back on the road.
choices.C: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and brake gently.
choices.D: Brake hard and stop completely on the shoulder.

en.explanation: If your wheels move off the pavement, do not suddenly steer or swerve back onto the pavement. Ease your foot off the gas pedal and brake gently.

en.question: If a vehicle is approaching you head-on in your lane, what should you do?

choices.A: Swerve into the left lane to avoid them.
choices.B: Decrease speed, pull over to the right, and sound your horn.
choices.C: Stop immediately in your lane and flash your headlights.
choices.D: Accelerate and steer to the left.

en.explanation: For a vehicle approaching head-on in your lane, decrease speed, pull over to the right and sound your horn to warn the other driver. Do not turn into the left lane.

en.question: If your vehicle goes into the water, why should you escape through a window rather than opening a door?

choices.A: The door handle will be locked by the water pressure.
choices.B: Opening a door would cause water to rush in and the car could turn over.
choices.C: The window provides a larger escape route.
choices.D: Opening the door will cause the airbags to deploy.

en.explanation: When escaping a vehicle in water, release your seat belt and escape through a window. An open door would cause water to rush in and the car could turn over on top of you.

en.question: What should you do if you see smoke coming from under the hood of your vehicle?

choices.A: Open the hood immediately to locate the source of the fire.
choices.B: Drive quickly to the nearest fire station.
choices.C: Pull off the road, turn off the ignition, get away from the car, and call the fire department.
choices.D: Use water from your windshield washer reservoir to extinguish the flames.

en.explanation: If you see smoke come from under the hood, pull off the road and park your vehicle. Turn off the ignition. Get away from the car and call the fire department. It is dangerous to try to fight the fire yourself.

en.question: How should you brake to recover from a rear-wheel skid if your vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes (ABS)?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly.
choices.B: Keep your foot with even pressure on the brake pedal.
choices.C: Brake hard and release repeatedly.
choices.D: Do not touch the brake pedal at all.

en.explanation: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS), keep your foot with even pressure on the brake pedal during a skid. Pumping the pedal is only for vehicles without ABS.

en.question: What should you do before backing into or out of a driveway when children are near?

choices.A: Rely solely on your rearview mirrors.
choices.B: Honk your horn three times before moving.
choices.C: Get out of the vehicle and check behind it.
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to minimize time in the driveway.

en.explanation: The manual states that before you back into a driveway, or out of it, you should get out of the vehicle and check behind your vehicle, and not rely only on mirrors when children are near.

en.question: If there is no sidewalk available, how should pedestrians walk along the road?

choices.A: On the side of the road facing traffic.
choices.B: On the side of the road moving in the same direction as traffic.
choices.C: In the center of the lane.
choices.D: On the right shoulder, regardless of traffic direction.

en.explanation: According to the manual, pedestrians are supposed to walk on the side of the road and face the traffic in the lane nearest them.

en.question: When must you yield the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian crossing with a guide dog or white cane?

choices.A: Only when they are in a marked crosswalk.
choices.B: Only when the traffic signal is in their favor.
choices.C: Always, even if traffic signals are not in their favor.
choices.D: Only during daylight hours.

en.explanation: A special right-of-way law requires drivers to always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing with a guide dog or white/metal cane, even if traffic signals are not in their favor.

en.question: According to the law, where are pedestrians permitted to stand to hitchhike?

choices.A: On the shoulder of an expressway.
choices.B: In the center median of a divided highway.
choices.C: In the road, as long as they wear reflective clothing.
choices.D: Pedestrians are never allowed to stand in the road to hitchhike.

en.explanation: The law requires pedestrians to never stand in the road to hitchhike or conduct business with motorists.

en.question: In New York City, more than 35% of pedestrian injury crashes occur during which driver maneuver?

choices.A: Parallel parking.
choices.B: Making a left turn.
choices.C: Making a right turn.
choices.D: Backing out of a driveway.

en.explanation: The manual notes that left turns can be a very dangerous maneuver, pointing out that > 35% of NYC pedestrian injury crashes occur when a driver is attempting to make a left turn.

en.question: What should you do if you approach a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk?

choices.A: Pass the vehicle slowly on the left.
choices.B: Honk your horn to alert the driver to move.
choices.C: Never pass the vehicle, as there may be pedestrians crossing.
choices.D: Pass the vehicle on the right if there is enough room.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Never pass vehicles stopped at a crosswalk. There may be people crossing where you can’t see.'

en.question: How can a vehicle's A-pillars affect your driving?

choices.A: They improve your peripheral vision.
choices.B: They can create blind spots that interfere with seeing clearly.
choices.C: They help reduce the glare from oncoming headlights.
choices.D: They automatically adjust your mirrors for better visibility.

en.explanation: Drivers must be aware of their vehicle's A-pillars (vertical supports around the glass) because they may interfere with seeing clearly and can create blind spots.

en.question: In which direction are bicyclists required to travel on the road?

choices.A: Facing oncoming traffic.
choices.B: In the same direction as motor vehicles.
choices.C: In whichever direction has the least traffic.
choices.D: On the left side of the road at all times.

en.explanation: The manual states that bicyclists have the right to share the road and travel in the same direction as motor vehicles.

en.question: Why should you reduce your speed when passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: To avoid splashing water on them.
choices.B: Because bicyclists are required to stop when being passed.
choices.C: Air pressure from a vehicle passing quickly can send the bicyclist off balance.
choices.D: To allow the bicyclist to grab onto your vehicle for a tow.

en.explanation: Drivers should give bicyclists room and reduce speed as they pass because air pressure from a vehicle that passes quickly can send them off balance.

en.question: What is the maximum number of bicyclists that may travel side-by-side in a single lane?

choices.A: One.
choices.B: Two.
choices.C: Three.
choices.D: Four.

en.explanation: Bicyclists must never travel with more than two side-by-side in a single lane.

en.question: According to New York law, which age group of bicyclists and their passengers are required to wear an approved helmet?

choices.A: Ages 1 to 13.
choices.B: Ages 5 to 16.
choices.C: Ages 10 to 18.
choices.D: All ages are required by state law.

en.explanation: The manual states that bicyclists and their passengers ages 1 - 13 must wear an approved helmet.

en.question: Under what condition may a bicyclist carry an infant under one year old as a passenger?

choices.A: If the infant is in an attached bicycle safety seat.
choices.B: If the infant is wearing an approved helmet.
choices.C: If the bicyclist is riding in a designated bicycle lane.
choices.D: Under no condition; it is against the law.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that a bicyclist must never carry an infant under a year old as a passenger, as it is against the law.

en.question: If a bicycle crash causes death or serious injury, within how many days must it be reported to the DMV?

choices.A: 3 days.
choices.B: 5 days.
choices.C: 10 days.
choices.D: 30 days.

en.explanation: Any bicycle crash that causes death or serious injury must be reported to the DMV within 10 days of the incident.

en.question: A bicycle driven on public highways must be equipped with a horn or bell that can be heard from at least how far away?

choices.A: 50 feet.
choices.B: 100 feet.
choices.C: 200 feet.
choices.D: 500 feet.

en.explanation: A bicycle driven on public highways must have adequate brakes and a horn or bell that can be heard at least 100 feet (30 m) away.

en.question: What lighting equipment is required for a bicycle used at night?

choices.A: A headlight visible from 100 feet ahead and a red taillight visible from 100 feet behind.
choices.B: A headlight visible from 300 feet ahead and a red taillight visible from 500 feet behind.
choices.C: A headlight visible from 500 feet ahead and a red taillight visible from 300 feet behind.
choices.D: Only spoke-mounted reflectors are required at night.

en.explanation: A bicycle used at night must have a headlight visible from at least 500 feet ahead and a red taillight visible from at least 300 feet behind.

en.question: What should a driver do before making a right turn on red to avoid hitting a bicyclist?

choices.A: Honk the horn to warn bicyclists before turning.
choices.B: Stop completely and look left-right-left and behind.
choices.C: Roll through the intersection slowly while looking right.
choices.D: Yield only to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Stop completely and look left-right-left and behind before turning right on red' to avoid hitting a bicyclist approaching from the right rear.

en.question: What is the purpose of a 'Bike Box' on the roadway?

choices.A: It is a designated parking area for bicycles.
choices.B: It is a marked area at an intersection ahead of where traffic stops to provide extra space for bicyclists.
choices.C: It is a storage container for shared city bicycles.
choices.D: It is a lane exclusively for motorized scooters.

en.explanation: The manual defines a Bike Box as 'a marked area at an intersection, ahead of where traffic is required to stop. This area provides extra space for bicyclists.'

en.question: What is the purpose of green painted bike lanes?

choices.A: To indicate areas where bicycles are prohibited.
choices.B: To increase visibility to cyclists in some high traffic areas.
choices.C: To show where pedestrians have the right-of-way over bicycles.
choices.D: To mark temporary detour routes for bicyclists.

en.explanation: The manual states that 'Green painted bike lanes are used to increase visibility to cyclists in some high traffic areas.'

en.question: Which of the following statements about motorcycles sharing a lane is true?

choices.A: A motorcycle can share a lane with a passenger car.
choices.B: Two motorcyclists are allowed to ride side-by-side in a single lane.
choices.C: Motorcyclists must ride in a single file line at all times.
choices.D: A motorcycle is not allowed to use the full width of a traffic lane.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'In addition to using the full lane, two motorcyclists are allowed to ride side-by-side in a single lane, but a motorcyclist cannot pass or share a lane with another motor vehicle that is not a motorcycle.'

en.question: How does the smaller size of a motorcycle affect a driver's perception of it?

choices.A: It makes the motorcycle appear to be moving slower than it actually is.
choices.B: It makes it difficult to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going.
choices.C: It makes the motorcycle's headlights appear brighter.
choices.D: It makes it easier to determine the motorcycle's exact lane position.

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'A motorcycle’s smaller size makes it seem much farther away, and makes it difficult to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going.'

en.question: Why might a motorcycle's turn signal be flashing even if the rider has no intention of turning?

choices.A: Motorcycle turn signals are designed to flash continuously for safety.
choices.B: The directional signal on most motorcycles does not turn off automatically after a turn.
choices.C: The rider is indicating that they are slowing down.
choices.D: The motorcycle is experiencing an electrical malfunction.

en.explanation: The manual explains that 'on most motorcycles, the directional signal does not turn off automatically after a turn, so their turn signal may be on inadvertently when the motorcyclist has no intention of turning.'

en.question: According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a significant percentage of fatal motorcycle crashes involve:

choices.A: A motorcycle rear-ending a stopped truck.
choices.B: Another vehicle turning left while the motorcycle is going straight or passing.
choices.C: A motorcycle losing control on loose gravel.
choices.D: Another vehicle turning right on red without stopping.

en.explanation: The manual notes that in 2015, 41 percent of fatal motorcycle crashes in the US occurred with 'the other vehicle turning left while the motorcycles were going straight, passing, or overtaking other vehicles.'

en.question: Why are motorcycle brake lights often less obvious to other motorists compared to car brake lights?

choices.A: They flash rapidly instead of staying solid.
choices.B: They are mounted lower than eye level and lack a Center High Mount Stop Light.
choices.C: They are usually painted over to match the motorcycle's color.
choices.D: They only illuminate when the front brake is applied.

en.explanation: The manual states that most cars have a 'Center High Mount Stop Light' at eye level, while 'Most motorcycle brake lights are mounted lower than eye level, which makes them less obvious to many motorists.'

en.question: Why might a motorcyclist quickly change speed or lane position?

choices.A: To avoid loose gravel, debris, or seams in the pavement.
choices.B: To communicate with other motorcyclists.
choices.C: To warm up their tires.
choices.D: To intentionally block faster-moving traffic.

en.explanation: The manual warns that a motorcyclist 'may quickly change speed or lane position to avoid loose gravel, debris, seams or grooves in the pavement, sewer or access covers or small animals.'

en.question: What rights and responsibilities do people on bicycles have on the road?

choices.A: They have the right-of-way at all times regardless of traffic signals.
choices.B: They have the same rights and responsibilities as people driving motor vehicles.
choices.C: They must always yield to motor vehicles.
choices.D: They are only allowed to ride on sidewalks and designated trails.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'People on bicycles have the same rights and responsibilities as people behind the wheel of a motor vehicle.'

en.question: What is a 2-way cycle track?

choices.A: A dirt path exclusively for off-road bicycles.
choices.B: A shared lane where bicycles and cars travel in opposite directions.
choices.C: A marked bicycle lane that allows travel in both directions.
choices.D: A highway lane designated for motorcycles and bicycles only.

en.explanation: The manual defines a 2-way cycle track as 'a marked bicycle lane that allows travel in both directions, similar to a sidewalk for pedestrians.'

en.question: How should a motor vehicle driver react when sharing the road with in-line skaters, skateboarders, and non-motorized scooters?

choices.A: Sound the horn continuously until they move off the road.
choices.B: Exercise due care by being aware, alert, and driving defensively.
choices.C: Pass them as closely as possible to encourage them to use the sidewalk.
choices.D: Assume they will always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual states that as a driver, you are responsible to 'exercise due care by being aware, alert, and driving defensively' around in-line skaters, skateboarders, and non-motorized scooters.

en.question: What precaution should you take before getting out of a parked vehicle on the side of a road?

choices.A: Turn on your hazard lights for at least one minute.
choices.B: Honk your horn to alert approaching traffic.
choices.C: Look for oncoming bicyclists to avoid opening your door into their path.
choices.D: Open the door quickly to minimize the time it is in the roadway.

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to 'Look before getting out of your parked vehicle; avoid opening your door into the path of an oncoming bicyclist.'

en.question: What is a true statement regarding motorcycle headlights during the day?

choices.A: They must be illuminated when driving, but they may not stand out due to other vehicles' daytime running lights.
choices.B: They are legally required to be turned off during daylight hours to save battery.
choices.C: They are equipped with special flashing bulbs to distinguish them from cars.
choices.D: They are only required to be used during inclement weather.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Headlights and taillights on motorcycles must be illuminated when driving. But, with so many vehicles equipped with daytime running lights... motorcycle headlights don’t stand out.'

en.question: What might a motorcyclist do when approaching a railroad crossing?

choices.A: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly
choices.B: Decrease speed and rise off the seat
choices.C: Swerve sharply into the oncoming lane
choices.D: Stop completely and walk the motorcycle across

en.explanation: According to the manual, when approaching a railroad crossing, a motorcyclist may decrease speed and rise off the seat to cushion the rough crossing and change direction to go across the tracks at a right angle.

en.question: Why might a motorcyclist move to the center of the lane on a steel deck bridge?

choices.A: To block faster moving traffic
choices.B: To adjust for an uneven surface
choices.C: To prepare for a U-turn
choices.D: To avoid the glare of oncoming headlights

en.explanation: The manual states that on steel deck bridges, a motorcyclist may move to the center of the lane to adjust for the surface that is not even.

en.question: Where are Class B and C mopeds permitted to be driven on the road?

choices.A: In any traffic lane
choices.B: Only on the shoulder of expressways
choices.C: Only in the right lane of traffic, as far to the right as possible
choices.D: In the left lane when traveling above 20 mph

en.explanation: Class B and C mopeds can be driven only in the right lane of traffic, as far to the right as possible, or on the shoulder.

en.question: Are mopeds allowed to be driven on expressways?

choices.A: Yes, but only in the right lane
choices.B: Yes, if they are Class A mopeds
choices.C: No, unless posted signs permit it
choices.D: No, under any circumstances

en.explanation: Mopeds are not permitted on expressways or other controlled access highways unless posted signs permit it.

en.question: In fatal crashes involving cars and big trucks, who usually contributes to the cause of the crash?

choices.A: The truck driver
choices.B: The car driver
choices.C: Pedestrians
choices.D: Highway maintenance workers

en.explanation: In more than 60 percent of all fatal crashes that involve cars and big trucks, the car driver, not the truck driver, contributes to the cause of the traffic crash.

en.question: How large can the blind spot be in front of a tractor with a long hood?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: Tractors with long hoods can have a blind spot of 20 feet in front of the vehicle, which drivers should avoid.

en.question: Why do tractor-trailers take much longer to stop than smaller vehicles?

choices.A: They have smaller brake pads
choices.B: Brake delay caused by air brakes
choices.C: Their tires have less traction
choices.D: The drivers have slower reaction times

en.explanation: For tractor trailers, the difference in stopping distance comes from brake delay. Air brakes transmit brake power from the tractor to the trailer and this can add many feet to the distance it takes to stop.

en.question: What maneuver do large trucks often make before executing a wide right turn?

choices.A: They move to the left
choices.B: They speed up significantly
choices.C: They drive onto the right shoulder
choices.D: They turn on their hazard lights

en.explanation: Because trucks make wide right turns, they move to the left before they turn right. Drivers should pay close attention to their turn signals.

en.question: Why should you not underestimate the speed of an approaching tractor-trailer?

choices.A: They are legally allowed to exceed the speed limit
choices.B: Their larger size makes them appear to move slower than they really are
choices.C: They always accelerate when approaching cars
choices.D: Their headlights distort your depth perception

en.explanation: Do not underestimate the size and speed of an approaching tractor-trailer. Its larger size will often make it appear to move at a slower speed than it really is.

en.question: Why should you leave extra space when stopped behind a truck or bus on a hill?

choices.A: The exhaust fumes are toxic at close range
choices.B: The vehicle could move backward slightly when it starts
choices.C: The driver needs room to open the rear doors
choices.D: To allow pedestrians to cross between the vehicles

en.explanation: Always leave space when you stop in back of a truck or bus at a traffic light or stop sign, especially when you face up a hill. The truck or bus could move backward slightly when it starts.

en.question: What does the "slow-moving vehicle" symbol look like?

choices.A: A yellow diamond
choices.B: A reflective orange triangle
choices.C: A red octagon
choices.D: A white rectangle with black lettering

en.explanation: The "slow-moving vehicle" symbol is a reflective orange triangle that must be displayed on the back of vehicles drawn by animals, most farm vehicles, and construction equipment.

en.question: How must all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) and snowmobiles cross state highways?

choices.A: Without stopping if the speed limit is under 45 mph
choices.B: At a 45-degree angle to minimize time on the road
choices.C: By coming to a stop, yielding, and crossing at a 90-degree angle
choices.D: Only at designated traffic lights

en.explanation: Before ATVs and snowmobiles cross highways, they must come to a stop and yield to traffic. They must go across at a 90-degree angle to the road surface.

en.question: Where are horse riders required to ride on the road?

choices.A: In the center of the lane
choices.B: Single file near the right curb or road edge
choices.C: Two abreast on the left shoulder
choices.D: On the sidewalk only

en.explanation: Horse riders are subject to the rules of the road and must ride single file near the right curb or road edge or on a right shoulder, lane or path that can be used.

en.question: What is the top speed range for a Class A limited use motorcycle (moped)?

choices.A: 20 mph or less
choices.B: 21 to 30 mph
choices.C: 31 to 40 mph
choices.D: 41 to 50 mph

en.explanation: According to the Guide to Limited Use Motorcycle (Moped) Operation chart, the top speed range for a Class A moped is 31 to 40 mph.

en.question: What should you do if a large truck is blocking the road to back into a loading area?

choices.A: Honk your horn to alert the driver
choices.B: Quickly pass close behind the truck
choices.C: Wait patiently until the backup maneuver is completed
choices.D: Drive on the sidewalk to bypass the truck

en.explanation: Never pass close behind a large vehicle that is backing up. It is far better to wait patiently until the large vehicle has completed its backup maneuver than to try to pass and risk entering a blind spot.

en.question: What is illegal to do when you approach or pass a horse being ridden or walked along a road?

choices.A: Pass the horse at a slow speed
choices.B: Sound your horn
choices.C: Leave a wide distance between your vehicle and the horse
choices.D: Yield the right-of-way

en.explanation: The manual states that it is illegal to sound your horn when you approach or pass a horse.

en.question: What type of violation is it to leave the scene of a traffic crash that involves a fatality or personal injury?

choices.A: A minor traffic infraction
choices.B: A civil penalty
choices.C: A moving violation
choices.D: A criminal violation

en.explanation: It is a criminal violation to leave the scene of an incident that involves a fatality or personal injury.

en.question: If you damage a parked vehicle or injure a domestic animal in a crash, what must you do?

choices.A: Leave a note on the windshield and drive away
choices.B: Try to find the owner or notify the police
choices.C: Wait 15 minutes and leave if no one shows up
choices.D: Report it to the DMV within 30 days

en.explanation: If a parked vehicle or property different from a vehicle is damaged or if a domestic animal is injured, you must try to find the owner or notify the police.

en.question: Under what circumstances should you move an injured person at a crash scene?

choices.A: Only if they ask you to help them stand up
choices.B: Only if it becomes necessary because of fire or another life-threatening danger
choices.C: Whenever they are blocking the flow of traffic
choices.D: Immediately upon arriving at the scene to make them comfortable

en.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless it becomes necessary because of fire or another life threatening danger.

en.question: If you must move an injured person away from a life-threatening danger, how should you pull them?

choices.A: By their arms
choices.B: By their legs
choices.C: Head first
choices.D: Sideways

en.explanation: Hold clothing with your hands and pull the victim head first away from the danger while keeping the back and neck as straight as possible.

en.question: What should you do if wires are touching a vehicle at a crash scene?

choices.A: Use a wooden stick to move the wires off the vehicle
choices.B: Open the doors to help the occupants escape quickly
choices.C: Warn the occupants to remain inside until help arrives
choices.D: Pull the wires away with heavy-duty gloves

en.explanation: If there are wires down, do not go near them. If wires touch the vehicle or lay near it, warn the occupants to remain inside until help arrives.

en.question: You must report a traffic crash to the DMV if it involves a fatality, personal injury, or property damage to any one person of at least what amount?
en.explanation: You must also report any traffic incident or crash that involves $1,000 or more in damage to the property of any one person.

en.question: How many days do you have to file a crash report (MV-104) with the DMV after a reportable accident?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: You must file a report with DMV within 10 days of the event.

en.question: What is a possible penalty for failing to report an accident to the DMV?

choices.A: A warning letter
choices.B: Mandatory driver retraining
choices.C: Suspension or revocation of your driver license and/or registrations
choices.D: A permanent mark on your credit report

en.explanation: The failure to report an accident is a criminal offense (misdemeanor) and can mean the suspension or revocation of your driver license and/or registrations and those of the vehicle owner.

en.question: If the driver is injured and unable to complete the required DMV crash report, who may do so?

choices.A: Only a police officer
choices.B: Only the driver's insurance agent

en.question: Which of the following Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) features are you NOT allowed to use during your driving test?

choices.B: Blind spot monitor
choices.C: Automatic parallel parking
choices.D: Forward collision warning

choices.C: In rain, snow, ice, or fog
choices.D: When driving under the speed limit

choices.B: Automatic parallel parking

choices.D: Self-driving autopilot

en.question: What is the driver's responsibility when operating a vehicle equipped with Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)?

choices.C: To disable all safety features before driving
choices.D: To let the vehicle steer itself on highways

en.explanation: Safety features are meant to assist you in the driving task, they are not there to drive the vehicle. You must remain engaged and always focused on the driving task.

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What does this sign indicate?

choices.A: Left turn only
choices.B: Traffic flows in one direction — to the left
choices.C: Keep left of the median
choices.D: Highway exit to the left

en.explanation: A black and white ONE WAY sign with an arrow indicates that traffic on this street moves in only one direction — the direction the arrow points.

en.question: What does this sign prohibit?

choices.A: Right turns
choices.B: Left turns
choices.C: U-turns
choices.D: Passing other vehicles

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign with a U-turn arrow crossed out means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What does this sign instruct drivers to do?

choices.A: Merge right
choices.B: Turn right only
choices.C: Keep to the right of a divider or obstruction
choices.D: Right lane ends ahead

en.explanation: A white regulatory KEEP RIGHT sign with an arrow means you must keep to the right side of a traffic island, median, or obstruction.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What road condition does this sign warn about?

choices.A: A winding road
choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions
choices.D: A roundabout ahead

en.explanation: A reverse curve sign warns of two curves in opposite directions ahead. Slow down and be prepared for the road to curve first one way, then the other.

en.question: What does this sign warn you to expect?

choices.A: A single sharp curve
choices.B: A slippery road surface
choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead
choices.D: A hill ahead

en.explanation: A winding road sign warns of a series of curves or turns ahead. Reduce your speed and be alert for changing road conditions.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to prepare for?

choices.A: A lane ending
choices.B: Traffic merging from another road
choices.C: A divided highway beginning
choices.D: A road narrowing to one lane

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped merge sign warns that traffic from another road will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to adjust your speed and position.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: What does this sign tell you to expect ahead?

choices.A: A yield sign
choices.B: A traffic signal
choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop
choices.D: A speed bump

en.explanation: This sign warns that there is a stop sign ahead. Begin slowing down and prepare to come to a complete stop at the stop sign.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

es.question: Según el Registro Done Vida del Estado de Nueva York (New York State Donate Life Registry), ¿cuántas vidas puede salvar una sola persona que dona sus órganos?

choices.A: Hasta 4 vidas
choices.B: Hasta 6 vidas
choices.C: Hasta 8 vidas
choices.D: Hasta 10 vidas

es.explanation: El manual indica que una sola persona que dona sus órganos puede salvar hasta ocho vidas.

es.question: Si usted tiene una licencia de conducir válida de otro estado, ¿cuál es la edad mínima requerida para conducir legalmente en el estado de Nueva York?
es.explanation: Según el manual, incluso si tiene licencia de otro lugar, las personas menores de 16 años no pueden conducir en el estado de Nueva York.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene para obtener una licencia de conducir de Nueva York después de convertirse en residente permanente?

choices.A: 10 días
choices.B: 30 días
choices.C: 60 días
choices.D: 90 días

es.explanation: Los conductores que se han mudado a Nueva York deben entregar su licencia de conducir de fuera del estado y obtener una licencia de Nueva York dentro de los 30 días posteriores a convertirse en residentes permanentes.

es.question: ¿Cuál es una posible consecuencia de alterar o falsificar una licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Una carta de advertencia del DMV
choices.B: Servicio comunitario obligatorio
choices.C: Suspensión o revocación de la licencia y proceso penal
choices.D: Un curso obligatorio de manejo defensivo

es.explanation: Es un delito alterar o falsificar cualquier documento de un vehículo motorizado, lo cual puede causar la suspensión o revocación de la licencia de conducir y un proceso penal que resulte en una multa o encarcelamiento.

es.question: Usted debe tener una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) si conduce un vehículo fabricado o utilizado para transportar ¿a cuántas personas además del conductor?

choices.A: 8 o más
choices.B: 10 o más
choices.C: 12 o más
choices.D: 15 o más

es.explanation: Se requiere una CDL si conduce cualquier vehículo fabricado o utilizado para transportar a 15 personas o más, además del conductor.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para obtener una licencia de Operador Clase D sin un Certificado de Finalización de educación vial?
es.explanation: La edad mínima para una licencia de Operador Clase D es de 18 años, o 17 años con un Certificado de Finalización de educación vial.

es.question: ¿Qué clases de ciclomotores (mopeds) se le permite operar con una licencia estándar de Operador Clase D?

choices.A: Solo Clase A
choices.B: Ciclomotores Clase B y C
choices.C: Ciclomotores Clase A y B
choices.D: No se permiten ciclomotores sin una licencia de motocicleta

es.explanation: El manual indica que usted puede operar ciclomotores Clase B y C con una licencia de conducir Clase D.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para obtener una licencia Clase DJ (Operador Junior)?
es.explanation: La edad mínima para obtener una licencia de Operador Junior, Clase DJ es de 16 años.

es.question: ¿Qué clase de licencia se requiere para transportar pasajeros por contrato en un vehículo diseñado para llevar 14 pasajeros o menos, como un taxi o vehículo de alquiler (livery)?

choices.A: Clase C
choices.B: Clase D
choices.C: Clase E
choices.D: Clase M

es.explanation: Una licencia de Taxi/Vehículo de alquiler, Clase E le permite transportar pasajeros por contrato en un vehículo diseñado o utilizado para llevar 14 pasajeros o menos.

es.question: ¿Para qué tipo de viaje se puede usar una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada (Enhanced Driver License) en lugar de un pasaporte?

choices.A: Viajes aéreos internacionales a Europa
choices.B: Cruces fronterizos terrestres y marítimos hacia y desde Canadá, México, las Bermudas y el Caribe
choices.C: Cualquier viaje internacional en todo el mundo
choices.D: Viajes a Sudamérica en crucero

es.explanation: Una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada se puede usar para cruces fronterizos terrestres y marítimos hacia y desde los EE. UU., Canadá, México, las Bermudas y el Caribe en lugar de un pasaporte.

es.question: Se requiere una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) para conducir un solo vehículo con una clasificación de peso bruto del vehículo (GVWR) del fabricante de más de:

choices.A: 10,000 libras
choices.B: 15,000 libras
choices.C: 20,000 libras
choices.D: 26,000 libras

es.explanation: Debe tener una CDL si conduce cualquier vehículo que tenga una clasificación de peso bruto del vehículo (GVWR) del fabricante de más de 26,000 libras.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes afirmaciones es verdadera con respecto a tener múltiples licencias de conducir?

choices.A: Puede tener una licencia de Nueva York y una licencia de otro estado simultáneamente.
choices.B: En la mayoría de los casos, es ilegal tener una licencia de conducir de Nueva York y una licencia de conducir de otro estado al mismo tiempo.
choices.C: Se requiere que tenga una licencia para cada estado en el que conduce con frecuencia.
choices.D: Puede tener legalmente hasta dos licencias de conducir comerciales (CDL).

es.explanation: En la mayoría de los casos, es ilegal tener una licencia de conducir de Nueva York y una licencia de conducir de otro estado al mismo tiempo. También es una violación de la ley federal y estatal tener más de una CDL.

es.question: Una licencia Clase DJ (Operador Junior) le permite conducir un vehículo con una clasificación de peso bruto del vehículo (GVWR) de no más de:

choices.A: 5,000 libras
choices.B: 10,000 libras
choices.C: 15,000 libras
choices.D: 26,000 libras

es.explanation: Una licencia de Operador Junior, Clase DJ, le permite conducir un vehículo con un GVWR de 10,000 libras o menos.

es.question: Debe tener una Licencia de Conducir Comercial (CDL) si conduce un vehículo que:

choices.A: Transporta cualquier cantidad de bienes comerciales
choices.B: Se utiliza únicamente para fines agrícolas
choices.C: Transporta materiales peligrosos que, por ley federal, requieren llevar un cartel (placard)
choices.D: Remolca un tráiler que pesa 2,000 libras

es.explanation: El manual especifica que debe tener una CDL si conduce cualquier vehículo que transporte materiales peligrosos que, por ley federal, requieran llevar un cartel (placard).

es.question: Si tiene una licencia de motocicleta y otro tipo de licencia de conducir, ¿cómo se mostrarán?

choices.A: En dos documentos separados
choices.B: Ambas clases aparecerán en un solo documento
choices.C: Debe elegir solo una para que esté activa
choices.D: La licencia de motocicleta reemplaza a la otra licencia

es.explanation: Según el manual, si tiene una licencia de motocicleta y otro tipo de licencia de conducir, ambas clases aparecerán en un solo documento (por ejemplo, 'Clase DM').

es.question: Según la Ley REAL ID, ¿qué debe presentar todo pasajero aéreo que vuele dentro de los Estados Unidos para pasar por seguridad en los aeropuertos de EE. UU.?

choices.A: Solo un pasaporte estadounidense válido
choices.B: Una REAL ID, una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada (Enhanced Driver License) u otra forma aceptable de identificación federal
choices.C: Una licencia de conducir estándar emitida por el estado y un certificado de nacimiento
choices.D: Una tarjeta de Seguro Social y una factura de servicios públicos

es.explanation: Todo pasajero aéreo que vuele dentro de los Estados Unidos debe presentar una REAL ID, una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada, o llevar otra forma aceptable de identificación determinada por el gobierno federal.

es.question: El endoso 'R' para Vehículos de Uso Personal es necesario para operar vehículos recreativos o de alquiler utilizados para transportar bienes domésticos personales si el vehículo excede ¿qué especificaciones?

choices.A: 10,000 libras de GVWR y/o 20 pies de largo
choices.B: 18,000 libras de GVWR y/o 30 pies de largo
choices.C: 26,000 libras de GVWR y/o 40 pies de largo
choices.D: 32,000 libras de GVWR y/o 50 pies de largo

es.explanation: El endoso 'R' es necesario para la operación de vehículos recreativos y/o de alquiler utilizados para transportar bienes domésticos personales cuando el vehículo supera las 26,000 libras de GVWR y/o los cuarenta (40) pies de largo.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes afirmaciones es verdadera con respecto a los requisitos de examen para obtener un endoso 'R'?

choices.A: Debe aprobar tanto un examen escrito como un examen práctico de manejo.
choices.B: Debe aprobar un examen escrito, pero no se requiere un examen práctico de manejo.
choices.C: No se requiere un examen escrito, pero debe aprobar un examen práctico de manejo.
choices.D: No se requiere ni un examen escrito ni un examen práctico de manejo.

es.explanation: Para obtener un endoso 'R', debe aprobar un examen práctico de manejo en el tamaño y tipo de vehículo que conducirá. El manual establece explícitamente: 'No se requiere examen escrito'.

es.question: ¿Quién debe acompañarlo para su examen práctico de manejo del endoso 'R'?

choices.A: Un instructor de manejo con licencia.
choices.B: Cualquier conductor con licencia mayor de 18 años.
choices.C: Un conductor que tenga al menos 21 años con una licencia válida para el vehículo que conducirá durante el examen.
choices.D: Un funcionario del DMV que posea una Licencia de Conducir Comercial.

es.explanation: Para el examen práctico de manejo, debe acompañarlo un conductor que tenga al menos 21 años, con una licencia válida para el vehículo que conducirá durante el examen.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo se emitirá su primera licencia de conducir de Nueva York?

choices.A: Exactamente 10 años
choices.B: Un período que no exceda los 5 años, en su mes y día de nacimiento
choices.C: Un período que no exceda los 8 años, en su mes y día de nacimiento
choices.D: Hasta que cumpla 21 años

es.explanation: Su primera licencia de conducir de Nueva York se emitirá por un período que no excederá los 5 años, en su mes y día de nacimiento.

es.question: Al solicitar su primera licencia, debe presentar documentos que prueben su nombre. ¿Cuántos puntos deben sumar estas pruebas en total?

choices.A: Cuatro puntos o más
choices.B: Seis puntos o más
choices.C: Ocho puntos o más
choices.D: Diez puntos o más

es.explanation: A los documentos que prueban su nombre se les asigna un valor en puntos. Debe presentar pruebas que sumen seis puntos o más en total.

es.question: Al presentar documentos para probar su nombre para una solicitud de licencia de conducir, ¿cuál es un requisito específico para al menos una de las pruebas?

choices.A: Debe contener su fotografía.
choices.B: Debe ser emitida por el gobierno federal.
choices.C: Debe tener su firma.
choices.D: Debe mostrar su dirección residencial actual.

es.explanation: El manual establece que al presentar pruebas de su nombre que sumen seis puntos o más, 'Al menos una de las pruebas debe tener su firma'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes documentos tiene un valor de 6 puntos al probar su nombre para una licencia de conducir de Nueva York?

choices.A: Un pasaporte válido de EE. UU.
choices.B: Una tarjeta de Seguro Social de EE. UU.
choices.C: Una licencia de conducir con foto o tarjeta de identificación de no conductor de Nueva York
choices.D: Una tarjeta de identificación militar con foto de EE. UU.

es.explanation: Una licencia de conducir con foto/permiso/tarjeta de identificación de no conductor de Nueva York (vigente o no vencida por más de 2 años) tiene un valor de 6 puntos.

es.question: ¿Cuántos puntos vale un pasaporte válido de EE. UU. al probar su identidad para una licencia de conducir de Nueva York?

choices.A: 2 puntos
choices.B: 3 puntos
choices.C: 4 puntos
choices.D: 6 puntos

es.explanation: Según la lista de documentos aceptables, un pasaporte o tarjeta de pasaporte válido de EE. UU. tiene un valor de 4 puntos.

es.question: Si sus documentos de prueba de identidad no están en inglés, ¿qué debe proporcionar?

choices.A: Una traducción certificada al inglés
choices.B: Una carta notariada de un ciudadano estadounidense
choices.C: Un permiso internacional de conducir
choices.D: Una traducción verbal en la oficina del DMV

es.explanation: El manual establece que todas las pruebas deben estar en inglés o acompañadas de una traducción certificada al inglés.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes es un documento aceptable para probar su fecha de nacimiento?

choices.A: Una identificación con foto de escuela secundaria de EE. UU. con boleta de calificaciones
choices.B: Una factura de servicios públicos de EE. UU.
choices.C: Una tarjeta de identificación militar con foto de EE. UU.
choices.D: Una tarjeta de crédito principal de EE. UU.

es.explanation: Bajo la sección 'Prueba de edad', una tarjeta de identificación militar con foto de EE. UU. figura como un documento aceptable para probar su fecha de nacimiento.

es.question: Para aprobar el examen de la vista para una licencia de conducir de Nueva York, ¿qué agudeza visual debe tener en al menos un ojo?
es.explanation: Para aprobar el examen de la vista, debe tener una visión de 20/40 en al menos un ojo, con o sin lentes correctivos.

es.question: Además de aprobar un examen de la vista y de conocimientos, ¿qué deben completar la mayoría de los conductores antes de tomar un examen práctico de manejo para su primera licencia?

choices.A: Un curso de manejo defensivo de 10 horas
choices.B: Un curso de pre-licencia aprobado de 5 horas
choices.C: Un programa de capacitación práctica al volante de 15 horas
choices.D: Una clase certificada de primeros auxilios y RCP

es.explanation: El manual establece que la mayoría de los conductores también deben completar un curso de pre-licencia aprobado de 5 horas y aprobar un examen práctico de manejo al solicitar su primera licencia.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito mínimo de visión para aprobar el examen de la vista para una licencia de conducir de Nueva York?

choices.A: Visión de 20/20 en ambos ojos
choices.B: Visión de 20/30 en al menos un ojo
choices.C: Visión de 20/40 en al menos un ojo
choices.D: Visión de 20/50 en ambos ojos

es.explanation: Según el manual, para aprobar el examen de la vista, debe tener una visión de 20/40 en al menos un ojo, con o sin lentes correctivos.

es.question: Para aprobar el examen escrito para una licencia Clase D, ¿cuántas preguntas debe responder correctamente en total?

choices.A: Al menos 10 de 20
choices.B: Al menos 14 de 20
choices.C: Al menos 16 de 20
choices.D: Las 20 preguntas

es.explanation: El manual establece que para aprobar el examen escrito, debe responder correctamente al menos 14 de las 20 preguntas formuladas.

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas sobre señales de tránsito debe responder correctamente para aprobar el examen de conocimientos escrito?

choices.A: Una de cuatro
choices.B: Dos de cuatro
choices.C: Tres de cuatro
choices.D: Cuatro de cuatro

es.explanation: El manual especifica que debe responder correctamente dos de las cuatro preguntas sobre señales de tránsito para aprobar el examen escrito.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima requerida para que un estudiante tome el examen escrito a través del programa de Aplicación de Examen de Conocimientos en Línea del DMV (OKTA, por sus siglas en inglés) en una escuela secundaria participante?

choices.A: 15 años
choices.B: 15 años y 6 meses
choices.C: 15 años y 11 meses
choices.D: 16 años

es.explanation: Antes de solicitar un permiso de aprendizaje, los estudiantes que tienen al menos 15 años y 11 meses de edad pueden tomar el examen escrito a través del programa OKTA.

es.question: Al practicar la conducción con un permiso de aprendizaje, ¿cuáles son los requisitos para su conductor supervisor?

choices.A: Debe tener al menos 18 años y cualquier licencia válida
choices.B: Debe tener al menos 21 años, una licencia válida para el tipo de vehículo y sentarse en el asiento delantero
choices.C: Debe ser un instructor de manejo con licencia
choices.D: Debe tener al menos 25 años y sentarse en el asiento trasero

es.explanation: Cuando practique, debe ser supervisado por un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos 21 años, que tenga una licencia válida para el tipo de vehículo que usted conduce y que esté sentado en el asiento delantero con usted.

es.question: Si tiene un Permiso Junior (Junior Permit) y conduce en la ciudad de Nueva York (los 5 distritos) entre las 5 a.m. y las 9 p.m., ¿qué equipo especial debe tener el vehículo?

choices.A: Una cámara de reversa
choices.B: Un letrero de estudiante de manejo
choices.C: Controles duales (frenos duales)
choices.D: Espejos laterales adicionales

es.explanation: Bajo las restricciones regionales para un Permiso Junior en la ciudad de Nueva York entre las 5 a.m. y las 9 p.m., el vehículo debe tener controles duales (frenos duales).

es.question: Con un Permiso Junior en el norte del estado de Nueva York (Upstate New York - todos los demás condados), ¿quién debe supervisarlo si conduce entre las 9 p.m. y las 5 a.m.?

choices.A: Cualquier conductor con licencia mayor de 18 años
choices.B: Cualquier conductor con licencia mayor de 21 años
choices.C: NO debe conducir durante estas horas
choices.D: Su padre, tutor, persona 'in loco parentis', profesor de educación vial o instructor de la escuela de manejo

es.explanation: En los condados del norte del estado, entre las 9 p.m. y las 5 a.m., el titular de un Permiso Junior solo debe conducir bajo la supervisión inmediata de un padre, tutor, persona 'in loco parentis', profesor de educación vial o instructor de la escuela de manejo.

es.question: Según las reglas generales para todos los conductores con permisos de aprendizaje, ¿dónde está estrictamente prohibido conducir?

choices.A: En cualquier calle dentro de un parque en la ciudad de Nueva York
choices.B: En cualquier autopista interestatal
choices.C: En zonas escolares durante el horario escolar
choices.D: En carreteras con un límite de velocidad superior a 40 mph

es.explanation: Si tiene un permiso de aprendizaje, no puede conducir en ninguna calle dentro de un parque en la ciudad de Nueva York ni en ningún puente o túnel bajo la jurisdicción de la Autoridad de Puentes y Túneles de Triborough (Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority).

es.question: ¿En cuál de las siguientes avenidas (parkways) del condado de Westchester NO se le permite conducir con un permiso de aprendizaje?

choices.A: Northern State Parkway
choices.B: Taconic State Parkway
choices.C: Garden State Parkway
choices.D: Palisades Interstate Parkway

es.explanation: Los titulares de un permiso de aprendizaje no pueden conducir en las avenidas (parkways) Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River o Taconic State en el condado de Westchester.

es.question: Si tiene un Permiso de Aprendizaje Junior (Junior Learner Permit), ¿cuál es la regla con respecto a los pasajeros menores de 21 años?

choices.A: No puede llevar ningún pasajero menor de 21 años
choices.B: Puede llevar hasta tres pasajeros menores de 21 años
choices.C: No puede conducir con más de un pasajero menor de 21 años a menos que sean familiares inmediatos o su supervisor sea un padre/tutor/instructor
choices.D: Puede llevar tantos pasajeros menores de 21 años como cinturones de seguridad haya

es.explanation: No puede conducir con más de un pasajero menor de 21 años a menos que sean miembros de su familia inmediata o si su conductor supervisor es su padre, tutor, persona 'in loco parentis', profesor de educación vial o instructor de la escuela de manejo.

es.question: Si tiene un permiso junior, ¿quién es el único pasajero al que se le permite sentarse en el asiento delantero con usted?

choices.A: Su conductor supervisor
choices.B: Un hermano menor de 18 años
choices.C: Cualquier pasajero mayor de 21 años
choices.D: No se permite a nadie en el asiento delantero

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente: 'Si tiene un permiso junior, el único pasajero permitido en el asiento delantero es su conductor supervisor'.

es.question: Antes de tomar su examen práctico de manejo, ¿cuántas horas en total de práctica de manejo supervisada es importante que haya completado?

choices.A: Al menos 20 horas
choices.B: Al menos 30 horas
choices.C: Al menos 40 horas
choices.D: Al menos 50 horas

es.explanation: Antes de tomar el examen, es importante que haya tenido al menos 50 horas de práctica.

es.question: Out of the total recommended hours of supervised driving practice before a road test, how many hours must be completed after sunset?

choices.A: At least 5 hours
choices.B: At least 10 hours
choices.C: At least 15 hours
choices.D: At least 20 hours

es.explanation: The manual states it is important to have at least 50 hours of practice, with at least 15 hours after sunset.

es.question: What must you complete before you can make a road test appointment?

choices.A: An advanced defensive driving course
choices.B: An approved safe driver course (Pre-Licensing course or driver education)
choices.C: A highway driving certification
choices.D: A vision re-test

es.explanation: Before you can make a road test appointment, you must first complete an approved safe driver course, which is fulfilled by a high school/college driver education course or a Pre-Licensing course.

es.question: If you have a Junior Permit and are driving in Long Island (Nassau & Suffolk) between 9 PM and 5 AM, what are the restrictions?

choices.A: You must be supervised by a parent or guardian
choices.B: You must NOT drive
choices.C: You must be supervised by any licensed driver over 21
choices.D: You can drive alone if going to work

es.explanation: According to the Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit chart, in Long Island (Nassau & Suffolk) between 9 PM and 5 AM, 'You must NOT drive.'

es.question: How long is the Pre-Licensing Course completion certificate valid for?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 years
choices.D: 5 years

es.explanation: According to the manual, when you complete the safe driving course, you will receive a certificate that is valid for one year.

es.question: Does the DMV-certified Point & Insurance Reduction Program (Defensive Driving Course) meet the Safe Driving course requirement for scheduling a road test?

choices.A: Yes, if completed online.
choices.B: Yes, for drivers over 18.
choices.C: No, it does not meet the requirement.
choices.D: Yes, if completed within the last 6 months.

es.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'The DMV-certified Point & Insurance Reduction Program (a.k.a. Accident Prevention Course or Defensive Driving Course) does NOT meet the Safe Driving course requirement.'

es.question: At what age are you eligible to change a junior driver license to a senior driver license if you have completed a state-approved driver education course?
es.explanation: If you are 17, you are eligible for a senior driver license (Class D or M) if you have a junior driver license and have completed a state-approved high school or college driver education course.

es.question: How long must a junior driver hold their permit in valid status before they are allowed to take the road test?

choices.A: A minimum of 3 months
choices.B: A minimum of 6 months
choices.C: A minimum of 9 months
choices.D: A minimum of 12 months

es.explanation: For Junior Drivers with Permits, the manual states: 'Your permit must be held, in valid status for a minimum of six months in order to take the road test.'

es.question: How many hours of supervised practice driving must a parent or guardian certify that a junior driver has completed prior to the road test?

choices.A: 30 hours, including 10 hours after sunset
choices.B: 40 hours, including 10 hours after sunset
choices.C: 50 hours, including 15 hours after sunset
choices.D: 60 hours, including 15 hours after sunset

es.explanation: The Certification of Supervised Driving (MV-262) requires a parent or guardian to certify that the driver completed at least 50 hours of practice driving, including at least 15 hours after sunset.

es.question: What is a requirement for the supervising driver who accompanies you to the road test site?

choices.A: They must be at least 18 years old.
choices.B: They must be at least 21 years old and hold a valid license for the vehicle.
choices.C: They must be a certified driving instructor.
choices.D: They must be a parent or legal guardian.

es.explanation: If you drive to the road test site, you must bring a supervising driver who is at least 21 and holds a license valid for the vehicle you will drive during the road test.

es.question: What must motorcycle applicants bring to their road test to transport the license examiner?

choices.A: A motorcycle with a sidecar
choices.B: A second motorcycle for the examiner
choices.C: A car or truck and a licensed driver
choices.D: A certified motorcycle instructor

es.explanation: Motorcycle applicants must bring a car or truck and a licensed driver to transport the license examiner during the test.

es.question: How many points can be reduced from your driving record if you complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP)?

choices.A: Up to 2 points
choices.B: Up to 3 points
choices.C: Up to 4 points
choices.D: Up to 5 points

es.explanation: If you are eligible for point reduction, as many as four (4) points can be reduced from your driving record by completing the PIRP course.

es.question: How often can you complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP) for the purpose of point reduction?

choices.A: Every 12 months
choices.B: Every 18 months
choices.C: Every 2 years
choices.D: Every 3 years

es.explanation: You can complete the Point and Insurance Reduction Program course every 18 months for the purpose of point reduction.

es.question: When driving with a Junior License, how many passengers under the age of 21 are allowed in the vehicle if they are NOT members of your immediate family?

choices.A: None
choices.B: No more than one
choices.C: No more than two
choices.D: No more than three

es.explanation: Under Junior Operator Restrictions, you cannot drive with more than one passenger under the age of 21 unless they are members of your immediate family.

es.question: According to the regional restrictions for a Junior License, when are you allowed to drive in New York City (the 5 Boroughs)?

choices.A: Between 5 AM and 9 PM only
choices.B: Only when accompanied by a parent or guardian
choices.C: Only when driving to or from school
choices.D: You must NOT drive at any time

es.explanation: The regional restrictions chart for a Junior License clearly states that in New York City (5 Boroughs), 'You must NOT drive' between 5AM - 9PM and 'You must NOT drive' between 9PM - 5AM.

es.question: If you hold a Junior License and drive in Upstate counties between 5 AM and 9 PM, what are the restrictions on driving alone?

choices.A: You may drive without being accompanied.
choices.B: You must be accompanied by a licensed parent or guardian.
choices.C: You may only drive alone to employment or school.
choices.D: You must not drive.

es.explanation: According to the regional restrictions chart, in Upstate (All Other Counties) between 5AM - 9PM, 'You may drive without being accompanied.'

es.question: What specific proof of employment must a Junior License holder carry to drive to work in Nassau or Suffolk counties?

choices.A: A recent pay stub
choices.B: A Certificate of Employment (MV-58A)
choices.C: A letter from their employer
choices.D: A copy of their work schedule

es.explanation: If you hold a Junior License and drive in the counties of Nassau or Suffolk, your employer can complete a Certificate of Employment (MV-58A) to serve as correct proof of employment.

es.question: What is a specific requirement for the passenger side seat belt in the vehicle used for a road test?

choices.A: It must be a five-point harness.
choices.B: It must be available and clean for use by the examiner.
choices.C: It must be inspected by a mechanic prior to the test.
choices.D: It must be disabled if the examiner prefers.

es.explanation: The manual states that the vehicle must be in good working order, and specifically notes: 'The passenger side seat belt must be available and clean for use by the examiner.'

es.question: What passenger restriction applies to a learner permit or junior license for a motorcycle or moped (Class M or MJ)?

choices.A: You may carry one passenger if they are wearing a helmet.
choices.B: You may carry immediate family members only.
choices.C: You cannot carry any passenger except your supervising driver.
choices.D: You may carry any passenger over the age of 21.

es.explanation: The manual states: 'Your learner permit or junior license (Class M or MJ) does not allow you to carry any passenger except your supervising driver.'

es.question: Who is permitted to ride as a passenger when you are operating a motorcycle or moped with a Class M or MJ learner permit?

choices.A: Any family member
choices.B: Only your supervising driver
choices.C: Anyone over the age of 18
choices.D: No passengers are allowed under any circumstances

es.explanation: According to the manual, a learner permit or junior license (Class M or MJ) does not allow you to carry any passenger except your supervising driver.

es.question: How close must a supervising driver remain when you are operating a motorcycle or moped with a learner permit?

choices.A: Within 100 feet
choices.B: Within one-quarter mile
choices.C: Within one-half mile
choices.D: Within one mile

es.explanation: The manual states that your supervising driver must exercise general supervision and control by remaining within one-quarter mile.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene para notificar al DMV si cambia su dirección residencial?

choices.A: 5 días
choices.B: 10 días
choices.C: 30 días
choices.D: 60 días

es.explanation: Si cambia de dirección, debe notificar al DMV dentro de 10 días por correo, en un Formulario de Cambio de Dirección o en línea.

es.question: ¿Con cuánta anticipación puede renovar su licencia de conducir antes de su fecha de vencimiento impresa?

choices.A: Hasta 30 días
choices.B: Hasta 45 días
choices.C: Hasta 6 meses
choices.D: Hasta un año

es.explanation: El manual indica que puede renovar su licencia hasta un año antes de su fecha de vencimiento impresa.

es.question: Al solicitar una REAL ID en el DMV, ¿cuántas pruebas de residencia del estado de Nueva York debe proporcionar?

choices.A: Una
choices.B: Dos
choices.C: Tres
choices.D: Cuatro

es.explanation: Para obtener una REAL ID, DEBE llevar a la oficina dos pruebas de residencia del estado de Nueva York, como una factura de servicios públicos o un estado de cuenta hipotecario.

es.question: Si renueva su licencia de conducir por correo o en línea, ¿dentro de qué plazo debe demostrar que ha aprobado un examen de la vista?

choices.A: Los últimos 30 días
choices.B: Los últimos 60 días
choices.C: Los últimos seis meses
choices.D: Los últimos dos años

es.explanation: Si renueva por correo o a través del sitio web del DMV, debe demostrar que ha aprobado un examen de la vista en los últimos seis meses (o dentro de un año, según lo determine un profesional de la salud con licencia).

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo se extiende automáticamente su licencia de conducir después de ser dado de baja del servicio militar activo?

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 60 días
choices.C: Seis meses
choices.D: Un año

es.explanation: Si ingresa al servicio militar, su licencia puede extenderse automáticamente durante todo su servicio activo y por seis meses después de ser dado de baja.

es.question: Después de establecer su residencia en el estado de Nueva York, ¿cuánto tiempo tiene para solicitar una licencia de conducir de Nueva York?

choices.A: 10 días
choices.B: 30 días
choices.C: 60 días
choices.D: 90 días

es.explanation: Para mantener una licencia legal, debe solicitar una licencia de conducir de Nueva York dentro de los 30 días posteriores a establecer que es residente del estado de Nueva York.

es.question: Si tiene 15 años y posee una licencia de conducir válida de otro estado, ¿cuáles son las reglas para conducir en el estado de Nueva York?

choices.A: Puede conducir solo si está acompañado por un padre.
choices.B: Puede conducir solo durante las horas de luz del día.
choices.C: No puede conducir en el estado de Nueva York bajo ninguna circunstancia.
choices.D: Puede conducir si obtiene un permiso de conductor menor (junior permit) de Nueva York.

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente: "Si tiene menos de 16 años de edad, no puede conducir en el estado de Nueva York, incluso si tiene una licencia de otro estado".

es.question: ¿Qué significa si su licencia de conducir es "revocada"?

choices.A: Se le retira por un período temporal y se le devuelve automáticamente.
choices.B: Es cancelada y debe volver a solicitarla al DMV una vez que termine el período.
choices.C: Debe pagar una multa pero puede seguir conduciendo.
choices.D: Está restringido a conducir solo hacia y desde el trabajo.

es.explanation: "Revocación" significa que su licencia (o privilegio para conducir) es cancelada. Para obtener una nueva licencia, debe volver a solicitarla al Departamento de Vehículos Motorizados (DMV) una vez que termine el período de revocación.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo se suspenderá un permiso o licencia de conductor menor (junior) si el conductor es condenado por una infracción de tránsito grave que valga tres o más puntos?

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 60 días
choices.C: 90 días
choices.D: 120 días

es.explanation: Su permiso, licencia o privilegios serán suspendidos por 60 días si es condenado por una infracción de tránsito grave (tres puntos o más) o por otras dos infracciones.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la sanción para un conductor con un permiso de conductor menor (junior permit) que es condenado por una infracción por enviar mensajes de texto o usar el teléfono celular?

choices.A: Una suspensión de 30 días
choices.B: Una suspensión de 60 días
choices.C: Una suspensión de 120 días
choices.D: Una revocación permanente

es.explanation: Su permiso de conductor menor (junior permit), licencia o privilegios serán suspendidos por 120 días cuando sea condenado por una infracción por enviar mensajes de texto o usar el teléfono celular.

es.question: What is the minimum amount of time you must hold a junior permit before you can schedule a road test?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 3 months
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

es.explanation: A junior permit must be held for a minimum of six months, excluding any time the permit is suspended or revoked, before a road test can be scheduled.

es.question: How long is the probation period for a newly licensed driver who is 18 or older when they pass their road test?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

es.explanation: If you are 18 or older when you pass your road test for a driver license, or obtain a license following revocation, you will be on probation for six months.

es.question: Which of the following convictions will result in a 60-day suspension for a newly licensed driver during their six-month probation period?

choices.A: A single parking ticket
choices.B: Speeding
choices.C: Failing to notify the DMV of an address change
choices.D: Driving with an expired inspection sticker

es.explanation: If you are convicted of DWAI (alcohol), speeding, reckless driving, following too closely, participating in a speed contest, or any two traffic violations while on probation, your license will be suspended for 60 days.

es.question: If you are convicted of a texting or cell phone violation while on a probationary license, how long will your license be suspended?

choices.A: 60 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 120 days
choices.D: 6 months

es.explanation: According to the manual, if you are convicted of a texting or cell phone violation, your probationary license will be suspended for 120 days.

es.question: What is a possible consequence if you receive a traffic ticket and do not respond to it?

choices.A: Your vehicle will be immediately impounded.
choices.B: You could be found guilty by default conviction and your license suspended indefinitely.
choices.C: You will automatically receive 3 points on your driving record.
choices.D: You will be required to take a mandatory defensive driving course.

es.explanation: The manual states that if you do not respond that you have received the ticket, you could be found guilty by default conviction and your driver license will be suspended indefinitely.

es.question: From which of the following areas outside of New York State will moving traffic convictions be added to your New York State 'violation point' driving record?

choices.A: New Jersey and Pennsylvania
choices.B: Ontario and Quebec
choices.C: California and Florida
choices.D: All Canadian provinces

es.explanation: The New York State DMV does not record convictions of moving traffic violations in other jurisdictions, except traffic offenses committed in the provinces of Ontario and Quebec in Canada.

es.question: If you are over 21 years old and are convicted of an alcohol- or drug-related driving violation in another state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least:

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 1 year

es.explanation: If you are over 21 years old and are convicted of an alcohol- or drug-related driving violation (e.g., DUI) in another state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least 90 days.

es.question: What is the penalty if a driver under 21 years old is convicted of an alcohol or drug-related violation that occurred out of state?

choices.A: A 90-day suspension
choices.B: A 6-month revocation
choices.C: Revocation for at least one year
choices.D: A warning and a $500 fine

es.explanation: If you are under 21 years old and convicted of any alcohol or drug-related violation that occurred out of state, your New York driver license will be revoked for at least one year.

es.question: What is the minimum revocation period for Aggravated driving while intoxicated (Agg-DWI) with a .18 blood alcohol content?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: 18 months

es.explanation: Aggravated driving while intoxicated (Agg-DWI), with .18 of one percent blood alcohol content (.18 BAC) carries a minimum one-year revocation.

es.question: A conviction for Driving while ability impaired by alcohol (DWAI) will result in a:

choices.A: 90-day suspension
choices.B: Six-month revocation
choices.C: One-year revocation
choices.D: 120-day suspension

es.explanation: The manual lists the penalty for Driving while ability impaired by alcohol (DWAI) as a 90-day suspension.

es.question: If a driver over age 21 refuses to take a chemical test for the first time, their license will be revoked for a minimum of:

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: 18 months

es.explanation: A chemical test refusal for drivers over age 21 results in a minimum one-year revocation.

es.question: Under the state's 'Zero Tolerance Law,' what happens if a driver under age 21 is found to have a BAC from .02 to .07?

choices.A: Their license is suspended for 90 days.
choices.B: Their license is suspended for six months.
choices.C: Their license is revoked for one year.
choices.D: They receive 3 points on their license.

es.explanation: Under the state's 'Zero Tolerance Law,' a driver under age 21 will have their license suspended for six months if found to have a BAC from .02 to .07.

es.question: Your driver license will be revoked for at least six months if you are found guilty of how many speeding and/or misdemeanor traffic violations within 18 months?

choices.A: Two
choices.B: Three
choices.C: Four
choices.D: Five

es.explanation: Your driver license will be revoked for at least six months if you are found guilty of three speeding and/or misdemeanor traffic violations within 18 months.

es.question: What is the penalty for operating an uninsured vehicle or allowing another person to operate your uninsured vehicle?

choices.A: A 90-day suspension
choices.B: A six-month suspension
choices.C: Revocation for at least one year
choices.D: An indefinite suspension until insurance is purchased

es.explanation: Your driver license will be revoked for at least one year if you operate or allow another person to operate your uninsured vehicle.

es.question: Which of the following will result in an indefinite suspension of your driver license?

choices.A: Failing to pay child support
choices.B: Getting two speeding tickets in a year
choices.C: Refusing a chemical test
choices.D: Passing a stopped school bus once
