choices.B: When following vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings, like buses
choices.C: When driving on a newly paved, dry road
choices.D: When passing a slow-moving vehicle on a straightaway

en.explanation: You should increase your following distance when following vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings, such as buses, or vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

en.question: At what distance must natural light conditions make it possible to clearly see objects ahead before headlights are required?

choices.A: 250 feet
choices.B: 500 feet
choices.C: 1,000 feet
choices.D: 2,000 feet

en.explanation: Lights must be on at any other time when natural light conditions do not make it possible to clearly see objects 1,000 feet ahead.

en.question: Under Ohio law, when are you required to use your headlights?

choices.A: Only from sunset to sunrise
choices.B: From sunset to sunrise, during poor visibility, and when windshield wipers are used
choices.C: Only when driving on unlit rural roads
choices.D: Between the hours of 8 PM and 6 AM

en.explanation: Ohio law requires headlights to be used from sunset to sunrise, at any time visibility is poor (rain, snow, fog, etc.), and any time the windshield wipers are in use because of precipitation.

en.question: How far ahead of a turn should you signal your intention to change direction?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that you must signal a turn at least 100 feet ahead of the turn to give other roadway users time to react.

en.question: How quickly can the temperature inside a vehicle increase by 20 degrees Fahrenheit, even with the windows cracked?

choices.A: 5 minutes
choices.B: 10 minutes
choices.C: 20 minutes
choices.D: 30 minutes

en.explanation: Even with the windows cracked, the temperature in a vehicle can increase 20 degrees (Fahrenheit) in just 10 minutes, making it extremely dangerous to leave pets or children inside.

en.question: Which pedestrians always have the right-of-way when crossing the street?

choices.A: Pedestrians jogging in a designated bike lane
choices.B: Pedestrians carrying a white cane or using a guide dog
choices.C: Pedestrians crossing outside of a marked crosswalk
choices.D: Pedestrians wearing highly reflective clothing

en.explanation: The manual specifies that pedestrians who are visually impaired or blind (carrying a white cane or using a guide dog) have the right-of-way.

en.question: What is the minimum recommended following distance when driving behind a motorcyclist under normal conditions?

choices.A: 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds
choices.D: 6 seconds

en.explanation: When following a motorcyclist, you should allow for a minimum 4-second following distance, or more in wet conditions, to ensure you have enough time to avoid a crash.

en.question: Why should you not automatically assume a motorcycle is turning just because its turn signal is flashing?

choices.A: Motorcyclists frequently use turn signals to indicate they are slowing down
choices.B: Motorcycle turn signals may not self-cancel and the rider may have forgotten to turn them off
choices.C: The flashing light indicates the motorcycle is experiencing mechanical issues
choices.D: Turn signals on motorcycles are only used for changing lanes, not turning

en.explanation: Do not assume a motorcycle is turning when you see its turn signal flashing because motorcycle turn signals may not self-cancel, and the motorcyclist may have forgotten to turn them off.

en.question: When passing a bicyclist, what is the minimum safety zone you must maintain between your motor vehicle and the bicycle?

choices.A: One foot
choices.B: Two feet
choices.C: Three feet
choices.D: Five feet

en.explanation: Drivers must maintain a safety zone of at least three feet between a motor vehicle and a bicycle when passing.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to squeeze between a large commercial vehicle and the curb when it is turning right?

choices.A: The commercial vehicle may accelerate suddenly
choices.B: The commercial vehicle may make a wide right turn from the left lane to clear the corner
choices.C: The curb may severely damage your vehicle's tires
choices.D: Commercial vehicles always have the right-of-way at all intersections

en.explanation: Trucks or buses may make a wide right turn from the left lane to clear the corner of a curb or other obstruction. Squeezing between the large vehicle and the curb will cause a serious crash.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in a large truck's side "No Zone" (blind spot)?

choices.A: You are driving exactly three car lengths behind the truck
choices.B: You cannot see the truck's brake lights
choices.C: You cannot see the truck driver's face in their side-view mirror
choices.D: You are driving in the lane immediately to the right of the truck

en.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large "No Zones" on both sides. If you cannot see the driver's face in the side-view mirror, the driver cannot see you.

en.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum stopping distance for a loaded truck traveling at 55 mph?

choices.A: 150 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 250 feet
choices.D: 335 feet

en.explanation: A loaded truck with good tires and properly adjusted brakes, under ideal conditions, traveling at 55 mph requires a minimum of 335 feet before coming to a complete stop.

en.question: What should you do if you see a child alone in a vehicle and they appear to be in distress or unresponsive?

choices.A: Wait by the car until the parents return
choices.B: Call 911 immediately and take action to remove the child, breaking a window if necessary
choices.C: Leave a note on the windshield warning the parents of the danger
choices.D: Go into nearby stores to page the owner of the vehicle before taking action

en.explanation: If a child is in distress or unresponsive, call 911 immediately and take action to remove the child from the vehicle, breaking a window if necessary. "Good Samaritan" laws protect people responding in an emergency.

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding bicyclists on the roadway?

choices.A: Bicyclists must ride against vehicular traffic to see oncoming cars
choices.B: Bicycles are considered vehicles and must ride with vehicular traffic
choices.C: Bicyclists are not required to obey traffic signs and signals
choices.D: Bicyclists must always ride on the sidewalk when one is available

en.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles when on roadways and must ride with, not against, other vehicular traffic. They are also required to obey all traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

en.question: In which of the following situations is it appropriate to use your vehicle's horn?

choices.A: To express anger at another driver's mistake
choices.B: To scare a bicyclist who is riding too slowly
choices.C: To alert a pedestrian who appears to be moving into your lane of travel
choices.D: To greet a friend walking on the sidewalk

en.explanation: You should tap your horn lightly to communicate to others when pedestrians or bicyclists appear to be moving into your lane of travel. Using your horn inappropriately could scare or anger another road user.

en.question: How can you help maintain a safe following distance for the driver behind your vehicle?

choices.A: By frequently tapping your brakes to keep them alert
choices.B: By keeping a steady speed and signaling your intentions in advance
choices.C: By speeding up rapidly to create more distance
choices.D: By moving into the blind spot of the vehicle next to you

en.explanation: You can help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance by keeping a steady speed, signaling in advance, and keeping more space to the front of your vehicle before reducing speed or turning.

en.question: Why is it important to always stop behind intersection stop lines?

choices.A: It prevents pedestrians from crossing the street
choices.B: It triggers the traffic light to change faster
choices.C: It sets you farther back to give larger vehicles more turning space
choices.D: It allows you to accelerate faster when the light turns green

en.explanation: Always stop behind intersection stop lines because these lines help to set you farther back at an intersection to give larger vehicles more turning space.

en.question: How far can the blind spots directly behind large vehicles extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 200 feet
choices.D: Up to 300 feet

en.explanation: Unlike passenger vehicles, large vehicles have huge blind spots directly behind them that extend up to 200 feet.

en.question: What must a driver do when an emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights and audible sirens is approaching?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the current lane
choices.B: Quickly and safely pull to the right side of the road and stop
choices.C: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
choices.D: Pull to the left side of the road and stop

en.explanation: When emergency vehicles are approaching, the driver must quickly and safely pull to the right side of the road and stop, avoiding blocking intersections.

en.question: Under Ohio's Move Over Law, what should you do if it is unsafe to change lanes when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with its warning lights activated?

choices.A: Stop immediately behind the emergency vehicle
choices.B: Maintain your speed and honk your horn
choices.C: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.D: Accelerate to pass the vehicle as quickly as possible

en.explanation: If a lane change is unsafe, the Move Over Law requires drivers to slow down and proceed with caution while maintaining a safe speed for traffic conditions.

en.question: What does a fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicate?

choices.A: The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials
choices.B: The vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph
choices.C: The vehicle is making frequent stops
choices.D: The vehicle is broken down

en.explanation: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle displayed on the rear of vehicles means the vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.

en.question: Under what condition are you permitted to cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow-moving vehicle?

choices.A: If the vehicle is traveling less than half the posted speed limit
choices.B: If the vehicle is a piece of farm machinery
choices.C: If you honk your horn before passing
choices.D: If you are driving in a rural area

en.explanation: You are permitted to cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow-moving vehicle as long as the vehicle is traveling less than half the posted speed limit, you do not exceed the speed limit, and there is sufficient clear space.

en.question: What is the proper procedure if your vehicle begins to skid?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes and steer straight ahead
choices.B: Accelerate quickly to regain traction
choices.C: Release pressure from the brake or accelerator and turn the wheel into the skid
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the skid

en.explanation: When you begin to skid, you should release pressure from the brake or accelerator and turn the wheel into the skid.

en.question: How must a driver treat an intersection with an inoperable traffic signal due to a power outage, if no law enforcement officer is present?

choices.A: As a yield sign
choices.B: As a four-way stop
choices.C: Proceed without stopping if the road appears clear
choices.D: Only the vehicles on the larger road have the right-of-way

en.explanation: By law, except when a law enforcement officer is present to direct traffic, drivers must treat a non-working traffic signal as a four-way stop.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle leaves the paved road surface and encounters an uneven surface drop-off?

choices.A: Jerk the steering wheel hard to return to the pavement immediately
choices.B: Slam on the brakes to stop the vehicle
choices.C: Accelerate to get back onto the road quickly
choices.D: Let off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and return to the pavement when safe

en.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the paved road surface, let off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and when safe to do so, return to the pavement.

en.question: If your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck and the vehicle is accelerating out of control, what gear should you shift into?

choices.A: PARK
choices.B: REVERSE
choices.C: NEUTRAL
choices.D: DRIVE

en.explanation: If your vehicle is accelerating out of control, you should turn on emergency flashers, shift to 'NEUTRAL' gear, and search for an escape route.

en.question: Which of the following is the correct action to take if you experience a tire blowout while driving?

choices.A: Brake hard immediately to stop the vehicle
choices.B: Do not brake; slow down gradually
choices.C: Accelerate slightly to maintain steering control
choices.D: Pump the brakes rapidly

en.explanation: In the event of a tire blowout, you should grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and do not brake; slow down gradually.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down, how far behind the vehicle should you place emergency flares if possible?

choices.A: 50 to 100 feet
choices.B: 100 to 150 feet
choices.C: 200 to 300 feet
choices.D: 400 to 500 feet

en.explanation: If possible, place emergency flares about 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle to alert other drivers and give them time to change lanes.

en.question: When exchanging information after a crash, what should you avoid discussing?

choices.A: The names and addresses of witnesses
choices.B: The license plate numbers of the vehicles involved
choices.C: Fault or insurance coverage
choices.D: The weather and road conditions

en.explanation: When exchanging information with others involved in the accident, you should provide contact and vehicle details, but do not discuss fault or insurance coverage.

en.question: In addition to a slow-moving emblem, what must farm machinery display when traveling at night?

choices.A: A white flashing light
choices.B: A red flashing light
choices.C: High beam headlights
choices.D: Hazard lights only

en.explanation: Farm machinery must display the slow-moving emblem, and use a red flashing light at night.

en.question: If your engine shuts off while you are driving (power failure), what should you expect regarding the steering wheel?

choices.A: The steering wheel will lock completely and cannot be turned
choices.B: The steering wheel will turn much easier than normal
choices.C: The steering wheel may be difficult to turn, but you can turn it
choices.D: The steering wheel will automatically steer the vehicle to the right

en.explanation: If the engine shuts off while driving, keep a strong grip on the steering wheel. Be aware that the steering wheel may be difficult to turn, but you can turn it.

en.question: Under what conditions may a driver file a Crash Report (form BMV 3303) with the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles?

choices.A: Within 30 days if the damage is over $1,000
choices.B: Within 6 months if damage exceeds $400 or there is injury, and the other driver was uninsured
choices.C: Within 1 year for any crash involving two or more vehicles
choices.D: Within 24 hours if there is any visible damage to either vehicle

en.explanation: The manual states a driver may file a Crash Report within six months if there was damage in excess of $400 or personal injury, and the driver or owner of the other vehicle did not have insurance.

en.question: What must you do if you are involved in a crash with an unattended vehicle?

choices.A: Wait by the vehicle until the owner returns
choices.B: Report the crash to the police or leave necessary information at the scene
choices.C: Only notify your insurance company
choices.D: Leave the scene immediately if there is no visible damage

en.explanation: If involved in a crash with an unattended vehicle, you must report the crash to the police or leave necessary information at the scene.

en.question: Which of the following vehicle components is checked during the vehicle inspection before the driving test begins?

choices.A: Air conditioning and radio
choices.B: Turn signals, brake lights, and horn
choices.C: Engine oil level and tire pressure
choices.D: Interior dome light and glove box latch

en.explanation: A vehicle inspection performed before the test begins will check the working order of turn signals, brake lights, horn, windshield wipers, and headlights.

en.question: What is a requirement for the vehicle's doors during the driving test inspection?

choices.A: All four doors must have child safety locks enabled
choices.B: The rear doors must open from the inside only
choices.C: The front doors must be able to open from the inside and outside
choices.D: The driver's door must have an automatic window

en.explanation: The manual specifies that front doors must be able to open from the inside and outside with the door handle.

en.question: What action results in an immediate failure during the maneuverability skills test?

choices.A: Stopping to check your mirrors
choices.B: Misjudging the stopping distance by a few inches
choices.C: Running over or knocking down a marker
choices.D: Completing the course too slowly

en.explanation: It is an immediate failure if a driver runs over or knocks down a marker, removes the marker from the designated area, or performs other dangerous actions.

en.question: In Step One of the maneuverability test, where must you stop the vehicle?

choices.A: When the front bumper touches the center marker
choices.B: When the rear bumper is even with the center marker
choices.C: When the vehicle is entirely past all five markers
choices.D: When the front bumper is even with the two rear markers

en.explanation: In Step One, you must steer straight ahead and stop when the rear bumper of the vehicle is even with the center marker and generally parallel with the course.

en.question: How long must an applicant under age 21 wait before retesting if they fail the driving test?

choices.A: 24 hours
choices.B: Two days
choices.C: One week
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: Under Age 21 applicants must wait two days before retesting after a test failure.

en.question: What is required for an applicant age 21 or older who fails the driving test for the first time, assuming they have not taken an approved driver education course recently?

choices.A: Wait 30 days before retesting
choices.B: Take an Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course
choices.C: Complete 50 hours of supervised driving
choices.D: Pay a $100 retesting fee

en.explanation: An applicant age 21 or older who fails the maneuverability or road skills portion of the driving test is required to take an Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course before attempting the driving test for a second time.

en.question: If an adult applicant chooses the option of 24 hours of driving with a licensed driver age 21 or older for their Abbreviated Adult Driver Training, what is the maximum number of driving hours allowed per day?

choices.A: Two hours
choices.B: Four hours
choices.C: Six hours
choices.D: Eight hours

en.explanation: Applicants who choose the option for 24 hours of driving with a licensed driver age 21 or older cannot complete more than four hours of driving in one day.

en.question: What specific form must an applicant under age 18 provide when purchasing their driver license?

choices.A: Twenty-Four Hour Affidavit (form BMV 5789)
choices.B: Notarized Fifty-Hour Affidavit (form BMV 5791)
choices.C: Proof of high school enrollment
choices.D: Medical clearance form

en.explanation: If the applicant is under age 18, they must bring a Notarized Fifty-Hour Affidavit (form BMV 5791) to the Deputy Registrar agency.

en.question: How long is a parent or legal guardian who co-signs a minor's application jointly liable for damages caused by the minor's negligence?

choices.A: Until the minor turns 21
choices.B: For the first six months of driving
choices.C: Until the minor's 18th birthday
choices.D: Until the minor purchases their own vehicle

en.explanation: The parent or legal guardian who co-signs a minor’s application is jointly and severally liable with the minor for any damages caused by negligence or willful misconduct until the minor’s 18th birthday.

en.question: How can a co-signer cancel their authorization for a minor's driver license?

choices.A: By calling the local police department
choices.B: By mailing the minor's license or a notarized letter to the BMV
choices.C: By emailing the ADA Coordinator
choices.D: By destroying the minor's physical license card

en.explanation: A cosigner can cancel authorization for a minor at any time by mailing the minor’s Driver License or TIPIC or a notarized letter requesting the cancelation to the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles.

en.question: How many documents proving an Ohio street address are required to obtain a Compliant Driver License card?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: Obtaining a Compliant card requires more identity documents than the Standard card, including two documents to prove an Ohio street address.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding a Standard Driver License card?

choices.A: It meets all national travel security requirements
choices.B: It requires more identity documents than the Compliant card
choices.C: It cannot be used to fly commercially without a passport or other TSA-approved document
choices.D: It is only issued to drivers under the age of 21

en.explanation: The Standard Card does not meet national travel security requirements and will need to be used in conjunction with a passport or other acceptable documents approved by the TSA in order to fly commercially.

en.question: What must be done with automated assistance tools, such as automated parking, during the driving test?

choices.A: They must be used to demonstrate proficiency
choices.B: They must be disabled
choices.C: They can be used only during the maneuverability portion
choices.D: They are required for all applicants over age 65

en.explanation: During the vehicle inspection before the test begins, automated assistance tools, such as automated parking, must be disabled.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five elements required for proof of identity when applying for an Ohio Driver License?

choices.A: Full Legal Name
choices.B: Social Security number
choices.C: Proof of Employment
choices.D: Date of Birth

en.explanation: Applicants must provide acceptable documentation for proof of identity that includes Full Legal Name, Date of Birth, Social Security number, Ohio Street Address, and Citizenship or Legal Presence.

en.question: During the first 12 months of holding a Driver License, a driver under age 18 may not operate a vehicle between what hours unless accompanied by a parent or guardian?

choices.A: 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.
choices.B: 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.C: Midnight to 6 a.m.
choices.D: 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.

en.explanation: During the first 12 months of holding a Driver License, a new driver under age 18 may not operate a vehicle from midnight to 6 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or guardian or meeting other specific exceptions.

en.question: A driver under age 18 in their first 12 months of holding a license may not operate a vehicle with more than how many non-family members as passengers without a parent or guardian?

choices.A: Zero
choices.B: One
choices.C: Two
choices.D: Three

en.explanation: The driver may not operate a vehicle with more than one non-family member as a passenger, unless accompanied by a parent or guardian.

en.question: After the first 12 months of holding a Driver License, what are the restricted driving hours for a driver under age 18 (unless an exception applies)?

choices.A: Midnight to 6 a.m.
choices.B: 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.
choices.C: 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.D: 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.

en.explanation: After the first 12 months of holding a Driver License, the driver under age 18 may not operate a vehicle from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. unless an exception applies.

en.question: For a driver under age 18, multiple traffic convictions before reaching age 18 may result in a license suspension of what length?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 6 months

en.explanation: Multiple traffic convictions before the driver reaches age 18 may result in a 90-day license suspension.

en.question: If you are under age 21, when does your Ohio Driver License expire?

choices.A: On your 18th birthday
choices.B: On your 21st birthday
choices.C: Four years from the date of issuance
choices.D: Eight years from the date of issuance

en.explanation: If you are under age 21, your Ohio Driver License expires on your 21st birthday and must be renewed in person.

en.question: What is the grace period for renewing your Ohio Driver License after it has expired?

choices.A: There is no grace period
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 6 months

en.explanation: There is no grace period for renewing your license. If you continue to drive after your license has expired, you risk a traffic citation.

en.question: Which Commercial Driver License (CDL) class is required for a single vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver?

choices.A: Class A
choices.B: Class B
choices.C: Class C
choices.D: Class D

en.explanation: A Class C CDL is required for any single vehicle or combination of vehicles not considered Class A or B that is designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.

en.question: Probationary moped license holders ages 14-15 are restricted to driving:

choices.A: Only with a parent or guardian
choices.B: Only during daylight hours
choices.C: Only on roads with a speed limit under 35 mph
choices.D: Only to and from school

en.explanation: Probationary moped license holders ages 14-15 are limited to daylight driving only.

en.question: To be classified as a moped or motorized bicycle, the vehicle's helper motor must NOT produce more than:

choices.A: One brake horsepower
choices.B: Two brake horsepower
choices.C: Three brake horsepower
choices.D: Five brake horsepower

en.explanation: A moped is equipped with a helper motor that produces no more than one brake horsepower.

en.question: What vehicles may a two-wheeled motorcycle endorsement holder operate?

choices.A: Only two-wheeled motorcycles
choices.B: Two-wheeled motorcycles and motor scooters only
choices.C: Two- or three-wheeled motorcycles and motor scooters
choices.D: Any motorcycle, but no motor scooters

en.explanation: A two-wheeled motorcycle endorsement or license holder may operate a two- or three-wheeled motorcycle and a scooter.

en.question: A motor scooter is characterized by having a motor that is capable of propelling the vehicle at a speed greater than:

choices.A: 15 mph on a level surface
choices.B: 20 mph on a level surface
choices.C: 25 mph on a level surface
choices.D: 30 mph on a level surface

en.explanation: A motor scooter is equipped with a motor between 50 cc and 100 cc that is capable of propelling the vehicle at a speed greater than 20 mph on a level surface.

en.question: Who is required to complete the Motorcycle Ohio program before applying for a motorcycle operator's endorsement or license?

choices.A: All first-time applicants regardless of age
choices.B: Individuals under age 18
choices.C: Individuals under age 21
choices.D: Anyone who fails the skills test on their first attempt

en.explanation: The Motorcycle Ohio program is required for individuals under age 18 before they can apply for a motorcycle operator’s endorsement and/or license.

en.question: After establishing residency in Ohio, how many days do new residents have to obtain an Ohio-issued Driver License?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: Within 30 days of establishing residency, Ohio drivers must have an Ohio-issued Driver License.

en.question: When applying for or renewing vehicle registration, Ohioans are asked if they want to contribute $1 to which fund to ensure children have healthy eyes?

choices.A: Second Chance Trust Fund
choices.B: Save Our Sight fund
choices.C: Ohio Vision Program
choices.D: Donate Life Ohio

en.explanation: When Ohioans apply for or renew their vehicle registration, they are asked if they want to contribute $1 to the Save Our Sight fund, which ensures children in Ohio have good vision and healthy eyes.

en.question: What Ohio fund receives voluntary donations to support the education of organ, eye, and tissue donation?

choices.A: Ohio Highway Safety Fund
choices.B: Second Chance Trust Fund
choices.C: Save Our Sight Fund
choices.D: Donate Life Ohio Fund

en.explanation: According to the manual, a voluntary donation to Ohio's Second Chance Trust Fund supports education of organ, eye, and tissue donation.

en.question: When you fill out a Voter Registration form at a Deputy Registrar License Agency, where does the Deputy Registrar send the completed form?

choices.A: The Ohio Department of Transportation
choices.B: The Federal Election Commission
choices.C: The County Board of Elections
choices.D: BMV Verification Services

en.explanation: The manual states that the Deputy Registrar will send completed voter forms to the County Board of Elections.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of the ID R KIDS Ohio photo ID card?

choices.A: To grant restricted driving privileges to minors
choices.B: To assist authorities if a child becomes lost or is reported missing
choices.C: To allow children to register to vote early
choices.D: To serve as a valid passport for international travel

en.explanation: Ohio photo ID cards for children (ID R KIDS) assist authorities in the event that a child becomes lost or is reported missing.

en.question: Can an Ohio ID card for a child be used for driving privileges?

choices.A: Yes, if the child is over 14 years old
choices.B: Yes, but only when accompanied by a parent
choices.C: No, it is used for identification purposes only
choices.D: No, unless they pass a written test

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that an Ohio ID card is used for identification purposes only, and cannot be used for anything else, including driving privileges.

en.question: What must you provide when applying for an Ohio ID card for your child at a Deputy Registrar License Agency?

choices.A: Identity documents from the Acceptable Documents List
choices.B: A completed Next of Kin form
choices.C: The child's school ID and report card
choices.D: A voter registration form

en.explanation: To apply for an Ohio ID card for a child, you must visit a Deputy Registrar License Agency and provide identity documents from the Acceptable Documents List.

en.question: Under the Next of Kin Emergency Contact Information program, what is the maximum number of emergency contacts an Ohioan can identify?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: Through the Next of Kin Emergency Contact Information program, Ohioans can identify up to two emergency contacts.

en.question: What is the purpose of the Next of Kin Emergency Contact Information program?

choices.A: To notify family members when a driver's license expires
choices.B: To allow law enforcement to notify contacts if an emergency leaves a person unable to communicate
choices.C: To provide a backup address for BMV mailings
choices.D: To register family members to vote

en.explanation: The program allows law enforcement to notify emergency contacts when an accident or emergency leaves the person unable to communicate with law enforcement or emergency medical responders.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid method to add emergency contact information to your driver record?

choices.A: Online through BMV Online Services
choices.B: In person at a Deputy Registrar License Agency
choices.C: By mail to BMV Verification Services
choices.D: Over the phone by calling 911

en.explanation: The manual lists three ways to add emergency contact information: Online, In Person, or By Mail. Calling 911 is not an option.

en.question: Can parents add Next of Kin emergency contact information to their child's Ohio ID card record?

choices.A: Yes, to be used in the event the child becomes lost or is reported missing
choices.B: No, the program is only for licensed drivers over 18
choices.C: Yes, but only by mailing a form to the County Board of Elections
choices.D: No, children cannot have emergency contacts listed

en.explanation: Parents of children who have an Ohio ID card may add contact information to their child's record for use in the event the child becomes lost or is reported missing.

en.question: Where does the living will designation display on an Ohio Driver License or ID card?

choices.A: On the front, below the photo
choices.B: On the back of the Driver License or ID card
choices.C: Embedded in the magnetic stripe only
choices.D: It does not display on the card itself

en.explanation: The manual states that the living will indication will display on the back of the Driver License or ID card.

en.question: Who is eligible to have the 'ARMED FORCES' designation displayed on their Ohio Driver License or ID card?

choices.A: Only retired military personnel
choices.B: Only active duty personnel deployed overseas
choices.C: Any veteran, active duty, or reservist of the Armed Forces of the United States
choices.D: Any immediate family member of a veteran

en.explanation: Any veteran, active duty, or reservist of the Armed Forces of the United States may have the 'ARMED FORCES' designation display on their Ohio Driver License or ID card.

en.question: Which of the following documents is acceptable to present when applying for the 'ARMED FORCES' designation on an Ohio Driver License?

choices.A: A DD214 form
choices.B: A high school diploma
choices.C: A voter registration card
choices.D: A birth certificate

en.explanation: To get the 'ARMED FORCES' designation, applicants must present their Ohio Driver License or ID card and one of the acceptable documents, which includes a DD214.

en.question: In addition to a DD214, which of the following can be used to prove eligibility for the 'ARMED FORCES' designation?

choices.A: A valid passport
choices.B: A copy of current orders
choices.C: A concealed carry permit
choices.D: A utility bill

en.explanation: Acceptable documents for the 'ARMED FORCES' designation include a DD214, Active or Retired Military ID Card, Veteran Identification Card, or a Copy of current orders.

en.question: Where can an applicant go to change their voter status or register to vote in person when dealing with licensing?

choices.A: Any Deputy Registrar License Agency
choices.B: Any local police station
choices.C: Any Ohio State Highway Patrol post
choices.D: Any public library

en.explanation: Voter status can be changed at any Deputy Registrar License Agency by filling out a Voter Registration/Change of Address Form.

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

en.question: What does the Ohio Driver Manual state about its legal authority in relation to state law?

choices.A: It supersedes the Ohio Revised Code if there is a conflict.
choices.B: It is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the Ohio Revised Code.
choices.C: It contains all applicable motor vehicle laws in their entirety.
choices.D: It serves as the primary legal document for traffic court proceedings.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'This manual is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the Ohio Revised Code or the Ohio Administrative Code.'

en.question: What is a potential outcome of the vision screening when applying for an Ohio Driver License?

choices.A: An automatic increase in your insurance rates.
choices.B: A requirement to complete an advanced driving course.
choices.C: The application of driving restrictions to your license.
choices.D: Immediate issuance of a commercial driver license.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Driving restrictions could apply based upon vision screening results.'

en.question: According to the manual's table of contents, in which section can you find information about Ohio's 'Move Over Law'?

choices.A: Section 6: State Laws and Penalties
choices.B: Section 7: Special Driving Situations
choices.C: Section 9: Sharing the Road
choices.D: Section 10: Emergency Situations

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Move Over Laws' under Section 9: Sharing the Road.

en.question: If you need to find information about the rules for parking, which section of the Ohio Driver Manual should you consult?

choices.A: Section 4: Rules of the Road
choices.B: Section 5: Learning to Drive
choices.C: Section 2: Before You Drive
choices.D: Section 11: Taking the Driving Test

en.explanation: The table of contents shows that 'Parking' is a topic covered in Section 5: Learning to Drive.

en.question: To learn about Ohio's child passenger restraint and safety laws, which section of the manual should you study?

choices.A: Section 2: Before You Drive
choices.B: Section 8: Safe Driving Tips
choices.C: Section 9: Sharing the Road
choices.D: Section 6: State Laws and Penalties

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Child Passenger Restraints/Safety Laws' under Section 6: State Laws and Penalties.

en.question: In which section of the manual can you find details about what to do in case of a vehicle malfunction, such as a tire blowout?

choices.A: Section 10: Emergency Situations
choices.B: Section 2: Before You Drive
choices.C: Section 7: Special Driving Situations
choices.D: Section 11: Taking the Driving Test

en.explanation: The table of contents indicates that 'Vehicle Malfunctions' are covered in Section 10: Emergency Situations.

en.question: To find information on how to properly inspect your vehicle before driving, which section of the manual should you consult?

choices.A: Section 5: Learning to Drive
choices.B: Section 8: Safe Driving Tips
choices.C: Section 2: Before You Drive
choices.D: Section 11: Taking the Driving Test

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Inspecting Your Vehicle' as the first topic in Section 2: Before You Drive.

en.question: According to the 'How to Get Your Driver License' checklist, what must you do before getting a Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card (TIPIC)?

choices.A: Schedule your driving test.
choices.B: Complete a driver education course.
choices.C: Renew your Ohio ID Card.
choices.D: Gather proof of identity documents from the Acceptable Documents List.

en.explanation: The checklist on page 1 lists 'Gather proof of identity documents using the Acceptable Documents List' as a step before getting a TIPIC.

en.question: If a driver wants to learn the meaning of different lane pavement markings, which section of the manual provides this information?

choices.A: Section 4: Rules of the Road
choices.B: Section 5: Learning to Drive
choices.C: Section 9: Sharing the Road
choices.D: Section 7: Special Driving Situations

en.explanation: The table of contents shows that 'Lane Pavement Markings' is a topic in Section 4: Rules of the Road.

en.question: Information about special programs like the 'Next of Kin – Emergency Contact Information' and 'Living Will Designation' can be found in which section?

choices.A: Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License
choices.B: Section 6: State Laws and Penalties
choices.C: Section 13: What Else Should I Know?
choices.D: Section 10: Emergency Situations

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Next of Kin – Emergency Contact Information' and 'Living Will Designation' under Section 13: What Else Should I Know?

en.question: Which section of the manual would you study to understand the proper procedures for navigating roundabouts or traffic circles?

choices.A: Section 4: Rules of the Road
choices.B: Section 9: Sharing the Road
choices.C: Section 8: Safe Driving Tips
choices.D: Section 5: Learning to Drive

en.explanation: The table of contents shows that 'Roundabouts or Traffic Circles' is a topic covered in Section 5: Learning to Drive.

en.question: According to the table of contents, where would a new resident find information on obtaining an Ohio Driver License?

choices.A: Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License
choices.B: Section 13: What Else Should I Know?
choices.C: Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License
choices.D: Section 6: State Laws and Penalties

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'New Ohio Residents' as the first topic in Section 13: What Else Should I Know?

en.question: The topic of 'Aggressive Driving' and its dangers are discussed in which section of the Ohio Driver Manual?

choices.A: Section 6: State Laws and Penalties
choices.B: Section 3: Be Alert
choices.C: Section 8: Safe Driving Tips
choices.D: Section 10: Emergency Situations

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Aggressive Driving' as a topic in Section 3: Be Alert.

en.question: Which section of the manual details the requirements for the Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course?

choices.A: Section 1: How to Get Your Driver License
choices.B: Section 5: Learning to Drive
choices.C: Section 11: Taking the Driving Test
choices.D: Section 12: Purchase Your Driver License

en.explanation: The table of contents lists 'Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course' as a topic in Section 11: Taking the Driving Test.

en.question: What is the official website provided in the manual for accessing Ohio BMV services online?

choices.A: www.ohio.gov/bmv
choices.B: www.dmv.ohio.gov
choices.C: www.bmv.ohio.gov
choices.D: www.ohiodrivers.com

en.explanation: The first page of the manual states, 'For additional information about Ohio’s BMV services, visit the BMV website at www.bmv.ohio.gov.'

en.question: What is the consequence if an applicant passes the knowledge test but fails to purchase a Temporary Instruction Permit Identification Card (TIPIC) within 60 days?

choices.A: They must pay a late fee when purchasing the TIPIC.
choices.B: They must retake only the knowledge test.
choices.C: They must retake both the vision screening and the knowledge test.
choices.D: They receive a 30-day extension to purchase the TIPIC.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If a TIPIC is not purchased within 60 days, the applicant must start over with the vision screening and knowledge test.'

en.question: For a TIPIC holder under the age of 16, who is legally permitted to occupy the front passenger seat while they are driving?

choices.A: Any licensed driver who is at least 18 years old.
choices.B: A sibling who is at least 18 and has a valid driver license.
choices.C: A person age 21 or older who acts in place of a parent (in loco parentis).
choices.D: Any friend who has held a driver license for at least one year.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If under age 16, the driver must have a parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or a person age 21 or older, who acts in loco parentis, occupying the front passenger seat beside the permit holder.'

en.question: A 16-year-old TIPIC holder is driving with a valid licensed driver who is 21 but is not their parent or guardian. During which hours is this prohibited?

choices.A: 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.
choices.B: 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
choices.C: Midnight to 6 a.m.
choices.D: 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.

en.explanation: For a TIPIC holder age 16 to 17, driving with any valid licensed driver age 21 or older is permitted, 'except from midnight to 6 a.m. when the driver must be accompanied by a parent, guardian, or custodian who holds a valid Driver License.'

en.question: According to the restrictions for all TIPIC holders, what is the rule regarding the number of occupants in the vehicle?

choices.A: The number of occupants is limited to four, regardless of vehicle size.
choices.B: The total number of occupants cannot exceed the total number of installed safety belts.
choices.C: Only family members are allowed as passengers.
choices.D: No more than one passenger is allowed in the back seat.

en.explanation: For all ages, a TIPIC restriction is that the 'Total number of occupants in the vehicle cannot exceed the total number of safety belts installed in the vehicle.'

en.question: For a temporary resident age 21 or older to obtain a Driver License, what is the minimum amount of time they must hold a TIPIC after completing their driver education requirements?

choices.A: 7 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 6 months

en.explanation: The manual states: 'To obtain a Driver License, a driver that is a temporary resident age 21 or older must... Hold the TIPIC for at least 14 days.'

en.question: A temporary resident holding an unexpired out-of-country license from which of the following countries is NOT exempt from Ohio's driver education requirements?

choices.A: Germany
choices.B: Japan
choices.C: Mexico
choices.D: South Korea

en.explanation: The manual states that temporary residents with licenses from 'Canada, France, Germany, Japan, South Korea or Taiwan' are exempt. Mexico is not on this list.

en.question: During a vehicle inspection, what is the requirement for the steering assembly?

choices.A: It must be a power-steering system.
choices.B: It must have no excessive play in the steering wheel.
choices.C: The steering wheel must have an airbag.
choices.D: It must be able to turn the wheels lock-to-lock in under three rotations.

en.explanation: Ohio law requires a 'Steering assembly that operates normally, with no excessive play in the steering wheel.'

en.question: According to Ohio law, the two red reflectors on the rear of a vehicle must be visible from what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1,000 feet

en.explanation: The vehicle must have 'Two red reflectors on the rear of the vehicle, visible from 300 feet.'

en.question: The white light that illuminates the rear license plate must be visible from a distance of at least:

choices.A: 25 feet
choices.B: 50 feet
choices.C: 100 feet
choices.D: 200 feet

en.explanation: The vehicle must have a 'White light to illuminate the rear license plate, visible from 50 feet.'

en.question: In addition to the service brake, what other braking system is required on a vehicle, and what must it be capable of doing?

choices.A: An anti-lock brake system (ABS) that prevents skidding.
choices.B: A secondary hydraulic brake for emergency stops.
choices.C: An engine brake for controlling speed on downgrades.
choices.D: A parking brake that can hold the vehicle on a grade.

en.explanation: A vehicle must have a 'Parking brake that is adequate to hold the vehicle on a grade.'

en.question: What is the maximum number of times an applicant is permitted to take the knowledge test online through BMV Online Services within a six-month period?

choices.A: One attempt
choices.B: Two attempts
choices.C: Three attempts
choices.D: Unlimited attempts

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Knowledge Testing is available... Online through BMV Online Services (two attempts permitted in a six-month period).'

en.question: Besides being in an unsafe condition that endangers a person, what else does Ohio law prohibit on a vehicle?

choices.A: Aftermarket window tinting of any kind.
choices.B: Any non-factory modifications to the exhaust system.
choices.C: Protruding objects or broken sharp edges.
choices.D: Bumper stickers that may be distracting to other drivers.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Additionally, no vehicle is to be equipped with or permitted to have protruding objects, broken sharp edges, or vehicle parts that would be dangerous to a person coming in contact with them.'

en.question: When applying for a TIPIC, applicants must present documents to prove several elements of identity. Which of the following is NOT one of the required elements listed?

choices.A: Full legal name
choices.B: Proof of employment
choices.C: Social Security number (if assigned)
choices.D: Citizenship or legal presence

en.explanation: The required elements are 'Full legal name, Date of birth, Social Security number (if assigned), Citizenship or legal presence, Ohio street address.' Proof of employment is not on the list.

en.question: The Ohio driver's knowledge test is available in several languages. Which of the following is NOT one of the languages offered directly by the BMV?

choices.A: Somali
choices.B: German
choices.C: Haitian Creole
choices.D: Russian

en.explanation: The manual lists the available languages as 'American Sign Language (ASL), Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Haitian Creole, Japanese, Russian, Somali, and Spanish.' German is not on this list, and would require the applicant to provide their own interpreter.

en.question: Which of the following is a specific disability accommodation that is available upon request at a Driver Exam Station for the knowledge or skills test?

choices.A: A test proctor to read the questions aloud and record the answers.
choices.B: An audio version of the knowledge test.
choices.C: Use of a personal electronic translator device.
choices.D: An extended time limit to complete the test.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Accommodations available upon request at the Driver Exam Station include an audio knowledge test, printed paper knowledge test, American Sign Language knowledge test, and visual instructions during driving test...'

en.question: According to Ohio law, what is the minimum distance from which a vehicle's horn must be audible?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states the horn must be in good working order and audible from 200 feet.

en.question: Where can a driver find the vehicle manufacturer's recommended tire pressure level?

choices.A: In the vehicle owner's manual
choices.B: On the tire's sidewall
choices.C: On the vehicle's door jamb
choices.D: On the gas cap door

en.explanation: The manual specifies that the vehicle manufacturer’s recommended tire pressure is indicated on the door jamb.

en.question: When using the 'penny test' to check tire tread depth, what indicates that the tires are too worn and need to be replaced?

choices.A: The tread does not reach the top of the Lincoln Memorial on the back of the penny.
choices.B: You can see the top of President Lincoln's head.
choices.C: The penny fits completely inside the deepest groove.
choices.D: The tread is level with the edge of the penny.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Place the coin with President Abraham Lincoln’s head into the tire’s deepest groove. If you see all of the President’s head, your tires are too worn.'

en.question: Under what circumstance should you avoid using your high beam headlights?

choices.A: When driving on a rural road with no other cars
choices.B: When driving in heavy fog or rain
choices.C: When an oncoming vehicle is approaching
choices.D: When driving faster than 55 mph

en.explanation: Ohio law allows high beam headlights to be used at any time headlights are used, except when an oncoming vehicle is approaching.

en.question: For proper driving posture and airbag safety, the top of the steering wheel should be positioned:

choices.A: Level with your chin
choices.B: No higher than the top of your shoulders
choices.C: Directly in front of your face for best control
choices.D: As low as possible while still being able to see the gauges

en.explanation: The manual states that when your seat is adjusted properly, 'The top of the steering wheel is no higher than the top of your shoulders and below chin level.'

en.question: What is the correct way to wear a shoulder safety belt?

choices.A: Tucked under your arm for comfort
choices.B: Loosely draped over your shoulder
choices.C: Behind your back if it is uncomfortable
choices.D: Across the shoulder and chest with minimal slack

en.explanation: The manual specifies that a shoulder belt should be worn across the shoulder and chest with minimal, if any, slack, and warns not to wear it under the arm or behind the back.

en.question: What type of corrective lenses should be avoided when driving at night?

choices.A: Bifocal lenses
choices.B: Anti-glare lenses
choices.C: Dark or tinted lenses
choices.D: Any type of contact lenses

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to 'Avoid using dark or tinted corrective lenses at night.'

en.question: What is the maximum allowable light transmission for the side windows of the front seat in Ohio?

choices.A: 70% light transmission
choices.B: 50% light transmission, plus or minus 3%
choices.C: 35% light transmission
choices.D: There are no restrictions on side windows

en.explanation: The manual states the window light transmission for 'Side windows of front seat: 50% light transmission, plus or minus 3%.'

en.question: According to the manual, what is the primary purpose of using your vehicle's hazard lights?

choices.A: To signal that you are about to make a turn in heavy traffic
choices.B: To indicate that you are double-parked for a short time
choices.C: To increase the visibility of a vehicle stopped on or near a roadway
choices.D: To warn other drivers that you are driving slower than the speed limit

en.explanation: The manual states to 'Use hazard lights to increase visibility of a vehicle stopped on or near a roadway.'

en.question: To properly adjust the left-side mirror to reduce blind spots, where should you position your head?

choices.A: Leaning to the right, directly above the center console
choices.B: Sitting upright in your normal driving position
choices.C: Resting your head against the closed driver-side window
choices.D: Leaning forward until your head is close to the steering wheel

en.explanation: To adjust the left-side mirror, the manual instructs you to 'Rest your head against the closed driver-side window' and adjust the mirror until the vehicle’s left-edge is barely visible.

en.question: Ohio's mandatory safety belt usage law requires which occupants of most passenger vehicles to wear safety belts?

choices.A: All occupants, regardless of seating position
choices.B: Only the driver of the vehicle
choices.C: Drivers and front-seat occupants
choices.D: All occupants under the age of 18

en.explanation: The manual states that Ohio's law 'requires drivers and front-seat occupants of most passenger vehicles to wear safety belts.'

en.question: A vehicle's red stop lights (brake lights) must be visible from what minimum distance when the brakes are applied?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1000 feet

en.explanation: The manual requires 'Two red stop lights (brake lights) visible from 500 feet when the brakes are applied.'

en.question: What is the primary mirror a driver should use for the view to the rear of the vehicle?

choices.A: The left-side outside mirror
choices.B: The right-side outside mirror
choices.C: The inside rear-view mirror
choices.D: A combination of both outside mirrors

en.explanation: The manual states, 'The rear-view mirror is the primary mirror for the view to the rear.'

en.question: In addition to taillights and brake lights, a vehicle must have two red reflectors on the rear that are visible from what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual lists a requirement for 'Two red reflectors on the rear of the vehicle, visible from 300 feet.'

en.question: For drivers age 18 and older, which of the following is a legal use of a cell phone while driving under Ohio's distracted driving law?

choices.A: Manually typing a text message while stopped at a red light.
choices.B: Holding the phone to your ear for a conversation, provided the call was started with a single touch.
choices.C: Supporting the phone with your shoulder to talk.
choices.D: Watching a video while traffic is stopped on the highway due to a road closure.

en.explanation: The law includes an exception for drivers 18 and older, allowing them to hold a phone to the ear during a conversation if the call is initiated or ended with a single touch or swipe.

en.question: A driver age 18 or older commits a third distracted driving offense in two years. What is a possible consequence in addition to a fine and points?

choices.A: A mandatory defensive driving course
choices.B: A 60-day license suspension
choices.C: A possible 90-day license suspension
choices.D: A permanent license revocation

en.explanation: According to the manual, a third or subsequent distracted driving offense in two years for a driver 18 or older can result in a possible 90-day suspension of the Driver License, along with 4 points and a fine up to $500.

en.question: What is the fine for a second violation of the distracted driving law for a driver under the age of 18?
en.explanation: The manual specifies that a second distracted driving violation for a driver under 18 results in a $300 fine and a 1-year license suspension.

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following best defines aggressive driving?

choices.A: Unintentionally making a driving error due to fatigue.
choices.B: Driving faster than the surrounding traffic.
choices.C: Intentionally committing an action that endangers others or property.
choices.D: Using a cell phone without a hands-free device.

en.explanation: The manual defines aggressive driving as occurring when an individual intentionally commits an action that endangers other persons or property.

en.question: Besides impairing judgment and reaction time, how can alcohol and drugs specifically affect your vision while driving?

choices.A: It can improve night vision.
choices.B: It can cause blurred vision and reduce the ability to judge distance.
choices.C: It has no effect on vision.
choices.D: It only affects peripheral vision.

en.explanation: The manual states that alcohol and drugs can affect vision by causing blurred vision, reducing the ability to focus, and impairing the ability to judge distance and speed.

en.question: When entering a limited access or interstate highway from an entrance ramp, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: To vehicles behind you on the ramp.
choices.B: To drivers already on the highway.
choices.C: To vehicles exiting the highway.
choices.D: You have the right-of-way to merge.

en.explanation: For the safety of all, you must yield the right-of-way to drivers already on a limited access or interstate highway when you are on the entrance or acceleration ramp.

en.question: When you are at an intersection preparing to make a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: To vehicles behind you.
choices.B: To pedestrians on the side street.
choices.C: To drivers in the opposing traffic lane.
choices.D: To vehicles turning right from the opposite direction.

en.explanation: The rules of the road require you to yield the right-of-way to drivers in the opposing traffic lane when you are making a left turn.

en.question: What does a traffic light marked with a green arrow indicate?

choices.A: You must stop before turning.
choices.B: You can turn in the direction of the arrow without stopping.
choices.C: The opposing traffic also has a green light.
choices.D: You must slow down and prepare to stop.

en.explanation: The manual states that a traffic light marked with a green arrow indicates you can turn in the direction of the arrow without stopping.

en.question: Under Ohio's distracted driving law, which of the following is an exception for drivers under age 18?

choices.A: Using a hands-free device to make a call.
choices.B: Using a device for navigation purposes.
choices.C: Changing the music on a phone while stopped at a red light.
choices.D: There are no exceptions for drivers under age 18.

en.explanation: For drivers under age 18, the law makes an exception for using a device for navigation purposes or for making emergency services calls.

en.question: According to the manual, what is a primary effect of fatigue on a driver?

choices.A: It makes reaction time faster.
choices.B: It increases alertness.
choices.C: It can decrease reaction time and affect vision.
choices.D: It only affects driving during long trips.

en.explanation: The manual states that fatigue, or physical/mental tiredness, can affect your vision and decrease your reaction time.

en.question: In addition to public safety vehicles and pedestrians, to which of the following must a driver yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: Mail delivery trucks.
choices.B: Vehicles in a funeral procession.
choices.C: Vehicles turning right on red.
choices.D: Vehicles that are speeding.

en.explanation: Ohio law requires drivers to yield the right-of-way to funeral processions for the safety of all.

en.question: A driver age 18 or older is cited for their first distracted driving offense in two years. What can this driver do to potentially avoid the fine and points assessment?

choices.A: Pay the fine within 24 hours.
choices.B: Contest the ticket in court.
choices.C: Complete a distracted driving course.
choices.D: Promise the officer not to do it again.

en.explanation: The manual states that for a first distracted driving offense in two years, completion of a distracted driving course can help the driver avoid the fine and points.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of Regulatory Signs?

choices.A: To warn drivers of possible dangers ahead.
choices.B: To provide information about points of interest and services.
choices.C: To give notice to travelers of traffic laws or regulations.
choices.D: To indicate the type of roadway, such as an interstate or state route.

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'Regulatory Signs regulate the movement of traffic. These signs give notice to travelers of traffic laws or regulations.'

en.question: According to the warning sign for a narrow bridge, which vehicle has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The larger vehicle.
choices.B: The vehicle traveling at a higher speed.
choices.C: The vehicle that arrives at the bridge first.
choices.D: The vehicle nearest the bridge.

en.explanation: The manual text accompanying the narrow bridge warning sign states: 'VEHICLE NEAREST THE BRIDGE HAS THE RIGHT OF WAY'.

en.question: If you encounter a person with a sign or flag directing traffic in a Work Zone, what must you do?

choices.A: Follow their instructions.
choices.B: Use your horn to signal your intention to proceed.
choices.C: Proceed with caution at the posted speed limit.
choices.D: Stop and wait for a police officer to arrive.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'In Work Zones, traffic may be controlled by a person with a sign or flag directing traffic. You must follow their instructions.'

en.question: What type of information do the shape and color of Route Number Signs indicate?

choices.A: The distance to the next city.
choices.B: The location of hospitals and gas stations.
choices.C: The type of roadway (interstate, U.S., state, etc.).
choices.D: The presence of a work zone ahead.

en.explanation: The manual explains that for 'Route Number Signs: The shape and color of these signs indicate the type of roadway — interstate, U.S., state, city, county, or local road.'

en.question: When driving on a road with a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, what is true for the motorist in the lane with the solid line?

choices.A: They may pass only when the road is clear.
choices.B: Passing is prohibited.
choices.C: They may pass only during daylight hours.
choices.D: They must prepare to merge into the other lane.

en.explanation: The manual states for a 'YELLOW SOLID LINE WITH A BROKEN (DASHED) LINE': 'Passing is prohibited for motorists traveling in the lane with the solid line.'

en.question: Besides making an immediate left turn, what is a prohibited use of a two-way left turn only lane?

choices.A: Stopping to wait for a gap in traffic.
choices.B: Using it as a travel or passing lane.
choices.C: Entering it from a side street.
choices.D: Yielding to oncoming traffic within the lane.

en.explanation: Regarding the two-way left turn only lane, the manual specifies, 'This is not a lane used for traveling or passing.'

en.question: Before turning the key or pushing the start button to start your vehicle's engine, what two things should you check?

choices.A: Foot is on the accelerator and gear is in neutral.
choices.B: Foot is on the brake pedal and gear is in park.
choices.C: Headlights are on and mirrors are adjusted.
choices.D: Gear is in 'D' (drive) and turn signal is on.

en.explanation: The manual instructs: 'To start the engine, place your right foot on the brake pedal and check the gear selector for park.'

en.question: When preparing to stop your vehicle, what is the first step you should take after identifying the need to stop?

choices.A: Press the brake pedal with firm pressure.
choices.B: Move your foot from the accelerator to the brake.
choices.C: Check your mirrors for traffic to the rear.
choices.D: Activate your emergency flashers.

en.explanation: The procedure for stopping the vehicle is: 'Check your mirrors for traffic to the rear of your vehicle. Move your foot from the accelerator to the brake pedal.'

en.question: When making a legal turn on a red light, what must a driver do after coming to a full stop?

choices.A: Proceed immediately if the path is clear.
choices.B: Honk to alert pedestrians and other traffic.
choices.C: Yield the right-of-way to all crossing traffic and pedestrians.
choices.D: Wait for the traffic signal to turn green.

en.explanation: The manual states a driver may proceed with a legal turn on red 'after coming to a full stop and yielding the right-of-way to all crossing traffic and to all pedestrians crossing the intersection.'

en.question: Which of the following color combinations is used for Guide Signs that provide information on services, points of interest, and directions?

choices.A: Yellow and black.
choices.B: Red and white.
choices.C: Orange and black.
choices.D: Green, brown, or blue.

en.explanation: The manual explains, 'Guide Signs’ shapes may be square or rectangular, and colors may be green, brown, or blue.'

en.question: What is the distinctive background color for most Work Zone signs?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: White
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: Green

en.explanation: The manual notes that 'Work Zone Signs: These signs generally have a distinctive orange background.'

en.question: What does a single, broken (dashed) yellow line separating lanes of traffic indicate?

choices.A: Passing is prohibited for all vehicles.
choices.B: It separates traffic moving in the same direction.
choices.C: Vehicles traveling in either direction may pass when it is safe.
choices.D: The lane is ending and you must merge.

en.explanation: The manual specifies for a 'YELLOW BROKEN (DASHED) LINE': 'Vehicles traveling in either direction may pass vehicles traveling in the same direction when safe to do so.'

en.question: If a crosswalk is present at an intersection but there is also a stop line painted on the road before the crosswalk, where must you stop?

choices.A: On the crosswalk lines.
choices.B: Anywhere before the intersection.
choices.C: The stop line must be obeyed.
choices.D: After the crosswalk but before the intersection.

en.explanation: The manual clarifies, 'You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians entering or in a crosswalk. If there is a stop line before the crosswalk, the stop line must be obeyed.'

en.question: When approaching a public safety vehicle with flashing lights on a divided highway, when are you NOT required to move to the right and stop?

choices.A: When the vehicle is more than 500 feet behind you
choices.B: When you are in the far left lane
choices.C: When the vehicle is traveling in the opposite direction
choices.D: During daylight hours

en.explanation: The manual states you must yield to a public safety vehicle displaying flashing lights "unless the vehicle is traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway."

en.question: When backing up your vehicle, where should you place your right arm for optimal visibility and control?

choices.A: On the steering wheel at the 4 o'clock position
choices.B: On the back of the passenger seat
choices.C: Out the driver's side window
choices.D: On the center console

en.explanation: The manual advises to "Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window."

en.question: While backup cameras and mirrors are useful, what is the primary way you should look when backing your vehicle?

choices.A: By looking only at the backup camera display
choices.B: By alternating between your side-view mirrors
choices.C: By looking directly through the rear window
choices.D: By opening the door and looking behind you

en.explanation: The manual states to "look directly through the rear window" and notes that mirrors and backup cameras may not show the entire area behind your vehicle.

en.question: When searching for oncoming and cross traffic at an intersection, what is the recommended visual scanning pattern?

choices.A: Look right, then left
choices.B: Look straight ahead, then left and right
choices.C: Look left, right, then left again
choices.D: Look right, left, then right again

en.explanation: The manual advises to search for oncoming and cross traffic at intersections by looking "left, right, then left again."

en.question: According to the Ohio Driver Manual, what common error should you avoid when making a right turn?

choices.A: Signaling less than 100 feet before the turn
choices.B: Turning into the lane furthest from the curb
choices.C: Swinging wide to the left before the turn
choices.D: Accelerating too slowly after the turn

en.explanation: When making a right turn, the manual explicitly states to "Avoid swinging wide to the left before making the turn."

en.question: When completing a left turn onto a four-lane highway, which lane should you enter?

choices.A: The right-most lane
choices.B: Any available lane
choices.C: The lane just to the right of the center dividing line
choices.D: The far right lane to allow others to pass

en.explanation: The manual states to "always turn left from the left-most portion of your lane into the lane furthest left, just to the right of the center dividing line of the street you’re turning onto. This pertains to four-lane highways as well."

en.question: Under what specific circumstance is a left turn on a red light permitted in Ohio?

choices.A: From any street onto a one-way street
choices.B: From a two-way street onto a one-way street
choices.C: From a one-way street onto a two-way street
choices.D: From a one-way street onto another one-way street

en.explanation: A left turn on red is permitted "only from the extreme left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street," unless a sign prohibits it.

en.question: Once you have entered a roundabout or traffic circle, what action is strictly prohibited?

choices.A: Using your turn signal to exit
choices.B: Maintaining your speed
choices.C: Changing lanes
choices.D: Yielding to pedestrians

en.explanation: The manual states, "Once you have entered the roundabout, keep moving. Do not stop or change lanes."

en.question: Besides passing or avoiding an obstruction, which of the following is a legal reason to drive on the left half of the roadway?

choices.A: To get a better view around a curve
choices.B: When directed by a police officer
choices.C: If the right lane is moving too slowly
choices.D: To avoid sun glare

en.explanation: The manual lists several exceptions for driving on the right half of the road, including when "Otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control device."

en.question: Before changing lanes, after checking your mirrors, what is the correct way to check your blind spots?

choices.A: Lean forward to see more in the side mirror
choices.B: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
choices.C: Briefly speed up to see past the car next to you
choices.D: Rely solely on your vehicle's blind spot monitor

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to check blind spots "by turning your head and looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move."

en.question: What is a key defensive driving action you should take as you approach any intersection?

choices.A: Increase your speed to clear it quickly
choices.B: Reduce your speed and search the area
choices.C: Change to the leftmost lane
choices.D: Focus only on the traffic signal

en.explanation: The manual states, "At all intersections, reduce your speed and search for" various hazards like traffic controls, vehicles, and pedestrians.

en.question: If you are waiting to turn and see an approaching vehicle with its turn signal on, what should you do?

choices.A: Immediately pull out, as they are required to turn
choices.B: Wait to ensure the driver is actually turning before you proceed
choices.C: Honk to acknowledge their signal
choices.D: Flash your headlights to signal it is safe for them to turn

en.explanation: The manual warns, "Do not assume the vehicle is turning. The driver may turn after passing your vehicle or may have forgotten to turn off their signal."

en.question: If you are stopped at a stop sign and your view of crossing traffic is blocked by a building or other large object, what should you do?

choices.A: Wait for another car to go first and follow them closely
choices.B: Honk your horn twice before proceeding slowly
choices.C: Edge forward slowly to check for traffic before entering
choices.D: Reverse and find a different, safer route

en.explanation: The manual advises, "When stopped at a stop sign where you cannot see crossing traffic, edge forward to check for traffic before entering the intersection."

en.question: What crucial safety check should be performed *before* you even get into your vehicle to back up?

choices.A: Check your tire pressure
choices.B: Check behind your vehicle for children or small objects
choices.C: Adjust your mirrors and seat
choices.D: Plan your route using a GPS

en.explanation: The manual states, "Check behind your vehicle before you get in. Children and small objects cannot be seen from the driver’s seat."

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito de edad mínima para completar el examen de la vista y el examen de conocimientos en Ohio?

choices.A: 15 años
choices.B: 15 años y seis meses
choices.C: 16 años
choices.D: 18 años

es.explanation: Según el manual, a la edad de 15 años y seis meses, usted cumple con el requisito de edad mínima para completar el examen de la vista y el examen de conocimientos.

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas tiene el examen de conocimientos para conductores de Ohio?

choices.A: 20 preguntas de opción múltiple
choices.B: 30 preguntas de opción múltiple
choices.C: 40 preguntas de opción múltiple
choices.D: 50 preguntas de opción múltiple

es.explanation: El manual establece que el examen de conocimientos consta de 40 preguntas de opción múltiple.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el porcentaje mínimo de aprobación necesario para pasar el examen de conocimientos?
es.explanation: El manual especifica que se necesita un porcentaje de aprobación del 75% para aprobar el examen de conocimientos de 40 preguntas de opción múltiple.
