choices.C: Vehicles traveling in either direction may use it only to make left turns.
choices.D: It is a reversible lane for rush hour traffic.

en.explanation: The manual explains that low beam headlights shine only about 250 feet ahead, and 'To avoid overdriving your headlights on a dark road at night, you should not drive faster than 45 mph.'

en.question: When do pavements typically become the most slippery during a rain storm?

choices.A: After it has been raining continuously for an hour.
choices.B: In the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rain storm.
choices.C: Only when the rain stops and the road begins to dry.
choices.D: When driving at speeds above 60 mph.

en.explanation: According to the Road Conditions section, 'Pavements can become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rain storm.'

en.question: In cold, wet weather, why should you be extra careful driving on sections of the road shaded by trees or buildings?

choices.A: They attract more wildlife to the roadway
choices.B: They are more prone to deep water accumulation
choices.C: These areas freeze more quickly and dry last
choices.D: They cause oil to rise to the surface faster

en.explanation: The manual states that in cold, wet weather, you should be extra careful driving on sections of road shaded by trees or buildings because these areas freeze more quickly and dry last.

en.question: At what speed can your vehicle begin to hydroplane when water is only 1/10 of an inch deep?

choices.A: 25 mph
choices.B: 35 mph
choices.C: 45 mph
choices.D: 55 mph

en.explanation: The manual notes that you can hydroplane at speeds as low as 35 mph, when water is only 1/10 of an inch deep.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if you find yourself hydroplaning?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately to stop the vehicle
choices.B: Turn the steering wheel sharply to regain traction
choices.C: Keep both hands on the steering wheel and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal
choices.D: Shift your vehicle into neutral and coast until traction returns

en.explanation: If you find yourself hydroplaning, the manual instructs you to keep both hands on the steering wheel and slowly take your foot off of the gas pedal to let your vehicle slow down.

en.question: Why is it extremely dangerous to drive when the temperature is near 32° Fahrenheit?

choices.A: Black ice forms exclusively at this temperature
choices.B: Precipitation turns to rain or sleet, creating a thin layer of water on top of ice that is more slippery than ice alone
choices.C: Your vehicle's anti-lock brakes will not function properly
choices.D: Windshield washer fluid is most likely to freeze on contact

en.explanation: The manual states it is extremely dangerous near 32° (Fahrenheit), when precipitation turns to rain or sleet, because a thin layer of water on top of ice is more slippery than ice alone.

en.question: How can you identify the potential presence of "black ice" on the roadway?

choices.A: The road looks wet but no spray is coming from the tires of other vehicles
choices.B: The road surface appears unusually white and textured
choices.C: You hear a loud crunching sound from your tires
choices.D: Puddles begin to form rapidly on the shoulder of the road

en.explanation: According to the manual, when the road looks wet but no spray is coming from the tires of other vehicles, "black ice" may be present.

en.question: What is the penalty if snow or ice falls from your moving vehicle and causes death or serious bodily injury to another person?

choices.A: A fine of $50 to $100
choices.B: A fine of $200 to $1,000 for each offense
choices.C: Immediate license suspension for one year
choices.D: A mandatory 30-day jail sentence

en.explanation: Under a law effective July 10, 2006, the operator of the vehicle from which the snow or ice came is subject to a fine of $200 to $1,000 for each offense if it causes death or serious bodily injury.

en.question: How should you adjust your following distance when driving on wet roads?

choices.A: Maintain the standard three-second following distance
choices.B: Increase your following distance to five or six seconds
choices.C: Leave about 10 times more space than normal
choices.D: Decrease your following distance to stay in the tracks of the vehicle ahead

en.explanation: When roads get slick, the manual advises to reduce your speed by 5 to 10 mph on wet roads and increase your following distance to five (5) or six (6) seconds.

en.question: Why should you avoid using cruise control when driving on slippery roads?

choices.A: It drains the vehicle's battery faster in cold weather
choices.B: It disables the anti-lock braking system
choices.C: It will continue to apply power if your wheels start spinning, keeping you from regaining control
choices.D: It causes the engine to overheat when traction is low

en.explanation: The manual warns not to use cruise control on slippery roads because if wheel-spin occurs, an activated cruise control system will continue to apply power, keeping your wheels spinning and preventing you from regaining control.

en.question: What is a recommended technique for approaching an intersection on icy or snow-packed roads?

choices.A: Accelerate quickly to pass through the intersection before the light changes
choices.B: Pump your brakes rapidly as you approach the stop line
choices.C: Shift into neutral and apply the emergency brake
choices.D: Time your arrival by letting your vehicle coast until the light turns green and vehicles ahead begin to move

en.explanation: On icy or snow-packed roads, the manual recommends trying to time your arrival at an intersection by letting your vehicle coast until the light turns green and vehicles ahead of you have begun to move, so you do not have to brake to stop and then accelerate.

en.question: What should you do if you get caught in dense fog and cannot see?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams and continue driving slowly
choices.B: Pull completely off the road, turn on hazard lights, and keep your seat belt fastened
choices.C: Stop in the middle of your lane and wait for the fog to clear
choices.D: Follow closely behind a large truck to use its taillights as a guide

en.explanation: If caught in dense fog, the manual states it is best to pull completely off of the road (preferably into a parking lot), turn your hazard lights on, and keep your seat belt fastened.

en.question: Why should you NOT use your high beam headlights when driving in fog?

choices.A: They will drain your vehicle's battery excessively
choices.B: They direct light up into the fog, which bounces back into your eyes and creates glare
choices.C: They are illegal to use during daylight hours
choices.D: They automatically disable your windshield wipers

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states not to use high beams in fog because they direct their light up and into the fog, which bounces the light back into your eyes, creating glare and making it harder to see.

en.question: How much can a dirty headlight reduce its light output?

choices.A: By 10 percent
choices.B: By 25 percent
choices.C: By more than 50 percent
choices.D: By up to 75 percent

en.explanation: When discussing clearing your vehicle for snowy conditions, the manual notes that a dirty headlight reduces light output by more than 50 percent.

en.question: When driving in snowy conditions during the daytime, why should you turn on your low beams?

choices.A: To melt snow falling on the headlights
choices.B: To increase your visibility to other drivers
choices.C: To activate your vehicle's defroster system
choices.D: To prevent your battery from freezing

en.explanation: The manual advises turning on your low beams, even during the daytime in snowy conditions, because this increases your visibility to other drivers.

en.question: If you encounter a snow squall while driving, what action should you take?

choices.A: Slam on your brakes immediately to stop
choices.B: Accelerate to get out of the squall as quickly as possible
choices.C: Exercise extreme caution by gradually slowing and activating your hazard lights
choices.D: Turn on your high beams to cut through the heavy snow

en.explanation: The manual advises that if you encounter a snow squall, you should exercise extreme caution by gradually slowing and activating your hazard lights for increased visibility, and specifically warns not to slam on your brakes.

en.question: What is the approximate total penalty, including fees, for failing to turn on your headlights when your wipers are in continuous or intermittent use?
en.explanation: According to the manual, motorists who do not comply with the headlight/windshield wiper law face a fine of $25, but with fees and other associated costs, the penalty approaches $100.

en.question: When driving in weather conditions that require continuous or intermittent use of your windshield wipers, what else must you do?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams.
choices.B: Turn on your headlights and tail lights.
choices.C: Rely only on your daytime running lights.
choices.D: Turn on your hazard flashers.

en.explanation: The law requires motorists to turn on their headlights anytime their wipers are in use due to weather. Daytime running lights are not enough, and tail lights must be illuminated as well.

en.question: If you are approaching an emergency scene or a tow truck picking up a disabled vehicle and cannot move into a nonadjacent lane, you must:

choices.A: Stop your vehicle immediately.
choices.B: Reduce your speed to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit.
choices.C: Maintain your speed but turn on your hazard lights.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert the emergency workers.

en.explanation: When approaching an emergency scene, police stop, or tow truck, you must move into a nonadjacent lane. If you cannot move over, you must reduce your speed to at least 20 miles per hour below the posted speed limit.

en.question: How should you handle a situation where you are approaching a bicyclist on your right and an oncoming vehicle at the same time?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the bicyclist before the vehicle reaches you.
choices.B: Move to the left lane and force the oncoming vehicle to slow down.
choices.C: Honk your horn so the bicyclist moves off the road.
choices.D: Slow down to let the oncoming vehicle pass, then move left to pass the bicyclist.

en.explanation: You should handle this situation by facing only one traffic condition at a time. Slow down to let the oncoming vehicle pass and then move left to pass the cyclist, leaving a sufficient amount of space.

en.question: What does an orange triangle displayed on the back of a vehicle indicate?

choices.A: The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
choices.B: The vehicle is designed to operate at 25 mph or less.
choices.C: The vehicle is broken down and waiting for a tow.
choices.D: The vehicle is a wide load.

en.explanation: In rural areas, an orange triangle is displayed on the back of farm tractors and horse-drawn vehicles designed to operate at 25 mph or less.

en.question: What should you do to communicate to drivers behind you that you are going to brake where they may not expect it?

choices.A: Turn on your hazard flashers.
choices.B: Use a hand signal for slowing down.
choices.C: Quickly tap your brake pedal three or four times.
choices.D: Honk your horn twice.

en.explanation: If you are going to brake where other drivers may not expect it, the manual advises to quickly tap your brake pedal three or four times to warn them.

en.question: When must you use your hazard (four-way) flashers on a limited access highway?

choices.A: When you are driving below 40 mph.
choices.B: When you are driving in the left lane.
choices.C: When you are passing a large truck.
choices.D: When you are approaching a toll booth.

en.explanation: If you must drive below 40 mph on a limited access highway, you must use your hazard (four-way) flashers to warn the drivers behind you.

en.question: Under Pennsylvania law, how far in advance must you use your turn signal if you are driving 35 mph or more?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 300 feet

en.explanation: If you are driving 35 mph or more, Pennsylvania law requires you to signal at least 300 feet before turning.

en.question: If you are driving less than 35 mph, how far before a turn must you use your turn signals?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 300 feet

en.explanation: Under Pennsylvania law, you must always use your turn signals at least 100 feet before turning if you are driving less than 35 mph.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway and you have pulled off the road and turned on your hazard flashers, what else should you do to let other drivers know your vehicle is disabled?

choices.A: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.
choices.B: Lift your hood.
choices.C: Honk your horn continuously.
choices.D: Place an orange triangle on your roof.

en.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, you should pull off the road, put on your hazard flashers, and lift your hood to let other drivers know your vehicle is disabled.

en.question: According to the manual, what is probably the most important factor to concentrate on when making a turn?

choices.A: The size of your vehicle
choices.B: Speed
choices.C: The type of road surface
choices.D: The time of day

en.explanation: The manual states: "Speed is probably the most important factor. When turning, reduce to a speed that allows you to maintain control of your vehicle..."

en.question: When turning onto a highway that has more than one lane traveling in the direction you wish to go, which lane should you turn into?

choices.A: The center lane.
choices.B: The lane furthest from you.
choices.C: The closest lane going in that direction.
choices.D: Any lane that is currently empty.

en.explanation: If you are turning onto a highway which has more than one lane in the direction you wish to travel, turn into the closest lane going in that direction.

en.question: A lane in the middle of a two-way street marked on both sides by a solid outer line and a broken inner line may only be used for:

choices.A: Passing slow-moving vehicles.
choices.B: Left turns.
choices.C: Right turns.
choices.D: Emergency parking.

en.explanation: A lane in the middle of a two-way street marked on both sides by two lines (one solid outer line and one broken inner line) means this lane may only be used for left turns.

en.question: Which of the following is a correct guideline for safely using a center turn lane?

choices.A: Enter the lane as early as possible to secure your spot.
choices.B: Leave the back end of your vehicle in the travel lane to block traffic.
choices.C: Enter the lane completely so you do not block traffic.
choices.D: Put on your right turn signal before entering.

en.explanation: When you enter the center turn lane, you must enter it completely. Do not leave the back end of your vehicle sticking into the normal travel lane, blocking traffic.

en.question: How long do dangerous snow squalls typically last for a specific roadway when a 'Snow Squall Warning' is issued?

choices.A: Less than 45 minutes
choices.B: 1 to 2 hours
choices.C: 3 to 4 hours
choices.D: An entire day

en.explanation: The National Weather Service issues Snow Squall Warnings for specific roadways where squalls are likely to cause great impact, typically lasting less than 45 minutes for a roadway.

en.question: How far in advance should you use your turn signal before making a turn?

choices.A: 1 to 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 to 4 seconds
choices.C: 5 to 6 seconds
choices.D: 10 seconds

en.explanation: To complete a turn safely, the manual states you must signal three (3) to four (4) seconds before your turn.

en.question: When choosing a place to make a U-turn, how far away must drivers coming from all directions be so they can see you clearly?

choices.A: At least 100 feet
choices.B: At least 250 feet
choices.C: At least 500 feet
choices.D: At least 1,000 feet

en.explanation: In choosing a place to make a U-turn, you must make sure drivers coming from all directions are at least 500 feet away from you and can see you clearly.

en.question: When crossing traffic, when is it considered safe to stop halfway across a street?

choices.A: When there is a stop sign in the middle of the intersection
choices.B: When cross traffic is moving at a slow speed
choices.C: When there is a center median turning lane large enough to hold your entire vehicle
choices.D: Whenever you have a green light but traffic is backed up

en.explanation: Stopping halfway across a street is safe only when there is a turning lane provided in the center median large enough to hold your entire vehicle.

en.question: If you are waiting to cross a street and an approaching vehicle has its turn signal on, what is the safest action?

choices.A: Pull out immediately because the vehicle will definitely turn
choices.B: Wait until the other driver actually starts to turn before you go
choices.C: Honk your horn to let them know you are crossing
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to cross before they reach the intersection

en.explanation: Do not pull out in front of an approaching vehicle with its turn signal on. The driver may have changed their mind or forgotten to turn off the signal. Wait until the other driver actually starts to turn before you go.

en.question: Which of the following actions is illegal when using an acceleration lane to merge onto a highway?

choices.A: Accelerating to the speed of traffic
choices.B: Looking for an opening in traffic
choices.C: Passing a vehicle ahead of you in the acceleration lane
choices.D: Using your turn signal before merging

en.explanation: Entrance ramps for highways often have acceleration lanes. The manual explicitly states that it is illegal to pass a vehicle ahead of you in an acceleration lane.

en.question: When passing on a two-lane road at 45 mph, how much clear roadway do you need to safely pass a slower vehicle?

choices.A: 1/8 mile
choices.B: 1/4 mile
choices.C: 1/2 mile
choices.D: 1 mile

en.explanation: Passing on a two-lane road requires good judgment. At 45 mph, this translates into 1/4 mile of clear roadway you need to safely pass a slower vehicle.

en.question: Approximately how much faster than the vehicle you are passing do you need to be traveling to pass safely?

choices.A: 5 mph faster
choices.B: 10 mph faster
choices.C: 15 mph faster
choices.D: 20 mph faster

en.explanation: According to the manual, you need to be going about 10 mph faster than the vehicle(s) you are passing.

en.question: Under which of the following conditions are you permitted to pass another vehicle on the right?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the posted speed limit
choices.B: When the driver you are passing is making or signaling a left turn
choices.C: When you are within 100 feet of an intersection
choices.D: When you are on a single-lane road and the vehicle ahead stops

en.explanation: You may pass another vehicle on the right when the driver you are passing is making or signaling a left turn, provided you stay on the berm or shoulder.

en.question: You may NOT pass another vehicle if you are within how many feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You may not pass if you are within 100 feet of or are crossing any intersection or railroad grade crossing, unless an official traffic control device says you may.

en.question: After passing a vehicle, how do you know it is safe to move back into your original lane?

choices.A: When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle
choices.B: When the driver you passed flashes their headlights
choices.C: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
choices.D: When three seconds have passed since you overtook the vehicle

en.explanation: Before you move back into the lane, make sure you can see both headlights on the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

en.question: Who must yield the right-of-way at a circular intersection (or roundabout)?

choices.A: Drivers already in the circle must yield to drivers entering.
choices.B: Drivers entering the circle must yield to drivers already in the circle.
choices.C: Drivers entering from the right must yield to drivers entering from the left.
choices.D: All drivers must stop and yield to the right.

en.explanation: Drivers entering a circular intersection (or roundabout) must yield the right-of-way to drivers already in the circle.

en.question: What must you do if you accidentally end up in a lane marked for turns only, but you want to go straight?

choices.A: Stop and wait for traffic to clear before merging into the through lane.
choices.B: Proceed straight through the intersection cautiously.
choices.C: You must make the turn.
choices.D: Reverse your vehicle to change lanes.

en.explanation: If you end up in a lane marked for turns only when you want to go straight through the intersection, you must make the turn.

en.question: When turning left from a dual left turn lane, why is it important not to change lanes during the turn?

choices.A: It will cause you to crash into the driver turning next to you.
choices.B: It is illegal to use your turn signal in an intersection.
choices.C: You will be forced to enter a jughandle.
choices.D: You will lose your right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: The manual states that you must not change lanes during a turn from a dual left turn lane, as this will cause you to crash into the driver turning next to you.

en.question: In over one-third of crashes involving 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania, the teen driver was doing what?

choices.A: Speeding on a left-bending curve.
choices.B: Pulling out from a stop sign or turning left across traffic.
choices.C: Failing to yield at a roundabout.
choices.D: Overtaking a bicyclist in an intersection.

en.explanation: Intersections are places where teenage drivers have a high percentage of crashes. In over one-third of these crashes, the teen driver was pulling out from a stop sign or turning left across traffic.

en.question: What is the correct procedure for turning left onto a divided highway?

choices.A: Cross both roadways at once without stopping in the middle.
choices.B: Turn left onto the first roadway you encounter.
choices.C: Cross the first roadway when safe, then turn left on the other side of the barrier when there is a safe gap in the second roadway.
choices.D: Enter the jughandle on the left side of the road.

en.explanation: To correctly turn left onto a divided highway, you need to cross the first roadway when there is a safe gap, and then turn left on the other side of the barrier when there is a safe gap in traffic on the second roadway.

en.question: About how much of a gap in traffic do you need in both directions to travel across an intersection with a two-way stop sign on a 30 mph street?

choices.A: A 3-second gap.
choices.B: A 6-second gap.
choices.C: A 9-second gap.
choices.D: A 12-second gap.

en.explanation: To travel across an intersection with a two-way stop sign, you need about a 6-second gap in both directions to cross a 30 mph street.

en.question: When making a right turn, approximately how large of a gap should you allow between you and any vehicle approaching from the left?

choices.A: 4 seconds
choices.B: 6 seconds
choices.C: 8 seconds
choices.D: 10 seconds

en.explanation: When turning right, you should allow a gap of about eight (8) seconds between you and any vehicle approaching from the left.

en.question: How can you avoid a 'tangle turn' with another left-turning driver coming from the opposite direction?

choices.A: By turning after you pass the center of the intersection.
choices.B: By turning before you reach the imaginary 'X' at the center of the intersection.
choices.C: By turning into the lane furthest from the centerline.
choices.D: By waiting until the other driver completes their turn first.

en.explanation: You can avoid a 'tangle turn' with another left-turning driver by imagining an 'X' at the center of the intersection and turning before you reach the 'X'.

en.question: Who has the right-of-way when you are pulling up to the yield line of a roundabout?

choices.A: The vehicle entering the roundabout.
choices.B: Circulating traffic within the roundabout.
choices.C: Vehicles approaching from the right.
choices.D: Vehicles exiting the roundabout.

en.explanation: When pulling up to the yield line of a roundabout, you must look to the left and check for approaching traffic, because circulating traffic has the right-of-way.

en.question: Which signal should you use as you approach your exit in a roundabout?

choices.A: Left turn signal
choices.B: Right turn signal
choices.C: Hazard lights
choices.D: No signal is required

en.explanation: As you approach your exit in a roundabout, you must use your RIGHT TURN SIGNAL.

en.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are driving inside a roundabout?

choices.A: Stop immediately inside the roundabout to let them pass.
choices.B: Speed up to exit the roundabout before the emergency vehicle enters.
choices.C: Immediately exit the roundabout and pull to the side.
choices.D: Pull over to the center island of the roundabout.

en.explanation: If you are in a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches, you must immediately exit the roundabout and pull to the side. You should NEVER STOP IN THE ROUNDABOUT.

en.question: What is the rule regarding bicyclists who are functioning as vehicles in a roundabout?

choices.A: You should honk to warn them to move to the pedestrian crosswalk.
choices.B: You may pass them if there is enough room on the left.
choices.C: You must never overtake a bicyclist acting as a vehicle in a roundabout.
choices.D: Bicyclists are not allowed to function as vehicles in a roundabout.

en.explanation: Bicyclists have the option to function as a vehicle in a roundabout. Motorists must NEVER OVERTAKE A BICYCLIST ACTING AS A VEHICLE IN A ROUNDABOUT.

en.question: What is the purpose of a jughandle on a busy commercial road?

choices.A: To allow vehicles to make a left turn by using a right turn lane curving back to intersect the major road.
choices.B: To provide a safe place for vehicles to make a U-turn across the physical barrier.
choices.C: To allow emergency vehicles to bypass heavy traffic at an intersection.
choices.D: To create a designated lane for bicyclists and pedestrians.

en.explanation: In a jughandle design, instead of making a left turn directly across oncoming traffic, you use a right turn lane curving back to intersect the major road at a traffic light to turn left.

en.question: When is the best time to slow down to maintain control on a curve?

choices.A: Just after you enter the curve.
choices.B: At the apex (middle) of the curve.
choices.C: Before you enter the curve.
choices.D: As you are exiting the curve.

en.explanation: To maintain control on curves, you must slow down, and you should do it BEFORE you enter the curve.

en.question: Where should you position your vehicle when safely driving through a right curve?

choices.A: In the middle of your lane.
choices.B: Slightly to the right of the lane center.
choices.C: Slightly to the left of the lane center.
choices.D: On the shoulder of the road.

en.explanation: To safely drive through curves, you should keep slightly to the right of the lane center on right curves and in the middle of your lane on left curves.

en.question: What is the most frequent crash type for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania?

choices.A: Rear-end collisions at stop lights.
choices.B: Head-on collisions on divided highways.
choices.C: Single-vehicle, run-off-the-road crashes.
choices.D: Tangle turns at intersections.

en.explanation: According to the manual's Teen Crash Fact, the most frequent crash type for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania is a single-vehicle, run-off-the-road crash.

en.question: When traffic entering and exiting a highway must share a short 'weaving lane', who must yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver exiting the highway
choices.B: The driver entering the highway
choices.C: The driver traveling at a higher speed
choices.D: The driver traveling at a lower speed

en.explanation: The manual states that if you are the driver entering the highway, you must yield to the exiting driver when sharing a weaving lane.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a highway?

choices.A: Stop and carefully back up on the shoulder
choices.B: Cross over the median to turn around
choices.C: Swerve across lanes to make the exit at the last second
choices.D: Take the next exit

en.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross over the median, as these maneuvers are illegal and hazardous.

en.question: When exiting a highway, when is the proper time to slow down?

choices.A: One mile before the exit ramp
choices.B: While still in the main traffic lane before changing lanes
choices.C: After you have moved into the exit lane
choices.D: As soon as you see the exit sign

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to get in the proper lane for exiting well in advance and to not slow down until after moving into the exit lane.

en.question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?

choices.A: Driving under the influence of prescription medications
choices.B: Staring straight ahead at the roadway for long periods of time and zoning out
choices.C: Driving at speeds exceeding 65 mph for more than an hour
choices.D: Looking back and forth rapidly between your mirrors and the road

en.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the roadway for long periods of time and stop actively scanning ahead, behind, and around your vehicle.

en.question: When parking on a street with a curb, what is the maximum distance your vehicle can be from the curb?

choices.A: 6 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 24 inches

en.explanation: If the street you are on has a curb, you must park as close to it as possible, but no more than 12 inches away.

en.question: When you must park on the roadway, your vehicle must be visible for at least how far in both directions?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: When you must park on the roadway, use your four-way flashers and make sure your vehicle can be seen at least 500 feet in both directions.

en.question: How should you position your steering wheel when parking your vehicle on a downhill grade, with or without a curb?

choices.A: Turn your wheels completely to the left
choices.B: Turn your wheels completely to the right
choices.C: Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead
choices.D: Turn your wheels parallel to the roadway

en.explanation: When parking your vehicle on a downhill with or without a curb, you should turn your steering wheel so your wheels are completely to the right.

en.question: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

choices.B: A minimum of 100 feet
choices.C: A minimum of 200 feet

en.question: How can you confirm you are headed in the right direction when entering a highway ramp?

en.question: What should you do regarding your following distance when driving in a work zone?

choices.D: Reduce your following distance by half

en.question: Whose authority overrides conventional traffic control devices in a work zone?

choices.A: Flaggers
choices.B: Construction workers
choices.C: Escort vehicles
choices.D: Electronic message boards

en.question: In which direction should you look as you approach a railroad crossing?

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets trapped on a railroad crossing and a train is approaching?

en.question: When is it safe to wave a pedestrian into the line of traffic?

choices.A: Only at marked crosswalks
choices.B: When you have come to a complete stop
choices.C: Only if there are no other vehicles approaching
choices.D: It is never safe to wave a pedestrian into the line of traffic

en.question: What should you do when approaching a stopped vehicle from behind?

choices.A: Honk your horn and pass quickly on the left
choices.B: Slow down and do not pass until you are sure no pedestrians are crossing in front of it
choices.C: Pass on the right shoulder if there is enough room
choices.D: Flash your high beams to warn the driver you are passing

en.explanation: When approaching a stopped vehicle from behind, you should slow down and do not pass until you are sure there are no pedestrians crossing in front of it.

en.question: When passing a truck, when is it safe to move back into the truck's lane?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the truck's front bumper

choices.C: When the truck driver flashes their headlights
choices.D: After you have maintained your speed for 5 seconds

en.explanation: After passing a truck, you should change lanes only when you can see the truck's headlights or front grill in your rearview mirror.

en.question: Why might you need to increase your speed when passing a truck on a downgrade?

choices.A: Because the truck's momentum will cause it to go faster
choices.B: Because the truck will intentionally speed up to prevent you from passing
choices.C: Because it is illegal to pass a truck slowly on a hill
choices.D: Because the wind turbulence is stronger on a downgrade

en.explanation: On a downgrade, a truck's momentum will cause it to go faster, so you may need to increase your speed to pass it safely.

en.question: Why should you avoid slowing down or stopping quickly immediately after passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: It will cause the bicyclist to lose their balance
choices.B: The bicyclist may crash into your vehicle
choices.C: It is illegal to brake in front of a non-motorized vehicle
choices.D: It creates excessive wind turbulence

en.explanation: After you have passed a bicyclist, do not slow down or stop quickly because a quick stop could lead to the bicyclist crashing into your vehicle.

en.question: How much lane space must you allow a motorcyclist or moped driver to use?

choices.A: Half of a lane
choices.B: One complete lane
choices.C: Only the right side of the lane
choices.D: As much space as they need up to the center line

en.explanation: According to the law, you must allow the motorcyclist or moped driver to use one complete lane.

en.question: Why should you not assume a motorcycle is turning just because its turn signal is flashing?

choices.A: Motorcyclists often use turn signals to indicate they are slowing down

choices.D: Motorcyclists use turn signals to test their battery

en.question: What should you do when a large truck is passing your vehicle?

choices.A: Increase your speed to get out of the way
choices.B: Reduce your speed slightly and keep it steady
choices.C: Brake hard to let the truck pass quickly
choices.D: Move into the truck's blind spot

en.explanation: When a truck passes your vehicle, you will make it easier for the truck driver if you reduce your speed slightly and then keep your speed steady. Do not increase your speed.

en.question: Which of the following is a safety rule you must follow when driving through a work zone?

choices.A: Always use your cruise control to maintain a steady speed
choices.B: Do not use your cruise control
choices.C: Stop to ask directions from workers if you are lost
choices.D: Cross solid white lines to avoid construction equipment

en.question: How much more likely are you to die in a crash involving a train compared to a crash with another vehicle?

choices.B: 20 times more likely
choices.C: 30 times more likely
choices.D: 40 times more likely

en.explanation: According to the manual, you are 40 times more likely to die in a crash involving a train than you are in a crash with another vehicle.

en.question: What is the recommended minimum following distance you should allow when driving behind a motorcycle?

choices.A: 2 seconds
choices.B: 3 seconds
choices.C: 4 seconds

en.explanation: You should allow the same 4-second following distance or more that you would allow for other vehicles when following a motorcycle or moped.

en.question: How does wind turbulence between your vehicle and an oncoming truck affect the vehicles?

choices.A: It pulls the vehicles together.
choices.B: It pushes the vehicles apart.
choices.C: It causes the truck to brake suddenly.
choices.D: It has no effect on passenger vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Remember, the wind turbulence pushes vehicles apart. It does not pull them together."

en.question: How can you ensure a truck driver can see your vehicle when you are following them?

choices.A: Turn your high beams on so you are visible.
choices.B: Honk your horn every few minutes.
choices.C: Position your vehicle so you can see the truck's side mirrors.
choices.D: Tailgate the truck closely to stay in their direct line of sight.

en.explanation: The manual states, "When following a truck or bus, if you cannot see the side mirrors of the vehicle in front of you, the driver of the large vehicle cannot see you."

en.question: Why should you leave plenty of room between your vehicle and a truck when coming to a stop on a hill?

choices.A: The truck's exhaust will damage your windshield.
choices.B: Trucks may roll back as the driver takes their foot off the brake.
choices.C: The truck needs extra room to make a wide turn.
choices.D: The truck's air brakes will release a loud noise.

en.explanation: The manual states, "Leave plenty of room between you and the truck when coming to a stop on a hill. Trucks may roll back as a driver takes their foot off of the brake."

en.question: What is the recommended minimum following distance to keep you out of a truck's rear blind spot?

choices.A: Two seconds
choices.B: Three seconds
choices.C: Four seconds
choices.D: Five seconds

en.explanation: The manual states, "At least four (4) seconds are needed to keep you out of the truck’s rear blind spot..."

en.question: When a truck is making a wide right turn, it may sometimes look like it is:

choices.B: Preparing to back up

choices.D: Speeding up to pass another vehicle

en.question: Under clear, dry conditions at 65 mph, what is the minimum stopping distance required for a loaded truck with good tires and properly adjusted brakes?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 400 feet
choices.C: 600 feet
choices.D: 800 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that a loaded truck traveling at 65 mph on a clear, dry roadway requires a minimum of 600 feet to come to a complete stop.

en.question: What is the purpose of escape ramps on long downgrades?

choices.A: For passenger vehicles to take a rest break.
choices.B: For police to monitor speeding vehicles.
choices.C: For large vehicles that are out of control or have brake failure.
choices.D: For oversized loads to allow traffic to pass.

en.explanation: The manual states, "These ramps are to be used only by large vehicles that are out of control or cannot stop because of brake failure."

en.question: When a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, how far away must you stop?

choices.B: At least 15 feet away
choices.C: At least 20 feet away
choices.D: At least 50 feet away

en.explanation: The manual states, "you must stop at least 10 feet away from the bus whether you are behind it or coming toward it on the same roadway..."

en.question: Under what condition are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?

choices.A: When you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.
choices.B: When you are approaching an intersection where the bus is stopped.
choices.C: When you are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway.
choices.D: When you are driving in a designated school zone.

en.explanation: The manual states, "If you are approaching a school bus... and you are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway... you do not have to stop."

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to stop for a school bus with a flashing red light and extended stop arm?

choices.A: A 30-day suspension, 3 points, and a fine

choices.D: A 6-month suspension, 6 points, and a fine

en.explanation: The manual states, "Failure to stop for a school bus with a flashing red light and extended stop arm will result in a 60-day suspension of your driver’s license, five (5) points on your driving record and a fine."

en.question: According to the Move Over law, what must you do if you cannot move into a lane that is not adjacent to an emergency response area?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle immediately until the emergency is cleared.

choices.C: Reduce your speed to at least 20 miles per hour below the posted speed limit.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert emergency workers of your presence.

en.explanation: The manual states, "If drivers cannot move over because of traffic or other conditions, they must reduce their speed to at least 20 miles per hour below the posted speed limit."

en.question: How many points are assessed to your driving record if you are convicted of violating the Move Over law?

choices.A: 2 points
choices.B: 3 points
choices.C: 4 points
choices.D: 5 points

en.question: What happens to the fines for traffic violations, including Move Over law violations, that occur in work zone areas?

en.question: What should you expect when encountering an oversized load on the road?

en.question: After an emergency vehicle passes you, what is the minimum distance you must keep away from it?

choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.question: Why is it dangerous to attempt to pass a snow plow?

choices.D: They frequently stop to pick up stranded motorists.

en.question: If an aggressive driver pursues you, what is the safest course of action?

en.question: According to the manual, approximately what percentage of highway deaths in Pennsylvania each year are attributed to aggressive driving?

en.question: When avoiding a collision at speeds above 25 mph, why is it usually better to steer to avoid the hazard than to brake?

choices.D: Steering requires less physical effort than braking.

en.question: Where should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel to minimize the risk of injury if the air bag deploys?

choices.D: One hand at 12 o'clock

choices.B: Resting on the center horn pad.
choices.C: Pointing directly toward your body.
choices.D: Along the face of the steering wheel.

en.explanation: You should keep your thumbs along the face of the steering wheel instead of gripping the inside of the rim.

en.question: To help prevent injury in a crash, what is the minimum recommended distance you should be positioned away from your air bag?

choices.A: 5 inches
choices.B: 10 inches
choices.C: 15 inches
choices.D: 20 inches

en.explanation: Injury prevention in a crash depends mostly on wearing your seat belt properly, having head restraints adjusted, and being positioned at least ten (10) inches away from your air bag.

en.question: How should you apply the brakes in an emergency if your vehicle does NOT have an anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

choices.A: Maintain firm and continuous pressure.
choices.B: Slam on the brakes and hold them down.
choices.C: Press and release the brakes repeatedly.
choices.D: Apply the parking brake immediately.

en.explanation: Without ABS, you should press and release the brakes repeatedly (pumping the brakes) to slow your vehicle and keep it under control. Slamming the brakes can lock your wheels.

en.question: What is the correct braking technique during an emergency if your vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes (ABS)?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly.
choices.B: Maintain firm and continuous pressure on the brake.
choices.C: Press the brake lightly and steer sharply.
choices.D: Slam the brakes and immediately release them.

en.explanation: With ABS, you should maintain firm and continuous pressure on the brake. Do not pump the brake pedal.

en.question: What should you do if the rear of your vehicle starts to skid to the right on an icy road?

choices.C: Slam on the brakes immediately.
choices.D: Shift into neutral and coast.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle begins to skid?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately
choices.B: Steer in the opposite direction the rear is skidding
choices.C: Steer in the direction the rear of your vehicle is skidding
choices.D: Shift into neutral and apply the parking brake

en.explanation: To stop a skid, you should steer in the direction the rear of your vehicle is skidding. It may take a few corrections to regain control.

en.question: Why should you avoid using your brakes when your vehicle is skidding?

choices.A: It will cause the engine to stall
choices.B: You risk locking your wheels and losing all steering control
choices.C: It will cause the accelerator to stick
choices.D: It will damage your transmission

en.explanation: When skidding, do not use your brakes. If you hit the brakes, the skid will be worse and you risk locking your wheels and losing all steering control.

en.question: How much moving water does it take to float many cars?

choices.C: Twelve inches

choices.D: Two feet

en.question: If your vehicle's accelerator (gas pedal) sticks, what is the first thing you should do with your vehicle's transmission?

choices.B: Shift into the lowest gear
choices.C: Shift into park
choices.D: Shift into reverse

en.question: If you need to slow or stop quickly because your accelerator is stuck, why should you avoid turning your ignition to the 'LOCK' position?

choices.D: It will deploy the airbags

en.question: If the brake system warning light comes on in a newer vehicle, what should you expect when pressing the brake pedal?

choices.C: The vehicle will immediately lock all four wheels
choices.D: The pedal will vibrate violently

en.question: When changing a flat tire, at what point should you loosen the lug nuts?

choices.C: After completely removing the hubcap and jacking the car up 12 inches
choices.D: Only after the spare tire is installed

en.question: What is a common indication that a front tire has blown out?

choices.C: The engine will suddenly race
choices.D: The brake pedal will drop to the floor

en.question: What is the most important thing to avoid doing immediately after a tire blowout?

choices.A: Holding the steering wheel tightly
choices.B: Taking your foot off the gas pedal
choices.C: Braking
choices.D: Steering smoothly

en.question: If your brakes suddenly fail in an older vehicle, what should you try doing to build up brake pressure?

choices.C: Pull the parking brake up as fast and hard as possible
choices.D: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly to the floor

en.question: If another vehicle is approaching you head-on in your lane, which direction should you try to escape if possible?

en.question: What must you do if you encounter a funeral procession at an intersection?

choices.B: They will have their headlights and emergency flashers turned on and bear a flag or insignia

en.question: What must all vehicles in a funeral procession have turned on?

choices.A: High beam headlights
choices.B: Headlights and emergency flashers
choices.C: Only emergency flashers
choices.D: Interior dome lights

en.explanation: According to the manual, all vehicles in a funeral procession must have their headlights and emergency flashers turned on and bear a flag or other insignia.

en.question: If the lead vehicle of a funeral procession enters an intersection on a green light, what may the following vehicles in the procession do?

en.question: What is the minimum fine for an adult convicted of knowingly and intentionally supplying minors with alcohol for the first offense?

en.question: What does the "one driver’s license" concept of the Driver’s License Compact (DLC) require?

choices.A: Drivers must carry their license at all times.
choices.B: Drivers must surrender an out-of-state license when applying for a license in another state.
choices.C: Drivers can hold licenses from up to two member states.
choices.D: Drivers must renew their license every year.

en.explanation: The "one driver’s license" concept requires the surrender of an out-of-state driver's license when application for a driver’s license in another state is made.

en.question: Which of the following drivers is required to have an Ignition Interlock system installed in their vehicle?

choices.A: A driver with a first offense of General Impairment (BAC .08 to .099).
choices.B: A driver who receives an operating privilege suspension for a chemical test refusal.
choices.C: Any driver caught speeding more than 20 mph over the limit.
choices.D: A driver convicted of underage drinking without driving.

en.explanation: First-time and repeat DUI offenders with high blood alcohol levels and individuals who receive an operating privilege suspension as a result of a chemical test refusal violation will be required to have an Ignition Interlock system installed.

en.question: If you are under 21 and convicted of DUI for the first time, what is the fine range you will have to pay?
en.explanation: If you are under 21 and are convicted of DUI for the first time, you will go to jail... your license will be suspended for a full year, and you will pay a fine of $500 to $5,000.

en.question: How must a chemical test refusal restoration fee be paid?

choices.A: By cash or personal check
choices.B: By credit card only
choices.C: By certified check or money order
choices.D: Through an online payment portal

en.explanation: A chemical test refusal restoration fee must be paid by certified check or money order.

en.question: The "High Rate" penalties (Table 2) apply to commercial vehicle drivers with a BAC of at least:
en.explanation: Table 2 - High Rate notes that this table also applies to commercial vehicle drivers with a BAC of .04 or more.

en.question: What will happen if you do not respond to an out-of-state traffic citation?

choices.A: You will be fined $500.
choices.B: Your Pennsylvania driving privilege will be indefinitely suspended.
choices.C: You will receive points on your driving record.
choices.D: Your vehicle will be impounded.

en.explanation: According to the manual, not responding to an out-of-state citation will result in the indefinite suspension of your Pennsylvania driving privilege until a response is made.

en.question: How many days do you have to notify PennDOT if you change your name or address?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: In accordance with Section 1515 of the Pennsylvania Vehicle Code, if your name or address is changed, you must notify PennDOT within 15 days of that change even if moving out of state.

en.question: According to Pennsylvania law, who is required to wear a seat belt in the front seat of a vehicle, light truck, or motor home?

choices.A: Only the driver
choices.B: Only passengers under 18
choices.C: All drivers and front seat passengers
choices.D: Only passengers without airbags

en.explanation: The manual states that all drivers and front seat passengers in vehicles, light trucks, and motor homes must wear seat belts.

en.question: Where must passengers who are age 8 or older, but less than age 18, wear a seat belt?

choices.A: Only in the front seat
choices.B: Only in the back seat
choices.C: No matter where they are riding in the vehicle
choices.D: Only if the vehicle lacks airbags

en.explanation: If you are transporting passengers age eight (8) or older but less than age 18, they must wear seat belts, no matter where they are riding in the vehicle.

en.question: If you are a driver under the age of 18, what is the maximum number of passengers you may transport?

choices.A: One passenger per vehicle
choices.B: Up to three passengers
choices.C: The number of passengers may not exceed the number of seat belts in the vehicle
choices.D: As many passengers as can fit safely in the back seat

en.explanation: If you are a driver under the age of 18, the number of passengers may not exceed the number of seat belts in the vehicle.

en.question: Hitting the instrument panel or windshield in a crash at 30 mph is comparable to what?

choices.A: Hitting the ground from the top of a three-story building
choices.B: Falling off a bicycle at 15 mph
choices.C: Hitting the ground from a one-story building
choices.D: Being tackled by a professional football player

en.explanation: The manual explains that hitting the vehicle's interior surfaces at 30 mph is like hitting the ground from the top of a three-story building.

en.question: How much greater are your chances of being killed if you are thrown from your vehicle during a crash?

choices.A: 5 times greater
choices.B: 10 times greater
choices.C: 25 times greater
choices.D: 50 times greater

en.explanation: Your chances of being killed are almost 25 times greater if you are thrown from your vehicle.

en.question: What is the penalty for a person under 16 years of age who uses a false identification card to buy alcohol?

choices.A: A $500 fine and immediate impoundment of their vehicle
choices.B: A driving suspension that starts on their 16th birthday
choices.C: They will not be able to take the driver's exam until their 21st birthday
choices.D: Mandatory attendance at an alcohol safety education class

en.explanation: People under 16 years of age who use a false identification card to buy alcohol will receive a driving suspension that starts on their 16th birthday.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense if a person under 21 years old consumes alcohol, but is not driving a motor vehicle?

choices.A: A 90-day driver license suspension and up to a $500 fine
choices.B: A 6-month probation
choices.C: Sentence to a corrections institution
choices.D: Points on the driving record

en.explanation: If a person under 21 years old consumes alcohol, but is not driving a motor vehicle, the penalty for a first offense is a 90-day driver license suspension and up to a $500 fine.

en.question: Is parental consent required for police to conduct breath, blood, and urine tests on a minor?

choices.A: Yes, from both parents
choices.B: Yes, from at least one parent
choices.C: Yes, for people under 16 years old
choices.D: No, it is not required

en.explanation: Parental consent to conduct breath, blood, and urine tests is not required.

en.question: If you are under age 21 and are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol for the first time, how long will your license be suspended?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: If you are under age 21 and are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, you will receive a 1-year license suspension for a first offense.

en.question: Which of the following out-of-state offenses will be treated as though it occurred in Pennsylvania and result in appropriate sanctions?

choices.A: A minor parking violation
choices.B: Driving 5 mph over the speed limit
choices.C: Failure to stop and render aid in an accident resulting in death or injury
choices.D: Driving with an expired inspection sticker

en.explanation: Failure to stop and render aid in the event of a vehicle accident resulting in the death or personal injury of another is an offense that, if committed in a member state, is treated as though it occurred in Pennsylvania.

en.question: Under Pennsylvania law, how must children younger than age 2 be secured in a vehicle?

choices.A: In a forward-facing car seat in the front seat
choices.B: In a rear-facing car seat until they outgrow the manufacturer's limits
choices.C: In a booster seat with a lap and shoulder belt
choices.D: With a standard seat belt in the back seat

en.explanation: Children younger than age 2 must be secured in a rear-facing car seat until the child outgrows the maximum weight and height limits of the car seat as designated by the manufacturer.

en.question: Why should you never install a rear-facing child safety seat in the front seat if an air bag is present?

choices.A: The air bag will hit the back of the child seat with tremendous force, causing severe injury or death.
choices.B: It blocks the driver's view of the right side mirror.
choices.C: The child will be distracted by the dashboard lights.
choices.D: The seat belt in the front seat is not long enough to secure the child seat.

en.explanation: In a crash, the air bag will hit the back of the child seat with tremendous force, which will be transmitted to the infant's head causing severe injury or death.

en.question: If the outside temperature is in the low 80s Fahrenheit, how quickly can the temperature inside a vehicle reach deadly levels?

choices.A: 10 minutes
choices.B: 30 minutes
choices.C: 45 minutes
choices.D: 1 hour

en.explanation: Even with a window rolled down two inches, if the outside temperature is in the low 80s Fahrenheit, the temperature inside a vehicle can reach deadly levels in only 10 minutes.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended tip to avoid tragically leaving a child in a hot vehicle?

choices.A: Roll the windows down at least two inches before leaving the vehicle.
choices.B: Place your purse, briefcase, or cell phone in the back seat.
choices.C: Leave the air conditioning running while you run errands.
choices.D: Keep a stuffed animal in the front seat at all times.

en.explanation: The manual recommends placing your purse, briefcase, cell phone, or something you will need in the back seat so you will be sure to see a child left in the vehicle.

en.question: How can thick winter coats affect the safety of a child's car seat?

choices.A: They make the child too warm, causing drowsiness.
choices.B: They prevent the seat belt from locking during a sudden stop.
choices.C: They can compress in a crash, creating significant slack in the harness.
choices.D: They interfere with the vehicle's LATCH system.

en.explanation: Thicker winter coats can compress enough in a crash to create significant slack in the harness, which must be snug on the child's body to provide the best protection.

en.question: According to the Child Passenger Protection Act 229, children under the age of four must be:

choices.A: Buckled into a federally-approved child passenger restraint system.
choices.B: Secured in a booster seat with lap and shoulder belts.
choices.C: Placed in the front seat with the air bag disabled.
choices.D: Secured using only the vehicle's standard lap belt.

en.explanation: Children under the age of four (4) must be buckled into a federally-approved child passenger restraint system (child safety seat), no matter where they ride in the vehicle.

en.question: What type of restraint is required for children ages four and older, but under the age of eight?

choices.A: A rear-facing infant seat.
choices.B: A federally-approved child booster seat used with lap and shoulder belts.
choices.C: A standard lap belt without a shoulder strap.
choices.D: No special restraint is required if they sit in the back seat.

en.explanation: Children ages four (4) and older, but under the age of eight (8) must be buckled into a federally-approved child booster seat, which must be used in conjunction with lap and shoulder belts.

en.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that children under age 18 are properly buckled up in a vehicle?

choices.A: The children themselves
choices.B: The vehicle owner
choices.C: The driver
choices.D: The parents of the children, regardless of who is driving

en.explanation: Drivers are responsible for securing children into an approved child passenger restraint system and ensuring children under age 18 are buckled up.

en.question: To be safe in case the air bag deploys, how far away from the steering wheel should the driver sit?

choices.A: At least 5 inches
choices.B: At least 10 inches
choices.C: At least 15 inches
choices.D: At least 20 inches

en.explanation: To be safe, in case the air bag deploys, you should be at least 10 inches away from the steering wheel.

en.question: What is the recommended position for holding the steering wheel to prevent injury if the air bag deploys?

choices.A: 10 and 2 o'clock
choices.B: 9 and 3 o'clock or 8 and 4 o'clock
choices.C: 12 and 6 o'clock
choices.D: One hand at 12 o'clock

en.explanation: Hold the steering wheel at the 9 and 3 o'clock or 8 and 4 o'clock positions. This will keep your wrists and arms from being injured or broken or forcibly hitting you in the face, if the air bag deploys.

en.question: It is recommended that all children of what age ride in the rear seat of a vehicle?

choices.A: Ages 8 and under
choices.B: Ages 10 and under
choices.C: Ages 12 and under
choices.D: Ages 15 and under

en.explanation: It is recommended that all children ages 12 and under ride in the rear seat because most collisions are frontal collisions, and children tend to fidget and may get too close to the air bag compartment.

en.question: If you need a sign language interpreter for the Knowledge or Road Test, how far in advance should you contact PennDOT?

choices.A: At least 24 hours prior
choices.B: At least 3 days prior
choices.C: At least 1 week prior
choices.D: At least 2 weeks prior

en.explanation: Make your initial contact with PennDOT at least two (2) weeks prior to the time you want to take the test, and PennDOT will do its best to secure a person who signs in your preference.

en.question: What alternative testing method is offered at all Driver License Centers for people who have trouble reading the Knowledge Test?

choices.A: Take-home tests
choices.B: Open-book tests
choices.C: Voice tests
choices.D: Group testing

en.explanation: Upon request, voice tests are offered at all Driver License Centers across the commonwealth for people who may have trouble reading.

en.question: What is the penalty for unlawfully parking in a designated parking area for persons with disabilities?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense.
choices.B: A fine between $50 and $200 and the vehicle may be towed.
choices.C: A fine of $300 and a 30-day license suspension.
choices.D: 3 points added to your driving record.

en.explanation: Any vehicle unlawfully parked in a parking area for disabled persons may be removed from that area by towing... Individuals convicted of this offense will be fined between $50 and $200.

en.question: Under Pennsylvania's anti-littering law, what is the maximum fine upon conviction for dropping waste from a vehicle?
en.explanation: A violation of this law, including any violation resulting from the conduct of any other persons present within any vehicle of which you are the driver, may result in a fine of up to $300 upon conviction.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a littering conviction, including violations resulting from the conduct of passengers in your vehicle?
en.explanation: A violation of the littering law, including conduct of any other persons present within the vehicle, may result in a fine of up to $300 upon conviction.

en.question: How often must your vehicle undergo a safety inspection at an authorized inspection station?

choices.A: Every 6 months
choices.B: Every 12 months
choices.C: Every 2 years
choices.D: Every 3 years

en.explanation: Your vehicle must have a safety inspection at an authorized inspection station every 12 months.

en.question: If a police officer notices faulty equipment on your vehicle, how many days do you have to fix it to avoid a citation?

choices.A: 3 days
choices.B: 5 days
choices.C: 10 days
choices.D: 15 days

en.explanation: If a police officer notices faulty equipment on your vehicle, you may be required to fix it within five (5) days to avoid a citation.

en.question: When passing a bicyclist, what is the minimum distance you must allow between your vehicle and the bicycle?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 6 feet

en.explanation: When passing, you must allow at least four (4) feet between your vehicle and a bicycle in order to pass safely.

en.question: Are you permitted to cross a center double yellow line to pass a bicyclist?

choices.A: No, it is always illegal to cross a double yellow line.
choices.B: Yes, but only if the bicyclist signals you to pass.
choices.C: Yes, if necessary and you can do it safely to maintain four feet of clearance.
choices.D: No, unless you are driving an emergency vehicle.

en.explanation: If necessary and if you can do it safely, you are permitted to cross the center double yellow line so you can maintain the four (4) feet of clearance between your vehicle and the bicycle.

en.question: Can a bicyclist be cited for traveling at less than the posted minimum speed limit?

choices.A: Yes, they must maintain the minimum speed limit.
choices.B: Yes, if they are impeding traffic.
choices.C: No, they may travel at less than the posted minimum speed and may not be cited for impeding traffic.
choices.D: No, but they must ride on the shoulder if they are traveling below the speed limit.

en.explanation: Bicyclists are considered to be vehicle operators and are expected to obey all traffic laws; however, they may travel at less than the posted minimum speed and may not be cited for impeding traffic.

en.question: What is the fine for a conviction under Pennsylvania's Anti-Texting Law?
en.explanation: Violating the Anti-Texting law is a primary, summary offense with convictions carrying a $50 fine.

en.question: Under the Anti-Texting Law, which of the following actions is a police officer authorized to take?

choices.A: Seize the driver's mobile device as evidence.
choices.B: Issue a citation for using a physically integrated GPS device.
choices.C: Issue a citation for texting, but they cannot seize the interactive wireless device.
choices.D: Enforce local ordinances that restrict device use more strictly than state law.

en.explanation: The law does not authorize the seizure of an Interactive Wireless Communication Device (IWCD). It also exempts GPS devices and preempts local ordinances.

en.question: What is the penalty for driving around signs closing a road due to hazardous conditions if emergency responders are called out because of your actions?

choices.A: A $250 fine and 2 points on your record.
choices.B: A fine up to $500 and liability for emergency response costs.
choices.C: A $50 fine and a 30-day license suspension.
choices.D: A $300 fine and 4 points on your record.

en.explanation: If emergency responders are called out because of your actions, the fine is increased to up to $500 and you will be held liable for repaying the emergency response costs.

en.question: What is the "Dutch Reach" method designed to prevent?

choices.A: Carbon monoxide poisoning in enclosed garages.
choices.B: Hitting an approaching bicyclist with an opening vehicle door.
choices.C: Skidding on flooded roadways.
choices.D: Texting while driving.

en.explanation: The "Dutch Reach" method involves opening the door with your far hand. It forces your body to turn, which will better allow you to see approaching bicyclists and prevents the door from opening too fast.

en.question: How far should bicyclists ride from parked cars to avoid getting hit by opening vehicle doors?

choices.A: At least one foot
choices.B: At least two feet
choices.C: At least three feet
choices.D: At least four feet

en.explanation: Bicyclists should ride at least three feet from parked cars to avoid doors, both on streets with and without bike lanes.

en.question: If you are under 18 years of age, how long must you wait after receiving your learner's permit before you can take your Road Test?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: If you are under 18 years of age, you may not take your Road Test for six (6) months after you have received your learner’s permit.

en.question: What is the recommended way to use the 511PA information service while traveling?

choices.A: Call 511 while driving on the interstate.
choices.B: Text 511 while stopped at a red light.
choices.C: Safely pull off the road to call the system or check before heading out.
choices.D: Use a hands-free device to browse the 511PA website while driving.

en.explanation: PennDOT encourages motorists to not call 511PA while driving. Callers should safely pull off the road to call the system, or check for travel delays before heading out.

en.question: Which of the following is a symptom of carbon monoxide exposure?

choices.A: Extreme hunger
choices.B: Nausea and/or vomiting
choices.C: Improved night vision
choices.D: Decreased heart rate

en.explanation: Symptoms of carbon monoxide exposure include fatigue, dizziness, headache, nausea and/or vomiting, rapid heart rate, irregular breathing, confusion, coughing, and chest pain.

en.question: What should you do to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning on snowy days?

choices.A: Warm up your vehicle in the garage with the door closed.
choices.B: Inspect your tail pipe and remove any snow or ice obstructing it.
choices.C: Keep all windows tightly rolled up while idling in traffic.
choices.D: Turn on your vehicle's air conditioning system to the maximum setting.

en.explanation: On snowy days, always inspect your tail pipe and remove any snow or ice that might be obstructing your vehicle’s tail pipe to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

en.question: What should you do to help prevent carbon monoxide poisoning if you are stuck in traffic in an idling vehicle?

choices.A: Turn on the vehicle's heater to the highest setting
choices.B: Partially open a window
choices.C: Keep all windows completely closed
choices.D: Turn on the interior dome light

en.explanation: The manual states that if you are stuck in traffic or otherwise sitting in an idling vehicle, you should make sure to partially open a window to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

en.question: When does the manual recommend checking or replacing the batteries in your vehicle's carbon monoxide detector?

choices.A: Every time you get an oil change
choices.B: Once a month during the winter
choices.C: When changing the time on clocks in the spring and fall
choices.D: Every 5,000 miles

en.explanation: The manual recommends considering installing a battery-operated carbon monoxide detector and checking or replacing the batteries when changing the time on clocks in spring and fall each year.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning in your vehicle?

choices.A: Drive to the nearest hospital immediately
choices.B: Turn off the engine and wait inside the vehicle
choices.C: Roll down the windows and continue driving
choices.D: Exit the vehicle immediately and get fresh air

en.explanation: If you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning in your vehicle, the manual instructs you to exit the vehicle immediately, get fresh air, and seek emergency medical attention right away.

en.question: To prevent dangerous exhaust fumes from entering your vehicle, you should ensure there are no obstructions in your:

choices.A: Air conditioning vents
choices.B: Tail pipe
choices.C: Radiator grill
choices.D: Glove compartment

en.explanation: The manual warns drivers to be aware of anything that might be obstructing the vehicle's tail pipe, which can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning.

choices.B: Agreeing to vehicle safety inspections

choices.A: Absolute Limit

choices.D: Armed Forces Seal

choices.A: Ramp Metering
choices.B: Flashing Yellow Arrows

choices.D: Lane Use Control

en.explanation: The manual covers "Ramp Metering" under the Traffic Signals section to manage highway entry.

choices.A: Speed traps

choices.D: Weigh stations

en.explanation: The manual details the "Obedience to Traffic-Control Devices Warning of Hazardous Conditions Law."

en.question: Which of the following sudden winter weather events is specifically addressed in the visibility conditions section of the manual?

choices.A: Hail storm
