en.question: What is required if an applicant provides a copy of a court document for a divorce decree as proof of a name change?

choices.A: A copied seal and signature are acceptable
choices.B: It must have an original signature/seal affixed to the copy
choices.C: Court documents cannot be used for name changes
choices.D: It must be accompanied by a birth certificate

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'Copy of court document with an original signature/seal that is affixed to copy is acceptable. Copy of court document with copied seal/ signature is not acceptable.'

en.question: Which of the following applicants is required to provide proof of Tennessee residency?

choices.A: Only ORIGINAL applicants for a first time ID
choices.B: Only NEW RESIDENT applicants
choices.C: ORIGINAL, NEW RESIDENT, and RETURNING RESIDENT applicants
choices.D: Applicants for DUPLICATES of an existing Tennessee DL

en.explanation: The Driver License Examiner will require proof of Tennessee residency for ORIGINAL applicants, NEW RESIDENT applicants, and RETURNING RESIDENT applicants.

en.question: If an applicant is a minor and uses a residency document in the name of a parent or legal guardian, what else is required?

choices.A: A letter from the minor's school
choices.B: Proof of relationship
choices.C: A notarized statement from a neighbor
choices.D: The minor's Social Security card

en.explanation: The manual states that if the applicant is a minor, the name of a parent or legal guardian can be used, but '(proof of relationship will be required if this type of proof is used)'.

en.question: If you have never been issued a Social Security Number, what must you do to process your driver license application?

choices.A: Provide a letter from your employer
choices.B: Apply online and check the 'No SSN' box
choices.C: Appear in person and sign a sworn affidavit
choices.D: Bring a passport and a birth certificate

en.explanation: Applicants who have never been issued a Social Security number must appear in person and sign a sworn affidavit to that effect in the presence of a Driver License Examiner or Notary Public.

en.question: As of January 1, 2016, how often do Tennessee driver licenses expire for persons over the age of 21?

choices.A: Every 4 years on your birthday
choices.B: Every 5 years from the date of issuance
choices.C: Every 8 years from the date of issuance
choices.D: Every 10 years on your birthday

en.explanation: As of January 1, 2016, Tennessee licenses for persons over the age of 21 expire every eight years from the date of issuance.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT an accepted method of payment at Tennessee Driver Service Centers?

choices.A: Cash
choices.B: American Express Credit Cards
choices.C: MasterCard
choices.D: Money Order

en.explanation: Accepted methods of payment at Driver Service Centers are Cash, Check, Money Order, MasterCard, Visa and Discover Credit Cards. American Express is not listed.

en.question: How many days do new residents holding an out-of-state driver license have to obtain a Tennessee driver license after establishing residency?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: New residents or those returning to Tennessee and holding a driver license from another state, must obtain a Tennessee driver license no later than thirty (30) days after establishing residency.

en.question: What test is required for ALL new or returning residents obtaining a Tennessee driver license?

choices.A: A vision screening
choices.B: A road skills test
choices.C: A written knowledge exam
choices.D: A physical medical exam

en.explanation: All new or returning residents must take a Tennessee vision screening at the Driver Service Center.

en.question: If a new resident's out-of-state license has been expired for more than six months, which tests must they take?

choices.A: Only a vision screening
choices.B: Vision screening and knowledge exam
choices.C: Knowledge exam and road skills test
choices.D: Knowledge exam, road skills test, and vision screening

en.explanation: New or returning residents whose out of state license has been expired for more than six months must take the Tennessee knowledge exam, road skills test, and vision screening.

en.question: When applying for a license, new residents must provide two proofs of Tennessee residency. Which of the following is a requirement for these documents?

choices.A: They must be photocopies
choices.B: They must be dated within the last 4 months
choices.C: They must use a P.O. Box address
choices.D: They must be dated within the last 12 months

en.explanation: Applicants must provide two Proofs of Tennessee Residency with their name and resident address - NO P.O. BOXES, and the documents must be current and dated within the last 4 months.

en.question: Under what condition does a valid Tennessee driver license remain valid indefinitely for a person in the United States Armed Forces?

choices.A: If they are a member of the National Guard
choices.B: If they are on active duty and based outside the State of Tennessee
choices.C: If they are a family member of military personnel
choices.D: If they are stationed at a base within Tennessee

en.explanation: The license remains valid regardless of the displayed expiration date as long as the person remains on active duty, is based outside the State of Tennessee, and the license is not surrendered, canceled or suspended.

en.question: After being discharged from the Armed Forces or reassigned to a duty station within Tennessee, how many days does a person have to renew their driver license?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: Once the person has been discharged or separated from such services or has been reassigned to a duty station within the state, he or she must renew his/her license within sixty (60) days following the date of separation.

en.question: If a Temporary Driver License (TDL) is lost or stolen, how can it be replaced?

choices.A: By applying online through the state website
choices.B: By mailing a request to the Department of Safety
choices.C: By applying in person at a driver license service center
choices.D: By calling the toll-free replacement hotline

en.explanation: Temporary Driver Licenses and Temporary Identification Licenses cannot be replaced online. If you must apply in person, you will need to present proper identification.

en.question: If you were issued a Tennessee driver license after January 1, 2001, what must you do at the time of your FIRST renewal?

choices.A: Renew online to verify your identity
choices.B: Provide documentation that you are a U.S. Citizen or lawful permanent resident at a Driver Service Center
choices.C: Retake the written knowledge exam
choices.D: Mail a photocopy of your birth certificate to the Department of Safety

en.explanation: Tennessee law requires anyone issued a license after January 1, 2001 to provide documentation that you are a United States Citizen or a lawful permanent resident at the time of your first renewal. You may not renew by mail or internet and must visit a Driver Service Center.

en.question: What is required of new residents from other countries when applying for a Tennessee driver license?

choices.A: They must surrender their foreign license
choices.B: They are only required to take a vision screening
choices.C: They must take a vision screening, knowledge exam, and road skills test
choices.D: They must wait six months before applying

en.explanation: New residents from other countries are required to take the following tests: vision screening, knowledge exam, and road skills test. They will be allowed to keep the license issued by that country.

en.question: What is the rule regarding the physical condition of documents presented for proof of identity and residency?

choices.A: High-quality photocopies are preferred
choices.B: Items must be original documents; no photocopies will be accepted
choices.C: Digital copies on a smartphone are acceptable
choices.D: Notarized photocopies are required for all secondary proofs

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Items must be original documents. No photocopies will be accepted!'

en.question: What is the late fee if your driver license has been expired for more than thirty (30) calendar days but less than six months?
en.explanation: According to the manual, if your license has expired more than thirty (30) calendar days, there will be a five-dollar ($5.00) late fee. After six months, the fee doubles to $10.00.

en.question: If you let five (5) years go by without renewing your driver license, what must you do to renew it?

choices.A: Pay a $50 late fee
choices.B: Pass the vision screening, knowledge, and skills test
choices.C: Take an approved driver education course
choices.D: Wait 180 days before applying for a new license

en.explanation: If you let five (5) years go by without renewing, not only will you have to pay the $10.00 late fee, you will also have to pass the vision screening, knowledge, and skills test.

en.question: By state law, how many days do you have to notify the Department of Safety if your residence address changes?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: If your residence address changes, you are required by state law to notify the Department of Safety within ten (10) days of this change.

en.question: When giving the Department of Safety your new address, which of the following is NOT accepted by itself as a residential address?

choices.A: A house number and street
choices.B: An apartment number and road
choices.C: A post office box
choices.D: A highway number and city

en.explanation: By law, your license must show your legal residential address. A post office box alone will not be accepted as a residential address.

en.question: Who is exempt from participating in the Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program?

choices.A: Anyone who is 16 years old and has a job
choices.B: Persons under 18 who have graduated high school or received their GED
choices.C: Anyone who has held an out-of-state permit for 90 days
choices.D: Persons who are 17 years old and have completed driver's education

en.explanation: The GDL law does not apply to anyone age 18 or older or to those persons under 18 who have graduated high school or received a GED.

en.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a Learner Permit in Tennessee?

choices.A: 14 years old
choices.B: 15 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 17 years old

en.explanation: To obtain a Learner Permit, you must be 15 years old and pass the standard written exams and vision screening.

en.question: Between what hours is a person holding a Learner Permit prohibited from driving?

choices.A: 8 P.M. and 6 A.M.
choices.B: 9 P.M. and 5 A.M.
choices.C: 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.
choices.D: 11 P.M. and 7 A.M.

en.explanation: Drivers holding a Learner Permit may not drive between the hours of 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.

en.question: When driving with a Learner Permit, you must be accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least:

choices.A: 18 years old and riding in the front seat
choices.B: 21 years old and riding in the front seat
choices.C: 21 years old and riding anywhere in the vehicle
choices.D: 25 years old and riding in the front seat

en.explanation: You may drive a car only when accompanied by a licensed driver 21 years or older who is riding in the front seat of the vehicle.

en.question: To obtain an Intermediate Restricted License, you must have verification of how many hours of driving experience?

choices.A: 30 hours (5 at night)
choices.B: 40 hours (10 at night)
choices.C: 50 hours (10 at night)
choices.D: 60 hours (15 at night)

en.explanation: You must have verification from a parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor stating you have completed fifty hours (ten hours at night) of driving experience.

en.question: To apply for the Intermediate Unrestricted License, you must be at least 17 years old and have held an Intermediate Restricted License for:

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: 180 days
choices.C: 1 year
choices.D: 2 years

en.explanation: To apply for the Intermediate Unrestricted from the Intermediate Restricted License, you must be 17 years old and have held an Intermediate Restricted License for 1 year.

en.question: Which of the following will prevent you from moving from an Intermediate Restricted to an Intermediate Unrestricted License?

choices.A: Having 1 safety belt violation
choices.B: Accumulating 4 points on your driving record
choices.C: Having a traffic accident that was your fault
choices.D: Failing to take an additional written test

en.explanation: To move to the Intermediate Unrestricted License, you cannot have had a traffic accident that was your fault. (You also cannot have 2 safety belt violations, or more than 6 points, and no additional tests are required).

en.question: Effective July 1, 2018, all licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age are printed in what format?

choices.A: Horizontal format
choices.B: Vertical format
choices.C: Square format
choices.D: Holographic format

en.explanation: Effective July 1, 2018 all licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age are in a vertical format.

en.question: What is the grace period for driving a vehicle after your driver license expires?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: There is no grace period

en.explanation: These are no 'grace periods.' When your license expires, you are no longer entitled to drive a vehicle or motorcycle.

en.question: If you are 15 years old and have a valid permit from your previous state, how can that out-of-state permit time count toward your 180-day Tennessee requirement?

choices.A: You must provide a certified driving record from your previous state issued within 30 days of application
choices.B: You must take a new road test immediately
choices.C: You must have your previous state's governor sign a waiver
choices.D: Out-of-state permit time cannot be counted under any circumstances

en.explanation: The length of time that you held the permit in your previous state may be included in the 180-day period as long as you can provide a certified driving record from your previous state issued within the thirty (30) days immediately preceding the date of the Tennessee application.

en.question: Under the Federal Driver Privacy Protection Act (DPPA), the Department of Safety will not release your personal information for a mailing list without:

choices.A: A court order
choices.B: Your express consent
choices.C: A background check
choices.D: A $10 processing fee

en.explanation: The Federal Driver Privacy Protection Act (DPPA) prohibits the dissemination or disclosure of personal information from a motor vehicle record without the 'express consent' of that driver.

en.question: If a new resident under 18 is providing a certified driving record from their previous state, within how many days of the Tennessee application must it be issued?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: The certified driving record must be issued within the thirty (30) days immediately preceding the date of the Tennessee application.

en.question: Which of the following license levels does NOT require the driver to carry a Restriction Card?

choices.A: Learner Permit
choices.B: Intermediate Restricted Class D
choices.C: Intermediate Unrestricted Class D
choices.D: Both Learner Permit and Intermediate Restricted

en.explanation: A driver with the second level Intermediate Unrestricted (IU) Class D does not have any restrictions on driving. Therefore there is no restriction card for this license level.

en.question: What is the penalty if a teen with an Intermediate Restricted license is convicted of forging a letter of parental approval?

choices.A: 90 days added to the Intermediate Restricted period
choices.B: Revocation of the license and re-issuance of a Learner Permit until age 18
choices.C: Completion of a certified driver education course
choices.D: A 6-month suspension of all driving privileges

en.explanation: According to the GDL Penalties table, a forged letter of parental approval after an Intermediate Restricted license is issued results in the revocation of the Intermediate Restricted and re-issuance of a Learner Permit only until the teen reaches the age of 18.

en.question: What penalty applies to a driver holding an Intermediate Restricted license who is convicted of a 2nd moving violation?

choices.A: They must maintain a Learner Permit until age 18
choices.B: 90 days are added to their Intermediate Restricted period
choices.C: They must complete a certified driver education course
choices.D: Their license is suspended for 180 days

en.explanation: The GDL Penalties table states that a conviction of a 2nd moving violation after an Intermediate Restricted license is issued requires the completion of a certified driver education course.

en.question: What responsibility does an adult assume when they sign a Minor/Teenage Affidavit and Cancellation form for an applicant under eighteen?

choices.A: They must ride in the passenger seat at all times
choices.B: They assume financial responsibility for the minor driver
choices.C: They must pay for the minor's vehicle registration
choices.D: They are required to log 50 hours of driving time with the minor

en.explanation: The Minor/Teenage Affidavit confirms that the adult signing the form joins in the application for the license and will be responsible for the actions of the minor driver. This includes assuming financial responsibility.

en.question: If a minor applies for an additional class of license, such as a motorcycle license, what is required from the parents or legal guardian?

choices.A: They must sign a second teenage affidavit for that license type
choices.B: They must pay a double application fee
choices.C: They must take a motorcycle safety course with the minor
choices.D: No additional documentation is required

en.explanation: If a minor applies for an additional class of license (such as motorcycle), the parents or legal guardian will be required to sign a second teenage affidavit for that license type.

en.question: How long is the Certificate of Compulsory School Attendance (Form SF1010) valid after being signed by a school official during the regular school year?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 14 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: The applicant must take the original, completed form to the Driver Service Center. This form is only valid for thirty (30) days from the date of signing by the school official.

en.question: If a Certificate of Compulsory School Attendance (Form SF1010) is signed within the last 30 days of the school year, how long is it accepted?

choices.A: Only until the last day of the school year
choices.B: Throughout the summer until 30 days after the start of the following school year
choices.C: For exactly 90 days from the date of signing
choices.D: Until the student's 18th birthday

en.explanation: During the traditional summer vacation months, a properly completed SF1010 form signed within the last 30 days of the school year will be accepted throughout the summer until 30 days after the start of the following school year.

en.question: Which of the following documents is NOT acceptable as proof of compliance with the school attendance law for a minor applying for a license?

choices.A: An original high school diploma
choices.B: A Certificate of Compulsory School Attendance (Form SF1010)
choices.C: Grade cards or school transcripts
choices.D: A letter from the local director of schools for home-schooled applicants

en.explanation: Grade cards or school transcripts are not acceptable as proof of compliance with this law. Due to the various grading scales... Driver License personnel are not authorized to interpret the information in these documents.

en.question: What happens to the driving privileges of a student fifteen years old or older who drops out of school?

choices.A: They are restricted to driving only to and from work
choices.B: The Department of Safety suspends the student's driving privileges
choices.C: They must pay a fine to keep their license
choices.D: They are downgraded to a Learner Permit

en.explanation: If a student fifteen years old or older drops out of school, the school is required to notify the Department of Safety which suspends the student’s driving privileges.

en.question: What type of license may be issued to an applicant under age 18 upon graduating from high school or receiving a GED?

choices.A: A Learner Permit only
choices.B: An Intermediate Restricted license
choices.C: A regular Class D operator's license
choices.D: A Hardship license

en.explanation: Upon graduating from high school or after receiving a GED before age 18, a regular Class D operator’s license may be issued.

en.question: If a 16-year-old applicant held an out-of-state license for less than 90 days, what combined period must they have held a valid learner permit and/or license to get an Intermediate Restricted License?

choices.A: At least 60 days
choices.B: At least 90 days
choices.C: At least 180 days
choices.D: At least 365 days

en.explanation: If the applicant had an out-of-state license for LESS than 90 days, the driving record must confirm that a valid learner permit and/or license class has been held for a combined period of at least 180 days.

en.question: If a teen with a Learner Permit accumulates six or more points on their driving record, what is the penalty?

choices.A: They must hold the permit until they maintain a record with less than 6 points for 180 consecutive days
choices.B: Their permit is revoked until age 18
choices.C: They must complete a certified driver education course
choices.D: They are immediately issued an Intermediate Restricted license

en.explanation: According to the GDL Penalties table, accumulating six or more points after a Learner Permit is issued requires the applicant to continue to hold the learner permit for an additional time period until they are able to maintain a record with less than 6 points for 180 consecutive days.

en.question: What happens if a teen commits a 2nd seatbelt violation during their Intermediate Restricted period, but the Department of Safety is not notified until after they are issued an Intermediate Unrestricted license?

choices.A: The violation is forgiven and no penalty applies
choices.B: The teen's license is permanently revoked
choices.C: The teen will be dropped back to an Intermediate Restricted license for 90 days
choices.D: The teen must pay a $500 fine

en.explanation: If any of the violations listed... occurred during the time the teen had an Intermediate Restricted license, but the DOS did not receive notice... until after we had already issued the teen an Intermediate Unrestricted license... The teen will be 'dropped back' to an Intermediate Restricted license for 90 days.

en.question: What happens the second time a student drops out of school?

choices.A: They must pay a $50 fine.
choices.B: They must wait until they turn 18 to apply for a license again.
choices.C: They must wait 6 months to reapply.
choices.D: They permanently lose their driving privileges.

en.explanation: According to the manual, the second time a student drops out, he or she must wait to turn eighteen (18) years old before being eligible to apply for a license again.

en.question: What is the reinstatement fee for a student who dropped out but returns to school to regain their driving privileges?
en.explanation: The manual states that a student returning to school will be required to pay a $20 reinstatement fee, in addition to the appropriate application and license fees.

en.question: What is a consequence for a learner permit holder caught using a cell phone while driving?

choices.A: A 180-day suspension of their permit
choices.B: 6 points added to their driving record
choices.C: A $100 fine
choices.D: Immediate revocation of their permit until age 18

en.explanation: The consequences of conviction for a teen using a cell phone while driving include a Class C misdemeanor, a $50 fine, 6 points added to a minor's driving record, and a 90-day delay in eligibility for an Intermediate Restricted Driver License.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a texting while driving violation?
en.explanation: Violations for texting while driving can result in a fine not to exceed Fifty Dollars ($50) and court costs not to exceed Ten Dollars.

en.question: According to the manual, what causes most work zone accidents?

choices.A: Speeding
choices.B: Head-on collisions
choices.C: Rear-end collisions
choices.D: Distracted driving

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states under work zone safety tips: "Don't tailgate! Most work zone accidents are caused by rear-end collisions."

en.question: What should you do with your vehicle's headlights when approaching a work zone?

choices.A: Turn them off to avoid blinding workers
choices.B: Flash them to alert workers of your presence
choices.C: Turn them on only if it is raining
choices.D: Turn them on before you enter the zone

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to "Turn your lights on before you enter the zone! Turn on your vehicle's headlights to become more visible to workers and other motorists."

en.question: What are the driving hour restrictions for a learner permit holder under the age of 18?

choices.A: Prohibited from driving between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.B: Prohibited from driving between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.C: Prohibited from driving between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
choices.D: Prohibited from driving between midnight and 6 a.m.

en.explanation: Anyone under the age of 18 who has a learner permit is prohibited from driving between the hours of 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

en.question: How long must a teen under 18 hold a learner permit before applying for an Intermediate Restricted license?

choices.A: A minimum of 3 months
choices.B: A minimum of 6 months
choices.C: A minimum of 9 months
choices.D: A minimum of 1 year

en.explanation: Anyone under the age of 18 must have their learner permit for a minimum of six months before applying for an intermediate restricted license.

en.question: If a learner permit holder accumulates 6 or more points on their driving record, what must happen before they can apply for an Intermediate Restricted license?

choices.A: They must pay a $50 reinstatement fee.
choices.B: They must complete a defensive driving course.
choices.C: They must maintain a record with less than 6 points for 180 consecutive days.
choices.D: They must wait until they turn 18.

en.explanation: If someone with a learner permit has driving offenses adding up to 6 or more points, they must continue to hold the learner permit until their record has less than 6 points for a full 180 consecutive days.

en.question: How many passengers is an Intermediate Restricted License holder allowed to have in the vehicle without any qualifying exceptions?

choices.A: Zero
choices.B: One
choices.C: Two
choices.D: Three

en.explanation: Those with an intermediate license can only have 1 other passenger in the vehicle, unless specific exceptions are met (such as a passenger 21 or older with an unrestricted license, or siblings with a parent's letter).

en.question: Between what hours is an Intermediate Restricted License holder generally prohibited from driving?

choices.A: 9 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.B: 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.C: 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.
choices.D: Midnight and 5 a.m.

en.explanation: Those with an Intermediate Restricted License are prohibited from driving between the hours of 11 p.m. and 6 a.m., unless they meet specific exemption circumstances.

en.question: What is the penalty for an Intermediate Restricted License holder caught with a forged letter giving permission to drive outside allowed hours?

choices.A: A $50 fine and 6 points on their record
choices.B: License revocation and reissuance of a learner permit until age 18
choices.C: A 90-day suspension of their license
choices.D: Immediate vehicle impoundment

en.explanation: A driver with an Intermediate Restricted License who is convicted of having a forged or fraudulent letter will have his/her Intermediate Restricted License revoked and will only be reissued a learner permit until he/she reaches the age of 18.

en.question: How long must an Intermediate Restricted License be held before applying for an unrestricted Intermediate license?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 18 months
choices.D: 2 years

en.explanation: Teens must hold their Intermediate Restricted License for a minimum of one year before they can apply for an unrestricted Intermediate license.

en.question: Who makes up four out of five deaths in highway work zones?

choices.A: Construction workers
choices.B: Pedestrians
choices.C: Drivers
choices.D: Flaggers

en.explanation: According to the manual, statistics show that drivers comprise four out of five deaths in highway work zones.

en.question: An Intermediate Restricted License holder may drive between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. if they are:

choices.A: Driving to or from a friend's house
choices.B: Driving to or from hunting or fishing and possess a valid hunting or fishing license
choices.C: Driving to a gym or fitness center
choices.D: Accompanied by a sibling who is at least 18 years old

en.explanation: An exception to the 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew is if the driver is driving to or from hunting or fishing between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. and has in their possession a valid hunting or fishing license.

en.question: Which of the following will cause a 90-day delay in becoming eligible for an Unrestricted Intermediate License?

choices.A: Receiving 4 points on your driving record
choices.B: Being convicted of a first seatbelt violation
choices.C: Contributing to a traffic crash
choices.D: Driving after 10:00 PM

en.explanation: A teen driver will be ineligible for an Unrestricted Intermediate License for an additional 90 days if they have contributed to a traffic crash, received 6 or more points, or been convicted of a second seatbelt violation.

en.question: If a teen driver gets a second moving violation while holding an Intermediate Restricted Driver License, what must they do before receiving an Unrestricted license?

choices.A: Pay a $50 fine
choices.B: Wait an additional 6 months
choices.C: Complete an approved Driver Education class
choices.D: Retake the road skills test

en.explanation: If the teen driver gets a second moving violation while holding the Intermediate Restricted Driver License, an approved Driver Education class MUST BE COMPLETED before receiving an Intermediate Unrestricted Driver License.

en.question: What is the driving curfew for a teen holding a Learner Permit (Class PD)?

choices.A: Cannot drive between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM
choices.B: Cannot drive between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM
choices.C: Cannot drive between 11:00 PM and 6:00 AM
choices.D: Cannot drive between midnight and 6:00 AM

en.explanation: The restrictions for a Learner Permit (Class PD) state that the driver cannot drive between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM.

en.question: What is the mandatory waiting period after failing the knowledge test?

choices.A: There is no waiting period
choices.B: 1 day
choices.C: 7 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: A mandatory 1-day waiting period is required after failing the knowledge test.

en.question: What happens if an applicant is caught cheating on a required driver license examination?

choices.A: They receive a warning and must restart the test
choices.B: They fail automatically and cannot re-attempt the test for 7 days
choices.C: They fail automatically and cannot re-attempt the test for 30 days
choices.D: They are permanently banned from obtaining a driver license

en.explanation: Any form of cheating by an applicant on a required examination will result in an automatic failure and the applicant will not be allowed to re-attempt the test for 30 days.

en.question: What is the minimum vision requirement to pass the vision screening for a driver license?

choices.A: 20/20 vision in each eye
choices.B: 20/30 vision in each eye
choices.C: 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together
choices.D: 20/50 vision in at least one eye

en.explanation: An applicant is required to have at least 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together. This may be with or without glasses or contact lenses.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT permitted during the computerized knowledge test?

choices.A: Taking the test in Spanish
choices.B: Using a translation dictionary with no notes or handwriting
choices.C: Taking the test in Korean
choices.D: Using an electronic dictionary or smart phone

en.explanation: The use of Personal Digital Assistants (PDAs), Smart Phones, Electronic Dictionaries and other similar electronic devices are NOT allowed during testing.

en.question: What percentage of the knowledge test is dedicated to Drugs and alcohol?
en.explanation: The knowledge test consists of four areas, with Drugs and alcohol making up 25% of the exam.

en.question: What is the format of all driver licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age?

choices.A: Horizontal format
choices.B: Vertical format
choices.C: Square format
choices.D: Color-coded red format

en.explanation: Effective July 1, 2018 all licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age are in a vertical format.

en.question: Under what weather conditions are road tests NOT given?

choices.A: Light rain
choices.B: Overcast skies
choices.C: Extreme weather such as heavy rain, dense fog, or icy roads
choices.D: Temperatures below 40 degrees

en.explanation: Road tests are not given in extreme weather (heavy rain/snow, dense fog, hail, high winds, icy roads, etc.).

en.question: How many hours of behind-the-wheel experience must be certified to obtain an Intermediate Restricted license?

choices.A: 30 hours, including 5 at night
choices.B: 40 hours, including 10 at night
choices.C: 50 hours, including 10 at night
choices.D: 60 hours, including 15 at night

en.explanation: To obtain an Intermediate Restricted license, you must provide certification of 50 hours behind-the-wheel experience, including 10 hours at night.

en.question: If an applicant under age 18 requests an oral knowledge test due to a learning disability, what must they provide?

choices.A: A parent or legal guardian to read the test to them
choices.B: A written statement from a physician or educational specialist
choices.C: A certified sign language interpreter
choices.D: Proof of high school graduation

en.explanation: If the applicant requesting an oral test is under age eighteen (18), a written statement from a physician or educational specialist stating that the applicant has a medical condition or learning disability will be required before the test can be administered.

en.question: What is the minimum vision requirement for an applicant to be issued a driver's license or permit?

choices.A: 20/20 vision in each eye
choices.B: 20/30 vision in each eye
choices.C: 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together
choices.D: 20/50 vision in at least one eye

en.explanation: An applicant is required to have at least 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together, with or without glasses or contact lenses.

en.question: If you fail the driver license knowledge test, how long must you wait before you can attempt the examination again?

choices.A: You can retake it immediately
choices.B: A minimum of one day
choices.C: Seven days
choices.D: Thirty days

en.explanation: A mandatory 1-day waiting period is required after failing any driver license knowledge test before returning to attempt it again.

en.question: What will happen if you are more than 5 minutes late for your scheduled road skills test appointment?

choices.A: You will lose 5 points on your driving test
choices.B: The examiner will skip the pre-trip vehicle inspection
choices.C: You must pay a late fee before testing
choices.D: Your road skills test will be canceled and you will need to reschedule

en.explanation: If you are more than 5 minutes late for your appointment time, your road skills test will be canceled and you will need to reschedule for a later date.

en.question: Under which of the following weather conditions will a road test NOT be given?

choices.A: Light rain
choices.B: Moderate fog
choices.C: Light snow
choices.D: Heavy rain and thunderstorms

en.explanation: Road tests will NOT be given in heavy rain, thunderstorms, thick fog cover, when roads are flooded, covered/packed with snow and ice, or during severe weather warnings.

en.question: Any passenger motor vehicle manufactured or assembled in what year or later must be equipped with safety belts?
en.explanation: Any passenger motor vehicle manufactured or assembled in 1969 or later must be equipped with safety belts and must be in good usable condition.

en.question: How many white headlights is a motor vehicle permitted to have?

choices.A: Exactly two
choices.B: At least two but no more than four
choices.C: At least four
choices.D: One to four

en.explanation: Motor vehicles must be equipped with at least two headlights but no more than four white headlights.

en.question: For a passenger car, window tinting material must transmit at least what percentage of visible light?
en.explanation: For a passenger car, no material which transmits less than 35% of visible light may be attached to any window.

en.question: Passenger cars must have bumpers that are within what range of height from the ground?

choices.A: 10 to 15 inches
choices.B: 14 to 22 inches
choices.C: 14 to 31 inches
choices.D: 20 to 30 inches

en.explanation: Passenger cars must have bumpers which are within a range of 14 to 22 inches from the ground.

en.question: Who is allowed in the vehicle with you during your driving test?

choices.A: You, the examiner, and one parent or guardian
choices.B: Only you and the examiner (or other authorized personnel)
choices.C: You, the examiner, and a language translator
choices.D: You, the examiner, and your driving instructor

en.explanation: The only people allowed in the vehicle are you and the examiner (or other authorized personnel). No animal may be in the vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following actions will result in an immediate automatic failure of the road test?

choices.A: Asking the examiner to repeat a direction
choices.B: A violation of any traffic law
choices.C: Braking too hard at a stop sign
choices.D: Failing to defog the windshield before starting

en.explanation: The applicant will be failed immediately for any of the following: Violation of any traffic law, lack of cooperation, any dangerous action, or contributing to an accident.

en.question: According to the retesting guidelines, if you commit 7 to 9 errors on your skills test, how long is the mandatory practice period before you can retest?

choices.A: Next (1) Day
choices.B: Seven (7) Days
choices.C: Fourteen (14) Days
choices.D: Thirty (30) Days

en.explanation: According to the Guidelines for Retesting Table 4.2, committing 7 to 9 errors/points requires a mandatory practice time period until the Next (1) Day.

en.question: If you automatically fail the driving test or commit 16 or more errors, how long must you wait before you are allowed to retest?

choices.A: Next (1) Day
choices.B: Seven (7) Days
choices.C: Fourteen (14) Days
choices.D: Thirty (30) Days

en.explanation: According to Table 4.2, 16 or more errors/points OR an Automatic Failure requires a mandatory practice time period of Thirty (30) Days.

en.question: By law, all automobiles must have which two separate methods of applying brakes?

choices.A: Front brakes and rear brakes
choices.B: A regular foot brake and a parking brake
choices.C: Anti-lock brakes and standard brakes
choices.D: A hand brake and an engine brake

en.explanation: By law all automobiles must have two separate methods of applying brakes. They must have a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

en.question: How early should you plan to arrive at the Driver License Service Center prior to your scheduled road test appointment?

choices.A: At the exact appointment time
choices.B: At least 5 minutes prior
choices.C: At least 15 minutes prior
choices.D: At least 30 minutes prior

en.explanation: You should plan to arrive at the Driver License Service Center at least 15 minutes prior to your scheduled appointment time to allow for paperwork processing.

en.question: What is the rule regarding tinting material affixed to the windshield of a motor vehicle?

choices.A: It must transmit at least 35% of visible light
choices.B: It is allowed if it transmits 50% of visible light
choices.C: No tinting material may be affixed to the windshield
choices.D: It is allowed only on the top 4 inches of the windshield

en.explanation: The manual states: 'No tinting material may be affixed to the windshield of any motor vehicle.'

en.question: What is the mandatory practice time period before retesting if an applicant commits 16 or more errors or has an automatic failure on the skills test?

choices.A: Seven (7) Days
choices.B: Fourteen (14) Days
choices.C: Thirty (30) Days
choices.D: Ninety (90) Days

en.explanation: The manual states that 16 or more errors/points, or an automatic failure, requires a mandatory practice time period of Thirty (30) Days before a retest is allowed.

en.question: How early should you arrive before your scheduled Road Test appointment?

choices.A: At least 5 minutes
choices.B: At least 10 minutes
choices.C: At least 15 minutes
choices.D: At least 30 minutes

en.explanation: You should arrive at least 15 minutes before your scheduled Road Test appointment to allow time for application paperwork.

en.question: Your road test appointment will have to be rescheduled if you are late by at least how many minutes?

choices.A: 5 minutes
choices.B: 10 minutes
choices.C: 15 minutes
choices.D: 20 minutes

en.explanation: To ensure timely service, if you are five (5) or more minutes late for the start of your road test appointment, it will have to be rescheduled.

en.question: Teenagers between the ages of 15 to 17 can take their written knowledge test online under the supervision of a parent or legal guardian using which application?

choices.A: Tennessee Driver Portal App
choices.B: Tennessee Proctor Identification (PID) App
choices.C: TDOSHS Secure Test App
choices.D: Tennessee Teen Driver App

en.explanation: Teenagers ages 15 to 17 can take the written test online under a proctor's supervision via the Tennessee Proctor Identification (PID) App.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to drive with your seat in a reclined or semi-reclined position?

choices.A: It increases the risk of the seatbelt unlatching.
choices.B: It reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergency situations.
choices.C: It causes the steering wheel to lock.
choices.D: It prevents the airbags from deploying.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'DO NOT DRIVE WITH THE SEAT IN A RECLINED OR SEMI-RECLINED POSITION. This is dangerous and reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergency situations.'

en.question: To prevent serious head or neck injuries from an air bag deployment, your body should be positioned how far back from the steering wheel?

choices.A: 4 to 6 inches
choices.B: 6 to 8 inches
choices.C: 10 to 12 inches
choices.D: 15 to 18 inches

en.explanation: Your body should be about 10 to 12 inches back from the steering wheel. Sitting closer could result in serious head or neck injuries from an air bag hitting the chin or face.

en.question: When adjusting your seat and steering column, the top of the steering wheel should be no higher than:

choices.A: The top of your shoulders.
choices.B: Your chin.
choices.C: Your nose.
choices.D: The top of your head.

en.explanation: The manual states that the top of the steering wheel should be no higher than the top of the shoulders.

en.question: Properly adjusted seat head restraints should be set to a level even with the back of the head to prevent:

choices.A: Airbag injuries.
choices.B: Whiplash if hit from behind.
choices.C: Drowsiness while driving.
choices.D: Blind spots.

en.explanation: Properly adjust seat head restraints to a level even with the back of the head. Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.

en.question: When preparing to drive, when should you adjust your mirrors?

choices.A: Before adjusting your seat.
choices.B: After the seat is adjusted correctly.
choices.C: While driving at a low speed.
choices.D: Only after checking your blind spots.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to adjust mirrors after the seat is adjusted correctly, and always before driving.

en.question: To properly adjust the driver's side-view (left) mirror, you should place your head against the left side window and set the mirror so you can:

choices.A: See the entire rear bumper of your car.
choices.B: See the center console of your vehicle.
choices.C: Barely see the side of your car in the right side of the mirror.
choices.D: See the rear window completely framed.

en.explanation: To adjust the left side mirror, place your head against the left side window and set the mirror so you can just barely see the side of your car in the right side of the mirror.

en.question: How should you position your head to properly adjust the passenger's side-view (right) mirror?

choices.A: Against the left side window.
choices.B: Just above the center console.
choices.C: Against the passenger side window.
choices.D: Looking straight ahead at the windshield.

en.explanation: To adjust the passenger's side-view mirror, position your head so that it is just above the center console.

en.question: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, what must you always do before attempting to turn or change lanes?

choices.A: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
choices.B: Turn your head and check blind spots.
choices.C: Flash your headlights twice.
choices.D: Rely entirely on your rearview mirror.

en.explanation: Even properly positioned mirrors cannot eliminate all blind spots. Always turn your head and check blind spots when you want to turn or change lanes.

en.question: How should a lap belt be properly positioned on your body?

choices.A: Loosely across the stomach.
choices.B: Firmly across the hips.
choices.C: High on the abdomen.
choices.D: Across the upper thighs and knees.

en.explanation: Lap belts should be positioned firmly across the hips while the shoulder belt is firmly across the shoulder.

en.question: Before starting an automatic transmission vehicle, you should place your foot on the brake pedal and ensure the gearshift selector is in which position?

choices.A: NEUTRAL
choices.B: DRIVE
choices.C: PARK
choices.D: REVERSE

en.explanation: Place foot on brake pedal and ensure gearshift selector is in the PARK position for automatic transmissions or in NEUTRAL for manual/standard transmissions.

en.question: What position should the gearshift selector be in before starting an automatic transmission vehicle?

choices.A: DRIVE
choices.B: REVERSE
choices.C: NEUTRAL
choices.D: PARK

en.explanation: Before starting an automatic transmission vehicle, place your foot on the brake pedal and ensure the gearshift selector is in the PARK position.

en.question: In a vehicle with a manual transmission, what must be done before the vehicle will start?

choices.A: The clutch must be depressed.
choices.B: The gearshift must be in first gear.
choices.C: The accelerator must be pumped twice.
choices.D: The steering wheel must be locked.

en.explanation: In vehicles with manual transmissions, the clutch must be depressed before the vehicle will start.

en.question: How does turning on low-beam headlights during normal daylight affect your vehicle's visibility?

choices.A: It drains the battery and reduces visibility.
choices.B: It makes the vehicle visible at twice the distance.
choices.C: It makes the vehicle visible at three times the distance.
choices.D: It has no effect on visibility during daylight.

en.explanation: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.

en.question: When should the lower gears (indicated by "L", "2", or "1") on an automatic transmission generally be used?

choices.A: Emergency deceleration if there is a brake failure.
choices.B: When driving on interstates or expressways.
choices.C: When backing up in a straight line.
choices.D: For normal stop-and-go traffic.

en.explanation: Lower gears are generally not used except for special or emergency situations, such as emergency deceleration if there is a brake failure, driving down steep mountain grades, or slow speed driving on slippery roads.

en.question: When driving a standard transmission vehicle, when should you hold the clutch pedal all the way down?

choices.A: Whenever you are driving down a steep hill.
choices.B: When coasting to save gas.
choices.C: At all times while the vehicle is in motion.
choices.D: When your speed drops below 10 MPH as you are coming to a stop.

en.explanation: You should hold the clutch pedal all the way down when starting, shifting gears, and when speed drops below 10 MPH as you are coming to a stop.

en.question: What does the manual state about coasting with the gears in neutral?

choices.A: It is recommended for saving fuel.
choices.B: It is illegal.
choices.C: It should only be done on steep hills.
choices.D: It is the safest way to slow down.

en.explanation: The manual states: "Don’t coast with the gears in neutral (it’s illegal) or with the clutch pedal pushed down except when shifting gears."

en.question: What is the basic rule a driver must follow when operating a vehicle with a steering wheel interlock system?

choices.A: Always lock the steering wheel before turning the ignition off.
choices.B: Never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion.
choices.C: Never use the interlock system while parked on a hill.
choices.D: Always keep one hand on the interlock release button.

en.explanation: The basic rule is to never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion, because the steering wheel will lock and control of the vehicle will be lost.

en.question: Why should you avoid driving with your elbow or arm propped on the door or out the window?

choices.A: It causes the steering wheel to lock.
choices.B: It is illegal in the state of Tennessee.
choices.C: You won't have full control of the steering wheel and a sideswipe could take off your arm.
choices.D: It interferes with the deployment of the side airbags.

en.explanation: Don’t develop the habit of driving with your elbow or arm propped on the door or out the window. You won’t have full control of the steering wheel and a sideswipe could take off your arm.

en.question: What is the recommended hand placement on the steering wheel to avoid injury from air bag deployment?

choices.A: 10 o'clock and 2 o'clock
choices.B: 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock
choices.C: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
choices.D: 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock

en.explanation: Drivers should place the left hand at the 9 o’clock position and the right hand at 3 o’clock position on the steering wheel. This position helps avoid injury from air bag deployment during an accident.

en.question: Why is crossing your arms when steering or turning discouraged?

choices.A: It causes the vehicle to accelerate unintentionally.
choices.B: It is illegal and will result in a failed driving test.
choices.C: It prevents the driver from using the turn signals.
choices.D: It may cause clothing and jewelry to interfere with safe turning and worsen air bag injuries.

en.explanation: Do not cross your arms when steering or turning. Crossing arms may cause clothing and jewelry to interfere with safe turning, and you would suffer more serious injuries should the air bag deploy.

en.question: Why is the Push-Pull steering method recommended for normal everyday driving over the Hand-over-Hand method?

choices.A: It allows for quicker wheel movement in emergencies.
choices.B: It keeps both hands on the steering wheel through the entire maneuver.
choices.C: It requires less physical effort to turn the wheel.
choices.D: It is the only method that works with power steering.

en.explanation: The Push-Pull method is recommended because it slows down turning movements making for a smoother, safer turn. It also keeps both hands on the steering wheel through the entire maneuver.

en.question: What is the proper hand placement and posture when backing up a vehicle with an automatic transmission?

choices.A: Grasp the steering wheel at 12 o'clock with the left hand, turn to the right, and place the right arm over the back of the seat.
choices.B: Grasp the steering wheel at 9 and 3 o'clock and look in the rearview mirror.
choices.C: Grasp the steering wheel at 6 o'clock with the right hand and look out the driver's side window.
choices.D: Keep both hands on the wheel and rely entirely on the backup camera.

en.explanation: When backing, grasp the steering wheel at the 12 o’clock position with your left hand, turn to the right, place your right arm over the back of the seat, and look over your shoulder through the rear window.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding carbon monoxide gas from a car engine?

choices.A: It has a strong, distinct odor that warns drivers of a leak.
choices.B: It appears as a thick black smoke when leaking into the cabin.
choices.C: It is only dangerous if the vehicle is parked in a closed garage.
choices.D: It has no taste, no smell, and no visibility, but it can kill.

en.explanation: Carbon monoxide gas from a car engine can kill (it has no taste, no smell or visibility). It generally leaks when the car heater is running, when the exhaust system is not working properly, or in heavy traffic.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the most common type of accident recorded annually in Tennessee?

choices.A: Head-on collisions
choices.B: Sideswipe collisions
choices.C: Rear-end collisions
choices.D: Intersection T-bone collisions

en.explanation: Like most states, Tennessee reports that rear-end collisions are the most common type of accident recorded annually.

en.question: If you are stopping at a curb for proper parking, how close should you move to the curb?

choices.A: Within 6 inches
choices.B: Within 12 inches
choices.C: Within 18 inches
choices.D: Within 24 inches

en.explanation: If stopping at a curb, move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended way to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning in your vehicle?

choices.A: Keep the fresh-air vent open in congested traffic.
choices.B: Leave the engine running in a closed garage to warm it up.
choices.C: Do not use a heater or air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.
choices.D: Only check the exhaust system if you smell gas.

en.explanation: The manual states to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, you should 'Do not use a heater/air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.'

en.question: What are the characteristics of carbon monoxide gas?

choices.A: It has a strong, sweet smell.
choices.B: It appears as a thick, black smoke.
choices.C: It has no taste, no smell, and no visibility.
choices.D: It smells like rotten eggs.

en.explanation: According to the manual, carbon monoxide gas from a car engine can kill because 'it has not taste, no smell or visibility'.

en.question: Under the Hands Free Tennessee law implemented in 2019, which of the following actions is illegal for a driver?

choices.A: Using a hands-free navigation device.
choices.B: Reaching for a cellphone in a manner that requires the driver to no longer be properly restrained by a seat belt.
choices.C: Using a vehicle information system display.
choices.D: Looking at visual displays for the driver's view behind the vehicle.

en.explanation: Public Chapter No. 412 makes it illegal to 'reach for a cellphone or mobile device in a manner that requires the driver to no longer be in a seated driving position or properly restrained by a seat belt.'

en.question: What is the law regarding mobile phone use for drivers 18 years or older in a marked school zone when flashers are operating?

choices.A: All phone use is strictly prohibited, including hands-free.
choices.B: Hand-held phone use is an offense, but hands-free mode is allowed.
choices.C: Hand-held phone use is allowed if driving under 15 mph.
choices.D: Only texting is prohibited; hand-held phone calls are allowed.

en.explanation: The manual states it is an offense for persons 18 or older to use a hand-held mobile phone in a marked school zone with flashers operating, but 'There is an exception if the phone is being used in hands free mode.'

en.question: Which of the following video devices is permitted to be visible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion?

choices.A: A screen displaying a television broadcast.
choices.B: A monitor playing a recorded movie.
choices.C: A global positioning device (GPS).
choices.D: A tablet broadcasting a live video feed.

en.explanation: State law prohibits video monitors displaying TV or video signals visible to the driver, but 'A navigation or global positioning device... are not prohibited.'

en.question: According to Tennessee safety belt laws, who is required to wear a safety belt in the front seat of a moving vehicle?

choices.A: Only the driver.
choices.B: Only passengers under 18 years old.
choices.C: All drivers and all passengers in the front seat.
choices.D: Only the driver and passengers under 17 years old.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all passengers in the FRONT seat, any time the vehicle is in motion.'

en.question: In Tennessee, backseat passengers must wear a safety belt if they are:

choices.A: Under 17 years old.
choices.B: 18 years or older.
choices.C: Sitting behind the driver's seat.
choices.D: Riding in a vehicle manufactured after 2010.

en.explanation: Safety belts are required for BACKSEAT passengers 'If the passengers are under 17 years old.' This provision no longer applies when back seat passengers are 18 years or older.

en.question: What type of child restraint system is required for a child under one year old or weighing less than 20 pounds?

choices.A: A forward-facing car seat.
choices.B: A rear-facing car seat.
choices.C: A belt-positioning booster seat.
choices.D: A standard adult seatbelt.

en.explanation: The manual specifies: 'A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) that is facing the rear of the car.'

en.question: A child who is four through eight years old and under four feet, nine inches tall must be secured in:

choices.A: A rear-facing car seat.
choices.B: A forward-facing car seat.
choices.C: A belt-positioning booster seat system.
choices.D: The front passenger seat with a standard seatbelt.

en.explanation: Children who are four through eight years old and whose height is under four feet, nine inches, must be in a belt positioning booster seat system and wearing a seatbelt.

en.question: If a child under age 16 is not properly restrained in a vehicle, who is generally held responsible and may be fined?

choices.A: The child.
choices.B: The driver of the vehicle.
choices.C: The owner of the vehicle, even if not present.
choices.D: The vehicle manufacturer.

en.explanation: The law makes the driver responsible for the protection of children up to the age of sixteen. If they are not properly restrained, the driver may be charged and fined $50.00.

en.question: If a child's parent or legal guardian is present in the car but is NOT driving, who is responsible for ensuring the child is properly transported?

choices.A: The driver.
choices.B: The parent or legal guardian.
choices.C: Both the driver and the parent equally.
choices.D: The child.

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'If the child’s parent or legal guardian is present in the car but not driving, then the parent or legal guardian is responsible for making sure that the child is properly transported and may be fined for non-compliance.'

en.question: What is the chance of being killed in a crash if you are ejected from a vehicle?

choices.A: One in two.
choices.B: One in four.
choices.C: One in eight.
choices.D: One in ten.

en.explanation: According to the Safety Belt Facts section, 'The chance of being killed in a crash by being ejected from a vehicle is one in eight.'

en.question: How should a pregnant woman wear a vehicle's safety belt?

choices.A: The lap belt above the abdomen and the shoulder belt behind the back.
choices.B: The lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.
choices.C: Only the lap belt, placed directly over the abdomen.
choices.D: Only the shoulder belt, placed under the arm.

en.explanation: The manual instructs: 'Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.'

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a driver caught using a hand-held phone to transmit or read a written message while the vehicle is in motion (excluding court costs)?

choices.A: Ten Dollars.
choices.B: Twenty-Five Dollars.
choices.C: Fifty Dollars.
choices.D: One Hundred Dollars.

en.explanation: Violations for using a hand-held phone to transmit or read a written message while in motion 'can result in a fine not to exceed Fifty Dollars, and court costs not to exceed Ten Dollars.'

en.question: What is the penalty for a driver who fails to use a car seat or booster seat for a child under nine years old or whose height is less than four feet, nine inches?

choices.A: A Class A misdemeanor and license suspension.
choices.B: A Class C misdemeanor, required class attendance, and possible fees/fines.
choices.C: A simple $10 fine with no other penalties.
choices.D: A warning for the first offense and a $50 fine for the second.

en.explanation: If the violation relates to not using a car seat or booster seat for children under nine or under 4'9", the punishment is greater: 'The driver can be charged with a Class C misdemeanor, required to attend a class on safely transporting children and required to pay possible fees and fines.'

en.question: According to the manual, how much more likely are ejected occupants to be killed in a crash compared to those who remain inside the vehicle?

choices.A: Two times more likely
choices.B: Three times more likely
choices.C: Four times more likely
choices.D: Ten times more likely

en.explanation: The manual notes that ejected occupants are four times more likely to be killed as those who remain inside the vehicle.

en.question: What happens to unfastened passengers when a vehicle is struck from the side?

choices.A: They will slide toward the point of the crash.
choices.B: They will slide away from the point of the crash.
choices.C: They will be pushed into the back seat.
choices.D: They will remain stationary while the vehicle moves.

en.explanation: When a vehicle is struck from the side, everything that is not fastened down, including passengers, will slide toward the point of the crash, not away from it.

en.question: When is a child considered big enough to transition from a child restraint system to using standard vehicle lap and shoulder belts?

choices.A: When they reach 40 pounds in weight.
choices.B: When they are at least 6 years old.
choices.C: When they can sit with their back against the seat back and their knees bend over the edge.
choices.D: When they can buckle the seatbelt themselves without assistance.

en.explanation: A child is big enough to use the vehicle lap and shoulder belt when they can sit with their back against the vehicle seat back and their knees bend over the edge of the vehicle seat.

en.question: Where should the lap belt lie securely on a child who has graduated to using standard vehicle safety belts?

choices.A: Across the stomach
choices.B: On the upper thigh, low and snug around the hips
choices.C: Across the ribcage
choices.D: Loosely over the knees

en.explanation: The manual specifies that the lap belt should lie securely on the child's upper thigh, low and snug around the hips.

en.question: At what age does the manual state children are safer riding in the back seat of a vehicle?

choices.A: Ages 8 and under
choices.B: Ages 10 and under
choices.C: Ages 12 and under
choices.D: Ages 15 and under

en.explanation: The manual emphasizes that children ages 12 and under are safer in the back seat of a vehicle.

en.question: What is the recommended distance a driver should sit from the steering wheel to give the air bag room to deploy safely?

choices.A: 4 to 6 inches
choices.B: 6 to 8 inches
choices.C: 10 to 12 inches
choices.D: 15 to 18 inches

en.explanation: Ten to twelve inches between the chest and the air bag module is recommended by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

en.question: Under Tennessee law, what is the rule regarding children under the age of 6 riding in the bed of a pickup truck?

choices.A: It is legal if they are supervised by an adult.
choices.B: It is illegal under all circumstances.
choices.C: It is legal only on county roads.
choices.D: It is legal if the truck is traveling under 30 mph.

en.explanation: It is illegal in Tennessee to allow any child under the age of 6 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck.

en.question: It is against the law to allow a child between the ages of 6 and 12 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on which type of road?

choices.A: Any state or interstate highway
choices.B: Any private road
choices.C: Any dirt road
choices.D: Any residential driveway

en.explanation: It is against the law to allow any child between the ages of 6 and 12 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on any state or interstate highway.

en.question: Which of the following is an exception that allows a child to ride in the bed of a pickup truck?

choices.A: When traveling to a school event
choices.B: When involved in agricultural activities
choices.C: When there are no seats left in the cab
choices.D: When driving to a state park

en.explanation: One exception to the law prohibiting children in the bed of a pickup truck is when the child is involved in agricultural activities.

en.question: It is an offense to knowingly leave a child unattended in a motor vehicle if the child is younger than what age?

choices.A: 5 years of age
choices.B: 7 years of age
choices.C: 9 years of age
choices.D: 12 years of age

en.explanation: It is an offense for a person responsible for a child younger than 7 years of age to knowingly leave that child unattended in a motor vehicle under certain conditions.

en.question: If a child under 7 is left in a motor vehicle with the engine running, they must be supervised by a person who is at least what age?

choices.A: 10 years of age
choices.B: 13 years of age
choices.C: 16 years of age
choices.D: 18 years of age

en.explanation: The law states the child must be supervised in the motor vehicle by a person who is at least 13 years of age.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of leaving a child unattended in a motor vehicle under illegal conditions?

choices.A: A Class C misdemeanor and a $50 fine
choices.B: A Class B misdemeanor and a $200 fine
choices.C: A Class A misdemeanor and a $500 fine
choices.D: A felony charge and license suspension

en.explanation: A violation of this section is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a fine of two hundred dollars ($200) for the first offense.

en.question: According to the manual, how much more likely are vehicle occupants to die in a crash if they are unbelted?

choices.A: 5 times more likely
choices.B: 10 times more likely
choices.C: 20 times more likely
choices.D: 32 times more likely

en.explanation: Vehicle occupants were 32 times more likely to die in a crash if they were unbelted.

en.question: If a child must ride in the front seat of a pickup truck with a passenger-side air bag, what should you do?

choices.A: Turn off the vehicle's engine.
choices.B: Move the seat back as far as possible and properly buckle the child.
choices.C: Have the child sit on an adult's lap.
choices.D: Place the child in a rear-facing safety seat.

en.explanation: If a child must ride in the front seat of a vehicle such as a pick-up truck with a passenger side air bag, the seat should be moved back as far as possible, and the child should be properly buckled up.

en.question: On a mild day with an outside temperature of 73 degrees, how hot can the interior of an SUV get in just 10 minutes?

choices.A: 85 degrees
choices.B: 90 degrees
choices.C: 100 degrees
choices.D: 120 degrees

en.explanation: According to the manual, even on a mild day at 73 degrees outside, an SUV can heat up to 100 degrees in 10 minutes.

en.question: What is the maximum penalty for a Class A Misdemeanor regarding leaving a child unattended in a vehicle?

choices.A: 6 months in jail and a $1,000 fine
choices.B: 11 months, 29 days and/or a fine up to $2,500
choices.C: 1 to 5 years in prison
choices.D: 15 to 60 years in prison

en.explanation: Class A Misdemeanors carry a penalty of not greater than 11 months, 29 days or a fine up to $2,500, or both.

en.question: Where is the safest place for children 12 years old and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with air bags?

choices.A: The front passenger seat
choices.B: The back seat
choices.C: The middle of the front bench seat
choices.D: The bed of a pick-up truck

en.explanation: The manual states that the safest place for children 12 and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with air bags is the back seat.

en.question: Which color is used for incident management traffic control signage, such as for traffic accidents or hazardous material spills?

choices.A: Orange
choices.B: Fluorescent Pink
choices.C: Brown
choices.D: Red

en.explanation: Fluorescent pink (sometimes called "coral") is used for incident management traffic control signage when needed for incidents such as traffic accidents, wildland fires, floods, and hazardous material spills.

en.question: What type of information is indicated by a brown traffic sign?

choices.A: Public recreation areas and cultural interest points
choices.B: Highway construction and detours
choices.C: Permissive parking regulations
choices.D: Police services and rest areas

en.explanation: Brown is used as a background color for guide information signs related to points of recreational and cultural interest.

en.question: What does an eight-sided (octagon) traffic sign mean?

choices.A: Yield right-of-way
choices.B: Railroad crossing ahead
choices.C: Stop
choices.D: School zone ahead

en.explanation: The octagon shape is the only eight-sided sign on the roadway. It will always be red with white lettering and it tells you that you must bring your car to a complete stop.

en.question: A circular (round) traffic sign indicates that you are approaching:

choices.A: A four-way intersection
choices.B: A railroad grade crossing
choices.C: A hospital zone
choices.D: A roundabout

en.explanation: A circular sign always means that you are approaching a railroad grade crossing and must slow down.

en.question: If a highway construction worker directs you to proceed, but the traffic light is red, what should you do?

choices.A: Wait for the light to turn green before proceeding.
choices.B: Obey the construction worker and proceed.
choices.C: Pull over and wait for a police officer.
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.

en.explanation: Drivers must obey directions from law enforcement, highway construction personnel or school crossing guards, even if the directions are different than what the traffic lights and signs indicate.

en.question: When approaching a three-sided triangular Yield sign, what must you do if other vehicles are approaching on the other roadway?

choices.A: Speed up to merge ahead of them.
choices.B: Maintain your speed and honk your horn.
choices.C: Stop and wait for the approaching vehicles.
choices.D: Proceed without stopping as you have the right-of-way.

en.explanation: A three-sided Yield sign means you must stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching from the right or left on the other roadway.

en.question: Which of the following is indicated by a blue traffic sign?

choices.A: Construction zones
choices.B: Motorist services such as police and rest areas
choices.C: General warnings
choices.D: Permissive parking regulations

en.explanation: Blue is used as a background color for information signs related to motorist services (including police services and rest areas) and the Emergency Route Marker.

en.question: According to child passenger restraint rules, when should a child be facing the rear of the car?

choices.A: If the child is under 1 year old and weighs less than 20 pounds.
choices.B: If the child is between 1 and 3 years old.
choices.C: If the child weighs more than 20 pounds.
choices.D: If the child is riding in the front passenger seat.

en.explanation: A child in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) should be facing the rear of the car if weighing less than 20 pounds and under 1 year old.

en.question: What does a red rectangular sign with the words "ALL WAY" placed below a stop sign mean?

choices.A: Only cross traffic must stop.
choices.B: All traffic approaching this intersection must stop.
choices.C: You may proceed without stopping if the way is clear.
choices.D: The road ahead is closed to all traffic.

en.explanation: A red rectangle added below a stop sign with "ALL WAY" means all traffic approaching this intersection must stop.

en.question: What should you do when approaching a three-sided Yield sign?

choices.A: Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.
choices.B: Speed up to merge smoothly with cross traffic.
choices.C: Slow down and enter the intersection with caution if no other cars are coming.
choices.D: Stop only if there is a traffic light present.

en.explanation: The manual states that at a Yield sign, if you are sure no other cars are coming you need not come to a complete stop but you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution.

en.question: What is the purpose of the smaller signs placed directly below a broad 'X' shaped railroad crossbuck sign?

choices.A: They indicate the speed limit for the crossing.
choices.B: They show the number of tracks at that particular crossing.
choices.C: They warn of the exact time trains usually pass.
choices.D: They indicate the distance to the next highway intersection.

en.explanation: The manual notes that the smaller signs placed on the post directly below the crossbuck show the number of tracks at a particular crossing.

en.question: According to the manual, why should you never try to 'beat' a train at a railroad crossing?

choices.A: Trains have the right-of-way only during daylight hours.
choices.B: You will usually misjudge the train's speed.
choices.C: It is illegal to cross tracks without stopping first.
choices.D: Your vehicle's engine will stall on the tracks.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly warns drivers: 'NEVER TRY TO BEAT THE TRAIN. YOU WILL USUALLY MISJUDGE ITS SPEED.'

en.question: Where is a triangular No Passing Zone sign typically placed on the roadway?

choices.A: On the right side of the roadway.
choices.B: Suspended directly over the center lane.
choices.C: On the left side of the roadway.
choices.D: On the pavement surface as a painted symbol.

en.explanation: The manual states that a triangular No Passing Zone sign is yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway.

en.question: What is the difference between a warning sign for a turn and a warning sign for a curve?

choices.A: A turn sign is used for recommended speeds of 30 mph or less, while a curve sign is for speeds between 30 and 55 mph.
choices.B: A turn sign is orange, while a curve sign is yellow.
choices.C: A turn sign indicates a dead end, while a curve sign indicates a winding road.
choices.D: A turn sign is for right turns only, while a curve sign is for left turns only.

en.explanation: The manual states the turn sign is used to mark turns with a recommended speed of 30 m.p.h. or less, whereas the curve sign marks curves with recommended speeds in the range between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

en.question: When you see a warning sign for falling rocks in hilly areas, what should you watch for?

choices.A: Rocks falling directly from overhead onto your vehicle.
choices.B: Rocks that may already be in the road.
choices.C: Construction vehicles dumping gravel.
choices.D: Pedestrians throwing rocks from overpasses.

en.explanation: The manual clarifies that this sign 'warns of rocks that may be in the road, not of rocks which may strike you from overhead. Watch the roadway, not the hill.'

en.question: What should you do when you see a warning sign alerting you to traffic blending into your main stream of travel?

choices.A: Speed up to block the merging traffic.
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn the merging vehicles to yield.
choices.C: Move into the other lane, if possible, to allow the merging motorist a clear path.
choices.D: Come to a complete stop and let the other vehicles merge.

en.explanation: The manual advises that after checking to your rear, you should move into the other lane, if possible, to allow the merging motorist a clear path.

en.question: What color and shape are construction, maintenance, or emergency operations signs generally?

choices.A: Red and white triangles.
choices.B: Yellow and black circles.
choices.C: Green and white rectangles.
choices.D: Orange with black letters or symbols, and diamond or rectangular shaped.

en.explanation: The manual states that work area signs are generally diamond or rectangular shaped, orange with black letters or symbols.

en.question: How should you drive when passing through a work zone guided by channeling devices like barricades or cones?

choices.A: Keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit.
choices.B: Drive as close to the cones as possible to leave room for workers.
choices.C: Frequently change lanes to find the fastest route through the zone.
choices.D: Straddle the center line to maintain a safe distance from the barricades.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit' when driving near channeling devices.

en.question: How are some school zone speed limit signs controlled to indicate when children may be crossing?

choices.A: By crossing guards holding stop paddles.
choices.B: By a time clock that flashes yellow lights while illuminating the speed limit.
choices.C: By motion sensors that detect approaching vehicles.
choices.D: By a permanent red traffic light.

en.explanation: The manual states that this type of sign is controlled by a time clock and flashes yellow lights while illuminating the speed limit.

en.question: On a highway with more than one lane going each direction, what does the sign requiring you to drive in the extreme right lane mean?

choices.A: You must drive in the right lane unless you want to pass a slower moving car or make a left turn.
choices.B: You must always drive in the right lane, even when passing.
choices.C: You should straddle the lanes if you are moving slower than other traffic.
