choices.D: You may only use the right lane for parking or emergencies.

en.explanation: The manual explains this sign means 'that you must drive in the extreme right lane unless you want to pass a slower moving car or make a left turn.'

en.question: What color clothing do flaggers, utility workers, and law enforcement officers wear in work zones to ensure they can be seen under low light and poor weather conditions?

choices.A: Dark blue or black uniforms.
choices.B: Fluorescent yellow-green clothing or vests.
choices.C: Pure white reflective suits.
choices.D: Camouflage jackets.

en.explanation: The manual mentions Law Enforcement Officers and flaggers/workers wear 'Fluorescent Yellow-Green Vests' and clothing to make sure they can be seen under normal conditions and under low light and poor weather conditions.

en.question: What action should you take when you see a flashing arrow panel alerting you to a lane closure ahead?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the construction zone quickly.
choices.B: Wait until the last possible moment to merge into the open lane.
choices.C: Begin to merge into the remaining open lane(s) well in advance of the sign.
choices.D: Stop your vehicle immediately and wait for a flagger's instructions.

en.explanation: The manual instructs: 'Flashing arrow panels alert approaching drivers of lane closures. You must begin to merge into the remaining open lane(s) well in advance of this sign.'

en.question: What should you do when driving near channeling devices in a work zone?

choices.A: Change lanes quickly to avoid them.
choices.B: Keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit.
choices.C: Drive on the shoulder to give workers more room.
choices.D: Speed up to exit the work zone faster.

en.explanation: The manual states that when driving near channeling devices in a work zone, you should keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are most likely to display a Slow-Moving Vehicle (SMV) emblem?

choices.A: Emergency vehicles responding to a call.
choices.B: Commercial buses and large trucks.
choices.C: Farm tractors, machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.
choices.D: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you may see the SMV emblem on slow-moving vehicles, such as farm tractors, machinery, construction equipment, or horse-drawn vehicles.

en.question: What is the purpose of an object marker sign?

choices.A: To mark the center line of a two-way highway.
choices.B: To indicate a pedestrian crossing ahead.
choices.C: To show the distance to the next highway exit.
choices.D: To warn of objects close to the edge of the road, such as bridge ends.

en.explanation: Object markers warn drivers of objects not actually in the roadway, but so close to the edge of the road that they need marking, such as bridge ends and underpass abutments.

en.question: What colors are used for Interstate Route Marker signs?

choices.A: Green and white
choices.B: Blue and red
choices.C: Black and white
choices.D: Yellow and black

en.explanation: The manual states that blue and red signs indicate that the route is part of the national system of interstate and defense highways.

en.question: What color are signs that direct motorists to service facilities like gas stations, restaurants, and motels?

choices.A: Green
choices.B: Brown
choices.C: Blue
choices.D: Orange

en.explanation: The blue color of service signs directs motorists to service facilities such as service stations, restaurants, and motels.

en.question: Who is legally permitted to park in spaces displaying the blue handicap symbol?

choices.A: Anyone who is parking for less than 5 minutes.
choices.B: Pregnant women and families with small children.
choices.C: Vehicles bearing disabled veteran or handicapped license plates, or a special handicapped decal.
choices.D: Elderly drivers over the age of 65.

en.explanation: Parking spaces displaying the blue handicap sign are reserved exclusively for vehicles bearing disabled veteran or handicapped license plates, or a special handicapped decal. Use by others is prohibited by law.

en.question: How often are emergency reference markers installed along heavily traveled sections of urban interstates in Tennessee?

choices.A: Every 500 feet
choices.B: Every 1,000 feet
choices.C: Every 1 mile
choices.D: Every 5 miles

en.explanation: In order to help motorists better identify their location, the state has installed interstate reference markers every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections of urban interstates.

en.question: When are you permitted to turn right on a red light?

choices.A: At any time, without stopping.
choices.B: Only when a green arrow is also illuminated.
choices.C: After coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present, unless otherwise posted.
choices.D: Right turns on red are never permitted in Tennessee.

en.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

en.question: According to Tennessee law, what is the minimum amount of time a yellow traffic light must be exhibited before turning red?

choices.A: Two seconds
choices.B: Three seconds
choices.C: Four seconds
choices.D: Five seconds

en.explanation: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red light.

en.question: What should you do if you are already IN the intersection when the yellow traffic light comes on?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.
choices.B: Put your vehicle in reverse and back out of the intersection.
choices.C: Speed up significantly to beat the red light.
choices.D: Do not stop, but continue cautiously through the intersection.

en.explanation: The manual instructs that if you are already IN the intersection when the yellow light comes on, do not stop, but continue cautiously through the intersection.

en.question: What does a red arrow traffic signal indicate?

choices.A: You may turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding.
choices.B: All turns in the direction of the arrow are prohibited, even if other lanes of traffic have a green signal.
choices.C: You must treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
choices.D: You may turn only if you are driving an emergency vehicle.

en.explanation: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited. This is true even if other lanes of traffic have a green signal and your path appears clear.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean at an intersection?

choices.A: You are allowed to turn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians.
choices.B: The traffic light is broken and you must stop completely.
choices.C: You have the protected right-of-way to turn left without yielding.
choices.D: Left turns are completely prohibited.

en.explanation: If you see a flashing yellow arrow, you are allowed to turn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to any bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

en.question: How should you treat an intersection if the traffic signal is malfunctioning and the light is out?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection without stopping if you are on the main road.
choices.B: Treat it as a yield sign.
choices.C: Treat it as an all-way stop intersection.
choices.D: Wait for a police officer to arrive before proceeding.

en.explanation: Tennessee state law requires that if a signal is not working, the intersection is to be treated as if it were an all-way stop intersection.

en.question: If two vehicles arrive at an all-way stop intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
choices.B: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
choices.C: The vehicle traveling at a faster speed goes first.
choices.D: The vehicle turning left always goes first.

en.explanation: The right-of-way law says that if there are two or more vehicles at the intersection stopping at the same time, the driver on the left would yield to the driver on the right.

en.question: How does Tennessee law define a pedestrian?

choices.A: Only a person walking on a designated sidewalk.
choices.B: Any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.
choices.C: Anyone riding a bicycle or skateboard.
choices.D: Any person crossing the street outside of a crosswalk.

en.explanation: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.

en.question: When are you required to turn on your vehicle's headlights at night?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise
choices.B: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
choices.C: 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise
choices.D: Only when there are no streetlights

en.explanation: The manual states that your car headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

en.question: Under what weather conditions are you required to turn on your headlights during daylight hours?

choices.A: Only when it is snowing heavily
choices.B: Whenever the sky is cloudy
choices.C: When precipitation requires the constant use of windshield wipers
choices.D: Only when driving on the interstate in the rain

en.explanation: Headlights must be turned on during daylight hours when rain, mist, snow, or other precipitation requires constant use of windshield wipers.

en.question: You must turn on your headlights during the day if daylight is not good enough to clearly see persons or vehicles at what distance ahead?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Your car headlights must be turned on at any time when daylight is not good enough for you to see persons or vehicles clearly at a distance of 200 feet ahead.

en.question: What is the rule regarding coasting while traveling on a downgrade?

choices.A: It is recommended to save gas
choices.B: You may coast in neutral but not with the clutch depressed
choices.C: You must never coast with the transmission in neutral or the clutch depressed
choices.D: Coasting is only allowed on roads with a speed limit under 45 mph

en.explanation: While traveling on a downgrade, NEVER coast with the transmission of the vehicle in neutral. Also, drivers of manual transmission vehicles must not coast with the clutch depressed.

en.question: If a traffic officer instructs you to do something that would ordinarily violate a traffic regulation, what should you do?

choices.A: Ignore the officer and follow the traffic signals
choices.B: Obey the officer's instructions at all times
choices.C: Ask the officer for their badge number before proceeding
choices.D: Pull over and wait for the traffic signal to change

en.explanation: You must obey traffic officers at all times. There will be times when an officer will instruct you to do something that ordinarily would be a violation of traffic regulations in case of an emergency.

en.question: According to statistics, where do half of all vehicle crashes occur?

choices.A: On interstate highways
choices.B: Within 25 miles of home
choices.C: In busy intersections
choices.D: During long road trips

en.explanation: Statistics show that half of all vehicle crashes occur within 25 miles of home.

en.question: How can you tell by the edge lines that you are driving the wrong way on a roadway?

choices.A: You have a white line to your right and a yellow line to your left
choices.B: You have a yellow line to your right and a white line to your left
choices.C: Both edge lines are white
choices.D: Both edge lines are yellow

en.explanation: If you ever find yourself with yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.

en.question: When are you permitted to cross two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic?

choices.A: To pass a slow-moving vehicle
choices.B: When there is no oncoming traffic in view
choices.C: To turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe
choices.D: You may never cross two solid yellow lines under any circumstances

en.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean you MAY NOT cross the lines from either direction to pass. However, you may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe to do so.

en.question: What does it mean if the center of the roadway is marked with one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line, and the broken line is on your side?

choices.A: You are in a passing zone and may pass if it is safe
choices.B: You are not allowed to pass in this area
choices.C: You must prepare to stop
choices.D: The lane is for turning only

en.explanation: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the 'passing zone' and may pass if it is safe to do so.

en.question: What does a single solid white line between lanes of traffic flowing in the same direction indicate?

choices.A: You may freely change lanes to pass
choices.B: You should stay in your lane and not cross unless in an emergency
choices.C: The lane is ending and you must merge left
choices.D: You are approaching a toll plaza

en.explanation: One solid white line between lanes of traffic means that you should stay in your lane and should not cross the line to pass (unless an emergency situation requires you to change lanes).

en.question: Where must you stop your vehicle at an intersection if there is no painted stop line or crosswalk?

choices.A: Just past the corner so you can see traffic clearly
choices.B: Before the front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street
choices.C: At least 10 feet back from the intersection
choices.D: Next to the stop sign post

en.explanation: If no stop line is painted on the pavement, all vehicles required to stop must stop the vehicle before the front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street, in order to keep the vehicle from protruding out into the cross street traffic.

en.question: What symbol on the pavement designates a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?

choices.A: A white crossbuck
choices.B: A painted circle with an X
choices.C: A diamond-shaped marking
choices.D: A large white arrow

en.explanation: High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lanes are designated on highways by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane.

en.question: What does it mean if your travel lane is marked with both a curved arrow and a straight arrow?

choices.A: You must turn in the direction of the arrow
choices.B: You may either turn in the direction of the arrow or go straight
choices.C: The lane is ending and you must merge
choices.D: You are approaching a roundabout

en.explanation: If your lane is marked with both a curved and a straight arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow or you may go straight.

en.question: What pavement marking acts as a warning for a railroad/highway grade crossing?

choices.A: A diamond shape with the letters RR
choices.B: A white crossbuck and the letters RR
choices.C: A solid yellow line with a red X
choices.D: A double solid white line

en.explanation: A white crossbuck and the letters RR are painted on the pavement as a warning marker for many railroad/highway grade crossings.

en.question: What does a pedestrian signal displaying a symbol of a raised hand mean?

choices.A: Pedestrians have the right-of-way to cross
choices.B: It is not safe to begin crossing the street
choices.C: Pedestrians should run across the intersection quickly
choices.D: Vehicles must stop and wait for pedestrians to approach

en.explanation: When the pedestrian signal shows the words 'DON’T WALK,' or a symbol of a raised hand appears, it is not safe to begin crossing a street or intersection.

en.question: When are you required to turn on your car headlights for night use in Tennessee?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise
choices.B: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
choices.C: 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise
choices.D: Only when it is completely dark outside

en.explanation: According to the manual, your car headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

en.question: In Tennessee, you are required by law to turn on your headlights during daylight or inclement weather when:

choices.A: Driving on any interstate highway.
choices.B: Constant use of windshield wipers is required due to precipitation.
choices.C: Driving in the leftmost lane of a multi-lane highway.
choices.D: Approaching a properly identified funeral procession.

en.explanation: The manual states that headlights must be turned on when rain, mist, snow, or other precipitation requires constant use of windshield wipers.

en.question: When must you dim or lower your vehicle's high beam headlights?

choices.A: When an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.
choices.B: When an oncoming vehicle is within 200 feet.
choices.C: When an oncoming vehicle is within 1,000 feet.
choices.D: Only when driving in congested urban areas.

en.explanation: You must dim or lower the beam when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet (approximately the distance of one city block) or when you are following another vehicle within 500 feet.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the use of parking lights while driving?

choices.A: They should be used instead of headlights in heavy fog.
choices.B: It is illegal to drive a vehicle with only the parking lights on at night or in inclement weather.
choices.C: They make your vehicle appear closer to other drivers than it actually is.
choices.D: They are required to be on at all times when driving in a school zone.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Do not drive a vehicle with only the parking lights on when driving at night or in inclement weather... the use of parking lights alone is not only unsafe, it is against the law.'

en.question: Effective January 1, 2018, steady-burning lights displayed to the front of a vehicle in Tennessee must be:

choices.A: White or amber
choices.B: Red or blue
choices.C: Green or yellow
choices.D: Any color as long as they do not flash

en.explanation: Effective January 1, 2018, no vehicle operated in Tennessee shall be equipped with any steady-burning lights that display to the front of the vehicle in any color other than white or amber (or a combination of the two).

en.question: What are the potential fines for a littering conviction in Tennessee?
en.explanation: Littering is against state law. Fines start at $50 and can be up to $3,000 based upon the amount of litter.

en.question: What does Tennessee law require of any motor vehicle transporting material likely to fall or be blown off onto the highway?

choices.A: The material must be tied down with bungee cords.
choices.B: The vehicle must travel at least 10 mph below the speed limit.
choices.C: The material must be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.
choices.D: The vehicle must display a 'Slow Moving Vehicle' sign.

en.explanation: Tennessee law requires any motor vehicle transporting litter or any material, likely to fall or be blown off onto the highway, to be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.

en.question: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle if you are traveling at a rate of speed that is:

choices.A: 5 mph or more below the lawful maximum speed.
choices.B: 10 mph or more below the lawful maximum speed.
choices.C: 15 mph or more below the lawful maximum speed.
choices.D: 20 mph or more below the lawful maximum speed.

en.explanation: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle if you are traveling at a rate of speed that is 10 miles per hour or more below the lawful maximum speed.

en.question: If you are driving a slow-moving vehicle, when must you turn or pull off the roadway safely?

choices.A: When 2 or more vehicles are lined up behind you.
choices.B: When 3 or more vehicles are lined up behind you.
choices.C: When 5 or more vehicles are lined up behind you.
choices.D: When 10 or more vehicles are lined up behind you.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely.'

en.question: What is the rule for passing a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway in Tennessee?

choices.A: You may pass if you honk your horn first.
choices.B: You may pass only if the procession is traveling below 45 mph.
choices.C: Vehicles following the procession may not attempt to pass it.
choices.D: You may pass if you turn on your hazard lights.

en.explanation: Tennessee law instructs that vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not attempt to pass such procession.

en.question: Which of the following best describes the Basic Speed Rule (BSR)?

choices.A: It is a strict Tennessee law that sets exact speed limits for all roads.
choices.B: It teaches that the speed you may drive is limited by current conditions.
choices.C: It requires all drivers to travel at exactly the posted speed limit.
choices.D: It states that driving slower is always safer.

en.explanation: The Basic Speed Rule (BSR) is not a Tennessee law, but a general safety principle. It does not set an exact speed limit; instead, it teaches that the speed you may drive is limited by current conditions.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways in Tennessee?
en.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 m.p.h.

en.question: What is the maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways?
en.explanation: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is 70 m.p.h., which is posted on most rural sections.

en.question: Under normal driving conditions, it is unlawful to drive less than what speed in the leftmost lane of any Interstate highway in Tennessee?
en.explanation: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle less than 55 m.p.h. in the left most lane of any Interstate highway, unless traffic congestion and flow prevent safe driving at such speed.

en.question: On Tennessee interstates, what is the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) under normal driving conditions?
en.explanation: On the interstates, the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 m.p.h., and under normal driving conditions, all vehicles must travel at least this fast.

en.question: What is the penalty for exceeding the speed limit in a school zone in Tennessee?

choices.A: An automatic two points added to your driving record
choices.B: An automatic four points added to your driving record
choices.C: An automatic six points added to your driving record
choices.D: An automatic license suspension for 30 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, the penalty for exceeding the school zone speed limit includes an automatic six points added to your driving record, which results in an advisory letter.

en.question: By law, exceeding the school zone speed limit is considered to be:

choices.A: Careless driving
choices.B: Reckless driving
choices.C: Aggressive driving
choices.D: A minor traffic infraction

en.explanation: The manual states that exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered to be reckless driving.

en.question: What are the minimum and maximum fines for violating the posted speed limit in active work zones in Tennessee?

choices.A: $50 minimum and $250 maximum
choices.B: $100 minimum and $300 maximum
choices.C: $250 minimum and $500 maximum
choices.D: $500 minimum and $1,000 maximum

en.explanation: Tennessee law mandates a minimum fine of $250 dollars and up to a maximum fine of $500 dollars for violations of the speed limit posted in active work zones.

en.question: How are highway work zones easily recognized by drivers?

choices.A: By the presence of blue and white signs and devices
choices.B: By the presence of orange or yellow-green signs, devices, and clothing
choices.C: By the presence of solid red signs and flashing green lights
choices.D: By the presence of black and white checkered flags

en.explanation: Highway work zones are easily recognized by the presence of orange (or yellow-green) signs and other orange traffic control devices, flashing lights on equipment, and workers dressed in highly visible clothing (orange or yellow-green).

en.question: By law, what braking equipment must all automobiles have?

choices.A: Only a regular foot brake
choices.B: Two separate methods of applying brakes, commonly a foot brake and a parking/emergency brake
choices.C: An anti-lock braking system (ABS) and a foot brake
choices.D: Front disc brakes and rear drum brakes

en.explanation: By law, all automobiles must have two separate methods of applying brakes. Commonly, these are the vehicle's regular brakes (foot brake) and a parking or emergency brake.

en.question: If your vehicle does NOT have anti-lock brakes and starts to skid, what should you generally do?

choices.A: Pump the brakes as fast as possible
choices.B: Slam on the brakes and hold the steering wheel straight
choices.C: Take your foot off the brake and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to regain traction

en.explanation: As a general rule for vehicles without anti-lock brakes, if the car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid, if safe to do so.

en.question: When slowing or stopping a vehicle equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), you should:

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly
choices.B: Apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal
choices.C: Lightly tap the brake pedal repeatedly
choices.D: Take your foot off the pedal if you feel vibration

en.explanation: When slowing or stopping with ABS, apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal. Never pump the pedal with ABS.

en.question: What should you expect to feel when your anti-lock braking system (ABS) is in use?

choices.A: The steering wheel will lock in place
choices.B: The brake pedal will go completely to the floor with no resistance
choices.C: Noise and vibration in the brake pedal
choices.D: The engine will temporarily stall

en.explanation: Expect noise and vibration in the brake pedal when your ABS is in use. These sensations tell you ABS is working.

en.question: What does the term 'riding the brake' mean?

choices.A: Hovering your foot over the brake pedal for a quicker response
choices.B: Keeping your foot resting or slightly pressed down on the brake pedal
choices.C: Pressing the brake and gas pedals at the same time
choices.D: Pumping the brake pedal repeatedly while driving down a hill

en.explanation: 'Riding the brake' is keeping your foot resting or slightly pressed down on the brake. This adds wear and tear and gives other drivers a false impression.

en.question: Is 'covering the brake' considered a safe driving practice?

choices.A: Yes, it allows for quicker response time in situations like approaching intersections
choices.B: No, it causes excessive wear and tear on the brake system
choices.C: No, it gives other drivers the false impression that a stop is imminent
choices.D: Yes, but only when driving on interstate highways

en.explanation: Covering the brake means the driver's foot hovers over the brake for quicker response time. The manual states that covering the brake is often a smart and safe driving practice.

en.question: To maintain a safe following distance under normal driving conditions, drivers should use:

choices.A: The one-second rule
choices.B: The two-second rule
choices.C: The five-second rule
choices.D: The ten-second rule

en.explanation: Nationally, safety agencies recommend a safe following distance. The manual advises using the Two-Second Rule to determine if you are following too closely.

en.question: During inclement weather, interstate highway driving at higher speeds, or night driving, the following distance should be increased to a minimum of:

choices.A: Two seconds
choices.B: Three seconds
choices.C: Four seconds
choices.D: Six seconds

en.explanation: During inclement weather, interstate driving at higher speeds, and night driving, the two-second rule should be increased to a minimum of four seconds to allow for better reaction time.

en.question: In the three steps of stopping a vehicle, what is 'Perception time'?

choices.A: The time it takes to move your foot from the gas to the brake pedal
choices.B: The length of time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation
choices.C: The distance the car travels while the brakes are applied
choices.D: The time it takes for the vehicle's brake pads to engage the rotors

en.explanation: Perception time is defined as the length of time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation.

en.question: What is a very common consequence of drivers following too closely (tailgating)?

choices.A: It improves the flow of heavy traffic
choices.B: It gives the driver a better view of road conditions ahead
choices.C: It causes rear-end crashes
choices.D: It increases the vehicle's fuel efficiency

en.explanation: The manual notes that rear-end crashes are very common and most of these crashes are caused by drivers who are 'tailgating' (following too closely).

en.question: When approaching a stop sign in a vehicle with a standard transmission, what should you do to slow down?

choices.A: Shift into neutral and coast to the stop sign
choices.B: Turn off the engine to save fuel
choices.C: Flash the brake lights to signal cars behind you, then shift down to a lower gear
choices.D: Ride the clutch until the vehicle comes to a complete stop

en.explanation: With a standard transmission, you can use the gearshift to slow down. First, flash the brake lights to signal any cars behind you. Then, shift down to a lower gear.

en.question: What are the three steps involved in stopping a vehicle?

choices.A: Observation time, slowing time, and stopping time
choices.B: Perception time, reaction time, and braking time
choices.C: Braking time, skidding time, and stopping time
choices.D: Reaction time, deceleration time, and resting time

en.explanation: According to the manual, there are three steps in stopping a vehicle: Perception time, Reaction time, and Braking time.

en.question: What is the average reaction time from the perception of danger to the start of braking?

choices.A: 1/2 of a second
choices.B: 2/3 of a second
choices.C: 1 second
choices.D: 1.16 seconds

en.explanation: The manual states that reaction time is the time from perception of danger to the start of braking, and the average is 2/3 of a second.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a factor that can widely vary a vehicle's stopping distance?

choices.A: Type and condition of the road or pavement
choices.B: Vehicle design and condition of the shock absorbers
choices.C: The color and visibility of the vehicle
choices.D: Vehicle weight when loaded or towing

en.explanation: Stopping distance varies due to factors like road condition, tires/brakes, shock absorbers, and vehicle weight. Vehicle color is not listed as a factor.

en.question: Where should you stop your vehicle at a stop sign if there is no pavement marking or crosswalk present?

choices.A: Ten feet before the stop sign
choices.B: When the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign's placement on the roadside
choices.C: Directly underneath the stop sign
choices.D: At the exact edge of the intersecting roadway

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If no pavement markings are present, stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign's placement on the roadside.'

en.question: When stopping behind another vehicle at an intersection, what is a basic rule of thumb for maintaining a safe 'gap' space?

choices.A: You should be at least one car length behind the vehicle.
choices.B: You should be able to see the license plate and/or the other vehicle's back tire where it meets the pavement.
choices.C: You should leave exactly 15 feet of space between vehicles.
choices.D: You should be close enough to read the expiration date on their license plate.

en.explanation: A basic rule of thumb is that you should be able to see the license plate and/or the other vehicle's back tire where it meets the pavement to provide a safety zone.

en.question: How must a driver respond to a flashing red traffic light?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.B: Yield to traffic on the right, but a stop is not required.
choices.C: Come to a complete stop, just as with a stop sign.
choices.D: Stop only if pedestrians are present in the crosswalk.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'A complete stop is required at a flashing red traffic light, just as with a stop sign.'

en.question: How do most law enforcement officers and driver education instructors define a complete stop?

choices.A: When the speedometer reads exactly zero for three seconds.
choices.B: When the driver feels the car lurch forward after all motion has ceased.
choices.C: When the vehicle has slowed to less than 5 mph.
choices.D: When the driver shifts the vehicle into park.

en.explanation: Most law enforcement officers and instructors agree that a vehicle has not come to a complete stop until the driver feels the car lurch forward after all motion has ceased.

en.question: When approaching a railroad crossing and a train is coming, where must you stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Between 10 and 30 feet from the railroad tracks
choices.B: Between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks
choices.C: Exactly 50 feet from the railroad tracks
choices.D: At least 100 feet from the railroad tracks

en.explanation: When you approach a railroad crossing and a train is coming, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks.

en.question: At what approximate distance are trains required to signal their horn before passing through a railroad crossing?

choices.A: 500 feet
choices.B: 1,000 feet
choices.C: 1,500 feet
choices.D: 2,000 feet

en.explanation: Trains are required to signal a horn when they are approximately 1,500 feet from passing through a railroad crossing.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is required by Tennessee law to stop before crossing ANY railroad grade crossing, even if no signs or signals are activated?

choices.A: Any passenger vehicle carrying children
choices.B: Church or school buses, regardless of whether they are carrying passengers
choices.C: All commercial delivery trucks
choices.D: Any vehicle towing a trailer

en.explanation: Church or school buses are required by law to stop before crossing ANY railroad grade crossing, regardless of whether such buses are carrying any passengers at the time.

en.question: How does the Tennessee Code define a 'stop'?

choices.A: Slowing down to a speed of less than 3 mph
choices.B: Complete cessation of movement
choices.C: Pausing for at least two seconds
choices.D: Yielding to all oncoming traffic

en.explanation: Tennessee Code defines 'stop' as 'complete cessation of movement.'

en.question: If an intersection has a marked crosswalk for pedestrians, where must you stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Inside the crosswalk to get a better view of traffic
choices.B: Just past the crosswalk
choices.C: Before the front of your vehicle reaches the nearest white line marking the border of the crosswalk
choices.D: Even with the stop sign, regardless of the crosswalk lines

en.explanation: If the intersection has a crosswalk marked on the pavement, you must stop before the front of your vehicle reaches the nearest white line marking the border of the crosswalk.

en.question: According to the manual's example, what is the total stopping distance for a vehicle traveling at 70 m.p.h. on a good road in good weather after a hazard suddenly appears?

choices.A: 128 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 290 feet
choices.D: 418 feet

en.explanation: At 70 m.p.h., you travel 128 feet before braking, and the braking distance is 290 feet, making the total stopping distance 418 feet.

en.question: Which of the following is a potential consequence of making a 'rolling stop'?

choices.A: Failing the driver examination road test
choices.B: Receiving a traffic ticket
choices.C: Being held completely liable by police and insurance companies in the event of a crash
choices.D: All of the above

en.explanation: Rolling stops are grounds for receiving a traffic ticket, failing the road test, and being held completely liable in the event of a crash.

en.question: What is the penalty for not stopping for a stopped school bus?

choices.A: Class B misdemeanor and a $100 fine
choices.B: Class C misdemeanor and a $50 fine
choices.C: Class A misdemeanor and a fine between $250 and $1,000
choices.D: Felony and a fine of $2,000

en.explanation: The manual states that it is a Class A misdemeanor and the driver can be fined between $250 and $1,000 for not stopping for a stopped school bus.

en.question: When driving on a highway with a shared center turn lane (a fifth lane), what must you do when meeting a stopped school bus with red flashing lights?

choices.A: Proceed with caution without stopping
choices.B: Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus
choices.C: Slow down to 15 mph and proceed
choices.D: Stop in both directions because a turn lane is not considered a barrier

en.explanation: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is NOT considered a barrier. Drivers meeting a stopped school bus on this type of road would be required to stop in both directions.

en.question: What do yellow flashing lights on the front and back of a school bus indicate?

choices.A: The bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children
choices.B: The bus has stopped and children are getting on or off
choices.C: The bus is experiencing mechanical difficulties
choices.D: The bus is backing up

en.explanation: When the yellow lights on the front and back of the bus are flashing, the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children. Motorists should slow down and prepare to stop.

en.question: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load and unload children, which drivers are required to stop?

choices.A: Only drivers behind the bus
choices.B: Only drivers approaching from the opposite direction
choices.C: Drivers from ALL directions
choices.D: Only drivers turning onto the street where the bus is stopped

en.explanation: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load and unload children, drivers from ALL directions are required to stop until the bus resumes motion.

en.question: If you are pulled over by a police officer after dark, what should you do before the officer approaches?

choices.A: Turn off your headlights
choices.B: Turn on your vehicle's interior light
choices.C: Step out of the vehicle to greet the officer
choices.D: Honk your horn to acknowledge the stop

en.explanation: The manual advises that if the stop is made after dark, you should turn on the vehicle's interior light before the officer approaches.

en.question: What should you do if you are directed to pull over by an UNMARKED police car at night and feel unsafe?

choices.A: Speed up to get away from the unmarked car
choices.B: Stop immediately in the middle of the road
choices.C: Drive slowly a short distance to the nearest populated area
choices.D: Refuse to pull over until a marked car arrives

en.explanation: If directed to pull over by an UNMARKED police car, you may drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people, such as a business parking lot or the next exit.

en.question: When stopped by a police officer, drivers should:

choices.A: Keep their hands hidden until asked to show them
choices.B: Keep their hands on the steering wheel
choices.C: Immediately reach into the glove compartment for their registration
choices.D: Exit the vehicle to inspect the rear of the car

en.explanation: During a traffic stop, drivers should keep their hands on the steering wheel and passengers should keep their hands in plain view.

en.question: According to the Left-Right-Left Rule for intersections, where should you look first?

choices.A: To the right
choices.B: To the left
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: In your rearview mirror

en.explanation: The Left-Right-Left Rule states you should look first to the left to make sure cross traffic is yielding the right-of-way, then look right, and then left again.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding lane changes and passing at an intersection?

choices.A: You may pass a vehicle in an intersection if the light is green
choices.B: You should make last-minute lane changes as you start through an intersection
choices.C: You must NOT pass a vehicle in an intersection
choices.D: You can change lanes in an intersection if you use your turn signal

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Do NOT make last minute lane changes as you start through an intersection. Do NOT pass a vehicle in an intersection."

en.question: What percentage of all motor vehicle crashes are implicated at intersections?

choices.A: 10 percent
choices.B: 21 percent
choices.C: 33 percent
choices.D: 50 percent

en.explanation: Intersections constitute a very small part of the street/highway systems, yet they are implicated in 33 percent of all motor vehicle crashes.

en.question: Which of the following best describes the law regarding the right-of-way?

choices.A: The law gives the right-of-way to the largest vehicle
choices.B: The law does not give anyone the right-of-way, it only says who must yield
choices.C: The law gives the right-of-way to the vehicle traveling the fastest
choices.D: The law gives the right-of-way to pedestrians in all situations regardless of traffic signals

en.explanation: The law does not really give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must yield the right-of-way. Think of the right-of-way as something to be given, not taken.

en.question: Under what condition are you NOT required to stop for a stopped school bus with red flashing lights?

choices.A: When traveling on a two-lane road in the opposite direction
choices.B: When you are running late for work
choices.C: When driving on a highway with separate roadways divided by a barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic
choices.D: When the bus is stopped at an intersection

en.explanation: When driving on a highway with separate roadways for traffic in opposite directions, divided by median space or a barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic, the driver need not stop, but should proceed with caution.

en.question: Is it legal to move into an intersection and block it after the traffic lights have changed?

choices.A: Yes, if you entered the intersection while the light was yellow
choices.B: Yes, if there are no signs posted advising 'Do Not Block Intersection'
choices.C: No, it is always illegal to block an intersection, whether marked or not
choices.D: No, unless you are driving a commercial vehicle

en.explanation: It is not only common sense, but it’s also illegal to block an intersection after the light has changed. It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether it is marked or not.

en.question: If you have a handgun permit and are armed when stopped by a police officer, you should:

choices.A: Hide the weapon under the seat
choices.B: Advise the officer that you have a permit and are armed
choices.C: Hand the weapon to the officer immediately
choices.D: Wait until the officer asks if you have a weapon before mentioning it

en.explanation: The manual states that drivers should advise officers if they have a handgun permit and if they are armed.

en.question: According to Tennessee law, who is legally given the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver who reaches the intersection first
choices.B: Pedestrians in all situations
choices.C: The law does not give anyone the right-of-way; it only says who must yield
choices.D: The vehicle on the right

en.explanation: The manual states that the law does not really give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must yield the right-of-way.

en.question: When a blind or visually impaired pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is crossing the roadway, you must stop at least how far away?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 20 feet

en.explanation: You must take special precautions to avoid injury to a blind or visually impaired pedestrian and stop at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway.

en.question: How can a driver identify a hearing impaired pedestrian who requires special right-of-way precautions?

choices.A: They are carrying a white cane with a red tip
choices.B: They are wearing a reflective yellow vest
choices.C: They are accompanied by a dog on a blaze orange leash
choices.D: They are using a motorized wheelchair

en.explanation: The manual specifies that you must yield to a hearing impaired person with a dog on a blaze orange leash crossing any portion of the roadway.

en.question: When is it legal to drive your vehicle on a sidewalk?

choices.A: When avoiding a traffic jam
choices.B: When parking your vehicle in a crowded downtown area
choices.C: Only when crossing it to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot
choices.D: It is never legal to drive on a sidewalk under any circumstances

en.explanation: It is illegal to drive on a sidewalk except to cross it, such as when entering or exiting a driveway, alley, or parking lot.

en.question: At a "T" intersection where one road dead-ends into another main crossing roadway, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the road that ends must yield to traffic on the main road
choices.B: The vehicles on the main road must yield to the vehicle on the road that ends
choices.C: The vehicle that arrives at the intersection first
choices.D: The vehicle making a right turn

en.explanation: At "T" intersections where one road dead-ends into another main crossing roadway, the vehicles on the road ending must yield to oncoming traffic from both directions on the main road.

en.question: What should you do if traffic in front of you is backed up and you cannot get completely through an intersection?

choices.A: Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear
choices.B: Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection
choices.C: Proceed slowly and honk your horn
choices.D: Move into the intersection and turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get through it without having to stop. You should wait until traffic in front of you clears so that you are not blocking the intersection.

en.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with a siren or flashing lights is approaching?

choices.A: Stop immediately in your current lane
choices.B: Speed up to stay ahead of the emergency vehicle
choices.C: Drive to a position parallel to and as close as possible to the right hand edge or curb and stop
choices.D: Pull over to the left side of the road and slow down

en.explanation: Tennessee law requires that when an emergency vehicle is approaching, all traffic must yield the right-of-way and immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to the right hand edge or curb of the roadway and stop.

en.question: If you are in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on, what should you do?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection
choices.B: Drive on through the intersection before pulling over to the right
choices.C: Put your vehicle in reverse and back out of the intersection
choices.D: Pull over to the left side of the intersection

en.explanation: If you are in an intersection, drive on through the intersection before pulling over, or you may block the emergency vehicle's path through the intersection.

en.question: Under Tennessee's Move Over Law, what must you do when approaching a stationary emergency or utility vehicle with flashing lights on a multi-lane road?

choices.A: Stop your vehicle and wait for the stationary vehicle to move
choices.B: Make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to the vehicle, or proceed with caution by reducing speed
choices.C: Maintain your speed and honk your horn to alert the workers
choices.D: Pull over to the shoulder and turn on your hazard lights

en.explanation: Tennessee's Move Over Law requires that when approaching any stationary emergency vehicle with lights flashing, you must make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to that of the vehicle, or proceed with caution by reducing the speed of the vehicle.

en.question: Are you required to stop for a transit bus (metro bus) that is stopped for passenger pick-up or drop-off?

choices.A: Yes, you must stop just as you would for a school bus
choices.B: Yes, but only if the bus has its hazard lights flashing
choices.C: No, you are not required to stop or forbidden to pass
choices.D: No, unless the bus is in a designated school zone

en.explanation: You are not required to stop for, nor forbidden to pass, transit buses when they are stopped for passenger pick-up or drop-off as you would be for a school bus in the same situation.

en.question: Which of the following actions is illegal regarding fire trucks or emergency vehicles responding to an emergency?

choices.A: Yielding the right-of-way to them at an intersection
choices.B: Following a fire truck responding to a fire alarm
choices.C: Turning down your radio volume when they approach
choices.D: Pulling over to the right curb when they approach

en.explanation: It is against the law to follow a fire truck or other emergency vehicle responding to a fire alarm or other emergency.

en.question: What is the first rule of turning?

choices.A: Turn from the closest lane in the direction you are traveling to the closest legal lane in the direction you want to go
choices.B: Always turn into the far left lane
choices.C: Signal for at least 50 feet before making the turn
choices.D: Honk your horn before initiating the turn

en.explanation: The first rule of turning is to turn from the closest lane in the direction you are traveling to the closest legal lane in the direction you want to go.

en.question: Which of the following is illegal for an unauthorized private vehicle to have installed or visibly shown?

choices.A: A white flashing light
choices.B: A yellow flashing emergency light
choices.C: A blue flashing emergency light or combination of blue and red
choices.D: A green flashing light

en.explanation: It is against the law for an unauthorized private vehicle to have a blue flashing emergency light or combination of blue and red flashing emergency lights installed, maintained or visibly shown on the vehicle in any manner.

en.question: If you have a green traffic light, but another vehicle is already in the intersection, what must you do?

choices.A: Proceed through the intersection since you have the right-of-way
choices.B: Honk your horn to force the other vehicle to move
choices.C: Yield to the vehicle already in the intersection
choices.D: Swerve around the vehicle to maintain traffic flow

en.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green traffic light.

en.question: How far in advance must you turn on your turn signal lights before making a turn?

choices.A: At least 25 feet
choices.B: At least 50 feet
choices.C: At least 100 feet
choices.D: At least 200 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that at least 50 feet before the turn, you must turn on your turn signal lights.

en.question: Does using your turn signal give you the right-of-way to change lanes or turn?

choices.A: Yes, if you signal at least 50 feet in advance.
choices.B: Yes, but only when entering a parking lot.
choices.C: No, signaling does NOT give you the right-of-way.
choices.D: No, unless you are using hand signals.

en.explanation: Your signal lets other drivers know your intentions to make a change in your vehicle's path of travel, but the manual explicitly states that signaling does NOT give you the right-of-way.

en.question: Why should you keep your vehicle's wheels straight while waiting to make a turn?

choices.A: It helps the power steering fluid circulate.
choices.B: It prevents your tires from wearing out unevenly.
choices.C: If you are hit from the rear, the impact could push you into oncoming traffic.
choices.D: It allows you to accelerate faster when the light turns green.

en.explanation: The manual warns not to turn your wheels in the direction of the turn while waiting for oncoming traffic to pass. If you are hit from the rear while your wheels are turned, the impact can push you into oncoming traffic.

en.question: If you plan to turn into a driveway just beyond an intersection, when should you signal?

choices.A: At least 50 feet before the intersection.
choices.B: Do not signal until you are in the intersection.
choices.C: Right as you begin to turn the steering wheel.
choices.D: You do not need to signal for driveways.

en.explanation: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal until you are in the intersection. If you signal earlier, another driver may think you intend to turn at the intersection and might pull into your path.

en.question: Under what weather condition does the manual specifically recommend using hand signals because your vehicle's signal lights might be hard to see?

choices.A: Heavy rain
choices.B: Dense fog
choices.C: When the sun is shining brightly
choices.D: During a snowstorm

en.explanation: Hand signals should be used when the sun is shining brightly. This makes your turn signal light harder for other drivers to see easily.

en.question: You should NOT use your turn signals to:

choices.A: Indicate you are pulling away from a parked position.
choices.B: Signal a driver behind you to come around and pass your vehicle.
choices.C: Show you are entering the interstate.
choices.D: Indicate you are slowing down suddenly.

en.explanation: The manual states you should NOT use your signals to signal a driver behind you to come around to pass your vehicle, as this is misleading to other drivers.

en.question: Why should you avoid shifting gears while in the intersection?

choices.A: It causes excessive wear on the clutch.
choices.B: It is illegal and carries a heavy fine.
choices.C: You could stall, causing an accident or blocking the intersection.
choices.D: It makes your turn signal turn off automatically.

en.explanation: The manual advises: "Don't shift gears in the intersection (If you stall you could cause an accident and/or block the intersection to other traffic)."

en.question: How can you attract attention with your brake lights when signaling a stop?

choices.A: Turn your hazard lights on.
choices.B: Lightly pump your brakes a few times.
choices.C: Press the brake pedal to the floor immediately.
choices.D: Shift into neutral before braking.

en.explanation: When signaling a stop, you should lightly pump your brakes a few times to attract attention with your brake lights.

en.question: When you meet another driver at an intersection and both of you want to turn left, how should you proceed?

choices.A: Each driver will turn to the right of the other.
choices.B: The driver who arrived first has the right-of-way to turn first.
choices.C: Each driver will turn to the left of the other.
choices.D: Both drivers must wait for a green arrow.

en.explanation: When you meet another driver at an intersection and both of you want to turn left, each will turn to the left of the other.

en.question: What color are the center lines on one-way streets?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: White
choices.C: Red
choices.D: Blue

en.explanation: According to the manual, center lines on two-way streets are yellow, while center lines on one-way streets are white.

en.question: What should you do with your arm when using a hand signal during the actual turn?

choices.A: Keep it fully extended until the turn is complete.
choices.B: Wave it in a circular motion.
choices.C: Bring your arm in to keep control of the steering wheel.
choices.D: Point to the lane you are turning into.

en.explanation: When you use hand signals, you should bring your arm in during the actual turn to keep control of the steering wheel.

en.question: What is a potential danger of forgetting to turn off your turn signal after using it?

choices.A: It will drain your vehicle's battery.
choices.B: It might tempt other drivers to pull out in front of you.
choices.C: It will cause your brake lights to stop working.
choices.D: It will automatically engage your emergency brake.

en.explanation: An unintended signal still means "turn" to other drivers. By leaving it on, you might tempt other drivers to pull out in front of you.

en.question: When making a routine left turn from a two-way street onto another two-way street, where should you drive just after entering the new street?

choices.A: Into the far right lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Just to the right of the center line in the first lane past the center line.
choices.C: Directly on top of the center line.
choices.D: Into any available lane that is free of traffic.

en.explanation: Drive just to the right of the center line of the street you're entering and be sure to turn into the first lane past the center line. This avoids conflict with other traffic making either right or left turns.

en.question: If you are waiting to make a left turn and the traffic light turns yellow while you are waiting for oncoming vehicles to clear, what should you do?

choices.A: Accelerate quickly to beat the red light.
choices.B: Proceed into the intersection immediately.
choices.C: DO NOT proceed into the intersection.
choices.D: Back up into the crosswalk.

en.explanation: The manual states: "If the light turns yellow while you are waiting for oncoming vehicles to clear the intersection, DO NOT proceed into the intersection."

en.question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

choices.A: The lane furthest to the right.
choices.B: The center lane.
choices.C: The first lane closest to the left curb.
choices.D: Any lane that is currently open.

en.explanation: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street, the manual instructs to 'Turn sharply into the FIRST lane... You should turn into the first lane closest to the left curb.'

en.question: Under what condition is a left turn permitted at a red light in Tennessee?

choices.A: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
choices.B: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
choices.C: When turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street.
choices.D: Left turns on red are never permitted.

en.explanation: A left turn at a red light is permitted at all intersections where a one-way street intersects with another one-way street, provided you come to a complete stop first and there are no signs prohibiting it.

en.question: Can you make a left turn on a red light when turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street?

choices.A: Yes, after coming to a complete stop.
choices.B: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.C: No, you CANNOT make this left turn on a red light.
choices.D: Yes, but only between the hours of midnight and 6 AM.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states regarding turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street: 'You CANNOT make this left turn on a red light.'

en.question: How far ahead of a right turn must you give a turn signal?

choices.A: At least 25 feet.
choices.B: At least 50 feet.
choices.C: At least 100 feet.
choices.D: At least 200 feet.

en.explanation: The manual states that you must 'Give a signal for a right turn for at least 50 feet.'

en.question: Why should you avoid swinging wide to the left before or during a right turn?

choices.A: It will cause your steering wheel to lock.
choices.B: The driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or turning left and try to pass you on the right.
choices.C: It is illegal to cross the white line.
choices.D: It will cause you to enter a roundabout.

en.explanation: If you swing wide to the left on a right turn, 'the driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or turning left and may try to pass you on the right.'

en.question: Why should you avoid passing a large truck on the right if there is a possibility it might make a right turn?

choices.A: Trucks accelerate faster than cars.
choices.B: Trucks must make wide turns and sometimes leave an open space to the right just before the turn.
choices.C: Trucks are not allowed to use turn signals.
choices.D: Trucks always have the right-of-way at intersections.

en.explanation: Large trucks and buses MUST make wide turns and sometimes leave an open space to the right just before the turn. Passing on the right can cause an accident.

en.question: In which direction must you always travel around a roundabout?

choices.A: Clockwise.
choices.B: Counter-clockwise (to the right).
choices.C: In a straight line through the center.
choices.D: Whichever direction has less traffic.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'Always travel around a roundabout to the right, in a counter-clockwise direction.'

en.question: What is the rule regarding passing other vehicles in a multi-lane roundabout?

choices.A: You may pass on the left only.
choices.B: You may pass on the right only.
choices.C: You may pass if the vehicle ahead is traveling under 15 mph.
choices.D: Do not overtake or pass any vehicles.

en.explanation: In a multi-lane roundabout, the manual explicitly states: 'do not overtake or pass any vehicles.'

en.question: You may NOT make a U-turn at any location where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1000 feet

en.explanation: You may not make a U-turn at any rural or urban location, or near a curve or hill crest, where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least 500 feet.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate highway in Tennessee?

choices.A: Use the emergency crossover in the median to turn around.
choices.B: Make a U-turn when the highway is clear.
choices.C: Drive on to the next exit ramp.
choices.D: Back up carefully on the shoulder.

en.explanation: It is illegal to make a U-turn on an interstate or use emergency crossovers. The manual advises: 'Drive on to the next exit ramp.'

en.question: Which phrase summarizes the principle of 'right hand traffic' on American roadways?

choices.A: Yellow on your right, white on your left
choices.B: White on your right, yellow on your left
choices.C: Keep right except to turn right
choices.D: Pass on the right, drive on the left

en.explanation: The manual states the overview of lane usage is summed up by the simple statement: 'White on your right, yellow on your left.'

en.question: What is the center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway used for?

choices.A: Passing slow-moving vehicles.
choices.B: Emergency parking only.
choices.C: Turning left only.
choices.D: Turning right only.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'The center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for turning left.'

en.question: Is it legal to make a U-turn at an intersection where a traffic light or police officer is controlling the traffic flow?

choices.A: Yes, if you have a green light.
choices.B: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.C: No, you may not make a U-turn at these intersections.
choices.D: Yes, but only in rural areas.

en.explanation: The manual lists locations where you may NOT make a U-turn, including: 'At any intersection where a traffic light or police officer is controlling the traffic flow.'

en.question: How should you indicate your intention to exit a roundabout?

choices.A: Flash your headlights.
choices.B: Use your left turn signal.
choices.C: Use your right turn signal.
choices.D: Sound your horn.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'Exit the roundabout carefully. Always indicate your exit using your right turn signal.'

en.question: On a four-lane highway, where should you generally drive?

choices.A: In the extreme left lane at all times
choices.B: In the extreme right lane except when passing or making a left turn
choices.C: In whichever lane has the least amount of traffic
choices.D: Straddling the dashed white line to maintain visibility

en.explanation: According to the manual, on a four-lane highway, you should 'Drive in the extreme right lane except when passing another vehicle or making a left turn.'

en.question: When attempting to use a designated crossover on a divided four-lane highway, what should you do if another vehicle is already in the crossover waiting for traffic to clear?

choices.A: Swing into the left side of the crossover next to the waiting vehicle
choices.B: Bunch up closely behind the waiting car inside the crossover
choices.C: Remain stopped in the left-most lane of the highway with your turn signal on
choices.D: Proceed to the next intersection to make a U-turn

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If a vehicle is already in the crossover waiting for traffic to clear, remain stopped in the left most lane of the four-lane highway with your turn signal on until the waiting vehicle has cleared the crossover.'

en.question: What does it mean if you see red reflectors facing you on the lane lines or edge lines of the road?

choices.A: You are approaching a construction zone
choices.B: You are facing traffic the wrong way and could have a head-on collision
choices.C: You are entering a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane
choices.D: The speed limit is reducing ahead

en.explanation: The manual warns: 'Red reflectors always mean you are facing traffic the wrong way and could have a head-on collision.'

en.question: What is the maximum distance you are permitted to travel in a shared center turn lane?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual specifies that shared center turn lanes 'cannot be used for passing and cannot be used for travel farther than 300 feet.'

en.question: If two vehicles enter a shared center turn lane from opposite directions at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle traveling at a higher speed
choices.B: The vehicle making a right turn
choices.C: The larger of the two vehicles
choices.D: The first vehicle to enter the lane

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'When vehicles enter the turn lane from opposite directions, the first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way.'

en.question: How are reversible lanes usually marked on the roadway?

choices.A: By double-broken yellow lines
choices.B: By solid white lines on both sides
choices.C: By a single solid yellow line
choices.D: By alternating red and white reflectors

en.explanation: The manual states that reversible lanes 'are usually marked by double-broken yellow lines.'

en.question: When driving in a reversible lane, what does a flashing yellow 'X' overhead mean?

choices.A: You cannot drive in the lane below
choices.B: The lane is only for turning
choices.C: The direction of the lane is changing
choices.D: You can drive straight ahead in the lane

en.explanation: The manual explains that 'A flashing yellow “X” means the lane is only for turning.'

en.question: What action should you take if you see a steady yellow 'X' over a reversible lane?

choices.A: Speed up to clear the lane quickly
choices.B: Stop immediately in the lane
choices.C: Move out of the lane as soon as it is safe to do so
choices.D: Use the lane for passing only

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'A steady yellow “X” means that the use/direction of the lane is changing and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe to do so.'

en.question: What does a sign reading 'HOV 2' indicate about a reserved lane?

choices.A: The lane is reserved for vehicles with at least two people in them
choices.B: The lane is reserved for heavy commercial vehicles only
choices.C: The lane is closed for the next two miles
choices.D: Only hybrid or electric vehicles may use the lane

en.explanation: The manual states: 'For example, “HOV 2” means there must be at least two people in the vehicle for you to legally drive in that lane.'

en.question: Why is it essential to look over your shoulder before changing lanes?

choices.A: To check the speed of the vehicle behind you
choices.B: To ensure your turn signal is functioning properly
choices.C: To check your blind spots for vehicles that cannot be seen in your mirrors
choices.D: To communicate your intentions to other drivers

en.explanation: The manual explains that a driver 'cannot see the motorcycle or other car just by checking his mirrors. He would need to physically turn his head and look over his shoulder in each direction to see those vehicles next to him' to check blind spots.

en.question: What should you do if a driver ahead of you signals their intention to change lanes?

choices.A: Speed up to pass them before they change lanes
choices.B: Slow down and leave space for the change
choices.C: Change lanes yourself to get out of their way
choices.D: Honk your horn to warn them not to move

en.explanation: The manual advises: 'When a driver ahead of you (in your lane or the lane next to you) signals a lane change, slow down and leave space for the change. Do NOT speed up or change lanes yourself...'

en.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on a two-lane road, what is a good rule regarding oncoming traffic?

choices.A: If you see any sign of an oncoming vehicle, it is too close for you to risk a pass
choices.B: You may pass if the oncoming vehicle is more than 100 feet away
choices.C: Flash your headlights so the oncoming vehicle slows down
choices.D: Accelerate rapidly to beat the oncoming vehicle

en.explanation: The manual states: 'As a rule, if you see any sign of an oncoming vehicle, it is too close for you to risk a pass. When in doubt, stay in your lane.'

en.question: Why should you stay well behind a vehicle you want to pass before initiating the maneuver?

choices.A: To build up enough speed to pass quickly
choices.B: To allow yourself a better view of the road ahead
choices.C: To avoid being hit by debris kicked up by their tires
choices.D: To hide in their blind spot until you are ready to pass

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to 'Stay well behind the vehicle you want to pass to allow yourself a better view of the road ahead.'

en.question: Why should you avoid swinging out across the center line just to get a look before passing?

choices.A: It is illegal to cross the center line under any circumstances
choices.B: It indicates you are either following too closely or attempting to pass unsafely
choices.C: It will cause your vehicle to lose traction
choices.D: It confuses drivers behind you into thinking you are turning left

en.explanation: The manual warns: 'Do NOT swing out across the center line for a look. If you need to do this to see, you are either following too closely or attempting to pass.'

en.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding crossovers on interstates?

choices.A: They can be used for U-turns if the median is paved
choices.B: They are reserved for high-occupancy vehicles only
choices.C: There are no crossovers provided for traffic on interstates
choices.D: They should be treated the same as a cross street

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'There are NO crossovers provided for traffic on interstates.'

en.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?

choices.A: When you are 50 feet ahead of the vehicle.
choices.B: As soon as you pass the front bumper of the vehicle.
choices.C: When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.
choices.D: When the driver you passed flashes their headlights.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Complete your pass as soon as possible. When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rear view mirror, signal right and return to your lane.'

en.question: In Tennessee, is it illegal to pass multiple vehicles at the same time?

choices.A: Yes, it is strictly prohibited by law.
choices.B: No, it is not illegal, but it is generally not recommended.
choices.C: Yes, unless you are on a multi-lane highway.
choices.D: No, it is the recommended way to pass slow-moving traffic.

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'As a general rule, it is NOT SAFE to pass more than one vehicle at a time, although it is not illegal in Tennessee to pass multiple vehicles. It is recommended that you not even consider passing multiple vehicles unless...'

en.question: Under which of the following conditions is passing on the right permitted?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead has signaled to make a left turn.
choices.B: When you use the paved shoulder of the highway.
choices.C: When you use a designated bike lane to bypass traffic.
choices.D: When the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit on a two-lane road.

en.explanation: Passing on the right is permitted 'When the vehicle overtaken has signaled to make or is about to make a left turn.' Passing off the pavement or in a bike lane is never permitted.

en.question: When are you allowed to pass a vehicle on the right using an emergency lane or parking lane?

choices.A: When the vehicle ahead is stopped for a red light.
choices.B: When you are within sight of a traffic light or stop sign.
choices.C: When the vehicle ahead is turning left.
choices.D: You are never allowed to pass on the right using a parking or emergency lane.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Do NOT pass on the right using a bike lane or parking lane at any location, nor in the emergency lane within sight of a traffic light or stop sign.'

en.question: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, how far before the crosswalk should you stop?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 30 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: According to the Safety Tip in the manual: 'When stopping for a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, you should stop about 30 feet before the crosswalk so you do not block visibility of the crossing pedestrians to drivers in the other lane(s).'

en.question: What does the end of a 'no-passing zone' indicate?

choices.A: It is automatically safe to pass.
choices.B: There is increased visibility ahead, but you must still determine if it is safe to pass.
choices.C: You are required to pass any slow-moving vehicles ahead.
choices.D: The speed limit increases.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'The end of a "no-passing zone" does not mean it is safe to pass. It means there is increased visibility ahead. It is still up to YOU to determine if it is safe to pass...'

en.question: Are you ever allowed to cross a solid yellow line marked on the pavement in a 'no-passing zone'?

choices.A: No, crossing a solid yellow line is never permitted.
choices.B: Yes, but only to pass a slow-moving tractor or bicycle.
choices.C: Yes, you may turn across the center line to enter or exit an alley, private road, or driveway.
choices.D: Yes, if you can complete the pass before oncoming traffic arrives.

en.explanation: The manual explains: 'You are allowed to turn across the center line if you are making a left turn into or coming out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway while in the "no-passing zone".'

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle is passing you and you observe an oncoming car approaching?

choices.A: Speed up so the passing vehicle can pull in behind you.
choices.B: Move to the left to block the passing vehicle.
choices.C: Slow down to allow the passing driver more space to pull back into the right lane.
choices.D: Sound your horn and maintain your current speed.

en.explanation: To help another driver pass safely, you should be 'Slowing down if you observe a car approaching from the other direction while you are being passed. By slowing down, you will allow the passing driver more space to pull back into the right lane...'

en.question: What is the minimum distance you must leave between your vehicle and a bicycle when passing them?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: The manual states: 'When passing and overtaking a bicyclist proceeding in the same direction, do so slowly and leave at least a distance between you and the bicycle of not less than 3 feet.'

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in a large truck or bus driver's blind spot while following them?

choices.A: You can see the driver's face in their rearview mirror.
choices.B: You cannot see the side mirrors on the truck or bus.
choices.C: You are following at a distance of more than 100 feet.
choices.D: You can see the entire trailer of the truck.

en.explanation: The manual provides an excellent point to remember: 'if you cannot see the side mirrors on the truck or bus you are following, then the truck or bus driver CANNOT SEE YOU.'

en.question: What is a dangerous mistake drivers often make after passing a large truck or bus?

choices.A: Accelerating too quickly after returning to the lane.
choices.B: Pulling in front of the truck or bus and slowing down.
choices.C: Canceling their turn signal too early.
choices.D: Leaving too much space between their car and the truck.

en.explanation: The manual instructs: 'Maintain your speed. NEVER pull in front of a truck or bus (or any type of vehicle) and slow down. This takes away the safety cushion of the driver you have just passed...'

en.question: How does traveling on a downgrade affect passing a large truck or bus?

choices.A: The truck will lose speed, making it easier to pass.
choices.B: The truck's momentum will cause it to go faster, so you may need to increase your speed to pass.
choices.C: The truck will be forced to pull over to the shoulder.
choices.D: Passing on a downgrade is strictly prohibited by law.

en.explanation: The manual explains that terrain matters: 'On a down grade, their momentum will cause them to go faster, so you may need to increase your speed to pass.'

en.question: What is the proper procedure when another driver is trying to pass you on the left?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from cutting in too sharply.
choices.B: Move to the left lane to block them if it is unsafe.
choices.C: Stay in your lane, move to the right, and maintain your speed.
choices.D: Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: When being passed, you should help the other driver by: 'Staying in your lane, and moving to the right if being passed on the left. Maintaining your speed. DO NOT speed up to keep the other driver from passing.'

en.question: Which of the following situations prohibits you from crossing the center line to pass?

choices.A: When approaching a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk.
choices.B: When the vehicle ahead is traveling 15 mph below the speed limit.
choices.C: When you are on a straight, level roadway with excellent vision.
choices.D: When the vehicle ahead is a bicycle.
