en.explanation: The manual lists several conditions where you may NOT cross the center line to pass, including: 'Do not pass a car that has stopped for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.'

en.question: When passing another vehicle, is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit?

choices.A: Yes, but only by a maximum of 5 mph.
choices.B: Yes, if you are passing a commercial truck with multiple trailers.
choices.C: No, it is illegal to exceed the posted speed limit even when passing.
choices.D: Yes, if you are on a downgrade and need to pass quickly.

en.explanation: The manual states: "Remember, it is illegal to exceed the speed posted speed limit even when passing other vehicles."

en.question: What is the proper way to look behind you when backing up your vehicle?

choices.A: Depend solely on your rearview and side mirrors.
choices.B: Open the door and stick your head out to see.
choices.C: Place your arm on the back of the seat and turn around to look directly through the rear window.
choices.D: Honk your horn and back up quickly while checking the rearview mirror.

en.explanation: Before backing, you should place your arm on the back of the seat and turn around so that you can look directly through the rear window. The manual explicitly warns against depending solely on mirrors or opening the door to look out.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your turn or exit on the interstate?

choices.A: Stop and back up carefully on the shoulder.
choices.B: Put on your hazard lights and back up in the travel lane.
choices.C: Make a U-turn across the median.
choices.D: Go on to the next turn or exit where you can safely and legally turn around.

en.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do NOT back up, but go on to the next turn or exit or where you can safely and legally turn around. It is illegal to back up on the interstate.

en.question: When parking adjacent to a roadway outside the city limits, your vehicle must be visible for at least how many feet in either direction?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: When parking adjacent to a roadway outside the city limits, your vehicle must be visible for at least 200 feet in either direction.

en.question: When parking outside city limits, you must ensure you leave at least how much road width for other traffic to pass your parked vehicle?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 12 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 18 feet

en.explanation: No matter what, you must ensure that you leave at least 18 feet of road width for other traffic to pass your parked vehicle when parking adjacent to a roadway outside city limits.

en.question: Which way should you turn your front wheels when parking on an uphill with a curb?

choices.A: Toward the curb (right)
choices.B: Away from the curb (left)
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: Parallel to the curb

en.explanation: On an uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb (left). This way, if the car starts to roll back, it will roll into the curb and stop.

en.question: It is illegal to park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 50 feet

en.explanation: The manual lists "Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant" under the NO PARKING ZONES where it is illegal to park.

en.question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: It is illegal to park within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the crosswalk marked area.

en.question: Upon completion of a parallel parking maneuver, your vehicle should be no farther away from the curb than:

choices.A: 6 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 24 inches

en.explanation: Upon completion of your parallel parking maneuver, the vehicle should be no farther away from the curb than 18 inches.

en.question: If you cannot move your disabled vehicle off the highway, what is one way to warn other motorists?

choices.A: Stand in the road and wave your arms.
choices.B: Tie a handkerchief on the left door handle or antenna.
choices.C: Flash your headlights continuously.
choices.D: Sound your horn every 10 seconds.

en.explanation: If you cannot move the vehicle off the highway, raise the hood or tie a handkerchief on the left door handle or antenna to warn other motorists of your stopped vehicle.

en.question: What should you do with your vehicle's transmission when parking a car with a manual transmission?

choices.A: Leave it in neutral and apply the parking brake.
choices.B: Leave it in park.
choices.C: Leave the vehicle in gear and set the parking brake.
choices.D: Leave it in neutral without the parking brake.

en.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you park. Leave the vehicle in gear if it has a manual transmission, or in park if it has an automatic transmission.

en.question: Is it legal to back into an intersection from a driveway?

choices.A: Yes, if you look both ways first.
choices.B: Yes, but only during daylight hours.
choices.C: No, it is illegal to back into an intersection from a driveway.
choices.D: No, unless you have a passenger guiding you.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "It is illegal to back into an intersection from a driveway."

en.question: What does the driver's manual state regarding walking on the interstate?

choices.A: It is allowed as long as you stay on the shoulder.
choices.B: It is legal only during daylight hours.
choices.C: It is both illegal and dangerous.
choices.D: It is recommended if your car breaks down and you need gas.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that walking on the interstate is both illegal and dangerous, and you should remain in your disabled vehicle until help arrives.

en.question: What is the penalty for improperly parking in a designated handicap space?

choices.A: A $50 fine and a written warning.
choices.B: A misdemeanor punishable by a $100 fine and the vehicle may be towed.
choices.C: A felony punishable by a $500 fine.
choices.D: Immediate license suspension for 30 days.

en.explanation: Improperly parking in designated handicap spaces is a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 fine, and the vehicle could be subject to being towed.

en.question: When backing out of an angle parking space, what should you remember about the front of your car?

choices.A: It will swing in the same direction as the turn.
choices.B: It will swing opposite to the direction of the turn.
choices.C: It will move straight back without swinging.
choices.D: It will swing toward the nearest curb.

en.explanation: Before backing out of an angle parking space, you must remember that the front of your car will swing opposite to the direction of the turn.

en.question: When passing a bicycle traveling in the same direction, motorists are required by law to allow a minimum distance of:

choices.A: 1 foot
choices.B: 2 feet
choices.C: 3 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: Motorists are required by law when passing a bicycle traveling in the same direction to allow a minimum distance of 3 feet.

en.question: When entering an interstate, what is the proper use of the acceleration lane?

choices.A: To park your vehicle in an emergency.
choices.B: To stop and wait for a large gap in traffic.
choices.C: To speed up and merge with fast-moving traffic.
choices.D: To allow interstate traffic a place to exit.

en.explanation: When entering an interstate, you must use the merging or acceleration lane to speed up and merge with fast-moving traffic already on the interstate.

en.question: Who has the right-of-way when you are attempting to enter the interstate from an on-ramp?

choices.A: The vehicle entering the interstate.
choices.B: Other cars already traveling on the interstate.
choices.C: Whichever vehicle is traveling faster.
choices.D: The vehicle on the right.

en.explanation: It is your responsibility to yield the right-of-way to other cars already on the interstate when you are entering.

en.question: What does a 'lane added' sign indicate to drivers already traveling on the interstate?

choices.A: They must merge left immediately.
choices.B: They should avoid making lane changes to the right at this location.
choices.C: They must yield to all entering traffic.
choices.D: The interstate is ending and they must exit.

en.explanation: The 'lane added' sign means a new right lane is added for incoming traffic. Traffic on the interstate should avoid making lane changes to the right because entering traffic will not expect vehicles to move into their path.

en.question: On interstates with several lanes traveling in the same direction, the extreme left lane should be used for:

choices.A: Entering traffic.
choices.B: Exiting traffic.
choices.C: Slower vehicles.
choices.D: Faster traffic.

en.explanation: On interstates with several lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction, you should leave the extreme left lane for faster traffic.

en.question: What is the minimum recommended following distance on the interstate in bad weather or at night?

choices.A: Two seconds
choices.B: Three seconds
choices.C: Four seconds
choices.D: Six seconds

en.explanation: You should stay at least two seconds behind vehicles in front of you, and increase this space to a minimum of four seconds in bad weather, night driving, and on higher speed rural sections.

en.question: How far ahead should you scan the roadway when driving on the interstate?

choices.A: 5-10 seconds
choices.B: 10-15 seconds
choices.C: 15-20 seconds
choices.D: 20-30 seconds

en.explanation: The manual advises to scan the roadway ahead and try to watch 15-20 seconds in front of your vehicle for cars braking, entering, or exiting.

en.question: If you spot a tie-up on the interstate causing you to slow down or stop, what should you do to alert drivers behind you?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams.
choices.B: Lightly tap your brake pedal several times.
choices.C: Sound your horn continuously.
choices.D: Swerve from side to side in your lane.

en.explanation: If you spot a tie-up causing you to slow down or stop, you should lightly tap your brake pedal several times to alert drivers behind you.

en.question: According to the manual's sample questions, the two-second rule for following at a safe distance holds true at:

choices.A: Speeds up to 30 m.p.h.
choices.B: Speeds up to 55 m.p.h.
choices.C: Any speed.
choices.D: Only highway speeds.

en.explanation: The sample test questions state that the two-second rule for following at a safe distance will hold true at any speed.

en.question: If you are going to exit the interstate, what is the safest way to prepare?

choices.A: Move to the right lane as early as possible to avoid hasty lane changes.
choices.B: Stay in the left lane until you reach the exit ramp.
choices.C: Speed up to pass slower traffic before cutting over to the exit.
choices.D: Stop in your lane and wait for a gap in the right lane.

en.explanation: If you are going to exit the interstate, move to the right lane as early as possible to avoid hasty lane changes, which could result in a dangerous situation.

en.question: What is the penalty for violating High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane rules?

choices.A: A $25 fine
choices.B: A $50 fine and court costs
choices.C: A $100 fine and 2 points on your license
choices.D: A $75 fine and mandatory traffic school

en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers found in violation of the HOV lane are subject to a $50 fine and court costs.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is permitted to use the High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane during peak traffic hours?

choices.A: A person driving alone to pass another vehicle
choices.B: A motorcycle occupied by one person
choices.C: A passenger car with only the driver
choices.D: A commercial truck with one driver

en.explanation: During high inbound and outbound traffic hours, the HOV lane is reserved for vehicles with 2 or more persons, buses with 2 or more occupants, motorcycles occupied by 1 person, and emergency vehicles.

en.question: If you are traveling in the left lane on an interstate and a vehicle comes up behind you at a faster speed, what should you do?

choices.A: Speed up to match their speed
choices.B: Tap your brakes to warn them to slow down
choices.C: Move one lane to your right
choices.D: Stay in your lane because you are driving the speed limit

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you are traveling in the left lane and someone comes up behind you at a faster speed, move one lane to your right. Left lane is for passing only.'

en.question: How do you make a left turn at a cloverleaf interchange?

choices.A: Take the left turn ramp before the overpass
choices.B: Take the right turn ramp just after the overpass
choices.C: Take the right turn ramp before the overpass
choices.D: Cross the path of traffic and turn left

en.explanation: At a cloverleaf interchange, all turns are right turns. To turn left, you must take the right turn just after the overpass.

en.question: When trucks and buses are entering the interstate, you should:

choices.A: Speed up to get past them quickly
choices.B: Honk your horn to let them know you are there
choices.C: Be cooperative and give them extra time and space to adjust to traffic flow
choices.D: Force them to yield by maintaining your speed and lane position

en.explanation: Remember that trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns. Be cooperative and give them extra time and space to adjust to the traffic flow.

en.question: When leaving the interstate, when should you begin to significantly reduce your speed?

choices.A: One mile before the exit
choices.B: As soon as you signal your intention to exit
choices.C: After you enter the deceleration lane
choices.D: While you are still in the main traffic lane

en.explanation: You should maintain your speed until you enter the deceleration lane, which is usually outlined by a series of white reflectors, and then reduce your speed to the exit ramp posted speed.

en.question: Under what condition is it legal to park a motor vehicle on the paved or unpaved portion of an interstate entrance or exit ramp?

choices.A: When you need to check your map or GPS
choices.B: Only if the vehicle is disabled
choices.C: When you need to make a phone call
choices.D: If you are waiting for another vehicle to catch up

en.explanation: It is illegal to park a motor vehicle upon the paved or unpaved portions of any entrance or exit ramp of any highway unless the vehicle is disabled.

en.question: What makes a 'weaving' interchange particularly hazardous?

choices.A: Traffic is both exiting and entering at the same lane
choices.B: The lanes are narrower than standard interstate lanes
choices.C: Drivers must make sharp left turns across traffic
choices.D: There are no speed limits posted on the ramps

en.explanation: One of the most hazardous lane management situations occurs when interstate traffic is both exiting and entering at the same lane, requiring complete attention and quick reactions.

en.question: Who is legally permitted to drive over or across the dividing section (median) of an interstate?

choices.A: Any driver who misses their exit
choices.B: Drivers of High Occupancy Vehicles (HOV)
choices.C: Only emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews
choices.D: Any driver during a severe traffic jam

en.explanation: On the interstate, you may NOT drive over or across any dividing section or separation. Only emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews may cross an interstate median.

en.question: What is the recommended practice regarding driving in the blind spots of other drivers on the interstate?

choices.A: Follow closely to the side so they can hear your engine
choices.B: Either stay behind or go around them
choices.C: Flash your headlights continuously while in the blind spot
choices.D: Maintain your speed and position regardless of their blind spot

en.explanation: Do not drive in the blind spot of other drivers. Traveling in a position where the driver ahead cannot see your vehicle is dangerous. Either stay behind or go around; do NOT follow to the side.

en.question: How are High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes utilized on weekends?

choices.A: They are closed to all traffic
choices.B: They are reserved strictly for emergency vehicles
choices.C: They serve as general purpose lanes for all vehicles
choices.D: They require three or more occupants instead of two

en.explanation: The HOV lane serves as a general purpose lane on weekends and during non-peak traffic times on weekdays.

en.question: According to the manual, why is night driving considered far more dangerous than day driving?

choices.A: Because speed limits are increased at night
choices.B: Because there are more commercial trucks on the road
choices.C: Due to fatigue, sharply reduced vision, and more drinking drivers
choices.D: Because interstate lighting is frequently turned off to save energy

en.explanation: Night driving is far more dangerous than day driving. Fatigue and sharply reduced vision are primarily responsible, and drinking drivers are more likely to be on the road at night.

en.question: How often should you stop and refresh yourself to help avoid interstate hypnosis?

choices.A: At least every 4 hours or 200 miles.
choices.B: At least every 2 hours or 100 miles.
choices.C: At least every 6 hours or 300 miles.
choices.D: Only when you need to refuel your vehicle.

en.explanation: To avoid interstate hypnosis, the manual recommends taking a break and getting out of the car at least every two hours, or every 100 miles or so.

en.question: To maintain safety on the road, what is the maximum number of hours you should drive per day?

choices.A: 6 hours
choices.B: 8 hours
choices.C: 10 hours
choices.D: 12 hours

en.explanation: The manual states that it is safest for you and others if you do not drive more than eight hours per day.

en.question: What do Dynamic Message Signs display when they are not in use?

choices.A: The current interstate speed limit.
choices.B: The local time and temperature.
choices.C: They are normally blank.
choices.D: Advertisements for local businesses.

en.explanation: Dynamic Message Signs provide real-time information to motorists, but the manual notes that these signs are normally blank when not in use.

en.question: Which driving behavior is described as slowing down to look at crashes or anything out of the ordinary, causing traffic congestion?

choices.A: Tailgating
choices.B: Rubbernecking
choices.C: Interstate hypnosis
choices.D: Unnecessary lane changes

en.explanation: The manual identifies 'rubbernecking' as slowing down to look at crashes or virtually anything else out of the ordinary, calling it one of the worst congestion offenders.

en.question: What should you do if traffic conditions make it unsafe to change lanes when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle on the shoulder?

choices.A: Stop in your lane until traffic clears.
choices.B: Speed up to pass the emergency vehicle as quickly as possible.
choices.C: Pull over to the opposite shoulder.
choices.D: Slow down and remain in the same lane.

en.explanation: ONLY when traffic conditions make it unsafe to make such a lane change is the motorist allowed to respond to this situation by simply slowing down and remaining in the same lane.

en.question: In addition to emergency and maintenance vehicles, Tennessee's Move Over Law also applies to:

choices.A: All moving vehicles on the interstate.
choices.B: Stationary motor vehicles with their emergency flasher lights on.
choices.C: Bicycles traveling on the shoulder.
choices.D: Pedestrians walking along the highway.

en.explanation: The manual states that in addition to stationary emergency vehicles, the Move Over law now applies to all stationary motor vehicles, such as your car or truck, with their emergency flasher lights on.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you need help, how should you signal other drivers and law enforcement?

choices.A: Stand in the middle of the lane and wave your arms.
choices.B: Raise your hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or radio antenna.
choices.C: Flash your headlights repeatedly.
choices.D: Honk your horn continuously.

en.explanation: If you have vehicle trouble and need help, the manual advises to raise your hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or radio antenna.

en.question: If you have vehicle trouble and pull to the shoulder, where is the safest place to wait for help?

choices.A: Walking along the interstate to find a phone.
choices.B: Sitting on the trunk of your car.
choices.C: In or near your vehicle on the side away from traffic.
choices.D: Standing in the lane next to your vehicle to direct traffic.

en.explanation: The manual states that if possible, it is better to stay in or near your vehicle on the side away from traffic, and notes that walking along the interstate is dangerous.

en.question: If you are involved in a traffic crash on the interstate, when does Tennessee law allow you to move the vehicle to the emergency lane?

choices.A: Only after the police have arrived and taken photos.
choices.B: If the vehicle is drivable and there are no serious personal injuries or deaths.
choices.C: You are never allowed to move a vehicle after a crash.
choices.D: Only if the crash involves more than three vehicles.

en.explanation: Under the 'Move It for Safety' section, if the vehicle is still drivable and there are NO SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURIES or deaths, you may pull the vehicle(s) to the emergency lane.

en.question: What number can you dial on your wireless phone at no charge to connect with the Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatch Center?
en.explanation: In the event of a highway emergency, you may dial *THP (*847) to be connected to the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatcher.

en.question: To help avoid interstate hypnosis, drivers should get into the habit of:

choices.A: Staring straight ahead at the road lines.
choices.B: Shifting their eyes left and right and checking the rear view mirror.
choices.C: Keeping the car's interior as warm as possible.
choices.D: Listening to steady sounds of wind and tire hum.

en.explanation: To fight interstate hypnosis, the manual advises drivers to keep shifting their eyes left and right and checking the rear view mirror, avoiding staring straight ahead.

en.question: If an emergency vehicle is stopped on the left shoulder of a multi-lane highway, what should you do according to the Move Over Law?

choices.A: Merge into the right lane of traffic to free the left most lane as a safety barrier.
choices.B: Merge into the left lane of traffic to get closer to the vehicle.
choices.C: Stop your vehicle in the left lane.
choices.D: Drive on the right shoulder to pass.

en.explanation: If the emergency vehicle is stopped on the left shoulder, the motorist merges into the right lane of traffic, freeing the left most lane as a safety barrier.

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following is a recommended item to carry in your car specifically for winter travel emergencies?

choices.A: A portable fan
choices.B: A window scraper for iced windows
choices.C: Extra engine coolant
choices.D: A sunshade

en.explanation: The suggested safety and emergency equipment section states that during winter travel, you should carry a blanket, a small portable heater, a window scraper for iced windows, and snow tires or tire chains.

en.question: What is the proper procedure when entering an interstate highway?

choices.A: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
choices.B: Check for cars, reduce speed to 25 MPH before entering the traffic lane.
choices.C: Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic and merge when the way is clear.
choices.D: Sound your horn, maintain your current speed, and merge directly into the right lane.

en.explanation: According to the manual's sample test questions, when entering an interstate highway, you should check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.

en.question: Who is legally permitted to use emergency crossovers on the interstate in Tennessee?

choices.A: Any driver who missed their exit.
choices.B: Any driver, as long as no other vehicles are present.
choices.C: Commercial truck drivers during heavy traffic.
choices.D: Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

en.explanation: Emergency crossovers on the interstate are legal in Tennessee for emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle is damaged in a crash on the interstate and there are no serious injuries?

choices.A: Leave the vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
choices.B: Move the damaged vehicle to the shoulder.
choices.C: Stop traffic to safely exchange insurance information.
choices.D: Abandon the vehicle and walk to the nearest exit.

en.explanation: The Tennessee Department of Transportation has placed signs reminding motorists to move their damaged vehicles to the shoulder if no serious injury has occurred.

en.question: Statistically, when do more fatal crashes take place than on any other day?

choices.A: Monday and Tuesday mornings.
choices.B: Wednesday and Thursday nights.
choices.C: Friday and Saturday nights.
choices.D: Sunday afternoons.

en.explanation: The manual states that more fatal crashes take place on Friday and Saturday nights than on any other day.

en.question: What is the basic rule for safe night driving?

choices.A: Always use your high beams.
choices.B: Never outrun your headlights.
choices.C: Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.
choices.D: Keep your interior dome light on.

en.explanation: The basic rule for safe night driving is: NEVER OUTRUN YOUR HEADLIGHTS, because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.

en.question: How should you avoid the glare of oncoming headlights at night?

choices.A: Look directly into the oncoming headlights to track the vehicle.
choices.B: Flash your high beams repeatedly at the oncoming driver.
choices.C: Watch the right edge of the road and use the white line or road edge as a steering guide.
choices.D: Close one eye until the vehicle passes.

en.explanation: To avoid the glare of oncoming lights, you should watch the right edge of the road and use the white line or road edge as a steering guide.

en.question: By law, your headlights must enable you to see clearly any person on the highway at least how far ahead of your car?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The law requires headlights that will enable you to see clearly any person on the highway at least two hundred (200) feet ahead of your car.

en.question: You must dim your headlights when meeting or overtaking vehicles within what distance?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You must adhere to the proper requirements of dimming your lights at night when meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet.

en.question: Whenever you park on or along a highway at night, what should you do?

choices.A: Leave your headlights on high beam.
choices.B: Leave your headlights on low beam.
choices.C: Leave your emergency and parking lights on.
choices.D: Turn off all lights to save battery.

en.explanation: Whenever you park on or along a highway at night, leave your emergency and parking lights on. Never leave your headlights on, as they may blind or confuse approaching drivers.

en.question: When is the pavement particularly treacherous and most slippery during rainy weather?

choices.A: After it has been raining heavily for several hours.
choices.B: When it first begins to rain.
choices.C: Right after the rain stops.
choices.D: When driving through deep puddles.

en.explanation: The pavement is particularly treacherous when it first begins to rain because accumulations of dirt and oil will mix with the water, creating a greasy film on the roadway.

en.question: When driving in rainy weather, which lights should you use?

choices.A: Parking lights only.
choices.B: Headlights on high beam.
choices.C: Headlights on low beam.
choices.D: Emergency flashers only.

en.explanation: Rainy weather calls for driving with headlights on low beam so the light will be on the road where you need it.

en.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog or smoke?

choices.A: Turn on your high beams and drive quickly through it.
choices.B: Follow the vehicle ahead of you very closely.
choices.C: DON'T drive in fog or smoke.
choices.D: Use only your parking lights.

en.explanation: The manual states that the best advice for driving in fog or smoke is "DON'T". If you must travel, you should take specific precautions.

en.question: If you must travel in fog or smoke, how should you use your vehicle's lights?

choices.A: Drive with your lights on high beam.
choices.B: Drive with your lights on low beam.
choices.C: Drive with just your parking lights on.
choices.D: Drive with just your fog lights on.

en.explanation: If you must travel in fog or smoke, you should drive with your lights on low beam. High beams will impair your visibility, and you should never drive with just parking or fog lights on.

en.question: If your car stalls or is disabled while driving in fog, what should you do?

choices.A: Stay inside the vehicle and wait for help.
choices.B: Stand directly behind the vehicle to wave traffic around.
choices.C: Move away from the vehicle to avoid personal injury.
choices.D: Leave the vehicle in the traffic lane and walk home.

en.explanation: If your car stalls or is disabled in fog, move away from the vehicle to avoid personal injury.

en.question: Why should you avoid flashing your high beams to warn an oncoming driver at night?

choices.A: It drains your vehicle's battery.
choices.B: It is illegal in all circumstances.
choices.C: It might serve as a distraction and interfere with their driving, resulting in a collision.
choices.D: It will cause your headlights to burn out faster.

en.explanation: You should avoid flashing your high beams to warn the other driver as it might serve as a distraction and interfere with their driving resulting in a collision.

en.question: What should you do if you must stop your vehicle in dense fog because you cannot see the road's edge?

choices.A: Stop in the middle of the traffic lane and turn on your high beams.
choices.B: Pull off as far to the right as possible, well out of the traffic lane, and turn on your emergency flashers.
choices.C: Stop on the roadway and sound your horn repeatedly to warn others.
choices.D: Pull off to the left shoulder and turn off all your lights.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you cannot see the road's edge in fog, you should pull off as far to the right as possible - well out of the traffic lane - and turn on your emergency flashers.

en.question: Why can pavement be very slippery for the first few minutes when it starts to rain on a hot day?

choices.A: The rain immediately freezes on the hot asphalt.
choices.B: The water mixes with dirt to create deep mud.
choices.C: Heat causes oil in the asphalt to come to the surface, making it extremely slippery until washed off.
choices.D: The hot pavement causes the rain to instantly vaporize, reducing tire traction.

en.explanation: According to the manual, heat causes oil in the asphalt to come to the surface, and this makes the road extremely slippery until the oil washes off.

en.question: What is required by Tennessee law when driving through dense fog, heavy rain, or snow during the daytime?

choices.A: Turn on your high beam headlights.
choices.B: Turn on your emergency flashers.
choices.C: Turn on your low beam headlights.
choices.D: Turn on your interior dome light.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'WHEN DRIVING THROUGH DENSE FOG, HEAVY RAIN OR SNOW DURING THE DAYTIME, TURN ON YOU LOW BEAM HEADLIGHTS... it is also a requirement of Tennessee law.'

en.question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what is the best way to slow down?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes immediately.
choices.B: Shift into neutral and coast.
choices.C: Pump the brakes rapidly.
choices.D: Slow down gradually by letting up on the gas.

en.explanation: The manual advises that if your vehicle starts to hydroplane, you should 'slow down gradually by letting up on the gas' and 'Don't slam on the brakes.'

en.question: Which of the following is a true statement regarding hydroplaning?

choices.A: It only occurs at speeds above 55 mph.
choices.B: Stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.
choices.C: It increases your steering control due to water resistance.
choices.D: It only happens when driving through deep floodwaters.

en.explanation: The manual notes that when hydroplaning occurs, 'Stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.' It also states tires can hydroplane at ANY speed.

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle begins to skid?

choices.A: Slam on the brakes to stop the vehicle quickly.
choices.B: Steer in the opposite direction you want the car to go.
choices.C: Stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want your car to go.
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to regain traction.

en.explanation: If your vehicle begins to skid, the manual instructs to 'Stay off the brake' and 'Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want your car to go.'

en.question: How should you react if your wheels get off the paved roadway?

choices.A: Jerk the steering wheel back toward the pavement suddenly.
choices.B: Slam on the brakes and hold the pedal down.
choices.C: Accelerate to get back onto the road quickly.
choices.D: Lift your foot off the gas pedal and brake lightly and briefly.

en.explanation: To regain control when off the pavement, you should 'Lift you foot off the gas pedal but do NOT suddenly apply the brake' and 'Brake lightly and briefly.'

en.question: What is the primary function of Rumble Stripes on Tennessee roads?

choices.A: To wake up drivers who fall asleep at the wheel.
choices.B: To improve wet-night visibility of the edge line.
choices.C: To indicate the approaching end of a highway.
choices.D: To slow down speeding vehicles in residential areas.

en.explanation: While rumble stripes have a secondary effect of vibration and noise, the manual states 'its primary function is to improve wet-night visibility of the edge line.'

en.question: How much moving water does it typically take to sweep away most cars?

choices.A: 6 to 12 inches
choices.B: 18 to 24 inches
choices.C: 36 to 48 inches
choices.D: At least 60 inches

en.explanation: The manual warns that 'most cars can be swept away in 18 to 24 inches of moving water.'

en.question: What can happen if a driver knowingly ignores clearly visible flood warning barricades and drives into a flooded area?

choices.A: They will only receive a verbal warning from law enforcement.
choices.B: They can be charged with reckless driving and held responsible for rescue costs.
choices.C: Their vehicle will be permanently confiscated by the state.
choices.D: They will automatically lose their license for five years.

en.explanation: According to the manual, ignoring flood warning signs or barricades can result in the driver being 'charged with reckless driving' and 'responsible for the restitution of funds for the cost of your rescue.'

en.question: What is the recommended action if you spot a tornado while driving?

choices.A: Try to outrun the tornado by driving at maximum speed.
choices.B: Stay in your car and park under an overpass.
choices.C: Get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area, and lie face down.
choices.D: Drive toward the tornado to get past it quickly.

en.explanation: If you spot a tornado, the manual advises: 'DON'T try to outrun it. Get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area and lie face down to protect yourself from flying debris.'

en.question: When a large truck or bus is passing you on the left, what should you do to handle the gusts of wind they create?

choices.A: Move as far as possible to the right of your lane and slow down.
choices.B: Move to the left side of your lane to block the wind.
choices.C: Accelerate quickly to stay ahead of the truck.
choices.D: Sound your horn to warn the truck driver.

en.explanation: The manual states that when a truck or bus is passing you on the left, you should 'move as far as possible to the right of your lane and slow down.'

en.question: How does a strong tailwind (wind blowing from behind your vehicle) affect your driving?

choices.A: It makes steering significantly more difficult.
choices.B: It decreases your speed, requiring you to accelerate more.
choices.C: It increases your speed, so you will have to decelerate and begin braking earlier to stop.
choices.D: It causes your vehicle to hydroplane on dry pavement.

en.explanation: The manual explains that 'A strong tailwind (wind blowing from behind your vehicle) will increase your speed, so you will have to decelerate and begin braking earlier to stop.'

en.question: If the sun is directly behind you while driving, what hazard should you be aware of?

choices.A: Your windshield wipers may stop functioning.
choices.B: Oncoming drivers may have a glare problem and might not see your turn signals.
choices.C: Your vehicle's engine may overheat more quickly.
choices.D: You will not be able to see your dashboard instruments.

en.explanation: The manual warns: 'If the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers may have the glare problem. Be aware that they may not be able to see your turn signals or your car.'

en.question: What is the correct technique for getting a vehicle unstuck from mud or snow?

choices.A: Shift to high gear and spin the wheels as fast as possible.
choices.B: Shift to low gear, keep front wheels straight, and gently step on the gas pedal.
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel sharply from side to side while accelerating heavily.
choices.D: Slam on the brakes while shifting between drive and reverse.

en.explanation: To get unstuck from mud or snow, the manual advises to 'Shift to low gear and keep the front wheels straight,' 'Gently step on the gas pedal,' and 'Avoid spinning the wheels.'

en.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck in deep mud or snow?

choices.A: Shift to high gear and spin the wheels as fast as possible.
choices.B: Shift to low gear and keep the front wheels straight.
choices.C: Pump the gas pedal rapidly to gain traction.
choices.D: Turn the steering wheel sharply from side to side.

en.explanation: When trying to get your vehicle unstuck, the manual advises to shift to low gear and keep the front wheels straight, while gently stepping on the gas pedal and avoiding spinning the wheels.

en.question: When should you install tire chains on your vehicle?

choices.A: After you get stuck in the snow.
choices.B: While driving in the middle of the roadway.
choices.C: Before driving in snow or mud.
choices.D: Only when driving on solid ice.

en.explanation: The manual states that you should drive as far as possible to the right side of the roadway before installing chains, and put them on the tires before driving in snow or mud.

en.question: Which of the following is considered one of the three big errors most drivers make in snow and ice?

choices.A: Over-steering and skidding the wheels.
choices.B: Using low beam headlights.
choices.C: Driving with a steady speed.
choices.D: Using the heater-defroster.

en.explanation: The three big errors of most drivers in snow and ice are: over-powering and spinning the wheels, over-braking and sliding the wheels, and over-steering and skidding the wheels.

en.question: Before driving in winter weather, from which windows should you clear snow, ice, or frost?

choices.A: Only the windshield.
choices.B: The windshield and front side windows.
choices.C: Only the rear window.
choices.D: ALL windows.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states to clear snow, ice or frost from ALL windows before driving.

en.question: When traveling at 20 M.P.H., low traction from ice and snow can increase your stopping distance to:

choices.A: 50 feet or more.
choices.B: 100 feet or more.
choices.C: 150 feet or more.
choices.D: 200 feet or more.

en.explanation: When traveling at 20 M.P.H., low traction can increase stopping distance to 200 feet or more.

en.question: How should you apply your brakes on snow or ice to maintain directional control?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly.
choices.B: Apply continuous hard pressure until the vehicle stops.
choices.C: Apply steady pressure to a point just short of lock up.
choices.D: Slam on the brakes and hold them down.

en.explanation: The manual advises to apply the brakes firmly, to a point just short of lock up, and to NOT pump the brake pedal, just apply steady pressure for the best combination of braking effort and directional control.

en.question: To make antilock brakes (ABS) work correctly during an emergency stop, you should:

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal.
choices.B: Apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal.
choices.C: Lightly tap the brakes.
choices.D: Use the parking brake instead.

en.explanation: To make antilock brakes work correctly, or work at all, you should apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal. During an emergency stop, push the brake pedal all the way to the floor if necessary.

en.question: Why should you be especially cautious when driving over bridges in freezing weather?

choices.A: Bridges are usually built with steeper inclines.
choices.B: Ice forms on bridges sooner than on adjoining roads.
choices.C: Bridges have less traffic to pack the snow.
choices.D: Bridges absorb more heat from the sun.

en.explanation: Usually, signs indicate that ice forms on bridges sooner than on the adjoining roads, making them unexpectedly slippery.

en.question: By law, what percentage of questions on the Tennessee driver's knowledge test must deal with alcohol and drugs?

choices.A: At least 10 percent.
choices.B: At least 15 percent.
choices.C: At least 20 percent.
choices.D: At least 25 percent.

en.explanation: By law, at least 25 percent of the questions on the knowledge test must consist of questions dealing with the topic of alcohol, other drugs, and driving.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take for the liver to oxidize one alcoholic drink?

choices.A: 15 minutes.
choices.B: 30 minutes.
choices.C: One hour.
choices.D: Two hours.

en.explanation: Upon reaching the liver, the alcohol immediately begins to be oxidized. However, the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour.

en.question: Which of the following is the only effective way to sober up after drinking alcohol?

choices.A: Drinking black coffee.
choices.B: Taking a cold shower.
choices.C: Exercising vigorously.
choices.D: Allowing time to pass.

en.explanation: The rate of oxidation cannot be increased by drinking coffee, exercising, taking a cold shower or anything else. Only time can sober a person who’s been drinking.

en.question: In Tennessee, what Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) level is always illegal for intoxication?
en.explanation: In most states, including Tennessee, .08 is the level of intoxication which is always illegal.

en.question: If two people weigh the same, how does body fat affect alcohol intoxication?

choices.A: The person with more body fat will show signs of intoxication first.
choices.B: The person with less body fat will show signs of intoxication first.
choices.C: Body fat has no effect on how quickly a person becomes intoxicated.
choices.D: Both people will become intoxicated at the exact same rate.

en.explanation: Alcohol is able to be absorbed in water, not fat. People with less body fat have more water in which to dilute the alcohol. So, drink for drink, if people weigh the same, the one with more body fat will show signs of intoxication first.

en.question: With a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of .10 percent, how much more likely are you to cause a crash compared to if you were sober?

choices.A: Two times more likely.
choices.B: Seven times more likely.
choices.C: Twenty-five times more likely.
choices.D: Fifty times more likely.

en.explanation: With a BAC of .10 percent, you are seven times more likely to cause a crash than if you were sober.

en.question: What are the two abilities most important to the driving task that are affected by small amounts of alcohol?

choices.A: Hearing and reaction time
choices.B: Judgment and vision
choices.C: Steering and braking
choices.D: Alertness and concentration

en.explanation: The manual states: 'The two abilities most important to the driving task are judgment and vision, both of which are affected by small amounts of alcohol.'

en.question: How does alcohol affect a driver's vision at night?

choices.A: It improves glare recovery time.
choices.B: It reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half.
choices.C: It increases side vision by 30 percent.
choices.D: It tightens eye muscles to focus better.

en.explanation: Alcohol decreases clearness of vision. The manual explicitly states that it reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half.

en.question: At what Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) does the law consider a driver to be legally intoxicated?

choices.A: .04 percent
choices.B: .05 percent
choices.C: .08 percent
choices.D: .10 percent

en.explanation: The manual indicates that a BAC of .08 percent and above is considered 'LEGAL INTOXICATION' and it is unlawful to drive while the alcohol concentration is .08 percent or higher.

en.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another depressant, like tranquilizers or sedatives?

choices.A: The effects cancel each other out.
choices.B: The effects are simply added together.
choices.C: The effects are multiplied.
choices.D: The alcohol acts as a stimulant to counteract the depressant.

en.explanation: When alcohol is combined with another depressant, like tranquilizers or sedatives, the results are not just added together; they are multiplied, making the effects much stronger and more dangerous.

en.question: According to Tennessee's Implied Consent Law, what is the likely penalty if you refuse to take a chemical test for alcohol or drugs when asked by a law enforcement officer?

choices.A: A fine of $500
choices.B: Suspension of driving privileges for 12 months
choices.C: Immediate 30-day jail sentence
choices.D: Required installation of an ignition interlock device

en.explanation: If you are placed under arrest and refuse a law enforcement officer's request to take the test, it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve (12) months.

en.question: Is it a valid defense for a DUI charge if the drug you were taking was prescribed by a doctor?

choices.A: Yes, as long as you have the prescription bottle in the car.
choices.B: Yes, prescription drugs do not impair driving.
choices.C: No, just because a drug is prescribed by law is no defense for driving under the influence of it.
choices.D: No, unless the doctor specifically gave you written permission to drive.

en.explanation: The manual clearly states: 'Just because a drug is prescribed, by law, this is NO defense for driving under the influence of it.'

en.question: What does the 'No Refusal' law, passed in 2012, allow law enforcement officials to do?

choices.A: Suspend a driver's license permanently on the first offense.
choices.B: Seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.
choices.C: Arrest passengers in a vehicle driven by an impaired driver.
choices.D: Confiscate the vehicle of anyone who refuses a breathalyzer.

en.explanation: The No Refusal law allows law enforcement officials to seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.

en.question: How does alcohol consumption affect a driver's alertness and concentration?

choices.A: It acts as a stimulant to increase alertness.
choices.B: It speeds up nerve impulses and body functions.
choices.C: It acts as a depressant and limits a driver's ability to be alert and concentrate.
choices.D: It has no effect on concentration until the BAC reaches .10 percent.

en.explanation: Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant. It slows all nerve impulses and body functions, limiting a driver's ability to be alert and to concentrate.

en.question: At what BAC level are reaction and coordination impaired?

choices.A: As low as .02 percent
choices.B: Only above .05 percent
choices.C: Exactly at .08 percent
choices.D: At .10 percent and above

en.explanation: The manual notes that reaction and coordination are impaired by alcohol consumption as low as .02 percent BAC.

en.question: Can a driver be convicted of a DUI with a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of .00 percent?

choices.A: No, a BAC of .00 percent clears a driver of any DUI charges.
choices.B: Yes, if their ability to drive is sufficiently impaired by drugs.
choices.C: Yes, but only if they are under 21 years of age.
choices.D: No, a BAC of at least .02 percent is required for a conviction.

en.explanation: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI if their ability to drive is sufficiently impaired by drugs. The level of BAC does not clear a driver when it is below .08 percent.

en.question: What is the relationship between alcohol and the eye muscles?

choices.A: Alcohol causes the eye muscles to tighten, improving focus.
choices.B: Alcohol relaxes the eye muscles, causing poor glare vision and inability to focus properly.
choices.C: Alcohol stimulates the eye muscles, increasing the speed of glare recovery.
choices.D: Alcohol has no effect on the eye muscles, only on the brain.

en.explanation: Glare vision is poor because of relaxed eye muscles. Eye muscles are relaxed by alcohol and cannot focus properly.

en.question: According to the manual, what percentage of the information used in driving is provided by the eyes?

choices.A: About 50 percent
choices.B: About 70 percent
choices.C: Almost 90 percent
choices.D: 100 percent

en.explanation: Because the eyes provide almost 90 percent of the information used in driving, any restriction in vision can cause disastrous results.

en.question: Are the penalties for a DUI arrest different if the driver was impaired by prescription drugs instead of alcohol?

choices.A: Yes, prescription drug DUIs carry lighter penalties.
choices.B: Yes, prescription drug DUIs only result in a warning for the first offense.
choices.C: No, the penalties are the same whether the driver was drinking alcohol or taking drugs.
choices.D: No, but prescription drug DUIs do not go on your driving record.

en.explanation: The penalties for a DUI arrest are the same whether the driver was drinking alcohol or taking drugs (even prescription or over-the-counter drugs).

en.question: What is the first thing affected after a person consumes alcohol?

choices.A: Coordination
choices.B: Vision
choices.C: Judgment
choices.D: Emotions

en.explanation: According to the manual, the first thing affected after drinking alcohol is a person's judgment.

en.question: Under the Drunk Driving Child Protection Act, what is the mandatory minimum jail sentence for violating DUI laws while accompanied by a child under 18?

choices.A: 48 hours
choices.B: 7 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 45 days

en.explanation: The Drunk Driving Child Protection Act imposes a mandatory minimum jail sentence of 30 days and a minimum fine of $1,000 for violating DUI laws when accompanied by a child under 18.

en.question: If you are 18, 19, or 20 years old and are convicted of purchasing or possessing an alcoholic beverage for the first time, how long will you lose your driving privilege?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 years
choices.D: Until you turn 21

en.explanation: If you are 18, 19 or 20 years old and are convicted of purchasing, attempting to purchase, or possessing any alcoholic beverage, you will lose your privilege to drive for one year for a first offense.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take to cancel the intoxicating effects of three alcoholic drinks?

choices.A: One hour
choices.B: Two hours
choices.C: Three hours
choices.D: Four hours

en.explanation: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink, so it takes about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.

en.question: What is the minimum jail time for a first DUI conviction if the driver's Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is 0.20% or more?

choices.A: 48 hours
choices.B: 7 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 45 days

en.explanation: For a 1st conviction, the jail time is 48 hours, but it increases to 7 days if the BAC is 0.20% or more.

en.question: If you are operating a motor vehicle under the influence and are involved in a crash resulting in the death of another person, you may be charged with:

choices.A: Aggravated Assault
choices.B: Vehicular Homicide
choices.C: Especially Aggravated Child Endangerment
choices.D: Reckless Endangerment

en.explanation: If you are operating a motor vehicle under the influence of a drug or alcohol, and you are involved in a crash resulting in the death of another person(s), you may be charged with vehicular homicide.

en.question: For a juvenile offender between the ages of 13 and 17, a first conviction for possessing alcohol or drugs results in a driving privilege suspension for:

choices.A: 6 months or until age 16, whichever is longer
choices.B: 1 year or until age 17, whichever is longer
choices.C: 2 years or until age 18, whichever is longer
choices.D: Until age 21

en.explanation: If you are between the ages of 13 and 17 and are found to have possessed, consumed or sold either alcohol or drugs, your driving privilege will be suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer.

en.question: The amount of alcohol in one 12-ounce bottle of beer is about equal to:

choices.A: A 1-ounce shot of whiskey
choices.B: Two 1-ounce shots of whiskey
choices.C: A 6-ounce glass of wine
choices.D: A half-ounce of pure alcohol

en.explanation: The manual states that the amount of alcohol in one (12 ounce) bottle of beer is about equal to that in a (1 ounce) shot of whiskey.

en.question: What is the fine range for a second DUI conviction?
en.explanation: According to the DUI Penalties chart, the fines for a 2nd Conviction range from $600 to $3,500.

en.question: Under the Under 21 BAC law, a person who is at least 16 but not yet 21 will be convicted of underage driving while impaired if found driving with a BAC of at least:

choices.A: .01 percent
choices.B: .02 percent
choices.C: .04 percent
choices.D: .08 percent

en.explanation: A person who is at least 16, but is not yet 21 years old, and who is found driving with a BAC of .02 percent will be convicted of underage driving while impaired.

en.question: As a condition of probation for a DUI conviction, an offender must complete litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts while wearing clothing that displays the message:

choices.A: "DUI OFFENDER"
choices.B: "I AM A DRUNK DRIVER"
choices.C: "COMMUNITY SERVICE WORKER"
choices.D: "DON'T DRINK AND DRIVE"

en.explanation: While removing litter, the offender has to wear a vest or other clothing displaying the message, "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."

en.question: How do the penalties for a DUI arrest involving prescription drugs compare to those involving alcohol?

choices.A: The penalties for prescription drugs are less severe.
choices.B: The penalties for prescription drugs are more severe.
choices.C: The penalties are the same for both.
choices.D: Prescription drugs do not result in a DUI arrest.

en.explanation: The penalties for a DUI arrest are the same whether the driver was drinking alcohol or taking drugs (even prescription or over-the-counter drugs).

en.question: A fourth or subsequent DUI conviction is classified as a:

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor
choices.B: Class C felony
choices.C: Class D felony
choices.D: Class E felony

en.explanation: The DUI Penalties chart indicates that a 4th or subsequent Conviction is a Class E felony.

en.question: If a person has two DUI convictions within a five-year period, they MUST operate a motor vehicle with an ignition interlock device for how long after reinstatement of driving privileges?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 3 years
choices.D: 5 years

en.explanation: A person with 2 DUIs in a five year period MUST operate a motor vehicle with the ignition interlock device for six months after reinstatement of driving privileges.

en.question: Why is a young driver's chance of a crash much greater with a BAC between .01-.08 percent compared to older drivers?

choices.A: Because young drivers tend to drive faster.
choices.B: Due to low tolerance of alcohol and limited driving experience.
choices.C: Because young drivers are more likely to drive at night.
choices.D: Due to a higher likelihood of using prescription drugs.

en.explanation: The young driver's chance of a crash is much greater with BAC between .01-.08 percent than older drivers. This is due to low tolerance of alcohol and limited driving experience.

en.question: According to the manual, what toll-free number can you call for referrals for help with drug and alcohol use and abuse?

choices.D: 1-800-DRIVING

en.explanation: The manual states to call the toll-free 'Redline' at 1-800-889-9789 for further information on drug and alcohol use or for referrals for help.

en.question: What does the Implied Consent Law mean in Tennessee?

choices.A: You consent to vehicle searches at any time.
choices.B: You agree to carry proper vehicle insurance.
choices.C: If asked, you will take a test to determine alcohol or drug content in the blood.
choices.D: You agree to pay all traffic fines within 30 days.

en.explanation: The Implied Consent Law means that if asked, you will take a test to determine alcohol or drug content in the blood.

en.question: What is the purpose of the Problem Driver Pointer System (PDPS)?

choices.A: To track unpaid parking tickets in Tennessee.
choices.B: To search the National Driver Register before issuing a driver license.
choices.C: To assign points to drivers for traffic violations.
choices.D: To monitor teenage drivers' school attendance.

en.explanation: The Problem Driver Pointer System (PDPS) is used by the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security to search the National Driver Register before issuance of a driver license.

en.question: Which of the following is a reason your Tennessee driver license may be revoked or suspended?

choices.A: Receiving one speeding ticket in a three-year period.
choices.B: Driving a motor vehicle away from a gas station without paying for fuel.
choices.C: Failing to wash your vehicle regularly.
choices.D: Parking in a loading zone for five minutes.

en.explanation: Driving a motor vehicle away from a gas station without paying for dispensed gas or diesel fuel is listed as a situation where a driver license may be revoked or suspended.

en.question: Persons under the age of 18 may lose their driving privileges for dropping out of school. How is 'dropping out' defined in this context?

choices.A: Having 5 consecutive unexcused absences in a semester.
choices.B: Having 10 consecutive or 15 total days of unexcused absences in a semester.
choices.C: Failing one subject during a grading period.
choices.D: Missing 20 days of school for any reason in a year.

en.explanation: Dropping out of school is defined as having 10 consecutive or 15 total days in a semester of unexcused absences.

en.question: To maintain driving privileges, a person under the age of 18 must make satisfactory progress in school. What does this generally mean?

choices.A: Maintaining a 3.0 GPA.
choices.B: Passing all subjects per grading period.
choices.C: Passing three subjects per grading period.
choices.D: Having perfect attendance.

en.explanation: Failure to make satisfactory progress in school generally means passing three subjects per grading period; failing to do so can result in lost driving privileges.

en.question: If your driver license is suspended or revoked, within how many days must it be turned in to the Department of Safety?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 20 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: Whenever a driver license is suspended or revoked, it must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days of the suspension or revocation.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to surrender your suspended or revoked driver license within the required time frame?

choices.A: A $50 fine
choices.B: A $75 fine in addition to any other fines and costs
choices.C: An additional 6 months of suspension
choices.D: A mandatory court appearance

en.explanation: Failure to surrender your license means that you will be fined $75 in addition to any other fines and costs you may owe.

en.question: If you have a new address, within how many days must you report it to the Department of Safety?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: If you have a new address, you must report it to the Department of Safety within ten (10) days of the change.

en.question: Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact, what happens if you ignore a traffic citation issued in another member state?

choices.A: Your Tennessee driving privileges will be suspended, revoked, or canceled.
choices.B: You will be arrested the next time you drive in Tennessee.
choices.C: The citation is automatically dismissed after one year.
choices.D: You will only be fined by the state of Tennessee.

en.explanation: If you ignore the citation from another member state, your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked or canceled until the court notifies the Department of Safety that the citation has been properly disposed of.

en.question: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) will receive a notice of proposed suspension if they accumulate how many points within a 12-month period?

choices.A: 6 or more points
choices.B: 8 or more points
choices.C: 10 or more points
choices.D: 12 or more points

en.explanation: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

en.question: An adult driver will receive an advisory letter to keep them aware of the possibility of losing their driving privileges if they accumulate how many points within any 12 months?

choices.A: 2 to 4 points
choices.B: 4 to 6 points
choices.C: 6 to 11 points
choices.D: 10 to 15 points

en.explanation: An advisory letter is mailed to any licensee having 6 to 11 points on his/her driving record within any 12 months.

en.question: How many reckless driving violations within a 12-month period will result in the revocation or suspension of a Tennessee driver license?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: In Tennessee, a driver license may be revoked or suspended for two reckless driving violations within 12 months.

en.question: Possession of what amount of methamphetamine in a vehicle by a driver can lead to license revocation or suspension?

choices.A: One or more grams
choices.B: Three or more grams
choices.C: Five or more grams
choices.D: Ten or more grams

en.explanation: A driver license may be revoked or suspended for possession by a driver of five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle.

en.question: Before a license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, the department will give you an opportunity for a hearing prior to action, EXCEPT in cases of:

choices.A: Accumulating 12 points in a 12-month period.
choices.B: Final judgments and convictions.
choices.C: Failing to pay child support.
choices.D: Dropping out of high school.

en.explanation: If your license is about to be suspended, revoked or cancelled, the department will give you an opportunity for a hearing prior to action, except in cases of final judgments and convictions.

en.question: How many points must an adult driver accumulate within a 12-month period to receive a notice of proposed suspension?

choices.A: 6 or more
choices.B: 8 or more
choices.C: 10 or more
choices.D: 12 or more

en.explanation: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

en.question: How often is the Defensive Driving Course option available to a driver to avoid or reduce a license suspension?

choices.A: Once every year
choices.B: Once every three years
choices.C: Once in any five-year period
choices.D: Once in a lifetime

en.explanation: The Defensive Driving Course option is only available once in any five-year period to avoid license suspension or to reduce the period of suspension.

en.question: What is a consequence of driving while your license is suspended?

choices.A: A warning letter is mailed
choices.B: The suspension period is extended and could result in criminal prosecution
choices.C: You must retake the written knowledge test
choices.D: Your vehicle will be permanently confiscated

en.explanation: Driving while your license is suspended will result in the extension of the suspension period and could also result in criminal prosecution.

en.question: How many points are added to your driving record for passing a stopped school, church, or youth bus taking on or discharging passengers?

choices.A: 4 points
choices.B: 5 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: According to the points chart, passing a stopped school, church or youth bus taking on or discharging passengers results in 8 points.

en.question: Drivers who lose consciousness or control due to conditions like epilepsy or diabetes must remain lapse-free for what minimum period before being eligible for license reinstatement?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 1 year
choices.D: 2 years

en.explanation: Drivers who lose consciousness or control due to epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or other conditions must be suspended and remain lapse free for a minimum of six (6) months before being eligible for license reinstatement.

en.question: How many points are assigned for failing to yield the right of way to emergency vehicles?

choices.A: 3 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: The points chart assigns 6 points for "Failure to yield right of way to emergency vehicles."

en.question: If a person obtains a restricted license after failing to satisfy a citation, where are they allowed to drive?

choices.A: To and from work only
choices.B: To work and full-time college
choices.C: Anywhere between 6 AM and 6 PM
choices.D: To work and religious services

en.explanation: For a restricted license due to Failure to Satisfy a Citation, the certified order allows the person to drive to and from work only.

en.question: How many points are assigned for speeding 16 to 25 m.p.h. in excess of the speed zone within a construction zone?

choices.A: 4 points
choices.B: 5 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: Speeding 16 thru 25 m.p.h. in excess of the speed zone normally carries 4 points, but in a Construction Zone it carries 5 points.

en.question: A restricted driver license after a DUI conviction is NOT an option for drivers who have a prior conviction of which of the following within 10 years?

choices.A: Reckless driving
choices.B: Speeding over 25 mph
choices.C: Adult driving while impaired
choices.D: Drag racing

en.explanation: A restricted license is not an option for drivers who have a prior conviction of DUI or adult driving while impaired within 10 years.

en.question: If the Department receives information that your ability to drive is affected by a physical or mental disorder, within how many days must you submit a medical report?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: The driver will be required to submit (within thirty (30) days of notification) a medical report from a medical doctor.

en.question: How many points are assigned to a driver under 18 years of age for operating a vehicle while using a cell phone?

choices.A: 3 points
choices.B: 4 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: The points chart specifies 6 points for "Operating vehicle while using cell phone (under 18)".

en.question: A minor who loses their license due to drug or alcohol-related charges may apply for a restricted license to drive to and from:

choices.A: Religious services and work
choices.B: The educational institution or work
choices.C: Outpatient treatment programs only
choices.D: Any location during daylight hours

en.explanation: A minor who loses his/her license because of drug- or alcohol-related charges may apply to the trial judge for a restricted license to operate a motor vehicle to and from the educational institution or to and from work.

en.question: How many points are assigned to a driver for contributing to the occurrence of a crash resulting in the death of another person?

choices.A: 4 points
choices.B: 5 points
choices.C: 6 points
choices.D: 8 points

en.explanation: The points chart assigns 8 points for "Contributing to occurrence of a crash resulting in the death of another person".

en.question: Upon completion of a suspension time, what type of insurance proof is specifically required for adult drivers before getting their regular license?

choices.A: Comprehensive insurance
choices.B: SR-22 insurance
choices.C: Collision insurance
choices.D: Uninsured motorist coverage

en.explanation: Upon the completion of the suspension time, you must pay the appropriate reinstatement fees and submit proof of liability insurance/financial responsibility (SR-22 insurance is required for adult drivers).

en.question: What will happen if a driver fails to respond to a departmental request for a medical report within the prescribed time?

choices.A: They will be fined $50.
choices.B: Their driving privilege will be suspended.
choices.C: Their vehicle registration will be revoked.
choices.D: They will be required to retake the written test only.

en.explanation: According to the manual, failure to respond to departmental requests for a medical report or submission to a driver license examination within the prescribed time will result in the suspension of the driving privilege.

en.question: Which type of insurance provides coverage for damages you cause to other persons?

choices.A: Collision insurance
choices.B: Uninsured motorist insurance
choices.C: Liability insurance
choices.D: Comprehensive insurance

en.explanation: The manual defines liability insurance as providing coverage for damages you cause to other persons.

en.question: Is collision insurance required by Tennessee law?

choices.A: Yes, for all drivers.
choices.B: Yes, but only for commercial vehicles.
choices.C: No, it is not required.
choices.D: No, unless you have a previous crash on your record.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states, "Although collision insurance is not required by Tennessee law, the Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility."

en.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an acceptable form of evidence of financial responsibility?

choices.A: An insurance binder
choices.B: A declaration page of your insurance policy
choices.C: A verbal promise from your insurance agent
choices.D: An insurance card from an authorized company

en.explanation: Acceptable forms of evidence include a declaration page, an insurance binder, an insurance card, a certificate of cash deposit/bond, or proof of qualification as a self-insurer. A verbal promise is not listed.

en.question: You must immediately notify the police of any crash involving death, injury, or property damage over what amount?
en.explanation: Drivers must immediately notify the local police, County Sheriff's office, or Highway Patrol of any crash involving death, injury, or property damage over fifty dollars ($50).

en.question: If a driver is physically unable to give immediate notice of a crash to the police, who is required to do so?

choices.A: The other driver involved
choices.B: A passenger capable of doing so
choices.C: The first witness on the scene
choices.D: The driver's insurance company

en.explanation: The manual states that if the driver is physically unable to give immediate notice, and there is a passenger capable of doing so, the passenger shall make or cause notice to be given.

en.question: A crash must be reported to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security as a "reportable crash" if property damage to any one person is in excess of:
en.explanation: Reportable crashes include any crash in which any person is killed or injured, or in which damage to the property of any one person is in excess of four hundred dollars ($400).

en.question: How many days do you have to file an Owner/Driver Report of a reportable crash to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 20 days

en.explanation: The operator and/or owner of a vehicle involved in a reportable crash must file an Owner/Driver Report of the crash within 20 days.

en.question: What should you do if you are involved in a crash with an unattended vehicle and cannot locate the owner?

choices.A: Leave a note on the windshield and drive away.
choices.B: Report the crash to the police.
choices.C: Wait at the scene until the owner returns.
choices.D: File an Owner/Driver report within 30 days.

en.explanation: If the crash involved an unattended vehicle or a domestic animal and you cannot locate the owner, you must report the crash to the police.

en.question: If your driving privileges are revoked for failure to establish financial responsibility for a crash, what form must your liability insurance carrier file before reinstatement?

choices.A: SR-22 form
choices.B: FR-44 form
choices.C: TN-10 form
choices.D: DL-12 form

en.explanation: Before driving privileges can be reinstated after such a revocation, you are required to pay a reinstatement fee and have a liability insurance carrier file a SR-22 form with the Department of Safety.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do to a damaged vehicle at a crash scene to prevent a fire?

choices.A: Disconnect the battery.
choices.B: Turn off the ignition.
choices.C: Pour water on the engine.
choices.D: Remove the gas cap.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "Turn off the ignition in the damaged vehicle to prevent a fire."

en.question: Under Tennessee law, when are you allowed to move your vehicle out of the traffic flow after a crash on the interstate?

choices.A: Only after the police have arrived and taken photos.
choices.B: If the vehicle is drivable and there are no serious personal injuries or deaths.
choices.C: You are never allowed to move a vehicle until a tow truck arrives.
choices.D: Only if the property damage is less than $50.

en.explanation: If you are involved in a traffic crash on the interstate, Tennessee law allows you to move the vehicle to prevent blocking traffic if the vehicle is still drivable and there are NO SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURIES or deaths.

en.question: When is it acceptable to move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle if you do not have medical or rescue training?

choices.A: When they ask you to move them.
choices.B: When they are blocking traffic.
choices.C: When there is an immediate danger such as a fire.
choices.D: When the ambulance is more than 10 minutes away.

en.explanation: Do not attempt to move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless you have the necessary medical or rescue training or there is an immediate danger such as fire.

en.question: If you arrive first at a crash scene and are not professionally trained to render aid, what should you do after calling 911?

choices.A: Stop and direct traffic around the crash.
choices.B: Slowly continue on in your vehicle so as not to interfere.
choices.C: Pull over and wait for the police to take your statement.
choices.D: Try to extract the passengers from the vehicles.

en.explanation: If you are not professionally trained to render aid, slowly continue on in your vehicle so not to interfere with the arrival of police and emergency services, preventing a secondary collision.

en.question: If you witness a crash occur, what is the proper procedure according to the manual?

choices.A: Pull safely off to the side of the road, turn on emergency flashers, and notify the police.
choices.B: Chase down the vehicles if it was a hit-and-run.
choices.C: Continue driving and call the police when you get home.
choices.D: Stop in the middle of the road to block traffic and protect the scene.

en.explanation: If you witnessed the crash occur, pull safely off to the side of the road and turn on your vehicle's emergency flashers. Notify the police officer or Tennessee State Trooper that you witnessed the crash.

en.question: According to the manual, a driver license may be revoked or suspended for which of the following reasons?

choices.A: Accumulating 8 points within a 12-month period
choices.B: Fraudulently altering a driver license
choices.C: Receiving a single parking ticket
choices.D: Driving 5 mph over the speed limit once

en.explanation: The manual states that a driver license may be revoked or suspended for fraudulently altering a driver license, or for frequent convictions resulting in 12 or more points within a 12-month period.

en.question: What does the safe driving practice 'Aim High In Steering' mean?

choices.A: Adjusting your steering wheel to the highest position
choices.B: Looking as far down the road as possible to uncover important traffic information
choices.C: Keeping your eyes focused directly on the hood of your car
choices.D: Steering with both hands at the very top of the wheel

en.explanation: To 'Aim High In Steering' means to look as far down the road as possible to uncover important traffic information to make appropriate decisions.

en.question: To 'Leave Yourself an Out' while driving, you should surround your vehicle with space in front and at least on:

choices.A: Both sides
choices.B: The rear
choices.C: One side
choices.D: The passenger side only

en.explanation: The manual advises to 'Leave Yourself an Out' by being prepared and surrounding your vehicle with space in front and at least on one side to escape conflict.

en.question: What are the most important driving attitudes you can develop to ensure safe driving?

choices.A: Aggressiveness and speed
choices.B: Courtesy and consideration toward others
choices.C: Confidence and assertiveness
choices.D: Competitiveness and alertness

en.explanation: According to the manual, courtesy and consideration toward others are the most important driving attitudes you can develop and are the key to safe driving.

en.question: When driving defensively, you should expect the other driver to:

choices.A: Always obey the rules of the road
choices.B: Yield the right-of-way to you
choices.C: Do the WRONG thing
choices.D: Use their turn signals correctly

en.explanation: A key rule of driving alertly is to expect the other driver to do the WRONG thing, and have a plan of action prepared to counter their error.
