en.question: Under which conditions should you increase your following distance to at least 3 to 4 seconds?

choices.A: When driving in residential neighborhoods
choices.B: When following large commercial trucks or buses on high-speed interstates
choices.C: When driving in heavy stop-and-go traffic
choices.D: When approaching a four-way stop

en.explanation: The manual states that on high-speed interstates, when following large commercial trucks or buses, and in inclement weather or limited visibility conditions, it is safest to increase following distance to at least 3 to 4 seconds.

en.question: What percentage of information about the road and our surroundings do we gather through our eyes while driving?
en.explanation: When driving, we gather 90% of the information about the road and our surroundings through our eyes.

en.question: How far ahead should defensive drivers try to focus their eyes while scanning the road?

choices.A: 2 to 3 seconds ahead
choices.B: 5 to 8 seconds ahead
choices.C: 10 to 15 seconds ahead
choices.D: 20 to 30 seconds ahead

en.explanation: Defensive drivers try to focus their eyes 10 to 15 seconds (about the distance of 1 city block) ahead to see things early and allow more time to react.

en.question: When entering an intersection, why should you look to the left first?

choices.A: Because cars coming from the left will be closer to you
choices.B: Because cars from the left always have the right-of-way
choices.C: Because left turns are illegal at most intersections
choices.D: Because traffic signs are usually posted on the left

en.explanation: At any intersection, look to the left first, since cars coming from the left will be closer to you.

en.question: How often should you use your rearview mirror to check the traffic behind you?

choices.A: About every 5 seconds
choices.B: About every 10 seconds
choices.C: About every 30 seconds
choices.D: Only when you are preparing to stop

en.explanation: You should use your rearview mirror to check the traffic behind you frequently, about every 10 seconds.

en.question: When should you develop the habit of using your turn signals?

choices.A: Only when you see other vehicles on the road
choices.B: Only when changing lanes on an interstate
choices.C: Even when you do not see other vehicles on the road
choices.D: Only during daylight hours

en.explanation: You should develop the habit of using your turn signals even when you do not see other vehicles on the road.

en.question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane to move into, what is the safest way to handle the situation?

choices.A: Slow down quickly to discourage the tailgater
choices.B: Wait until the road ahead is clear and passing is legal, then slowly reduce your speed
choices.C: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater
choices.D: Tap your brakes repeatedly to flash your brake lights

en.explanation: If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and passing is legal, then slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to drive around you. Never slow down quickly.

en.question: While scanning the road, which of the following is a clue that a vehicle might pull into your path?

choices.A: The vehicle's windows are rolled down
choices.B: The vehicle has a dirty windshield
choices.C: The vehicle has turned wheels or exhaust smoke
choices.D: The vehicle is parked near a fire hydrant

en.explanation: You should look for clues like exhaust smoke, brake or back-up lights, and turned wheels on vehicles, as these indicate that the vehicles may pull into your path.

en.question: When meeting oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road, where should you position your vehicle?

choices.A: Directly on the centerline
choices.B: Slightly to the right of your lane so as not to crowd the centerline
choices.C: Slightly to the left of your lane to see better
choices.D: On the right shoulder of the road

en.explanation: When meeting oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road, stay slightly to the right of your lane so as not to 'crowd' the centerline.

en.question: A driver license may be revoked or suspended for frequent convictions of traffic law violations resulting in how many points within a 12-month period?

choices.A: 6 or more points
choices.B: 8 or more points
choices.C: 10 or more points
choices.D: 12 or more points

en.explanation: A driver license may be revoked or suspended for frequent convictions of traffic law violations resulting in 12 or more 'points' within a 12-month period.

en.question: What is the minimum gap needed whenever you change lanes, enter a roadway, or merge with another traffic lane?

choices.A: Two-second gap
choices.B: Three-second gap
choices.C: Four-second gap
choices.D: Five-second gap

en.explanation: According to the manual, a minimum four-second gap is needed whenever you change lanes, enter a roadway, or when your lane merges with another traffic lane.

en.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safest to return to the driving lane?

choices.A: As soon as your vehicle is ahead of the other vehicle's front bumper.
choices.B: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
choices.C: When the driver you passed flashes their headlights at you.
choices.D: After exactly three seconds have passed since you changed lanes.

en.explanation: To finish a pass defensively, it is safest not to return to the driving lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you just passed in the rearview mirror.

en.question: Approximately how much time do you need to complete a pass of a single vehicle at 55 M.P.H.?

choices.A: About 5 seconds
choices.B: About 10 seconds
choices.C: About 15 seconds
choices.D: About 20 seconds

en.explanation: At 55 M.P.H. you will need about ten (10) seconds to complete the pass of a single vehicle, which means you need a ten-second gap in oncoming traffic.

en.question: According to the NHTSA, approximately what percentage of all traffic fatalities annually are caused by aggressive driving behaviors?
en.explanation: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) says about 66% of all traffic fatalities annually are caused by aggressive driving behaviors.

en.question: If an aggressive driver follows you, what is the recommended action?

choices.A: Drive home immediately and lock your doors.
choices.B: Stop your vehicle and confront the driver.
choices.C: Go to a police station or a public place where you can get help.
choices.D: Speed up to lose the driver in traffic.

en.explanation: Tips to Avoid Road Rage state that if a driver follows you, you should go to a police station or a public place where you can get help.

en.question: Under what weather conditions do most accidents happen?

choices.A: In clear weather
choices.B: In snow
choices.C: In rain
choices.D: In fog

en.explanation: According to the manual's short test on special driving conditions, most accidents happen in clear weather, noting that 'pretty days can be deadly too!'

en.question: What are the three options a driver has to avoid a collision?

choices.A: Stop, Turn, Speed Up
choices.B: Brake, Honk, Swerve
choices.C: Stop, Reverse, Turn
choices.D: Accelerate, Honk, Brake

en.explanation: In avoiding a collision, drivers have three options: 1. Stop, 2. Turn, 3. Speed Up.

en.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle is equipped with an Antilock Braking System (ABS), you should:

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly to avoid skidding.
choices.B: Press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it firmly.
choices.C: Apply the brakes gently and gradually increase pressure.
choices.D: Press the brake pedal hard and let up immediately if you feel it pushing back.

en.explanation: With ABS, you should press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it firmly. You should NOT let up on the brake pedal even if you feel it pushing back.

en.question: What should you do if you must stop quickly, you do NOT have ABS, and your brakes lock up causing a skid?

choices.A: Keep pressing the brake pedal as hard as possible.
choices.B: Quickly let up on the brake pedal, then push down again once the skidding stops.
choices.C: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the opposite direction.
choices.D: Apply the parking brake immediately.

en.explanation: Without ABS, if the brakes lock up and you start to skid, you should quickly let up on the brake pedal. As soon as the vehicle stops skidding, push down on the brake pedal again.

en.question: To make quick evasive turns, what is the recommended hand position on the steering wheel?

choices.A: 10 o'clock and 2 o'clock
choices.B: 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock
choices.C: 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock
choices.D: 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock

en.explanation: For most turns, especially quick turns, it is best to have your hands at about the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions.

en.question: Why is the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock hand position recommended on the steering wheel?

choices.A: It allows you to reach the turn signal more easily.
choices.B: It keeps your wrists and forearms out of the main impact area of the air bag.
choices.C: It prevents the steering wheel from locking during a sharp turn.
choices.D: It provides the most leverage for turning the wheel with one hand.

en.explanation: Having your hands at 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock keeps your wrists and forearms out of the main impact area of the air bag located in the steering wheel should you become involved in a collision.

en.question: What does the driving rule 'Split the difference' mean?

choices.A: Straddle the lane line when passing a bicycle.
choices.B: Steer a middle course between two hazards, leaving more room on the most dangerous side.
choices.C: Cross multiple lanes of traffic one lane at a time.
choices.D: Maintain a two-second following distance in normal traffic.

en.explanation: 'Split the difference' means steering a middle course between two hazards. If one is more dangerous than the other, you leave a little more space on the most dangerous side.

en.question: When crossing traffic at an intersection, what must you ensure before entering?

choices.A: That you can get halfway across and wait in the median.
choices.B: That you have a large enough gap to get all the way across without blocking the intersection.
choices.C: That the vehicle behind you is also ready to cross.
choices.D: That you speed up to beat the approaching traffic.

en.explanation: When you cross traffic, you need a large enough gap to get all the way across the road. You must NOT block intersections or get caught with a portion of your vehicle left in a traffic lane.

en.question: If another driver makes a mistake, such as passing you without enough room, what should you do?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from entering your lane.
choices.B: Honk your horn and flash your lights to warn them.
choices.C: Slow down and allow room for them to safely return to the driving lane.
choices.D: Move onto the shoulder and stop completely.

en.explanation: If another driver makes a mistake, such as passing without enough room, you should handle the error defensively by slowing down and allowing room for passing drivers to safely return to the driving lane.

en.question: What is the recommended hand position for basic driving?

choices.A: 10 o'clock and 2 o'clock
choices.B: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
choices.C: 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock
choices.D: 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock

en.explanation: The manual states that the basic driving position is returning your hands to the left at 9 o'clock and right at 3 o'clock.

en.question: What happens in an emergency or slippery condition if your vehicle does NOT have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS) and you brake hard?

choices.A: The wheels will not lock and the car remains stable.
choices.B: The car will automatically speed up to avoid a collision.
choices.C: All wheels will lock, the car will begin to skid, and it will not be steerable.
choices.D: The brakes will electronically pump much faster than you can manually.

en.explanation: In emergency or slippery conditions without ABS, all wheels lock; the car begins to skid and is not steerable.

en.question: If your vehicle does not have ABS, what must you do to turn quickly while braking?

choices.A: Stomp and hold the brake pedal firmly while turning.
choices.B: Let up on the brake pedal and then turn the steering wheel.
choices.C: Pump the brakes rapidly while jerking the steering wheel.
choices.D: Accelerate while turning the steering wheel sharply.

en.explanation: Without ABS, as you are braking you will need to let up on the brake pedal and then turn the steering wheel to turn quickly.

en.question: When might it be best or necessary to speed up to avoid a collision?

choices.A: When you are approaching a deer crossing sign.
choices.B: When another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room to the front.
choices.C: When you are driving in a school zone and a car is tailgating you.
choices.D: When you are approaching a sharp curve without ABS.

en.explanation: Sometimes it is best to speed up to avoid a collision when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or from behind and there is room to the front of your vehicle to get out of danger.

en.question: Which season is the peak time for deer-car crashes?

choices.A: Spring
choices.B: Summer
choices.C: Fall
choices.D: Winter

en.explanation: Fall is the peak season for deer-car crashes because Autumn is both mating season and hunting season, making deer more active.

en.question: Why should you avoid flashing your headlights at a deer in the road?

choices.A: It will cause the deer to charge at your vehicle.
choices.B: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing them may cause the animal to freeze in the road.
choices.C: It will temporarily blind oncoming drivers.
choices.D: It will cause the deer to run unpredictably into oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing them may cause the animal to freeze in the road.

en.question: What should you do if a collision with an animal seems inevitable?

choices.A: Swerve sharply to the left or right to avoid the animal.
choices.B: Speed up to minimize the impact time.
choices.C: Keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway without swerving.
choices.D: Pump your brakes rapidly and jerk the steering wheel.

en.explanation: If a collision seems inevitable, don't swerve to avoid the animal; your risk of personal injury may be greater if you do. Keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway.

en.question: What is the correct braking technique when using Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS) in a real emergency situation?

choices.A: Pump the brake pedal rapidly.
choices.B: Lightly tap the brakes to warn other drivers.
choices.C: Push hard and hold the pedal down, even if it pulsates.
choices.D: Let up on the brakes slightly when you feel the pedal pulsate.

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers with ABS to 'Stomp. Slam that brake pedal. Push hard and hold the pedal down.' You should not let up even if the pedal pulsates.

en.question: Why should you NEVER pump the brake pedal of a vehicle equipped with ABS?

choices.A: Pumping the brakes will cause the engine to stall.
choices.B: The ABS system is already electronically pumping the brakes much faster than you can manually.
choices.C: It will cause the steering wheel to lock up.
choices.D: It will disable the vehicle's airbags.

en.explanation: You should never pump the brake pedal of an ABS-equipped vehicle because the pulsating feeling is simply the ABS system electronically 'pumping' the brakes much faster than you could ever do manually.

en.question: What are the three major components of the highway transportation system that must be considered when driving?

choices.A: Driver, Vehicle, and Road
choices.B: Weather, Traffic, and Speed
choices.C: Vision, Hearing, and Reflexes
choices.D: Signs, Signals, and Markings

en.explanation: There are three major components to our highway transportation system that must be considered when driving: 1. Driver, 2. Vehicle, 3. Road.

en.question: What is the single most common cause of traffic crashes?

choices.A: Poor weather conditions
choices.B: Mechanical failure
choices.C: Human error
choices.D: Poorly maintained roads

en.explanation: The manual states that human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes.

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following is one of the leading factors in traffic crashes?

choices.A: Driving with the radio on
choices.B: Excessive speed
choices.C: Using high-beam headlights at night
choices.D: Driving an older vehicle

en.explanation: The leading factors in crashes are Excessive Speed, Lack of Concentration, and Improper Evasive Action.

en.question: Which of the following temporary conditions can make you an unsafe driver?

choices.A: Anger, worry, and fatigue
choices.B: Wearing sunglasses during the day
choices.C: Having a passenger in the back seat
choices.D: Driving an ABS-equipped vehicle

en.explanation: Anger, worry, frustration, fatigue and minor illnesses such as a cold are a few of the temporary conditions that can make you an unsafe driver.

en.question: Why must a driver use their side mirrors and glance to the side occasionally?

choices.A: Because you cannot focus on things to the side using only peripheral vision.
choices.B: To ensure the rear doors are securely closed.
choices.C: To monitor the speed of vehicles in the opposite lane.
choices.D: To avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights.

en.explanation: Because you can't focus on things to the side, you also must use your side mirrors and glance to the side occasionally if necessary.

en.question: What should you do if you hit a large animal, such as a deer or farm animal?

choices.A: Move the animal off the roadway yourself.
choices.B: Report the crash to the police.
choices.C: Leave the scene immediately if your car is drivable.
choices.D: Wait by the animal until its owner arrives.

en.explanation: You should report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or farm animal.

en.question: What does Restriction Code 01 on your driver license indicate?

choices.A: You are restricted to driving only during daylight hours.
choices.B: You must have a licensed adult in the vehicle at all times.
choices.C: You must wear corrective lenses at all times when driving.
choices.D: You are restricted from driving on interstate highways.

en.explanation: The manual states that if your driver license indicates you must wear corrective lenses (Restriction Code 01), you must wear them at all times when driving.

en.question: Why should you avoid using dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night?

choices.A: They increase the glare from oncoming headlights.
choices.B: They cut down the light you need to see clearly.
choices.C: They cause your eyes to become fatigued much faster.
choices.D: They are illegal to wear while driving in Tennessee.

en.explanation: The manual advises to avoid using dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night because they cut down the light you need to see clearly.

en.question: How can drivers with a hearing impairment compensate to remain safe on the road?

choices.A: By relying more on their vision.
choices.B: By driving at slower speeds than the posted limit.
choices.C: By keeping their windows rolled down at all times.
choices.D: By installing louder horns on their vehicles.

en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers who have a hearing impairment can adjust and compensate by relying more on their vision to be a safe driver.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended tip to help avoid fatigue when driving on an extended trip?

choices.A: Eat a large meal before beginning the trip.
choices.B: Stop every hour or more often if needed to take a break.
choices.C: Drive late at night when there is less traffic on the road.
choices.D: Take over-the-counter medicine to help you stay alert.

en.explanation: To avoid fatigue, the manual recommends taking breaks by stopping every hour or more often if needed to walk around and get fresh air.

en.question: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if they are under a doctor's care and have been seizure-free for a minimum of:

choices.A: Three months
choices.B: Six months
choices.C: One year
choices.D: Two years

en.explanation: The manual states that in Tennessee, you may drive if you are under the care of a doctor and have been seizure-free for a minimum of six months.

en.question: Why should drivers with diabetes have their eyes checked regularly?

choices.A: Because insulin causes the eyes to become overly sensitive to glare.
choices.B: To ensure they do not need Restriction Code 01 added to their license.
choices.C: Because diabetes causes the eyes to dry out faster while driving.
choices.D: To check for possible night blindness or other vision problems.

en.explanation: The manual notes that if you have diabetes, you should have your eyes checked regularly for possible night blindness or other vision problems.

en.question: If you tend to be an impatient person, what should you do to avoid unsafe driving actions?

choices.A: Listen to fast-paced music to stay alert.
choices.B: Drive slightly above the speed limit to avoid heavy traffic.
choices.C: Always plan extra time for your driving trips.
choices.D: Only drive during off-peak hours.

en.explanation: The manual advises that if you tend to be an impatient person, you should always plan extra time for your driving trips to avoid speeding or other unsafe actions.

en.question: Which of the following is a sign that your braking system needs to be checked by a mechanic?

choices.A: The brake pedal feels firm and resists pressure.
choices.B: The vehicle stops smoothly without pulling to one side.
choices.C: The brake pedal goes to the floor.
choices.D: The brakes are completely silent when applied.

en.explanation: The manual warns that it is very dangerous if brakes are not working properly, such as making a lot of noise, smelling funny, or if the brake pedal goes to the floor.

en.question: Car batteries tend to run down more rapidly in what type of weather?

choices.A: Hot and dry weather
choices.B: Cold or damp weather
choices.C: Humid and sunny weather
choices.D: High-altitude conditions

en.explanation: According to the vehicle maintenance section, car batteries tend to run down more rapidly in cold or damp weather.

en.question: What is a common cause of a film building up on the inside of a vehicle's glass?

choices.A: Using the heater/defroster too often.
choices.B: Using non-freezing windshield washer fluid.
choices.C: Smoking inside the vehicle.
choices.D: Leaving the windows down during rain.

en.explanation: The manual states to keep the inside of your windows clean, especially if anyone using the vehicle smokes, because smoking causes a film to build up on the inside of the glass.

en.question: What is a consequence of driving with unbalanced tires and low tire pressure?

choices.A: It improves fuel economy and ride comfort.
choices.B: It makes the vehicle easier to steer in wet conditions.
choices.C: It decreases the chance of hydroplaning.
choices.D: It causes faster tire wear and reduces fuel economy.

en.explanation: The manual explains that unbalanced tires and low pressure cause faster tire wear, reduce fuel economy, and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

en.question: When using a penny to check tire tread, the tire is considered illegal and unsafe if the tread does not come at least to:

choices.A: The top of the Lincoln Memorial
choices.B: Lincoln's head (2/32 inch)
choices.C: The date printed on the penny
choices.D: The words 'In God We Trust'

en.explanation: The manual states that if you stick a penny into the tread head first and the tread does not come at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch), the tire is illegal and unsafe.

en.question: Where can you usually find the vehicle's recommended tire pressure on many newer cars?

choices.A: On the steering wheel column.
choices.B: On the sticker in the driver's side front door jamb.
choices.C: On the inside of the glove compartment door.
choices.D: On the vehicle's rear bumper.

en.explanation: The manual notes that on many newer cars, the vehicle's recommended tire pressure is on the sticker in the door jamb, usually located on the driver's side front door.

en.question: How often does the manual recommend having your eyes checked by an eye specialist?

choices.A: Every six months
choices.B: Every year or two
choices.C: Every five years
choices.D: Only when renewing your driver license

en.explanation: Because seeing well is so important to safe driving, the manual recommends having your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist.

en.question: Where is the recommended tire pressure usually located for a vehicle's original tires?

choices.A: Printed directly on the tires themselves
choices.B: On a sticker in the driver's side front door jamb
choices.C: On the steering wheel column
choices.D: Engraved on the engine block

en.explanation: On many newer cars, the vehicle's recommended tire pressure is on the sticker in the door jamb, usually located on the driver's side front door.

en.question: Why should you NOT use the tire pressure printed on the tires themselves?

choices.A: It is the minimum pressure required to drive safely.
choices.B: It is only applicable for winter driving conditions.
choices.C: It is the maximum recommended pressure and may not match your vehicle's specifications.
choices.D: It is meant only for aftermarket tires of a different size.

en.explanation: The manual states: "Do not use the tire pressure psi printed on the tires themselves. This is the maximum recommended pressure for the tire and may not match up with your vehicle's manufacturer specifications."

en.question: What will happen if you turn your vehicle's ignition to the 'lock' position while the vehicle is in motion?

choices.A: The brakes will immediately engage.
choices.B: The steering wheel will lock in place and you will lose control of the vehicle.
choices.C: The engine will overheat rapidly.
choices.D: The vehicle will safely glide to a stop.

en.explanation: Never turn your vehicle's ignition to the 'lock' position while the vehicle is in motion. This will cause the steering wheel to lock in place and you will lose control of the vehicle.

en.question: If your vehicle continues to bounce after a bump or a stop, what system likely needs to be checked by a mechanic?

choices.A: The exhaust system
choices.B: The steering system
choices.C: The engine cooling system
choices.D: The suspension system

en.explanation: If the vehicle continues to bounce after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, you may need new shocks or other suspension parts.

en.question: What is a dangerous warning sign that your vehicle may have an exhaust leak?

choices.A: The steering wheel becomes difficult to turn.
choices.B: You or your passengers get a sleepy feeling when driving or riding.
choices.C: The vehicle bounces excessively after coming to a stop.
choices.D: The engine temperature gauge drops suddenly.

en.explanation: If you ever start to notice that you and/or your passengers tend to get a sleepy feeling when driving or riding in your car you may have an exhaust leak that needs to be repaired immediately.

en.question: What should you do if you are sitting in a vehicle with the motor running (idling) for a prolonged period?

choices.A: Turn the ignition to the 'lock' position.
choices.B: Check the radiator coolant level.
choices.C: Open a window to provide fresh air.
choices.D: Sound your horn periodically to stay alert.

en.explanation: When sitting for prolonged periods in a vehicle with the motor running (idling), open a window to provide fresh air to prevent Carbon Monoxide fumes from overcoming people in the vehicle.

en.question: When is the ONLY safe time to check your radiator's antifreeze/coolant level?

choices.A: Immediately after operating the vehicle
choices.B: While the engine is running
choices.C: When the vehicle is parked on an incline
choices.D: When the vehicle is cool

en.explanation: Be careful to check your radiator ONLY when the vehicle is cool, not immediately after operation.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to have loose objects on the floor of your vehicle?

choices.A: They can roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping.
choices.B: They will cause the suspension system to bounce.
choices.C: They can cause an exhaust leak.
choices.D: They will drain the vehicle's battery.

en.explanation: Make sure there are no objects on the floor that could roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping the vehicle.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the ONLY appropriate use for your vehicle's horn?

choices.A: To greet friends on the road
choices.B: To encourage slow drivers to speed up
choices.C: As a warning to others
choices.D: To signal that you are parking

en.explanation: The horn may not seem like it is important for safety, but as a warning device, it could save your life. ONLY use your horn as a warning to others.

en.question: How much gas should you ensure your vehicle has before starting any trip of significant length?

choices.A: At least a quarter tank
choices.B: At least a half tank
choices.C: A completely full tank
choices.D: Enough to reach the nearest gas station

en.explanation: Be sure your vehicle always has at least a half tank of gas before starting any trip of significant length.

en.question: According to the manual, collisions involving multiple vehicles often happen when:

choices.A: Drivers use their horns too frequently.
choices.B: Drivers go faster or slower than other traffic.
choices.C: Vehicles have aftermarket tires installed.
choices.D: Drivers check their tire pressure too often.

en.explanation: Vehicles moving in the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another. Collisions involving multiple vehicles often happen when drivers go faster or slower than other traffic.

en.question: Why do you need to lower your speed and be alert in shopping centers, parking lots, and downtown areas?

choices.A: Because the speed limit is always 15 mph in these areas.
choices.B: Because these areas always have rumble strips.
choices.C: Because vehicles and people are stopping, starting, and moving in different directions quickly and randomly.
choices.D: Because carbon monoxide levels are higher in these areas.

en.explanation: Shopping centers, parking lots and downtown areas – these are busy areas with vehicles and people stopping, starting and moving in different directions quickly and randomly.

en.question: Why might you need to slow down when crossing some railroad crossings?

choices.A: To check your tire pressure
choices.B: Because some crossings are bumpy
choices.C: To read the manufacturer's specifications
choices.D: To let the exhaust system cool down

en.explanation: Railroad crossings – you need to make sure that there are no trains coming and that you have room to cross. Some crossings are bumpy so you need to slow down to safely cross.

en.question: By state law, who is considered a pedestrian?

choices.A: Only people walking on foot
choices.B: Any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair
choices.C: Anyone riding a bicycle or motor-driven bicycle
choices.D: Only children and the elderly

en.explanation: Any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair are considered a pedestrian by state law.

en.question: Which groups of pedestrians are the most frequent victims in auto-pedestrian collisions?

choices.A: Teenagers and young adults
choices.B: Joggers and runners
choices.C: Pedestrians walking in large groups
choices.D: Young, elderly, disabled, and intoxicated pedestrians

en.explanation: You should be especially alert for young, elderly, disabled and intoxicated pedestrians. They are the most frequent victims in auto-pedestrian collisions.

en.question: Which of the following statements about crosswalks is true?

choices.A: Crosswalks only exist where there are painted lines.
choices.B: Pedestrians only have the right-of-way in marked crosswalks.
choices.C: There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines do not mark the crossing.
choices.D: Drivers may block a crosswalk if waiting to make a right turn.

en.explanation: According to the manual, there is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines and boundaries do not mark the crossing.

en.question: Why should drivers avoid stopping with a portion of their vehicle over the crosswalk area?

choices.A: It will trigger a red light camera.
choices.B: It forces pedestrians to go around the vehicle and puts them in a dangerous situation.
choices.C: It causes excessive wear on the vehicle's tires.
choices.D: It blocks the view of the traffic signal for other drivers.

en.explanation: Blocking the crosswalk forces pedestrians to go around your vehicle and puts them in a dangerous situation.

en.question: What must a driver do in a marked school zone when warning flashers are in operation and a pedestrian is crossing?

choices.A: Slow down to 15 mph and proceed with caution.
choices.B: Honk the horn to warn the pedestrian.
choices.C: Stop and yield the right-of-way until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway.
choices.D: Swerve into the adjacent lane to avoid the pedestrian.

en.explanation: When in a marked school zone with warning flashers in operation, a driver must stop to yield the right-of-way and remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway.

en.question: You must always yield to a blind pedestrian who is using a guide dog or carrying what type of cane?

choices.A: A solid black cane.
choices.B: A white, metallic, or red-tipped white cane.
choices.C: A wooden walking stick.
choices.D: A yellow reflective cane.

en.explanation: Drivers must always yield to blind pedestrians carrying a white, metallic, red-tipped white cane or using a guide dog.

en.question: When there are no sidewalks available, where should pedestrians walk?

choices.A: On the right side of the road with traffic.
choices.B: In the center of the road.
choices.C: On the left side of the road facing traffic.
choices.D: On the shoulder of the road in the same direction as traffic.

en.explanation: When there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic so they can see sudden dangers coming at them.

en.question: How should two or more pedestrians walk when traveling on a road with no sidewalks?

choices.A: Side by side to increase visibility.
choices.B: In a single file line.
choices.C: Holding hands across the lane.
choices.D: One on the left side of the road and one on the right.

en.explanation: The manual states that two or more pedestrians should walk in single file and never side by side of each other when walking on the road.

en.question: Why is it important for pedestrians to keep a safe distance when standing on street corners?

choices.A: To avoid splashing water from puddles.
choices.B: Because trucks and buses make wide right turns and occasionally run up onto the corner of the sidewalk.
choices.C: To give bicyclists room to ride on the sidewalk.
choices.D: Because cars often run red lights at high speeds.

en.explanation: Trucks and buses make wide right turns and occasionally run up onto the corner of the sidewalk, so it is important for pedestrians to be alert and move back.

en.question: What should you do if you are in the middle of the street and the "DON'T WALK" signal starts flashing?

choices.A: Stop immediately and wait for the next WALK signal.
choices.B: Turn around and run back to the curb you started from.
choices.C: Continue walking to complete the crossing.
choices.D: Stand in the center median until traffic clears.

en.explanation: If you are in the middle of the street and the DON'T WALK signal starts flashing, continue walking. You will have time to complete the crossing.

en.question: What does a WALK signal or a green traffic light indicate to a pedestrian?

choices.A: It is completely safe to cross without looking.
choices.B: All oncoming traffic is guaranteed to stop.
choices.C: It is your turn to cross, but you must still look and proceed only if it is safe.
choices.D: You must run across the intersection as quickly as possible.

en.explanation: The WALK signal and the green traffic light indicate that it’s your turn to cross, but they do NOT mean it is SAFE to cross. It means LOOK and then IF it’s safe, proceed.

en.question: Even if you have the legal right-of-way as a driver, what should you NEVER do to a pedestrian in front of your car?

choices.A: Wait patiently for them to cross.
choices.B: Honk your horn or rev your engine to rush or scare them.
choices.C: Make eye contact with them.
choices.D: Yield the right-of-way.

en.explanation: Don’t honk your horn, rev up your engine or do anything to rush or scare a pedestrian in front of your car, even if you have the legal right-of-way.

en.question: What is the recommended looking procedure for a pedestrian before beginning to cross a street?

choices.A: Look right-left-right.
choices.B: Look straight ahead only.
choices.C: Look left-right-left, and over your shoulder for turning vehicles.
choices.D: Look up at the traffic light and proceed immediately.

en.explanation: Before crossing, stop at the curb and look left-right-left, and if it’s clear, begin crossing, look over your shoulder for turning vehicles.

en.question: Why should a pedestrian never walk behind a truck when it is backing up?

choices.A: The truck's exhaust fumes are toxic.
choices.B: Truck drivers cannot see directly behind the truck and could seriously injure you.
choices.C: The truck might drop its cargo.
choices.D: It is illegal to walk behind any commercial vehicle.

en.explanation: Never walk behind a truck when it is backing up; truck drivers cannot see directly behind the truck and could seriously injure you due to large blind spots.

en.question: When entering or leaving a driveway, alley, or parking lot, what must a driver do if their path crosses a sidewalk?

choices.A: Sound their horn to warn pedestrians to stop.
choices.B: Yield to pedestrians walking on the sidewalk.
choices.C: Proceed quickly to avoid blocking the sidewalk.
choices.D: Flash their headlights to gain the right-of-way.

en.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians walking on the sidewalk when entering or leaving a driveway, public parking garage, alley or parking lot and their path of travel crosses the sidewalk.

en.question: What is the safest bet for a pedestrian to be seen at night by drivers?

choices.A: Walking exclusively in crosswalks.
choices.B: Wearing dark clothing to reduce glare.
choices.C: Carrying a flashlight and wearing bright or reflective clothing.
choices.D: Walking on the right side of the road.

en.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing and carrying a flashlight is your safest bet for being seen at night.

en.question: What are the most common causes of collisions between vehicles and bicycles?

choices.A: Bicyclists running stop signs or red lights.
choices.B: Drivers turning left in front of an oncoming bicycle or turning right across the path of the bicycle.
choices.C: Bicyclists riding against the flow of traffic.
choices.D: Drivers passing bicyclists too closely on a multi-lane highway.

en.explanation: The most common causes of collisions are drivers turning left in front of an oncoming bicycle or turning right, across the path of the bicycle.

en.question: If your vehicle is sharing the left turn lane with a bicyclist, what should you do?

choices.A: Honk your horn to make them move out of your way.
choices.B: Pass them on the right before making your turn.
choices.C: Stay behind them until they have safely completed their turn.
choices.D: Pull up beside them and turn at the same time.

en.explanation: If your vehicle is sharing the left turn lane with a bicyclist, stay behind them until they have safely completed their turn.

en.question: Where are bicyclists prohibited from riding?

choices.A: On two-lane rural roads.
choices.B: On city streets with speed limits over 35 mph.
choices.C: On limited-access highways, expressways, and certain other marked roadways.
choices.D: In designated bicycle lanes.

en.explanation: Bicyclists are prohibited on limited-access highways, expressways and certain other marked roadways.

en.question: In Tennessee, what is the minimum distance a driver must leave when passing a bicyclist proceeding in the same direction?

choices.A: 2 feet
choices.B: 3 feet
choices.C: 4 feet
choices.D: 5 feet

en.explanation: When passing and overtaking a bicyclist proceeding in the same direction, do so slowly and leave at least a distance between you and the bicycle of not less than 3 feet. It’s the law in Tennessee!

en.question: What should you do if you are about to pass a bicycle on a narrow road and you think the rider doesn't know you are coming?

choices.A: Blast your horn to ensure they hear you.
choices.B: Tap your horn gently and briefly as a signal.
choices.C: Rev your engine loudly.
choices.D: Pass them as closely as possible so they notice you.

en.explanation: If you are about to pass a bicycle on a narrow road and you think the rider doesn’t know your coming, tap your horn gently and briefly as a signal that you’re going to pass.

en.question: What is the proper hand signal for a bicyclist to indicate a left turn?

choices.A: Extend the left arm out sideways bent at a 90-degree angle, hand pointing upward.
choices.B: Extend the left arm or right arm sideways and bend at a 90-degree angle, hand pointing downwards.
choices.C: Extend the left arm out sideways with all fingers extended or use the index finger to point left.
choices.D: Extend the right arm out straight with the palm facing backward.

en.explanation: Left Turn: Extend your left arm out sideways with all fingers extended or use your index finger to point left.

en.question: How does a bicyclist signal that they are stopping or slowing down?

choices.A: By extending the left arm out sideways with all fingers extended.
choices.B: By extending the left arm out sideways bent at a 90-degree angle, hand pointing upward.
choices.C: By extending the right arm out straight with all fingers extended.
choices.D: By extending the left or right arm sideways and bending it at a 90-degree angle, hand pointing downwards.

en.explanation: Stopping or Slowing: Extend your left arm or right arm sideways and bend your arm at a 90-degree angle at the elbow joint, hand pointing downwards and the palm of your hand facing backwards.

en.question: When is a bicyclist allowed full use of the lane?

choices.A: When the lane is too narrow for both a vehicle and a bicycle to safely share the lane.
choices.B: Whenever they are riding in a residential neighborhood.
choices.C: Only when they are riding in a group of three or more.
choices.D: Bicyclists are never allowed full use of the lane.

en.explanation: A bicyclist should be allowed full use of the lane when... The lane is too narrow for both a vehicle and a bicycle to safely share the lane. In this case it is safest to let the bicycle take the full lane.

en.question: According to Tennessee law, what lighting equipment is required on a bicycle used at night?

choices.A: A white light on the front visible from 500 feet and a red reflector or red light on the rear visible from 500 feet.
choices.B: A yellow light on the front visible from 300 feet and a white reflector on the rear.
choices.C: Only a red reflector on the rear visible from 200 feet.
choices.D: A flashing white light on the front and a flashing yellow light on the rear.

en.explanation: Tennessee law requires that a bicycle used at night must be equipped with a lamp on the front that emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet to the front and either a red reflector or lamp emitting a red light that is visible from distance of 500 feet to the rear.

en.question: Why do bicyclists tend to move toward the center of the lane when traveling past parked cars?

choices.A: To block traffic from passing them.
choices.B: To avoid injuring or being injured by persons getting out of those cars.
choices.C: Because the pavement is smoother in the center of the lane.
choices.D: To prepare for a right turn.

en.explanation: When cyclists are traveling past parked cars, they tend to move away from the cars, toward the center of the lane. This is to avoid injuring or being injured by persons getting out of those cars.

en.question: What should you do regarding your headlights when you see an oncoming bicycle rider at night?

choices.A: Use your high beams so you can see them clearly.
choices.B: Honk your horn continuously to let them know you are there.
choices.C: Do not use high beams.
choices.D: Flash your high beams repeatedly to warn them.

en.explanation: At night, do not use high beams when you see an oncoming bicycle rider.

en.question: Why is it dangerous for a bicyclist to ride against the flow of traffic?

choices.A: It makes the bicyclist travel too fast.
choices.B: It may cause the bicyclist to miss traffic control devices, such as traffic signs and stop lights.
choices.C: It is illegal for vehicles to pass a bicyclist riding against traffic.
choices.D: It causes the bicycle's tires to wear out unevenly.

en.explanation: Ride on the right side, with the flow of traffic. Riding against traffic may cause you to miss traffic control devices, such as traffic signs and stop lights.

en.question: Why should a bicyclist never sneak in between a large truck or bus and the curb?

choices.A: The truck or bus driver might ask them for directions.
choices.B: The bicyclist might get a flat tire from debris near the curb.
choices.C: Trucks and buses make wide right turns, and the bicyclist could get crushed.
choices.D: The bicyclist will be forced to ride on the sidewalk.

en.explanation: Trucks and buses make wide right turns. Never sneak in between a truck or bus and the curb or you could get crushed.

en.question: What is the "No-Zone" in relation to large trucks?

choices.A: A designated parking area for trucks only.
choices.B: Blind spots in the front, back, and on the sides of the truck where the driver cannot see you.
choices.C: A zone where trucks are not allowed to drive.
choices.D: The area immediately in front of a truck where bicyclists have the right-of-way.

en.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in the front, back and on the sides, which make it difficult for the driver to see around them. These are known as the No-Zone.

en.question: What does a red or orange pennant flag on a bicycle's antennae indicate to drivers?

choices.A: The rider is a child.
choices.B: The rider is carrying hazardous materials.
choices.C: The rider has impaired hearing.
choices.D: The rider is a beginner.

en.explanation: If you see a bicyclist with a red or orange pennant flag on the antennae attached to the bike, slow down: this is a common symbol to indicate the rider has impaired hearing.

en.question: According to research, what causes two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions?

choices.A: The motorcyclist speeding or driving aggressively.
choices.B: The driver of the car turning in front of the motorcycle.
choices.C: Pedestrians crossing the street illegally.
choices.D: Large trucks changing lanes without signaling.

en.explanation: Research shows that two-thirds of car-motorcycle collisions are caused, not by the motorcyclist, but by the driver who turned in front of the motorcycle.

en.question: When driving alongside a motorcycle in the same lane, you should:

choices.A: Share the lane with the motorcycle to improve traffic flow.
choices.B: Honk your horn to let them know you are passing.
choices.C: Never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.
choices.D: Force the motorcycle to the edge of the lane.

en.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to the use of the full lane. You must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle, and you should always respect the cycle's space and position in traffic.

en.question: What is the minimum recommended following distance a driver should allow when behind a motorcycle?

choices.A: One second
choices.B: Two seconds
choices.C: Four seconds
choices.D: Five seconds

en.explanation: Allow at least a two-second following distance, so the motorcycle rider has enough time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.

en.question: Why should you avoid passing a motorcycle too close or too fast?

choices.A: The motorcycle may try to race you.
choices.B: The blast of air can blow a motorcycle out of control.
choices.C: The motorcyclist might not hear your engine.
choices.D: It is illegal to pass a motorcycle on a multi-lane highway.

en.explanation: Pass as you would pass a car, and don't pass too close or too fast as the blast of air can blow a motorcycle out of control.

en.question: How might a motorcyclist react when crossing a railroad grade crossing?

choices.A: Speed up to cross as quickly as possible.
choices.B: Stop completely and walk the motorcycle across.
choices.C: Slow down and possibly zigzag to cross the tracks.
choices.D: Ride on the shoulder to avoid the tracks entirely.

en.explanation: Railroad grade crossings are a particular hazard to cyclists, and will usually cause them to slow down and possibly zigzag to cross the tracks.

en.question: What should a driver expect an experienced motorcyclist to do when riding over a metal or grated bridge?

choices.A: Accelerate rapidly to minimize time on the bridge.
choices.B: Move to the shoulder of the bridge.
choices.C: Slow down and move to the center of the lane.
choices.D: Stand up on the foot pegs and weave.

en.explanation: Metal or grated bridges cause a cycle to wobble much more than a car. An experienced cyclist slows down and moves to the center of the lane to allow room for handling the uneven surface.

en.question: What is the most important piece of equipment a motorcyclist can wear when riding?

choices.A: Leather gloves
choices.B: A DOT-approved helmet
choices.C: Steel-toed boots
choices.D: A reflective jacket

en.explanation: Helmets are the most important piece of equipment you can wear when riding your motorcycle. Beware of helmets that do not meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

en.question: Where are the blind spots, or "No-Zones," located on a large truck?

choices.A: Only directly behind the truck.
choices.B: Only on the right side of the truck.
choices.C: In the front, back, and on both sides of the truck.
choices.D: Only directly in front of the truck.

en.explanation: Trucks have large No-Zones on both sides, the front and behind the truck. Truck drivers cannot see you when you ride in these blind spots.

en.question: When passing a large truck, when is it safe to pull back in front of it?

choices.A: As soon as your rear bumper clears the truck's front bumper.
choices.B: When you can see the front of the truck in your rear-view mirror.
choices.C: When the truck driver honks their horn.
choices.D: When you are exactly one car length ahead of the truck.

en.explanation: When passing, look for the front of the truck in your rear-view mirror before pulling in front and avoid braking.

en.question: In crashes involving large trucks and cars, what percentage of fatalities are sustained by the occupants of the car?

choices.A: 25 percent
choices.B: 50 percent
choices.C: 78 percent
choices.D: 95 percent

en.explanation: In crashes involving large trucks, the occupants of a car, usually the driver, sustain 78 percent of fatalities.

en.question: Why is a large truck's front blind spot particularly dangerous for a motorcyclist?

choices.A: Motorcycles accelerate much slower than trucks.
choices.B: Motorcycles can stop much faster than trucks, and the truck may not be able to stop in time.
choices.C: The truck's headlights will blind the motorcyclist.
choices.D: The truck's exhaust fumes can overwhelm the motorcyclist.

en.explanation: The front blind spot is particularly dangerous if you need to stop quickly. Because of their lightweight and braking system, motorcycles can stop much faster than trucks. A truck may not be able to stop as quickly as you do.

en.question: Why do children riding bicycles create special problems for drivers?

choices.A: They are not capable of proper judgment in determining traffic conditions.
choices.B: They always ride faster than the speed limit.
choices.C: They are required to ride on the left side of the road.
choices.D: They use hand signals that are difficult to understand.

en.explanation: Children are not capable of proper judgment in determining traffic conditions, therefore drivers should be alert to the possibility of erratic movement and sudden changes in direction when children on bicycles are present.

en.question: Why do drivers often fail to see motorcyclists on the road?

choices.A: Motorcycles are painted in colors that blend into the road.
choices.B: Drivers tend to look for other cars and trucks, and the motorcycle's narrow profile makes it harder to see.
choices.C: Motorcycles are usually driven below the speed limit.
choices.D: Motorcyclists are not required to use headlights during the day.

en.explanation: Drivers tend to look for other cars and trucks, not for motorcycles. The profile of a motorcycle is narrow and the body is short, making it harder to see and making it harder for a driver to estimate the cycle's distance and speed.

en.question: What makes bicyclists especially difficult to see at night?

choices.A: They are not allowed to use reflectors.
choices.B: They ride exclusively in the middle of the lane at night.
choices.C: Lights from approaching traffic may make them even harder to see.
choices.D: They travel much faster at night than during the day.

en.explanation: Bicyclists riding at night present visibility problems for drivers... Lights from approaching traffic may make them even harder to see at night.

en.question: According to the manual, how long does it take a truck traveling at 55 MPH to stop compared to a car?

choices.A: A truck stops in 240 feet, the same as a car.
choices.B: A truck takes about 300 feet to stop.
choices.C: A truck takes about 450+ feet to stop.
choices.D: A truck takes over 600 feet to stop.

en.explanation: A car traveling at 55 MPH can stop in 240 feet; however, a truck traveling at the same speed of 55 MPH takes about 450+ feet to stop.

en.question: What is a crucial rule of thumb to remember regarding a large truck's blind spots?

choices.A: If you are within 50 feet of the truck, you are in a blind spot.
choices.B: If you can't see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the truck driver can't see you.
choices.C: Trucks only have blind spots on their right side.
choices.D: Honk your horn to ensure the driver knows you are in their blind spot.

en.explanation: The manual states: "if you can't see the truck driver in the truck's mirror, the truck driver can't see you."

en.question: Why is it dangerous to try to get in between a large truck and the curb when the truck is making a turn?

choices.A: The truck may accelerate suddenly and strike your vehicle.
choices.B: Trucks often swing wide to the left to safely negotiate a right turn, creating a dangerous "squeeze" play.
choices.C: The truck's exhaust is directed toward the curb and can obscure your vision.
choices.D: It is illegal to pass a truck on the right under any circumstances.

en.explanation: Truck drivers sometimes need to swing wide to the left in order to safely negotiate a right turn. Cutting in between the truck and the curb increases the possibility of a crash by catching you in a "squeeze".

en.question: A typical fully loaded tractor-trailer combination may weigh up to how much?

choices.A: 40,000 pounds
choices.B: 60,000 pounds
choices.C: 80,000 pounds
choices.D: 100,000 pounds

en.explanation: A typical tractor-trailer combination, a loaded semi-trailer hinged and being pulled by a tractor unit, may weigh up to 80,000 pounds or 40 tons.

en.question: What should you do if you are stopped behind a truck on an uphill grade?

choices.A: Stay to the right in your lane and honk your horn.
choices.B: Stay to the left in your lane so the driver can see you and leave extra space.
choices.C: Pull up as close to the truck's bumper as possible to prevent rollback.
choices.D: Shift your vehicle into neutral and apply the parking brake.

en.explanation: If you are stopped behind a truck on an uphill grade, stay to the left in your lane so the driver can see you. Leave extra space in front of your car in case the truck rolls back.

en.question: What does it mean if a truck driver blinks their vehicle headlights after you pass them?

choices.A: They are warning you of a police officer or hazard ahead.
choices.B: They are signaling that you are cleared to pull back in front of their vehicle.
choices.C: They are angry that you passed them too closely.
choices.D: Their headlights are malfunctioning and you should speed up.

en.explanation: If the truck or bus driver blinks their vehicle headlights after you pass, it's a signal that you are cleared to pull back in front of their vehicle.

en.question: How far to the rear can a large truck's blind spot extend?

choices.A: Up to 50 feet
choices.B: Up to 100 feet
choices.C: Up to 150 feet
choices.D: Up to 200 feet

en.explanation: A truck's blind spots are immediate in front, on either side of the car and up to 200 feet in the rear.

en.question: If a tractor has a long hood, the trucker may not be able to see the first how many feet in front of the bumper?

choices.A: 5-10 feet
choices.B: 10-20 feet
choices.C: 20-30 feet
choices.D: 30-40 feet

en.explanation: If the tractor has a long hood, the trucker may not be able to see the first 10-20 feet in front of the bumper, plenty of room for a motorcycle or car to slip unnoticed into a dangerous position.

en.question: What should you do when driving near a Commercial Vehicle Weigh Station?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the station as quickly as possible.
choices.B: Avoid driving in the right lane so slow-moving trucks can easily merge back onto the roadway.
choices.C: Move into the right lane to follow the trucks closely.
choices.D: Flash your high beams at merging trucks to warn them of your presence.

en.explanation: When you are near a Commercial Vehicle Weigh Station, avoid driving in the right lane so slow-moving trucks can easily merge back onto the roadway.

en.question: Why is it important to dim your headlights at night when driving near large trucks?

choices.A: Bright lights can drain your vehicle's battery faster.
choices.B: Bright lights reflected in the truck's mirrors can blind the driver.
choices.C: Truck drivers use night-vision goggles that are sensitive to light.
choices.D: It helps the truck driver see the road lines better.

en.explanation: Dim your lights at night. Bright lights reflected in the mirrors can blind the driver.

en.question: Why should you never underestimate the speed of an approaching large truck or bus?

choices.A: They are always exceeding the posted speed limit.
choices.B: Because of their large size, they often appear to be traveling more slowly than their actual speed.
choices.C: They have special engines that allow them to accelerate silently.
choices.D: Their speedometers are often inaccurate by up to 10 MPH.

en.explanation: Never underestimate the size and speed of approaching trucks and buses. Because of their large size they often appear to be traveling more slowly than their actual speed.

en.question: According to the manual, what is the single most important thing you can do to save your life, especially in a crash with a large truck?

choices.A: Swerve into the ditch to avoid the impact.
choices.B: Wear your safety belt.
choices.C: Honk your horn continuously before impact.
choices.D: Brace yourself firmly against the steering wheel.

en.explanation: Wearing a safety belt is the single most important thing you can do to save your life, especially in a crash with a large truck. It keeps you from striking the steering wheel, being thrown around, and being ejected.

en.question: What should you anticipate when passing a large truck on a downhill grade?

choices.A: The truck will likely lose speed due to engine braking.
choices.B: The truck will travel faster due to its weight, and you may have to increase your speed to pass.
choices.C: The truck will pull over to the shoulder to let you pass.
choices.D: The truck driver will apply the emergency brake to maintain a slow speed.

en.explanation: Because of their weight, trucks travel faster downhill and you may have to increase your speed to pass a truck on a downhill grade.

en.question: Why should you avoid driving directly behind a truck or bus and instead keep a reasonable distance?

choices.A: To avoid breathing in harmful exhaust fumes.
choices.B: To give yourself a better view of the road to anticipate problems and room for an emergency "out".
choices.C: Because drafting behind a commercial vehicle is illegal in Tennessee.
choices.D: To prevent the truck's tires from throwing rocks at your windshield.

en.explanation: Keep a reasonable distance between your vehicle and the large vehicle ahead. This gives you a better view of the road to anticipate problems, and you will give yourself room for an emergency "out".

en.question: When passing a truck on a downhill grade, what is the safest course of action?

choices.A: Slow down to match the truck's speed before passing.
choices.B: Complete your pass as quickly as possible and maintain your speed.
choices.C: Stay alongside the truck to prevent it from speeding up.
choices.D: Pass the truck and immediately brake to control your speed.

en.explanation: Because of their weight, trucks travel faster downhill. You should complete your pass as quickly as possible, don't stay alongside the truck, and maintain your speed after passing without slowing down.

en.question: When meeting a truck or bus coming from the opposite direction, how does wind turbulence affect the vehicles?

choices.A: It sucks the vehicles together.
choices.B: It pushes the vehicles apart.
choices.C: It pulls the smaller vehicle under the truck.
choices.D: It has no effect on the vehicles.

en.explanation: When meeting a truck or bus from the opposite direction, the wind turbulence between the vehicles PUSHES vehicles APART; it does NOT suck them together.

en.question: Why should you avoid moving into the open space on the right side of a truck making a right turn?

choices.A: The truck driver is preparing to back up into that space.
choices.B: The truck may be carrying hazardous materials that could spill.
choices.C: The truck driver may not see you and your car can be crunched or sideswiped.
choices.D: The truck will accelerate rapidly through the turn.

en.explanation: Trucks make wide right turns and often leave an open space on the right. If you are between the truck and the curb, the driver may not be able to see you and your car can be crunched or sideswiped by the trailer.

en.question: What is the purpose of runaway truck ramps?

choices.A: To provide a rest area for tired commercial drivers.
choices.B: To allow trucks to safely load and unload cargo.
choices.C: To stop out-of-control trucks or buses going down steep downgrades.
choices.D: To weigh trucks before they enter the highway.

en.explanation: Runaway truck ramps are designed to stop out-of-control trucks or buses going down steep downgrades. Vehicles should never stop or park in these areas.

en.question: The front 'NO-ZONE' of a large vehicle extends approximately how far directly in front of the truck?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 20 feet
choices.C: 50 feet
choices.D: 100 feet

en.explanation: The area approximately up to 20 feet directly in front of a large vehicle is considered a NO-ZONE, where cutting in too soon can cause a crash.

en.question: Children should stay at least how far away from a school bus to remain out of the Danger Zone?

choices.A: 5 feet
choices.B: 10 feet
choices.C: 15 feet
choices.D: 20 feet

en.explanation: The Danger Zone is the area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger. Children should stay ten feet away from the school bus and NEVER go behind it.

en.question: According to the manual, when are children at the greatest risk of being hurt regarding school buses?

choices.A: While riding inside the bus on the highway.
choices.B: When the bus is involved in a rear-end collision.
choices.C: Outside the bus when they are getting on or off.
choices.D: When sitting in the front row of the bus.

en.explanation: The reality of school bus safety is that more children are hurt outside a bus than inside one. Children are at greatest risk when they are getting on or off the school bus.

en.question: What does the 'slow moving vehicle' emblem look like?

choices.A: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with black lettering.
choices.B: A fluorescent or reflective orange triangle.
choices.C: A red octagon with a white border.
choices.D: A white rectangle with a black tractor symbol.

en.explanation: The 'slow moving vehicle' emblem is a fluorescent or reflective orange triangle that must be displayed on the rear of vehicles drawn by animals, and most farm vehicles and construction equipment.

en.question: Because farm machinery usually does not have turn signals, how might an operator prepare to make a right turn?

choices.A: By flashing their headlights three times.
choices.B: By pulling wide to the left first, then turning right.
choices.C: By stopping completely and waving traffic around.
choices.D: By driving on the right shoulder before turning.

en.explanation: Farm machinery usually does not have turn signals and to make a right turn, operators of farm machinery may first pull wide to the left, then turn to the right.

en.question: Which of the following is true about animal-drawn vehicles on Tennessee roadways?

choices.A: They are only allowed on unpaved rural roads.
choices.B: They must yield the right-of-way to all motor vehicles.
choices.C: They have the same rights to use the road as a motor vehicle.
choices.D: They are not required to follow standard rules of the road.

en.explanation: Animal-drawn vehicles have the same rights to use the road as a motor vehicle and must follow the same rules of the road.

en.question: If you are following a truck down a steep hill and notice smoking wheels or high speed, what should you do?

choices.A: Speed up and pass the truck immediately.
choices.B: Honk your horn to alert the driver.
choices.C: Fall back and DO NOT pass.
choices.D: Pull over to the left shoulder and stop.

en.explanation: Smoking wheels or a high speed can be a sign of brake loss on a heavy vehicle. If you encounter this situation, fall back and DO NOT pass.

en.question: Why should you avoid driving too close to trucks transporting hazardous materials?

choices.A: They make frequent stops, such as at railroad crossings.
choices.B: They travel much faster than standard commercial trucks.
choices.C: They create more wind turbulence than other trucks.
choices.D: They are not equipped with standard brake lights.

en.explanation: Don't drive too close to trucks that are transporting hazardous materials, since they make frequent stops, such as railroad crossings.

en.question: What should you do when a truck or bus is passing you?

choices.A: Speed up to get out of the truck's blind spot.
choices.B: Move to the center of your lane and maintain speed.
choices.C: Keep to the far side of your lane and reduce your speed slightly.
choices.D: Flash your high beams to warn the truck driver.

en.explanation: When a truck passes you, you can help the driver by keeping to the far side of your lane and reducing your speed slightly. NEVER SPEED UP AS A TRUCK OR BUS IS PASSING.

en.question: In many school systems, children are taught to escape the school bus danger zone by taking:

choices.A: Three small steps away from the bus.
choices.B: Five giant steps as soon as they exit the bus.
choices.C: Ten normal steps toward the rear of the bus.
choices.D: Two giant steps toward the front of the bus.

en.explanation: In many school systems, children are taught to escape the danger zone by taking five giant steps as soon as they exit the bus.

en.question: In most cases, large farm machinery on rural highways will be traveling at speeds less than:
en.explanation: In most cases, farm machinery vehicles will be traveling at less than 25 M.P.H.

en.question: What should you avoid doing when approaching or passing a horseback rider?

choices.A: Slowing down
choices.B: Sounding your horn or revving your engine
choices.C: Leaving a reasonable distance
choices.D: Passing on the left

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Do NOT sound your horn or "rev" your engine loudly when approaching or passing a horse.'

en.question: What is the normal speed range for slow-moving vehicles?

choices.A: 15 to 30 mph
choices.B: 5 to 20 mph
choices.C: 10 to 25 mph
choices.D: 20 to 40 mph

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'Normal speeds for slow-moving vehicles may range from 5 to 20 mph.'

en.question: When lights are required on slow-moving vehicles, how far to the rear is the self-luminous red lamp normally visible?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 250 feet
choices.C: 500 feet
choices.D: 1000 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that a self-luminous red lamp on the rear of a slow-moving vehicle is normally visible for 500 feet to the rear.

en.question: Which lane should slower traffic use?

choices.A: The left-hand lane
choices.B: The center lane
choices.C: The right-hand lane
choices.D: Any lane as long as they maintain a constant speed

en.explanation: The manual dictates, 'Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.'

en.question: What color background do all temporary signs in work zones have?

choices.A: Yellow
choices.B: Red
choices.C: Orange
choices.D: White

en.explanation: The manual states, 'All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols.'

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a speed violation in a work zone where the speed has been reduced and workers are present?
en.explanation: Under Tennessee law, speed violations in work zones with reduced speeds and workers present will result in a fine up to a maximum of $500.

en.question: How far does a car traveling at 60 M.P.H. travel in one second?

choices.A: 44 feet
choices.B: 60 feet
choices.C: 88 feet
choices.D: 120 feet

en.explanation: The manual notes, 'A car traveling 60 M.P.H. travels 88 feet per second.'

en.question: What is the most common type of accident in a work zone?

choices.A: Head-on collisions
choices.B: Rear-end collisions
choices.C: Sideswipes
choices.D: Rollovers

en.explanation: The manual warns drivers not to tailgate because 'Most work zone accidents are caused by rear-end collisions.'

en.question: How long does it take for a train traveling at 55 miles per hour to stop?

choices.A: A quarter of a mile
choices.B: Half a mile
choices.C: A full mile
choices.D: Two miles

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'A train traveling at 55 miles per hour takes a full mile to stop.'

en.question: How much more likely are you to die in a collision with a train compared to a collision with a car?

choices.A: 5 times more likely
choices.B: 10 times more likely
choices.C: 20 times more likely
choices.D: 30 times more likely

en.explanation: The manual states, 'You are 30 times more likely to die in a collision with a train than with a car or even a large truck or bus.'

en.question: Where do most train collisions with cars occur?

choices.A: Within 25 miles of the driver's home
choices.B: On rural, unmarked dirt roads
choices.C: At night in poorly lit areas
choices.D: More than 100 miles from the driver's home

en.explanation: The manual explains that 'Most of the collisions occur within 25 miles of the driver’s home, suggesting that drivers KNEW the tracks were there...'

en.question: Who has the right-of-way when a car and a train are approaching a crossing?

choices.A: The vehicle that arrives first
choices.B: The train ALWAYS has the right-of-way
choices.C: The car, if it is traveling at highway speeds
choices.D: The train, but only if warning lights are flashing

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states, 'Drivers must ALWAYS yield the right of way to trains because IT’S THE LAW.'

en.question: What color apparel will workers normally wear in a work zone to ensure they are highly visible?

choices.A: Bright orange
choices.B: Bright yellow-green
choices.C: Reflective white
choices.D: Neon pink

en.explanation: The manual states, 'In these work zones, workers will normally be wearing bright yellow-green apparel such as shirts, vests or hardhats to ensure they are highly visible.'

en.question: How should horseback riders position themselves when riding on the road?

choices.A: Two abreast in the right lane
choices.B: Single file near the right curb or road edge
choices.C: Single file near the center line
choices.D: On the left shoulder facing traffic

en.explanation: The manual requires that horseback riders 'must ride single file near the right curb or road edge, or on a usable right shoulder, lane or path.'

en.question: When approaching a railroad crossing equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices, where must you bring your vehicle to a complete stop?

choices.A: Within 100 feet, but no closer than 25 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.B: Within 50 feet, but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.C: Within 30 feet, but no closer than 10 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.D: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail.

en.explanation: The manual states that railroad crossings equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices require the operator to bring the vehicle to a complete stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.

en.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train is approaching, in which direction should you run after exiting the vehicle?

choices.A: In the same direction the train is traveling.
choices.B: Directly away from the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
choices.C: Toward the train at a 45-degree angle.
choices.D: Parallel to the tracks in the opposite direction of the train.

en.explanation: According to the manual, if a train is approaching, you should run toward the train at a 45-degree angle to be away from and behind the point of impact.

en.question: Why should you run toward an approaching train at a 45-degree angle if your vehicle stalls on the tracks?

choices.A: To signal the train engineer to stop.
choices.B: To get a better view of the train's speed.
choices.C: To reach the Emergency Notification System sign faster.
choices.D: To be away from and behind the point of impact to prevent injury from flying debris.

en.explanation: The manual explains that running toward the train at a 45-degree angle allows you to be away from and behind the point of impact, preventing injury from flying debris.

en.question: What should you do if you are already crossing railroad tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or the gates start coming down?

choices.A: Stop immediately and back up.
choices.B: Keep moving and finish driving through the crossing.
choices.C: Stop your vehicle on the tracks and exit immediately.
choices.D: Put your vehicle in reverse and carefully back off the tracks.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "If you are crossing the tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or the gates start coming down, don’t stop. KEEP MOVING!"

en.question: Which of the following vehicles are required to stop at all railroad crossings whether signals are activated or not?

choices.A: Motorcycles and mopeds.
choices.B: 15-passenger vans and recreational vehicles.
choices.C: School buses, passenger buses, and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
choices.D: Tow trucks and emergency vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual notes that School Buses, Passenger Buses, and Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop at all crossings whether signals are activated or not.

en.question: What information is provided on the blue Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a railroad crossing?

choices.A: The train schedule and expected arrival times.
choices.B: The speed limit for trains passing through the crossing.
choices.C: An emergency contact number and the DOT crossing number.
choices.D: The distance to the next highway intersection.

en.explanation: The manual states that the ENS sign provides an emergency number to call and the DOT crossing number to identify your location if your vehicle stalls on the tracks.

en.question: What type of special endorsement or license is required to operate a 15-passenger van in the State of Tennessee?

choices.A: A Commercial Driver License (CDL).
choices.B: A Class D license with a passenger endorsement.
choices.C: A chauffeur's license.
choices.D: No special endorsements or licenses are needed.

en.explanation: The manual states: "There are no special endorsements or licenses needed to operate a 15-passenger van in the State of Tennessee."

en.question: When loading a 15-passenger van, why should passengers sit as far toward the front of the vehicle as possible?

choices.A: To allow the driver to hear them better.
choices.B: Because the rear seat is behind the rear axle, which pushes the center of gravity further back.
choices.C: To leave the rear seats open for heavy cargo and luggage.
choices.D: Because the front seats are equipped with better airbags.

en.explanation: The manual advises having passengers sit towards the front because the rear seat is located behind the rear axle, causing uneven weight distribution and pushing the center of gravity further back.

en.question: In a 15-passenger van, under-inflation of the rear tires is a major cause of what dangerous issue?

choices.A: Engine overheating.
choices.B: Brake failure.
choices.C: Tread separation.
choices.D: Transmission slipping.

en.explanation: According to the manual, under-inflation of the rear tires (especially the left rear) is a major cause of tread separation in 15-passenger vans.

en.question: How should weight be distributed in a Recreational Vehicle (RV) to provide better handling and maintain a proper center of gravity?

choices.A: Closer to the roof and mostly on the right side.
choices.B: Closer to the ground and equal on both sides.
choices.C: Entirely in the rear of the vehicle.
choices.D: Mostly in the front near the driver's seat.

en.explanation: The manual states that distributing the weight closer to the ground and equal on both sides keeps the center of gravity low and will provide better handling of your RV.

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding the blind spots, or "No-Zones," of a Recreational Vehicle (RV)?

choices.A: RVs do not have blind spots if the mirrors are adjusted correctly.
choices.B: RV mirrors allow the driver to see everything on the road.
choices.C: RVs have large blind spots, and mirrors do not allow the driver to see everything.
choices.D: Only the right side of an RV has a blind spot.

en.explanation: The manual warns that RVs are large and have many blind spots, and while mirrors are important, they do not allow the driver to see everything on the road.
