choices.D: You are permanently disqualified from getting a license

en.explanation: If you do not pass the knowledge and driving exams on your first attempt, your application will be held for 90 days.

en.question: At what age are individuals required to successfully complete an approved driver education course to apply for a license?

choices.A: Younger than 18 years of age
choices.B: Younger than 21 years of age
choices.C: Younger than 25 years of age
choices.D: All applicants regardless of age

en.explanation: Individuals younger than 25 years of age are required to successfully complete an approved driver education course.

en.question: Who may ask the DPS to cancel the license of a minor under 18 years of age?

choices.A: A school principal
choices.B: The person who signed the application under oath
choices.C: Any licensed driver over 21
choices.D: A law enforcement officer

en.explanation: The person who signs (parent, guardian, employer, or county judge) may ask DPS to cancel your license any time before your 18th birthday.

en.question: Which of the following will result in an automatic failure of your driving exam?

choices.A: Having more than 10 points deducted
choices.B: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
choices.C: Refusing to follow instructions
choices.D: Using a back-up camera while parallel parking

en.explanation: Your application for a license will not be approved if you: 1. Violate the law 2. Refuse to follow instructions 3. Drive dangerously or have a crash 4. Have more than 30 points deducted.

en.question: When taking the driving exam, what is the policy regarding the use of vehicle parking technology?

choices.A: You may use an automated vehicle parking function
choices.B: You may use a back-up camera, but not an automated vehicle parking function
choices.C: You cannot use mirrors or cameras
choices.D: You must disable all electronic sensors

en.explanation: You may use the back-up camera on your vehicle for parallel parking; however, the use of an automated vehicle parking function will not be allowed.

en.question: During the quick stop portion of the driving exam, at what speed may you be asked to stop your car as quickly as possible?

choices.A: About 10 mph
choices.B: About 20 mph
choices.C: About 30 mph
choices.D: About 40 mph

en.explanation: Quick stop – You may be asked to stop your car as quickly as possible at about 20 mph without skidding your tires.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first conviction of driving without a license?

choices.A: A fine of up to $200
choices.B: A fine of $25 to $200
choices.C: Confinement in jail for up to 30 days
choices.D: A fine up to $4,000

en.explanation: According to the Penalties for Driving Without a License table, a 1st conviction results in a fine of up to $200.

en.question: What is the penalty if a driver operates a vehicle without a license and insurance, and causes a crash resulting in serious bodily injury or death?

choices.A: A fine of up to $500
choices.B: A Class C misdemeanor
choices.C: A Class A misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $4,000 and/or up to 365 days in jail
choices.D: A felony punishable by up to 5 years in prison

en.explanation: Driving without a license, operating a vehicle without insurance at the time of the offense, and driver causes a crash resulting in serious bodily injury or death is a Class A misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $4,000 and/or confinement in jail for not more than 365 days.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four basic skills all drivers are graded on during the driving exam?

choices.A: Control
choices.B: Observation
choices.C: Speeding
choices.D: Positioning

en.explanation: All drivers are graded on four basic skills: Control, Observation, Positioning, and Signaling.

en.question: If you pass the driving exam, to whom must you show your driver license upon request?

choices.A: Only a state trooper
choices.B: Any peace officer, judge, or anyone with whom you are involved in a crash
choices.C: Any licensed driver who asks to see it
choices.D: Only a judge or justice of the peace

en.explanation: If you pass the driving exam, always carry your license with you when driving and upon request, show it to: 1. Any peace officer, sheriff, constable, judge, justice of the peace, or state trooper 2. Anyone with whom you are involved in a crash.

en.question: How many times can you fail the knowledge and driving exams before a new application and fee are required?

choices.A: Two times
choices.B: Three times
choices.C: Four times
choices.D: Five times

en.explanation: After 90 days or three failed exams, a new application and fee will be required.

en.question: When operating a standard transmission vehicle during the driving exam, when should you hold the clutch all the way down?

choices.A: Only when starting the motor
choices.B: Whenever you are driving above 30 mph
choices.C: When starting the motor, shifting gears, stopping, and when speed drops below 10 mph
choices.D: You should drive with your foot resting on the clutch at all times

en.explanation: On standard transmissions, hold the clutch all the way down when starting the motor, shifting gears, when stopping, and once your speed drops below 10 mph. Do not drive with your foot resting on the clutch.

en.question: How many days do you have to report a change of address to the Texas DPS?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, a change of address must be reported to DPS within 30 days.

en.question: How often must a Texas driver license be renewed?

choices.A: Every 4 years
choices.B: Every 6 years
choices.C: Every 8 years
choices.D: Every 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states that a Texas driver license must be renewed every eight years.

en.question: How often must a person appear in a driver license office in person for a vision exam and to update their photo, signature, and fingerprints?

choices.A: At least once every 8 years
choices.B: At least once every 10 years
choices.C: At least once every 12 years
choices.D: At least once every 16 years

en.explanation: A person must appear in a driver license office at least once every sixteen (16) years for a vision exam and to update the photo, signature, and fingerprints.

en.question: What is the reinstatement fee for an Administrative License Revocation (ALR)?
en.explanation: The manual specifies that Administrative License Revocations (ALR) require a $125 reinstatement fee.

en.question: Which of the following groups of drivers is NOT eligible to renew their driver license using alternate methods like online or by mail?

choices.A: Drivers over the age of 50
choices.B: Commercial driver license (CDL) holders
choices.C: Drivers who have held a license for more than 10 years
choices.D: Active duty military personnel

en.explanation: Alternate methods to renew will not be extended to Commercial driver license (CDL) holders, among other specific groups.

en.question: Under Administrative Suspensions and Revocations, your license may be suspended for repeated traffic violations if you have:

choices.A: Two or more traffic convictions within any 12-month period
choices.B: Three or more traffic convictions within any 24-month period
choices.C: Four or more traffic convictions occurring separately within any 12-month period
choices.D: Five or more traffic convictions within any 24-month period

en.explanation: DPS has the authority to suspend or revoke a license for repeated violations of traffic laws, including four or more traffic convictions occurring separately within any 12-month period.

en.question: If you are returning to Texas from military service and your license has been expired for over two years, how long do you have after being honorably discharged to renew without taking the knowledge and driving exams?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: Within 90 days of being honorably discharged, military personnel returning from active duty can present separation papers to obtain a renewal without taking the exams when the license has been expired for over two years.

en.question: Which of the following offenses will result in an automatic suspension of driving privileges for individuals under 21 years of age?

choices.A: Failure to complete a tobacco awareness class when required
choices.B: Parking in a loading zone
choices.C: Driving with an expired vehicle registration
choices.D: Failing to wear a seatbelt

en.explanation: For individuals under 21, failure to complete a tobacco awareness class when required is a Health and Safety Code Violation that will result in automatic suspension of the driving privilege.

en.question: What must you do to change information on your driver license other than your address?

choices.A: Mail a completed DL-64 form
choices.B: Visit a driver license office
choices.C: Call the DPS hotline
choices.D: Update it through the online portal

en.explanation: The manual states: 'To change any other information on your driver license or ID card, you will need to visit a driver license office.'

en.question: What is the purpose of a restriction placed on your driver license?

choices.A: To punish you for past traffic violations
choices.B: To increase the cost of your auto insurance
choices.C: To make you a safer driver
choices.D: To limit the number of passengers you can carry

en.explanation: A restriction may be placed on your license. This is not meant to interfere with your driving but to make you a safer driver.

en.question: What is the reinstatement fee required for a Drug Education Course suspension?
en.explanation: The manual notes that there is a $100 reinstatement fee for a Drug Education Course.

en.question: If an eligible out-of-state Texas licensee renews by mail, how long is the renewed license valid once they return to Texas?

choices.A: Until 30 days after returning to Texas
choices.B: Until 60 days after returning to Texas
choices.C: Until 90 days after returning to Texas or the expiration date, whichever comes first
choices.D: Until 180 days after returning to Texas

en.explanation: For out-of-state Texas licensees renewing by mail, the license will be renewed and valid to the expiration date shown or until 90 days after your return to Texas, whichever comes first.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a reason for an Administrative Suspension or Revocation rather than an automatic Mandatory Suspension?

choices.A: Driving while intoxicated (DWI) by use of alcohol or drugs
choices.B: Intoxication manslaughter or intoxication assault
choices.C: Causing a serious crash while driving a motor vehicle
choices.D: Overtaking and passing a school bus (subsequent conviction)

en.explanation: Causing a serious crash while driving a motor vehicle is listed under Administrative Suspensions and Revocations, whereas DWI, intoxication manslaughter, and passing a school bus are Mandatory Suspensions.

en.question: Under the Administrative License Revocation (ALR) law, DPS is authorized to suspend the license of an individual over 21 years of age who fails a breath or blood test indicating a blood alcohol content (BAC) of at least:
en.explanation: DPS is authorized to suspend a license for individuals over 21 who fail a breath or blood test indicating a BAC level of 0.08 or more.

en.question: For individuals under 21 years of age, DPS is authorized to suspend a license or driving privilege for what amount of alcohol under the ALR law?

choices.A: A BAC of 0.08 or more
choices.B: A BAC of 0.04 or more
choices.C: A BAC of 0.02 or more
choices.D: Any detectable amount of alcohol

en.explanation: DPS is authorized to suspend the license of individuals under 21 years of age for any detectable amount of alcohol.

en.question: Which of the following situations requires the cancellation of a driver license or ID card?

choices.A: Receiving a single speeding ticket
choices.B: Incomplete driver education
choices.C: Parking in a handicapped zone without a permit
choices.D: Failing to wear a seatbelt

en.explanation: Cases that require cancellation of a driver license or ID card include incomplete driver education, false statements on an application, and parental authorization withdrawn for minors.

en.question: Upon receipt of a court order, DPS will suspend, revoke, or cancel a license or driving privilege for which of the following reasons?

choices.A: Delinquent child support
choices.B: Accumulating two parking tickets
choices.C: Driving 5 mph over the speed limit
choices.D: Failing to yield right-of-way at a yield sign

en.explanation: Upon receipt of a court order, DPS will suspend, revoke, or cancel a license for delinquent child support, among other reasons like being mentally incapacitated or chemically dependent.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of driving a motor vehicle while your driver license is suspended, cancelled, denied, or revoked (DWLI) without any aggravating factors?

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor, punishable by up to a $4,000 fine
choices.B: Class B misdemeanor, punishable by up to a $2,000 fine
choices.C: Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $500
choices.D: A fine of $125 and 10 hours of community service

en.explanation: Driving while a license is suspended, cancelled, denied, or revoked is a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $500.

en.question: Driving While License Invalid (DWLI) becomes a Class A misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $4,000 and/or up to 365 days in jail if the person was operating without insurance and:

choices.A: Was caught speeding more than 20 mph over the limit
choices.B: Caused a crash which resulted in serious bodily injury or death of another
choices.C: Refused to submit to a breathalyzer test
choices.D: Had a previous conviction for the exact same offense

en.explanation: DWLI is a Class A misdemeanor if the person was operating without insurance at the time of the offense and caused a crash which resulted in serious bodily injury or death of another.

en.question: For a first offense non-driving alcohol-related violation by a minor, how long will their driver license be suspended (or privilege denied)?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For a 1st offense non-driving alcohol-related violation by a minor, the driver license will be suspended (or privilege denied if not licensed) for 30 days.

en.question: What is the penalty for a 3rd offense non-driving alcohol-related violation for a minor who is at least 17 years of age but less than 21?

choices.A: Class C misdemeanor with a 30-day suspension
choices.B: Class C misdemeanor with a 60-day suspension
choices.C: Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $250 to $2,000 and a 180-day suspension
choices.D: Class A misdemeanor punishable by up to a $4,000 fine and a 365-day suspension

en.explanation: A 3rd offense for a minor at least 17 but less than 21 is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $250 to $2,000, and the driver license will be suspended for 180 days.

en.question: What is the penalty for a person who purchases, furnishes, or sells an alcoholic beverage to a minor?

choices.A: A fine of up to $500 and 20 hours of community service
choices.B: A fine of up to $2,000 and/or confinement in jail for up to 180 days
choices.C: A fine of up to $4,000 and/or confinement in jail for up to one year
choices.D: A mandatory 180-day driver license suspension

en.explanation: A person who purchases, furnishes, or sells an alcoholic beverage to a minor is subject to a fine of up to $4,000 and/or confinement in jail for up to one year.

en.question: What is an occupational license (also called an essential need license)?

choices.A: A license issued exclusively to commercial truck drivers
choices.B: A special restricted license for individuals whose license has been suspended or revoked but who can prove an essential need to drive
choices.C: A license that allows minors to drive to and from school
choices.D: A temporary permit issued while waiting for a permanent ID card in the mail

en.explanation: An occupational license is a special type of restricted license issued to individuals whose driver license has been canceled, suspended, revoked, or denied, and who can prove to a court there is an essential need to drive.

en.question: What is the fee for an occupational license if it is authorized for one year?
en.explanation: The fee for an occupational license is $10 for one year or $20 if authorized for two years.

en.question: How long may the court order for an occupational license be used for driving purposes while the official license is being processed?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 45 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: The court order may be used for 45 days for driving purposes while the occupational license is being processed.

en.question: Which type of vehicle may NOT be driven with an occupational license?

choices.A: A passenger car
choices.B: A pickup truck
choices.C: A commercial motor vehicle
choices.D: A sports utility vehicle

en.explanation: The manual states that an occupational license may not be issued to drive a commercial motor vehicle.

en.question: DPS is authorized to deny the issuance of a driver license to an applicant for which of the following reasons?

choices.A: Acquiring motor vehicle fuel without payment
choices.B: Receiving a single parking violation
choices.C: Failing to register to vote
choices.D: Having out-of-state vehicle insurance

en.explanation: An applicant may be denied a driver license for acquiring motor vehicle fuel without payment, among other reasons like delinquent child support or certain criminal mischief.

en.question: For registration purposes, how long is a passing Vehicle Inspection Report (VIR) valid?

choices.A: 30 days from the month of inspection
choices.B: 60 days from the month of inspection
choices.C: 90 days from the month of inspection
choices.D: 1 year from the month of inspection

en.explanation: The VIR is only valid for 90 days from the month of inspection for registration purposes.

en.question: A vehicle's foot brake must be able to stop the car within a distance of 25 feet when traveling at what speed?

choices.A: 10 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 40 mph

en.explanation: The foot brake must stop the car within a distance of 25 feet at a speed of 20 mph.

en.question: A vehicle's horn must be capable of being heard for a minimum distance of:

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Horns must be heard for a minimum distance of 200 feet.

en.question: What is the minimum required tread depth for tires on a vehicle?

choices.A: 1/32 of an inch
choices.B: 2/32 of an inch
choices.C: 3/32 of an inch
choices.D: 4/32 of an inch

en.explanation: All vehicles are required to have tires in proper and safe condition with a minimum depth of 2/32 of an inch.

en.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem must be displayed on certain vehicles, such as farm tractors, that are assigned to travel at or below what speed?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 30 mph

en.explanation: Farm tractors and machinery, road construction machinery, animal-drawn vehicles and certain other motor vehicles assigned to travel at 25 mph or less must display the slow-moving vehicle emblem.

en.question: It is illegal to have anything extending more than how many inches beyond the left side of your car's body, running board, or fenders?

choices.A: 2 inches
choices.B: 3 inches
choices.C: 5 inches
choices.D: 6 inches

en.explanation: You must not have anything extending more than three inches beyond the left side or six inches beyond the right side of the body, running board, or fenders of your car.

en.question: Which of the following is considered unsafe and is NOT allowed on a standard passenger vehicle?

choices.A: A red light showing from the front
choices.B: A white license plate light
choices.C: Amber parking lights on the front
choices.D: Two backup lights

en.explanation: A red light showing from the front is considered unsafe and is not allowed except on an emergency vehicle.

en.question: What is the state requirement regarding minimum road clearance for a modified vehicle?

choices.A: The body must be at least 6 inches above the ground.
choices.B: The body must not be below the lowest part of the wheel rims.
choices.C: The vehicle must have at least 10 inches of clearance.
choices.D: The bumpers must be at least 16 inches from the road surface.

en.explanation: A vehicle must not be modified or weighted in such a manner where the body is below the lowest part of the rims of the wheels.

en.question: When is it illegal to use your vehicle's backup lights?

choices.A: When parking in a dark area
choices.B: When the vehicle is in forward motion
choices.C: When backing out of a driveway
choices.D: When warning of unusual traffic hazards

en.explanation: Two backup lights are permitted separately or in combination with other lights, but you must not use them when the vehicle is in forward motion.

en.question: How many days does an owner have to register a newly purchased vehicle?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 15 days
choices.C: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: An owner must register a newly purchased vehicle within 30 days of purchase.

en.question: How long are buyers' temporary tags recognized as valid?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: Buyers' temporary tags are recognized for 60 days.

en.question: A vehicle's rearview mirror must be able to reflect a view of the highway for a distance of at least:

choices.A: 100 feet to the rear
choices.B: 200 feet to the rear
choices.C: 300 feet to the rear
choices.D: 500 feet to the rear

en.explanation: A rearview mirror must be able to reflect a view of the highway for a distance of at least 200 feet to the rear of the vehicle.

en.question: At what height must the two red reflectors on the rear of a vehicle be placed?

choices.A: 10 to 40 inches
choices.B: 15 to 60 inches
choices.C: 20 to 70 inches
choices.D: 24 to 80 inches

en.explanation: Reflectors must be placed at a height of 15 to 60 inches and be visible up to 600 feet.

en.question: Which of the following devices is strictly prohibited on your vehicle?

choices.A: A radar interference device
choices.B: A GPS navigation system
choices.C: A dashboard camera
choices.D: A hands-free communication device

en.explanation: A radar interference device designed, manufactured, used, or intended to be used to interfere with, scramble, disrupt, or cause to malfunction a radar or laser device used to measure a vehicle's speed is not allowed.

en.question: For which of the following purposes may a farm registered vehicle NOT be used?

choices.A: Attending church or school
choices.B: Visiting doctors for medical treatment
choices.C: Gainful employment
choices.D: Transporting family members for home necessities

en.explanation: The manual states that farm registered vehicles may be used for family necessities like church, school, or medical visits, but they may not be used for gainful employment.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is NOT required to be registered or inspected when temporarily operated on highways?

choices.A: Passenger cars
choices.B: Power sweepers
choices.C: Commercial delivery trucks
choices.D: Motorcycles

en.explanation: Power sweepers are included in the list of vehicles that are not required to be registered, inspected, or display a license plate when temporarily operated on highways.

en.question: How many days does a nonresident have to register their vehicle in Texas after establishing residency or entering into gainful employment?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: When a nonresident establishes residency in Texas or enters into gainful employment, his/her vehicle may be operated for 30 days. After 30 days, the vehicle must be registered in Texas.

en.question: What must a new Texas resident do before applying for a Texas driver license?

choices.A: Register every vehicle he/she owns
choices.B: Surrender their out-of-state license plates
choices.C: Complete a defensive driving course
choices.D: Pay a $55,000 deposit to the state comptroller

en.explanation: A new Texas resident must register every vehicle he/she owns before applying for a Texas driver license.

en.question: What is the minimum amount of liability insurance required against property damage in Texas?
en.explanation: As of January 1, 2011, the minimum amount of liability insurance includes $25,000 against property damage.

en.question: Under the Texas Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act, what is the minimum liability insurance required against injury or death of two or more individuals?
en.explanation: The minimum amount of liability insurance includes $60,000 against injury or death of two or more individuals.

en.question: Which of the following is an acceptable form of evidence of financial responsibility in Texas?

choices.A: A verbal promise to pay for damages
choices.B: A certificate showing a $55,000 deposit with the state comptroller
choices.C: A valid Texas driver license
choices.D: A vehicle inspection report

en.explanation: Accepted evidence of financial responsibility includes a certificate issued by the state comptroller showing the owner has on deposit money or securities for at least $55,000.

en.question: If a driver receives a second conviction for driving without evidence of financial responsibility, how long will their vehicle be impounded?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For a 2nd and subsequent conviction, the vehicle driven or operated by the person shall be impounded for 180 days, provided the defendant was an owner at the time of the offense and conviction.

en.question: A driver's license or driving privilege will be suspended if a judgment resulting from a crash has not been satisfied within how many days?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: The vehicle registration, license or driving privilege of a driver will be suspended if a judgment resulting from a crash has not been satisfied within 60 days of the judgment.

en.question: When driving on an unpaved road that intersects with a paved road, what must you do?

choices.A: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the paved road
choices.B: Take the right-of-way if you arrive first
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles approaching from the right
choices.D: Stop and wait for a signal from other drivers

en.explanation: If you are driving on an unpaved road that intersects with a paved road, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the paved road.

en.question: If you are driving on a single or two-lane road that intersects with a divided road or a road with three or more lanes, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle on the single or two-lane road
choices.B: The vehicle that arrives at the intersection first
choices.C: Vehicles traveling on the divided or three or more lane road
choices.D: The vehicle approaching from the left

en.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the divided or three (3) or more lane road when intersecting from a single or two-lane road.

en.question: When approaching an intersection not controlled by signs, signals, multi-lanes, or pavement, to which vehicle must you yield the right-of-way?

choices.A: Any vehicle approaching on your left
choices.B: Any vehicle approaching on your right
choices.C: The largest vehicle at the intersection
choices.D: The vehicle traveling at the highest speed

en.explanation: When approaching this type of intersection, yield the right-of-way to any vehicle that has entered or is approaching the intersection on your right.

en.question: What must you do when entering a street from a private road, alley, or driveway?

choices.A: Sound your horn and proceed without stopping
choices.B: Stop prior to the sidewalk and yield to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles, as pedestrians must yield to you
choices.D: Accelerate quickly to merge into traffic

en.explanation: When entering or crossing a road, street, or highway from a private road, alley, building, or driveway, you must stop prior to the sidewalk and yield the right-of-way to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

en.question: What is the penalty if a driver fails to yield the right-of-way and causes serious bodily injury to another person?

choices.A: A fine of $175 to $350
choices.B: A fine of $500 to $2,000
choices.C: A fine of $1,000 to $4,000
choices.D: A fine of $5,000 and license revocation

en.explanation: If a driver commits a traffic offense of failing to yield the right-of-way and causes serious bodily injury to another, the penalty is a fine of $1,000 to $4,000.

en.question: When approaching a T-intersection from a street that ends at the intersection, you must:

choices.A: Maintain your speed and merge into the right lane.
choices.B: Stop and yield the right-of-way to vehicles on the through street.
choices.C: Yield only if there is a posted stop or yield sign.
choices.D: Take the right-of-way if you are turning right.

en.explanation: When approaching an intersection of a through street traveling from a street that ends at the intersection, you must stop and yield the right-of-way to vehicles on the through street.

en.question: On a road divided into three or more lanes with traffic moving in the same direction, if a vehicle entering a lane from the right meets a vehicle entering the same lane from the left, who must yield?

choices.A: The vehicle entering from the right must yield the right-of-way.
choices.B: The vehicle entering from the left must yield the right-of-way.
choices.C: Both vehicles must stop and wait for the other to proceed.
choices.D: The vehicle traveling at the faster speed has the right-of-way.

en.explanation: On a road divided into three or more lanes, a vehicle entering a lane of traffic from the right must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle entering the same lane of traffic from the left.

en.question: When approaching a railroad grade crossing where a train is approaching, at what distance must you stop your vehicle?

choices.A: Between 10 and 30 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.B: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.C: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail.
choices.D: At least 100 feet from the nearest rail.

en.explanation: When approaching a railroad grade crossing, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail if a train is approaching, a signal warns of a train, or a crossing gate is lowered.

en.question: What is the fine for failing to obey the law regarding railroad grade crossings?
en.explanation: A person who fails to obey the law regarding railroad grade crossings is subject to a fine of $50 to $200.

en.question: If your car stalls on railroad tracks and a train is approaching, what is the safest course of action?

choices.A: Stay in the vehicle, buckle your seatbelt, and call 911 immediately.
choices.B: Get out and run straight down the tracks away from the train.
choices.C: Get out quickly and run toward the approaching train to the side of the tracks.
choices.D: Try to restart the car until the train is within 500 feet, then exit.

en.explanation: If a train is approaching and your vehicle is stalled, get out quickly and move away from the tracks. Run toward the approaching train to the side of the tracks and avoid flying debris.

en.question: You are not allowed to follow within how many feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance when its flashing red lights are on?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: You are not allowed to follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance when the flashing red lights are on.

en.question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights activated on a highway with a speed limit of 45 mph, and you cannot vacate the closest lane, you must:

choices.A: Slow to a speed of 25 mph or less.
choices.B: Slow to a speed of 15 mph or less.
choices.C: Slow to a speed of 5 mph or less.
choices.D: Maintain your speed but proceed with extreme caution.

en.explanation: If you cannot vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle, you must slow to a speed not more than 20 mph less than the posted speed limit when the posted speed limit is 25 mph or more. (45 mph - 20 mph = 25 mph).

en.question: When you approach a school bus displaying alternately flashing red lights, you must stop and may NOT pass until:

choices.A: The children have safely crossed the street and reached the sidewalk.
choices.B: You have waited for at least 60 seconds.
choices.C: The bus has resumed motion, the driver signals you to proceed, or the red lights stop flashing.
choices.D: The bus driver turns on the yellow hazard lights.

en.explanation: Do not pass the school bus until: 1. The school bus has resumed motion; 2. You are signaled by the driver to proceed; or 3. The red lights are no longer flashing.

en.question: In which of the following situations are you NOT required to stop for a school bus?

choices.A: When you are traveling in the opposite direction on a two-lane road.
choices.B: When you are on a different road or a controlled-access highway where the bus is in a loading zone and pedestrians aren't permitted to cross.
choices.C: When you are driving a commercial vehicle or an emergency vehicle.
choices.D: When the bus is stopped at a railroad crossing with its hazard lights on.

en.explanation: It is not necessary to stop when passing a school bus on a different road or when on a controlled-access highway where the bus is stopped in a loading zone and pedestrians aren’t permitted to cross.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first conviction of failing to yield the right-of-way to a school bus?

choices.A: A fine of $50 to $200.
choices.B: A fine of $200 to $500.
choices.C: A fine of $500 to $1,250.
choices.D: A fine of $1,000 to $2,000.

en.explanation: According to Table 15, the penalty for a 1st conviction of failing to yield the right-of-way to a school bus is a fine of $500 - $1,250.

en.question: If a traffic light changes to green while a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk, what should you do?

choices.A: Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian to hurry.
choices.B: Proceed carefully around the pedestrian.
choices.C: Give the pedestrian the right-of-way to finish crossing.
choices.D: The pedestrian must immediately turn back to the sidewalk.

en.explanation: If the light changes after the pedestrian has entered the crosswalk, still give the pedestrian the right-of-way.

en.question: Where are 'In-Street Pedestrian Crossing' signs placed?

choices.A: On the left- or right-hand side of the road.
choices.B: Over the roadway at the crosswalk.
choices.C: In the road at the crosswalk location on the center line, on a lane line, or on a median island.
choices.D: 500 feet before the crosswalk on the right shoulder.

en.explanation: The 'In-Street Pedestrian Crossing' signs are placed in the road at the crosswalk location on the center line, on a lane line, or on a median island. They will not be posted on the left- or right-hand side of the road.

en.question: What information is provided on the blue and white Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a railroad crossing?

choices.A: The train schedule and maximum speed limit.
choices.B: The railroad's emergency contact number and the USDOT National Crossing Inventory Number.
choices.C: The distance to the nearest hospital and police station.
choices.D: The fine amount for stopping on the tracks.

en.explanation: The ENS sign includes the railroad's emergency contact number and the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) National Crossing Inventory Number, which identifies the exact location.

en.question: What is the purpose of in-roadway lights?

choices.A: To illuminate the highway during severe power outages.
choices.B: To warn roadway users they are approaching a condition on or near the road that might require them to slow down or stop.
choices.C: To indicate the speed limit in a school zone during active hours.
choices.D: To guide emergency vehicles to the scene of an accident.

en.explanation: In-roadway lights are special types of lights installed in the roadway surface to warn roadway users they are approaching a condition on or near the road they may not see, which might require them to slow down or come to a complete stop.

en.question: What must you do when approaching a steady red light at an intersection?

choices.A: Stop only if pedestrians are present.
choices.B: Stop before entering the crosswalk or intersection.
choices.C: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.D: Yield to traffic on the right and proceed.

en.explanation: The manual states for a Steady Red Light (Stop): "Stop before entering the crosswalk or intersection."

en.question: If a law enforcement officer is directing traffic and tells you to do something ordinarily considered against the law, what should you do?

choices.A: Obey the traffic signals instead of the officer.
choices.B: Ask the officer for clarification before proceeding.
choices.C: Obey the law enforcement officer at all times.
choices.D: Pull over and wait for the officer to leave.

en.explanation: The manual states: "You must obey a law enforcement officer at all times when they are directing traffic even if he/she is telling you to do something which is ordinarily considered against the law."

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left-turns indicate?

choices.A: You have the right-of-way to turn left.
choices.B: You are not allowed to turn left.
choices.C: You may turn left, but must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
choices.D: You must stop completely before turning left.

en.explanation: According to the manual, "A flashing yellow arrow allows a driver to turn left, but the driver must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic."

en.question: What does a brown traffic sign indicate?

choices.A: Motorist services guidance
choices.B: Public recreation and scenic guidance
choices.C: Construction and maintenance warning
choices.D: General warning or caution

en.explanation: The Standard Colors table describes brown signs as indicating "Public recreation and scenic guidance."

en.question: Which sign shape is used exclusively to warn of existing or possible hazards on roads or adjacent areas?

choices.A: Diamond
choices.B: Pentagon
choices.C: Pennant
choices.D: Round

en.explanation: The Signs by Shape table states that a Diamond shape is "Exclusively to warn of existing or possible hazards on roads or adjacent areas."

en.question: What type of sign is shaped like a pennant?

choices.A: School advance warning
choices.B: Yield sign
choices.C: Advance warning of no pass zones
choices.D: Railroad advance warning

en.explanation: The Signs by Shape table indicates that a Pennant shape is used for "Advance warning of no pass zones."

en.question: When you encounter a warning sign, what is one of the actions you must take?

choices.A: Stop immediately
choices.B: Reduce speed to at least the posted speed signs
choices.C: Honk your horn to alert others
choices.D: Pull over to the shoulder

en.explanation: The manual states that when you encounter a warning sign, you must: "1. Pay attention 2. Follow instructions 3. Reduce speed to at least the posted speed signs."

en.question: When driving on a wet road and approaching a sign warning you to slow down, what actions should you avoid?

choices.A: Using your windshield wipers
choices.B: Suddenly turning, speeding up, or stopping
choices.C: Checking your rearview mirror
choices.D: Driving in the right-hand lane

en.explanation: The description for the wet road warning sign advises: "Slow down on wet road. Do not suddenly turn, speed up, or stop."

en.question: How should you drive when you see a warning sign indicating the road surface is covered with loose gravel?

choices.A: Speed up to maintain traction
choices.B: Apply brakes suddenly if you start to slide
choices.C: Go slow enough to keep complete control and do not make sharp turns
choices.D: Shift into neutral gear

en.explanation: The manual states for loose gravel: "Go slow enough to keep complete control of your vehicle. Do not apply brakes suddenly or make sharp turns."

en.question: Why must you use extreme caution to avoid running off the paved portion of the highway when a soft shoulder sign is present?

choices.A: The dirt on the side of the pavement is soft and may cause you to lose control.
choices.B: There are hidden ditches that will damage your tires.
choices.C: Pedestrians frequently walk on soft shoulders.
choices.D: It is illegal to drive on the shoulder under any circumstances.

en.explanation: The manual explains that for a soft shoulder, you should "Use extreme caution to avoid running off the paved portion of the highway, because the dirt on the side of the pavement is soft and may cause you to lose control of the car."

en.question: Why is pavement sometimes grooved, and who should be especially cautious when encountering it?

choices.A: To reduce noise; large trucks should use caution.
choices.B: To lessen the possibility of slippery pavement in wet weather; motorcyclists should use caution.
choices.C: To slow down speeding vehicles; sports cars should use caution.
choices.D: To mark pedestrian crossings; bicyclists should use caution.

en.explanation: The manual states: "The pavement has been grooved to lessen the possibility of slippery pavement in wet weather. Motorcyclists should use caution."

en.question: What action may be necessary when you see a warning sign indicating you are approaching a downgrade?

choices.A: Shift into a higher gear to save fuel.
choices.B: Turn off your engine to prevent overheating.
choices.C: Use a lower gear to slow your vehicle.
choices.D: Apply the parking brake lightly.

en.explanation: The manual advises for a downgrade: "You are approaching a downgrade; all drivers approach with caution. It may be necessary to use a lower gear to slow your vehicle."

en.question: What does it mean if a green arrow is displayed at the same time as a red light?

choices.A: You must stop and wait for a solid green light before turning.
choices.B: You can proceed carefully in the direction of the arrow after yielding the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians.
choices.C: The traffic signal is malfunctioning and should be treated as a four-way stop.
choices.D: You may only proceed straight ahead, but cannot turn.

en.explanation: The manual states: "A green arrow displayed at the same time as a red light means the driver can proceed carefully in the direction of the arrow after yielding the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians."

en.question: Which shape is used exclusively for stop signs?

choices.A: Pentagon
choices.B: Octagon
choices.C: Equilateral Triangle
choices.D: Vertical Rectangle

en.explanation: The Signs by Shape table lists "Octagon" with the description "Exclusively for stop signs."

en.question: When you see a warning sign indicating that two roads come together and an additional lane begins, what are you required to do?

choices.A: You must merge immediately into the left lane.
choices.B: You must come to a complete stop before entering the new lane.
choices.C: You are not required to merge, but you should watch for traffic in the new lane.
choices.D: You must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles in the adjacent lane.

en.explanation: The manual describes the added lane sign: "You are approaching a point where two roads come together and an additional lane begins. You are not required to merge. Watch for traffic in the new lane."

en.question: On a roadway with multiple lanes traveling in the same direction, what is the farthest left lane intended for?

choices.A: Slower traffic
choices.B: Passing only
choices.C: Emergency stopping
choices.D: Carpools only

en.explanation: According to the manual, on roadways with more than one lane with vehicles traveling in the same direction, slower traffic should travel in a lane other than the farthest left lane. The farthest left lane is for passing only.

en.question: When is it permissible to use the center turn lane for passing other vehicles?

choices.A: When traffic is moving below the posted speed limit
choices.B: During daylight hours only
choices.C: When the right lane is blocked by construction
choices.D: It should never be used for passing

en.explanation: The manual states that the center lane is only used for vehicles turning left, and should never be used for passing or moving through traffic.

en.question: When required to stop at a railroad crossing, what is the correct stopping distance from the nearest rail?

choices.A: Within 5 to 10 feet
choices.B: Within 15 to 50 feet
choices.C: Within 50 to 100 feet
choices.D: At least 100 feet away

en.explanation: At railroad crossings, you must stop within 15 feet to 50 feet of the nearest rail when directed by a flag person, when there are flashing red lights, or when a warning device tells you a train is coming.

en.question: What does a steady yellow 'X' on an overhead lane-use control signal indicate?

choices.A: You are permitted to drive in the lane
choices.B: You must stop immediately in that lane
choices.C: You should prepare to safely vacate the lane
choices.D: The lane is reserved for left turns only

en.explanation: A steady yellow X means a driver should prepare to safely vacate the lane over which the signal is located because a lane control change is being made.

en.question: What restriction applies to the use of wireless communication devices in a school zone?

choices.A: They may only be used with a hands-free accessory
choices.B: Their use is completely prohibited
choices.C: They may be used if driving under 15 mph
choices.D: They are permitted for texting but not calling

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that the use of a wireless communication device is prohibited in the school zone.

en.question: If two vehicles arrive at an all-way stop intersection at the exact same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle turning left
choices.B: The vehicle on the left
choices.C: The vehicle on the right
choices.D: The larger vehicle

en.explanation: At an intersection where all approaching traffic must stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right.

en.question: For which of the following reasons is it acceptable to stop on the shoulder of the road?

choices.A: To answer a phone call
choices.B: To rest if you are tired
choices.C: To check a map for directions
choices.D: For a mechanical breakdown or tire trouble

en.explanation: The manual designates that the shoulder of the road should only be used by vehicles required to stop because of mechanical breakdown, tire trouble, lack of fuel, or other emergencies.

en.question: What does a double white line on the roadway indicate to drivers?

choices.A: Drivers should not change lanes or turn across the lines
choices.B: The lane is ending and drivers must merge left
choices.C: Passing is permitted if the way is clear
choices.D: The road is changing from one-way to two-way traffic

en.explanation: According to the manual, drivers should not change lanes or turn across double white lines.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of mileposts erected on interstate highways?

choices.A: To indicate the current speed limit
choices.B: To identify the location of crashes or emergencies
choices.C: To show the distance to the next rest area
choices.D: To mark the boundary of a different county

en.explanation: Mileposts provide a means of identifying the location of crashes, breakdowns, or other emergencies. They are erected every mile on interstate highways.

en.question: During what hours are High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) preferential lanes restricted to buses and carpools according to the provided text?

choices.A: 7 a.m. to 10 a.m., Monday through Friday
choices.B: 6 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday through Friday
choices.C: 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Friday
choices.D: 24 hours a day, seven days a week

en.explanation: The manual states that buses and vehicles used for carpools may use the HOV lane only between the hours of 6 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday through Friday.

en.question: When approaching a stop sign, which of the following actions is required?

choices.A: Slow down to 5 mph and proceed if the intersection is clear
choices.B: Come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or intersection
choices.C: Yield only to vehicles approaching from the right
choices.D: Stop only if pedestrians are actively crossing

en.explanation: The stop sign means come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians or other vehicles, and then proceed carefully. Stop before the crosswalk, intersection, or stop sign. Slowing down is not adequate.

en.question: What does an Advisory Speed Sign placed before a curve indicate?

choices.A: The minimum speed required on the highway
choices.B: The highest speed at which you can safely travel around the curve ahead
choices.C: The speed limit for commercial trucks only
choices.D: The speed at which you must enter the freeway

en.explanation: An Advisory Speed Sign gives the highest speed which you can safely travel around the curve ahead.

en.question: What is the function of a ramp meter?

choices.A: It weighs commercial vehicles entering the highway
choices.B: It directs motorists when to enter the freeway
choices.C: It measures the speed of vehicles on the exit ramp
choices.D: It counts the number of passengers in a carpool

en.explanation: The ramp meter (red or green) directs motorists when to enter the freeway.

en.question: On a multi-lane highway with four or more lanes, what does a double yellow line indicate?

choices.A: You may cross to pass if the way is clear
choices.B: You are entering a school zone
choices.C: Do not cross the double yellow line to pass
choices.D: The lane is reserved for left turns only

en.explanation: On a multi-lane highway (four or more lanes), you must not cross the double yellow line to pass. You should stay in your lane as much as possible.

en.question: What is the proper use of a center lane on a multi-lane highway?

choices.A: As a through-traffic lane for faster vehicles
choices.B: For passing slower vehicles on the left
choices.C: To slow down or stop in order to make a safe left turn
choices.D: For parking in emergency situations

en.explanation: The center lane is at a point where the vehicle will have time to slow down or stop in order to make a safe left turn maneuver. It should never be used for passing or as a through-traffic lane.

en.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road indicate?

choices.A: A no-passing zone
choices.B: Passing is permitted if safe
choices.C: You are approaching a crosswalk
choices.D: The lane is ending

en.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side of the road marks a 'no-passing zone.' Broken or dashed lines permit you to pass or change lanes, if safe.

en.question: What is the rule regarding pavement markings consisting of double solid white lines?

choices.A: Crossing is permitted with caution
choices.B: Crossing is prohibited
choices.C: They indicate a pedestrian crosswalk
choices.D: They mark a center left-turn lane

en.explanation: According to the manual, crossing is prohibited where there is a pavement marking of double solid white lines.

en.question: What happens to traffic fines for violations that occur in construction zones?

choices.A: They remain the same as normal violations
choices.B: They are reduced by half
choices.C: They double when workers are present
choices.D: They triple regardless of worker presence

en.explanation: Traffic fines double for violations that occur in construction zones where workers are present anywhere in the construction zone.

en.question: When approaching a barricade or vertical panel, what do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the right indicate?

choices.A: The road is completely closed
choices.B: The driver should bear to the left
choices.C: The driver should bear to the right
choices.D: There is a pedestrian crossing ahead

en.explanation: Stripes sloping downward to the right means the driver should bear to the right to pass.

en.question: What should you do if a flag person in a work zone instructs you to stop?

choices.A: Stop in your lane and do not veer right or left
choices.B: Pull over to the right shoulder and stop
