choices.C: Do not drive, stop, or park your vehicle on the tracks.
choices.D: You should race the train to the crossing to avoid delays.

en.explanation: The safety rules for light rail explicitly state: 'Do not drive, stop, or park your vehicle on the tracks. It’s dangerous and illegal.'

en.question: What is a common cause of car-bicycle crashes at intersections involving stop signs?

choices.A: The bicyclist rides too fast through the intersection.
choices.B: A motorist pulls away from a stop sign and fails to yield the right-of-way to bicycle cross traffic.
choices.C: The bicyclist fails to use hand signals.
choices.D: The motorist stops for too long at the stop sign.

en.explanation: One of the most common car-bicycle crashes caused by a motorist is when a motorist pulls away from a stop sign and fails to yield the right-of-way to bicycle cross traffic.

en.question: Which of the following is a recommended tip to avoid becoming distracted while driving?

choices.A: Adjust your mirrors while driving at a slow speed
choices.B: Engage in complex conversations to stay awake
choices.C: Review maps and plan your route before you begin driving
choices.D: Only text when stopped at a red light

en.explanation: To avoid becoming distracted, the manual recommends that you "Review maps and plan your route before you begin driving."

en.question: Under what circumstances may you legally use a cell phone while driving?

choices.A: To read a text message if you do not reply
choices.B: To contact law enforcement or during an emergency
choices.C: When traveling under 20 mph
choices.D: When you are using a hands-free device to text

en.explanation: The manual states: "You may use a cell phone to contact law enforcement or during an emergency."

en.question: When a person drinks alcohol or uses drugs, what is one of the first effects they experience?

choices.A: They lose their judgement and their sight is impaired
choices.B: Their reaction time to sounds becomes faster
choices.C: Their ability to judge speed improves
choices.D: They become more coordinated

en.explanation: According to the manual, "When a person drinks alcohol or uses drugs, one of the first effects is they lose their judgement and their sight is impaired..."

en.question: What effect does caffeine have on a drunk driver?

choices.A: It improves their ability to operate a vehicle
choices.B: It speeds up the time it takes to get sober
choices.C: It helps them stay alert but cannot make them sober
choices.D: It decreases their blood alcohol concentration

en.explanation: The manual notes: "While caffeine can help drowsy drivers stay alert, it can’t make a drunk driver sober. Studies show ordinary amounts of caffeine don’t improve a drunk driver’s ability to operate a vehicle."

en.question: What is a dangerous consequence of mixing alcohol with other drugs?

choices.A: Alcohol can mask the effects of other drugs
choices.B: Alcohol neutralizes the effects of tranquilizers
choices.C: It improves the driver's responsive reactions
choices.D: It decreases the overall cumulative effect of the drugs

en.explanation: The manual warns that taking more than one drug is dangerous because "Besides escalating the overall effects of the other drugs, alcohol can also mask the effects of those drugs, increasing a person’s risk of poor decision making..."

en.question: In Texas, a person age 21 and over is considered legally intoxicated if they have a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of:

choices.A: 0.04 or more
choices.B: 0.06 or more
choices.C: 0.08 or more
choices.D: 0.10 or more

en.explanation: The manual states: "In Texas, a person, age 21 and over, is considered legally intoxicated if the person has a BAC of 0.08 or more."

en.question: What is the maximum fine for a conviction of possessing an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle passenger area?
en.explanation: Conviction of possessing an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle passenger area is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

en.question: Which of the following is the only way to minimize the effects of alcohol and become sober?

choices.A: Taking a cold shower
choices.B: Drinking black coffee
choices.C: Exercising vigorously
choices.D: Time

en.explanation: The manual debunks myths about getting sober, stating: "Only time, based on body weight, number of drinks, and food intake can minimize the effects of alcohol."

en.question: Approximately how long does it take for the body to rid itself of each alcoholic drink consumed?

choices.A: 30 minutes
choices.B: One hour
choices.C: Two hours
choices.D: Four hours

en.explanation: According to the manual, "It takes about one hour for the body to rid itself of each drink consumed."

en.question: What does the Texas Zero Tolerance law mean for minors operating a motor vehicle?

choices.A: They can have a BAC up to 0.02 without penalty
choices.B: They are allowed one drink per hour of driving
choices.C: Any detectable amount of alcohol in their system is a criminal offense
choices.D: They are only penalized if their BAC is 0.08 or higher

en.explanation: Zero tolerance means that if a minor has "any detectable amount of alcohol in his/her system while operating a motor vehicle in a public place... the minor committed the criminal offense of Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol by a Minor."

en.question: What is the license suspension period for a minor's first non-driving alcohol-related offense?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 180 days

en.explanation: For a 1st offense non-driving alcohol-related violation by a minor, the penalty includes that their "license will be suspended (or privilege denied if not licensed) for 30 days."

en.question: Which of the following is a sign that another driver may be distracted?

choices.A: They are maintaining a consistent speed
choices.B: They are traveling at inconsistent speeds
choices.C: They are using their turn signals properly
choices.D: They are maintaining a safe following distance

en.explanation: To recognize distracted drivers, the manual advises to watch for "Vehicles traveling at inconsistent speeds."

en.question: According to the manual, how do typical social doses of marijuana affect a driver?

choices.A: They improve sensory and perceptual abilities
choices.B: They have no effect on concentration
choices.C: They impair sensory and perceptual abilities
choices.D: They make the driver more coordinated and alert

en.explanation: The manual states: "People who are under marijuana influence have impaired sensory and perceptual abilities."

en.question: Under the Implied Consent Law, what is the penalty for a minor's first offense of refusing to provide a breath or blood specimen?

choices.A: 60-day license suspension
choices.B: 90-day license suspension
choices.C: 180-day license suspension
choices.D: 1-year license suspension

en.explanation: A minor's first offense for refusing to provide a specimen results in a driver license suspended (or privilege denied if not licensed) for 180 days.

en.question: If a minor provides a breath or blood specimen confirming any detectable amount of alcohol below the 0.08 BAC limit, what is the license suspension for a first offense?

choices.A: 30 days
choices.B: 60 days
choices.C: 90 days
choices.D: 120 days

en.explanation: A minor who provides a specimen confirming a detectable amount of alcohol below the 0.08 BAC legal limit will have their license suspended for 60 days for a 1st offense.

en.question: What type of offense is Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) with a passenger under 15 years of age?

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor
choices.B: Class B misdemeanor
choices.C: State jail felony
choices.D: Second degree felony

en.explanation: DWI with a passenger under 15 is a state jail felony punishable by a fine not to exceed $10,000 and confinement in state jail for 180 days to 2 years.

en.question: If an adult refuses to give a blood or breath specimen for analysis, how long will their driver license be suspended for a first offense?

choices.A: 90 days
choices.B: 180 days
choices.C: 365 days
choices.D: 730 days

en.explanation: A person who refuses to give a blood or breath specimen for analysis will have their driver license suspended for 180 days for a first offense.

en.question: Which of the following contains approximately the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce can of beer?

choices.A: A 3-ounce glass of wine
choices.B: A 5-ounce glass of wine
choices.C: A 10-ounce wine cooler
choices.D: A mixed drink with 3 ounces of liquor

en.explanation: A drink may include a 12 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 1.5 ounces of liquor or a 5 ounce glass of wine. They all contain approximately the same amount of alcohol.

en.question: For a minor's first DWI offense, possession of an open container of an alcoholic beverage increases the minimum jail confinement to:

choices.A: 3 days
choices.B: 6 days
choices.C: 10 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: For a minor's first DWI offense, possession of an open container of an alcoholic beverage increases the minimum confinement to six days.

en.question: What is the maximum fine for an adult's first Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) offense?

choices.A: Up to $500
choices.B: Up to $1,000
choices.C: Up to $2,000
choices.D: Up to $4,000

en.explanation: The penalty for an adult's 1st DWI offense includes a fine of up to $2,000.

en.question: Intoxication manslaughter is classified as a:

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor
choices.B: State jail felony
choices.C: Third degree felony
choices.D: Second degree felony

en.explanation: Intoxication manslaughter is a second degree felony punishable by a fine not to exceed $10,000 and imprisonment for 2 to 20 years.

en.question: In addition to having a BAC of 0.08 or more, how else is the legal limit of intoxication defined in Texas?

choices.A: Having any detectable amount of alcohol in the system
choices.B: Any amount which results in the loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties
choices.C: Refusing to take a breathalyzer test
choices.D: Driving with an open container in the vehicle

en.explanation: The legal limit in Texas is 0.08 BAC or any amount which results in the loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties.

en.question: What is the penalty if a minor refuses to provide a breath or blood specimen for a second or subsequent time?

choices.A: Driver license suspended for 180 days
choices.B: Driver license suspended for 1 year
choices.C: Driver license suspended for 2 years
choices.D: Driver license permanently revoked

en.explanation: For a minor's 2nd and subsequent offenses of refusing to provide a specimen, their driver license will be suspended for 2 years.

en.question: How many hours of community service are required for a minor's first offense of Driving Under the Influence (DUI) of Alcohol and Drugs?

choices.A: 8 to 12 hours
choices.B: 20 to 40 hours
choices.C: 40 to 60 hours
choices.D: 80 to 100 hours

en.explanation: A minor's 1st DUI offense is a Class C misdemeanor that requires community service of 20 to 40 hours.

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following combinations represents approximately the same amount of alcohol?

choices.A: A 16 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 2 ounces of liquor, or an 8 ounce glass of wine
choices.B: A 12 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 1.5 ounces of liquor, or a 5 ounce glass of wine
choices.C: An 8 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 1 ounce of liquor, or a 4 ounce glass of wine
choices.D: A 12 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 2 ounces of liquor, or a 6 ounce glass of wine

en.explanation: The manual states that a drink may include a 12 ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 1.5 ounces of liquor, or a 5 ounce glass of wine, and they all contain approximately the same amount of alcohol.

en.question: If you are involved in a crash that is not investigated by a law enforcement officer and results in property damage of $1,000 or more, what is the deadline to file a written report with TxDOT?

choices.A: No later than the 5th day after the date of the crash
choices.B: No later than the 10th day after the date of the crash
choices.C: No later than the 15th day after the date of the crash
choices.D: No later than the 30th day after the date of the crash

en.explanation: If a crash is not investigated by law enforcement and results in damage of $1,000 or more, you must make a written report and file it with TxDOT no later than the 10th day after the date of the crash.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you always notify the appropriate law enforcement agency as soon as possible after a crash?

choices.A: When the damage to either vehicle appears to be less than $500
choices.B: When you suspect a driver involved is intoxicated
choices.C: When the crash occurs in a residential neighborhood
choices.D: When both vehicles can be safely driven away from the scene

en.explanation: The manual lists four specific situations where you should always notify law enforcement: injury or fatality, vehicles cannot be moved, a driver leaves the scene, or you suspect a driver is intoxicated.

en.question: What must you do if you are in a crash resulting ONLY in damage to a vehicle, and the vehicles can be normally and safely driven?

choices.A: Leave the vehicles exactly where they are until police arrive to take pictures
choices.B: Move the vehicles as soon as possible to a designated crash investigation site or other suitable location
choices.C: Drive home immediately and call your insurance company
choices.D: Push the vehicles into the center median and wait for a tow truck

en.explanation: If a crash results only in damage to a vehicle and each vehicle can be normally and safely driven, drivers must move their vehicle as soon as possible to a designated crash investigation site, frontage road, or nearest suitable cross street.

en.question: What is required if you collide with and damage an unattended vehicle and cannot locate the operator or owner?

choices.A: Leave the scene if the damage appears to be less than $200
choices.B: Wait by the vehicle for up to one hour before leaving
choices.C: Securely attach a written notice in a visible way providing your name, address, and a statement of the circumstances
choices.D: Call a tow truck to have the unattended vehicle removed from the roadway

en.explanation: If you damage an unattended vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must securely attach a written notice in a visible way providing your name, address, and a statement of the circumstances of the collision.

en.question: What is the penalty for a first offense of failing to stop at the scene of a crash resulting in the death of a person?

choices.A: Class A misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year in jail
choices.B: First degree felony punishable by life in prison
choices.C: Second degree felony punishable by a fine up to $10,000 and 2 to 20 years imprisonment
choices.D: Third degree felony punishable by a fine up to $10,000 and 2 to 10 years imprisonment

en.explanation: A 1st offense crash resulting in a death of a person where the driver fails to stop is a Second degree felony punishable by a fine not to exceed $10,000 and imprisonment in the TDCJ for 2 to 20 years.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to stop at a crash resulting in less than $200 in damages to a vehicle (1st offense)?

choices.A: Class C misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed $500
choices.B: Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed $2,000
choices.C: Class A misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year in jail
choices.D: State jail felony punishable by up to 2 years in jail

en.explanation: For a 1st offense failure to stop with less than $200 in damages, the penalty is a Class C misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

en.question: When aiding an injured person at the scene of a crash, what is the proper protocol regarding moving the victim?

choices.A: Move them to the side of the road immediately to prevent further injury from traffic
choices.B: Do not move or lift the victim unless it is absolutely necessary
choices.C: Have the victim stand up and walk around to check for broken bones
choices.D: Place the victim in your vehicle to keep them warm until the ambulance arrives

en.explanation: The manual advises: 'Do not move or lift the victim(s) unless it is absolutely necessary. If a victim must be moved, get help and try not to change the position in which the victim was found.'

en.question: According to pedestrian safety rules, where should you walk if there are no sidewalks available?

choices.A: On the right side of the road with the flow of traffic
choices.B: On the left side of the road facing traffic
choices.C: In the center of the road where you are most visible
choices.D: On the shoulder of the road walking in a zigzag pattern

en.explanation: Pedestrian safety rules state: 'Walk on the left side of the road if there are no sidewalks. Step off the pavement when a car approaches.'

en.question: Who has the right-of-way if a pedestrian crosses a street at any point other than within a crosswalk at an intersection?

choices.A: The pedestrian always has the right-of-way
choices.B: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles
choices.C: Vehicles must yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian
choices.D: The right-of-way goes to whoever arrived at the crossing point first

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you cross a street at any point other than within a crosswalk at an intersection, you (the pedestrian) must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles.'

en.question: According to the Texas Driver Handbook, what are the most common causes of crashes in Texas?

choices.A: Poor weather conditions, road construction, and vehicle malfunctions
choices.B: Speeding, failure to yield or stop appropriately, and driving under the influence of alcohol
choices.C: Distracted driving, inexperienced drivers, and nighttime driving
choices.D: Tailgating, improper passing, and ignoring traffic signals

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'Most crashes in Texas result from speeding, failure to yield or stop appropriately, and driving under the influence of alcohol.'

en.question: If you need the address and telephone number of the other driver's insurance company after a crash and it is not listed on their card, who should you call?

choices.A: The Texas Department of Transportation
choices.B: The Texas Department of Public Safety
choices.C: The Texas Department of Insurance
choices.D: The local police department's non-emergency line

en.explanation: The manual instructs: 'If you have the name of the driver's insurance company and the information is not listed directly on the insurance card, call the Texas Department of Insurance at (800) 252-3439 to get the company address and telephone number.'

en.question: According to the Texas Department of Insurance, what type of coverage will pay for damages in hit-and-run crashes if reported to a law enforcement agency?

choices.A: Comprehensive coverage
choices.B: Collision coverage
choices.C: Liability coverage
choices.D: Uninsured motorist coverage

en.explanation: The manual states: 'The Texas Department of Insurance advises uninsured motorist coverage will pay for damages in hit-and-run crashes reported to a law enforcement agency.'

en.question: When crossing a street at a crosswalk, what position should a pedestrian maintain?

choices.A: Keep to the left side of the crosswalk
choices.B: Keep to the right side of the crosswalk if possible
choices.C: Walk exactly in the center of the crosswalk
choices.D: Walk diagonally across the crosswalk

en.explanation: The pedestrian safety rules state: 'When crossing at a crosswalk, keep right if possible.'

en.question: Who is legally permitted to carry a white cane on a public street or highway?

choices.A: Any pedestrian walking at night.
choices.B: Pedestrians crossing outside of a crosswalk.
choices.C: Blind, partially blind, or disabled individuals.
choices.D: Traffic control officers and crossing guards.

en.explanation: The manual states that blind, partially blind, or disabled individuals may carry a white cane while walking. Others must not display a white cane on any public street or highway.

en.question: How are traffic law violations handled for a person operating a bicycle?

choices.A: They receive a warning instead of a citation.
choices.B: They are subject to the same penalties as a person operating a motor vehicle.
choices.C: They are only fined half the amount of a motor vehicle violation.
choices.D: Bicycle violations are not placed on an individual's driver record.

en.explanation: Any person who operates a bicycle is subject to the same penalties for violating a traffic law as a person operating a motor vehicle, and convictions will be placed on their driver record.

en.question: How should a bicyclist signal that they are stopping?

choices.A: By pointing their left arm horizontally.
choices.B: By pointing their right arm horizontally.
choices.C: By pointing their left arm upward.
choices.D: By pointing their left arm downward.

en.explanation: Bicyclists must signal a stop by using their left arm pointed downward.

en.question: Where should a bicyclist ride when operating on a one-way road with two or more marked traffic lanes?

choices.A: In the center of the rightmost lane.
choices.B: As near as possible to the left curb or edge of the road.
choices.C: As near as possible to the right curb or edge of the road.
choices.D: In any lane that is moving faster than traffic.

en.explanation: When operating a bicycle on a one-way road with two or more marked traffic lanes, the rider must ride as near as possible to the left curb or edge of the road.

en.question: What type of front light is required on a bicycle used at nighttime?

choices.A: A yellow light visible from 300 feet.
choices.B: A white light visible from at least 500 feet.
choices.C: A flashing red light visible from 200 feet.
choices.D: A white light visible from at least 1000 feet.

en.explanation: Every bicycle used at nighttime must be equipped with a lamp on the front that emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet.

en.question: What is the rule regarding bicyclists carrying packages or bundles?

choices.A: They must not carry any packages weighing more than 10 pounds.
choices.B: They must use a front basket for all packages.
choices.C: They must not carry anything that prevents keeping at least one hand on the handlebars.
choices.D: They are prohibited from carrying any packages while riding on a public road.

en.explanation: A bicyclist must never carry any package, bundle, or article which prevents the rider from keeping at least one hand on the handlebars.

en.question: According to defensive driving principles, what does the law require drivers to do regarding other drivers' mistakes?

choices.A: Report them immediately to law enforcement.
choices.B: Honk their horn to alert the other driver.
choices.C: Protect each other from their own mistakes.
choices.D: Maintain their right-of-way regardless of the mistake.

en.explanation: To avoid crashes, the defensive driver should know that the law requires drivers to protect each other from their own mistakes.

en.question: Under what conditions is a child under 8 years old exempt from being secured in a child car seat?

choices.A: If they are riding in the back seat of a pickup truck.
choices.B: If they are more than 4'9" tall.
choices.C: If they are wearing a standard adult safety belt.
choices.D: If they are accompanied by a parent or guardian.

en.explanation: Any child under 8 years old must be secured in a federally approved child car seat if occupying a seat in a vehicle equipped with a safety belt, unless the child is more than 4’9” tall.

en.question: How much greater are your chances of being killed in a crash if you are thrown from your car?

choices.A: Two times greater.
choices.B: Three times greater.
choices.C: Four times greater.
choices.D: Five times greater.

en.explanation: Safety belts help keep you from being thrown from your car. Your chances of being killed are five times greater if you are thrown from your car.

en.question: What is the penalty assessed to a driver if a passenger under 17 years old is riding without a safety belt?

choices.A: A fine of $25 to $50.
choices.B: A fine of $50 to $100.
choices.C: A fine of $100 to $200.
choices.D: A fine of $200 to $500.

en.explanation: According to the penalties table, passengers under 17 years old riding without a safety belt result in a fine assessed to the driver of $100 to $200.

en.question: It is generally an offense to allow a child to occupy the bed of an open bed truck or trailer if they are younger than what age?

choices.A: 15 years of age.
choices.B: 16 years of age.
choices.C: 17 years of age.
choices.D: 18 years of age.

en.explanation: It is an offense to drive an open bed truck, an open flatbed truck, or to draw an open flatbed trailer when a child who is younger than 18 years of age is occupying the bed of the truck or trailer.

en.question: Which of the following is a valid defense to prosecution for driving with a child younger than 18 in the open bed of a pickup truck?

choices.A: The vehicle is traveling under 25 mph.
choices.B: The vehicle is being operated on a beach.
choices.C: The child is accompanied by an adult in the truck bed.
choices.D: The vehicle is traveling a distance of less than 5 miles.

en.explanation: It is a defense to prosecution that the driver was operating or towing the vehicle on a beach, in a parade/emergency, transporting farm-workers, in the only vehicle owned by the household, or in a permitted hayride.

en.question: What is one purpose of a shared lane marking on a roadway?

choices.A: To designate a lane exclusively for bicycle use.
choices.B: To reduce the chance of a bicyclist impacting the open door of a parked vehicle.
choices.C: To indicate where bicyclists must dismount and walk.
choices.D: To warn motorists of an upcoming pedestrian crosswalk.

en.explanation: The shared lane marking may be used to assist bicyclists with lateral positioning in a shared lane with on-street parallel parking in order to reduce the chance of a bicyclist impacting the open door of a parked vehicle.

en.question: What does the manual state regarding pedestrians and alcohol?

choices.A: Pedestrians under the influence must walk on the left side of the road.
choices.B: Pedestrians may consume alcohol on the road if they wear reflective clothing.
choices.C: Pedestrians should not walk on a road when under the influence of alcohol.
choices.D: Pedestrians under the influence have the right-of-way over vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual states: "Do not walk on a road when you are under the influence or consuming an alcoholic beverage. Alcohol is a contributing factor to pedestrian traffic crashes."

en.question: Under Texas law, it is an offense to operate a motor vehicle towing a boat or personal watercraft if a person riding in or on the boat is younger than what age?

choices.A: 15 years of age
choices.B: 16 years of age
choices.C: 18 years of age
choices.D: 21 years of age

en.explanation: It is an offense for a person to operate a motor vehicle that is towing a boat or personal watercraft in or on which a person who is younger than 18 years of age is riding.

en.question: Which of the following is a valid defense to prosecution for operating a truck while another person occupies a trailer being drawn by the truck?

choices.A: The person in the trailer is over 21 years old.
choices.B: The vehicle is traveling on an interstate highway.
choices.C: The trailer is designed for human habitation.
choices.D: The driver is traveling under 30 mph.

en.explanation: It is a defense to prosecution that the person occupying the trailer or semi-trailer was in a part of the vehicle designed for human habitation.

en.question: What should you do with your vehicle's lights if you are stopped by law enforcement at night?

choices.A: Turn off all lights to avoid blinding the officer.
choices.B: Turn on your high beams.
choices.C: Turn on the interior dome light.
choices.D: Flash your headlights repeatedly.

en.explanation: If stopped by law enforcement at night, you should turn on the interior dome light.

en.question: When stopped by a law enforcement officer, where should you keep your hands while waiting for instructions?

choices.A: In your lap or pockets.
choices.B: Clearly in sight on top of the steering wheel.
choices.C: Outside the driver's side window.
choices.D: Reaching into the glove box for your license.

en.explanation: You should keep both hands clearly in sight on top of the steering wheel and wait for the law enforcement officer to give you instructions.

en.question: If an authorized emergency vehicle approaches to stop you, but you feel the area is unsafe to stop immediately, what is one step you should take?

choices.A: Speed up to find a safe location faster.
choices.B: Turn on your hazard lights and drive slowly below the posted speed limit.
choices.C: Turn off all your lights so the officer knows you are looking for a spot.
choices.D: Stop abruptly in the middle of the lane.

en.explanation: If you feel the area is unsafe to stop immediately, you can turn on your hazard lights and drive slowly and carefully below the posted speed limit.

en.question: Why should drivers and passengers remain in the vehicle during a traffic stop unless asked to exit?

choices.A: Exiting the vehicle is a traffic violation that carries a fine.
choices.B: Exiting the vehicle may be perceived as aggressive behavior and a threat to the officer's safety.
choices.C: It is illegal to stand on the side of a highway.
choices.D: The officer needs to inspect the exterior of the vehicle first.

en.explanation: Drivers and passengers should not exit the vehicle unless asked to do so. Exiting your vehicle may be perceived as aggressive behavior and a threat to the officer’s safety.

en.question: When is the best time to retrieve your driver license and insurance documents during a traffic stop?

choices.A: As soon as you see the police lights behind you.
choices.B: While the officer is walking up to your vehicle.
choices.C: After informing the officer where they are located and following their directions.
choices.D: Only after the officer threatens to arrest you.

en.explanation: Before reaching into your glove box or under the seat to retrieve your proof of insurance or driver’s license, inform the officer of where the items are located and follow the officer’s directions.

en.question: If you are lawfully arrested during a traffic stop, what information are you required by law to provide to the officer?

choices.A: Your name, residence address, and date of birth.
choices.B: Your social security number and employer.
choices.C: Only your name and phone number.
choices.D: You are not required to provide any information.

en.explanation: If you are lawfully arrested, you are also required to give your name, residence address, and date of birth.

en.question: Under what circumstance can a law enforcement officer search your vehicle without your consent?

choices.A: If you are driving a red sports car.
choices.B: If you refuse to answer their questions.
choices.C: If the officer has probable cause to believe your vehicle contains evidence of a crime.
choices.D: An officer can never search your vehicle without your consent.

en.explanation: If an officer has probable cause to believe that your vehicle contains evidence of a crime, it can be searched without your consent.

en.question: What offense is committed if a person gives a fictitious name to a law enforcement officer who has lawfully detained them?

choices.A: Evading arrest
choices.B: False Identification Offense
choices.C: Aggressive driving
choices.D: Class C Misdemeanor

en.explanation: A person commits a False Identification Offense if he/she gives a false or fictitious name to a law enforcement officer who has lawfully arrested or detained the person.

en.question: Which of the following actions will subject you to higher penalties if you are evading arrest or detention?

choices.A: Fleeing on foot through a residential neighborhood.
choices.B: Using a vehicle or watercraft while evading arrest.
choices.C: Refusing to answer the officer's questions.
choices.D: Denying consent to search your vehicle.

en.explanation: You will be subject to higher penalties if you use a vehicle or watercraft while evading arrest or cause injury to another person.

en.question: To help avoid road rage, how should you use your vehicle's horn if necessary?

choices.A: Hold the horn down for at least five seconds.
choices.B: Tap the horn.
choices.C: Sound the horn repeatedly while making eye contact.
choices.D: Never use the horn under any circumstances.

en.explanation: Should you need to use the horn, tap the horn; do not hold down the horn.

en.question: Which of the following is an example of aggressive driving behavior that should be avoided?

choices.A: Using your turn signal before changing lanes.
choices.B: Intentionally speeding up to keep someone from passing or entering your lane.
choices.C: Allowing extra time for your trip in case of traffic.
choices.D: Following other vehicles at a safe distance.

en.explanation: Tips to Avoid Road Rage include: Do not intentionally slow down, slam on your brakes, or speed up to keep someone from passing or entering your lane of travel.

en.question: If you are transporting a handgun in your vehicle, what are you encouraged to do regarding your license and insurance documentation?

choices.A: Keep the handgun in the exact same compartment as your documents.
choices.B: Hand the weapon to the officer along with your documents.
choices.C: Keep the handgun in a separate location from your license and insurance documentation.
choices.D: Place the handgun on the passenger seat before the officer approaches.

en.explanation: Drivers who transport handguns in their vehicles are encouraged to keep them in a separate location from license and insurance documentation.

en.question: A neighborhood electronic vehicle may only be operated on a street or highway if the posted speed limit is:

choices.A: 30 mph or less
choices.B: 35 mph or less
choices.C: 45 mph or less
choices.D: 55 mph or less

en.explanation: Neighborhood electronic vehicles may only be operated on a street or highway when the posted speed limit is 45 mph or less.

en.question: What is the maximum posted speed limit for a street or highway where a motor assisted scooter may be operated?

choices.A: 25 mph
choices.B: 30 mph
choices.C: 35 mph
choices.D: 45 mph

en.explanation: A motor assisted scooter may only be operated on a street or highway when the posted speed limit is 35 mph or less.

en.question: How does the Texas Driver Handbook define an Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Device (EPAMD)?

choices.A: A four-wheeled off-road vehicle with a gas motor
choices.B: A two, non-tandem wheeled device designed for transporting one person that is self-balancing
choices.C: A gas-powered scooter with a motor not exceeding 40 cc
choices.D: A bicycle with wheels larger than 14 inches in diameter

en.explanation: An EPAMD, such as a Segway, is defined as a two, non-tandem wheeled device designed for transporting one person that is self-balancing and propelled by an electric propulsion system.

en.question: When operating an Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Device (EPAMD) on a public roadway, where should it be ridden?

choices.A: In the center of the lane
choices.B: As close as practicable to the left-hand edge
choices.C: As close as practicable to the right-hand edge
choices.D: On the shoulder facing oncoming traffic

en.explanation: When operated on a public roadway, an EPAMD shall be ridden as close as practicable to the right-hand edge.

en.question: According to the 'Keys to Safe Driving', which of the following is true regarding courtesy and right-of-way?

choices.A: Right-of-way comes before safety
choices.B: Safety comes before the right-of-way
choices.C: You should always insist on taking the right-of-way
choices.D: Courtesy is only required in residential areas

en.explanation: Under 'Your Keys to Safe Driving', the manual states for Courtesy: 'Safety comes before the right-of-way'.

en.question: When transporting loose materials on public highways, the load must be completely enclosed and covered. Which of the following materials is exempt from this requirement?

choices.A: Dirt and sand
choices.B: Gravel
choices.C: Wood chips
choices.D: Agricultural products in their natural state

en.explanation: The manual states that no person shall transport loose material capable of blowing or spilling (such as dirt, sand, gravel, wood chips) unless enclosed and covered, except for agricultural products in their natural state.

en.question: When one vehicle is towing another, the drawbar, chain, rope, cable, or other connection must not be longer than:

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 25 feet

en.explanation: When one vehicle is towing another, the connection must not be longer than 15 feet from one vehicle to another.

en.question: What type of flag must be attached to the connection when one vehicle is towing another?

choices.A: A red flag not less than 10 inches square
choices.B: A white flag not less than 12 inches square
choices.C: A yellow flag not less than 15 inches square
choices.D: An orange flag not less than 18 inches square

en.explanation: When towing, you must attach a white flag not less than 12 inches square to the connection.

en.question: To prevent carbon monoxide poisoning, which of the following should you NOT do?

choices.A: Make sure you are getting plenty of fresh air
choices.B: Leave vents open when following closely behind another car
choices.C: Move a poisoning victim to fresh air
choices.D: Call 911 if you encounter a poisoning victim

en.explanation: The manual explicitly lists 'Leave vents open when following closely behind another car' under the 'Don't' section for preventing carbon monoxide poisoning.

en.question: If you apply for the 'Communication Impediment with a Peace Officer' restriction code on your Texas driver license, where will the code be placed?

choices.A: On the front of the license in red text
choices.B: On the back of your license
choices.C: On your vehicle's license plate
choices.D: On your vehicle's registration sticker

en.explanation: The code for 'Communication Impediment with a Peace Officer' will go on the back of your license, similar to other codes like organ donor or corrective lenses.

en.question: According to the glossary, an autocycle can be operated under which type of driver license?

choices.A: Class A driver license
choices.B: Class B driver license
choices.C: Class C driver license
choices.D: Class M (Motorcycle) driver license

en.explanation: The glossary states that an autocycle can be operated under a Class C driver license.

en.question: What is the definition of the 'basic speed law'?

choices.A: You must always drive exactly at the posted speed limit
choices.B: You may not drive faster than is safe and prudent for existing conditions, regardless of posted speed limits
choices.C: You can exceed the speed limit by 5 mph to pass another vehicle
choices.D: You must drive at least 10 mph below the speed limit in bad weather

en.explanation: The basic speed law means you may not drive faster than is safe and prudent for existing conditions, regardless of posted speed limits.

en.question: According to the glossary, a bicycle is propelled by human power and has two tandem wheels. To be classified as a bicycle, at least one of these wheels must be more than what size in diameter?

choices.A: 10 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 14 inches
choices.D: 16 inches

en.explanation: A bicycle is defined as having two tandem wheels either of which is more than 14 inches in diameter.

en.question: Safety chains are generally required when towing a trailer. Which of the following is an exception to this rule?

choices.A: Towing a house trailer for recreational use
choices.B: Towing a boat trailer to a lake
choices.C: Towing a trailer or semi-trailer used for agricultural purposes
choices.D: Towing a broken-down vehicle to a mechanic

en.explanation: The requirements for safety chains do not apply to a passenger car or light truck towing a trailer or semi-trailer used for agricultural purposes.

en.question: When changing lanes, what should you do with your turn signal after the lane change is complete?

choices.A: Leave your turn signal on for at least one mile
choices.B: Turn your turn signal off after you complete your lane change
choices.C: Only use your turn signal if there is a vehicle directly behind you
choices.D: Honk your horn before changing lanes instead of using a signal

en.explanation: The manual states: 'Properly signal your intentions to change lanes and change lanes when it is safe to do so. Turn your turn signal off after you complete your lane change.'

en.question: What is a blind spot?

choices.A: An area where the driver's vision is blocked by the sun
choices.B: An area rearview mirrors cannot show
choices.C: A zone in front of the vehicle where small objects are hidden
choices.D: A section of the road without streetlights

en.explanation: According to the manual, a blind spot is an area rearview mirrors cannot show.

en.question: What does blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) measure?

choices.A: The amount of alcohol in the blood expressed as a percentage of ethyl alcohol related to the volume of fluids in the bloodstream
choices.B: The number of alcoholic drinks consumed in one hour
choices.C: The legal limit of alcohol allowed for commercial drivers
choices.D: The rate at which the liver processes alcohol

en.explanation: Blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) is defined as the amount of alcohol in the blood expressed as a percentage of ethyl alcohol related to the volume of fluids in the bloodstream.

en.question: A vehicle is considered a commercial motor vehicle if it is designed to transport how many passengers (including the driver)?

choices.A: 8 or more
choices.B: 10 or more
choices.C: 12 or more
choices.D: 16 or more

en.explanation: A commercial motor vehicle includes a vehicle that is designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.

en.question: What is a crossbuck?

choices.A: A pedestrian crossing zone in a school area
choices.B: A large white X-shaped sign located prior to a railroad crossing
choices.C: An intersection where four roads meet at equal angles
choices.D: A warning sign for deer crossings

en.explanation: A crossbuck is a large white X-shaped sign located prior to a railroad crossing.

en.question: What is the definition of defensive driving?

choices.A: Driving below the speed limit at all times to avoid collisions
choices.B: Protecting yourself and others from dangerous and unexpected driving situations by using a space management system
choices.C: Yielding the right-of-way to all other vehicles at intersections
choices.D: Swerving to avoid obstacles in the roadway

en.explanation: Defensive driving is protecting yourself and others from dangerous and unexpected driving situations by using a space management system.

en.question: In Texas, a minor can be charged with Driving Under the Influence (DUI) if they are driving with:

choices.A: A blood-alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher
choices.B: Any detectable amount of alcohol in their system
choices.C: A blood-alcohol concentration above 0.05%
choices.D: Open containers of alcohol in the vehicle

en.explanation: Driving under the influence (DUI) is a Class C misdemeanor for which a minor can be charged in Texas if driving with any detectable amount of alcohol in the minor’s system.

en.question: What causes highway hypnosis?

choices.A: Driving under the influence of hallucinogens
choices.B: Staring at the headlights of oncoming traffic at night
choices.C: Concentration on the road ahead and the monotony of driving
choices.D: Lack of sleep before a long road trip

en.explanation: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy or trance-like condition caused by concentration on the road ahead and monotony of driving.

en.question: Hydroplaning occurs when:

choices.A: A vehicle's brakes fail due to excessive moisture
choices.B: A tire patch loses contact with the road by rising up on top of water
choices.C: A driver loses visibility during a heavy rainstorm
choices.D: A vehicle is driven into a flooded intersection

en.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when a tire patch loses contact with the road by rising up on top of water.

en.question: What does the implied-consent law mean for drivers?

choices.A: Drivers automatically consent to vehicle searches at border checkpoints
choices.B: Drivers automatically consent to be tested for blood-alcohol content and other drugs if stopped for suspicion of usage
choices.C: Drivers agree to pay all fines for traffic violations within 30 days
choices.D: Drivers consent to organ donation upon receiving their license

en.explanation: The implied-consent law means anyone who receives a driver license automatically consents to be tested for blood-alcohol content and other drugs if stopped for suspicion of alcohol or drug usage while driving.

en.question: What type of insurance provides compensation for damages which the insured is legally obligated to pay and covers others when you are at fault?

choices.A: Collision insurance
choices.B: Comprehensive insurance
choices.C: Liability insurance
choices.D: No-fault insurance

en.explanation: Liability insurance provides compensation for damages which the insured is legally obligated to pay; covers others when you are at fault.

en.question: A moped is a motor-driven cycle that cannot attain a speed in one mile of more than:

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: A moped is a motor-driven cycle that cannot attain a speed in one mile of more than 30 mph.

en.question: What is the difference between the cancellation and denial of a driver license?

choices.A: Cancellation is temporary, while denial is permanent
choices.B: Cancellation is the withdrawal of a license until the driver is qualified, while denial is withholding a license because the person is ineligible
choices.C: Cancellation applies to commercial drivers, while denial applies to regular drivers
choices.D: Cancellation is issued by a court, while denial is issued by a police officer

en.explanation: Cancellation is the withdrawal of a driver license or privilege until the driver is qualified or eligible. Denial is the withholding of a driver license or privilege because the person is ineligible for a license.

en.question: What is an ignition interlock device?

choices.A: A device that prevents a vehicle from being stolen by locking the steering wheel
choices.B: A mechanical control device where a driver must exhale into it to start the vehicle
choices.C: A system that automatically turns off the engine if the vehicle idles for too long
choices.D: A tool used by mechanics to test the emissions of a vehicle

en.explanation: An ignition interlock device is a special mechanical control device installed on a motor vehicle’s dashboard. A driver must exhale into the device to start the vehicle.

en.question: Which of the following describes a drag race?

choices.A: Driving a vehicle off-road in a reckless manner
choices.B: Two or more vehicles accelerating side by side in a competitive attempt to outdistance each other
choices.C: Weaving in and out of traffic on a controlled-access highway
choices.D: Fleeing from a law enforcement vehicle at high speeds

en.explanation: A drag race is the operation of two or more vehicles from a point side by side at accelerating speeds in a competitive attempt to outdistance each other, or comparing speeds over a selected course.

en.question: What does it mean to 'over drive' your headlights?

choices.A: Driving with high beams on in foggy conditions
choices.B: Driving at a speed making your stopping distance longer than the distance lighted by your headlights
choices.C: Using headlights during daylight hours to increase visibility
choices.D: Driving with headlights aimed too high, blinding oncoming traffic

en.explanation: Over driving headlights means driving at a speed making your stopping distance longer than the distance lighted by your headlights.

en.question: When parallel parking, how far must your vehicle be from the curb?

choices.A: 6 to 18 inches
choices.B: 12 to 24 inches
choices.C: 2 to 10 inches
choices.D: 18 to 24 inches

en.explanation: When parallel parking, the vehicle lines up parallel or going the same direction as the curb and must be 6 to 18 inches from the curb.

en.question: Which of the following is an example of a passive restraint device?

choices.A: A manual lap belt
choices.B: A child safety seat
choices.C: An airbag
choices.D: A headrest

en.explanation: A passive restraint device, such as an airbag or an automatic safety belt, works without the passenger or driver initiating the device.

en.question: What defines a protected left turn?

choices.A: A left turn made at a stop sign
choices.B: A left turn made from a shared center lane
choices.C: A left turn made without a special left turn light
choices.D: A left turn made on a left-turn green arrow while oncoming traffic is stopped

en.explanation: A protected left turn is a left turn made on a left-turn, green arrow, or delayed green light while oncoming traffic is stopped.

en.question: What is the definition of a driver license revocation?

choices.A: The temporary withdrawal of a driver license for a definite period of time
choices.B: The termination of a driver license or privilege for an indefinite period of time
choices.C: A restriction placed on a license requiring an ignition interlock device
choices.D: A warning issued before a license is suspended

en.explanation: Revocation is the termination of a driver license or privilege for an indefinite period of time. It may be restored when all requirements have been satisfied.

en.question: When making a right turn on red, what must you do before turning?

choices.A: Slow down to 5 mph and proceed if clear
choices.B: Stop behind the intersection guides
choices.C: Honk your horn to warn pedestrians
choices.D: Wait for the pedestrian signal to flash

en.explanation: A right turn on red involves turning right when the red signal is on, after stopping behind the intersection guides, unless specifically prohibited to turn.

en.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the pavement?

choices.A: To provide better traction in rain or snow
choices.B: To alert drivers of approaching roadway construction, tollbooth plazas, or other traffic conditions
choices.C: To mark the boundary of a school zone
choices.D: To indicate a shared left-turn lane

en.explanation: Rumble strips are sections of rough pavement intended to alert drivers of approaching roadway construction, tollbooth plaza, or other traffic conditions.

en.question: What is a staggered stop?

choices.A: Stopping when the white line visually disappears under the hood line to allow extra space for left-turning vehicles
choices.B: Stopping at a stop sign, moving forward, and stopping again
choices.C: Pumping the brakes repeatedly to come to a gradual stop
choices.D: Stopping behind a vehicle with enough space to steer around it

en.explanation: A staggered stop is stopping when the white line visually disappears under the hood line. This allows extra space for left-turning vehicles.

en.question: How does a license suspension differ from a revocation?

choices.A: A suspension is for an indefinite period, while a revocation is permanent
choices.B: A suspension is the temporary withdrawal of a license for a definite period of time
choices.C: A suspension only applies to commercial drivers
choices.D: A suspension requires the installation of an interlock device

en.explanation: Suspension is the temporary withdrawal of a driver license or privilege for a definite period of time, whereas revocation is for an indefinite period.

en.question: What is tunnel vision?

choices.A: The inability to see clearly at night
choices.B: When objects in your peripheral vision become blurred as speed increases
choices.C: The ability to see in a narrow field of vision of 140 degrees or less with little effective peripheral vision
choices.D: The area a person can see around the central field of vision

en.explanation: Tunnel vision is the ability to see in a narrow field of vision of 140 degrees or less with little effective peripheral vision.

en.question: What defines an uncontrolled intersection?

choices.A: An intersection where the traffic lights are flashing yellow
choices.B: An intersection that has no signs or signals to regulate traffic
choices.C: An intersection with a traffic circle
choices.D: An intersection where multiple lanes merge into one

en.explanation: An uncontrolled intersection is an intersection that has no signs or signals to regulate traffic, including railroad crossings that do not have flashing red lights or crossing gates.

en.question: What does the zero tolerance law state?

choices.A: It is illegal for anyone to drive with a blood alcohol concentration over 0.08%
choices.B: It is illegal for individuals under 21 years of age to drive with any measurable amount of alcohol in their blood
choices.C: Drivers will lose their license immediately if caught speeding in a school zone
choices.D: No driver may refuse a breathalyzer test

en.explanation: The zero tolerance law states it is illegal for individuals who are under 21 years of age to drive with any measurable amount of alcohol in their blood.

en.question: What visual effect occurs when objects in your peripheral vision become blurred and distorted as your speed increases?

choices.A: Tunnel vision
choices.B: Night blindness
choices.C: Speed smear
choices.D: Reduced visibility

en.explanation: Speed smear occurs when objects in your peripheral vision become blurred and distorted as your speed increases.

en.question: What is the technique of 'rocking a vehicle' used for?

choices.A: Testing the suspension system of the vehicle
choices.B: Moving a vehicle out of deep snow, mud, or sand
choices.C: Warning other drivers of a vehicle malfunction
choices.D: Executing a turnabout in a narrow driveway

en.explanation: Rocking a vehicle is repeating the sequence of driving forward a little then back a little to move your vehicle out of deep snow, mud, or sand.

en.question: Which type of insurance covers costs up to a certain amount if you are struck by another vehicle whose driver has no insurance?

choices.A: No-fault insurance
choices.B: Property-damage insurance
choices.C: Under-insured motorist insurance
choices.D: Uninsured motorist insurance

en.explanation: Uninsured motorist insurance covers costs up to a certain amount if you are struck by another vehicle whose driver has no insurance.

en.question: How does the Texas Driver Handbook define 'visibility'?

choices.A: The distance a vehicle takes to stop
choices.B: The ability to see
choices.C: The brightness of a vehicle's headlights
choices.D: The clarity of the windshield

en.explanation: The manual defines visibility simply as 'the ability to see'.

en.question: What is the purpose of a warning sign?

choices.A: To indicate the maximum speed limit
choices.B: To alert you to possible hazards and road conditions
choices.C: To provide directions to a destination
choices.D: To show where parking is prohibited

en.explanation: A warning sign is defined as 'a sign alerting you to possible hazards and road conditions'.

en.question: What does it mean if a warning light on your instrument panel stays on?

choices.A: The system is functioning optimally
choices.B: It is a reminder to turn on your headlights
choices.C: There is a system malfunction
choices.D: The vehicle is due for an oil change

en.explanation: A warning light is an instrument panel light warning of a system malfunction and usually stays on while the system is malfunctioning.

en.question: What does it mean to 'yield' on the roadway?

choices.A: To come to a complete stop and wait for a green light
choices.B: To allow another vehicle or roadway user to proceed first
choices.C: To merge into traffic without slowing down
choices.D: To honk your horn to warn other drivers

en.explanation: To yield means 'to allow another vehicle or roadway user to proceed first'.

en.question: The 'zero tolerance law' applies to individuals under what age?
en.explanation: The zero tolerance law makes it illegal for individuals who are under 21 years of age to drive with any measurable amount of alcohol in their blood.

en.question: Under the zero tolerance law, how much alcohol is an individual under 21 allowed to have in their blood while driving?

choices.A: Less than 0.08%
choices.B: Less than 0.04%
choices.C: Any measurable amount is illegal
choices.D: Up to one standard drink

en.explanation: The zero tolerance law states it is illegal for individuals under 21 to drive with 'any measurable amount of alcohol in their blood'.

en.question: Approximately how many driver license offices (DLO) does the DPS offer statewide for in-person services?

choices.A: More than 50
choices.B: More than 100
choices.C: More than 220
choices.D: More than 500

en.explanation: DPS offers appointments for in-person DL/ID services at more than 220 driver license offices (DLO) statewide.

en.question: How many service counters can be found at DPS 'mega centers'?

choices.A: Up to 10
choices.B: Up to 15
choices.C: Up to 20
choices.D: Up to 25

en.explanation: Mega centers offer up to 25 service counters to serve customers.

en.question: Which of the following is an alternative service option encouraged by the DPS for eligible driver license renewals?

choices.A: Online renewals
choices.B: Drive-thru renewals
choices.C: Kiosk renewals at grocery stores
choices.D: Home visit renewals

en.explanation: The DPS encourages customers to utilize alternative service options such as online, telephone, or mail-in renewals when eligible.

en.question: What is required to receive in-person Driver License or ID services at a DPS office?

choices.A: A scheduled appointment
choices.B: A walk-in ticket
choices.C: A written request by mail
choices.D: A referral from a driving school

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'All in person DL/ID services are provided by scheduled appointment.'

en.question: How far in advance can you book an appointment for in-person driver license services?

choices.A: Up to one month
choices.B: Up to three months
choices.C: Up to six months
choices.D: Up to one year

en.explanation: Appointments for in-person DL/ID services may be booked up to six months in advance.

en.question: What should you do if you are unable to keep your scheduled driver license appointment?

choices.A: Transfer it to a friend
choices.B: Cancel it so other customers may be served
choices.C: Show up the next day instead
choices.D: Nothing, it will automatically expire

en.explanation: The manual states: 'If you are unable to keep your appointment, please cancel it so other customers may be served promptly.'

en.question: Why is the DPS expanding third-party education and testing options?

choices.A: To replace all state-run driver license offices
choices.B: To provide more flexibility to customers getting a license for the first time
choices.C: To increase the cost of getting a driver license
choices.D: To make the driving test more difficult

en.explanation: The department is expanding third-party education and testing options 'to provide more flexibility to customers who are getting a license for the first time.'

en.question: Why is the DPS working to make more service options available online?

choices.A: To reduce the number of required driver license office visits
choices.B: To eliminate the need for driving tests
choices.C: To phase out physical driver licenses
choices.D: To increase state revenue

en.explanation: The department is working to make more service options available online 'to reduce the number of required DLO visits.'

en.question: Appendix C of the Texas Driver Handbook provides study and review questions for which type of operators?

choices.A: Class A Operators
choices.B: Class B Operators
choices.C: Class C Operators
choices.D: Commercial Drivers

en.explanation: The title of Appendix C is 'Study and Review Questions for Class C Operators.'

en.question: When is the $1 administrative fee NOT charged for a driver's license transaction?

choices.A: When the transaction is completed online
choices.B: When the transaction is completed in person
choices.C: When the transaction is conducted through the mail
choices.D: When completing more than one transaction at the same time

en.explanation: According to Appendix D: Fees, the $1 administrative fee is not charged for transactions conducted through the mail.

en.question: How long is a new Class C driver's license valid for a person between the ages of 18 and 84?

choices.A: 2 years
choices.B: 4 years
choices.C: 6 years
choices.D: 8 years

en.explanation: The manual states that a new driver license (Class A, B or C) for ages 18 to 84 expires after eight years on the driver's birthday.

en.question: What is the renewal fee and expiration period for a driver's license for an individual age 85 and older?

choices.A: $33, expires in 8 years
choices.B: $16, expires in 6 years
choices.C: $9, expires in 2 years
choices.D: Free, expires in 4 years

en.explanation: For individuals age 85 and older, a driver license renewal costs $9 and expires two years after the previous expiration date.

en.question: What is the fee for a new or renewed driver's license for a 60% disabled veteran who meets the fee exemption requirements?

choices.D: Free

en.explanation: Appendix D indicates that a new or renewed driver license for a 60% disabled veteran is free, provided they meet the requirements for fee exemption.

en.question: How much does it cost to replace a lost, stolen, or damaged driver's license?
en.explanation: The fee to replace a lost, stolen, or damaged driver license is $11, and the current expiration date does not change.

en.question: What is the fee for a new or renewed Identification (ID) card for an individual age 60 and older?
en.explanation: According to the Identification Card (ID) Fees table, a new or renewed ID card for someone age 60 and older costs $6.

en.question: What does Restriction Code A on a Texas driver's license indicate?

choices.A: Daytime driving only
choices.B: With corrective lenses
choices.C: Automatic transmission
choices.D: Power steering

en.explanation: Appendix E: Restriction Codes lists Code A as requiring the driver to drive 'With corrective lenses'.

en.question: If a driver has Restriction Code B on their license, what is required when they drive?

choices.A: They must not exceed 45 mph
choices.B: They must drive a vehicle with an automatic transmission
choices.C: A licensed driver 21 years of age or older must be in the front seat
choices.D: They are restricted to daytime driving only

en.explanation: Restriction Code B mandates that 'A licensed driver 21 years of age or older (LOFS) must be in the front seat'.

choices.D: The motorcycle is restricted to three wheels

choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only

choices.B: A single curve ahead
choices.C: A series of two curves in opposite directions

choices.C: A series of curves or turns ahead

choices.C: A stop sign where you must stop

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

es.question: ¿Cuáles son los propósitos principales del Manual del Conductor de Texas?

choices.A: Servir como referencia legal oficial en los tribunales y proporcionar tarifas de seguros.
choices.B: Ayudarle a calificar para una licencia de conducir de Texas y ayudarle a convertirse en un conductor más seguro.
choices.C: Registrar su vehículo y proporcionar una lista de escuelas de manejo locales.
choices.D: Resumir el Código Penal de Texas y programar exámenes de manejo.

es.explanation: El manual establece que su propósito principal es: 1) ayudarle a calificar para una licencia de conducir de Texas, y 2) ayudarle a convertirse en un conductor más seguro.

es.question: Si desea leer el lenguaje exacto de las leyes de tránsito o penales a las que se hace referencia en el manual, ¿qué documentos debe consultar?

choices.A: El Apéndice del Manual del Conductor de Texas
choices.B: El Código Administrativo de Texas
choices.C: El Código de Transporte de Texas y el Código Penal de Texas
choices.D: El Libro de Reglas del Departamento de Seguridad Pública

es.explanation: El manual no es una referencia legal oficial. Para conocer el lenguaje exacto de las leyes de tránsito o penales, debe consultar el Código de Transporte de Texas y el Código Penal de Texas.

es.question: ¿Con qué frecuencia se reúne la Legislatura de Texas para realizar cambios regulares a las leyes de tránsito?

choices.A: Cada seis meses
choices.B: Cada año
choices.C: Cada dos años
choices.D: Cada cuatro años

es.explanation: El texto señala que la Legislatura de Texas se reúne cada dos años y realiza cambios regulares a las leyes de tránsito.

es.question: ¿Con cuánto tiempo de anticipación debe avisar si necesita hacer arreglos especiales para adaptarse a una discapacidad antes de visitar una oficina de licencias de conducir?

choices.A: Al menos 24 horas
choices.B: Al menos 48 horas
choices.C: Al menos de tres a cuatro días hábiles
choices.D: Al menos de cinco a siete días hábiles

es.explanation: El manual solicita que se comunique con ellos al menos de cinco a siete días hábiles antes de su visita para tener tiempo de atender una solicitud de la ADA (Ley sobre Estadounidenses con Discapacidades).

es.question: ¿Aproximadamente cuántas millas de vías públicas hay en el estado de Texas?

choices.A: Más de 100,000 millas
choices.B: Más de 250,000 millas
choices.C: Más de 314,000 millas
choices.D: Más de 500,000 millas

es.explanation: Según la carta del Coronel, Texas es un estado grande con más de 314,000 millas de vías públicas.

es.question: ¿Aproximadamente cuántas personas mueren en accidentes de tránsito cada año en Texas?
es.explanation: El manual establece que, trágicamente, cada año en Texas, aproximadamente 3,500 personas mueren en accidentes de tránsito.

es.question: Para prevenir consecuencias trágicas en la carretera, el Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas aconseja a los conductores mantenerse alerta ante conductores incapacitados y evitar ¿qué cosa en sus propios vehículos?

choices.A: Escuchar la radio
choices.B: Distracciones
choices.C: Llevar pasajeros
choices.D: Conducir de noche

es.explanation: El manual enfatiza que los conductores deben evitar distracciones en su propio vehículo mientras se mantienen alerta ante conductores incapacitados o inseguros.

es.question: Según la Tabla de Contenido, ¿de qué otra manera se conoce a una Licencia Ocupacional?

choices.A: Licencia por Dificultades
choices.B: Licencia de Necesidad Esencial
choices.C: Licencia Provisional
choices.D: Licencia Restringida

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido enumera la 'Licencia Ocupacional (Licencia de Necesidad Esencial)' en el Capítulo 1.

es.question: ¿Qué capítulo del Manual del Conductor de Texas cubre la Ley de Seguro de Responsabilidad Civil y la Evidencia de Responsabilidad Financiera?

choices.A: Capítulo 1
choices.B: Capítulo 2
choices.C: Capítulo 3
choices.D: Capítulo 4

es.explanation: Según la Tabla de Contenido, el Capítulo 3: Responsabilidad de Seguridad cubre la Ley de Seguro de Responsabilidad Civil y la Evidencia de Responsabilidad Financiera.

es.question: Según la Tabla de Contenido, ¿cuál de los siguientes temas se cubre en el Capítulo 4: Derecho de Paso?

choices.A: Ceder el Derecho de Paso a los Autobuses Escolares
choices.B: Equipo Requerido para Vehículos
choices.C: Sanciones por Conducir sin Licencia
choices.D: Señales de Tránsito

es.explanation: La Tabla de Contenido muestra que 'Ceder el Derecho de Paso a los Autobuses Escolares' es una sección dentro del Capítulo 4: Derecho de Paso.

es.question: ¿Dónde se pueden encontrar los Procedimientos de Quejas del Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas si no recibe adaptaciones razonables de la ADA?

choices.A: El Código Penal de Texas
choices.B: 37 Código Administrativo de Texas §1.41
choices.C: El Código de Transporte de Texas
choices.D: Capítulo 5 del Manual del Conductor de Texas

es.explanation: El manual establece que los Procedimientos de Quejas del DPS se pueden encontrar en el 37 Código Administrativo de Texas §1.41.

es.question: ¿En qué capítulo del manual encontraría información sobre el 'Equipo que no debe tener' en su vehículo?

choices.A: Capítulo 1: Su licencia de conducir
choices.B: Capítulo 2: Inspección y registro del vehículo
choices.C: Capítulo 3: Responsabilidad de seguridad
choices.D: Capítulo 5: Señales, letreros y marcadores

es.explanation: El índice enumera el 'Equipo que no debe tener' bajo el Capítulo 2: Inspección y registro del vehículo.

es.question: ¿Qué división del Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas es responsable de publicar el Manual del Conductor de Texas?

choices.A: La División de Patrulla de Caminos
choices.B: La División de Inspección de Vehículos
choices.C: La División de Licencias de Conducir
choices.D: La División de Seguridad Vial

es.explanation: La introducción establece que el Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas (DPS), División de Licencias de Conducir, proporciona el manual.

es.question: Según el índice, ¿el Capítulo 1 incluye información sobre las sanciones por cuál de las siguientes infracciones cometidas por menores?

choices.A: Exceso de velocidad en una zona escolar
choices.B: Infracciones relacionadas con el alcohol no relacionadas con la conducción
choices.C: Conducir sin cinturón de seguridad
choices.D: Enviar mensajes de texto mientras se conduce

es.explanation: El índice del Capítulo 1 enumera una sección titulada 'Sanciones por infracciones relacionadas con el alcohol no relacionadas con la conducción por menores'.

es.question: Según el manual, ¿cuál es el asesino número uno en las carreteras?

choices.A: El exceso de velocidad
choices.B: La conducción distraída
choices.C: El alcohol
choices.D: El mal tiempo

es.explanation: El manual establece explícitamente que 'El asesino número uno es el alcohol' en el capítulo que cubre el impacto del alcohol y las drogas en la capacidad de conducir.

es.question: ¿Cómo afecta el aumento de velocidad a su capacidad de conducir?

choices.A: Aumenta su tiempo de reacción
choices.B: Reduce su campo de visión
choices.C: Mejora la tracción de su vehículo
choices.D: Amplía su campo de visión

es.explanation: El manual incluye una sección específica titulada 'La velocidad reduce su campo de visión' en el capítulo de Velocidad y límites de velocidad.

es.question: Al acercarse a vehículos de emergencia o de las fuerzas del orden detenidos a un lado de la carretera, ¿qué acción específica se destaca en el capítulo de límites de velocidad?

choices.A: Tocar la bocina
choices.B: Mantener su velocidad
choices.C: Reducir la velocidad o cambiar de carril (Slow Down or Move Over)
choices.D: Detenerse inmediatamente

es.explanation: El manual incluye la regla de 'Reducir la velocidad o cambiar de carril' (Slow Down or Move Over) en el capítulo sobre velocidad y límites de velocidad.

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de emblema se requiere específicamente para ciertos vehículos que viajan a velocidades más bajas?

choices.A: Emblema de vehículo de alta ocupación
choices.B: Emblema de vehículo de movimiento lento
choices.C: Emblema de vehículo comercial
choices.D: Emblema de carga ancha

es.explanation: El manual enumera el 'Emblema de vehículo de movimiento lento' en la sección de señales y letreros.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones está categorizada explícitamente como una 'Situación especial de conducción' en el manual?

choices.A: Conducir en una zona escolar
choices.B: Estacionamiento en paralelo
choices.C: Conducción en invierno
choices.D: Ceder el paso en una intersección

es.explanation: La 'Conducción en invierno' aparece en el capítulo titulado 'Algunas situaciones especiales de conducción'.

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de marca en el pavimento se menciona específicamente en el capítulo de leyes y seguridad para bicicletas?

choices.A: Línea amarilla continua
choices.B: Marca de carril compartido
choices.C: Línea blanca discontinua
choices.D: Marca de cruce peatonal

es.explanation: La 'Marca de carril compartido' se enumera específicamente en el capítulo de Leyes y seguridad para bicicletas.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes es un tipo específico de choque descrito en el capítulo de choques de vehículos de motor?

choices.A: Choque que involucra un vehículo desatendido
choices.B: Choque que involucra a un peatón
choices.C: Choque que involucra una bicicleta
choices.D: Choque que involucra un tren

es.explanation: "Choque que involucra un vehículo desatendido" (Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle) aparece explícitamente como una sección en el capítulo de Choques de vehículos de motor.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer un conductor con respecto a las señales de advertencia y las barricadas?

choices.A: Conducir alrededor de ellas con cuidado
choices.B: Moverlas si bloquean el camino
choices.C: Obedecer las señales de advertencia y las barricadas
choices.D: Reportarlas a las autoridades

es.explanation: El manual instruye explícitamente a los conductores a "Obedecer las señales de advertencia y las barricadas" en la sección de señales de tránsito.

es.question: ¿Qué gas peligroso se destaca específicamente como un consejo de seguridad adicional a tener en cuenta?

choices.A: Dióxido de nitrógeno
choices.B: Monóxido de carbono
choices.C: Dióxido de azufre
choices.D: Ozono

es.explanation: El "Monóxido de carbono" se enumera en el capítulo de Consejos de seguridad adicionales.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes se considera un "Camión grande" según la sección de compartir el camino?

choices.A: Una camioneta de reparto
choices.B: Una camioneta pickup con remolque
choices.C: Una combinación de camión-tractor
choices.D: Un vehículo de pasajeros de servicio pesado

es.explanation: El manual especifica "Camiones grandes y combinaciones de camión-tractor" en la sección sobre compartir el camino con camiones.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la responsabilidad de un conductor cuando está involucrado en un choque donde alguien resulta herido, según el capítulo de choques?

choices.A: Esperar a los servicios de emergencia sin intervenir
choices.B: Ayudar a los heridos
choices.C: Dirigir el tráfico alrededor del choque
choices.D: Mover los vehículos inmediatamente

es.explanation: "Ayudar a los heridos" (Aiding the Injured) se enumera como una sección específica en el capítulo de Choques de vehículos de motor.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes se enumera como una categoría específica de señales de tránsito?

choices.A: Señales sugestivas
choices.B: Señales de guía
choices.C: Señales opcionales
choices.D: Señales temporales

es.explanation: Las "Señales de guía" (Guide Signs) se enumeran explícitamente como una categoría bajo Señales de tránsito.

es.question: Además de los camiones grandes, motocicletas y bicicletas, ¿con qué otro medio de transporte específico instruye el manual a los conductores a "Compartir el camino"?

choices.A: Tren ligero
choices.B: Aviones
choices.C: Carruajes tirados por caballos
choices.D: Peatones

es.explanation: "Compartir el camino con el tren ligero" (Share the Road with Light Rail) es una sección específica en el capítulo de Situaciones especiales de manejo.

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de choque involucra a un conductor que abandona la escena sin proporcionar su información?

choices.A: Choque desatendido
choices.B: Choques de atropello y fuga
choices.C: Choque contra un objeto fijo
choices.D: Choque por infracción en movimiento

es.explanation: Los "Choques de atropello y fuga" (Hit-and-Run Crashes) se enumeran explícitamente en el capítulo de Choques de vehículos de motor.

es.question: ¿Qué se requiere de las bicicletas antes de que puedan ser operadas de manera segura en la vía pública?

choices.A: Deben estar registradas en el estado
choices.B: Deben tener un motor acoplado
choices.C: Deben estar debidamente equipadas
choices.D: Deben estar pintadas de un color brillante

es.explanation: El manual establece que "Las bicicletas deben estar debidamente equipadas" en el capítulo de Leyes y seguridad para bicicletas.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene un nuevo residente con una licencia válida de otro estado para establecer su residencia y obtener una licencia de conducir de Texas?

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 60 días
choices.C: 90 días
choices.D: 120 días

es.explanation: Según el manual, los nuevos residentes que están intercambiando una licencia válida de otro estado tienen 90 días para establecer su residencia en Texas con el fin de obtener una licencia de conducir de Texas.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes personas está exenta de tener una licencia de conducir de Texas?

choices.A: Una persona que conduce un vehículo comercial de motor a través de las fronteras estatales
choices.B: Una persona que opera temporalmente un tractor agrícola en una carretera
choices.C: Un joven de 16 años que conduce el automóvil familiar a la escuela
choices.D: Un nuevo residente que ha vivido en Texas durante 6 meses

es.explanation: Cualquier persona que opere o mueva temporalmente maquinaria vial, un tractor agrícola o un implemento agrícola en una carretera está exenta de tener una licencia de Texas, a menos que el vehículo sea un vehículo comercial de motor.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para que un no residente conduzca un vehículo de Clase C o Clase M en Texas usando una licencia de conducir válida de su estado de origen o provincia canadiense?

choices.A: 15 años
choices.B: 16 años
choices.C: 18 años
choices.D: 21 años

es.explanation: Cualquier no residente que tenga al menos 16 años de edad y posea una licencia de conducir válida emitida en su estado de origen o provincia canadiense puede conducir un vehículo que esté permitido operar con una licencia de conducir de Clase C o Clase M en Texas.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo sigue siendo válida una licencia de conducir de Texas para una persona en las fuerzas armadas de los EE. UU. después de ser dada de baja con honores del servicio o regresar a Texas?

choices.A: 30 días
choices.B: 60 días
choices.C: 90 días
choices.D: 180 días

es.explanation: Una licencia de conducir de Texas en posesión de una persona en las fuerzas armadas de los EE. UU. sigue siendo válida mientras continúe el servicio y la persona permanezca ausente de Texas, siempre que la ausencia no exceda los 90 días a partir de la fecha en que es dada de baja con honores del servicio o regresa a Texas.

es.question: ¿Cuáles son los requisitos para el conductor con licencia que debe acompañar a un estudiante de manejo con una licencia de aprendizaje?

choices.A: Debe tener al menos 18 años con 6 meses de experiencia de manejo
choices.B: Debe tener al menos 21 años con al menos un año de experiencia de manejo
choices.C: Debe ser un padre o tutor legal mayor de 25 años
