choices.D: Up to 8 years from the date of your last birthday

en.explanation: A standard driver license is valid for up to six years from the date of your last birthday.

en.question: What travel privilege does an Enhanced Driver License (EDL) provide that a standard license does not?

choices.A: It allows you to board international flights to Europe.
choices.B: It allows you to cross the borders of Canada and Mexico by land or sea.
choices.C: It allows you to drive in foreign countries without an international permit.
choices.D: It allows you to bypass customs when returning to the United States.

en.explanation: Washington's enhanced driver license (EDL) is REAL ID compliant, valid for air travel within the U.S., and can be used to cross the borders of Canada and Mexico by land or sea.

en.question: What is the minimum age to get an instruction permit if you are NOT enrolled in an approved driver-training course?

choices.A: 15 years old
choices.B: 15-1/2 years old
choices.C: 16 years old
choices.D: 18 years old

en.explanation: To be issued an instruction permit, you must be at least 15-1/2 years old, or 15 years old if enrolled in an approved driver-training course.

en.question: How many hours of driving experience must a parent or guardian certify you have completed before you can get an intermediate license?

choices.A: 30 hours, including 5 hours at night
choices.B: 40 hours, including 10 hours at night
choices.C: 50 hours, including 10 hours at night
choices.D: 60 hours, including 15 hours at night

en.explanation: You must show that your parent or guardian certifies you have had at least 50 hours of driving experience, including 10 hours at night.

en.question: To get an intermediate license, you must pass an approved driver-training course that includes at least how many hours of classroom instruction?

choices.A: 10 hours
choices.B: 20 hours
choices.C: 30 hours
choices.D: 40 hours

en.explanation: You must show proof that you have passed an approved driver-training course with at least 30 hours of classroom and six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.

en.question: What are the restricted driving hours for an intermediate driver license holder, unless accompanied by a qualifying person?

choices.A: 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.
choices.B: 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
choices.C: 12 a.m. to 5 a.m.
choices.D: 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.

en.explanation: An intermediate license restricts you from driving between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless you are with a parent, a guardian, or a licensed driver who is at least 25 years old.

en.question: During the first six months of holding an intermediate license, what is the restriction regarding passengers?

choices.A: No passengers are allowed under any circumstances.
choices.B: No passenger under the age of 20 may be with you unless they are a member of your immediate family.
choices.C: You may only carry one passenger under the age of 20.
choices.D: You may carry any passengers as long as they are wearing seatbelts.

en.explanation: For the first six months of an intermediate license, no passenger under the age of 20 may be with you while you drive unless that person is a member of your immediate family.

en.question: Under an intermediate license, you cannot drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or a licensed driver who is at least what age?

choices.A: 18 years old
choices.B: 21 years old
choices.C: 25 years old
choices.D: 30 years old

en.explanation: The manual states that with an intermediate license, you cannot drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless you are with a parent, a guardian, or a licensed driver who is at least 25 years old.

en.question: For the first six months of holding an intermediate license, who may ride as a passenger in your vehicle?

choices.A: Up to three passengers under age 20
choices.B: No passengers under age 20 unless they are immediate family
choices.C: Any licensed driver under age 20
choices.D: Only passengers over the age of 25

en.explanation: According to the manual, for the first six months of an intermediate license, no passenger under the age of 20 may be with you while you drive unless that person is a member of your immediate family.

en.question: What is the penalty for a second violation of intermediate license restrictions during the first year?

choices.A: A warning letter is sent to your parent or guardian
choices.B: Your license is suspended for six months or until age 18
choices.C: Your license is suspended until age 21
choices.D: You must retake the driving test

en.explanation: The manual states that for a second violation, you are suspended for six months (or until age 18 if that comes first).

en.question: When is a driver with an intermediate license permitted to use a cell phone while operating a vehicle?

choices.A: When using a hands-free device
choices.B: When stopped at a red light
choices.C: To report illegal activity or summon emergency help
choices.D: To get directions from a GPS application

en.explanation: Intermediate license holders may not use a cell phone unless using the device to report illegal activity, summon medical or other emergency help, or prevent injury to a person or property.

en.question: At what age does an intermediate license automatically become a standard driver license without restrictions?
en.explanation: The manual states: "On your 18th birthday, your license will become a standard driver license without the intermediate license restrictions."

en.question: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass the knowledge test?

choices.A: 25 out of 30
choices.B: 32 out of 40
choices.C: 35 out of 40
choices.D: 40 out of 50

en.explanation: The knowledge test is a multiple-choice test with 40 questions, and you must correctly answer 32 of them to pass the test.

en.question: How long is a passing score on the knowledge test valid?

choices.A: 6 months
choices.B: 1 year
choices.C: 2 years
choices.D: 5 years

en.explanation: According to the manual, a passing test score on the knowledge test is good for two years.

en.question: Who is allowed in the vehicle with you and the examiner during the driving test?

choices.A: A parent or guardian
choices.B: A foreign language interpreter
choices.C: A service animal or an interpreter for the deaf
choices.D: A licensed driving instructor

en.explanation: The manual specifies that only you, the examiner, a service animal, and an interpreter for the deaf or hard of hearing are allowed in the vehicle during the test.

en.question: What must you do when backing your vehicle during the driving test?

choices.A: Rely solely on your rearview mirror
choices.B: Turn your head and look to the rear
choices.C: Honk your horn before moving
choices.D: Use only your side mirrors

en.explanation: During the test, you must turn your head and look to the rear for motor vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians when you are backing your vehicle.

en.question: How long can a renewed Washington driver license be valid?

choices.A: Up to 4 years
choices.B: Up to 5 years
choices.C: Up to 6 years
choices.D: Up to 8 years

en.explanation: The manual states: "Your renewed license can be valid for up to six years and will expire on your birthday."

en.question: You must pay an additional late fee if you renew your license more than how many days after it has expired?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you renew your license more than 60 days after it has expired, you must pay an additional late fee.

en.question: How many days do you have to notify the Department of Licensing of an address or legal name change?

choices.A: 5 days
choices.B: 10 days
choices.C: 15 days
choices.D: 30 days

en.explanation: You must notify the Department within ten days of an address change or a legal name change.

en.question: Which of the following is a reason you can lose your driver license?

choices.A: Receiving a single parking ticket
choices.B: Refusing to allow a police officer to test you for alcohol
choices.C: Driving 5 mph over the speed limit
choices.D: Failing to renew your license one day after it expires

en.explanation: The manual lists "refusing to allow a police officer to test you for alcohol" as one of the reasons you can lose your license.

en.question: If you choose not to remove an item that obstructs a full view of your face for your license photo (and do not have a medical or religious exception), what will happen?

choices.A: Your license will be marked "Not Valid for Identification"
choices.B: You will be denied a driver license entirely
choices.C: You must pay an additional fee
choices.D: You will be issued a temporary permit instead

en.explanation: The manual states that if you choose not to remove an obstruction to your face and head, your license will be marked "Not Valid for Identification."

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement for the vehicle you bring to your driving test?

choices.A: It must be less than 10 years old
choices.B: It must have dual controls for the examiner
choices.C: It must be legally licensed, registered, and have no defective parts
choices.D: It must have an automatic transmission

en.explanation: For the driving test, you must bring a vehicle that is legally licensed and registered, and it must not have defective parts.

en.question: If you are an uninsured driver involved in a collision, your license may be suspended for up to how long?

choices.A: 1 year
choices.B: 3 years
choices.C: 5 years
choices.D: 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states that the Department of Licensing may suspend the license of an uninsured driver involved in a collision for up to three years.

en.question: Failing to settle a civil court judgment resulting from a collision can result in a license suspension for how many years?

choices.A: 3 or more years
choices.B: 5 or more years
choices.C: 10 or more years
choices.D: 13 or more years

en.explanation: Failing to settle a civil court judgment resulting from a collision can result in a suspension for 13 or more years.

en.question: Which of the following actions can result in the loss of your driver license?

choices.A: Leaving a gas station without paying for fuel you have pumped.
choices.B: Parking more than 12 inches from the curb.
choices.C: Driving 5 mph over the speed limit on a highway.
choices.D: Failing to wash your vehicle regularly.

en.explanation: According to the manual, you can lose your license for leaving a gas station without paying for fuel you have pumped.

en.question: How many traffic offenses must you receive while driving with an intermediate license to lose your driving privilege?

choices.A: One or more
choices.B: Two or more
choices.C: Three or more
choices.D: Four or more

en.explanation: You can lose your license for receiving two or more traffic offenses while driving with an intermediate license.

en.question: If you get a ticket and do not comply within 15 days, the court notifies the Department of Licensing. How many days do you then have to comply before your driving privilege is suspended?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 45 days
choices.D: 60 days

en.explanation: If you don't comply within 15 days, the court notifies the department and they mail a Notice of Suspension. You then have 45 days to comply or your driving privilege will be suspended.

en.question: Sex offenders and kidnapping offenders in Washington State must register with the county sheriff within how many days of establishing residence?

choices.A: Three business days
choices.B: Five business days
choices.C: Ten business days
choices.D: Thirty days

en.explanation: Sex offenders and kidnapping offenders in Washington State must register within three business days of establishing, or re-establishing, residence.

en.question: To register to vote at a driver licensing office, you must be a United States citizen, a Washington State resident, and at least what age?
en.explanation: To register to vote, you must be a United States citizen whose civil rights are not currently revoked, a Washington State resident, and at least 18.

en.question: What happens if a male applicant under the age of 26 declines to register with the Selective Service System when applying for a driver's license?

choices.A: His application will be immediately denied.
choices.B: He will be issued a restricted license.
choices.C: He may not be denied the requested document if he meets all other requirements.
choices.D: He must pay an additional fee to receive his license.

en.explanation: An applicant who declines to register with the SSS may not be denied the requested document if they meet all of the other requirements to receive the requested document.

en.question: The Department of Licensing asks if you are a twin or triplet in cooperation with which institution for medical research?

choices.A: Washington State University
choices.B: University of Washington
choices.C: LifeCenter Northwest
choices.D: The Department of Health

en.explanation: The department asks if you are a twin or triplet in cooperation with the University of Washington, which has the largest twin registry in the United States.

en.question: Which of the following is permitted with an Enhanced Driver License but NOT with a Standard Driver License?

choices.A: Operating a motor vehicle
choices.B: Domestic air travel
choices.C: Access to federal facilities that don't require ID
choices.D: International border crossing by land or sea

en.explanation: An Enhanced Driver License allows international border crossing by land or sea, while a Standard Driver License does not.

en.question: Risk is generated by all three components of the Highway Transportation System. What are these three components?

choices.A: The driver, the vehicle, and the roadway environment
choices.B: The weather, the vehicle, and the driver
choices.C: The pedestrians, the roadway, and the weather
choices.D: The speed limit, the driver, and the vehicle

en.explanation: Risk is generated by all three components of the Highway Transportation System: the driver, the vehicle, and the roadway environment.

en.question: According to Washington crash data from 2009 to 2011, what was the most common factor present in fatal crashes?

choices.A: Speeding
choices.B: Running off the roadway
choices.C: Driver impairment
choices.D: Driver distraction

en.explanation: Driver impairment was the most common factor, present in 50.1% of fatal crashes.

en.question: What is the leading cause of death for young people ages 16 to 25 in Washington?

choices.A: Drug overdose
choices.B: Motor vehicle crashes
choices.C: Drowning
choices.D: Workplace accidents

en.explanation: Motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of death for young people ages 16 to 25 in Washington.

en.question: What may happen if you are caught driving while your privilege is suspended due to a Failure to Appear (FTA) violation?

choices.A: You will be given a warning.
choices.B: You may be arrested and your vehicle may be impounded.
choices.C: Your vehicle will be confiscated permanently.
choices.D: You will be required to retake the driving test immediately.

en.explanation: If you do not comply, your driving privilege is suspended. You may be arrested and your vehicle may be impounded if you are caught driving while your privilege is suspended.

en.question: Who is eligible to be issued a photo identification card by the Department of Licensing?

choices.A: Only individuals over the age of 18.
choices.B: Only individuals who have passed a written driving test.
choices.C: Non-drivers of any age.
choices.D: Only individuals who have a suspended driver's license.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'We issue photo identification cards to non-drivers of any age.'

en.question: What is the minimum liability insurance required for property damage in any one collision in Washington?
en.explanation: You must have an automobile liability policy that provides $10,000 or more, payable for injury to or destruction of property of others in any one collision.

en.question: Which of the following vehicles is exempt from the state's liability insurance requirement?

choices.A: Passenger cars manufactured after 1993
choices.B: Mopeds
choices.C: Sport utility vehicles (SUVs)
choices.D: Commercial delivery vans

en.explanation: Drivers of government vehicles, mopeds, and common or contract carrier vehicles are exempt from this insurance requirement.

en.question: What is the minimum legal tire tread depth in Washington?

choices.A: 1/32 inch
choices.B: 2/32 inch
choices.C: 3/32 inch
choices.D: 4/32 inch

en.explanation: If the tread does not come at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch) when checking with a penny, the tire is illegal and unsafe and needs to be replaced.

en.question: When is the best time to check your tire air pressure?

choices.A: Immediately after driving on the highway
choices.B: When the tires are cold
choices.C: During the hottest part of the day
choices.D: When the tires are warm to the touch

en.explanation: The manual advises to check tire air pressure with an air pressure gauge when the tires are cold.

en.question: Why should you never turn your vehicle's ignition to the 'lock' position while it is in motion?

choices.A: It will cause the engine to overheat.
choices.B: It will drain the vehicle's battery.
choices.C: It will cause the steering to lock and you will lose control.
choices.D: It will permanently damage the transmission.

en.explanation: Turning the ignition to 'lock' while in motion will cause the steering to lock if you try to turn the steering wheel, resulting in a loss of control of your vehicle.

en.question: What is a potential danger of a leaky exhaust system?

choices.A: It can cause your windshield to fog up.
choices.B: It can cause death inside a vehicle in a very short time.
choices.C: It will cause the steering wheel to shake.
choices.D: It increases the chance of a flat tire.

en.explanation: Gases from a leaky exhaust can cause death inside a vehicle in a very short time. You should never run the motor in a closed garage.

en.question: Passenger vehicles manufactured after 1993 are required to have:

choices.A: A third rear brake light mounted high in the center of the vehicle.
choices.B: Wipers for the rear windows and headlights.
choices.C: A backup camera system.
choices.D: Automatic emergency braking.

en.explanation: Passenger trucks, cars, vans, and sport utility vehicles (SUVs) manufactured after 1993 must have a third rear brake light mounted high in the center of the vehicle.

en.question: If your vehicle continues to bounce after a bump or a stop, which system likely needs to be checked by a mechanic?

choices.A: Braking system
choices.B: Steering system
choices.C: Suspension system
choices.D: Exhaust system

en.explanation: If the vehicle continues to bounce after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, you may need new shocks or suspension parts and should have a mechanic check it.

en.question: When is a load in a vehicle or trailer considered legally secure?

choices.A: When it is tied down with at least one rope.
choices.B: When nothing can slide, shift, fall, sift onto the roadway, or become airborne.
choices.C: When it is covered by a tarp, even if it can shift.
choices.D: When the vehicle is traveling under 40 mph.

en.explanation: A load must be securely fastened and is only considered secure when nothing can slide, shift, fall, or sift onto the roadway, or become airborne.

en.question: Under Maria's Law, what is the maximum penalty for failing to properly secure a load that causes an injury or death?

choices.A: A $500 fine and a suspended license
choices.B: A misdemeanor charge and 30 days in jail
choices.C: A gross misdemeanor charge, up to one year in jail, and a $5,000 fine
choices.D: A felony charge and up to five years in prison

en.explanation: A person who causes an injury or death by failing to secure a load properly can be charged with a gross misdemeanor and can face a maximum penalty of one year in jail and a $5,000 fine.

en.question: What charge can a driver face if their unsecured items cause property damage?

choices.A: A traffic infraction
choices.B: A misdemeanor
choices.C: A gross misdemeanor
choices.D: A felony

en.explanation: A driver whose unsecured items cause property damage can be charged with a misdemeanor.

en.question: What should you do if you see a vehicle driving with an unsecured load?

choices.A: Honk your horn continuously until they pull over.
choices.B: Pull up closely beside them to warn the driver.
choices.C: Stay as far away as possible and call 911 when it is safe.
choices.D: Flash your high beams to get their attention.

en.explanation: If you see a vehicle driving with an unsecured load, you should stay as far away as possible and call 911 when it is safe for you to do so.

en.question: What is a consequence of driving with unbalanced tires or low tire pressure?

choices.A: It reduces fuel economy and makes the vehicle harder to steer and stop.
choices.B: It causes the engine to lose power and stall.
choices.C: It improves traction on wet roads.
choices.D: It causes the exhaust system to overheat.

en.explanation: Unbalanced tires and low pressure cause faster tire wear, reduce fuel economy, and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

en.question: According to the manual, what percentage of highway litter comes from unsecured loads?
en.explanation: According to the Washington State Department of Ecology, roughly 40% of highway litter comes from unsecured loads, which causes hundreds of crashes per year.

en.question: What is the maximum penalty for driving with an unsecured load in Washington State?

choices.A: 6 months in jail and a $1,000 fine
choices.B: 1 year in jail and a $5,000 fine
choices.C: 2 years in jail and a $10,000 fine
choices.D: A $500 fine and a 30-day license suspension

en.explanation: The manual states that driving with an unsecured load carries a maximum penalty of one year in jail and a $5,000 fine.

en.question: How much can dirt on the lenses of your headlights, backup, brake, and tail lights reduce the light they emit?

choices.A: 10 percent
choices.B: 25 percent
choices.C: 50 percent
choices.D: 75 percent

en.explanation: According to the manual, dirt on the lenses can reduce the light by 50 percent.

en.question: When adjusting your seat and steering wheel before driving, at least how much of the steering wheel should be between your hands?

choices.A: One-quarter
choices.B: One-third
choices.C: One-half
choices.D: Two-thirds

en.explanation: You should have clear vision in all directions, all controls should be within reach, and at least one-third of the steering wheel should be between your hands.

en.question: How should you position your seat in relation to the vehicle's air bag?

choices.A: So the air bag will hit you in the face
choices.B: So the air bag will hit you in the chest
choices.C: So the air bag will deploy above your head
choices.D: So the air bag will hit your stomach

en.explanation: You should sit so the air bag will hit you in the chest if there is a collision.

en.question: How should you adjust your side mirrors to best see the traffic behind you?

choices.A: So you cannot see any part of your own vehicle
choices.B: So you can see the entire side of your vehicle while sitting back
choices.C: So you can see a small amount of the side of your vehicle when you lean forward slightly
choices.D: So they point directly at the ground behind your rear tires

en.explanation: Adjust the side mirrors so that you can see a small amount of the side of your vehicle when you lean forward slightly. This will help you see the traffic behind you.

en.question: Who is responsible for paying the fine if a 17-year-old passenger is caught not wearing a seat belt?

choices.A: The driver of the vehicle
choices.B: The 17-year-old passenger
choices.C: The passenger's parents
choices.D: Both the driver and the passenger

en.explanation: Passengers over 16 years are responsible for wearing their seat belts and for paying any fine.

en.question: A driver can be cited and fined for which of the following unrestrained passengers?

choices.A: Only passengers under age 12
choices.B: Only passengers under age 16
choices.C: Only passengers sitting in the front seat
choices.D: Any passenger regardless of age

en.explanation: The driver will be fined for any passengers under age 16 who are not properly wearing a seat belt or secured in a child safety restraint.

en.question: What is the correct way to wear a vehicle's lap belt?

choices.A: Across your stomach
choices.B: Across your hip bones below your stomach
choices.C: Loosely across your thighs
choices.D: Tucked under your arm

en.explanation: To buckle up correctly for the best safety, adjust the lap belt across your hip bones below your stomach.

en.question: Under Washington law, children must use a child safety restraint until they reach what age or height?

choices.A: Their 6th birthday or 4'5" tall
choices.B: Their 8th birthday or 4'9" tall
choices.C: Their 10th birthday or 5'0" tall
choices.D: Their 12th birthday or 4'9" tall

en.explanation: Children up to their 8th birthday, unless they are 4’9” tall (whichever comes first), must use a child safety restraint.

en.question: According to Washington's child restraint law, children under what age are to be transported in the back seat where it is practical to do so?

choices.A: Under 8 years old
choices.B: Under 10 years old
choices.C: Under 12 years old
choices.D: Under 13 years old

en.explanation: Washington’s child restraint law requires children under 13 years old to be transported in the back seat where it is practical to do so.

en.question: Which type of child safety restraint is described as the best seat for a young child because it cradles and moves with the child to reduce stress to the fragile neck and spinal cord?

choices.A: A forward-facing car seat
choices.B: A booster seat
choices.C: A rear-facing car seat
choices.D: A standard seat belt

en.explanation: A rear-facing car seat is the best seat for your young child to use. It has a harness that, in a crash, cradles and moves with your child to reduce the stress to the child’s fragile neck and spinal cord.

en.question: What are the rules regarding wireless device use for teens with intermediate driver licenses or learner permits?

choices.A: They may only use hands-free devices while driving.
choices.B: They may not use a wireless device at all while driving, unless reporting an emergency.
choices.C: They may text while stopped at a red light.
choices.D: They may use a handheld cell phone if they are driving alone.

en.explanation: Teens with intermediate driver licenses or learner permits may not use a wireless device at all while driving, including hands-free devices, unless they’re reporting an emergency.

en.question: According to the manual, what safety benefit do hands-free devices offer compared to handheld devices?

choices.A: They reduce the risk of a crash by 50 percent.
choices.B: They allow the driver to maintain full visual focus on the road.
choices.C: They offer no safety benefit.
choices.D: They are completely safe to use in heavy traffic.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Hands-free devices offer no safety benefit. Parking your phone is the only safe way to drive."

en.question: The Occupant Protection law in Washington State is a "primary enforcement" law. What does this mean?

choices.A: Officers can only issue a warning for a first offense.
choices.B: Officers can stop and cite drivers solely for not wearing a seat belt.
choices.C: Officers must observe another traffic violation before citing for a seat belt offense.
choices.D: Only the primary driver of the vehicle can be cited.

en.explanation: The Occupant Protection law in Washington State is "primary enforcement", meaning a law enforcement officer can stop and cite drivers when they or their passengers are seen to not be wearing their seat belt.

en.question: What is the maximum number of people allowed in the front seat if it blocks your view or interferes with the control of your vehicle?

choices.A: Two people
choices.B: Three people
choices.C: Four people
choices.D: There is no limit

en.explanation: The manual states: "You may not drive with more than three people in the front seat if it blocks your view or interferes with the control of your vehicle."

en.question: Under what circumstances may a driver with a permit use a wireless device while driving?

choices.A: When using a hands-free device.
choices.B: Only when reporting an emergency.
choices.C: When pulled over to the shoulder for a non-emergency.
choices.D: When stopped at a red light.

en.explanation: The manual states that drivers with permits may not use a wireless device at all while driving, including hands-free devices, unless they are reporting an emergency.

en.question: What should you do if you approach an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution.
choices.B: Yield to the vehicle on your right without stopping.
choices.C: Come to a complete stop and yield as if it were a four-way stop.
choices.D: Wait for a police officer to arrive before proceeding.

en.explanation: If a traffic signal is not working, you must come to a complete stop, then yield to traffic as if it were a four-way stop.

en.question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?

choices.A: The light is about to change to red and you must stop if it is safe to do so.
choices.B: You should speed up to clear the intersection before the light turns red.
choices.C: You must come to a complete stop immediately, regardless of surrounding traffic.
choices.D: Left turns are protected and you have the right-of-way.

en.explanation: A steady yellow traffic light means the traffic light is about to change to red. You must stop if it is safe to do so.

en.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean?

choices.A: Left turns are prohibited.
choices.B: Left turns are allowed, but you must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians.
choices.C: You have a protected left turn and oncoming traffic must stop.
choices.D: The traffic signal is broken and you must treat it as a four-way stop.

en.question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a steady red traffic light?

choices.A: Whenever there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.B: Only when turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street.
choices.C: When turning onto a one-way street with traffic moving left, after coming to a full stop and if no sign prohibits it.
choices.D: It is never legal to turn left on a red light.

en.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street with traffic moving left after coming to a full stop if there is no sign prohibiting turns on a red light.

en.question: When turning right or left, when must you stop for pedestrians and bicyclists crossing in front of your vehicle?

choices.A: Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
choices.B: If they are in, or within, one lane of your half of the roadway.
choices.C: Only if they have a walk signal.
choices.D: If they are anywhere on the roadway, regardless of distance.

en.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians and bicyclists if they are in, or within, one lane of your half of the roadway.

en.question: What do warning signs typically look like?

choices.A: Square and white with black lettering.
choices.B: Round and yellow with an 'X' symbol.
choices.C: Diamond shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols.
choices.D: Rectangular and orange with black letters.

en.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black lettering or symbols and most are diamond shaped.

en.question: Approximately how long can it take for a train with 100 cars to come to a full stop?

choices.A: One-quarter of a mile.
choices.B: One-half of a mile.
choices.C: Up to a mile.
choices.D: Two miles.

en.explanation: Trains are large and may be moving faster than they look, it can take up to a mile for a train to come to a full stop with 100 cars.

en.question: What does a white X-shaped 'crossbuck' sign at a railroad crossing mean?

choices.A: It has the same meaning as a 'Yield' sign.
choices.B: It indicates a mandatory full stop.
choices.C: It warns that there is more than one track ahead.
choices.D: It means the crossing is currently closed to traffic.

en.explanation: A white X-shaped sign or 'crossbuck' with 'Railroad Crossing' on it is located at the railroad crossing. This sign has the same meaning as a 'Yield' sign.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your vehicle becomes disabled on a railroad crossing and no train is approaching?

choices.A: Try to push the vehicle off the tracks yourself.
choices.B: Call 911 immediately.
choices.C: Call the Emergency Notification System (ENS) using the number on the blue sign at the crossing.
choices.D: Walk down the tracks to look for an oncoming train.

en.explanation: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the crossing, you should immediately call the Emergency Notification System (ENS). The phone number is located on the blue sign attached to the railroad track-crossing gate.

en.question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?

choices.A: The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
choices.B: The vehicle is traveling less than 25 mph.
choices.C: The vehicle is an emergency responder.
choices.D: The vehicle is broken down and waiting for a tow.

en.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle means it is traveling less than 25 mph. This is known as a Slow Moving Vehicle sign.

en.question: What happens to fines for moving violations in construction areas when workers are present?

choices.A: They are reduced by half.
choices.B: They remain the same as normal violations.
choices.C: They are doubled.
choices.D: They result in an automatic license suspension.

en.explanation: Fines double for moving violations in construction areas when workers are present.

en.question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?

choices.A: To warn drivers of sharp curves and hazards ahead.
choices.B: To give information about rules for traffic direction, lane use, speed, and parking.
choices.C: To indicate where services like gas and food are located.
choices.D: To warn that people are working on or near the roadway.

en.explanation: Regulatory signs give you information about rules for traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, parking, and other special situations.

en.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?

choices.A: At all times to prevent traffic backups.
choices.B: Only in ideal driving conditions.
choices.C: Only when driving in the left lane.
choices.D: Whenever you are running late for an emergency.

en.explanation: The maximum limit should be driven only in ideal driving conditions and you must reduce your speed when conditions require it.

en.question: What is a primary function of Variable Speed Limit Signs?

choices.A: To permanently change the speed limit of a highway.
choices.B: To warn drivers of backups ahead and evenly distribute the flow of traffic.
choices.C: To display the current speed of passing vehicles.
choices.D: To indicate the minimum speed required to drive on a highway.

en.explanation: Variable Speed Limit Signs are digital signs that post variable speed limits that help warn drivers of backups ahead in an attempt to evenly distribute the flow of traffic.

en.question: What is the penalty for failing to use chains when required by a Traction Advisory sign?
en.explanation: According to the manual, there is a $500 penalty for failing to use chains when required by Traction Advisory signs.

en.question: What does a triangular No Passing Zone sign look like and where is it placed?

choices.A: It is red and white and placed on the right side of the roadway.
choices.B: It is yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway.
choices.C: It is green and white and placed on the left side of the roadway.
choices.D: It is black and white and placed on the right side of the roadway.

en.explanation: The manual states that a triangular No Passing Zone sign is yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway.

en.question: What is the fine for parking in a disabled parking stall without displaying the required placard or plate?
en.explanation: There is a $250 fine for parking in stalls without displaying the required placard or plate and for blocking the access aisle next to a reserved space.

en.question: What does a dashed white line between lanes of traffic mean?

choices.A: You may cross it to change lanes if it is safe.
choices.B: You should stay in your lane unless a special situation requires it.
choices.C: You are approaching a no-passing zone.
choices.D: You are driving in a reversible lane.

en.explanation: A dashed white line between lanes of traffic means that you may cross it to change lanes if it is safe.

en.question: When there is both a solid and a dashed yellow line between opposing lanes of traffic, when are you permitted to pass?

choices.A: Only if the solid yellow line is on your side.
choices.B: Only if the dashed line is on your side.
choices.C: Whenever there is no oncoming traffic.
choices.D: Passing is never permitted when a solid line is present.

en.explanation: If the dashed line is on your side you are in the passing zone and may pass if it is safe. You may not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side.

en.question: What must a driver do when approaching an intersection with a green bicycle box on a red light?

choices.A: Stop inside the bicycle box.
choices.B: Stop behind the bicycle box even when it is empty.
choices.C: Pull through the bicycle box to check for cross traffic.
choices.D: Yield to bicycles but stop past the box.

en.explanation: Drivers must stop behind the bicycle box (even when it’s empty) and wait for a green light.

en.question: What is the designed speed for driving in a roundabout?
en.explanation: Slow down as you approach the intersection; roundabouts are designed for speeds of 15-20 mph.

en.question: What does a steady yellow "X" over a reversible lane indicate?

choices.A: The lane is only for turning.
choices.B: The lane is open for passing only.
choices.C: The use of the lane is changing and you should move out.
choices.D: You must stop immediately.

en.explanation: A steady yellow “X” means that the use of the lane is changing and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe to do so.

en.question: Which of the following statements about crosswalks is true according to the manual?

choices.A: Crosswalks are only present where marked with white lines.
choices.B: Every intersection is legally defined as a crosswalk regardless of markings.
choices.C: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles in unmarked crosswalks.
choices.D: You only need to yield if the in-pavement lights are flashing.

en.explanation: Not all crosswalks are marked; every intersection is legally defined as a crosswalk regardless of whether a crosswalk marking is present.

en.question: What is the shape and color of a Yield sign?

choices.A: An eight-sided red sign with white letters.
choices.B: A square sign with a white horizontal line inside a red ball.
choices.C: A downward pointing triangle that is red and white.
choices.D: A round yellow sign with black letters.

en.explanation: A Yield sign is a downward pointing triangle. It is red and white with red letters.

en.question: How are reversible lanes usually marked on the roadway?

choices.A: Solid white lines
choices.B: Double-dashed yellow lines
choices.C: Single dashed white lines
choices.D: Solid yellow lines with crosshatchings

en.explanation: Reversible lanes are designed to carry traffic in one direction at certain times and in the opposite direction at other times. These lanes are usually marked by double-dashed yellow lines.

en.question: When driving in a lane controlled by overhead signals, what does a flashing yellow 'X' indicate?

choices.A: The lane is closed to all traffic.
choices.B: The lane is only for turning.
choices.C: The lane use is changing and you should move out.
choices.D: The lane is reserved for high occupancy vehicles.

en.explanation: According to the manual, a flashing yellow 'X' means the lane is only for turning.

en.question: What is the maximum distance you are permitted to travel in a two-way left turn lane?

choices.A: 100 feet
choices.B: 200 feet
choices.C: 300 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that two-way left turn lanes cannot be used for passing and cannot be used for travel further than 300 feet.

en.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a freeway?

choices.A: Stop and back up carefully on the shoulder.
choices.B: Put your vehicle in reverse and back up in the travel lane.
choices.C: Make a U-turn through the center median.
choices.D: Go on to the next exit or where you can safely turn around.

en.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up, but go on to the next turn or exit or where you can safely turn around. It is illegal to back up on a shoulder or a freeway.

en.question: On a road with three or more lanes traveling in the same direction, which lane should you use if there is a lot of entering or exiting traffic?

choices.A: The far left lane
choices.B: The center travel lane
choices.C: The far right lane
choices.D: The shoulder

en.explanation: On a road with three or more lanes traveling in the same direction, if there is a lot of entering or exiting traffic, use the center travel lane.

en.question: If you are pulled over by a law enforcement officer at night, what should you do before the officer approaches your vehicle?

choices.A: Step out of the vehicle to greet the officer.
choices.B: Turn on your vehicle's interior dome light.
choices.C: Reach into your glove box to retrieve your registration.
choices.D: Turn off your headlights and turn on your hazard lights.

en.explanation: If it is dark, turn on the vehicles’ interior dome light after stopping and before the officer approaches your vehicle.

en.question: What is the penalty for recklessly endangering a worker or property in an emergency zone?

choices.A: A 30-day license suspension
choices.B: A 60-day license suspension
choices.C: A 90-day license suspension
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver license

en.explanation: The driver license of a person who recklessly endangers a worker or property in an emergency zone is subject to a 60-day suspension.

en.question: What happens to traffic infraction fines for speeding in an emergency zone?

choices.A: They are waived if it is your first offense.
choices.B: They are reduced by half.
choices.C: They are doubled.
choices.D: They are tripled.

en.explanation: The fines for traffic infractions issued for speeding in an emergency zone or improper passing of a designated stationary vehicle are doubled.

en.question: On limited access roadways with three or more lanes in one direction, which vehicles are generally prohibited from using the left-hand lane?

choices.A: Vehicles carrying more than three passengers
choices.B: Motorcycles and bicycles
choices.C: Vehicles towing a trailer or weighing over 10,000 pounds
choices.D: Hybrid and electric vehicles

en.explanation: On limited access roadways of three or more lanes in one direction, vehicles towing a trailer or vehicles over ten thousand pounds may not use the left-hand lane unless otherwise posted.

en.question: What is the maximum speed limit when driving on permitted ocean beaches in Washington?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: When driving on permitted ocean beaches, the speed limit is 25 mph and pedestrians and bicyclists have the right-of-way at all times.

en.question: Which of the following toll bridges allows drivers to pay cash on site at toll booths?

choices.A: State Route 520 Bridge in both directions
choices.B: State Route 16 Tacoma Narrows Bridge traveling eastbound
choices.C: State Route 520 Bridge traveling westbound only
choices.D: State Route 16 Tacoma Narrows Bridge traveling westbound

en.explanation: SR 16 Tacoma Narrows Bridge has the additional option of toll booths, allowing drivers to pay cash on site when traveling eastbound.

en.question: How are infractions from automated traffic safety cameras processed?

choices.A: As a moving violation that adds points to your driving record
choices.B: As a criminal misdemeanor
choices.C: As a parking infraction not included on your driving record
choices.D: As a felony if the speed exceeded 20 mph over the limit

en.explanation: These infractions are not included in a driving record, and are instead processed as a parking infraction with a maximum fine of $250.

en.question: What should you do if you encounter a ferry holding lane where other vehicles are already lined up?

choices.A: Cut in front of the line if you have a reservation.
choices.B: Drive past the line and merge near the terminal entrance.
choices.C: Find a safe place to turn around and go to the back of the line.
choices.D: Park on the shoulder and walk to the terminal.

en.explanation: If other vehicles have already lined up in the ferry holding lane, do not cut in front of these vehicles—find a safe place to turn around and go to the back of the line.

en.question: When pulled over by a law enforcement officer, when should you show your driver license and vehicle registration?

choices.A: Immediately upon stopping the vehicle
choices.B: Only when requested by the officer
choices.C: After stepping out of the vehicle
choices.D: Before turning off the engine

en.explanation: During a law enforcement stop, you should show your driver license and/or vehicle registration only when requested.

en.question: What is a High Occupancy Toll (HOT) lane?

choices.A: A lane exclusively for emergency vehicles and tow trucks
choices.B: A lane reserved only for buses and motorcycles
choices.C: An HOV lane open to solo drivers who choose to pay a toll
choices.D: A lane where all vehicles must pay a toll in cash

en.explanation: High occupancy toll (HOT) lanes and Express toll lanes are high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes for carpools that are also open to solo drivers who choose to pay a toll.

en.question: When making a right turn, why should you avoid moving wide to the left before going into the turn?

choices.A: It allows pedestrians to cross first.
choices.B: The driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or turning left and try to pass on the right.
choices.C: It is required by law to stay within 12 inches of the curb.
choices.D: It gives you a better view of oncoming traffic.

en.explanation: The manual states: 'On right turns avoid moving wide to the left before going into the turn. If you swing wide, the driver behind you may think you are changing lanes or turning left and may try to pass you on the right.'

en.question: Under what conditions should you NOT make a U-turn?

choices.A: On any multi-lane highway.
choices.B: In a residential neighborhood.
choices.C: On any curve or when approaching the crest of a hill when your vehicle cannot be seen by others.
choices.D: At an intersection with a traffic signal.

en.explanation: According to the manual, U-turns should not be made on any curve or when approaching the crest of a hill when your vehicle cannot be seen by others.

en.question: On what type of roads are Neighborhood Electric Vehicles (NEV) and Medium Electric Vehicles (MEV) generally permitted to operate?

choices.A: Only on roads with a posted speed limit of 25 mph or less.
choices.B: On roads with a posted speed limit of up to 35 mph, unless banned by local law.
choices.C: On any state highway system.
choices.D: On roads with a posted speed limit of up to 50 mph.

en.explanation: Persons operating a NEV or MEV are permitted on roads with a posted speed limit of up to 35 mph, unless banned by local law. Only San Juan County permits operation up to 45 mph.

en.question: What is the minimum penalty for parking a vehicle in an electric vehicle charging station if the vehicle is not connected to the charging equipment?
en.explanation: It is a parking infraction with a minimum penalty of $124 to park a vehicle in an electric vehicle charging station if the vehicle is not connected to the charging equipment.

en.question: Which of the following statements about right-of-way laws is true?

choices.A: The law gives the right-of-way to the larger vehicle.
choices.B: The law says who must yield the right-of-way, but it does not give anyone the right-of-way.
choices.C: Pedestrians always have the right-of-way, even when crossing outside of a crosswalk.
choices.D: Bicyclists must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'The law says who must yield the right-of-way, it does not give anyone the right-of-way.'

en.question: When must a driver stop for a pedestrian or bicyclist crossing the roadway at an intersection?

choices.A: Only when the crosswalk is marked with painted lines.
choices.B: If the pedestrian or bicyclist is in the driver's half of the roadway or within one lane of their half.
choices.C: Only if the pedestrian makes eye contact with the driver.
choices.D: When the pedestrian is waiting on the sidewalk.

en.explanation: Drivers must stop if a pedestrian or bicyclist is in their half of the roadway or if they are within one lane of their half of the roadway.

en.question: What should you do if you encounter a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?

choices.A: Honk your horn lightly to let them know you are there.
choices.B: Yield the right-of-way only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
choices.C: Give them absolute right-of-way and do not use your horn.
choices.D: Drive around them slowly.

en.explanation: Pedestrians using a guide dog or other service animal or carrying a white cane have absolute right-of-way. You should not use your horn as it could confuse or frighten the pedestrian or the service animal.

en.question: At an intersection where there is no stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal, who must a driver yield to?

choices.A: Vehicles coming from the left.
choices.B: Vehicles in the intersection and those coming from the right.
choices.C: Only vehicles turning left.
choices.D: The vehicle that is traveling the fastest.

en.explanation: At an intersection where there is no stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal, drivers must yield to vehicles in the intersection and to those coming from the right.

en.question: What should you do if you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren and flashing lights?

choices.A: Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.
choices.B: Pull over to the right edge of the intersection and stop.
choices.C: Drive through the intersection before you pull over to the right and stop.
choices.D: Speed up to clear the intersection and continue driving.

en.explanation: If you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for the emergency vehicle.

en.question: You are NOT required to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing when the bus is traveling in the opposite direction and the roadway:

choices.A: Has a speed limit of 35 mph or more.
choices.B: Has three or more marked traffic lanes.
choices.C: Is in a residential neighborhood.
choices.D: Has a designated bicycle lane.

en.explanation: You are not required to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing when traveling in the opposite direction if the roadway has three or more marked traffic lanes, is separated by a median, or is separated by a physical barrier.

en.question: What is the penalty for passing a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing?

choices.A: A warning for the first offense.
choices.B: Fines are doubled and the penalty may not be waived, reduced, or suspended.
choices.C: Immediate impoundment of your vehicle.
choices.D: A mandatory 30-day license suspension.

en.explanation: Fines are doubled for anyone that passes a stopped school bus. The penalty for failing to stop for a stopped school bus may not be waived, reduced, or suspended.

en.question: When must you yield to a transit vehicle (bus)?

choices.A: At all times, regardless of the situation.
choices.B: Only when the bus is traveling in a dedicated bus lane.
choices.C: When the bus has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway.
choices.D: Only when the bus is picking up passengers.

en.explanation: You must yield to any transit vehicle (bus) that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway.

en.question: When is it legal to enter an intersection?

choices.A: As soon as the traffic light turns green, even if traffic is backed up.
choices.B: Only when you can get through it without having to stop and block the intersection.
choices.C: When you are turning right on red.
choices.D: If you are following a large truck.

en.explanation: Drivers must not enter an intersection unless they can get through it without having to stop. You should wait until traffic ahead clears so you are not blocking the intersection.

en.question: What happens if you commit an infraction for failing to stop or yield the right-of-way for a pedestrian in a crosswalk marked with school or playground speed zone signs?

choices.A: You receive twice the scheduled penalty.
choices.B: Your license is automatically suspended.
choices.C: You must attend a mandatory defensive driving course.
choices.D: You receive a standard parking ticket.

en.explanation: Infractions for failing to stop or yield the right of way for pedestrian or bicyclist within a crosswalk that is marked with school or playground speed zone signs receive twice the scheduled penalty.

en.question: Which of the following is a requirement for operating a golf cart on public roads in approved golf cart zones?

choices.A: You must be at least 18 years old.
choices.B: You must have a special golf cart endorsement on your license.
choices.C: You must be at least 16 years old and have completed a driver education course or have previous licensed driving experience.
choices.D: You must wear a DOT-approved helmet.

en.explanation: A person may operate a golf cart on public roads in approved golf cart zones if they are at least 16 years old and have either completed a driver education course or have previous experience driving as a licensed driver.

en.question: What must you do when a transit vehicle (bus) has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway?

choices.A: Honk your horn and pass quickly.
choices.B: Yield to the transit vehicle.
choices.C: Maintain your speed and right-of-way.
choices.D: Move to the left lane and accelerate.

en.explanation: The manual states that you must yield to any transit vehicle (bus) that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of using the 'Dutch Reach' method to open your vehicle door?

choices.A: To prevent the door from locking automatically.
choices.B: To force your body to turn so you can better see approaching bicyclists.
choices.C: To stretch your arm muscles after a long drive.
choices.D: To ensure the child safety locks are disengaged.

en.explanation: The 'Dutch Reach' method involves opening the door with your far hand. It forces your body to turn, which will better allow you to see approaching bicyclists and prevents the door from being opened too fast.

en.question: It is against the law to leave children alone in a parked car with the engine running if they are under what age?

choices.A: 10 years of age
choices.B: 12 years of age
choices.C: 14 years of age
choices.D: 16 years of age

en.explanation: The manual states that it is against the law to leave children under 16 years of age alone in a parked car with the engine running.

en.question: You are not allowed to park your vehicle within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

choices.A: 10 feet
choices.B: 15 feet
choices.C: 20 feet
choices.D: 30 feet

en.explanation: The manual lists no parking zones, which includes a restriction against parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

en.question: How far away must you park from a traffic signal, stop sign, or yield sign?

choices.A: At least 15 feet
choices.B: At least 20 feet
choices.C: At least 30 feet
choices.D: At least 50 feet

en.explanation: You cannot park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign, or yield sign.

en.question: What does a white painted curb indicate?

choices.A: Only short stops are permitted.
choices.B: It is a loading zone for commercial vehicles only.
choices.C: Parking is reserved for disabled persons.
choices.D: No stopping or parking at any time.

en.explanation: Other parking restrictions may be indicated by painted curbs; white indicates that only short stops are permitted.

en.question: Which way should you turn your steering wheel when parking facing uphill with a curb?

choices.A: Toward the curb
choices.B: Away from the curb
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: Toward the center of the road

en.explanation: When you park on a hill with a curb and are facing uphill, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. This way, if your vehicle starts to roll, it will roll into the curb.

en.question: When parking facing downhill, which direction should you turn your steering wheel?

choices.A: Toward the curb
choices.B: Away from the curb
choices.C: Straight ahead
choices.D: Parallel to the roadway

en.explanation: When you park on a hill facing downhill, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

en.question: When parallel parking, your vehicle must be within how many inches of the curb?

choices.A: 6 inches
choices.B: 12 inches
choices.C: 18 inches
choices.D: 24 inches

en.explanation: When you parallel park, you must park within 12 inches of the curb.

en.question: What is the recommended hand position on the steering wheel?

choices.A: Left hand at 10 o'clock and right hand at 2 o'clock
choices.B: Left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock and right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock
choices.C: Both hands resting at the bottom of the wheel at 6 o'clock
choices.D: Left hand at 9 o'clock and right hand resting on the gear shift

en.explanation: Place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock and right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock). This allows you to make turns without taking your hands off the wheel and keeps them out of the way of the air bag.

en.question: To drive safely and anticipate situations, how far down the road should you look?

choices.A: At least 5 seconds
choices.B: At least 10 seconds
choices.C: At least 15 seconds
choices.D: At least 20 seconds

en.explanation: The manual advises drivers to look well down the road, at least 15 seconds, and to look to both sides of the road and the rear.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on streets of cities and towns?

choices.A: 20 mph
choices.B: 25 mph
choices.C: 30 mph
choices.D: 35 mph

en.explanation: Speed limits, unless otherwise posted, are 25 mph on streets of cities and towns.

en.question: What is the maximum speed limit on county roads unless otherwise posted?

choices.A: 40 mph
choices.B: 45 mph
choices.C: 50 mph
choices.D: 60 mph

en.explanation: Speed limits, unless otherwise posted, are 50 mph on county roads.

en.question: Speeding is a factor in approximately what percentage of all traffic fatalities in Washington?
en.explanation: According to the manual, speeding is a factor in nearly 40% of all traffic fatalities in Washington.

en.question: What is the minimum fine for violating the distracted driving law in Washington?
en.explanation: The minimum fine for violating one or more of these restrictions is $124 and can be more if you cause a crash.

en.question: What happens to the fine for a second and all subsequent distracted driving violations?

choices.A: It remains the same
choices.B: It is doubled
choices.C: It is tripled
choices.D: The driver's license is suspended

en.explanation: Second and all subsequent violations are subject to have the fine doubled.

en.question: When can a law enforcement officer issue a violation for "Dangerously Distracted Driving"?

choices.A: Only if you cause a collision
choices.B: As a primary offense when they see you eating
choices.C: As a secondary action when stopped for a suspected violation of a separate traffic infraction
choices.D: Only if you are using a cell phone

en.explanation: A law enforcement officer may also include a violation for Dangerously Distracted Driving as secondary action when a driver of a motor vehicle has been stopped for a suspected violation for a separate traffic infraction.

en.question: Under which of the following circumstances is it permissible to use a personal electronic device while driving?

choices.A: To read a text message at a red light
choices.B: To report illegal activity or summon emergency help
choices.C: To check a map on your phone while on the highway
choices.D: To change the music playlist

en.explanation: Activities that may be permissible include reporting illegal activity and summoning medical or other emergency help.

en.question: What are the rules regarding wireless communication devices for drivers with an Instruction Permit or Intermediate License?

choices.A: They can use hands-free devices only
choices.B: They can use hand-held devices if stopped at a light
choices.C: They cannot use any wireless communication device unless in an emergency
choices.D: They can use devices only for GPS navigation

en.explanation: Drivers with an Instruction Permit or Intermediate License cannot use any wireless communication device (regardless if hand-held or hands-free) while driving unless in an emergency situation.

en.question: When is it legal to have a television broadcast visible to the driver while operating a motor vehicle on a public road?

choices.A: When driving under 25 mph
choices.B: When the vehicle is in cruise control
choices.C: Only when it provides live video of the motor vehicle backing up
choices.D: When the broadcast is a news program

en.explanation: No person is allowed to operate a motor vehicle with equipment capable of receiving a television broadcast when the moving images are visible to the driver... An exemption is provided for live video of the motor vehicle backing up.

en.question: What is the Washington state law regarding wearing earphones while driving?

choices.A: You may wear them if the volume is low
choices.B: You may wear them in one ear only
choices.C: It is illegal to drive with head or earphones that cover or go in your ears
choices.D: They are required for hands-free calling

en.explanation: Do not drive with head or earphones that cover or go in your ears. These are illegal in Washington and many other states and make it hard to hear emergency horns or sirens.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the "5 Ds" of distracted driving mentioned in the manual?

choices.A: Dangerous
choices.B: Deceptive
choices.C: Disrespectful
choices.D: Destructive

en.explanation: The "5 Ds" of distracted driving are: Dangerous, Deceptive, Destructive, Disabling, and Deadly.

en.question: According to the NHTSA, more than 80% of all crashes can be avoided if drivers have how much additional time to react?

choices.A: One additional second
choices.B: Two additional seconds
choices.C: Three additional seconds
choices.D: Five additional seconds

en.explanation: According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), more than 80% of all crashes can be avoided if drivers have one additional second of time to react.

en.question: How far ahead does the average driver look while driving?

choices.A: 1-2 seconds
choices.B: 3-5 seconds
choices.C: 10-12 seconds
choices.D: 15 seconds

en.explanation: The average driver looks only 3-5 seconds ahead of the car.

en.question: To gather critical information earlier and respond sooner to hazards, how far ahead should you scan?

choices.A: At least 5 seconds
choices.B: At least 10 seconds
choices.C: At least 15 seconds
choices.D: At least 30 seconds

en.explanation: If you scan at least 15 seconds ahead, you are able to gather critical information earlier and respond sooner to problems and hazards.

en.question: When driving in city traffic, 15 seconds ahead is approximately equal to what distance?

choices.A: One car length
choices.B: One block
choices.C: Four blocks
choices.D: Half a mile

en.explanation: In the city look 15 seconds ahead; 15 seconds is about one block.

en.question: Vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists most often cross or enter your path within what time range?

choices.A: A two-second range
choices.B: A four-second range
choices.C: An eight-second range
choices.D: A ten-second range

en.explanation: As other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists may cross or enter your path anytime, most often within a four second range, look to the sides to make sure no one is coming.

en.question: What percentage of all crashes in the United States each year occur at intersections?

choices.A: Over 10%
choices.B: Over 20%
choices.C: Over 30%
choices.D: Over 40%

en.explanation: According to the manual, over 30% of all the crashes that take place in the United States each year occur at intersections.

en.question: Before you turn left or right across oncoming traffic, how far ahead should you turn on your signal?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 300 feet

en.explanation: The manual states: "Before you turn left or right across oncoming traffic, turn on your signal at least 100 feet ahead and look for a safe gap in the traffic."

en.question: Which of the following is true regarding turning on a red light after stopping?

choices.A: You may never turn left on a red light.
choices.B: You may turn right on red unless prohibited.
choices.C: You may only turn right on red if a sign permits it.
choices.D: You may turn left on red onto any two-way street.

en.explanation: The manual states that after stopping, you may turn right on red unless prohibited. You may also turn left from a one-way or two-way street into a one-way street unless prohibited.

en.question: What should you do if you are stopped at an intersection and your view of the cross street is blocked?

choices.A: Honk your horn and proceed quickly.
choices.B: Wait for another vehicle to pull up next to you.
choices.C: Edge forward slowly until you can see.
choices.D: Turn on your high beams before crossing.

en.explanation: If you were stopped and your view of a cross street is blocked, you should edge forward slowly until you can see. This allows crossing drivers to see the front of your vehicle before you can see them.

en.question: If you are approaching a railroad crossing and are not sure it is safe to cross, you should:

choices.A: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
choices.B: Turn your radio down, put the window down, and listen for a train.
choices.C: Stop on the tracks to get a better view.
choices.D: Rely solely on the crossing lights to warn you.

en.explanation: The manual advises that if you are not sure it is safe to cross the tracks, turn your radio down or off, stop talking, put the window down, and look and listen for a train.

en.question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, why should you wait until a passing train is well down the track before crossing?

choices.A: The train may suddenly reverse direction.
choices.B: The crossing gates take a long time to reset.
choices.C: The passing train may hide another train behind it.
choices.D: It is illegal to cross within one minute of a train passing.

en.explanation: At crossings with more than one track, you must wait until the passing train is well down the track because a train that just passed may hide another train behind it.

en.question: Why is it necessary to look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move when changing lanes?

choices.A: To check your vehicle's blind spots that you cannot see through your mirrors.
choices.B: To ensure your turn signal is functioning properly.
choices.C: To communicate your intentions to pedestrians.
choices.D: To check the speed of the vehicle directly in front of you.

en.explanation: You must look over your shoulder because there are "blind spots" near the rear corners of your vehicle that you cannot see through your mirrors.

en.question: How much space is recommended before attempting to merge in front of a commercial vehicle?

choices.A: One car length for every 5 miles of speed.
choices.B: One car length for every 10 miles of speed.
choices.C: Two car lengths regardless of speed.
choices.D: 100 feet of space at all times.

en.explanation: Before attempting to merge in front of a commercial vehicle, it is recommended that one car length of space for every 10 miles of speed be used.

en.question: What is the recommended technique for looking behind your vehicle while backing up?

choices.A: Depend solely on your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Depend solely on your side mirrors.
choices.C: Place your right arm on the back of the seat and turn around to look directly through the rear window.
choices.D: Open your driver's side door and look backward.

en.explanation: When backing up, you should place your right arm on the back of the seat and turn around so you can look directly through the rear window, rather than depending solely on mirrors.

en.question: By law, when must your vehicle's headlights be turned on?

choices.A: From sunset to sunrise.
choices.B: From a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise.
choices.C: From an hour after sunset until an hour before sunrise.
choices.D: Only when it is completely dark outside.

en.explanation: By law, your vehicle's headlights must be turned on from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, or any time conditions make it difficult to see.

en.question: You must dim your high beams whenever you come within what distance of an oncoming vehicle?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states you must dim your high beams whenever you come within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

en.question: You should use your low beams when you are following another vehicle within:

choices.A: 100 feet or less.
choices.B: 200 feet or less.
choices.C: 300 feet or less.
choices.D: 500 feet or less.

en.explanation: You should use your low beams when following 300 feet or less behind another vehicle.

en.question: Why should you use low beams instead of high beams in fog, snow, or hard rain?

choices.A: High beams will drain the battery faster in cold weather.
choices.B: Light from high beams will reflect back, causing glare and making it difficult to see.
choices.C: Low beams are required by law during all daylight hours.
choices.D: High beams can melt falling snow onto your windshield.

en.explanation: In fog, snow, or hard rain, light from high beams will reflect back, causing glare and making it difficult to see ahead. Low beams should be used instead.

en.question: If a vehicle comes toward you with its high beams on, where should you look to avoid being blinded?

choices.A: Directly at the oncoming headlights.
choices.B: Toward the left side of the road.
choices.C: Toward the right side of the road.
choices.D: Down at your dashboard.

en.explanation: If a vehicle comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car has passed to keep from being blinded.

en.question: When is it especially important to check behind your vehicle when slowing down?

choices.A: When you are driving up a steep hill.
choices.B: When you slow down quickly or at points where a following driver would not expect it.
choices.C: When you are approaching a green traffic light.
choices.D: When you are driving in the right lane of a freeway.

en.explanation: You must check behind your vehicle whenever you slow down, which is very important when you slow down quickly or at points where a following driver would not expect you to slow down, such as driveways or parking spaces.

en.question: What should you do regarding your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

choices.A: Turn them on only if it is getting dark.
choices.B: Use your parking lights instead.
choices.C: Turn them on whenever you turn on your wipers.
choices.D: Flash your high beams continuously.

en.explanation: The manual states that in rainy, snowy, or foggy conditions, headlights make your vehicle easier to see. A good rule to remember is: if you turn on your wipers, turn on your headlights.

en.question: Why should you turn on your headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun?

choices.A: It helps you see the road ahead more clearly.
choices.B: It helps drivers coming toward you see your vehicle.
choices.C: It prevents the sun from glaring in your rearview mirror.
choices.D: It signals to other drivers that you are slowing down.

en.explanation: According to the manual, when driving away from a rising or setting sun, drivers coming toward you may have trouble seeing your vehicle, so turning on your headlights helps them see you.

en.question: In which of the following situations should you avoid using your horn?

choices.A: When a child is about to run into the street.
choices.B: When passing bicyclists or approaching horses.
choices.C: When a driver is not paying attention.
choices.D: When exiting a narrow alley.

en.explanation: The manual lists several occasions when you should not use your horn, which includes around blind pedestrians, passing bicyclists, and when approaching horses.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you need to warn other road users, how far behind your vehicle should you place emergency flares?

choices.A: 50 to 100 feet
choices.B: 100 to 150 feet
choices.C: 200 to 300 feet
choices.D: 400 to 500 feet

en.explanation: If you are having vehicle trouble and have to stop, you should place emergency flares 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle to allow other drivers to change lanes if necessary.

en.question: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway and you do not have flares, how can you signal an emergency?

choices.A: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.
choices.B: Tie a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror, or door handle.
choices.C: Sound your horn in a continuous blast.
choices.D: Turn on your parking lights only.

en.explanation: The manual advises that if you do not have flares, you should lift the hood or tie a white cloth to the antenna, side mirror, or door handle to signal an emergency.

en.question: Why should you never stay beside a large vehicle such as a truck or bus?

choices.A: They travel at much higher speeds than passenger cars.
choices.B: They have large blind spots known as the No-Zone.
choices.C: They frequently make sudden lane changes without signaling.
choices.D: They kick up more gravel and dirt from the road.

en.explanation: You should never stay beside a large vehicle such as a truck or bus because these vehicles have large blind spots, often referred to as the NO-ZONE.

en.question: How far in advance should you signal before you change lanes, turn, merge, or park?

choices.A: At least 50 feet
choices.B: At least 100 feet
choices.C: At least 200 feet
choices.D: At least 300 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that you must signal at least 100 feet before you make your move.

en.question: What should you do if another vehicle is about to enter the street between you and where you plan to turn?

choices.A: Signal early to warn the other driver of your approach.
choices.B: Wait until you have passed the vehicle to signal your turn.
choices.C: Tap your horn and signal immediately.
choices.D: Flash your headlights and brake sharply.

en.explanation: If another vehicle is about to enter the street between you and where you plan to turn, wait until you have passed it to signal. If you signal earlier, the other driver may think you plan to turn where they are and pull into your path.

en.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are going to stop or slow down at a place they might not expect?

choices.A: Turn on your emergency flashers.
choices.B: Use a hand signal for turning left.
choices.C: Tap your brake pedal three or four times quickly.
choices.D: Sound a sharp blast on your horn.

en.explanation: If you are going to stop or slow down at a place where another driver does not expect it, tap your brake pedal three or four times quickly to let those behind you know you are about to slow down.

en.question: How does your stopping distance at 60 mph compare to your stopping distance at 30 mph?

choices.A: It takes twice as far to stop.
choices.B: It takes three times as far to stop.
choices.C: It takes four times as far to stop.
choices.D: The stopping distance is exactly the same.

en.explanation: The faster your vehicle is going, the more distance it will take to stop. For example, at 60 mph it may take you three times as far to stop as it takes to stop at 30 mph.

en.question: What is the safest way to navigate a curve in the road?

choices.A: Maintain your speed and brake gently while in the curve.
choices.B: Accelerate slightly before entering the curve.
choices.C: Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in it.
choices.D: Apply your brakes firmly at the apex of the curve.

en.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve so you do not have to brake in the curve. Braking in a curve can cause the vehicle to skid.

en.question: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on a road with packed snow?

choices.A: Reduce your speed by 10 mph.
choices.B: Cut your speed in half.
choices.C: Slow to a crawl.
choices.D: Maintain the posted speed limit but increase following distance.

en.explanation: According to the manual, on a wet road you should reduce your speed by about 10 mph, but on packed snow, you should cut your speed in half.

en.question: In Washington, during which months are standard studded tires legally permitted on the roads?

choices.A: October 1 through April 30
choices.B: November 1 through March 31
choices.C: December 1 through February 28
choices.D: They are illegal year-round

en.explanation: In Washington, studded tires are legal during winter months and can only be used between November 1 and March 31.

en.question: Why do overpasses and bridges tend to have icy spots even when the rest of the pavement is dry?

choices.A: They are exposed to more wind than regular roads.
choices.B: They do not have earth underneath them to help insulate against the cold.
choices.C: They are usually constructed from smoother concrete.
choices.D: Water drains onto them from surrounding hills.

en.explanation: The pavement on bridges can be icy even when other pavement is not because bridges do not have earth underneath them to help insulate against the cold.

en.question: Why can the pavement be very slippery for the first few minutes when it starts to rain on a hot day?

choices.A: The rain mixes with dust to form a thick mud.
choices.B: Heat causes the oil in the asphalt to come to the surface.
choices.C: The sudden cooling causes the asphalt to contract and become slick.
choices.D: The water creates a hydroplaning effect immediately.
