en.explanation: If it starts to rain on a hot day, pavement can be very slippery for the first few minutes because heat causes the oil in the asphalt to come to the surface. The road is more slippery until the oil washes away.

en.question: Why can bridges be icy even when other pavement is not?

choices.A: They are exposed to more wind.
choices.B: They do not have earth underneath them to help insulate against the cold.
choices.C: They are made of different asphalt materials.
choices.D: They collect more moisture from the air.

en.explanation: According to the manual, bridges can be icy even when other pavement is not because they do not have earth underneath them to help insulate against the cold.

en.question: At what speed can your tires lose all traction with the road during heavy rain (hydroplaning)?

choices.A: About 35 mph
choices.B: About 40 mph
choices.C: About 50 mph
choices.D: About 60 mph

en.explanation: In a heavy rain, your tires can lose all traction with the road at about 50 mph due to hydroplaning.

en.question: What should you do if it feels like your tires have lost traction with the surface of the road?

choices.A: Pump the brakes rapidly to regain traction.
choices.B: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the direction of the skid.
choices.C: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and keep the steering wheel straight.
choices.D: Accelerate slightly to push through the water.

en.explanation: If your tires lose traction, you should ease your foot off the gas pedal, keep the steering wheel straight, and not try to stop or turn until your tires are gripping the road again.

en.question: If you are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a two-lane road where it is unsafe to pass, when must you pull over to let others pass?

choices.A: When three or more vehicles are in a line behind you.
choices.B: When five or more vehicles are in a line behind you.
choices.C: When the vehicle behind you honks its horn.
choices.D: When you are traveling 15 mph below the speed limit.

en.explanation: If you are driving a slow moving vehicle on a two-lane road where it is unsafe to pass, and five or more vehicles are in a line behind you, you must pull over and stop when safe to let them pass.

en.question: What is the proper procedure for entering traffic from a high-speed roadway ramp?

choices.A: Drive to the end of the ramp, stop, and wait for a gap.
choices.B: Signal and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.
choices.C: Enter the roadway at a slower speed than traffic to be safe.
choices.D: Yield to traffic by stopping halfway down the ramp.

en.explanation: When you merge with traffic, signal, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving. High-speed roadways generally have ramps to give you time to build up your speed.

en.question: When leaving traffic via an exit ramp on a high-speed roadway, when should you slow down?

choices.A: About 100 feet before the exit ramp.
choices.B: As soon as you turn your turn signal on.
choices.C: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.
choices.D: Gradually slow down while still in the main traffic lane.

en.explanation: If the road you are traveling has exit ramps, do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

en.question: What is a potential penalty for recklessly endangering workers or other motorists in a work zone?

choices.A: A 30-day license suspension.
choices.B: A 60-day license suspension.
choices.C: A 90-day license suspension.
choices.D: Permanent revocation of your driver's license.

en.explanation: Recklessly endangering workers, other motorists or property in a work zone could lead to a 60-day license suspension.

en.question: How are traffic fines affected if you commit a violation in a work zone?

choices.A: Fines are the same as normal roadways.
choices.B: Fines are increased by $50.
choices.C: Fines are double.
choices.D: Fines are triple.

en.explanation: Traffic fines are double in the work zones.

en.question: If you have good tires and brakes and dry pavement, about how far does it take to react and bring your vehicle to a stop at 50 mph?

choices.A: About 100 feet
choices.B: About 200 feet
choices.C: About 300 feet
choices.D: About 400 feet

en.explanation: At 50 mph, it can take about 400 feet to react to something you see and bring your vehicle to a stop. That is about the length of a city block.

en.question: At night, your headlights will let you see about how far ahead?

choices.A: 200 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 400 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: Your headlights will let you see about 400 feet ahead. You should drive at a speed that allows you to stop within this distance.

en.question: Which rule should you use to tell if you are driving too fast for conditions based on your sight distance?

choices.A: The Two-Second Following Rule
choices.B: The Three-Second Space Rule
choices.C: The Four-Second Sight Distance Rule
choices.D: The Five-Second Reaction Rule

en.explanation: To tell if you are driving too fast for conditions, use the Four-Second Sight Distance Rule. If you reach your chosen stationary object before finishing your count, you are going too fast.

en.question: Can you get a ticket for driving under the posted speed limit?

choices.A: No, as long as you are below the posted limit, you are driving legally.
choices.B: Yes, if you are traveling too fast for conditions like wet or icy roads.
choices.C: Yes, but only if you are driving more than 15 mph below the limit.
choices.D: No, speed limits account for all weather conditions.

en.explanation: Even if you are driving under the posted speed limit, you can get a ticket for traveling too fast under conditions such as wet or icy roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic.

en.question: On roadways with multiple lanes going in the same direction, what does the law require regarding lane usage?

choices.A: You must stay in the center lane unless exiting.
choices.B: You must keep right except to pass.
choices.C: You must keep left except to pass.
choices.D: You may travel in any lane as long as you maintain the speed limit.

en.explanation: On roadways with multiple lanes going in the same direction, the law requires you to keep right except to pass.

en.question: What is the recommended following distance rule when driving at speeds higher than 30 mph?

choices.A: The two-second rule
choices.B: The three-second rule
choices.C: The four-second rule
choices.D: The five-second rule

en.explanation: According to the manual, if you are driving at speeds higher than 30 mph, the best rule to use is the four-second rule to maintain a safe following distance.

en.question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane to move into, what should you do?

choices.A: Brake quickly to discourage the tailgater
choices.B: Speed up to increase the distance between vehicles
choices.C: Wait until the road ahead is clear and reduce your speed slowly
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights and maintain your speed

en.explanation: If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear then reduce speed slowly. This will encourage the tailgater to drive around you. Never slow down quickly to discourage a tailgater.

en.question: How close are you legally allowed to follow a fire truck?

choices.A: No closer than 200 feet
choices.B: No closer than 300 feet
choices.C: No closer than 400 feet
choices.D: No closer than 500 feet

en.explanation: The manual states that police vehicles, ambulances, and fire trucks need additional room to operate, and you must not follow closer than 500 feet to a fire truck.

en.question: Why should you leave extra space when stopped on a hill or incline behind another vehicle?

choices.A: To improve your visibility of the traffic light
choices.B: Because the vehicle ahead may roll back when it starts up
choices.C: To allow room for pedestrians to cross between vehicles
choices.D: Because it reduces the wear on your brakes

en.explanation: You should leave extra space when stopped on a hill or incline because the vehicle ahead may roll back when it starts up.

en.question: When you want to merge with other traffic, how large of a gap do you generally need?

choices.A: About two seconds
choices.B: About three seconds
choices.C: About four seconds
choices.D: About six seconds

en.explanation: Anytime you want to merge with other traffic, you need a gap of about four seconds. This ensures both you and the vehicle behind you have a two-second following distance.

en.question: What should you do if you are overtaking a bicycle and an oncoming vehicle is approaching at the same time?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the bicycle before the vehicle reaches you
choices.B: Honk your horn so the bicycle rider moves off the road
choices.C: Squeeze between the bicycle and the oncoming vehicle
choices.D: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first

en.explanation: When possible, take potential hazards one at a time. If you are overtaking a bicycle and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first so that you can give extra room to the bicycle rider.

en.question: What is the safest way to change multiple lanes?

choices.A: Move across all lanes at once to minimize time spent changing lanes
choices.B: Take them one at a time, like going up or down stairs
choices.C: Slow down drastically before crossing multiple lanes
choices.D: Straddle two lanes until a large gap opens up

en.explanation: If you want to move over several lanes, take them one at a time. Like going up or down stairs one-step at a time, it is safest and easiest to merge one lane at a time.

en.question: What can happen if you enter an intersection on a green light but vehicles are blocking your way, causing you to get caught in the intersection when the light turns red?

choices.A: You have the right-of-way to back up
choices.B: You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection
choices.C: Oncoming traffic must yield to you
choices.D: Your license will be immediately suspended

en.explanation: Even if you have a green light, do not start across an intersection if there are vehicles blocking your way. If caught in the intersection when the light changes to red, you will block traffic and can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

en.question: What should you do if you are being followed closely by another vehicle?

choices.A: Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn the driver
choices.B: Decrease your following distance from the vehicle ahead of you
choices.C: Try to allow extra room in front of your vehicle
choices.D: Move to the far left lane

en.explanation: When being followed closely, you should try to allow extra room in front of you. You will then be able to stop without being hit from behind.

en.question: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a highway with less than four lanes, what must you do if it is safe?

choices.A: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
choices.B: Slow down and pass to the left
choices.C: Pull over to the right shoulder and stop
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert the emergency workers

en.explanation: On highways with less than four lanes, slow down, and pass to the left, if it is safe to do so when approaching a stopped roadside assistance, emergency, or police vehicle using flashing lights.

en.question: Why is it dangerous to drive in the far left lane when you are not passing?

choices.A: It causes excessive wear on the left-side tires
choices.B: It frustrates other drivers and may contribute to aggressive driving
choices.C: It makes it difficult to see road signs on the right
choices.D: It increases your vehicle's fuel consumption

en.explanation: Driving in the far left lane when you’re not passing is dangerous because it frustrates other drivers and may contribute to 'road rage' and aggressive driving behavior.

en.question: Why do you need extra following distance when driving behind a motorcycle on a wet or icy road?

choices.A: Motorcycles take longer to stop than cars
choices.B: The chances of a motorcycle rider falling are greatest on these surfaces
choices.C: Motorcycles spray more water onto your windshield
choices.D: Motorcycles are required to drive slower in bad weather

en.explanation: If the motorcycle or bicycle rider should fall, you need extra distance to avoid the rider. The chances of a fall are greatest on wet or icy roads, gravel roads, or metal surfaces.

en.question: What should you do if you are crossing traffic and there is a median divider?

choices.A: Stop halfway across only if the median divider is large enough for your vehicle
choices.B: Always stop in the median divider, regardless of its size
choices.C: Never stop in a median divider under any circumstances
choices.D: Stop halfway across even if part of your vehicle sticks into traffic

en.explanation: Stopping halfway across is only safe when there is a median divider large enough for your vehicle. Do not stop in a divider where part of your vehicle is sticking into traffic.

en.question: If you want to parallel park and there is traffic behind you, what is the correct procedure?

choices.A: Stop suddenly in the lane and back into the space
choices.B: Put on your turn signal, pull next to the space, and allow following vehicles to pass before parking
choices.C: Pull into the space head-first to avoid holding up traffic
choices.D: Wave the traffic around you while you slowly back up

en.explanation: If you want to parallel park and there is traffic behind you, put on your turn signal, pull next to the space, and allow following vehicles to pass before you park.

en.question: How should you handle steering between two hazards, such as an oncoming tractor-trailer and parked cars?

choices.A: Steer closer to the parked cars to avoid the moving vehicle
choices.B: Steer a middle course, but leave a little more room on the side of the tractor-trailer
choices.C: Steer closer to the tractor-trailer because it has better brakes
choices.D: Stop completely until the tractor-trailer has passed

en.explanation: You should split the difference between two hazards. However, if one is more dangerous than the other, leave a little more space on the dangerous side. For example, if the oncoming vehicle is a tractor-trailer, leave a little more room on the side that the truck will pass.

en.question: What should you do if you have a green light but there are vehicles blocking the intersection ahead?

choices.A: Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
choices.B: Honk your horn until the vehicles move.
choices.C: Do not start across the intersection.
choices.D: Slowly weave through the blocking vehicles.

en.explanation: Even if you have a green light, do not start across an intersection if there are vehicles blocking your way. If caught in the intersection when the light changes to red, you will block traffic and can get a ticket.

en.question: Why should you be particularly cautious when an approaching motorcycle has its turn signal on?

choices.A: Motorcycles are required to keep their signals on at all times.
choices.B: Motorcycle turn signals often do not cancel by themselves.
choices.C: Motorcycles turn much faster than cars.
choices.D: Motorcycle signals are usually harder to see.

en.explanation: You should wait until the other driver actually starts to turn because motorcycle signals often do not cancel by themselves, and the rider may have forgotten to turn it off from a prior turn.

en.question: At a speed of 55 mph, approximately how much distance do you need to safely pass another vehicle on a two-lane roadway?

choices.A: 400 feet
choices.B: 800 feet
choices.C: 1600 feet
choices.D: 3200 feet

en.explanation: At 55 mph, you and an oncoming vehicle will travel over 800 feet in ten seconds. That means you need over 1600 feet or about one-third of a mile to pass safely.

en.question: You should not start to pass a vehicle if you are within what distance of a hill or curve?

choices.A: One-quarter of a mile
choices.B: One-third of a mile
choices.C: One-half of a mile
choices.D: One mile

en.explanation: You have to be able to see at least one-third of a mile or about 15 seconds ahead. Do not start to pass if you are within one-third of a mile of a hill or curve.

en.question: When is it safe to return to the driving lane after passing another vehicle?

choices.A: When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.
choices.B: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
choices.C: As soon as you activate your right turn signal.
choices.D: When the driver of the passed vehicle flashes their headlights.

en.explanation: When you return to the driving lane, be sure to leave enough room. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you just passed in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

en.question: Under what circumstances is a motor vehicle driver permitted to drive in a bicycle lane?

choices.A: When passing a slower vehicle on the right.
choices.B: When traffic is heavily congested.
choices.C: Only when making a turn or crossing it to park near the curb.
choices.D: Drivers are never permitted to drive in a bicycle lane under any circumstances.

en.explanation: Do not drive in a bicycle lane except when making a turn or when you need to cross the bicycle lane to park near the curb.

en.question: How much space must a driver allow when overtaking or passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: At least one foot
choices.B: At least two feet
choices.C: At least three feet
choices.D: At least five feet

en.explanation: Drivers must allow at least three feet of space between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle when overtaking or passing a bicyclist.

en.question: What should you do if you are about to make a right turn and a bicyclist is riding ahead of you?

choices.A: Speed up and pass the bicyclist immediately before the turn.
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn the bicyclist to move out of the way.
choices.C: Slow down and let the bicyclist clear the intersection before making your turn.
choices.D: Share the lane with the bicyclist while making the turn.

en.explanation: If you are about to make a right turn, do not pass a bicyclist immediately before the turn; slow down and let the bicyclist clear the intersection before making your turn rather than cutting in front of the rider.

en.question: What must a bicyclist do when riding on a two-lane road where it is unsafe to pass, and five or more vehicles are in a line behind them?

choices.A: Increase their speed to match the flow of traffic.
choices.B: Move to the center of the lane to prevent unsafe passing.
choices.C: Pull over and stop when it is safe to let vehicles pass.
choices.D: Signal the vehicles to pass them on the right.

en.explanation: When riding on a two-lane road where it is unsafe to pass, and five or more vehicles are in a line behind you, bicyclists must pull over and stop when, in the rider's judgment, it is safe to let vehicles pass.

en.question: When a bicyclist chooses to ride on a sidewalk, what must they do before passing a pedestrian?

choices.A: Move onto the roadway temporarily.
choices.B: Use an audible signal to warn the pedestrian.
choices.C: Flash a front-mounted white light.
choices.D: Dismount and walk the bicycle past the pedestrian.

en.explanation: Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians on sidewalks or in crosswalks. Use an audible signal to warn pedestrians before passing.

en.question: By Washington state definition, an electric-assisted bicycle has a motor capable of propelling the bike at no more than what speed on level ground?

choices.A: 15 mph
choices.B: 20 mph
choices.C: 25 mph
choices.D: 30 mph

en.explanation: Electric-assisted bicycles are defined as bicycles that can be operated with pedals, but also have an electric motor capable of propelling the bike not more than 20 mph on level ground.

en.question: Are bicyclists permitted to ride on the shoulders of freeways and other highways?

choices.A: Yes, except where signs say it is illegal.
choices.B: Yes, but only during daylight hours.
choices.C: No, bicycles are strictly prohibited on all freeways.
choices.D: No, unless they are riding an electric-assisted bicycle.

en.explanation: Bicyclists may use the shoulders of freeways and other highways, except where signs say it is illegal.

en.question: Why should a driver avoid slowing down or stopping quickly immediately after passing a bicyclist?

choices.A: The bicyclist may become caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
choices.B: A motor vehicle's brakes are more powerful than a bicycle's, which could cause a crash.
choices.C: It is illegal to brake within 100 feet of passing a bicycle.
choices.D: The bicyclist is required to pass the vehicle on the right.

en.explanation: Be careful after you have passed a bicyclist. Do not slow down or stop quickly. A motor vehicle's brakes are more powerful than a bicycle's, and if you stop suddenly you could cause a crash.

en.question: When judging whether you have enough room to pass safely, what is the general rule regarding the number of vehicles you should pass?

choices.A: Pass as many vehicles as possible to maintain traffic flow.
choices.B: Pass no more than three vehicles at once.
choices.C: Generally, only pass one vehicle at a time.
choices.D: Pass multiple vehicles only if you are driving a large truck.

en.explanation: Do not count on having enough time to pass several vehicles at once. Be safe. Generally, only pass one vehicle at a time.

en.question: When a bicyclist is operating on a roadway at a speed less than the normal flow of traffic, which of the following is true regarding their lane positioning?

choices.A: They must always ride on the unpaved shoulder.
choices.B: They are legally required to ride on the sidewalk if one is available.
choices.C: Lane positioning is in the rider's judgment, and they may legally use the full lane.
choices.D: They must ride exactly on the solid white line.

en.explanation: Lane positioning for safety is in the rider's judgment, and a bicyclist may legally use the full lane. They must ride as near to the right of the roadway as is safe, but can use the full lane.

en.question: When must a bicyclist pull over and stop to let vehicles pass?

choices.A: When 3 or more vehicles are behind them
choices.B: When 5 or more vehicles are in a line behind them
choices.C: Whenever a single vehicle wants to pass
choices.D: Bicyclists are never required to pull over

en.explanation: According to the manual, if five or more vehicles are in a line behind a bicyclist, they must pull over and stop when it is safe to let vehicles pass.

en.question: What must a bicyclist do before passing a pedestrian on a sidewalk?

choices.A: Flash their headlight
choices.B: Pass on the right side only
choices.C: Use an audible signal to warn the pedestrian
choices.D: Dismount and walk the bicycle past the pedestrian

en.explanation: Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians on sidewalks or in crosswalks and must use an audible signal to warn pedestrians before passing.

en.question: What lighting equipment is required for a bicycle when riding at night?

choices.A: A white headlight visible for 300 feet and a red taillight visible for 300 feet
choices.B: A steady white headlight visible for 500 feet and a red reflector visible for 600 feet to the rear
choices.C: A flashing white headlight and a flashing red taillight
choices.D: Reflective tape on the pedals and a white reflector on the front

en.explanation: When riding at night, a bicycle must have a steady white headlight visible for 500 feet and a red reflector visible for 600 feet to the rear.

en.question: What is the legal requirement for bicycle brakes?

choices.A: They must be able to stop the bicycle within 15 feet at 10 mph
choices.B: They must be equipped with anti-lock braking technology
choices.C: They must make the wheels skid on dry, level, clean pavement
choices.D: They must operate on both the front and rear wheels simultaneously

en.explanation: Every bicycle must be equipped with a brake that makes the wheels skid on dry, level, clean pavement.

en.question: Under what condition may a bicyclist carry packages while riding?

choices.A: Only if the packages are secured in a backpack
choices.B: If the rider can keep at least one hand on the handlebars at all times
choices.C: Only if the packages weigh less than 10 pounds
choices.D: Bicyclists are strictly prohibited from carrying packages

en.explanation: Bicyclists cannot carry packages unless the rider can keep at least one hand on the handlebars at all times.

en.question: What should you do with your bicycle helmet if you have been in a crash?

choices.A: Inspect it for cracks and reuse it if it looks fine
choices.B: Have it recertified by a bike shop
choices.C: Always get a new helmet
choices.D: Wash it with mild soap and water before wearing it again

en.explanation: The manual states that you should always get a new helmet if yours has been in a crash.

en.question: How much space should a bicyclist leave between themselves and parked cars to avoid opened doors?

choices.A: About one foot
choices.B: About two feet
choices.C: About three feet
choices.D: At least five feet

en.explanation: Bicyclists should leave about three feet between themselves and parked cars so that an opened door will not block their path.

en.question: Why should bicyclists avoid passing vehicles on the right side at intersections?

choices.A: It is illegal to ride on the right side of the road
choices.B: Motorists turning right may not look for or see a bicycle passing on the right
choices.C: Bicycles must always pass on the left in all situations
choices.D: The right side of the road usually has more potholes

en.explanation: Bicyclists should not pass on the right side of vehicles at intersections because motorists turning right may not look for, or see, a bicycle passing on the right.

en.question: What should a bicyclist do if a dog continues to chase them after being yelled at?

choices.A: Pedal as fast as possible to outrun the dog
choices.B: Kick at the dog to scare it away
choices.C: Get off the bike and put it between themselves and the dog
choices.D: Swerve into the traffic lane to avoid the dog

en.explanation: If a dog starts to chase you and does not stop when you yell 'NO!', you should get off your bike and put it between you and the dog.

en.question: What is a common cause of serious car and motorcycle crashes?

choices.A: Motorcycles rear-ending cars at stop signs
choices.B: Cars turning left in front of an oncoming motorcyclist
choices.C: Motorcycles passing cars on the right shoulder
choices.D: Cars and motorcycles sideswiping each other on the freeway

en.explanation: Cars turning left in front of an oncoming motorcyclist may cause serious car/motorcycle crashes because drivers may fail to see the rider or judge their speed.

en.question: What should you do if you are waiting to turn and see an approaching motorcycle with its turn signal flashing?

choices.A: Proceed immediately because the motorcycle is definitely turning
choices.B: Honk your horn to remind the motorcyclist to turn off their signal
choices.C: Wait to be sure the motorcycle is actually turning before you proceed
choices.D: Flash your headlights to warn the motorcyclist

en.explanation: Most motorcycles do not have turn signals that turn off automatically. Before turning in front of a motorcycle with a flashing signal, be sure the motorcycle is actually turning and not continuing straight.

en.question: When is it permissible for a car to share the same lane alongside a motorcycle?

choices.A: When the lane is extra wide
choices.B: When the motorcyclist is riding far to the right side of the lane
choices.C: When traffic is moving at less than 15 mph
choices.D: Never; motorcyclists are entitled to the full lane width

en.explanation: Motorcyclists are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles. You should never move into the same lane alongside a motorcyclist, even if the lane is wide.

en.question: What is the recommended following distance you should allow between your vehicle and a motorcycle?

choices.A: Two seconds
choices.B: Three seconds
choices.C: More than four seconds
choices.D: At least six seconds

en.explanation: You should allow more than four seconds following distance between your vehicle and a motorcycle to allow enough time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.

en.question: Under what condition may a motorcyclist pass a bicyclist occupying the same lane?

choices.A: If they pass on the right with at least two feet of clearance
choices.B: If they pass on the left with at least three feet of clear passing distance
choices.C: Only if the bicyclist signals them to pass
choices.D: Motorcyclists are never allowed to pass a bicyclist in the same lane

en.explanation: Motorcyclists may overtake and pass a bicyclist in the same lane provided they pass to the left with at least three feet of clear passing distance.

en.question: Why should drivers use extra caution and avoid following snowplows too closely?

choices.A: Snowplows frequently stop and back up without warning
choices.B: Snowplows drop large amounts of salt that can damage windshields
choices.C: The blades force snow up, potentially causing blizzard-like conditions and reduced visibility
choices.D: Snowplows travel at high speeds and may brake suddenly

en.explanation: You should use extra caution around snowplows because their blades force snow up and off the road, potentially causing blizzard-like conditions and reduced visibility for drivers following too closely.

en.question: How much distance does it take a loaded truck with properly adjusted brakes to come to a complete stop when traveling 55 mph on a dry road?

choices.A: 250 feet
choices.B: 300 feet
choices.C: 450 feet
choices.D: 500 feet

en.explanation: According to the manual, it takes a loaded truck with properly adjusted brakes 450 feet to come to a complete stop when traveling 55 mph on a dry road.

en.question: How can you tell if you are driving in a large vehicle's blind spot directly behind them?

choices.A: You cannot see the vehicle's taillights.
choices.B: You cannot see the driver's mirrors.
choices.C: You are following closer than 200 feet.
choices.D: You cannot see the vehicle's license plate.

en.explanation: The manual states: "If you are following a large vehicle and you cannot see the driver's mirrors, then the driver cannot see you either."

en.question: What should you do if a large vehicle ahead of you is angling into the left lane while signaling a right turn?

choices.A: Quickly pass them on the right side.
choices.B: Honk your horn to warn them they are in the wrong lane.
choices.C: Stay behind them and do not try to squeeze by on the right side.
choices.D: Move into the oncoming traffic lane to pass them on the left.

en.explanation: When turning right, large vehicle drivers may angle into the left lane to make the turn without hitting the curb. The manual warns: "Do not try to squeeze by on the right side when a large vehicle is making a turn."

en.question: What must all vehicles carrying hazardous materials do at railroad crossings?

choices.A: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
choices.B: Stop at all railroad crossings.
choices.C: Sound their horn before crossing.
choices.D: Turn on their hazard lights and proceed without stopping.

en.explanation: The manual explicitly states that "All vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings, so be prepared to stop if you are following one."

en.question: What is the purpose of "escape" or "runaway" ramps on long, steep grades?

choices.A: To provide a safe place for slow vehicles to let others pass.
choices.B: To serve as a rest area for tired drivers.
choices.C: To stop vehicles whose brakes have failed.
choices.D: To allow large trucks to weigh their cargo.

en.explanation: The manual notes that drivers should not park in or near escape or runaway ramps, as "These ramps should only be used to stop vehicles whose brakes have failed."

en.question: Why should you give extra room to pedestrians walking in the same direction as the traffic flow?

choices.A: They are required by law to have the right-of-way.
choices.B: They have their backs to you and cannot see you approaching.
choices.C: They are likely to suddenly cross the street.
choices.D: They are usually distracted by electronic devices.

en.explanation: The manual lists pedestrians walking in the same direction as traffic flow under "Those who cannot see you," explaining that "Since they have their back to you, they cannot see you."

en.question: What should you do if another driver makes a mistake while trying to pass you?

choices.A: Speed up so they can merge behind you.
choices.B: Honk your horn and maintain your speed.
choices.C: Move onto the shoulder of the road.
choices.D: Slow down and let them return to the drive lane safely.

en.explanation: Under the 'Drivers in trouble' section, the manual advises: "If another driver makes a mistake in passing you, do not make it worse. Slow down and let them return to the drive lane safely."

en.question: Approximately what percentage of all fatal collisions involve a vehicle that left the roadway?
en.explanation: The manual states that "Nearly 44% of all fatal collisions involve a vehicle that left the roadway."

en.question: Which of the following factors is involved in more than half of all run-off-the-road fatalities?

choices.A: Speeding
choices.B: Vehicle equipment failure
choices.C: Poor weather conditions
choices.D: Animal crossings

en.explanation: According to the text, "Speeding was involved in more than half of run-off-the-road fatalities and in just under half of serious injuries reported."

en.question: How many vehicles are typically involved in fatal and serious injury run-off-the-road collisions?

choices.A: Over 90% involve only one vehicle.
choices.B: Most involve two vehicles colliding head-on.
choices.C: About 50% involve a vehicle and a bicyclist.
choices.D: They almost always involve a large commercial truck.

en.explanation: The manual notes that "Over 90% of fatal and serious injury run-off-the-road collisions involve only one vehicle."

en.question: What period of driving is considered the most critical for any novice driver due to a higher likelihood of crashing?

choices.A: The first month
choices.B: The first six months
choices.C: The first year
choices.D: The first two years

en.explanation: The manual states: "The first six months of driving for any novice driver, regardless of age, are the most critical because the new driver is more likely to be involved in a crash due to lack of experience."

en.question: Why is flexibility of the neck and torso important for safe driving?

choices.A: It helps you sit comfortably on long trips.
choices.B: It allows you to use your best possible vision to check for hazards before turning or backing.
choices.C: It is required to pass the physical portion of the driving test.
choices.D: It helps you reach the pedals and steering wheel more easily.

en.explanation: The manual explains that physical abilities, including flexibility of the neck and torso, are important "when using best possible vision for safety hazards before turning, backing, changing lanes, or merging."

en.question: What could happen if your driver license requires corrective lenses and you are stopped by law enforcement while driving without them?

choices.A: You will be given a warning.
choices.B: Your vehicle will be impounded immediately.
choices.C: You could get a ticket.
choices.D: You will be required to retake the vision test on the spot.

en.explanation: The manual warns: "If your driver license says you must wear corrective lenses and you get stopped without them, you could get a ticket."

en.question: Because you cannot focus clearly on things in your side vision, what must you do to spot vehicles and potential trouble?

choices.A: Turn your head completely around every few seconds.
choices.B: Rely entirely on your peripheral vision.
choices.C: Use your side mirrors and glance to the side if necessary.
choices.D: Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead at all times.

en.explanation: The manual states regarding side vision: "Because you cannot focus on things to the side, you must also use your side mirrors and glance to the side if necessary."

en.question: Why should you allow extra room for drivers or bicyclists who are slowing down for no apparent reason?

choices.A: They are likely preparing to make an illegal U-turn.
choices.B: They may be able to see a hazard that you cannot see from your lane position.
choices.C: They are trying to force you to pass them.
choices.D: They are testing their brakes.

en.explanation: When discussing people who may be confused, the manual advises watching for those slowing for no apparent reason, noting: "Remember that they may be able to see something you can’t see from your lane position."

en.question: Why should you avoid using dark glasses or tinted contact lenses at night?

choices.A: They can cause temporary color blindness.
choices.B: They reflect too much light into the eyes of oncoming drivers.
choices.C: They will cut down the light that you need to see clearly.
choices.D: They are illegal to wear while driving in all states.

en.explanation: The manual advises to avoid using dark glasses or tinted contact lenses at night because they will cut down the light that you need to see clearly.

en.question: According to studies, how do the driving records of hearing-impaired drivers compare to drivers with good hearing?

choices.A: They have significantly more collisions.
choices.B: They are just as good as drivers with good hearing.
choices.C: They have fewer minor accidents but more major ones.
choices.D: They are slightly worse due to the inability to hear sirens.

en.explanation: Studies have shown that the driving records of hearing impaired drivers are just as good as those drivers with good hearing because they learn to rely more on their vision and stay alert.

en.question: To help prevent getting tired on a long trip, how often should you take a break?

choices.A: Every hour or so.
choices.B: Every three hours.
choices.C: Only when you need to refuel.
choices.D: Every 200 miles.

en.explanation: The manual recommends taking breaks by stopping every hour or so, or when you need to, to walk around and get fresh air.

en.question: How does eating a large meal before a trip affect your driving?

choices.A: It provides necessary energy for long-distance driving.
choices.B: It improves your reaction time.
choices.C: It can make you sleepy.
choices.D: It helps you stay alert during night driving.

en.explanation: The manual advises to eat lightly and not eat a large meal before you leave, because some people get sleepy after they eat a big meal.

en.question: Alcohol is involved in approximately what percentage of traffic collisions in which someone is killed?
en.explanation: According to the manual, alcohol is involved in about 40% of the traffic collisions in which someone is killed.

en.question: How does alcohol affect the central nervous system?

choices.A: It acts as a stimulant to speed up brain activity.
choices.B: It acts as a depressant to slow the activity of the brain and spinal cord.
choices.C: It has no effect on the central nervous system until it is digested.
choices.D: It improves coordination and reaction time temporarily.

en.explanation: Alcohol is a drug that depresses the central nervous system, slowing the activity of the brain and the spinal cord.

en.question: How long does it usually take for alcohol to be absorbed directly into the bloodstream through the stomach and small intestine?

choices.A: 5 to 10 minutes
choices.B: 20 to 40 minutes
choices.C: 1 to 2 hours
choices.D: 3 to 4 hours

en.explanation: Once swallowed, alcohol is absorbed directly into the blood stream through the walls of the stomach and small intestine, usually within 20 - 40 minutes.

en.question: Which of the following is considered a typical alcoholic drink containing an equal amount of alcohol?

choices.A: 12 oz. of 80-proof liquor
choices.B: 5 oz. of beer
choices.C: 1 1/2 oz. of 80-proof liquor
choices.D: 12 oz. of wine

en.explanation: A typical alcoholic drink is 1 1/2 oz. of 80-proof liquor (one shot glass), 12 oz. of beer, or a 5 oz. glass of wine.

en.question: How does the human body dispose of most of the alcohol consumed?

choices.A: Through sweat and breath
choices.B: Through oxidation in the liver
choices.C: Through the digestive tract
choices.D: Through the kidneys and urine

en.explanation: While very small quantities are eliminated through sweat, breath, and urine, the body disposes of most alcohol through oxidation (burning) in the liver.

en.question: Approximately how long does it take for your body to get rid of each typical alcoholic drink?

choices.A: 30 minutes
choices.B: One hour
choices.C: Two hours
choices.D: Four hours

en.explanation: The oxidation of alcohol takes place at a constant rate, and it takes about one hour for your body to get rid of each drink.

en.question: Why can consuming marijuana-infused foods be particularly dangerous for drivers?

choices.A: They contain a higher percentage of alcohol than typical drinks.
choices.B: They cause immediate and severe hallucinations.
choices.C: It takes longer to feel the effects, making it easier to consume too much.
choices.D: They permanently damage the central nervous system.

en.explanation: Consuming marijuana-infused foods can be dangerous because it takes longer to feel the effects, making it easier to have too much because the effects are delayed.

en.question: According to the manual, marijuana has been shown to impair performance on driving tasks for up to how long?

choices.A: 1 hour
choices.B: 3 hours
choices.C: 5 hours
choices.D: 12 hours

en.explanation: Marijuana has been shown to impair performance on driving tasks and on driving courses for up to 5 hours.

en.question: What is a potential danger of taking "uppers" or energy drinks to stay awake while driving?

choices.A: They permanently improve your reaction time.
choices.B: They can later cause you to be nervous, dizzy, and unable to concentrate.
choices.C: They slow down the absorption of alcohol in the bloodstream.
choices.D: They act as a depressant on the central nervous system.

en.explanation: Pep pills, "uppers", and energy drinks can make a driver feel more alert for a short time, but later they can cause a person to be nervous, dizzy, unable to concentrate, and can affect vision.

en.question: What are the penalties for driving under the influence of prescription or over-the-counter drugs?

choices.A: A simple warning for the first offense.
choices.B: A mandatory driver improvement class.
choices.C: The penalties are the same as for any alcohol violation.
choices.D: A minor traffic infraction fine.

en.explanation: The manual states that if you are arrested or convicted of driving under the influence of drugs, the penalties are the same as for any alcohol violation.

en.question: What happens when you mix drugs and alcohol before driving?

choices.A: The effects of the drugs and alcohol cancel each other out.
choices.B: It causes a compounded effect where the effects of the drug multiply.
choices.C: It has the exact same effect as drinking alcohol alone.
choices.D: It only impairs your driving if you take illegal drugs.

en.explanation: According to the manual, mixing drugs and alcohol can cause a compounded effect, which means that the effects of the drug multiply to become more than 1+1.

en.question: If you are 21 or older, you can be arrested for driving with a Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) of what amount or higher?
en.explanation: The manual states that you can be arrested for driving with a BAC of .08 or more if you are 21 or older.

en.question: If you are under 21, you can be arrested for a THC/marijuana level of more than:

choices.A: 0.00 nanograms per milliliter of blood
choices.B: 2.00 nanograms per milliliter of blood
choices.C: 5.00 nanograms per milliliter of blood
choices.D: 8.00 nanograms per milliliter of blood

en.explanation: If you are under 21, you can be arrested for a THC/marijuana level of more than 0.00 nanograms per milliliter of blood.

en.question: What must an arresting officer do if a parent is arrested for a drug- or alcohol-related driving offense while a child under age 13 is present in the car?

choices.A: Impound the vehicle permanently.
choices.B: Promptly notify child protective services.
choices.C: Issue an additional $5,000 fine on the spot.
choices.D: Revoke the driver's license for an additional 10 years.

en.explanation: When a child under age 13 is present in the car of a parent/legal custodian/guardian being arrested for a drug- or alcohol-related driving offense, the arresting law enforcement officer must promptly notify child protective services.

en.question: What should you do if you are angry or excited before driving?

choices.B: Drive to a secluded area to lose them.

en.question: What is the first thing you should do if your brakes suddenly stop working?

choices.D: Pull the parking brake up as fast and hard as possible.

choices.D: The vehicle will automatically shift into neutral.

en.question: What is the correct sequence of actions if your gas pedal sticks and the motor keeps going faster?

choices.A: Turn off the engine, shift to neutral, pull off the road.
choices.B: Shift to neutral, pull off the road, turn off the engine.

choices.D: Shift to a lower gear, pump the brakes, turn off the engine.

choices.D: Accelerate, brake, or brace for impact.

en.question: How should you brake in an emergency if your vehicle is equipped with an antilock braking system (ABS)?

choices.D: Driving with a heavy load in the trunk.

en.question: What should you do if a collision is imminent to minimize the impact?

choices.C: Accelerate to pass the vehicle before it hits you.

choices.C: Conductores menores de 18 años de edad
choices.D: Conductores de vehículos eléctricos

es.explanation: Según el manual, los conductores de vehículos gubernamentales, ciclomotores (mopeds) y vehículos de transporte público o por contrato están exentos del requisito de seguro de responsabilidad civil.

es.question: ¿A partir de qué fecha las licencias de conducir estándar ya no serán aceptadas para abordar vuelos nacionales?

choices.A: 7 de mayo de 2024
choices.B: 7 de mayo de 2025
choices.C: 1 de enero de 2025
choices.D: 1 de octubre de 2026

es.explanation: Para el 7 de mayo de 2025, las licencias de conducir estándar ya no serán una forma aceptable de identificación para abordar vuelos nacionales e ingresar a algunas instalaciones federales seguras.

es.question: ¿Cuál es el requisito de sujeción infantil para bebés y niños menores de dos años?

choices.A: Deben usar un sistema de sujeción de seguridad infantil orientado hacia adelante.
choices.B: Deben usar un asiento elevado (booster seat).
choices.C: Deben usar un sistema de sujeción de seguridad infantil orientado hacia atrás.
choices.D: Pueden usar un cinturón de seguridad estándar si son lo suficientemente altos.

es.explanation: El manual establece que los bebés y niños menores de dos años deben usar un sistema de sujeción de seguridad infantil en la posición orientada hacia atrás.

es.question: ¿A qué estatura puede un niño normalmente dejar de usar un asiento elevado (booster seat) y usar un cinturón de seguridad estándar de regazo y hombro del vehículo?
es.explanation: Los niños de cuatro años o más deben usar un asiento elevado hasta que midan 4'9" de estatura y puedan ajustarse correctamente el cinturón de seguridad de regazo y hombro del vehículo.

es.question: ¿Qué vehículos están exento del requisito de usar un asiento elevado (booster seat) para niños?

choices.A: Vehículos equipados únicamente con cinturones de seguridad de regazo
choices.B: Vehículos fabricados antes de 2005
choices.C: Vehículos con bolsas de aire laterales
choices.D: Vehículos de transporte público o por contrato

es.explanation: El manual especifica que los vehículos equipados únicamente con cinturones de seguridad de regazo están exentos del requisito de usar un asiento elevado.

es.question: ¿Qué puede suceder con las multas de tráfico en una zona de obras señalizada?

choices.A: Se exoneran para quienes cometen la infracción por primera vez.
choices.B: Pueden duplicarse.
choices.C: Se reducen a la mitad.
choices.D: Resultan en una suspensión automática de la licencia.

es.explanation: Los automovilistas deben obedecer todas las indicaciones y reducir la velocidad en cualquier zona de obras señalizada, y las multas de tráfico pueden duplicarse en un área de zona de obras.

es.question: Bajo la ley de Moverse a otro carril/Reducir la velocidad (Move Over/Slow Down), si no puede cambiarse a otro carril al pasar un vehículo de emergencia con luces intermitentes, ¿qué debe hacer?

choices.A: Detenerse por completo hasta que el vehículo se retire.
choices.B: Mantener su velocidad pero tocar la bocina.
choices.C: Reducir su velocidad a 10 mph por debajo del límite de velocidad indicado.
choices.D: Reducir su velocidad a 20 mph por debajo del límite de velocidad indicado.

es.explanation: Al pasar vehículos de respuesta a emergencias con luces intermitentes, debe cambiarse a otro carril si es posible, y si no, reducir su velocidad a 10 mph por debajo del límite de velocidad indicado.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes se considera un vehículo de respuesta a emergencias bajo la ley de Moverse a otro carril/Reducir la velocidad (Move Over/Slow Down)?

choices.A: Autobuses escolares
choices.B: Camiones de residuos sólidos y grúas
choices.C: Camionetas de reparto
choices.D: Autobuses de transporte público

es.explanation: Los vehículos de respuesta a emergencias incluyen los de las fuerzas del orden, bomberos/ambulancias, respuesta a incidentes, mantenimiento de carreteras, servicios públicos, residuos sólidos y grúas.

es.question: Además de las señales y semáforos, ¿quién de los siguientes puede proporcionar control de tráfico?

choices.A: Peatones en un cruce peatonal
choices.B: Guardias de cruce escolar
choices.C: Cualquier conductor con licencia
choices.D: Voluntarios de vigilancia vecinal

es.explanation: El control de tráfico también puede ser proporcionado por las fuerzas del orden, personal de construcción o mantenimiento de carreteras, o guardias de cruce escolar.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes NO es una forma de pago aceptable para los servicios en línea en el Departamento de Licencias (DOL)?

choices.A: Tarjeta de débito Visa
choices.B: Tarjeta de crédito MasterCard
choices.C: American Express
choices.D: Tarjetas de regalo

es.explanation: Las formas de pago aceptables para los servicios en línea incluyen tarjetas de débito o crédito Visa, MasterCard o American Express (no se aceptan tarjetas de regalo).

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes elementos se incluye en el resumen de su historial de conducción?

choices.A: Multas de estacionamiento
choices.B: Historial crediticio
choices.C: Avisos de falta de comparecencia (Failure-to-Appear)
choices.D: Registros de mantenimiento del vehículo

es.explanation: El estado mantiene un registro de las solicitudes de licencia, infracciones de tránsito, condenas por violaciones de vehículos motorizados, participación en colisiones y avisos de falta de comparecencia (Failure-to-Appear).

es.question: ¿Qué tipo de identificación de Washington cumple con la ley REAL ID y es válida para viajes aéreos dentro de los Estados Unidos?

choices.A: Licencia de conducir estándar
choices.B: Licencia de conducir mejorada (EDL)
choices.C: Permiso de conducir temporal
choices.D: Tarjeta de registro de votante

es.explanation: Las licencias de conducir mejoradas (EDL) de Washington cumplen con la ley REAL ID y son válidas para viajes aéreos dentro de los Estados Unidos.

es.question: ¿Cómo debe colocarse el cinturón de seguridad en un niño que ya es demasiado grande para un asiento elevado (booster seat)?

choices.A: A través del área del estómago y el cuello
choices.B: Debajo del brazo o detrás de la espalda
choices.C: Sobre los huesos de la cadera y ajustado a través del hombro y el pecho
choices.D: Suelto a través de la cintura para permitir el movimiento

es.explanation: El cinturón de seguridad debe quedar sobre los huesos de la cadera y estar ajustado a través del hombro y el pecho para sujetar al niño de forma segura en un choque. No debe apoyarse en el área del estómago ni en el cuello.

es.question: ¿De qué colores pueden ser las señales de advertencia de Cruce Escolar y Cruce de Peatones?

choices.A: Rojo o naranja
choices.B: Verde fluorescente o amarillo
choices.C: Blanco o negro
choices.D: Azul o verde

es.explanation: Según la sección de Señales de Advertencia, el color de las señales de Cruce Escolar y Cruce de Peatones puede ser verde fluorescente o amarillo.

es.question: Si tiene 15 años o más y va a obtener su primera licencia de conducir de Washington, ¿qué servicio en línea puede ahorrarle tiempo antes de visitar una oficina?

choices.A: Examen de conducir en línea
choices.B: Servicio de presolicitud
choices.C: Examen de la vista virtual
choices.D: Toma de huellas dactilares en línea

es.explanation: Si tiene 15 años o más, o es nuevo en el estado, use nuestro servicio de presolicitud en línea. Esto le ahorrará tiempo cuando visite nuestra oficina.

es.question: Según el texto proporcionado, ¿cuál de las siguientes tareas de registro de vehículos se puede completar en línea?

choices.A: Solicitar un diseño de placa (matrícula) personalizada
choices.B: Renovar las calcomanías (tabs) de su vehículo
choices.C: Impugnar una multa de estacionamiento
choices.D: Programar un examen de conducir

es.explanation: El manual enumera 'Renovar las calcomanías (tabs) de su vehículo' en los servicios de Registro de Vehículos en línea.

es.question: Si necesita estimar su impuesto especial de la Autoridad Regional de Tránsito (RTA), ¿cómo indica el manual que puede hacerlo?

choices.A: En una estación de policía local
choices.B: A través de los servicios de registro de vehículos en línea
choices.C: Llamando al Departamento de Licencias
choices.D: En una estación de inspección de vehículos

es.explanation: El texto enumera 'Estimar su impuesto especial de la Autoridad Regional de Tránsito (RTA)' como uno de los servicios de Registro de Vehículos en línea disponibles.

es.question: Según los servicios en línea del manual, un cambio de dirección de 'Flota' se aplica a un mínimo de ¿cuántos vehículos?

choices.A: 2 o más
choices.B: 3 o más
choices.C: 5 o más
choices.D: 10 o más

es.explanation: La sección de servicios en línea especifica 'Cambio de dirección: Flotas (5 o más vehículos)'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes solicitudes de audiencia se puede enviar en línea según el manual?

choices.A: Audiencia por multa de exceso de velocidad
choices.B: Solicitud de audiencia por DUI
choices.C: Audiencia por infracción de estacionamiento
choices.D: Audiencia por cámara de luz roja

es.explanation: El texto enumera explícitamente 'Enviar su solicitud de audiencia por DUI' en los servicios de registros en línea.

es.question: En la sección 'Antes de conducir', ¿cuál de los siguientes se enumera como un paso necesario?

choices.A: Comprobar las emisiones de escape del vehículo
choices.B: Asegurar su carga
choices.C: Mejorar sus faros delanteros
choices.D: Rotar sus neumáticos

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Asegurar su carga' como un tema bajo el capítulo 'Antes de conducir'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes temas se trata en la sección 'Reglas de la carretera'?

choices.A: Reventón de neumático
choices.B: Carriles HOT y carriles de peaje exprés
choices.C: Falla de frenos
choices.D: Certificado de propiedad

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Carriles HOT y carriles de peaje exprés' en el capítulo 'Reglas de la carretera'.

es.question: Según el índice, ¿dónde buscaría información sobre 'Vehículos eléctricos de batería de baja velocidad'?

choices.A: La licencia de conducir
choices.B: Reglas de la carretera
choices.C: En condiciones para conducir
choices.D: Licenciamiento de vehículos

es.explanation: La información sobre 'Vehículos eléctricos de batería de baja velocidad' se encuentra en la sección 'Reglas de la carretera' del manual.

es.question: ¿En qué sección del manual se encuentran los temas de 'Conducción distraída' y 'Dispositivos electrónicos personales'?

choices.A: Consejos para una conducción segura
choices.B: Emergencias
choices.C: Licenciamiento de vehículos
choices.D: Antes de conducir

es.explanation: El índice ubica 'Conducción distraída' y 'Dispositivos electrónicos personales' en el capítulo 'Consejos para una conducción segura'.

es.question: Si experimenta una situación en la que el 'pedal del acelerador se queda pegado', ¿qué sección del manual ofrece orientación?

choices.A: Reglas de la carretera
choices.B: Consejos para una conducción segura
choices.C: Emergencias
choices.D: En condiciones para conducir

es.explanation: El tema 'El pedal del acelerador se queda pegado' aparece en el capítulo 'Emergencias' del índice.

es.question: Según la sección 'En condiciones para conducir', ¿cuál de los siguientes temas se aborda específicamente junto con el consumo de alcohol y la conducción?

choices.A: Comer mientras se conduce
choices.B: Marihuana y otras drogas
choices.C: Escuchar música a alto volumen
choices.D: Hablar con los pasajeros

es.explanation: El capítulo 'En condiciones para conducir' enumera específicamente 'Marihuana' y 'Otras drogas' inmediatamente después de los temas de 'Consumo de alcohol y conducción'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes aparece como un tema específico bajo 'Licenciamiento de vehículos'?

choices.A: Informe de venta
choices.B: Ajuste de asiento y espejos
choices.C: Carriles reversibles
choices.D: Cómo evitar colisiones

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Informe de venta' en el capítulo 'Licenciamiento de vehículos'.

es.question: En la sección 'Consejos para una conducción segura', ¿las responsabilidades de qué grupos específicos se destacan junto con el hecho de compartir la carretera?

choices.A: Responsabilidades de los peatones
choices.B: Responsabilidades de ciclistas y motociclistas
choices.C: Responsabilidades de los conductores de camiones comerciales
choices.D: Responsabilidades de las fuerzas del orden

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Responsabilidades de los ciclistas' y 'Responsabilidades de los motociclistas' en el capítulo 'Consejos para una conducción segura'.

es.question: ¿En qué capítulo principal incluye el manual una sección específica sobre el 'Registro de delincuentes sexuales/delincuentes por secuestro'?

choices.A: Reglas de la carretera
choices.B: La licencia de conducir
choices.C: En condiciones para conducir
choices.D: Emergencias

es.explanation: El índice ubica el 'Registro de delincuentes sexuales/delincuentes por secuestro' en el capítulo 'La licencia de conducir'.

es.question: Según el índice, ¿cuál de los siguientes se considera parte del capítulo 'Emergencias'?

choices.A: Ajustarse al tráfico
choices.B: Cómo lidiar con derrapes
choices.C: Mantenerse a la derecha excepto para rebasar
choices.D: Exploración visual (Scanning)

es.explanation: El tema 'Cómo lidiar con derrapes' aparece en el capítulo 'Emergencias'.

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes documentos se analiza específicamente en la sección 'Licenciamiento de vehículos'?

choices.A: Prueba de identidad
choices.B: Certificado de propiedad (Título)
choices.C: Real ID
choices.D: Licencia probatoria

es.explanation: El índice enumera 'Certificado de propiedad (Título)' en el capítulo 'Licenciamiento de vehículos'.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tienen los nuevos residentes para obtener una licencia de conducir del estado de Washington después de convertirse en residentes?

choices.A: 10 días
choices.B: 30 días
choices.C: 60 días
choices.D: 90 días

es.explanation: Según el manual, los nuevos residentes deben obtener una licencia de conducir del estado de Washington dentro de los 30 días posteriores a la fecha en que se conviertan en residentes.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes acciones lo convierte en residente del estado de Washington para fines de obtención de la licencia?

choices.A: Visitar el estado para unas vacaciones de tres meses
choices.B: Registrarse para votar en el estado
choices.C: Alquilar una habitación de hotel por dos semanas
choices.D: Conducir a través del estado en un viaje por todo el país

es.explanation: El manual establece que usted es residente si se registra para votar en este estado, entre otros criterios como pagar la matrícula estatal (in-state tuition) o recibir beneficios estatales.

es.question: ¿Qué edad debe tener un no residente o un visitante a corto plazo para operar un vehículo motorizado en Washington con una licencia válida de otro estado?

choices.A: Al menos 15 años de edad
choices.B: Al menos 15 años y medio de edad
choices.C: Al menos 16 años de edad
choices.D: Al menos 18 años de edad

es.explanation: Si usted es un no residente o un visitante a corto plazo, puede operar un vehículo motorizado en este estado si tiene una licencia de conducir válida de su estado de origen y tiene al menos 16 años de edad.

es.question: Después del 3 de mayo de 2023, ¿para qué sigue siendo válida una licencia de conducir estándar de Washington?

choices.A: Abordar vuelos nacionales
choices.B: Ingresar a bases militares seguras
choices.C: Ingresar a plantas de energía nuclear
choices.D: Conducir a través de las fronteras estatales o viajar en tren

es.explanation: Aunque una licencia estándar ya no será aceptable para abordar vuelos nacionales o ingresar a instalaciones federales seguras, seguirá funcionando para viajes dentro de los EE. UU., como conducir en Washington, cruzar fronteras estatales o viajar en tren.

es.question: ¿Quién debe supervisar a un conductor que opera un vehículo con un Permiso de instrucción (Instruction Permit)?

choices.A: Cualquier conductor con licencia mayor de 18 años
choices.B: Un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos cinco años de experiencia en la conducción con licencia
choices.C: Un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos 25 años de edad
choices.D: Solo un padre o tutor legal

es.explanation: Un Permiso de instrucción le permite operar un vehículo motorizado mientras es supervisado por un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos cinco años de experiencia en la conducción con licencia.

es.question: ¿Dónde debe sentarse el conductor supervisor cuando acompaña a un conductor con un Permiso de instrucción?

choices.A: En el asiento trasero directamente detrás del conductor
choices.B: En cualquier lugar del vehículo
choices.C: En el asiento del pasajero delantero derecho
choices.D: En el asiento trasero del lado del pasajero

es.explanation: El manual especifica que el conductor con licencia que supervisa al titular de un Permiso de instrucción debe sentarse en el asiento del pasajero delantero derecho.

es.question: ¿A qué edad se le puede otorgar a un conductor una licencia de conducir intermedia en Washington?

choices.A: 15 o 16 años de edad
choices.B: 16 o 17 años de edad
choices.C: 18 o 19 años de edad
choices.D: 21 años de edad

es.explanation: Si tiene 16 o 17 años y cumple con los requisitos, Washington le otorgará una licencia intermedia con restricciones.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo es válida una licencia de conducir estándar de Washington?

choices.A: Hasta 4 años a partir de la fecha de su último cumpleaños
choices.B: Hasta 5 años a partir de la fecha de su último cumpleaños
choices.C: Hasta 6 años a partir de la fecha de su último cumpleaños
choices.D: Hasta 8 años a partir de la fecha de su último cumpleaños

es.explanation: Una licencia de conducir estándar es válida por hasta seis años a partir de la fecha de su último cumpleaños.

es.question: ¿Qué privilegio de viaje ofrece una Licencia de conducir mejorada (EDL) que una licencia estándar no ofrece?

choices.A: Le permite abordar vuelos internacionales a Europa.
choices.B: Le permite cruzar las fronteras de Canadá y México por tierra o mar.
choices.C: Le permite conducir en países extranjeros sin un permiso internacional.
choices.D: Le permite evitar la aduana al regresar a los Estados Unidos.

es.explanation: La licencia de conducir mejorada (EDL) de Washington cumple con la ley REAL ID, es válida para viajes aéreos dentro de los EE. UU. y puede usarse para cruzar las fronteras de Canadá y México por tierra o mar.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para obtener un permiso de instrucción si NO está inscrito en un curso de capacitación para conductores aprobado?

choices.A: 15 años de edad
choices.B: 15 años y medio de edad
choices.C: 16 años de edad
choices.D: 18 años de edad

es.explanation: Para que se le otorgue un permiso de instrucción, debe tener al menos 15 años y medio, o 15 años si está inscrito en un curso de capacitación para conductores aprobado.

es.question: ¿Cuántas horas de experiencia de conducción debe certificar un padre o tutor que usted ha completado antes de que pueda obtener una licencia intermedia?

choices.A: 30 horas, incluyendo 5 horas por la noche
choices.B: 40 horas, incluyendo 10 horas por la noche
choices.C: 50 horas, incluyendo 10 horas por la noche
choices.D: 60 horas, incluyendo 15 horas por la noche

es.explanation: Debe demostrar que su padre o tutor certifica que ha tenido al menos 50 horas de experiencia de conducción, incluyendo 10 horas por la noche.

es.question: Para obtener una licencia intermedia, debe aprobar un curso de capacitación para conductores aprobado que incluya al menos ¿cuántas horas de instrucción en el aula?

choices.A: 10 horas
choices.B: 20 horas
choices.C: 30 horas
choices.D: 40 horas

es.explanation: Debe presentar un comprobante de que ha aprobado un curso de capacitación para conductores aprobado con al menos 30 horas de instrucción en el aula y seis horas de instrucción al volante.

es.question: ¿Cuáles son las horas restringidas de conducción para el titular de una licencia de conducir intermedia, a menos que esté acompañado por una persona calificada?

choices.A: De 10 p. m. a 5 a. m.
choices.B: De 11 p. m. a 6 a. m.
choices.C: De 12 a. m. a 5 a. m.
choices.D: De 1 a. m. a 5 a. m.

es.explanation: Una licencia intermedia le prohíbe conducir entre la 1 a. m. y las 5 a. m., a menos que esté con un padre, un tutor o un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos 25 años de edad.

es.question: Durante los primeros seis meses de tener una licencia intermedia, ¿cuál es la restricción con respecto a los pasajeros?

choices.A: No se permiten pasajeros bajo ninguna circunstancia.
choices.B: Ningún pasajero menor de 20 años puede estar con usted a menos que sea un miembro de su familia inmediata.
choices.C: Solo puede llevar a un pasajero menor de 20 años.
choices.D: Puede llevar a cualquier pasajero siempre que use el cinturón de seguridad.

es.explanation: Durante los primeros seis meses de una licencia intermedia, ningún pasajero menor de 20 años puede estar con usted mientras conduce, a menos que esa persona sea un miembro de su familia inmediata.

es.question: Bajo una licencia intermedia, no puede conducir entre la 1 a. m. y las 5 a. m. a menos que esté acompañado por un padre, tutor o un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos ¿qué edad?

choices.A: 18 años
choices.B: 21 años
choices.C: 25 años
choices.D: 30 años

es.explanation: El manual establece que con una licencia intermedia, no puede conducir entre la 1 a. m. y las 5 a. m. a menos que esté con un padre, un tutor o un conductor con licencia que tenga al menos 25 años de edad.

es.question: Durante los primeros seis meses de tener una licencia intermedia, ¿quién puede viajar como pasajero en su vehículo?

choices.A: Hasta tres pasajeros menores de 20 años
choices.B: Ningún pasajero menor de 20 años a menos que sea familia inmediata
choices.C: Cualquier conductor con licencia menor de 20 años
choices.D: Solo pasajeros mayores de 25 años

es.explanation: Según el manual, durante los primeros seis meses de una licencia intermedia, ningún pasajero menor de 20 años puede estar con usted mientras conduce, a menos que esa persona sea un miembro de su familia inmediata.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la sanción por una segunda infracción de las restricciones de la licencia intermedia durante el primer año?

choices.A: Se envía una carta de advertencia a su padre o tutor
choices.B: Su licencia se suspende por seis meses o hasta los 18 años
choices.C: Su licencia se suspende hasta los 21 años
choices.D: Debe volver a tomar el examen de conducción

es.explanation: El manual establece que por una segunda infracción, se le suspende la licencia por seis meses (o hasta los 18 años, lo que ocurra primero).

es.question: ¿Cuándo se le permite a un conductor con una licencia intermedia usar un teléfono celular mientras opera un vehículo?

choices.A: Cuando usa un dispositivo de manos libres
choices.B: Cuando está detenido en un semáforo en rojo
choices.C: Para denunciar una actividad ilegal o solicitar ayuda de emergencia
choices.D: Para obtener indicaciones de una aplicación de GPS

es.explanation: Los titulares de licencias intermedias no pueden usar un teléfono celular a menos que utilicen el dispositivo para denunciar una actividad ilegal, solicitar ayuda médica o de otra emergencia, o para evitar lesiones a una persona o propiedad.

es.question: ¿A qué edad una licencia intermedia se convierte automáticamente en una licencia de conducir estándar sin restricciones?
es.explanation: El manual establece: "En su cumpleaños número 18, su licencia se convertirá en una licencia de conducir estándar sin las restricciones de la licencia intermedia".

es.question: ¿Cuántas preguntas debe responder correctamente para aprobar el examen de conocimientos?
es.explanation: El examen de conocimientos es una prueba de opción múltiple con 40 preguntas, y debe responder correctamente 32 de ellas para aprobar el examen.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo es válido el resultado aprobado del examen de conocimientos?

choices.A: 6 meses
choices.B: 1 año
choices.C: 2 años
choices.D: 5 años

es.explanation: Según el manual, el resultado aprobado del examen de conocimientos tiene una validez de dos años.

es.question: ¿A quién se le permite estar en el vehículo con usted y el examinador durante el examen de conducción?

choices.A: Un padre o tutor
choices.B: Un intérprete de idiomas extranjeros
choices.C: Un animal de servicio o un intérprete para personas sordas
choices.D: Un instructor de conducción con licencia

es.explanation: El manual especifica que solo usted, el examinador, un animal de servicio y un intérprete para personas sordas o con dificultades auditivas están permitidos en el vehículo durante el examen.

es.question: ¿Qué debe hacer al retroceder su vehículo durante el examen de conducción?

choices.A: Confiar únicamente en su espejo retrovisor
choices.B: Girar la cabeza y mirar hacia atrás
choices.C: Tocar la bocina antes de moverse
choices.D: Usar solo sus espejos laterales

es.explanation: Durante el examen, debe girar la cabeza y mirar hacia atrás para detectar vehículos motorizados, ciclistas y peatones cuando esté retrocediendo su vehículo.

es.question: ¿Por cuánto tiempo puede ser válida una licencia de conducir de Washington renovada?

choices.A: Hasta 4 años
choices.B: Hasta 5 años
choices.C: Hasta 6 años
choices.D: Hasta 8 años

es.explanation: El manual establece: "Su licencia renovada puede ser válida hasta por seis años y vencerá en su cumpleaños".

es.question: ¿Debe pagar un cargo por demora adicional si renueva su licencia más de cuántos días después de que haya vencido?

choices.A: 10 días
choices.B: 30 días
choices.C: 60 días
choices.D: 90 días

es.explanation: Según el manual, si renueva su licencia más de 60 días después de su vencimiento, debe pagar un cargo por demora adicional.

es.question: ¿Cuántos días tiene para notificar al Departamento de Licencias sobre un cambio de dirección o de nombre legal?

choices.A: 5 días
choices.B: 10 días
choices.C: 15 días
choices.D: 30 días

es.explanation: Debe notificar al Departamento dentro de los diez días posteriores a un cambio de dirección o un cambio de nombre legal.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes es una razón por la que puede perder su licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Recibir una sola multa de estacionamiento
choices.B: Negarse a permitir que un oficial de policía le realice una prueba de alcohol
choices.C: Conducir a 5 mph sobre el límite de velocidad
choices.D: No renovar su licencia un día después de su vencimiento

es.explanation: El manual enumera "negarse a permitir que un oficial de policía le realice una prueba de alcohol" como una de las razones por las que puede perder su licencia.

es.question: Si decide no quitarse un artículo que obstruye la vista completa de su rostro para la foto de su licencia (y no tiene una excepción médica o religiosa), ¿qué sucederá?

choices.A: Su licencia se marcará como "No válida para identificación"
choices.B: Se le negará la licencia de conducir por completo
choices.C: Deberá pagar un cargo adicional
choices.D: Se le emitirá un permiso temporal en su lugar

es.explanation: El manual establece que si decide no retirar una obstrucción de su rostro y cabeza, su licencia se marcará como "No válida para identificación" (Not Valid for Identification).

es.question: ¿Cuál de los siguientes es un requisito para el vehículo que traiga a su examen de conducción?

choices.A: Debe tener menos de 10 años de antigüedad
choices.B: Debe tener controles duales para el examinador
choices.C: Debe tener licencia y registro legales, y no tener partes defectuosas
choices.D: Debe tener transmisión automática

es.explanation: Para el examen de conducción, debe traer un vehículo que tenga licencia y registro legales, y no debe tener partes defectuosas.

es.question: Si usted es un conductor sin seguro involucrado en una colisión, ¿por cuánto tiempo se le puede suspender la licencia?

choices.A: 1 año
choices.B: 3 años
choices.C: 5 años
choices.D: 10 años

es.explanation: El manual establece que el Departamento de Licencias puede suspender la licencia de un conductor sin seguro involucrado en una colisión por hasta tres años.

es.question: ¿No cumplir con una sentencia de un tribunal civil derivada de una colisión puede resultar en la suspensión de la licencia por cuántos años?

choices.A: 3 o más años
choices.B: 5 o más años
choices.C: 10 o más años
choices.D: 13 o más años

es.explanation: No cumplir con una sentencia de un tribunal civil derivada de una colisión puede resultar en una suspensión por 13 o más años.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes acciones puede resultar en la pérdida de su licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Irse de una gasolinera sin pagar por el combustible que ha bombeado.
choices.B: Estacionarse a más de 12 pulgadas del bordillo.
choices.C: Conducir a 5 mph por encima del límite de velocidad en una autopista.
choices.D: No lavar su vehículo regularmente.

es.explanation: Según el manual, usted puede perder su licencia por irse de una gasolinera sin pagar por el combustible que ha bombeado.

es.question: ¿Cuántas infracciones de tránsito debe recibir mientras conduce con una licencia intermedia para perder su privilegio de conducir?

choices.A: Una o más
choices.B: Dos o más
choices.C: Tres o más
choices.D: Cuatro o más

es.explanation: Usted puede perder su licencia por recibir dos o más infracciones de tránsito mientras conduce con una licencia intermedia.

es.question: Si recibe una multa y no cumple en un plazo de 15 días, el tribunal notifica al Departamento de Licencias. ¿Cuántos días tiene entonces para cumplir antes de que se suspenda su privilegio de conducir?

choices.A: 15 días
choices.B: 30 días
choices.C: 45 días
choices.D: 60 días

es.explanation: Si no cumple en un plazo de 15 días, el tribunal notifica al departamento y este envía por correo un Aviso de Suspensión. Luego tiene 45 días para cumplir o se le suspenderá su privilegio de conducir.

es.question: Los delincuentes sexuales y los delincuentes por secuestro en el estado de Washington deben registrarse con el alguacil del condado (sheriff) ¿dentro de cuántos días después de establecer su residencia?

choices.A: Tres días hábiles
choices.B: Cinco días hábiles
choices.C: Diez días hábiles
choices.D: Treinta días

es.explanation: Los delincuentes sexuales y los delincuentes por secuestro en el estado de Washington deben registrarse dentro de los tres días hábiles posteriores a establecer, o restablecer, su residencia.

es.question: Para registrarse para votar en una oficina de licencias de conducir, debe ser ciudadano de los Estados Unidos, residente del estado de Washington y tener al menos ¿qué edad?
es.explanation: Para registrarse para votar, debe ser ciudadano de los Estados Unidos cuyos derechos civiles no estén revocados actualmente, residente del estado de Washington y tener al menos 18 años.

es.question: ¿Qué sucede si un solicitante masculino menor de 26 años se niega a registrarse en el Sistema de Servicio Selectivo (SSS) al solicitar una licencia de conducir?

choices.A: Su solicitud será denegada de inmediato.
choices.B: Se le otorgará una licencia restringida.
choices.C: No se le puede denegar el documento solicitado si cumple con todos los demás requisitos.
choices.D: Debe pagar una tarifa adicional para recibir su licencia.

es.explanation: A un solicitante que se niegue a registrarse en el SSS no se le puede denegar el documento solicitado si cumple con todos los demás requisitos para recibir dicho documento.

es.question: ¿El Departamento de Licencias pregunta si usted es gemelo o trillizo en cooperación con qué institución para la investigación médica?

choices.A: Washington State University
choices.B: University of Washington
choices.C: LifeCenter Northwest
choices.D: The Department of Health

es.explanation: El departamento pregunta si usted es gemelo o trillizo en cooperación con la Universidad de Washington, que cuenta con el registro de gemelos más grande de los Estados Unidos.

es.question: ¿Cuál de las siguientes acciones está permitida con una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada (EDL) pero NO con una Licencia de Conducir Estándar?

choices.A: Operar un vehículo motorizado
choices.B: Viajes aéreos nacionales
choices.C: Acceso a instalaciones federales que no requieren identificación
choices.D: Cruce de fronteras internacionales por tierra o mar

es.explanation: Una Licencia de Conducir Mejorada permite el cruce de fronteras internacionales por tierra o mar, mientras que una Licencia de Conducir Estándar no lo permite.

es.question: El riesgo es generado por los tres componentes del Sistema de Transporte por Carretera (HTS). ¿Cuáles son estos tres componentes?

choices.A: El conductor, el vehículo y el entorno de la carretera
choices.B: El clima, el vehículo y el conductor
choices.C: Los peatones, la carretera y el clima
choices.D: El límite de velocidad, el conductor y el vehículo

es.explanation: El riesgo es generado por los tres componentes del Sistema de Transporte por Carretera: el conductor, el vehículo y el entorno de la carretera.

es.question: Según los datos de accidentes de Washington de 2009 a 2011, ¿cuál fue el factor más común presente en los accidentes fatales?

choices.A: Exceso de velocidad
choices.B: Salirse de la calzada
choices.C: Deterioro del conductor (impairment)
choices.D: Distracción del conductor

es.explanation: El deterioro del conductor fue el factor más común, presente en el 50.1% de los accidentes fatales.
