choices.B: 加速して交通流に合流する
choices.C: 減速し、車両や歩行者に進路を譲る
choices.D: 停止せずに進む

ja.explanation: 赤と白の三角形の「YIELD（譲れ）」標識は、減速し、車両や歩行者に優先権を譲らなければならないことを意味します。他者が安全に通過できるように、必要に応じて停止しなければなりません。

ja.question: この標識は何を意味していますか？

choices.A: この先、通行止め
choices.B: 駐車禁止
choices.C: 進入禁止
choices.D: この先、行き止まり

ja.question: この標識を見かけたら、どうすべきですか？

choices.A: Uターン（転回）する
choices.B: 注意深く運転を続ける
choices.C: 停止して、バックするか向きを変える。あなたは逆走しています
choices.D: そのエリアを早く抜けるために加速する

ja.question: この標識は何を示していますか？

choices.B: 交通は一方通行（左方向）です

choices.D: 左側に高速道路の出口があります

ja.question: この標識は何を禁止していますか？

choices.B: 左折
choices.C: Uターン（転回）
choices.D: 追い越し

ja.question: この標識によって禁止されている行為は何ですか？

choices.A: 右折
choices.B: 左折
choices.C: Uターン（転回）
choices.D: 直進

ja.question: この標識は何を意味していますか？

choices.B: 左折禁止
choices.C: 右折禁止
choices.D: 追い越し禁止

ja.explanation: 右折の矢印に斜線が引かれた白い規制標識は、その場所での右折が禁止されていることを意味します。

ja.question: この標識は何を示していますか？

choices.B: この区間では他車を追い越してはいけません

ja.question: この標識はドライバーに何を指示していますか？

choices.B: 右折専用

ja.question: 形と色に基づくと、これはどの種類の標識ですか？

choices.B: 案内標識

choices.D: 工事標識

ja.question: この黄色い菱形の標識は何を警告していますか？

choices.B: このエリアでは鹿が頻繁に道路を横断します

choices.D: 近くに野生動物保護区があります

ja.question: この標識は何を警告していますか？

ja.question: この標識の形は何を示していますか？

choices.B: 工事区域
choices.C: スクールゾーンまたは学校周辺の横断歩道

ja.question: この円形の黄色い標識は何を警告していますか？

choices.A: この先にラウンドアバウトがある
choices.B: 病院区域
choices.C: この先に踏切がある
choices.D: 追い越し禁止区域

ja.explanation: 黒いXと2つのRが描かれた円形の黄色い標識は、この先に踏切があることを知らせる事前警告標識です。速度を落とし、列車の音や姿を確認してください。

ja.question: この標識は通常どこで見かけますか？

choices.A: 学校周辺の横断歩道
choices.B: 踏切
choices.C: 病院の入り口
choices.D: 歩道橋

ja.question: この黄色いひし形の標識は何を示していますか？

choices.A: この先で行き止まり
choices.B: 右折必須
choices.C: この先に右カーブがある
choices.D: この先に回り道（デトア）がある

ja.question: この標識はカーブの標識とどのように異なりますか？

choices.C: 右折専用であることを意味する

ja.question: この標識はどのような道路状況を警告していますか？

choices.B: この先に1つのカーブがある

choices.D: この先にラウンドアバウトがある

ja.question: この標識は何を予測するよう警告していますか？

choices.A: 1つの急なカーブ
choices.B: 滑りやすい路面
choices.C: この先に連続するカーブや曲がり角がある
choices.D: この先に坂道がある

ja.explanation: 「ワインディングロード（曲がりくねった道）」の標識は、この先に一連のカーブや曲がり角が続くことを警告しています。速度を落とし、変化する道路状況に注意してください。

ja.question: この標識は何に備えるよう伝えていますか？

choices.A: 車線の減少
choices.B: 他の道路からの交通の合流
choices.C: 中央分離帯のある道路の始まり
choices.D: 道幅が狭くなり1車線になる

ja.explanation: 黄色いひし形の合流（マージ）標識は、他の道路からの車両が自分の車線に合流してくることを警告しています。速度や位置を調整する準備をしてください。

ja.question: この標識は何を警告していますか？

choices.A: この先に橋がある
choices.B: この先で道幅が狭くなる
choices.C: 車線の終了
choices.D: 中央分離帯のある道路の終了

ja.explanation: この警告標識は、この先の道幅が狭くなることを示しています。道路の幅が減少することに備え、車線内の位置を調整してください。

ja.question: この標識はこの先に何があることを示していますか？

choices.A: 行き止まり
choices.B: 対面通行
choices.C: 分離道路の始まり
choices.D: 高速道路の出口

ja.explanation: この標識は、この先の道路が中央分離帯や障壁によって対向車線と分けられた分離道路（divided highway）になることを警告しています。右側を通行してください。

ja.question: この標識は何について警告していますか？

choices.A: 分離道路の始まり
choices.B: 分離道路が終わり、対面通行に戻る
choices.C: この先に合流地点あり
choices.D: この先に道路工事あり

ja.explanation: この標識は、分離道路が終了することを警告しています。対向車線が中央分離帯で区切られなくなります。対面通行に備えてください。

ja.question: この標識は何について警告していますか？

choices.A: 分離道路の始まり
choices.B: この先に追い越し区間あり
choices.C: この先に対面通行あり — 車両が双方向に通行する
choices.D: この先に車線移動あり

ja.explanation: この標識はこの先が対面通行であることを警告しています。一方通行の道路や分離道路から出て、反対方向に進む車両と遭遇する可能性があります。

ja.question: この標識はどのような路面状況について警告していますか？

choices.A: 路面の凍結
choices.B: 濡れている時に滑りやすい
choices.C: この先に曲がりくねった道あり
choices.D: 路面の凹凸

ja.explanation: 「スリップ注意（slippery when wet）」の標識は、雨や路面が濡れている時に非常に滑りやすくなる可能性があることを警告しています。速度を落とし、急ブレーキや急ハンドルを避けてください。

ja.question: この標識は何について警告していますか？

choices.A: 路面の隆起
choices.B: 路面の凹凸
choices.C: この先に急な下り坂または勾配あり
choices.D: 道路工事

ja.explanation: この標識はこの先に急な坂道や勾配があることを警告しています。特にトラックや牽引中の場合は、速度を調整し、低いギアにシフトダウンする必要があるかもしれません。

ja.question: この標識は何に備えるよう警告していますか？

choices.A: この先に一時停止の標識あり
choices.B: この先に信号機あり
choices.C: 通学路の横断歩道
choices.D: 検問所

ja.explanation: この標識はこの先に信号機があることを警告しています。赤信号や黄信号の場合に停止できるよう準備してください。この標識は、遠くから信号機が見えにくい場所に設置されることが多いです。

ja.question: この標識はこの先に何があることを示していますか？

choices.A: 譲れ（yield）の標識
choices.B: 信号機
choices.C: 一時停止しなければならない停止標識
choices.D: スピードバンプ（段差）

ja.explanation: この標識はこの先に一時停止の標識があることを警告しています。減速を開始し、停止標識の場所で完全に停止できるよう準備してください。

ja.question: この標識は何について警告していますか？

choices.A: この先に踏切あり
choices.B: この先に十字路または交差点あり
choices.C: この先に病院あり
choices.D: 歩行者用横断歩道

ja.explanation: この標識はこの先に十字路または四差路の交差点があることを警告しています。脇道から進入してくる車両に注意してください。

ja.question: この標識は何について警告していますか？

choices.A: この先に丁字路（T字路）あり
choices.B: 右側から合流する脇道あり
choices.C: 道路のカーブ
choices.D: 行き止まり

ja.explanation: この標識は右側から脇道が合流していることを警告しています。脇道から幹線道路に進入してくる車両に注意してください。

ja.question: この標識はどういう意味ですか？

choices.A: 車線が合流している
choices.B: 車線が減少している
choices.C: 新しい車線が追加される — 合流の必要なし
choices.D: 右折が必要

ja.explanation: 「付加車線（added lane）」の標識は、合流を必要とせずに新しい車線が道路に加わることを意味します。ランプから進入する車両には、専用の新しい車線が用意されています。

ja.question: この標識は何を禁止していますか？

choices.A: いかなる時の停車
choices.B: この区域での駐車
choices.C: 停車またはアイドリング
choices.D: 荷物の積み下ろし

ja.explanation: 赤と白の「NO PARKING（駐車禁止）」の標識は、この区域に車両を駐車できないことを意味します。乗客の乗り降りのために短時間停車することは許可されています。

ja.question: この標識がある場所に駐車できるのは誰ですか？

choices.A: 15分未満であれば誰でも
choices.B: 高齢者のみ
choices.C: 有効な身体障害者用駐車標章またはナンバープレートを掲示している車両のみ
choices.D: 障害のある乗客を乗せているすべての運転者

ja.explanation: 車椅子のシンボルが描かれた青い標識は、身体障害者専用の駐車場であることを示しています。有効な身体障害者用駐車標章またはライセンスプレート（ナンバープレート）を掲示している車両のみが、これらのスペースに駐車できます。違反した場合は高額な罰金が科せられます。

en.question: According to the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook, driving is considered:

choices.A: A constitutional right
choices.B: A privilege and a very important responsibility
choices.C: A requirement for all citizens over 18
choices.D: An optional hobby

en.explanation: The handbook states, "It's also crucial to remember that driving is a privilege and a very important responsibility."

en.question: Which of the following is listed in the handbook as a safe behavior to help take control of your drive?

choices.A: Driving slightly above the speed limit to keep up with traffic
choices.B: Sharing the road with pedestrians and bicyclists
choices.C: Relying solely on your passengers to watch for motorcycles
choices.D: Multitasking while operating the vehicle

en.explanation: The handbook lists "Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists" as one of the safe behaviors to develop behind the wheel.

en.question: Which organization is specifically mentioned as being responsible for educating the public about rules of the road and enforcing Wisconsin traffic laws?

choices.A: Wisconsin Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
choices.B: Wisconsin State Patrol
choices.C: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
choices.D: Wisconsin Department of Transportation

en.explanation: The manual states, "Wisconsin State Patrol educates the public about rules of the road and enforces Wisconsin traffic laws."

en.question: What is the primary role of the DMV as described in the introductory section of the handbook?

choices.A: To enforce Wisconsin traffic laws on the highway
choices.B: To engineer Wisconsin's roads through a Safe System approach
choices.C: To ensure drivers are trained and qualified to operate a vehicle
choices.D: To operate the National Human Trafficking Hotline

en.explanation: The text notes that "DMV ensures drivers are trained and qualified to operate a vehicle, including through helpful resources like this Motorists' Handbook."

en.question: What is the goal of Wisconsin's Safe System approach to highway safety?

choices.A: To ensure all drivers pass the knowledge test on their first try
choices.B: To design and operate the transportation system so driver mistakes do not become deadly
choices.C: To eliminate all traffic stops by the Wisconsin State Patrol
choices.D: To replace all traditional intersections with roundabouts

en.explanation: The manual explains that the Safe System approach "aims to design and operate Wisconsin's transportation system so driver mistakes do not become deadly."

en.question: Where can you find the Online Class D Driver License Practice Test?

choices.A: KnowToDrive.com/Wisconsin
choices.B: wisconsindmv.gov
choices.C: love146.org/online-safety
choices.D: tatnonprofit.org/youth

en.explanation: The handbook states that the Online Class D Driver License Practice Test "can be found on our DMV website wisconsindmv.gov."

en.question: In how many counties in Wisconsin have cases of human trafficking been reported?

choices.A: 10 counties
choices.B: 25 counties
choices.C: 50 counties
choices.D: All 72 counties

en.explanation: The human trafficking section explicitly states, "Cases of human trafficking have been reported in all 72 counties in Wisconsin."

en.question: According to the human trafficking information in the handbook, anyone under what age who exchanges sex acts for money or other things of value is considered a victim?

choices.A: Under age 16
choices.B: Under age 18
choices.C: Under age 21
choices.D: Under age 25

en.explanation: The text states, "Anyone under age 18 that exchanges sex acts for money or other things of value is considered a victim of human trafficking."

en.question: What word can you text to BeFree (233733) to contact the National Human Trafficking Hotline?

choices.A: SAFE
choices.B: HELP
choices.C: STOP
choices.D: ALERT

en.explanation: The manual provides the contact information for the National Human Trafficking Hotline as "1-888-3737-888 or text HELP to BeFree (233733)."

en.question: How do human traffickers often meet their victims according to the handbook?

choices.A: Through driver's education courses
choices.B: At DMV service centers
choices.C: Online while pretending to be someone else
choices.D: Through the Driver Education Grant Program

en.explanation: The "Stay safe" section warns that "Traffickers often meet their victims online while they are pretending to be someone else."

en.question: According to Section 1 of the handbook's Table of Contents, which of the following is a requirement for the driving test?

choices.A: A medical physical exam
choices.B: A Highway Signs Test
choices.C: An emissions test
choices.D: A background check

en.explanation: Section 1 (Driving Test Requirements) lists Vision Screening, Highway Signs Test, Knowledge Test, and Skills Test.

en.question: Based on the Progression of Licenses outlined in Section 2, which license comes immediately after an Instruction Permit?

choices.A: Occupational License
choices.B: Regular Driver License
choices.C: Probationary License
choices.D: Commercial Driver License

en.explanation: Section 2 (Progression of Licenses) lists the order as Sponsorship, Instruction Permit, Probationary License, then Regular Driver License.

en.question: Which of the following topics is classified under "Dangerous Driving Behaviors" in Section 9 of the handbook?

choices.A: Backing up
choices.B: Drowsy Driving
choices.C: Farm Safety
choices.D: Winter Driving

en.explanation: Section 9 (Dangerous Driving Behaviors) includes Alcohol, Drugs and Driving; Distracted Driving; and Drowsy Driving.

en.question: Section 10 of the handbook covers "Sharing the Road." Which of the following is a topic included in this section?

choices.A: No-Zones
choices.B: Metered Ramps
choices.C: Diverging Diamond Interchanges
choices.D: Roundabouts

en.explanation: Section 10 (Sharing the Road) lists Pedestrians, Emergency Vehicles, School Buses, Motorcycles, Bicycles, and No-Zones.

en.question: According to Section 11 of the Table of Contents, what system does Wisconsin use to track your driving privilege?

choices.A: The Demerit System
choices.B: The Point System
choices.C: The Strike System
choices.D: The Citation System

en.explanation: Section 11 (Your Driving Privilege) lists the "Point System" as its first topic.

en.question: What is the minimum visual acuity required in at least one eye to pass the vision screening for a regular car license?
en.explanation: According to the manual, Wisconsin requires regular car applicants to have a visual acuity of at least 20/40 in one eye (corrected or uncorrected).

en.question: What is the required field of vision from the center of each eye to pass the vision screening?

choices.A: 50 degrees
choices.B: 70 degrees
choices.C: 90 degrees
choices.D: 120 degrees

en.explanation: The manual states that applicants must have a 70-degree field of vision from the center of each eye.

en.question: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass the Highway Signs Test?

choices.A: 10 out of 15
choices.B: 12 out of 15
choices.C: 15 out of 20
choices.D: 40 out of 50

en.explanation: There are 15 questions on the Highway Signs Test, and you need to answer 12 questions (80%) correctly to pass.

en.question: What is the fee for taking the knowledge test in person at a DMV customer service center?

choices.D: It is free

en.explanation: The manual states that tests in a DMV customer service center are free.

en.question: If an applicant is between ages 15 and 17, how much does it cost to take the knowledge test online?

choices.A: It is free

en.explanation: Applicants between ages 15 and 17 may take the knowledge test online for a fee of $10.

en.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a vehicle part the DMV examiner will check before your skills test?

choices.A: Horn
choices.B: Engine oil level
choices.C: License plates
choices.D: Mirrors

en.explanation: Before the test, the examiner checks the horn, lights/signals, license plates, doors, mirrors, and more. Engine oil level is not listed.

en.question: How many documents proving you live in Wisconsin must you bring when applying for a license?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Four

en.explanation: To apply for a license, you must bring two documents that prove you live in Wisconsin, such as a utility bill or financial statement.

en.question: What does it mean when an adult signs as a sponsor for a driver under age 18?

choices.A: They must ride in the vehicle at all times.
choices.B: They pay for the driver's education course.
choices.C: They accept legal and financial liability for incidents caused by the minor.
choices.D: They guarantee the minor will pass the skills test.

en.explanation: The sponsor accepts liability, meaning they are legally and financially responsible for incidents caused by the minor driving.

en.question: Under which condition must a minor file proof of insurance instead of having a sponsor?

choices.A: They are 16 years old and live with their parents.
choices.B: They are married and their spouse is under 18 years of age.
choices.C: They have completed 50 hours of supervised driving.
choices.D: They are taking the knowledge test online.

en.explanation: You must file proof of insurance instead of having a sponsor if you are married and your spouse is under 18 years of age, among other specific criteria.

en.question: How old must you be to apply for an instruction permit if you are enrolled in a driver education program?

choices.A: 14 years old
choices.B: 15 years old
choices.C: 15 and a half years old
choices.D: 16 years old

en.explanation: If under 18, you must be at least 15 years old and enrolled in a driver education program to apply for an instruction permit.

en.question: If you hold an instruction permit and are driving during hours of darkness, who must accompany you in the passenger seat?

choices.A: Any licensed driver over 18
choices.B: A sibling who is at least 16 years old
choices.C: A qualified instructor or a licensed person 25 years of age with at least two years of licensed driving experience
choices.D: Any person with a valid probationary license

en.explanation: If operating a vehicle during hours of darkness, you must be accompanied by a qualified instructor or a licensed person 25 years of age with at least two years of licensed driving experience occupying the seat beside you.

en.question: The person accompanying an instruction permit holder in the passenger seat must have at least how many years of licensed driving experience?

choices.A: One year
choices.B: Two years
choices.C: Three years
choices.D: Five years

en.explanation: The class D instruction permit holder must drive with someone else in the car who has at least two years of licensed driving experience.

en.question: How long must a driver under 18 hold their instruction permit before they can get a probationary license?

choices.A: 3 months
choices.B: 6 months
choices.C: 9 months
choices.D: 12 months

en.explanation: If under 18 years old, you need to have your instruction permit for at least six months and turn 16 years old to get a probationary license.

en.question: How many total hours of supervised driving practice must a minor complete before getting a probationary license?

choices.A: 30 hours
choices.B: 40 hours
choices.C: 50 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: With a valid instruction permit, you must practice driving for at least 40 hours during daylight and 10 hours during darkness, totaling 50 hours.

en.question: While driving with a probationary license, when are you allowed to use a phone?

choices.A: When stopped at a red light
choices.B: Only to report an emergency
choices.C: When using a hands-free device
choices.D: You are never allowed to use a phone under any circumstances

en.explanation: The manual states for probationary licenses: "Remember that phones are not allowed while driving unless you need to report an emergency."

en.question: How long are the Graduated Driver License (GDL) passenger and hour restrictions required for drivers under 18?

choices.A: For the first 6 months
choices.B: For the first 9 months
choices.C: For the first 12 months
choices.D: Until the driver turns 21

en.explanation: According to the manual, GDL restrictions are required for the first nine months, unless you turn 18 years old before then.

en.question: Under a Graduated Driver License (GDL), where are you allowed to drive alone between midnight and 5 a.m.?

choices.A: Anywhere within your home city limits
choices.B: Only between home, school, and/or work
choices.C: Only to medical emergencies
choices.D: You are never allowed to drive alone during these hours

en.explanation: The manual states that from 12 p.m. (midnight) to 5 a.m., you can drive alone only IF driving between home, school and/or work.

en.question: What will cause your Graduated Driver License (GDL) restrictions to be extended for six months?

choices.A: Receiving a parking ticket
choices.B: Being convicted of a moving traffic violation
choices.C: Failing to renew your license 90 days early
choices.D: Driving with an immediate family member

en.explanation: The graduated driver license restrictions will be extended six months if you are convicted of a moving traffic violation, violate any restrictions, or your license is suspended/revoked.

en.question: How often does a regular Wisconsin driver's license need to be renewed?

choices.A: Every 4 years
choices.B: Every 5 years
choices.C: Every 8 years
choices.D: Every 10 years

en.explanation: The manual states that renewing your driver's license needs to be done every eight years.

en.question: If you move to Wisconsin with a regular driver's license from another state, within how many days should you apply for a Wisconsin license?

choices.A: 10 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: For a regular out of state driver license, you should apply for a Wisconsin driver license within 60 days after moving.

en.question: How is a REAL ID-compliant driver's license marked in Wisconsin?

choices.A: With a gold circle
choices.B: With a star
choices.C: With a bald eagle
choices.D: With a barcode on the front

en.explanation: The manual notes that the Wisconsin DMV issues REAL-ID that meets Homeland Security requirements, which is marked with a star.

en.question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the exact same time, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The driver on the left
choices.B: The driver on the right
choices.C: The driver going straight
choices.D: The driver turning right

en.explanation: According to the right-of-way rules, if one or more driver arrives to the stop at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

en.question: When encountering a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?

choices.A: Honk your horn to let them know you are there
choices.B: Stop at least ten feet away until they are off the roadway
choices.C: Yield only if they are in a marked crosswalk
choices.D: Drive around them slowly

en.explanation: You must yield right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane by stopping at least ten feet away until the person is off the roadway.

en.question: What rule should you use to determine a safe following distance under normal driving conditions?

choices.A: The Two Second Rule
choices.B: The Three Second Rule
choices.C: The Four Second Following Distance Rule
choices.D: The One Car Length Rule

en.explanation: The manual instructs drivers to drive at a speed where they can always safely stop by using the “Four Second Following Distance Rule.”

en.question: What is the normal speed limit in a school zone when children are present in Wisconsin?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour
choices.B: 20 miles per hour
choices.C: 25 miles per hour
choices.D: 35 miles per hour

en.explanation: The manual specifies that the normal speed limit in a school zone when children are present is 15 miles per hour.

en.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in residential areas?

choices.A: 15 miles per hour
choices.B: 25 miles per hour
choices.C: 30 miles per hour
choices.D: 35 miles per hour

en.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential areas is 25 miles per hour.

en.question: When merging onto a high-speed roadway from an acceleration lane, what is your responsibility?

choices.A: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap
choices.B: Force other drivers to change their speed so you can enter
choices.C: Find a safe gap in traffic to legally merge
choices.D: Drive on the shoulder until a gap opens up

en.explanation: In the acceleration lane, you speed up as you merge. The manual states it is your responsibility to find a safe gap in traffic to legally merge.

en.question: To maintain better control of your vehicle, how far ahead should you be able to see?

choices.A: 3 to 5 seconds ahead
choices.B: 5 to 10 seconds ahead
choices.C: 10 to 15 seconds ahead
choices.D: 20 to 30 seconds ahead

en.explanation: To have better control of your vehicle, the driver needs to be able to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their vehicle.

en.question: What is the recommended searching pattern before going through an intersection?

choices.A: Look right, then left
choices.B: Look straight ahead only
choices.C: Look left, right, and left again
choices.D: Look at your rearview mirror, then left

en.explanation: The manual advises to be alert by searching left, right and left again before going through the intersection even if you have the right-of-way.

en.question: Who must you yield the right-of-way to at an uncontrolled T-intersection?

choices.A: The vehicle on the terminating street
choices.B: Cross traffic
choices.C: The vehicle turning left
choices.D: The vehicle that honks first

en.explanation: According to the right-of-way rules in the manual, you should yield right-of-way to cross traffic in an uncontrolled T-intersection.

en.question: What does it mean to 'coast' while driving, which the manual advises against?

choices.A: Driving without using the accelerator
choices.B: Putting your car in the neutral position
choices.C: Driving with the parking brake partially engaged
choices.D: Turning off the engine while moving

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Do not coast while driving, this means putting your car in the neutral position. Stay in "gear" so that you can have full control over your vehicle.'

en.question: How often should you check your rearview mirror to see if someone is following you too closely?

choices.A: Every 3 to 5 seconds
choices.B: Every 6 to 8 seconds
choices.C: Every 10 to 12 seconds
choices.D: Every 15 to 20 seconds

en.explanation: The manual advises, 'Check your rearview mirror every 6 to 8 seconds to see if someone is following too closely (tailgating).'

en.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

choices.A: Tap your brakes quickly to warn them
choices.B: Speed up to increase the distance between your vehicles
choices.C: Slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to drive around you
choices.D: Change lanes immediately without signaling

en.explanation: The manual states, 'If someone is tailgating you, slowly reduce your speed. This should encourage them to drive around you.'

en.question: Why is it important to keep your steering wheel straight while waiting to make a left turn?

choices.A: It prevents your power steering fluid from overheating
choices.B: It helps you accelerate faster when the path is clear
choices.C: It keeps you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if someone hits you from behind
choices.D: It signals to other drivers that you are yielding the right-of-way

en.explanation: The manual explains, 'If you turn your wheel to the left and someone hits you from behind, you will be pushed into oncoming traffic. It is important to keep your steering wheel, vehicle wheels and vehicle straight.'

en.question: Under what condition are you permitted to make a U-turn on a rural two-lane highway?

choices.A: Only when there is a designated U-turn lane

en.explanation: If you refuse a PAC test, the officer must arrest you for violation of the Implied Consent Law, and you will lose your driving privileges for at least one year.

en.question: When are instruction permit and probationary license holders allowed to use a cell phone while driving?

choices.A: When using a hands-free device
choices.B: Only to report an emergency
choices.C: When stopped at a red light
choices.D: When reading GPS directions

en.explanation: Instruction permit and probationary license holders can only use a cell phone to report an emergency.

en.question: What must you do if you approach a police car stopped on the side of the road with its lights and sirens on?

choices.A: Stop immediately in your lane and wait for them to leave
choices.B: Honk your horn to let them know you are passing
choices.C: Move over into the lane not nearest the stopped vehicle or slow down
choices.D: Speed up to get past the scene quickly

en.explanation: If you see a police car is stopped on the side of the road with their lights and sirens on, move over or slow down, it's the law. If approaching an emergency vehicle with its lights flashing, make sure to move into the lane not nearest the stopped vehicle.

en.question: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, how far away must you stop?

choices.A: At least 10 feet
choices.B: At least 15 feet
choices.C: At least 20 feet
choices.D: At least 50 feet

en.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing you need to stop at least 20 feet from it.

en.question: Under what condition are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?

choices.A: When you are traveling in the same direction as the bus on a multi-lane road
choices.B: When you are on a divided highway and on the opposite side of the barrier from the bus
choices.C: When you are running late for an emergency
choices.D: When there are no children visible outside the bus

en.explanation: If you are on a divided highway/roadway and not on the side of the school bus, you do not need to stop. A divided highway has a barrier between lanes going opposite directions.

en.question: How much room must you give a bicyclist when passing them?

choices.A: At least one foot
choices.B: At least two feet
choices.C: At least three feet
choices.D: At least five feet

en.explanation: Give bicyclists at least three feet of room when you pass.

en.question: What is a "No-Zone" when sharing the road with large trucks?

choices.A: A designated lane where trucks are not allowed to drive
choices.B: An area about 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front of large trucks where they cannot see you
choices.C: A zone near schools where commercial vehicles must reduce speed
choices.D: The area on a divided highway where passing is prohibited

en.explanation: No-Zones are where large vehicles cannot see you. This area is about 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front of large trucks.

en.question: How many demerit points within a 12-month period will cause your driving privilege to be suspended or revoked?

choices.A: 6 or more points
choices.B: 8 or more points
choices.C: 10 or more points
choices.D: 12 or more points

en.explanation: You will not be able to drive if you get 12 or more demerit points within any 12-month period. Your driving privilege will be suspended or revoked.

en.question: If you hold a probationary license, what happens to your demerit points upon your second traffic conviction?

choices.A: Your points are reduced by half
choices.B: Your points are doubled
choices.C: Your points are erased if you take a safety class
choices.D: Your points remain the same but your fines are doubled

en.explanation: If you hold a probationary license, ID card or no type of license, you will have your points doubled. These points are doubled on the second conviction and any thereafter.

en.question: A habitual traffic offender is someone who is convicted of four or more major traffic violations or 12 or more minor violations within what time frame?

choices.A: One year
choices.B: Three years
choices.C: Five years
choices.D: Ten years

en.explanation: A habitual offender is someone who is convicted of four or more major traffic violations or 12 or more minor violations within five years.

en.question: An occupational license allows you to drive up to how many hours per week for work, school, and household maintenance?

choices.A: 20 hours
choices.B: 40 hours
choices.C: 50 hours
choices.D: 60 hours

en.explanation: An occupational license allows you to drive up to 12 hours a day and up to 60 hours a week to and from work, school, and places that you need to visit to maintain your household.

en.question: According to Wisconsin law, who is required to wear a seat belt in a vehicle?

choices.A: Only the driver and front-seat passengers
choices.B: Only passengers under the age of 18
choices.C: The driver and all passengers at any age
choices.D: Only passengers in vehicles without airbags

en.explanation: Wisconsin law requires that you and your passengers wear seat belts (safety belts) at any age.

en.question: If your vehicle is equipped with air bags, do you still need to wear your seat belt?

choices.A: No, air bags replace the need for seat belts.
choices.B: Yes, you still need to wear your seat belt even if your vehicle has air bags.
choices.C: Only if you are driving on the highway.
choices.D: Only passengers in the back seat need to wear them.

en.explanation: The manual states, "You still need to wear your seat belt even if your vehicle has air bags." Seat belts help keep you in position to control the vehicle and avoid injury.

en.question: How should the lap belt of your seat belt be positioned?

choices.A: Loosely across your thighs
choices.B: Snugly across your stomach
choices.C: Snugly across your hip bones just under your stomach
choices.D: High up on your waist

en.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones just under your stomach.

en.question: What is the proper way to wear a shoulder belt?

choices.A: Tucked under your arm for comfort
choices.B: Across your chest with enough room to put your fist between the belt and your chest
choices.C: Loosely hanging over your shoulder
choices.D: Behind your back if it rubs against your neck

en.explanation: The shoulder belt should be worn across your chest. Adjust your belt so that you can put your fist between the belt and your chest. Never put the shoulder belt under your arm.

en.question: Generally, at what age can a child transition out of a child safety seat and into a booster seat?

choices.A: Age two
choices.B: Age four
choices.C: Age six
choices.D: Age eight

en.explanation: Generally, children must be in a child safety seat until they reach age four and in a booster seat until age eight.

en.question: Generally, children must remain in a booster seat until they reach what age?

choices.A: Age four
choices.B: Age six
choices.C: Age eight
choices.D: Age ten

en.explanation: Generally, children must be in a child safety seat until they reach age four and in a booster seat until age eight.

en.question: What type of car insurance is required to drive in Wisconsin?

choices.A: Comprehensive insurance
choices.B: Collision insurance
choices.C: Valid liability car insurance
choices.D: Uninsured motorist coverage only

en.explanation: You must have valid liability car insurance to drive in Wisconsin and present proof of it if a police officer requests it.

en.question: If you are driving someone else's car, whose responsibility is it to make sure the vehicle has insurance?

choices.A: The vehicle owner's responsibility
choices.B: Your responsibility as the driver
choices.C: The insurance company's responsibility
choices.D: The DMV's responsibility

en.explanation: If you are driving someone else’s car, it is your job to make sure it has insurance.

en.question: If you choose to report an invisible disability to the DMV, who will have access to this disclosure?

choices.A: Only your insurance company
choices.B: The general public
choices.C: Law enforcement officers and WisDOT employees
choices.D: Only medical professionals

en.explanation: The disclosure that you make will be available to law enforcement officers and employees of the Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT).

en.question: What are the minimum age and citizenship requirements to start the petition process for a free ID card for voting in Wisconsin?

choices.A: 16 years of age and a U.S. citizen
choices.B: 17 years of age and a U.S. citizen
choices.C: 18 years of age and a U.S. citizen
choices.D: 18 years of age and a permanent resident

en.explanation: You must be at least 17 years of age and a U.S. citizen to start the petition process for a free ID for voting.

en.question: If you are 18 years old or older and register to be an organ and tissue donor, who can override your decision?

choices.A: Your parents
choices.B: Your spouse
choices.C: Your doctor
choices.D: No one can override your decision

en.explanation: If you are 18 years old or older, your decision to be an organ and tissue donor may not be overridden by your family or any other person.

en.question: How does low air pressure in your tires affect your vehicle?

choices.A: It increases fuel mileage.
choices.B: It decreases fuel mileage.
choices.C: It improves braking distance.
choices.D: It prevents wear and tear on the engine.

en.explanation: Low air pressure in tires decreases fuel mileage.

en.question: Which driving habit helps save fuel and your brakes?

choices.A: Stop-and-go driving in heavy traffic
choices.B: Slowing down little by little
choices.C: Braking abruptly at intersections
choices.D: Driving with low tire pressure

en.explanation: When you slow down little by little this helps save fuel and your brakes.

en.question: What is the purpose of the Driver Education Grant Program?

choices.A: To pay for college tuition for safe drivers
choices.B: To provide free vehicles to low-income families
choices.C: To pay for classroom and/or behind-the-wheel driver training for income-eligible teens
choices.D: To reimburse drivers for auto insurance premiums

en.explanation: The Driver Education Grant Program enables teens who are income eligible to have their classroom and/or behind-the-wheel driver training paid for by the state.

en.question: What should you do if you have a health problem that could affect your driving?

choices.A: Stop driving entirely without notifying anyone.
choices.B: Report the health condition to the DMV.
choices.C: Only tell your insurance company.
choices.D: Wait until your license expires to mention it.

en.explanation: Many health problems can affect your driving. You should report health conditions that could affect your driving to the DMV.

en.question: What is the maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages with no posted speed limit?

choices.A: 25 mph
choices.B: 35 mph
choices.C: 45 mph
choices.D: 55 mph

en.explanation: According to the practice quiz in the manual, the maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages with no posted speed limit is 35 mph.

en.question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, which of the following is a required action?

choices.A: Leave the scene immediately
choices.B: Wait for the other driver to call for help
choices.C: Determine if anyone is injured
choices.D: Move the vehicles before checking on passengers

en.explanation: The manual states that if you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, you must stop, determine if anyone is injured, and call 911.

en.question: What number should you call if you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash?
en.explanation: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, the manual instructs you to stop, check for injuries, and call 911.

en.question: When turning left at an intersection, who must you yield to?

choices.A: Passing cars only
choices.B: Oncoming cars moving straight ahead or turning right
choices.C: Vehicles turning left from the opposite direction
choices.D: No one in particular

en.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming cars moving straight ahead or turning right.

en.question: What type of headlights should you use when driving in fog?

choices.A: High beams
choices.B: Low beams
choices.C: Parking lights only
choices.D: Hazard lights

en.explanation: When driving in fog, heavy rain, or snow, you should use your low beams.

en.question: If you are driving in heavy rain or snow, which lights are appropriate to use?

choices.A: Low beams
choices.B: High beams
choices.C: Driving lights only
choices.D: Interior dome lights

en.explanation: You should use low beams when driving in fog, heavy rain, or snow.

en.question: How should you react as you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

choices.A: Wait for a green light
choices.B: Stop completely before crossing through
choices.C: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
choices.D: Slow down and proceed with caution

en.explanation: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must slow down and proceed with caution.

en.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic indicate?

choices.A: The lanes are going in the same direction
choices.B: You may not pass under any circumstances
choices.C: You may pass if safe to do so and lanes go in opposite directions
choices.D: You must stop before crossing the line

en.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means the lanes are going in opposite directions and you may pass if it is safe to do so.

en.question: What color line separates traffic moving in opposite directions?

choices.A: White
choices.B: Yellow
choices.C: Red
choices.D: Blue

en.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic where the lanes are going in opposite directions.

en.question: What is the proper procedure for merging onto an interstate highway?

choices.A: Always stop before entering the highway
choices.B: Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic
choices.C: Merge over two lanes at once and speed up
choices.D: Force your way into traffic so other drivers yield

en.explanation: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.

en.question: Under what conditions is it acceptable to drive faster than the posted speed limit?

choices.A: If you do not see any other traffic in your lane
choices.B: As long as there are safe conditions to do so
choices.C: When passing another vehicle
choices.D: Never

en.explanation: According to the manual's practice quiz, it is never OK to drive faster than the posted speed limit.

en.question: How far down the road should you look ahead when driving?

choices.A: 1 to 2 blocks
choices.B: 200 to 250 yards
choices.C: 10 to 15 seconds
choices.D: 5 to 8 seconds

en.explanation: When driving, you should look 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

en.question: If you want to pass a bicycle but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?

choices.A: Speed up to pass the bicycle before the car approaches
choices.B: Honk at the bicycle to move off the road
choices.C: Slow down and let the car pass, then pass the bicycle
choices.D: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely

en.explanation: If you are wanting to pass a bicycle and there is an oncoming vehicle, you should slow down and let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.

en.question: What is a recommended safety practice when driving at night?

choices.A: Always use your high beams
choices.B: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles
choices.C: Drive closer to the vehicle ahead to see their taillights
choices.D: Increase your following distance

en.explanation: When driving at night, you should increase your following distance.

en.question: What does this sign mean?

choices.A: Slow down and proceed with caution
choices.B: Come to a complete stop
choices.C: Yield to oncoming traffic
choices.D: Stop only if other vehicles are present

en.explanation: A red octagonal STOP sign means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

en.question: What does this sign require you to do?

choices.A: Come to a complete stop
choices.B: Speed up to merge with traffic
choices.C: Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians
choices.D: Proceed without stopping

en.explanation: A red and white triangular YIELD sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. You must stop if necessary to let others pass safely.

en.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

choices.A: Make a U-turn
choices.B: Continue driving carefully
choices.C: Stop and back up or turn around — you are going the wrong way
choices.D: Speed up to exit the area quickly

en.explanation: A red and white WRONG WAY sign means you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or highway ramp. Stop immediately and safely turn around or back up.

en.question: What action is prohibited by this sign?

choices.A: Turning right
choices.B: Turning left
choices.C: Making a U-turn
choices.D: Going straight

en.explanation: A white regulatory sign showing a left turn arrow crossed out means left turns are not allowed at this intersection.

en.question: What type of sign is this, based on its shape and color?

choices.A: A warning sign
choices.B: A guide sign
choices.C: A regulatory sign
choices.D: A construction sign

en.explanation: White rectangular signs with black lettering are regulatory signs. Speed limit signs tell you the maximum legal speed for the area under ideal conditions.

en.question: What does this yellow diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

choices.A: A zoo or animal park ahead
choices.B: Deer frequently cross the road in this area
choices.C: Hunting area ahead
choices.D: A wildlife refuge nearby

en.explanation: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a deer silhouette warns that deer frequently cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch for animals, especially at dawn and dusk.

en.question: What does the shape of this sign indicate?

choices.A: A railroad crossing
choices.B: A construction zone
choices.C: A school zone or school crossing
choices.D: A hospital zone

en.explanation: A pentagon-shaped (5-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch for children.

en.question: Where would you typically see this sign?

choices.A: At a school crossing
choices.B: At a railroad crossing
choices.C: At a hospital entrance
choices.D: At a pedestrian bridge

en.explanation: The white X-shaped railroad crossbuck sign is placed at railroad crossings. It means you must yield to trains. If a train is approaching, you must stop.

en.question: How does this sign differ from a curve sign?

choices.A: It indicates a less severe turn
choices.B: It warns of a sharp turn requiring a greater speed reduction
choices.C: It means turn right only
choices.D: It is only used on highways

en.explanation: A sharp turn sign (with a more angled arrow) indicates a sharper turn than a curve sign. You need to reduce your speed more significantly before this turn.

en.question: What does this sign indicate is ahead?

choices.A: Road ends
choices.B: Two-way traffic
choices.C: A divided highway begins
choices.D: Highway exit

en.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic. Keep to the right.

en.question: Who is allowed to park in a space marked with this sign?

choices.A: Anyone for less than 15 minutes
choices.B: Senior citizens only
choices.C: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability placard or plate
choices.D: Any driver with a passenger who has a disability

en.explanation: A blue sign with the wheelchair symbol marks parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying a valid disability parking placard or license plate may park in these spaces. Violations carry heavy fines.

en.question: According to the handbook's introductory letter, what is a key responsibility of the Wisconsin State Patrol?

choices.A: Designing and engineering safer highways.
choices.B: Issuing driver licenses and instruction permits.
choices.C: Educating the public and enforcing traffic laws.
choices.D: Providing online practice tests for new drivers.

en.explanation: The handbook states, 'Wisconsin State Patrol educates the public about rules of the road and enforces Wisconsin traffic laws.'

en.question: The handbook lists several common places where human trafficking can occur. Which of the following locations is specifically mentioned?

choices.A: Public libraries
choices.B: Movie theaters
choices.C: Shopping malls
choices.D: Truck stops

en.explanation: The manual states that human trafficking can happen at locations including 'hotels and motels, truck stops, rest stops, casinos, restaurants, nail salons, farms, and more.'

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, which of the following topics is covered under Section 8, 'Handling Emergencies'?

choices.A: Drowsy Driving
choices.B: Roadside Emergencies
choices.C: Roundabouts
choices.D: Winter Driving

en.explanation: The Table of Contents shows that Section 8, 'Handling Emergencies,' includes the topic 'Roadside Emergencies.'

en.question: Based on the Table of Contents, which section of the handbook would you consult for information on driving in severe weather?

choices.A: Section 3: The Basics
choices.B: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls
choices.C: Section 7: Driving Conditions
choices.D: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Severe Weather' as a topic under Section 7, 'Driving Conditions.'

en.question: What is the phone number for the National Human Trafficking Hotline provided in the handbook?

choices.B: 1-800-SAFE-RIDE

en.explanation: The handbook provides the National Human Trafficking Hotline number as 1-888-3737-888 for those who need help or want to report a tip.

en.question: The Table of Contents indicates that information on the Diverging Diamond Interchange (DDI) can be found in which section?

choices.A: Section 3: The Basics
choices.B: Section 4: Signs
choices.C: Section 6: Driving Situations
choices.D: Section 8: Handling Emergencies

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Diverging Diamond Interchange (DDI)' under Section 6: Driving Situations.

en.question: In which section of the handbook would you find information specifically about the dangers of drowsy driving?

choices.A: Section 1: Driving Test Requirements
choices.B: Section 7: Driving Conditions
choices.C: Section 8: Handling Emergencies
choices.D: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors

en.explanation: The Table of Contents shows that 'Drowsy Driving' is a subsection within Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.

en.question: The introductory letter from the DMV Administrator lists several key behaviors for safe driving. Which of the following is one of the listed recommendations?

choices.A: Always drive in the right-most lane.
choices.B: Avoid driving during rush hour.
choices.C: Eliminate distractions and focus on the vehicle.
choices.D: Check your tire pressure before every trip.

en.explanation: The handbook's introductory letter advises new drivers to 'Eliminate distractions and focus on safely operating the vehicle.'

en.question: The handbook provides a resource for learning about online safety to prevent human trafficking. What is the website mentioned for these tips?

choices.A: wisconsindmv.gov
choices.B: tatnonprofit.org/youth
choices.C: love146.org/online-safety
choices.D: KnowToDrive.com/Wisconsin

en.explanation: To learn tips for staying safe online from traffickers, the handbook directs readers to love146.org/online-safety.

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, information about the rules for driving near school buses is located in which part of the manual?

choices.A: Section 3: The Basics
choices.B: Section 6: Driving Situations
choices.C: Section 10: Sharing the Road
choices.D: Section 4: Signs

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'School Buses' as a topic under Section 10: Sharing the Road.

en.question: How does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook define human trafficking?

choices.A: The act of illegally crossing state lines.
choices.B: Driving without a valid license or insurance.
choices.C: Manipulating someone to work or provide sex acts for money.
choices.D: Knowingly transporting undocumented individuals.

en.explanation: The handbook defines human trafficking as when 'a person manipulates or takes advantage of someone else so they will work for them or provide sex acts for money.'

en.question: If you wanted to review the meanings of different types of line markings on the road, which section of the handbook should you consult?

choices.A: Section 3: The Basics
choices.B: Section 4: Signs
choices.C: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls
choices.D: Section 7: Driving Conditions

en.explanation: The Table of Contents indicates that Section 5 covers 'Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls,' which includes types of line markings.

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, which of the following is NOT a category of sign discussed in Section 4?

choices.A: Regulatory
choices.B: Service
choices.C: School Zone
choices.D: Destination

en.explanation: The Table of Contents for Section 4 lists Warning, Regulatory, Construction, Destination, Service, Mile Marker, Route Number, and Railroad Crossing signs. 'School Zone' is a type of sign but not listed as a main category in this section.

en.question: For drivers aged 15-17, the handbook cover promotes taking the knowledge test at home. What website is provided for this purpose?

choices.A: wisconsindmv.gov
choices.B: KnowToDrive.com/Wisconsin
choices.C: love146.org/online-safety
choices.D: tatnonprofit.org/youth

en.explanation: The cover of the handbook directs 15-17 year olds to KnowToDrive.com/Wisconsin to learn more about taking the knowledge test at home.

en.question: The handbook describes a three-part commitment to safety from the Wisconsin Department of Transportation. Besides the DMV and the Wisconsin State Patrol, what is the third component mentioned?

choices.A: County sheriff departments enforcing local ordinances.
choices.B: Driver education schools providing behind-the-wheel training.
choices.C: The engineering of roads using a Safe System approach.
choices.D: The court system which penalizes unsafe drivers.

en.explanation: The letter from the DMV Administrator states that safety is achieved through the DMV, the State Patrol, and the fact that 'Wisconsin’s roads are engineered through a strategic Safe System approach to highway safety.'

en.question: Based on the Table of Contents, where would you find information regarding farm safety and rural driving?

choices.A: Section 3: The Basics
choices.B: Section 10: Sharing the Road
choices.C: Section 8: Handling Emergencies
choices.D: Section 7: Driving Conditions

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'Farm Safety/Rural Driving' as a topic under Section 7, 'Driving Conditions.'

en.question: Approximately how much time should you allow to complete the Wisconsin knowledge test at a DMV customer service center?

choices.A: 15 minutes
choices.B: 30 minutes
choices.C: 45 minutes
choices.D: 60 minutes

en.explanation: Section 1, Part C states, 'This test will take about 45 minutes to complete.'

en.question: What is the minimum percentage of questions you must answer correctly to pass both the Highway Signs Test and the Knowledge Test?
en.explanation: Section 1 states you need to answer 12 of 15 questions (80%) correctly on the signs test and 40 of 50 questions (80%) correctly on the knowledge test.

en.question: During the skills test, the DMV examiner will test your ability to perform specific maneuvers. Which of the following is listed as a required maneuver?

choices.A: Three-point turn
choices.B: Y-turn
choices.C: Parallel parking on a hill
choices.D: Emergency braking

en.explanation: Section 1, Part D lists maneuvers tested, including 'a Y-turn, roadside stop/start and parking.'

en.question: When presenting documents to the DMV to apply for a driver license, what is a key requirement for all items?

choices.A: They can be photocopies if the original is not available.
choices.B: They must be original or certified copies, and not expired.
choices.C: They can be expired by up to 30 days.
choices.D: Only proof of residency must be original.

en.explanation: Section 2 states, 'All the items above must be valid – no photocopies and not expired.'

en.question: According to the manual, which of the following is an acceptable document to prove your identity?

choices.A: A student ID card from your school.
choices.B: A credit card with your name on it.
choices.C: A Social Security card with your signature.
choices.D: A utility bill in your name.

en.explanation: Section 2 lists 'Social Security card with your signature or a state issued ID card with your photograph' as examples of proof of identity.

en.question: Besides accepting legal and financial liability, what must an adult sponsor for a driver under 18 also verify?

choices.A: That the minor has their own car insurance.
choices.B: That the minor has a GPA of 2.0 or higher.
choices.C: That the minor is enrolled in a school program and not habitually truant.
choices.D: That the minor has completed a first-aid course.

en.explanation: Section 2, Part A states the sponsor will 'sign and verify that the person under 18 years of age is enrolled in a school program and is not habitually truant.'

en.question: What does the manual state regarding a sponsor's ability to withdraw their sponsorship for a minor driver?

choices.A: Sponsorship can only be removed if the minor gets a traffic ticket.
choices.B: Sponsorship can be removed at any time.
choices.C: Sponsorship can only be removed with a court order.
choices.D: Sponsorship is permanent until the driver turns 18.

en.explanation: Section 2, Part A states, 'The sponsor may remove their sponsorship at any time.'

en.question: If a teen applicant under 18 is not living with a parent or legal guardian, who is permitted to sign as a sponsor?

choices.A: A close family friend over age 25.
choices.B: A teacher or school principal.
choices.C: A sibling who is 18 years of age or older.
choices.D: A licensed driver who has known the applicant for 5 years.

en.explanation: Section 2, Part A lists 'Sibling 18 years of age or older' as a potential sponsor if the teen applicant is not living with a parent or legal guardian.

en.question: If you do not pass the vision screening at the DMV, you will be referred to a vision specialist with what specific form?

choices.A: MV2020 Vision Report
choices.B: Certificate of Vision Examination by Competent Authority (MV3030V/T579)
choices.C: Driver Vision Health Certificate (DVHC-1)
choices.D: Medical Examination Report (MV3030B)

en.explanation: Section 1, Part A specifies that if you do not pass the vision test, you will be given the 'Certificate of Vision Examination by Competent Authority (MV3030V/T579)' to take to a vision specialist.

en.question: How many total questions are on the Wisconsin driver license knowledge test?
en.explanation: Section 1, Part C states, 'The knowledge test will include 50 questions.'

en.question: Before your skills test begins, the DMV examiner will perform a safety check on your vehicle. Which of the following items will be checked?

choices.A: Tire tread depth and air pressure
choices.B: Engine oil and coolant levels
choices.C: Radio and air conditioning
choices.D: Horn, lights, and mirrors

en.explanation: Section 1, Part D states the examiner will check the 'horn, lights/signals, license plates, doors, mirrors and more.'

en.question: Which of the following is listed as an acceptable example of a document that proves you live in Wisconsin?

choices.A: A letter from a friend
choices.B: A library card
choices.C: A personal check with your address
choices.D: A utility bill with your name and address

en.explanation: Section 2 gives 'Utility bill or financial statement with your name and WI address listed' as examples for proving you live in Wisconsin.

en.question: For a driver under age 18, how long is an adult sponsor required?

choices.A: Only for the instruction permit phase.
choices.B: Until the driver completes 50 hours of practice.
choices.C: Through the probationary phase until the driver turns 18.
choices.D: For the first six months of the probationary license.

en.explanation: Section 2, Part A states, 'You will still need a sponsor during your probationary phase until you turn 18.'

en.question: According to the Table of Contents, which section of the manual contains information about Wisconsin's driver Point System?

choices.A: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors
choices.B: Section 11: Your Driving Privilege
choices.C: Section 12: Other Important Information
choices.D: Section 2: Progression of Licenses

en.explanation: The Table of Contents shows 'Section 11: Your Driving Privilege' contains the subsection 'A. Point System.'

en.question: Based on the Table of Contents, where would you find information on the minimum Insurance Requirements for drivers in Wisconsin?

choices.A: Section 12: Other Important Information
choices.B: Section 10: Sharing the Road
choices.C: Section 11: Your Driving Privilege
choices.D: Section 1: Driving Test Requirements

en.explanation: The Table of Contents lists 'E. Insurance Requirements' under 'Section 12: Other Important Information.'

en.question: What kind of instructions should you expect from the DMV examiner during your skills test?

choices.A: Trick questions to test your attention
choices.B: Vague directions to see how you react
choices.C: Simple, direct commands like 'turn left' or 'Make a Y-Turn'
choices.D: A complete list of all maneuvers before the test begins

en.explanation: Section 1, Part D states, 'The DMV examiner will give you instructions like, “At the next intersection, turn left,” or “Make a Y-Turn.”'

en.question: If an instruction permit holder under 18 is driving with a person who is not a qualified instructor, parent, guardian, or spouse, what is the minimum age for that accompanying person?
en.explanation: The manual states the accompanying person can be 'A person 21 years of age or older. If the permit holder is under 18 years old, the accompanying licensed person is required to have written authorization from the minor’s parent or guardian...'

en.question: Under Graduated Driver License (GDL) restrictions, how many people who are NOT immediate family members can ride with you between 5 a.m. and midnight?

choices.A: One
choices.B: Two
choices.C: Three
choices.D: Zero

en.explanation: The manual states that from 5 a.m. to midnight, a GDL holder can drive with 'One other person' in addition to immediate family or a qualified accompanying driver.

en.question: Beginning on what date will a REAL ID-compliant card (or other acceptable form of ID) be required to fly within the U.S. or visit a military base?

choices.A: January 1, 2025
choices.C: July 4, 2026
choices.D: December 31, 2024

en.explanation: According to the manual, 'you will be required to show identification that is REAL ID-compliant...beginning May 7, 2025.'

en.question: For a probationary license holder, what happens to the demerit points for a second or future moving traffic violation conviction?

choices.A: They are cut in half
choices.B: They stay the same
choices.C: They are doubled
choices.D: They are forgiven

en.explanation: The manual states, 'The restrictions are similar to the permit as the points on second or future convictions double.'

en.question: To get a probationary license, a driver under 18 must complete a minimum of how many hours of supervised driving during hours of darkness?

choices.A: 5 hours
choices.B: 10 hours
choices.C: 20 hours
choices.D: 40 hours

en.explanation: The manual requires a total of 50 hours of practice, '10 of which must be during hours of darkness.'

en.question: What is the maximum amount of time in advance of its expiration date that you can renew a regular Wisconsin driver license?

choices.A: 60 days
choices.B: 90 days
choices.C: 6 months
choices.D: 1 year

en.explanation: The manual states, 'You can renew your license up to a year in advance from the expiration date.'

en.question: If you move to Wisconsin and your previous state's driver license is a REAL ID, what must you do to get a Wisconsin REAL ID?

choices.A: Your REAL ID status automatically transfers.
choices.B: You only need to show your old REAL ID card.
choices.C: You must present all acceptable documents again in Wisconsin.
choices.D: You must wait 60 days before applying.

en.explanation: When asked if a REAL ID from another state will transfer, the manual answers, 'No. You will need to present all acceptable documents to Wisconsin.'

en.question: If you are an instruction permit holder who is at least 16 years old, under what condition can an additional person ride in a seat other than the front?

choices.A: The person is an immediate family member.
choices.B: The person is also a qualified instructor.
choices.C: The person is licensed, 25 or older, with at least 2 years of experience.
choices.D: No additional passengers are ever allowed.

en.explanation: The manual notes: 'If you are at least 16 years of age, in addition to the licensed accompanying driver, one other licensed person 25 years of age or more with at least 2 years driving experience may occupy a seat in the vehicle other than the front seat.'

en.question: If you are under 18 and enrolled in a driver education program, what signed form must your behind-the-wheel school provide before you can apply for an instruction permit?

choices.A: A school report card
choices.B: A certificate of completion
choices.C: Wisconsin Driver License (DL) Application MV3001
choices.D: A parental consent form MV2002

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Your behind-the-wheel school will provide you with a signed Wisconsin Driver License (DL) Application MV3001. You must have this completed before applying for your instruction permit.'

en.question: While driving with a probationary license between 5 a.m. and midnight, how many of your immediate family members are allowed to ride with you?

choices.A: Only one
choices.B: Only your parents
choices.C: Any number
choices.D: Two, if one is a parent

en.explanation: The manual specifies that from 5 a.m. to midnight, 'Any number of immediate family members can ride along' with a GDL holder.

en.question: What is the minimum age for a qualified instructor who is accompanying an instruction permit holder?
en.explanation: The person in the passenger seat must be one of the following: 'A qualified instructor age 19 or older...'

en.question: To qualify for a probationary license, a minor must complete a minimum of 50 total hours of supervised driving. How many of those hours must be during daylight?

choices.A: 10 hours
choices.B: 25 hours
choices.C: 40 hours
choices.D: 50 hours

en.explanation: The manual requires a driver to 'practice driving for at least 40 hours during daylight and 10 hours during darkness (50 total hours).'

en.question: How long before your birthday in your license expiration year will the DMV send you a renewal reminder notice for your regular driver license?

choices.A: 10 to 20 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.C: 45 to 60 days
choices.D: 90 days

en.explanation: The manual states, 'You will receive a renewal reminder notice 45 to 60 days before your birthday in the year your driver license expires.'

en.question: What is the name of the mobile app mentioned in the manual that a sponsor can use to keep track of a student driver's practice hours?

choices.A: DMV Drive
choices.B: RoadReady
choices.C: WI Practice Log
choices.D: GDL Tracker

en.explanation: The manual suggests a sponsor can print a driving log 'or they can download our RoadReady mobile app.'

en.question: To obtain an instruction permit, what must a person who is 18 years or older do?

choices.A: Enroll in a driver education program.
choices.B: Pass the knowledge test, signs test, and vision screening.
choices.C: Complete 50 hours of supervised driving first.
choices.D: Have a sponsor sign their application.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'If you are 18 years or older you can start by passing the knowledge test, highway signs test and the vision screening.' Unlike minors, they are not required to be enrolled in a driver education program.

en.question: Beginning May 7, 2025, what type of identification will be required to fly within the U.S. or visit federal buildings?

choices.A: Any valid state driver license
choices.B: A driver license with a photo
choices.C: A REAL ID-compliant license or another acceptable form, like a passport
choices.D: A vehicle registration certificate

en.explanation: The manual states that beginning May 7, 2025, you will be required to show identification that is REAL ID-compliant (or show another acceptable form of identification, such as a passport) to fly within the U.S. or visit federal buildings.

en.question: Besides your driver license, what two other documents should you ensure you have in your vehicle before driving?

choices.A: Vehicle title and owner's manual
choices.B: Proof of insurance and vehicle registration
choices.C: Birth certificate and social security card
choices.D: Your last vehicle inspection report and a map

en.explanation: Section 3 states that before driving, you should make sure you have your valid driver license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration.

en.question: When using the 'Four Second Following Distance Rule,' you reach your selected stationary object before you finish counting to 'one thousand four.' What does this indicate?

choices.A: You are driving too slowly for conditions.
choices.B: You are following at a safe distance.
choices.C: The vehicle in front of you has slowed down unexpectedly.
choices.D: You are going too fast or following too closely.

en.explanation: The manual explains that if you reach the object before you finish saying, 'one thousand four,' you are going too fast.

en.question: According to the 'Four Second Following Distance Rule,' what adjustment should you make for adverse conditions like rain or snow?

choices.A: Decrease the count to two seconds.
choices.B: Maintain the four-second count regardless of conditions.
choices.C: Add a second for every adverse condition.
choices.D: Only use the rule in perfect weather.

en.explanation: The manual states to 'Add a second for every adverse condition such as heavier traffic, rain, snow and/or ice' when using the following distance rule.

en.question: On a multi-lane road, if you are driving slower than most other traffic, which lane should you use?

choices.A: The far-left lane
choices.B: The center lane
choices.C: The far-right lane
choices.D: Any lane is acceptable

en.explanation: The manual advises, 'Drive in the far-right lane of a multi-lane road if you are driving slower than most traffic.'

en.question: In addition to speeding, which two driving behaviors are explicitly mentioned in the manual as being illegal?

choices.A: Coasting and tailgating
choices.B: Racing and driving recklessly
choices.C: Driving too slowly and not using a turn signal
choices.D: Merging too quickly and changing lanes frequently

en.explanation: The text states, 'Racing and driving recklessly are not allowed and are illegal.'

en.question: When you merge with traffic, you should try to enter at the same speed as traffic in order to avoid what?

choices.A: Getting a speeding ticket
choices.B: Using too much fuel
choices.C: Forcing another driver to change speed or direction
choices.D: Missing your exit

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Avoid forcing another driver to change speed or direction because of you merging.'

en.question: What is the primary function of a deceleration lane, also known as an off-ramp?

choices.A: To allow vehicles to speed up before entering a highway.
choices.B: To provide a space for emergency parking.
choices.C: To allow traffic to slow down gradually when leaving a high-speed roadway.
choices.D: To serve as a U-turn lane on a highway.

en.explanation: The manual explains that 'In the deceleration lane (off-ramp) traffic slows down, this is where you will gradually slow down as well.'

en.question: The manual defines an intersection as where two points cross. Which of the following is listed as an example of an intersection?

choices.A: A sharp curve in the road
choices.B: A driveway or parking lot entrance
choices.C: A bridge or overpass
choices.D: A designated rest area

en.explanation: Section 3 defines intersections and states, 'This includes cross streets, driveways, parking lot entrances and railroad crossings.'

en.question: If your view of an intersection is blocked by trees, buildings, or parked vehicles, how should you proceed?

choices.A: Honk your horn and proceed quickly.
choices.B: Stop completely and wait for another car to go first.
choices.C: Approach at a slow pace and move forward with caution.
choices.D: Turn on your high beams to alert other drivers.

en.explanation: The manual advises, 'Approach a blocked intersection at a slow pace. If you cannot see, move forward with caution.'

en.question: To avoid a crash caused by distraction, what specific roadside activity does the manual warn drivers NOT to look at?

choices.A: Billboards and advertisements
choices.B: Unusual architecture or scenery
choices.C: Drivers that have been pulled over by police
choices.D: Animals grazing near the road

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Do not look at drivers that have been pulled over or other roadside activity. This could cause a crash.'

en.question: If another vehicle is driving in the lane right next to you, what should you do to maintain a safe space cushion around your vehicle?

choices.A: Speed up to get in front of them quickly.
choices.B: Honk your horn to make them move.
choices.C: Stay in the same position and let them pass.
choices.D: Move ahead or drop behind the other vehicle when it is safe.

en.explanation: The manual advises, 'If a vehicle is driving right next to you on a roadway move ahead or move behind the vehicle when it is safe. This will keep space all around your vehicle.'

en.question: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

choices.A: The vehicle that is moving faster.
choices.B: The vehicle on the left.
choices.C: The vehicle coming from the right.
choices.D: The vehicle on the wider road.

en.explanation: The manual states you should yield right-of-way to 'Vehicles coming from the right when there are no signals or traffic lights (uncontrolled intersections).'

en.question: When making a left turn, you must yield the right-of-way to:

choices.A: Vehicles behind you
choices.B: Vehicles turning right from the same direction
choices.C: Approaching vehicles from the opposite direction
choices.D: All pedestrians, even if they are not in a crosswalk

en.explanation: The manual lists that you should yield right-of-way to 'Approaching vehicles if you are making a left turn or a U-turn.'

en.question: The manual recommends adding extra following distance beyond the standard four seconds when you are:

choices.A: driving in light city traffic.
choices.B: following a motorcycle or a large truck.
choices.C: approaching a green traffic light.
choices.D: driving on a straight, dry road.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'You might need to give additional seconds of space in front of you if: ... You are following trucks, buses, vans, large vehicles, motorcycles or bicycles'.

en.question: To maintain awareness of the situation behind your vehicle, how frequently does the manual recommend checking your rearview mirror?

choices.A: Every 2 to 4 seconds.
choices.B: Every 6 to 8 seconds.
choices.C: Every 10 to 12 seconds.
choices.D: Only when you plan to change lanes or turn.

en.explanation: The manual advises to 'Check your rearview mirror every 6 to 8 seconds to see if someone is following too closely (tailgating).'

en.question: Why should you leave extra space for large vehicles like trucks and buses when they are turning?

choices.A: They are required by law to stop completely before turning.
choices.B: They may cross over the center line to complete the turn.
choices.C: Their brake lights are often difficult to see.
choices.D: They have the absolute right-of-way at all intersections.

en.explanation: The manual says to 'Leave extra space to large vehicles such as trucks and buses as they may cross the center line during a turn.'

en.question: When waiting to make a left turn at an intersection with oncoming traffic, where should you position your vehicle?

choices.A: Behind the white stop line until the path is completely clear.
choices.B: In the crosswalk, blocking pedestrians.
choices.C: About halfway into the intersection.
choices.D: In the right lane to allow others to pass.

en.explanation: The manual instructs to 'Slowly approach the intersection and wait about halfway in the intersection. Make sure to leave room for oncoming traffic to turn in front of you.'

en.question: If you are turning left from a street with multiple left-turn lanes and you start in the middle lane, which lane must you enter on the new street?

choices.A: The right-most lane.
choices.B: The left-most lane.
choices.C: The middle lane.
choices.D: Any available lane.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'If you are in the middle lane you need to end up in the middle lane of the street you are turning onto.'

en.question: During the third step of a Y-Turn, what action should you take after stopping at the opposite curb?

choices.A: Signal right and pull forward into the lane of traffic.
choices.B: Turn your steering wheel all the way to the right and stop.
choices.C: Look over your right shoulder and reverse the car enough to move forward.
choices.D: Honk your horn to alert traffic before backing up.

en.explanation: The third step of a Y-Turn is to 'Look behind you, over your right shoulder. Reverse your car enough so that you can move forward again. Stop.'

en.question: What is the correct and safe response if another vehicle is trying to pass you?

choices.A: Speed up to prevent them from passing.
choices.B: Move to the left to block them.
choices.C: Stay in your lane and slow down.
choices.D: Flash your headlights to signal it is unsafe.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'If someone is trying to pass you, stay in your lane and slow down.'

en.question: What is the proper way to check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left?

choices.A: Look only in your rearview mirror.
choices.B: Look only in your left side mirror.
choices.C: Check over your left shoulder.
choices.D: Lean forward to get a better view in your mirrors.

en.explanation: The manual instructs, 'If moving to the left lane, check over your left shoulder.' It also clarifies, 'You cannot see these areas by only looking in your mirrors.'

en.question: What does the manual state about passing multiple vehicles at once?

choices.A: It is allowed if you have a clear view of the road ahead.
choices.B: You should pass only one vehicle at a time.
choices.C: It is safer than passing vehicles individually.
choices.D: You may pass two vehicles at a time, but no more.

en.explanation: The manual warns, 'There might not be enough time to pass several vehicles at once...' and instructs to 'Pass only one vehicle at a time on the left side.'

en.question: When backing up, in addition to using your mirrors and backup camera, what should you do to ensure safety?

choices.A: Turn on your interior dome light.
choices.B: Turn your body and look over your right shoulder through the rear window.
choices.C: Open your driver's side door to look behind you.
choices.D: Rely on the sound of your backup alarm.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'Do not only depend on your mirrors and backup camera when backing up. Turn your body and look behind you and out of your windows. Look over your right shoulder through the rear window.'

en.question: When parking your vehicle with an automatic transmission on a level surface, what should you do after shifting to (P) Park?

choices.A: Turn your wheels towards the curb.
choices.B: Leave the engine running.
choices.C: Set the parking brake.
choices.D: Turn on your hazard lights.

en.explanation: The manual instructs, 'When parking on a level surface, put your vehicle in (P) Park (or in gear if you have a manual transmission) and set the parking brake.'

en.question: How can you help a driver who is following you?

choices.A: By braking suddenly to get them to back off.
choices.B: By speeding up to create more space.
choices.C: By keeping a steady speed and signaling in advance.
choices.D: By weaving slightly within your lane.

en.explanation: The manual suggests, 'You can help a driver behind you by keeping a steady speed and signaling in advance when you need to slow down or turn.'

en.question: When you need to cross traffic on a multi-lane road, what is the most important consideration?

choices.A: Ensuring you have enough room to get all the way across.
choices.B: Honking your horn before you start to cross.
choices.C: Crossing as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting someone off.
choices.D: Waiting for a police officer to direct you.

en.explanation: The manual states, 'When you cross traffic and multi-lane roads make sure there is enough room to get all the way across.'

en.question: According to the manual, what type of unsafe action when turning can lead to a crash?

choices.A: Signaling too early.
choices.B: Making a last-second change in your path.
choices.C: Turning too slowly.
choices.D: Checking your mirrors more than once.

en.explanation: The manual warns, 'Last second changes are unsafe and could cause a crash.'

en.question: On a multi-lane road, what is the intended use of the lane farthest to the left?

choices.A: For drivers traveling at or below the speed limit.
choices.B: For vehicles to go around slower ones.
choices.C: For emergency vehicles only.
choices.D: For vehicles preparing to exit on the right.
